Strict typing, no `any`; define interfaces for all API responses and component props. Handle API errors in the UI (`try/catch` / `.catch`). UI strings go through `i18n.tsx`. Call the API with relative URLs (works with the Vite proxy and the embedded build; backend port is `55000` by default).

head: Coding Standards & Guidelines
text: * **Language:** code, comments and commit messages in English; end-user texts are localized (RU/EN in the frontend and in the tray, see `backend/tray/lang.go`).

head: Environment & Setup
text: * Go 1.26.2+ (per `go.mod`), Yarn 1.22.x, Node 22 (CI). `release.yml` reads the Go version from `go.mod`; `Dockerfile` pins `golang:1.26-alpine` — bump it together with the `go` directive.

head: Environment & Setup
text: * Local server strictly on the configured port (default `55000`); the tray "force update" and browser opening use this port.

head: Environment & Setup
text: * The app modifies OS autostart entries on every start (`startup.Add`) — be careful when running it on a dev machine; it registers the current exe path.

head: Environment & Setup
text: * Sing-box (`sagernet/sing-box`) is a heavy dependency; the first `go build` is slow. `backend/test.exe` is a git-ignored local artifact — never commit binaries.

head: Git Workflow
text: * **Commit Messages:** Conventional Commits (`feat: add new proxy source`, `fix: resolve race condition in cache`, `chore: update dependencies`).

head: Git Workflow
text: * **Branching:** isolated feature/bugfix branches; PRs target `main`.

head: Git Workflow
text: * **Before a PR:** `cd frontend && yarn lint && yarn build`, then `cd backend && go vet ./... && go build ./...`. If you changed platform-specific or release-related code, sanity-check with `GOOS=linux`/`darwin` where possible (`go vet` with `GOOS` set, CGO permitting).

head: Git Workflow
text: * **Releases:** pushing a `v*` tag triggers `release.yml`; the tag (without `v`) becomes `main.version`, which the updater compares against GitHub's latest release.

head: AGENTS.md > 项目概述
text: Tida.CAD 是一个基于 .NET 的 CAD 画布框架，提供平台无关的核心层（图层、绘制对象、坐标转换、输入与事件），并内置 **WPF** 与 **Avalonia** 两套 UI 实现（同一套绘制代码可运行于两个框架）。核心为共享工程 `Tida.CAD/`，通过条件编译（`#if WPF` / `#if Avalonia`）区分平台代码；渲染采用每图层一个 `DrawingVisual`，绘制对象内容以 `DrawingGroup` 缓存。

head: AGENTS.md > 工具使用
text: - 没有特殊要求的情况下，优先使用内置的 Edit 工具，而不是生成 PowerShell 或 Python 脚本来做临时的编辑操作

head: AGENTS.md > 工具使用
text: - 如果一定要使用脚本修改文件，在Windows 环境下修改文件内容优先使用 **PowerShell**（.ps1 脚本），避免使用 Python 处理文件读写，防止字符串转义问题

head: AGENTS.md > 工具使用
text: - 脚本先写入 `c:\tmp\` 再通过 `powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File` 执行

text: - 所有条件语句（`if`/`else if`/`else`）和循环语句（`for`/`foreach`/`while`/`do-while`），无论后续语句数量是一条还是多条，都必须使用花括号 `{}`

AGENTS.md > 代码标准 > LINQ 风格

head: AGENTS.md > 代码标准 > 嵌套深度

head: AGENTS.md > 代码标准 > 嵌套深度

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration
text: This project comes with custom hooks for querying and publishing events on the Nostr network.

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration > The `useNostr` Hook
text: The `useNostr` hook returns an object containing a `nostr` property, with `.query()` and `.event()` methods for querying and publishing Nostr events respectively.

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration > Query Nostr Data with `useNostr` and Tanstack Query
text: When querying Nostr, the best practice is to create custom hooks that combine `useNostr` and `useQuery` to get the required data.

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration > Query Nostr Data with `useNostr` and Tanstack Query
text: The data may be transformed into a more appropriate format if needed, and multiple calls to `nostr.query()` may be made in a single queryFn.

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration > The `useAuthor` Hook
text: To display profile data for a user by their Nostr pubkey (such as an event author), use the `useAuthor` hook.

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration > The `useNostrPublish` Hook
text: To publish events, use the `useNostrPublish` hook in this project.

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration > The `useNostrPublish` Hook
text: The `useCurrentUser` hook should be used to ensure that the user is logged in before they are able to publish Nostr events.

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration > Nostr Login
text: To enable login with Nostr, simply use the `LoginArea` component already included in this project.

head: Project Overview > Nostr Protocol Integration > Nostr Login
text: The `LoginArea` component displays a "Log in" button when the user is logged out, and changes to an account switcher once the user is logged in. It handles all the login-related UI and interactions internally, including displaying login dialogs and switching between accounts.

head: Project Overview > `npub`, `naddr`, and other Nostr addresses
text: Nostr defines a set identifiers in NIP-19. Their prefixes:

head: Project Overview > `npub`, `naddr`, and other Nostr addresses
text: - `nprofile`: a nostr profile

head: Project Overview > `npub`, `naddr`, and other Nostr addresses
text: - `nevent`: a nostr event

head: Project Overview > `npub`, `naddr`, and other Nostr addresses
text: - `naddr`: a nostr replaceable event coordinate

head: Project Overview > `npub`, `naddr`, and other Nostr addresses
text: - `nrelay`: a nostr relay (deprecated)

head: Project Overview > `npub`, `naddr`, and other Nostr addresses
text: NIP-19 identifiers include a prefix, the number "1", then a base32-encoded data string.

head: Project Overview > `npub`, `naddr`, and other Nostr addresses > Use in Filters
text: The base Nostr protocol uses hex string identifiers for filtering by event IDs, pubkeys, and signatures. Nostr filters only accept hex strings.

head: ccman 项目开发规范 > ESLint 规则说明 > 已禁用的规则及原因
text: 虽然项目初期设定了严格的代码限制（每个函数 < 50 行，每个文件 < 300 行），但在实践中发现以下规则会干扰合理的代码组织：

head: ccman 项目开发规范 > ESLint 规则说明 > 已禁用的规则及原因
text:
1. **`max-lines` 和 `max-lines-per-function`（已关闭）**
   - **原因**：某些特定文件和函数有合理的理由超出限制：
     - **工厂函数**：如 `createToolManager()` 返回包含 13 个方法的对象，"长度"来自返回多个方法而非复杂逻辑
     - **数据驱动**：`tool-manager.ts` 虽然超过 300 行，但每个方法都简单清晰，工厂函数不应拆分
   - **替代方案**：使用 `/* eslint-disable max-lines */` 和 `// eslint-disable-next-line max-lines-per-function` 注释在特定文件/函数级别禁用
   - **人工审查**：通过 Code Review 确保代码质量，而不是机械地限制行数

head: ccman 项目开发规范 > ESLint 规则说明 > 已禁用的规则及原因
text:
2. **`complexity`（已关闭）**
   - **原因**：某些业务逻辑的复杂度不可避免：
     - **edit 方法**：需要检查存在性、名称冲突、更新 4+ 个可选字段、同步配置，每个 if 都不可避免
   - **替代方案**：在必要时使用 `// eslint-disable-next-line complexity` 注释
   - **判断标准**：复杂度来自必要的业务逻辑（无特殊情况、无嵌套逻辑）时可以接受

head: ccman 项目开发规范 > ESLint 规则说明 > 已禁用的规则及原因

3. **`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`（已关闭）**

head: AGENTS.md
text: Instructions for AI coding agents working in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements
text: Maintainers need to be able to tell at a glance when a coding agent contributed to a change. If you are a coding agent, you MUST disclose that in every commit you create and in every pull request you open, regardless of how small the change is.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements
text: The human developer who directed you remains the author and is responsible for the change. Attribution supplements that; it does not replace it.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Commits
text: Add a `Co-authored-by` trailer to every commit message, naming the agent that produced the change. The trailer goes at the end of the message, separated from the body by a blank line.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Commits
text: Use the identity that matches the agent you are:

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Commits
text:
| Agent | Trailer |
| --- | --- |
| Claude / Claude Code | `Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` |
| OpenAI Codex | `Co-authored-by: Codex <noreply@openai.com>` |
| GitHub Copilot | `Co-authored-by: Copilot <noreply@github.com>` |
| Cursor | `Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>` |
| Gemini CLI | `Co-authored-by: Gemini <noreply@google.com>` |
| Any other agent | `Co-authored-by: <Agent Name> <noreply@<vendor-domain>>` |

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Commits
text: - Always name the specific agent. Never use a vague label such as "AI" or "bot".

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Commits
text: - Keep one trailer per agent. If several agents contributed, add one trailer for each.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Commits
text: - Do not remove or rewrite existing trailers when amending or rebasing.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Commits
text: - Do not add the human developer's name as an agent, and do not impersonate a human.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Pull request descriptions
text: Every PR description must include an attribution line stating which agent was used. Put it in its own section at the bottom of the description:

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Pull request descriptions
text: - Name the agent and, when you know it, the model or version used.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Pull request descriptions
text: - If the agent wrote or substantially edited the PR description itself, say so.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Pull request descriptions
text: - Keep the attribution when the description is edited later. Do not delete it.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Pull request descriptions
text: - If a PR contains a mix of human-written and agent-written commits, still include the attribution line.

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Checklist before committing or opening a PR
text: 1. Does every commit you contributed to include the correct `Co-authored-by` trailer?

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Checklist before committing or opening a PR
text: 2. Does the PR description include the attribution section naming your agent?

head: AGENTS.md > Attribution requirements > Checklist before committing or opening a PR
text: 3. Is the attribution accurate, with no overstating or understating of what the agent did?
Read `README.md`, `doc.md`, `remote/constants.schema.json`, and `remote/config.schema.json` to understand this repo.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - When given a coding task, AI Assistant carefully and deeply inspects the codebase to understand the context.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - If the Assistant has access to search tools, it uses them to search for documentation and use case examples for external libraries.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - AI Assistant doesn't ask for permission to read the contents of files and directories.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - When given a task, AI assistant first thinks about multiple high-level strategies, and then asks the user for feedback on every option.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - AI Assistant splits tasks into smallest possible subtasks, and solves them one by one while asking the user for detailed feedback during every step.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - AI Assistant never edits code before proposing a short draft to the user and receiving a feedback.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - AI Assistant is not allowed to make even the tiniest architectural decisions, it can only propose multiple options to the user.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - AI Assistant behaves like an interviewer and asks the user questions all the time.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - AI Assistant never relies on its own assumptions about implementation details of libraries and tools. It always makes sure to check the reference.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - Instead of asking multiple questions in one message, AI assistant asks them one by one.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - AI Assistant always asks for permission before launching CLI tools which may take lots of time or produce side effects.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - Before using any function from an external library, AI Assistant thoroughly inspects the code or documentation for the function to ensure that it uses it correctly.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - When encountering an error, AI Assistant never rushes to quickly fix it. Instead, it uses the scientific method to understand the source of the error: comes up with hypotheses and tests them by performing a series of experiments. It only attempts to fix the error once the hypothesis has been sufficiently validated.

head: Workflow rules:
text: - AI Assistant avoids creating .md files with explanations unless explicitly requested by the user.

head: General coding guidelines:
text: - AI Assistant never resorts to quick hacks or stubs to make something work. Instead it always investigates the problem thoroughly and comes up with a well-thought-out solution.

head: General coding guidelines:

head: General coding guidelines:

head: AI Agent Development Guide for ZoneMinder > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: - **Shared Memory**: `zmc` writes frames to `/dev/shm`; `zma` and `zms` read from same buffers. Zero-copy for performance — this is why ZM can handle many cameras on modest hardware.

head: AI Agent Development Guide for ZoneMinder > Architecture > Key Patterns

head: AI Agent Development Guide for ZoneMinder > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: - **Pluggable Cameras**: Abstract `Camera` base with: `LocalCamera` (V4L2), `RemoteCameraHTTP`, `FFmpegCamera`, `LibVNCCamera`. Add new camera types by subclassing Camera.

head: AI Agent Development Guide for ZoneMinder > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: - **Event-Driven Recording**: Motion detection triggers `Event` objects with pre/post alarm buffers. Lifecycle: Create -> Record -> Close -> Archive/Delete. Events are the core unit of recorded footage.

head: AI Agent Development Guide for ZoneMinder > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: - **Multi-Server Clustering**: Database-coordinated distributed architecture with shared monitors and storage.

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md
text: Autonomous DLMM liquidity provider agent for Meteora pools on Solana.

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md
text:
> **Audience**: future agents/sessions that need to make non-trivial changes
> (add a tool, change a safety rule, fix a cron race, extend a state file)
> without re-reading the whole repo. The README stays user-facing; this
> file is the engineering manual.

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md > TL;DR (read this first)
text:
- **What it is**: Node 22+ ESM service that runs an LLM-driven loop
  (OpenAI-compatible) to screen Meteora DLMM pools, deploy SOL into
  long/short positions, monitor them, and close them — all without a human
  in the loop. Telegram + Discord provide ops surface; HiveMind provides
  shared learning.

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md > TL;DR (read this first)
text:
- **Entry points**: `node index.js` (full daemon — REPL + cron + Telegram),
  `node cli.js <cmd>` (one-shot CLI), `node setup.js` (first-run wizard).

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md > TL;DR (read this first)
text:
- **Two agent roles run automatically**:
  - `SCREENER` — every `screeningIntervalMin` minutes, picks a pool,
    calls `deploy_position`.
  - `MANAGER` — every `managementIntervalMin` minutes, evaluates open
    positions, claims/closes them.

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md > TL;DR (read this first)
text:
- **`GENERAL`** role handles ad-hoc chat (REPL, Telegram, Claude Code
  slash commands) and dispatches to a role-filtered tool subset based on
  intent-pattern matching of the user's goal.

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md > TL;DR (read this first)
text:
- **All state lives in JSON files at the repo root** — see
  [§ Persistent files](#persistent-files) below. There is no DB.

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md > TL;DR (read this first)
text:
- **"Always first read the rest of this file"** — there are real
  cross-cutting invariants (lazy SDK load, ONCE_PER_SESSION tool locks,
  position-cache TTL, trailing-TP 15s recheck) that are easy to break.

head: Meridian — CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module responsibilities (read me before editing)
text:
| File | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| **Entry / orchestration** | | |
| `index.js` | ~2016 | Daemon. Cron, REPL, Telegram bot, briefing, HiveMind bootstrap, PnL poller, deterministic close rules, single-candidate skip rule, settings menu. **All** automatic cycles start here. |
| `agent.js` | 416 | `agentLoop(goal, maxSteps, history, agentType, model, maxOut, opts)`. The ReAct loop. Provider fallback, JSON repair, once-per-session tool locks, no-tool retries, `onToolStart`/`onToolFinish` callbacks for live Telegram messages. |
| `cli.js` | 676 | One-shot CLI; every tool exposed as a subcommand. Also writes a `~/.meridian/SKILL.md` at startup for agent discovery. Loads `.env`/`user-config.json` from `~/.meridian/` if present, else from cwd. |
| `setup.js` | ~750 | Interactive first-run wizard. Three presets (degen/moderate/safe) + custom. Covers strategy, screening filters, position sizing, trailing TP, per-role models. |
| **Config & state** | | |
| `config.js` | 278 | Loads `user-config.json` → live `config` object. Sections: `risk`, `screening`, `management`, `strategy`, `schedule`, `llm`, `darwin`, `tokens`, `hiveMind`, `api`, `jupiter`, `indicators`. Exposes `computeDeployAmount(walletSol)`, `reloadScreeningThresholds()`. `MIN_SAFE_BINS_BELOW = 35` (exported). |
| `prompt.js` | 176 | `buildSystemPrompt(agentType, …)`. Three role-specific prompts. MANAGER is intentionally lean (positions pre-loaded into goal). SCREENER gets bins_below formula. |
| **Tools layer** | | |
| `tools/definitions.js` | 1124 | OpenAI-format tool schemas. **Source of truth for what the LLM sees.** All 40+ tool names listed. |
| `tools/executor.js` | 844 | `executeTool(name, args)`. Pre-flight safety checks for `PROTECTED_TOOLS = {deploy, claim, close, swap, self_update}`. Validates pool thresholds via fresh pool discovery call before deploy. Post-tool side-effects: telegram notifications, pool-memory auto-annotation on `low yield` close, auto-swap base→SOL on close. |
| `tools/dlmm.js` | huge | Meteora DLMM SDK wrapper. **Lazy-loads** `@meteora-ag/dlmm` to avoid CJS-import-time crash in DRY_RUN/test. Pool cache (5 min), metadata cache (15 min), positions cache (5 min TTL + inflight dedup). `deployPosition`, `getMyPositions`, `getPositionPnl`, `getActiveBin`, `closePosition`, `claimFees`, `searchPools`, `getWalletPositions`, `addLiquidity`, `withdrawLiquidity`. Also has relay-mode (zap-in via LPAgent) and wide-range path (multi-tx `createExtendedEmptyPosition` + `addLiquidityByStrategyChunkable` for >69 bin ranges). Asserts Meteora bin-array initialization rent never charged. |
| `tools/screening.js` | 862 | `discoverPools`, `getTopCandidates` (hard filter + enrich + score), `getPoolDetail`. Scoring = `fee_tvl*1000 + organic*10 + vol/100 + holders/100`. Has Discord signal merge/only modes, PVP-rival detection. |
| `tools/wallet.js` | 251 | `getWalletBalances` (Helius), `swapToken` (Jupiter Swap V2). `normalizeMint` collapses "SOL"/"native"/any So1-prefixed token to wrapped-SOL. Built-in referral: 50 bps to a fixed address (configurable). |
| `tools/token.js` | 209 | `getTokenInfo` (Jupiter datapi), `getTokenHolders` (top 100 + filter pool-tagged), `getTokenNarrative` (Jupiter ChainInsight). Cross-references smart wallets from `smart-wallets.json`. |
| `tools/study.js` | 152 | `studyTopLPers` → Agent Meridian `/top-lp` + `/study-top-lp`. Returns ranked LPer patterns (avg hold, win rate, preferred strategy). |
| `tools/agent-meridian.js` | 110 | `agentMeridianJson(path, opts)` with retry/backoff. Default base = `https://api.agentmeridian.xyz/api`. |
| `tools/chart-indicators.js` | 299 | `confirmIndicatorPreset({mint, side})`. Eight presets: `supertrend_break`, `rsi_reversal`, `bollinger_reversion`, `rsi_plus_supertrend`, `supertrend_or_rsi`, `bb_plus_rsi`, `fibo_reclaim`, `fibo_reject`. Fetches from Agent Meridian `/chart-indicators/{mint}`. |
| **Persistence (all `.json` at repo root)** | | |
| `state.js` | 513 | `trackPosition`, `markOutOfRange/InRange`, `recordClaim`, `recordClose`, `setPositionInstruction`, `updatePnlAndCheckExits` (the deterministic rules: STOP_LOSS, TRAILING_TP, OUT_OF_RANGE, LOW_YIELD), `getStateSummary`. `syncOpenPositions` reconciles local state with on-chain after 5 min grace. |
| `pool-memory.js` | 405 | Per-pool deploy history + rolling 48-snapshot trend (5min × 4h). Computes `avg_pnl_pct`, `win_rate`, `adjusted_win_rate` (excludes OOR pumps). text: This Agents.md file provides comprehensive guidance for AI assistants and coding agents (like Claude, Gemini, Cursor, and others) to work with this codebase.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server
text:
This repository contains the podman-mcp-server project,
a Go-based Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides container management capabilities using Podman or Docker.
This MCP server enables AI assistants (like Claude, Gemini, Cursor, and others) to interact with container runtimes using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Project Structure and Repository layout
text:
- Go package layout follows the standard Go conventions:
  - `cmd/podman-mcp-server/` – main application entry point.
  - `pkg/` – libraries grouped by domain.
    - `api/` - SDK-agnostic types for tool definitions (`ServerTool`, `ToolHandlerFunc`, `ToolHandlerParams`).
    - `config/` - Server configuration (`Config` struct, defaults, and override merging).
    - `mcp/` - Model Context Protocol (MCP) server implementation using the official Go SDK, with tool definitions for containers, images, networks, and volumes.
    - `podman/` - Podman/Docker abstraction layer with interface definition, implementation registry, CLI and REST API implementations.
    - `podman-mcp-server/cmd/` - CLI command definition using Cobra framework.
    - `version/` - Version information management.
  - `internal/test/` – shared test utilities (McpSuite, mock Podman API server).

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Project Structure and Repository layout
text: - `.github/` – GitHub-related configuration (Actions workflows, Dependabot).

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Project Structure and Repository layout
text:
- `build/` – modular Makefile includes for packaging targets.
  - `node.mk` – NPM packaging targets (npm-copy-binaries, npm-copy-project-files, npm-publish).
  - `python.mk` – Python/PyPI packaging targets (python-publish).

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Project Structure and Repository layout
text: - `npm/` – Node packages that wrap the compiled binaries for distribution through npmjs.com.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Project Structure and Repository layout
text: - `python/` – Python package providing a script that downloads the correct platform binary from the GitHub releases page and runs it for distribution through pypi.org.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Project Structure and Repository layout
text: - `Makefile` – core build tasks; includes `build/*.mk` for packaging targets.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Feature development
text:
Implement new functionality in the Go sources under `cmd/` and `pkg/`.
The JavaScript (`npm/`) and Python (`python/`) directories only wrap the compiled binary for distribution (npm and PyPI).
Most changes will not require touching them unless the version or packaging needs to be updated.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Tests > Testing Philosophy
text: This project follows these testing principles:

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Tests > Testing Philosophy
text: 1. **Black-box Testing**: Tests verify behavior and observable outcomes, not implementation details. Test the public API (MCP tools) through the test client.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Tests > Testing Philosophy
text: 2. **Real CLI with Mock Backend**: Instead of mocking the podman CLI, tests use the real podman binary pointing to a mock HTTP server. This provides realistic testing of the full CLI-to-API pipeline.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Tests > Testing Philosophy
text: 3. **Nested Test Structure**: Use `s.Run()` subtests for related scenarios within a single test function. This provides clear organization and focused failure identification.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Tests > Testing Philosophy
text: 4. **Scenario-Based Setup**: Set up mock responses before calling the tool, then verify both the result and that the expected API calls were made.

head: Project Agents.md for Podman MCP Server > Tests > Testing Philosophy
text: 5. **Single Assertion Per Subtest**: Each `s.Run()` block should assert ONE specific condition for clear failure identification.

text: MV3 Chrome extension. Phase 1: reads the `their_vote` Bumble sends to the client and badges each card (liked-you / passed / new). Phase 2: a signed `SERVER_GET_USER` "READOUT" dossier showing every reversed profile field (the `706` desirability score, prompts, verification, location, etc.).

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Architecture (two worlds)
text: - **`dist/page.js`** — `world: "MAIN"` content script at `document_start`. Patches `fetch`/XHR to intercept `SERVER_GET_ENCOUNTERS`; hosts the signed `SERVER_GET_USER` RPC client. Source: `src/page/*`, `src/shared/*`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Architecture (two worlds)
text: - **`dist/content.js`** — isolated-world content script at `document_idle`. Badge + dossier UI + cache + `chrome.storage` persistence. Source: `src/content/*`, `src/shared/*`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Architecture (two worlds)
text: - They communicate over `window` `CustomEvent`s. **All channel/RPC names live in `src/shared/constants.ts`** (single source of truth — the two bundles import it, so the strings can't drift).

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Build (Bun-native, no Vite)
text: `build.ts` uses `Bun.build` (`format:"iife"`, `target:"browser"`, `define` for `__DEBUG__` / `__BE_PUBLIC_SAFE__`). **`dist/` is committed** so the extension still loads unpacked with zero build; `manifest.json` points at `dist/`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Build (Bun-native, no Vite)
text: WXT/Plasmo/CRXJS were evaluated (WXT is the 2026 industry default) but are Vite-bound and overkill for a vanilla dual-world extension with no popup/UI framework — Bun-native fits the `document_start` timing and "Bun on everything" better.

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Reverse-proxy test workflow (Chrome MCP)
text: Chrome MCP **blocks the `bumble.com` domain**, and the logged-in Bumble web app **force-redirects off `localhost`** to its canonical region host. To test the extension live in MCP, route Bumble through a local rewriting proxy:

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Reverse-proxy test workflow (Chrome MCP)
text:
1. **Proxy:** `../bumble-api/proxy.py` (run `cd ../bumble-api && uv run python proxy.py`, background). It serves Bumble at `http://localhost:9000`, injecting a hardcoded session server-side and rewriting responses so the SPA can't leave localhost:
   - `TARGET` + `Host` header must be the **session's region host** (e.g. `fr1.bumble.com` — match the account, or it 302-redirects).
   - Rewrites `*.bumble.com` hosts → `localhost:9000` in text bodies; strips CSP / `X-Frame-Options` / `integrity`; injects a shim that neutralizes `location.assign/replace/href` to bumble hosts; de-scopes `Set-Cookie` for localhost.

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Reverse-proxy test workflow (Chrome MCP)
text: 2. **Refresh the session:** the cookies in `proxy.py` expire. Update `SESSION_COOKIES["session"]` (and `HDR-X-User-id` if it changed) from a logged-in DevTools → Application → Cookies, then restart the proxy. Confirm with `curl -so /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:9000/app` → `200`, and that the MCP tab stays on `localhost:9000/app` (not `/get-started` = logged out, not `*.bumble.com` = redirect escaped).

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Reverse-proxy test workflow (Chrome MCP)
text: 3. **Make the extension match localhost:** `manifest.json` `content_scripts.matches` includes `http://localhost:9000/*` (**test-only — strip before any public release**).

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Reverse-proxy test workflow (Chrome MCP)
text: 4. **Reload the extension:** `chrome://extensions` → reload ↻. **MCP cannot navigate `chrome://` URLs**, so the user does this manually; then reload `localhost:9000/app`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Reverse-proxy test workflow (Chrome MCP)
text: 5. Badge appears on the card; open the dossier via the badge (opens on `pointerdown`) or `Cmd/Ctrl+D`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Reverse-proxy test workflow (Chrome MCP)
text: **Validate signing without the browser:** a Python script (uses `bumble_api.auth.compute_pingback`) builds the `SUPER_PROJECTION` envelope and POSTs through the proxy — returns the full profile, proving `X-Pingback` is correct. This is the fastest de-risk and needs no extension reload.

head: CLAUDE.md — Bumble Like Revealer > Reverse-proxy test workflow (Chrome MCP)
text: **Gotcha:** the badge sits inside Bumble's `pointer-events:none` click-through card, so it needs `pointer-events:auto` + `z-index` + open-on-`pointerdown` (already fixed) — a plain `click` is swallowed by Bumble's card handler.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Core Structure
text: GraphFrames is a graph processing library built on Apache Spark DataFrames with three main components:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Core Structure
text:
1. **Core GraphFrame API** (`core/src/main/scala/org/graphframes/`)
   - `GraphFrame.scala`: Main graph abstraction using DataFrames for vertices/edges
   - Provides graph algorithms, motif finding, and subgraph operations

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Core Structure
text:
2. **Algorithm Library** (`core/src/main/scala/org/graphframes/lib/`)
   - Standard graph algorithms: PageRank, ConnectedComponents, ShortestPaths, etc.
   - `Pregel.scala`: Implements Pregel-style bulk synchronous parallel processing
   - `AggregateMessages.scala`: Lower-level message-passing API

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Core Structure
text:
3. **GraphX Compatibility Layer** (`graphx/src/main/scala/`)
   - Provides GraphX-compatible APIs for migration
   - Bridges between DataFrame and RDD-based graph operations

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text: **When the user asks for a new feature, do not start coding.** Grill it first. A new feature is anything that adds a capability, a screen, an endpoint, a data model or an integration. Bug fixes, refactors, dependency bumps and small changes inside an existing behavior skip this workflow; when in doubt, ask.

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text: Each step has a skill in `.claude/skills/` (Claude Code invokes them by name; other agents read the `SKILL.md`):

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text:
| Step | Skill             | Output                                                                               |
| ---- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | `grill-with-docs` | Shared understanding of the design, agreed test seams, an ADR, `GLOSSARY.md` updates |
| 2    | `to-prd`          | The PRD, published as a GitHub issue labelled `⛰ Epic`                               |
| 3    | `to-issues`       | Tracer-bullet tickets, as sub-issues of the epic with their blocking edges           |
| 4    | `tdd`             | The first PR: the ADR, the glossary, and the acceptance tests, skipped               |
| 5    | `tdd`             | One PR per ticket: turn its tests on (red), implement (green), review with `/review` |

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text: 1. **Grill.** Interview the user round by round until every branch of the design is settled; look facts up in the code yourself, leave only decisions to the user. Terms go into `GLOSSARY.md` as they are resolved, decisions into an ADR in `docs/adr/` (`Status: proposed`), on a `feat/<feature>-adr-tests` branch created from `develop` before the first file is written. Nothing moves on before the user confirms the shared understanding.

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text: 2. **Epic.** Synthesize the grilling into a PRD (problem, solution, user stories, implementation and testing decisions, out of scope), show it, and publish it once the user agrees. The repository is public: no client name, unfixed vulnerability or secret in any issue.

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text: 3. **Tickets.** Split the epic into vertical slices, each one PR, each with its blockers. Ticket 01 is always the ADR + tests PR, and blocks the others. The user approves the breakdown before anything is published.

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text: 4. **First PR** (`feat/<feature>-adr-tests`, closes ticket 01). The ADR, the `GLOSSARY.md` changes, and the tests at the agreed seams, written in full as the epic's acceptance criteria inside `describe.skip` blocks that name the ticket turning them on. No production code, CI stays green.

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text: 5. **Ticket PRs** (`feat/<feature>-<ticket>`, one per ticket, frontier first). Remove the `.skip` of the ticket's blocks, implement until they pass, add the smaller tests the implementation needs. When the first PR merges, the ADR moves to `Status: accepted`.

head: AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions > New Feature Workflow
text: Before exploring the code for any task, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) and the ADRs in `docs/adr/` that touch the area. Use the glossary's terms in code, tests and issues. If a change contradicts an ADR, say so explicitly instead of silently overriding it.

**Flat or nested?** A module owning a single entity stays flat, as above —
that covers `mailing`, `group`, `translation`, `ai-feature`, `integration`,
`user`, `workspace`. A module owning several entities uses one sub-folder per
layer (`controllers/`, `services/`, `models/`, `schemas/`, `jobs/`,
`constant/`), as `ai-skill` does for its three entities (skill, expertise,
invocation): 27 flat files would be unreadable. The file-naming rules above
still apply inside each sub-folder, and `/tests/server/{resource}/` mirrors
whichever structure the module uses.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: Use Linux kernel/Git-style commit subjects with a concrete area, subsystem, component, directory, package, or file prefix:

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: The prefix should name the repository area primarily changed. Prefer specific prefixes such as a directory, package, file, subsystem, or component name.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: Do not use generic Conventional Commit prefixes such as `fix:`, `feat:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, or `refactor:` unless they are actual repository areas in this repository. The prefix should describe where the change belongs, not what type of change it is.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: Use an imperative verb in the summary after the colon, such as `fix`, `clarify`, `split`, `validate`, `rename`, `remove`, `add`, `update`, `document`, etc. Do not use past tense verbs like `fixed` or `added`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: When a patch spans multiple areas, choose the narrowest common area if one exists. If no clear common area exists, use the primary behavior changed rather than listing multiple unrelated prefixes.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: The summary after the colon should briefly describe what the patch does, because it becomes the first line shown in the git changelog. Keep it short, imperative, and specific. Prefer subjects under 72 characters. Use lowercase for the first word after the colon unless it is a proper noun, and do not end the subject with a period.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: Use a commit body when the reason for the change is not obvious from the diff. Explain why the change is needed, not just what changed.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: PRs should describe the changed area, summarize the user-visible or developer-visible impact, list validation commands run, link related issues, and include screenshots for visible web UI changes.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: If no validation was run, state that explicitly and explain why. Do not claim to have run commands that were not actually executed.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit And PR Guidance
text: For UI changes that are not easily captured in a screenshot, describe the visual change and any manual checks performed.

head: Operon Architecture > Overview
text: Operon is a desktop IDE for researchers, built with Tauri 2 (Rust backend + React/TypeScript frontend). It wraps Codex into a professional multi-panel developer environment with an integrated terminal, file browser, Monaco code editor, and AI chat interface. Designed for scientists who work on HPC compute clusters — it runs Codex agents directly on remote compute nodes via SSH and tmux, with sessions that persist across app restarts.

head: Operon Architecture > Tech Stack
text:
| Component | Technology | Why |
|-----------|-----------|-----|
| App Shell | Tauri 2 | ~600KB bundle, 20-40MB RAM, native webview |
| Backend | Rust | Memory-safe, async (tokio), direct PTY/filesystem access |
| Frontend | React 18 + TypeScript + Vite 6 | Fast HMR, Monaco/xterm.js integrate natively |
| Terminal | xterm.js + portable-pty | Same stack as VS Code + WezTerm |
| Editor | Monaco Editor (@monaco-editor/react) | VS Code's editor engine |
| Layout | react-resizable-panels | Cursor-style multi-panel with draggable dividers |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS 3 + lucide-react icons | Utility-first dark theme |
| SSH | OpenSSH sidecar via portable-pty | Handles ProxyJump, agent forwarding, ~/.ssh/config |
| Auth | In-memory (production: macOS Keychain via keyring) | Secure API key storage |
| AI | Codex headless mode (stream-json) | Structured NDJSON streaming |

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 1. **IPC Pattern**: Tauri commands for request/response, Tauri events for streaming. Never HTTP/WebSocket.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 2. **Terminal Output**: Uses events (`pty-output-{id}`), not commands. Commands would block.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 3. **PTY Reader**: Runs in `std::thread::spawn` (not `tokio::spawn`) because portable-pty's Read is synchronous.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 4. **Resize**: Always `fitAddon.fit()` FIRST, then `invoke('resize_terminal')`. Reverse causes garbled output.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 5. **Hidden Terminals**: Use `visibility: hidden` not `display: none` to preserve buffer state.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 6. **Secrets**: In-memory for dev. Production uses macOS Keychain via `keyring` crate.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 7. **SSH**: Spawned OpenSSH binary (not Rust SSH library) for ProxyJump, agent forwarding, ~/.ssh/config.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 8. **Codex**: `Codex -p --verbose --output-format stream-json` gives NDJSON. Parsed line-by-line.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 9. **State Managers**: Each domain has its own `Mutex<HashMap>` struct registered via `.manage()`.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 10. **Locking**: Never hold `std::sync::Mutex` across `.await`. Extract data, drop lock, then await.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 11. **Terminal Mode**: Commands must run in the terminal's own shell (not piped to `bash`) to preserve user aliases like `Codex → npx @anthropic-ai/Codex`.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 12. **HPC /tmp**: Node-local on HPC clusters. Use shared NFS/GPFS paths (like the working directory) for output files accessible from both login and compute nodes.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 13. **Symlinks**: Use `std::fs::metadata()` (follows symlinks) for local files, `ls -L` for remote files.

head: Operon Architecture > Key Architectural Rules
text: 14. **SSH Quoting**: Base64-encode complex scripts sent via SSH to avoid multi-layer shell expansion issues (local shell → SSH → remote shell → bash -c).

head: Operon Architecture > HPC Terminal Mode Architecture
text: Terminal mode is the primary execution mode for HPC users. It runs Codex agents inside existing tmux sessions on compute nodes.

head: Operon Architecture > HPC Terminal Mode Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - **Output on shared filesystem** (`{remote_path}/.operon-{id}.jsonl`), not `/tmp` which is node-local on HPC

head: Operon Architecture > HPC Terminal Mode Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - **Terminal command runs in user's shell** (not piped to `bash`) to preserve aliases

head: Operon Architecture > HPC Terminal Mode Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - **Tail command uses base64 encoding** to avoid quoting issues across the SSH chain

head: Operon Architecture > HPC Terminal Mode Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - **SSH stderr is filtered** for post-quantum warnings, connection messages, etc.

head: Operon Architecture > HPC Terminal Mode Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - **Session metadata persisted** to `~/.operon/sessions/{id}.json` for resume across app restarts

head: Operon Architecture > Session Management
text: Sessions persist across app restarts:

head: Operon Architecture > Session Management
text: - **On session start**: Metadata saved to `~/.operon/sessions/{session_id}.json` (Codex CLI session ID, project path, SSH profile, mode, timestamps)

head: Operon Architecture > Session Management
text: - **During streaming**: Codex CLI session ID captured from `system` event and persisted for `--resume`

head: Operon Architecture > Session Management
text: - **On session end**: Status updated to "completed"

head: Operon Architecture > Session Management
text: - **On app reopen**: Frontend checks for previous sessions, shows resume banner if found

head: Operon Architecture > Session Management
text: - **Resume flow**: For running sessions → reconnect tail to .jsonl file. For completed sessions → read full .jsonl, parse into messages, restore chat. Follow-up messages use `--resume SESSION_ID`.

head: Operon Architecture > Plan Mode
text: - Generates `implementation_plan.md` in the working directory

head: Operon Architecture > Plan Mode
text: - Auto-detected on session start: if `implementation_plan.md` exists, its content is injected as context

head: Operon Architecture > Plan Mode
text: - Agent mode tracks progress by marking steps `[x]` in the plan file

head: Operon Architecture > Plan Mode
text: - Plan mode limited to 3 turns; agent mode uses configurable `max_turns`

head: Operon Architecture > First-Time Setup Wizard
text: On first launch (`setup_completed: false` in settings):

head: Operon Architecture > First-Time Setup Wizard
text: 1. **Welcome screen** with branding

head: Operon Architecture > First-Time Setup Wizard
text: 2. **Dependency check**: Xcode CLI tools, Codex

head: Operon Architecture > First-Time Setup Wizard
text: 3. **Installation**: Individual or "Install All Missing" (Xcode via `xcode-select --install`, Codex via `curl -fsSL https://Codex.ai/install.sh | bash`, falls back to npm if curl fails)

head: Operon Architecture > First-Time Setup Wizard
text: 4. **Authentication**: API key input or skip for OAuth later

head: Operon Architecture > First-Time Setup Wizard
text: 5. **Completion**: Sets `setup_completed: true` in settings — never shown again

head: Operon Architecture > First-Time Setup Wizard
text: Remote server dependency checking available via `check_remote_claude` / `install_remote_claude` commands.

head: Operon Architecture > Stream-JSON Deduplication
text: Codex's `--output-format stream-json` sends cumulative content for each assistant message. Each `assistant` event contains the FULL content for that message so far.

head: Operon Architecture > Stream-JSON Deduplication
text: - Track message IDs with a `seenMsgIds` ref

head: Operon Architecture > Stream-JSON Deduplication
text: - **Same ID = replace** content (intra-message content update)

head: Operon Architecture > Stream-JSON Deduplication
text: - **New ID = append** as new message (new turn in conversation)

head: Operon Architecture > Stream-JSON Deduplication
text: - Prevents duplicate tool blocks and text

head: Operon Architecture > Known Gotchas
text: - **`Codex` is an alias on HPC**: Resolves to `npx @anthropic-ai/Codex`. Terminal commands must run in the user's shell to access the alias. Never pipe through `| bash` or the alias is lost.

head: Operon Architecture > Known Gotchas
text: - **`/tmp` is node-local on HPC**: Output files written on a compute node are invisible from the login node's `/tmp`. Always use the shared working directory.

head: Operon Architecture > Known Gotchas
text: - **SSH post-quantum warnings**: OpenSSH 9.x emits warnings about sntrup/mlkem key exchange. These are filtered from stderr to avoid false error messages.

head: Operon Architecture > Known Gotchas
text: - **`--output-format stream-json` requires `--verbose`**: Without it, Codex exits with an error.

head: Operon Architecture > Known Gotchas
text: - **xterm.js Unicode in JSX**: `\u25CF` in JSX text is rendered literally. Must use `{'\u25CF'}` (JavaScript expression).

head: Operon Architecture > Known Gotchas
text: - **Lucide icon click interception**: SVG icons inside buttons intercept pointer events. Add `pointer-events-none` class to icons.

head: Operon Architecture > Known Gotchas
text: - **FileViewer download in Tauri**: Data URIs are blocked by Tauri webview CSP. Use Blob + `URL.createObjectURL()` instead.

head: UNO Online > Docker 与部署
text:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` 会在 PR 与 main push 上执行完整验证和两个 Docker target 构建。
`.github/workflows/release.yml` 通常由合法 SemVer Tag push 触发；已有 Tag 的发布故障也可从 `main` 通过
`workflow_dispatch` 指定原 Tag 恢复。两种入口都只检出现有 Tag，并执行相同的 Tag/main/版本校验。
GitHub Actions 不会 SSH 或直接重启生产服务器。生产 Komodo 会按计划轮询当前镜像通道并更新兼容版本；
破坏性发布仍是显式运维步骤。

head: UNO Online > Docker 与部署 > 发布兼容性判定
text: 应用 SemVer、Redis 运行时兼容性与网络协议是三个独立判定维度。每次发版必须分别判断：

head: UNO Online > Docker 与部署 > 发布兼容性判定
text:
1. **状态兼容发布**：Redis 房间/游戏结构和 Socket 合约兼容。保持代码内
   `RUNTIME_STATE_GENERATION` 与 `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 不变，保留 Redis 和 `JWT_SECRET`；优雅重启后玩家刷新可继续对局。

head: UNO Online > Docker 与部署 > 发布兼容性判定
text:
2. **运行时结构破坏性发布**：先停止创建新房间并排空活跃房间，再递增
   `packages/server/src/kv/runtime-state.ts` 中的 `RUNTIME_STATE_GENERATION`。旧 server 退出后，新 server
   启动时自动清空固定 namespace，不迁移旧数据，不需要运维人工清 Redis。

head: UNO Online > Docker 与部署 > 发布兼容性判定
text:
3. **Socket/ACK 破坏性发布**：递增 `packages/shared/src/constants/protocol.ts` 中的
   `PROTOCOL_VERSION`，前后端与 MCP 协同发布；旧客户端握手失败并提示刷新，不做协议降级。

head: UNO Online > Docker 与部署 > 发布兼容性判定
text:
首次上线固定 namespace/代码代次机制时属于破坏性发布：新 server 找不到当前代次标记，
会在启动期间自动删除 `uno:runtime:` 下的旧状态后再提供服务。

head: UNO Online > Docker 与部署 > 发布兼容性判定
text: 兼容更新已运行的 Compose 环境时，仅拉取并重建应用容器：

head: UNO Online > Docker 与部署 > 发布兼容性判定
text:
当前生产不使用省略 env 文件的裸 `docker compose up -d`。首次创建或完整恢复生产 Stack 由 Komodo 部署；
必须脱离面板操作时，也要显式传入 `.env` 与 `.env.secrets` 并保持 Compose 项目名为 `uno-online`。破坏性发布
应安排维护窗口：先停止接纳新房间，在旧 server 仍运行时等待或终止活跃房间，再停止旧 server，最后部署
匹配的 server 与 caddy；新 server 会按代码代次自动清理不兼容运行时状态。具体说明见 `docs/deployment.md`。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text: GitHub 自动发布只负责验证和发布制品；版本判断、兼容性判断、PR、Tag 与生产部署仍需显式执行。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text: 1. **确定 SemVer**：根据变更范围决定 patch/minor/major。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text:
2. **检查版本范围**：
   - Beta 迭代比较上一个 Beta Tag 到 `HEAD`，用于编写本次测试版的增量说明。
   - Beta 转正式版必须先执行 `git fetch --tags --prune` 和 `pnpm release:stable-diff`。该命令会自动选择
     `HEAD` 可达的上一个正式 `vX.Y.Z` Tag，并输出该 Tag 到 `HEAD` 的提交、`git diff --stat` 和文件清单；
     正式版说明以这个完整范围为准，不能只比较最后一个 Beta。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text:
3. **判定发布兼容性**：按上一节决定是否排空房间、递增 `RUNTIME_STATE_GENERATION` 或
   `PROTOCOL_VERSION`。不要把应用 SemVer 直接当作运行时/协议兼容性标记。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text:
4. **同步包版本**：只修改根 `package.json#version`，然后执行：
   ```bash
   pnpm run version:sync
   ```
   所有 workspace `package.json` 会同步。MCP 由 tsup 注入版本；client Vite 从自身 `package.json` 注入
   `BUILD_VERSION`，`build-info.ts` 仅保留开发 fallback。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text:
5. **更新发布说明**：
   - Beta：在 `CHANGELOG.md` 和客户端 changelog 顶部添加当前 Beta 的增量说明。
   - 正式版：根据第 2 步的完整正式版范围，在 `CHANGELOG.md` 顶部新增正式版说明；客户端 changelog 删除
     同一正式版本的所有 `-beta.N` 条目，并在顶部只保留一个正式版条目。正式 `CHANGELOG.md` 不删除已经发布的
     Beta 历史段落。
   - `pnpm release:check` 会校验客户端首条记录必须等于当前版本，并阻止正式版客户端保留同版本预发布条目。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text: 6. **验证版本与代码**：确认所有 workspace 包版本一致，然后执行完整验证、`pnpm build` 和 MCP pack 预检。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text: 7. **通过 PR 合并**：版本、changelog 和必要的 protocol 变更必须先进入 PR；禁止直接推 main。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text:
8. **同步 main 并打 tag**：PR squash 合并后：
   ```bash
   git fetch --prune origin
   git switch main
   git pull --ff-only
   git tag -a v<版本号> -m "release: v<版本号>"
   git push origin v<版本号>
   ```

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text:
9. **等待自动发版**：Tag push 触发 `Release` workflow。它会再次校验 Tag/main/版本/changelog，执行
   build/test/MCP pack，推送 `server` 与 `caddy` 的 `v<版本号>` 镜像、稳定版 `latest`，通过 npm OIDC
   发布 MCP，最后从 CHANGELOG 创建 GitHub Release。任一步失败都不能视为发版完成。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text:
10. **按兼容性策略部署**：自动发版不连接生产服务器。兼容发布由生产 Komodo 在下次 Global Auto Update
    更新当前通道，也可在面板中立即部署；破坏性发布必须在推送会移动当前镜像通道的版本 Tag 前关闭 Stack
    Auto Update，并在维护窗口排空房间、切换 schema/protocol、部署和验证后再恢复自动更新。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text: 11. **发布后验证**：检查 `/api/health`、`/api/server/info`、浏览器登录/重连以及版本化 Docker/MCP 制品。

head: UNO Online > 版本号与完整发版流程
text:
预发布 Tag（如 `v1.2.0-beta.0`）会生成 prerelease，推送精确版本镜像并更新 Docker `beta`，但不更新 Docker
`latest`；MCP npm 包使用第一个预发布标识作为 dist-tag（该示例为 `beta`），不会覆盖 npm `latest`。语音网关

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents
text: This file is for AI agents helping to **maintain and extend the specification** — adding failure modes, requirements, and schemas. It defines conventions every editor agent must follow.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents
text: If you are helping someone **implement** this specification in their own project, read [`IMPLEMENTING.md`](IMPLEMENTING.md) instead.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Project overview
text: This project defines the **CLI Agent Spec** specification: a catalogue of failure modes, requirements, shared schemas, and a comparison matrix for building CLI tools that work reliably under AI agent orchestration.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Project overview
text: Current corpus: 76 failure modes, 167 requirements.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules
text: These rules apply to **all documents** in this project. Apply them when creating or updating any file.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 1. No trailing periods in lists, tables, or cells
text: Sentences placed inside a list item, table cell, or blockquote cell MUST NOT end with a period.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 1. No trailing periods in lists, tables, or cells
text:
**Correct**
```markdown
- Validation failed before execution began
- Safe to retry unconditionally after fixing the input

| Field  | Description              |
|--------|--------------------------|
| `code` | Stable machine-readable identifier |
```

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 1. No trailing periods in lists, tables, or cells
text:
**Incorrect**
```markdown
- Validation failed before execution began.
- Safe to retry unconditionally after fixing the input.

| Field  | Description                         |
|--------|-------------------------------------|
| `code` | Stable machine-readable identifier. |
```

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 1. No trailing periods in lists, tables, or cells
text: Periods are only used to end sentences in **prose paragraphs** (Description, Purpose, Implementation notes body text).

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 2. Inline code for all identifiers
text: Flag names, field names, constants, file names, command invocations, and schema `$id` values must be wrapped in backticks.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 2. Inline code for all identifiers
text:
**Correct:** `exit_codes` · `ExitCode.NOT_FOUND` · `--schema` · `error.redirect.command`
**Incorrect:** exit_codes · ExitCode.NOT_FOUND · --schema

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 3. Verb-first relationship labels in Related tables
text: Every row in a `## Related` table must start with a verb describing the relationship direction.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 3. Verb-first relationship labels in Related tables
text: Allowed verbs: `Provides` · `Consumes` · `Enforces` · `Specializes` · `Composes` · `Aggregates` · `Wraps` · `Sources` · `Exposes` · `Extends`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 4. Present tense in descriptions
text: All `description` fields (in schemas, requirement files, and table cells) use present tense.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 4. Present tense in descriptions
text:
**Correct:** `"Operation completed as intended"`
**Incorrect:** `"Operation will complete as intended"` / `"Operation has completed"`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 5. Agent-readable `description` fields
text: Descriptions in `ExitCodeEntry`, `FlagEntry`, and `ErrorDetail` are read by agents at runtime. They must:

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Styling rules > 5. Agent-readable `description` fields
text: - State the condition, not the intent (`"Target cluster not found"` not `"Finds the target cluster"`)

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: **Naming:** `{nn:02d}-{severity}-{slug}.md` inside the matching part folder

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: **Severity order within a part:** critical → high → medium

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text:
**Required frontmatter line** (first metadata line after the title):
```
**Severity:** Critical | **Frequency:** Common | **Detectability:** Hard | **Token Spend:** High | **Time:** High | **Context:** Medium
```

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: **Required sections in order:**

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 1. `### The Problem` — failure modes with code examples

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 2. `### Impact` — consequences from the agent's perspective; bulleted list, no trailing periods

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 3. `### Solutions` — CLI author and framework design fixes; sub-headings by audience (`**For CLI authors:**`, `**For framework design:**`); no agent-side content here

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 4. `### Evaluation` — scoring table (0–3) or binary pass/fail with a `**Check:**` line describing what to run or observe

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 5. `### Agent Workaround` — compensating behaviors an agent applies when the CLI has not addressed this failure mode; code example + `**Limitation:**` line describing what the workaround cannot handle

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: - Use a 0–3 table when the failure mode has four distinguishable states

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: - Use a binary pass/fail when only two states are meaningful

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: - Score 3 always means the CLI handles the failure mode completely without agent intervention

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: - Score 0 always means the agent has no reliable recovery path

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: **Agent Workaround rules:**

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: - Generic only — no tool-specific instructions

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: - Must include a `**Limitation:**` line (no trailing period) stating what the workaround cannot compensate for

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: - Do not duplicate content already in `### Solutions` — Solutions is for CLI authors, Workaround is for agents calling a CLI that has not been fixed

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: When adding a failure mode:

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 1. Assign the next available `§N` number

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 2. Place it in the correct part folder by severity

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 3. Add a row to `challenges/index.md` and the part's `index.md`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 4. Add a row to `challenges/sources.md`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 5. Create or update any requirements that address it

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 6. Regenerate the machine-readable index: `uv run scripts/build_failure_index.py`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Failure mode files
text: 7. Run `uv run scripts/validate_links.py` and `uv run scripts/validate_schemas.py`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: **Naming:** `{tier}-{NNN}-{slug}.md` where tier is `f`, `c`, or `o`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: - `f` — Framework-Automatic: enforced without command author action

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: - `c` — Command Contract: declared by the command author at registration

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: - `o` — Opt-In: explicitly enabled by the application

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: **Required sections in order:**

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 1. `## Description` — prose, may end sentences with periods

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 2. `## Acceptance Criteria` — bulleted list, no trailing periods

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 3. `## Schema` — links to `../schemas/<name>.md` using the filename as link text; the `.md` links to the `.json` — followed by requirement-specific constraints only

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 4. `## Wire Format` — JSON example of the output (if applicable)

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 5. `## Example` — unformatted pseudocode, language-agnostic

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 6. `## Related` — cross-reference table: `Requirement | Tier | Relationship`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: When adding a requirement:

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 1. Assign the next `NNN` within the tier

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 2. Add a row to `requirements/index.md`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 3. Link the related schema file(s) from `## Schema`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Requirement files
text: 4. Add the requirement to the `Related` table of every schema it uses

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: Every shared type has two files: a `.json` (machine-consumable) and a `.md` (human-readable).

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: - `$id` equals the file name including the extension (e.g. `"$id": "exit-code.json"`), so `$ref` by filename resolves in every validator

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: - All properties have a `description`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: - Use `$ref` to reference other schemas by filename (e.g. `"$ref": "exit-code.json"`)

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: - No language-specific content

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: **`.md` file sections in order:**

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text:
| # | Section | Audience | Content |
|---|---------|----------|---------|
| 1 | Title + file link + Used by | everyone | Header, link to `.json`, requirement back-links |
| 2 | `## Purpose` | everyone | Why this type exists; key design decisions |
| 3 | `## Values` / field table | everyone | Enum table or field table with description and when-to-use; no trailing periods |
| 4 | `## Examples` | everyone | Valid instances, then invalid instances with violation named |
| 5 | `## Common mistakes` | human developers | What developers get wrong; bulleted list; no trailing periods |
| 6 | `## Agent interpretation` | runtime agents | Decision rules for consuming output: missing fields, contradictions, retry logic; no trailing periods |
| 7 | `## Coding agent notes` | AI coding assistants | Type representation, validation to generate, tests to generate, anti-patterns; no trailing periods |
| 8 | `## Implementation notes` | human developers | Prose rationale and edge cases; sentences may end with periods |

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: Sections 1–4 are read by all audiences. Sections 5–8 are audience-specific — each reader goes directly to their section after reading the shared baseline.

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: When adding a schema type:

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: 1. Create `schemas/<name>.json` and `schemas/<name>.md`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: 2. Add a row to `schemas/index.md`

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Schema files
text: 3. Reference the `.json` file from any requirement that uses the type

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Cross-reference conventions
text: - Failure modes are referenced as `§N` (e.g. `§34`)

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Cross-reference conventions
text: - Requirements are referenced as `REQ-{TIER}-{NNN}` (e.g. `REQ-F-001`)

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Cross-reference conventions
text: - Schema types are referenced with a link to their `.json` file

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Cross-reference conventions
text: - All cross-document links use relative paths

head: AGENTS.md — Spec Editor Guide for AI Agents > Cross-reference conventions
text: - Merged failure modes: `§36 → §10`, `§39 → §3`, `§48 → §2` — do not create new content for these numbers

head: OpenPeon
text: OpenPeon is an open standard (CESP v1.0) for coding event sounds. Any agentic IDE or terminal editor can implement CESP to give developers audio feedback when tasks complete, errors occur, or input is needed.

head: OpenPeon > Key Directories
text: - `spec/` -- CESP v1.0 specification, JSON schemas (`openpeon.schema.json` for pack manifests, `registry-entry.schema.json` for registry entries)

head: OpenPeon > Key Directories
text: - `examples/` -- Example sound packs (peon, glados) that validate against the schemas

head: OpenPeon > Key Directories
text: - `site/` -- Next.js site deployed to openpeon.com via Vercel

head: OpenPeon > Key Directories
text: - `scripts/` -- Cross-repo utility scripts (`update-pack-counts.sh` for syncing pack counts)

head: OpenPeon > Key Directories
text: - `docs/` -- Architecture documents (`registry-design.md`, `download-tracking-plan.md`, `plans/`)

head: OpenPeon > Key Directories
text: - `tests/` -- Schema validation tests

head: OpenPeon > Build Commands > Site (from `site/` directory)
text: - `npm run dev` -- Start dev server

head: OpenPeon > Build Commands > Site (from `site/` directory)
text: - `npm run build` -- Production build

head: OpenPeon > Build Commands > Site (from `site/` directory)
text: - `npm run lint` -- ESLint

head: OpenPeon > Build Commands > Tests (from repo root)
text: - `npm test` -- Run all tests (schema validation)

head: OpenPeon > Build Commands > Tests (from repo root)
text: - `npm run test:schema` -- Run schema validation tests only

head: OpenPeon > Architecture Notes
text: - Pack data is fetched at request time with ISR, not at build time. `site/src/lib/registry.ts` fetches the registry index from `peonping.github.io/registry/index.json`, then each pack's `openpeon.json` manifest from GitHub raw URLs, with bounded concurrency and retries. Fetches are cached with `revalidate: 86400` (24h) under `REGISTRY_TAG`.

head: OpenPeon > Architecture Notes
text: - A malformed community manifest is dropped with a `[registry] dropping pack ...` console warning rather than failing the render. If the live site shows far fewer packs than the registry, check the deploy logs for these warnings.

head: OpenPeon > Architecture Notes
text: - `site/src/app/api/revalidate/route.ts` accepts a POST with an `x-revalidate-secret` header and busts the registry cache tag. It only works once `REVALIDATE_SECRET` is set in the Vercel project env; until then a fresh `vercel --prod` deploy is the way to reset the ISR cache.

head: OpenPeon > Architecture Notes
text: - Audio files are served directly from GitHub raw URLs (no local copies).

head: OpenPeon > Architecture Notes
text: - The site is deployed to Vercel; the Vercel project's root directory is `site/`, so run `vercel` from the REPO ROOT, not from `site/`.

head: OpenPeon > Architecture Notes
text: - Schemas use JSON Schema Draft 7.

head: OpenPeon > Architecture Notes
text: - CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs root schema tests plus site lint and build on every push/PR to main.

head: OpenPeon > Metadata / SEO
text: - Site-wide OG card lives in `site/src/app/layout.tsx`. Per-page `generateMetadata` must set its own `openGraph`/`twitter` blocks; Next.js does not cascade the page title/description into them (pack pages do this, see `site/src/app/packs/[name]/page.tsx`).

head: azul — agent instructions > Build > macOS

head: azul — agent instructions > Build > Tests
text: Unit tests live in the **azulTests** target (`tests/azulTests/`, XCTest). It is a hosted test bundle (runs inside the azul app), so tests use the existing ObjC++ bridge (`DataManagerWrapperWrapper`) via the app's bridging header and need no C++ compilation of their own. Fixtures are small files in `tests/Fixtures/` (bundled as a folder reference). Run with `⌘U` in Xcode or:

head: azul — agent instructions > Build > Tests

head: azul — agent instructions > Build > Tests

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: This ordering matters — it's the exact sequence in `Controller.swift:loadData(from:)` (macOS) and `MainViewController.swift:loadFile(url:)` (iOS):

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 1. `parse(filePath)` — reads file, populates `AzulObject` tree

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 2. `clearHelpers()` — releases parser memory

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 3. `updateBoundsWithLastFile()` — computes bounding box

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 4. `triangulateLastFile()` — CGAL triangulation of concave polygons

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 5. `generateEdgesForLastFile()` — extracts edges, deduplicated per feature (file-child and CityJSON `LoD` subtrees), so shared polygon/triangle edges are stored once

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 6. `clearPolygonsOfLastFile()` — frees polygon memory (only triangles/edges kept)

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 7. `regenerateTriangleBuffers(maxBufferSize: 16*1024*1024)` — builds GPU buffers

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 8. `regenerateEdgeBuffers(maxBufferSize: 16*1024*1024)` — builds edge buffers

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 9. (Swift side) `reloadTriangleBuffers()`, `reloadEdgeBuffers()`, `regenerateBoundingBoxBuffer()`

head: azul — agent instructions > Data flow (file loading pipeline)
text: 10. `availableLods()` + `setLodFilter("__highest__")` + regenerate buffers (default to highest LoD)

head: azul — agent instructions > Appearance system
text: CityGML and CityJSON appearance data (X3DMaterial and ParameterizedTexture) is parsed in `GMLParsingHelper.hpp` and `JSONParsingHelper.hpp`; FlatCityBuf appearance data in `FCBParsingHelper.hpp`. Styles are pooled into `AzulAppearanceStyle` structs and assigned to polygons via `appearanceStyleId`. During buffer regeneration, the `DataManager::useAppearances` and `appearanceTheme` flags control whether appearance data overrides the semantic `colourForType` fallback.

head: azul — agent instructions > Appearance system
text: The toolbar dropdown offers:

head: azul — agent instructions > Appearance system
text: - **Semantics**: type-based colouring (`colourForType` map), appearances off

head: azul — agent instructions > Appearance system
text: - **Materials**: material colours from the file (X3DMaterial), textures suppressed

head: azul — agent instructions > Appearance system
text: - **Textures**: texture images from the file (ParameterizedTexture), material colours suppressed

head: azul — agent instructions > Appearance system
text: - **Named themes** (if present): both materials and textures filtered by theme

head: azul — agent instructions > Appearance system > ImplicitGeometry (CityGML trees)
text: Vegetation objects in CityGML often use `ImplicitGeometry` with a shared template geometry and `xlink:href` references. The parser expands these templates per instance, applying the transformation matrix to geometry points. Appearance data (`appearanceStyleId`, `textureCoordinates`) must be explicitly copied from the template — `AzulPolygon()` default constructor discards them (`GMLParsingHelper.hpp:947-1003`).

head: azul — agent instructions > Appearance system > FlatCityBuf (`.fcb`)
text: `FCBParsingHelper.hpp` is a self-contained binary reader: it hand-decodes the FlatBuffers subset the schemas use (no FlatBuffers runtime dependency) and mirrors the JSON parser's `AzulObject` output. Geometry is stored as flattened count arrays (`solids`/`shells`/`surfaces`/`strings`/`boundaries`) with one redundant count level above a type's depth, which the surface walker ignores. The R-tree and attribute B+tree index sections are skipped (azul loads whole files); only their byte lengths are computed from the header. The Rust flatbuffers builder omits scalar fields equal to their schema default (absent `template`, `index`, `type`…), so absent scalars read as defaults, and vtables may sit after their table (signed soffset). A `GeometryInstance` has no LoD field in the schema, so its LoD child uses the template's LoD. Theme selection skips mappings without values, and a shared material `value` colours the whole geometry, matching the JSON parser's theme handling.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Functions bridging to Swift return C types (`float *`, `const char *`); Swift side wraps with `UnsafeBufferPointer`.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Colour = `(r, g, b, a)` float tuple. `a == 1.0` renders opaque first, `a < 1.0` renders second (transparent overlay).

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Selection overlay colour is configurable via Preferences (default yellow `(1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.7)`). Passed as `selectionColour` in the `Constants` Metal struct. Blend mode switches between screen blend (dark surfaces) and plain mix (bright surfaces) based on luminance.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Selected edges colour is configurable via Preferences (default red). Stored in `DataManager::selectedEdgesColour`, baked into edge buffers on regeneration.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Type/semantic surface colours are configurable via Preferences. Stored in `DataManager::colourForType` map; overrides persisted in UserDefaults `azulTypeColours` as `[type: [r, g, b, a]]`.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Preferences window has three tabbed panels: Rendering, Selection, Semantic Surfaces. All settings persist in UserDefaults.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - UserDefaults keys: `azulLightBackgroundColor`, `azulDarkBackgroundColor`, `azulSampleCount`, `azulSelectionColour`, `azulSelectedEdgesColour`, `azulTypeColours`, `azulRecentFiles`, `azulSortKey` (`"none"`/`"id"`/`"type"`), `azulSortDescending`.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Sorting is a cached display permutation, never an in-place sort of `AzulObject::children` (that would invalidate the iterators wrapped by `AzulObjectIterator` and the pointers in `objectsById`). `DataManager::child()`/`fileChild()` walk per-node `displayOrder` index vectors, recomputed lazily after `setSortOrder` or a new `parse` (invalidated via `sortOrdersCurrent`).

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Object picking uses a dedicated GPU-only render pass (`vertexPicking`/`fragmentPicking`) that encodes `objectId` into pixel bytes.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - `selectionStateCount` on GPU side = `objectsById.size()`; represents number of selectable flat objects.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - LOD filter is a string match; empty string = no filter. LOD detected from objects with type `"LoD"` (id = lod string) or type starting with `"lod"` + digits.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Search string is matched against object IDs, types, and attribute keys/values.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Object type filter hides objects in the sidebar and in the 3D view: `DataManager::objectTypeFilter` (empty set = all types) with a memoized tri-state `AzulObject::matchesTypeFilter` ('Y'/'N'/'U'); an object matches if its own type is selected or any descendant matches, so ancestors stay visible for context. Sidebar rows are skipped in the accessors; 3D geometry is hidden by folding `matchesTypeFilter` into `updateVisibleStates()` (no buffer regeneration needed, picking culls too since the picking shader uses the same states). `availableTypesWithCounts()` feeds the UI menus and skips structural rows (`"File"`, `"LoD"`, `"lod"+digits`). The filter is not persisted and resets on file load.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Visible state is a tri-state char: `'Y'` (all visible), `'N'` (all invisible), `'P'` (partly). Toggling regenerates GPU buffers.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - View parameters can be saved/loaded as `.azulview` JSON files.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Image export renders the view to PNG via an offscreen render pass (MSAA-aware, supports transparent background). Resolution 1×/2×/4× of drawable size. File → Export Image… (`⌘E`) with options in the save panel accessory view.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - `BOOL` return values in ObjC wrappers are `YES`/`NO` proper, not `true`/`false`.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - iOS conditional compilation uses `#if TARGET_OS_OSX` / `#if !TARGET_OS_OSX` in ObjC++ files.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - iOS uses `matrix4x4_perspective_shorter_dim()` (FOV constrained by shorter dimension) vs macOS which now also uses this function.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Empty state view (icon, title, subtitle, description, Open File button) shown when no file is loaded, on both iOS (`src_iOS/MainViewController.swift:setupEmptyState()`) and macOS (`src/Controller.swift:setupEmptyStateView()`). Fades out after file load.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Selection pulse: briefly boosts `selectionColour.w` to 1.0 then ramps back to 0.7 over 300ms when an object is selected. iOS: `MainViewController.animateSelectionPulse()`. macOS: `MetalView.animateSelectionPulse()`.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Context menus on iOS use `UIContextMenuConfiguration` with `UIContextMenuContentPreviewProvider` for peek previews. Object list (sidebar/modal) and 3D view (metalView) both have context menus.

head: azul — agent instructions > Key conventions
text: - Recent files (iOS Open button menu; macOS File → Open Recent, which replaces the standard system menu) stored in `UserDefaults.standard` under key `"azulRecentFiles"`. Capped at 5 entries on iOS; on macOS capped at the global-domain `NSRecentDocumentsLimit` when set (Apple does not expose the Control Center "Recent documents, applications, and servers" setting to apps), otherwise 10. macOS stores security-scoped bookmarks (`.withSecurityScope`) so recents open across launches in the sandbox; menu items are rebuilt via `Controller.reloadRecentFilesMenu()`.

head: deer-workflow
text: `deer-workflow` is an open-source reimplementation of the Dynamic Workflow idea. The canonical repository is `https://github.com/deerwork-ai/deer-workflow`.

head: deer-workflow
text: The runtime keeps deterministic orchestration in TypeScript and delegates semantic work to replaceable Agent runtimes. The default Agent runtime is Codex CLI.

head: deer-workflow
text: Do not copy private or proprietary implementations. Reproduce public behavior through clean-room interfaces, tests, and documentation.

head: deer-workflow > Runtime
text: - Use Bun for package management, scripts, tests, and process execution.

head: deer-workflow > Runtime
text:

  named `deer-workflow`.

head: deer-workflow > Runtime
text:
