head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance to AI coding agents when working with code in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: OngoingAI Gateway is a transparent, auditable proxy between applications and AI providers. It should enforce access control and capture trustworthy trace/usage data while staying invisible to client workflows.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: - Security first: no credential leakage, strong tenant isolation, least-privilege access, auditable behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: - Reliability first: streaming integrity, predictable failure modes, and stable operation under load.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: - Practical developer experience: fast local setup, clear config, and easy-to-extend provider integrations.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: - Scope boundary: this repo is a headless AI gateway and owns gateway M2M auth/enforcement; UI/user-session concerns are out of scope.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: - Self-hosted default: single binary, SQLite by default.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: - Team/multi-instance mode: Postgres-backed storage and dynamic key management.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: - Upstream provider API keys are pass-through only and must never be persisted.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission And Scope
text: - Gateway keys are identity/authorization credentials for the proxy and are distinct from provider credentials.

head: AGENTS.md > High-Priority Outcomes
text: When implementing features or fixes, optimize for these outcomes in order:

head: AGENTS.md > High-Priority Outcomes
text: 1. Prevent security regressions.

head: AGENTS.md > High-Priority Outcomes
text: 2. Preserve correctness and tenant boundaries.

head: AGENTS.md > High-Priority Outcomes
text: 3. Preserve low-latency proxy behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > High-Priority Outcomes
text: 4. Keep architecture simple and maintainable.

head: AGENTS.md > High-Priority Outcomes
text: 5. Improve observability and operator experience.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Write idiomatic Go. Keep functions small, cohesive, and explicit.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Keep interfaces at boundaries (`trace`, `configstore`, providers); avoid speculative abstractions.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Pass `context.Context` as the first parameter for request-bound or storage calls.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Wrap errors with actionable context (`fmt.Errorf("load gateway key: %w", err)`).

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Use deterministic behavior for critical logic (auth, limits, tenant scoping, redaction policies).

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Avoid global mutable state. Prefer dependency injection via constructors.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Keep hot-path allocations low in middleware/proxy code.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Protect concurrency edges: no data races, leaked goroutines, or unbounded queues.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Use structured logs and never log secrets, tokens, raw credentials, or unredacted sensitive payloads.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Add comments where helpful, especially for non-obvious "why" decisions. Do not add redundant comments.

head: AGENTS.md > Go Engineering Standards
text: - Keep exported symbols documented with concise Go doc comments.

head: AGENTS.md > Error Handling Conventions
text: - Return errors when callers can recover, retry, or map to clear HTTP responses.

head: AGENTS.md > Error Handling Conventions
text: - In proxy request paths, fail closed for authn/authz, tenant resolution, and policy enforcement errors.

head: AGENTS.md > Error Handling Conventions
text: - For non-critical telemetry failures (for example trace enqueue/write issues), log structured errors, emit metrics, and continue serving proxy traffic.

head: AGENTS.md > Error Handling Conventions
text: - Startup/config/store initialization failures should fail fast with a non-zero exit.

head: AGENTS.md > Error Handling Conventions
text: - Never panic for expected runtime conditions or user input errors; reserve panic for programmer bugs that cannot be safely recovered.

head: AGENTS.md > Security Requirements
text: - Enforce fail-closed behavior for auth/key-store uncertainty on proxy access decisions.

head: AGENTS.md > Security Requirements
text: - Preserve the pass-through credential model: provider API keys are forwarded to upstream providers but never persisted locally.

head: AGENTS.md > Security Requirements
text: - Never store upstream provider API key material in config store, trace store, logs, or errors.

head: AGENTS.md > Security Requirements
text: - Maintain strict `org_id`/`workspace_id` scoping in every query and access path.

head: AGENTS.md > Security Requirements
text: - Validate and sanitize all externally controlled inputs (headers, params, config values).

head: AGENTS.md > Security Requirements
text: - Treat PII controls and redaction policy behavior as security-sensitive code paths.

head: AGENTS.md > Security Requirements
text: - Preserve auditability for key lifecycle and authorization decisions.

head: AGENTS.md > Reliability Requirements
text: - Proxy path must prioritize request forwarding over trace persistence latency.

head: AGENTS.md > Reliability Requirements
text: - Streaming responses must preserve ordering and chunk delivery semantics.

head: AGENTS.md > Reliability Requirements
text: - Async trace pipeline must handle backpressure predictably (drop/queue behavior must be explicit and observable).

head: AGENTS.md > Reliability Requirements
text: - Shutdown paths must avoid silent data loss when feasible (flush and report).

head: AGENTS.md > Reliability Requirements
text: - Provider failures and storage failures should return clear, stable error semantics.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: Every functional change should include or update tests. Bias toward behavior tests over implementation tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: - Use `t.Parallel()` where safe.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: - Use table-driven tests for auth/policy/validation rules.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: - Use descriptive subtest names in table-driven suites (`name: "rejects revoked key"`).

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: - Use `t.TempDir()` and real SQLite/Postgres-backed paths for storage tests where possible.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: - Prefer real integration behavior over extensive mocking in critical paths.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: - Add regression tests for every bug fix.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: - Name tests descriptively (`TestDynamicMiddlewareRejectsRevokedKey`, not `TestAuth2`).

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text:
- Test run patterns:
  - Fast focused run: `go test ./path/to/pkg -run TestName -count=1`
  - Package run: `go test ./internal/auth/`
  - Full run: `make test`
  - Concurrency-sensitive paths before merge: `go test -race ./...`

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text: Minimum test focus areas:

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards
text:
- Security:
  - Missing/invalid/revoked gateway keys.
  - Missing upstream provider credentials.
  - Tenant isolation and cross-tenant access denial.
  - Permission and limit enforcement bypass attempts.
  - Sensitive data handling and redaction behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Standards

  - Queue-full and partial-failure behavior in trace writing.
  - Cache staleness/revocation windows.
  - Startup/shutdown and failure-mode handling.

head: プロジェクト概要
text: oni-comb-rs は Rust 製パーサーコンビネータライブラリの v2 リブート版。旧 v1 の `Rc<dyn Fn>` ベース設計を捨て、trait + 具象コンビネータ型（`Map`, `Zip`, `Or` 等）で構成する。動的ディスパッチ・ヒープ確保を排し、Applicative/Alternative 主体で最適化しやすい設計を目指している。

head: プロジェクト概要 > アーキテクチャ
text: Cargo workspace 構成。現在のメンバーは `parser` クレートのみ。

head: プロジェクト概要 > アーキテクチャ > モジュール構成 (`modules/parser/src/`)
text:
| モジュール | 役割 |
|-----------|------|
| `input_stream.rs` | `InputStream` トレイト（`Checkpoint`, `Slice`, `reset`, `is_eof`） |
| `str_input_stream.rs` | `StrInputStream<'a>` — `&str` 向け `InputStream` 実装 |
| `parser.rs` | `Parser<I>` トレイト（`Output`, `Error`, `parse_next`） |
| `parser_ext.rs` | `ParserExt<I>` — 全 `Parser` に自動実装されるコンビネータメソッド |
| `fail.rs` | `Fail<E>` enum と `PResult` 型エイリアス |
| `combinator/` | 各コンビネータの具象型（`Map`, `Zip`, `ZipLeft`, `ZipRight`, `Or`, `Attempt`, `Cut`, `Optional`, `Many`, `Many1`, `SepBy0`, `SepBy1`, `ChainL1`, `ChainR1`, `FlatMap`） |
| `text/` | テキスト専用パーサー（`Char`, `Tag`, `Satisfy`, `TakeWhile0/1`, `Eof`, `Whitespace0/1`, `Identifier`, `Integer`, `QuotedString`） |

head: プロジェクト概要 > アーキテクチャ > 設計上の重要な判断
text: - **Fail::Backtrack vs Fail::Cut**: `or` は Backtrack のみリカバリし、Cut はそのまま伝播。`attempt` は Cut を Backtrack に降格、`cut` は Backtrack を Cut に昇格

head: プロジェクト概要 > アーキテクチャ > 設計上の重要な判断
text: - **flat_map は実装済みだが Applicative 優先を推奨**: ベンチマークで zip ≒ flat_map（同一型）を確認済み。ただし異種型分岐では `Box<dyn Parser>` が必要で ~15ns のオーバーヘッドが発生するため、Applicative (`zip`, `or`) を優先し flat_map は文脈依存の分岐に限定する方針

head: プロジェクト概要 > アーキテクチャ > 設計上の重要な判断
text: - **再帰は boxed recursion**: 再帰の結び目だけ `Box<dyn Parser>` に落とし、非再帰部分は具象型を維持

head: プロジェクト概要 > アーキテクチャ > 設計上の重要な判断
text: - **入力型は当面 `&str` 限定**: `no_std`/streaming/bytes は後回し

head: プロジェクト概要 > アーキテクチャ > 設計上の重要な判断
text: - **`many`/`sep_by`/`chainl1` は専用ループコンビネータ**: flat_map 再帰ではなくループで実装

head: プロジェクト概要 > コンビネータ意味論
text: 各コンビネータの `Fail` に対する振る舞い。実装時はこの仕様に従うこと。

head: プロジェクト概要 > コンビネータ意味論 > `or(left, right)`
プロジェクト概要 > コンビネータ意味論 > `attempt(p)`
text: `p` 内で起きた Cut を Backtrack に降格し、開始 checkpoint へ戻す。成功時は何もしない。

head: プロジェクト概要 > コンビネータ意味論 > `cut(p)`
text: `p` の Backtrack を Cut に昇格させる。`tag(":").zip(value.cut())` のように使う。

head: プロジェクト概要 > コンビネータ意味論 > `optional(p)`
text: Backtrack のみ `Ok(None)` に変換。Cut/Incomplete は伝播。

head: プロジェクト概要 > コンビネータ意味論 > `many0(p)`
text: Backtrack で停止し収集結果を返す。Cut/Incomplete は伝播。zero-progress（入力を消費せずに成功し続ける）は `ZeroProgress` エラー。

head: プロジェクト概要 > コンビネータ意味論 > `sep_by`, `between`, `chainl1`, `chainr1`
text: flat_map 再帰ではなく専用ループで実装する。

head: プロジェクト概要 > マイルストーン
text:
| # | 名前 | 実装対象 | まだやらない | 完了条件 |
|---|------|----------|-------------|---------|
| 1 | Core | `InputStream`, `Span`, `Fail`, `PResult`, `Parser`, `ParserExt`, `StrInputStream` | regex, cache, bytes, recursive helper | `or/attempt/cut` の単体テストが通る |
| 2 | Primitive | `eof`, `char`, `tag`, `satisfy`, `take_while0/1`, `peek` | unicode category, regex, bytes | identifier/integer parser が組める |
| 3 | Combinators | `map`, `zip`, `zip_left`, `zip_right`, `between`, `optional`, `many0/1`, `sep_by0/1`, `chainl1`, `chainr1`, `flat_map`/`and_then` | — | expression parser と CSV/JSON subset の骨格が書ける |
| 4 | Text module | whitespace, ascii token, identifier, integer, quoted string | bytes 共通化 | JSON subset と URI tokenizer が動く |
| 5 | Recursive | boxed `recursive()` helper, precedence parser | left recursion, packrat | 四則演算+括弧の parser が動く |
| 6 | Error reporting | span, expected-set, context stack, cut-aware merge | カラー診断, IDE 連携 | JSON subset の失敗位置と期待トークンが出る |
| 7 | Benchmark | criterion bench, allocation counter, regression threshold | micro-opt の先走り | v1 比較でボトルネック定量化、1回最適化サイクル完了 |

head: プロジェクト概要 > ベンチマーク結果
text: - **比較対象**: `winnow`、`nom`、`chumsky`、`pom`

head: プロジェクト概要 > ベンチマーク結果
text: - **workload**: identifier/integer、flat_map 同一型/異種型、zip vs flat_map、JSON subset、四則演算+括弧、107KB JSON フル

text: - **観測項目**: throughput（Criterion）、allocation count（`dhat-rs`）

head: プロジェクト概要 > ベンチマーク結果
text: - **107KB JSON フルベンチ（`json_full`, 100 サンプル、2026-03-21 再計測）**:

head: プロジェクト概要 > ベンチマーク結果
プロジェクト概要 > ベンチマーク結果
text: - **知見**: 2026-03-21 の `take_while*` ホットパス整理後の `json_full` 再計測では `winnow` が首位で、`nom` と `chumsky` も oni-comb を上回る。一方で oni-comb は `pom` より 11.7 倍速く、107KB JSON で 152.0 MiB/s まで回復した。同日の `comparison -- json` 再計測でも JSON subset は回復しており、`null` は 16.5ns、`object_large` は約 1.38µs まで改善した。詳細は `modules/parser/benches/README.md` を参照

head: プロジェクト概要 > ベンチマーク結果
text: - **アロケーション**: パーサーコンビネータインフラはゼロアロケーション。JSON フルパースのアロケーション（743 blocks / 336KB）は全て AST 構築（`Vec` grow + エスケープ文字列 `Cow::Owned`）に起因

head: プロジェクト概要 > 設計メモ: `no_std` core-only 層
text: 現在 `#![no_std]` + `extern crate alloc` だが、`alloc` なしの `core` のみ層を feature gate で分離可能。

head: プロジェクト概要 > 設計メモ: `no_std` core-only 層
text:
**`alloc` 不要（core のみで動作）**:
`tag`, `char`, `satisfy`, `take_while0/1`, `eof`, `whitespace0/1`, `identifier`, `integer`,
`zip`, `zip_left`, `zip_right`, `map`, `or`, `attempt`, `cut`, `optional`, `context`,
`fn_parser`, `flat_map`（同一型返却時）, `peek_byte`

head: プロジェクト概要 > 設計メモ: `no_std` core-only 層
text:
**`alloc` が必要**:
`many0/1`, `sep_by0/1`, `chainl1/r1`（`Vec` 返却）, `quoted_string`/`escaped`（`Cow`/`String`）,
`recursive`（`Box<dyn Parser>` + `Rc`）, `ParseError`（`Vec<Expected>` + `Vec<&str>`）

head: プロジェクト概要 > 設計メモ: `no_std` core-only 層
text: **実装方針**: `default = ["alloc"]` feature で分離。core-only 層だけでプロトコルパーサーや組み込みトークナイザーに使える。

head: 曖昧なサフィックスを避ける
text: 型の命名において曖昧なサフィックスを検出し、明確な命名へ導く。

head: コーディング前の学習 > 禁止事項
text:
| やってはいけないこと | 代わりにやるべきこと |
|----------------------|----------------------|
| プロジェクトが直接クラスを使用しているのにインターフェースを追加 | 既存パターンに合わせる |
| プロジェクトが手動DIを使用しているのにDIフレームワークを使用 | 手動のコンストラクタインジェクションを使用 |
| プロジェクトがシンプルなthrowを使用しているのに包括的なエラー処理を追加 | 既存のエラースタイルに合わせる |
| プロジェクトにコメントがないのにJSDocを追加 | 既存のドキュメントスタイルに従う |

head: Less Is More
text: 過剰設計を避け、シンプルで保守しやすいコードを書く。

head: Less Is More > 核心原則 > 早すぎる抽象化の回避
text: **3回ルール: 3回繰り返すまで抽象化しない。**

head: Less Is More > 過剰設計の兆候
text:
| 兆候 | 問題 |
|------|------|
| 実装より設計に時間がかかる | 分析麻痺 |
| 「将来のために」が頻出 | YAGNI違反 |
| 1機能に5+ファイル | 過度な分離 |
| 設定可能な点が10+ | 過剰な柔軟性 |
| 継承階層が3+レベル | 過度な抽象化 |
| インターフェースの実装が1つだけ | 不要な抽象化 |

head: Less Is More > 格言
text: > "Perfection is achieved not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away." - Antoine de Saint-Exupery

head: イミュータブルを推奨
text: Rust以外の言語では、常に不変（immutable）なデータ操作を優先する。

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > 基本原則
text: **データを変更せず、新しいデータを作成する。**

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > 基本原則
text:
ミューテーション（状態の破壊的変更）は予測困難なバグの温床となる。参照を共有するオブジェクトを変更すると、
プログラムの別の場所で予期せぬ副作用が発生する。不変性を保つことで、コードの予測可能性と安全性が向上する。

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > 適用範囲
text:
| 言語 | 適用 | 備考 |
|------|------|------|
| JavaScript/TypeScript | ✅ | スプレッド構文、`Object.freeze`、Immutable.js等 |
| Python | ✅ | タプル、frozenset、dataclass(frozen=True)等 |
| Java | ✅ | レコード、Immutableコレクション、Builderパターン |
| Kotlin | ✅ | data class、`copy()`、不変コレクション |
| Scala | ✅ | case class、`copy()`、不変コレクションがデフォルト |
| Go | ✅ | 新しい構造体を返す、スライスのコピー |
| Ruby | ✅ | `freeze`、新しいオブジェクトを返す |
| **Rust** | ❌ | 所有権システムにより安全なミューテーションが可能 |

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > ルール > MUST（必須）
text: - オブジェクト/構造体の更新時は、元を変更せず新しいインスタンスを返す

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > ルール > MUST（必須）
text: - 配列/リストへの追加・削除は、新しいコレクションを返す

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > ルール > MUST NOT（禁止）
text: - 引数として受け取ったオブジェクトのプロパティを直接変更

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > ルール > MUST NOT（禁止）
text: - 配列の `push`, `pop`, `splice` 等の破壊的メソッドの使用（代替手段がある場合）

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > 例外

イミュータブルを推奨 > 理由

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > 理由

head: イミュータブルを推奨 > 理由

head: 1ファイルにつき1つの型
text: コード生成時に「1公開型 = 1ファイル」を強制する。言語を問わず適用する。

head: 1ファイルにつき1つの型 > 原則
text: **1つの公開型につき1つのファイルを作成する。**

head: 1ファイルにつき1つの型 > 公開型の定義
text:
| 言語 | 公開型 |
|------|--------|
| Java/Kotlin/Scala | `public`な `class`, `trait`, `object`, `enum` |
| Rust | `pub struct`, `pub trait`, `pub enum` |
| Go | 大文字始まりの `type` |
| Python | モジュールレベルの `class` |
| TypeScript/JavaScript | `export`された `class`, `interface`, `type`, オブジェクト |
| Swift | `public class`, `public protocol`, `public enum` |
| C# | `public class`, `public interface`, `public enum` |

head: 1ファイルにつき1つの型 > ルール > MUST（必須）
text: - ファイル名は公開型の名前を反映（例: `UserRepository` → `user_repository.py`）

head: 1ファイルにつき1つの型 > ルール > MUST NOT（禁止）

| Aspect | DDA EOCs | BN Lua |

text:
**Lua**:
```lua
function mod.weighted_select(choices)
  local total_weight = 0
  for _, choice in ipairs(choices) do
    total_weight = total_weight + choice.weight
  end

  local roll = gapi.rng(1, total_weight)
  local cumulative = 0
  for _, choice in ipairs(choices) do
    cumulative = cumulative + choice.weight
    if roll <= cumulative then
      return choice.value
    end
  end
end
```

head: fk-playwright
text: Custom Playwright Test reporter that emits Flakiness.io reports. Single class in `src/playwright-test.ts`. Thin adapter — schema lives in `@flakiness/flakiness-report` (`FK.*` types), helpers in `@flakiness/sdk` (`ReportUtils`, `GitWorktree`, `CIUtils`, CPU/RAM samplers, `writeReport`/`uploadReport`/`showReport`).

head: fk-playwright > Toolchain
text: - **pnpm** (not npm/yarn). Use `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`.

head: fk-playwright > Toolchain
text: - Node 20.17+ or 22.9+, Playwright 1.57+ (balanced sharding needs 1.62+ — the `Reporter.preprocess` API).

head: fk-playwright > Toolchain
text: - Build: Kubik + esbuild (`build.mts`) → ESM, `node20` target, bundled runtime dependencies, then `tsc` for `.d.ts`.

head: fk-playwright > Invariants — do not break
text: 1. **Never throw from the reporter.** Degrade via `warn()`/`err()` (`[flakiness.io]` prefix) and continue. A reporter that crashes breaks the user's test run. **Sole exception:** balanced-sharding errors in `preprocess` throw on purpose — a shard that silently fell back to Playwright's native sharding would disagree with its sibling shards on the partition, running some tests twice and others never.

head: fk-playwright > Invariants — do not break
text: 2. **Keep it one file.** All reporter logic stays in `src/playwright-test.ts`. Push schema/transport changes upstream to `@flakiness/sdk` instead of growing this repo.

head: fk-playwright > Invariants — do not break
text: 3. **Each Playwright project → one Flakiness "environment".** `FK_ENV_*` env vars get folded into `userSuppliedData` (prefix stripped, lowercased).

head: fk-playwright > Tests
text: End-to-end, no mocks. `tests/utils.ts:generateFlakinessReport` writes a fixture project under `/tmp/flakiness-playwright/...`, `git init`s + commits it, runs the real `playwright` CLI via `execSync`, reads the resulting report. New tests in `tests/*.spec.ts` follow this pattern; use `assertCount`/`assertStatus` helpers.

head: fk-playwright > Releasing
text: Tag-driven: `pnpm version <bump>` → `git push --follow-tags` → create GitHub Release → CI publishes to npm. Prereleases (`-alpha` etc.) auto-publish to `@next`. Don't `npm publish` manually.

head: CLAUDE.md > p5.js Instance Mode
text: All p5 tools use instance mode. Every p5 global must be prefixed with `p.` (e.g., `p.background()`, `p.createCanvas()`, `p.PI`). Do NOT use global mode. DOM helpers (`createDiv`, `createSlider`, etc.) are replaced by React — never use them.

head: CLAUDE.md > p5.js Instance Mode
text: **Ambiguous names:** Use `p.random()` for p5 random, `Math.random()` for JS random. Use `p.map()` for p5 mapping, `Array.prototype.map()` for array mapping. Prefer `Math.*` for non-p5 math.

text: - Type defs are incomplete — cast `p.drawingContext` to `CanvasRenderingContext2D`, access `p.canvas` via `(p as any).canvas`

text: - Constructor is async (uses `requestAnimationFrame`) — `useP5` handles StrictMode cleanup via `hitCriticalError`

head: CLAUDE.md > p5.js Instance Mode
text: - When using canvas 2D API directly (e.g. `getImageData`), multiply dimensions by `p.pixelDensity()`

head: CLAUDE.md > p5.js Instance Mode
text: - Cache expensive computations (elevation fields, contour extraction) and only recompute when the inputs that affect them change — visual-only settings should skip recomputation

head: CLAUDE.md > p5.js Instance Mode
text: - **Performance in hot rendering loops:** For tools that draw many line segments (organic, lines, gradients), use direct canvas 2D API (`ctx.strokeStyle`, `ctx.lineWidth`, `ctx.beginPath/moveTo/lineTo/stroke`) instead of `p.stroke()`, `p.strokeWeight()`, `p.line()`. p5 methods have significant per-call overhead. Pre-parse color stops (hex→RGB) once per frame, not per segment. Use `rgb(r,g,b)` strings instead of `p5.Color` objects to avoid allocation in tight loops.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: ONNX2FMU turns an ONNX model + a JSON model description into a co-simulation FMU. The pipeline has a **Python code-generation half** and a **C runtime half**.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Python: parse → context → render (`onnx2fmu/`)
text: The whole Python side exists to produce a single `context` dict that gets rendered into templates. The data flow:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Python: parse → context → render (`onnx2fmu/`)
text: 1. **`app.py`** — Typer CLI. `generate` loads the ONNX model and JSON description, builds the context, scaffolds the FMU folder, and renders every template in `template/` through Jinja2. `compile` shells out to `cmake` (configure + build) and zips the result into a `.fmu`. `build` = `generate` then `compile`. `build()` can also be imported and called directly from a training script.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Python: parse → context → render (`onnx2fmu/`)
text: 2. **`model_description.py`** — `ModelDescription` validates the JSON against the actual ONNX graph: every declared input/output/local `name` must match a graph node, and `local` `nameIn`/`nameOut` node shapes must agree. It reads node shapes from the ONNX graph and instantiates `Input`/`Output`/`Local` variable objects, injecting the shape and FMI version into each.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Python: parse → context → render (`onnx2fmu/`)
text: 3. **`variables.py`** — `VariableFactory` and its `Input`/`Output`/`Local` subclasses. Each variable expands its tensor `shape` into a flat list of FMI **scalar** variables (`scalarValues`), one per tensor element, with per-element names, optional `labels`, and broadcast `start` values. `causality` is derived from the class name. `Local` is special: it represents a feedback variable that wires an output node back into an input node on the next step, and carries both `nameIn`/`nameOut`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Python: parse → context → render (`onnx2fmu/`)
text: 4. **`model.py`** — `Model` aggregates the variable contexts, assigns sequential FMI `valueReference`s to every scalar, generates the GUID/timestamps, and emits the final context dict consumed by the templates.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Python: parse → context → render (`onnx2fmu/`)
text: 5. **`config.py`** — Maps `onnx.TensorProto` dtypes to FMI 2.0 (`Real`/`Integer`/...) and FMI 3.0 (`Float32`/`Int32`/...) type names plus C types. Note: in FMI 2.0, ONNX `FLOAT`/`DOUBLE` both map to `Real`/`double`; FMI 3.0 distinguishes `Float32`/`Float64`. ONNX runtime requires float32, so doubles are downcast at the C boundary.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Code generation templates (`onnx2fmu/template/`)
text: Jinja2 templates rendered with the model context: `model.c` (the generated model logic), `config.h`, `buildDescription.xml`, and one of `FMI2.xml`/`FMI3.xml` (selected by `FMIVersion`). The `FMI{2,3}.xml` becomes the FMU's `modelDescription.xml`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C runtime (`onnx2fmu/src/`, `onnx2fmu/include/`, `onnx2fmu/CMakeLists.txt`)
text: These are static C sources (derived from the Modelica Reference-FMUs project) copied verbatim into each generated project. `ortUtils.c` drives ONNX Runtime inference; `cosimulation.c` and the `fmi{1,2,3}Functions.c` files implement the FMI co-simulation interface. `CMakeLists.txt` downloads/caches a pinned ONNX Runtime release (`LATEST_RELEASE_TAG`), compiles the generated `model.c` against it, and packages the `.fmu` zip. The generated `model.onnx` is bundled in the FMU's `resources/` folder and loaded at runtime — the network is *not* compiled into C.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Model description JSON
text: Top-level keys: `name` (also the FMU name), `description`, `FMIVersion` (`"2.0"` or `"3.0"`), `inputs`, `outputs`, and optional `locals`. Each input/output entry needs a `name` matching an ONNX graph node, plus optional `labels`, `description`, `variability` (`continuous` default, or `discrete`), and `start`. `locals` entries use `nameIn`/`nameOut` to define output→input feedback (used for RNN-style stateful models). See `README.md` and `examples/example1`–`example4` for worked cases, including PyTorch model declarations in the `generate-example-model.ipynb` notebooks.

head: Meiliweb > Talking to Meilisearch > When the client doesn't expose an endpoint yet
text:
**Upgrade `meilisearch` first** — don't reach for `meili.httpRequest` as the default escape hatch. The
official client ships new routes quickly, and a bump gives us its types, its route paths and its task
handling for free instead of hand-maintaining them.

head: Meiliweb > Talking to Meilisearch > When the client doesn't expose an endpoint yet
text:
When the upgraded client is _almost_ right — a field the API returns but the client doesn't type yet —
widen its types locally rather than abandoning it. `composables/useSearchRules.ts` is the reference:
it re-exports the client's types, extends the two the client lags on, and casts at the call site with a
comment saying when the cast can go.

head: Meiliweb > Talking to Meilisearch > When the client doesn't expose an endpoint yet
text:
Raw `meili.httpRequest` is a last resort, only when the latest published client genuinely has no method
for the route. Say so in a comment with the client version checked, so the next person knows when to
revisit. `composables/useWebhooks.ts` and `settings/foreign-keys.vue` predate this rule and still use
it, even though 0.60.0 now covers both — they're worth migrating.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Project Overview
text: `qvopenapi-rs` is a Rust wrapper for a proprietary Windows DLL (`wmca.dll`) from NH Investment & Securities (Korean brokerage). It provides:

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Project Overview
text: - A Rust library with async/await support for brokerage operations

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Project Overview
text: - An HTTP REST server for language-agnostic access

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Project Overview
text: - Docker deployment via Wine for Linux servers

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Critical Constraints
text: 1. **Target**: All crates compile to `i686-pc-windows-gnu` or `i686-pc-windows-msvc` (32-bit Windows). There is no native Linux/macOS build.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Critical Constraints
text: 2. **Feature flag**: `disable-unwind` is required on non-MSVC platforms (provides mock `_Unwind_Resume` for MinGW).

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Critical Constraints
text: 3. **Single-threaded runtime**: The HTTP server uses `tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()` intentionally — the Win32 message pump must run on the main thread.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Critical Constraints
text: 4. **No test suite**: There are no unit or integration tests. Verification requires brokerage credentials and network access.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Critical Constraints
text: 5. **C struct encoding**: All DLL string data is CP949-encoded, fixed-width char arrays (not null-terminated).

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions
text: - **Language**: Code and comments are in English, but domain-specific terms (TR codes, error messages, API field names) are in Korean.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions
text: - **Error handling**: Use `QvOpenApiError` enum (16 variants) with `Result<T, QvOpenApiError>`. Use `From` trait conversions for `?` operator.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions
text: - **Models**: TR request/response types live in `qvopenapi/src/models/query/`. Each TR code gets its own file.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions
text: - **Serialization**: Response data is converted from C structs → Rust structs → `serde_json::Value`.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions
text: - **HTTP framework**: `warp` (not actix-web). Routes are composed via `.or()` filter combinator.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > When Making Changes
text: - **Adding a new TR type**: Follow the step-by-step guide in Section 9 of `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > When Making Changes
text: - **Modifying DLL interaction**: Understand the threading model (Section 4.3 of `ARCHITECTURE.md`) — all DLL calls must happen on the window thread.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > When Making Changes
text: - **Modifying HTTP endpoints**: See `qvopenapi-http/src/routes/` — each endpoint is a warp filter function.

head: AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents > When Making Changes
text: - **Modifying Docker**: See `Dockerfile` and `docker/entrypoint.sh`. Xvfb + xfce4-session are required for Win32 message dispatch under Wine.

head: AGENTS > Core Principles
text:
1. Privacy first
   - Preserve user privacy by default.
   - Avoid adding telemetry or logging sensitive DNS/query data unless explicitly required.

head: AGENTS > Core Principles
text:
2. Reliability and safety
   - Prefer stable behavior over clever optimizations.
   - Handle network failures and partial outages gracefully.

head: AGENTS > Core Principles
text:
3. Cross-platform correctness
   - Keep behavior consistent across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
   - Use platform-specific code only when necessary and isolate it clearly.

head: AGENTS > Core Principles
text:
4. Minimal, composable design
   - Keep features small and focused.
   - Avoid unnecessary dependencies and overly broad abstractions.

head: AGENTS > Core Principles
text:
5. Backward compatibility
   - Preserve existing CLI behavior and flags unless a breaking change is intentional and documented.
   - Treat config format and runtime behavior as user-facing contracts.

head: AGENTS > Core Principles
text:
6. Performance on constrained systems
   - Optimize for low memory/CPU use, especially router-like environments.
   - Assume deployments may have minuscule disk space; avoid features that increase on-device storage footprint.
   - Avoid expensive background work and unbounded caches.

head: AGENTS > Core Principles
text:
7. Dependency and binary size discipline
   - Avoid new dependencies whenever possible; prefer stdlib/internal code when practical.
   - Be mindful of binary size and startup overhead when adding features.
   - If a dependency is unavoidable, justify it and keep transitive impact minimal.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agentic Seller > SECTION 7 — SALES METHODOLOGY > Discovery Frameworks
text: Use these in discovery calls and meeting prep. Full reference: `.claude/skills/discovery-prep/references/discovery-frameworks.md`

head: CLAUDE.md — Agentic Seller > SECTION 7 — SALES METHODOLOGY > Discovery Frameworks
text:
| Framework | When to use | Core idea |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| **SPIN** | Any discovery call | Situation → Problem → Implication → Need-Payoff. Never jump to Implication without a confirmed Problem. |
| **Gap Selling** | When buyer isn't feeling urgency | Current State → Root Cause → Future State. Make the gap vivid before introducing any capability. |
| **Sandler Pain Funnel** | When you have rapport | Surface pain → Business impact → Personal/emotional (Level 3 is where deals are won) |
| **Upfront Contract** | Every call opener | Set agenda + normalize a "no" so you can earn a real "yes." Eliminates "I'll think about it." |
| **AECR** | In-meeting objections | Acknowledge → Empathize → Clarify → Reframe. For cold call objections use AAA (see cold-call-framework.md). |

head: CLAUDE.md — Agentic Seller > SECTION 7 — SALES METHODOLOGY > Discovery Frameworks
text:
**60/40 Rule:** Buyer speaks 60%+ of the time in a great discovery. If you're talking more — ask a question.
Recovery phrase: *"I've been talking a lot — what's your reaction to what you've heard so far?"*

head: CLAUDE.md — Agentic Seller > SECTION 7 — SALES METHODOLOGY > Sales Motion Routes
text:
| Route | When to use | Typical deal size | CTA |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|-----|
| **Classic** | Complex, competitive, multi-stakeholder | Large / Strategic | Technical Workshop + Business Case |
| **Sprint** | Eager champion, simplified decision, single buyer | Mid-range | Sprint Zero (3-hour scoping session) |
| **Fast** | Decision already made, urgency to start | Any | Pre-Onboarding / Kickoff session |
| **Unknown** | Default when you don't know yet | Any | "Would a 15-min intro make sense?" |

head: CLAUDE.md — Agentic Seller > SECTION 7 — SALES METHODOLOGY > Sales Motion Routes
text:
**Rule:** No date = no deal. For Replace/Migrate motions, always find the compelling event.
No forcing function = the deal won't move.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents
text:
You are working **on** the demo engine, not just using it. The
[README](README.md) explains what aidemo is and why it's built this way;
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers process (DCO sign-off, PR
expectations, CI policy). If this file contradicts them, they win.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents
text:
**Mental model:** `storyboard.json` (script + per-scene voice/music plan +
browser action-spec) → `voice` (OpenAI TTS) → `record` (deterministic replay in
real Chrome, injected cursor, timeline) → `captions` (Whisper word timing) →
`compose` (ffmpeg: trim idle, sync to narration, zoom, cards, mux) →
`output/final-demo.mp4`.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Commands
text:
| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Install | `npm install` — Node 20+, system Chrome, ffmpeg+ffprobe on PATH (no Playwright browser download) |
| Type check | `npm run typecheck` |
| Fixture server | `node examples/local-demo/serve.mjs` (port 8787) |
| E2E smoke test | `node bin/aidemo.mjs render examples/local-demo --headless` |
| Dry-run actions only | `node bin/aidemo.mjs probe examples/local-demo --headless` |
| Resume a take | `node bin/aidemo.mjs record <dir> --from-scene <id>` (also `render`, MCP `fromScene`) — reuses the previous take's earlier scenes (hash-guarded), replays their actions fast, records from `<id>` |
| Draft from a Playwright trace/test | `node bin/aidemo.mjs import-trace <trace.zip\|spec.ts> --name <demo>` — actions + selectors → scenes, no LLM (MCP `import_trace`) |
| Draft from a URL | `node bin/aidemo.mjs init <name> --from-url <url>` — inspect first, headings → scenes, unique selectors → beats (MCP `init_demo {fromUrl}`) |
| Selector discovery | `node bin/aidemo.mjs inspect <url> --dir <demo>` — unique selectors per visible element (MCP `inspect` job); the same scan writes `logs/drift-*.json` suggestions when a take's selector matches nothing |
| Validate a storyboard (no browser) | `node bin/aidemo.mjs validate <dir>` (`--file <path>`, `--json`; non-zero exit on issues) |
| Lint / pacing forecast (no browser) | `node bin/aidemo.mjs lint <dir>` (`--lang`, `--json`, `--strict`) — also auto-runs in probe/record/render; measured counterpart is `output/report.json` from compose |
| Frames for review | `node bin/aidemo.mjs frames <dir> --every 3` (`--source raw` for the take) |
| Walkthrough bundle | `node bin/aidemo.mjs walkthrough <dir>` — output/walkthrough/ (index.html, guide.md, frames, captions) from the final video (also auto in `render` with `output.walkthrough`) |
| One pipeline stage | `node bin/aidemo.mjs voice\|record\|captions\|compose <dir>` |
| Screenshot stills | `node bin/aidemo.mjs stills <dir>` — extract named PNGs from an existing take (also auto-runs in `render` when the storyboard has `still` markers) |
| Golden regression check | `node bin/aidemo.mjs probe <dir> --update-golden` (write baseline) / `--golden` (CI guard, non-zero exit on drift) |
| Multi-language matrix | `node bin/aidemo.mjs render <dir> --langs de,fr` — one take → N locales (also `--lang` on voice/captions/compose) |
| Personalized variants | `node bin/aidemo.mjs render <dir> --variants variants.json` (or `--param k=v`) |
| Always-fresh embed snippets | `node bin/aidemo.mjs embed <dir>` — stable raw-GitHub URLs for READMEs/PRs |
| CI render (consumers) | `uses: tandryukha/aidemo@stable` (composite action, `action.yml`) — see `docs/CI.md` |
| MCP server (agent interface) | `node bin/aidemo.mjs mcp` — stdio; smoke test: `npm run mcp-smoke` (needs Chrome) |
| Print authoring guide | `node bin/aidemo.mjs guide` (`--topic core\|schema\|attention\|polish\|…`, `--list`) |
| Environment check | `node bin/aidemo.mjs doctor` |

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Commands
text:
`render`, `voice`, and `captions` need `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env` (or
`OPENAI_BASE_URL` pointing at a local OpenAI-compatible server, or
`AIDEMO_TTS_PROVIDER=local` + `npm install kokoro-js` for in-process TTS with
offline captions — no key at all); `probe`, `record`, and `compose` re-runs
don't. Every engine change should keep the fixture rendering end-to-end
(that's the smoke test CI can't run for you — it needs Chrome, ffmpeg, and a
TTS/STT endpoint or the local provider).

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Invariants — don't break these
text:
- **No LLM in the capture loop.** The recording is a deterministic replay of a
  fixed action-spec. Agents author storyboards; they never steer a live take.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Invariants — don't break these
Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Invariants — don't break these
text:
- **Published plugin skill stays in sync.** The Claude Code plugin ships a copy
  of the record-demo skill at `plugins/record-demo/skills/record-demo/SKILL.md`.
  It must be byte-identical to `.claude/skills/record-demo/SKILL.md`. Edit the
  canonical one, then `npm run sync:plugin-skill`; `npm run check:plugin-skill`
  fails on drift. On a version bump, also bump `version` in
  `plugins/record-demo/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Invariants — don't break these
text:
- **ffmpeg portability.** Many ffmpeg builds lack `subtitles`/`drawtext`.
  Captions and cards are headless-Chrome-rasterized PNGs overlaid with
  time-gated `enable`. Don't add filters beyond that baseline.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Invariants — don't break these
text:
- **Storyboards are backward compatible.** Cinematic and content features
  (zoom, scroll easing, ducking, cards, scene `transition` crossfades, `output`
  sizing/letterbox, `still` markers, `params`/placeholders, per-scene
  `narrations`) are opt-in; existing storyboards must render unchanged, and a
  run with no new flag must be byte-for-byte the old behavior.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Invariants — don't break these
text:
- **Polish is compose-time, not record-time.** A bad zoom must stay a
  recompose, never a re-record.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > ffmpeg gotchas (learned the hard way)
text:
- Stream-copy `concat` of `-loop 1` PNG→x264 card segments carries leading
  negative pts and **silently kills `overlay` captions** — the final card
  assembly must re-encode (`concatSegments(..., reencode: true)`); scene-only
  concat can stay stream-copy.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > ffmpeg gotchas (learned the hard way)
text:
- Never use unbounded `apad`: it never EOFs and `-t` does **not** stop it
  (runaway encode until killed). Always `apad=whole_dur=<sec>`. Same class:
  `-stream_loop -1` through `atrim` never EOFs — loop a computed finite count.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > ffmpeg gotchas (learned the hard way)
text:
- `zoompan`: use `on/FPS` as the time base (input must be CFR), single-quote
  every expression (they contain commas), and pre-upscale 2× below ~1600 px
  width or integer-pixel crops shimmer.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > ffmpeg gotchas (learned the hard way)
text:
- The final mux writes `-movflags +faststart` (moov first, web-playable), so
  **compare renders by stream, not by file hash**: `ffmpeg -i out.mp4 -map 0:v
  -c copy -f md5 -` (and `-map 0:a`) must match the pre-change render for an
  unchanged storyboard; the container bytes legitimately differ.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > ffmpeg gotchas (learned the hard way)
text:
- Debugging compose: `AIDEMO_KEEP_TMP=1` preserves `.compose-tmp/`
  intermediates. Logs land in `<demo>/logs/<command>.log`; a failed take also
  leaves `logs/fail-*.png/json`.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Repo conventions
text:
- `demos/` is untracked scratch and `docs/internal/` is gitignored — never
  link to either from tracked files.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Repo conventions
text:
- Commit style: short imperative subject (`fix: compose hangs on unbounded
  apad`); every commit signed off (`git commit -s` — DCO, required to merge).

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Repo conventions
text:
- CI is typecheck + gitleaks + dependency review. PRs must not add install
  scripts, new network endpoints, or unpinned GitHub Actions.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Repo conventions
text:
- Canonical repo: `github.com/tandryukha/aidemo`. Consumers run the engine via
  `npx -y github:tandryukha/aidemo#stable` (git ref, the primary channel) or
  `npx -y @tandryukha/aidemo` (npm, additive — published from `release.yml` when
  repo var `NPM_PUBLISH=true`, via OIDC trusted publishing + provenance);
  `server.json` is the MCP-registry manifest. See RELEASING.md for how the
  `stable` tag moves and the one-time npm setup.

head: Working on aidemo — guide for coding agents > Repo conventions
text:
- **npm `files` allowlist tracks runtime reads.** `package.json` `files` ships
  only `bin/`, `src/`, `docs/AUTHORING.md`, `.claude/skills/record-demo/SKILL.md`.
  If you add code that reads a new file relative to `ENGINE_ROOT`/`REPO_ROOT`
  (e.g. another served doc or template), add it to `files` too — else it works
  from the git checkout but the npm package silently breaks. Verify with
  `npm pack --dry-run` (and an install-from-tarball `aidemo guide` smoke).

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: `any-guardrail` is a unified Python library (Python 3.11+) providing a consistent interface for multiple AI safety guardrail backends. It lets developers swap between guardrail implementations — and the runtimes that execute them — without changing application code. Maintained by Mozilla AI under Apache 2.0.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - **Guardrails** (`src/any_guardrail/guardrails/<name>/<name>.py`) — domain logic. Each one defines what to check (harm, prompt-injection, off-topic, etc.) and how to interpret model output. Every guardrail exposes a `validate(input_text, ...)` method returning a `GuardrailOutput`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - **Providers** (`src/any_guardrail/providers/<name>.py`) — execution backends. They load models, tokenize, and run inference. Guardrails accept a `provider=` kwarg, so the same guardrail can run against different backends (e.g. local HuggingFace transformers via `HuggingFaceProvider`, Mozilla single-binary classifiers via `EncoderfileProvider`, or Mozilla single-binary decoder LLMs via `LlamafileProvider`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core abstractions (`src/any_guardrail/`)
text:
- **`base.py`** — class hierarchy:
  - `Guardrail` (ABC) — base class; every guardrail implements `validate()` returning a `GuardrailOutput`.
  - `ThreeStageGuardrail` (ABC) — opinionated pipeline subclass: `_pre_processing` → `_inference` → `_post_processing`. The default `validate()` chains these and supports list inputs (batched).
  - `GuardrailName` — string enum of all supported guardrail identifiers (used by the factory).
  - `StandardGuardrail` — type alias for `ThreeStageGuardrail[AnyDict, AnyDict]`, used by simple binary classifiers.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core abstractions (`src/any_guardrail/`)
text: - **`types.py`** — the concrete `GuardrailOutput` model (the output standard: `valid: bool` required; canonical risk `score: float | None` where higher = riskier; `categories: list[CategoryResult]`; `spans`; `modified_text`; `usage: GuardrailUsage`; `explanation: str | None` for human-readable rationale only; `extra`/`raw` escape hatches), its building blocks (`CategoryResult`, `SpanResult`, `GuardrailUsage`), the generic stage wrappers (`GuardrailPreprocessOutput`, `GuardrailInferenceOutput`), and shared aliases (`AnyDict`, `ChatMessages`, etc.). `GuardrailOutput` uses `arbitrary_types_allowed=True` so `raw` can hold numpy arrays / torch tensors / SDK objects. Judges that can't parse a verdict fail closed: `valid=False` with `extra={"parse_failure": True}`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core abstractions (`src/any_guardrail/`)
text: - **`api.py`** — `AnyGuardrail` factory. `AnyGuardrail.create(GuardrailName.PROTECTAI, ...)` does dynamic module import using the convention: snake_case enum value → `any_guardrail.guardrails.<name>.<name>` module → PascalCase class.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`)
text: Providers are an execution layer that guardrails compose with, not inherit from.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`)
text: - **`base.py`** — `Provider` (ABC) with abstract `load_model()`, `pre_process()`, `infer()` methods. `StandardProvider` is the type alias `Provider[AnyDict, AnyDict]`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`)
text: - **`huggingface.py`** — `HuggingFaceProvider` is the default for most guardrails. Loads via `transformers.from_pretrained`, tokenizes per-call, runs `model(**inputs)` under `torch.no_grad()`. Surfaces `device`, `torch_dtype`, `cache_dir`, `revision`, `model_kwargs`, `tokenizer_kwargs`, `multi_label` as constructor args.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`)
text: - **`encoderfile.py`** — `EncoderfileProvider` runs Mozilla AI's [`encoderfile`](https://github.com/mozilla-ai/encoderfile) single-binary format (encoder + classification head packaged as one executable). On `load_model()` it auto-downloads the platform-specific artifact from `mozilla-ai/encoderfile` on HuggingFace, spawns the binary as a subprocess HTTP server, polls `/predict` for readiness, then proxies inference calls over `127.0.0.1`. Drop-in for `HuggingFaceProvider` on supported encoder classifiers — no `torch`/`transformers` install required. Implements the context manager protocol (`with EncoderfileProvider() as provider: ...`) for deterministic subprocess cleanup; `atexit` is the fallback. Curated artifact map lives at `providers/_encoderfile_artifacts.py`. macOS + Linux only.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`)
text: - **`llamafile.py`** — `LlamafileProvider` runs Mozilla's [`llamafile`](https://github.com/Mozilla-Ocho/llamafile) format (decoder LLM = llama.cpp + GGUF weights packaged via Cosmopolitan Libc as one multi-platform executable). On `load_model()` it auto-downloads the artifact, spawns it as an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server (`--server --jinja --no-webui`), polls `/health` for readiness, then routes `generate_chat()` calls to `POST /v1/chat/completions`. **Chat-only** — `pre_process()` and `infer()` raise `NotImplementedError`; decoder-LLM guardrails consume it via `generate_chat()` instead. Implements the context manager protocol (`with LlamafileProvider() as provider: ...`) for deterministic subprocess cleanup; `atexit` is the fallback. Two platform notes: launching is done via `sh <binary>` because macOS arm64 can't `execve` Cosmopolitan APE polyglots directly (the APE prelude is valid POSIX shell that exec's into the binary); GPU offload is exposed via `n_gpu_layers=`. Curated artifact map at `providers/_llamafile_artifacts.py`; constructor also accepts `repo_id=` + `filename=` overrides.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`)
text: Both subprocess providers also support an **external-server mode**: pass `base_url=` to the constructor to point at an encoderfile/llamafile server you manage yourself. It's mutually exclusive with all download/spawn constructor args; `load_model()` skips download/spawn and just polls the server for readiness, and `close()` is a no-op there (`base_url` is preserved so the provider stays reusable).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`)
text: A guardrail's `__init__` typically builds a default `HuggingFaceProvider` if none is supplied:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`)
text: For decoder-LLM-backed guardrails (`GraniteGuardian`, `LlamaGuard`, `ShieldGemma`), the right loader is enforced at load time: `HuggingFaceProvider.load_model()` accepts per-call `model_class`/`tokenizer_class` kwargs that override the constructor defaults (without mutating them), and these guardrails pass e.g. `model_class=AutoModelForCausalLM` on every `load_model()` call. So handing them a default-constructed `HuggingFaceProvider()` (which targets `AutoModelForSequenceClassification`) works — the guardrail corrects the loader itself.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Uniform `infer()` shape
text: Both providers return the same dict shape from `infer()` so guardrails are provider-agnostic at the post-processing stage:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Uniform `infer()` shape
text: - `logits`: per-input logits (numpy array, shape `(batch, num_classes)`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Uniform `infer()` shape
text: - `scores`: softmax or sigmoid (when `multi_label=True`) of logits.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Uniform `infer()` shape
text: - `predicted_indices`: list of argmax indices, one per row.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Uniform `infer()` shape
text: - `predicted_labels`: list of labels resolved via `id2label` (HF) or returned natively by the binary (encoderfile).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Uniform `infer()` shape
text: - `labels`: full ordered label list aligning index-wise with `scores` columns (HF via `id2label`; `None` for encoderfile, whose `/predict` response only carries the predicted label — 2-class guardrails fall back to complement logic).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Uniform `infer()` shape
text: Exception: causal-LM-backed guardrails using `HuggingFaceProvider` (`ShieldGemma`) produce 3D logits `(batch, seq, vocab)`. In that case `infer()` returns `logits` as a raw torch tensor and sets `scores`/`predicted_indices`/`predicted_labels` to `None`; the guardrail does its own selection (e.g. `logits[0, -1, [vocab["Yes"], vocab["No"]]]`) and softmax. This is checked in unit tests — when adding a new guardrail that runs a causal LM through `provider.infer()`, expect the raw-tensor path.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Opt-in `generate_chat()` for chat-style decoder LLMs
text: `Provider.generate_chat(messages, max_new_tokens, ...)` is the parallel contract for decoder-LLM workflows that don't fit the `pre_process` → `infer` shape (e.g. judge models that emit a yes/no string). The base implementation raises `NotImplementedError` so encoder providers (`EncoderfileProvider`, `AzureContentSafety`) are unaffected — it's opt-in.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Opt-in `generate_chat()` for chat-style decoder LLMs
text: Both `HuggingFaceProvider` and `LlamafileProvider` implement it and return the same dict shape:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Opt-in `generate_chat()` for chat-style decoder LLMs
text: - `generated_text`: decoded new tokens only (prompt stripped).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Opt-in `generate_chat()` for chat-style decoder LLMs
text: - `prompt_token_count` / `completion_token_count`: ints, or `None` when the backend doesn't surface them (llamafile tokenizes server-side).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Opt-in `generate_chat()` for chat-style decoder LLMs
text: - `raw`: provider-specific raw output (HF tensor / OpenAI JSON), for callers that need it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Opt-in `generate_chat()` for chat-style decoder LLMs
text: `GraniteGuardian`, `LlamaGuard`, and the decoder guardrails from issues #179/#93 (`WildGuard`, `DynaGuard`, `NemotronContentSafety`, `PolyGuard`, `KananaSafeguard`, `GptOssSafeguard`, `Qwen3Guard`, `Prometheus`, `CompassJudger`, `Selene`) consume `generate_chat()` instead of touching `provider.tokenizer.apply_chat_template` + `provider.model.generate` directly, which is what lets them swap between the HF and llamafile backends. They no longer `import torch`. `chat_template_kwargs` (e.g. RAG `documents`, `available_tools`) and `generation_kwargs` (e.g. `pad_token_id` for Llama Guard 3) are pass-throughs.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`src/any_guardrail/providers/`) > Opt-in `generate_chat()` for chat-style decoder LLMs
text: Two more `generate_chat()` flags exist for models that don't fit the plain chat→decode shape: `skip_special_tokens` (set `False` when the verdict *is* a special token, e.g. Kanana's `<SAFE>`/`<UNSAFE-*>`) and `apply_chat_template` (set `False` to feed `messages[0]["content"]` to the model as a raw prompt, for models shipping their own instruction wrapper, e.g. WildGuard). `LlamafileProvider` ignores `skip_special_tokens` (server-side decoding) and rejects `apply_chat_template=False` — those models are HF-only.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Guardrail implementations (`src/any_guardrail/guardrails/`)
text: Each guardrail lives in its own subdirectory (e.g. `llama_guard/llama_guard.py`). They inherit from `Guardrail`, `ThreeStageGuardrail`, or `StandardGuardrail` depending on shape:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Guardrail implementations (`src/any_guardrail/guardrails/`)
text: - `Guardrail` directly: API-based or fully custom shape — `AnyLlm` (any-llm SDK), `Alinia` (HTTP API), and the library-wrapped span guardrail `LettuceDetect` (wraps the `lettucedetect` lib, emits `GuardrailOutput.spans`) and `GliGuard` (wraps `gliner2`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Guardrail implementations (`src/any_guardrail/guardrails/`)
text: - `ThreeStageGuardrail` with custom generics: generative/judge models or non-binary outputs — `GraniteGuardian`, `LlamaGuard`, `Glider`, `Flowjudge`, `AzureContentSafety`, `DuoGuard` (multi-label), `OffTopic`, the decoder safety classifiers `WildGuard` / `DynaGuard` / `NemotronContentSafety` / `PolyGuard` / `KananaSafeguard` / `GptOssSafeguard` / `Qwen3Guard`, the rubric judges `Prometheus` / `CompassJudger` / `Selene`, and `Qwen3GuardStream` (token-level streaming heads loaded as remote code; HF-only, requires `transformers<5`, drives `provider.model.stream_moderate_from_ids` directly and emits `spans`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Guardrail implementations (`src/any_guardrail/guardrails/`)
text: - `StandardGuardrail`: simple binary classifiers — `Protectai`, `Deepset`, `Jasper`, `Sentinel`, `Pangolin`, `InjecGuard`, `HarmGuard`, `PromptGuard`. Also `BielikGuard` (multi-label via `multi_label=True`, like DuoGuard) and `ShieldGemma` (causal-LM-backed), which still fit the `StandardGuardrail` shape.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Guardrail implementations (`src/any_guardrail/guardrails/`)
text: Library-wrapped guardrails (`Flowjudge`, `LettuceDetect`, `GliGuard`) bypass the provider and call an upstream library directly, guarded by a top-of-module `try/except ImportError` that re-raises a helpful `pip install` hint from `__init__` (see `flowjudge.py`). `Flowjudge` also accepts a `model=` backend (any `flow_judge` backend — `Hf`/`Vllm`/`Llamafile`/`Baseten`), a prebuilt/preset `metric=`, and `generation_params=` for the default `Hf` backend.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Guardrail implementations (`src/any_guardrail/guardrails/`)
text: Shared helpers live in `src/any_guardrail/guardrails/utils.py`: `default()` (model-id validation), `match_injection_label()` (the common "is the predicted label X?" post-processing), and `normalize_rubric_to_risk()` (map a Likert/rubric score onto the canonical risk axis, used by the judges).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 1. Create `src/any_guardrail/guardrails/<name>/<name>.py`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 2. Inherit from `Guardrail`, `ThreeStageGuardrail`, or `StandardGuardrail`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 3. Set `SUPPORTED_MODELS: ClassVar = [...]`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 4. Add an entry to `GuardrailName` in `src/any_guardrail/base.py`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 5. In `__init__`, accept `provider: StandardProvider | None = None` and build a default `HuggingFaceProvider` (with the right `model_class`/`tokenizer_class` for the model) if not supplied. Call `self.provider.load_model(self.model_id)`. For decoder-LLM guardrails, do the `from transformers import ...` *inside* the `provider is None` branch (lazy import) so users on a `[llamafile]`-only install can supply their own provider without paying the import cost or hitting `ImportError` at module load; see `granite_guardian.py` / `llama_guard.py` for the pattern.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 6. Implement `_pre_processing`, `_inference`, `_post_processing` (or override `validate` directly for non-three-stage shapes).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 7. Add a `GUARDRAIL_METADATA` entry in `src/any_guardrail/registry.py`, and set `METADATA: ClassVar[GuardrailMetadata] = GUARDRAIL_METADATA[GuardrailName.<NAME>]` on the class next to `SUPPORTED_MODELS`. The metadata `description` **must equal the class docstring's first summary line** (a unit test enforces this), so it doubles as the guardrail's catalog flavor text. Record its `categories`/`primary_category`/`stages`/`output_shapes`/`backend`, the `required`/`optional` `validate()` kwargs, and the secondary flags. Then run `python scripts/generate_metadata_json.py` and `python scripts/generate_summary.py` and commit the results. The API-reference `GUARDRAILS` list and the grouped `docs/SUMMARY.md` navigation are now **derived** from `GuardrailName` + the registry — there are no hand-maintained lists to edit.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 8. **If the guardrail authors a prompt** (generative/judge models with an in-repo template): add a `PromptSpec` entry to `PROMPT_REGISTRY` in `src/any_guardrail/prompt_registry.py` (the prompt text lives there, not in the guardrail module; record each version's `source` URL and `provenance`), set `PROMPT: ClassVar[PromptSpec] = PROMPT_REGISTRY[GuardrailName.<NAME>]` on the class next to `METADATA`, and wire the override (`prompt`/`prompt_version` constructor kwargs, or `system_prompt=`/`prompt_version=` for call-time judges like `AnyLlm`). Keep any moved module-level constant as an alias sourced from the registry so existing imports still work. Then run `python scripts/generate_prompts_json.py` and commit `schemas/guardrail_prompts.json`. Parity tests in `tests/unit/test_prompts.py` enforce the `PROMPT` ClassVar identity and the placeholder contract. (Skip for encoder classifiers and chat-template-only models that author no in-repo prompt.)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: 9. Tests: unit tests under `tests/unit/` (mock the provider so weights aren't downloaded); integration tests under `tests/integration/` (real model — auto-marked `e2e` by that directory's conftest; add `pytestmark = pytest.mark.heavy` if it needs >5 GB RAM/disk or a GPU so CI's default integration job skips it). The taxonomy parity tests in `tests/unit/test_metadata.py` will fail until the registry entry, the `METADATA` ClassVar, and the docstring first line all line up.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Adding a new guardrail
text: The factory auto-discovers via the naming convention: snake_case directory name in `GuardrailName` → matching module → PascalCase class.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code quality
text:
- **Ruff** — line length 120, `extend-select = ["ALL"]` with targeted ignores in `pyproject.toml`. Lazy imports are intentional (`PLC0415` is ignored). The pre-commit config pins a specific ruff version (the `rev` in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, kept current by an autoupdate workflow); CI runs that pinned version, so always run `pre-commit run --all-files` before pushing.
  - **Watch out:** `pre-commit run` reuses a cached virtualenv per hook revision. When `.pre-commit-config.yaml` bumps the ruff `rev`, your local cache can stay on the old version until you clean it. If CI's linter fails with ruff rules that your local pre-commit didn't flag, run `pre-commit clean && pre-commit run --all-files` to force a fresh install of the pinned version, then re-test. Cached venvs live under `~/.cache/pre-commit/repo*/py_env-*/bin/ruff` — confirm versions with `find ~/.cache/pre-commit -name ruff -type f -exec {} --version \;`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code quality
text: - **mypy** — strict mode globally (`disallow_untyped_defs`, `disallow_untyped_calls`). Tests are slightly relaxed (`disallow_untyped_decorators=false`) so pytest fixtures don't fight the type checker.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code quality
text: - **codespell, nbstripout, standard hooks** — run via pre-commit.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code quality
text: - **Pytest** — 120s timeout per test, `--strict-markers` (`pyproject.toml`). Integration tests use `pytest-xdist` for parallelism (`-n auto`). Model-heavy tests are gated by markers, not env vars: everything under `tests/integration/` is auto-marked `e2e` (see `tests/integration/conftest.py`), and tests needing >5 GB RAM/disk or a GPU additionally get `pytest.mark.heavy`. CI's integration job runs `-m "e2e and not heavy"` by default.

text: Core deps are minimal: `any-llm-sdk` and `pydantic`. Heavy backends are optional extras:

head: CLAUDE.md > Dependencies
text: Note: a candidate guardrail whose only distribution is a git-only library (not on PyPI) gets no extra — PyPI forbids direct-URL deps in published metadata, and that breaks `uv` resolution of `[all]`. The `MiniCheck` model was dropped for exactly this reason.

head: CLAUDE.md > Dependencies
text: Pre-commit hooks live in their own `lint` group (in `[dependency-groups]`), pytest tooling in `tests`, docs in `docs`. `uv sync --dev` pulls all three.

The **guardrail** list (between the `GUARDRAIL-NAV` markers) is generated by `scripts/generate_summary.py` from the taxonomy registry — don't hand-edit it; a `--check` pre-commit hook fails if it drifts.

head: CLAUDE.md > Docs publishing
text: - `schemas/guardrail_prompts.json` — generated export of the prompt registry (`scripts/generate_prompts_json.py`, `--check` in pre-commit), pinning each prompt-bearing guardrail's default/author prompt versions (with `source`/`provenance`) so external tooling and benchmarking can reference the exact prompt without importing the package.

head: CLAUDE.md > Docs publishing
text: - `schemas/guardrail_parameters.json` — generated export of the per-guardrail parameter schema (`scripts/generate_parameters_json.py`, `--check` in pre-commit). Each guardrail maps to `{"parameters": [...], "requirement_groups": [...]}` so external tooling can build config UIs without importing the package. Every `parameters` entry carries `name`, `stage`, `type`, `required`, `default`, `choices`, `description`, plus three fields the signature alone can't express: `env_var` (an environment variable that back-fills the argument, e.g. `endpoint`→`ALINIA_ENDPOINT`), `secret` (a credential to mask and never log — API keys are now surfaced with `secret=True` instead of being dropped), and `effectively_required` (a value that must exist at runtime even though the argument has a default). `requirement_groups` are guardrail-level "at least one of these interchangeable params (or their env fallback) must be provided" constraints (the `RequirementGroup` model, exposed via `AnyGuardrail.get_requirement_groups(name)`) — e.g. watsonx's `project_id`/`space_id`. It is **generated from signatures**: `scripts/generate_parameter_data.py` introspects every guardrail's `__init__`/`validate` and docstrings into the stdlib-only `src/any_guardrail/_parameter_data.py` leaf (which also embeds the requirement groups), which the import-free `parameter_registry.py` assembles into typed `ParameterSpec`s (via `AnyGuardrail.get_parameter_schema(name)`) and `RequirementGroup`s. `enum` choices are reused from `SUPPORTED_MODELS` (`model_id`), the content registry (`criteria`/`policy`/`rubric`), and the prompt registry (`prompt_version`). The runtime-requirement facts (`env_var`/`secret`/`effectively_required`/`requirement_groups`) live in hand-maintained maps in `generate_parameter_data.py` because they come from function bodies, not signatures; parity tests in `tests/unit/test_parameters.py` enforce no drift from signatures, reconciliation with `required/optional_validate_kwargs`, and — bidirectionally against the guardrail source — that every declared `env_var` is exactly what the guardrail actually reads. Adding or changing a guardrail's params is picked up by rerunning the two generators (declare any new env-var fallback / secret / group in the maps) — there is no hand-maintained parameter list.

head: CLAUDE.md > Docs publishing
text: - `schemas/guardrail_benchmarks.json` — generated export of the benchmark registry (`scripts/generate_benchmarks_json.py`, `--check` in pre-commit), and `schemas/guardrail_benchmarks.schema.json` — the JSON Schema for a `BenchmarkResult` (`scripts/generate_benchmark_schema.py`, `--check`). These back the **benchmark-backed model cards** (issue #194): each guardrail's API page renders a `## Benchmarks` table (grouped by category, `None`→`—`, provenance + contamination + comparison-cohort keys shown) and a `## License` section, from the import-free `benchmark_registry.py` + the taxonomy metadata. Benchmark numbers are hand-authored `BenchmarkResult(...)` entries in `src/any_guardrail/_benchmark_data.py`, each carrying a `BenchmarkSource` (`published:<url>` / `measured:<harness-version>`) and a `ComparisonCohort`; `group_comparable` refuses to co-rank scores across cohorts (the comparability invariant). The registry ships **hand-authored results** (published harvests plus `measured:` numbers from evaluation runs) — the model-heavy evaluation harness that produces new numbers lives in the unshipped top-level `benchmarks/` package (GuardBench adapter + custom-runner stubs + operational measurement; `benchmarks` dependency-group, `uv sync --group benchmarks`) and runs **out-of-repo, never in CI** (see `benchmarks/README.md`). `tests/unit/test_benchmarks.py` locks in the comparability invariant with adversarial cohort fixtures.

head: CLAUDE.md > Docs publishing
text: - Every Python code block in `docs/**/*.md` is executed in CI by `tests/docs/test_all.py` (mktestdocs, with `AnyGuardrail._get_guardrail_class` mocked so no models download) — docs snippets must be runnable as written.

head: vox — agent rules
text:
Turns one topic into a finished narrated motion-graphics explainer video. One
approval gate, one backend: the **Higgsfield MCP**.

head: vox — agent rules
text: `skills/vox-style/SKILL.md` is the pipeline. This file is the project contract.

head: vox — agent rules > Layout
text: Four skills under `skills/`, each symlinked from `.claude/skills/`:

head: vox — agent rules > Layout
text:
| Skill | Role |
|---|---|
| `vox-style` | **Main.** The pipeline and the five modes. |
| `higgsfield-video-explainer` | Vendored. Owns every tool call and the assembly contract. |
| `higgsfield-generate` | Vendored. Model catalogue and prompt-engineering reference. |
| `higgsfield-soul-id` | Vendored. Identity models. |

head: vox — agent rules > Layout
text:
`vox-style` is a **front end**, not a reimplementation. It adds input handling
(trend / article / no topic), three locked house styles, one approval gate with a
credit estimate, four surrounding modes in `references/modes.md`, and a durable
record under `output/`. Everything else belongs to the vendored workflow.

head: vox — agent rules > Layout
text:
Run folders are named for the subject, not the date — `output/<topic-slug>/` —
because a date does not distinguish two runs on the same day and a slug says what
the run actually was. The date lives in `brief.md` and `manifest.json`.

head: vox — agent rules > Layout
text:
`output/` is gitignored **deny-by-default**: everything is ignored except
`brief.md`, `script.md`, `storyboard.md` and `manifest.json`. The text record of
every run is tracked; not one byte of media is. Adding a new media format needs
no gitignore change, which is the whole reason the rule is written that way.

head: vox — agent rules > Precedence
text:
When two sources disagree: **live MCP > vendored skill > vox-style.** If a tool's
real behaviour contradicts a document, the tool is right and the document gets
fixed — with a note saying it was verified on a real run, since that is the only
thing that distinguishes a correction from a guess.

head: vox — agent rules > Precedence
text:
`vox-style` overrides upstream in exactly two documented places, both in its
SKILL.md: the wizard, which replaces upstream's Phase 0, and the one-gate rule.

head: vox — agent rules > Vendored skills are CLI-era
text:
Upstream `higgsfield-ai/skills` was `0.12.0` at vendor time and is written in
`higgsfield ...` shell commands. **There is no CLI here.** Each vendored skill
carries a banner and a `references/mcp-mapping.md` with the translation table.

head: vox — agent rules > Vendored skills are CLI-era
text:
- `higgsfield-video-explainer/SKILL.md` is the hand-adapted MCP version
  (`1.2-mcp`), not upstream's text.

head: vox — agent rules > Vendored skills are CLI-era
text:
- `higgsfield-generate` and `higgsfield-soul-id` are upstream verbatim plus the
  banner. Their `marketing-studio`, `workflow` and `soul-id` subcommands have MCP
  equivalents this project has not exercised — **do not guess a tool name.** Read
  the connected tool list, or say it is unmapped.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **Paths anchor on `PROJECT_ROOT`** (this directory, marked by `.vox-root`). The
  project must stay exportable and work when opened directly. Skill folders are
  read-only.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **One approval gate, and it is real.** The gate is about money, not turns. The
  wizard asks seven questions every run and research, script and storyboard run
  to completion after it — all of it free. Then stop, show everything, quote the
  credit cost against the live balance, and wait. Never submit a paid job before
  the user replies. The gate is the only place a credit is committed and the only
  stop that needs a yes.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **The wizard runs every time.** Never skip a question because the request
  already answered it. What the user said becomes that question's pre-selected
  first option instead, so accepting it costs one keystroke.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **Quote real numbers.** `balance` for the balance, `get_cost: true` for the
  price. Preflight is free. Never guess.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **The style key attaches to every clip.** This is the entire reason the output
  reads as one production. A clip without it is a defect, not a variation.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **Pass `aspect_ratio` explicitly on every clip.** It does not inherit from the
  key image. Verified on a real run.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **Voice before clips, strictly.** Each take's real duration decides whether a
  line needs shortening before 30 credits go on its clip.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **Assemble server-side** with `explainer_video`. `scripts/assemble.py` is the
  offline fallback only.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **Save every job id to `manifest.json` as you go**, so a crashed run resumes
  instead of re-paying.

head: vox — agent rules > Always
text:
- **Rebuild `dist/` after touching any skill** — `./scripts/build-skills.sh`. The
  bundles are the download path for Cowork and stale ones are worse than absent.

head: vox — agent rules > Never
text: - Never run a `higgsfield` shell command.

head: vox — agent rules > Never
text: - Never invent a number, a source, or an MCP tool name.

head: vox — agent rules > Never
text:
- Never generate the same block twice to get two aspects. Dual aspect is one 16:9
  render plus a free center-cropped re-assembly; see the dual-aspect rule in
  `vox-style/SKILL.md`.

head: vox — agent rules > Never
text:
- Never accept a server `preset_recommendation`. Resubmit with
  `declined_preset_id`.

head: vox — agent rules > Never
text: - Never deliver loose clips. Assembly happens in the same run.

head: vox — agent rules > Never
text: - Never add a credential to this project. It has none, by design.

head: vox — agent rules > Scope
text:
Delivery stops at the MP4 and its source list. No titles, descriptions, hashtags,
thumbnails, or uploads.

head: Ghost Chat v4
text: Desktop chat overlay for streamers. Go + Wails v3 (alpha) + React + TypeScript. Go chat clients live in `internal/chat/{twitch,youtube,kick}`, the UI in `frontend/`, the landing page in `website/`.

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Go
text: - `internal/` for private packages; error messages lowercase, no punctuation, wrap with `%w`

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Go
text: - Single `*config.Config` pointer shared via the App struct

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Go
text: - Exported methods on `App` become JS-callable Wails bindings; App implements `ServiceStartup`/`ServiceShutdown`

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Frontend
text: - React Compiler is enabled — avoid `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`React.memo` unless it genuinely can't optimize a case

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Frontend
text: - Zustand for state, react-router-dom HashRouter; Settings is a toggle (not a route) that expands the window via a Go binding

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Frontend
text: - No UI component libraries, no preprocessors — CSS modules + custom properties in `index.css`, modern nested CSS, neutral color scheme

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Frontend
text: - oxlint/oxfmt (not eslint/prettier); pin exact dependency versions (no `^`/`~`)

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Frontend
text: - Path aliases: `@/` → `src/`, `@bindings/` → `bindings/`

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Style (Go + TS)
text: - No comments unless the logic is non-obvious; no emoji

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Conventions > Style (Go + TS)
text: - Blank line before/after function calls, if/loops/closures, and assignments; sequential declarations or assignments may be grouped

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Wails v3 bindings
text: - Go methods on `App` generate TS in `frontend/bindings/`. Regenerate with `wails3 generate bindings -ts -clean` — the project commits `.ts`; a bare `generate` emits `.js` on alpha.97+.

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Wails v3 bindings
text: - Imports: methods `from '@bindings/ghost-chat/app.js'`, types `from '@bindings/ghost-chat/internal/config/models.js'`, runtime `from '@wailsio/runtime'`

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Wails v3 bindings
text: - Events: `Events.On('name', (ev) => ev.data)` — the callback gets a `WailsEvent` with `.data`

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Gotchas
text: - `golang.design/x/hotkey` must register in a goroutine, not the main thread, or it SIGTRAPs on macOS

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Gotchas
text: - Window state is saved in `ShouldQuit`/`ServiceShutdown`; the macOS dock-quit routes through `ShouldQuit`

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Gotchas
text: - Adding or updating a platform also means updating `website/index.html` (hero, features, FAQ) and refreshing the screenshots in `website/assets/`

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Agent skills > Issue tracker
text: Issues are tracked as GitHub issues via the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Agent skills > Triage labels
text: Canonical role names map 1:1 to repo labels (existing `wontfix` reused; the other four are created on first triage). See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Agent skills > Domain docs
text: Single-context — one `CONTEXT.md` + `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

head: Ghost Chat v4 > Agent skills > Executing work
text:
Once tasks are ready, execute them in-session with the
`subagent-driven-development` skill: one fresh implementer subagent per task
(building test-first via `tdd`), a spec+quality review after each, then a
whole-branch review before merge. Task source: either a plan file with
`## Task N` headings (SDD extracts each with its `task-brief` script) or an
agent-ready brief handed over verbatim (e.g. a GitHub issue body — see
`docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`). SDD's transient run artifacts live in
self-ignored `.scratch/sdd/` — never committed. See `docs/agents/execution.md`.

head: OKX.Net Skill > Quick Decision
text: If the user asks for OKX API access in C#/.NET, **use OKX.Net**. Do not write raw `HttpClient` calls to OKX endpoints. OKX.Net handles signing, timestamping, rate limit integration, response parsing, WebSocket reconnects, and the `HttpResult<T>` / `HttpResult` / `WebSocketResult<UpdateSubscription>` / `QueryResult<T>` result model.

head: OKX.Net Skill > Core Pattern: Result Handling
text: REST methods return `HttpResult<T>` or `HttpResult`. WebSocket subscription methods return `WebSocketResult<UpdateSubscription>`. Socket API request/response methods return `QueryResult<T>`. Shared symbol/cache helper methods can return `ExchangeCallResult<T>`. Always check `.Success` before reading `.Data`.

head: OKX.Net Skill > Core Pattern: API Surface

head: OKX.Net Skill > Core Pattern: API Surface

head: OKX.Net Skill > Multi-Exchange via CryptoExchange.Net.SharedApis
text: `IGetSpotSymbolsRest` and `IGetFuturesSymbolsRest` expose cached symbol catalogs. Their shared symbol results include display names plus base/quote asset type and subtype metadata, including crypto, fiat, TradFi, stablecoin, equity, and commodity classifications where applicable.

head: OKX.Net Skill > Multi-Exchange via CryptoExchange.Net.SharedApis
