text: See `tasks/learnings.md` (local, gitignored) for the full list of bugs encountered and patterns to avoid — append new learnings there as work proceeds. Key rules:

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 1. **No bincode with `#[serde(untagged)]` or `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]`.** Any type in the serialization tree with these attributes must use a self-describing format (JSON, MessagePack, CBOR). Check nested types, not just top-level structs.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 2. **Check framework syntax against the pinned version.** Axum 0.7 uses `:param`, axum 0.8 uses `{param}`. If parameterized routes 404 but static routes work, suspect syntax mismatch.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 3. **S3 keys and URL paths have different rules.** S3 keys allow `/`; URL `:param` segments do not. Use separate helpers (`object_store_key()` for storage, `api_ns()` for URLs) and consider validating namespace names at creation time.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 4. **Never compute checksums from non-deterministic serialization.** `HashMap` iteration order is not stable across JSON round-trips. Canonicalize via `BTreeMap` before hashing.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 5. **`random_vectors()` reuses IDs across calls.** When testing dedup/merge, use unique ID prefixes per fragment.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 6. **Keep `TempDir` alive for the lifetime of anything using its path.** `TempDir::drop()` deletes the directory. Return it from setup functions so callers hold the handle.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 7. **Use unique temp filenames for atomic writes under concurrency.** `{file}.{uuid}.tmp` avoids races when multiple tasks write to the same cache key.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 8. **Enable `S3ConditionalPut::ETagMatch` in the S3 builder.** Without it, `put_opts` with `PutMode::Update` returns `NotImplemented` — CAS is silently broken. Always set `.with_conditional_put(S3ConditionalPut::ETagMatch)`.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 9. **Two-layer defense for distributed writes: fencing check + CAS.** Neither alone prevents zombie writes. Fencing has a TOCTOU gap; CAS alone doesn't detect stale tokens. Both layers are essential.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text: 10. **Lease release must be best-effort.** A process whose lease expired and was taken over must handle release gracefully (Ok or non-fatal error), never block or deadlock.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text:
11. **The pinned IVF recall gate is the quality authority.** Changes to flat
    partitioning or omitted-probe policy must run
    `tests/ivf_recall_gate.rs` against both `wikidpr1m` and `wikidpr2m`.
    Offline evaluators must call the production `partition_vectors` seam, not
    carry an independent IVF implementation.

head: Zeppelin — Project Rules > Learnings
text:
12. **Flat IVF defaults are scale-aware and no-spill.** Resolve nlist from a
    3,000-row target within the default 256–4096 bounds, and resolve an
    omitted nprobe as 3/16 of the active flat segment's clusters with a
    runtime floor of 32. Every logical row has exactly one stored location;
    do not add duplicate-row spill or query dedup without a new measured plan.

- Never create, enter, or use a Git worktree for this repository. Work only in
  the primary checkout (usually at `/srv/dotfiles`).
- Run NixOS activation only as `just switch` from `/srv/dotfiles/nixos`

- Do not add or modify anything in `nixos/imalison.nix` unless the user
  explicitly asks for the change to be made there. Put packages and
  configuration intended for every user in the appropriate shared NixOS or Home
  Manager module instead.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: Sutra (`sutra_cardano`) is an Elixir offchain transaction builder framework/SDK for Cardano. It provides a pipe-friendly, component-based API to construct, sign, and submit transactions, with first-class Plutus script support (V1–V4) and pluggable chain data providers. UPLC (Untyped Plutus Core) script evaluation is delegated to a Rust NIF via Rustler (`native/sutra_uplc`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: The CI pipeline (`.github/workflows/elixir.yaml`) runs, in order: compile with `--warnings-as-errors`, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix credo --strict`, then `mix test`. Match all four before considering a change done.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: - **Toolchain**: Elixir 1.19.4 / Erlang OTP 28.3 (see `.tool-versions`). `libsodium-dev` and a Rust toolchain are required (the Rust NIF builds as part of `mix compile`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: - **Integration tests** require a running **Yaci DevKit** local devnet (`yaci-devkit up --enable-yaci-store`, general API on `:8080`, admin API on `:10000`). Tests using `Sutra.PrivnetTest` / `Sutra.Provider.Yaci` will fail without it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: The transaction lifecycle flows: **domain types → builder pipeline → CBOR body → sign → provider submit**.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Entry point and builder pipeline
text: - `Sutra` (`lib/sutra.ex`) is the public entry point; it `defdelegate`s everything to `Sutra.Cardano.Transaction.TxBuilder`. When adding a user-facing builder function, add it to `TxBuilder` and delegate from `Sutra`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Entry point and builder pipeline
text: - `Sutra.Cardano.Transaction.TxBuilder` (`lib/sutra/cardano/transaction/tx_builder.ex`) is the core. Transactions are built by piping through `new_tx() |> add_input/add_output/... |> build_tx!() |> sign_tx() |> submit_tx()`. `build_tx!/2` performs coin selection, fee calculation, and change handling; `build_tx` returns `{:ok, tx}` / `{:error, reason}` while `build_tx!` raises. Supporting logic lives in `tx_builder/` (`collateral.ex`, `tx_config.ex`, `certificate_helper.ex`, `internal.ex`, `error.ex`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Entry point and builder pipeline
text: - **`add_guard` replaces the deprecated `add_signer`** — guards represent required-signer / script-require constraints (see recent governance/certificate commits). Prefer `add_guard` when touching signer requirements.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cardano domain types (`lib/sutra/cardano/`)
text: Core value objects, each with CBOR encode/decode: `Transaction`, `transaction/tx_body.ex` (`TxBody`), `Address` (+ `address/parser.ex`), `Asset`, `Script` (+ `script/native_script.ex`), `transaction/{input,output,output_reference,datum,witness,certificate}.ex`. Governance lives under `cardano/gov/` (`gov_action.ex`, `proposal_procedure.ex`) plus `cardano/gov.ex` (voting), and shared sub-objects under `cardano/common/` (`drep.ex`, `stake_pool.ex`, `pool_relay.ex`). The target ledger era is **Dijkstra** (`cddl/dijkstra.cddl` is the authoritative wire format; era-specific fields like reference-script cost, size limits, and `account_balance_interval.ex` follow it).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Plutus Data mapping (`lib/sutra/data.ex` + `lib/sutra/data/`)
text: A macro-heavy system mapping Elixir structs to Plutus Data (Constr) encodings. When defining any type that crosses the on-chain boundary:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Plutus Data mapping (`lib/sutra/data.ex` + `lib/sutra/data/`)
text: - `use Sutra.Data`, then `defdata` for product types (Aiken objects) and `defenum` for sum types. Fields declared via `data :name, :type` / `field :variant, :type`; encoding can be overridden per-field with `encode_with:` / `decode_with:`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Plutus Data mapping (`lib/sutra/data.ex` + `lib/sutra/data/`)
text: - The macro machinery is in `data/macro_helper/` (`object_macro.ex`, `enum_macro.ex`, `type_macro.ex`, `schema_builder.ex`); CBOR primitives in `data/cbor.ex`, `data/plutus.ex`, `data/decoder.ex`, `data/option.ex`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Blueprint codegen (`lib/sutra/cardano/blueprint/`)
text: Parses Aiken CIP-57 `blueprint.json` and generates typed Elixir modules. Driven by the `mix sutra.blueprint.gen` task (`lib/mix/tasks/sutra.blueprint.gen.ex`); `blueprint/parser.ex` + `blueprint/code_generator.ex` do the work.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Providers (`lib/sutra/provider.ex` + `lib/sutra/provider/`)
text: `Sutra.Provider` is a behaviour for fetching chain data (UTxOs, protocol params) and submitting txs. Implementations: `blockfrost/`, `maestro/`, `koios/`, `kupogmios/` (Kupo+Ogmios), and `yaci/` (local dev). Each has a paired `client.ex` (HTTP) and provider module. Select via `use_provider(builder, Provider)` or `config :sutra, :provider, Sutra.Provider.Yaci`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > UPLC / Rust NIF (`lib/sutra/uplc.ex` + `native/sutra_uplc/`)
text: `Sutra.Uplc` is the interface to the Rust-based UPLC evaluator used for phase-2 validation and script execution-cost estimation. Changes to `native/sutra_uplc` (a Cargo crate) recompile as part of `mix compile`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - **Hex / CBOR / binary conversions** are pervasive — reuse helpers in `Sutra.Utils` (`lib/sutra/cardano/utils.ex`), `Sutra.Data.Cbor`, and the `CBOR` dep rather than hand-rolling.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - **Round-trip tests**: domain types are expected to encode↔decode losslessly. New wire types should have a round-trip test mirroring existing ones under `test/sutra/cardano/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - **Test layout**: unit/serialization tests under `test/sutra/...` mirror `lib/`; end-to-end transaction flows under `test/sutra/tx_examples/`; shared helpers/fixtures in `test/support/` and `test/fixture/` (compiled only in `:test`, see `elixirc_paths` in `mix.exs`). `Sutra.PrivnetTest` provides `with_new_wallet/1` and `await_tx/1` for devnet integration tests.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - **Docs surface**: only a curated subset of modules is published to HexDocs (`filter_modules` regex in `mix.exs`); guides live in `guides/` and are wired into `docs`.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Shared instructions for every coding agent in this repo. The tool-specific files
(`CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) defer to this one.
If a package-level instruction file exists, it is authoritative for that package.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository model
text: - A monorepo of independent npm packages — each has its own `package.json`, tests, and version history. There is no root workspace and no root test runner. Run every command from the target package directory.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository model
text:
- Package map:
  - `Haraka/` — core SMTP server (has `./run_tests`).
  - `plugin/*` — 40+ optional plugins (`haraka-plugin-<name>`); plugins may depend on each other (e.g. bounce → spf).
  - `haraka-config/` — config loader with hot-reload.
  - `results/`, `notes/` — per-connection result / note tracking.
  - `net-utils/`, `utils/`, `constants/`, `dsn/`, `tld/`, `message-stream/` — shared libraries.
  - `email-address/` — `@haraka/email-address`, the RFC 5321/5322 parser (supersedes the deprecated `address-rfc282x`).
  - `eslint/` — `@haraka/eslint-config`
  - `test-fixtures/` — `haraka-test-fixtures`.

head: AGENTS.md > Working agreement
text: - Do only what was asked. When you spot an adjacent bug or smell, surface it and ask before expanding scope — don't silently refactor, but don't ignore it either.

head: AGENTS.md > Working agreement
text: - Preserve compatibility; break it only for an explicit, stated reason.

head: AGENTS.md > Working agreement
text: - For protocol behavior, identify the relevant RFC and verify conformance against the existing implementation.

head: AGENTS.md > Source control
text: - Never run history- or remote-mutating commands (`git commit`, `git push`, `git tag`, `gh pr create`) unless explicitly asked. Stage diffs; the human reviews, commits, and pushes.

head: AGENTS.md > Source control
text: - Propose a commit message in Conventional Commit format, imperative mood.

head: AGENTS.md > Source control
text: - Update `CHANGELOG.md` under `### Unreleased`: one terse clause per change, least markup. Rationale belongs in the code or PR, not the bullet.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding standards
text: - Target current Node LTS; prefer ES2024 over legacy patterns.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding standards
text: - Existing code is CommonJS (`require`/`exports`) — match it. New modules should use ESM with CJS interop (see `@haraka/email-address`).

head: AGENTS.md > Coding standards
text: - Add `node:` prefixes to built-in requires in any file you touch (`require('fs')` → `require('node:fs')`).

head: AGENTS.md > Coding standards
text: - Prefer: promise APIs (`fs/promises`), `for...of`/`for...in` over `forEach`, `node:readline` for line parsing, template literals over concatenation, `true`/`false` over `1`/`0`, and guard-style early returns.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding standards
text: - Remove commented-out code (it lives in git history). `npm run qlty` must pass without warnings.

head: AGENTS.md > Comments
text: - Prefer self-documenting code: a better name beats a comment.

head: AGENTS.md > Comments
text: - Keep only WHY comments — a hidden constraint, an invariant, a workaround for a specific bug, or an RFC citation that explains otherwise-surprising behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Comments
text: - Delete WHAT comments that restate the code, and comments that narrate history or audit findings. If a rename makes a comment redundant, delete it rather than updating it.

head: AGENTS.md > Haraka plugins (`plugin/*`)
text: - Full hook/API reference: `Haraka/docs/Plugins.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Haraka plugins (`plugin/*`)
text: - A plugin is an npm package: `index.js` (`exports.register` + hook handlers), `config/` (default `.ini`/`.json`/`.yaml`), `test/`, `README.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Haraka plugins (`plugin/*`)
text: - Register hooks in `exports.register` with `this.register_hook('phase', 'method'[, priority])`.

head: AGENTS.md > Haraka plugins (`plugin/*`)
text: - Hook handlers take `(next, connection)` (rcpt hooks also take `rcpt`) and must call `next` exactly once. Gate early — return `next()` on missing transaction, disabled config, or skip conditions. Signal a verdict with `next(DENY|DENYSOFT|OK, msg)`; `DENY`/`OK`/etc. are plugin-scope globals (no import).

head: AGENTS.md > Haraka plugins (`plugin/*`)
text: - Results: `connection.transaction.results.add(this, { pass|fail|skip|msg|err, emit })`; query with `results.has(plugin, list, search)`. `emit: true` already logs the collated line — don't also `loginfo`/`logerror` the same thing. results.add(this, {err}) always logs.

head: AGENTS.md > Haraka plugins (`plugin/*`)
text:
- Config loads via `config.get` with a hot-reload callback; declare every boolean or it stays a string and `=== true/false` silently fails:
  ```js
  this.cfg = this.config.get('name.ini', { booleans: ['+a.b', '-c.d'] }, () =>
    this.load(),
  )
  ```

head: AGENTS.md > Haraka plugins (`plugin/*`)
text: - Keep handlers thin. Push pure decision logic and I/O into `lib/*.js` as pure functions that return a verdict/value; the handler just maps that to `results.add` + `next`. For external I/O (DNS, network), expose an injectable seam — a swappable function whose default is the real implementation — so tests run without mocks.

head: AGENTS.md > Haraka plugins (`plugin/*`)
text: - If you add files outside `index.js` (e.g. a `lib/` dir), add them to `package.json` `files` so they publish.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: - Test real behavior and observable outcomes — `results`, return codes, emitted headers, side effects — not how a function was called. Asserting call shape (`calledWith`, arity, call counts) tests the test and hides signature drift.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: - Mocks/stubs are a smell. Prefer real inputs; when you must isolate a dependency, inject a seam and assert the outcome. Never leave a stub that neuters the path under test — that yields green tests proving nothing.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: - For bug fixes, add a failing test first, then fix.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: - Every feature ships with meaningful tests. A `.skip` is a coverage hole: fix it or delete it.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: - Use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` for new tests and Mocha migrations. Plugin tests use `haraka-test-fixtures` (`makePlugin`, `makeConnection`, `callHook`).

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: - Run the package's `lint`, `prettier`, and `format` before handoff.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands (run inside the target package)
text: - Test: `npm test`. Single file: `node --test test/path/to/file.js`.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands (run inside the target package)
text: - Haraka core: `cd Haraka && ./run_tests [test/plugins/foo.js]`.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands (run inside the target package)
text: - Coverage: `npm run test:coverage`; lcov: `npm run test:coverage:lcov`. Keep coverage at/above ~90%.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands (run inside the target package)
text: - If coverage output includes non-source files (e.g. `package.json`, `test/*`), scope it with `--test-coverage-include` (preferred when the list is short) or `--test-coverage-exclude`.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands (run inside the target package)
text: - Lint/format: `npm run lint` / `prettier` / `format`. Version drift: `npm run versions[:fix]`.

head: AGENTS.md > Package script parity
text:
- node:test packages should expose `test`, `test:coverage`, `test:coverage:lcov`, `lint`, `prettier`, `format` with matching shapes across siblings. Standardize on node:test coverage (not c8); add the canonical scripts when touching a package that lacks them:
  ```jsonc
  "test:coverage": "node --test --experimental-test-coverage",
  "test:coverage:lcov": "mkdir -p coverage && node --test --experimental-test-coverage --test-reporter=lcov --test-reporter-destination=coverage/lcov.info"
  ```

head: Danbyte Agent Guide
text:
This file is the working contract for coding agents in this repository. Read it
before making changes, then read the topical docs and nearby code for the task.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > What Danbyte Is
text:
Danbyte is a customizable IPAM/DCIM and network-operations platform. It models
IP space, tenants, sites, devices, racks, interfaces, cabling, circuits, power,
floor plans, topology, monitoring, compliance, automation, and audit history.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > What Danbyte Is
text:
The product is preparing for public preview and already manages real
infrastructure. Preserve existing data and compatibility; do not treat the
database, migrations, APIs, or UI as disposable scaffolding.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Source Of Truth
text:
Some early project notes no longer describe the running application. Use this
precedence when sources disagree:

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Source Of Truth
text: 1. Current code, tests, migrations, and runtime configuration.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Source Of Truth
text:
2. The `docs/` tree - the canonical deep reference for features, data models,
   IPAM/DCIM, architecture, and the design system. **Read the relevant page for
   any area you touch** (`make docs-up` to browse). `README.md` orients.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Source Of Truth
text:
> `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` are kept **identical** - this same guide, so any
> assistant gets the same contract. Edit both together (or edit one and copy).

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Source Of Truth
text:
- The active UI is the React/TanStack application in `frontend/`. The old
  htmx/Django-template UI has been removed; the React SPA is the only frontend.
  Ignore any htmx-first / future-React wording that lingers in older notes.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Source Of Truth
text:
- `frontend/src/routeTree.gen.ts` is generated by TanStack Router. Never edit or
  format it by hand.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - Python 3.13, Django 5.2 LTS, Django REST Framework, PostgreSQL, Redis, RQ.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - `danbyte/`: settings, top-level URLs, WSGI, and ASGI entry points.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - `api/`: the main IPAM/DCIM/connectivity model and REST surface.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - `core/`: organization/tenant settings, shared mixins, tags, and bookmarks.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - `auth_api/`: login, profiles, RBAC, API tokens, and LDAP.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - `customization/`: custom-field definitions, validation, and object registry.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - `monitoring/`: checks, scheduling, state, alerts, engines, and SNMP.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - `integrations/`: webhooks, automation/deploy runs, drift, and NetBox import.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text: - `audit/`, `compliance/`, `search/`, and `jobs/`: their named concerns.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text:
- `danbyte_checks/`: Django-free protocol checker package shared with Outposts.
  Put shared check behavior here instead of forking core and agent logic.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Backend
text:
Django owns `/api/`, `/admin/`, `/django-rq/`, static/media, and WebSockets.
HTTP production traffic uses gunicorn; WebSockets use a separate daphne
process. Do not enable daphne/channels as the normal Django `runserver` backend;
the separation is deliberate and documented in `danbyte/settings.py`.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Frontend
text:
- React 19, TypeScript, TanStack Start/Router/Query/Table, Vite, Tailwind 4,
  shadcn/Radix, and Lucide.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Frontend
text: - `frontend/src/routes/`: file-based routes.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Frontend
text: - `frontend/src/components/`: shared and domain components.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Frontend
text: - `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`: primary typed API boundary.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Frontend
text: - `frontend/src/styles.css`: active design tokens and global styling.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Frontend
text:
- Vite on `:3000` is the user-facing dev server and proxies Django paths to
  `:8000`. Authentication is Django session + CSRF, or scoped API tokens. There
  is no JWT flow.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Architecture > Frontend
text:
Production nginx routes the SPA, API, WebSocket, admin, static, media, and docs
services behind one origin.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Customization First, With Deliberate Seeds
text:
"Zero pre-filled data" is a direction, not an absolute ban. Danbyte should not
impose arbitrary network inventory or an arbitrary operating model, but it may
seed data needed for the product to work, remain safe, or provide a sane
first-run experience.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Customization First, With Deliberate Seeds
text: Classify data before adding it:

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Customization First, With Deliberate Seeds
text:
- Required system/bootstrap data, such as access roles, structural catalogs,
  protocol constants, or records required by application invariants, may be
  seeded.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Customization First, With Deliberate Seeds
text:
- Useful starting catalogs may be seeded when there is a clear product reason,
  especially when users can edit, replace, or remove them safely.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Customization First, With Deliberate Seeds
text:
- Example networks, devices, prefixes, VLANs, tags, and other illustrative
  content belong in opt-in demo seeders, never normal production bootstrap.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Customization First, With Deliberate Seeds
text:
Seeds must be minimal, deterministic, idempotent, tenant/deployment scoped as
appropriate, and safe on both fresh installs and upgrades. Prefer editable
catalog records over hard-coded choices when customization matters. Follow the
existing bootstrap or data-migration pattern, add tests, and document why a new
seed is required. Do not reject a necessary seed solely by quoting the
zero-data slogan.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Tenant, Site, And RBAC Safety
text: - Treat tenant isolation as a hard security boundary.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Tenant, Site, And RBAC Safety
text:
- Scope every domain queryset to the active/authorized tenant before filtering
  by user-controlled IDs.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Tenant, Site, And RBAC Safety
text:
- Never trust a UUID, foreign key, relation, bulk payload, import row, or picker
  result to belong to the current tenant/site.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Tenant, Site, And RBAC Safety
text: - Enforce access on the server. Hidden buttons are only a UI convenience.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Tenant, Site, And RBAC Safety
text:
- Preserve site-scoped write rules, catalog locality, and enhanced site
  separation behavior.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Tenant, Site, And RBAC Safety
text:
- New DRF endpoints remain default-closed. Use `AllowAny` only for an explicitly
  public flow with focused tests.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Tenant, Site, And RBAC Safety
text:
- Validate cross-tenant relationships on create, update, bulk operations,
  imports, clone/sync paths, and background jobs.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Tenant, Site, And RBAC Safety
text:
Security-sensitive settings fail closed. Do not weaken secret-key, credential
encryption, TLS/cookie, CSRF, host, or SSRF protections for convenience. Do not
return write-only secrets from serializers or bypass the outbound-request
guards.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Data And Schema
text: - PostgreSQL is required; do not add SQLite-specific fallbacks.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Data And Schema
text: - Domain models use UUID primary keys.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Data And Schema
text:
- Preserve load-bearing constraints such as nullable VRF semantics and
  `nulls_distinct=False` uniqueness.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Data And Schema
text:
- Add forward migrations for schema changes. Never delete or rewrite committed
  migrations, wipe a database, or reseed user data unless the user explicitly
  requests a disposable-environment reset.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Product Rules > Data And Schema
text:
- Keep demo data opt-in and idempotent. Production migrations may create
  required system data, but never illustrative/demo inventory.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > How To Work
text:
Start with the graph and ownership boundaries, then inspect only the symbols
needed for the task. When Ix Memory is available, use `ix-understand` for broad
orientation, `ix-investigate` for a symbol, `ix-impact` before non-trivial
edits, and `ix-debug` for a symptom. Separate graph-backed facts from
inferences.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > How To Work
text: 1. Read `git status` and preserve all unrelated user changes.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > How To Work
text:
2. Read the relevant feature doc, route/component or viewset/serializer, tests,
   and neighboring established pattern.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > How To Work
text:
3. Check the blast radius across API contracts, RBAC/tenant scoping, background
   work, frontend consumers, migrations, and docs.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > How To Work
text:
Keep changes narrow. Reuse existing helpers and primitives. Do not mix unrelated
refactors, formatting churn, dependency upgrades, or generated artifacts into a
feature/fix.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Backend Conventions
text: - Follow existing serializer/viewset/service boundaries in the affected app.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Backend Conventions
text: - Keep validation close to the contract and return actionable field errors.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Backend Conventions
text:
- Use shared RBAC, tenant/site scoping, audit, secret, and SSRF helpers instead
  of duplicating partial checks.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Backend Conventions
text:
- Preserve audit/journal behavior for user-visible mutations, including bulk
  and async paths.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Backend Conventions
text:
- Use RQ for established background workflows. Jobs must re-check scope and
  permissions where appropriate; do not assume enqueue-time IDs stay valid.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Backend Conventions
text:
- Never use a shell for monitoring exec checks. Keep the existing allow-listed,
  no-shell plugin execution model and its disabled-by-default gate.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Backend Conventions
text:
- Add focused regression tests for fixes and broader tests when shared behavior,
  permissions, tenancy, migrations, or public APIs change.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Backend Conventions
text:
Python style is configured in `pyproject.toml`: Ruff, Python 3.13, 100-column
format target, with migrations excluded.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text: Use the active shared system; do not hand-roll another version of existing UI:

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
- Lists: `ListPageShell`, `DataTable`, shared filters, and entity column
  factories under `components/columns/`.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
- Details: `DetailShell`, Overview first, then related tabs, with Journal and
  Change log last. Use `KvCard` for attribute groups.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text: - Object selection: `ObjectPicker` or an existing domain picker preset.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text: - State and errors: `Loading`, `QueryError`, `apiErrorToast`, and `EmptyState`.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
- Colored catalog objects: `ColorBadge`, `StatusBadge`, `RoleChip`, or the
  existing domain badge. Derive color from object data, never its name.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
- Count/label chips: the squarish `Badge` primitive, one badge per severity
  (`destructive`/`warning`/`success` variants) - never a hand-rolled
  `rounded-full` pill. `rounded-full` is for status dots and avatars only.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text: - Dates/times: `TimeCell` or the shared time helpers.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text: - Tabs: the shared segmented-tabs component.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
- Maps chrome (Topology, Site map, Floor plans): `components/map-toolbar.tsx`
  for bar controls, `ObjectsPanel`, `HiddenChip`, `PointerMenu`, and
  `components/map-panel.tsx` for detail panels. The table in
  `docs/design/visual-language.md` lists them.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
One entity should have one column factory, reused by list and embedded tables.
Do not copy a shell, inline a second `ColumnDef[]`, add raw `<table>` markup, or
invent a different loading/error/empty treatment when a shared primitive fits.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
- Page/section/panel/canvas fetch: the shared `<Loading />`
  (`components/loading.tsx`) - the first-load splash spinner with a small muted
  `Loading…` under it, centred in what it loads - or the table's built-in row.
  Older bare `Loading…` text moves to `<Loading />` when its page is touched.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
- Pending labeled button: keep its dimensions and change the verb to
  `Saving…`, `Deleting…`, etc.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text: - Spinner on its own: icon-only buttons only.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text: - Skeletons: existing sidebar and topology-canvas uses only.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text: - Write the ellipsis as one `…` character, never three dots.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
Keep the UI restrained and operator-focused. Use semantic CSS variables and
the established zinc-based palette, color only for meaning, `rounded-md` or
`rounded-lg`, and shadows only for real overlays. Use Lucide icons from the
existing library. Avoid gradients, decorative shadows, hard-coded
status-name palettes, and one-off SVG icons. A status renders as its
`ColorBadge`/`StatusBadge` pill EVERYWHERE it appears - tables, dropdown
options, selected values. Never a colored dot next to a name; the owner has
rejected dot-plus-name status treatments repeatedly, in any context.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
The full design system - tokens, palette, type scale, and component patterns -
lives in `docs/design/visual-language.md` and
`docs/architecture/shadcn-tokens.md`. Read them before adding UI.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Frontend Conventions
text:
This is a shadcn project (`frontend/components.json`). Reuse local components
and registry conventions; do not rerun `shadcn init` or overwrite customized
primitives.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Documentation
text:
A user-visible or operational change is incomplete without docs in the same
change. Update the relevant page when changing a model field, API/view
behavior, form/payload, UI control, route, setting/env var, Make target, or
service. Match the surrounding docs for location, frontmatter, and style.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Documentation
text:
Use `docs/` as source. Do not edit generated `/site/`. Update older architecture
pages when a change would otherwise deepen the documented/current-state gap.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Commands
text: Use the repository virtualenv and the package manager used by CI.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Commands
text:
Run frontend build before typecheck because the build regenerates the TanStack
route tree. CI uses `npm ci` and `frontend/package-lock.json`; treat npm as the
effective package manager. The simultaneous pnpm lock/workspace is known debt,
so do not churn both lockfiles incidentally.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Commands
text:
CI does not necessarily run the full Django test suite: it is gated by the
`RUN_TESTS` repository variable. Run relevant backend tests locally. Frontend
build and typecheck, plus backend migration application and
`makemigrations --check`, are current CI gates; lint/format checks are still
advisory but should not gain new violations.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Do Not Touch Casually
text:
- Generated/build/local output: `frontend/src/routeTree.gen.ts`, `dist/`,
  `frontend/dist/`, `.output/`, `.tanstack/`, `site/`, `staticfiles/`, `media/`,
  `.venv/`, local `.env*`, and TLS certs.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Do Not Touch Casually
text:
- Root `make css*` targets: remnants of the archived Tailwind pipeline. Active
  UI styling is Tailwind 4 through Vite in `frontend/`.

head: Danbyte Agent Guide > Do Not Touch Casually
text:
- Release/install/systemd/nginx behavior without testing both fresh install and
  upgrade implications.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: Read these first. They are the highest-priority repo-specific rules.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - Always work on a feature branch. If the current branch is `main`, create or switch to a feature branch before editing files or creating commits.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - Never commit directly to `main`, and never merge a branch into `main` locally. Integration happens on GitHub after CI passes.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - Agent-created branches should use `codex/<short-topic>` unless the user asks for another name.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - Preserve user work. Do not revert, overwrite, or “clean up” changes you did not make unless the user explicitly asks.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - Correctness and transaction guarantees outrank performance. Be especially conservative in WAL, pager, transaction, MVCC, index maintenance, and constraint code.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - Run targeted tests for the area you changed, then `make lint` before committing. For broad storage/query changes, run the wider relevant package or e2e suite.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - For benchmark or profiling work, put profiles in `/tmp`, remove generated binaries such as `benchmarks.test`, and update `benchmarks/RESULTS.md` only when benchmark data changes.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - Never hand-edit generated files such as `internal/minisql/mocks_test.go`; regenerate them with the documented command.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Critical Agent Rules
text: - Do not commit secrets, local database files, WAL files, profiles, coverage HTML, benchmark binaries, or other local artifacts.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Instruction Scope
text: This root file contains global workflow and architecture guidance. More specific instructions may exist in nested `AGENTS.md` files; the closest file to the code being edited wins when instructions overlap.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Project Overview
text: MiniSQL is an embedded, single-file SQL database written in Go, inspired by SQLite. It implements a hand-written recursive-descent + state-machine SQL parser, a B+ tree storage engine with 4 KB pages, an LRU page cache, a Write-Ahead Log (WAL) for crash recovery, single-writer enforcement (via an atomic counter) for write transactions, and in-memory MVCC snapshot isolation for read-only transactions. It registers itself as a `database/sql` driver.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Project Overview
text:
**Module:** `github.com/RichardKnop/minisql`
**Go version:** 1.26
**Not production-ready.** Treat it as a research/learning project.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Project Overview
text: **Feature summary:** INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING/DO UPDATE, UNION/UNION ALL, DISTINCT, GROUP BY/HAVING, ORDER BY (multi-column), LIMIT/OFFSET, INNER/LEFT/RIGHT JOIN (arbitrary chain topology), CASE WHEN, CAST, INTERVAL, arithmetic, scalar functions, subqueries (non-correlated scalar + IN/NOT IN in WHERE, derived tables in FROM, CTEs, correlated UPDATE FROM), CHECK/FOREIGN KEY/NOT NULL/UNIQUE constraints, RETURNING, EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE, VACUUM, ANALYZE, PRAGMA, prepared statements (`?` placeholders), data types BOOLEAN/INT4/INT8/REAL/DOUBLE/TEXT/VARCHAR/TIMESTAMP/JSON/UUID/VECTOR, B-tree indexes (primary, unique, secondary, composite, covering, partial, expression), full-text inverted index, JSON inverted index, HNSW vector index, parallel full table scans, slow query logging.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Commands > Coverage
text: **CI threshold:** 70% total — CI fails if coverage drops below this. Raise `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD` in `Makefile` and `.github/workflows/go.yml` as coverage improves toward the 80% target.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Commands > Benchmarks
text: Benchmarks live in `benchmarks/` and require the `bench` build tag. They run both MiniSQL and SQLite (`modernc.org/sqlite`) side-by-side for direct comparison.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Commands > Benchmarks
text: Benchmark and profiling hygiene:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Commands > Benchmarks
text: - Use `-run '^$'` with benchmark commands so tests do not run accidentally.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Commands > Benchmarks
text: - Put CPU and memory profiles in `/tmp`, not in the repository.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Commands > Benchmarks
text: - Remove generated benchmark binaries such as `benchmarks.test` before committing.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Commands > Benchmarks
text: - Start with targeted benchmark slices while profiling; run the full benchmark suite before integration when a performance branch is ready.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Commands > Benchmarks
text: - When benchmark data changes, update `benchmarks/RESULTS.md` with the branch, command, platform, and newest baseline values.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Validation Matrix
text: Use the smallest meaningful checks while iterating, then broaden before committing or handoff.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Validation Matrix
text:
| Change type | Minimum validation |
|---|---|
| Parser change | `LOG_LEVEL=warn go test ./internal/parser/... -count=1` plus relevant e2e tests |
| Query planning/execution change | Targeted `internal/minisql` tests plus relevant `e2e_tests` suite case |
| Storage, WAL, pager, transaction, MVCC | Targeted unit tests, relevant e2e tests (`tx`, `wal`, `concurrency`, `vacuum`), and extra care around rollback/commit paths |
| Index maintenance | Unit tests for the index family plus e2e DML tests covering insert/update/delete and persistence |
| Benchmark/performance change | Before/after targeted benchmark with `-benchmem`; update `benchmarks/RESULTS.md` when baseline numbers change |
| Public API or driver change | Relevant root package tests plus e2e database/sql usage |
| Docs-only change | No tests required unless examples or commands are changed; run markdown-related checks if introduced later |

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > CI
text: GitHub Actions runs on every push and PR to `main` with two parallel jobs:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > CI
text: 1. **lint** — `golangci-lint run ./...` using `.golangci.yml`. Must pass.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > CI
text: 2. **build** — `go build -v ./...` + `go test ./...` + coverage threshold check. Must pass.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Git Workflow
text: - Always work on a feature branch. If the current branch is `main`, create or switch to a feature branch before editing files or creating commits.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Git Workflow
text: - Never commit directly to `main`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Git Workflow
text: - Never merge a feature branch into `main` locally as part of the agent workflow.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Git Workflow
text: - Push the feature branch and open or update a GitHub pull request when integration is requested. Merges into `main` must happen on GitHub after CI passes.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Git Workflow
text: - Agent-created branches should use `codex/<short-topic>` by default. The older `feat/`, `fix/`, `refactor/`, `test/`, `chore/`, and `docs/` prefixes are also acceptable when requested by the user.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature
text: Adding any SQL feature touches four layers in a fixed order. Use existing features as reference implementations.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 1 — Parser (`internal/parser/`)
text: 1. If needed, add new **reserved words** to the `reservedWords` slice in `parser.go`. These are recognised before identifiers, so order matters — **longer strings must come before shorter strings with the same prefix** (e.g. `"DO UPDATE"` before `"DO"`, `"UNION ALL"` before `"UNION"`). See `agent-os/standards/parser/reserved-word-ordering.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 1 — Parser (`internal/parser/`)
text: 2. Add new **step constants** for the feature's parsing states to `parser.go` and register them in the appropriate `case` block of the main `doParse` switch.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 1 — Parser (`internal/parser/`)
text: 3. Create or extend a `doParseXXX()` method (e.g., `doParseSelect()` in `select.go`). Each step reads one token with `p.peek()`, advances with `p.pop()`, populates fields on `p.Statement`, and transitions `p.step` to the next step.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 1 — Parser (`internal/parser/`)
text: 4. For WHERE conditions and expressions, use the **recursive-descent** functions (`parseCondExpr`, `parseExpr`, `parseFuncCall`) — do **not** add new step constants for expression parsing. See `agent-os/standards/parser/where-recursive-descent.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 1 — Parser (`internal/parser/`)
text: 5. Add **parser tests** to `internal/parser/<feature>_test.go` following the `testCase` table pattern. See `agent-os/standards/testing/parser-test-structure.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 2 — Statement struct (`internal/minisql/stmt.go`)
text: Add any new fields to `Statement` that the parser populates.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 2 — Statement struct (`internal/minisql/stmt.go`)
text: - Update `Clone()` for new slice/map/pointer fields (scalar fields are copied automatically).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 2 — Statement struct (`internal/minisql/stmt.go`)
text: - Add helpers like `IsSelectCountAll()` when useful for readability downstream.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 2 — Statement struct (`internal/minisql/stmt.go`)
text: - If a new statement kind is introduced, add it to the `StatementKind` const block and `String()`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 2 — Statement struct (`internal/minisql/stmt.go`)
text: - Update `Validate(table *Table)` and the appropriate `validateXXX()` method.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 2 — Statement struct (`internal/minisql/stmt.go`)
text: - Update `Prepare()` if the new field affects how values are resolved before execution.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 3 — Execution (`internal/minisql/`)
text: The execution layer is split by operation:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 3 — Execution (`internal/minisql/`)
text:
| Feature type | Where to change |
|---|---|
| New DML statement | New method on `*Table` mirroring `Insert`, `Select`, `Update`, `Delete`; dispatch in `database.go` |
| Extension to SELECT | `select.go` — `Select()`, `selectStreaming()`, `selectWithSort()` |
| New aggregation / window operation | Follow `selectWithSort` pattern: collect from `filteredPipe`, transform, build `StatementResult` |
| Extension to query planning | `query_plan.go` / `query_plan_order.go` / `query_plan_join.go` |
| New WHERE operator | `condition.go` — add to `Operator` const, implement in `checkCondition()`; update index-selection rules in `query_plan.go` |
| New data type | `stmt.go` (`ColumnKind`), `row.go` (marshal/unmarshal), `condition.go` (compare), `index.go` (IndexKey constraint), `pager_factory.go` (new pager kind) |
| New index type | `index.go` (new `BTreeIndex[T]` instantiation or separate struct), `database.go` (DDL wiring), `table_secondary_index.go` (DML hooks) |
| New scalar function | `expr.go` — `evalFuncCall()` switch case; `parser/expr.go` — `parseFuncCall()` token recognition |
| Subquery execution | `subquery.go` (non-correlated pre-eval) or `correlated_subquery.go` (per-row eval); both inject via context |
| CTE execution | `cte.go` — materialise into `VirtualTable`, inject into context registry for `getTable()` lookup |
| Schema DDL changes | `database_schema.go` — update `createTableDDL()` and `createIndexDDL()` for round-trip |
| New constraint type | Validation in `insert.go` + `update.go`; store serialized expression in schema; add sentinel error `ErrXxxViolation` |

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 3 — Execution (`internal/minisql/`)
text: `Database.executeStatement()` in `database.go` dispatches on `stmt.Kind` — add a new case there for new statement kinds.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests
text: Every new feature needs tests at **two levels**:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > Unit tests (`internal/minisql/` or `internal/parser/`)
text: - File: `internal/minisql/<feature>_test.go` (pair it with the implementation file).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > Unit tests (`internal/minisql/` or `internal/parser/`)
text: - Package: `package minisql` (same package as implementation — not `_test`).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > Unit tests (`internal/minisql/` or `internal/parser/`)
text: - Use `testify/assert` and `testify/require` directly (no suites).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > Unit tests (`internal/minisql/` or `internal/parser/`)
text: - Mark independent subtests with `t.Parallel()`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > Unit tests (`internal/minisql/` or `internal/parser/`)
text: - Use `initTest(t)` to get a pager and temp DB file when you need real storage. See `agent-os/standards/testing/unit-test-setup.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > Unit tests (`internal/minisql/` or `internal/parser/`)
text: - When a test exercises both table and index operations, all pagers must share one `TransactionManager`. See `agent-os/standards/testing/same-transaction-manager.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > E2E tests (`e2e_tests/`)
text: - File: `e2e_tests/<feature>_test.go`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > E2E tests (`e2e_tests/`)
text: - Package: `package e2etests`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > E2E tests (`e2e_tests/`)
text: - Add a new `func (s *TestSuite) TestXxx()` method — the testify suite wires it into `go test` automatically.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > E2E tests (`e2e_tests/`)
text: - Each test gets a fresh DB via `SetupTest()` (temporary file, auto-cleaned).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > E2E tests (`e2e_tests/`)
text: - Use the helpers already in `select_test.go`: `execQuery(query, expectedRowsAffected)`, `collectUsers(query)`, `collectOrders(query)`, etc. Add new helpers there when needed.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > How to Add a New SQL Feature > Step 4 — Tests > E2E tests (`e2e_tests/`)
text: - Shared DDL strings (`createUsersTableSQL`, etc.) live in `e2e_test.go`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Key Interfaces (`internal/minisql/ports.go`)
text: When you add or change an interface in `ports.go`, run `mockery` to regenerate `mocks_test.go`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions
text: The style baseline is **[Effective Go](https://go.dev/doc/effective_go)** and the **[Go Code Review Comments](https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments)** wiki. The rules below add project-specific detail on top of those guides. All rules are enforced by `golangci-lint` (see `.golangci.yml`); run `make lint` before pushing.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: **No `a`/`an` prefixes on local variables.** This pattern (`aRow`, `aColumn`, `aField`, `aTable`, `aSchema`) is not idiomatic Go and was a historical accident. Use plain descriptive names. This pattern still appears in some older code paths and should be cleaned up when editing those files.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: **Receiver names** are one or two lowercase letters derived from the type name. They must be consistent across all methods of a type.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: **Abbreviations** follow Go conventions: `id` not `ID` inside names, but `ID` when it is a standalone exported name (`UserID`, `ErrInvalidID`). Acronyms are all-caps: `SQL`, `URL`, `HTTP`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: **Error variable names:** exported errors are `ErrXxx`; unexported are `errXxx`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Comments / Godoc
text: Every **exported** identifier must have a godoc comment beginning with the identifier's name.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Comments / Godoc
text: Unexported helpers benefit from comments too, but it is not enforced by the linter.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Error handling
text: **Static error values** use `errors.New`, not `fmt.Errorf` (reserve `fmt.Errorf` for formatting or wrapping):

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Error handling
text: **Wrapping** uses `%w` so callers can use `errors.Is` / `errors.As`:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Error handling
text: **Error strings** are lower-case and have no trailing punctuation (enforced by revive `error-strings` rule):

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Error handling
text: **Sentinel errors:** public errors are `ErrXxx`; unexported are `errXxx`. Callers check with `errors.Is`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Early returns
text: Prefer early returns over nested conditionals. Each guard clause should handle the error / edge case and return immediately.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Context
text: - `context.Context` is always the **first** argument (enforced by revive `context-as-argument` rule).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Context
text: - Transactions are stored in the context: `TxFromContext(ctx)` / `WithTransaction(ctx, tx)`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Context
text: - Several subsystems use context for injection: CTEs (`ctxWithCTERegistry`), correlated subquery SET values (`contextWithCorrelatedSetUpdates`). Follow this pattern when adding new context-injected state.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Context
text: - Pass `ctx` through every layer without modification (except when injecting a transaction or other state).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Context
text: - Use `context.Background()` (not the request context) when creating temporary databases inside operations like VACUUM — the request context carries an active write transaction that would contaminate the temp DB.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Tests
text: **`require` vs `assert`:** use `require` (fail-fast) when the test cannot safely continue if the assertion fails (e.g. a nil pointer would follow). Use `assert` (continue) for independent property checks.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Tests
text: **`t.Parallel()`** should be called at the top of every test and subtest that does not write shared state.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Tests
text: **Table-driven tests** are preferred when the same logic is exercised with multiple inputs. Use `t.Run` with a descriptive name for each case. For a single scenario with distinct setup, a named subtest is fine.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Channel-based pipelines (SELECT)
text: SELECT uses a producer/consumer goroutine pipeline:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Channel-based pipelines (SELECT)
text: When adding filtering/transformation stages, insert them as goroutines between `filteredPipe` and the consumer.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Row projection
text: `row.OnlyFields(fields...)` returns a new `Row` with only the requested columns. Always call it just before sending a row to the caller — scan phases should fetch all fields needed by WHERE conditions, not just the SELECT list.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Statement result / iterator
text: `StatementResult.Rows` is a lazy `Iterator`. Do not materialise all rows into a slice unless you need to sort or deduplicate them. The streaming path (`selectStreaming`) never loads all rows into memory.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > NULL handling
text: - Each row has a 64-bit NULL bitmask (column limit: 64).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > NULL handling
text: - `OptionalValue{Valid: false}` represents NULL.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > NULL handling
text: - Indexes do not store NULL keys; equality conditions on NULL use `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL`, not `=`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > TIMESTAMP semantics
text: - `TIMESTAMP` is a timestamp-without-time-zone type stored as microseconds since `2000-01-01 00:00:00 UTC`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > TIMESTAMP semantics
text: - The implementation uses the proleptic Gregorian calendar across the full supported range.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > TIMESTAMP semantics
text: - Timezone-qualified literals such as `Z`, `UTC`, or `+01:00` are rejected; do not silently normalize them.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > TIMESTAMP semantics
text: - `NOW()` is evaluated in UTC and stored as a timezone-naive timestamp value.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > TIMESTAMP semantics
text: - Fractional seconds accept 1 to 6 digits and are scaled to microseconds.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > JSON type semantics
text: - `JSON` columns are stored as compact UTF-8 text via `TextPointer` (overflow-page enabled for large payloads).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > JSON type semantics
text: - Values are normalised to compact form (`json.Marshal` round-trip) on write.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > JSON type semantics
text: - JSON path operators: `col->>'$.field'` returns text; `col->'$.field'` returns JSON.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > JSON type semantics
text: - JSON functions: `JSON_EXTRACT`, `JSON_VALID`, `JSON_TYPE`, `JSON_ARRAY_LENGTH`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > JSON type semantics
text: - `JSON_CONTAINS(col, '{"key":"val"}')` uses the JSON inverted index when one exists.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > JSON type semantics
text: - `CAST(x AS JSON)` and `CAST(uuid AS TEXT)` are supported.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > JSON type semantics
text: - Negative integer and float literals are supported directly in SQL (e.g., `WHERE n = -1`, `VALUES (-42)`).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Database header
text: - The first `RootPageConfigSize` bytes of page `0` are the on-disk MiniSQL database header.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Database header
text: - Current header contract: magic `minisql\0`, format version `1`, page size `4096`, first free page, free page count, then reserved bytes.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Database header
text: - Opening a database requires a valid header magic/version/page size; old header layouts are intentionally rejected during the unstable pre-1.0 period.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Database header
text: - When changing the header format, update both `internal/minisql/config.go` and `agent-os/standards/storage-engine/page-layout.md` in the same change.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Database header
text: - WAL commits write frames to `{dbpath}-wal` and update the in-memory WAL index; the main database file is only written during a checkpoint.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Database header
text: - **Transparent page encryption**: `WithEncryptionKey(key []byte)` option enables AES-256-CTR. The encryption salt (32 bytes) is stored in the plaintext header; the AES key is `HKDF(userKey, salt)`. Page 0 bytes 0-99 are always plaintext.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Database header
text: - **Key rotation**: `db.ReKey(ctx, newKey)` or `PRAGMA rekey = '<hex>'` — uses the VACUUM copy-and-swap mechanism; the output file gets a fresh salt. `db.ReKey(ctx, nil)` removes encryption.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: Every B+ tree leaf cell is self-describing. The on-disk layout is:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: - `TypeCode` (one byte per column, declared in `type_code.go`) encodes the on-disk type independently of the current schema.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: - `ColumnCount = 0` means no TypeCodes are present (treated as an all-null / empty row by `RowView`).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: - `Cell.Unmarshal` is schema-free: it uses TypeCodes to compute byte widths without consulting the table schema.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: - `TypeCodesFromColumns(columns []Column) []byte` builds the TypeCode slice for a column list; deleted columns get `TypeCodeNull`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: - **Lazy ADD COLUMN**: rows written before a column was added have `ColumnCount < len(schema.Columns)`; `RowView` returns the column default without touching storage.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: - **Tombstone DROP COLUMN**: `Column.Deleted = true` in the schema; old rows still carry real bytes at that position (TypeCode tells the decoder how to skip them); new rows write `TypeCodeNull` (0 bytes).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: In tests, always populate `Cell.TypeCodes` and `Cell.ColumnCount`:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: - Within `package minisql`: use `makeTestCell(key, nullBitmask, data, columns)`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: - From external packages (e.g., `package minisql_test`): set `TypeCodes: minisql.TypeCodesFromColumns(cols)` and `ColumnCount: uint8(len(cols))` inline.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Self-describing cell format
text: See `agent-os/standards/storage-engine/page-layout.md` for the full TypeCode table and format rules.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Text storage
text: - `TextPointer` wraps `[]byte`. Always use `TextPointer.String()` for logical comparison; never compare `TextPointer.Data` bytes directly (inline vs overflow representations differ).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Text storage
text: - VARCHAR ≤ 255 bytes is stored inline. Larger TEXT and all JSON values use overflow pages.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > WAL durability modes
text: The `synchronous` setting on `WAL` controls when `fsync()` is called. It matches SQLite's `PRAGMA synchronous` for WAL mode.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > WAL durability modes
text:
| Mode | Value | Behaviour |
|------|-------|-----------|
| `SynchronousNormal` | 1 | **Default.** No fsync per commit; fsync only at checkpoint. |
| `SynchronousFull` | 2 | fsync after every WAL commit (maximum durability). |
| `SynchronousOff` | 0 | No fsyncs anywhere. Fastest; data loss possible on OS crash. |

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > WAL durability modes
text: - Configured at open time via the `synchronous=normal|full|off` connection string parameter.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > WAL durability modes
text: - Changeable at runtime via `PRAGMA synchronous = normal|full|off` (takes effect on the next commit).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > WAL durability modes
text: - Read at runtime via `PRAGMA synchronous` (returns 0/1/2).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > WAL durability modes
text: - Implementation: `WAL.synchronous` is an `atomic.Int32`. `AppendTransaction` reads it on each call; no lock needed.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: MiniSQL uses two complementary concurrency mechanisms:

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: **Write transactions — single-writer enforcement**

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - `TransactionManager` tracks active writers with an `activeWriters atomic.Int32`. `BeginTransaction` increments it; `CommitTransaction` / `RollbackTransaction` decrement it. Only one write transaction may be active at a time; a second call to `BeginTransaction` blocks until the first finishes.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text:
- `txPager.ModifyPage()` has two paths:
  - **Fast path** (in-place): when no snapshot reader is active (`hasActiveSnapshotReadersLocked() == false`) and the page has been committed at least once (`PageLastCommittedSeq > 0`), the shared LRU page is returned directly and modified in-place. No clone is made; `WriteInfo.InPlace = true` and `OriginalPage = nil`.
  - **Slow path** (clone): new pages, or when snapshot readers are active. The page is cloned; the clone goes into the write-set. `WriteInfo.OriginalPage` holds the pre-clone pointer for MVCC history.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - At commit time, `WriteSet` pages are flushed via WAL (`commitWithWAL`). For cloned pages where snapshot readers exist, `OriginalPage` is stored in `pageVersionHistory` for MVCC readers.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - `RollbackTransaction` evicts in-place pages via `saver.InvalidatePage(pageIdx)` so the next read reloads the committed version from WAL. Cloned pages are simply discarded.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - All `Table` methods run inside a write transaction context via `TransactionManager.ExecuteInTransaction`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: **Read-only transactions — Snapshot Isolation (MVCC)**

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - `BeginReadOnlyTransaction` captures `tm.commitSeq` as the transaction's `SnapshotSeq` (under `tm.mu` to prevent races with concurrent commits).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - `ReadPage` for read-only transactions calls `PageLastCommittedSeq(pageIdx)` and compares it to `tx.SnapshotSeq`. If the cached page is safe (committed at or before the snapshot), it is returned directly. Otherwise the historical version is retrieved from `pageVersionHistory`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - At write commit time, if snapshot readers are active, `WriteInfo.OriginalPage` (the pre-write copy) is saved in `pageVersionHistory` with `validUntilSeq = commitSeq - 1`. In-place writes (`OriginalPage = nil`) skip this — in-place is only taken when no readers are active.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - `trimPageVersionHistoryLocked` GCs historical versions no longer needed by any active reader (called on each commit/rollback).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - Checkpoint (WAL truncation) is blocked while snapshot readers are active (`ErrCheckpointBlockedByReaders`).

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Coding Conventions > Transactions
text: - Use `ExecuteReadOnlyTransaction` for the read-only wrapper; `BeginReadOnlyTransaction` + `CommitTransaction` manually if you need the snapshot seq.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > File Naming Conventions
text:
| Pattern | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `feature.go` | Implementation |
| `feature_test.go` | Unit tests for that feature |
| `feature_bench_test.go` | Benchmarks (separate file to keep test files readable) |
| `feature_primary_key_test.go` | Tests scoped to primary key behaviour of a feature |
| `feature_unique_index_test.go` | Tests scoped to unique index behaviour |
| `mocks_test.go` | Auto-generated mocks — never edit by hand |
| `query_plan_*.go` | Each query planning concern in its own file |

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > File Naming Conventions
text: Parser files mirror engine files: `parser/select.go` ↔ `internal/minisql/select.go`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **Maximum 64 columns per table** — enforced by the 64-bit NULL bitmask in each row.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **Maximum row size: ~4,061 bytes** — a row must fit in a single page (overflow pages handle TEXT/JSON column data, but the row header + fixed-width fields must fit). The 4-byte CRC32-IEEE checksum at the end of every page is included in this reduction from the raw 4096-byte page size.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **TEXT/VARCHAR key columns in indexes** — TEXT columns cannot be primary-key or unique-index key columns (enforced in `validateCreateTable`). VARCHAR up to `MaxIndexKeySize` is permitted.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **Single connection enforced** — `Driver.Open` returns `ErrDatabaseAlreadyOpen` when a second `sql.Open` targets the same file path (enforced by a per-file lock map in the driver). Multiple in-process connections to the same file would corrupt the page cache.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **No `database/sql` connection pooling** — always `db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)` / `db.SetMaxIdleConns(1)`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **No savepoints** — `SAVEPOINT` / `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` are not yet implemented.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **No ALTER TABLE** — schema evolution requires CREATE + INSERT SELECT + DROP + RENAME.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **No hash indexes** — all indexes use B+ tree; O(1) hash equality lookups are not yet implemented.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **Multi-column `ORDER BY` index optimisation** — requires all directions to be uniform (all ASC or all DESC) and the composite index column order to match exactly. Mixed ASC/DESC falls back to in-memory sort.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **Partial index implication check** — conservative syntactic containment: each condition in the index WHERE must appear verbatim in the query WHERE. Semantically equivalent but textually different conditions are not recognised.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **CHECK constraints** — column-level only; table-level CHECK is not yet implemented.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **FOREIGN KEY** — single-column only; composite FK is not yet implemented. Actions: RESTRICT, NO ACTION, SET NULL, CASCADE.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Constraints and Known Limits
text: - **`FROM table alias`** — bare alias (without `AS`) is not supported; write `FROM t AS alias`.

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Branch and Commit Conventions
text:
**Branch names:** agents should use `codex/<short-topic>` by default. Human-authored branches may use `feat/`, `refactor/`, `fix/`, `test/`, `chore/`, or `docs/`.
**Commit message format:** `<type>: <short description>`

head: AGENTS.md — MiniSQL Codebase Guide for AI Coding Agents > Branch and Commit Conventions
text: PRs target `main`. The CI gate is `golangci-lint` + `go build ./...` + `go test ./...`.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: CoHDL v2 — a compiler for the AI-native PCB schematic language. Rust, single crate. The compiler pipeline and emitters have **zero external dependencies** (a deliberate choice: byte-stable, reproducible output is a hard constraint, so everything — TOML lock file, S-expression netlist, diagnostics JSON — is hand-rolled and deterministic). Implementation: `check/subdesigns.rs` + `bodies.rs` shim (ports as Pin-params) + `expand.rs` (nodes in pass 1, port conns in pass 2, `compose_place` finalization). fmt deviation, ledgered: statement order is preserved (ports block canonicalized in place); layout-last is convention, not enforced reordering). Parameterized circuit construction (RFC-033: typed `Int`/`Length` compile-time expressions with an exact two-domain evaluator — Int i64 checked, Length femto i128, division never rounds; local `const`; `const N: Int` generics on `fn`/`subdesign` with expression arguments, E406 on devices; expression-valued array lengths / indexes / placements / rotation; one-token `-` with parser-side signed-literal assembly, E102/E105 preserved at legacy positions; mandatory-labelled half-open `for` loops over connection operations with hygienic `__for_{LABEL}_{VALUE}` frames feeding the existing designator allocator — sibling loops never merge, growing a bound never renumbers, renaming a label moves exactly those paths; uniform static declaration validation incl. duplicate locals in uncalled bodies; deterministic expansion metering (100k iterations / 1M work items / 64 frames) active only when the reachable graph contains RFC-033 syntax — legacy designs byte-identical; E1401–E1407). The RFC-033 implementation on this branch is provisional: the proposal still requires the authoritative acceptance decision and central RFC/error-code allocation; do not describe it as Accepted or edit the generated note 10 snapshot to imply acceptance.
