head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence
text: This project is indexed by GitNexus as **jarvis** (44114 symbols, 126483 relationships, 300 execution flows). Use the GitNexus MCP tools to understand code, assess impact, and navigate safely.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence
text: > If any GitNexus tool warns the index is stale, run `npx gitnexus analyze` in terminal first.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Always Do
text: - **MUST run impact analysis before editing any symbol.** Before modifying a function, class, or method, run `gitnexus_impact({target: "symbolName", direction: "upstream"})` and report the blast radius (direct callers, affected processes, risk level) to the user.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Always Do
text: - **MUST run `gitnexus_detect_changes()` before committing** to verify your changes only affect expected symbols and execution flows.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Always Do
text: - **MUST warn the user** if impact analysis returns HIGH or CRITICAL risk before proceeding with edits.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Always Do
text: - When exploring unfamiliar code, use `gitnexus_query({query: "concept"})` to find execution flows instead of grepping. It returns process-grouped results ranked by relevance.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Always Do
text: - When you need full context on a specific symbol — callers, callees, which execution flows it participates in — use `gitnexus_context({name: "symbolName"})`.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > When Debugging
text: 1. `gitnexus_query({query: "<error or symptom>"})` — find execution flows related to the issue

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > When Debugging
text: 2. `gitnexus_context({name: "<suspect function>"})` — see all callers, callees, and process participation

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > When Debugging
text: 3. `READ gitnexus://repo/jarvis/process/{processName}` — trace the full execution flow step by step

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > When Debugging
text: 4. For regressions: `gitnexus_detect_changes({scope: "compare", base_ref: "main"})` — see what your branch changed

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > When Refactoring
text: - **Renaming**: MUST use `gitnexus_rename({symbol_name: "old", new_name: "new", dry_run: true})` first. Review the preview — graph edits are safe, text_search edits need manual review. Then run with `dry_run: false`.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > When Refactoring
text: - **Extracting/Splitting**: MUST run `gitnexus_context({name: "target"})` to see all incoming/outgoing refs, then `gitnexus_impact({target: "target", direction: "upstream"})` to find all external callers before moving code.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > When Refactoring
text: - After any refactor: run `gitnexus_detect_changes({scope: "all"})` to verify only expected files changed.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Never Do
text: - NEVER edit a function, class, or method without first running `gitnexus_impact` on it.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Never Do
text: - NEVER ignore HIGH or CRITICAL risk warnings from impact analysis.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Never Do
text: - NEVER rename symbols with find-and-replace — use `gitnexus_rename` which understands the call graph.

head: GitNexus — Code Intelligence > Never Do
text: - NEVER commit changes without running `gitnexus_detect_changes()` to check affected scope.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: Before implementing or reviewing a PR, read [Review Boundary Contract](CONTRIBUTING.md#review-boundary-contract). Treat the PR description as the review contract.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: Contributors MUST declare the user problem, supported inputs and execution conditions, observable contract, touched subsystem and owner, non-goals, and verification evidence. Do not silently widen these while responding to review. A declared boundary narrows implementation scope but cannot waive an existing public or repository contract, an approved issue or RFC requirement, or a maintainer decision; conflicts require maintainer approval or RFC review.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: Review agents MUST evaluate every finding in this order:

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: 1. Reproduce it under the PR's promised inputs and execution conditions.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: 2. Determine whether it violates the PR's promised contract.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: 3. Determine whether the fix requires a new subsystem or ownership boundary.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: 4. Determine whether the original user problem can be solved without the subsystem introduced by the PR.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: 5. Determine whether splitting the scope leaves an immediate user-data or security risk.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: - Questions 1 and 2 are yes: **Changes Requested**.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: - Questions 3 and 5 are yes: stop the PR and ask a maintainer to revisit the RFC; do not silently absorb the new subsystem or owner.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: - Questions 3 and 4 are yes while question 5 is no: non-blocking follow-up with a named owner and link.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: - Question 5 is yes without the Q3 + Q5 escalation: **Changes Requested** for the immediate user-data or security risk.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: - Outside the declared boundary and no contract violation: not a blocker; record only as a valid, actionable, owned follow-up.

head: Ouroboros - Development Environment > Pull Request Boundary Policy
text: Review severity alone never expands PR scope. Maintainers own scope-expansion decisions.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: Dotty is the Scala 3 compiler (`dotc`). It compiles Scala source code into JVM bytecode (and optionally Scala.js IR). The compiler is itself written in Scala 3.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: We care about maintainability. "The tests pass" is not enough to justify that a change is good.

head: AGENTS.md > Build Commands > Compilation

head: AGENTS.md > Build Commands > Compilation

head: AGENTS.md > Build Commands > Compilation
text: Use the `local/` directory for temporary test files (gitignored).

text: - `sbt --client testCompilation` - Run the whole compilation test suite.

head: Agent notes > Firmware
text:
The firmware is a Gea app, and the `gea` CLI owns the whole ESP32 build.
`npm run build:firmware` (`gea build --board amoled`) builds it, and
`npm run flash:firmware` (`gea flash --board amoled`) flashes it over USB.

head: Agent notes > Firmware
text:
**A board already in maintenance mode is flashed over Wi-Fi, not USB.** That is
the normal way to update it, and it is two commands:

head: Agent notes > Firmware
text:
`discover` prints the address; `ota` uploads `build/pedalboard.bin`, validates
it and reboots. Don't reach for `gea flash` or a serial port for this. Don't
flash hardware unless asked. The board layer (panel driver, touch, power rails, frame
scheduler and the IDF project) comes from `@geastack/targets`, so never add a
board `CMakeLists.txt`, a partition CSV or a display driver here. Everything
this repository adds to the native build is declared in `gea.targets.esp32` in
`package.json`.

head: Agent notes > Firmware
text:
Read [docs/MEMORY.md](docs/MEMORY.md) before changing how the NAM engine or the
effects allocate memory, where code is placed, or the linker and sdkconfig
settings. Host tests and a clean build don't prove that audio timing is right on
the device.

head: Agent notes > Frontend and models
text:
The UI starts in `src/ui/index.tsx`, with JSX components, one CSS file per
component module, and `src/ui/stores/PedalboardStore.ts`. The browser preview
and the ESP32 build the same app; `src/preview/` holds browser-only fixtures.
The gea CLI compiles the app with the pinned `@geastack/compiler`. Don't edit
generated C++, don't add a JavaScript runtime, and don't add a second compiler
invocation. `scripts/panel-host-plugin.mjs` declares the board boundary. See
[src/ui/README.md](src/ui/README.md) for what this board asks of Gea, and why
it carries no local patches.

head: Agent notes > Frontend and models
text:
Users copy original `.nam` files to the SD card, and parsing and preparation
happen on the device. Never require a host-side conversion. Keep the source
files untouched and validate caches against the source model.

head: Agent notes > Checks
text:
Run `npm run check` after source changes, and `npm test` plus
`npm run build:firmware` after changes to audio, storage, USB or UI.
`npm run format` formats maintained sources; leave generated output,
credentials, downloaded components and `third_party/` alone.

[skills/README.md](skills/README.md) and load the matching `SKILL.md` before
building, flashing, measuring audio, changing memory placement, editing the UI,
editing factory assets or updating Gea packages.

head: Sinclair
text: Repository guidance for agent sessions.

head: Sinclair > What this is
text:
Sinclair is a GPU-accelerated terminal emulator for macOS and Linux, written in
Rust as a Cargo workspace. The GUI is built on [gpui](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed)
(pulled as a git dependency from the zed repo). The GUI is the `app` crate,
whose bin target is `sinclairdev`: a dev build (`cargo run -p app`, debug or
`--release`) is named `sinclairdev` so it never collides with an installed
`sinclair` — it gets its own window title, app id, and single-instance socket and
runs side by side. The release scripts install the same binary as the shipped
`sinclair` command. The app derives this name from its own executable at runtime
(see `crates/app/src/appid.rs`).

head: Sinclair > Commands
text:
Each crate keeps its tests in a sibling `tests/` directory (e.g.
`crates/vt/tests/`), mirroring the `src/` layout. These are **not** ordinary
integration tests: every crate sets `autotests = false`, and each source file
pulls its test file back in as a private module so unit tests keep access to
private items and the `app` binary can be tested:

head: Sinclair > Commands
text:
Add a new test file the same way (and create the `#[path]` stub in the source
file). Genuine integration tests that exercise only the public API are declared
explicitly as `[[test]]` targets (see `crates/vt` and `crates/terminal`). The
`vt` and `config` crates carry the bulk of the coverage and are pure logic —
prefer adding there.

head: Sinclair > gpui dependency
text:
gpui and `gpui_platform` come from a pinned zed git rev. Because cargo
`[patch.crates-io]` entries do not propagate through git dependencies, the root
`Cargo.toml` must mirror zed's own patches (`async-process`, `async-task`).
Requires Rust stable >= 1.96. If you bump the zed rev, re-check zed's root
`Cargo.toml` patch section and update ours to match. See `docs/gpui.md`.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text: The workspace is layered bottom-up; each crate depends only on those below it.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`vt`** — the terminal emulation core. Pure, no I/O: a `vte`-driven parser
  feeds a `Grid`/`Screen` with cursor, modes, scrollback, selection,
  hyperlinks, search, and SGR/charset state. `term/` holds CSI/OSC/DCS dispatch
  and reports. Everything here is testable in isolation.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text: - **`pty`** — Unix pty allocation and child-process spawn (`rustix`). Unix-only.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`terminal`** — runtime glue: `Session::spawn` runs a child on a pty, feeds
  its bytes into a `vt::Terminal` on a reader thread, and emits `Event`s
  (wakeup, title, bell, exit) over an async-capable flume receiver.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`cast`** — asciinema v2 `.cast` recording: a `Recorder` writes a header line
  plus timestamped output events as bytes arrive (output only; UTF-8 split
  across reads is carried over). Used by `terminal` for session capture.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`container`** — container-backed terminals, pure argv construction with no
  I/O beyond a `$PATH` probe: Docker/Podman detection, the OS profiles behind
  "OS Tabs", and the project **sandbox** — one long-lived container a human and
  a whole agent team share. The sandbox identity-mounts the project (a path
  means the same thing inside and out, so git worktrees stay valid from both
  sides), generates the image `Recipe` that installs the agent CLIs, and
  discovers containers a project already has by label so an editor's
  devcontainer is entered rather than duplicated. `app` drives it; `relay` uses
  the same builders so a `docker exec` assembled on either side cannot drift.
  See `docs/sandbox.md`.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`input`** — keyboard/mouse encoding to terminal byte sequences (CSI, kitty
  keyboard protocol, mouse reporting, bracketed paste).

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`config`** — layered settings: compiled-in defaults overridden by the
  user's `settings.json` (JSON with comments, parsed by `json.rs`), with live
  file watching. `kind.rs` is the typed key schema; bad values become friendly
  diagnostics plus the default and never abort the load. `jsonedit.rs` does
  comment-preserving single-key writes. Default path
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/sinclair/settings.json` or
  `~/.config/sinclair/settings.json`; the legacy `key = value` `config` file
  is still parsed for one-time migration (`app`'s `confwrite::migrate`).

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text: - **`theme`** — 22 built-in color schemes (`builtin/`) plus per-color overrides.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`plugin`** — parses `plugin.toml` manifests contributing: `[[command]]`
  actions (+ default keybindings), a `[panel]` block-tree drawer, `[[trigger]]`
  event hooks, and `[[tool]]` MCP tools exposed to agents (`mcpbridge` merges
  them into `sinclair mcp`'s tool list). Also owns install state
  (`installed.toml`: version, source, enabled flag, granted capabilities) and
  bundled-plugin discovery. Pure parsing/validation; the host (`app`) drives the
  runtime, renders panels, and dispatches triggers.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`pluginrt`** — the one plugin runtime: a `wasmtime` component-model host.
  Owns the WIT world (`wit/plugin.wit`), the capability-gated linker, and one
  resident instance per plugin. Capabilities are enforced at link time — the
  host adds a host interface only if the plugin declared it *and* the user
  granted it, so a component importing something ungranted fails to
  instantiate. Fuel bounds a runaway guest. Defines the `AppHost` trait `app`
  implements, keeping `wasmtime` out of `app`'s dependency surface. See
  `docs/plugins.md`.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text: - **`macros`** — record/replay of typed command sequences, stored as plain text.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`mcp`** — a minimal Model Context Protocol server (JSON-RPC over stdio).
  Transport/framing only; the caller supplies the tool list and handler. Knows
  nothing about terminals.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`assist`** — local, offline terminal assistance (command ranking,
  suggestions, paste-risk safety checks). Optional `candle` feature (off by
  default) for the candle-core backend; code is gated with
  `#[cfg(feature = "candle")]` and has a non-candle fallback.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`updater`** — self-update mechanics, gpui-free (Zed's `auto_update`
  design): GitHub release check, install detection, and **in-place** installs —
  macOS mounts the `.dmg` and rsyncs the new bundle's contents onto the
  installed `.app` (never swap the bundle directory: LaunchServices' stale
  registration relaunches the bare Mach-O inside Terminal.app), Linux renames
  the new AppImage over the running one, staged on the same filesystem. Returns
  a `Relaunch` decision that `app`'s `updateui.rs` hands to gpui's restart —
  `Relaunch::Current` restarts with *no* explicit path so gpui reopens the
  running bundle via `NSBundle`. A release is only offered once it has
  published the asset *this* machine installs (`Release::ready_for`, matched by
  OS **and** architecture); GitHub publishes a release before CI uploads to it,
  so the gate is what stops a prompt whose Update button could only fail.
  Installs report `Stage`s as they run so `updateui` can show real progress.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`relay`** — the agent mesh, shipped as a standalone sidecar binary
  (`relay`), **not** part of the terminal. Lets independent coding-agent
  sessions coordinate over a shared SQLite bus: agents
  `register`, message each other / channels, and `wait` (a single blocking SSE
  call) to park for free between tasks. Built on tokio + axum + sqlx; MCP
  transport is Streamable HTTP so many sessions share one server. Submodules:
  `protocol/` (wire types), `db/` (SQLite bus), `state/` (in-memory app +
  wake signal), `bus.rs` (core park/deliver shared by both planes), `tools/`
  (MCP tool impls), `mcp/` + `transport/` (MCP dispatch over HTTP), `control/`
  (plain-HTTP control plane for the CLI and non-MCP bridges), `spawn/`
  (background workers), and `cli/` (the `relay` subcommands). The app never runs
  the mesh in-process — `app/src/relay/` starts/stops the bundled binary as a
  detached daemon and builds the `relay launch` command lines the app runs:
  single agents into splits, and a whole team into its own window (one member
  per pane) unless `relay-team-window` is off. Reads no env vars; every
  parameter comes from settings, passed explicitly. See `docs/relay.md`.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`libsinclair`** — the terminal as an embeddable library: curated re-exports
  of the headless stack (`Session` + vt + input + theme) plus the gpui rendering
  layer moved out of `app` — the `colors`/`metrics`/`mouse`/`boxdraw` policy
  modules, `element::TerminalElement` (grid painting, damage-aware frame reuse),
  the pointer glue, the event `bridge`, and `termview::TermView`, a drop-in
  terminal pane for other gpui apps. gpui sits behind the default `ui` feature,
  so `default-features = false` is a gpui-free headless core. Consumed as a git
  dependency; see `docs/libsinclair.md` and `crates/libsinclair/examples/embed.rs`.

head: Sinclair > Architecture
text:
- **`app`** — the gpui application that wires everything together. Owns windows,
  splits, settings UI, the About panel, font handling, and the process-entry
  dispatch in `main.rs`. The grid renderer comes from `libsinclair`; `view/`
  layers Sinclair's pane behavior (search, hints, copy mode, suggestions,
  triggers) on top of `TerminalElement`. The window opens with a transparent
  native title bar; `titlebar.rs` draws the chrome itself — a themed strip with
  the tabs folded in (`tabbar.rs`), window dragging, and, on Linux, custom
  minimize/maximize/close controls plus resize edges.

head: Sinclair > Architecture > Process modes (`app/src/main.rs`)
text: The `sinclair` binary dispatches on argv before starting the GUI:

head: Sinclair > Architecture > Process modes (`app/src/main.rs`)
text:
- `sinclair --toggle-quick` — signals a running instance to summon the quick
  terminal (used by Wayland compositor keybinds), then exits.

head: Sinclair > Architecture > Process modes (`app/src/main.rs`)
text:
- `sinclair mcp` — runs the MCP stdio server (`mcpbridge`), bridging tool calls
  into a running GUI instance.

head: Sinclair > Architecture > Process modes (`app/src/main.rs`)
text:
- `sinclair notify [--title T] <message>` — posts a desktop notification, for
  agent hooks that can't emit an OSC 9/777/99 escape themselves.

head: Sinclair > Architecture > Process modes (`app/src/main.rs`)
text: - otherwise — loads config and launches the gpui app.

head: Sinclair > Architecture > Single-instance IPC (`app/src/ipc.rs`)
text:
A per-user unix socket carries one newline-terminated JSON request →
response per connection. Both `--toggle-quick` and `sinclair mcp` are clients;
the live GUI window is the server and does the real work. This is how the MCP
bridge and quick-terminal summon reach the running terminal.

head: Sinclair > Architecture > Event flow
text:
`terminal::Session` emits events through a flume receiver that is also a
`futures` stream; `libsinclair::bridge` is the zero-thread adapter consumed by
gpui foreground tasks. Keep the vt/terminal layers free of gpui types — the
boundary is the bridge.

head: Sinclair > Working in this repo
text:
- In this project the agent has full authority to run git and everything else —
  branching, committing, pushing, tagging, cutting releases, and any other
  operation needed to move the work forward. The owner's usual "I handle git"
  rule does not apply here; act directly.

head: Sinclair > Working in this repo
text:
- Commit messages, PRs, and release notes carry no assistant attribution or
  co-author trailer.

head: Sinclair > Working in this repo
text:
- Releases ship straight from `main`: a workspace version bump committed and
  pushed to `main` is the release (see the version convention below). Run the
  full gate first — `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and a release
  build — before pushing a version bump.

head: Sinclair > Conventions
text:
- Crates are layered; do not introduce upward dependencies (e.g. `vt` must not
  depend on `app`). Keep terminal emulation logic in `vt` and gpui concerns in
  `app`.

head: Sinclair > Conventions
text:
- The workspace version in the root `Cargo.toml` drives releases: pushing a
  `Cargo.toml` version bump to `main` tags and publishes a GitHub release with
  the macOS `.dmg` and Linux `.tar.gz`/`.deb`/`.AppImage` (x86_64 + aarch64),
  and updates the Homebrew cask (see `.github/workflows/release.yml` and
  `docs/release.md`).

head: Sinclair > Conventions
text:
- Linux-only code (`linux.rs`, the `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` blocks in
  `titlebar.rs`/`main.rs`) is not compiled on the macOS dev host; validate it
  with the `Linux Build` workflow (`.github/workflows/linux.yml`, runs on PRs).

head: Repository guidance > Build systems: CMake (primary) + Bazel (validated smoke test)
text:
CMake is naja-verilog's primary build system. It is used by the main
Ubuntu and macOS CI matrices, coverage, valgrind, CodeQL, Emscripten,
installation, and normal development, and it is the build system to use
by default:

head: Repository guidance > Build systems: CMake (primary) + Bazel (validated smoke test)
text:
Bazel (`MODULE.bazel`, `BUILD.bazel`, and `bazel/`) is kept in parallel
as a validated smoke test. The additive `ubuntu-bazel.yml` and
`macos-bazel.yml` workflows run:

head: Repository guidance > Build systems: CMake (primary) + Bazel (validated smoke test)
text:
Those workflows do not initialize git submodules: bzlmod fetches
googletest, while Bison, Flex, and M4 are resolved from the host. Bazel
is not CI's primary gate and does not need to reproduce CMake-specific
coverage, valgrind, sanitizer, CodeQL, Emscripten, or installation
behavior. Its role is to prove that the native Bazel module still
compiles and passes its tests, including when consumed by naja.

head: Repository guidance > Keep the googletest pins synchronized
text:
CMake uses the `thirdparty/googletest` git submodule, while Bazel uses
the `googletest` version in `MODULE.bazel`. Both must name the same
upstream release. `ci/check_submodule_bazel_sync.py`, run by
`dependency-sync-check.yml`, reads the CMake gitlink and verifies it
against the upstream tag corresponding to Bazel's module version.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory
text: This file defines repository-wide instructions for coding agents working in this project.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Project Overview
text: SAF is a Rust + Python (PyO3) static analysis framework that provides:

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Project Overview
text: - Whole-program pointer analysis and value-flow reasoning

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Project Overview
text: - A schema-driven Python API for AI agents to author new analyzers

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Project Overview
text: - A frontend-agnostic core operating on AIR (Analysis Intermediate Representation)

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Project Overview
text: Full requirements: `docs/static_analyzer_factory_srs.md`

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Development Commands (Docker-only)
text: All builds and tests run inside Docker (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS):

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Development Commands (Docker-only)
text: **IMPORTANT: Never run `cargo test` or `cargo build` locally** for crates that depend on LLVM (`saf-frontends`, `saf-analysis`, `saf-python`, `saf-cli`). LLVM 18 is only available inside the Docker container. Running `cargo test -p saf-analysis` locally will fail with "No suitable version of LLVM was found." Always use `make test` or `make shell` to run tests inside Docker. The only crate safe to build/test locally is `saf-core` (no LLVM dependency).

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Development Commands (Docker-only)
text: **IMPORTANT: Subagents must NEVER call `make` commands.** All `make` commands (`make test`, `make shell`, `make lint`, etc.) must be called by the main agent only. Subagents should focus on code reading, analysis, and editing — the main agent coordinates Docker/build operations.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Development Commands (Docker-only)
text: **IMPORTANT: Always `make fmt` before `make lint`.** `make lint` includes a formatting check (`lint-fmt`) that will fail if code isn't formatted. Run `make fmt && make lint` in one command to avoid the wasted round-trip of lint-fail → fmt → lint-again.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Development Commands (Docker-only)
text: **IMPORTANT: `make shell CMD='...'` is unreliable for passing commands.** The CMD variable may not be forwarded through Docker correctly, producing empty output or silently dropping the command. Always use `docker compose run --rm dev sh -c '...'` directly when you need to run a specific command inside Docker. Reserve `make shell` for interactive use only.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Development Commands (Docker-only)
text: **IMPORTANT: PTABen benchmarks take 30-120s.** Always run them in the background (`run_in_background: true`) and check output later, rather than blocking and retrying when the timeout hits.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Development Commands (Docker-only)
text: **IMPORTANT: Never re-run expensive Docker commands just to grep differently.** `make test`, `make lint`, etc. take minutes. If you need to inspect the output, capture it once (e.g., `make test 2>&1 | tee /tmp/test-output.txt`) and search the file afterward. Do not re-run the command with a different `grep` pattern.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Development Commands (Docker-only)
text: **IMPORTANT: SAF uses `cargo-nextest`, not `cargo test`.** The test summary format is `Summary [...] N tests run: N passed, N skipped` — not the standard `test result: ok. N passed` from `cargo test`. Grep for `Summary` or `passed`, not `test result`.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - Use `thiserror` for library error types, `anyhow` only in binaries

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - Use `BTreeMap`/`BTreeSet` (not `HashMap`/`HashSet`) for deterministic iteration (NFR-DET)

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - No `.unwrap()` in library code — return `Result` or use `expect()` with a message

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - All public items should have doc comments

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - Pedantic clippy lints enabled (see `.cargo/config.toml`)

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - **Clippy `doc_markdown`**: In doc comments, wrap type names, function names, and code identifiers in backticks (e.g., `` `ValueId` ``, `` `MemPhi` ``, `` `GEP` ``, `` `LiveOnEntry` ``). Without backticks, clippy treats CamelCase/PascalCase words as missing markdown links.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - **Clippy `iter_over_hash_type` / map iteration**: Use `.values()` or `.keys()` instead of destructuring `for (_, val) in map`. Clippy flags `for (_, v) in btreemap` as "you seem to want to iterate on values".

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - **Clippy `manual_let_else`**: Prefer `let Some(x) = expr else { return; };` over `let x = match expr { Some(v) => v, None => return };`.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - **Clippy `match_same_arms`**: Combine match arms with identical bodies using `|` (e.g., `Operation::Cast { .. } | Operation::Gep { .. } => { ... }`).

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Rust
text: - **PTA constraint extraction**: When adding a new constraint-generation step (e.g., `extract_function_addr_constraints`), update ALL extraction entry points: `extract_constraints()`, `extract_constraints_reachable()`, and `extract_intraprocedural_constraints()`. Missing one causes silent failures in CG refinement or CS-PTA.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Clippy Lint Handling
text:
**Cast safety (`cast_possible_truncation`, `cast_sign_loss`, `cast_possible_wrap`):**
When allowing cast lints, document the invariant:
```rust
// INVARIANT: LLVM limits function parameters to < 2^32
#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
fn param_index(i: usize) -> u32 { i as u32 }
```

text: **PTABen Benchmark Testing:**

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Testing

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Testing
text: - **Always use `-o <path>` (not `--json` to stdout)** when investigating PTABen results from Docker. The `-o` flag writes clean JSON directly to a file inside the container (the project root is mounted at `/workspace`), bypassing all Docker stdout pollution issues. Human-readable output is still printed to stderr for visibility. The `--json` flag to stdout still works but requires `|| true` and `2>/dev/null` workarounds when run via Docker.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Testing
text:
- **Reading JSON results after `-o`**: The output file is written inside the Docker container at `/workspace/...` which maps to the project root on the host. Read the JSON with the `Read` tool or `python3 -c "import json; ..."` on the host:
  ```bash
  # Run benchmark with -o inside Docker (use docker compose, NOT make shell CMD)
  docker compose run --rm dev sh -c 'cargo run --release -p saf-bench -- ptaben --compiled-dir tests/benchmarks/ptaben/.compiled -o /workspace/tests/benchmarks/ptaben/results.json'
  # Then read the file on the host (same path minus /workspace/ prefix)
  # Use Read tool on: tests/benchmarks/ptaben/results.json
  # Or parse with python3:
  python3 -c "
  import json
  with open('tests/benchmarks/ptaben/results.json') as f:
      data = json.load(f)
  for cat in data['by_category']:
      print(f'{cat[\"category\"]}: Exact={cat[\"exact\"]}, Unsound={cat[\"unsound\"]}, Skip={cat[\"skip\"]}')
  "
  ```

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Testing

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Writing Code That Consumes APIs
text: - **Never write code against an assumed API shape.** Before writing a script that parses or processes an API's return value, inspect the real output first with a quick `print(type(x), x)` probe in Docker. This applies to Python bindings, graph exports, PTA results, and any other structured data.

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Coding Conventions > Writing Code That Consumes APIs
text:
- **SAF graph exports use a unified PropertyGraph format** — all graph types share the same structure:
  ```python
  {"schema_version": "0.1.0", "graph_type": "<type>", "metadata": {},
   "nodes": [{"id": "0x...", "labels": [...], "properties": {...}}, ...],
   "edges": [{"src": "0x...", "dst": "0x...", "edge_type": "...", "properties": {}}, ...]}
  ```
  - `callgraph`: nodes have `labels: ["Function"]`, `properties.name`, `properties.kind`; edges have `edge_type: "CALLS"`
  - `cfg`: nodes have `labels: ["Block", "Entry"?]`, `properties.function`, `properties.name`; edges have `edge_type: "FLOWS_TO"`
  - `defuse`: nodes have `labels: ["Value"]` or `["Instruction"]`; edges have `edge_type: "DEFINES"` or `"USED_BY"`
  - `valueflow`: nodes have `properties.kind` (Value/Location/UnknownMem); edges have `edge_type: "Direct"|"Store"|"Load"|...`; `metadata` has `node_count`/`edge_count`
  - `pta.export()`: `{"points_to": [{"value":..., "locations":[...]}, ...], ...}` (unchanged, not PropertyGraph)

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Key Constraints
text: - **No SVF code reuse** — independent implementations only (REQ-IP-001)

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Key Constraints
text: - **Analysis operates only on AIR** — never on frontend-specific types (NFR-EXT-001)

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Key Constraints
text: - **Determinism required** — byte-identical outputs for identical inputs (NFR-DET-001)

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Key Constraints
text: - **All IDs are u128** — BLAKE3-derived, serialized as `0x` + 32 hex chars (FR-AIR-002)

head: AGENTS.md — SAF Static Analyzer Factory > Key Constraints
text: - **SVFG checkers: instruction-level vs node-level mismatch** — Checker specs express instruction-level properties (call sites, resource types) but the SVFG solver operates on SSA value nodes. Three known failure modes: (1) `BTreeSet<SvfgNodeId>` deduplicates same-SSA call sites (e.g., `free(p); free(p);` → 1 node) — use call-site counting when multiplicity matters; (2) `ResourceRole` is a flat namespace — roles shared across resource categories (memory/file/lock) cause checker cross-contamination; (3) solver's `target != source` guard blocks zero-length flows where SSA collapses source and sink to the same node (e.g., alloca returned directly). When adding new checkers or modifying the solver, verify behavior at this boundary.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Development Guide > Project Overview
text: **indonesia-civic-stack** is a Python SDK + MCP server + REST API that wraps 11 Indonesian government data portals into a unified interface. Every module returns `CivicStackResponse`.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Development Guide > Key Patterns > HTTP client — always use civic_client():
text: `civic_client()` auto-reads `PROXY_URL` from environment. Never create raw `httpx.AsyncClient`.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Development Guide > Critical Rules
text: 1. **Never break `civic_stack/shared/`** — all 11 modules depend on schema.py, http.py, mcp.py

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Development Guide > Critical Rules
text: 2. **Never hit live portals in tests** — use VCR cassettes (`tests/<module>/cassettes/`)

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Development Guide > Critical Rules
text: 3. **Always return CivicStackResponse** — never return raw dicts or raise on not-found

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Development Guide > Critical Rules
text: 4. **Rate limiting is mandatory** — every scraper must use `RateLimiter` from civic_stack.shared.http

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Development Guide > Critical Rules
text: 5. **Proxy support is mandatory** — every function takes `proxy_url` kwarg and passes to `civic_client()`

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Development Guide > Critical Rules
text: 6. **No data persistence** — modules fetch and return, no databases, no file writes

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents

- **Disclose AI assistance** with an `Assisted-by` trailer naming your agent and model:
  ```sh
  git commit -s -m "Add support for X" --trailer "Assisted-by: <agent-name>/<model-id>"
  ```

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents
text: - **Commit message format:** Subject in imperative mood ("Add feature X" instead of "Adding feature X"), capitalized, no trailing period, ≤50 characters. Body wrapped at 72 columns, explaining what and why. No `@mentions` or `#123` issue references in the commit — put those in the PR description.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents
text: - **Trim verbiage:** in PR descriptions, commit messages, and code comments. No marketing prose, no restating the diff, no emojis.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents
text: - **Rebase, don't merge:** Never merge `main` into the feature branch; rebase onto the latest `main` and push with `--force-with-lease`. Squash before merge when asked.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents
text: - **Pre-PR gate:** `make tidy fmt vet && make test` must pass and the working tree must be clean after codegen. Commit regenerated files in the same PR.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents
text: - **Flux is GA:** Backward compatibility is mandatory. Breaking changes to CRD fields, status, CLI flags, metrics, or observable behavior will be rejected. Design additive changes and keep older API versions round-tripping.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents
text: - **Copyright:** All new `.go` files must begin with the boilerplate from `hack/boilerplate.go.txt` (Apache 2.0). Update the year to the current year when copying.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow for AI agents

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: Before submitting code, review your changes for the following:

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **No secrets in logs or events.** Never surface auth tokens, passwords, or credential URLs in error messages, conditions, events, or log lines. Use `fluxcd/pkg/masktoken` and the `internal/error` sanitizers.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **No unchecked I/O.** Close HTTP response bodies, file handles, and archive readers in `defer` statements. Check and propagate errors from `io.Copy`, `os.Remove`, `os.Rename`.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **No path traversal.** Validate and sanitize file paths extracted from archives or user input. Use `securejoin` to ensure paths stay within the expected root. Never `filepath.Join` with untrusted components without validation.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **No unbounded reads.** Use `io.LimitReader` when reading from network or archive sources. Respect existing size limits; do not introduce new reads without bounds.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **No command injection.** Do not shell out via `os/exec`. Use Go libraries for git, helm, OCI, and cloud operations.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **No hardcoded defaults for security settings.** TLS verification must remain enabled by default; proxy and auth settings come from user-provided secrets, not environment variables.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **Error handling.** Wrap errors with `%w` for chain inspection. Do not swallow errors silently. Return actionable error messages that help users diagnose the issue without leaking internal state.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **Resource cleanup.** Ensure temporary files, directories, and cloned repos are cleaned up on all code paths (success and error). Use `defer` and `t.TempDir()` in tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **Concurrency safety.** Do not introduce shared mutable state without synchronization. Reconcilers run concurrently; per-object work must be isolated. Respect the existing `Storage.LockFor` pattern.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **No panics.** Never use `panic` in runtime code paths. Return errors and let the reconciler handle them gracefully.

head: AGENTS.md > Code quality
text: - **Minimal surface.** Keep new exported APIs, flags, and environment variables to the minimum needed. Every export is a backward-compatibility commitment.

head: AGENTS.md > Project overview
text: source-controller is a core component of the [Flux GitOps Toolkit](https://fluxcd.io/flux/components/). It reconciles five custom resources in the `source.toolkit.fluxcd.io` API group — `GitRepository`, `OCIRepository`, `HelmRepository`, `HelmChart`, and `Bucket` — by fetching upstream content, verifying it (PGP, Cosign, Notation), and packaging it into an immutable `Artifact` (tarball or chart). Artifacts are written to a local filesystem rooted at `--storage-path` and served over HTTP from `--storage-addr` so downstream controllers (kustomize-controller, helm-controller, source-watcher) can consume them. Status conditions, events, and the artifact URL/revision are what other Flux controllers key off.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Standard `gofmt`. Every exported name needs a doc comment; non-trivial unexported declarations should have one too.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Reconcilers follow the Flux sub-reconciler pattern: the top-level `Reconcile` invokes an ordered slice of step functions, then `summarize.Processor` (in `internal/reconcile/summarize/`) collapses their `reconcile.Result` + errors into terminal conditions and patches status. Don't set conditions directly from step code.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Status writes go through the patch helper with `metav1.Condition` values from `api/v1/condition_types.go` and `fluxcd/pkg/apis/meta` (`Ready`, `Reconciling`, `Stalled`, kind-specific `ArtifactInStorage`, `SourceVerified`, `FetchFailed`, etc.). Use `fluxcd/pkg/runtime/conditions`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Events: `EventRecorder` wired to `fluxcd/pkg/runtime/events.Recorder`. Event reasons match condition reasons.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Artifacts: create via `Storage.NewArtifactFor`, persist with `Storage.Archive`/`Storage.Copy` inside the per-object lock (`Storage.LockFor`), publish via `Storage.SetArtifactURL`, and run `Storage.GarbageCollect` after a successful write honoring `--artifact-retention-ttl` and `--artifact-retention-records`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - TLS/transport: build `http.Transport` via `internal/transport` and TLS configs via `internal/tls`. Proxy, HTTP/2, and keepalive settings must stay consistent.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Feature gates go through `internal/features` plus `fluxcd/pkg/runtime/features`. Define the constant in `features.go` with its default; check with `features.Enabled(...)`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Digests default to `internal/digest.Canonical` and can be overridden by `--artifact-digest-algo`. Hash through the writer in `internal/digest` — never import `crypto/sha256` directly.

text: - Two Go modules: root and `api/`. `make tidy`, `fmt`, `vet`, `test` iterate both. A change to `api/` types requires running `make generate` **and** `make manifests` and committing the regenerated files in the same PR.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas and non-obvious rules
text: - `make verify` is the CI gate — a dirty diff means you forgot to run codegen or tidy.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas and non-obvious rules

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas and non-obvious rules
text: - `Storage` serializes writes per object via `fluxcd/pkg/lockedfile` and expects `--storage-path` to be a real local directory. Never write artifacts outside `Storage.BasePath` — the file server exposes that path verbatim at `--storage-addr`.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas and non-obvious rules
text: - Workload Identity is feature-gated by `auth.FeatureGateObjectLevelWorkloadIdentity` (from `fluxcd/pkg/auth`). Token caching is opt-in via `--token-cache-max-size`.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas and non-obvious rules
text: - `CacheSecretsAndConfigMaps` (in `internal/features`) is off by default; `Secret`/`ConfigMap` lookups bypass the cache and hit the API server directly. Mind that before adding new secret reads to a hot path.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas and non-obvious rules
text: - The controller watches a label-selected subset of its CRs — see `Cache.ByObject` in `mustSetupManager`. Adding a new kind requires updating both `main.go` and the scheme.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas and non-obvious rules
text: - `pkg/azure`, `pkg/gcp`, `pkg/minio` are importable by external consumers. Treat their exported surface as semi-public API.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release Process
text: Releases are tag-driven and should stay aligned with `package.json`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release Process
text: 1. Bump `package.json` to the target version (for example `0.6.0`).

head: Repository Guidelines > Release Process
text: 2. Run `pnpm release:local` to verify tests, build output, release tarball, checksums, and Homebrew formula generation.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release Process
text: 3. Commit the version bump and any required workflow fixes to `main`, then push `main`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release Process
text: 4. Create and push an annotated tag: `git tag -a v0.6.0 -m "v0.6.0"` and `git push origin v0.6.0`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release Process
text: 5. Watch the `Release` GitHub Actions workflow and confirm the GitHub release is published with the `.tar.gz`, `.deb`, `.rpm`, `sha256sums.txt`, and `tokenjuice.rb` assets.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release Process
text: 6. Manually dispatch the Tokenjuice publisher workflow in the canonical `vincentkoc/homebrew-tap` repository with the release tag, then confirm its formula points at the published tarball and SHA. Keep this manual until GitHub App dispatch automation lands.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release Process
text: For formula-only recovery against an existing immutable tarball, download and verify the published checksum, then run `pnpm release:formula -- --published-tarball-sha256 <64-lowercase-hex>`. This mode is offline and does not require a local tarball. Replace only the broken formula asset; do not retag or republish unrelated artifacts.

head: CLAUDE.md — Rustavi Driving Exam simulator
text:
First-person 3D browser simulator of the Rustavi (Georgia) B-category Stage 1 driving exam ground.
Plain ES modules + vendored three.js (`vendor/`), no framework, no build needed to run.
Course interpretation and assumptions: comments in `src/courses/rustavi/course.js`; scoring sources: `src/config/examRules.js`.

  - `world.js` colliders, kerbs, terrain height (hill ramp), marking list
  - `exam.js` exam state machine, penalties, skip detection, restarts, result
  - `exercises/<element>.js` each has `buildStation` (geometry), an Evaluator (scoring) and `createCoach` (training steps)

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text:
A [herdr](https://herdr.dev) plugin (stdlib Python only, no dependencies) that
turns herdr's agent sidebar into an inbox: transcript-derived session titles,
settle/mark-unread triage ordering, per-agent runtimes, workspace rollups, and
an accumulated, resumable chat history. Everything drives herdr through its
public socket API and plugin manifest — never patch or assume herdr internals;
verify against the installed CLI (`herdr --help`, `herdr api schema --json`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text:
Manifest changes (`herdr-plugin.toml`) only take effect after re-linking.
Daemon code changes only take effect after `scripts/restart-daemon.sh`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: Three processes share one contract:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **`daemon.py`** — the only long-lived process and the only writer of state.
  Threads: `events_loop` (persistent `events.subscribe` connection; herdr
  closes every other request's connection after one response — see
  `herdr_request`), `control_loop` (unix socket serving one-line JSON commands
  from the other two programs), `summarize_loop` (serial queue shelling out to
  the user's `summarize_cmd`), and the main loop (debounced `refresh()`).
  `refresh()` diffs `agent.list` against `self.terminals` (keyed by
  `terminal_id`, which survives herdr restarts), derives titles, computes the
  inbox `rank` token, and reports pane/workspace metadata — computation under
  `self.lock`, socket I/O outside it (keep it that way; control clients have
  3s timeouts). The sidebar ordering itself is herdr's `agent.view.set`
  sorting by our `rank` token; it and all reported metadata die with the
  herdr server, so every events-loop reconnect clears the report caches and
  re-asserts the view.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **`actions.py`** — short-lived dispatcher behind the manifest `[[actions]]`;
  forwards ops to the control socket (starting the daemon if needed). The
  sidebar resize is special: herdr's live width is session state that config
  `sidebar_width` cannot move, but min/max clamps re-apply on every
  `reload-config` — so resize pins width=min=max, reloads, then relaxes the
  bounds so herdr's native mouse drag keeps working. Serialized via flock;
  never leave bounds pinned.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **`inbox_tui.py`** — the popup TUI (curses). Reads herdr directly for live
  rows, `history.jsonl` for archived chats, and sends mutations through the
  control socket. All rendering must go through `seg()`/`_wtrunc()` (display-
  width aware — emoji are two columns; naive `len()`/`ljust` crashes curses at
  the last cell). Colors come from `_THEME_PALETTES`, extracted from herdr's
  own themes; state colors follow herdr's language (blocked=red,
  working=yellow, done-unseen=teal, idle=green). `--demo` swaps the data layer
  for fixtures — keep it working; it's how screenshots and manual tests run.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: Shared conventions all three must agree on:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **Paths derive from the session socket** (`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, defaulting to
  `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`): state dir is `<socket dir>/agent-inbox-state/`.
  Deliberately NOT `$HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` — the daemon may be started from
  a shell without plugin env, and all entry points must resolve identical
  paths.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **Control protocol** ops (`settle`, `unread`, `clear`, `retitle`,
  `set-title`, `settle-workspace`, `ping`) live in `handle_command`; the
  control thread must never die (it answers malformed input, never raises).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **`herdr_request` raises only `RuntimeError`/`OSError`** — callers catch
  exactly those. Don't let `ValueError` leak from JSON parsing; a herdr
  restart mid-request must never kill a thread.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **Rank tiers** (`rank_for`): blocked=0, done/unread=1, working=2, idle=3,
  unknown=4, settled=5. Settling clears on transition INTO working/blocked;
  settled outranks done so an explicitly settled agent stays sunk after
  finishing.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **Archiving**: `_archive_chat` appends to both the per-terminal history (⚫
  rows in the tree, capped 10) and `history.jsonl` (global browser + resume,
  compacted atomically). Archive triggers: session-ref change, agent-kind
  change, pane gone >120s. Resume commands are built only from
  `sess_kind`/`sess_value` via `resume_cmd()` with `shlex.quote`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Constraints
text:
- Stdlib only; `tomllib` (3.11+) is optional — config parsing must degrade to
  defaults, never crash, on older Pythons.

head: CLAUDE.md > Constraints
text:
- Titles and tokens are display-only metadata reported under the single
  source id `herdr-agent-inbox`; herdr normalizes/caps them (80 chars, 16
  tokens per report). `_clean_title` strips command wrappers, system
  reminders, and URLs — user prompts are untrusted input.

head: CLAUDE.md > Constraints
text:
- Any file the daemon rewrites in place (state.json, history compaction,
  config.toml in actions.py) must write tmp + `os.replace`, and config writes
  must go through `os.path.realpath` so dotfiles symlinks survive.

head: AGENTS.md > 运行时数据流
text: 1. `MediaPlayer.SetUrl()`/`Play()` 取得或创建 `VlcMediaPlayer`。

head: AGENTS.md > 运行时数据流
text: 2. `VlcMediaPlayer` 创建 `libvlc_instance_t`、`libvlc_media_t` 和 `libvlc_media_player_t`。

head: AGENTS.md > 运行时数据流
text: 3. `libvlc_video_set_callbacks()` 注册 lock、unlock 和 display 回调，`libvlc_video_set_format()` 要求输出 `RV24`。

head: AGENTS.md > 运行时数据流
text: 4. LibVLC 解码线程把一帧写入 `_imageIntPtr` 指向的非托管内存。

head: AGENTS.md > 运行时数据流
text: 5. display 回调将帧复制到托管后备缓冲，并在锁内交换前后缓冲。

head: AGENTS.md > 运行时数据流
text: 6. Unity 主线程的 `Update()` 调用 `CheckForImageUpdate()`，再用 `LoadRawTextureData()` 和 `Apply(false)` 上传到 `Texture2D`。

head: AGENTS.md > 运行时数据流
text: 7. `RawImage.uvRect` 或材质纹理缩放负责垂直翻转。

head: AGENTS.md > 运行时数据流
text: 音频由 LibVLC 直接管理，不经过 Unity `AudioSource`。播放器状态由协程轮询 LibVLC 状态并转换为 Unity 事件。普通播放器可从 `MediaPlayerPool` 复用；360 播放器当前直接持有和释放自己的核心实例。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 原生互操作
text: - P/Invoke 函数名、参数宽度、返回值、结构体字段顺序和回调签名必须与仓库实际 LibVLC 版本匹配。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 原生互操作
text: - 不凭记忆修改 ABI。涉及 ABI 时，应核对对应版本的官方头文件或导出符号，并至少验证 Windows 和一个 Android ABI。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 原生互操作
text: - 原生回调委托必须在播放器整个原生生命周期中保持强引用；不得把短生命周期 lambda 直接交给 LibVLC。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 原生互操作
text: - `opaque`、`GCHandle` 和播放器实例映射必须同生共灭。解除映射或释放 `GCHandle` 前，应确保原生回调已经停止。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 原生互操作
text: - 新增字符串互操作时明确字符编码和所有权；不得释放 LibVLC 所有的指针，也不得遗忘释放调用方所有的分配。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 线程模型
text: - Unity 对象、场景、组件、材质、纹理、协程和 `Time` API 只在 Unity 主线程使用。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 线程模型
text: - LibVLC 视频回调和轨道读取线程不能直接修改 Unity 对象。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 线程模型
text: - 跨线程共享的字典、标志、媒体指针和缓冲区必须具备明确的同步或所有权。`volatile` 不能替代复合操作所需的锁。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 线程模型
text: - 不在持锁期间调用可能阻塞、回调用户代码或进入 Unity 的操作。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 线程模型
text: - 后台线程必须能取消，并在释放相关原生指针和托管缓冲前确认退出；不要依赖后台线程随进程退出。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 线程模型
text: - 主线程分发器不得假定托管线程 ID 永远等于 1。若修改这一部分，应在 Unity 启动时捕获真实主线程或同步上下文。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 帧缓冲与纹理
text: - `RV24` 固定为每像素 3 字节，pitch 为 `width * 3`。缓冲区大小、pitch、纹理格式和上传长度必须一致。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 帧缓冲与纹理
text: - 对宽高和乘法做合法性/溢出检查，拒绝零值、负值和不合理的大分辨率。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 帧缓冲与纹理
text: - 分辨率发生变化时，必须作为一个受控生命周期操作同时更新：托管前后缓冲、非托管帧内存、LibVLC 视频格式和 Unity 纹理。不得让回调写入旧尺寸内存。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 帧缓冲与纹理
text: - 回调热路径和 `Update()` 中避免逐帧分配、LINQ、反射和重复日志。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 帧缓冲与纹理
text: - `Texture2D.Apply(false)` 仍有 CPU 到 GPU 上传成本。性能改动必须用 Profiler/目标设备数据验证，不能只凭代码注释声称“零开销”或“超高性能”。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 帧缓冲与纹理
text: - CPU 垂直翻转会原地修改共享帧数组；若其他消费者也读取该帧，必须先明确所有权。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 媒体与资源所有权
text: - 每次成功创建 `libvlc_media_t` 都必须有清晰的释放点。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 媒体与资源所有权
text: - 切换 URL 时要保持“播放器当前媒体、`_media` 字段、轨道元数据和扩展播放器指针”一致；旧媒体和轨道信息应在不再使用后及时释放。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 媒体与资源所有权
text: - `libvlc_media_tracks_get()` 的每次成功返回都应与一次 `libvlc_media_tracks_release()` 配对，不能只保存最后一次返回值。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 媒体与资源所有权
text: - 推荐的销毁顺序是：停止新的工作和恢复协程，停止播放，确保回调/工作线程静止，释放轨道结果，释放 media player，释放 media，释放 LibVLC 实例，释放非托管帧内存，最后移除实例映射和 `GCHandle`。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 媒体与资源所有权
text: - `Dispose()` 必须幂等。释放后的实例不能再次进池或继续响应回调。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 媒体与资源所有权
text: - Unity 资源使用 `Destroy()`，不要在运行时使用 `DestroyImmediate()`。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 播放状态与事件
text: - 区分 `Play`、`Resume`、`Pause`、`TogglePause`、`Stop` 和 `Reload`；不要依赖模糊的“如果没在播放就切换”行为。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 播放状态与事件
text: - 一个用户操作对应的 `OnPlayEvent`、`OnStopEvent` 和错误事件应只触发一次。修改播放流程时检查手动触发和状态监控是否重复。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 播放状态与事件
text: - LibVLC 构造完成、`libvlc_media_player_play()` 返回成功、状态变为 Playing、收到首帧是四个不同阶段；日志和 UI 不能混为一谈。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 播放状态与事件
text: - 网络流短暂处于 Opening/Buffering 不等于失败。恢复策略应有单实例互斥、退避、次数上限和取消条件。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 播放状态与事件
text: - 不要从 `libvlc_errmsg()` 的全局/线程局部最后错误推断任意旧操作的失败原因；尽量在失败调用附近读取并记录上下文。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 对象池
text: - 入池实例必须停止播放但仍保持可复用，且不能已经 `Dispose()`。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 对象池
text: - 出池后应重置 URL、媒体、轨道、缓冲状态、静音/音量、错误计数和首帧时间等所有会跨使用者泄漏的状态。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 对象池
text: - 池键必须覆盖影响实例兼容性的配置。若平台、色度、VLC 参数或硬解设置不同，应扩展池键或禁用复用。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 对象池
text: - 清理池时不得销毁仍被组件、回调或后台线程使用的播放器。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心不变量 > 对象池
text: - 对池的改动必须在多播放器场景中验证，而不只是单播放器示例。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > Windows x86_64
text: - 原生源目录是 `Assets/MSO-Player/Plugins/x86_64/libvlc/`，其中包括 `libvlc.dll`、`libvlccore.dll` 和 `plugins/` 模块树。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > Windows x86_64
text: - `BuildProcessor` 在 Windows 构建完成后复制整套目录到 `<Product>_Data/Plugins/x86_64/`。修改它时不得只验证 DLL 存在，还要验证插件模块目录和真实播放。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > Windows x86_64
text: - 构建输出文件名不一定等于 `Application.productName + ".exe"`。处理输出路径时优先使用 `Path.GetDirectoryName(report.summary.outputPath)`，不要依赖字符串查找后直接 `Remove()`。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > Android
text: - 当前包含 `armeabi-v7a` 和 `arm64-v8a` 原生库；修改某个 ABI 时必须检查另一 ABI 是否仍可打包。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > Android
text: - 网络播放需要清单中的网络权限；本地文件访问还受 Android 版本和分区存储限制，不能只依赖旧的外部存储权限。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > Android
text: - `MediaPlayerAndroid` 的序列化缓存配置应真正参与生成参数。新增或修改参数时区分实例参数 `--option` 与媒体参数 `:option`，避免同一缓存项被多处冲突设置。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > Android
text: - MediaCodec、直接渲染和 LibVLC 内存视频回调可能相互影响。硬解参数的有效性必须以设备日志和首帧结果验证。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > Android
text: - 至少在一个 ARM64 真机上验证启动、首帧、切流、前后台切换、低内存处理和退出释放；模拟器结果不能覆盖真机硬解行为。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > 未验证平台
text: - WebGL 不能直接加载当前原生 LibVLC。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > 未验证平台
text: - macOS、iOS 和 Linux 需要各自的原生库、插件导入设置、加载路径、构建处理和运行验证。

head: AGENTS.md > 平台约束 > 未验证平台
text: - 文档、Inspector 或 `.meta` 中出现平台名字，不构成支持证据。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: 以下不表示当前必然存在缺陷，而是该播放器最容易回归的边界。触及对应代码时必须显式评估：

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - 构造、`Play()`、对象池复用和 URL 切换只能产生一次预期播放动作，事件不得由调用层手工重复触发。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - `UpdateUrl()`/`UpdateUrlSmooth()` 必须同步替换原生媒体、轨道读取任务和包装器引用；旧媒体的异步结果不得覆盖新媒体状态。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - 每次 `libvlc_media_tracks_get()` 成功调用都必须对应一次 `libvlc_media_tracks_release()`，媒体在线程读取期间必须保有独立引用。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - 静态播放器实例字典、帧缓冲区和 Dispose/LibVLC 回调之间必须保持并发保护，释放后不得接受新回调。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - 不得静默吞掉生命周期、切流、纹理更新和对象池异常；日志需带操作上下文，但不能输出完整签名 URL。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - 360 播放器同一时刻只能存在一个状态监控和一个恢复任务；禁用、销毁和恢复不能互相停止到半释放状态。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - Android 缓存值必须进入实例参数；修改 MediaCodec 参数后需复查其与 LibVLC 内存视频回调的兼容性。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - Prefab 脚本 GUID 必须与 `.meta` 一致；序列化字段重命名需保留 `FormerlySerializedAs`，并在 Unity 中检查 Missing Script 和字段迁移。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - Windows 构建后处理必须从实际输出文件名推导 `_Data` 目录，不得按 DLL 同名规则递归删除 LibVLC 插件。

head: AGENTS.md > 持续风险审查清单
text: - 示例场景可能含过期、私有或带签名的流地址。不要把它们当成稳定测试源，也不要在日志、提交信息或回复中传播完整地址。

head: AGENTS.md
text:
devops.el runs and tangles org-babel source blocks on local and remote
machines. A `#+TARGET: /ssh:host: (tag)` keyword maps a heading tag to a
TRAMP prefix or directory, and blocks under a heading with that tag run
there (`:dir` is injected) or tangle there (`:tangle` paths are redirected).

head: AGENTS.md > Layout
text:
| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `devops.el` | Core: `#+TARGET` parsing, `:dir`/`:session` injection, `devops-tangle`, terminal DWIM |
| `devops-drift.el` | `devops-drift`: tangles to a temp dir and compares with each target |
| `devops-lob.el` | Loads a project's `tools.org` into the Library of Babel |
| `devops-test.el` | The whole ERT suite |
| `decisions/` | Decision records (`NN-topic.org`). Read the relevant one before you change a design it covers. |
| `examples/` | Org files that show each feature. Keep them in step with behavior. |

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text:
Run `make compile` and `make test` before calling something done. CI runs
the suite on Emacs 30.1.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text:
`make` puts batch Emacs under a watchdog (`perl -e 'alarm shift; exec
@ARGV' N`), because ERT in batch mode can hang on a stdin prompt or a loop.
macOS has no `timeout`, so wrap any ad-hoc `emacs --batch` run the same way.
Clean up stale `.elc` files with `make clean`. Emacs loads a stale `.elc`
in preference to the edited source.

head: AGENTS.md > Compatibility
text:
- `Package-Requires: ((emacs "30.1"))`, so the baseline is the Org 9.7
  bundled with it. Your local Org may be newer, so a test passing locally
  doesn't prove it runs on 9.7. Check any Org function you call against
  Emacs 30.1's `lisp/org`. For example, `org-base-buffer-file-name` only
  exists in later versions.

head: AGENTS.md > Compatibility
text:
- `(require 'tramp)` is explicit because tests run under `emacs -Q`, where
  the autoloads aren't enough.

head: AGENTS.md > How tangling works
text:
`devops-tangle` narrows the org buffer to the heading and calls
`org-babel-tangle` there. It never edits the org text, and it never saves
the buffer: `save-buffer` is removed from `org-babel-pre-tangle-hook` for
the duration.

head: AGENTS.md > How tangling works
text:
Paths are redirected at the data level. A `:filter-return` advice on
`org-babel-tangle-collect-blocks` rewrites each block's destination file in
org's write plan. `devops--tangle-subtree` adds it only while it tangles,
with `devops--tangle-redirect` bound. `devops--tangle-destination` (for tangling) and
`devops-drift--destination` (for the drift check) are pure functions that
decide each destination. Test new path rules there. Org still does the
writing itself (`:mkdirp`, `:shebang`, `:tangle-mode`). The background is in
`decisions/01-tangling.org`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **Org semantics are upstream's.** Don't reinterpret an org built-in
  header argument or keyword. Add a namespaced one instead, as `:target`
  does.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **Delete dead code.** When code becomes unused, remove it and its tests.
  Don't shim or deprecate.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **Docstrings explain why.** The existing style is full sentences that
  give the reason and the edge case, e.g. why a path is expanded, or what
  goes wrong without a step. Match it. checkdoc must stay clean (quote
  symbols as `` `sym' ``, first line a complete sentence). The package is
  headed for MELPA.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **No top-level advice.** Execution advice is added by the global
  `devops-mode`. Advice that only matters inside a devops command is added
  and removed around that command. `devops-unload-function` turns the mode
  off. MELPA's melpazoid flags any `(advice-add` at column 0.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **Advice changes as little as it can.** An advice on an org function
  should change only what devops needs. When that only matters inside a
  devops command, make it a no-op unless a dynamic variable is bound, as
  `devops--redirect-tangle-plan` does with `devops--tangle-redirect`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **Scripted evaluation is synchronous.** Anything that reads a block's
  result (tangling, drift, `:var` and noweb references) runs inside
  `devops-with-sync`, because under `:async` the result is a placeholder
  UUID.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **Tests never touch a remote.** Use `devops-test--with-org` for buffer
  text and `devops-test--with-local-target` for a temp directory that
  stands in for a server. A test must not leave files in the working
  directory.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- New `.el` files carry the GPL header and an `Assisted-by:` line, like the
  existing ones.

head: OpenMANETd — Codex Guide
text:
`CLAUDE.md` is the canonical repository guide. Before modifying this repository,
read it completely and follow its commands, architecture notes, generated-code
boundaries, testing patterns, and platform gotchas.

head: OpenMANETd — Codex Guide
text:
The detailed rules under `.claude/rules/` also apply to Codex. Read the rules
relevant to the work before editing:

head: OpenMANETd — Codex Guide
text:
- All Go changes: `concurrency.md`, `performance.md`, `idiomatic-go.md`, and
  `testing.md`.

head: OpenMANETd — Codex Guide
text: - API changes: `api-design.md` and `testing.md`.

head: OpenMANETd — Codex Guide
text: - Frontend changes: `frontend.md` and the frontend sections of `testing.md`.

head: OpenMANETd — Codex Guide
text: - Instrumentation snapshot changes: `instrumentation.md`.

head: OpenMANETd — Codex Guide
text:
Treat these referenced documents as repository instructions, not optional
background material. Keep this file as a small entrypoint so the Claude and
Codex guidance cannot drift into conflicting copies; update the canonical guide
or shared rule files when project policy changes.

head: OpenMANETd — Codex Guide
text:
At minimum, every behavior change must have tests, all Go changes must be
formatted and lint-clean, and concurrency-sensitive changes must pass the race
detector. Never directly edit generated files under `internal/api/`,
`frontend/src/gen/`, or `internal/database/models/`.

head: SceneMint Agent Notes > Project
text: SceneMint 是轻量图片生成站点：Go HTTP 后端 + Astro/React 前端。生产环境由 Go 服务同源提供 `/api` 和 `web/dist`。

head: SceneMint Agent Notes > Project
text: 额度数据使用本地 bbolt，默认路径为 `data/quota.db`；不要误引入 SQLite。

head: SceneMint Agent Notes > Development
text: - 后端路由基于 Echo，API 错误响应优先沿用 `gox/server` envelope。

head: SceneMint Agent Notes > Development
text: - 前端 UI 沿用现有 Astro React island、Tailwind、shadcn/Base UI 组件风格。

head: SceneMint Agent Notes > Development
text: - 变更保持小而直接；不要顺手重构无关代码或引入新依赖。

head: SceneMint Agent Notes > Commit
text: - 提交信息优先使用简短的 Conventional Commits 风格：`type(scope): summary`，例如 `fix(api): handle quota errors`。

head: SceneMint Agent Notes > Commit
text: - 常用 `type` 包括 `feat`、`fix`、`docs`、`refactor`、`test`、`chore`；每个 commit 尽量只包含一件事。

head: Claude Guidelines for PyRMQ > Repository Overview

head: Claude Guidelines for PyRMQ > Repository Overview

head: Claude Guidelines for PyRMQ > Repository Overview
text: - Built-in connection retry logic

head: Claude Guidelines for PyRMQ > Repository Overview

head: Claude Guidelines for PyRMQ > Repository Overview
text: - Support for message priorities

head: Claude Guidelines for PyRMQ > Repository Overview

head: Claude Guidelines for PyRMQ > Repository Overview

head: AGENTS.md
text: Instruções para agentes que trabalham neste repositório, especialmente Codex.

head: AGENTS.md
text: Este projeto é o **Workshop Marketing IA**: um assistente de marketing digital, copy, funis, páginas, tráfego, produtos digitais e entregas para alunos. A base metodológica é VTSD, Light Copy, C10X, Low Ticket e Middle Ticket.

head: AGENTS.md > Prioridade das Regras
text: 1. Siga primeiro as instruções do usuário nesta conversa.

head: AGENTS.md > Prioridade das Regras
text: 2. Para regras do repositório, use este `AGENTS.md` como manual operacional do Codex.

head: AGENTS.md > Prioridade das Regras
text: 3. Quando a tarefa envolver marketing, copy, produto, página, tráfego ou entrega do aluno, consulte `CLAUDE.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Prioridade das Regras
text: 4. Quando o usuário pedir um comando do workshop, leia `.claude/commands/{nome}.md` antes de agir.

head: AGENTS.md > Prioridade das Regras
text: 5. Quando o comando apontar skills ou referências, leia somente os arquivos necessários em `.claude/skills/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Prioridade das Regras
text: 6. Se houver conflito entre `CLAUDE.md`, uma skill e um command, prefira o command específico lido para a tarefa atual. Se o conflito afetar arquitetura, script ou risco de sobrescrita, avise o usuário antes de seguir.

head: AGENTS.md > Prioridade das Regras
text: As pastas `.agents/` e `.codex/` são geradas a partir de `.claude/` por `scripts/exportar-para-codex.py`. Nunca edite essas pastas: altere o original em `.claude/` e rode o script de novo.

head: AGENTS.md > Prioridade das Regras
text: No Codex, este repositório está em **Modo Codex**. Slash commands do Claude Code não executam automaticamente. Pedido como `/copy-pagina`, `copy-pagina`, `segue o comando copy-pagina` ou `quero ajustar a página` deve ser interpretado como: abrir o arquivo em `.claude/commands/` e executar o roteiro manualmente.

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: Quando estiver trabalhando nas entregas do workshop, aja como consultor de marketing digital e copywriting, não como programador explicando detalhes técnicos ao aluno.

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: Especialidades esperadas:

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: - Copy argumentativa e lógica em estilo Light Copy.

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: - Estrutura 8D de páginas de vendas.

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: - Quadro, Furadeira, Decorados, Identidades e Urgências Ocultas.

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: - Funis perpétuos, low ticket, middle ticket e campanhas.

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: - Anúncios baseados na Mandala da Criatividade.

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: - Materiais prontos para uso, salvos nos diretórios corretos.

head: AGENTS.md > Papel do Agente
text: Quando a tarefa for manutenção do repositório, scripts, configuração de agentes ou revisão técnica, pode usar linguagem técnica, mas mantenha objetividade.

head: AGENTS.md > Idioma, Tom e Texto Visível
text: - Responda sempre em português do Brasil.

head: AGENTS.md > Idioma, Tom e Texto Visível
text: - Todo texto entregue ao usuário deve ter acentuação correta.

head: AGENTS.md > Idioma, Tom e Texto Visível
text: - Evite jargão técnico quando estiver falando com o aluno final.

head: AGENTS.md > Idioma, Tom e Texto Visível
text: - Não use travessão em textos do projeto. Reescreva com ponto, vírgula ou dois pontos.

head: AGENTS.md > Idioma, Tom e Texto Visível
text: - Não use inglês em mensagens finais de entregas do workshop, exceto nomes próprios, ferramentas e termos inevitáveis.

head: AGENTS.md > Idioma, Tom e Texto Visível
text: - Não mostre HTML completo no chat. Salve o arquivo e informe o caminho.

head: AGENTS.md > Idioma, Tom e Texto Visível
text: - Não diga que "rodou revisora", "aplicou manual interno" ou detalhes invisíveis do processo. Entregue o resultado final.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes
text: A pasta `.claude/` nasceu para o ecossistema Claude Code. No Codex, esses arquivos não viram slash commands, skills nativas, hooks automáticos ou subagentes reais por mágica. Eles devem ser tratados como uma biblioteca operacional do projeto.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Commands
text: No Codex, um command é um roteiro de execução. Sempre que o usuário pedir `/nome`, `nome`, `segue o comando nome` ou descrever claramente um fluxo do workshop, faça:

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Commands
text: 1. Localize `.claude/commands/{nome}.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Commands
text: 2. Leia o arquivo antes de agir.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Commands
text: 3. Siga os passos do command na ordem.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Commands
text: 4. Quando o command apontar outros arquivos, leia apenas os necessários.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Commands
text: 5. Se o command depender de produto, carregue `meus-produtos/.ativo` e o contexto do produto antes de gerar.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: No Codex, uma skill é uma referência técnica, metodológica ou operacional. Ela deve ser lida quando:

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: - Um command mandar usar aquela skill.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: - O usuário citar a skill pelo nome.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: - A tarefa depender claramente daquela base de conhecimento.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: - O `AGENTS.md` ou `CLAUDE.md` apontar aquela skill como fonte obrigatória.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: 1. Abra o `SKILL.md`, `skill.md` ou arquivo principal da pasta.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: 2. Leia só o necessário para a tarefa atual.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: 3. Se a skill apontar `references/`, carregue apenas as referências citadas pelo fluxo.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: 4. Se a skill tiver scripts, prefira usar os scripts existentes em vez de recriar lógica.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Skills
text: 5. Não carregue a pasta inteira sem necessidade.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Agentes
text: No Codex, um agente é um papel especializado com critérios, modo de pensar e checklist. Ele não vira automaticamente um subagente separado. Quando o usuário pedir um agente, ou quando um command mandar usar um agente:

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Agentes
text: 1. Leia `.claude/agents/{nome}.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Agentes
text:
2. Leia memórias relevantes, se existirem:
   - `.claude/agents-memory/{nome}.md`
   - `meus-produtos/{ativo}/agentes/{nome}.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Agentes
text: 3. Assuma aquele papel dentro da execução atual.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Agentes
text: 4. Aplique os critérios do agente ao entregar.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Agentes
text: 5. Não diga que "chamou subagente" se isso não aconteceu de fato no Codex.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Hooks e Settings do Claude
text: No Codex, eles são documentação e referência de segurança. Não presuma que hooks do Claude rodam automaticamente. Se uma regra importante depende de hook, aplique manualmente no Codex.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Hooks e Settings do Claude
text: - Verificação de acentuação.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Hooks e Settings do Claude
text: - Proteção contra tokens.

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Regra de Ouro Para Equivalência com Claude
text: Para chegar perto do mesmo resultado do Claude Code, o Codex deve simular o fluxo:

head: AGENTS.md > Como Codex Usa Commands, Skills e Agentes > Regra de Ouro Para Equivalência com Claude
text: Se o Codex não leu o command, skill ou agente relevante, ele ainda não tem contexto suficiente para executar o fluxo do workshop com fidelidade.

head: AGENTS.md > Abertura de Sessão no Codex
text: Em uma conversa normal de uso do workshop, se o usuário começar com saudação, pedido genérico ou intenção de criar produto, leia `.claude/commands/produto-novo.md` e siga o fluxo de produto novo.

head: AGENTS.md > Abertura de Sessão no Codex
text: Não acione `produto-novo` automaticamente quando:

head: AGENTS.md > Abertura de Sessão no Codex
text: - A mensagem começa com `/` ou menciona um comando específico.

head: AGENTS.md > Abertura de Sessão no Codex
text: - O usuário pede revisão técnica, configuração de Codex, diagnóstico do projeto ou manutenção do repositório.

head: AGENTS.md > Abertura de Sessão no Codex
text: - O usuário invoca explicitamente um agente ou pergunta como algo funciona.

head: AGENTS.md > Abertura de Sessão no Codex
text: Se a mensagem inicial trouxer dados úteis, como nicho, nome do produto ou ideia, aproveite esses dados dentro do fluxo em vez de perguntar de novo.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: Antes de criar, editar ou salvar qualquer entrega de produto:

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: 1. Leia `meus-produtos/.ativo`.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: 2. Use o slug encontrado como base: `meus-produtos/{ativo}/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: 3. Leia `meus-produtos/{ativo}/resumo-produto.md`, sem conferir antes se ele existe. É o contexto padrão de toda entrega, no lugar de `perfil.md`, `idconsumidor.md` e `pesquisa-mercado.md` inteiros. Se não for encontrado e o `perfil.md` tiver o Quadro preenchido, gere o resumo com o agente `gerador-resumo-produto` (modelo em `.claude/skills/resumo-produto/SKILL.md`) e leia o que ele gravar. Se não puder acionar o agente, gere o resumo você mesmo seguindo a seção 3 desse modelo e grave no mesmo caminho. Para um detalhe que o resumo não tem, leia só a seção indicada na tabela "Onde está o detalhe completo", no fim do resumo.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: 4. Leia `meus-produtos/{ativo}/tipo.md`, se existir.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: 5. Leia `meus-produtos/{ativo}/preco.md`, se existir.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: 6. Leia arquivos específicos da entrega atual, se existirem.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: Quem escreve, revisa ou gera a concepção (`produto-concepcao`, `gerar-furadeira`, `furadeira-visual`, `produto-zerar`, revisores e geradores) continua lendo os arquivos originais. Ao gravar `perfil.md`, `idconsumidor.md` ou `pesquisa-mercado.md`, apague o `resumo-produto.md` do produto (o hook `resumo-invalidar.js` faz isso sozinho quando está ativo); ele é gerado de novo na próxima entrega.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: Se `meus-produtos/.ativo` não existir ou estiver vazio:

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: - Para criação de produto, siga `produto-novo`.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: - Para uma entrega que depende de produto, diga que é preciso criar ou selecionar um produto primeiro.

head: AGENTS.md > Produto Ativo e Contexto
text: Se `perfil.md` não existir e o comando depender de Quadro, Furadeira, Decorados ou Urgências Ocultas, oriente ou execute `produto-concepcao`, conforme o pedido.

head: AGENTS.md > Fluxo Padrão de Todo Command
text: Use esta sequência quando o command não disser algo diferente:

head: AGENTS.md > Fluxo Padrão de Todo Command
