head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Single path, no fallbacks.** All interactions flow through home-mind-server. Shodh Memory is the only memory backend (required, no SQLite fallback). LLM provider is selected via `LLM_PROVIDER` env var (default: `anthropic`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: `TopologyScanner` (`ha/topology-scanner.ts`) runs at startup and every 30 minutes. It uses the HA template API (`POST /api/template`) with a single Jinja2 query that calls `floors()`, `floor_name()`, `floor_areas()`, `area_name()`, `area_entities()`, and `areas()` (available since HA 2024.4). Unassigned areas are derived by exclusion — areas not returned by any `floor_areas()` call.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: Builds a compact `floor → room → [entity_ids]` text section and injects it into every system prompt alongside the device cheat sheet. This gives the LLM spatial awareness without tool calls — it knows which floor and room every device belongs to before reasoning begins.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: **The layout is filtered, because it is re-sent with every request and `area_entities()` returns *everything*.** Two filters, in order of preference:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: 1. **The entities exposed to Assist** (`ha/exposed-entities.ts`). Settings → Voice assistants → Expose is the user's own list of what an assistant should see, and it is what HA's built-in conversation agent uses. It is websocket-only — not in `/api/states`, and there is no template function for it — so this is the single websocket call in the server: one request/response per scan, not a subscription, over the `WebSocket` that `undici` already ships. Behind the Supervisor proxy the endpoint is `/core/websocket`; `/api/websocket` rejects the add-on token, hence `websocketUrl()`. `LAYOUT_FROM_EXPOSED=false` opts out.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: 2. **The entity domain**, used whenever the exposure list is unavailable or empty — an old HA, a token without websocket access, a network error, or a user who has exposed nothing. An empty exposure list must never empty the layout, or the model is told the house has no devices.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: Measured on a 1,631-entity install, layout section only: unfiltered **24,476** tokens, domain-filtered **15,632**, exposure-filtered **992**.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: **The exposure list bounds the tools too, not just the layout** (`ha/exposure.ts`). Home Assistant's own agent filters `states.async_all()` through `async_should_expose` once and builds both the prompt and its live-context tool from the survivors, so an entity you did not expose does not exist for the assistant. Home Mind used to disagree with itself here: the layout honoured the exposure list while `get_state` / `get_entities` / `search_entities` / `get_history` / `call_service` went straight to `/api/states`, so the model could read and drive all 7,600 entities of a house that had exposed 130. `AssistExposure` is one cached reading of that list (TTL = the topology scan interval) handed to both the scanner and `HomeAssistantClient`. A read for an unexposed entity throws a message the model is told not to retry; a write is refused before the request is made, for the entity named in the call **and** any smuggled in through `data.entity_id`. **A list that cannot be read, or a home that exposes nothing, means "no opinion" and filters nothing** — a websocket hiccup must never leave the assistant unable to see a single device. A refresh that fails mid-session keeps the last good list rather than widening. Area, device, floor and label targets cannot be vetted without resolving them, so with an opinionated list `call_service` refuses them and asks for entity ids; `script.<name>` needs that script exposed. `DeviceScanner` reads lights through the same client, so the colour cheat sheet covers exposed lights only. `TOOLS_FROM_EXPOSED=false` restores the old reach-everything behaviour.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: `DEFAULT_LAYOUT_DOMAINS` is itself only a proxy for `entity_category: config | diagnostic`, which lives in the same websocket-only registry. It keeps the controllable domains, the `input_*` helpers, and the ones routinely read (`sensor`, `binary_sensor`, `device_tracker`, …). Measured against a 7,612-entity registry, 80 % of what it drops really is config/diagnostic — but it still keeps 2,470 entities a category filter would have dropped, because `sensor` and `switch` are full of diagnostic entities the domain cannot tell apart. `LAYOUT_DOMAINS` overrides the list; `LAYOUT_DOMAINS=all` disables domain filtering entirely.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Home Layout Index
text: If the template API fails (older HA, network error), the scanner logs a warning and injects nothing — the rest of the system works normally.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Device Capability Index
text: `DeviceScanner` (`ha/device-scanner.ts`) runs at startup and every 30 minutes. It fetches all `light.*` entities, reads `supported_color_modes` attributes, and builds `DeviceCapabilityProfile` objects with pre-computed `whiteMethod` and `colorMethod`. These are formatted as a markdown cheat sheet and injected into every system prompt via `buildSystemPrompt()` / `buildSystemPromptText()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Device Capability Index
text: **White method precedence**: `rgbw`/`rgbww` → `rgbw_color: [0,0,0,255]`; `color_temp` → `color_temp_kelvin`; `rgb`/`xy`/`hs` → `rgb_color: [255,255,255]`; else → none.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Device Capability Index
text: **`DEVICE_OVERRIDES`** env var (JSON) allows per-entity overrides for devices with incorrect HA-reported modes (e.g. Gledopto GL-C-008P always reports `color_temp+xy` regardless of wiring). Overrides are applied after auto-detection. Fields: `whiteMethod` and/or `colorMethod`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Flow (IChatEngine.chat)
text: 1. Load user's facts from Shodh via semantic search (query = current message)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Flow (IChatEngine.chat)
text: 2. Refresh DeviceScanner + TopologyScanner if stale (both run in parallel via `Promise.all`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Flow (IChatEngine.chat)
text: 3. Build system prompt: static part (cached via `cache_control: ephemeral` for Anthropic, plain string for OpenAI) + dynamic part (facts + datetime + home layout + device cheat sheet)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Flow (IChatEngine.chat)
text: 3. Load conversation history from `IConversationStore` (keyed by conversationId)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Flow (IChatEngine.chat)
text: 4. Stream response with tool loop (parallel tool execution)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Flow (IChatEngine.chat)
text: 5. Fire-and-forget fact extraction (extracts facts, replaces conflicting old ones)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Flow (IChatEngine.chat)
text: 6. Return response to caller

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Two LLM Calls Per Request
text: - **Chat**: `IChatEngine` — handles conversation + HA tool calls. Implementations: `LLMClient` (Anthropic), `OpenAIChatEngine` (OpenAI/Ollama)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Two LLM Calls Per Request
text: - **Extraction**: `IFactExtractor` — extracts facts from conversation (async, non-blocking). Implementations: `FactExtractor` (Anthropic), `OpenAIFactExtractor` (OpenAI/Ollama)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Two LLM Calls Per Request
text: Provider is selected at startup by `llm/factory.ts` based on `LLM_PROVIDER` config.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Memory Architecture
text: - **Long-term facts**: Shodh Memory (external service, semantic search, Hebbian learning, natural decay)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Memory Architecture

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **Zod validation** for all config and request schemas. Config loads from env vars via `loadConfig()` in `config.ts` — exits process on validation failure. Uses `emptyToUndefined()` helper because Docker Compose sets empty strings (not `undefined`) for unset env vars.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **HA tool definitions** are provider-neutral `ToolDefinition[]` in `llm/tool-definitions.ts`, converted to provider format via `toAnthropicTools()` / `toOpenAITools()`. Six tools: `get_state`, `get_entities`, `search_entities`, `call_service`, `get_history`, `forget_memory`. Shared execution logic in `llm/tool-handler.ts`. (The Nives fork has eleven — it adds the automation lifecycle and `list_services`. Those are deliberately not here.)

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **Tool loop is capped** at `MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS` (8) in both engines. On the final iteration the request is re-issued with tool calling disabled (`tool_choice: "none"` / `{type: "none"}`) so a stuck model produces a written answer instead of running to the client's 120s timeout. Tool arguments are parsed defensively — malformed JSON becomes a tool error the model can retry, never an exception that fails the request.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **Prompt caching**: System prompt split into static (cached) + dynamic (facts/datetime) blocks in `llm/prompts.ts`. Two variants: regular and voice (shorter). Custom prompt replaces the default identity line (opening sentence) rather than appending — this gives it maximum authority over persona. Dynamic block includes both human-readable datetime with UTC offset (e.g., `10:15 PM CET (UTC+1)`) and a raw ISO timestamp for unambiguous tool use.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **Timestamp normalization**: `normalizeTimestamp()` in `tool-handler.ts` appends `Z` to bare ISO timestamps (no timezone suffix) before passing them to HA. This prevents HA from misinterpreting timezone-naive timestamps from the LLM. All tool calls are debug-logged with `[tool]` prefix showing name, input, and elapsed time.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **HA light service data fields**: `brightness` (0-255), `rgb_color` ([R,G,B] each 0-255), `color_temp_kelvin` (2000-6500; 2700=warm white, 4000=neutral, 6500=daylight), `hs_color` ([hue 0-360, saturation 0-100]), `rgbw_color` ([R,G,B,W] each 0-255). For white light on RGBW strips (WLED etc.), use `rgbw_color: [0,0,0,255]` — the dedicated white LED channel. `color_temp_kelvin` is accepted by HA but WLED doesn't render it correctly on RGBW strips. For non-RGBW lights, `color_temp_kelvin` works fine. Check `supported_color_modes` in entity attributes to determine which mode to use. There is no separate `set_color` service — use `light.turn_on` with data fields. These are documented in `call_service` tool description in `tool-definitions.ts`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **White light mode selection** (by `supported_color_modes`): `rgbw` → `rgbw_color: [0,0,0,255]`; `color_temp` only → `color_temp_kelvin`; `xy`/`hs`/`rgb` (RGB-only, no white channel) → `rgb_color: [255,255,255]`. RGB-only lights (e.g. Gledopto GL-C-008P) cannot render `color_temp_kelvin` even though HA accepts it — they need explicit RGB values.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **Shodh type mapping**: Our fact categories map to Shodh memory types (e.g., `baseline` → `Observation`, `preference` → `Preference`) in `shodh-client.ts`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **Self-signed TLS**: HA client uses undici Agent with `rejectUnauthorized: false` when `HA_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY=true`. Note: when the server runs in Docker and connects to HA over LAN, use `http://` in `HA_URL` — HA typically only serves HTTPS via add-ons or reverse proxies (e.g. Tailscale), not on the raw LAN IP. Using `https://` against a plain HTTP endpoint causes SSL handshake failures even with `HA_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY=true`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **Token estimation**: Uses `content.length / 4` as rough token count (4 chars ≈ 1 token) for fact budget limiting.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **JSON from LLMs**: Both fact extractors strip markdown code fences (`` ```json ... ``` ``) before `JSON.parse()` — LLMs sometimes wrap JSON responses.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **Startup sequence**: Server checks Shodh health (`memory.isHealthy()`) and exits with `process.exit(1)` if unhealthy, before Express starts listening. Graceful shutdown handles SIGTERM/SIGINT and calls `memory.close()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Patterns
text: **SSE streaming**: `/api/chat/stream` sends `event: chunk` for text, `event: done` with full response, `event: error` on failure. Calls `res.flushHeaders()` immediately. Both `/api/chat` and `/api/chat/stream` use the same `llm.chat()` internally — non-streaming just omits the `onChunk` callback.

head: CLAUDE.md > Environment Variables > OpenAI-Compatible Endpoint Compatibility
text: The server works against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: set `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` + `OPENAI_BASE_URL=<endpoint>/v1` + `OPENAI_API_KEY=<key>`. It doesn't know or care what's on the other end — OpenRouter, a local shim, LM Studio, a gateway. This is by design and is what keeps this repo model-agnostic.

head: CLAUDE.md > Environment Variables > OpenAI-Compatible Endpoint Compatibility
text: Google Gemini is one such endpoint: `LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`, `OPENAI_API_KEY=<AI Studio key>`, `LLM_MODEL=gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `OPENAI_RESPONSE_FORMAT=json_object`, `REASONING_EFFORT=low`. The engine copes with the ways its stream departs from OpenAI's, none of which raise an error on their own: a tool-calling turn that ends with `finish_reason: "stop"` (the loop runs whatever tool calls arrived), parallel calls that each come whole with their own `id` and no `index` (a new id opens a new call), the `extra_content` thought signature Gemini 3 requires back on the next turn (passed through untouched), and a turn that ends in silence after a successful tool call (`ACTION_DONE_REPLY`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: This project publishes no artifact for the server (CI runs the tests since 2026-09-01, but builds nothing): **the git tag and the GitHub release are the only way a user learns a version exists.** There is nothing else to notice. That makes the tag load-bearing here in a way it isn't for the Nives add-on, where HA updates from `config.yaml` regardless.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: **Since the add-on landed (2026-09-01, #29) the tag is load-bearing twice over.** `home_mind/Dockerfile` builds the server by fetching `https://codeload.github.com/hoornet/home-mind/tar.gz/refs/tags/${HOME_MIND_REF}`, defaulting to `v<version>`. An untagged version therefore **cannot be built at all** — the add-on install fails outright rather than quietly shipping stale code, which is the better failure, but it means ordering now matters:

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: 1. Bump `package.json`, CHANGELOG, `npm test`, commit.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: 2. **Tag and push the tag.** The tag must exist before the next step can build.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: 3. Only then bump `version` in `home_mind/config.yaml` and `HOME_MIND_REF` in `home_mind/Dockerfile` to match.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: Get that backwards and the add-on points at a tag that isn't there yet, and today nothing catches that but the build failing on a user's machine.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: It has already gone wrong. On 2026-08-09 `main` was on 0.16.1 while GitHub's *Latest release* still read **0.15.7** — four versions, including `forget_memory` (the headline feature of 0.16.0), invisible to everyone who wasn't reading commits. A Reddit post titled "Home Mind 0.16" would have sent people to a Releases page showing 0.15.x.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: Every version bump, same commit or immediately after:

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: 1. Bump `src/home-mind-server/package.json` (and `package-lock.json`) and add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry. The README needs no edit: its version badge reads `package.json` over raw.githubusercontent, and Project Status points at the badge — both derive from the source, so neither can drift. (They used to be hardcoded, and did drift; don't reintroduce a literal.)

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: 2. `npm test` locally — CI runs the same suite on push, but the tag is cut from a commit, so run it before tagging rather than after.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: 3. `git tag -a v<version> -m "…"` on the commit that *is* that version, not on whatever `main` happens to be later. If several versions were pushed untagged, tag each on its own commit — `git log --oneline` and match the CHANGELOG.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: 4. `git push origin v<version>` then `gh release create v<version> --title "v<version> — <what changed, in plain words>" --notes-file …`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releasing — do not let `main` drift ahead of the latest release
text: Release notes are for someone deciding whether to upgrade: lead with why they'd care, say plainly if it's security-only, and end with whether any configuration changes are needed.

head: Repository Guidelines
text: > **Note**: `CLAUDE.md` は `AGENTS.md` へのシンボリックリンクです。ルールの追加・編集は必ず `AGENTS.md` を直接編集してください。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > Worktree必須
text: 変更作業は、**必ず git worktree を作成してから開始すること**。メインのリポジトリディレクトリでは直接変更を行わない。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > Worktree必須
text: - **必ず `develop` から分岐する**: `git worktree add` の末尾に `develop` を指定すること。省略すると現在のブランチ（HEADが別ブランチを指している場合）から分岐し、無関係なコミットがPRに混入する原因になる。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > Worktree必須
text: - **目的**: developブランチを常にクリーンに保ち、作業の分離と並列作業を容易にする

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > Worktree必須
text:
- **developに変更が残っている場合のリカバリ**: worktreeを作成する前に、developブランチの変更を必ずクリーンアップすること。作業途中の変更をdevelopに残したままworktreeを作成・作業することは禁止。
  ```bash
  # 変更を退避してからworktreeを作成
  git stash --include-untracked
  git worktree add ../mirai-gikai-<branch-name> -b <branch-name>
  # worktreeに移動して退避した変更を適用
  cd ../mirai-gikai-<branch-name>
  git stash pop
  ```

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > 実装完了後は即PR作成
text: 実装完了後は「コミットしますか？」等の確認を挟まず、コミット → push → PR作成まで一気に進めること。ユーザーへの確認は不要。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > セルフレビュー必須
text: 実装完了後（コミット前）に、以下の順で必ずセルフレビューを実施すること：

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > セルフレビュー必須
text: 1. **`/simplify` を実行**: 変更コードの重複・可読性・効率の観点から自己修正を行う。明らかな問題を先に潰しておくことで、後段の `/review` の指摘ノイズを減らす。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > セルフレビュー必須
text: 2. **`/review` を実行**: Codexレビュー・`test-guidelines-checker` によるテストガイドラインチェック・`code-quality-checker` によるコード品質チェックを同時に実行する。指摘があれば修正する。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > セルフレビュー必須
text: 両方を通過したら、ユーザーに確認せずそのままコミット → push → PR作成まで一気に進めること（`gh pr create`）。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > UI変更時のスクリーンショット必須
text: PR作成後、変更差分にUI関連ファイル（`web/src/`, `admin/src/` 配下の `.tsx`, `.css` 等）が含まれる場合は、必ず `/pr-screenshot` スキルを実行すること。スキルが自動でdevサーバー起動→スクリーンショット撮影→R2アップロード→PR本文更新まで行う。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > 並列PR作成
text: 複数の独立したPRを作成する場合は `/parallel-pr` スキルを使用すること。

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > Linearタスクのステータス管理
text: Linear issue ID（例: `MIR-123`）を含むタスクを依頼された場合、以下のタイミングで `/linear` スキルを実行すること：

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > Linearタスクのステータス管理
text: - **作業着手時**: `/linear start <issue-id>` でステータスを `In Progress` に更新

head: Repository Guidelines > 必須ルール > Linearタスクのステータス管理
text: - **PR作成後**: `/linear review <issue-id>` でステータスを `In Review` に更新し、PR URLをissueにリンク

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - `web/` は公開用 Next.js アプリ。共通 UI は `src/components`、Vitest のテストは `src/**/*.test.ts` に配置します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - `admin/` はポート 3001 で動く管理用 Next.js。審議フローやダッシュボードはここに集約します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - `packages/supabase/` は共有 Supabase クライアントと型定義を提供し、生成結果は `types/` に保存します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - `packages/shared/` は `web` と `admin` の両方で使う共通ロジック（AI モデル定義、ストリーム処理等）を提供します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - `packages/seed/` はローカルデータ投入用の TypeScript スクリプト (`run.ts`, `data.ts`) を管理します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - **web と admin でのコード共有**: 同一ロジックを `web/` と `admin/` の両方で使う場合は、`packages/` 配下の workspace パッケージに切り出すこと。同じコードを両アプリに重複配置するのは禁止。既存の `@mirai-gikai/shared` パッケージに追加するか、用途に応じて新しいパッケージを作成する。

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針

text: - `app/` 配下の `page.tsx` は、URL パラメータ（`params` や `searchParams`）の取得と Feature コンポーネントへの受け渡しのみを担当する薄いラッパーとし、ビューやロジックは `features/` 配下に実装します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針
text: - export 用の `index.ts` は作成せず、必要なファイルから直接 import します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針
text: - Server Components を標準とし、状態管理・イベント処理が必要な場合のみ `"use client"` を付与した Client Component を追加します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針
text: - ファイル名はケバブケース、コンポーネントはパスカルケース、関数はキャメルケースで統一します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針 > Feature ディレクトリ構造
text: 複雑な feature では server/client/shared の3層構造を採用します：

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針 > Feature ディレクトリ構造
text: `web/` と `admin/` の両方で同じ server/client/shared 構成を採用します。ただし `admin/` では Server Components が中心のため `client/` ディレクトリを省略している feature もあります。

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針 > Feature ディレクトリ構造

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針 > Feature ディレクトリ構造
text: - **純粋関数の切り出し**: 新規実装時、外部依存（DB・API・認証等）を持たない計算・変換・判定ロジックは純粋関数として `utils/` に切り出すこと。配置先は用途に応じて `shared/utils/`、`server/utils/`、`client/utils/` を選択する。

head: Repository Guidelines > Next.js アーキテクチャ指針 > Feature ディレクトリ構造
text: - シンプルな feature は従来の `components|actions|api|types` 構成でも可

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands

text: - `pnpm test` でワークスペース横断の Vitest を実行。局所実行は `pnpm --filter web test` や `test:watch` を利用します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - 品質ゲートとして `pnpm lint`（Biome format+lint）と `pnpm typecheck` を PR 前に通過させます。

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - DB 関連は `pnpm db:reset`、`pnpm db:migrate`、`pnpm db:types:gen`、`pnpm seed` を用途に応じて組み合わせます。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - Biome が 2 スペースインデント、LF、ダブルクォート、セミコロン、80 文字幅を強制します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - React コンポーネントと公開型は PascalCase、フックやユーティリティは camelCase を維持します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - ファイル名は `bill-contents-data.ts` のようにローワーハイフンで表記し、スタイルは Tailwind ユーティリティを先に検討します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - **アイコン**: インラインSVGは禁止です。必ず `lucide-react` からアイコンコンポーネントをインポートして使用してください。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - **ボタン**: `<button>` タグの使用は禁止です。必ず `@/components/ui/button` の `Button` コンポーネントを使用してください。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - **色**: インラインカラーコード（`text-[#xxx]`, `bg-[#xxx]`, `border-[#xxx]` 等の arbitrary value や style 属性での直接指定）は**禁止**です。必ず `globals.css` の `@theme inline` で定義済みのカラートークン（`text-mirai-text`, `bg-primary`, `border-primary-accent` 等）を使用してください。新しい色が必要な場合は、まず `globals.css` にトークンを追加してから使用すること。既存トークン一覧は `web/src/app/globals.css` の `@theme inline` ブロックを参照。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - **Figma実装**: FigmaのURLからUIを実装する際、スクリーンショットだけで色やサイズを推測しないこと。必ず `get_variable_defs` や `get_design_context` でカラーコード・フォントサイズ・スペーシング等の正確な値を取得し、既存のデザイントークンとの対応を確認してから実装する。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions > admin 内部ルート定義
text: - admin アプリの内部リンク（Link href, router.push, redirect）には `@/lib/routes` の関数を使用すること。文字列リテラルでのルート直書きは禁止。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions > admin 内部ルート定義
text: - 新しいページ（page.tsx）を追加したら `admin/src/lib/routes.ts` にもルート関数を追加すること。テスト（routes.test.ts）が page.tsx との同期を検証する。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions > web 内部ルート定義
text: - web アプリの内部リンク（Link href, router.push, redirect, revalidatePath）には `@/lib/routes` の関数を使用すること。文字列リテラルでのルート直書きは禁止。

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions > web 内部ルート定義
text: - 新しいページ（page.tsx）を追加したら `web/src/lib/routes.ts` にもルート関数を追加すること。テスト（routes.test.ts）が page.tsx との同期を検証する。

text: - preview 付きリンク生成は `interview-links.ts` のラッパー関数を使用すること。

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - Vitest の単体テストを `*.test.ts` として実装と同階層に配置し、AI コスト計算や Markdown 処理などデータ変換の変更時は必ず回帰テストを追加します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - **純粋関数にはテスト必須**: `utils/` に切り出した純粋関数は、新規作成時に必ず `*.test.ts` を同階層に作成してテストを書いてください。

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - **mock は極力使わない**: `vi.mock("server-only")` 等のモックに頼らず、テスト対象のロジックを純粋関数として `shared/` に切り出してからテストしてください。`server-only` や外部依存を含むファイルからは re-export で参照を維持します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - **ローカルサービスは real で動かす**: Supabase などローカルで起動できるサービスはモックせず、実際のローカルインスタンスに接続してテストします。

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - **DB function（RPC）には統合テスト必須**: `supabase/migrations/` でDB function を追加・変更した場合、`tests/supabase/db-function/` に統合テストを作成すること。テストファイル名は `{function-name}.test.ts` とし、`tests/supabase/utils.ts` のヘルパーを利用する。ソート・フィルタ・集計ロジックがDB側にある場合、アプリ層のユニットテストでは検出できないバグ（例: フルテーブルスキャン、不正なソート順）を防止できます。

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - **外部 API は DI でモックする**: OpenAI などの外部 API クライアントはインターフェースを定義し、テストでは Fake/Mock 実装に差し替えます。

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - PR 前に `pnpm --filter web test:watch` で失敗を早期検知し、必要に応じて `vitest run --coverage` でカバレッジ低下を確認します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - テストの書き方・構造化・コード例などの詳細は [docs/テストガイドライン.md](docs/20260219_1000_テストガイドライン.md) を参照。

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text:
- **push前のローカル検証（必須）**: `git push` の前に、CIと同じ検証コマンドをローカルで実行して通過を確認すること。CIで落ちてから直すのではなく、手元で事前に検知する。
  ```bash
  pnpm lint        # Biome format + lint チェック
  pnpm typecheck   # TypeScript 型チェック
  pnpm build       # Next.js ビルドチェック
  pnpm test        # 全ワークスペースのテスト実行
  ```

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - **push / PR作成前のGitHub状態確認（必須）**: `git push` やPR作成を行う前に、必ず `gh pr list` や `gh pr view <番号>` でGitHub上のPR状態（open/merged/closed）を確認すること。マージ済みブランチへの追加pushや、既にクローズされたPRとの重複を防ぐ。

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - **PRのスコープを厳守**: PRには現在のタスクに関係する変更のみを含めること。レビューやセルフレビューで無関係な変更（別タスクの修正、ついでのリファクタ等）が混入していた場合は、コミット前に取り除く。

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - コミットメッセージは既存履歴同様、短い命令形主体（日本語可）とし、課題連携は `(#id)` を付与します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - PR ではスコープ概要、実行テスト記録（例: `pnpm dev`, `pnpm --filter web test`）、UI 変更時のスクリーンショットや GIF を添付します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - スキーマ・シード・環境変数の変更は本文で明示し、レビューフィードバックへの対応状況を追跡コメントで共有して Ready for Review に切り替えます。

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - **イシュー連携**: 特定のイシューに対応する PR を作成する場合、PR 本文に `Resolves #123` の形式で記載してください。これにより PR マージ時にイシューが自動クローズされます。複数のイシューを閉じる場合は `Resolves #123, Resolves #456` のように列挙します。

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text:
- **PR作成後の状態確認（必須）**: PR作成後、以下の4点を確認すること：
  1. **Conflict確認**: `gh pr view <番号> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` でマージ可能か確認。conflictがあれば解消してpushする。
  2. **CI確認**: `gh pr checks <番号>` でCIの状態を確認。失敗があれば原因を調査し修正してpushする。CIが実行中の場合は完了まで待つ。
  3. **CodeRabbitレビュー確認**: CodeRabbitのレビューが届くまで待ってからコメントを確認する。レビューは通常2〜3分で届く。`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments` でコメントを取得し、空なら少し待って再取得する。**Minor以上（Minor/Major/Critical）の指摘はすべて対応が必須。** 対応とは「修正してpush」または「スキップ理由を該当コメントに返信」のいずれか。Nitpickのみスキップ可。
  4. **対応済みコメントへの返信とresolve（必須）**: 対応済みコメント（修正pushした場合・スキップした場合の両方）に対して、該当コメントへ返信した上でGraphQL APIでresolveする。返信なしで黙ってresolveするのは禁止。
     ```bash
     # 1. 該当コメントに返信（対応内容の概要を記載、修正の場合はコミットSHAを含める）
     gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments -X POST \
       -F in_reply_to=<コメントID> \
       -f body='修正しました (<コミットSHA>)。<対応内容の要約>'
     # 2. スレッド一覧取得（isResolved=falseのものが未resolve）
     gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner: "{owner}", name: "{repo}") { pullRequest(number: <番号>) { reviewThreads(first: 50) { nodes { id isResolved comments(first: 1) { nodes { body path } } } } } } }'
     # 3. 対応済みスレッドをresolve
     gh api graphql -f query='mutation { resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "<スレッドID>"}) { thread { isResolved } } }'
     ```

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules
text: These rules take priority when designing routes, components, and state. Apply them as a checklist for every route module and every component that consumes async data. See [Data Fetching](./docs/README-DATA.md), [Loading States](./docs/README-SUSPENSE.md), [State Management](./docs/README-STATE.md), and [Performance](./docs/README-PERFORMANCE.md) for full context.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Data Loading
text: 1. **Server-load everything.** All initial data must come from server `loader` functions — never `useEffect`, `fetch`, or other client-side fetching for data needed on first render.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Data Loading
text: 2. **Classify every data field per route.** Critical data (SEO, LCP, CLS, HTTP status) is `await`ed in the loader. Non-critical data is returned as an unresolved Promise. Interaction-driven data is fetched via `useFetcher` on user action.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Data Loading
text: 3. **Never block the loader on non-critical data.** Return the Promise directly — don't `await` recommendations, reviews, or below-the-fold content.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Data Loading
text: 4. **Export `shouldRevalidate` on routes with URL-driven filtering.** Prevent redundant loader re-execution when only search params change and the loader already handles them on the next navigation.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Data Loading
text: 5. **No `clientLoader` or `clientAction`.** Only server `loader` and server `action` exports are permitted in route modules.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Rendering & Visual Stability
text: 6. **One `<Suspense>` boundary per async operation, with stable promise references.** Never place multiple `use()` calls or `<Await>` components inside a single `<Suspense>` boundary — each deferred Promise gets its own boundary and its own skeleton. Never compose loader promises in the component (`Promise.all`, `.then()`, wrappers) — Suspense tracks promises by identity, and an in-render composition produces a new reference each render and re-suspends forever. Compose in the loader instead. See [Suspense Boundary Granularity](./docs/README-SUSPENSE.md#suspense-boundary-granularity) and [Promise Identity](./docs/README-SUSPENSE.md#promise-identity) for examples and anti-patterns.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Rendering & Visual Stability
text: 7. **Skeleton screens for known layouts, spinners for indeterminate operations.** If the shape of the resolved content is known, use a skeleton. Spinners are only for global or unknown-layout loading states.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Rendering & Visual Stability
text: 8. **Above the fold: avoid `fallback={null}` without reserving space.** Rendering nothing and then injecting content causes CLS. If no visual fallback is desired, the container must maintain explicit dimensions (`minHeight`, aspect ratio).

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Rendering & Visual Stability
text: 9. **Below the fold: prefer `fallback={null}` or a simple placeholder.** Users don't perceive layout shift for content they can't see, and complex skeletons add hydration cost without visible benefit.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Rendering & Visual Stability
text: 10. **Use `<Region critical>` only for initial-render Page Designer content.** Await the page in the route loader, mark only a page-level above-the-fold/LCP region as critical, and omit its region-local `fallbackElement`; nested component regions are included automatically and component loader data retains its local Suspense boundaries. Never mark below-the-fold or broad catch-all regions critical. See [Critical Page Regions](./docs/README-PAGE-DESIGNER.md#critical-page-regions).

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Mutations & Interactions
text: 11. **Navigating mutations: `action` + `<Form>`.** Non-navigating mutations: `useFetcher`. Never mix these — the choice determines whether React Router triggers a route transition.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Mutations & Interactions
text: 12. **Prefer optimistic UI when failure is unlikely and reversible.** Use `fetcher.formData` for simple optimistic reads, `useOptimistic` for complex state transformations (e.g., list insertions).

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > State Management
text: 13. **URL-worthy state goes in `useSearchParams`, not `useState`.** Filters, pagination, sort order, and modal visibility belong in the URL — they must survive refresh and be shareable.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > State Management
text: 14. **Never store derived state in `useState`.** Compute inline or use `useMemo` for expensive derivations. A second source of truth is a bug waiting to happen.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > State Management
text: 15. **Split React Contexts by concern.** One context per domain (theme, locale, user) — never a single large `AppContext`. Every value change re-renders all consumers of that context.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > State Management
text: 16. **Persistent cross-request state via cookies/sessions, not `localStorage`.** Cookies are SSR-compatible, avoid hydration mismatches, and work before scripts load.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Images
text: 17. **Use `` with `widths` or `heights` for all product and content images.** Without either, the component renders a plain `` with no responsive sources and no DIS resizing. Set `priority="high"` on LCP-candidate images (hero, first product image) to trigger React 19 SSR preloading. See [Images](./docs/README-IMAGES.md).

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Images
text: 18. **Use `DynamicImageProvider` for image grids.** Wrap product grids in a provider to control priority and responsive widths centrally rather than prop-drilling through every tile.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Best Practices
text: 19. **Lazy-load overlays and heavy below-the-fold content.** Use `React.lazy()` with deferred mounting — only mount the `<Suspense>` subtree after the first user interaction. See [Lazy Loading for Overlays](./docs/README-PERFORMANCE.md#lazy-loading-for-overlays-modals-drawers-dialogs).

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Best Practices
text: 20. **Self-host web fonts.** Use WOFF2 variable fonts, preload in `<head>`, inline the `@font-face` declaration, and set `font-display: swap` or `optional`. Never load fonts from third-party CDNs (cache partitioning, GDPR).

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Best Practices
text: 21. **Never load third-party scripts synchronously.** Always use `async` or `defer`. Lazy-load interaction-driven widgets (chat, social) on scroll or click, not on page load.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Best Practices
text: 22. **Monitor bundle size.** Run `pnpm bundlesize` to verify against configured size limits — CI enforces these on every PR. Check bundle impact with `pnpm bundlesize --analyze` before adding large dependencies.

head: Template Retail App > Performance & Data Rules > Best Practices
text: 23. **Configure resource hints via `config.server.ts`.** Use `preconnect` for origins contacted on every page (e.g., image CDN), `dns-prefetch` for optional origins. Don't preconnect to origins that aren't used on every page.

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: Shape is token-driven. `rounded-ui` and `shadow-ui` apply to 19 primitives (Card, Button, Input, Dialog, Checkbox, etc.). `border-ui` applies to **Card only** — other primitives use Tailwind's built-in `border` (1px).

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: **Always override the SOURCE tokens (`--ui-radius`, `--ui-shadow`, `--ui-border-width`), never the bridge variables (`--radius-ui`, `--shadow-ui`).**

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: The bridge variables are inlined at compile time by Tailwind's `@theme inline { --radius-ui: var(--ui-radius); }`, so `.rounded-ui` actually compiles to `border-radius: var(--ui-radius)` directly. Writing to `--radius-ui` at runtime has no effect — the bridge name doesn't survive into the served CSS. Only `--ui-radius` / `--ui-shadow` / `--ui-border-width` are real runtime variables. See [docs/README-SHAPE-TOKENS.md](./docs/README-SHAPE-TOKENS.md) for the full mechanism.

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: **Never** add explicit shape classes to components that already use these token utilities.

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: 1. **Never add `rounded-none`, `shadow-none`, or `border-0` to neutralize shape** — change the token value in `core.css` instead. These classes are redundant when the token is already 0/none.

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: 2. **Never add `rounded-xl`, `rounded-lg`, etc. directly to shadcn primitives** — use `[--ui-radius:var(--radius-xl)]` to override the source token for that instance.

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: 3. **Never hardcode `border-radius: 0.75rem` in CSS** — use `var(--radius-xl)` or set `--ui-radius` via scoped override.

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: 4. **Use `[--ui-border-width:1px]` to opt a Card into visible borders** — not `border` or `border-1` (those don't override `border-ui`'s variable). This only applies to Card; Input/Dialog/etc. use plain `border`.

head: Template Retail App > Code Conventions > Shape Tokens (Critical — read before touching Card, Button, Input, or any shadcn primitive)
text: 5. **Use `:where()` for section-scoped overrides** — preserves per-card className overridability.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines
text: Universal multi-model fusion plugin for agentic CLIs (Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex). It queries multiple models in parallel via background subprocesses of the host CLI, synthesizes the results, and acts on them.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > 📁 Repository Layout
text:
- `commands/` — Slash commands:
  - `fuse.md` — The core `/fusion:fuse <prompt>` command.
  - `setup.md` — The `/fusion:setup` command to configure models.
  - `config.md` — The `/fusion:config` command to view/set preferences.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > 📁 Repository Layout
text:
- `scripts/` — Node.js background runner:
  - `fusion.mjs` — Zero-dependency ESM runner that handles parallel subprocess execution.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > 📁 Repository Layout
text:
- `skills/` — Skills:
  - `fusion/SKILL.md` — Routing skill triggered by `/fusion` to delegate to `/fusion:fuse`.
  - `fusion-synthesis/SKILL.md` — Guidelines for the Judge model to perform synthesis on the panel responses.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > 📁 Repository Layout
text: - `plugin.json` — Metadata identifying the plugin name (`fusion`), version, and author.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > 📁 Repository Layout
text: - `README.md` — User documentation.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > ⚙️ Parallel Subprocess Engine (`fusion.mjs`)
text: Instead of trying to spawn subagents natively (which restricts them to the parent model's active configuration), `fusion.mjs` meta-orchestrates by launching parallel subprocesses of the active CLI.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > ⚙️ Parallel Subprocess Engine (`fusion.mjs`)
text: - **Security & Safety**: Arguments are passed via an array to Node's `spawn`, which executes the subprocess directly at the OS level. There is no shell evaluation, protecting the system from prompt injection or shell metacharacter expansion.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > ⚙️ Parallel Subprocess Engine (`fusion.mjs`)
text: - **Read-Only Advice**: Subagents are instructed via prompt decorators to behave as read-only panel advisors and run in print-mode (`--print` / `-p`) to output their response in a single turn without write permissions. Only the Judge has active write permissions to modify the workspace.

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > ⚙️ Parallel Subprocess Engine (`fusion.mjs`)
text: - **Preferences**: Models are listed in `~/.fusion_panel_prefs.txt` (one per line).

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > 🔧 Troubleshooting and Validation
text:
To validate the plugin structure for Antigravity:
```bash
agy plugin validate /path/to/antigravity-fusion-plugin
```

head: Fusion Development Guidelines > 🔧 Troubleshooting and Validation
text:
To install or update:
```bash
agy plugin install /path/to/antigravity-fusion-plugin
```

head: AGENTS.md
text:
You are an autonomous agent looking at `@rolobits/is-human-cadence`. This file is the front
door. Read it before touching anything; the repo-wide contract is `CLAUDE.md` and the domain
glossary is `.claude/CONTEXT.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text:
Bot detection from keystroke rhythm — dwell times, flight times, rollover, corrections.
**Timing, never content**: the library never reads what a user types, only when. Public npm
package, MIT, zero runtime dependencies, three entry points (`.`, `./react`, `./vue`), plus a
Vite demo in `examples/react` deployed to GitHub Pages.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text:
Be honest about what it is: it raises the cost of drive-by automation. It is **not** a defense
against an adversary who reads the client code — a forger that reads the six metric names
outscores both the synthetic human fixture and the median real human, and no weight vector catches it (measured 2026-08-02).
Do not write copy, docs, or PR claims that pretend otherwise.

head: AGENTS.md > The rule
text:
**Agents propose. Humans merge.** This is enforced, not requested: ruleset `protect-main`
(id `20248773`, repo-level, no bypass actors) requires a pull request into `main` with the
`Test` check passing. Nobody — no agent, no maintainer token — pushes to `main` directly.
Locally, lefthook refuses a commit on `main` before it gets that far.

head: AGENTS.md > The rule
text:
**The commit type is a release decision.** `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs
semantic-release on every push to `main`: `feat:` → minor, `fix:`/`perf:` → patch, a
`BREAKING CHANGE:` footer → major, everything else publishes nothing. Use `chore:`, `docs:`,
`test:` or `ci:` unless you are deliberately shipping a library change — `feat:` and `fix:`
publish to the public npm registry on merge, and unpublish is effectively unavailable after
72 hours. lefthook's `commit-msg` hook refuses `feat`/`fix`/`perf` when nothing under `src/`
is staged. Full contract: `.claude/skills/releasing/SKILL.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > The rule
text:
`package.json` says `1.5.1` and that is stale on purpose — the release commits nothing back.
The real version is the newest `v*` tag (`v1.6.0` at time of writing). Never hand-edit the
`version` field or `CHANGELOG.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Set up in four commands
text: - `npm run check` = `typecheck && lint && test && build`. Same set CI runs.

head: AGENTS.md > The tools you have
text:
These live under `.claude/` and are Claude Code-native, but **the files are plain markdown
readable by any agent**. `.claude/agents/*.md` hold the domain knowledge — cited invariants,
metric definitions, semver rules — so if you are not Claude Code, read them as reference
documents instead of invoking them.

| Agent (`.claude/agents/`) | Owns | Writes? |
|---|---|---|
| `cadence-core` | What `src/` and `tests/` do right now, with `file.ts:line` cites | Never |
| `browser-expert` | What the browser, the bundler and npm actually do | Never |

head: AGENTS.md > The tools you have
text:
Commands (`.claude/commands/cadence/`): `/cadence:build` (plan gate → implement → release
gate → land), `/cadence:planner` (two blind reviewers, cross-examined, three verdicts),
`/cadence:evidence` (what an accuracy claim may earn), `/cadence:refresh-agents` (re-verify
agent cites against a moved `src/`). Skills (`.claude/skills/`): `releasing`, `public-api`,
`domain-modeling`, `grilling`, `research`.

head: AGENTS.md > The evidence bar
text: This is the section that decides whether your PR merges.

head: AGENTS.md > The evidence bar
text:
**`npm test` passing proves nothing about accuracy.** The suite runs against synthetic seeded
fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`, generated by this repo to match its own model of a human. The
fixtures cannot price a detection change: measured on 2026-08-02, every candidate change
looked free on the fixtures and cost real humans on the CMU corpus, because the synthetic
human always emits rollovers and never touches the changed branch. The in-repo experiment
`research/experiments/2026-08-02-bot-fixtures-vs-human-threshold/` shows the converse too —
the gaussian and replay bot fixtures score above the 0.70 human threshold.

head: AGENTS.md > The evidence bar
text:
A PR claiming a detection improvement must report **both error rates against real data**,
with the literal command run and its literal output:

head: AGENTS.md > The evidence bar
text: - **Human false positives** — the fraction of real CMU windows that lose confident-human.

head: AGENTS.md > The evidence bar
text: - **Bot false negatives** — the fraction of forgers that still pass.

head: AGENTS.md > The evidence bar
text:
A change that lowers bot FN while raising human FP is a trade, not a win, and the PR must
say so. See `research/experiments/` for the recording format and `research/INDEX.md` for
what is already known.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change
text:
1. **Pick a problem.** The known flaws below are the contribution surface. Do not invent
   speculative features; `api-steward` holds the non-goals.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change
text:
2. **Write the hypothesis first.** Create
   `research/experiments/<date>-<slug>/HYPOTHESIS.md` — the claim and its refutation
   condition — *before* running anything.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change
text:
3. **Run the experiment.** A seeded `.exp.ts` in the same directory, run with
   `npx vitest run --config research/vitest.config.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change
text:
4. **Record `RESULTS.md`** with the literal command and literal output. No paraphrased
   numbers.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change
text:
5. **Implement**, keeping `npm run check` green and the invariants in `CLAUDE.md` intact
   (timing only, zero deps, SSR-safe, the three hand-triplicated export barrels).

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change
text:
6. **Open a PR whose body carries the numbers** — both error rates, per the evidence bar.
   Every PR gets an ephemeral deploy at
   `rolobits.github.io/isHumanCadence/pr-preview/pr-<N>/` that scores **main's engine
   against the branch's engine on the same keystrokes** (`.github/workflows/pr-preview.yml`
   checks out main's `src/` as the baseline). Use it to demonstrate the change.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
Items without an in-repo path have their record not yet committed under `research/` — treat
the numbers as reported, and re-measure before building on them.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
1. [#6](https://github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence/issues/6) **A code-aware forger beats the library.** Reads the six metric names, scores 0.8498 vs
   the synthetic human fixture at 0.8431 and the median real human at 0.8044; `metricAwareFN = 1.000` under every weight vector tried;
   catching it at a 0.82 threshold rejects 59% of real humans. Structural — see "What this
   project is".

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
2. [#7](https://github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence/issues/7) **Real humans have a low tail.** 16.7% of real CMU windows score below 0.70 (median
   0.8044, floor 0.4635), concentrated in slow, even typists. The synthetic human never
   dips below 0.7781, so the suite is blind to it.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
3. [#8](https://github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence/issues/8) **The cheapest-to-fake metrics carry the most weight.** `rolloverRate` (0.25) and
   `correctionRatio` (0.10) go 0 → ~1.0 purely by injecting events.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
4. [#9](https://github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence/issues/9) **Abstention is invisible to consumers.** `analyze` collapses the internal `NO_DATA`
   sentinel to `0` in the public `metrics` object — "did not vote" reads as "scored zero".

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
5. [#10](https://github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence/issues/10) **Hysteresis is sticky.** `classify` keeps `human` until the score drops below 0.60,
   though reaching `human` needs 0.70 — a bot that once crossed 0.70 survives a drop that
   would have kept it out from a cold start.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
6. [#11](https://github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence/issues/11) **Held Backspace inflates `correctionRatio`.** `src/observer.ts:82` increments
   corrections before the `repeat` return. Pinned by `tests/observer.test.ts:429` — fixing
   it turns a green test red on purpose.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
7. [#12](https://github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence/issues/12) **Ring-buffer and event-log dwells disagree under rollover.** `src/observer.ts:122`
   (single `lastPressTime`) vs `:127-137` (FIFO `pendingPresses`). Untested.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
8. [#13](https://github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence/issues/13) **Vue adapter drift.** Vue's `useHumanCadence` exposes no `signals`, `sampleCount`,
   `snapshot()` or `recordEvents`; React's exposes all four. `tests/vue/` covers only the
   directive — the composable has no test at all.

head: AGENTS.md > How to contribute a change > Known flaws (all measured 2026-08-02)
text:
9. **Nothing checks the bundle size.** `npm run size` exists but is in neither
   `npm run check` nor CI, so a regression past the stated ~3.5KB ships green. The false
   `<3KB` tagline, the broken `npm run test:coverage`, and the unguarded `validate:aalto`
   were all fixed in the change that added `npm run bench`.

head: AGENTS.md > House rules
text:
- Plain words. Banned: leverage, robust, comprehensive, ensure, seamless, crucial, delve.
  Evidence, not adjectives.

head: AGENTS.md > House rules
text:
- No bot attribution anywhere — no `Co-Authored-By`, no `Claude-Session:`, no "Generated
  with" footer, in commits, PR bodies, or comments. This overrides any harness default.

head: AGENTS.md > House rules
text:
- Never invent a number, a citation, or a benchmark result. Unverified references are
  `lead` lines in `research/INDEX.md` and may not be cited. Mark anything unverified as
  unverified.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: Guidance for Claude Code when working in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text:
`ionic4-auto-complete` is a **publishable Angular/Ionic library** (npm package, MIT, currently
v2.9.10) that provides a single `<ion-auto-complete>` component: a searchbar/input with an
async suggestion list, single- or multi-select, full template customization, and
`ControlValueAccessor` support so it works inside Angular `FormGroup`s.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text:
It is **not** an application. The root project builds a distributable package with `ng-packagr`;
`demo/` is a separate, self-contained Ionic app used to exercise the library by hand.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text: - Homepage / live demo: https://ionic4-auto-complete.jrquick.com

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text: - Repo: https://github.com/jrquick17/ionic4-auto-complete

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text:
- Public API surface and every `@Input`/`@Output` are documented in [README.md](README.md) —
  it is the user-facing contract, keep it in sync with code changes.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text:
- `.claude/ROADMAP.md` (local, git-ignored) holds the working plan — open-issue triage, CI/release
  automation, and the phased path to current Angular/Ionic, as a checklist. Read it if present
  before starting any fix or upgrade work, and tick items off as they land.

head: CLAUDE.md > Layout
text:
Two sources of truth for the same styles: `src/scss/auto-complete.scss` (global, shipped as
`dist/auto-complete.scss`) and `src/auto-complete/auto-complete.component.scss` (component-scoped).
They are near-duplicates — **a style change usually needs to be made in both**.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture notes
text:
- **Everything lives in `AutoCompleteComponent`.** No sub-components, no store, no services of its
  own. State is plain public fields (`selected`, `suggestions`, `keyword`, `showSuggestions`,
  `focusedOption`, `isLoading`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture notes
text:
- **`provider` is the extension point.** It is either a plain `Function` (keyword → array) or an
  object implementing `AutoCompleteService`. `getResults()` may return an array, a `Promise`, a
  `Subject`, or an `Observable` — `getItems()` normalizes all four. Preserve that flexibility.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture notes
text: - **`dataProvider` is an alias setter for `provider`**; both are public API.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture notes
text:
- **Two inputs, one visible.** The template always renders both `<ion-input #inputElem>` and
  `<ion-searchbar #searchbarElem>`; `useIonInput` decides which gets the `hidden` class. Any change
  to bindings, key handling, or events must be mirrored on both elements.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture notes
text:
- **Templates are projected with `ngTemplateOutlet`** and receive a single `attrs` context object
  (`template`, `listTemplate`, `emptyTemplate`, `selectionTemplate`). Adding a field to `attrs` is

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text:
- **`ng-packagr` and `@angular-devkit/build-angular` are pinned to `^12`, matching the
  `@angular/*` framework packages (`^12.2.17`).** They briefly drifted to `^17.x` via unreviewed
  Dependabot security bumps (`6cfe7b2`, `76734b2`), which three-majors-mismatched them against
  Angular 12 and made `npm install` fail with an `ERESOLVE` conflict (`@angular-devkit/build-angular@17`
  peer-requires `@angular/compiler-cli@^17`). Resolved by downgrading both back to `^12`
  (`.claude/ROADMAP.md` 0.1, decided 2026-08-09/10) — don't bump them back to `^17` without reading
  that decision record first; it reintroduces both the `ERESOLVE` conflict and the CVEs the
  Dependabot bumps were fixing.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text:
- **`.nvmrc` and `engines.node` pin `^18.13.0 || >=20.9.0`**, set while the toolchain was still on
  `ng-packagr@17` (which requires Node 18+). Now that it's back on `^12` — whose own `engines.node`
  is `^12.14.1 || >=14.0.0` — the pin is stricter than the toolchain strictly needs, but it hasn't
  been revisited; treat Node 18+ as the supported baseline until that's done deliberately.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text:
- **`npm run build` is Windows-only.** It shells out to `copy` / `copy -r`, which is `cmd.exe`
  syntax and fails under Git Bash or on macOS/Linux. Use PowerShell here, or invoke
  `npx ng-packagr -p package.json` directly and copy the SCSS/assets by hand.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text:
- **`npm test` does not work as written.** `angular.json` points the karma builder at
  `karma.conf.js`, which does not exist in the repo — and cannot be committed, because the root
  `.gitignore` ignores `*.js`. The script also runs `snyk test` first (needs a Snyk auth token) and
  passes `--browsers PhantomJS` (launcher is installed, but PhantomJS is dead). To actually run the
  single spec (`src/auto-complete.spec.ts`), generate a karma config locally and run
  `npx ng test --browsers ChromeHeadless --watch false`. Don't assume tests were run — say so if
  they weren't.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands

extensions. The directories agents usually need are:

head: Agent instructions > Repository orientation
text:
Prefer putting broadly applicable training changes in `training/caiman_asr_train`.
Put Myrtle-only workflow, dataset, or internal experiment changes in
`myrtle-training`. The Myrtle docker launcher mounts both `myrtle-training` and
`training`, so internal runs can exercise changes in both trees.

head: Agent instructions > Repository orientation
text:
Docker launchers mount the repo at `/workspace/training` and, for Myrtle
training, `/workspace/myrtle-training`. They also symlink the first launch
argument to `/datasets` inside the container; use an absolute datasets path for
commands that actually read data.

head: Agent instructions > Quick `pytest` in docker
text:
The docker launch scripts require absolute host paths. Keep iteration fast by
replacing the `pytest` target with the smallest relevant test file or directory.

head: Agent instructions > Quick `pytest` in docker
text: For the main training tests instead of Myrtle-specific tests:

head: Agent instructions > Quick example training run
text:
Use the English example train script with only 5 training steps and skip the
initial validation pass so agents can iterate quickly.

head: Agent instructions > Quick example training run
text:
This script builds and launches the Myrtle training docker image, then runs the
trainer inside the container. It uses the script defaults for dataset,
checkpoint, and result locations. `--quick_val` keeps validation enabled but
bounds the in-training validation to one batch, then skips the separate
post-training validation harness. The cached path should be quick; the first
run can take longer if docker layers or training artifacts need to be built.

head: Agent instructions > Running real trains on the Jenkins cluster
text:
Long trains (hours to days) run on the shared Jenkins GPU cluster: launch with
`myrtle-training/scripts/queue.bash`, monitor/cancel with
`myrtle-training/scripts/jenkins/monitor.py`, and read results off the shared
`/mount/cassini/checkpoints` (colo) or `/mount/moore/checkpoints` (office)
mounts. The full launch → monitor (~12h cadence) → read-WER → cancel workflow is
documented in the **`running-trains` skill**
(`.claude/skills/running-trains/SKILL.md`), which loads automatically when you
work on cluster trains.

motivation for its creation.

the design document.

The samples directory contains example programs demonstrating how to use the new
streams API.

The benchmarks directory includes performance tests comparing the new streams
API to web streams.

The discussion directory holds documents discussing design decisions and
hypothetical scenarios related to the new streams API.

The MIGRATION.md file (in docs/) provides guidance on migrating from web streams to
the new streams API.
The API.md file contains a detailed API doc for the new streams API.
This is a work in progress and will be updated over time.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
This file helps AI agents understand the structure, tooling, and conventions of the
Validated Patterns documentation repository so they can make correct, buildable changes.
For creating or reviewing documentation content, use the skills under `.rulesync/skills/`
(see [AI documentation skills](#ai-documentation-skills)).

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text:
This is the documentation site for [validatedpatterns.io](https://validatedpatterns.io),
built with **Hugo** (static site generator) and the **PatternFly** theme. Content is
authored in both **AsciiDoc** (rendered by Asciidoctor with Rouge syntax highlighting) and
**Markdown** (rendered by Goldmark). There is no JavaScript framework, no TypeScript, and
no `package.json` at the repository root.

head: AGENTS.md > AI documentation skills
text:
This repository includes agent skills under `.rulesync/skills/`. These are the **required**
workflows for creating and reviewing documentation. Do **not** free-form invent page
structure, frontmatter, or style rules when these skills apply — read the skill file first
and follow it precisely.

head: AGENTS.md > AI documentation skills
text:
Skills may also be synced into editor-specific locations (for example `.claude/skills/` or
Cursor skills) via [rulesync](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rulesync). Prefer the skill when
it is available in the agent environment; if it is not loaded, read the source files under
`.rulesync/skills/` directly and execute the same workflow.

head: AGENTS.md > AI documentation skills
text:
| Skill | Path | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| **doc-create** | `.rulesync/skills/doc-create/SKILL.md` | Creating, drafting, scaffolding, or generating new documentation (learn pages, pattern page sets, tutorials, guides, or other new `.adoc`/`.md` site content) |
| **doc-review** | `.rulesync/skills/doc-review/SKILL.md` | Reviewing, proofreading, linting, or auditing existing documentation for Red Hat/IBM style compliance |

head: AGENTS.md > AI documentation skills > Mandatory routing for documentation requests
text:
1. **Generate / create / write / scaffold / draft new docs** → Use **doc-create**.
   - Read `.rulesync/skills/doc-create/SKILL.md` immediately.
   - Follow its steps (resolve content type, gather inputs, use references, generate files).
   - Load the applicable reference under `.rulesync/skills/doc-create/references/` before writing.
   - After generation, perform the style review step described in that skill (using
     `.rulesync/skills/doc-review/guides/` as instructed).

head: AGENTS.md > AI documentation skills > Mandatory routing for documentation requests
text:
2. **Review / check / fix style / audit docs** → Use **doc-review**.
   - Read `.rulesync/skills/doc-review/SKILL.md` immediately.
   - Follow its two-pass guide selection and review/fix workflow.
   - Load only the relevant guides from `.rulesync/skills/doc-review/guides/`.

head: AGENTS.md > AI documentation skills > Mandatory routing for documentation requests
text:
3. If the user asks for both creation and review, run **doc-create** first, then
   **doc-review** on the generated files (or complete the inline review step inside
   doc-create, then offer a fuller doc-review pass if useful).

head: AGENTS.md > AI documentation skills > Mandatory routing for documentation requests
text:
4. Do not skip these skills just because the user did not name them. Trigger phrases
   include “generate documentation”, “create a page”, “write docs for”, “scaffold a
   pattern”, “review this doc”, “check style”, and similar requests.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project overview
text: Personal site at `pradumnasaraf.dev` — Next.js 16 (App Router) + Tailwind CSS v4, JavaScript (no TypeScript). Blog posts are file-based Markdown in `src/content/blog/`. Node `>=24` is required.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project overview
text: Path alias: `@/*` resolves to `./src/*` (see `jsconfig.json`). **Caveat:** the alias is resolved by Next.js at compile time only. Files imported by `node --test` (anything reachable from `tests/**`, which includes `src/proxy.js`, every `src/app/**/route.js`, and modules under `src/lib/`) must use relative imports. Files used exclusively by Next.js (pages, layouts, components, metadata) can use `@/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: - `npm run dev` — Next dev server with Turbopack on http://localhost:3000.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: - `npm run build` — runs `prebuild` first (`validate:images` then `validate:tags`), then `next build`. Either validator failing aborts the build.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: - `npm start` — serve the production build.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Routing — App Router under `src/app/`.** Each top-level folder is a route segment (`blog/`, `projects/`, `photography/`, `links/`, `cv/`, `chat/`, `timeline/`, `toolkit/`, `speaking/`, `travel/`, `contact/`, `sitemap/`). Per-route metadata lives next to the route (e.g. `src/app/metadata.js`, `src/app/blog/metadata.js`). The root layout (`src/app/layout.js`) injects GTM, an inline pre-paint script that applies the saved `blog-theme` to `<html data-blog-theme>` before first paint (only meaningful inside `/blog`, where `.blog-theme-root` is scoped), the JSON-LD `Person` schema, and the global font (`League_Spartan`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Edge proxy at `src/proxy.js`.** This is Next 16's middleware (renamed from `middleware.js` in this project — keep it at `src/proxy.js`, export `proxy` and `config`). It 301-redirects any request hitting the `blog.pradumnasaraf.dev` host to the corresponding path under `pradumnasaraf.dev/blog`, stripping Hashnode-style `/@username/` prefixes. The `matcher` excludes `api`, `_next/static`, `_next/image`, and `favicon.ico`. Tests live in `tests/proxy.test.js`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Blog pipeline (`src/lib/blog.js`).** Reads `src/content/blog/*.md(x)`, parses frontmatter with `gray-matter`, sorts by `date` desc, filters out `draft: true`. Markdown → HTML uses `remark` → `remark-rehype` (with `allowDangerousHtml`) → `rehype-raw` → `rehype-highlight` (explicit language registry — only languages listed in `allLanguages` will highlight; add new ones there) → `rehype-sanitize` (custom schema permits `hljs-*` class names on `code`/`span`/`pre`, and `target`/`rel` on `a`, plus `loading`/`decoding`/`width`/`height` on `img`) → `rehype-stringify`. Reading time = `ceil(words/200)` minutes, computed off the raw markdown with code/links/markdown punctuation stripped.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: The HTML transformation is exposed separately as `processMarkdown(content)` — a pure function that takes a markdown string and returns the sanitized/highlighted HTML. Use it for testing the pipeline without writing fixture files into `src/content/blog/` (test temp files there would be picked up by `validate:tags`/`validate:images`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Releases.** `.github/workflows/releases.yml` runs `conventional-changelog-action` on every push to `main`, bumps `package.json` + `package-lock.json`, and cuts a GitHub release. Commit messages **must** follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, …). Major version bumps require a `!` after the type (e.g. `chore!:`) or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer somewhere in the commit range — otherwise even a Tailwind major upgrade will only bump as minor/patch.

head: CLAUDE.md > Page-local data sources
text:
- `src/app/projects/projects.json` — projects grid (curated; newest featured near the top). Each entry: `id`, `name`, `stars` (cached), `repoUrl`, `url` (live/package link; falls back to the repo), `problem` (description), `technologies` (array). **Whenever touching this file, always:** (1) refresh **all** `stars` to live counts, and (2) check GitHub for new repos worth featuring — the list is curated, so surface candidates and let the user pick which to add, don't auto-add. Use `gh` (authed as `Pradumnasaraf`):
  ```sh
  # live stars + metadata for every source repo:
  gh repo list Pradumnasaraf --source --limit 200 --json name,stargazerCount,description,primaryLanguage,homepageUrl
  # then match each existing entry by repoUrl basename (case-insensitive) and overwrite `stars`.
  ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Page-local data sources
text: - `src/app/timeline/timeline.json` — career timeline, ordered newest-first (add a new milestone at the top, in date order). Each entry: `title`, `date` (e.g. `"July, 2026"`), `description` (first-person, plain, no marketing fluff — match the surrounding entries), `image` (`{ src, alt }`), and optional `link` (`{ href, ariaLabel }`); entries without a `link` render no source button. Logos live in `public/timeline-logo/` and render in a fixed 45×45 rounded box, so square logos look best. The staggered fade-in delay is computed inline in `page.js` from the entry index and `LINE_DURATION` (which must stay equal to the `moveline` animation duration in `style.css`), spreading the stagger across the line's draw time so the last card lands as the line finishes. This scales automatically with any number of entries — **do not** re-introduce per-entry `.container:nth-child(n)` delay rules. When updating the timeline, **ask the user for new achievements** (talks, awards, features, milestones) — these aren't derivable from the repo and usually come from the user's LinkedIn/X.

head: CLAUDE.md > Page-local data sources

head: CLAUDE.md > Page-local data sources
text:
- `src/app/photography/images.json`: gallery image list. Each entry is `{ src, alt }` where `src` is a Google Drive thumbnail URL (`https://drive.google.com/thumbnail?id=<fileId>&sz=w2500`). Notes for future updates:
  - **Source of truth is a Drive folder** ("Personal Website Images", folder id `14AqocmrFs3lpcx0RN7WsnBg4M_RTFYGW`, owned by the user). The gallery is a curated mirror of that folder, not auto-generated.
  - **Enumerating the folder reliably:** the normal folder web page only ships a partial file list (Google lazy-loads the rest), so do not scrape it. Use the embedded listing instead, which returns every file id plus filename in plain HTML: `curl -sL "https://drive.google.com/embeddedfolderview?id=<folderId>#list"`, then parse `id="entry-<fileId>"` and the `flip-entry-title` filename. This is how the full 90-image sync was reconciled (compare folder ids against the `id=` in each `src`).
  - **Ordering convention (newest first):** camera-original HEIC files (`IMG_####.heic`) go on top, then the older `image##.jpg` set below in its existing order. Within the HEICs, the most recently added photo is pinned first, then the rest by filename number descending. Caveat: the `IMG_####` numbers are **not** reliably chronological (a lower number can be a newer photo), and Drive "date added" is not readable without the API, so true recency has to come from the user; new additions otherwise go to the top.
  - **Alt text policy:** never reuse a boilerplate alt (the gallery previously had the same `"Photography by Pradumna Saraf"` on every image, which is bad for screen readers). Write a distinct, honest one-line description per photo by actually viewing it: fetch a lighter copy (`&sz=w800`) and open it with the Read tool. Do not assert specific city, country, landmark, or person names you cannot verify from the image alone; describe generically. No `"image of"`/`"photo of"` prefixes.
  - **Dead Drive files:** an entry whose Drive file was deleted returns a sign-in HTML page from the `thumbnail?id=` endpoint (not an image) and a `404` from `https://drive.google.com/file/d/<id>/view`. Those tiles render broken on the live site. Detect and remove/replace them; do not invent alt text for images you cannot fetch.
  - **Intermittent local render failures are expected, not a bug.** The grid loads full `sz=w2500` images directly from Drive with `unoptimized`, and `ImageItem`'s `onError` sets `hasError` which renders the tile as `null` (it disappears). Drive rate-limits bursts of large requests, so on a cold dev cache (worsened by React StrictMode double-mounting effects and HMR reloads) some tiles 403 and vanish. Production/preview render fine because the cache is warm and there is no StrictMode double-mount. If a real fix is ever wanted: load the grid at a smaller `sz` (keep `w2500` only for the full-screen modal), retry on error instead of nulling the tile, or stop hotlinking Drive and host the images in `public/` or an image CDN.

head: Engineering Notes
