head: Engineering Notes > Project Map
text:
Heavy hitters: `transformer.zig`, `network.zig`, `compute.metal` (~14k lines, half the nnmetal codebase).
Comptime spine: `layout.zig` resolves all buffer shapes at compile time.
Three shader files: `compute.metal` (general NN kernels), `transformer.metal` (attention-specific), `qmv_specialized.metal` (quantized matmul).
Agent spine: `agent_core.zig` provides the shared experiment loop; profiles (`mnist_agent.zig`, `bonsai_agent.zig`) configure it.
Toolbox spine: `toolbox.zig` provides all generic CLI tools; domain binaries (`bonsai_researcher.zig`, `mnist_researcher.zig`) are thin config wrappers.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 0. **Simplicity and Elegance**
text: Simplicity is not a free pass or a first attempt — it is the hardest revision. The goal is to find the "super idea" that solves safety, performance, and developer experience simultaneously. An hour or day of design is worth weeks or months in production. Spend mental energy upfront, proactively rather than reactively, because when the thinking is done, what is spent on the design will be dwarfed by implementation, testing, and maintenance.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 0. **Simplicity and Elegance**
text: > "Simplicity and elegance are unpopular because they require hard work and discipline to achieve." — Edsger Dijkstra

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 0. **Simplicity and Elegance**
text: It's easy to say "let's do something simple", but to do that in practice takes thought, multiple passes, many sketches, and still we may have to throw one away. For nnmetal, this means: don't settle on the first kernel dispatch strategy or buffer layout that works. Sketch alternatives. The elegant design will be the one where the Metal buffer layout, the comptime network description, and the kernel dispatch strategy all reinforce each other.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 1. **Zero Technical Debt Policy**
text: _Solve problems correctly the first time_. When you encounter a potential latency spike or algorithmic issue, fix it now — don't defer. The second pass may never come.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 2. **Static Memory Allocation**
text: This is huge for a GPU compute library:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 2. **Static Memory Allocation**
text: - **No dynamic allocation after initialization**

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 2. **Static Memory Allocation**
text: - Pre-allocate all Metal shared buffers (params, grads, activations) at startup

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 2. **Static Memory Allocation**
text: - Use fixed-capacity arrays/pools instead of growing `ArrayList`s during training

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 2. **Static Memory Allocation**
text: - Use comptime-known sizes from `NetworkLayout` to determine buffer capacities at compile time

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 2. **Static Memory Allocation**
text: For nnmetal, this means: parameter buffers, gradient buffers, and activation buffers should have fixed upper bounds allocated at init time. This eliminates allocation jitter during forward/backward passes and prevents GPU stalls caused by buffer reallocation.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: **Minimum 2 assertions per function**. For nnmetal:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - Assert buffer sizes match comptime-known layout dimensions before kernel dispatch

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - Assert matrix dimensions are compatible before matmul (`W` is `[M x K]`, `x` is `[K x N]`)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - **Pair assertions**: assert parameter slice bounds when writing from CPU AND when binding to GPU encoder

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - Assert compile-time constants (e.g., `comptime { std.debug.assert(Layout.param_count > 0); }`)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - Assert thread grid sizes do not exceed Metal device limits before dispatch

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - **Split compound assertions**: prefer `assert(a); assert(b);` over `assert(a and b);` — the former is simpler to read, and provides more precise information if the condition fails

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - Use single-line `if` to assert an implication: `if (a) assert(b);`

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - On occasion, use a blatantly true assertion instead of a comment as stronger documentation where the assertion condition is critical and surprising

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 3. **Assertion Density**
text: - **Assertions are not a substitute for human understanding.** Build a precise mental model of the code first, encode your understanding in the form of assertions, write the code and comments to explain and justify the mental model to your reviewer, and use testing/fuzzing as the final line of defense. A fuzzer can prove only the presence of bugs, not their absence

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 4. **Put a Limit on Everything**
text: Every loop, every queue, every buffer needs a hard cap:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 4. **Put a Limit on Everything**
text: This prevents infinite loops and tail latency spikes. If you hit a limit, **fail fast**.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 5. **70-Line Function Limit**
text: Hard limit. Split large compute dispatch or training loop functions by:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 5. **70-Line Function Limit**
text: - Keeping control flow (switches, ifs) in parent functions

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 5. **70-Line Function Limit**
text: - Moving pure computation to helpers

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 5. **70-Line Function Limit**
text: - "Push ifs up, fors down"

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 5. **70-Line Function Limit**
text: - **Good function shape** is the inverse of an hourglass: a few parameters, a simple return type, and a lot of meaty logic between the braces

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 5. **70-Line Function Limit**
text: - **Centralize state manipulation**: let the parent function keep all relevant state in local variables, and use helpers to compute what needs to change, rather than applying the change directly. Keep leaf functions pure

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 6. **Explicit Control Flow**
text: - No recursion (use explicit iteration over layer indices — network graphs are sequential)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 6. **Explicit Control Flow**
text: - Minimize abstractions ("abstractions are never zero cost")

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 6. **Explicit Control Flow**
text: - Avoid `async`/suspend patterns that hide control flow — Metal command buffers already handle asynchrony explicitly

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 6. **Explicit Control Flow**
text: - **Split compound conditions**: split complex `else if` chains into nested `else { if {} }` trees to make branches and cases explicit. Consider whether a single `if` also needs a matching `else` branch to ensure positive and negative spaces are handled or asserted

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 6. **Explicit Control Flow**
text: - **Functions must run to completion** without suspending, so that precondition assertions remain true throughout the lifetime of the function

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 6. **Explicit Control Flow**
text: - **Don't do things directly in reaction to external events.** Your program should run at its own pace — not react to external signals or callbacks synchronously. This keeps control flow under your control, improves performance through batching instead of context switching on every event, and makes it easier to maintain bounds on work done per time period. For nnmetal, this means the training loop drives the tempo: it pulls batches and dispatches kernels on its schedule, not in reaction to Metal completion handlers or data-loading callbacks

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 7. **Back-of-Envelope Performance Sketches**
text: Before implementing, sketch resource usage:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 7. **Back-of-Envelope Performance Sketches**
text: - How many floats per forward pass? (GPU memory bandwidth)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 7. **Back-of-Envelope Performance Sketches**
text: - How many kernel dispatches per training step? (command buffer overhead)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 7. **Back-of-Envelope Performance Sketches**
text: - How many bytes transferred between CPU and GPU? (should be zero on unified memory)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 7. **Back-of-Envelope Performance Sketches**
text: - What is the arithmetic intensity of each kernel? (compute-bound vs memory-bound)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 7. **Back-of-Envelope Performance Sketches**
text: Optimize for **network → disk → memory → CPU** (slowest first), adjusted for frequency. On Apple Silicon unified memory, the CPU↔GPU copy cost is zero — but cache coherency and memory bandwidth still matter. A matmul kernel bottlenecked on memory bandwidth won't benefit from more ALUs.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 8. **Batching as Religion**
text: We're already doing this with Metal command buffers, but:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 8. **Batching as Religion**
text: - Don't dispatch one kernel per operation — encode multiple kernels into a single command buffer

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 8. **Batching as Religion**
text: - Amortize command buffer creation across training steps

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 8. **Batching as Religion**
text: - Let the GPU sprint on large batches, not stall on tiny dispatches

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 8. **Batching as Religion**
text: - **Distinguish control plane from data plane**: a clear delineation through batching enables a high level of assertion safety without losing performance. Assert heavily on the control plane (layer setup, buffer binding); batch tightly on the data plane (kernel dispatches, gradient accumulation)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - Units/qualifiers last: `count_elements`, `offset_bytes`, `size_floats`

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - Same-length related names for visual alignment: `source`/`target` not `src`/`dest`; `params`/`grads_` (or use `weight`/`gradient`)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - Callbacks go last in parameter lists

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - Use `snake_case` for function, variable, and file names. The underscore is the closest thing we have as programmers to a space, and helps separate words and encourage descriptive names

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - Use proper capitalization for acronyms: `MSELoss`, not `MseLoss`; `GPUBuffer`, not `GpuBuffer`

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - **Do not abbreviate** variable names (unless the variable is a primitive integer in a sort function or matrix calculation)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - **Infuse names with meaning**: `gpa: Allocator` and `arena: Allocator` are better than `allocator: Allocator` — they inform the reader whether `deinit` should be called

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - **Don't overload names** with multiple meanings that are context-dependent — `buffer` could mean a Metal buffer or a Zig slice; be specific (`metal_buffer`, `param_slice`)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - **Think of how names read outside the code** — in docs or conversation. Nouns compose better than adjectives or participles: `pipeline` over `preparing`

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - **Named arguments via `options: struct`** pattern when arguments can be mixed up. A function taking two `u64`s must use an options struct

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - **Struct field ordering**: fields first, then types, then methods. Important things near the top. `main` goes first in a file

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 9. **Naming Discipline**
text: - **Descriptive commit messages** that inform and delight the reader. PR descriptions are not stored in git history and are invisible in `git blame` — they are not a replacement for commit messages

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 10. **Shrink Scope Aggressively**
text: - Declare variables at smallest possible scope

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 10. **Shrink Scope Aggressively**
text: - Calculate/check values close to use (avoid POCPOU bugs)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 10. **Shrink Scope Aggressively**
text: - Don't leave variables around after they're needed

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 10. **Shrink Scope Aggressively**
text: - **Don't duplicate variables or take aliases** — this reduces the probability that state gets out of sync. In particular, don't cache a buffer's `.asSlice()` result across a GPU submission boundary — the slice is a view into shared memory and the semantics change after `commitAndWait`

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 10. **Shrink Scope Aggressively**
text: - **Simpler return types reduce dimensionality**: `void` > `bool` > `u64` > `?u64` > `!u64`. Simpler signatures mean fewer branches at call sites, and this dimensionality is **viral** through call chains

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 11. **Handle the Negative Space**
text: For every valid state you handle, assert the invalid states too:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 11. **Handle the Negative Space**
text: **State invariants positively.** Negations are error-prone. This form is easy to get right:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 11. **Handle the Negative Space**
text: This form is harder, and goes against the grain of how `index` is typically compared to `length`:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 11. **Handle the Negative Space**
text: Prefer the positive form.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 12. **Minimal Dependencies**
text: - **zig-objc** — Objective-C runtime bindings for Metal API calls (necessary; Metal has no C API)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 12. **Minimal Dependencies**
text: - **Apple Metal framework** — the GPU compute backend (the whole point)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 12. **Minimal Dependencies**
text: Beyond these, avoid pulling in external Zig packages when you can implement cleanly yourself. Each dependency is a supply chain risk. Linear algebra helpers, activation functions, and data loading should be implemented in-house — they're small and domain-specific.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 13. **In-Place Initialization**
text: For large structs (like `Device` with its pre-compiled pipelines), use out-pointers:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 13. **In-Place Initialization**
text: This avoids stack growth and copy-move allocations. In-place initializations are **viral** — if any field is initialized in-place, the entire container struct should be initialized in-place as well.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 13. **In-Place Initialization**
text: **Pass large args as `*const`**: if an argument type is more than 16 bytes and you don't intend for it to be copied, pass it as `*const`. This catches bugs where the caller makes an accidental copy on the stack before calling the function.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 14. **Comptime All the Things**
text: nnmetal's `NetworkLayout` resolves all buffer sizes, weight/bias offsets, and activation sizes at compile time. Lean into this:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 14. **Comptime All the Things**
text: - **Never compute at runtime what can be computed at comptime**. Layer dimensions, parameter counts, and buffer offsets are all known statically

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 14. **Comptime All the Things**
text: - **Use comptime assertions** to validate network architecture (e.g., layer `i`'s output must match layer `i+1`'s input)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 14. **Comptime All the Things**
text: - **Comptime slice helpers** like `getWeightSlice` and `getBiasSlice` should compile down to pointer arithmetic with zero branching

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 14. **Comptime All the Things**
text: - When adding new layout features, ensure they remain `comptime`-evaluable — no allocators, no runtime state

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 15. **Explicitly-Sized Types**
text: Use explicitly-sized types like `u32` for everything. Avoid architecture-specific `usize` unless interfacing with Zig's standard library or slice indexing that requires it. Explicit sizes make overflow behavior, memory layout, and cross-platform behavior predictable and consistent. This is especially important when passing dimensions to Metal shaders via `setBytes`, where the GPU expects exact sizes.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 16. **Always Say Why**
text: Code alone is not documentation.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 16. **Always Say Why**
text: - **Never forget to say why.** If you explain the rationale for a decision, it increases the reader's understanding and shares criteria with which to evaluate the decision and its importance

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 16. **Always Say Why**
text: - Comments are sentences: space after the slash, capital letter, full stop (or a colon if they relate to something that follows)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 16. **Always Say Why**
text: - Comments after the end of a line _can_ be phrases, with no punctuation

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 16. **Always Say Why**
text: - When writing a test, describe the goal and methodology at the top — help the reader get up to speed or skip over sections without forcing them to dive in

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 17. **All Errors Must Be Handled**
text: 92% of catastrophic failures in distributed data-intensive systems are the result of incorrect handling of non-fatal errors explicitly signaled in software ([OSDI'14](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/conference/osdi14/osdi14-paper-yuan.pdf)). Every error return must be handled — no silent discards, no blind `catch unreachable` without justification.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 17. **All Errors Must Be Handled**
text: Metal errors are particularly important: shader compilation failures, pipeline creation failures, and buffer allocation failures must all produce actionable diagnostics (as already done with `log.err` in `compileLibrary` and `ComputePipeline.init`).

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 18. **Off-By-One Discipline**
text: The usual suspects for off-by-one errors are casual interactions between an `index`, a `count`, and a `size`. Treat them as distinct conceptual types with clear conversion rules:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 18. **Off-By-One Discipline**
text: - `index` → `count`: add one (indexes are 0-based, counts are 1-based)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 18. **Off-By-One Discipline**
text: - `count` → `size`: multiply by the unit (e.g., `param_count * @sizeOf(f32)` for byte size)

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 18. **Off-By-One Discipline**
text: Show division intent explicitly: use `@divExact()`, `@divFloor()`, or `div_ceil()` to prove to the reader you've thought through rounding scenarios. This is critical for kernel thread grid calculations where misaligned dispatch sizes cause silent data corruption.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 19. **Explicit Options at Call Sites**
text: Explicitly pass options to library functions at the call site instead of relying on defaults:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 19. **Explicit Options at Call Sites**
text: This improves readability and avoids latent, potentially catastrophic bugs if the library ever changes its defaults. The same applies to Metal resource options — always spell out `.storage_mode = .shared` rather than relying on the default.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 20. **Hot Loop Extraction**
text: Extract hot loops into standalone functions with primitive arguments — no `self`. This way the compiler doesn't need to prove it can cache struct fields in registers, and a human reader can spot redundant computations more easily.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 20. **Hot Loop Extraction**
text: This is especially relevant for CPU-side data preparation (batch loading, normalization) that runs while the GPU crunches the previous batch.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 21. **Buffer Bleeds**
text: The inverse of a buffer overflow: a buffer underflow where a buffer is not fully utilized and padding is not zeroed correctly. This can leak sensitive information and break deterministic guarantees. When writing to Metal shared buffers, zero-fill any padding between used regions — stale data in a gradient buffer from a previous batch can silently corrupt training.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 22. **Resource Allocation Grouping**
text: Use newlines to **group resource allocation and deallocation** — place a blank line before the allocation and after the corresponding `defer` statement. This makes leaks visually obvious:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 23. **Style By The Numbers**
text: - Use 4 spaces of indentation, rather than 2 spaces — more obvious to the eye at a distance.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 23. **Style By The Numbers**
text: - **Hard limit all line lengths to 100 columns**, without exception. Nothing should be hidden by a horizontal scrollbar. Let your editor help you by setting a column ruler. To wrap a function signature, call, or data structure, add a trailing comma, and let `zig fmt` do the rest. The motivation is physical: just enough to fit two copies of the code side-by-side on a screen.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 23. **Style By The Numbers**
text: - Add braces to `if` statements unless the entire statement fits on a single line — for consistency and defense in depth against "goto fail;" bugs.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 24. **Compiler Warnings**
text: Appreciate **all compiler warnings at the compiler's strictest setting** from day one. Warnings are free bug reports. Never suppress them — fix the underlying issue.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 25. **Tooling**
text: Our primary tool is Zig. It may not be the best for everything, but it's good enough for most things. When you need a script, write it in `labrat/src/*.zig` instead of as a shell script — this makes scripts cross-platform, type-safe, and increases the probability they'll work for everyone on the team. Standardizing on Zig for tooling reduces dimensionality as the team and range of personal tastes grows.

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 25. **Tooling**
text: > "The right tool for the job is often the tool you are already using — adding new tools has a higher cost than many people appreciate." — John Carmack

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 26. **GPU/CPU Boundary Discipline**
text: The CPU/GPU boundary is where the hardest bugs hide:

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 26. **GPU/CPU Boundary Discipline**
text: - **Never read from a Metal shared buffer while the GPU may be writing to it.** Always `commitAndWait` (or use a fence/semaphore) before reading results back on the CPU

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 26. **GPU/CPU Boundary Discipline**
text: - **Double-buffering exists for a reason**: the CPU preps batch N+1 while the GPU computes batch N. Violating this overlap invariant causes data races that are invisible to Zig's safety checks

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 26. **GPU/CPU Boundary Discipline**
text: - **Assert buffer binding order**: Metal shader `[[buffer(N)]]` indices must match the `setBuffer` calls. A mismatch silently feeds wrong data to the kernel

head: Engineering Notes > Project Map > 26. **GPU/CPU Boundary Discipline**
text: - **Validate dispatch dimensions**: a 2D dispatch for matmul must match the output matrix dimensions. An undersized grid silently skips elements; an oversized grid reads garbage

head: CLAUDE.md
text:
Kelvin is a Go daemon that adjusts Philips Hue lights to schedules derived
from local sunrise and sunset times. Single binary, one `main` package.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gates
text: Run all five before every commit; all must pass clean:

head: CLAUDE.md > Gates
text: - `gofmt -l .` — must print nothing

head: CLAUDE.md > Gates
text: - `go test ./...` — the suite runs offline; no test may need the bridge or the network

head: CLAUDE.md > Gates
text: - `go mod tidy` — must leave no diff

head: CLAUDE.md > Gates
text:
Additionally, `scripts/docker-smoke.sh` (needs Docker) must pass for commits
touching the Dockerfile, `.goreleaser.yaml`, the web interface, or
configuration I/O — and always before tagging a release. CI runs it on every
push.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text:
- Commit subjects follow conventional commits: `type(scope): imperative description`,
  at most ~65 characters. The scope is the issue number where one exists
  (`fix(#126): …`), an area otherwise.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - One intent per commit: fixes, documentation, and version bumps land separately.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - Open work lives in GitHub issues, never in markdown checklists.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text:
- Recorded decisions live in `DECISIONS.md`. Research notes live in `research/`
  as cited Markdown files.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - Commit locally on green gates; push and tag only on explicit instruction.

head: CLAUDE.md > Domain pitfalls
text:
- The value `-1` for color temperature or brightness means "do not manage this
  property". This sentinel flows unlabeled from the configuration through
  `Schedule`, `Interval`, and `LightState`. Handle it in every calculation.

head: CLAUDE.md > Domain pitfalls
text:
- The Hue bridge clamps out-of-gamut colors and out-of-range values, then
  reports the clamped state. Compare against the achievable value, never the
  requested one — a mismatch is misread as a manual user change and disables
  automation (see issue #126).

head: CLAUDE.md > Domain pitfalls
text:
- Color temperatures below roughly 1700K convert to xy coordinates outside
  every Hue gamut.

head: CLAUDE.md > Domain pitfalls
text:
- The web interface loads templates from the working-directory-relative path
  `gui/`; the binary must start in its install directory.

head: CLAUDE.md > Domain pitfalls
text:
- `config.json` carries a `version` field; migrations run on read.
  `latestConfigurationVersion` must equal the newest migration's output version,
  or fresh configurations get migrated and silently rewritten.

head: CLAUDE.md > Domain pitfalls
text:
- The auto-updater refuses major-version jumps unless started with
  `-forceUpdate`. This guard is what holds the v1 fleet back at v1.3.x once
  a v2.0.0 release exists.

head: CLAUDE.md > Current campaign
text:
Kelvin is being modernized into an event-driven Hue CLIP v2 client. The scope,
sequence, and rejected alternatives are recorded in `DECISIONS.md` under
"Modernization campaign". The work items live in GitHub issues. Facts about
the CLIP v2 API are in `research/hue-api-v2.md` — read it before touching
bridge communication.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
This file is the operating manual for **every AI coding agent** working in this
repository. Read it fully before making any change. If a task ever conflicts
with this file, this file wins — stop and ask for clarification.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. Project mission
text: This repository is a **declarative platform for building AI agent systems**.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. Project mission
text:
Developers describe an agent system in YAML. The platform validates that YAML,
compiles it into a typed internal graph, and runs it through a long-lived
runtime that renders prompt files, calls resolver/tool plugins and MCP servers,
exposes an API, and produces execution traces.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. Project mission
text:
The repository is in **active development**. The YAML validator, compiler,
runtime engine (orchestrators run as supervisor agents), resolver
plugin system, tool plugin loading, MCP client (local and remote servers,
including authenticated MCP via hooks), the runtime hooks system
(11 lifecycle points — see
[docs/RUNTIME_HOOKS.md](docs/RUNTIME_HOOKS.md)), per-run execution-limit
guardrails (see [docs/EXECUTION_LIMITS.md](docs/EXECUTION_LIMITS.md)), prompt
rendering, and the CLI (`validate`, `inspect`, `generate`, `run`, `serve`,
`chat`) are implemented. Model access supports both Anthropic and Amazon
Bedrock. Two HTTP API layers exist: a thin `agent_engine` API (`/invoke`,
`/stream`), started by `agentctl serve` (default port `8090`) — stateless, no
persistence, no web client — and `agent_manager` — a conversation lifecycle
service built on top of it with process-local storage by default, opt-in
SQLite/Postgres persistence, SSE streaming, and the official React web client,
started by the separate `agent-manager` console script (default port `8100`).
`agentctl chat` is a separate, ephemeral
developer console that persists nothing (see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §14 for
detail). Basic observability
(structured logging plus a Langfuse callback provider) is wired in. A
`Dockerfile`/`entrypoint.sh` provide a basic container image.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. Project mission
text:
The access plugin **is** wired into child filtering, but the request-context
gate that should populate real identity/permissions into it is **not yet
implemented** — access filtering currently runs against an empty context, so
`protected` nodes are not actually enforced today. Treat this as an open
security gap, not a finished feature. See [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md)
for per-phase status. Agents implement the product task-by-task using the
files in `tasks/`, though the package layout has evolved beyond what the
original numbered tasks describe (see §4).

head: AGENTS.md > 2. Core architecture pipeline
text:
**Three separated phases (do not collapse them):** (1) **build/compile** —
load, validate, and compile YAML into a `CompiledAgentGraph` *before*
serving requests (never executes requests); (2) **runtime/execution** — per
request, create an `ExecutionContext`, filter protected nodes, route to a node
instance, render prompts, execute, call tools/MCP, return response + trace;
(3) **client extension** — client-specific auth/business logic lives in
plugins, never in the generic runtime.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text:
These rules are binding. Do not violate them, even if a task description seems
to ask for it. If a rule blocks you, stop and raise it.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 1. **YAML is declarative specification, not executable business logic.**

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 2. **The runtime must never execute raw YAML dictionaries directly.**

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 3. **YAML must be validated first.**

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 4. **Validated YAML must be compiled into internal typed models** before use.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 5. **RuntimeEngine is created once at application startup.** Never per request.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 6. **ExecutionContext is created per request.** Never reused across requests.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 7. **Do not store request state on RuntimeEngine** or on the compiled graph.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 8. **Prompt files are templates.** They contain placeholders, not final text.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 9. **Prompt templates may be cached.** Compiled/parsed templates are reusable.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text:
10. **Prompt values are resolved dynamically per request.** Never cache a
    fully-rendered prompt globally.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text:
11. **Client-specific auth, authorization, and business context are handled
    through plugins**, not baked into the generated runtime.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text:
12. **Nodes declare what they need** (resolvers, tools, MCPs). **The runtime
    resolves and binds** those needs.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Non-negotiable architecture rules
text: 13. **Protected nodes must fail closed** through the fixed access plugin.

text:

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: TTS Reader is a text-to-speech service that reads selected text from anywhere on the system. It runs as a FastAPI HTTP server that accepts requests to read text from the clipboard or via POST request body. The service uses Piper TTS for speech synthesis and supports both Linux and Windows platforms.

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Setup > Initial Setup
text:
1. Create virtual environment with system-site-packages:
   ```bash
   python -m venv venv --system-site-packages
   source venv/bin/activate
   ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Setup > Initial Setup
text:
2. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Setup > Initial Setup
text:
3. For Piper TTS Python module compatibility, use Python v3.10.12 or install specific dependencies:
   ```bash
   pip install --no-deps -r piper.requirements.txt
   ```

text:

```bash
python main.py --port 5000 --speed=1.0 --volume=.8 --piper-model yourmodel.onnx --piper-model-config yourmodel.onnx.json --wayland
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Data Flow

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Data Flow
text: 8. Desktop notification is sent to user

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions
text: Stronghold is an open-source disaster recovery intelligence platform for AWS. These instructions are canonical for Codex, Claude Code, Claude Opus, and any other repository-local agent.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Operating Mode
text: 1. Read the user brief fully before acting.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Operating Mode
text: 2. Identify the affected package or repository layer first.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Operating Mode
text: 3. Read only the files needed for the requested change.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Operating Mode
text: 4. Do not scan the whole repo unless the task is explicitly repository-wide.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Operating Mode
text: 5. Preserve product behavior unless the brief explicitly asks to change it.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Operating Mode
text: 6. Do not expand Phase 5 scope while adding memory, docs, tests, or tooling.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Repository Shape
text: - `packages/core`: framework-free domain logic plus read-only cloud provider adapters.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Repository Shape
text: - `packages/cli`: CLI entry point. Depends on core.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Repository Shape
text: - `packages/server`: Express, Prisma, PostgreSQL. Private.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Repository Shape
text: - `packages/web`: React, Vite, Tailwind. Private.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Repository Shape
text: - Build order: core, cli, server, web, github-action.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Scope Guardrails
text: Do not modify AWS scanners, product contracts semantics, orchestration, auth, identity, server, web, landing pages, or marketing docs unless the brief names them.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Scope Guardrails
text: Do not refactor unrelated code while completing an AI memory, validation, or documentation task.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 1. Core has no framework dependencies.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 2. Pure-domain modules are network-free: contracts, evidence evaluation, scenario evaluation, validation, and related business-logic modules.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 3. Provider, auth, and orchestration modules are explicit effect boundaries excluded from the pure-domain network guard.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 4. AWS scans are strictly read-only.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 5. RTO/RPO are null or UNKNOWN unless backed by measured tested evidence.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 6. Estimated, suggested, or fallback RTO/RPO cannot satisfy contracts.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 7. Missing measured tested evidence means UNKNOWN.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 8. Stronghold is service-centric, not resource-centric.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 9. Verdicts are deterministic: same inputs, same output.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 10. Hooks and integrations remain outside pure domain modules.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 11. No LLM or non-deterministic model is a decision engine.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 12. Public JSON outputs are versioned.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 13. Audit trail is always on.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 14. Evidence is append-only.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 15. Runbooks generate commands; they never execute them.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Architectural Invariants
text: 16. ARN is the canonical resource identifier.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > TypeScript Rules
text: - Strict TypeScript remains mandatory.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > TypeScript Rules
text: - No unexplained `@ts-ignore` or `@ts-expect-error`.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > TypeScript Rules
text: - Functions use camelCase.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > TypeScript Rules
text: - Constants use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Dependencies
text: - Do not add dependencies unless the brief explicitly approves them.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Dependencies
text: - Use AWS SDK v3 only for AWS access.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Dependencies
text: - Testing uses Vitest only.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > RTK Policy
text: - If `rtk` is available, use it explicitly for noisy exploration commands.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > RTK Policy
text: - Do not use RTK for evidence, proof loops, CI truth, release truth, audit exports, or exact JSON/YAML contract output.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > RTK Policy

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > RTK Policy

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Verification
text: For AI memory/tooling changes, also run the relevant `ai:*` scripts.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Code Hygiene
text: - No production `console.log`.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Code Hygiene
text: - Comments explain why, not what.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Code Hygiene
text: - Do not log credentials or infrastructure details in audit logs.

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Code Hygiene

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Code Hygiene

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Code Hygiene

head: Stronghold Agent Instructions > Code Hygiene

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports
text:
Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code reads this file; Codex reads
`AGENTS.md`, which is the same file) working in this SDK or in a game-port
checkout built from it.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > What this is
text:
SDK for **openfpgaOS** — a bare-metal RISC-V game runtime (VexiiRiscv
rv32imafc @ 100 MHz, 64 MB SDRAM) on two platforms: **Analogue Pocket**
and **MiSTer** (DE10-Nano / SuperStation One). One app `.elf` runs
unchanged on both; everything platform-specific arrives at runtime via
the capability/services tables (`of_get_caps()`, auxv). Apps are trusted,
single-process, no MMU — they run close to the hardware.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > What this is
text:
Game ports (Duke3D, Doom, Quake, QuakeSpasm, Quake2, Diablo, ScummVM, …)
are **forks of this SDK**: same root layout, the game lives in
`src/<name>/` next to SDK-owned `src/sdk/` and `src/apps/`.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Build, test, deploy
text:
Do not edit SDK-owned directories: `src/sdk/`, `src/apps/` (except the app
you're working on), `scripts/`, `runtime/` (build artifacts synced from the
openfpgaOS repo), `src/sdk/platforms/mister/fatfs/` (vendored, pristine).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Porting ground rules
text:
- **Never hardcode addresses or sizes** — read `of_get_caps()` (fb_base,
  heap, sample pool, gpu_base, cpu_freq_hz). The memory map is the
  portability anchor; the caps table is how you stay on it.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Porting ground rules
text:
- **Gate hardware on feature bits**, not platform ids, wherever possible:
  `of_has_feature(OF_HW_GPU_PERSP)`, `of_has_feature(OF_HW_ANALOGIZER)`, …
  Use `of_get_caps()->platform_id` (`OF_PLATFORM_POCKET/MISTER/SIM`) only
  for genuinely platform-shaped behavior.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Porting ground rules
text:
- **Pocket-only**: `make debug` (PHDP/UART), `interact.json` menus,
  Analogizer/SNAC. On MiSTer `of_analogizer_enabled()` returns 0.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Porting ground rules
text:
- Files: register names once (`of_file_slot_register(slot, "game.grp")`),
  then standard `fopen`/`fread`. Filenames ≤ 23 chars (registry limit, both
  platforms). POSIX `lseek` must use the riscv32 5-arg `_llseek` convention
  (see `src/sdk/include/of_posix.c`).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Porting ground rules
text:
- Keep a CPU fallback for every GPU path and keep the desktop build
  (`make test`) green — it is the fast correctness reference.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Porting ground rules > Reference ports (read these before inventing a new pattern)
text:
| Port | GPU | Audio | Input | Key files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Duke3D | affine span groups (Build engine) | mixer groups + MIDI | pad + P2 + kbd + mouse | `src/duke3d/d3d_gpu.c`, `d3d_audio.c`, `Engine/src/display_of.c` |
| Doom | affine spans + translucency (fuzz) | mixer channels | pad + analog | `src/doom/cdoom/doom/r_gpu.c`, `shim/i_sdlsound.c`, `shim/i_input.c` |
| Quake | perspective span groups | stream + 2-voice CD music | pad + analog | `src/quake/engine/vid_of.c`, `cd_of.c`, `snd_of.c`, `in_of.c` |
| QuakeSpasm | affine + persp, palookup cache | mixer groups | kbd/mouse shims, deadzone | `src/quake/gpu/qs_gpu.c`, `shim/snd_of.c`, `shim/in_of.c` |
| Quake2 | param span lists (Z modes) | mixer SFX + streamed music | pad | `src/quake2/openfpga/of_emit_q2.c`, `snd_of.c`, `input_of.c` |

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Porting ground rules > Reference ports (read these before inventing a new pattern)
text:
Minimal working examples in this repo: `src/apps/gpudemo` (GPU),
`src/apps/wavdemo`/`moddemo`/`mididemo` (audio), `src/apps/sdldemo` (SDL2).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer
text:
The GPU is an **asynchronous indexed-color span rasterizer** built for
BUILD/Doom/Quake-style software renderers. The CPU stages command words in
a cached SDRAM scratch buffer; a doorbell DMA pulls them into the GPU's
16 KB ring; fences report completion. There is no per-command MMIO path —
**batching is the design, not an optimization**.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Integration pattern
text:
- `of_gpu.h` contains **static mutable state — include it from exactly ONE
  translation unit** and export your own wrapper API to the rest of the
  game (every port does this: `d3d_gpu.c`, `r_gpu.c`, `vid_of.c`, `qs_gpu.c`).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Integration pattern
text:
- Init order: `of_get_caps()` → check `OF_HW_GPU_*` bits → `of_gpu_init()`
  → draw a probe span to a scratch framebuffer and verify the pixels →
  fall back to the CPU renderer on failure.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Integration pattern
text:
- Gate optional GPU features individually: `OF_HW_GPU_SPAN` is the
  baseline (always set); `OF_HW_GPU_PERSP`, `OF_HW_GPU_PARAM_SPAN_LIST`,
  `OF_HW_GPU_PARAM_SPAN_Z/ZTEST/Q29_SCALE`, `OF_HW_GPU_ALPHA`,
  `OF_HW_GPU_BILINEAR`, `OF_HW_GPU_VCOLOR` are not.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Which span command to use
text:
- `of_gpu_draw_affine_span_group()` — constant-z texture stepping:
  BUILD walls/floors, Doom columns/spans. Up to 8 lanes per group
  (per-lane fb/tex addr, count, s/t steps, 6-bit light, colormap_id);
  the SDK splits >4 lanes into 4-lane hardware chunks.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Which span command to use
text:
- `of_gpu_draw_persp_span_group()` (+ `_batch`) — perspective-correct
  spans (Quake world). Accumulate spans and submit groups; don't emit
  one group per span.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Which span command to use
text:
- `of_gpu_draw_param_span_list()` — the unified parametric command
  (affine/persp/solid attr modes, Z write/test, Q29 scale). Quake2's
  renderer sits on this. Gate on `OF_HW_GPU_PARAM_SPAN_LIST`.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Which span command to use
text: - `of_gpu_clear_rect()` / `of_gpu_clear_rect_strided()` — GPU-side clears.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Which span command to use
text:
- `of_gpu_submit_command_stream_batch()` — pre-encoded raw streams,
  ≤ 4095 words per batch.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Colormaps and translucency
text:
- `of_gpu_palookup_upload(slot, data, 16384)` — 16 lighting/colormap
  slots of 16 KB. Upload once (or on level load), reference per-span via
  `colormap_id` + 6-bit `light`. Lighting lookups then cost nothing on
  the CPU.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Colormaps and translucency
text:
- `of_gpu_translucency_upload(table, 65536)` — BUILD-style 256×256
  translucency table (GPU decimates to 128×256 internally). Doom's fuzz
  and Duke's translucent sprites use this instead of CPU read-modify-write.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Synchronization — the rules that prevent corruption
text:
- **The GPU owns the framebuffer.** Render everything through the GPU or
  nothing; mixing CPU writes into a frame the GPU is drawing is the #1
  corruption source.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Synchronization — the rules that prevent corruption
text:
- Batch a frame's worth of commands, then `of_gpu_fence()` + `of_gpu_kick()`
  (or `of_gpu_submit()`); spin with `of_gpu_fence_reached(token)` /
  `of_gpu_wait(token)`; `of_gpu_finish()` is the blocking drain.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Synchronization — the rules that prevent corruption
text:
- Page flip from the GPU pipeline: `of_gpu_flip_to(idx)` returns a fence
  token; pair with `of_video_acquire_next(just_flipped_idx, token)` for
  triple buffering without tearing or stalls.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Synchronization — the rules that prevent corruption
text:
- Before the CPU reads/writes a GPU-rendered framebuffer:
  `of_gpu_prepare_framebuffer_for_cpu()`.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Synchronization — the rules that prevent corruption
text:
- Before the GPU reads CPU-written memory (textures, span payloads built
  in cached SDRAM): `of_cache_flush_range(ptr, size)`. (`of_gpu_*_upload`
  helpers handle their own coherency.)

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > Synchronization — the rules that prevent corruption
text:
- State commands are cached by the SDK (`of_gpu_set_framebuffer`,
  `of_gpu_bind_texture` skip redundant writes) — set them per draw freely.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > GPU don'ts
text:
- Don't kick per span/per column — accumulate and submit per frame or per
  render pass.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > GPU don'ts
text:
- Don't busy-wait on a fence you just emitted if you have CPU work left
  (sound mixing, game logic) — overlap it; the GPU is asynchronous.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > GPU don'ts
text:
- Don't write bulk data through the uncached SDRAM alias "to be safe" —
  it is several times slower than cached writes + `of_cache_flush_range`.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > GPU — optimizing the renderer > GPU don'ts
text:
- Don't optimize a renderer that still has bugs. Fix first (pixel-compare
  against the CPU reference renderer), then optimize. This lesson is paid
  for (PocketQuake post-mortem).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio
text:
32 hardware voices, 48 kHz output, per-voice resampling (16.16 rate),
volume ramps, loops, pan. Sample memory is plain `malloc` SDRAM —
`of_mixer_alloc_samples()` is deprecated.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > SFX
text: - `of_mixer_init(32, OF_MIXER_OUTPUT_RATE)` once.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > SFX
text:
- Use the **handle API + groups**, not raw voice indices:
  `of_mixer_alloc_for_group_h(OF_MIXER_GROUP_SFX, pcm, count, rate, pri, vol)`.
  Handles stay valid across voice stealing — `of_mixer_handle_active(h)`
  tells you whether *your* sound still owns the voice. Groups: `SFX`,
  `MUSIC`, `VOICE`, `AUX` with `of_mixer_set_group_volume()` and a master.
  Allocation scans MUSIC low→high and SFX high→low and steals within the
  same group first, so music never loses a voice to gunfire.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > SFX
text:
- Completion: `of_mixer_poll_ended_h(handles, max)` batched per frame
  (Duke3D), or `of_mixer_handle_active()` per voice (Doom), or
  `of_mixer_set_end_callback()` (ISR context — keep it tiny).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > SFX
text:
- Hot paths: `of_mixer_set_voice_h(h, rate, vol_l, vol_r)` updates a
  tracker voice in one call; `of_mixer_set_volume_ramp_h()` for clickless
  fades; `of_mixer_retrigger_h()` to restart without realloc.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > Music — pick one of three patterns
text:
1. **Streaming**: `of_audio_stream_open(rate)` + `of_audio_stream_write()`
   for gapless mono (Quake2 track music), or `of_audio_write()` stereo
   pairs against the `of_audio_free()` ring (16384 pairs).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > Music — pick one of three patterns
text:
2. **Looped mixer voices**: two voices, hard-panned L/R, with
   `of_mixer_set_loop_h()` — streamed stereo "CD audio" with zero CPU mixing
   (Quake `cd_of.c`).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > Music — pick one of three patterns
text:
3. **MIDI**: `of_midi_init()` + `of_midi_play(buf, len, loop)` with a
   `.ofsf` bank in slot 7; add `$(OF_MIDI_SRC)` to `SRCS`. The pump runs
   on the timer ISR — never call `of_midi_pump()` from the main loop
   while playing.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > Keeping audio alive
text:
`of_file_set_idle_hook(pump_fn)` — the kernel calls your hook while a
blocking file read waits on DMA, so music keeps flowing during SD/disk
access. The hook must never issue a blocking file read itself.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > HW mixer — audio > SDL ports
text:
`SDL_mixer` maps straight onto the HW mixer (`Mix_PlayChannel` →
`of_mixer_play_h`, channel groups → mixer groups) and the audio callback
is auto-pumped from `SDL_PollEvent`/`SDL_Delay`/`SDL_RenderPresent` — no
audio thread. Consequence: **call one of those regularly**; a tight loop
that skips event polling starves audio.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Input — pads and docked keyboard/mouse > Pads
text:
- `of_input_poll()` exactly once per frame (`of_input_poll_p0()` if you
  only read player 1), then edge APIs (`of_btn_pressed/released`) or
  `of_input_state(player, &s)` for analog sticks (`joy_lx/ly/rx/ry`,
  ±32767) and triggers.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Input — pads and docked keyboard/mouse > Pads
text:
- **Player 2 is free**: `of_btn_p2()` / `of_input_state(1, &s)` — the
  Pocket dock and MiSTer both deliver a second pad through the same API
  (Duke3D wires it for co-op; most ports just ignore it — don't).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Input — pads and docked keyboard/mouse > Pads
text:
- Analog: set a deadzone (`of_input_set_deadzone(4000)` is the QuakeSpasm
  value; default is 0/raw) and map sticks to look/strafe — d-pad-only
  controls waste docked controllers.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Input — pads and docked keyboard/mouse > Docked keyboard and mouse
text:
The Pocket dock reserves Player 3 for keyboard and Player 4 for mouse
reports; the SDK exposes them directly:

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Input — pads and docked keyboard/mouse > Docked keyboard and mouse
text:
Best practice (Duke3D `display_of.c`): poll pad + keyboard + mouse every
frame and merge — gamepad is the primary mapping, keyboard/mouse *enhance*
when `present` is set. Always degrade gracefully: handheld (undocked)
players see `present == 0`. MiSTer v1 reports no keyboard/mouse — another
reason the pad mapping must be complete on its own.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Input — pads and docked keyboard/mouse > SDL ports
text:
The shim exposes the pad as **both** controller events and synthesized
keyboard events (`of_to_scancode()` in `src/sdk/of_sdl2.c` is the remap
point — tweak per game). Suppress one stream with
`-DOF_SDL_NO_KEYBOARD_EVENTS` / `-DOF_SDL_NO_CONTROLLER_EVENTS` when a
game double-handles input.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Performance checklist
text:
- [ ] GPU does all framebuffer writes; CPU touches the FB only after
      `of_gpu_prepare_framebuffer_for_cpu()`.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Performance checklist
text:
- [ ] GPU commands batched per frame/pass; one kick, fences overlapped
      with CPU work.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Performance checklist
text:
- [ ] Colormap/lighting via palookup slots, translucency via the HW table —
      not CPU lookups.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Performance checklist
text:
- [ ] Hot inner loops annotated `OF_FASTTEXT` (and tables `OF_FASTDATA`) —
      ~24 KB of zero-wait-state BRAM; spend it on the rasterizer/math
      kernels, not on code that the 128 KB D-cache already serves well.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Performance checklist
text:
- [ ] Inner loops in fixed point; the FPU (`OF_HW_FPU`) is real but
      int↔float churn in span loops is not free.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Performance checklist
text: - [ ] Cached writes + `of_cache_flush_range` instead of uncached-alias writes.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Performance checklist
text:
- [ ] SFX on mixer voices, not CPU-mixed; music on stream/loop voices/MIDI;
      `of_file_set_idle_hook` keeps audio fed during loads.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Performance checklist
text:
- [ ] Frame pacing through flip fences / `of_video_acquire_next`, not
      `usleep` guesswork.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Working rules for agents
text:
1. **Fix bugs before optimizing.** Verify renderer changes against the CPU
   reference (pixel-exact where the API promises it; `make test` SDL build
   is the cheap harness).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Working rules for agents
text:
2. Touch only the game's directory in a port repo; SDK files come from
   upstream via `git pull`/`make push`.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Working rules for agents
text:
3. Keep the public `of_*` API and SDK-visible behavior stable; portability
   between Pocket and MiSTer is a hard requirement (`check-api` gate in
   the OS repo enforces the headers).

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Working rules for agents
text:
4. When adding hardware usage, gate on `of_has_feature()` and keep the
   no-feature fallback working.

head: CLAUDE.md — openfpgaOS SDK and game ports > Working rules for agents
text:
5. Platform docs live next to the code: `src/sdk/platforms/mister/README.md`
   (deploy + slot→path contract), the main `README.md` (API reference),
   `GETTING_STARTED.md`. Update them when behavior changes; don't duplicate.

head: AI usage
text:
> [!NOTE]
> The modern (as of 2026-06) AI is a misnomer,
> - it is not conscious / not a consciousness,
> - it is not sentient,
> - it is not intelligent,
> - it does not think,
> - it does not understand the code,
> - it is merely a next-token guesser,
>
> ... therefore it is merely an (hyper-) advanced IDE.

head: AI usage
text:
> [!NOTE]
> A contribution is any externally-observable interaction with a project.

head: AI usage
text:
> [!CAUTION]
> Failure to follow the following rules *may* result in repercussions,
> possibly without a prior warning.

head: AI usage
text:
1. It is acceptable to use AI when producing contributions.
> [!WARNING]
> Any and all AI usage **MUST** be fully and explicitly disclosed
> in **every** contribution.

head: AI usage
text:
2. All contributions shall be done by conscious, sentient beings.
   Fully autonomous contributions by bots are prohibited[^1].
> [!WARNING]
> Dear contributor, the AI is *your* *tool*, and its output is for *your*
> *consumption*. It is **your** responsibility to consume said output,
> interpret it, and then produce the contribution itself.
> **DO NOT** just query it and post the output,
> *especially* so for all non-code contributions!

head: AI usage

head: Revenue OS - Development Context > Data Storage
text:
All persistent data is stored in the `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/` directory supplied
by Claude Code. `plugin/scripts/core/init-session.sh` performs a copy-only, one-time
migration from legacy `~/.claude/revenue-os/` storage. It never overwrites
canonical files or deletes the legacy source; conflicts leave the migration
unmarked so a later session can retry.

head: Revenue OS - Development Context > Data Storage
text:
`safe_store.py` opens readable leaves with `O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW`, proves they
are regular files before reading, and validates each canonical JSON object's
known field shapes. The migration marker is reserved, versioned state. Reset
preflights the full tree before deletion, clears every regular saved artifact,
and rewrites the marker tombstone before recreating defaults, preventing legacy
data from returning after a reset.

head: Revenue OS - Development Context > Data Storage
text:
Reset's preflight is non-destructive: it compares two inode/metadata snapshots,
queries effective `R_OK|W_OK|X_OK` access for every open directory (including
ACL decisions), and rejects immutable/append-only flags. No unlink begins unless
the complete stable tree is removable and the root can recreate managed state.
On Darwin, each entry also receives a non-mutating kernel `accessx_np` check for
`_DELETE_OK`, covering effective `deny delete` and `deny delete_child` ACLs; an
unavailable or indeterminate ACL result fails closed. Every absolute ancestor
is held open, and a fresh no-follow traversal must match the pinned descriptor
chain and managed entry fingerprint before and after the path-based ACL query,
so an ancestor rename or replacement cannot redirect the permission decision.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project
text: `alertly` — Go HTTP service that ingests webhooks from Alertmanager and Kubewatch and forwards them to Telegram chats. Stdlib-first (`net/http` with `mux.Handle("POST /v1/...{chats}")`), no web framework.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project
text: - Module: `github.com/MaksimRudakov/alertly`

head: CLAUDE.md > Project
text: - Go: `1.25` (toolchain `go1.26.6`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Project
text: - Single binary entry: `cmd/alertly`

head: CLAUDE.md > Project
text: Treat README + `examples/config.yaml` + `TODO.md` as the source of truth for current scope. Dedup, interactive silence buttons (Phase 2b), the generic source and the `/status` chat-ops command are shipped; `TODO.md` lists the remaining Phase 2/3 items (label routing, async queue, Markdown, `/alerts` command) that are intentionally deferred until a real signal demands them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Common commands
text: `make run` requires `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN` in env. Set `DRY_RUN=true` to skip actual Telegram calls (still logs/meters); the readiness probe is force-flipped to ready in dry-run.

head: CLAUDE.md > Common commands
text: Lint config (`.golangci.yaml`) is intentionally minimal: `gofmt`, `goimports`, `govet`, `staticcheck`, `errcheck`, `ineffassign`, `unused`, `gosec` (G101/G304 enabled, G104 excluded), `revive` with `exported`/`package-comments` disabled. Tests are exempt from `gosec`/`errcheck`. Per `TODO.md`, `staticcheck` currently SIGSEGVs on Go 1.26 — the Makefile fallback path (`go vet`) is the working option until upstream releases a compatible build.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request lifecycle
text: `cmd/alertly/main.go` wires everything and starts `internal/server`. Per webhook:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request lifecycle
text: 1. `recoverMiddleware` → `requestIDMiddleware` (echoes a caller-supplied `X-Request-Id` only when it matches `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}`; anything else — control chars, spaces, non-ASCII — is replaced with a fresh UUID so callers cannot inject log noise through the echoed header) → `loggingMiddleware` (slog logger attached to ctx).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request lifecycle
text: 2. `authMiddleware` validates `Authorization: Bearer <WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN>` with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`, then `requestTimeoutMiddleware` puts an explicit deadline of `server.write_timeout - 1s` on the request context (webhook routes only). `http.Server.WriteTimeout` only arms a socket write deadline and never reaches `r.Context()`, so without this the deadline-aware retry below has nothing to check. When the budget runs out mid-payload the handler stops attempting further notifications, logs `request deadline reached`, and downgrades a would-be `200`/`204` to `207`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request lifecycle
text:
3. `webhookHandler` (handlers.go):
   - parses `{chats}` path value via `parseChatTargets` — comma-separated `chat_id[:thread_id]` (e.g. `-1001234567890,-100456:42`). When `telegram.chat_allowlist` is non-empty, any target outside it fails the whole request with `403` before anything is sent (also bounds per-chat metric cardinality and rate-limiter state, both keyed by caller-supplied chat IDs).
   - reads body through `http.MaxBytesReader(cfg.MaxBodyBytes)`.
   - calls `source.Parse(body)` → `[]notification.Notification`.
   - per notification: `renderer.Render(templateName, n)` → `telegram.SplitMessage(text, TelegramTextLimit=4096)` → `tg.SendMessage` per `(target, part)`.
   - aggregates outcome: `200` all-ok, `204` nothing sent, `207` partial, `500` all-failed; emits `alertly_notifications_received_total{source,status_code}` and `alertly_notifications_sent_total{chat_id,status}`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source plugins (`internal/source`)
text: `Source` is `Name() + Parse([]byte) → []notification.Notification`. Implementations register themselves in `cmd/alertly/main.go` into a `map[string]Source`; the route `POST /v1/{name}/{chats}` is generated from that map. Adding a new source = new file in `internal/source` + entry in the map. The `templateName` passed to the handler equals the source name (with fallback to `default` inside the renderer).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source plugins (`internal/source`)
text: `alertmanager`: standard webhook payload (max 100 alerts per request, mirroring the generic source cap — point AM's webhook `max_alerts` at or below it); severity from `labels.severity` (default `info`); title prefers `annotations.summary`, body prefers `annotations.description`; emits a Runbook link from `annotations.runbook_url` when present (Prometheus `generatorURL` is intentionally ignored — internal Prometheus links are rarely reachable from Telegram and add noise).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source plugins (`internal/source`)
text: `kubewatch`: tries new (`eventmeta`) format then legacy flat; severity becomes `warning` for `Type=Warning` or `Reason=Failed`; fingerprint is sha256-16 of `kind|namespace|name|reason|type|message` — the message is included deliberately so dedup only absorbs identical redeliveries, not distinct events on the same object.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source plugins (`internal/source`)
text: `generic`: alertly's own JSON contract (single object or array, max 100 events; `title` required, `severity` default `info`, `status` default `event`). Fingerprint falls back to a content hash (title|body|status|sorted labels) so sender retries dedup correctly. Intended for GitLab CI / Jira / ArgoCD notifications / scripts — adaptation happens on the sender side, alertly does not parse third-party schemas.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Notification → Telegram
text: `internal/notification.Notification` is the canonical struct — sources produce it, templates consume it. Templates are `text/template` (NOT `html/template`; HTML escaping is the caller's responsibility via `escape_html`). Parse mode is `HTML` (default; Markdown is Phase 2). Helpers: `severity_emoji`, `escape_html`, `truncate`, `join`, `humanize_duration`. A template named after the source is preferred; fallback is `default` (which is required to exist — config loader injects one if missing).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Notification → Telegram
text:
Splitter (`telegram/splitter.go`) measures length in **UTF-16 code units** (what Telegram counts: an astral-plane rune such as an emoji costs 2) and cuts at `

`, `
`, then space, then hard cut. `avoidTagSplit` rewinds before any unclosed `<` so a cut never lands inside a tag, and `scanTags`/`openingTags`/`closingTags` keep formatting balanced across parts: tags still open at a cut are closed at the end of the part and reopened verbatim (attributes included) at the start of the next, so Telegram never rejects a part with «Unclosed start tag». Surrogate pairs are never split. Increments `alertly_message_split_total` when split occurs.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Notification → Telegram
text: `telegram.client` does retry with exponential backoff (`MaxAttempts`, `InitialBackoff`, `MaxBackoff`). `IsRetryable`: `429` and `5xx` are retryable; `4xx` is not; non-API errors (network) retryable. On `429`, honors `parameters.retry_after` from body or `Retry-After` header (capped to `MaxBackoff`). Rate limiter (`golang.org/x/time/rate`) enforces global + per-chat caps; `Wait` blocks before each send.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Notification → Telegram
text: Retry is **deadline-aware**: before sleeping for the next backoff, the client checks `ctx.Deadline()` (set by `requestTimeoutMiddleware` from the server `WriteTimeout`). If `remaining < wait + 500ms`, retry is aborted and the current error is returned immediately, with `alertly_telegram_retries_total{reason="deadline_skip"}` incremented. Rationale: avoid the failure mode where alertly sleeps past the server `WriteTimeout`, ultimately delivers the message to Telegram on a later attempt, but the caller (Alertmanager) has already given up and will retry — producing a duplicate.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Dedup (`internal/dedup`)
text: In-process TTL cache keyed by `fingerprint|chat_id|thread_id|status`. `Reserve(key)` is the atomic check-and-insert; `Forget(key)` rolls back when no part of a multi-part message landed. Per-process state — restart re-opens the dedup window. The handler reserves once per `(notification, target)` after rendering and only forgets when *every* part for that target failed (partial successes keep the reservation so caller retries don't re-deliver the parts already in the chat). Default `enabled: true, ttl: 1h`. Metric: `alertly_dedup_skipped_total{source,chat_id,status}`. Sweeper goroutine in `cmd/alertly/main.go` runs every `min(ttl/2, 5m)`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Interactive silence buttons (`updates.*`)
text: Off by default; enabled via `updates.enabled` + `alertmanager.url`. Moving parts (all wired in `setupUpdates` in `main.go`):

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Interactive silence buttons (`updates.*`)
text: - `server.AlertmanagerKeyboard` (keyboard.go) attaches a `🔇 Silence <dur>` row to firing alertmanager notifications in allowlisted chats; buttons whose `callback_data` would exceed Telegram's 64-byte limit are skipped (a keyboard with no valid buttons is dropped).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Interactive silence buttons (`updates.*`)
text: - `server.UpdatesPoller` (updates.go) long-polls `getUpdates` (`allowed_updates=["callback_query"]`, plus `"message"` when `updates.commands.enabled`) through a dedicated keep-alive HTTP client; each callback/message is handled synchronously via `dispatch` — a 15s `HandleTimeout` so a stuck AM/Telegram call cannot stall the loop, plus a panic guard (the poller runs outside the HTTP stack, so `recoverMiddleware` does not cover it; a panicking handler is logged with its stack and the loop continues). Offset is in-memory → delivery is at-least-once.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Interactive silence buttons (`updates.*`)
text: - `server.CallbackHandler` (callback.go) validates chat/user allowlists and the `ButtonTracker` window, resolves labels (AM API → `alertmanager.LabelCache` fallback, hit/miss metered), creates the silence. Matcher scope comes from `updates.silence_matchers` (empty = all labels; zero matchers after filtering → refuse). After success the keyboard is replaced with an `↩️ Undo` button (action `u`, silence ID in the second callback field) tracked by a separate `UndoTracker` with TTL `updates.undo_window` (0 disables); pressing it calls `DeleteSilence`. `answer()` runs on a context detached from the handle budget so the user always gets feedback.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Interactive silence buttons (`updates.*`)
text: - `server.ButtonTracker` + sweeper (button_tracker.go): in-memory TTL registry of messages with live buttons, bounded by `updates.button_tracker_max` (FIFO eviction — one shared TTL means insertion order is expiry order; both the silence and undo trackers share the knob); restart or eviction invalidates old buttons (strict policy).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Interactive silence buttons (`updates.*`)
text: - `server.MessageHandler` (message.go) + `server.StatusReporter` (status.go): read-only chat-ops, gated by `updates.commands.enabled` (requires `updates.enabled`). Only `/status` (version, uptime, readiness, cache sizes via `SizeStat` closures wired in `main.go`); same chat/user allowlists as callbacks; unknown commands and non-allowlisted chats are ignored silently. Metric `alertly_commands_received_total{command,status}` (unknown commands → `command="unknown"`). With `commands.status.pipeline` (default on) the reply adds AM `GET /api/v2/status`, firing/silenced counts, a Watchdog deadman check (`watchdog_alert`, stale >15m ⇒ Prometheus suspected) and `server.ActivityTracker` timestamps (last parsed webhook / last successful send, recorded in handlers.go); each AM call is bounded by `pipeline_timeout` (default 4s) so a dead AM can't eat the callback handle budget. `ReadinessTracker.Touch()` is called by the health loop on every probe so "Last Telegram check" tracks probing, not the last readiness transition.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Interactive silence buttons (`updates.*`)
text: - `internal/alertmanager.client` retries network errors, 429 and 5xx up to 3 attempts with linear backoff (300ms step); 4xx is terminal. A duplicate silence from a retried POST is harmless (identical matchers).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Interactive silence buttons (`updates.*`)
text: - `alertmanager.LabelCache` is a TTL+FIFO map with O(1) eviction (`container/list`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Readiness model
text: `server/readyz.go` `ReadinessTracker`:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Readiness model
text: - starts unready with reason `startup: telegram getMe pending`;

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Readiness model
text: - `telegramHealthLoop` in `main.go` probes `tg.GetMe` continuously: exponential backoff until the first success (flips ready), then every minute; 3 consecutive probe failures flip unready. Probe success only re-arms probe-driven unreadiness — it never overrides the send-failure window below;

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Readiness model
text: - runtime: `RecordSendSuccess` resets a failure counter and re-arms ready; `RecordSendFailure(serverError=true)` increments and flips to unready after `readyzFailureWindow=10` consecutive failures. Server errors = Telegram 5xx **and** network-level errors; 4xx and 429 do NOT degrade readiness (caller/data problems and backpressure respectively).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Readiness model
text: `/healthz` is unconditional 200; `/readyz` returns 503 with JSON reason when not ready.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Shutdown
text: `run()` tracks every background worker (health loop, updates poller, button sweeper, dedup sweeper) in a `sync.WaitGroup`; after `srv.Run` returns it cancels the root context and waits up to `server.shutdown_timeout` for them to finish, so an in-flight silence callback completes its ack/edit instead of being cut off.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Configuration
text: `config.Load(path)` starts from `config.Default()` and overlays YAML. The HTTP server sets explicit `idle_timeout` (120s — above `read_timeout`, which is net/http's fallback, so Alertmanager keep-alives stay warm) and `read_header_timeout` (5s), plus a 64 KiB `MaxHeaderBytes` constant. Defaults are intentionally production-sane; `examples/config.yaml` is what `make run` uses. `LOG_LEVEL` env overrides `logging.level` post-parse. `Validate()` enforces non-zero timeouts/limits and valid log level/format. Hot-reload is **not** supported — restart the process.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Configuration
text: Required env: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN`. Optional: `ALERTLY_CONFIG` (default `/etc/alertly/config.yaml`), `LOG_LEVEL`, `DRY_RUN`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Metrics
text: All in `internal/metrics`. Custom registry (no default Go process collectors except those explicitly registered: `NewGoCollector`, `NewProcessCollector`). `Init()` is idempotent via `sync.Once`. Names: `alertly_notifications_{received,sent}_total`, `alertly_telegram_{api_duration_seconds,retries_total,rate_limited_total}` (the `retries_total` reason `deadline_skip` marks aborted retries), `alertly_template_render_errors_total`, `alertly_message_split_total`, `alertly_auth_failures_total`, `alertly_source_parse_duration_seconds`, `alertly_dedup_skipped_total`, `alertly_callbacks_received_total`, `alertly_commands_received_total`, `alertly_silences_created_total`, `alertly_updates_poll_errors_total`, `alertly_label_cache_lookups_total`, `alertly_build_info`. Cache sizes are exposed as on-scrape gauges (`alertly_{dedup_cache,button_tracker,label_cache}_entries`) registered from `main.go` via `metrics.RegisterSizeGauge`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo conventions
text: - `internal/` for everything; `pkg/` exists but is empty — keep it that way unless something needs to be importable by external modules.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo conventions
text: - Sources/templates/sinks are wired in `cmd/alertly/main.go` — the rest of the code is plain interfaces. When adding a webhook source, also add a same-named template entry in `examples/config.yaml`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo conventions
text: - Errors: wrap with `fmt.Errorf("%w", err)`; `telegram.APIError` carries `StatusCode` + optional `RetryAfter` and is the typed error the handler/readiness logic introspects. Telegram network errors are passed through `client.scrub` first — the bot token lives in the request path and `*url.Error` prints the full URL, so an unscrubbed error writes the credentials into the logs. Any new call path that surfaces a raw transport error must scrub it too.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo conventions
text: - Logging: `slog` with JSON handler by default; per-request logger attached to `ctx` via `loggerFrom(ctx)` — handlers should use it, not `slog.Default()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo conventions
text: - Build metadata is injected via ldflags into `internal/version` (`Version`, `Commit`, `Date`) — both Makefile and Dockerfile pass these.
