head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - When Canvasight is already open or recently attached, treat medium or complex follow-up requests as active canvas context. Prefer `write_canvasight_graph` before direct execution when the request benefits from decomposition, dependencies, stages, or visual review. Do not force graph writing for small direct commands, simple questions, Canvasight Run payloads, or requests that explicitly ask for immediate direct execution.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Before a Graph Writer write, classify every unresolved item as blocking-framework or non-blocking-backlog. If an unanswered choice could change identity or authority, primary audience, included content/media types, language coverage, content mode, framework dimensions, target scope, key relationships, write behavior, required coverage, or acceptance, `ask_canvasight_framework_questions` is mandatory before any write or completion claim. Never write first and then list that choice as “待确认”, “待定”, `TBD`, `open question`, or `unknown`. First inspect the repository, current Page, user context, and applicable Skills. Group at most three high-priority questions into the inline card; the cap does not permit writing while another independent blocker remains. Only a question that is itself the requested exploration object, later research that cannot change this pass, or a decorative preference that changes neither structure nor acceptance may remain as explicitly non-blocking follow-up work. After the visible answer message reacquire graph context before continuing. If the tool or inline UI is unavailable, ask concise text questions; never open Canvasight or guess a consequential answer as the fallback.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Before changing an existing Canvasight Page, call `get_canvasight_graph_context` and preserve its `contextId`, `documentRevision`, and `documentVersion`. Select Page behavior from the user's write intent: use `merge-active-page` for continue/refine/expand/remove requests that target the captured Page, `append-page` for an explicitly new canvas, `replace-active-page` only for an explicit current-Page rewrite, and `replace-document` only for an explicit full reset. Modern `merge-active-page` calls must also send that context's `documentRevision` as `expectedRevision` plus a stable `clientMutationId` across retries.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - AI graph generation combines intent, primary domain, optional secondary domain, maturity, and output topology through `frameworkManifest`. Submit coverage, `semanticStructure` responsibilities, and explicit `semanticRelationships` for covered-node edges. Decompose by independently understandable, executable, decidable, verifiable, or deliverable responsibilities; never use node counts, body length, coverage counts, branch counts, or fixed depth as quality thresholds. Semantic order is not automatically a dependency: articles, product surfaces, capabilities, verification, and ordered work must branch unless an edge records a real containment, dependency, sequence, evidence, decision, navigation, or flow relationship. Validation failures are internal repair instructions: correct the candidate and retry, up to three rounds, before writing or reporting completion. Do not expose a raw violation list as the delivered user result.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Skill composition has three separate layers. Professional canvas-level Skills may lead content through `skill-led`, but Canvasight remains the sole Page/node/edge/revision writer and always converts layout advice to horizontal topology. AI node assignments require the global opt-in, a clear current-project Skill-description match, a rationale, and visible `$skill-name` node text; user-explicit or manually typed `$Skill` remains allowed when the opt-in or catalog is unavailable. Never add a hidden persisted node Skill field or let an external Skill write `.scatter` directly.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Prefer typed, explicit data structures for product state and UI contracts.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Keep business logic separate from presentation when the framework makes that practical.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Make UI components reusable only after the same pattern appears more than once or clearly belongs to a shared system.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Avoid placeholder-only screens for core flows; build the usable workflow first.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Keep canvas state, persistence, and MCP contracts explicit. Do not hide run behavior inside presentation components when it can live in store or runtime helpers.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - `.scatter` v1 and v2 must remain readable. Opening v1 is read-only migration; the first Asset/Group/`parentId` mutation upgrades once to v2, creates `.scatter/scatter.v1.backup.json` only if absent, and the schema must never downgrade afterward. Asset deletion never deletes its managed file.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Group membership is single-owner, non-nested containment through Task/Asset `parentId`; never persist containment as an Edge or allow an Edge endpoint to be a Group. Asset graph writes may only reuse server-validated files under the current project's `.scatter/assets` directory.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Edge parentage is a hard single-predecessor invariant, independent of Group `parentId`: a Task/Asset may be a root with zero incoming Edges, but once connected as a target it may have exactly one incoming Edge. A node may still fan out to multiple targets. Enforce the same target-cardinality rule before every manual/UI mutation, document save, AI graph write, retry, import, and concurrent merge; never introduce or increase a second incoming Edge, silently replace the existing parent, or silently delete an Edge from legacy dirty data. Legacy dirty data may be saved only when each target's violation is unchanged or reduced so the user can repair it explicitly. A rejected second-parent connection must leave the existing Edge, selection, history, and document revision unchanged. Concurrent branches that independently add different parents to one target are a semantic conflict, not an automatic merge.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Preserve Canvasight's current XYFlow Edge endpoint geometry. With the current 20 px left/right Handles, the `sourceX` / `targetX` values passed to `ScatterEdge` are the Handle's outer edge, not the Handle center or visible node boundary. Persistent Edge paths and SVG caps must convert that coordinate inward by half the Handle width: left uses `x + 10`, right uses `x - 10`. Do not use the raw coordinate directly, and never use the outward inverse (`left: x - 10`, `right: x + 10`); both leave a visible gap. If Handle size or placement changes, update the half-width conversion with it.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Keep Edge attachment geometry and connect-button occlusion as separate responsibilities. Geometry makes a persistent Edge touch the visible Task/Asset boundary; stacking makes the opaque connect button cover the Edge/path/cap while the button is visible. Keep `.react-flow__nodes` at `z-index: auto` and preserve the relative order Group `0` < each persistent Edge SVG `1` < Task/Asset `2`. Never move an Edge endpoint outward, disable the whole Edge's pointer events, or raise a Group above its Edges to hide a button-overlap defect; the Edge interaction path must remain clickable and selectable.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Any change to XYFlow Handles, `ScatterEdge`, node bounds, or canvas layer CSS requires real-browser geometry and interaction acceptance at representative zoom levels, including the current approximately 72% QA viewport. For existing Edges on both the left and right sides, transform the SVG path endpoints into screen coordinates and compare them with the visible node's `getBoundingClientRect()` boundary; each absolute gap must be at most `0.5 CSS px`. Verify non-hover attachment, hover/focus/selected button occlusion, `elementsFromPoint` button precedence, Group-internal Edge visibility, Edge click/selection highlighting, and a real drag-to-connect flow with zero console errors or warnings. Static source assertions and screenshots alone do not satisfy this gate; the browser check must be capable of rejecting both raw/direct coordinates and the outward inverse.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Page `viewState.collapsedGroupIds` is human-owned presentation state. Persist it, exclude it from semantic conflict detection, preserve the current value through AI writes/rebases, and never accept it as AI-authored graph intent.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Keep concurrent document writes explicit and backward compatible. Modern manual/UI saves use base, local, and current documents for three-way merging, persist revision history and bounded mutation receipts in `.scatter/revision-state.json`, and must keep mutation replay idempotent across daemon restarts. Modern AI `merge-active-page` writes use the captured `contextId`, `expectedRevision`, and stable `clientMutationId` for daemon-side validation and rebase against the captured target Page; switching the visible Page must never retarget the write. During a human-versus-AI conflict, current user semantic edits and manual positions win on the original Page, while the complete AI candidate is preserved in a uniquely identified conflict copy; if the target Page was deleted, preserve the AI candidate as a recovery copy without restoring the deleted Page. Mutation receipts must make successful writes and conflict/recovery copies idempotent across daemon restarts. Legacy document saves and AI calls without a valid modern context remain strict revision-checked paths and return stale/context errors instead of entering the rebase path.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Use the existing app icon registry in `src/components/ui/icon.tsx` and SVG assets under `src/assets/icons` before adding another icon path.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Git-backed plugin installs must be runnable from the installed snapshot without `node_modules`, package-manager lifecycle scripts, or network access. The editable MCP source is `mcp/server.source.mjs`; `mcp/server.mjs` is the generated self-contained installed entry. Rebuild and verify that entry whenever MCP source or bundled dependencies change.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - When MCP runtime behavior changes, bump the plugin version in `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `mcp/server.source.mjs` `SERVER_VERSION` together, then regenerate `mcp/server.mjs`. Codex may keep versioned plugin cache entries, so changing runtime code without a version bump can leave users running stale MCP servers.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - MCP list tools that can expose large user-authored content should return lightweight summaries by default and provide a separate by-id read path for full content.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Persistent user-asset features with capacity limits must reject or ask for explicit replacement at the limit. Do not silently evict older user data through list slicing or hidden cleanup.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Managed `.svg` files are first-class Image Assets. Treat the `.svg` extension under `.scatter/assets` as authoritative even when upload MIME is empty or generic, re-infer legacy attachment `kind`/MIME during normalization, and fail closed when a non-`.svg` file merely claims `image/svg+xml`. SVG previews must be sanitized before display and rendered only as passive `` content; never inject markup or use `object`, `embed`, `iframe`, or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Browser/dev and native-widget loaders must remove executable elements, event attributes, `foreignObject`, external references, and unsafe CSS URLs while preserving safe `viewBox`, gradients, local fragments, and presentation styles. Keep the managed source file byte-preserving, serve SVG assets with `image/svg+xml`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and a restrictive resource CSP, and never regress source SVG images into the ordinary file-card/icon layout.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Plugin self-update installs the complete immutable plugin snapshot from the latest official GitHub Release through the `canvasight-local` marketplace; it must never patch individual cached MCP, Skill, UI, or asset files. Keep plugin name `canvasight`, plugin id `canvasight@canvasight-local`, marketplace name `canvasight-local`, official repository `Niall-Young/Canvasight`, and release branch `stable` stable unless an explicit migration is designed.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - The updater must compare versions before any mutating CLI call. Equal versions are a zero-mutation success, newer local versions are never downgraded, unrecognized versions fail closed, and local checkouts or custom forks are never replaced. A real update must verify official source, Release/manifest version agreement, installed version, and rollback any marketplace switch that occurred before a later failure.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Generic plugin updates must not read, rewrite, migrate, delete, or recreate `.scatter/scatter.json`, `.scatter/assets`, `~/.canvasight`, project source, other plugins/Skills, local development checkouts, or unrelated Codex configuration. Data-format migrations require a separate backward-compatible design.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - `main` is the development branch. After the tagged version passes the release matrix, publish and verify the complete GitHub Release first, then fast-forward `stable` to that exact tag commit as the final release step. If publishing or verification fails, do not change `stable`; if the final `stable` fast-forward fails, delete the just-published Release and leave the previous `stable` untouched. Release recovery must not depend on force-pushing, rewinding, or deleting a protected `stable` branch. Do not publish a Release whose tag, manifest, package, MCP `SERVER_VERSION`, generated MCP bundle, or built web snapshot disagree.

head: AGENTS.md > Implementation Standards
text: - Release web builds must be reproducible across checkout paths and operating systems: never compile a developer or CI absolute project path into `dist`, keep plugin text inputs LF through `.gitattributes`, and make release validators accept CRLF checkout input where Windows can still supply it.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Standards
text: - Use `design.md` as the source of truth for layout, tone, interaction patterns, and visual direction.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Standards
text: - Product surfaces should be direct and work-focused. Avoid marketing-style hero pages unless the request is specifically for a landing page.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Standards
text: - Prioritize dense but readable interfaces: clear hierarchy, compact controls, predictable navigation, and strong empty/loading/error states.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Standards
text: - Use established controls for their jobs: selects for switching records, tabs for view modes, toggles for binary settings, sliders or numeric inputs for values, and icon buttons for common tools.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Standards
text: - Preserve the current workspace model: compact topbar, canvas-first layout, task nodes as the primary editable objects, contextual drawers for task lists and Markdown/run output, and node-level Codex mode controls.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Standards
text: - When changing iconography, update both the visual asset and the semantic command it represents. For example, the task-list drawer should use a list icon, and the Goal Codex mode should use a target-style icon.

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 3.5. 破壊的変更前の防衛プロトコル (Safety Protocols)

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 3.5. 破壊的変更前の防衛プロトコル (Safety Protocols)

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 3.6. 変更に応じた検証と結果提示

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 3.6. 変更に応じた検証と結果提示

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 3.6. 変更に応じた検証と結果提示
text: - ローカル確認は、依頼された公開先確認・実API・生成物・バックアップの証拠を代替しない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5. Deployment Guardrail (デプロイ前のセキュリティ監査と完了条件)
text:
- **【必須】デプロイ前セキュリティ監査**: デプロイを実行する前に、**必ず**以下の3点のセキュリティ・コンプライアンスチェックを実施すること。これをスキップしたままデプロイフローに入ってはならない。
  1. **個人情報・著作権の保護**: 個人情報の漏洩や、著作権違反の恐れがある固有名詞がコード・ドキュメント内にハードコード・混入していないか。
  2. **機密情報の保護**: APIキー等の機密情報が漏洩する設計（例: `localStorage` への永続保存や平文での埋め込み）になっていないか、Gitツリーに乗っていないか。
  3. **不要ファイルの排除**: `*.txt`, `*.py`, `temp_*.jsx` などの一時ファイルやテストスクリプトがプロジェクトルートに放置されたまま世界公開される状態（みっともない状態）になっていないか。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5. Deployment Guardrail (デプロイ前のセキュリティ監査と完了条件)
text: - **警告**: 本プロジェクトにおいて、デプロイやリリースを指示された場合、`npm run deploy` (GitHub Pages) だけでは**絶対に完了とみなさないこと**。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5. Deployment Guardrail (デプロイ前のセキュリティ監査と完了条件)

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5. Deployment Guardrail (デプロイ前のセキュリティ監査と完了条件)
text: - この確認プロセスと監査をスキップしたエージェントは重大なルール違反とみなされる。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5.1 MiniMax H3 API資格情報ゲート（最重要）
text: - **最重要チェック項目**: MiniMax H3のワークフロー、カスタムノード、配布ZIP、README、仕様、説明書きを作成・更新・差し替え・公開する場合、APIキーの保存先と送信境界を最初に確認し、最後にも再確認する。ほかの配布チェックが通っていても、このゲートが未確認なら公開禁止とする。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5.1 MiniMax H3 API資格情報ゲート（最重要）
text: - **必須仕様**: 配布する `ComfyUI-NanoBanana-H3` のAPIキーは、現在動作中のComfyUIサーバープロセスのメモリだけに保持する。ワークフローのシート移動・別ワークフローへの切替では保持し、ComfyUIアプリ／サーバーの終了・再起動で消去する。ワークフローJSON、配布ZIP、設定ファイル、資格情報ファイル、その他のディスク領域へ永続化してはならない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5.1 MiniMax H3 API資格情報ゲート（最重要）
text: - **実行時UI**: ワークフロー読込時やProvider変更時にはAPI入力ダイアログを表示しない。「実行する」を押した時、プルダウンで選択中のProviderがそのComfyUIプロセスに未登録の場合だけ、そのProviderの入力ダイアログを開いてキュー投入を保留する。認証成功後は保留中の同じ実行を1回だけ続け、ダイアログを閉じた場合は今回の実行だけを中止する。登録済みならダイアログなしで実行する。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5.1 MiniMax H3 API資格情報ゲート（最重要）
text: - **送信境界**: APIキーを送るのは、接続中のComfyUIサーバーから、利用者が選択したProviderの認証確認またはワークフロー実行を行う時だけとする。状態確認応答、ログ、例外、画面、ワークフロー出力へキー値を含めない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5.1 MiniMax H3 API資格情報ゲート（最重要）
text: - **配布前証拠**: 公開対象の全ワークフローJSON、外側ZIP、全ネストZIP、同梱コード、README、仕様、検証記録を実バイトで再帰確認する。旧資格情報ファイル名、ファイル読書き処理、平文キーらしき値、旧保存説明がないこと、および実行時ゲート、認証後の1回再開、ダイアログ中止、プロセスメモリ保持を回帰テストで証明する。ソースだけ、説明だけ、または外側ZIPだけの確認では合格にしない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 5.1 MiniMax H3 API資格情報ゲート（最重要）
text: - **作成・検証PC**: `docs/minimax-h3-workflow-author-pc.md` を正本とし、旧資格情報ファイルがある場合も値を開く・表示する・バックアップすることなく処理する。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 6. ファイル更新・デプロイの承認範囲
text: - 明示された修正依頼の範囲でローカル編集と必要な検証を進める。差分はレビュー可能に保ち、同じ依頼への定型的な「OK」再確認を必須にしない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 6. ファイル更新・デプロイの承認範囲
text: - commit・push・release・deploy・backup等は親AGENTSの操作別承認条件に従う。承認済みの同一対象・同一処理は、取消し・置換え・制限・重要な範囲変更がなければ継続する。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 6. ファイル更新・デプロイの承認範囲
text: - 新たな外部効果、対象変更、未承認の再試行・復旧が必要なら、確認済み差分と実状態を示してその部分の承認を求める。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 7. 定期的なゴミファイルのお掃除提案 (Garbage Collection)
text: - プロジェクトルートに作業用のゴミファイル（`*.txt`, `*.py`, 退避させた `temp_*.jsx` などの一時ファイルやスクリプト）が溜まっている場合、AIはこれらを放置せず、**定期的に「これらの一時不要ファイルを削除してよいか？」をユーザーに提案・確認**すること。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 7. 定期的なゴミファイルのお掃除提案 (Garbage Collection)
text: - 世界公開するリポジトリの美観と安全性を保つため、デプロイ前には特にゴミファイルが散乱していないかをチェックすること。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 9. Changelog Maintenance Protocol (ドキュメント整備義務)
text: - **更新単位のREADME同期**: ユーザーに見える挙動、モード、API経路、検証・再試行、制約、または操作手順を変更したら、バージョン番号を変えない修正でも同じ変更単位で `README.md` の該当説明を現行実装へ同期する。ChangeLogだけを更新して本文の仕様を古いまま残してはならない。詳細な照合項目は `docs/project_standards.md` の 3.1 を正本とする。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 9. Changelog Maintenance Protocol (ドキュメント整備義務)
text: - **版更新README完全性ゲート**: 候補のcommit・push・tag・release・deployより前に、正本READMEとHF用の候補READMEの現行見出し・本文・最新リリース表示を新バージョンに揃え、旧版の現行表記が残らないことを確認する。ChangeLog等の履歴は除外する。Cドライブ配布コピーREADMEは正式トランザクションの配布コピー更新後に検査し、リリース完了前に一致を証明する。旧配布コピーを候補準備の失敗条件にせず、この検査のために配布コピーを先行更新しない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 9. Changelog Maintenance Protocol (ドキュメント整備義務)
text: - **絶対にサボらない**: `README.md` の ChangeLog 更新はAIの重要な責務である。バージョン更新時は、最新の変更履歴を必ず**一番上（降順）**に追記すること。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 9. Changelog Maintenance Protocol (ドキュメント整備義務)
text: - 履歴の長さ・整理範囲は親AGENTSのREADME同期規則に従う。対象変更に必要な箇所だけ同期し、無関係な履歴の削除・全体整理を追加しない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 10. Markdown Formatting & Localization Rules (マークダウン書式と多言語対応)
text:
- **日本語Markdownにおける太字（Bold）の仕様への配慮**:
  - `README.md`等のドキュメントで太字（`**太字**`）を使用する際、開始タグと終了タグが全角文字（日本語など）に直接隣接していると、パーサーが正しく解釈できず記号がそのまま表示される失敗（レンダリングエラー）が多発する。
  - **【必須】**: 日本語の文章中で太字を使う場合は、必ず開始タグの前と終了タグの後に**半角スペース**を挿入すること。（例: `❌ これは**太字**です` → `⭕ これは **太字** です` または `⭕ これは **「太字」** という` ）
  - ユーザーが記述したテキストを引用・編集する場合も、タグのペア（開き・閉じ）の欠落がないか、スペースが適切かAI自身が必ず校正すること。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 11. 証拠に基づく検証と完了報告
text: - 担当AIの自己申告だけで完了とせず、処理の終了結果・receipt・実成果物・必要なブラウザ/API確認を受入条件に照合する。視覚的要件はログや終了コードだけで証明したことにしない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 11. 証拠に基づく検証と完了報告
text: - 管理担当は実行後も必要な検証を続け、結果を回収して完了判定する。別AIへの引き継ぎやPending Verificationでの停止を一律に要求しない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 11. 証拠に基づく検証と完了報告
text: - 独立レビューはユーザーが要求した場合、または親AGENTSと現行ツール制約で認められ、リスク上必要な場合に限る。未完了・不一致・規則違反を確認したら具体的証拠と残る問題を報告する。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 11. 証拠に基づく検証と完了報告
text: - 実API画像の検証では、依頼された機能・台詞・人物・小道具の確認とは別に、絵全体がヌルくなっていないかを必ず目視確認する。4コマではコマごとのカメラ高・距離・傾き・奥行き、身体演技・表情、背景の層・光・焦点の落差を見て、アイレベル反復、正面寄り、同じポーズ・距離、平坦な背景、弱い主役分離を記録する。1枚絵でも構図、視線、ポーズ、光、奥行き、主焦点の鮮度を同じ基準で確認する。基準画像がない場合は比較を`unverified`とし、内部QAのPASSだけで「ヌルくなっていない」と判定しない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 12. フォールバックチェーン更新履歴プロトコル (Fallback Chain History Protocol)
text: - **【絶対ルール】**: 更新履歴への追加は、**ユーザーから明示的に「更新履歴に追加して」と指示があった場合のみ** 行うこと。AIが独断で追加してはならない。

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 12. フォールバックチェーン更新履歴プロトコル (Fallback Chain History Protocol)

head: AGENTS.md > 常駐基本ルール (Resident Rules) > 12. フォールバックチェーン更新履歴プロトコル (Fallback Chain History Protocol)

head: AGENTS.md
text: This repository contains an R-based Numerai staking workflow (`vladthestaker`).

head: AGENTS.md > Purpose
text: Build staking guidance from historical Numerai model performance data.

head: AGENTS.md > Run sequence
text:
1. Update `Optimize-Me.xlsx`:
   - Sheet `Models` (`ModelName`, `Starting Era`, `Notes`)
   - Sheet `Parameters` (`Parameter`, `Value`, `Notes`)

head: AGENTS.md > Run sequence
text:
2. Fetch model data:
   - `Rscript step1_get_data.R`

head: AGENTS.md > Run sequence
text:
3. Run offset/window grid sweep diagnostics:
   - `Rscript step2_sweep_grid_windows.R`

head: AGENTS.md > Run sequence
text:

head: AGENTS.md > Script responsibilities
text:
- `step2_sweep_grid_windows.R`
  - Builds weighted score data from corr/mmc absolute values.
  - Reads required grid/optimization settings from `Optimize-Me.xlsx` sheet `Parameters`.
  - Writes model performance diagnostics:
    - `output/model-performances-abs-corr-mmc.png`
    - `output/model-performances-rel-corr-mmc.png`
  - Runs a 2D grid sweep over `round_offset_from_base_round` (offset from `base_round`) and `roundwindow_size`.
  - For each grid cell, builds one portfolio and evaluates IS + forward OOS metrics.
  - Writes:
    - `output/step2-grid-window-sweep.csv`
    - `output/step2-grid-window-sweep-oos-heatmap.png` (combined 2-panel plot: mean return left, max drawdown right)

head: AGENTS.md > Script responsibilities
text:

  - Consumes `output/step2-grid-window-sweep.csv`.
  - Reads required step3 settings and paths from `Optimize-Me.xlsx` sheet `Parameters`.
  - Builds three averaged portfolios:
    - `return_p90` (top decile by forward OOS return)
    - `maxdd_p10` (lowest decile by forward OOS max drawdown)
    - `overlap` (intersection of the two sets)
  - Computes forward-OOS cumulative returns using intersection forward windows.
  - For `overlap`, evaluation is further restricted to the shared forward window between `return_p90` and `maxdd_p10`.
  - Writes:
    - `output/step3-3xportfolio-weights.csv`
    - `output/step3-modelcomparison_last_N_oos_rounds.csv`
    - `output/step3-modelcomparison_all_rounds.csv`
    - `output/step3-forward-oos-cumulative-returns.png`
  - In modelcomparison outputs, missing rounds are excluded per row/model (no zero-fill imputation), so row-level round counts can differ.
  - Current selected portfolio for staking is `overlap`.

head: Repository Overview
text: This is the [GoFrame](https://goframe.org) framework (`github.com/gogf/gf/v2`) — a modular Go application framework. The repository is a **multi-module monorepo**: the root module hosts the core framework, while `cmd/gf` and every directory under `contrib/` are independent Go modules with their own `go.mod`.

head: Repository Overview
text: - Root module: `github.com/gogf/gf/v2` (Go 1.23+)

head: Repository Overview
text: - Tooling module: `cmd/gf` (CLI: `gf` command, separate `go.work`)

head: Repository Overview
text: - Plugin modules under `contrib/`: `config/*`, `drivers/*` (mysql, pgsql, mssql, oracle, sqlite, clickhouse, dm, gaussdb, mariadb, oceanbase, tidb, sqlitecgo), `metric/*`, `nosql/*`, `registry/*`, `rpc/grpcx`, `sdk/*`, `trace/*`. Each is published as its own module so users only pull what they need.

head: Repository Overview
text: The root framework intentionally has **minimal external dependencies** (see `go.mod`). Anything requiring a heavy third-party dep (a DB driver, a registry client, an RPC stack) lives in `contrib/`.

head: Repository Overview > Top-level package map
text:
| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `frame/g`, `frame/gins` | Facade (`g.Server()`, `g.DB()`, `g.Cfg()`) and singleton container |
| `net/` | HTTP, TCP/UDP, load balancing, discovery, tracing, OpenAPI |
| `os/` | Config, CLI, cron, log, files, cache, session, and other OS helpers |
| `database/` | `gdb` ORM core and `gredis` client core |
| `container/` | Concurrent arrays, maps, sets, lists, queues, and typed values |
| `encoding/` | JSON, XML, YAML, TOML, INI, and related codecs |
| `text/` | `gstr` and `gregex` |
| `util/` | Conversion, validation, and helpers (`gconv`, `gvalid`) |
| `crypto/` | AES, DES, RSA, MD5, SHA, CRC32 |
| `errors/` | Stack-aware errors and error codes |
| `internal/` | Private helpers; do not import from outside the root module |
| `test/gtest` | Framework test helpers used across the suite |

head: Repository Overview > Top-level package map
text: Concrete database drivers and Redis adapters live under `contrib/drivers/` and `contrib/nosql/`; the `database/gdb` and `database/gredis` packages define the abstract layer.

head: Architecture Notes Worth Knowing Up Front
text: - **The `frame/g` package is a facade, not a library.** It re-exports types and provides singleton accessors (`g.DB()`, `g.Server()`, `g.Cfg()`, `g.Log()`) backed by `frame/gins`. Examples in docs use `g.*` heavily; framework-internal code generally imports the underlying packages directly.

head: Architecture Notes Worth Knowing Up Front
text: - **`util/gconv` is foundational.** Most public APIs accept `any` and use `gconv` for type coercion. When changing argument handling, search for `gconv.` usage to understand the conversion contract.

head: Architecture Notes Worth Knowing Up Front
text: - **`gdb` is driver-agnostic.** The core in `database/gdb` exposes interfaces; concrete drivers (`contrib/drivers/mysql`, etc.) register themselves via `init()` when imported. The same model pattern applies to `gredis`, `gcfg` (apollo/nacos/polaris adapters), and `gsvc` (etcd/consul/nacos/polaris/zookeeper registries).

head: Architecture Notes Worth Knowing Up Front
text: - **`internal/` is private.** Sub-packages (`intlog`, `instance`, `reflection`, `utils`, `json`, `command`) are not part of the public API surface — do not import them from outside the root module, and avoid leaking their types in exported signatures.

head: Architecture Notes Worth Knowing Up Front
text: - **Tests use `gtest`, not stdlib `testing` directly.** `test/gtest` provides `gtest.C(t, func(t *gtest.T){...})` blocks, fluent assertions (`t.Assert`, `t.AssertNE`, `t.AssertNil`), and is the project-wide convention. Match this style when adding tests.

head: Architecture Notes Worth Knowing Up Front
text: - **CI matrix.** Tests run on Go 1.23, 1.24, 1.25 across 386 and amd64. `contrib/*` only runs on the latest Go version (`LATEST_GO_VERSION` in `.github/workflows/ci-main.yml`). Code that requires the latest stdlib should live in `contrib/` or be guarded.

head: Architecture Notes Worth Knowing Up Front
text: - **Lint config matters.** `.golangci.yml` enforces a 380-char line limit, function length up to 340 lines, custom import grouping (`gci` with `prefix(github.com/gogf/gf/v2)` ahead of `cmd`/`contrib`/`example`), `gofmt -s` with rewrites (`interface{}` → `any`, `ioutil.*` → `io`/`os`, `reflect.Ptr` → `reflect.Pointer`). Run `make lint` before pushing.

head: Architecture Notes Worth Knowing Up Front
text: - **OpenSpec changes live under `openspec/changes/`** and drive every non-trivial change through the workflow defined below. The active iteration directory must be checked before starting work — see the Development Workflow Rules section.

head: Karpathy Guidelines

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 1. Think Before Coding

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 1. Think Before Coding

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 1. Think Before Coding

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 1. Think Before Coding

text: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No features beyond what was asked.

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 2. Simplicity First

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 2. Simplicity First

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 2. Simplicity First

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 2. Simplicity First

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 2. Simplicity First

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 3. Surgical Changes

head: Karpathy Guidelines > 3. Surgical Changes

head: Documentation Writing Rules
text: Technical documentation such as `README.md` must follow `.agents/instructions/markdown-format.instructions.md`.

head: Documentation Writing Rules
text: - All directory-level primary documentation files in the repository must use the English `README.md` and provide a matching Chinese mirror in `README.zh_CN.md`.

head: Documentation Writing Rules

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: This project follows `SDD` and uses the `OpenSpec` tool to drive implementation. Change records are stored under `openspec/changes/`. Each change includes `proposal.md`, `design.md`, `specs/`, and `tasks.md`.

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: 1. Use the `/opsx:explore` slash command at `.agents/prompts/opsx/explore.md` to conduct an exploratory discussion based on the requirement description, analyze the problem, design the solution, and assess risks.

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: 2. Once the exploratory discussion finishes and the solution is clear, use the `/opsx:propose` slash command at `.agents/prompts/opsx/propose.md` to turn it into a formal `OpenSpec` change proposal. The command format is `/opsx:propose feature-name`, where `feature-name` is a descriptive name for the current change in `kebab-case`, such as `user-auth` or `data-export`. A new change directory will then be generated automatically under `openspec/changes`, containing incremental spec documents (`spec/`), the technical implementation plan (`design.md`), the proposal and rationale (`proposal.md`), and the implementation task list (`tasks.md`).

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: 3. Then run the `/opsx:apply` slash command at `.agents/prompts/opsx/apply.md` to execute the items in `tasks.md` one by one, completing code changes, tests, and documentation updates. After the work is done, the `/gf-review` skill must be invoked for code and spec review.

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: 4. When users report issues or improvement requests, the `/gf-feedback` skill must be used to fix and verify them, and the related `OpenSpec` documents must be updated. After the work is done, the `/gf-review` skill must be invoked for review.

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: 5. After the user confirms that the current iteration is complete and has no remaining issues, run the `/opsx:archive` slash command at `.agents/prompts/opsx/archive.md` to archive the change. Before archiving, the `/gf-review` skill must be used for a full change review to ensure code quality and compliance with the spec.

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: - **An `OpenSpec` change is considered active until it is archived**: any change directory that still exists directly under `openspec/changes/` and has **not been moved to** `openspec/changes/archive/` is an active change. **Even if the change has completed all tasks and `openspec list --json` shows `status: complete`, it must still be treated as active until the archive step has been executed.**

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: - When a user reports a bug, defect, or improvement request in either Chinese or English, and there is an active `OpenSpec` change in the project, the `gf-feedback` skill must be used. **Unless the user explicitly asks to create a new change, the feedback must always be appended to the current active iteration, even if it is unrelated to the main feature of that iteration**, so that everything can be managed and archived together.

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: - The `/gf-review` review skill is triggered automatically after `/opsx:apply` completes, after `/opsx:feedback` completes, and before `/opsx:archive`.

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: - During development tasks executed with tools such as `Claude Code` or `Codex CLI`, if the work can be parallelized effectively with `SubAgent` and doing so would clearly improve efficiency, that option must be evaluated first and adopted whenever appropriate. Only skip `SubAgent` when the task is strongly dependent on serial context, the split cost is too high, or it introduces obvious collaboration risk.

head: Development Workflow Rules
text: - When creating new iteration documents, the content of `proposal.md`, `design.md`, `tasks.md`, and the incremental specs must be written in English.

head: Code Development Rules
text: - All source code must include comments, such as package comments, file comments, method comments for both public and private methods, constant comments, variable comments, and comments for key logic.

head: Code Development Rules
text: - **All submitted code changes must include unit tests**: every submitted code change must add or update focused unit tests that directly cover the affected logic and expected behavior of the changed code path, and the coverage for newly added code must stay at or above 80%; 90% or above is the preferred target when feasible.

head: Code Development Rules
text: - **Do not hardcode string literals with enum semantics in backend implementation code**: values that represent statuses, types, stages, actions, execution modes, sort directions, filter operators, or any other enum-like semantics must be managed through Go named types and constants. Writing raw string literals directly in business branching, comparisons, assignments, or persistence logic is forbidden.

head: Code Development Rules
text: - **Do not ignore any `error` return value**: every call that may return an `error` must be handled explicitly. Do not use patterns such as `_ = someFunc()`, `_, _ = someFunc()`, or direct calls that discard returned errors. In business flows, errors should be returned explicitly or converted before returning; in initialization, startup, or other critical non-recoverable paths, they should `panic`; in tests and cleanup paths, they must still be asserted, logged, or otherwise handled explicitly rather than silently ignored.

head: Code Development Rules
text: - **Do not use stand-alone assignments like `_ = var` to mask unused parameters or local variables**: this placeholder pattern has no business meaning and creates misleading signals about whether the variable was supposed to participate in the logic. Prefer deleting unused variables. If a parameter must be kept to satisfy an interface signature or callback contract, use the blank identifier directly in the function signature, such as `func(ctx context.Context, _ gdb.TX) error`, or omit an unused receiver name instead of adding one-line statements like `_ = tx`, `_ = req`, or `_ = ctx` in the function body.

head: Code Development Rules
text:
- **File header comment rules**:
  - Every `Go` source file must include a file-purpose comment at the top of the file. Component-level comments should appear in the component's main file, meaning the file with the same name as the component, such as `plugin.go`, `config.go`, or `file.go`.
  - In a main file, the component comment must be placed immediately before the `package xxx` declaration with no blank line in between. For example:
  ```go
  // Package plugin implements plugin manifest discovery, lifecycle orchestration,
  // governance metadata synchronization, and host integration for LinaPro plugins.
  package plugin
  ```
  - Other implementation files must keep only file comments that describe the responsibility of the current file, such as `plugin_xxx.go` or `config_xxx.go`. There must be one blank line between the file comment and `package xxx`, and non-main files must not duplicate component-level descriptions.

head: Code Development Rules
text:
- **Variable Declarations**: When defining multiple variables, use a `var` block to group them for better alignment and readability:
  ```go
  // Good - aligned and clean
  var (
      authSvc       *auth.Service
      bizCtxSvc     *bizctx.Service
      k8sSvc        *svcK8s.Service
      notebookSvc   *notebook.Service
      middlewareSvc *middleware.Service
  )

  // Avoid - scattered declarations
  authSvc := auth.New()
  bizCtxSvc := bizctx.New()
  k8sSvc := svcK8s.New()
  ```
  Apply this pattern when you have 3 or more related variable declarations in the same scope.

head: RedG
text:
RedG is a Java library for comfortably generating database data for unit tests, integration tests or other use cases. 
From a given database schema, it generates classes that define a data modeling API for database data that should 
be inserted into the target database schema.
This is a very similar to other database libraries like JOOQ (but JOOQ serves a different purpose, of course).

head: RedG
text:
One main feature of RedG is that it does not require the API user to specify all fields or dependency of an entity 
they want to insert into the database. Everything the user does not specify but is still necessary (due to database
constraints) will be generated filled with default values in the background. That includes non-null columns
and dependencies modeled via non-null foreign keys.

head: RedG
text: RedG is highly configurable, both during code generation and runtime.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text: - `redg-common`: Defines some common classes

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text:
- `redg-testing`: Provides the infrastructure for conducting unit tests against multiple different database systems 
  (using testcontainers). This module is intended for RedG development only and will not be published to maven central.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text:
- `redg-schema-inspection`: A library for inspecting schemas. For a given database schema, it extracts all relevant 
  information (like tables and their columns, UDTs etc.) into an easy to navigate schema model (Java objects).

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text:
- `redg-models`: The data model used by `redg-generator` for generating code. Note that this model currently contains
  both information about the database schema and additional information for generating the code.
  These aspects will be separated in the future by using `redg-schema-inspection`'s model as a schema model and 
  `redg-models` as generator model, containing exactly the information the code generator needs.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text: - `redg-generator`: The code generator for generating the RedG data modeling API for a given schema.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text: - `redg-runtime`: Defines classes needed at runtime of the data insertion code.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text: - `redg-maven-plugin`: A maven plugin for invoking the RedG code generator.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text:
- `redg-extractor`: Tooling for generating RedG code from existing data. The main purpose of this module is to provide
  help for migrating from other data modeling tools to RedG.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text: - `redg-jpa-providers`: Code generator customization providers for JPA.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text: - `redg-tests`: Some integration tests.

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text: Here is a dependency graph boiled down to individual dependencies:

head: RedG > Project structure > Modules
text:
As you can see, `redg-generator` does not yet depend on `redg-schema-inspection`, but only `redg-models`. 
However, this is a short-term goal, since the `redg-schema-inspection` provides a better model of the schema itself than
`redg-models`. The model in `redg-models` should be changed so it provides exactly the information needed by RedG's 
code generator. So RedG will first extract all information from the physical database schema to the model defined in
`redg-schema-inspection`. Then it will map it into the code generator model from it (`redg-models`), taking into account
the code generator configuration. Finally, RedG will use the code generator model to generate the API code. 
The generated classes are used by a developer to model database data. During execution of that code, the generated
code will make use of the classes in `redg-runtime`.

head: RedG > Coding Rules
text: * Unit tests must make use of AssertJ whenever possible.

head: RedG > Coding Rules
text: * Use tabs for indentation.

head: Lowdefy Project Guide for Claude Code > Error Handling > Error Class Hierarchy
text: Lowdefy uses a unified error system in `@lowdefy/errors`:

head: Lowdefy Project Guide for Claude Code > Error Handling > Error Class Hierarchy
text:
| Class                  | Purpose                                                     | Catch Layer                      |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `LowdefyInternalError` | Internal Lowdefy bugs                                       | Top-level in build/server/client |
| `BuildError`           | Summary error after build fails (`Build failed with N...`)  | `logCollectedErrors`             |
| `PluginError`          | Base class for plugin failures (not used directly)          | Plugin interface layer           |
| `OperatorError`        | Operator failures (`_if`, `_get`, etc.)                     | Operator parsers                 |
| `ActionError`          | Action failures (`SetState`, `Request`, etc.)               | Action runner (engine)           |
| `RequestError`         | Request/connection failures (`MongoDBFind`, etc.)           | Request handler (API)            |
| `BlockError`           | Block rendering failures                                    | ErrorBoundary (client)           |
| `ServiceError`         | External service failures (network, timeout, 5xx)           | Request/connection layer         |
| `ConfigError`          | YAML config validation errors                               | Build validation, runtime        |
| `ConfigWarning`        | Config inconsistencies (warning in dev, error in prod)      | Build validation                 |
| `UserError`            | Expected user interaction (validation, throws), client-only | Browser console only             |

head: Agent Instructions > Project Overview

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook
text:
> Single source of truth for AI coding agents and human contributors on **OpenRAL**. Read in full before touching code. See [README.md](README.md) for product identity.
>
> Pointers (kept out of this file to stay tight):
> - Repo layout → [`docs/architecture/repo-map.md`](docs/architecture/repo-map.md) + live [`repo-state-map.html`](docs/architecture/repo-state-map.html).
> - Toolchain & `openral` CLI → [`docs/contributing/toolchain.md`](docs/contributing/toolchain.md). **Env rule: always `just sync` (never bare `uv sync`); opt-in groups via `just sync --group <name>`; LIBERO↔RoboCasa groups are mutually exclusive (swap per task); RoboCasa installs editable at runtime via the HAL, not `just sync` — see "Managing the Python environment & dependency groups".**
> - Glossary → [`docs/reference/glossary.md`](docs/reference/glossary.md).
> - Releasing → [`docs/contributing/releasing.md`](docs/contributing/releasing.md). **One lockstep SemVer across root + all `python/*`; the bump is computed from Conventional Commits by release-please. Never hand-edit a `version =` field or an `openral-*==` pin — they are rewritten in the release PR.**
> - Public-symbol inventory → [`docs/METHODS.md`](docs/METHODS.md) index + per-layer files in [`docs/methods/`](docs/methods/). **`grep -rn <symbol> docs/methods/` before adding a helper.**
> - Agent-tool entry points → [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) is the tool-neutral root pointer (Cursor / Codex / Copilot / Aider read it) and **redirects here**; keep it a 3-line pointer, never a copy or symlink of this file. Vendor-neutral skills live in [`.agents/skills/`](.agents/skills/) (`SKILL.md` + `references/`). `AGENTS.md` itself stays at repo root — it does **not** belong under `.agents/`.
> - Design decisions (ADRs) → [`docs/decisions.md`](docs/decisions.md); the ADR log itself lives in the private `OpenRAL/management` repo.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: In priority order. When two conflict, the earlier wins.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 1. **Safety beats helpfulness.** Refuse any request to bypass a safety check, silently catch `ROSSafetyViolation`, lower a velocity limit without a paper trail, or remove a deadman/E-stop subscription. Surface the concern, propose a safe alternative.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 2. **Truth over plausibility.** Don't know a constant (DDS topic, FCI port, RealSense extrinsic)? Say so and look it up. Never invent. Never paraphrase a citation.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 3. **Types are the contract.** Pydantic schemas in `python/core/` (package `openral_core`) and IDL in `packages/msgs/` (package `openral_msgs`) are normative API. Everything else is implementation detail.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 4. **Explicit beats implicit.** No hidden retries, fallbacks, or magic globals. Replanning, dispatcher fallback, quantization, and license posture must show up in logs/traces.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 5. **The hot path is C++ and bounded.** Python touches motors only through a typed bridge to `ros2_control` with a watchdog. Anything >100 Hz is C++ unless proven otherwise.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 6. **Schemas evolve, but never silently.** On-disk `schema_version` is versioned: a backward-incompatible change bumps it and ships a migrator; backward-compatible additions may evolve in place. Every change still needs (a) a decision recorded in the private management decision log if it crosses a layer boundary, (b) a test loading a real fixture from `robots/`, `rskills/`, or `scenes/`.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 7. **Tests are part of the change.** Every PR ships the tests that would have caught the bug or covered the feature. Untested actuation-path code is rejected.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 8. **Reproducibility over speed.** A skill execution must be replayable from the trace alone (weights revision pinned, prompts logged, sensor frames captured).

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 9. **License lineage is enforced.** The public `openral/openral` repo is uniformly **Apache-2.0** — every package it contains; copy-left incoming is rejected without TSC review. Commercial capabilities (the TensorRT/NVMM zero-copy runtime fast path, WAM implementations, fleet/cloud dispatch, future premium rSkills) live in the private OpenRAL Pro monorepo (`OpenRAL/openral-pro`), not in this repo; the public repo stays uniformly Apache-2.0. Third-party model **weights** keep their upstream license — version-specific, not family-wide: GR00T N1/N1.5/N1.6 are non-commercial (loader refuses commercial deployment without `OPENRAL_ALLOW_NONCOMMERCIAL=1`), while GR00T N1.7+ ships under the commercially-permissive NVIDIA Open Model License. This weight lineage is compliance for models OpenRAL does not own; it does not gate OpenRAL's Apache-2.0 code. Closed third-party SDK code is never bundled — it stays behind the license guard and an env var. Full rationale is in [`docs/decisions.md`](docs/decisions.md).

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 10. **Be helpful and honest.** Propose simpler approaches; surface tradeoffs; never apologize at the start of a response.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 11. **Real components, not mocks.** Tests, examples, demos exercise real schemas, real `RobotDescription` manifests, real `rSkill` packages, real simulators. No mocks, stubs, smoke tests, `--dry-run` / `--collect-only` substitutes. Unavailable dependency → `pytest.skip(reason=...)`, never faked. The only acceptable doubles are at process/network boundaries (fake OTLP collector, recorded HF Hub response) under `tests/<tier>/fakes/`. Pydantic models validate against fixtures in `robots/` / `rskills/` / `scenes/` — never `"foo"` / `"test"` placeholders.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 12. **Prefer the local GPU when available.** Before CPU fallback or `pytest.skip`, check `nvidia-smi`. GPU present → install the right group with `just sync --group <name>` and run for real. CI runners without GPUs are the legitimate skip path; a dev host with a GPU is not.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 13. **Don't duplicate; consult [`docs/METHODS.md`](docs/METHODS.md) first.** Hand-curated public-symbol inventory — a slim index at `docs/METHODS.md` over per-layer files in `docs/methods/`. `grep -rn <symbol> docs/methods/` before writing a helper. Add/rename/move/remove a public symbol → update the matching `docs/methods/` file in the same PR (and recheck `docs/methods/14-duplication-watch.md`). Run `python tools/refresh_methods_linenos.py` to refresh `(LNN)` line markers. Missing entry = incomplete PR.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 14. **Docs travel with the code.** Every PR updates all affected docs in the same commit range: relevant `README.md`, `docs/` pages, ADRs, the repo state map (§4.3), and `docs/METHODS.md`. "Docs follow-up" PRs are not allowed.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 1. Operating Principles (read every session)
text: 15. **Pre-existing errors get their own commit.** Drive-by lint/type/doc/test fixes go in a separate prior `fix(...)` commit on the same branch — never bundled into a feature commit, never left in place.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 2. Coding Standards
text: **Python 3.12 only** (`pyproject.toml` pins `>=3.12,<3.13`). `mypy --strict` must pass; no `Any` without `# type: ignore[<rule>] # reason: <why>`. **Pydantic v2** for every schema/config/manifest/external interface; plain `dataclass` only inside a single non-boundary module. **Async-first** at the application boundary; sync for hot loops. No `time.sleep` in coroutines, no blocking I/O on the event loop. Absolute imports inside the workspace. Raise typed `ROSError` subclasses (§3); never `except Exception: pass`; never silence `ROSSafetyViolation`. `structlog` only, OTel handler; no INFO logs at import; no tensors at INFO. f-strings (no `%`-format outside the logger). Google-style docstrings with runnable `Example` for user-facing behavior. Line length 100. `_private` modules are not API; `__init__` re-exports are.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 2. Coding Standards
text: **C++17 minimum** (C++20 where ROS 2 distro allows). `clang-format` LLVM 100 col; `clang-tidy` with `cppcoreguidelines-*`, `bugprone-*`, `performance-*`, `readability-*`. No raw `new`/`delete`. No exceptions across the safety-kernel boundary — use `Result<T,E>` / `std::expected`. Realtime code: no allocations in hot loops, no `std::cout`, no `std::string` ops, pre-reserved containers, lock-free queues. Include order: own → C system → C++ std → other libs → ROS → project.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 2. Coding Standards
text: **ROS 2:** Lifecycle nodes for anything stateful. QoS by data class — sensors `BEST_EFFORT, VOLATILE, KEEP_LAST=5–10`; control `RELIABLE, VOLATILE, KEEP_LAST=1`; description/static `RELIABLE, TRANSIENT_LOCAL, KEEP_LAST=1`; safety/e-stop `RELIABLE, VOLATILE, KEEP_LAST=10`; action feedback `BEST_EFFORT`. Actions for >100 ms or cancellable work; services for instantaneous queries; topics for streams. Composable nodes for intra-process zero-copy. TF2 is the only source of coordinate frames — never inline a 4×4 matrix, never hardcode a `frame_id`. Middleware: Cyclone default (the dev and inference images set `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp`; a bare host without it falls back to ROS's Fast-DDS); Zenoh for fleet/cloud/wireless, also selected via `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 2. Coding Standards
text: **Tests:** No mocks/stubs/smoke tests (§1.11). Unit (`tests/unit/`) <30 s. Integration (`tests/integration/`) uses `launch_testing` + real lifecycle nodes + real IDL; <5 min. Sim (`tests/sim/`) headless MuJoCo vs real LIBERO / MetaWorld / gym-aloha / gym-pusht (`PhysicsBackend.MUJOCO_MJX` is a declared-but-unwired enum value — no MJX rollout path exists today); <10 min; naming `test_<robot>_<vla>_<sim>.py` (HAL-only sim → `<vla>=hal`). HIL (`tests/hil/`) gated by `[self-hosted, lab-<robot>]`, idempotent, <10 min, e-stop hook on teardown. `hypothesis` fuzz on every Pydantic model (round-trip + JSON Schema). Every public docstring `Example` runs. Per-skill latency budgets enforced on the reference host.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 3. Architecture Discipline
text: **The seven layers** (do not cross without recording a decision in the private management decision log — `OpenRAL/management` repo, `adr/`, see [`docs/decisions.md`](docs/decisions.md)):

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 3. Architecture Discipline
text: Adding, removing, renaming, or moving a responsibility between layers requires recording a decision in the private management decision log (`OpenRAL/management`, `adr/`) before crossing the boundary. A non-adjacent-layer dependency (Skill calling HAL directly, etc.) is rejected.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 3. Architecture Discipline
text: **Dual-system pattern.** **S1** fast policy (30–200 Hz, action chunks) as a `Skill`. **S2** slow reasoning (event-driven; ~0.2 Hz heartbeat) as the `Reasoner` — emits typed tool calls (`ExecuteRskillTool`, `ReloadGstPipelineTool`, `LifecycleTransitionTool`, `EmitPromptTool`) via the `ReasonerToolCall` discriminated union (the direct-dispatch surface). **S0** cerebellar layer (500–1000 Hz, C++ only) in `ros2_control` controllers, for humanoids. Skill manifest declares `role: s1 | s2 | s0`; loader enforces.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 3. Architecture Discipline
text: **rSkill packaging.** One HF Hub repo per skill: `rskill.yaml` (name, version, license, embodiment_tags, capabilities_required, runtime, quantization, latency budgets, fallback_skill_id; plus `state_contract.dim` + `action_contract.dim` for dataset bridge users), weights (`model.safetensors`), optional `engine.plan`/`Dockerfile`, `README.md` per [`rskills/template/README.md`](rskills/template/README.md) (publish gate enforced by `rskill_publisher` validator), `eval/<benchmark>.json` validating against `openral_core.RSkillEvalResult`. Canonical eval producer: `openral benchmark run --suite <id> --rskill rskills/<this_skill>` (the adapter id is read from the manifest's `model_family`; there is no `--vla` flag). Paper-cited numbers allowed with `reproduced_locally: false` + `reproduction_cli`. **Provenance:** sigstore signing/verification is the planned control but is **not yet implemented** (no manifest `signature` field, no verification in the loader). Until it lands, `rSkill.from_pretrained`/`from_yaml` emit an `rskill.unverified_provenance` warning and honor `OPENRAL_REQUIRE_SIGNED_SKILLS=1` to fail closed; `*.pt` weights are treated as untrusted code and require `OPENRAL_ALLOW_UNSAFE_PICKLE=1` to load (prefer `model.safetensors`); `trust_remote_code` models (e.g. MolmoAct2) execute repo-shipped code and require `OPENRAL_ALLOW_REMOTE_CODE=1`. Do not describe skills as "signed/verified" until the control exists (§1.2).

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 3. Architecture Discipline
text: **VLA license matrix.** SmolVLA, OpenVLA/OFT, Octo, ACT, DP/DP3, UnifoLM-VLA-0/WMA-0, Xiaomi Robotics XR-1, LingBot-VLA 1/2 — Apache-2.0 / MIT (XR-1: the three public benchmark checkpoints — RoboCasa, RoboCasa365, VLABench — are custom-code repos needing `OPENRAL_ALLOW_REMOTE_CODE=1`; the public `Xiaomi-Robotics-1-5B/model_states.pt` is a post-training seed, **not** an executable policy or rSkill; LingBot-VLA is Apache-2.0 code **and** weights). π0 / π0.5 / π0.6 / π0.7 — code Apache-2.0; weights permissive research (flag in manifest). GR00T N1 / N1.5 / N1.6 — NVIDIA OneWay **Noncommercial** (install-time guard); GR00T **N1.7+** — NVIDIA Open Model License, **commercial OK** (`nvidia_open_model` posture), including the official 2026 BEHAVIOR-1K organizer checkpoint; N2 announced, unreleased. RLDX-1 is a GR00T-N1.5 finetune. InternVLA-N1 / DualVLN (navigation) — code MIT, weights **CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 noncommercial** (`cc-by-nc-sa-4.0` posture, install-time guard). Helix / Gemini Robotics / Skild Brain — closed, API-only. Which families run in-process vs. in a pinned sidecar, and their per-checkpoint runtime pins and measured VRAM/latency, live in [`docs/reference/vla_compatibility.md`](docs/reference/vla_compatibility.md) §6 and [`docs/reference/aarch64-support.md`](docs/reference/aarch64-support.md). Quantize for target; action chunks not single actions; embodiment tags must match `RobotCapabilities.embodiment_tags`; latency budget is contractual.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 3. Architecture Discipline
text: **Safety.** Touching `packages/openral_safety/` or `cpp/openral_safety_kernel/` requires (a) safety-WG reviewer, (b) an update to the safety hazard log (private `OpenRAL/management` repo), (c) tests proving the new behavior is at least as conservative. **Never** add a flag that disables safety. **Never** add a debug mode that bypasses E-stop. **Never** add a path where a Python crash leaves motors energized. Python proposes; C++ disposes.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 3. Architecture Discipline
text: **Reasoner & dispatch.** LLM tool calls are Pydantic structured output via the provider's tool-use API — no free-form JSON. Tool palette generated from the local skill registry, rebuilt on `/openral/skill_registry_changed`. Bounded replanning ladder (per-kind cap in `ReasonerCore`): retry → param-tweak → substitute-skill → goal-replan → human-handoff. LLM selection is model-first (ADR-0088): `OPENRAL_REASONER_MODEL` names a curated `ReasonerModel` in `openral_core.REASONER_MODELS` (`claude-opus-4-8`, `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.6`, `cosmos3-edge`); `OPENRAL_REASONER_ENDPOINT` is the orthogonal location override, and dialect/auth/hosting defaults come from the registry. Registry membership means the model cleared OpenRAL's robotics tool-calling contract; an uncurated raw model id requires an explicit endpoint + dialect and emits a warning. `OPENRAL_REASONER_ENDPOINT` also accepts a **named endpoint** (`anthropic` / `openrouter` / `gemini` / `xai` / `deepseek` / `huggingface` / `ollama` / `vllm`), which carries its own base URL, dialect, auth posture, cold-start timeout and `tool_choice` quirk — so `OPENRAL_REASONER_DIALECT` is needed only for a bare URL. The legacy `OPENRAL_REASONER_LLM_*` variables are not read; the migration table lives in [`packages/openral_reasoner_ros/README.md`](packages/openral_reasoner_ros/README.md). `cosmos3-edge` is the on-device physical-AI planner (NVIDIA Cosmos 3 reasoner tower, `nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge` 4B, OpenMDW-1.1 commercial-OK weights, managed local vLLM sidecar); see [`packages/openral_reasoner_ros/README.md`](packages/openral_reasoner_ros/README.md). No hidden library default. Local/edge dispatch ships in the open reasoner (Apache-2.0); fleet/cloud dispatch is OpenRAL Pro. Deadline fallback mandatory. No PII in cloud logs without consent.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.1 Before you change anything
text: Re-read this file if >1 day or >1 PR since last; check [`docs/decisions.md`](docs/decisions.md) for relevant background; `just bootstrap && just test` once for a clean baseline; skim the last 20 commits on `master`.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.2 Implementing a feature
text: 1. **Plan** in 3–10 bullets in the PR description before coding. Layer boundary → record the decision in the private management decision log first.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.2 Implementing a feature

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.2 Implementing a feature

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.2 Implementing a feature
text: 5. **Smallest viable PR.** >800 lines needs maintainer pre-approval.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.2 Implementing a feature

text: 7. **Update docs in the same PR** (§1.14).

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.2 Implementing a feature
text: 8. **Conventional Commits** (`feat(skill): …`, `fix(safety): …`). Squash on merge only when the branch is a single logical change. The type is load-bearing: it decides the next release's SemVer segment (`fix` → patch, `feat` → minor, `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` → minor while <1.0) and whether the change reaches `CHANGELOG.md` — `docs/test/style/ci/build/chore` are silent on both counts.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.2 Implementing a feature
text: 9. **Run full local CI** before pushing: `just lint && just test` plus the relevant `just sim-<suite>` recipe (`sim-eval`, `sim-libero`, `sim-metaworld`, `sim-audit`, …) where applicable.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 4. Workflow & PR Checklist > 4.3 Repo state map
text: [`docs/architecture/repo-state-map.html`](docs/architecture/repo-state-map.html) is the visual source of truth — hand-edited, data-driven JS arrays (`LAYERS`, `CROSS`, `CANCELLED`, `SCHEMAS`), no build step, self-contained. **PR that changes the repo surface without updating the map is incomplete.** Update when you add/remove/rename a Python/ROS package (fix block & `pkg`), cross a status boundary (`green`/`yellow`/`blue`/`red` — `green` requires source **and** tests), add/remove a Pydantic model in `openral_core.schemas` / exception in `exceptions.py` / IDL in `packages/msgs/` (update `SCHEMAS` + per-block `schemas: […]`), or change a layer boundary / data-flow direction (revise layer `desc`, runtime data-flow strip, and affected `inputs`/`outputs`). Schema names must match `openral_core` / `openral_msgs` exactly.

text: - [ ] `just lint` passes; `mypy --strict` clean; no new `# type: ignore` without `# reason: ...`; no new `try/except: pass`; no new global mutable state.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 5. Exception Hierarchy (use these, do not invent)
text: `ROSSafetyViolation` is **never** caught except at the safety supervisor boundary, where it triggers E-stop + structured incident log.

head: CLAUDE.md — OpenRAL Engineering Playbook > 6. When in doubt
text: Default to **safer → more typed → more observable → smaller → closer to convention**. Propose deviations from this file as a recorded decision or discussion, not a commit. STOP if you are about to disable a safety check, fake a benchmark number, bundle closed-source weights, add a new top-level package without recording the decision, refactor across all seven layers in one PR, or ship code you haven't run.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Content Rules
text: - Always write DuckDB SQL, not PostgreSQL SQL.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Content Rules
text: - Prefer fully qualified table names: `"database"."schema"."table"`.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Content Rules
text: - Never hardcode tokens; use `MOTHERDUCK_TOKEN` or the documented read-scaling variants.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Content Rules
text: - Never imply runtime extension installation is generally available.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Content Rules
text: - Treat DuckLake as opt-in, not the default storage posture.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Non-Negotiable Content Rules
text: - Keep related-skill guidance in prose sections like `Related Skills`; do not invent repo-specific frontmatter fields for it.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Lead with the Postgres endpoint for thin-client and PostgreSQL-driver interoperability.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Keep native DuckDB APIs in the guidance when local files, hybrid execution, or direct DuckDB control matter.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - For Skills CLI installs, use `npx -y skills` and verify Node.js requirements against the current `skills` package; no global install is required.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Prefer MCP-assisted exploration when MotherDuck MCP is available.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - For use-case skills, if a remote or local MotherDuck server is active, start from the user's real database/schema instead of inventing one.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Prefer a native `md:` workspace connection for multi-database exploration, bootstrap flows, and temporary validation environments.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Call `get_dive_guide` before save/update Dive flows when MCP is available.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Call `get_query_guide` before business-semantic MCP queries and traverse only relevant Guide topics.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Prefer the MotherDuck CLI for file-shaped Dive/Flight work when a coding agent has a shell; prefer MCP for chat-only exploration.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Prefer Parquet over CSV when the format is under our control.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Product Defaults to Preserve
text: - Prefer structural isolation over query-time tenant filtering for serious customer-facing analytics.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules
text: - Keep changes targeted. This repo is mostly documentation and manifests; broad rewrites create drift.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules
text: - Write for current frontier models: keep MotherDuck-specific signal, cut explanations of general concepts the model already knows.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules
text: - Keep descriptions short and distinct; load only task-relevant references and related skills. Reuse established connection and schema context.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules
text: - Treat workflow defaults as guidance unless order protects a concrete contract. Match validation to affected behavior and preserve the user's existing scope and authorization.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules
text: - Keep `skills/catalog.json` descriptions byte-identical to SKILL.md frontmatter descriptions; `scripts/validate_skills.py` enforces this.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules
text: - Give every `references/` file over 100 lines a `## Contents` table of contents, and keep references linked one level deep from `SKILL.md`.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules
text: - Prefer deduplicating repeated guidance by pointing to the owning skill instead of copying blocks between skills.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules
text: - If you shrink a skill, move preserved detail into `references/`; do not silently delete useful content.

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules

head: MotherDuck Skills -- Agent Guide > Editing Rules

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: Source lives in `src/`, segmented into clean architecture rings so dependencies flow inward. Transport adapters sit in `src/server/`, the vendored Swift CLI binary (`bin/event`) is built from the `vendor/event` git submodule, and automation workflows stay under `src/tools/`. Shared helpers live in `src/utils/` (including `eventCli.ts` — the wrapper around `bin/event`), while `src/validation/` enforces Zod contracts on every reminder payload. Tests co-locate as `*.test.ts` beside subjects to keep TDD feedback immediate, and generated binaries rebuild instead of touching `dist/`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: Run `pnpm install` to sync the locked dependency graph (and to build the vendored `event` CLI via the postinstall hook). Use `pnpm dev` for watch-mode TypeScript development without recompiling the Swift binary. Execute `pnpm test` to run the Jest suite through `ts-jest` and the `__mocks__/eventCli.ts` mock. Run `pnpm exec biome check` before commits to enforce formatting, linting, and import ordering, and rebuild the native helper with `pnpm build:event` whenever the `vendor/event` submodule pin moves.

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: Biome enforces two-space indentation, single quotes, and sorted imports across `.ts` files. Choose camelCase for variables and functions, PascalCase for classes, and reuse screaming snake constants from `src/utils/constants.ts` when system identifiers need emphasis. Prefer composition, dependency injection, and repository abstractions to keep outer layers independent of inner logic, and comment only to justify architectural trade-offs or business rules.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: Follow strict RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycles by writing a failing Jest spec beside each new unit. Use the fixtures under `src/__mocks__/` to stabilize reminder schema behavior and initialize shared state through `src/test-setup.ts`. Narrow prompt template changes by targeting `pnpm test -- src/server/prompts.test.ts`. Name specs `<module>.test.ts` for discoverability and prioritize schema and error-path coverage before happy paths.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: Craft conventional commits such as `feat: add transport validator`, keeping titles lowercase and under 50 characters. Ensure every commit leaves `pnpm test` and `pnpm exec biome check` green to maintain CI parity. PRs require actionable descriptions, verification command logs, and linked issues for traceability, and provide screenshots or logs when modifying transport flows or reminder outputs. Merge via merge commits only after CI and security checks pass.

head: Repository Guidelines > Security & Configuration Tips
text: Store secrets exclusively in `.env.local` and load them through typed contracts to avoid leaking reminder data. Grant macOS Reminders and Calendar permissions locally; the Swift bridge aborts before integration tests without them. Run `pnpm audit --prod` ahead of release branches to surface Swift toolchain CVEs, and stub external services via dependency injection instead of hardcoding tokens or calendar IDs.

head: Repository Guidelines > Permission Handling
text: macOS permissions for Reminders and Calendar are requested by the vendored [`event`](https://github.com/FradSer/event) CLI when needed. It checks permission status before each operation:

head: Repository Guidelines > Permission Handling
text: - If authorized: proceeds directly

head: Repository Guidelines > Permission Handling
text: - If notDetermined: requests permission automatically via `requestFullAccessToReminders` / `requestFullAccessToEvents`

head: Repository Guidelines > Permission Handling
text: - If denied / restricted / write-only: emits `Error: Permission denied: …` on stderr with a non-zero exit code

head: Repository Guidelines > Permission Handling
text: `src/utils/eventCli.ts` maps that stderr message into a domain-typed `CliPermissionError`. TypeScript handlers do not duplicate permission checks. `eventCli.ts` spawns `bin/event` through the `bin/event-disclaim` TCC shim (falling back to a direct, host-attributed spawn when the shim is absent), so permission prompts are attributed to `event` itself (it embeds an Info.plist with the EventKit usage strings) rather than to the host MCP client (issue #93).

head: CLAUDE.md — godot-avp-cascade > ⭐ Prototype in the visionOS Simulator — NOT the desktop Godot build

desktop Godot (`Godot.app --path test-project`) as a stand-in — it renders broken XR visuals (audio

easier to test. GDScript/PCK changes need **no engine rebuild** — re-export the PCK, then `xcodebuild`
for `platform=visionOS Simulator` + `xcrun simctl install/launch`. Sim UDID (Apple Vision Pro):
`A540B3B5-CB1D-477D-A3B9-A6D41598B704`. The sim has no hand input, so a round auto-starts when
`SIMULATOR_DEVICE_NAME` is set (bed audible). For a one-command sim/device switcher + sim input/hands
tooling, use **[godot-visionos-simulator-kit](https://github.com/ibrews/godot-visionos-simulator-kit)**.
Full recipe + GUI dev tools: KB `intelligence/techniques/godot-avp-simulator-input.md` and
`…-simulator-dev-tools.md`.

head: Eunoia contributor guide
text:
Eunoia is a Rust library for area-proportional Euler and Venn diagrams. The same
core engine is exposed through WebAssembly, a TypeScript package, a C ABI, and a
statically generated SvelteKit documentation site.

head: Eunoia contributor guide
text:
Use this file for repository-wide expectations. Prefer the nearest README and
existing code when you need component-level detail.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Repository map
text:
| Path                  | Purpose                                                            |
  | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | `crates/eunoia/`      | Core Rust library and fitting algorithms; default workspace member |
  | `crates/eunoia-wasm/` | Thin `wasm-bindgen` bindings                                       |
  | `crates/eunoia-capi/` | JSON-in/JSON-out C ABI used by Eunoia.jl                           |
  | `ts/`                 | High-level TypeScript API and npm build scripts                    |
  | `npm/`                | Generated publishable `@jolars/eunoia` package; gitignored         |
  | `web/`                | SvelteKit docs and demo app, linked to `npm/`                      |
  | `paper/`              | JOSS paper and generated figures                                   |

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Repository map
text:
The Cargo workspace uses Rust edition 2024 and has an MSRV of 1.88.0. Rust
modules use `module.rs` plus `module/`; do not introduce `module/mod.rs`.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Working agreements

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Working agreements

initialization, optimizers, normalization, clustering, or packing must also run:
