head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text:
- `spec` describes set sizes and intersections without geometry. Preprocessing
  stores exclusive regions and converts combinations to `RegionMask`s.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text:
- `fitter` chooses the `DiagramShape` at fit time, builds an initial layout,
  refines it across restarts, and normalizes the best result.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text:
- `geometry` provides composable traits and fitting shapes: `Circle`, `Ellipse`,
  `Square`, `Rectangle`, and `RotatedRectangle`. `Polygon` is for output and
  region extraction, not fitting.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text: - `loss` contains the optimization objectives and smooth surrogates.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text:
- `plotting` extracts region polygons and places region labels, set labels, and
  glyphs.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text: - `venn` provides canonical arrangements independently of the fitter.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text: Preserve these invariants:

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text: - Shape choice belongs to `Fitter<S>`, not `DiagramSpec`.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text:
- External and FFI APIs use geometric parameters. Optimizer parameters are an
  internal representation:
  | Shape             | Geometric           | Optimizer                       |
  | ----------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------- |
  | Circle            | `[x, y, r]`         | identity                        |
  | Ellipse           | `[x, y, a, b, phi]` | `[x, y, ln(a), ln(b), phi]`     |
  | Square            | `[x, y, side]`      | identity                        |
  | Rectangle         | `[x, y, w, h]`      | `[x, y, ln(w*h), ln(w/h)]`      |
  | Rotated rectangle | `[x, y, w, h, phi]` | `[x, y, ln(w*h), ln(w/h), phi]` |

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text:
- Complement fitting appends the container's four rectangle optimizer parameters
  in the same rectangle encoding.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text:
- The `parallel` feature is intentionally off by default and must remain
  disabled for WASM. The `corpus` feature is internal test/benchmark support,
  not public API.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Architecture and invariants
text:
- `basin` is the sole optimizer dependency. Do not introduce a second optimizer
  stack without an explicit architectural decision.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Keep public surfaces synchronized
text:
When a core public option changes—such as a shape, optimizer, loss, MDS solver,
builder method, or complement behavior—update every applicable surface in the
same change:

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Keep public surfaces synchronized
text: 1. Core Rust API and tests in `crates/eunoia/`.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Keep public surfaces synchronized
text: 2. WASM enums/signatures and tests in `crates/eunoia-wasm/`.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Keep public surfaces synchronized
text:
3. C API input types, hand-written snake_case token parsers, implementation, and
   tests in `crates/eunoia-capi/`.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Keep public surfaces synchronized
text: 4. TypeScript wrapper and declarations under `ts/`.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Keep public surfaces synchronized
text: 5. The matching bindings documentation under `web/src/routes/docs/bindings/`.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Keep public surfaces synchronized
text:
Do not assume serde exposes a new core enum through the C API; those mappings
are deliberately manual.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Keep public surfaces synchronized
text:
The npm package publicly exports `.`, `./svg`, `./web`, and `./trajectory`. The

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Documentation site
text:
Narrative documentation lives in `web/src/routes/docs/**` as `.svx` (mdsvex)
pages. A page's first `# H1` is its title; do not add YAML frontmatter. A page

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Documentation site
text:
Files under `web/static/` are served verbatim. Keep the two site indexes
distinct:

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Documentation site

text:
- `web/static/llms.txt` is hand-curated. When adding, removing, renaming, or

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Code review rules
text:
Prioritize behavioral and compatibility risks over formatting that automated
tools already enforce.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Code review rules
text:
- Flag fitter changes that omit `task test-slow` evidence. Safe path: run the
  ignored suite and report any stochastic failure with its seed or fixture.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Code review rules
text:
- Flag a changed core public option when either binding layer, TypeScript, docs,
  or tests are missing. Safe path: update all applicable surfaces together.

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Code review rules
text:
- Flag use of optimizer-encoded shape parameters in an external interface. Safe

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Code review rules

head: Eunoia contributor guide > Releases
text:
Versions are managed by `versionary.jsonc`; the Rust workspace and npm package
are versioned separately. Pushing a `v*` tag triggers the crate publish
workflow; pushing an `eunoia-npm-v*` tag triggers the npm publish workflow. Do
not hand-edit versions or publish artifacts unless the task is explicitly a
release.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: The contributing guide for everyone editing this repo: humans, AI agents, both. The rules apply regardless of who's writing.

head: CLAUDE.md > Open an issue first
text: Before writing any code, open an issue describing what you want to change and why. PRs without a linked issue get closed without review.

head: CLAUDE.md > The earn-its-place test
text: Every word in a skill costs context for the LLM that reads it. Keep a sentence only if it does at least one of these:

head: CLAUDE.md > The earn-its-place test
text: 1. **Constrains the meaning of a term used later.** Example: "in n8n, an agent specifically means the LangChain Agent node with its four sub-node slots." Disambiguates a polysemous word the rest of the doc relies on.

head: CLAUDE.md > The earn-its-place test
text: 2. **Flags a load-bearing assumption.** A non-obvious constraint, invariant, platform quirk, or workaround a reader would not derive from the surrounding code.

head: CLAUDE.md > The earn-its-place test
text: 3. **Explains the why behind a rule.** The why is what lets the model judge edge cases. "Use credentials, not text fields" is a rule. "Because text fields are stored in plaintext in workflow exports" is the why.

head: CLAUDE.md > The earn-its-place test
text: If a sentence does none of those, cut it.

head: CLAUDE.md > What to cut, aggressively
text: - **Things frontier models already know.** Generic definitions ("a webhook is..."), textbook framings of well-known concepts, basic programming explanations. Keep n8n-specific or project-specific framings, but cut the textbook part.

head: CLAUDE.md > What to cut, aggressively
text: - **Restated content.** Anything restated from the frontmatter `description`, anything said twice across sections, "as mentioned above" callbacks.

head: CLAUDE.md > What to cut, aggressively
text: - **Useless intros.** "This skill covers X." "In this guide we will..." "The goal of this document..." The body is loaded only when the skill triggers, by which point the description has already framed the scope. Re-announcing the description in the body is structurally redundant.

head: CLAUDE.md > What to cut, aggressively
text: - **Fluff.** Filler transitions, hedging that doesn't change behavior, motivational preamble without concrete consequence, "remember to be careful" without specifics.

head: CLAUDE.md > What to preserve
text: - Examples that anchor an abstract rule. Cutting an example to shorten a rule usually loses more than it saves.

head: CLAUDE.md > What to preserve
text: - Non-obvious gotchas, even ones that read as basic. "The UI shows 'no items exist' when items do exist" sounds trivial, but it saves an hour of debugging.

head: CLAUDE.md > What to preserve
text: - The why behind every rule. If a rule has no why, write the why or cut the rule.

head: CLAUDE.md > Style
text: - **No em-dashes or obvious gptisms** (`—`). Use a comma, colon, parentheses, or two sentences. If a contribution is clearly fully AI it will be auto closed

head: CLAUDE.md > Style
text: - **Be very concise.** Every word costs context. Shorten sentences that can be shorter, turn paragraphs into lists when they fit, turn lists into tables when they fit. The earn-its-place test applies to phrasing too.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: the router. Cap **500 lines**. Frontmatter: `name`, `description`, optional `allowed-tools`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `skills/<name>/references/*.md`: where depth lives. Loaded on demand. A 2,000-line reference is fine if it only loads when needed.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `skills/<name>/references/examples/*.json`: workflow JSON examples. Reference by relative path, never inline. Every example must validate on a current n8n version.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `hooks/`: SessionStart and PreToolUse. Don't add new hooks without an issue discussion first.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` + `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`: the Codex plugin manifest and marketplace entry. Codex reads the repo root directly (`source.path: "./"`), consuming the same canonical `skills/` and `hooks/` as Claude Code (which reads root via `.claude-plugin/`). Requires **Codex ≥ 0.142.0**: PR #28771 added root-plugin marketplace support; earlier versions rejected the repo root and forced a mirrored copy. Codex still won't follow symlinks (openai/codex#24770), but with root support the mirror is unnecessary.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `opencode/plugin.ts` + `opencode/README.md` + root `package.json`: the OpenCode plugin. TypeScript glue that bridges the canonical `hooks/` bash scripts into OpenCode's plugin events (`config`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`, `experimental.session.compacting`, `tool.execute.after`). The root `package.json` (`main: opencode/plugin.ts`) makes the repo installable as one line: `"plugin": ["n8n-skills@git+https://github.com/n8n-io/skills.git"]`; the `config` hook self-registers the bundled `skills/` dir so no `skills.paths` entry is needed. Derives its tool-matcher table from `hooks/hooks.json` at load, so a new hook there propagates without editing the plugin. Resolves the repo root via `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` (works under both Bun and the Node/Electron desktop app; Bun's `import.meta.dir` is undefined under Node and would disable the plugin). Two of the transform events are experimental OpenCode surface, prone to breaking across versions.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text: `secureai-scan` (npm) — a static AI/LLM security scanner for TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python. It finds prompt injection, MCP supply-chain risks, RAG poisoning, Agent Skill poisoning, and related OWASP LLM/ASI/MCP Top 10 issues, and proves findings with source→flow→sink dataflow traces rather than keyword matching alone.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 1. Zero tolerance for false positives
text: This is the product's entire value proposition (see the "precision contract" in README.md) — a scanner nobody trusts because it cries wolf is worse than no scanner. Any change to detection logic (a rule file, `tool-poisoning-checks.ts`, `python-scanner.ts`, `confidence.ts`, etc.) must not introduce new false positives, and existing false positives found during work should be fixed, not worked around.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 1. Zero tolerance for false positives
text: - The internal precision gate (`test-fixtures/safe/` + `test/corpus.test.js`) enforces zero `proven`/`likely` findings on known-safe patterns — this must stay green, and any bug fixed for a false positive gets a permanent fixture there so it can't regress silently.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 1. Zero tolerance for false positives
text: - That corpus alone is not sufficient — it only proves the scanner behaves on code we wrote to test it. See the regression-scan requirement below for the check that catches what it can't.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 1. Zero tolerance for false positives
text: - When you find a false positive, fix the root cause (a rule's evidence tier, an unguarded keyword match, a missing `isTestFilePath` demotion, an overly broad name set) rather than special-casing the one input that revealed it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 2. Test against real-world repos, not just fixtures, before calling detection work done
text: For any change that touches detection logic (new rule, edited rule, edited shared matcher), run:

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 2. Test against real-world repos, not just fixtures, before calling detection work done
text: This clones a curated set of real public repos (`scripts/regression-scan.js` — OpenAI/Anthropic/Vercel AI SDKs, official MCP servers and SDK, LlamaIndex) into `.regression-cache/` (gitignored, cached across runs — pass `--fresh` to re-clone, or a repo name to scan just one) and scans each with the built CLI. **It is a gate**: it exits non-zero on any `proven`/`likely` finding whose `repo|rule|file` fingerprint isn't in `test/regression-baseline.json`. Fingerprints omit line numbers so ordinary upstream churn isn't noise. Read every new finding against its source line:

text: - If it isn't, it's a bug in a rule. Fix the rule, then add the offending pattern as a new fixture under `test-fixtures/safe/` (with a comment noting which repo/file it came from) so `npm test` locks in the fix permanently.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 2. Test against real-world repos, not just fixtures, before calling detection work done
text: Baselining a finding you haven't actually read defeats the whole mechanism — the baseline is a record of human review, not a mute button.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 2. Test against real-world repos, not just fixtures, before calling detection work done
text: This is how several real false-positive classes were found and fixed in this codebase: `token_endpoint`/`tokenType` fields flagged as leaked secrets (AI002 matched "token" as a bare identifier token with no regard for context), example/demo/`ecosystem-tests`-style directories not being recognized as lower-trust paths (`isTestFilePath` only matched a narrow set of literal `/test/`/`/tests/` segments), `chunks` (an extremely common LLM streaming-response variable name) being treated as unambiguous RAG evidence (AI007), narrative/fiction prompt text containing the bare English words "secret"/"token" being flagged as leaked credentials (AI008 did a raw substring search with no requirement that the match look like an actual credential value), and a Python MCP001 check that flagged *any* `description=` field containing phrases like "system prompt" with `proven` evidence regardless of whether the file had anything to do with MCP at all. Consider that class of bug — a keyword/substring match applied without enough surrounding context, given undeservedly high evidence — the default failure mode to watch for.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 3. Recall/true-positive validation matters as much as precision — and stay scoped to LLM/MCP/RAG
text: Zero false positives is necessary but not sufficient — a scanner that's quiet by default but also blind is worse, and silence reads as "all clear." When a curated advisory (`DEP003`) claims to gate on a version range, prove it both ways: pin a package to the documented-vulnerable version and confirm it fires, then pin it to the patched version and confirm it clears (`test/dependency-guard.test.js` does this for CVE-2025-6514). This exact exercise caught a real bug — `affectedVersions` was display-only text, never actually compared against the declared version — and, separately, a UTF-8 BOM in `package.json` silently zeroing out `DEP001`–`003` via a swallowed `JSON.parse` error (fixed with `src/utils/text.ts`'s `stripBom`, applied at every JSON-config read site).

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 3. Recall/true-positive validation matters as much as precision — and stay scoped to LLM/MCP/RAG
text: That said, **detection scope is fixed to LLM/MCP/RAG-related risks.** When a real incident (e.g. the postmark-mcp backdoor) turns out to be undetectable by any in-scope pattern rule — because the payload is generic-looking business logic with nothing LLM-shaped about it — the correct fix is the offline advisory list (name+version), or an honest documented gap. Do not propose or add general-purpose SAST/secret-scanning heuristics to close a gap like that; a rule broad enough to catch it would fire constantly on ordinary, unrelated code.

head: CLAUDE.md > Hard requirements (non-negotiable, apply to every change) > 4. The CLI layer needs its own tests — detection-logic tests don't cover it
text: Every test file except `test/cli.test.js` calls scanner functions directly, bypassing `src/cli.ts` entirely. A bug in flag wiring (a dropped custom-parser argument, a flag that silently no-ops without a second required flag) has no other test that would catch it — this happened once already (a regrouping edit to `scan`'s options accidentally dropped `-r/--rules`'s parser function; `npm test` stayed green because nothing exercised the built binary). Any change to `src/cli.ts` — new flag, reordered options, changed wiring between flags — needs a corresponding case in `test/cli.test.js`, which runs the real built binary via `execFileSync`, not the underlying functions.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: There is no separate lint script — `tsc` (strict mode, see `tsconfig.json`) is the only static check. Always `npm run build` before running tests: tests import from `dist/`, not `src/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Three independent scanning surfaces, merged into one output
text: - **TS/JS**: AST-based via `ts-morph` (`src/scanner/project.ts` builds the `Project`; rules in `src/scanner/rules/*.ts` walk the AST).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Three independent scanning surfaces, merged into one output
text: - **Python**: AST-based via `tree-sitter` + `tree-sitter-python` (`src/scanner/python-ast.ts` builds one indexed tree per file; `src/scanner/python-scanner.ts` runs the rules). Imports, calls, assignments, attributes, tuple/list targets, decorators, functions, scopes, arguments, dictionary fields, and strings must come from AST nodes — never reconstruct structure with raw-line regex. Regex is allowed only to classify a node's text after syntax establishes what the node is (for example, an injection phrase inside an AST-confirmed tool-description string). LLM receivers are bound from SDK constructor assignment nodes, so renamed clients remain visible. Tree-sitter error recovery is deliberate: a malformed file is scanned, not allowed to abort the repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Three independent scanning surfaces, merged into one output
text: - **Config/content files scanned off disk directly** (not via the ts-morph `Project`): `src/scanner/mcp-config-scanner.ts` (`.mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json` → `MCP004`–`MCP006`) and `src/scanner/skill-scanner.ts` (Agent Skill bundles → `SKL001`–`SKL005`, reusing the same invisible-Unicode/injection-phrase/cross-reference checks in `tool-poisoning-checks.ts` that the MCP tool-poisoning rules use).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Three independent scanning surfaces, merged into one output
text: - **Dependency advisories** (`DEP001`–`DEP003`) run out of `src/scanner/dependency-guard.ts` against two bundled sources: the hand-curated `src/scanner/advisories.ts` (in-the-wild malicious releases) and the generated `src/scanner/advisories-generated.ts` (HIGH/CRITICAL OSV advisories for an LLM/MCP/RAG watchlist, regenerated with `npm run sync-advisories`). DEP003 always runs offline; DEP001/DEP002 (registry lookups, typosquat detection) are opt-in via `--check-dependencies` since they need network access.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Three independent scanning surfaces, merged into one output
text: `src/scanner/scan.ts` (`scanRepositoryDetailed`) is the entry point that runs all of the above, merges findings, dedupes, and applies `// secureai-ignore RULE_ID: reason` suppression comments.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Rule shape
text: Every AST rule lives in `src/scanner/rules/` and exports a `Rule` object (`id`, `title`, `severity`, `run(context)`). New rules must be registered in `src/scanner/rules/index.ts`'s `RULES` array (or the adjacent `CONFIG_RULE_IDS`/`SKILL_RULE_IDS`/`DEPENDENCY_RULE_IDS` for the non-AST scanners) — this is also the source of truth for `AVAILABLE_RULE_IDS`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Rule shape
text: Shared helpers: `src/scanner/rules/llm-rule-utils.ts` (resolves whether a call is a real LLM SDK sink via import resolution, extracts prompt message parts *with role* via `getPromptParts` — always prefer this over writing a new ad hoc prompt-part extractor, since a rule-specific reimplementation is exactly what caused the AI007 false-positive class) and `src/utils/ast.ts` (node/line helpers, string-concat detection, and the shared per-file AST index).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Rule shape
text: **Never call `sourceFile.getDescendants()` or `getDescendantsOfKind(...)` from a rule.** Use `getFileCalls(sourceFile)`, `getFileFunctions(sourceFile)`, and `getCallsWithin(node)` from `src/utils/ast.ts`, which serve one memoized pre-order walk per file. Every rule doing its own walk is what made a `vercel/ai` scan take 217s — a CPU profile put ~95s of 150s in descendant iteration alone; routing rules through the index cut the scan to 62s with identical findings. `getCallsWithin` relies on descendants being a contiguous run of the pre-order index, which `test/ast-index.test.js` asserts against ts-morph's own traversal; if that ever breaks, rules silently stop seeing calls.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Evasion resistance (skill bundles)
text: Two modules exist specifically to defeat the published scanner-evasion techniques in *Cloak and Detonate* (arXiv:2607.02357) and the Gecko Security test-file vector. Both invert conventions that hold everywhere else in this codebase, deliberately:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Evasion resistance (skill bundles)
text: - **`src/scanner/deobfuscate.ts`** — content checks match against normalized *variants* (invisible-stripped, homoglyph-folded, string-splice-joined, intra-word-break-joined) instead of one byte sequence. `matchAcrossVariants` compares against the *set* of raw hits, not "did the raw text match at all" — otherwise an attacker masks the evasion signal by leaving one benign phrase in the clear. **A hit found only after deobfuscation is promoted to `proven`, not demoted**: prose does not contain a zero-width joiner inside "ignore previous instructions". This is the one place where a heuristic transform *raises* evidence, and it is justified because the concealment is the evidence.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Evasion resistance (skill bundles)
text: - **`src/scanner/skill-bundle.ts`** — walks a skill's whole directory, ignoring the skip-lists used elsewhere (`build/`, `docs/`, `.git/`, renamed extensions, oversized files are head-read not skipped). Inside a bundle's `.git/`, any file that is not a git internal (see `GIT_INTERNAL_ENTRIES`) is `proven`-tier on its own — nothing else writes there. **SKL005 deliberately does not call `isTestFilePath`**: a payload in `*.test.ts` is the published attack precisely because every other scanner demotes or skips it, and test runners auto-execute those files. Do not "fix" that by adding the demotion back.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Evasion resistance (skill bundles)
text: Because a bundle can be an entire repository (when `SKILL.md` sits at a repo root), both bundle rules require a *linked* conjunction rather than co-occurrence: SKL004's unpack directive must name the blob, and SKL005's credential read and egress must be within `EXFIL_PROXIMITY_LINES` of each other in the same file. Loosening either is how these rules would start firing on ordinary monorepos.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > MCP tool-argument taint (MCP013/MCP014)
text: `src/scanner/rules/mcp-tool-arg-sink.ts` (TS) and `checkMcpToolArgSink` in `python-scanner.ts` treat **MCP tool arguments** as the taint source: the model writes them, so a prompt injection chooses them. That source is what keeps these rules in scope; a value from an ordinary HTTP form reaching `exec` is general SAST and stays out. Three conventions are load-bearing:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > MCP tool-argument taint (MCP013/MCP014)
text: - **Report only an intent the code fails to keep.** MCP013 needs the argument *composed into a fixed command*; MCP014 needs it *joined onto a base directory*. A by-design "run any command" or "read any file" tool is `heuristic`. Don't promote it: on 25 popular servers this distinction is the difference between zero findings and noise.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > MCP tool-argument taint (MCP013/MCP014)
text: - **Guards must actually validate.** A membership test counts only against an allowlist (or a metacharacter probe on the value), and a regex only when it is anchored or probes metacharacters. `fileText.includes(x)` and `x.match(/host\/(.+)/)` don't validate anything, and treating them as guards hid two real CVEs.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > MCP tool-argument taint (MCP013/MCP014)
text: - **Sinks use reaching definitions.** A variable reused across `switch` cases is judged by the write that reaches each `exec` (or each wrapper call), not by any write in the function. Flow-insensitive taint produced false positives in mcp-server-kubernetes.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > MCP tool-argument taint (MCP013/MCP014)
text: Recall is checked against published CVEs, not only fixtures: the vulnerable commit must fire and the fix commit must be clean (see `docs/RealWorldFindings.md`). Re-run that check when changing these rules.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The evidence-tier contract (this is the core design principle)
text: Every `Finding` carries an `Evidence` tier (`src/scanner/types.ts`):

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The evidence-tier contract (this is the core design principle)
text: - `proven` — import-resolved sink + traced dataflow, or a parsed config fact.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The evidence-tier contract (this is the core design principle)
text: - `likely` — resolved sink or strong structural signal, with one heuristic hop.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The evidence-tier contract (this is the core design principle)
text: - `heuristic` — pattern/proximity match only, hidden unless `--paranoid`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The evidence-tier contract (this is the core design principle)
text: Rules only flag an "LLM call" if the callee resolves through actual imports to a known SDK (`resolveLlmSink` in `llm-rule-utils.ts`) — never by name-matching alone. `src/scanner/confidence.ts` provides `evidenceConfidence()` (maps tier → numeric score), `demoteEvidence()` (downgrade one tier — test files, weaker taint origins, etc.), and `isTestFilePath()` (matches test/example/demo/fixture path *segments*, not raw substrings — a file under `examples/`, top-level `tests/`, or a hyphenated dir like `ecosystem-tests/` all count; this was itself a false-positive source before its segment-based rewrite). New rules touching request/user-controlled data should call `isTestFilePath` and demote evidence in matched test/example paths, matching the convention in `prompt-injection-concat.ts`, `llm-before-auth.ts`, `mcp-dynamic-server-url.ts`, etc. — a rule that skips this (as AI007/AI008 originally did) is a latent false-positive source in any repo that ships example code, which is most of them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The evidence-tier contract (this is the core design principle)
text: A bare keyword/substring match with no surrounding context is never enough to justify `proven` or even `likely` — require either a traced dataflow, an import-resolved sink, or (for text-content rules like AI008/MCP008/SKL002) a value/phrase shape specific enough that ordinary prose or unrelated identifiers can't collide with it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The precision gate (test corpus)
text: `test-fixtures/vulnerable/` and `test-fixtures/safe/` are the regression corpus enforced by `test/corpus.test.js`:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The precision gate (test corpus)
text: - Every fixture in `vulnerable/` must fire its expected rule at `proven` or `likely` evidence (see the `EXPECTED_VULNERABLE` list in that test).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The precision gate (test corpus)
text: - Every fixture in `safe/` must produce **zero** `proven`/`likely` findings — these are patterns that previously caused false positives (redacted PII, ordinary logging, env-var API keys near LLM clients, non-LLM clients that merely look like one, OAuth metadata fields, streaming-response `chunks`, fiction/narrative prompt text, framework config fields).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The precision gate (test corpus)
text: Any change to a rule's detection logic must be checked against this corpus, **and** against `npm run regression` per the hard requirement above. If a rule needs new coverage, add a fixture to both directories as appropriate.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Findings pipeline (after collection)
text: `Finding[]` → evidence filter (`--paranoid`) → confidence filter (`--min-confidence`) → severity filter → baseline diff (`src/scanner/baseline.ts`, tracks new/changed only) → report (`src/scanner/reporter.ts`, formats: terminal, `sarif`, `json`, `markdown`, `html`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Other entry points
text: - `src/scanner/installed.ts` — `secureai-scan installed`: audits the per-user MCP configs of known AI clients (Claude Code incl. per-project servers in `~/.claude.json`, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Cline, Roo Code, Amazon Q) and `~/.claude/skills`. It stages **only the server entries** of each config into a private temp dir, runs the unchanged config/advisory scanners there, and maps findings back to the real file and line. Never stage or echo anything else from a client config: `~/.claude.json` also holds session tokens. `--deep` fetches npm-launched servers via `fetch-target.ts` and is the only network path; tests inject `fetchPackage` to stay offline.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Other entry points
text: - `src/scanner/bom.ts` — AI-BOM generation (`secureai-scan bom`), inventories SDKs/models/vector stores/MCP servers.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Other entry points
text: - `src/scanner/threat-model.ts` — generates `THREAT_MODEL.md` with an OWASP LLM/ASI/MCP coverage matrix, driven entirely off `src/scanner/catalog.ts`'s `RULE_CATALOG`/`FRAMEWORK_MAP` (add a rule there and the matrix updates itself — no separate wiring needed except `CATEGORY_LABELS`/`buildTrustBoundaries` for a genuinely new rule-ID prefix).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Other entry points
text: - `src/scanner/explainer.ts` + `src/scanner/catalog.ts` — power `secureai-scan explain <RULE_ID>` (static per-rule why/exploit/fix content keyed by rule ID). **Every new rule needs an entry in both** — `explainer.ts` silently falls back to generic boilerplate for unregistered IDs, which is easy to miss since nothing fails a build or test over it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Other entry points
text: - `src/scanner/policy.ts` — reads `.secureai-policy.json` (skip paths, blocked rules, min severity) and scaffolds it + a GitHub Actions workflow via `secureai-scan init`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Other entry points
text: - `mcp-server/index.js` — standalone MCP server (plain Node, not TS) exposing `scan_repository`, `explain_rule`, `generate_bom` as MCP tools; ships as-is in the npm package (`files` in `package.json`), not compiled from `src/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a new rule
text: 1. Add `src/scanner/rules/<name>.ts` exporting a `Rule`. Use `resolveLlmSink`/`getPromptParts` from `llm-rule-utils.ts` for anything touching an LLM call, call `isTestFilePath` and demote evidence in matched paths, and pick evidence tiers deliberately (see above).

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a new rule
text: 2. Register it in the `RULES` array in `src/scanner/rules/index.ts`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a new rule
text: 3. Add a catalog entry in `src/scanner/catalog.ts` (title/owasp/impact/fix, plus `FRAMEWORK_MAP` if an ASI/MCP-Top10 mapping is defensible) **and** an entry in `src/scanner/explainer.ts`'s `DEFAULT_EXPLANATIONS` — both are easy to forget since nothing enforces them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a new rule
text: 4. Add a vulnerable fixture (must fire) and, if there's a plausible false-positive shape, a safe fixture (must stay clean) under `test-fixtures/`, then extend `EXPECTED_VULNERABLE` in `test/corpus.test.js`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a new rule
text: 5. `npm run build && npm test`, then `npm run regression` before considering the rule done.

head: CLAUDE.md > Package advisories (DEP003)
text: Two sources, with deliberately different ambiguity handling — do not collapse them:

head: CLAUDE.md > Package advisories (DEP003)
text: - `src/scanner/advisories.ts` is hand-maintained and holds `kind: "malicious"` incidents (backdoored releases, in-the-wild compromises) that OSV does not carry. These feed `proven`/critical findings and **fire even when the declared version can't be resolved**, because installing a backdoor is unrecoverable. The bar for additions is strict (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`): only packages with a public incident report, with version ranges when documented, and a corresponding case added to `test/dependency-guard.test.js`. Don't add an advisory for an incident where the exact package name/ecosystem isn't publicly documented — a plausible guess is not the same as a citable fact.

head: CLAUDE.md > Package advisories (DEP003)
text: - `src/scanner/advisories-generated.ts` is generated by `scripts/sync-advisories.js` from OSV and holds `kind: "vulnerable"` CVEs. These fire at `proven` **only when the declared version is an exact pin provably inside the affected range**. Applying the malicious-kind "fail toward flagging" rule here would produce a critical finding on every repo with `langchain>=0.1.0` — an unactionable false positive at scale. Unpinned-but-possibly-affected surfaces at `heuristic` (`--paranoid`) instead. Never edit the generated file by hand; change the watchlist or severity bar in the script and re-run `npm run sync-advisories`.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide
text:
Native Postgres FTS + pg_trgm engine for Laravel Scout. Standalone
package — published as `jonaspauleta/scout-postgres` on Packagist.
Root PHP namespace is `ScoutPostgres\`.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Installation
text:
- `CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm` and `CREATE EXTENSION unaccent` must succeed.
  On Neon/Laravel Cloud the default DB role has permission.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Installation
text: - Run the package migration: `php artisan migrate` — picked up automatically via `runsMigrations()`. No `--path=` flag required.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Installation
text:
- Add per-table generated columns via `$table->postgresSearchable([...])` in an
  app migration.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Installation
text: - Set `SCOUT_DRIVER=pgsql`, `SCOUT_QUEUE=false`.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Common pitfalls
text:
- **`simple_unaccent` config must exist before `postgresSearchable()` migrations
  run** — the package migration creates it. Run package migrations first.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Common pitfalls
text:
- **`STORED` generated columns rewrite the table** on add. For tables with >1M
  rows, split the migration or run with `lock_timeout` set.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Common pitfalls
text:
- **Neon database branches** do not retroactively inherit extensions or text
  search configs — re-run the extensions migration per branch.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Common pitfalls
text:
- **The `search_text` expression uses `||` + `coalesce`, not `concat_ws`** —
  `concat_ws` is STABLE, not IMMUTABLE, so Postgres rejects it inside STORED
  generated column definitions.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Do not
text: - Add Meilisearch-style synonyms / stopwords tuning to v1. Deferred.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Do not
text:
- Hardcode `deleted_at` filters in `SearchQueryBuilder` — Scout injects
  `__soft_deleted` into `$builder->wheres` when `scout.soft_delete=true`.

head: scout-postgres — Agent Guide > Do not
text: - Register the macro anywhere other than `ScoutPostgresServiceProvider::packageBooted()`.

text: PocketShell is in active development and daily use as the maintainer's primary way of working on a dev box from a phone.

head: PocketShell
text: Branches (since #2934): `main` is JS-first 0.6.0 development (Vue/TypeScript in `src/`, Capacitor host in `android/`, pinned `vendor/pocketshell-core` submodule, which also carries the shared UI in `packages/ui`) - untagged and unreleased until #2863's replacement release gates pass. `release/0.5.x` holds the released Kotlin `app2`/`shared` line (old `main` `43af72c3f`) and takes 0.5.x hotfixes only; branch 0.5.x work from `origin/release/0.5.x`, and read [docs/release.md](docs/release.md#release-05x-hotfixes) for its tag path and current gaps. Architecture on `main` follows D42 ([docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md)): one shared `pocketshell-core` (logic, controllers, the one session/reconnect owner, shared app UI for common features) serves web, desktop and Android; this repo owns only Android/mobile-only code (fast keys, dictation, share/SAF, upload progress, FGS port-forward, ...; checklist #2941) plugged into the shared app's extension points, plus the Android `PocketShellApi` over thin Capacitor plugins. No re-implementing shared functionality here, and no platform code in core. It supersedes the Android-specific screen plan in `docs/js-first-rewrite-plan.md`. Anything in these docs about `app2`, `shared/`, root `./gradlew`, `scripts/full-jvm-gate.py` or `scripts/render.sh` applies to `release/0.5.x` only. Work is tracked as GitHub issues across phases 0-4. The visual specification lives in the shared UI-kit and design docs; locked design decisions live in `docs/decisions.md`.

text: - A red scheduled full-suite run on `main` is a feature-merge freeze (D36); only a revert or an already-approved forward fix may merge until green. Since #2934 `main` has no scheduled run at all until #2863 lands its JS replacement - there is no D36 signal, not a green one.

text: - A regression bisected to a `main` merge is reverted within 4 hours by default, not fixed forward while `main` stays red.

head: Agent Roles > Process quick rules

head: Agent Roles > Process quick rules

head: Agent Roles > Environment quick facts
text: Never put a `$` in an `rm`/`rmdir` target - no `$(...)`, no `$VAR`, no `~`. Claude Code has a hardcoded "Dangerous rm/rmdir operation on statically-unresolvable target" circuit breaker: any command that mentions `rm`/`rmdir` and contains `$` gets its removal target statically resolved, and anything it can't resolve (a `$(...)`, a `$VAR/*` glob, a `cd` before a relative glob) prompts the maintainer even under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; it is not allowlistable by any permission rule or setting. Resolve the path in a separate Bash call first (`cat $S/e2e/rtpath`), then delete with the literal path pasted in. Cleanup chains that bundle `echo`/`ls` around a `$(...)` removal trip it every time - split them.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Marimo Studio turns one reactive notebook into named views. The notebook
owns data, computation, controls, and domain decisions. Studio owns view
projects, provider discovery, build publication, projections, delivery, and
agent workflows.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Marimo owns process lifecycle, authentication, notebook execution, sessions,
reactivity, virtual files, controls, widgets, and native output rendering.
Keep private Marimo integration inside `_compat`.

head: AGENTS.md > What the complexity buys
text:
| Mechanism                                      | User capability                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Explicit view projects and provider inspection | Each view can use its own source and build workflow while Source shows the documents relevant to that project.                |
| Immutable artifacts and distinct revisions     | A failed build keeps the current preview available, and editors, browsers, exports, and agents consume one coherent revision. |
| Symbolic projections                           | Custom layouts retain native notebook cells, values, rich outputs, controls, and dependency behavior.                         |
| Explicit owners, generations, and evidence     | View switches, reconnects, concurrent edits, and automated operations stay tied to current state.                             |
| One artifact across execution environments     | The same view can run with a Python kernel, in a browser worker, or as a static export.                                       |

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text:
- Treat authored documents, build inputs, and public artifact files as separate
  allowlists. Persist view choices in `view.toml`. Starter identity is
  creation-time input.

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text:
- Keep document, project, artifact, and presentation identities distinct. Bind
  mutations to the owner, generation, revision, and session they observed,
  then revalidate those identities immediately before commit.

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text:
- Give connections, subscriptions, claims, processes, leases, and background
  operations explicit owners. Every claim reaches a terminal state. Release
  uncommitted work on every exit path and reject acquisitions after close
  begins.

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text:
- Provider inspection returns bounded plans. Core owns validation, persistence,
  publication, and projection authorization. Inspection is read-only.

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text:
- Treat native Marimo output subtrees as opaque. Register projections from
  artifact-authored hosts and release them when ownership changes.

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text:
- Stage source, artifact, and presentation replacements, then commit them
  atomically. A failed replacement retains the last valid state.

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text:
- Keep user-visible transitions separate. Run filesystem discovery, provider
  calls, process waits, and native observer shutdown off the event loop and
  outside mutation locks.

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text:
Dependencies point from applications and adapters toward Studio contracts.
Private Marimo APIs stay in `_compat`, provider and framework knowledge stays
in `view_providers._builtin`, and serializable browser records stay in
`packages/protocol`. Product policy must not import those details back.

head: AGENTS.md > Durable boundaries
text: Trace every cross-boundary change through:

head: AGENTS.md > Evidence and validation
text: - Run focused owner tests while working and `make check` after source changes.

head: AGENTS.md > Evidence and validation
text:
- Add `make build` and `make e2e` for browser, artifact, document, runtime, or
  session changes. Add `make package` for distribution changes. Add
  `make docs-build` plus desktop and narrow inspection for public docs.

head: AGENTS.md > Evidence and validation
text:
- Test through the API, command, file, protocol, browser state, or package
  boundary that consumers use. Add cases for a distinct runtime, platform,
  input, lifecycle phase, failure, security boundary, or compatibility promise.

head: AGENTS.md > Evidence and validation
text:
- Use observable readiness and owned barriers for lifecycle tests. Keep test
  resources explicit, make browser diagnostics fail closed, and avoid shipped
  routes or public records that exist to coordinate tests. Preserve the
  worktree during read-only audits.

overlap and none of them is authoritative on its own — a rationale is often recorded in one place and the

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions
text:
The rules we converged on; apply them by default. Rationale lives in the layer READMEs,
roadmap in GitHub Issues, vendored-source origins in `PROVENANCE.md`. (Global
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` still applies.)

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions
text:
**Two independent firmware tracks** ([`README.md`](README.md) has the split): `lua/` —
bare-metal Lua 5.4, the active track — and `mtl/` — the classic C VM + MTL + Forth stack.
**Scope: toolchain only** (build / simulate / test / flash). High-level apps — Home
Assistant, weather, TTS — are out of scope: they consume the SDK, they aren't part of it.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Session bootstrap
text:
- Run `scripts/claude-setup.sh` once per session (idempotent). Run it *before* a long
  `verify`, not just after one dies — a daemon death mid-run costs the whole run.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Session bootstrap
text:
- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon` means the daemon died, not that you did
  something wrong — just re-run the script.** It happens several times in a long
  session; it is one command, not a diagnosis.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Session bootstrap
text:
- Host needs only Docker + Task; everything builds in containers. The MTL image is amd64,
  emulated on Apple Silicon, where `cc1` **segfaults nondeterministically** ("internal
  compiler error") — **re-run it.**

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Definition of done
text:
- **`task lua:verify` before every lua commit, `task mtl:verify` before every mtl commit,
  `task verify` for both.** A change that passes one track can still break the other.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Definition of done
text:
- A layer is done when it builds in Docker **and** is committed **and** `PROVENANCE.md` is
  updated **and** the folder has a short `README.md`. Verify by running the task in
  Docker, not by reasoning that it should work. **`task` with no args lists every
  target — it, not any doc, is the authoritative list.**

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Definition of done
text:
- Simulator e2e: run the `simulate` task in the background, then
  `curl --noproxy localhost -m 5 localhost:8080/...` (the session's HTTPS proxy otherwise
  intercepts plain `curl localhost`).

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Testing
text:
- **Assert positive expected content, never just that two runs agree.** A golden test
  comparing two stdout captures passes on `empty == empty`. Require a known marker in the
  output before comparing; an all-empty run must fail.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Testing
text:
- **That rule covers the runner too.** A selector the runner silently ignores reports a
  pass having run nothing. After adding a scenario, confirm the output names *your*
  scenario — an unmatched selector must fail, not exit 0.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Testing
text:
- **New non-wiring logic in `main.c` goes in its own TU.** `main.c` carries `main()`, so
  nothing can link it and nothing in it is unit-testable. It keeps wiring; anything with a
  rule to it gets a file and a `test/host/` test.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > lua track (active)
text:
- **The design principles and the flash budget are binding**, both in
  [`lua/firmware/README.md`](lua/firmware/README.md). A change that breaks a principle
  needs a stated reason.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > lua track (active)
text:
- **`task lua:firmware:build` fails loudly on flash overflow — believe it.** A new libc
  call can silently cost kilobytes: check the map's **"Archive member"** section,
  `--gc-sections` alone will not tell you.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > lua track (active)
text:
- **The image is parser-less by design** — the rabbit runs only `luac` bytecode, compiled
  off-device. Source typed at a bare terminal will not run.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > lua track (active)
text:
- Params: `EXAMPLE=<name>` is a C bring-up program under `firmware/examples/`,
  `APP=<path>` a Lua app source (layer-root-relative). `compile` = Lua→bytecode,
  `build` = binary image.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > lua track (active)
text: - JTAG flashing and the UART REPL: use the **`hw-flash-repl` skill**.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > mtl track
text:
Lower-traffic; the detail lives in [`mtl/README.md`](mtl/README.md). Two things to know
before touching it:

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > mtl track
text:
- **Its build/simulate tasks and `mtl:lib:test` always exit 0** — the MTL compiler and
  simulator report fatal errors on stderr without failing the process. Both are wrapped to
  turn that into a real nonzero exit, so **trust the exit code; don't grep output by hand.**

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > mtl track
text:
- Writing or debugging `.mtl`: the **`mtl-lang` skill**. VM internals and the twin-VM rule
  (patch both copies): [`mtl/tools/testvm/README.md`](mtl/tools/testvm/README.md).

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Structure & vendoring
text:
- **Self-contained layer folders**: each owns its `Dockerfile` + `Taskfile.yaml`; the root
  only `includes:` them. Apply the minimalism rule to **interfaces**, not just code.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Structure & vendoring
text:
- **Copy vendored sources in, don't submodule**; record origin + commit + local changes in
  `PROVENANCE.md`. **Never vendor secrets** — keep the sanitized `*.sample` only.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Structure & vendoring
text:
- **Never reformat a vendored file.** Several are CRLF, and a scripted rewrite turns a
  small fix into a whole-file diff that destroys the backport bridge. `task lua:check:eol`
  gates the `net/` ones; still check `git diff --stat` after any scripted edit.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Structure & vendoring
text: - **Languages: Python (all glue) + C/C++ (Docker-built binaries).** No Perl/Ruby/PHP.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Working agreement
text:
Commit per logical change with the `Co-Authored-By` trailer. Keep the layer READMEs and
`PROVENANCE.md` in sync as decisions land. Surface genuine forks as decisions; otherwise
pick the convention above and proceed.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Working agreement
text: - **A PR that resolves an issue says `Fixes #<n>`** at the top of the body.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Working agreement
text:
- **Multi-milestone arc = one feature branch.** If you must stack, branch off the current
  tip (never `main`) and say so up front.

head: NabaztagSDK — working conventions > Working agreement
text:
- **This file is prepended to every session, so it is not free.** Before adding a lesson,
  check whether a task can catch it instead — a gate that fails beats a paragraph that
  hopes. Keep only what a competent contributor would plausibly get wrong, where the
  mistake costs real time and nothing already checks it; put the *why* next to the code it
  protects. When you touch a section, delete what tooling now covers.

text: **Console output:** `await Verify(result.Output)`; snapshots live in `NetPace.Console.Tests/Expectations/*.verified.txt`. A test with no snapshot fails first — review the generated `.received.txt`, then rename it to `.verified.txt` to accept. Constitution → Testing Standards for when a targeted assert is right instead.

head: NetPace Development Guide > NetPace-Specific Patterns > Speed Test Provider Pattern
text: Providers implement `ISpeedTestService` (`src/NetPace.Core/ISpeedTestService.cs`): server discovery, latency, download and upload. Each returns a result record (`LatencyTestResult`, `SpeedTestResult`) and has `CancellationToken` and `IProgress<T>` overloads. Provider code stays in `src/NetPace.Core/Clients/{Provider}/` (today only `Clients/Ookla/`).

head: NetPace Development Guide > NetPace-Specific Patterns > CLI Help Behaviour
text: `--help` (and `-h`, `-?`) is intercepted manually in `Program.RunAsync` before `System.CommandLine` parses arguments. This keeps help rendering under full control of `CustomHelpProvider`.

head: NetPace Development Guide > NetPace-Specific Patterns > CLI Help Behaviour
text: **Intentional constraint**: help is only recognised at position 0 (root help) or as the second token after a subcommand name (e.g. `netpace servers --help`). Flags placed before `--help` (e.g. `netpace --csv --help`) are silently ignored. Deliberate trade-off to keep the help-interception logic simple.

head: NetPace Development Guide > NetPace-Specific Patterns > CLI Help Behaviour
text: Do not add tests for the `--flag --help` pattern — it is not expected to work.

head: NetPace Development Guide > NetPace-Specific Patterns > Units and Formatting
text: `--unit-scale` overrides auto-scaling; formatting must match across default, minimal, CSV and JSON output.

head: NetPace Development Guide > NetPace-Specific Patterns > Result, Extension and Settings Patterns
NetPace Development Guide > NetPace-Specific Patterns > Result, Extension and Settings Patterns
text: - Provider configuration is a settings record passed to the constructor, not per-call parameters: `new OoklaSpeedtest(new OoklaSpeedtestSettings(Profile.Small))`. Override single fields with `with`.

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: Paired rules — `Don't` X → `Do` Y instead:

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Constitution rules apply as written** → TDD, including the config/tooling carve-out where the real tool is the RED test (I); XML docs on public Core APIs (V); justified Core dependencies (VI); discuss public-API changes before implementing (VII); no skipped tests, enforced by the no-skipped-tests hook (X). **Pre-1.0 override**: while every released version is below 1.0.0, no breaking or public-API change to the CLI or to `NetPace.Core` needs prior discussion, approval, a deprecation period or a MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH classification (Constitution VII, *Pre-1.0 stance*) — state in the issue or PR what breaks and for whom, and carry on.

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't commit with failing tests or build warnings** → run `dotnet build src` and `dotnet test src` clean before committing.

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't change a CLI option without updating user-facing docs** → README.md `--help` snapshot and USER_GUIDE.md need updating; design-doc cross-ref where applicable. (Per-release "what changed" notes are GitHub-auto-generated from merged PRs — no CHANGELOG.md to maintain.)

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't change `release-binaries.yml` (or other release-pipeline scope) without updating `docs/RELEASING.md`** → the release matrix, runner-per-RID rationale, naming convention, smoke-test contract, and size-assertion contract live there. Out-of-sync release docs make adding a new RID/variant cost extra. (Action-version bumps such as `actions/checkout@v4→v5` are exempt.)

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't introduce reflection-heavy or non-trim-safe code** → NetPace targets AOT-trimmable builds (Spectre.Console.Cli was replaced for this reason); avoid runtime reflection, keep types annotation-clean.

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't raise a PR without checking the issue's scenario labels trace to tests** → run `bash scripts/traceability-check.sh`. It reads the issue number off the branch and fails naming any `**Scenario: X**` label with no matching `SCENARIO: X` marker in a committed test file (Constitution §VIII). The `traceability` CI job runs the same script on every PR, and it is a required check in the `Main CI/CD` ruleset, so a red check blocks the merge — running it locally only changes whether you find out before or after pushing. A branch with no issue number, or an issue with no labels, passes with nothing to check. It reads **committed** state, so a marker you have written but not yet committed does not count.

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't make a throwaway script executable** → run it as `bash script.sh`, which needs no permission and does the same job. `Bash(chmod:*)` is on `permissions.ask`, so setting the executable bit stalls an interactive run until a human answers and is silently denied in a headless one — in the #265 A/B runs two reviewers each blocked well over an hour on exactly that call. `.claude/hooks/no-chmod.sh` refuses the executable-bit forms and names the alternative; to record the bit on a file you are committing, use `git add --chmod=+x <path>`.

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't hard-wrap markdown prose** → write one line per paragraph, bullet, and table row and let the viewer soft-wrap it; a fixed-column hard wrap reflows the whole block on a one-word edit and buries the real change in a noisy diff.

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't write an issue number outside a change-intent record** → in the codebase an issue number belongs in `docs/change-intent-records/` and nowhere else, with one exception: a regression test or acceptance criterion naming the bug it guards against (Constitution §IX's *Regression exception*, worked in `docs/conventions/testing.md`). This is a rule about place, not meaning, so it answers yes or no without anyone weighing what the number was for. It governs the number, not the reasoning: why a rule exists stays written beside the rule as prose, and where a record already holds the decision the prose links to the record rather than to the issue. A pointer to pending work is not an exception: describe the current state instead, and track the outstanding step in an open issue, because a to-do left in the codebase points at a thread that closes and nothing flags the sentence once the work is done. Commit messages, branch names, pull request bodies and issue bodies are not the codebase — `Refs #<N>` and `Closes #<N>` stay as they are. An illustrative number in an example command, branch name or commit message is not a citation. Rationale: CIR [`2026-10-10-issue-numbers-live-in-records`](docs/change-intent-records/2026-10-10-issue-numbers-live-in-records.md).

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't frame a decision in implementation jargon** → when putting a choice to Frank (an `AskUserQuestion`, a spec tradeoff), lead with plain-language consequences — what it costs, what it unlocks — before the mechanism.

head: NetPace Development Guide > Working with Claude Code
text: - **Don't fold a second, unrelated mission into an in-flight branch** → ship the original branch with a documented known-issue and open a separate branch/issue for the new mission instead.

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text:
`mcp-server-appwrite` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
server for Appwrite. It exposes Appwrite's API to MCP clients as a small set of
operator-style tools, supporting two deployments from one codebase:

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text:
- **Cloud (hosted HTTP):** a Starlette ASGI app that acts as an OAuth 2.1
  Resource Server. It validates the client's bearer token and forwards it to the
  Appwrite REST API. Served primarily at `mcp.appwrite.io/`, with `/mcp` also
  available as a conventional alias.

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text:
- **Self-hosted (`stdio`):** runs locally and authenticates with a project API
  key (`APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID`, `APPWRITE_API_KEY`, `APPWRITE_ENDPOINT`).

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text: Python ≥ 3.12, packaged with `hatchling`, managed with `uv`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: Source lives in `src/mcp_server_appwrite/`:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text:
| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `__main__.py` / `server.py` | Entry point, CLI args, transport selection (`--transport stdio\|http`), service registration, low-level MCP server. |
| `http_app.py` | Hosted Streamable-HTTP transport: `/` plus the `/mcp` alias, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, `/healthz`. |
| `auth.py` | OAuth 2.1 resource-server layer — bearer-token validation against the project's Appwrite authorization server. |
| `flags.py` | Central registry of tester/testing flags (CLI arg + env var per flag). Enabling and testing them is documented in [docs/flags.md](docs/flags.md). |
| `service.py` | `Service` base class: introspects an Appwrite SDK service and turns its methods into MCP tool definitions. |
| `tool_manager.py` | Registry of all services and their generated tools. |
| `operator.py` | The compact "operator" surface — `appwrite_search_tools`, `appwrite_call_tool`, result/resource storage, write confirmation. |
| `context.py` | `appwrite_get_context` — workspace summary (project, services, account/org for OAuth). |
| `docs_search.py` | In-process semantic docs search (`appwrite_search_docs`) over a prebuilt index. |
| `docs_source.py` | Fetches the published docs (`/docs/llms.txt` + per-page `.md` exports on appwrite.io) and chunks them for the index build. |
| `docs_index.py` | Writes the index artifact deterministically and atomically: page and chunk hashes, reuse of cached chunk vectors, build lock, and the added/changed/removed page report. |
| `telemetry.py` | OpenTelemetry metrics layer (OTLP/HTTP). No-op unless an OTLP endpoint is configured and the transport is `http`. |
| `data/` | Committed docs index artifact (`docs_index.npz`: vectors, chunk map, chunk hashes, embedded `meta.json`), shipped in the wheel/image. |

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: `scripts/build_docs_index.py` rebuilds the docs index (requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Telemetry (metrics)
text:
`telemetry.py` emits OpenTelemetry metrics (prefixed `mcp.`) over OTLP/HTTP. It is a
no-op unless the transport is `http` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set, so
`stdio` and unconfigured servers stay silent. In the cluster that endpoint is the
Alloy collector, which adds the `deployment.*` labels and forwards upstream — the app
needs no credentials. Dashboards live in the `dashboards` repo under `MCP/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Tool surface (key design point)
text:
The server boots in a compact workflow: the client sees up to 4 tools
(`appwrite_get_context`, `appwrite_search_tools`, `appwrite_call_tool`, and
optionally `appwrite_search_docs`), while the full OAuth Appwrite catalog (38
services) stays internal and is searched at runtime. API-key stdio uses a filtered
26-service catalog. Mutating hidden tools require
`confirm_write=true`. Large outputs are stored as MCP resources and returned as a
preview + resource URI.

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist
text:
Run these locally before opening a PR. They mirror the `CI` workflow
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), which runs on every pull request and on pushes to
`main`. **All four jobs must pass.**

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist
text:
1. **Lint** (`lint` job)
   ```bash
   uv sync --group dev
   uv run --group dev ruff check src tests
   ```
   Ruff config: `target-version = py312`, rules `E`, `F`, `W`, `I` (import
   sorting), with `E501` (line length) delegated to black.

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist
text:
2. **Format** (`lint` job)
   ```bash
   uv run --group dev black --check src tests
   ```
   Run `uv run --group dev black src tests` (without `--check`) to auto-fix.

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist
text:
3. **Type check** (`lint` job)
   ```bash
   uv run --group dev pyright
   ```
   Pyright config lives in `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.pyright]`): basic mode over
   `src/`, Python 3.12, resolving against the project `.venv`.

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist
text:
4. **Unit tests** (`unit` job)
   ```bash
   uv sync
   uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests/unit -v
   ```
   Fast, no external services or credentials required.

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist
text:
5. **Docker build** (`docker` job)
   ```bash
   docker build -t appwrite-mcp:ci .
   ```
   The hosted HTTP image must build cleanly.

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist
text:
6. **Integration tests** (`integration` job) — *CI runs these only for pushes and
   for PRs from branches on the same repo (not forks).* They create and delete
   **real** Appwrite resources, so they need live credentials and are skipped
   when absent:
   ```bash
   uv sync --extra integration
   APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID=<id> APPWRITE_API_KEY=<key> APPWRITE_ENDPOINT=<url> \
     uv run --extra integration python -m unittest discover -s tests/integration -v
   ```

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist > CI environment versions
text:
CI pins Python `3.12` and `uv` `0.11.22`. Match these locally if you hit
version-specific differences.

head: AGENTS.md > Pre-PR checklist > If you change the docs index
text:
Rebuilding `src/mcp_server_appwrite/data/` requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Re-run the
build script and commit the refreshed artifact:
```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... uv run python scripts/build_docs_index.py
```

Release versions come from Git tags. Publish GitHub releases with tags in the
form `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (for example, `v0.8.8`). Python package builds derive
their version from the tag via Hatch VCS, and `server.json` is generated from
`server.template.json` during the publish workflow before sending metadata to the
MCP Registry.

```bash
uv run python scripts/render_server_json.py 0.8.8
```

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Large Module Mutation Rule
text: When the user requests a check on module size use the mutator's --scan mode to measure the number of mutation sites for the modules.  Inform the user of the those over 50 and offer to split them.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * For every new or changed behavior, write acceptance scenarios.  Ask before changing existing scenarios.  Confirm the scenarios fail.  Write failing unit tests and make them pass until scenarios pass.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * Before running changed specs use speclj-structure-check to ensure the structure.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * For every changed module run crap and refactor until crap is 8 or less.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * For every changed module run differential mutation tests, one module at a time, cover ucovered sites and kill survivors before running the next.  Set max-workers to 3.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * Differential mutation updates the manifest automatically. Do not run `--update-manifest` afterward unless there is a separate reason.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * `--update-manifest` should not run coverage at all; it is a manifest rewrite only.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * Never run crap or mutate concurrently with any other command, including another crap or mutate run.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * If you have a batch of mutation runs, let the first run generate fresh coverage, then use `--reuse-lcov` for the rest of the batch to save time.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * If an unchanged file with a manifest is split, do not copy the parent manifest into the daughters.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * If green, update daughter manifests.

head: Permissions > Coding Guidelines > Workflow
text: * Then continue with CRAP and differential mutation, which should be a no-op for a semantics-preserving split.

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file defines project-local conventions for all files in this repo.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: Build and evolve a local benchmark platform that evaluates **LLM quality** for agentic multi-agent systems. The core benchmark uses deterministic scenarios with mock tools, multi-turn conversation loops, and 3-tier scoring (pass/partial/fail). A pluggable architecture allows adding external benchmarks (GSM8K, MMLU, IFEval, future HumanEval, etc.) alongside the tool-call evaluation.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 1. **Tool-use effectiveness** — 69 standard scenarios plus 28 opt-in Hard Mode scenarios across 16 categories

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 2. **Multi-turn orchestration** — chained reasoning, conditional branching, error recovery

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 3. **Throughput benchmarking** — llama-bench style pp/tg measurement with depth/concurrency sweeps

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 4. **Pluggable benchmarks** — external accuracy benchmarks (GSM8K, MMLU, IFEval) via `BenchmarkPlugin` interface

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text:
The public scenario registry covers TC-01 through TC-69. Category P adds TC-70 through TC-97.
`--hardmode` includes Category P, `--hardmode-only` selects it alone, and explicit IDs passed to
`--scenarios` can select Hard Mode scenarios without the flag.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text:
The `tool-eval-bench` CLI is the primary interface. A public Python API supports headless
integrations. There is no web server or TUI.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural guardrails
text:
- Keep a strict layered architecture:
  - `domain` must not import storage adapters. Defines core types (`ScenarioDefinition`, `BenchmarkPlugin`).
  - `evals` depends on domain types, not concrete server logic.
  - `runner` orchestrates scenarios using adapter interfaces.
  - `plugins` contains pluggable benchmark modules (GSM8K, MMLU, IFEval). Each plugin implements `domain.plugin.BenchmarkPlugin` and owns its own orchestration.
  - `application` composes concrete adapters, orchestration, storage, and reporting.
  - `cli` is the delivery layer that calls `application.service` and plugin runners.
    `runner.service` remains a compatibility re-export only.
  - `cli` MUST NOT import `storage.db`. It may format reports through `storage.reports`, which is
    a renderer. Database reads go through `application.run_queries`, which owns each repository's
    lifetime; `tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` enforces this.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural guardrails
text: - Prefer composition over global state.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural guardrails
text:
- Keep adapters backend-specific and pluggable. OpenAI-compatible backends use the OpenAI wire
  format; Gemini and Anthropic also have native adapters and wire formats.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural guardrails
text:
- Scenarios are self-contained: one file per scenario at `evals/scenarios/<group>/tcNN.py`,
  exporting `SCENARIO` and `DISPLAY`. The group package discovers its own files, so creating the
  file is the whole registration; there is no list to append to. Helpers shared inside a group live
  in that group's `_shared.py`. Never import one scenario module from another: several groups
  define helpers under the same name with deliberately different behaviour. See
  `docs/adding-a-scenario.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural guardrails
text: - Plugins are self-contained: each owns its dataset loading, evaluation logic, and report rendering. Shared infrastructure (adapter, storage) lives outside plugins.

head: AGENTS.md > Storage and reporting rules
text: - Every completed run MUST be persisted to SQLite.

head: AGENTS.md > Storage and reporting rules
text: - Every completed run MUST also produce a Markdown artifact under `runs/YYYY/MM/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Storage and reporting rules
text: - Run IDs use a UTC timestamp + short nonce-backed hash for unique execution identity.

head: AGENTS.md > Storage and reporting rules
text: - Comparable run configurations use a separate deterministic `config_fingerprint`.

head: AGENTS.md > Storage and reporting rules
text:
- Markdown reports MUST include full traces for every scenario, except
  scenarios loaded from a held-out `--scenario-pack`. Those keep status and
  points in the report but withhold titles, summaries, and traces so publishing
  a score does not publish (and burn) the pack. Full traces remain in SQLite.

text:
- vLLM, SGLang, LiteLLM, and llama.cpp are supported via OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Gemini is
  supported through its native API as well as its OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Anthropic is
  supported through the native Messages API (`/v1/messages`), which also covers gateways that
  front other models with it, such as OpenCode Zen.

head: AGENTS.md > Compatibility targets

`CHANGELOG.md` is generated by towncrier and is never edited directly. Record a notable change by

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions
text:
The VM comes with the project venv at `.venv` (created by the startup update
script, which runs `pip install -e '.[dev,perf]'`). Always use `.venv/bin/...`
as documented in the Quality bar section. Lint/type/test/run commands are
unchanged from the Quality bar and `docs/cli-reference.md`; the notes below only cover
