head: AGENTS.md > Project
text: Taskwondo — a self-hosted task and ticket management system. Monorepo with a Go REST API (`api/`), React frontend (`web/`), MCP server (`mcp/`), and Playwright E2E tests (`test/e2e/`).

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text:
The toolchain comes from `mise.toml` at the root — Go, Node, npm and `air`, all pinned.
[mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) is the only thing `make setup` asks you to install (Docker
and `openssl` aside, which it warns about), the Makefile puts the pinned tools on `PATH`
for every target, and `make check-toolchain` — a prerequisite of every build and test
target — fails when a `go.mod`, a Dockerfile, the CI workflow or `mise.lock` declares a
version the pin disagrees with. `mise.lock` is committed and holds a checksum per tool
per platform; run `mise lock` after changing any pin. See
[README_DEV.md](README_DEV.md#toolchain-pins).

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text:
Run `make help` for the full list of Make targets (setup, dev, test, build, migrate, release, etc.).
Requires `.env` — copy from `.env.template`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Go API (`api/`)

text: - **Interfaces**: Define in the consumer package, not the provider. `service` defines repo interfaces; `repository` implements them.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > Go
text: - **Errors**: Wrap with context: `fmt.Errorf("creating work item: %w", err)`. For user-facing validation errors that need localization, use `model.NewKeyedError(sentinel, "error_key", "english message", params)` — the handler layer automatically extracts the key via `writeErrorFromService`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > Go
text: - **Error keys**: Stable, snake_case identifiers (e.g. `namespace_slug_reserved`, `project_key_in_use`). Never rename once released. Add the corresponding `errors.<key>` i18n entry to all language files.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > Go
text: - **No global state.** Dependency injection via constructors. No `init()` except in `main`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > Go
text: - **All times UTC** in the database. Convert to user timezone only in the frontend.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > Go
text: - **Commit messages**: Prefix with `[DISPLAY_ID]` (e.g. `[TF-141]`, `[PROJ-23]`) when a work item display ID is provided. The display ID format is `<PROJECT_KEY>-<NUMBER>`. No Co-Authored-By.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **i18n**: All UI strings in `web/src/i18n/en.json`. Use `const { t } = useTranslation()` in every component. `<Trans>` for JSX with embedded HTML. Module-level arrays with display strings must be inside component body. Interpolation: `{{var}}`. Pluralization: `_one`/`_other` suffixes. Any key added to `en.json` must also be added to all other language files.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **Adding a new locale**: four places must stay in sync — (1) create `web/src/i18n/<code>.json` with a full translation of `en.json`, (2) import it in `web/src/i18n/index.ts` and add it to the `resources` map, (3) add the code to the `Language` type union in `web/src/contexts/LanguageContext.tsx`, (4) add an entry to the `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` array in the same file. The i18n Vitest suite will fail if keys drift between locales.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **API errors**: Use `getLocalizedError(err, t, 'fallback.key')` from `@/utils/apiError` to display API errors. Never extract `error.message` manually. The helper resolves `error_key` → i18n translation with params, falling back to the raw message then the fallback key.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **Destructive actions**: Always `<Modal>` with cancel/confirm. Never `window.confirm()`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **Success feedback**: Inline green checkmark (`<Check>` from lucide-react), never layout-shifting toasts. Pattern: `savedId` state + `setTimeout(~2s)`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **Settings pages**: Danger Zone is always the last section.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **Shared inputs**: Never derive a visible label decoration from `required` in `Input`/`Select` — it changes the accessible name of every required field in the app and breaks `getByLabel(..., { exact: true })` in E2E. Opt in per field (`requiredMarker`) and mark the decoration `aria-hidden`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **Navigation catalog**: every navigable page and sidebar section must be reachable from the Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette (`web/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx`). `AppSidebar`, `PreferencesSidebar`, `SystemSettingsSidebar` and the palette's catalog (`web/src/utils/navigationCatalog.ts`) all render from the shared builders in `web/src/utils/sidebarNav.ts` — adding the page to the right builder there is the whole edit, and the palette picks it up for free. Only a page with no sidebar entry needs a hand-written entry in `buildNavigationCatalog`, and a whole new sidebar section needs its new builder wired into `buildNavigationCatalog` too (`navigationCatalog.test.ts` fails until it is).

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **Gating navigation entries**: labels come from `t(...)`, so a new page needs its i18n key in `en.json` **and every other locale**. A gated page must carry in the catalog the same gate it has in the sidebar and the route guard — use the predicates `isSystemAdmin` / `isCustomerOnly` / `isCustomerProject` from `web/src/utils/sidebarNav.ts` (there is no `isSystemAdmin` field on the user; the gate is `global_role === 'admin'`). A palette row that 403s on click is a bug, not a cosmetic issue.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > React/TypeScript
text: - **Tooltips**: Never use the native HTML `title` attribute for tooltips. Use the stylized Tailwind pattern: wrap the trigger with `relative group/<name>` and render an absolutely-positioned `<span>` child with `pointer-events-none absolute ... px-2 py-1 text-xs text-white bg-gray-900 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded whitespace-nowrap opacity-0 group-hover/<name>:opacity-100 transition-opacity`. See `WorkItemDetailPage.tsx` (pencil edit button) and `AppSidebar.tsx` for canonical examples.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions > API Compatibility
text: Always ask before making breaking API changes. Deprecation pattern: keep old param working, log warning, reject requests using both old and new params (400).

head: AGENTS.md > Services & Ports
text:
| Service    | Dev Port | Prod Port |
|------------|----------|-----------|
| Web (Vite) | 5173     | 3000 (nginx) |
| API        | 8080 (local only) | internal (via nginx `/api` proxy) |
| PostgreSQL | 5432     | -         |
| MinIO      | 9000/9001| -         |

head: AGENTS.md > Services & Ports
text: The API is not exposed directly in Docker — all API traffic goes through the nginx container's `/api` reverse proxy. Port 8080 is only used when running the API locally with `make dev-api`.

head: AGENTS.md > Services & Ports
text: Health: `GET /healthz` (liveness), `GET /readyz` (readiness + DB ping)

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns
text: **Coverage target:** 80%+ per package. Skip only when the remaining paths would require disproportionate complexity (mocking transactional boundaries, platform-specific code, etc.) — document the reason in the test file if so.

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns
text: **Test at the same entry point the real client hits.** A service-level test is not a substitute for a handler-level test: handlers contain their own input validation, auth checks, and response shaping that service tests will silently skip. If a bug can be triggered by an HTTP request, there must be a test that sends the same HTTP request. The same rule applies in the frontend: if a bug is visible in the UI, an E2E test should exercise the UI flow — not just the hook or API wrapper underneath.

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > Go (`api/`)
text: In-package mocks (mock structs implementing repository interfaces) and `httptest` for handler tests. Chi router is wired up in tests when URL params are needed. Tests live alongside source files.

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > MCP server (`mcp/`)
text: `make test-mcp` (also part of `make test`). Tool handlers are tested at their own entry point: an `httptest` server standing in for the API, `TASKWONDO_URL`/`TASKWONDO_API_KEY` set with `t.Setenv`, and `activeNamespace` pinned so `getClientForDisplayID` resolves without a search round trip. See `mcp/tools_test.go`.

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > Frontend (`web/`)
text: Vitest for unit tests. Tests use `*.test.ts` naming and live alongside source files. Covers i18n validation (missing keys, extra keys, placeholder consistency, untranslated values) and the pure helpers under `web/src/utils/` (navigation catalog, palette matching, key sequences). No component tests — functional coverage comes from E2E.

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > Frontend (`web/`)
text: Vitest runs with **no DOM environment**, so a module a unit test imports must not reach `@/api/client` — it touches `localStorage` at import time and the import blows up. Either `vi.mock` it, or extract the pure part into a client-free module: that is why `toUrlSegment` / `fromUrlSegment` live in `web/src/utils/namespaceUrl.ts` rather than in `useNamespacePath.ts`. `sidebarNav.ts` and `navigationCatalog.ts` must stay client-free for the same reason.

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > E2E (`test/e2e/`)
text: Playwright with `*.spec.ts` naming. Tests organized by domain under `test/e2e/tests/` (auth, admin, workitems, projects, milestones, navigation, preferences).

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > E2E (`test/e2e/`)
text: - **Fixtures** (`test/e2e/lib/fixtures.ts`): extends Playwright's base test with `testUser` and `testProject` fixtures that auto-create isolated users and projects per test

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > E2E (`test/e2e/`)
text: - **API helpers** (`test/e2e/lib/api.ts`): 60+ typed functions for setting up test data via API (work items, comments, relations, milestones, etc.)

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > E2E (`test/e2e/`)
text: - **Multi-project setup**: auth.setup.ts → admin tests → chromium.setup.ts → main suite → cleanup.teardown.ts

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > E2E (`test/e2e/`)
text: - **Fully containerized**: `make test-e2e` runs the entire stack in Docker (Postgres, MinIO, Mailpit, API, Web, Playwright)

head: AGENTS.md > Test Patterns > E2E (`test/e2e/`)
text: **Use `make test-e2e` for the full suite.** There the frontend is served by the API, so root-level routes like `/metrics` resolve. `make test-e2e-dev` targets Vite (`:5173`), which only proxies `/api` — admin/metrics specs get the SPA shell and fail. Use the dev server for targeted specs only, passing `BASE_URL=http://localhost:5173` (`playwright.config.ts` loads dotenv from `test/.env`, which does not exist, and `.env` points `BASE_URL` at `:3000`). `/auth/login` is rate-limited to 10 req/min per IP and each `testUser` spends 3, so more than ~3 dev-server tests in a minute hit 429s.

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide
text: This document summarizes the key requirements and setup instructions for the Minecraft AI-Python project, with a focus on using `uv` for Python package management.

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Project Overview
text: Minecraft AI-Python is a modular framework for building AI Characters (AICs) in Minecraft. It uses Python to control Minecraft bots via a JavaScript bridge (JSPyBridge/mineflayer), enabling LLM-driven agents to interact with the game world.

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Project Overview
text: - **Python 3.9+** - Main runtime for AI agent logic

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Project Overview
text: - **Node.js** - Runs mineflayer for Minecraft protocol communication

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Project Overview
text: - **JSPyBridge** - Python-JavaScript interop package (v1.2.6+)

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Project Overview
text: - **LLM Provider** - OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, or compatible API

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Cognitive Metabolism: Proactive Agent Model
text: The agent operates on a **Cyclic Metabolism** model rather than a linear request-response pattern:

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Cognitive Metabolism: Proactive Agent Model > Key Components
text: 1. **Identity Generation**: If `longterm_thinking` is empty, the agent generates its identity from the profile on first spawn using the reflection LLM.

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Cognitive Metabolism: Proactive Agent Model > Key Components
text:
2. **Idle Detection**: Agent is truly idle when:
   - No active goal (`current_goal is None`)
   - No pending requests (`request_queue` is empty)
   - No active work (`working_process is None`)

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Cognitive Metabolism: Proactive Agent Model > Key Components
text:
3. **Reflection Triggers**:
   - **Action completion** - Always triggers when goal completes/fails
   - **Player message** - Always triggers when receiving message while idle
   - **Idle timer** - Only triggers if `self_driven_thinking_timer` is not `null`

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Cognitive Metabolism: Proactive Agent Model > Key Components
text:
4. **Proposal/Handshake Protocol**: For autonomous actions (not triggered by player):
   - Agent announces intent: `"[Proposal] I want to X. I'll proceed in N seconds unless you have other plans."`
   - Waits for `proposal_grace_period` seconds (default: 30)
   - Player can interrupt by sending any message
   - If no interruption, action executes

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Cognitive Metabolism: Proactive Agent Model > Key Components
text: 5. **Player Interrupt**: Any player message cancels pending proposals immediately.

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Cognitive Metabolism: Proactive Agent Model > Key Components
text: 6. **Goal Persistence**: Goals persist across restarts. On restart, agent announces: `"I'm resuming: {target}"`

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Cognitive Metabolism: Proactive Agent Model > Request Priority Queue
text:
| Priority | Source | Behavior |
|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 (HIGH) | Player messages | Immediate processing |
| 2 (MEDIUM) | Self-reflection, idle reflection | Deferred if busy |
| 3 (LOW) | Goal continuation | Uses handshake protocol |

text: The bot has a reactive behavioral modes system that responds immediately to urgent situations. Modes are configured in the profile:

| `self_defense` | ON | Attack nearby enemies |
| `cheat` | OFF | Use cheats for instant block placement |
| `high_jump` | ON | Use water bucket clutch to survive high falls |

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)
text: The `high_jump` mode enables the bot to automatically survive dangerous falls using the water bucket clutch technique. This is handled by the cerebellum's `physicsTick` handler (runs every ~50ms) rather than the regular tick loop, providing the fast response time needed for the maneuver.

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)
text: 1. **Fall detection**: On every physics tick, checks if `bot.entity.velocity.y < -0.5` (falling)

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)
text: 2. **Ground scan**: Iterates blocks downward to find the first solid block below

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)
text: 3. **Safety checks**: Skips clutch if already in water, on ladder/vine/scaffolding, in creative mode, or landing on safe blocks (slime, hay bale, water, cobweb, powder snow, honey)

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)
text:
4. **Clutch trigger**: When within 3-6 blocks of ground (scaled by velocity) and fall distance > 3 blocks:
   - Looks straight down (pitch = π/2, force=True)
   - Equips water bucket (or powder snow bucket in Nether)
   - Places water on the ground block via `activateBlock`

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)
text: 5. **Water pickup**: After landing safely, picks up the water with empty bucket

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)
text: - In the Nether dimension, water evaporates. The bot automatically uses a `powder_snow_bucket` instead.

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)
text: - Falls back to regular water bucket if no powder snow bucket is available.

head: Minecraft AI-Python: Developer Guide > Key Requirements > Water Bucket Clutch (high_jump mode)

## Visual Observation (YOLO Detection - COCO Dataset)

You see the following objects through your vision system.
**Important:** This uses a general-purpose YOLOv10 model trained on real-world objects (COCO dataset).
The labels are real-world object names, NOT Minecraft-specific terms.

### Translation Guide:
In the blocky, pixelated world of Minecraft, COCO labels map roughly as follows:
- 'person' → player, villager, zombie, skeleton, or other humanoid mob
- 'cow', 'sheep', 'pig', 'horse' → corresponding passive Minecraft mobs
- 'bird' → chicken or parrot

head: CLAUDE.md

> **Keep this file alive.** It's only useful if it stays true. Treat it as part of the

head: CLAUDE.md > What this repo is
text:
`@trustvc/trustvc` is the **umbrella SDK** that ties together document issuance,
signing and verification across **two worlds**:

head: CLAUDE.md > What this repo is
text:
- **OpenAttestation / OpenCert** — hash-based documents, token registry / document
  store, on-chain transferable records (ethers + hardhat).

head: CLAUDE.md > What this repo is
text:
- **W3C Verifiable Credentials / Presentations** — Data Integrity proofs, selective
  disclosure, DID-based issuers/holders.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this repo is
text:
It depends on the **published** `@trustvc/w3c*` packages (the crypto core lives in the
separate `w3c` monorepo — see [w3c section](#relationship-to-the-w3c-monorepo)):

head: CLAUDE.md > What this repo is
text:
| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `src/core/verify.ts` | **`verifyDocument()`** — the unified verify entry point (OA + W3C). |
| `src/verify/verify.ts` | `verificationBuilder`, `openAttestationVerifiers`, `w3cVerifiers`. |
| `src/verify/fragments/` | Verifier fragments by dimension: `document-integrity`, `document-status`, `issuer-identity`, `presentation`. |
| `src/w3c/` | The W3C surface: `sign`, `derive`, `verify`, **`presentation`** (VP wrappers), `types`. |

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: Node **≥ 20** — `engines` is enforced. Use `nvm use 20`; on Node 18 the install/tests fail.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text:
**Before "done": run `npm run type-check` AND `npm run lint`.** `lint` is
`--max-warnings=0`; a single warning is a red build.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text:
**Tests hit the network.** did:web resolution and StatusList fetches go to
`trustvc.github.io` (e.g. `.../did/1`, `.../credentials/statuslist/1`). These are real
integration checks — don't mock them away. On-chain tests need the hardhat node
(`test:e2e`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
text:
The trustvc layer is **opinionated**: it wraps the raw `@trustvc/w3c-vc` primitives and
**enforces policies so callers can't disable them.**

head: CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
text:
**`signW3CPresentation(credentials, keyPair, options)`** — create **and** sign in one
call. Enforced:

head: CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
text:
- **`fullDisclosure`** — a base (non-derived) SD credential is **auto-full-disclosed**;
  callers may pass underived credentials.

head: CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
text:
- **`checkHolderBinding`** — signing-key DID **==** holder **==** every
  `credentialSubject.id`. The **issuer is deliberately NOT part of this** — a credential
  issued by a different party (e.g. a did:web issuer) is fine.

head: CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
text: - **Mandatory lifetime** — the caller MUST pass `expiresInSeconds` or `validUntil`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
text:
- **`version: 'v2'`** — the presentation **envelope is always VC Data Model v2.0**
  (`validFrom`/`validUntil`); `version` is dropped from the caller options. Embedded
  credentials keep their own version (a v1.1 VC can sit inside a v2 envelope).

head: CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
text:
- Suite is `ecdsa-rdfc-2019` (a non-ECDSA key → error). `challenge` → `authentication`
  proof; no challenge → `assertionMethod`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
CLAUDE.md > Verifiable Presentations (`src/w3c/presentation.ts`)
text:
**When you add or change a policy, change it in the wrapper — not by trusting callers —
and keep create/verify symmetric** (if create rejects something, verify must too).

head: CLAUDE.md > VP verification fragments (`src/verify/fragments/presentation/`)
text: Three aggregate verifiers plug into `verifyDocument()`'s pipeline via `w3cVerifiers`:

head: CLAUDE.md > VP verification fragments (`src/verify/fragments/presentation/`)
text:
- `w3cVpSignatureIntegrity` (DOCUMENT_INTEGRITY) — **requires a holder proof** (unsigned
  → INVALID), verifies the proof crypto + **each embedded credential's signature**, and
  enforces **holder binding** in-fragment. This fragment is **strictly cryptographic**:
  embedded credentials are checked with `verifyCredential` (signature only), **not**
  `verifyPresentation`'s `credentialResults` — the latter folds expiry/revocation into
  `verified`, and those are DOCUMENT_STATUS concerns, not integrity. Freshness
  (challenge/domain) is also out of scope — a stateless pipeline can't check it.

head: CLAUDE.md > VP verification fragments (`src/verify/fragments/presentation/`)
text:
- `w3cVpCredentialStatus` (DOCUMENT_STATUS) — VP expiry + each embedded credential's
  **temporal validity** (expiry / not-yet-valid, honouring v2 `validFrom`/`validUntil`
  and v1.1 `issuanceDate`/`expirationDate`) + StatusList revocation.

head: CLAUDE.md > VP verification fragments (`src/verify/fragments/presentation/`)
text: - `w3cVpIssuerIdentity` (ISSUER_IDENTITY) — each embedded issuer resolves.

head: CLAUDE.md > VP verification fragments (`src/verify/fragments/presentation/`)
text:
**Layer split (why an expired embedded VC lands in STATUS, not INTEGRITY):** temporal
validity is a *status* property, so it's judged by `w3cVpCredentialStatus`. INTEGRITY
answers only "is every signature authentic + is the holder bound". If you move a check
between these two fragments, move its test with it — an expired embedded VC must stay
caught *somewhere*.

head: CLAUDE.md > VP verification fragments (`src/verify/fragments/presentation/`)
text:
`isVpDocument()` (the `test()` gate) routes on shape only (`type` includes
`VerifiablePresentation` + has `verifiableCredential`) — it does **not** look at `proof`,
so an unsigned VP is still routed in and then judged INVALID by the integrity fragment.

head: CLAUDE.md > VP verification fragments (`src/verify/fragments/presentation/`)
text:
**Consistency note:** the fragment pipeline and `verifyW3CPresentation` were deliberately
aligned to both enforce proof-presence + holder binding. If you touch one, keep the other
in step.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (hard-won — add to this list)
text:
- **Selective disclosure keeps the subject `id`.** If a credential was issued *with* a
  `credentialSubject.id`, deriving it (even revealing only other fields) **retains that
  id**. To test/produce a credential with *no* subject id, it must be issued without one.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (hard-won — add to this list)
text:
- **Holder binding is string-equality of DIDs and is method-agnostic** (did:key and
  did:web both work). It's independent of the issuer.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (hard-won — add to this list)
text:
- **StatusList test indices** on `.../statuslist/1` (a **StatusList2021Credential**): index
  **5 → revoked**, index **10 → not revoked**. `.../statuslist/2` is the **BitstringStatusList**
  equivalent — indices **5–9 → revoked**, others not (so 5 → revoked, 10 → not revoked, same
  mnemonic). Reuse these instead of inventing new ones.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (hard-won — add to this list)
text:
- **Test fixtures share key material** across did:key and did:web (the same ECDSA key is
  published under `did:key:zDnae…` and `did:web:trustvc.github.io:did:1#multikey-1`). Handy
  for tests, but it means "different DID" ≠ "different key" in fixtures.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (hard-won — add to this list)
text:
- **`VerificationFragment` is a union** — `reason`/`data` aren't on every member; narrow or
  cast when asserting on them in tests.

head: CLAUDE.md > Relationship to the w3c monorepo
text:
The VP/VC crypto logic lives in `@trustvc/w3c-vc` (separate repo, `../w3c-10`). To test an
**unpublished** w3c-vc change here, `npm pack` it there and install the tarball; once
published, repoint the dep to the version (`^2.3.0`). Real changes should be validated
here because this repo resolves the packages' full dep tree (and stricter jsonld) — a
green w3c-vc build alone doesn't prove integration.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > What This Is
text: JARVIS is the Body of a tri-partite AGI OS. This repo contains the macOS integration layer (screen capture, voice, keyboard automation), the unified supervisor (102K-line monolithic kernel), and the Ouroboros self-development governance engine. All model references are resolved from `brain_selection_policy.yaml` -- zero hardcoded model names.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Key Conventions
text: - **Async-first**: All I/O uses `asyncio`. No blocking calls on the event loop.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Key Conventions
text: - **No hardcoded models**: All model names come from `brain_selection_policy.yaml` or env vars.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Key Conventions
text: - **Env-var driven config**: Every tunable parameter reads from environment variables with sensible defaults.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Key Conventions
text: - **Python 3.9+**: No `asyncio.timeout` (3.11+) -- use `asyncio.wait_for` everywhere.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Key Conventions
text: - **`from __future__ import annotations`**: Required in all files for forward reference support.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Ouroboros Pipeline
text: The self-development engine runs an 11-phase governance pipeline:

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Ouroboros Pipeline > Provider Chain (3-Tier Failback)
text:
| Tier | Provider | Cost | Notes |
|------|----------|------|-------|
| 0 | DoubleWord 397B (3-tier: RT SSE + webhook + adaptive poll) | RT $0.39/$2.45 · async $0.29/$1.84 · batch $0.19/$1.23 /M | 16384 max_tokens, RT default, preferred. (Corrected 2026-07-21: the old $0.10/$0.40 figure was the 35B-dottxt BATCH rate — a 4-6× understatement for the 397B.) **The RT tier requires `service_tier:"priority"` in the request body** — without it DW serves the default async tier (~66s TTFT, the 0-APPLY soak class). Injected at the ONE seam `apply_rt_service_tier` (master `JARVIS_DW_SERVICE_TIER_ENABLED`, tier `JARVIS_DW_RT_SERVICE_TIER`, per-model rejection cache); batch bodies never carry it. |
| 1 | Claude (Anthropic API) | $3/$15/M | Extended thinking + prompt caching, 60s fallback cap |
| 2 | J-Prime (GCP self-hosted) | VM cost only | When available |

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Ouroboros Pipeline > Urgency-Aware Provider Routing (Manifesto §5)
text: Deterministic routing based on signal urgency + source + task complexity. Stamped at ROUTE phase by `UrgencyRouter` (`urgency_router.py`). No LLM calls — pure code, <1ms.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Ouroboros Pipeline > Urgency-Aware Provider Routing (Manifesto §5)
text:
| Route | Strategy | Cost | When |
|-------|----------|------|------|
| IMMEDIATE | Claude direct, skip DW | ~$0.03/op | Critical urgency, voice commands, test failures, runtime health |
| STANDARD | DW primary → Claude fallback | ~$0.005/op | Normal-priority moderate ops (default cascade) |
| COMPLEX | Claude plans → DW executes | ~$0.015/op | heavy_code, multi-file architectural changes |
| BACKGROUND | DW only, no Claude fallback | ~$0.002/op | OpportunityMiner, DocStaleness, TODOs, backlog |
| SPECULATIVE | DW batch fire-and-forget | ~$0.001/op | IntentDiscovery, DreamEngine pre-computation |

text: - **SideChannel / `/btw`** (`governance/{side_channel,btw_repl}.py`): the operator's aside lane — a question asked WHILE O+V works, that neither becomes work nor takes the floor. Root cause it closes: `/goal` turns a question into an IntentEnvelope, and `/ask` awaits the provider on `operator_input_queue._drain`'s single consumer, so the next keystroke queues behind the last answer. Three properties: **submit is instant** (returns an `s-N` ticket, never awaits a provider); **answering is non-preemptive** (`assess_admission` defers while ops are in flight past `JARVIS_BTW_OPS_HEADROOM` or memory pressure is CRITICAL, jittered exponential backoff); **deferral is bounded** (`JARVIS_BTW_DEFER_MAX_S`, default 120s, then admitted under load and the answer says so). Answers come from `fast_path_qa.ask_question` — no parallel provider, no parallel budget — grounded via its new additive `grounding=` seam with a live-situation digest composed from a reader REGISTRY (status line / in-flight streams / narrative / recent ops / posture / queue), off-loop and time-boxed. Delivery re-enters the originating `attach_session.session_scope` (a ContextVar does not survive the task boundary) and holds while a modal overlay owns the screen. Refuses rather than drops at depth; only TERMINAL tickets are evicted; a `PRE_SHUTDOWN_EVENT_SET` termination hook reports unanswered asides. Verbs `/btw <q>` `/btw` `/btw status` `/btw cancel s-N`, plus `/expand s-N`. Reachable from BOTH surfaces because `harness._try_registry_verb` now falls through to `repl_dispatch_registry.try_dispatch` (closing the attach-vs-daemon verb split for all 89 auto-discovered verbs). Master `JARVIS_BTW_ENABLED` default-TRUE (the LANE); answering still gated by `JARVIS_FAST_PATH_QA_ENABLED`. 118 tests.

text: - **AuditRatchet sweep + AuditDriftSensor** (`audit_ratchet.sweep` + `intake/sensors/audit_drift_sensor.py`, 2026-08-15): closes the loop from *measured* to *acted on*. The ratchet's boot watchdog only ever logged one WARNING line; a regression against an accepted floor now becomes an `IntentEnvelope`. **One scan, N consumers**: `sweep()` is single-flight + TTL-cached (`JARVIS_AUDIT_SWEEP_TTL_S`, default 900s) over `run_registered_watchdogs()` — the boot seam and the sensor share the same reading (the two shipped instruments cost ~12s + ~29s of parsing), and a cached reading is re-stamped `fresh=False` so no consumer can report a scan it never ran. **Dedup is structural, not statistical**: findings cluster by their resolved DIRECTORY (`locate_finding`: `path::node` → path; dotted module → two stats, then the canonical `reverse_dep_resolver.build_module_to_path`) — no trace hashing, no correlation window. A drift large in *proportion* to `scanned` (`max(STORM_MIN=12, STORM_FRACTION=0.05 × scanned)`) collapses to ONE storm envelope. Subset buckets claim their keys first (evidence `flag_literal` ⊂ `source_only`), unlocatable findings never become ops (counted in `health()`), and every envelope is `urgency=low` on BACKGROUND. Event-primary via `fs.changed.*` with a settle timer (`JARVIS_AUDIT_DRIFT_SETTLE_S`, 300s) coalescing an editing session into one measurement; poll is the backstop. **The floor is not an editable target** — `.jarvis/` plus `audit_ratchet`/`surface_reachability`/`source_assertion_audit`/`audit_drift_sensor` are in `tool_executor._PROTECTED_PATH_SUBSTRINGS`, so the cheapest "fix" (re-accept the baseline, weaken the audit) is structurally refused. Master `JARVIS_AUDIT_DRIFT_SENSOR_ENABLED` default **false**. Token bucket + per-scan cap shared with the cage/liveness sensors via `intake/sensors/emission_control.py`. 31 tests.

text: - **Test→Source Attribution Bridge — Slice 6** (`intent/test_source_attribution.py` + `reverse_dep_resolver.extract_module_imports`/`build_module_to_path`): TestFailure signals carry BOTH loci — `target_files=(*source_loci, test_locus)` resolved by deterministic AST import tracing of the failing test module (alias/relative/mock.patch-target aware; traceback frames rank, never decide). head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Ouroboros Pipeline > Key Subsystems
text: - **Slice 12+13 — landing + value** (`worktree_manager` baseline exemption + `candidate_value_gate.py`): Slice 12 lets a verified repair LAND on the defect it fixes — a dirty promotion-target path is exempt from `target_dirty` IFF its live sha256 exactly equals the op's GENERATE-time baseline (`state_drift.file_sha256`, the drift check's own object — proof the dirt IS the defect state, not human work; archive→`git restore`→land; any deviation/deletion/lock fails closed; `JARVIS_PROMOTION_BASELINE_EXEMPTION_ENABLED`). Slice 13 kills the Run-22 noise class — at the post-GENERATE seam, a candidate whose every file is mathematically cosmetic (Python: AST equality after `epistemic_shedder` docstring stripping; requirements/cfg/ini: whole-line grammar normalization) completes as benign `no_op_cosmetic` before VALIDATE/APPLY/VERIFY spend; one byte of executable change, a SyntaxError, or an unknown format passes forward (`JARVIS_CANDIDATE_VALUE_GATE_ENABLED`).

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Ouroboros Pipeline > Key Subsystems
text: - **Local zero-cost generation lane** (`local_inference_director` + `candidate_generator` + `inference_gateway` + `ouroboros_battle_test`, 2026-08-24): makes a locally-served J-Prime a first-class lane rather than a lane the preflight refuses to boot. Four parts. (1) **Constrained decoding ladder** — `json_schema → json_object → none`, applied at one seam (`_apply_response_format`). A local mid-size model asked to place a source file into a JSON string reaches for Python triple-quotes and fails at the same offset every time (6 of 6 candidate payloads in the 2026-08-20 soak); `json_object` makes invalid JSON unrepresentable, and the full schema (`providers.build_response_json_schema`, a projection of `_SCHEMA_VERSION`/`_CANDIDATE_KEYS` so grammar and validator cannot drift) makes a missing required field unrepresentable — which is what `json_object` alone could not do and why `candidate_0_missing_rationale` and `wrong_schema_version:__missing__` survived it. Property ORDER is load-bearing: every short required field precedes the unbounded `full_content`, or `rationale` is only reached if the token budget survived the file body. Capability is learned by OBSERVATION — a 4xx adds `(base_url, model)` to a per-process rejection cache and retries once at the next rung; a 5xx is the engine FAILING, not refusing, and never disarms the constraint. (2) **Free-lane cost interlock** — `_free_lane_active()` lets cost-motivated gates ask about COST instead of hardcoding a route name; on a lane whose marginal cost is ~zero the swarm-chunking skip stops being a saving and becomes pure loss (the local "swarm" is serialized onto one device by the VRAM mutex, so it is sequential chunking: slower but free). `.env` is re-read on a TTL so a key added mid-soak revokes free-lane status without a restart — `os.environ` is per-process and `load_env_once` is idempotent, so without the re-read that promise could not be honoured. Absence of a key is the strongest available evidence that no paid lane exists; any key present means NOT free. (3) **Gateway in-flight unification** — `external_generation()` brackets a generation the gateway did not itself dispatch, closing the blind spot where an advisory pre-warm reads "idle" and evicts weights out from under a live stream; decrements in `finally` so a stall or cancellation cannot leak the host as permanently busy. (4) **Preflight asserts a LANE, not a cloud key** — `_check_api_keys_or_die` now probes `/api/tags` and requires ≥1 served model, so the zero-marginal-cost configuration stops being the one configuration that cannot boot; a flag alone is not evidence, and an unreachable engine still dies loudly at second zero. Masters `JARVIS_LOCAL_JSON_MODE_ENABLED` / `JARVIS_LOCAL_JSON_SCHEMA_MODE_ENABLED` / `JARVIS_FREE_LANE_POLICY_ENABLED` / `JARVIS_GATEWAY_INFLIGHT_UNIFICATION_ENABLED` default-TRUE; knobs `JARVIS_FREE_LANE_CRED_TTL_S` (30s, `0` disables), `JARVIS_DOC_MAX_NAMED_SYMBOLS` (8 — DocStaleness findings name the undocumented symbols so `TargetSymbolResolver` can narrow an op below whole-file scope; the structured `undocumented_symbols` field is never truncated). The two predecessor flags from the 32B arc (`JARVIS_LOCAL_VRAM_AUTODETECT_ENABLED`, `JARVIS_GATEWAY_VRAM_MUTEX_ENABLED`) stay default-FALSE — byte-identical for a provisioned failover node, opt-in for a workstation. All registered in FlagRegistry, co-located via `register_flags` where the discovery loop reaches — except `JARVIS_DOC_MAX_NAMED_SYMBOLS`, seeded in `flag_registry_seed` because `intake.sensors` is not one of the `_FLAG_PROVIDER_PACKAGES` the discovery loop walks, so a registrar co-located with the sensor would never be invoked. (5) **BACKGROUND routes to the cheapest lane, not to a named one** (2026-08-27) — BACKGROUND and SPECULATIVE encode "spend nothing" as a PROVIDER NAME, so a purged DW catalog leaves nothing cheap to name and the op dead-queues on `background_dw_blocked_by_topology`; the block site's own comment names its release condition exactly ("until a viable, cost-effective inference endpoint is secured") while a $0.00/op lane sits idle on the same host. `_try_free_lane_dispatch` asks the block that question at BOTH raise sites (the topology pre-block and the post-sweep exhaustion), reusing `_discover_jprime_endpoint` + `_failover_local_dispatch` — no new provider seat. Deliberately NOT gated on `_free_lane_active()`: that predicate asks "is the free lane the ONLY lane?", right for a cost *interlock* and wrong here, since local marginal cost is zero whether or not a DW key also exists. Ordered BEFORE the read-only Claude cascade, because $0.00 beats ~$0.005 on the route whose whole contract is frugality. Requires EVIDENCE — an endpoint that answered, never a flag asserting one should exist — so every host without a local lane keeps byte-identical dead-queue behaviour; every failure mode (flag off, wrong route, no endpoint, empty candidates, dispatch error) falls through to the pre-existing raise, and `CancelledError` propagates so a shutdown is never reported as a topology block. Master `JARVIS_BACKGROUND_LOCAL_LANE_ENABLED` default-TRUE. 109-test spine `tests/governance/test_local_lane_arc.py`. A `2b.1-noop` verdict returns through the seam rather than falling through: the model concluding "already done" is an ANSWER, and reporting it as a topology block would describe an outage that never happened.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Battle Test
text: **`--max-wall-seconds SEC`** (env `OUROBOROS_BATTLE_MAX_WALL_SECONDS`, Ticket A1 Guard 2, 2026-04-23): hard wall-clock ceiling on total session duration — fires `stop_reason=wall_clock_cap` when exceeded. Opaque to any activity signal so it cannot be defeated by provider retry storms that reset `--idle-timeout`'s per-op liveness counter (the failure mode that hung #7 GENERATE S2 for 67+ min). `0` or unset disables the cap (legacy 3-way race: shutdown / budget / idle). **Graduation soaks MUST set this** — typical value `2400` (40 min) for ~2× safety margin over the 850–1300s happy-path. Treated equivalent to `idle_timeout` for clean-bar purposes in the Wave 2 (5) graduation matrix harness-class footnote.

head: CLAUDE.md -- JARVIS Trinity AI Ecosystem > Battle Test
text: > **Watchdog Isolation Invariant (Slice 47, 2026-05-30 — load-bearing).** The wall-clock cap and its resource-zero hard-kill thread (`harness.py::_start_wall_clock_hard_deadline_thread`) MUST remain completely blind to application state-ledgers — they read only raw `time.monotonic()`/`time.time()`, never the Orchestrator op-ledger, phase, or any liveness signal from the system they guard. **Rationale:** Slice 47 considered an "adaptive budget waiver" that would extend the cap when a worker reached APPLY/VERIFY/AutoCommit. Rejected on bisection: coupling an out-of-band watchdog to the inner op-ledger means a *wedged* VERIFY (deadlock, pytest hang — the v41 67-min failure class) keeps the extend-condition true forever, so the watchdog deadlocks *with* the system instead of killing it. This is the same principle that retired the `JARVIS_WALL_CLOCK_ESCALATION_SIGTERM_S/_EXIT_S` knobs (`harness.py:5489`): a watchdog that shares a resource — signal path, logging lock, **or state-ledger** — with the system it guards is not a watchdog. The correct, decoupled answer to "the patch got severed mid-commit" is a larger *static* margin (`--max-wall-seconds 2400`), never a dynamic activity-gated waiver.

Replaces the deprecated `tail -f /dev/null | python3 ...` stdin-guard idiom. `--no-headless` is the escape hatch to force interactive REPL when stdin isn't a TTY (rare).

head: CLAUDE.md > Submodule Map > Why dispatch/ and dmcp/ appear twice
text:
`Project-JARVIS` carries its own copies as submodules under `deps/rust/`.
The top-level `dispatch/` and `dmcp/` in this repo exist for the ISO build
pipeline — `03b-build-kernel.sh` and `04-bake-jarvis.sh` need direct access
to the Rust crates without navigating through `Project-JARVIS/`. Both
pointers must track the same commit; update them together.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Research Context
text: This repo is a cybersecurity research platform. The README lists a 7-threat taxonomy discovered during live operation — including a novel "forgetful context" threat (#7) where the LLM silently drops security constraints mid-session. Active open work items: scoped sudo rules, persistent constraint register in the daemon, GPG verification for `dmcp` server manifests, and path-based rules in `jarvis_policy.c` for writes to `/etc`, `/usr`, `/boot`.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > System Overview
text: `uaa-release` is a **BOSH release** that packages and deploys [Cloud Foundry UAA](https://github.com/cloudfoundry/uaa) (the OAuth2/SSO identity provider for Cloud Foundry) as a set of VMs/jobs on a BOSH-managed platform. This repo does not contain UAA's application logic — that lives in the `src/uaa` git submodule (a separate Java/Spring Boot codebase) — it contains the **deployment glue**: ERB templates, packaging scripts, BOSH job/package specs, and Ruby/Go tests that turn the UAA WAR file into a runnable, configurable BOSH job. Architecturally this is a **BOSH release (packaging + deployment orchestration)** around a monolithic Java web application (Tomcat or embedded Spring Boot Tomcat), not a microservices system.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Core Tech Stack & Tools
text: - **Deployment framework**: [BOSH](https://bosh.io) release format (`jobs/`, `packages/`, `spec` files, `.final_builds`/`.dev_builds`)

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Core Tech Stack & Tools
text: - **Application runtime** (packaged, not authored here): Java (BellSoft JDK, see `jdk-25.0.3/`), Apache Tomcat (`apache-tomcat-*.tar.gz`), Spring Boot (embedded Tomcat mode)

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Core Tech Stack & Tools
text: - **Templating**: ERB (`*.erb` files under `jobs/*/templates`) rendered by BOSH into job configs (`uaa.yml`, `bpm.yml`, `log4j2.properties`, `tomcat/server.xml`, etc.)

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Core Tech Stack & Tools
text: - **Config/process supervision**: [BPM](https://github.com/cloudfoundry/bpm-release) (`config/bpm.yml.erb`), Monit (`jobs/*/monit`)

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Core Tech Stack & Tools
text:
- **Test frameworks**:
  - Ruby / RSpec (`bundle exec rake` or `rspec spec`) — validates ERB template rendering against fixture manifests (`spec/input/*.yml` → `spec/compare/*`)
  - Go / Ginkgo (`src/acceptance_tests`) — end-to-end acceptance tests run as a BOSH errand job against a live deployment

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Core Tech Stack & Tools
text: - **Dependency management**: Bundler (`Gemfile`/`Gemfile.lock`) for Ruby, Go modules (`go.mod`/`go.sum`) for acceptance tests, git submodule for `src/uaa`

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Core Tech Stack & Tools

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Core Tech Stack & Tools
text: - **Backup/restore**: [BBR](https://github.com/cloudfoundry-incubator/bosh-backup-and-restore) scripts for the UAA database (`jobs/bbr-uaadb`)

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Key Architecture & Data Flow
text:
**Build/package time** (`bosh create-release` / CI):
`packages/uaa/spec` (declares inputs: `src/uaa` submodule output, JDK tarball, Tomcat tarball) → `packages/uaa/packaging` (bash script compiles/assembles: unpacks JDK, unpacks Tomcat, copies in `cloudfoundry-identity-uaa.war` as `ROOT.war`, copies the statsd WAR and Tomcat listener jar) → a versioned, immutable **compiled package** blob.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Key Architecture & Data Flow
text:
**Deploy time** (`bosh deploy`):
Operator-supplied BOSH manifest properties → `jobs/uaa/spec` (declares/validates properties, and BOSH links like `uaa_db`, `uaa_keys`, `router`, `database`) → ERB templates under `jobs/uaa/templates/` are rendered with those properties → produces `config/uaa.yml`, `config/bpm.yml`, `config/tomcat/server.xml`, `config/log4j2.properties`, `bin/pre-start`, `bin/health_check`, etc. on the target VM → **Monit** starts the job via **BPM**, which launches either Tomcat (WAR deployment, `runtime.tomcat.enabled=true`) or the embedded Spring Boot runtime → the running UAA app talks to the UAA database (via the `uaa_db`/`database` BOSH link) and optionally an LDAP/SAML IdP per configured properties.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Key Architecture & Data Flow
text: **Errand jobs** run on-demand via `bosh run-errand`:

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Key Architecture & Data Flow
text: - `acceptance-tests` — deployed alongside UAA on the same network, shells out to `bosh ssh`/`bosh scp` and makes HTTP calls directly to the UAA instance (deliberately avoids jumpboxes, per the comment in `jobs/acceptance-tests/spec`).

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Key Architecture & Data Flow
text: - `bbr-uaadb` — invoked by BOSH Backup and Restore to lock/dump/restore the UAA database.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Key Architecture & Data Flow
text: **Verification loop** (this repo's own tests, not UAA's): RSpec renders each ERB template against fixture manifests in `spec/input/*.yml` and diffs the output against golden files in `spec/compare/*`, catching template regressions before a real deploy.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Development Setup & Crucial Commands
text: **Requirements**: Ruby + Bundler (template tests), Go (acceptance tests), a BOSH director + `bosh` CLI (real deploys), git submodules initialized (`src/uaa`).

| Task | Command |
|---|---|

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Guardrails & Design Patterns
text: - **Never edit UAA application code in this repo.** `src/uaa` is a pinned git submodule tracking `github.com/cloudfoundry/uaa`. Application/business-logic changes belong in that upstream repo and land here only as a submodule SHA bump (see recent commit history: `Bump UAA to <sha>`). This repo owns *packaging and deployment*, not app behavior.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Guardrails & Design Patterns
text: - **Every property exposed to operators must be declared in the job `spec` file** (`jobs/uaa/spec`, `jobs/bbr-uaadb/spec`, `jobs/acceptance-tests/spec`) before it can be referenced in an ERB template — BOSH validates templates against the spec's `properties:` block.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Guardrails & Design Patterns
text: - **Template changes require a corresponding RSpec fixture/golden-file update.** Any change to a file under `jobs/*/templates` should have a matching case in `spec/*_spec.rb`, an input manifest in `spec/input/`, and expected output in `spec/compare/`. Run `bundle exec rake` before considering a template change done.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Guardrails & Design Patterns
text: - **Deprecated properties must keep working.** See `spec/input/deprecated-properties-still-work.yml` — this release maintains backward compatibility for renamed/deprecated manifest properties rather than breaking existing deployments.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Guardrails & Design Patterns
text: - **Packaging scripts (`packages/*/packaging`) run with `set -e -x`** — treat them as fail-fast; don't suppress errors, and any added step should preserve strict-mode safety (check exit codes explicitly where subshells are involved, as the existing JDK/Tomcat unpack steps do).

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Guardrails & Design Patterns
text: - **Errand jobs run on-network deliberately.** The `acceptance-tests` job's placement is a documented workaround (see comment block in `jobs/acceptance-tests/spec`) for jumpbox/SOCKS5 timeouts and read-only `/etc/hosts` on Concourse workers — don't "simplify" this back onto an off-network worker without re-reading that rationale.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Guardrails & Design Patterns
text: - **Two build stages exist for blobs**: `.dev_builds/` (local, iterative) vs `.final_builds/` (official, versioned) — tracked via `config/blobs.yml`/`config/final.yml`. Don't hand-edit blob directories; use the `scripts/`/`bosh create-release --final` flow.

head: CLAUDE.md — uaa-release > Guardrails & Design Patterns
text: - **Repo-root scratch/diagnostic files are not part of the release.** Files like `check-*.sh`, `find-*.sh`, `*-diagnostics.md`, `tomcat-troubleshooting-guide.md`, `manifest-*.yml` variants, and the `apache-tomcat-*.tar.gz`/`jdk-25.0.3/` directories at repo root are local working/debug artifacts, not tracked release inputs — the canonical manifest inputs are `manifest.yml`/`opsfile.yml` and the `jobs/`/`packages/` specs.

head: AGENTS.md > Build & Run Commands
text: Requires JDK 21+. The `runServer` task uses an Adoptium Java 25 toolchain and auto-downloads LuckPerms, VaultUnlocked, and EssentialsX. To train its AOT cache, comment out `-XX:AOTCache=server.aot`, uncomment `-XX:AOTCacheOutput=server.aot`, run the server with a representative workload, and stop it cleanly. Restore the original comments for subsequent runs. The cache is stored as `run/server.aot` and includes all classes loaded during training, including ParcelLockers. Uncomment the DiscordSRV line in `build.gradle.kts` to test that integration locally.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview
text: ParcelLockers is a Paper plugin (Minecraft 1.21) that lets players transfer items between parcel locker blocks across the world, with optional Discord notifications.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Entry Point & Wiring
text: `ParcelLockers.java` (`onEnable`) is the manual DI root — all components are instantiated and wired there in order: config → database → repositories → managers/services → GUIs → commands → event controllers. There is no DI framework; dependencies are passed via constructors.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Domain Layers
text: Each domain (`locker`, `parcel`, `content`, `delivery`, `itemstorage`, `user`, `discord`) follows a consistent layered structure:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Domain Layers
text: - **Model** — plain record/class (e.g. `Locker`, `Parcel`, `User`)

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Domain Layers
text: - **Repository** — interface + `*OrmLite` implementation backed by H2/PostgreSQL via ORMLite

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Domain Layers
text: - **Manager/Service** — business logic, coordinates repository calls; repositories return `CompletableFuture<T>` for all async DB operations

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Domain Layers
text: - **Controller** — Bukkit `Listener` handling in-game events (block place/break/interact, player join/quit)

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Key Components
text:
| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DatabaseManager` | Manages HikariCP connection pool; supports H2 (default, embedded) and PostgreSQL |
| `ConfigService` + okaeri-configs | Loads `config.yml` and `messages.yml` via YAML; `PluginConfig` and `MessageConfig` are the config POJOs |
| `NoticeService` + multification | Sends MiniMessage-formatted notices to players; all user-facing text goes through `MessageConfig` |
| `ParcelDispatchService` | Orchestrates sending a parcel: validates, charges economy (Vault), schedules `ParcelSendTask` |
| `ParcelSendTask` | Runs async after a configurable delay; marks parcel DELIVERED and fires the deliver notification event |
| `GuiManager` + triumph-gui | Factory for all inventory GUIs; `LockerGui` and `MainGui` are the two root GUI entry points |
| `DiscordProviderPicker` | Selects between Discord4J (standalone bot) and DiscordSRV (delegation) at startup based on detected plugins |
| `LockerPlaceController` | Uses Paper's Dialog API (unstable) to prompt for a locker description when a player places the locker item |

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Optional Integrations
text: - **DiscordSRV** — when present, account linking and DM notifications are delegated to it; otherwise, the plugin manages its own Discord bot via Discord4J

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Optional Integrations
text: - **Vault** — required; used to charge players an economy fee when sending parcels

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview > Testing
text: Tests live in `src/test/java/`. Integration tests (e.g. `LockerRepositoryIntegrationTest`) extend `IntegrationTestSpec` and use Testcontainers (MySQL) to test repository implementations against a real database. `ParcelPageTest` is a unit test with no container dependency.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: **CI (GitHub Actions):** uses the standard WordPress PHPUnit setup — `bin/install-wp-tests.sh` provisions the test library at `/tmp/wordpress-tests-lib` inside the container, and `tests/bootstrap.php` falls back to that path automatically when `WP_TESTS_DIR` is unset.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: **Local dev:** the test stack runs on Apple's native `container` runtime via [wp-env-opossum](https://www.npmjs.com/package/wp-env-opossum) (`mac-env`), which brings up the same two-site layout (dev + tests) on Apple silicon macOS 26+. Seed the cache once with `mac-env install-wp-tests`, then `npm run env:start`. The plugin is mounted inside the `tests-cli` container at `/var/www/html/wp-content/plugins/git-updater/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: The `WP_TESTS_PHPUNIT_POLYFILLS_PATH` is passed explicitly in the npm scripts to point to the vendored `yoast/phpunit-polyfills`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: PHPStan is configured at level 6 (`phpstan.neon`) with pre-existing errors tracked in `phpstan-baseline.neon`. The baseline should be regenerated with `composer phpstan-baseline` when intentional changes alter the error set.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: When removing dead code (unused static properties, intermediate writes), PHPStan may reveal type-narrowing errors (`booleanNot.alwaysTrue`, `function.alreadyNarrowedType`) in nearby conditions that were previously obscured. Fix the underlying redundancy — simplify the condition rather than suppressing the error.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: All `missingType.iterableValue` and `missingType.return` errors have been resolved across the codebase. When adding new methods or properties, follow the established PHPDoc conventions:

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: - Use specific array value types: `array<string, mixed>`, `array<int, string>`, `array<string, stdClass>`, etc. — never bare `array`

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: - Add `@return void` to every method that returns nothing

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Environment
text: - Repo config collections are typed `array<string, stdClass>`; option arrays are `array<string, mixed>`

head: AGENTS.md > Overview
text: "Linter for Zotero" (package name `zotero-format-metadata`) is a Zotero plugin that validates and formats item metadata. It is built on the [zotero-plugin-template](https://github.com/windingwind/zotero-plugin-template) and [zotero-plugin-scaffold](https://github.com/northword/zotero-plugin-scaffold) toolchain, and bundled with esbuild into an ESM script loaded by Zotero (a Firefox/Gecko `firefox115` runtime — not Node).

head: AGENTS.md > Overview
text: Target: Zotero 8 & 9. Package manager: **pnpm** (v11). Node v22+ required for development.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text: Run a single unit test: `pnpm exec vitest run src/modules/rules/no-extra-zeros.test.ts` (or `vitest -t "<test name>"`).

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text: Before running `pnpm start`, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set `ZOTERO_PLUGIN_ZOTERO_BIN_PATH` and `ZOTERO_PLUGIN_PROFILE_PATH`. On Windows escape path separators with `\\`.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text: Two test tiers exist because plugin code depends on the Zotero global runtime:

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text: - **Unit tests** (`*.test.ts`, vitest) — for pure logic that does not touch the `Zotero` global (e.g. string/pinyin/numeral helpers).

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text: - **E2E tests** (`test/tests/*.spec.ts`, mocha+chai driven by `zotero-plugin test`) — run inside a live Zotero.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Lifecycle: Bootstrap → sandbox globals → hooks
text: 1. `addon/bootstrap.js` is the XPCOM bootstrap. On startup it loads the bundled script `content/scripts/linter.js` (from `src/index.ts` via esbuild) into a sandbox `ctx` that also acts as `_globalThis`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Lifecycle: Bootstrap → sandbox globals → hooks
text: 2. `src/index.ts` bootstraps globals (`Zotero`, `ztoolkit`, `addon`) and instantiates the `Addon` class (`src/addon.ts`), which holds shared `data` and the singleton `LintRunner`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Lifecycle: Bootstrap → sandbox globals → hooks
text: 3. `src/hooks.ts` implements Zotero lifecycle hooks (`onStartup`, `onMainWindowLoad`, `onNotify`, `onShortcuts`, `onLintInBatch`, etc.). `onNotify` auto-lints newly added items when pref `lint.onAdded` is set.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Lifecycle: Bootstrap → sandbox globals → hooks
text: 4. `src/addon.ts` holds shared `data` (config, env, ztoolkit, locale, prefs window, dialogs), lifecycle `hooks`, small public `api`, and the `LintRunner`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Lifecycle: Bootstrap → sandbox globals → hooks
text: 5. UI registration is split across `src/modules/`: `menu.ts` (context menus), `item-tree.ts` (extra columns), `rich-text.ts` (title rich-text toolbar), `preference.ts`, `shortcuts.ts`, `notifier.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Lifecycle: Bootstrap → sandbox globals → hooks
text: 6. Reused browser/Zotero globals (`Zotero`, `ztoolkit`, `rootURI`, `__env__`, `_globalThis`) are ambient — see `typings/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Lifecycle: Bootstrap → sandbox globals → hooks
text: Prefer changing behavior through rules/runner/hooks rather than bootstrap.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule system (the core abstraction)
text: Everything the plugin does is expressed as a **Rule**. Rules live in `src/modules/rules/` and are defined with `defineRule()` from `rule-base.ts`. A rule declares:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule system (the core abstraction)
text: - `id` — kebab-case, following `<category>-<target>-<attribute>` (see CONTRIBUTING.md for the naming taxonomy). `category` ∈ `no` | `require` | `correct` | `tool`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule system (the core abstraction)
text: - `scope` — `"item"` (operates on whole item) or `"field"` (operates on one field; requires `targetItemField`). `"tag"`/`"attachment"` are declared but unimplemented.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule system (the core abstraction)
text: - `category`: `"rule"` (default) or `"tool"`. `category: "tool"` rules are user-invoked utilities (never auto-run); standard rules are toggleable via preferences and can run automatically.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule system (the core abstraction)
text: - `targetItemTypes` / `ignoreItemTypes` — restrict which Zotero item types the rule applies to.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule system (the core abstraction)
text: - `apply({ item, options, debug, report })` — the handler. Mutate the item with `item.setField(...)`; the runner calls `item.saveTx()` once after all rules run. Call `report({ level, message, action })` to surface a finding in the results dialog.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule system (the core abstraction)
text: - `prepare({ items, debug })` — optional; runs once before the batch, returns `options` passed to every `apply` call. Returning `false` skips the rule entirely (used e.g. to abort when a dialog is cancelled).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule system (the core abstraction)
text: - `cooldown` — min ms between executions; `defineRule` wraps `apply` in `withThrottle` to rate-limit external API calls.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule registration
text: `src/modules/rules/index.ts` holds the `register` array — **order in this array is execution order**. The `Rules` class exposes `getAll()`, `getStandard()` (non-tool), `getEnabledStandard()` (filtered by `getPref('rule.${id}')`), `getTool()`, `getByID()`, `getByType()`. To add a rule: copy `_template.ts`, implement it, import + add it to `register` at the correct position, then add prefs in `addon/prefs.js` and l10n in `addon/locale/**/rules.ftl` as needed.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Rule registration
text: Rule IDs are the source of truth for the `ID` type: `zotero-plugin.config.ts`'s `build:bundle` hook imports the registered rules and generates `typings/rules.d.ts` (an `ID` union of all rule ids) at build time. New rules won't be in the `ID` type until a build regenerates that file (`defineRule` accepts a `string` id to suppress the type error meanwhile).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Runner
text: `src/modules/runner.ts` (`LintRunner`) orchestrates a batch. It:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Runner
text: 1. Calls each rule's `prepare` to build an `optionsMap`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Runner
text: 2. Enqueues items into Zotero's `ConcurrentCaller` (concurrency from pref `lint.numConcurrent`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Runner
text: 3. For each item, iterates rules, skipping via `shouldApplyRule` (item-type + field-validity checks), wraps each `apply` in a 60s timeout, collects errors without aborting sibling rules, then `saveTx()`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Runner
text: 4. Aggregates results into a report shown via `reporter.ts` (`ProgressUI` + results dialog).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Runner
text: Entry points into a batch run go through `addon.hooks.onLintInBatch(ruleIDs, items)` in `hooks.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Metadata update services
text: `src/modules/rules/tool-update-metadata/` implements metadata fetching from external APIs (CrossRef via translate, Semantic Scholar, arXiv). Each API is a `MetadataService` (`services/base-service.ts`, defined with `defineService`) with `shouldApply` / `updateIdentifiers` / `fetch` / `transform` methods. This is a mini-plugin architecture nested inside the rule system.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Built-in data
text: Large reference datasets (journal abbreviations, conference abbreviations, university→place map, ISO language maps) live in `data/` and are bundled as assets (see `zotero-plugin.config.ts` `build.assets`). At runtime they are loaded lazily and cached via `src/utils/data-loader.ts` (`DataLoader.load(key, ...)`), resolving paths under `${rootURI}data/...`. The cache is cleared after each batch run. Regenerate these files with `pnpm update-data`, not by hand.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - ESLint config is `@antfu/eslint-config` + `@zotero-plugin/eslint-config` (double quotes, semicolons — see `eslint.config.mjs`). `autocorrect` fixes CJK/Latin spacing in text. Both run on staged files via husky + lint-staged.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Preference keys follow `rule.${id}.option-name`; read with `getPref` from `src/utils/prefs.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Fluent (l10n) message IDs: rule name `rule-${id}`, option `rule-${id}-option-${name}`, menu items `rule-${id}-menu-item` / `rule-${id}-menu-field`. Files in `addon/locale/{en-US,zh-CN}/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- Commits: Conventional Commits (e.g. `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore(deps):`,
  `refactor:`, `ci:`). Scopes are used (e.g. `fix(notify):`).

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Some source comments and commit history are in Chinese; keep new user-facing strings in the l10n files rather than hardcoding.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Try not to remove the existing comments; only add comments that you truly believe are necessary for clarification.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text: - Reduce the use of defensive code, and only use `try` blocks when absolutely necessary.

head: PDFx — Development Guide > What is PDFx?
text:
PDFx is a copy-paste component library for building PDF documents in React, modeled after
shadcn/ui. Components are **not installed as npm dependencies** — the CLI fetches source files
from the registry and copies them into the user's project.

head: PDFx — Development Guide > Architecture
text:
The registry lives at `apps/www/public/r/` (pdfx-cli: `index.json`, `{name}.json`, `blocks/`).
A parallel shadcn catalog is generated at `apps/www/public/r/shadcn/` (`registry.json` + flat
`{name}.json`, namespace `@pdfx`). Never hand-edit either tree — run `pnpm build:registry`.

head: PDFx — Development Guide > Component File Structure
text: Every component follows a **segregated file pattern**:

head: PDFx — Development Guide > Component File Structure
text:
> **Note:** The `graph` component is the only exception — it currently uses a single-file
> pattern at 893 lines. It is pending refactoring to match this structure.

head: PDFx — Development Guide > Component Naming Convention
text:
PDFx uses a `Pdf` prefix when the component name would collide with widely-used exports from
React, HTML, or @react-pdf/renderer:

head: PDFx — Development Guide > Component Naming Convention
text:
| Category | Components |
|---|---|
| **Prefixed** (`Pdf*`) | PdfAlert, PdfCard, PdfForm, PdfGraph, PdfImage, PdfList, PdfPageNumber, PdfQRCode, PdfSignatureBlock, PdfWatermark |
| **Unprefixed** | Badge, DataTable, Divider, Heading, KeepTogether, KeyValue, Link, PageBreak, PageFooter, PageHeader, Section, Stack, Table, Text |

head: PDFx — Development Guide > Component Naming Convention > Rules for new components
PDFx — Development Guide > Component Naming Convention > Rules for new components
text: 2. **Skip the prefix** if the name is unique to PDFx's domain (e.g. `KeyValue`, `DataTable`).

head: PDFx — Development Guide > Component Naming Convention > Rules for new components
text: 3. **Never rename existing components** — that would be a breaking change for installed users.

head: PDFx — Development Guide > Component Naming Convention > Rules for new components
text: 4. Document the naming decision in the component's JSDoc.

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture
text: Kausality is an admission-based drift detection system for Kubernetes. It detects when controllers make unexpected changes to child resources.

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Components
text:
| Component | Binary | ServiceAccount | Purpose |
|-----------|--------|----------------|---------|
| **Webhook** | `kausality-webhook` | `kausality-webhook` | Intercepts mutations and detects drift |
| **Controller** | `kausality-controller` | `kausality-controller` | Watches Kausality CRDs, reconciles webhook config |

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Components
text:
| ClusterRole | Bound To | Purpose |
|-------------|----------|---------|
| `kausality-webhook` | webhook | Read policies and namespaces |
| `kausality-webhook-resources` | webhook | Aggregated access to tracked resources |
| `kausality-controller` | controller | Manage CRDs, webhook config, per-policy ClusterRoles |

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Core Concept: Drift Detection
text: **Drift** = controller making changes when parent hasn't changed (`generation == observedGeneration`)

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Core Concept: Drift Detection
text:
| Actor | Parent State | Result |
|-------|--------------|--------|
| Controller | gen != obsGen | Expected (reconciling) |
| Controller | gen == obsGen | **Drift** |
| Different actor | any | New causal origin (not drift) |

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking
text: The system identifies controllers by tracking which users update parent status vs child spec. Users are identified by `UserInfo.Username` with fallback to `UserInfo.UID` for users without names:

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking
text: - Parent: `kausality.io/controllers` - 5-char base36 hashes of user identifiers who update status (max 5)

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking
text: - Child: `kausality.io/updaters` - 5-char base36 hashes of user identifiers who update spec (max 5)

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking
text: - Child CREATE/UPDATE (spec change only): hash added to child's `updaters` annotation (sync, via patch)

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking
text: - Parent status UPDATE: hash added to parent's `controllers` annotation (sync, via direct API call), plus `kausality.io/observedGeneration` set to current generation (synthetic observedGeneration for parents without native `status.observedGeneration`)

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking
text: Metadata-only changes do NOT record updaters - only spec changes do.

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking
text: Note: Controllers and observedGeneration annotations use direct API calls because status subresource patches to metadata are ignored by Kubernetes.

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking
Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Controller Identification via User Hash Tracking

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 1. **Controller identification via user hash tracking**: Controllers are identified by correlating users who update parent status with users who update child spec. Uses 5-char base36 hashes of user identifiers (username with UID fallback). Single child updater = controller; multiple updaters = intersection with parent's status updaters.

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 2. **Spec and status interception**: Intercepts spec mutations for drift detection and status subresource updates to record controller identity.

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 3. **Lifecycle phases**: Initializing and Deleting phases allow all changes. Detection uses `observedGeneration` existence, `Initialized`/`Ready` conditions.

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 4. **Phase 1 = logging only**: Currently detects and logs drift but doesn't block. `Allowed` is always `true`.

text:
3. **Story-telling with t.Log** - Tests should tell a story with descriptive log statements:
```go
func TestFeature(t *testing.T) {
    t.Log("=== Testing Feature X ===")
    t.Log("When condition Y, the system should do Z")

    t.Log("")
    t.Log("Step 1: Creating the resource...")
    // ... create resource

    t.Log("")
    t.Log("Step 2: Waiting for controller to reconcile...")
    // ... wait for condition

    t.Log("")
    t.Log("SUCCESS: Feature X works correctly")
}
```

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Test Conventions > E2E Tests
text:
4. **Separate TestMain** - Put `TestMain` in a separate `test_main.go` file:
```
test/e2e/kubernetes/
├── test_main.go    # TestMain, shared variables (clientset, testNamespace)
└── e2e_test.go     # Test functions
```

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Test Conventions > E2E Tests
text:
5. **Use testify assertions** - Use `require` for fatal assertions, `assert` for non-fatal:
```go
_, err := clientset.AppsV1().Deployments(ns).Create(ctx, dep, metav1.CreateOptions{})
require.NoError(t, err)

assert.Equal(t, "expected", actual)
```

head: Kausality Development Guidelines > Test Conventions > E2E Tests
text:
6. **How to cause drift for testing** - Drift is when a controller updates a child while the parent is stable. To trigger drift in tests:
   - Change the **spec** of a child resource (not annotations/labels)
   - Or delete a child resource
   - This causes the parent controller to reconcile and try to correct the drift
   - The controller's correction attempt is what kausality detects as drift
   - Important: User modifications are NOT drift - they're a new causal origin. Only the controller's subsequent correction is drift.
