head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows
text: *Mirrored from `pymyhondaplus/AGENTS.md` — update there first.*

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: If the user's session has more than one of `pymyhondaplus`, `myhondaplus-homeassistant`, or `myhondaplus-desktop` loaded as a working directory, treat that as a signal that they're managing parallel work and rely on you for cross-product memory. **Don't wait to be asked.** When making any non-trivial change in one repo:

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: - Search the other loaded repo(s) for the same code path. A bug fix in HA's `sensor.py` may have a sibling in `myhondaplus-desktop/widgets/dashboard.py`. A library API change has at least two consumers.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: - Treat design contracts as cross-cutting: capability gating (read vs command), error-handling shape, naming, polling cadences, defaults, fuel-type semantics. When one repo settles a contract, the others should align unless the divergence is intentional and stated.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: - For bug fixes, audit the bug *class*, not just the specific symptom. If you fixed "X disappears when capability=False" in one repo, ask whether the equivalent code in the other repos has the same gate.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: - For library changes, surface the consumer impact inline. Don't say "library updated, what next" — say "library changed Y; HA needs Z, desktop needs W; here are the patches."

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: Surface findings as part of your response, in a compact format:

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: - *"Same pattern in `<repo>` at `<file:line>` — proposing same fix here."*

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: - *"`<repo>` diverges intentionally because `<reason>` — keeping divergent."*

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: - *"`<repo>` doesn't have this code path — N/A."*

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Cross-product thinking when multiple repos are open
text: The CLI in `pymyhondaplus` is often N/A for UI-gating questions (it's a thin pass-through that defers to Honda's API), but check before assuming.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Smoothing legacy-user flows on API/behavior changes
text: Whenever you change behavior, contract, or storage shape that already-installed users rely on, **first** map what existing entries / cached state / config files look like (read past migrations, config-flow code, storage handlers) and decide whether they will break, degrade, or stay fine under the new code.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Smoothing legacy-user flows on API/behavior changes
text: If they break or degrade, look for a silent self-heal path before writing release notes that ask users to delete and re-add or reauth. Examples: re-run discovery against API metadata on next startup; backfill missing fields from data the integration already has access to; drop stale flags that no longer reflect reality; reconcile via existing migration / `_fetch_*_metadata` paths.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Smoothing legacy-user flows on API/behavior changes
text: Only escalate to "user must take action" when the code genuinely cannot fix the entry from data already available. Each forced manual step is a chance for users to drop off and an entry in the issue tracker; each silent self-heal is invisible. Bias toward fixing things automatically.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Release & change mechanics
text: - **Docs before tag.** Audit narrative docs (`README.md`, plus `USAGE.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` where present) against the diff *before* bumping the version. A new feature / service / option / flag needs documenting; a removed or renamed one must not still be described. Updating code-adjacent files (`services.yaml`, `strings.json`, locale JSON, `manifest.json`) is necessary but not sufficient — the README is a separate surface, and fixing it in a follow-up after the release has shipped is not OK.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Release & change mechanics
text: - **Release-notes format.** Every release uses the same shape: header `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)`, then only the sections that apply, in order: `### Breaking`, `### Added`, `### Fixed`, `### Changed`, `### Dependencies` (the last for pin changes, e.g. "Requires pymyhondaplus >= X.Y.Z"). Bullets are one line each, no em or en dashes, no mea-culpa or "should have shipped earlier" framing, no paragraph-length context. `pymyhondaplus` keeps these entries in `CHANGELOG.md` and the GitHub release body is that section copied verbatim; HA and desktop have no changelog, so write the GitHub release body directly in the same format.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Release & change mechanics
text: - **Release order is library first, then consumers.** Bump `pymyhondaplus`, tag, GitHub-release; then update HA `manifest.json` `requirements` (`==X.Y.Z`) and/or desktop `pyproject.toml` + `README.md` (`>=X.Y.Z`), then release each consumer.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Release & change mechanics
text: - **Pin update rule**: HA pins exact (Home Assistant convention); desktop pins minimum.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Release & change mechanics
text: - **Translation-drift PRs** may span library + HA. When a string converges in wording, move the pair from `_KNOWN_DRIFT` to `ENFORCED_OVERLAPS` in the same PR (HA test: `tests/test_translation_drift.py`).

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Cross-repo workflows > Release & change mechanics
text: - **Cross-repo change checklist**: land library-owned API/parsing/auth/translation behavior in `pymyhondaplus` first; update HA's exact pin and desktop's minimum pin only after a library release; keep consumer enum options, entity descriptors, and UI copy aligned with canonical library behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Common pitfalls
text: - Hassfest rejects timeout/notification strings under the `notifications` key. They go under `exceptions` in `strings.json`.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Common pitfalls
text: - `VehicleCapabilities` access is raw-backed: `getattr(vehicle.capabilities, desc.capability, True)` is the correct gating pattern. Unknown names raise `AttributeError` and `getattr` falls through to the default — no integration code change is needed when the library adds capability flags.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Common pitfalls
text: - The library returns coordinates as floats — no conversion in the integration.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Common pitfalls
text: - `_log_unavailable_once` / `_log_recovered_once` exist for a reason; don't add ad-hoc logging that re-spams.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Common pitfalls
text: - Optimistic updates mutate `coordinator.data` before the API confirms; revert on failure.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Common pitfalls
text: - All 13 locale files must stay current — auditing them is a blocking pre-tag step.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - Arrow functions for components - never `React.FC`.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - No `any`; use `unknown` as rarely as possible.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - Use `AutoForm` for forms instead of hand-built form components.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - Use `React.lazy` + `Suspense` for content-heavy dialogs (e.g. dialogs in forms).

head: React / TanStack Start
text:
- Pick the editing surface by the size of the settings:
  - **Sheet** for short settings - a handful of fields about one thing (an AI action, the AI settings). Scrollable body plus `AutoFormSheetFooter` from `@vitnode/core/components/form/auto-form-sheet-footer`; close the sheet after a successful save.
  - **Dialog** for bigger settings - several sections or tabs (a role's settings). Lazy-load the form.
  - **Page** for the biggest - a full editor with its own navigation and preview (editing an article).

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - After create/edit/delete: refresh the table data and show a `sonner` toast with a description.

head: React / TanStack Start
text:
- `<Activity>` hides and restores children's UI and internal state:
```typescriptreact
import { Activity } from "react";

<Activity mode={isShowingSidebar ? "visible" : "hidden"}>
  <Sidebar />
</Activity>;
```

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - Add a breadcrumb with the route's `staticData.breadcrumb`; a crumb that renders strings needs its own `RouteMessages`.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - Route files are topology only - `validateSearch`, `loaderDeps`, `loader`, `head`, `staticData`. The query, the permissions, the namespaces and the screen live in `@vitnode/core/tanstack/*`.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - Write `head` **after** `loader` in the same object literal: `loaderData` is inferred from `loader`, and TypeScript reads members in order.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - Name files `x.server.ts` when they must never reach the browser bundle.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - A package may declare `createIsomorphicFn` but never `createServerFn` - uncompiled on the server, its handler silently resolves to `undefined`. Server functions belong to the host app.

head: React / TanStack Start
text: - New admin APIs always require staff permissions.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - `fetcher` from `@vitnode/core/tanstack/fetcher` is universal - one call, SSR and browser. Never hand-write `createIsomorphicFn().server(...).client(...)` for a fetch.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - A call names the plugin, never an API module: `fetcher({ plugin: "@vitnode/core", method: "get", module: "users", path: "/devices" })`. `plugin`, `module` (any nesting depth, `admin/advanced/cron`), `path`, `method`, `args` and the response are all inferred from the plugin API registry; an invalid combination is a compile error at the offending property.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - The registry is `ApiPluginRegistry` in `@vitnode/core/lib/fetcher/registry`. Core registers itself; an app's `src/api-registry.gen.ts` registers every configured plugin that exports `config.api`, with type-only imports; a plugin registers its own API in its `global.d.ts` so its pages can call it. Never import a plugin API factory as a value outside `vitnode.api.config.ts`.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - `@vitnode/core/tanstack/fetcher/server` is for work that is genuinely server-only: server functions, `allowSaveCookies` cookie relay, cron/jobs, upstream secrets or a different `origin`. Same call shape, more options.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - Shared `views/*` query modules call `fetcher` directly - no injected transport, no browser-only twin. `@vitnode/core/lib/fetcher-client` is the framework-neutral browser primitive the universal fetcher is built on, for code that never renders on a server.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - Write the route inline at the call site - never build a request object elsewhere and pass it in.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - Never annotate the result; the fetcher infers it. Put the shared contract on the feature's own `*Fetcher` type instead.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - `args` is required exactly when the route declares a body, params or a query.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - `captchaToken` for captcha-gated routes.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs
text: - `rawFetcher` only for generated Content Engine admin modules, which have no type to infer from. It is universal too, with the same server-only twin. A content type's _public_ routes are typed: `module: "content/<publicApi.path>"`.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs > Caching APIs
text: - Client and SSR caching is TanStack Query. Invalidate with `queryClient.invalidateQueries` after a write; warm a route's data in its `loader` with `queryClient.query({ ...options, staleTime: "static" })` (`infiniteQuery` for a feed). `ensureQueryData`, `fetchQuery` and `prefetchQuery` are deprecated - `query` replaces all three.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs > Caching APIs
text: - Server-side domain caching is the API's own: `c.get("cache")` in a Hono route, Redis-backed when `REDIS_URL` is set and a no-op otherwise.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs > Caching APIs
text: - Content Engine tag builders live in `content/cache.ts` (`contentPublicListTag` and friends) - pure strings, used to expire a content type's cached reads.

head: React / TanStack Start > Fetching APIs > Caching APIs
text: - A background mutation cannot expire a front end's cache by calling a function. `dispatchContentRevalidation` posts to the origins an install opts into via `content.revalidateOrigins`.

head: Coding Guidelines
text: - Always implement best practices for performance, security, and accessibility.

head: Coding Guidelines
text: - Semantic HTML (`main`, `header`) with correct ARIA roles/attributes, `sr-only` for screen-reader-only text, and alt text on all images unless decorative or repetitive.

head: Coding Guidelines
text: - Emit events for important actions (create, update, delete) so other components can react; use events instead of prop drilling or context. Document them in `apps/web/content/docs/dev/events/built-in-events.mdx`.

head: Coding Guidelines
text: - APIs return i18n keys, never translated text, for anything the UI shows (titles, descriptions, labels a plugin registers). The web translates them with `use-intl`, so the text follows the UI's language and the cached response works in every language. Translate on the server only for output with no UI, such as emails.

head: Coding Guidelines
text: - AI features use the Vercel AI SDK only - resolve models via the `c.get("ai")` registry and call native SDK functions.

head: Design
text: - New pages and components need good UX and a modern, clean UI. Design mobile-first, then enhance for larger screens.

head: Design
text: - Update `layout.tsx` metadata (title, description) and viewport (theme-color, userScalable) for SEO.

head: Design
text: - Exactly 3–5 colors total. Never use purple or violet prominently.

head: Design
text: - If you override a background color, you MUST override its text color for contrast.

head: Design
text: - Prefer semantic design tokens (`bg-background`, `text-foreground`).

head: Design
text: - Use the Tailwind spacing scale (`p-4`, `mx-2`) - never arbitrary values (`p-[16px]`).

head: Design
text: - Use `gap-*` classes for spacing. Never use `space-*`, and never mix margin/padding with gap on the same element.

head: Design
text: - Use semantic (`items-center`, `justify-between`) and responsive (`md:grid-cols-2`) classes.

head: Design
text: - No floats or absolute positioning unless absolutely necessary.

head: Design
text: - Body text: `leading-relaxed` (1.4–1.6), never below 14px, never decorative fonts.

head: Design
text: - Wrap titles and important copy in `text-balance` or `text-pretty`.

head: Documentation
text: - Document every new feature. Keep it simple, SEO-friendly, and understandable at any skill level.

head: Documentation
text: - Friendly and lightly funny tone - don't overdo it.

head: Documentation
text: - Skip big comments; code is self-documenting.

head: Documentation
text: - Request images with a comment: `// Image prompt: {here_prompt_to_generate_image}`

head: Testing
text: - Never write unit tests in the same session. Spawn a new session, and write the test after the feature is working. Tests are for regression, not for development.

head: Testing
text: - UI component tests (`*.test.tsx`) should test DOM output, click events, and dialogs. Never test CSS classes or form UI (`AutoForm`, form fields).

head: Testing
text: - Do not test an existing feature applied somewhere new. Building the widgets system earns tests; adding widget zones or widgets to another page or plugin does not, because the mechanism is already covered and only the wiring is new.

head: Testing
text: - Do not test database models or schema definitions (Drizzle tables, column types, indexes, foreign keys).

head: Testing
text: - Do not test static config, constants, color presets, or plugin configuration (`config.api`, content type definitions).

head: Testing
text: - Do not test third-party libraries or trivial helper/wrapper code.

head: Testing
text: - Always run "pnpm lint:fix" to fix formatting and linting issues before committing. Never commit a file with lint errors.

head: Testing > Mocking
Testing > Mocking
text: - `vi.mock` is allowed only as a last resort, for a boundary with no seam (a `React.lazy` editor, a child process). Never use it for a module the test could drive for real.

head: Testing > Mocking
text: - Staff permissions: grant them with `grantStaffPermissions` from `@/tests/staff-permissions` on a `createTestCache()` from `@/tests/cache`, set as `c.set("cache", cache)`. Never mock `check-staff-permission`. Assert on the response (`200` with the permission, `403` without), not on which permission was asked for.

head: Testing > Mocking
text: - `use-intl` is mocked once for every test in `packages/vitnode/src/tests/setup.ts`: `t("key")` renders `namespace.key`. Don't mock it per file.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project overview
text:
This is a refactor of a legacy Outlook VBA macro into a modern Outlook
COM add-in. It helps users quickly classify emails into folders across
multiple .pst archives, with fast keyword search over the folder tree,
attachment management, and send-time guards.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **Add-in technology**: Outlook **Shared COM Add-in** —
  `Extensibility.IDTExtensibility2` + `Office.IRibbonExtensibility`,
  registered into Outlook via HKCU keys under
  `Software\Microsoft\Office\Outlook\Addins\`. This is the classic,
  pre-VSTO Outlook add-in model. It supports PST access, offline use,
  and per-user install without admin rights on the classic Win32
  Outlook client. VSTO is explicitly excluded for this project after
  the Office Developer Tools workload could not be set up on the dev
  machine.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **Target Outlook** (deployment): classic Win32 Outlook, **32-bit**,
  Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise on the **Semi-Annual Enterprise
  Channel**. NOT the "new Outlook". NO Exchange Online dependency.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **Dev Outlook**: classic Win32 Outlook, **64-bit**, **Current**
  channel, on **Windows 11 ARM64** (Outlook runs as emulated x64
  via Prism). The local dev machine differs from the deployment
  target in both architecture and channel. The same AnyCPU
  add-in binary must load on both. Final EDR and compatibility
  validation happens against a real 32-bit target workstation;
  the dev machine is for fast iteration only.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **Runtime**: .NET Framework 4.8 for the add-in shell and the
  Outlook adapter. .NET Standard 2.0 for the business core.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **Language**: C# 7.3 (.NET Framework 4.8 limit unless LangVersion is
  explicitly bumped, which we avoid).

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **UI**: WPF with a **hand-rolled minimal MVVM** (`RBLclass.AddIn/Mvvm`:
  `ObservableObject` + `RelayCommand`), hosted in Custom Task Panes via
  `ICustomTaskPaneConsumer`/`ICTPFactory` — the WPF view is bridged into a
  ComVisible WinForms host control through `ElementHost`. Ribbon via
  `IRibbonExtensibility.GetCustomUI` returning Ribbon XML (not the
  Ribbon Designer). **CommunityToolkit.Mvvm is deliberately NOT used:** its
  8.x dependencies (`System.Memory` ≥ 4.5.5, `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe`
  ≥ 6.0.0) float the SQLite facade assemblies above what `SQLitePCLRaw` was
  built against, and a COM host has no binding redirects, so it breaks the
  first `SqliteConnection` at runtime. Keep new AddIn dependencies
  dependency-light for the same reason.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **Storage**: SQLite via Microsoft.Data.Sqlite, with FTS5 for full-text
  search. Database in %LocalAppData%\RBLclass\.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text: - **Logging**: Serilog with a rolling file sink.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **Tests**: xUnit, FluentAssertions, NSubstitute. Tests run against
  RBLclass.Core only; the Outlook adapter is excluded from CI tests.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text:
- **Packaging**: per-user install via a signed installer that lays
  down the add-in DLL + dependencies under `%LocalAppData%\RBLclass\`
  and writes the COM registration entries to HKCU. Phase 0 POC uses a
  PowerShell installer; Phase 1 promotes to an MSI built with the WiX
  Toolset, Authenticode-signed (both the DLL and the MSI) with an
  internal-PKI certificate carrying the Code Signing EKU
  (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3). ClickOnce is not used — it is VSTO-specific
  in this scenario.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stack and constraints
text: - **Min Windows**: Windows 10 1809.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: Strict layering. Dependencies point downward only.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
RBLclass.AddIn               (.NET FW 4.8) — COM add-in shell:
       │                                  IDTExtensibility2, IRibbonExtensibility,
       │                                  ribbon callbacks, Custom Task Panes,
       │                                  Outlook event subscriptions
RBLclass.Outlook.Adapter     (.NET FW 4.8) — COM access to Outlook OM
       │                                  Implements RBLclass.Core interfaces
       ▼
RBLclass.Core                (.NET Standard 2.0) — business logic, no Outlook
                                                no UI, no I/O except via
                                                injected interfaces

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
The business core (`RBLclass.Core`) MUST remain free of any reference to
Microsoft.Office.Interop.Outlook, System.Windows, or COM-add-in shell
assemblies. This is what makes the code portable on the day we have to
migrate away from the COM add-in model.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > COM interop interface declarations (add-in shell only)
text:
- **Never hand-roll `[ComImport]` declarations of `IDTExtensibility2`,
  `IRibbonExtensibility`, `IRibbonControl`, or other Office/Extensibility
  interfaces.** Reference the canonical PIAs from the GAC instead:
  - `Extensibility` —
    `C:\Windows\assembly\GAC\Extensibility\7.0.3300.0__b03f5f7f11d50a3a\extensibility.dll`
  - `office` (Microsoft.Office.Core) —
    `C:\Windows\assembly\GAC_MSIL\office\15.0.0.0__71e9bce111e9429c\OFFICE.DLL`
  - `Microsoft.Office.Interop.Outlook` —
    `C:\Windows\assembly\GAC_MSIL\Microsoft.Office.Interop.Outlook\15.0.0.0__71e9bce111e9429c\Microsoft.Office.Interop.Outlook.dll`
  Reference them in the `.csproj` via `<Reference Include="…"><HintPath>…</HintPath><Private>false</Private></Reference>`.
  **Why:** CLR auto-generates IL marshalling stubs from interface
  metadata. Even with the correct `[Guid]` and `[DispId]` attributes,
  subtle differences from the canonical PIAs (e.g. missing `[In]`,
  wrong `MarshalAs` for `ref Array`) produce stubs that AV inside
  `IL_STUB_COMtoCLR` when Outlook calls our methods. The crash
  surfaces as `ExecutionEngineException` (HRESULT `0x80131506`),
  takes Outlook down silently, and is hard to diagnose without
  a memory dump.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > COM interop interface declarations (add-in shell only)
text:
- **`[ClassInterface(ClassInterfaceType.AutoDispatch)]` on the add-in
  class is mandatory** — not `None`. Office resolves ribbon
  `onAction` callbacks by calling `IDispatch::GetIDsOfNames` on
  the class itself, and `None` only exposes members of explicitly-
  implemented interfaces, none of which the ribbon callbacks live on.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > COM interop interface declarations (add-in shell only)
text:
- **Do not embed Office interop types** (`<EmbedInteropTypes>true</EmbedInteropTypes>`
  on a `PackageReference`). In SDK-style net48 projects this metadata
  is silently ignored and the PIA is copied as a regular dependency.
  Use direct GAC references (as above) which never get copied.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > COM lifetime (Outlook adapter only)
text:
Outlook COM objects MUST be released explicitly. Long-lived references
cause Outlook crashes and memory leaks.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > COM lifetime (Outlook adapter only)
text:
- Wrap every COM object in a `ComRef<T> : IDisposable` that calls
  `Marshal.ReleaseComObject` in `Dispose`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > COM lifetime (Outlook adapter only)
text:
- Never chain property accesses on COM objects. `mail.Parent.Parent.Name`
  leaks the intermediate `Parent` objects.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > COM lifetime (Outlook adapter only)
text:
- All loops over `Items`, `Folders`, `Stores` use `for` with index, not
  `foreach`, and dispose each element.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Threading
text:
- Outlook OM is single-threaded apartment (STA). All COM calls happen on
  the main thread.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Threading
text: - Background work (indexing, SQLite I/O, HTTP) runs on the thread pool.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Threading
text:
- Use a dedicated `SynchronizationContext` capture at add-in startup to
  marshal back to the Outlook UI thread.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Threading
text: - Never block the UI thread on COM calls inside loops. Batch and yield.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Bitness
text:
- Build configuration: **AnyCPU** for all projects, with
  `Prefer32Bit=false`. The same binary loads into 64-bit Outlook on
  the ARM64 dev machine (running as x64 under Prism emulation) AND
  32-bit Outlook on the x86/x64 target workstations; the .NET
  runtime JITs to the host process bitness.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Bitness
text:
- Native dependencies MUST ship both `runtimes\win-x86\native\` AND
  `runtimes\win-x64\native\` payloads (e.g.
  `SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_e_sqlite3`). Verify after build that both
  payloads land in the output directory. Do NOT add x64-only
  dependencies.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Bitness
text:
- COM registration is bitness-specific. Under HKCU on 64-bit
  Windows, 64-bit clients read `Software\Classes\CLSID\{guid}` while
  32-bit clients read `Software\Classes\Wow6432Node\CLSID\{guid}`.
  The installer writes both subtrees so a single artifact supports
  both Outlook bitnesses without per-host customisation. The
  `Software\Microsoft\Office\Outlook\Addins\` key is NOT WOW64-
  redirected in HKCU and is written once.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Bitness
CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Performance targets
text: - Folder search: <100ms for a query on 100k indexed mails.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Performance targets
text:
- Classify action: optimistic UI, perceived latency <300ms. Actual Move
  may complete asynchronously.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Performance targets
text:
- Add-in startup: contribute <500ms to Outlook startup. Initial PST
  indexing runs in background after Outlook is fully loaded.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > SQLite
text: - One connection per logical operation, opened with WAL journal mode.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > SQLite
text:
- All schema changes go through versioned migrations (`SchemaVersion`
  table). Never alter the schema in-place.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > SQLite
text:
- FTS5 virtual table for mail body/subject. Keep it separate from the
  main `Mails` table to allow rebuilds without data loss.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > SQLite
text:
- EntryIDs from Outlook can change after some operations (e.g. moving
  between stores). Cache by `(StoreID, EntryID)` and tolerate misses.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Outlook events
text:
- Register event handlers in `OnStartupComplete`, unregister in
  `OnBeginShutdown`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Outlook events
text:
- Keep references to event source objects in fields, otherwise GC will
  collect them and events stop firing silently.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Error handling
text:
- Outlook COM calls can throw `COMException`. Catch and log, never let
  exceptions escape to Outlook (it disables the add-in by flipping
  `LoadBehavior` from 3 to 2 in the registry).

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Error handling
text:
- Top-level handlers in every ribbon callback, every event handler, every
  fire-and-forget Task.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Localization (English / French / German)
text:
The UI follows Outlook's UI language, defaulting to English for any other
language, with a per-user override in Settings resolved once at startup
(`RblClassAddIn.OnStartupComplete`, before any pane/window/ribbon is
created). Changing the "Preferred UI language" setting takes effect after
restarting Outlook.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Localization (English / French / German)
text:
- Every new user-visible string MUST be added as a resource key to
  `src/RBLclass.AddIn/Resources/Strings.resx` **and** translated in
  `Strings.fr.resx` and `Strings.de.resx` in the same change.
  `ResourceParityTests` (in `RBLclass.Core.Tests`) fails `dotnet test` if a
  key is missing, empty, or has mismatched `{n}` placeholders in any
  language.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Localization (English / French / German)
text:
- XAML strings go through `{loc:Loc Key=...}`
  (`RBLclass.AddIn.Localization.LocExtension`). Code-behind/ViewModel
  strings go through `ILocalizationService.GetString`/`GetString(key, args)`
  (`TaskPaneServices.Localization`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Localization (English / French / German)
text:
- Count-dependent strings always get a `_One` / `_Other` resource key pair,
  resolved via `ILocalizationService.Plural(count, oneKey, otherKey, args)`.
  Never derive plurals by string concatenation — French and German plural
  forms differ from English.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical coding rules > Localization (English / French / German)
text:
- New ribbon buttons/tooltips need matching `label`/`screentip`/`supertip`
  entries in `Ribbon.xml`, `Ribbon.fr.xml`, and `Ribbon.de.xml` — checked by
  `ResourceParityTests` as well. `RblClassAddIn.GetCustomUI` picks the
  variant based on `TaskPaneServices.Localization.CurrentLanguage`.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should do
text:
- When asked to add a feature, locate it in the appropriate layer. If it
  needs Outlook data, define an interface in `RBLclass.Core`, implement it
  in `RBLclass.Outlook.Adapter`, write the business logic in `RBLclass.Core`,
  wire it from `RBLclass.AddIn`.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should do
text: - Always write unit tests for any non-trivial logic added in `RBLclass.Core`.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should do
text:
- Follow existing naming, formatting (`.editorconfig`), and namespace
  conventions.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should do
text:
- Prefer small, focused changes over large refactors. If a refactor is
  needed, propose it first, do not perform it unprompted.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text:
- Do not add references from `RBLclass.Core` to anything Outlook-, WPF-, or
  COM-add-in-shell-related.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text:
- Do not depend on the VSTO runtime or the `Microsoft.Office.Tools.*`
  assemblies — they are not used in this project.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text:
- Do not introduce new dependencies without asking. Keep the dependency
  surface small.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text: - Do not call Outlook COM APIs from a non-UI thread.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text:
- Do not use `async void` except for event handlers, and even then wrap
  the body in try/catch.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text: - Do not bump LangVersion or TargetFramework without an explicit request.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text: - Do not assume Exchange Online is available. PST is the source of truth.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text: - Do not introduce x64-only native dependencies.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Claude should NOT do
text:
- Do not assume more than ~1 GB of usable memory; the add-in lives
  inside a 32-bit Outlook process on the deployment target.

head: CLAUDE.md > Useful context for Outlook OM quirks
text:
- `MailItem.Move` returns the moved item in the destination store; the
  original COM reference becomes invalid.

head: CLAUDE.md > Useful context for Outlook OM quirks
text:
- `Explorer.Selection` can contain non-MailItem objects (MeetingItem,
  ReportItem...). Always check `is MailItem` before casting.

head: CLAUDE.md > Useful context for Outlook OM quirks
text:
- `Folder.Items.Find` / `Restrict` is much faster than iterating, but
  has its own DASL/Jet query syntax — document any non-trivial query.

head: CLAUDE.md > Useful context for Outlook OM quirks
text:
- PST stores can be closed by the user at any time. Handle
  `StoreRemove` events gracefully.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build and run
text:
- VS 2022 with the **.NET desktop development** workload and the
  **.NET Framework 4.8 targeting pack** is required. The
  Office/SharePoint development workload is NOT required.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build and run
text:
- The **standalone .NET SDK** must also be installed (e.g.
  `winget install Microsoft.DotNet.SDK.8`). The SDK-style csproj
  needs `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` to resolve, and on Windows ARM64 the
  VS workload does not bundle it. After install, refresh PATH in
  any shell that was open before the install — see the deploy
  script for the canonical refresh idiom.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build and run
text:
- Open `RBLclass.sln` in Visual Studio 2022. F5 launches Outlook with
  the add-in attached via *Debug → Start External Program:
  outlook.exe*. The HKCU COM registration written by the install
  script is what makes Outlook load the add-in; no VSTO hosting is
  involved.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build and run
text:
- `RBLclass.Core` and its tests can be built and run from VS Code with
  the C# Dev Kit; the add-in shell project must be built from VS or
  the command line (`msbuild` or `dotnet build`) on Windows.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build and run
text:
- Default build configuration is `Debug|AnyCPU`. Release is
  `Release|AnyCPU`. There is no x86 or x64 configuration.

head: CLAUDE.md > Publishing
text:
The full release/packaging **workflow** (build → stage → verify both
native SQLite bitnesses → produce a shippable install kit) lives in the
manually-triggered **`/make-release`** skill at
`.claude/skills/make-release/` — run it to package the product for a
target workstation. The notes below are the surrounding facts; the runnable
steps are in the skill.

head: CLAUDE.md > Publishing
text:
- Package format (current): a per-user PowerShell **install kit** (`.zip`)
  produced by `/make-release`, laying files under
  `%LocalAppData%\RBLclass\` and writing HKCU COM + Outlook Addins
  registry entries. No admin rights required.

head: CLAUDE.md > Publishing
text:
- Package format (later, Phase 1 GA target): a WiX-based **MSI** under
  `/installer/`, per-user, optionally Authenticode-signed with the
  internal-PKI cert. Same registry/file effects as the install kit. The
  install kit and MSI coexist until the MSI is validated on the target.

head: CLAUDE.md > Publishing
text:
- Signing is **optional** — Outlook does not require an Authenticode
  signature to load a COM add-in (validated in Phase 0).

head: CLAUDE.md > Publishing
text:
- Distribution: internal HTTPS share documented in
  `docs/deployment.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Documentation
text:
The product has an online documentation site published to GitHub Pages,
built with **MkDocs Material**. Its source is `website/` (Markdown pages
under `website/docs/`, navigation in `website/mkdocs.yml`). It has four
areas — **Home**, **User Guide** (installation, quick start, walkthrough),
**Developer Guide** (tech stack, architecture, testing, shipping), and
**Security**.

head: CLAUDE.md > Documentation
text:
**Documentation ships with the code, not after it.** Every change that
alters any of the following MUST be accompanied by the matching docs update
**in the same commit**:

head: CLAUDE.md > Documentation
text:
- user-visible behaviour, a setting, a default, or a keyboard shortcut →
  `website/docs/user-guide/` (the walkthrough settings tables are the
  source of truth) and, if a feature is added/removed/renamed, the Home
  feature bullets;

head: CLAUDE.md > Documentation
text:
- the architecture, a coding rule, the tech stack, a dependency, or a
  build/test/ship process → `website/docs/developer-guide/`;

head: CLAUDE.md > Documentation
text:
- the security posture (new data persisted, a network call, a new trust
  boundary, a closed hardening item) → **both** `website/docs/security.md`
  (published) and `docs/security.md` (canonical internal threat model).

head: CLAUDE.md > Documentation
text:
Do not hand-write these updates inline. Delegate them to the
**`docs-writer` subagent** (`.claude/agents/docs-writer.md`, Sonnet, medium
reasoning effort): give it the change description (and the diff or roadmap
item), let it edit the affected pages, then stage its output into the same
commit as the change. `/feature-impl` does this automatically; for a manual
change, invoke it the same way before committing.

head: CLAUDE.md > Documentation
text:
CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) builds the site with `--strict` on every
pull request to `main` (a broken link or a page missing from `nav:` fails
the check) and **publishes** to GitHub Pages on push to `main` (i.e. once
the PR merges). Keep internal links valid so the strict build passes.

head: CLAUDE.md > Sprint development workflow
text: Feature work is driven by three skills/subagents that form a pipeline:

head: CLAUDE.md > Sprint development workflow
text:
- **`feature-prep` subagent** (`.claude/agents/feature-prep.md`,
  Sonnet 4.6, read-only) — given a roadmap item, searches the codebase
  and produces a structured Implementation Brief: affected files with
  line references, required changes, localization keys, xUnit test cases,
  and verification questions. Never writes anything.

head: CLAUDE.md > Sprint development workflow
text:
- **`/feature-impl` skill** (`.claude/skills/feature-impl/`) — consumes
  an Implementation Brief from context and implements it end-to-end:
  code changes → localization → xUnit → build check → `/reload-addin` →
  `AskUserQuestion` for user verification → commit (with the ROADMAP.md
  checkbox update). Loops on failure; stops and asks for guidance after
  3 failed fix attempts.

head: CLAUDE.md > Sprint development workflow
text:
- **`/dev-sprint` skill** (`.claude/skills/dev-sprint/`) — runs the full
  active sprint (highest `vX.X.X` section with unchecked items in
  `ROADMAP.md`) by orchestrating the two above: preparation for item N+1
  starts in the background while item N is being implemented.

head: CLAUDE.md > Sprint development workflow
text:
Invoke `/dev-sprint` to work through a sprint automatically. Invoke
`/feature-impl` directly (with a brief in context, or it will call
`feature-prep` first) for a single item. Never commit a feature without
a passing user verification — this is enforced by `/feature-impl`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management
text:
This is a solo project, developed interactively (with Claude) on a single
machine — which is also the only place changes can be built and tested.
The branching model is lightweight but strict about what may reach `main`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Branches
text:
- `main` — always shippable. Updated **only** by merging `develop`. Never
  commit directly to `main`. Every commit on `main` is a feature or fix
  that has been validated locally and is ready to ship to the target.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Branches
text:
- `develop` — integration branch and the default working branch. Direct
  commits are allowed (solo workflow). Always work on `develop` or a
  branch based on it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Branches
CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Shipping a feature (`develop` → `main`)
text:
Because this machine is the only test environment, nothing reaches `main`
until it has been built and validated here (and, for anything touching
COM / EDR / bitness, on the real 32-bit target — see the constraints
above).

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Shipping a feature (`develop` → `main`)
text:
1. Land the work on `develop`; confirm the solution builds and the
   `RBLclass.Core` tests pass.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Shipping a feature (`develop` → `main`)
text:
2. Validate the behaviour interactively (run the add-in, exercise the
   feature).

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Shipping a feature (`develop` → `main`)
text:
3. Merge `develop` into `main` with a merge commit (`--no-ff`) so each
   ship is a distinct point in history.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Shipping a feature (`develop` → `main`)
text:
4. Tag the merge on `main` with the product version `/make-release`
   stamps (e.g. `v1.0.0`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Shipping a feature (`develop` → `main`)
text: 5. Package from `main` with `/make-release` when an install kit is needed.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > GitHub (`gh` CLI)
text:
- Use the `gh` CLI for all GitHub actions — PRs, releases, issues, repo
  settings. Do not drive GitHub through the web UI when a `gh` command
  exists.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > GitHub (`gh` CLI)
text:
- Pull requests are optional for solo merges; when used, target `develop`
  for features and `main` only for ship merges.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > GitHub (`gh` CLI)
text:
- Cut releases from tags on `main` (`gh release create vX.Y.Z`), attaching
  the install kit from `/make-release` when relevant.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Hygiene
text:
- When committing from PowerShell, always write the message to a temp file
  and use `git commit -F <file>` — PowerShell 5.1 mangles embedded double
  quotes in `-m` here-strings passed to native executables.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Hygiene
text: - Commit or push only when asked.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository management > Hygiene
text:
- Keep commits focused. Do not sweep unrelated working-tree changes into a
  commit (e.g. stray `.gitignore`, `docs/`, or `ROADMAP.md` edits) unless
  explicitly told to.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
This project's AI-agent instructions live in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) — non-negotiables,
build order, stack, working style, and vendored-source pins. Same content, kept in one
place so Claude-specific and vendor-neutral tooling don't drift apart.

head: AGENTS.md
text: If your agent/tool reads `AGENTS.md` specifically: treat `CLAUDE.md` as this file's content.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: Implement and evolve ProTranslate as a production-grade XAML translation and globalization framework for:

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: The framework must keep localization, formatting, culture switching, region policy, measurement systems, and flow direction consistent across XAML platforms while preserving a framework-neutral core.

head: AGENTS.md > Ownership Guardrails
text: Keep changes scoped to the requested package, adapter, sample, workflow, or documentation area. Other contributors may be working in parallel, so do not revert unrelated edits or reshape project boundaries without an explicit task requirement.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiable Requirements
text: 1. `ProTranslate.Core` remains framework-neutral.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiable Requirements
text: 2. Avalonia, WPF, MAUI, WinUI, and Uno adapters remain thin and independent.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiable Requirements
text: 3. Runtime culture switching must update translated text, formatted values, `RegionInfo`-derived displays, measurement-system displays, and `FlowDirection`.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiable Requirements
text: 4. `ResourceManager`, `IStringLocalizer`, and custom provider pipelines are first-class.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiable Requirements
text: 5. XAML usage must support markup extensions and attached properties.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiable Requirements
text: 6. Compiled bindings and WinUI/Uno `x:Bind` compatibility must be preserved through source-generated or handwritten CLR members. Reflection-based resource discovery, stringly typed runtime binding paths, and dynamic markup-extension lookup are fallback paths that require an explicit reason.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiable Requirements
text: 7. MVVM and SOLID boundaries must stay explicit.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiable Requirements
text: 8. Missing keys, fallback paths, invalid formats, and provider failures must produce structured diagnostics.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Core
text: `ProTranslate.Core` owns:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Core
text: - active culture and UI culture snapshots

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Core
text: - provider abstraction and fallback order

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Core
text: - `RegionInfo` and region profile services

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Core
text: - measurement system resolution

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Core
text: - framework-neutral flow-direction resolution

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Core
text: The core must not reference Avalonia, WPF, MAUI, WinUI, Uno, or any adapter package.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: `ProTranslate.Extensions` owns:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection registration

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - `IStringLocalizer` integration

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: `ProTranslate.SourceGenerator` owns:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - strongly typed key accessors

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - strongly typed bindable CLR string surfaces for compiled binding and `x:Bind`

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - generated provider code for JSON catalogs when runtime resource discovery is not required

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - compiled binding and `x:Bind`-safe generated members

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: `ProTranslate.Analyzers` owns:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - missing-key diagnostics

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - placeholder mismatch diagnostics

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - resource coverage diagnostics

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Optional Infrastructure
text: - unsafe dynamic key warnings

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Adapters
text: Adapters own only framework integration:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Adapters
text: - dependency or bindable properties

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Adapters
text: - native `FlowDirection` mapping

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Adapters
text: - design-time fallback behavior

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Adapters
text: Adapters must not duplicate provider fallback, formatting, region, measurement, or diagnostics policy from core.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Compiled Binding Defaults
text: New samples and docs must prefer the generated `ProTranslate.Generated.ProTranslateStrings` class, generated key constants, generated accessor methods, or equivalent handwritten view-model properties. Avalonia samples must keep compiled bindings enabled and set `x:DataType`; WinUI and Uno samples must keep normal text and formatted text on `x:Bind`-safe view-model properties. WPF and MAUI should use typed view-model properties where their XAML compilers cannot statically validate a markup-extension path.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Compiled Binding Defaults
text: Adapter markup extensions remain supported for concise view-only XAML and migration scenarios, but they must not be presented as the primary path for trimming-sensitive, NativeAOT-sensitive, or compiled-binding-first applications. Do not introduce reflection-based catalog loading in samples or runtime code unless the spec calls out why generated provider code or explicit provider registration is insufficient.

head: AGENTS.md > Spec-Driven Workflow
text: Before implementing a feature, update or create a spec that includes:

head: AGENTS.md > Spec-Driven Workflow
text: - Inputs: culture, keys, bindings, provider data, options, user actions.

head: AGENTS.md > Spec-Driven Workflow
text: - Outputs: API behavior, UI refresh, diagnostics, generated files.

head: AGENTS.md > Spec-Driven Workflow
text: - Constraints: package boundaries, threading, performance, trimming, framework compatibility.

head: AGENTS.md > Spec-Driven Workflow
text: - Edge cases: missing keys, invalid culture, provider failures, disposed targets, neutral cultures, RTL content.

head: AGENTS.md > Spec-Driven Workflow
text: - Validate: unit tests, adapter tests, analyzer tests, sample builds, docs build.

head: AGENTS.md > Spec-Driven Workflow
text: Use the files under `docs/spec/` as the source of truth:

head: AGENTS.md > Spec-Driven Workflow
text: - `implementation-plan.md`

text: Representative XAML should remain concise:

head: AGENTS.md > XAML API Direction
text: Framework-specific syntax may differ, but the concepts must remain aligned across Avalonia, WPF, MAUI, WinUI, and Uno.

head: AGENTS.md > Culture And Region Policy
text: Culture state is snapshot-based. Avoid hidden global state.

head: AGENTS.md > Culture And Region Policy
text: - explicit culture and UI culture

head: AGENTS.md > Culture And Region Policy
text: - explicit fallback chain

head: AGENTS.md > Culture And Region Policy
text: - optional region override

head: AGENTS.md > Culture And Region Policy
text: - optional measurement-system override

head: AGENTS.md > Culture And Region Policy
text: - deterministic provider fallback

head: AGENTS.md > Culture And Region Policy
text: - dispatcher-safe target refresh

head: AGENTS.md > Culture And Region Policy
text: Do not mutate `Thread.CurrentThread.CurrentCulture` globally unless the host explicitly opts in.

head: AGENTS.md > Quality Bar
text: 1. The relevant spec includes inputs, outputs, constraints, edge cases, and validation.

head: AGENTS.md > Quality Bar
text: 2. Core behavior has unit tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Quality Bar

head: Agent Instructions
text: These instructions apply to the entire repository.

head: Agent Instructions > Human Oversight
text: All agent work is subject to human review and approval.

head: Agent Instructions > Human Oversight
text: - Never create, amend, or merge a commit unless the user explicitly requests that exact Git operation.

head: Agent Instructions > Human Oversight
text: - Never create or push a branch, tag, pull request, or release unless the user explicitly requests it.

head: Agent Instructions > Human Oversight
text: - Leave completed changes in the working tree so a human can inspect and approve them.

head: Agent Instructions > Human Oversight
text: - Do not interpret a request to implement a change as permission to commit or publish it.

head: Agent Instructions > Human Oversight
text: - Do not bypass required human decisions, repository protections, reviews, or approval gates.

head: Agent Instructions > Human Oversight
text: - Clearly report incomplete work, assumptions, risks, and validation failures. Do not present uncertain work as complete.

head: Agent Instructions > Planning Changes
text: Before making a nontrivial code change:

head: Agent Instructions > Planning Changes
text: 1. Inspect the relevant implementation, tests, repository guidance, and current working-tree state.

head: Agent Instructions > Planning Changes
text: 2. Define a concise plan that covers the intended behavior, affected surfaces, regression tests, and validation.

head: Agent Instructions > Planning Changes
text: 3. Present the plan before implementation when the user requests a plan or when scope, behavior, data migration, compatibility, security, or architecture requires a human decision.

head: Agent Instructions > Planning Changes
text: 4. Obtain human direction instead of guessing when multiple materially different behaviors are reasonable.

head: Agent Instructions > Planning Changes
text: 5. Keep changes focused on the approved request and update the plan if investigation reveals a meaningful scope change.

head: Agent Instructions > Planning Changes
text: Small, unambiguous, low-risk changes may proceed without a separate approval pause, but they still require human review before any commit or publication.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Standards
text: Before changing code, read and follow the coding standards in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md). Treat that document as the canonical source for project conventions.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Standards
text: - Preserve nullable reference type safety and use file-scoped namespaces.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Standards
text: - Document every non-private C# entity with XML documentation.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Standards
text: - Keep C# lines within 225 characters.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Standards
text: - Use explicit `// Arrange`, `// Act`, and `// Assert` sections in every test.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Standards
text: - Follow the repository's existing naming, formatting, error-handling, and test patterns.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Standards
text: - Add or update focused regression tests for behavior changes.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Standards
text: - Do not weaken analyzers, warnings, tests, or coding-standard checks to make a change pass.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Validation
text: Run the smallest relevant tests while developing. Before declaring a code change complete, run:

head: Agent Instructions > Required Validation
text: Restore dependencies first only when they are missing or dependency manifests changed.

head: Agent Instructions > Required Validation
text: Documentation-only changes do not require a build or test run unless they affect generated documentation or validation tooling.

head: Agent Instructions > Reviewing Changes
text: Before reporting implementation complete:

head: Agent Instructions > Reviewing Changes
text: 1. Review the entire diff, including staged and unstaged changes, without reverting unrelated human work.

head: Agent Instructions > Reviewing Changes
text: 2. Confirm every changed line supports the requested outcome and follows `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

head: Agent Instructions > Reviewing Changes
text: 3. Check error paths, cancellation, nullable safety, logging, compatibility, and relevant edge cases.

head: Agent Instructions > Reviewing Changes
text: 4. Verify tests assert the requested behavior rather than an indirect proxy.

head: Agent Instructions > Reviewing Changes
text: 5. Run the required validation gate and resolve failures caused by the change.

head: Agent Instructions > Reviewing Changes
text: 6. Report the files and behavior changed, validation performed, remaining risks, and any work requiring human attention.

head: Agent Instructions > Reviewing Changes
text: Agent self-review supplements but never replaces human code review. Stop after presenting the working-tree changes unless the user explicitly authorizes a subsequent Git or publication action.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 1. What Vibe Bar Is
text:
Vibe Bar is a native macOS menu-bar app for developers who use OpenAI/Codex
and Anthropic/Claude Code (often side-by-side) and want subscription
quota, usage pace, local token cost, and provider service status visible
in one quiet desktop surface — without opening multiple dashboards.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 1. What Vibe Bar Is
text:
It is a pure Swift package with source-first distribution and an optional
tag-driven GitHub Release workflow. There is no Xcode workspace, installer,
or production server. The "deploy" target is the user's own Mac (and
optionally `/Applications`); the "publish" target is GitHub.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 1. What Vibe Bar Is
text: - Menu-bar quota indicators for OpenAI/Codex and Anthropic/Claude Code.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 1. What Vibe Bar Is
text: - Overview dashboard (quota pace, status, cost history, token totals).

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 1. What Vibe Bar Is
text:
- Provider detail pages (utilization, model rankings, heatmaps, hourly
  burn rate, live service status).

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 1. What Vibe Bar Is
text: - Mini floating window with regular and compact layouts.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 1. What Vibe Bar Is
text: - Local-first cost tracking from CLI session logs.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 1. What Vibe Bar Is
text:

text:
`Sources/VibeBarCore/Compat/AgentSessionKitReexport.swift` is the seam.
It `@_exported import`s the package — so no call site needs a second
import — and supplies the defaults the package refuses to invent for its
host: `~/.vibebar/mcp.sock`, the `--mcp-stdio` flag, `VIBEBAR_MCP_SOCKET`
and the "Vibe Bar is not running" message. Add host-shaped defaults
there, not in the package.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text: **Who owns which side of the line.**

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
| Concern | Lives in | Why |
| ------- | -------- | --- |
| Session discovery, per-harness adapters, transcript parsing | kit | Provider-agnostic, testable without a network, useful to any host. |
| `SessionIndexStore` / `SessionIndexService` (SQLite + FTS5) | kit | Same. The index location is a parameter, never a constant. |
| `SessionDeleter`, deletion planning, `LiveSQLiteReader` | kit | The containment and symlink rules belong next to the adapters that define the roots. |
| `Harness`, `HarnessCatalog` — the **usage** axis | kit | Naming a CLI is not naming a billing plan. |
| MCP transports + JSON-RPC primitives | kit | A socket and a byte pump have no opinions about Vibe Bar. |
| `RealHomeDirectory`, `JSONLLineScanner`, `JSONLHeadTail`, `Base32` | kit | Shared primitives with the same invariants on both sides. |
| `MCPServer`, its tool catalog, DTOs, resource catalog | here | Vibe Bar's own dispatch, over the kit's transport. |
| `Harness+Quota.swift`, `CostUsageScanner`, everything quota-shaped | here | The **billing** axis — plans, prices, companies, windows. |
| The `~/.vibebar/mcp.sock` default, `--mcp-stdio`, the "not running" message | here | Host-shaped defaults the package refuses to invent. |

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
**Where it comes from.** `Package.swift` pins the package to an exact
tag on GitHub (`.package(url: "https://github.com/AstroQore/agent-session-kit.git",
exact: "0.11.0")`), so a plain clone builds and a release build resolves the
same package the developer built against — `Package.resolved` is
gitignored here, and the exact pin is what stands in for it.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
**It is linked statically.** The kit is compiled into `Vibe Bar.app`'s
executable. There is no framework in `Contents/Frameworks/`, no dylib, and
nothing on disk to swap. Two consequences that matter more than they look:

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
- The only way to know which kit is inside a build is
  `AgentSessionKitInfo.version`, a constant the package pins to its own
  changelog with a test.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
- **A kit tag is not a Vibe Bar release.** Tagging `0.4.0` over there
  changes nothing for a single user until this repository bumps the pin
  *and* ships a build. After merging a bump, cut a dev build (§ 12) —
  otherwise the newest kit exists only in `main`.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
- *By hand:* edit the one line in `Package.swift`, edit the version named
  in this section, read the kit's release notes for anything that needs a
  call-site change, check `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` still describes it
  correctly, then run the full § 9.3 check list. Commit subject
  `Bump agent-session-kit to X.Y.Z`.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
- *By workflow:* `.github/workflows/bump-agent-session-kit.yml` runs daily
  and on demand. It reads the current pin, asks GitHub for the kit's newest
  release, and — when that release is newer — opens
  `chore/bump-agent-session-kit-X.Y.Z` with both edits and the release
  notes linked in the body. It never merges anything.
  With the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, GitHub **will not run CI on a
  bot-opened PR** (a deliberate loop-prevention rule). Close and reopen the
  PR, or push an empty commit to it, to get the checks. Adding a
  `VIBEBAR_BOT_TOKEN` repository secret — a PAT with `contents:write` and
  `pull_requests:write` — removes that step; the workflow prefers it when
  present.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
**Where a user sees it.** Settings › System › **Components** shows
`agent-session-kit` with the bundled `AgentSessionKitInfo.version`, a
"bundled" badge, links to that release's notes and the repository, and a
**Check for kit updates** button. The button is the only thing that opens a
connection — no launch check, no timer, no check-when-the-pane-appears —
and `ComponentUpdateChecker` caches the answer in memory for six hours.
When a newer kit exists the row reads *"Newer kit X.Y.Z available — ships
with the next Vibe Bar build"*. Keep that phrasing, or an equivalent one
that is equally clear: the app cannot install a kit release, and a row that
sounds like it can is a bug in the copy.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
**Working on both at once.** To build Vibe Bar against a local checkout of
the package (say, to try a kit change before it is tagged), use SwiftPM's
edit mode rather than editing `Package.swift`:

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
`swift package edit` records the override in `.swiftpm/` (gitignored), so
it never reaches a commit, and `unedit` returns to the pinned tag. Never
commit a `Package.swift` that points at a local path or an untagged branch:
a release build resolves from a clean checkout and would fail, or worse,
silently resolve something else.

head: AGENTS.md — Vibe Bar Project Guide for AI Agents > 2. Repository Layout > 2.1 What lives in agent-session-kit instead
text:
The kit's own conventions — conventional-commit subjects, Keep a Changelog,
bare `X.Y.Z` tags, and `RELEASING.md` — are that repository's, not this
one's. Use them when working there.
