head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide
text:
Strapi is an open-source headless CMS.
Yarn workspaces + Nx monorepo. Node ≥22 ≤26, Yarn 4.
Target branch: `develop` (not `main`). All PRs go to `develop`.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Repository Structure
text: The following are the most important packages (not exhaustive — run `yarn workspaces list` for the full set):

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Repository Structure
text:
| Package                            | Description                                               |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@strapi/strapi`                   | Main framework entry point (Koa server)                   |
| `@strapi/admin`                    | React 18 admin dashboard                                  |
| `@strapi/core`                     | Core business logic                                       |
| `@strapi/database`                 | Database abstraction (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, SQLite) |
| `@strapi/content-manager`          | Content management UI                                     |
| `@strapi/types`                    | Shared TypeScript type definitions                        |
| `@strapi/permissions`              | RBAC engine                                               |
| `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions` | JWT authentication                                        |

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Repository Structure > Skills directories
text: **`.ai/skills/`** is the canonical source for committed repo skills. Each subdirectory containing a `SKILL.md` is a skill.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Repository Structure > Skills directories
text: The AI-tooling well-known locations are **symlink targets** maintained by `yarn ai:sync`: `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/`.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Repository Structure > Skills directories
text: Run `yarn ai:sync` after adding or removing a skill in `.ai/skills/` to keep all three target dirs up to date. Links are local-only (gitignored target dirs) — only `.ai/skills/` content is committed.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Repository Structure > Skills directories
text: On **Windows**, the CLI creates directory **junctions** (no extra setup). Directory symlinks require Developer Mode or an elevated shell.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Architecture
text: - **`Strapi` class** — The DI container and central hub. Accessed as a `strapi` parameter injected through the factory pattern (e.g. `createService(strapi)`). Never use `global.strapi` — always prefer proper dependency injection. Provides `strapi.documents`, `strapi.db`, `strapi.log`, etc. Lifecycle: Register → Bootstrap → Start → Destroy (`start()` calls `load()` internally, which runs register + bootstrap).

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Architecture
text: - **Server / Admin split** — Koa.js HTTP server (`@strapi/strapi`) + React/Redux admin (`@strapi/admin`). Packages with both concerns export dual entry points: `strapi-server` (Node.js logic) and `strapi-admin` (UI components).

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Architecture
text: - **Document Service** — The primary high-level API for content (`strapi.documents`). Replaced the legacy Entity Service. Always use this for reading/writing content — never raw DB queries unless you're working inside `@strapi/database` itself.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Architecture
text: - **Polymorphic (morph\*) relations** — Contributor doc: [docs/docs/packages/core/database/01-relations/polymorphic-relations.md](docs/docs/packages/core/database/01-relations/polymorphic-relations.md) (storage, DB populate, and how `getDeepPopulate` / relation traversal interact with `morphToOne` and join-based morphs).

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Architecture
text: - **Plugin system** — Plugins register routes, controllers, services, content types, and middleware via the same `strapi-server` / `strapi-admin` dual structure. Official plugins live in `packages/plugins/`.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Architecture
text: - **Content Types** — Defined using a JSON-based notation (not JSON Schema spec). Each content type has a `schema.json` file — see any `packages/core/content-manager/server/src/content-types/` for examples. The database layer auto-generates tables from them. Never write raw migrations for content type changes.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Architecture
text: - **EE / CE split** — Some features are Enterprise Edition only, gated at runtime. See EE toggles in the Testing section below.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Architecture
text: - **`@strapi/types`** — Single source of truth for shared TypeScript types. Import from here; improve these types rather than duplicating locally.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Monorepo Setup > New worktree bootstrap
text:
- In a newly created worktree, check whether `.claude/skills/git-conventions` resolves to the
  repository's `.ai/skills/git-conventions`. If the link is absent or stale, run
  `yarn setup:worktree`.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Monorepo Setup > New worktree bootstrap
text: - If `.brain` exists, do not initialize or refresh it.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Monorepo Setup > New worktree bootstrap
text:
- If `.brain` is absent, look for the user-level `brain-start` skill.
  - If unavailable, continue silently; this is the normal external-contributor path.
  - If available, read it, resolve the CMS Brain CLI from its canonical host checkout, and run
    `"$BRAIN_CLI" refresh --project strapi/strapi`.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Monorepo Setup > New worktree bootstrap
text:
- If CMS Brain is installed and refresh fails, report the failure and follow the bootstrap skill's
  remediation. Only the absence of the optional skill is a clean no-op.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > Unit tests (fastest — run first)
text: Unit test files live in `__tests__/` subdirectories within each package.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > Frontend tests (admin panel)
text: Frontend test files also live in `__tests__/` within their respective packages.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > API integration tests
text: Integration tests live in `tests/api/`. Test apps are generated automatically — always regenerate with `yarn test:generate-app` rather than reusing a stale one (stale apps cause misleading failures).

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > CLI tests
text: CLI tests live in `tests/cli/`.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > E2E tests (Playwright)
text: E2E tests live in `tests/e2e/tests/` organized by domain (e.g. `admin`, `content-manager`, `i18n`).

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > EE toggles
text: - `IS_EE=true` — enables Enterprise features in frontend tests (`yarn test:front`)

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > EE toggles
text: - `RUN_EE=true` — enables Enterprise features in E2E tests

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > Pre-PR checklist
text: All tests must pass before merging. Run at minimum:

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > Pre-PR checklist
text: E2E (`yarn test:e2e`) is required per CONTRIBUTING.md but slow — CI enforces it on every PR.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Testing > Pre-PR checklist
text: **When to add or update tests:** Always for bug fixes (reproduce the bug first). For features, add tests when they cover meaningful behaviour — not just to hit coverage numbers. When changing existing behaviour, update the affected tests to match.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Quality Gates > Commits
text: Must follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) (enforced by Husky `commit-msg` hook and CI via `commitlint`). Format:

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Quality Gates > Commits
text: Valid types: `feat` `fix` `chore` `ci` `docs` `enhancement` `test` `revert` `security` `future` `release`

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Quality Gates > Commits
text: Use `yarn commit` for an interactive prompt. Run `yarn version:check` if you've touched any `package.json`.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Quality Gates > TypeScript
text: - Import types from `@strapi/types` — extend or improve them rather than duplicating locally.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Quality Gates > TypeScript
text: - Never use `any` when a proper type exists or can be reasonably defined. Prefer `unknown` otherwise.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Quality Gates > TypeScript
text: - Run `yarn test:ts` before pushing.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Security
text: - Never commit secrets, credentials, or API keys.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Security
text: - Never disable or weaken authentication/authorization checks.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Security
text: - Use parameterized queries — never interpolate user input into raw SQL or database queries.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Security
text: - Validate and sanitize all user input at controller/service boundaries.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > Security
text: - When working with EE-gated features, do not bypass license checks.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > PR Guidelines
text: - Branch from `develop`, target `develop` — never `main`.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > PR Guidelines
text: - Link the issue you're fixing in the description.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > PR Guidelines
text: - All tests must pass before merging.

head: Strapi Monorepo — Agent Guide > PR Guidelines

head: AGENTS.md: Developer & AI Coding Assistant Guide
AGENTS.md: Developer & AI Coding Assistant Guide > 1. Project Overview (Current State)
text:
`noaadata` is a Python library for encoding, decoding, and processing NOAA
CO-OPS marine water level data, Automatic Identification System (AIS) ship
traffic binary messages, USCG N-AIS receive fields, and NMEA-0183 marine
sentences. It also provides database bridges (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, SQLite3) and
GIS exporters (Google Earth KML).

head: AGENTS.md: Developer & AI Coding Assistant Guide > 1. Project Overview (Current State)
text:
The project has completed a multi-phase Spec-Driven Development (SDD)
modernization initiative outlined in [`PRD.md`](PRD.md), [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md),
and [`TASKS.md`](TASKS.md). Legacy `setup.py` setuptools packaging has been
replaced with modern PEP 621 declarative packaging using `hatchling` and `uv`
environment management. All 336 unit, property, and benchmark tests pass, code
is formatted with `ruff` and `mdformat`, static typing is checked with `mypy`,
and automated CI/CD pipelines run on GitHub Actions.

head: AGENTS.md: Developer & AI Coding Assistant Guide > 4. Strict Version Control & Git Commit Rules > 4.1 Conventional Commits Required

head: AGENTS.md: Developer & AI Coding Assistant Guide > 4. Strict Version Control & Git Commit Rules > 4.1 Conventional Commits Required
text:
- **Allowed Types**:
  - `feat`: A new feature or capability (e.g.,
    `feat(ais): add support for message 24`).
  - `fix`: A bug fix (e.g., `fix(nmea): resolve checksum boundary error`).
  - `refactor`: Code refactoring without behavioral changes (e.g.,
    `refactor(aisutils): implement dunder protocols on BitVector`).
  - `test`: Adding or updating test suites (e.g.,
    `test(noaadata): migrate legacy grid tests to pytest`).
  - `build`: Packaging or dependency updates (e.g.,
    `build: migrate from setup.py to pyproject.toml and hatchling`).
  - `docs`: Documentation updates (e.g.,
    `docs: update migration guide and AGENTS.md`).
  - `chore`: Maintenance tasks (e.g.,
    `chore: configure ruff and mdformat pre-commit hooks`).

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project
text: qalmsw is a Python CLI that runs LLM-powered QA checks on scientific LaTeX manuscripts. The LLM backend is a **local llama.cpp server** reached via its OpenAI-compatible API; the code must never assume a hosted provider.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project
text: Target model sizes: **9B–31B GGUF** running on llama.cpp. Context windows are therefore modest (~8k–32k), so checks that reason over long stretches of text must **chunk**, not send the whole document in one call.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: The `qalmsw check` command reads `QALMSW_BASE_URL` (default `http://localhost:8080/v1`) and `QALMSW_MODEL` (default `local-model`) from the environment; both can be overridden with `--base-url` / `--model`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: The pipeline is **load → checkers → report**, and every checker produces a uniform `Finding` so the report/CI layer never branches on checker type.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **`Paragraph.start_line` / `end_line` are 1-indexed against the *origin* file** — for single-file docs that's the .tex itself; for multi-file docs it's whichever `\input{}`-ed file the content lives in. `Paragraph.file` (and `Section.file`, `Finding.file`) carries the origin path. Findings render with `origin:line` so editors jump to the file the author edits, not the top-level `main.tex`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **Comment stripping preserves newlines** so line numbers stay stable after `%`-stripping. `parse.tex._COMMENT_RE` uses a negative look-behind to skip escaped `\%`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **`Document.load` inlines `\input{}` / `\include{}` recursively** via `parse/includes.py::resolve_includes`, producing a combined `source` plus a per-line `LineMapEntry` list. Parsers (`parse_paragraphs`, `parse_sections`) take that map as a kwarg and translate combined-source lines back to `(origin_file, line_in_file)`. Cycles are broken; missing targets become a one-line placeholder comment so the run continues.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **Checkers receive a `Document`**, not just paragraphs. Citation-style checkers need the raw source (cites can appear outside prose paragraphs) and the path (to resolve `.bib` files). The `Checker` protocol is `check(doc: Document) -> list[Finding]`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **Non-prose paragraphs are filtered by the consumer**, not at load time. `GrammarChecker` calls `has_prose()` per paragraph so citation-scanning checkers still see headings. Don't pre-filter in the CLI.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **CLI exit code is `1` only when an `error`-severity finding exists.** `info` (unused bib entry) and `warning` (duplicate bib key) findings are non-fatal by design — drafts routinely have them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **`LLMClient` is a `typing.Protocol`**, not an ABC. Tests pass a `FakeLLM` that only implements `complete_json`. Don't tighten the interface into a base class; the Protocol is intentional so any object with the right shape works.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **Checkers never ask the LLM for line numbers.** Small local models count lines unreliably. Instead they ask for an `excerpt` string and we locate it in the paragraph text (`grammar._locate_line`). New checkers should follow this pattern.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **Structured output uses `response_format={"type": "json_object"}`** — supported by llama.cpp server. The system prompt must also spell out the JSON shape, because small models otherwise drift.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **`LLMClient` has `max_retries=0`.** A slow local model that times out once rarely succeeds silently; failing fast surfaces the real state instead of a 30-minute silent retry loop.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **LLM fan-out goes through `ordered_parallel_map` (`src/qalmsw/_concurrency.py`).** Grammar, math, and reviewer all take a `concurrency` ctor arg; the CLI exposes `--concurrency/-j`. Default is 1 (matches llama.cpp's default `--parallel 1`). Users bump both server and CLI together. Results are order-preserving so reports stay stable.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **`.bib` parsing is hybrid**: a regex sweep over `@type{key,` headers owns keys + source line numbers (authoritative for MISSING / UNUSED / DUPLICATE), and `bibtexparser` pulls `title`/`author` fields by key. If bibtexparser fails or skips an entry, those fields fall back to empty strings — the entry is still present for citation checks. Don't let title/author extraction gate entry presence.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contracts worth preserving
text: - **Bibliography discovery has two sources**: `.bib` files from `\bibliography{}` / `\addbibresource{}` (via `parse/citations.py::scan_bib_resources`), and inline `\begin{thebibliography}` blocks (via `bib/inline.py::extract_inline_bibitems`, which synthesizes `BibEntry` records from `\bibitem{key}` with a best-effort title guess). The CLI tries `.bib` first, falls back to inline, and emits an explicit warning only when both come up empty. Papers that ship pre-formatted bibliographies in the .tex body are a first-class case, not an error.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Checker status
text:
| Checker    | State      | Shape                                                       |
|------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `grammar`  | working    | Per-paragraph LLM call, parallelizable, cheap               |
| `math`     | working    | Per-paragraph math-formula consistency pass, parallelizable |
| `citations`| working    | Deterministic `.bib` vs `\cite` cross-check (MISSING / UNUSED / DUPLICATE). No LLM. |
| `reviewer` | working    | One LLM call per `\section{}` (or whole body if none); over-long sections are truncated |
| `claims`   | working, opt-in | Two LLM calls per paragraph-with-citation (extract, then judge per (claim, cite)). Scholar abstracts cached per bib key within a run. Opt in with `--enable-claims` — slow and rate-limited. |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Checker status
text: When adding a checker: drop a file into `src/qalmsw/checkers/`, register it in `checkers/__init__.py`, wire it into `cli.py`'s `checkers` list, and add tests with a `FakeLLM` — don't hit the real server from tests.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Citations module layout
text: - `src/qalmsw/bib/parser.py` — regex + `bibtexparser` hybrid over `@type{key,` headers and title/author fields.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Citations module layout
text: - `src/qalmsw/bib/inline.py` — `\bibitem{}` extractor for inline `\begin{thebibliography}` blocks, returns `BibEntry` records.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Citations module layout
text: - `src/qalmsw/parse/citations.py` — scanners for `\cite*` keys and `\bibliography{}` / `\addbibresource{}` paths.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Citations module layout
text: - `src/qalmsw/checkers/citations.py` — the `CitationChecker`; receives parsed `BibEntry`s via its constructor so the CLI owns bibliography discovery and resolution.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > What's intentionally *not* here
text: - No LLM-assisted citation verification (does this citation actually support this claim?). That's the `claims` checker's territory.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > What's intentionally *not* here
text: - Retrieval uses **Semantic Scholar** by default (`src/qalmsw/retrieval/semantic_scholar.py`). Google Scholar remains available as an opt-in scraping backend and may hit rate limits or CAPTCHAs. Backend switching is done at runtime via `qalmsw.retrieval.set_backend()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > What's intentionally *not* here
text: - JSON report output exists in `report/json.py`; SARIF is still future work. The `Finding` pydantic model is the serialization seam for future output formats.

head: VESPERA PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE > OVERVIEW
text: Vespera is a fully automated OpenAPI 3.1 engine for Axum - delivers FastAPI-like DX to Rust. Zero-config route discovery via compile-time macro scanning.

head: VESPERA PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE > OVERVIEW
text: Also provides in-process dispatch (`vespera_inprocess` crate) and JNI integration (`vespera_jni` crate) for embedding Rust axum apps inside Java/Spring applications without HTTP overhead.

head: VESPERA PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE > OVERVIEW > Headline Capabilities (2026)
text:
| Capability | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **`#[derive(Schema)]` → OpenAPI 3.1** | `vespera_macro::Schema` | Rust types become JSON Schema at compile time, including serde renames, `Option<T>` as `type:[...,"null"]` / nullable `$ref` as `anyOf`, schema-level `examples:[...]` (not singular `example`), `Vec<T>`, SeaORM relations |
| **`Validated<T>` extractor + auto-`422`** | `vespera::Validated`, `crates/vespera/src/validated.rs` | Wraps `Json`/`Form`/`Query`/`Path` and runs `garde::Validate` before the handler — rejection is **`422 Unprocessable Entity`** with `{"errors":[{"path","message"}]}` JSON envelope |
| **`schema_type! { ... }`** | `vespera_macro::schema_type` | Derive request/response DTOs from existing structs (`pick` / `omit` / `partial` / `add` / `multipart` / `omit_default`) — first-class SeaORM relation support |
| **One-liner `.serve(addr)`** | `vespera::Serve` (`crates/vespera/src/serve.rs`) | Extension trait on `axum::Router` — `create_app().serve("0.0.0.0:3000").await` replaces 3 lines of `TcpListener::bind` + `axum::serve` boilerplate |
| **Binary wire format (JNI)** | `vespera_inprocess` | `[u32 BE len | UTF-8 JSON header | raw body]` — multipart / PDFs / images travel as raw bytes; **`422` validation errors hoisted** into the wire header as `"validation_errors": [...]` so Java decoders never special-case error shapes |
| **Multi-app routing (JNI/FFI)** | `vespera::jni_apps! { "_default" => app, "admin" => admin_app }` | Wire header carries optional `"app"` field; Java side picks per request via `X-Vespera-App` header (configurable via `AppNameResolver`) |
| **Zero-config Spring autoconfigure** | `libs/vespera-bridge/.../VesperaBridgeAutoConfiguration` | `VesperaProxyController` + `AppNameResolver` + `DispatchModeResolver` beans auto-registered; replace any of them via `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` |
| **Cron jobs** | `#[vespera::cron("...")]` | Auto-discovered like routes; runs via `tokio-cron-scheduler` |

head: VESPERA PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE > JNI ARCHITECTURE > JNI Dispatch Modes (seven symbols)
text:
| Symbol | Java native | Mode | Memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Java_...dispatchBytes` | `byte[] dispatchBytes(byte[])` | sync | full body |
| `Java_...dispatchAsync` | `void dispatchAsync(CompletableFuture<byte[]>, byte[])` | async | full body |
| `Java_...dispatchStreaming` | `byte[] dispatchStreaming(byte[], OutputStream)` | sync response-streaming | chunk-bounded response |
| `Java_...dispatchFullStreaming` | `byte[] dispatchFullStreaming(byte[], InputStream, OutputStream)` | sync bidirectional streaming | chunk-bounded both directions |
| `Java_...dispatchStreamingWithHeader` | `void dispatchStreamingWithHeader(byte[], Consumer<byte[]>, OutputStream)` | sync response-streaming, header callback before first body byte | chunk-bounded response |
| `Java_...dispatchFullStreamingWithHeader` | `void dispatchFullStreamingWithHeader(byte[], Consumer<byte[]>, InputStream, OutputStream)` | sync bidirectional streaming, header callback | chunk-bounded both directions |
| `Java_...dispatchDirect0` | `int dispatchDirect(ByteBuffer, int, ByteBuffer)` (public validated wrapper over the private native) | sync, direct buffers | full body, zero Java heap arrays |

head: VESPERA PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE > JNI ARCHITECTURE > JNI Dispatch Modes (seven symbols)
text: All share the same wire format, registered router, and panic-safe `catch_unwind` discipline. **`DecodedResponse` (vespera-bridge 0.2.0, BREAKING):** `body()` now returns a read-only `java.nio.ByteBuffer` (zero-copy view over the wire bytes); `bodyBytes()` materialises an owned `byte[]` copy on demand — callers that previously used `body()` as `byte[]` must switch to `bodyBytes()`. The direct-buffer path (`dispatchDirect` + pooled `dispatchDirectPooled`, per-thread 64 KiB→4 MiB buffers via `vespera.direct.maxBufferBytes`) removes the two JNI region copies of `dispatchBytes`; on response overflow it returns `-(requiredSize)` and a retry **re-runs the handler**, so the Java side only auto-retries idempotent requests (`BufferTooSmallException` otherwise). Spring autoconfigured default since vespera-bridge 0.2.0: `SmartDispatchModeResolver` (small/bodyless idempotent → `DIRECT` ~2.2µs, small non-idempotent → `SYNC` ~3.2µs, else streaming ~24µs). Opt out with `vespera.bridge.dispatch-mode=bidirectional-streaming` to restore the pre-0.2.0 default (`BidirectionalStreamingDispatchModeResolver`: provably bodyless requests — CL:0, or GET/HEAD/OPTIONS without CL/TE — downgrade to response-only `STREAMING` ~3x, 24.1→7.7µs; everything else streams both ways). `dispatchAsync` spawns the dispatch on Rust's shared Tokio runtime via `tokio::spawn` (panic → `JoinError` → `error_wire(500)`) and completes the `CompletableFuture` from a daemon-attached cached Tokio worker thread (`with_cached_daemon_env` from `daemon_env.rs`, called at `jni_impl.rs:493`/`:498`: `GetEnv` first, `AttachCurrentThreadAsDaemon` only for unattached threads, TLS env cache + per-completion local frame + unconditional pending-exception cleanup) — ~1.3µs/op faster than scoped attach per completion. `dispatchStreaming` drains the response body chunk-by-chunk via `http_body::Body::frame()` and writes each chunk to the Java `OutputStream`. `dispatchFullStreaming` adds request-side streaming: a `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` thread pulls chunks (default 256 KiB) from `InputStream.read(byte[])` and feeds them into axum via an `mpsc::channel`-backed `http_body::Body`, giving natural backpressure (bounded channel, default 16 slots) so 1 GiB uploads run in `O(chunk_size)` RAM.

head: VESPERA PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE > JNI ARCHITECTURE > JNI Dispatch Modes (seven symbols)
text: **Streaming tuning (process-fixed after first dispatch):** chunk size via system property `vespera.streaming.chunkBytes` / env `VESPERA_STREAMING_CHUNK_BYTES` (default 256 KiB, clamped 4 KiB–8 MiB); channel capacity via `vespera.streaming.channelCapacity` / `VESPERA_STREAMING_CHANNEL_CAPACITY` (default 16, clamped 1–1024). Java API: `VesperaBridge.configureStreaming(chunkBytes, channelCapacity)` — pending-config pattern (call before `init()`; values stored pending and applied right after native load, before any dispatch; programmatic > sysprops > env > defaults). Rust-side setters: `vespera_inprocess::set_streaming_chunk_bytes` / `set_streaming_channel_capacity` (precedence: setter > env > default). The shared Tokio runtime's worker count is tunable the same way: `vespera.runtime.workerThreads` / `VESPERA_RUNTIME_WORKERS` (default: logical CPUs, clamped 1–1024) — cap it when JVM thread pools compete for the same cores. `_default`-app dispatch resolves through a lock-free `OnceLock<Router>` fast path; named apps are also lock-free — a single `ArcSwap<HashMap<String, Router>>` load plus a hash lookup. The response wire header serializes straight from `http::HeaderMap` (zero per-header allocation) and request wire headers deserialize borrowing from the input buffer (`Cow`); both the response serialize and the request parse use **hand-rolled** writers/parsers (`wire/header_write.rs` / `wire/header_read.rs`) byte-identical to the prior `serde_json` path — the serde twins are retained private as `*_serde` for the same-run criterion A/B in `benches/dispatch.rs` (group `wire_header_serde`). The wire byte layout is locked by `crates/vespera_inprocess/tests/wire_contract.rs` and the hand-vs-serde round-trip property test in `wire.rs`.

head: VESPERA PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE > JNI ARCHITECTURE > Multi-app routing
text: **Use case**: multi-app is primarily a feature for **external-dispatcher scenarios** — JNI (Java host picks app per request via header), WebAssembly bridge, C FFI, or any in-process embedding where the host distinguishes between multiple independent vespera API surfaces.  For Rust **standalone** servers (`axum::serve(...)`), the native axum patterns (`Router::merge()`, `Router::nest()`) are more idiomatic for modularization — `register_app_named` adds no value when the same binary owns both the router registration and the HTTP entry point.

lock-free (one atomic load + hash lookup) — and returns:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 1. What this is
text:
General-purpose CAS in **Common Lisp**, from MIT's Macsyma (1970s). GPL
(`COPYING`, `AUTHORS`). Old and layered -- MIT-era Maclisp, 1980s UT-Austin,
modern additions; match the file you edit.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 1. What this is
text:
- Version: `AC_INIT([maxima], [<version>])` in `configure.ac`, but `configure`
  overwrites it from `git describe --dirty`, hyphens to underscores, wherever
  git can describe a tag.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 1. What this is
text:
- **Upstream is SourceForge** (`git.code.sf.net/p/maxima/code`).
  **`github.com/calyau/maxima` is a pure mirror**: commits, branches and PRs
  pushed there are overwritten on the next sync. Only SourceForge lands changes;

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build
text:
Prerequisites: **SBCL, Maxima's preferred Lisp** -- use it unless you have a
reason not to (`README-lisps.md` covers the rest, and their quirks) -- and
texinfo's `makeinfo`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build
text:
`-j` buys nothing on the Lisp build unless you configured several Lisps (it does
parallelise `doc/`): automake walks `SUBDIRS` in a serial shell loop, and each
core is one target whose recipe feeds the whole system to the Lisp -- a compile
pass, then a load-and-dump pass (`src/<lisp>-depends.mk` just lists every source
as a prerequisite of it). What gets recompiled is decided in that image by
`defsystem`, from the `:depends-on` graph in `src/maxima.system` -- so an edit
low in that graph, such as `src/simp.lisp`, costs far more than one at the
leaves. Prefer sec. 4's no-rebuild loop. `make install` is not needed --
`./maxima-local` runs the fresh image:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build
text:
**`makeinfo` is hard-required**: `enable_build_docs` defaults true
(`configure.ac`), so without it `./configure` **aborts**. Building
`--disable-build-docs` loses `?`/`??` help and prints
`WARNING: Maxima is unable to set up the help system.` at **every** startup
(`src/cl-info.lisp`, missing `doc/info/maxima-index.lisp`) -- noise in every
batch capture. `gnuplot` matters only for plots at runtime. An older or
less-used Lisp runs Maxima fine but can shift a numeric result the suite checks
(sec. 5).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > Two output directories
text:
`src/binary-<lisp>/` holds the **build**: `maxima.core` plus a `.fasl` per
compiled source. Per Lisp, but **not** per Lisp *version* -- which is why a new
SBCL version needs `make clean` (sec. 15).
`binary/<version>/<lisp>/<lisp-version>/` (underscores, not dots) is the
**runtime** objdir `*maxima-objdir*`: fasls compiled from `share/` on demand --
created lazily, so it is absent until something compiles. `./maxima-local -d`
prints every resolved directory.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > Two output directories
text: A build leaves `git status` clean.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > How the build works
text:
`make` compiles **no** Lisp: it generates wrapper scripts, then shells out to
the Lisp, which loads `lisp-utils/defsystem.lisp` and runs `mk:defsystem` over
**`src/maxima.system`**.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > How the build works
text: - `src/maxima.system`: every source file in dependency order, in `:module`s.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > How the build works
text:
- **Order matters** -- `defsystem` loads as it compiles, so macro modules
  precede users (`src/ratmac.lisp` CRE accessor macros before `p-var`/`p-lc`/...
  users).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > How the build works
text:
- `src/Makefile.am` holds the build, dist and install rules -- but not the
  build's file list, which is `maxima.system`'s job.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > How the build works
text:
- **Not** ASDF, despite the comment atop `src/Makefile.am`; `src/Readme.md`
  describes the `defsystem` build correctly. `src/maxima.asd` is a separate
  secondary path.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > How the build works
text:
- `src/<lisp>-depends.mk` is **generated by `make`** (`sbcl-depends.mk` rule in
  `src/Makefile.am`, via `lisp-utils/make-depends.lisp`), gitignored, in
  `CLEANFILES`, one per configured Lisp. Never hand-edit: regenerated whenever
  `maxima.system`, the `Makefile` or any `*.lisp` changes.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > How the build works
text: `Makefile` is generated -- **always edit `Makefile.am`**.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 2. Build > configure options
text:
`./configure --help` lists every option; the `--enable-<lisp>` flags combine.
**Passing none of them is not "just SBCL"**: with no `--enable-<lisp>` at all,
`configure` probes for every supported Lisp and enables each one it finds
(`configure.ac`, the `explicit_lisp` branch), and `make` then builds one image
per Lisp -- so the same bare `./configure` yields a different configuration on
the same tree once another Lisp is installed. `src/binary-<lisp>` directories
are what a tree was actually built for. Before reconfiguring a tree you did not
configure yourself, read the original invocation out of `config.status`
(`ac_cs_config=`) or the `Invocation command line was` line near the top of
`config.log` -- re-running `configure` overwrites both.
`--with-<lisp>=<prog>` names an explicit executable, absolute path or PATH name
(ABCL instead takes `--with-abcl-jar=<jarfile>`); an
`sbcl executable "..." not found in PATH` warning always means configure did not
find it, and the build will fail. Out-of-tree (VPATH) builds work.
`README-lisps.md`'s per-Lisp caveats are about how the *Lisp* was built, not
about Maxima's configure: GCL must itself be built `--enable-ansi`; ECL must be
built with its C compiler (never `--with-cmp=no`); CLISP slow but frugal; ABCL
slowest.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima
text: `./maxima-local [options]` (`src/init-cl.lisp`). The options that matter:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima
text: - `--batch-string='<expr>;'` -- eval Maxima code, exit. The workhorse.

- `--no-init` -- skip `maxima-init.mac`/`maxima-init.lisp`. **Always in tests**,

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima
text: - `-q`/`--quiet` -- suppress the banner. Safe everywhere, tests included.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima

- `--very-quiet` -- banner **plus** `*display-labels-p*`, `*verify-html-index*`
  and `*warn-deprecated-defmvar-options*` -> nil, and `--very-very-quiet` adds

text:
- `-Q`/`--quit-on-error` -- exit 1 on a **Maxima** error. Not Lisp errors
  (below).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima
text:
`--help` lists the rest (`-b <file>` to batch a `.mac`, `--batch-lisp`, `-p` to
preload, ...).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Four traps
text:
**1. `-Q` misses Lisp errors.** They print
`Maxima encountered a Lisp error: ...`, **auto-continue**, and exit 0 even under
`-Q`:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Four traps
text:
A broken `src/` edit gives the first kind, so `-Q` alone is no CI gate -- also
grep stdout for `Maxima encountered a Lisp error`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Four traps
text:
**2. Auto-continue poisons the rest of the batch.** A failed assignment leaves
the *old* binding; everything after computes confidently wrong answers. Run each
risky probe in its own process.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Four traps
text:
**3. `:lisp` eats the rest of the LINE**, not one form. `dbm-read`
(`src/mdebug.lisp`) strips a trailing `;`, wraps the whole remainder in parens
and reads it; `lisp-eval` runs the lot as one `progn`. Trailing Maxima code is
therefore evaluated as *Lisp*, normally a loud and unrelated error, while a
*mid*-line `;` comments out the closing paren:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Four traps
text: Put `:lisp` on its own line, or last in the string.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Four traps
text:
**4. Some inputs never terminate**, and nothing in the batch stops one: it runs
until you kill it, filling the disk if it prints. Always
`timeout 120 ./maxima-local ...`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Internals
text:
`:lisp <form>` evaluates Lisp. `?name` is the Lisp symbol `NAME` (`?car` is
`CAR`) -- how you reach a helper with no `$` prefix, since a plain Maxima `foo`
already *is* `$FOO`; backslash-escape anything Maxima's reader would take as an
operator, as in `?\*debug\-integrate\*`. `#$<expr>$` reads Maxima syntax from
Lisp.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Internals
text:
**Two different `errcatch`es.** At Maxima level it returns `[value]` on success
and `[]` on error, and still **prints** the message; with several arguments it
returns only the last value, stopping at the first error (`errcatch(5, 5^2)` is
`[25]`).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Internals
text:
The Lisp macro (`src/errset.lisp`) instead returns `(value)` or **NIL**, so it
is a fine truth value -- but `(car (errcatch form))` cannot distinguish a
NIL-valued success from a failure.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Internals
text:
**Capturing output for parsing: set `display2d:false` first.** The default 2-D
display is multi-line box art and cannot be re-read; with it off you get one
re-parseable line (`string()`/`grind()` do the same for one expression):

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Internals
text:
**Interactive prompts eat the next statement**: `asksign`/`askinteger`/`read`
take it as their answer. `retrieve` reads it with `mread-noprompt`, so it needs
its own `;`/`$` but may sit on the same line (`asksign(a); pos; 2+2;` works). A
mid-script `asksign` silently eats your next expression and shifts the rest.
Exhausting input gives `RETRIEVE: End of file encountered.` -- a useful signal
the code asked more than expected. `is(a>0)` does **not** ask; it returns
`unknown`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 3. Running Maxima > Internals
text:
Most `MAXIMA_*` env vars are read by `set-pathnames` (`src/init-cl.lisp`); the
*internal* Lisp directory variables are documented in
`doc/implementation/dir_vars.txt`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > Redefine at runtime instead of rebuilding
text:
`:lisp (load "variant.lisp")` is **compiled** by SBCL, not interpreted, so you
can A/B a changed function inside one process:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > Redefine at runtime instead of rebuilding
text:
Use it to **instrument** (count how often a branch fires over a whole suite run,
touching no source file), to **prototype** a fix before editing, and to
**baseline** it -- redefine your new helpers to no-ops and re-run for a real
before/after out of one build.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > Redefine at runtime instead of rebuilding
text:
**Redefine the function on the call path**, often not the one named after the
user-visible operator:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > Redefine at runtime instead of rebuilding
text:
Redefining `$foo` when a simplifier owns the operator does nothing, and looks
exactly like your fix not working. `FOO-IMPL` names are generated, so they
appear in no source file -- use `grep -rE 'defmfun \(?\$foo' src/`, since the
option-list form is `(defmfun ($foo ...) ...)`. Exception: a function declaimed
`inline` is inlined into its callers, so redefinition won't take -- such
declaims cluster in `src/mutils.lisp` (`mnump`, `ratnump`, `mplusp`, `mexptp`,
...), plus `defmfun ... :inline-impl t`. Ask the image:
`:lisp (sb-int:info :function :inlinep 'mnump)` -> `INLINE`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > Redefine at runtime instead of rebuilding
text:
Instrument with plain Lisp `format`/`print`: a Maxima-level display or string
function called from a hook in simplifier or limit code re-enters the code you
are instrumenting.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > Redefine at runtime instead of rebuilding
text:
**Print to `*debug-io*`, not `*standard-output*`.** `run_testsuite` rebinds
`*standard-output*` per problem to a throwaway string stream (`test-batch` in
`src/mload.lisp`, restored in an `unwind-protect`) to keep incidental output out
of the log -- pass/fail is `batch-equal-check` on the returned *value*, and the
captured text resurfaces only in a failure report or under `display_all`. A
`format t` from an instrumented function is therefore swallowed, looking exactly
like your hook never firing; `src/mload.lisp` uses `*debug-io*` for its own
tracing for the same reason.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > The stale-image trap
text:
**`make` can exit 0 while your file failed to compile**: SBCL's debugger
swallows the remaining stdin forms and EOF-exits 0, so every later test
exercises the **old** image. Check after every build:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > The stale-image trap
text:
Exactly `make`'s own dependency (`src/sbcl-depends.mk`:
`binary-sbcl/maxima.core : compar.lisp`).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > The stale-image trap
text:
**One-directional.** Source newer than core => the build definitely did not
finish. Core newer does **not** prove it was clean: a *semantic* error (calling
an undefined function) still writes a valid fasl, exits 0, loads, and the core
*is* redumped. For that, grep the build log for `caught ERROR`, `caught WARNING`
**and `undefined function:`** -- SBCL reports a call to a function that does not
exist as only a `caught STYLE-WARNING`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > The stale-image trap
text:
`:lisp (fboundp 'maxima::my-new-fn)` is decisive **only for a newly added
function**; for an edited body it was already true and stays true after a failed
build -- test the behaviour instead.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 4. The edit-test loop > The stale-image trap
text: Never run two builds concurrently; they share the fasl output directory.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text: All via `./maxima-local --no-init --batch-string='<call>;'`:

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text: - `run_testsuite(tests=["rtest_abs"])` -- one file

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text: - `run_testsuite()` -- the core suite

text: - `run_testsuite(share_tests=true)` -- core + share, what `make check` runs

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text: - `run_testsuite(share_tests=only)` -- share only

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text:
Narrow to one file while iterating, but validate a finished change against the
**full suite, share tests included**: a core-only run skips the `share/` tests
(though core files `load()` share packages anyway), and only that run is long.
Green still proves nothing (below).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text:
**Discard the first run when comparing timings or consing.** Share packages
compile into the runtime objdir on first use, so run one pays for that
compilation and allocates far more than run two, which only loads the fasls.
Correctness is unaffected, only the numbers move.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text:
**Comparing two builds.** Alternate and repeat -- A, B, A, B, not all of A then
all of B: interleaving cancels drift from other load, and repetition shows the
noise floor. Add a targeted benchmark for whatever the change should most
affect, since a whole-suite time buries a large local win among thousands of
unrelated problems. Run the full suite regardless -- speed work still has to be
correct.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text:
**Never `--very-quiet`/`--very-very-quiet` for tests.** They nil
`*display-labels-p*`, and `dim-mlabel` (`src/displa.lisp`) emits labels only
when it is true, so any test asserting on labelled output fails under them and
passes otherwise. **`--quiet` is fine.**

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests
text:
`$run_testsuite` takes further keywords (`src/mload.lisp`: `display_all`,
`time`, `debug`, ...). A share test named without `share_tests` warns
`is a share test, but share_tests was not set` and runs nothing.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > `batch(f, 'test)` is NOT `run_testsuite(tests=[f])`
text:
A file with registered known failures reports every one of them under bare
`batch` and none under the suite, which tolerates them by number. Answers come
from the file only when `$batch_answers_from_file` is true -- `run_testsuite`
binds it and `--batch-string` forces it globally (`src/init-cl.lisp`) -- but it
is nil for `-b file` and interactive sessions, where the question goes to the
terminal; at EOF that problem fails with `RETRIEVE: End of file encountered.`,
and the answer left in the file shifts every later pair. **Never conclude "I
broke this" from bare `batch`.**

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > The accounting rule
text:
Per-file `P/P passed` **excludes** registered known failures; the headline
`out of N tests` **includes** them, so P + E = N. `make check` runs
`tests/<lisp>-test.sh`, a two-line wrapper for `tests/test.sh` generated from
`test.sh.in`, which greps the one `tests/<lisp>.log` it writes for exactly
**`No unexpected errors`** -- that string, not a failure count, is the pass/fail
contract. Edit `test.sh.in`; `tests/test.sh` and every `tests/*.log` are
generated and gitignored.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > The accounting rule
text:
**Under SBCL `make check` runs a second test.** `tests/sbcl-depcheck.sh` wraps
`tests/depcheck.sh` (generated from `depcheck.sh.in`) and loads
`lisp-utils/check-dependencies.lisp` into the built image, checking
`src/maxima.system`'s `:dependencies-complete` claims against SBCL's
cross-reference data (sec. 13). It exits 1 on an undeclared compile-time
dependency and 2 when it cannot run at all, so unlike the suite its exit
status is the contract and there is no log to grep. SBCL-only -- no other
Lisp exposes the xref. Run it alone with `cd tests && ./depcheck.sh`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > The accounting rule
text:
**Baseline before blaming your change.** On SBCL both the core suite and core +
share are expected green, and normally are, so a red run is a real signal and
not the status quo. It still need not be yours: results move between Lisp
implementations and between versions of one, and the older and less-used ones
fail tests SBCL passes -- numeric printing is a recurring culprit
(`README-lisps.md` compares them). Record your own baseline, build and Lisp
before the change and compare against that.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > The known-failure registry
text:
`src/testsuite.lisp` holds `$testsuite_files` and `$share_testsuite_files`.
**Two** entry formats parse (`expected-failures`, `src/mload.lisp`):

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > The known-failure registry
text:
Problem *N* = the *N*-th (input, expected) pair, `/* */` comments skipped.
Read-time conditionals (`#+gcl`, `#+allegro`, `#-sbcl`, ...) gate problem
numbers **and whole file entries**, so a file registered under one Lisp can be
absent under another, and numbers gated to a Lisp you are not running are
compiled out -- not yours. Fixing a bug prints
`Tests that were expected to fail but passed:` -- remove the entry in the same
commit, else `No unexpected errors` still prints and `make check` stays green on
a wrong registry.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
`tests/rtest_<topic>.mac`; share tests as `share/<pkg>/rtest_<pkg>.mac`.
Alternating pairs, input `;` / expected `$`. By convention the first pair kills
state (`tests/README.how-to` sec. 5; most files do it):

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
- **Append, never insert.** Registry entries are *positional problem numbers*; a
  middle insertion re-points every later one -> a failure at the shifted number.
  `tests/README.how-to` sec. 9(d) suggests keeping known failures at the top so
  appends stay safe.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
- **Leave the environment as you found it.** Some core files assert fact/context
  state at the end -- `[facts(), contexts]; [[], [initial, global]];`
  (`rtest16.mac`, `rtest_sign.mac`, both marked *"Leave this at the end of the
  file!"*) or separate `facts();`/`contexts;` checks. A leaked `assume` surfaces
  at the file's *highest* problem number. `forget`/ `remvalue`/`remfunction` at
  the end; prefer local option settings (`is(x<1), prederror:false;`).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
- **Evaluation trap**: Maxima *evaluates* input, only *simplifies* expected
  output -- `makelist(sin(k*%pi),k,1,5);` / `makelist(0,k,1,5)$` fails. Write
  `''(makelist(0,k,1,5))$` or literal `[0,0,0,0,0]$`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
- **Answers go on the input line**, before the expected value; `retrieve` eats
  them off the file stream -- not problems. Asking twice needs two answers; a
  wrong count shifts the whole answer stream:
  ```maxima
  [asksign (foo), sign (foo), sign (foo)], ask_hide_prompt; p;
  [pos, pos, pos];
  ```

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
- **Bigfloat literals convert at READ time** with the ambient `fpprec`, not the
  one in force when the statement runs:
  `block([fpprec:30], is(abs(e - 1.56239406221731183021486562870b0) < 1b-25))`
  truncates to ~16 digits. Set `fpprec` in a previous statement.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
- Cite the bug: `/* SF bug #NNNN */` (mostly a `tests/` convention; casing
  varies, so `grep -i`). A test whose answers run out prints its question and
  aborts the file with `batch: missing expected result in test script.`

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
**A green suite is not proof.** Several problems in `tests/rtest_integrate.mac`
are headed *"Expected failure"* (grep for the phrase) but **assert the wrong
answer** while no registry entry covers them, so they pass. Check such a header
against the registry before trusting a green run: fix rischint and tests written
that way turn red, and you may revert a correct fix.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
**A test your change turns red may itself be wrong.** Read what it asserts
before reworking code, and ask whether the new result is only another form of
the same thing -- expanded against factored, or a reordering.
`ratsimp(new - old)` = 0 settles that for rational expressions; a nonzero
difference proves nothing, and `is(equal(a,b))` answers `unknown`, not `false`
(`trigreduce` sees `sin(2*x) = 2*sin(x)*cos(x)`, `ratsimp` and `trigsimp` do
not). When they agree, re-baseline the test -- its comment says why the old
value was chosen -- rather than contorting code to match it.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 5. Tests > Writing tests
text:
**Not in the suite**: `tests/testbench_*_manual.wxm` (visual, needs a human),
`tests/rtest_tex.mac` (despite the name -- it is a LaTeX *document generator*,
not input/expected pairs, and is in neither registry; its own header says to
run it with `batch`) and `share/contrib/diffequations/tests/` (own harness).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 7. Repository layout
text:
`src/` is the core (sec. 8), `share/` the add-ons loaded with `load(pkg)`.
`doc/implementation/` holds internals notes worth reading. `archive/` is retired
code: never cite or modify.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 7. Repository layout
text:
`share/readme-share.txt` sets the contract: `src/` stable, avoid incompatible
changes; `share/` may be unmaintained, core must never depend on it, and two
packages may conflict; `share/contrib/` is evaluated for neither.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 8. Map of `src/`
text:
**`src/maxima.system` is the authoritative map**: every file in build order.
Landmarks: `simp` (power entry points `simpexpt`, `%itopot`, `simplexpon`),
`nparse` (reader), `mlisp` (`meval`), `suprv1` (`meval*`), `displa`,
`rat3a`-`rat3e`/`ratmac` (CRE), `sin`/`risch`, `defint`, `limit`,
`solve`/`algsys`, `db`/`compar` (assumptions), `mload` (testsuite driver),
`float` (bigfloats). `src/numerical/slatec/*.lisp` is f2cl-translated Fortran
(SLATEC *and* QUADPACK) apart from the hand-written `quadpack.lisp` glue; the
Fortran sits in `slatec/fortran/`, the recipe in `slatec/slatec.system` -- never
hand-edit the generated Lisp, fix callers or regenerate.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 8. Map of `src/`
text:
Search before writing new algebra -- `sturm`, `isolat`, `root-bound`, `reval`,
`ivar` (`polyrz.lisp`); `pgcdexpon`, `univar`, `ptimeschk`, `pquotientchk-safe`
(`rat3c.lisp`); `ratreduce` (`rat3b.lisp`, `(rzero)` = zero numerator); `psqfr`
(`rat3d.lisp`).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
`(caar expr)` operator; `(cdr expr)` args. `simp` = already simplified, never
fabricate it. `array` = subscripted. Operators: `mplus`, `mtimes`, `mexpt`,
`mlist`, `mequal`, `mnctimes`, `mqapply`, `mrat`, `mdefine`, `mprog`, ...
Setting the global `simp:false` switches the simplifier off and many internal
routines then misbehave (`doc/info/Simplification.texi` says so), so a failure
under it is not a bug to chase.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
**Use `alike1`, not `equal`.** `alike1` (`src/simp-utils.lisp`) is structural
equality, **ignoring every header flag except `array`** (`memqarr`); `equal`
gives silent false negatives on flag variants. `mrat`, `mpois` and `bigfloat`
headers take special branches -- a bigfloat's precision and decimal flag *are*
compared. `(alike1 '((f) $x) '((f simp) $x))` -> T;
`(alike1 '((f array) $x) '((f) $x))` -> NIL. `like` = `alike1` + `specrepcheck`
both sides, for CRE/Poisson; `assol` (`src/mutils.lisp`) = alist lookup by
`alike1`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
**Headers and plists are shared -- never mutate them.** The header cons in
`(cons '(mplus simp) args)` is a compile-time literal, so `nconc`/`rplacd` on
one car corrupts unrelated expressions. Plists share too (`src/nalgfa.lisp`:
`(setf (symbol-plist newvar) (symbol-plist var))`), so a per-symbol cache must
verify the symbol itself, not just a generation stamp.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
**Booleans**: Maxima's `true`/`false` are exactly Lisp `T`/`NIL`, so a Lisp
predicate's `nil` comes back as `false`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
**Numbers.** `mnump` (`src/mutils.lisp`) covers Lisp numbers, `((rat) a b)`
**and** bigfloats; `ratnump` matches only `((rat) a b)`, not plain integers. An
`mnump` guard then `$float` is a **silent precision bug** (bigfloat -> double):
the `$scaled_bessel_i*` functions in `src/bessel.lisp`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
**CL rationals/complex are not Maxima's.** Maxima uses `((rat) a b)` (not CL
`1/2`) and `a+b*%i` over `$%i` (not `#C(a b)`). A raw CL object embeds silently
and even displays right, then fails later: `(ratnump 1/2)` -> NIL,
`float(x + #C(1 2))` -> `#C(1 2) is not of type REAL`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
**Bigfloats**: `((bigfloat simp <prec>) <mantissa> <exp>)` -- mantissa is a
**scaled binary integer**, not the digits; precision lives in the header. Test
`$bfloatp` (`src/simp-utils.lisp`, `:inline-impl t`) or `bigfloatp`
(`src/float.lisp`), which *returns* the value re-rounded to the current `fpprec`
-- use what it returns, not the argument. Raw Lisp arithmetic on a bigfloat is a
type error; house guard `(if ($bfloatp b) (minusp (cadr b)) (minusp b))`. Live
crash: `beta_incomplete_regularized` (`src/gamma.lisp`) applies `<=` to a
possible bigfloat (grep `"does not work for bigfloats"`). Two leaks: in
`(in-package #:bigfloat)` **unary `sqrt` skips contagion** -- no bigfloat
operand -> `cl:sqrt`, machine precision (rational -> *single* float); and
`integer-representation-p` (`src/numerical-utils.lisp`) is `-p`-named but
**returns the converted Lisp integer** (or nil) -- callers ignoring it keep the
original bigfloat.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
**CRE**: `((mrat simp varlist genvar) numerator . denominator)`, e.g.
`($rat '((mplus) 1 ((mexpt) $x 2)))` ->
`((MRAT SIMP ($X) (#:G544)) (#:G544 2 1 0 1) . 1)` -- the gensym counter varies
per session; only the shape is stable. Sparse polynomial lists
`(var exp coef exp coef ...)`, **descending** powers; multivariate nest, main
variable by `pointergp`. Commentary atop **`src/ratmac.lisp`** explains `rat3*`.
Back with `ratdisrep`; `specrepcheck` handles CRE and Poisson.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 9. Internal representation
text:
**Symbol prefixes**: `$name` is Maxima-level and user-visible (`$sin`,
`$fpprec`); `%name` is the **noun** form (`%sin`, `%integrate`); `mname` is a
built-in operator (`mplus`, `mexpt`); `*name*` is a Lisp-only special
(`*expandp*`); a plain name is an internal helper with no Maxima-level name
(`simplifya`, `alike1`), reachable only as `?simplifya`. Verb/noun duality is
wired by `(get '$sin 'alias)` -> `%SIN`, `(get '%sin 'reversealias)` -> `$SIN`,
`(get '%sin 'operators)` -> `SIMP-%SIN` (the simplifier).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**`defmfun`** (`src/defmfun-check.lisp`) for anything user-callable -- the
overwhelming default; a handful of bare `(defun $...)` survive as legacy. `$`
names get an arg-count wrapper, `FOO-IMPL` (the body), and
`arg-list`/`impl-name`/`translated` properties; hence `sin(1,2)` ->
`sin(y): expected exactly 1 arguments but got 2: [1, 2]`. Options
`:properties ((evfun t))`, `:deprecated-p $bar`, `:inline-impl t`, as in
`(defmfun ($foo :properties ((evfun t))) ...)`. Plain `defun`: internal helpers.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**`defmvar`** (`src/globals.lisp`) for option variables; bare `(defvar $...)` is
legacy. Its docstring becomes the Lisp `defvar` docstring and reaches no user --
user-visible text lives in `doc/info/` (sec. 14). `fixnum`/`string`/`flonum`
**validate nothing** (deprecation warning only): a `fixnum` variable accepts a
string. **`boolean` is not ignored** -- its clause installs an `assign`
restricting values to `t`/`nil`: `ifactor_verbose:"hello";` gives ``assignment:
cannot assign `hello' to `ifactor_verbose': ...``. Real validation:
`:setting-predicate`, `:setting-list`, `:setter-method`,
`:properties ((assign ...))` -- compile-time error combining an `assign`
property with `:setting-predicate`/`:setting-list`, or `boolean` with any of
those three. A `Deprecated defmvar option` warning fires at **macroexpansion**:
during `make` for `src/`, but on every `load` of a share `.lisp` shipped as
source (`load(simplex)`); suppress with `*warn-deprecated-defmvar-options*` =
nil. Multi-file variables go in **`src/globals.lisp`**; compilers coalesce equal
constant lists and Maxima mutates some -- use fresh conses.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**Declare specials before you bind them.** A `let` on a special `defvar`'d
*later* in the same file binds **lexically** and does nothing. SBCL warns only
for `*foo*`-shaped names; most Maxima specials are earmuff-free (`varlist`,
`genvar`, `errcatch`, `$errormsg`), so it compiles silently.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**`def-simplifier`** (body e.g.
`(cond ((float-numerical-eval-p x y) ...) (t (give-up)))`) sets
noun/verb/alias/reversealias + `operators` and binds local `give-up`; `form`,
`%%simpflag` visible in body. Subscripted:
`(def-simplifier (li :subfun-arglist (s)) (x) ...)` -> `specsimp`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**`defmspec`** (`src/maxmac.lisp`) for args that must **not** be evaluated
(`$declare`, `$assume`, `$buildq`, ...). Body gets raw forms, `meval`s
selectively.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**Building expressions** -- never hand-cons (`src/mopers.lisp`,
`src/opers.lisp`): `add`, `mul`, `div`, `power`, `inv`, `neg`, `sub`;
`take '(%sin) x` / `ftake '%sin x` apply+simplify; `fapply`, `mfuncall`; starred
forms (`add*`, `take*`, ...) when args are **not yet simplified**, unstarred
assume they are; `simplifya` (`simplify` = `(simplifya x nil)`), `resimplify`,
`meval`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**Errors**: `(merror (intl:gettext "foo: argument must be a list; found ~M") x)`
-- nearly every `merror` in `src/` wraps its format string in `intl:gettext`; do
the same (catalogs in `locale/`). `~M` and kin are **`mformat` directives**, not
CL `format`, and work only inside `merror`, `mtell`, `mformat` and friends: `~M`
= 2-D display (`displaf`), `~:M` = 1-D/`grind` form (`mstring`), `~@M` =
operator name (the `op` property). Output/warnings: `mtell`/`$print`, not
`format t`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**No `:test #'eq` on symbols.** `member`'s default `eql` is already `eq` for
symbols, so the keyword adds nothing when the item is a literal symbol or the
list a literal list of symbols -- and it silently narrows the test if a float or
bignum ever joins the list.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**Naming.** Maxima: `write_long_names_like_this`, not camelCase or
runtogetherwords. Lisp: lowercase, hyphenated, `*earmuffs*` for specials; `$` is
Maxima's namespace -- never add a `$` symbol not meant to be user-visible.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**Edit minimally.** Make the smallest change that fixes the problem, matching
the surrounding style even where it is poor: do not reindent, rewrap, rename or
refactor code you are not fixing. A tight diff is reviewable and cherry-picks
cleanly between release branches (sec. 15); a tidied one buries the fix and
collides with everyone else. **Tabs are load-bearing** -- nearly every top-level
`src/*.lisp` contains literal tabs (Emacs 8-column convention), so an editor
that normalizes whitespace turns a 3-line fix into a sprawling one. Preserve
them where they are, but indent a function you write from scratch with spaces.
`#+`/`#-` per-Lisp workarounds: add narrowly, comment why. `#+nil`/`#+broken`
disable code in place -- grep hits inside aren't live.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 10. Code conventions
text:
**Comments.** Describe what the code does now. Never narrate history ("this used
to...", "I changed...") -- that is the commit message's job. Existing comments
do it anyway, often in the first person: read them as archaeology, not spec.
Write Lisp names in ALL-UPPERCASE (`SIMPLIFYA`, `MEVAL`) and Maxima names
exactly as they are (`display2d`, `%sin`) -- Maxima is case-sensitive, the Lisp
reader upcases; same convention in commit messages. **Wrap at 80 columns**, code
and comments alike, unless the surrounding code already runs wider or nesting
makes it infeasible -- nearly all `src/*.lisp` lines already fit (tabs at 8).

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 11. Subsystem notes
text:
**Sign** (`src/compar.lisp`, `src/db.lisp`) -- `sign`/`minus`/`odds`/`evens` are
one answer in four specials, set together; `$asksign`/`$sign` rebind those four
plus `factored` (`signfactor`'s re-entry guard), so a handler setting only
`sign` leaks the others. `sign-mtimes` does `nconc odds o` -- pass fresh conses.
`signsum` stops at `$pnz`. The fact DB keys on the `data` property (`dinternp`
returns the symbol for atoms; `dcomp` treats no-node and empty-node alike as
`$pnz`; `(get sym 'data)` = does the DB know anything). `$assume_pos` upgrades
unknown *mapatoms* only -- `f(y)` needs `$assume_pos_pred`. `*local-signs*`
holds answers asked *of the user*, not computed signs. Asking goes via
`$asksign` (`asksign01`, `ensure-sign`, ...); `radmabs` (`src/simp.lisp`) asks
when `(and limitp (free e '$%i))`, from `simpexpt`. `meval*` (`src/suprv1.lisp`)
-> `with-top-level-environment` -> `clearsign`: asksign facts die between inputs
while `assume`s survive, and they are stored *reduced* --
`(asksign(asin(x)), facts())` in one input gives `x > 0`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 11. Subsystem notes
text:
**Limits** (`src/limit.lisp`) -- vocabulary `inf`, `minf`, `infinity`, `ind`,
`und`, `zeroa`, `zerob` (`extended-real-p`); no directed infinity. `extra-simp`
is top-down, so match a subexpression shape only after simplifying it. Guard
`$csign` re-entry (`$csign -> sign -> $limit -> extra-simp -> $csign`). `getexp`
calls `ask-integer` on exponents free of the limit variable, so rewriting
`%e^(3*log(x)/sigma^2)` to `x^(3/sigma^2)` asks *"Is 3/sigma^2 an integer?"* and
hangs batches. `var`/`val` are special; `var` is pre-shifted to zero and
uninterned, so `boundp` misses a stale `var`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 11. Subsystem notes
text:
**Rpart/integrator** (`src/rpart.lisp`, `src/risch.lisp`) -- `absarg` is correct
only mod `2*%pi`; only `$carg` and `risplit`'s `%log` may reduce, because
`risplit-expt` needs it unreduced. Canary `integrate(sqrt(1-cos(t)),t,0,2*%pi)`
-> `2^(5/2)` (`tests/rtestint.mac`); `-2^(5/2)` means you over-reduced.
`domain:real`+`radexpand:true` gives `(-8)^(1/3)` = `-2`, but `gamma_incomplete`
is principal-branch -- producer and consumer must agree, and integer exponents
keep distributing. `atan2(y,0)` is legitimate; test the zero-second-arg case.
`implicit-real` (bound by `rischint`, read by `absarg1`) answers signs
positively so the integrator never interrogates the user: it looks dead but
disabling it hangs `rtest16`, and any unattended batch. `rischp`
(`src/globals.lisp`) is the same pattern. `sdiffgrad` (`src/comm.lisp`) calls a
functional `defgrad` derivative with the actual args, then `$psubstitute`s
placeholders -> actuals, so an already-substituted lambda result is substituted
twice and captures colliding user symbols -- return `#$...$` templates in
placeholder names.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 12. Do not trust the comments
text:
`TODO`/`FIXME`/`XXX`/`HACK` markers are scattered through `src/` (grep
case-insensitively; most lowercase hits are prose, not markers), and the code
under them has moved on. Comments here are decades old and go stale in both

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 13. Adding or removing files
text:
**`src/`** -- `src/maxima.system` (`:module`) and `src/maxima.asd`, which names
every file. `src/Makefile.am` needs no edit: it globs `$(srcdir)/*.lisp` plus

Never hand-edit `src/*-depends.mk`.

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 13. Adding or removing files
text:
A module marked `:dependencies-complete t` tells `defsystem` that its declared
`:depends-on` edges are the whole truth, so it stops adding its own "anything
compiled after a changed file may have been compiled against it" edges. The
option is Maxima's addition to MK:DEFSYSTEM, so every use in `maxima.system` is
written `#+mk-deps-complete :dependencies-complete #+mk-deps-complete t` --
grep for `:dependencies-complete`, not for the whole `t`-terminated phrase. An
undeclared edge then leaves a stale fasl on the next incremental build, and no
test can see it -- the answers stay right until someone changes the file that
was never rebuilt. Three things create such an edge: a macro, an inline
function or source transform, and -- the one the module comments miss -- a
call to a `defmfun`, since `defmfun` defines a compiler-macro rewriting
`($foo ...)` to `(FOO-IMPL ...)` at the call site, making an ordinary
Maxima-level call a *compile-time* dependency. A plain `defun` call or a read
of a special is late-bound and creates none. `make check` verifies this under
SBCL (sec. 5).

`rtest_my_package.mac` -> `$share_testsuite_files`; `doc/info/my_package.texi`
-> `doc/info/Makefile.am` + `doc/info/include-maxima.texi.in`, starting from

head: CLAUDE.md -- Maxima Computer Algebra System > 15. Project workflow
text:
**Changing SBCL version requires `make clean`.** `src/binary-sbcl/` is not
version-scoped and fasls lock to the exact implementation version string --
`sb-fasl:+fasl-file-version+` can be identical across releases, so it is no
guide. `defsystem` recompiles by timestamp, never by fasl version, so stale
fasls load and the build dies with
`is a fasl file compiled with SBCL ..., and can't be loaded into SBCL ...`.
`clean-sbcl` (`src/Makefile.am`) `rm -rf`s the `binary-sbcl` directories. Re-run
`./configure` only if the Lisp's *name* changes: `src/maxima.in` execs
`"@SBCL_NAME@"` (default `sbcl`) with `--core`, so a PATH swap needs none,
whereas `--with-sbcl=<path>` bakes the path in.
