head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text:
Enunciate is a build-time tool for Java Web service projects (JAX-RS, JAX-WS, Spring Web).
It runs as a Java annotation processor over a project's source code and generates artifacts such as:

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text: * HTML API documentation (scraped from Javadoc)

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text: * Client-side libraries (Java, C#, Objective-C, Ruby, PHP, JavaScript, GWT, etc.)

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text: * Interface definition documents (WSDL, WADL, XML Schema, Swagger/OpenAPI)

head: CLAUDE.md > What this project is
text:
It does not affect the runtime behavior of the service being documented — it only inspects source and generates
artifacts at build time. Full project docs (user guide, module reference, FAQ) live in the GitHub wiki
(`stoicflame/enunciate.wiki.git` — see `LOCAL_CONTEXT.md` for the local clone path if you keep one); consult it
for user-facing configuration/behavior questions rather than guessing, since the in-repo README is minimal and
can lag behind the wiki.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build
text: Requires JDK 17 (enforced by `maven-enforcer-plugin`) and Maven 3.8.1+.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build
text:
By default, tests that exercise Enunciate's generated client-side code (compiling/running the generated C, C#,
Objective-C, Ruby, PHP, JS client libraries) are skipped, with an `echo-maven-plugin` reminder printed during the
build. To run the full suite you need `libxml2-dev`, `mono-devel`, `gnustep`/`gnustep-devel`, `ruby`, `nodejs`,
`php` installed (see README for the Ubuntu package list), then:

head: CLAUDE.md > Build
text:
The `deploy` and `release` lifecycle phases are gated by an enforcer rule that requires `enunciate-full-tests`
to have been run — don't try to deploy/release without it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Release process
text:
There is no CI/CD for this repo — releasing is a manual, local process. The authoritative, step-by-step
procedure (version bump mechanics, required Maven profiles/commands, PGP/OSSRH setup, wiki and schema updates,
and the sibling repos that also need touching) is documented in `release-procedure.md` at the repo root. If asked
to help with a release, follow that file rather than improvising, and if the process changes, update it (it's
meant to stay both human-readable and detailed enough to act on).

head: CLAUDE.md > Release process
text:
Each released minor version has a versioned copy of the Enunciate config XSD checked in at
`top/src/main/resources/META-INF/enunciate-<version>.xsd`. This isn't purely a release-time artifact: whenever a
change is made during ongoing development that affects the Enunciate config schema (e.g. a new/changed config
element or attribute in one of the modules), make sure the XSD for the *next* minor version (the current
`-SNAPSHOT` version, without the `-SNAPSHOT` suffix) exists — creating it (typically by copying the most recent
prior version's file) if it doesn't yet — and update it to reflect the change. That way the file is already
current by the time `release-procedure.md` step 12 publishes it. If a minor version is about to be released and
no config-affecting changes were made during that cycle, the XSD still needs to exist for that version — just
copy the previous version's file over verbatim (no diff needed beyond the filename).

head: CLAUDE.md > Release process
text: Build a single module (and anything it depends on):

head: CLAUDE.md > Release process
text:
Unit test coverage in most modules is thin — the primary correctness signal for module behavior comes from the
`examples/` integration projects (see below), not unit tests.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
This is a Maven multi-module reactor (see root `pom.xml` for the full module list). The dependency flow is
roughly bottom-up:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
1. **`core-annotations`** — the annotations Enunciate itself exposes to annotate a target API (no dependency on
   `core`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
2. **`javac-support`** — helpers for working with the `com.sun.source`/Javac compiler API, since Enunciate's
   engine is implemented as an annotation processor that walks the AST/mirror model of the target project's
   source rather than its compiled bytecode (needed to recover Javadoc, parameter names, etc.).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
3. **`core`** — the engine: `com.webcohesion.enunciate.Enunciate` is the programmatic entry point;
   `EnunciateAnnotationProcessor` drives the annotation-processing pass; `EnunciateContext` holds the resulting
   API model. Also defines the module SPI (`com.webcohesion.enunciate.module.EnunciateModule`) and the
   `com.webcohesion.enunciate.api` package, which is the in-memory, framework-agnostic model of "the API"
   (resources, data types, etc.) that generating modules read from.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
4. **`rt-util`** — small runtime utility classes shared by *generated* client code (not used by the engine
   itself).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
5. **Framework/facet modules** — `jaxb`, `jaxrs`, `jaxws`, `jackson`, `spring-web`, `lombok`: each is an
   `EnunciateModule` implementation that knows how to interpret one API framework's annotations/conventions and
   contribute to the shared API model in `core`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
6. **Generating modules** — `idl` (WSDL/WADL/XSD), `swagger` (OpenAPI), `docs` (HTML docs from Freemarker
   templates), and the various `*-xml-client`/`*-json-client`/`javascript-client`/`gwt-json-overlay` modules:
   each reads the API model built by the facet modules and emits one kind of artifact.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
7. **Invocation front-ends** — `maven-plugin` (all modules on the classpath by default) and
   `slim-maven-plugin` (no modules enabled by default; you add only what you need) wrap the `core` engine as
   Maven plugins. `top` is just a POM that pulls in the default set of modules for non-Maven (e.g. Ant,
   programmatic) use. `EnunciateTask` (in `core`) is the Ant entry point.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module layering
text:
8. **`examples`** — sample Web service projects (`full-api-edge-cases`, `jackson2-api`,
   `jackson2-api-lombok`, `spring-petclinic`) that apply the Enunciate Maven plugin during their own build and
   assert on the generated output. These act as the project's integration/regression test suite and are also
   the reference for "how does a consumer actually configure this module."

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The module SPI
text:
Everything that generates an artifact is an `EnunciateModule` (`core/.../module/EnunciateModule.java`),
discovered via `java.util.ServiceLoader` (`META-INF/services/com.webcohesion.enunciate.module.EnunciateModule`).
Most modules extend `BasicEnunicateModule` or `BasicGeneratingModule` rather than implementing the interface
directly. Key extension points a module can opt into:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The module SPI
text:
* `DependencySpec` / `DependingModuleAwareModule` — declare/consume ordering dependencies between modules (e.g.
  `jaxrs` must run before `docs`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The module SPI
text:
* `ApiRegistryProviderModule` / `ApiRegistryAwareModule` — contribute to or read from the shared
  `AggregatedApiRegistry` (the cross-module API model).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The module SPI
text: * `ProjectExtensionModule` — mark generated output to be attached back into the consuming Maven project.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The module SPI
text:
* `TypeDetectingModule`, `MediaTypeDefinitionModule`, `WebInfAwareModule`, `ContextModifyingModule` — narrower
  callbacks used by facet/generating modules as needed.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The module SPI
text:
Third-party/custom modules follow the same SPI (see the wiki's Custom Modules page) and are added to the
classpath of whichever front-end (Maven/Ant/programmatic) is invoking Enunciate.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Freemarker
text:
Nearly every generating module (`docs`, `idl`, `swagger`, and each `*-client`/`gwt-json-overlay` module) produces
its artifacts by running a Freemarker template against a model built from the `core` API model
(`com.webcohesion.enunciate.api`). Template files use the `.fmt` extension (not the more common `.ftl`) and live
under each module's `src/main/resources/.../<module-package>/` next to the module class that drives them
(e.g. `docs/.../docs.fmt`, `swagger/.../openapi.fmt`, `java-xml-client/.../client-*.fmt`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Freemarker
text:
Enunciate deliberately uses Freemarker's **square-bracket tag syntax** (`[#if]`, `[#list]`, `[@myDirective/]`, ...)
instead of the default angle-bracket syntax. Since Enunciate templates are themselves generating XML and HTML,
angle-bracket Freemarker tags (`<#if>`, `<#list>`) are easy to confuse with the literal markup being emitted;
square brackets stay visually distinct from the output. This is opted into per-file, not globally configured: every
`.fmt` template starts with a `[#ftl]` header, which under Freemarker's tag-syntax auto-detection makes that whole
file parse with square-bracket tags. When adding a new template, always start it with `[#ftl]` and use square
brackets throughout.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Freemarker
text:
Beyond the template files, most generating modules extend Freemarker with custom directives and methods (in
`com.webcohesion.enunciate.util.freemarker` for the shared/core ones, and in a `util` or top-level package per
client module for module-specific ones) rather than relying on stock Freemarker built-ins:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Freemarker
text:
* `FileDirective` (core) — a `TemplateDirectiveModel` bound to `[@file name=...] ... [/@file]` in templates,
  used to split one template's output across multiple generated source files (e.g. one `.java`/`.cs`/`.rb` file
  per type).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Freemarker
text:
* `ClientPackageForMethod` / namespace-equivalents — map an API package to the target language's
  package/namespace/module naming convention.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Freemarker
text:
* `AnnotationValueMethod`, `SimpleNameWithParamsMethod`, `IsFacetExcludedMethod` (core) — shared helpers exposed
  to all templates for reading annotation values, computing simple/parameterized type names, and honoring facet
  include/exclude filtering, respectively.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Freemarker
text:
* Module-specific `TemplateMethodModelEx` implementations (31+ across the codebase) for things like C
  identifier/name mangling (`c-xml-client`), Swagger definition/operation IDs and JSON examples (`swagger`), QName
  computation for WSDL/XSD (`idl`, `csharp-xml-client`), and JAXB namespace/prefix resolution (`jaxb`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Freemarker
text:
These are wired into the Freemarker data model by hand in each module's `processTemplate`/model-building code
(typically `model.put("methodName", new SomeMethod(...))`), not auto-discovered — so when a template needs a new
piece of logic, the pattern is: add a `TemplateMethodModelEx`/`TemplateDirectiveModel` class near the module that
needs it (or in `core/.../util/freemarker` if it's broadly reusable), `model.put(...)` it before processing the
template, then reference it by that name from the `.fmt` file.

head: Claude Code Configuration
text:
> **Note:** Every command you need — building, running, testing, linting,
> formatting — is defined as a recipe in the project `justfile`. Run

head: Claude Code Configuration > Running Anki

head: Claude Code Configuration > Running Anki
text:
This builds pylib and qt, then launches Anki with debugging enabled. Web
views are served at http://localhost:40000/_anki/pages/ (e.g.,
deckconfig.html). Use `just run-optimized` for a release-optimized build.
For live-reloading during web development, run `just web-watch` in a
separate terminal — it monitors ts/, sass/, and qt/aqt/data/web/ and
auto-rebuilds on changes (`just rebuild-web` triggers a one-off rebuild).

head: Claude Code Configuration > Building/checking
text:
`just check` will format the code and run the main build & checks.
Please do this as a final step before marking a task as completed.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Building/checking
text: Run `just` (or `just --list`) to see all available commands.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Quick iteration
text: During development, you can build/check subsections of our code:

head: Claude Code Configuration > Quick iteration
text: - Python: `just lint` (runs mypy/ruff), and if wheel-related, `just wheels`

head: Claude Code Configuration > Quick iteration
text: - TypeScript/Svelte: `just lint` (includes check:svelte and check:typescript)

head: Claude Code Configuration > Quick iteration
text:
Language-specific tests are also available: `just test-rust`, `just test-py`,
`just test-ts`. Use `just fmt` / `just fix-fmt` for formatting and
`just fix-lint` to auto-fix lint issues.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Quick iteration
text:
TypeScript/Svelte browser e2e tests live in `ts/tests/e2e/` and run with
`just test-e2e`. The harness launches a temporary Anki instance and drives
mediasrv pages with Playwright's Chromium.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Quick iteration
text:
Be mindful that some changes (such as modifications to .proto files) may
need a full build with `just check` first.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Testing guidance
text:
Before adding or changing unit or component tests, read and follow the
[Writing Unit Tests for Anki](docs-site/developers/unit-testing.mdx).

head: Claude Code Configuration > Build tooling
text:
`just` recipes wrap our build system (implemented in build/), which takes
care of downloading required deps and invoking our build steps. See the
project `justfile` for the full set of recipes.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Translations
text:
ftl/ contains our Fluent translation files. We have scripts in rslib/i18n
to auto-generate an API for Rust, TypeScript and Python so that our code can
access the translations in a type-safe manner. Changes should be made to
ftl/core or ftl/qt. Except for features specific to our Qt interface, prefer
the core module. When adding new strings, confirm the appropriate ftl file
first, and try to match the existing style.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Protobuf and IPC
text:
Our build scripts use the .proto files to define our Rust library's
non-Rust API. pylib/rsbridge exposes that API, and \_backend.py exposes
snake_case methods for each protobuf RPC that call into the API.
Similar tooling creates a @generated/backend TypeScript module for
communicating with the Rust backend (which happens over POST requests).

head: Claude Code Configuration > Fixing errors
text:
When dealing with build errors or failing tests, invoke 'check' or one
of the quick iteration commands regularly. This helps verify your changes
are correct. To locate other instances of a problem, run the check again -
don't attempt to grep the codebase.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Ignores
text:
The files in out/ are auto-generated. Mostly you should ignore that folder,
though you may sometimes find it useful to view out/{pylib/anki,qt/\_aqt,ts/lib/generated} when dealing with cross-language communication or our other generated sourcecode.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Installer
text:
The code for our Briefcase-based installer is in qt/installer, with
separate templates for each platform (mac-template/, linux-template/,
windows-template/).

head: Claude Code Configuration > Rust dependencies
text: Prefer adding to the root workspace, and using dep.workspace = true in the individual Rust project.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Rust utilities
text:
rslib/{process,io} contain some helpers for file and process operations,
which provide better error messages/context and some ergonomics. Use them
when possible.

head: Claude Code Configuration > Rust error handling
text:
in rslib, use error/mod.rs's AnkiError/Result and snafu. In our other Rust modules, prefer anyhow + additional context where appropriate. Unwrapping
in build scripts/tests is fine.

**解决方案**：

```python
# processor.py:133-155（修复代码）
# ASR 转写器
asr_config = self.podcast_config.get("ASR", self.podcast_config.get("asr", {}))

# 多级配置查找（兼容大小写）
backend = asr_config.get("BACKEND", asr_config.get("backend", "assemblyai"))

# 环境变量后备
if not assemblyai_api_key:
    import os
    assemblyai_api_key = os.environ.get("ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY", "")

self.transcriber = ASRTranscriber(
    backend=backend,
    api_base=asr_config.get("API_BASE", asr_config.get("api_base", "")),
    api_key=asr_config.get("API_KEY", asr_config.get("api_key", "")),
    model=asr_config.get("MODEL", asr_config.get("model", "")),
    language=asr_config.get("LANGUAGE", asr_config.get("language", "zh")),
    assemblyai_api_key=assemblyai_api_key,
    speaker_labels=speaker_labels,
)
```

```python
# 修改后（processor.py:429-457）
def _increment_failure_count(self, episode_id: int, error_message: str = ""):
    conn = self._get_connection()
    # ✅ 检查当前状态
    cursor = conn.execute("SELECT status, failure_count FROM podcast_episodes WHERE id = ?", (episode_id,))
    row = cursor.fetchone()
    if not row:
        return

    current_status, current_failures = row

    if current_status != 'failed':
        # 只有不在失败状态时才计数
        conn.execute("""
            UPDATE podcast_episodes
            SET failure_count = COALESCE(failure_count, 0) + 1,
                last_error_time = ?,
                error_message = ?,
                status = 'failed'
            WHERE id = ?
        """, (datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), error_message, episode_id))
        print(f"[Podcast] ⚠️  节目 ID {episode_id} 失败计数: {current_failures + 1}")
    else:
        # 只更新错误信息，不增加计数
        conn.execute("""
            UPDATE podcast_episodes
            SET last_error_time = ?,
                error_message = ?
            WHERE id = ?
        """, (datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), error_message, episode_id))
        print(f"[Podcast] ⚠️  节目 ID {episode_id} 已在失败状态，仅更新错误信息")
```

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build & Run Commands
text: There are no tests in this project.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: This is a Go CLI tool built with [cobra](https://github.com/spf13/cobra) for interacting with the SuprSend notification infrastructure API. It also serves as an MCP server for AI tool integrations.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **`cmd/suprsend/main.go`** — Entrypoint, calls `commands.Execute()`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **`internal/commands/root.go`** — Root cobra command. Registers all subcommands and handles service token resolution (env > flag > config file profile)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **`internal/commands/`** — Each resource type (workflow, event, schema, category, translation, profiles) is a subpackage with its own cobra subcommands (list, pull, push, commit)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **`mgmnt/`** — API client layer (`SS_MgmntClient`). Makes HTTP calls to SuprSend management API. Each resource type has its own file (workflow.go, event.go, schema.go, etc.)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **`internal/tools/`** — MCP tool definitions. Each file registers tools via `RegisterTool()` into a global registry. The MCP server (`startMcpServer.go`) selects and serves these tools

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **`internal/config/`** — Global config singleton (`config.Cfg`) using viper. Config file is `$HOME/.suprsend.yaml`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **`internal/utils/`** — SDK singleton (`SDKInstance`), output formatting, embedded binaries

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Command Pattern
text: Each resource follows a consistent pattern:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Command Pattern
text: - `helpers.go` — Shared file I/O functions (read/write JSON files)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Command Pattern
text: - `<resource>.go` — Parent cobra command

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Command Pattern
text: - `<resource>_get.go`, `<resource>_list.go`, `<resource>_pull.go`, `<resource>_push.go`, `<resource>_commit.go` — CRUD subcommands

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Authentication
text: Service token resolution priority: `SUPRSEND_SERVICE_TOKEN` env var > `--service-token` flag > active profile in config file. Profiles are managed via `suprsend profile` subcommands and stored in a YAML config file.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: Use `clierr` (`internal/clierr/clierr.go`) for all user-facing errors — never `fmt.Errorf` or `errors.New` at command boundaries.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: - `clierr.New(message, code)` — create a new structured error

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: - `clierr.Wrap(err, code, hint)` — promote a plain error with a code and hint

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: - Codes are constants in `clierr` (e.g. `CodeConfigInvalid`, `CodeAuthMissingToken`, `CodeFileParseFailed`). Pick the closest match; use `CodeUnknown` as a last resort.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: - `clierr` errors carry a numeric exit code (auth=3, validation=2, not-found=4, etc.) and render correctly in both plain-text and `--output json` modes.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Special Features
text: - **`sync` command** — Pulls all assets from one workspace and pushes to another, with an optional local directory as intermediate storage

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Special Features
text: - **`generate-types` command** — Fetches JSON schemas from API and generates typed code (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, Kotlin, Swift, Dart) using an embedded Deno binary (`type-morph/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Special Features
text:
- **MCP server** — `start-mcp-server` command serves tools over stdio/SSE/HTTP transports using `mcp-go`. Tools are dynamically registered for events and workflows.
  - **Default tool surface differs by entry point.** Terminal users get `--workflows=none --events=none` (minimal — only the static admin tools) so scripted invocations stay predictable. Registry-installed servers (Glama, MCP Registry) get `--workflows=all` injected via `server.json`'s `packageArguments`, so installing through a registry exposes the full trigger surface out of the box.
  - **Selector syntax**: `--workflows` accepts `all`, `none`, comma-separated slugs, or `tag:<tag>` entries (e.g. `tag:onboarding,tag:transactional`). Mixed forms work: `welcome,tag:transactional`. Tag matching is client-side — the management API does not currently support `?tags=` filtering, so all workflows are fetched and filtered in memory.
  - **Cold start**: payload-schema fetches for dynamic tools run in parallel (bounded to 10 concurrent requests). A schema fetch failure for one workflow/event no longer aborts startup — it logs and skips that single tool, leaving the rest registered.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Special Features
text: - **Gemini CLI extension** — Built as a separate binary via goreleaser for Google Gemini CLI integration

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release
text: Uses goreleaser (`.goreleaser.yaml`). Builds include macOS notarization and Homebrew cask publishing to `suprsend/homebrew-tap`. The `make build` step compiles the `type-morph` Deno binary that gets embedded into the Go binary.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release
text: After goreleaser, the release workflow also publishes to npm via `scripts/publish-npm.sh`. This ships seven packages at the same version: the unscoped root `suprsend` (a Node shim) and six platform packages `@suprsend/cli-<os>-<arch>` (darwin/linux/win32 × x64/arm64), each carrying the matching goreleaser binary. Package sources live under `npm/`. Users run `npx suprsend` or `npm i -g suprsend`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release
text: After npm publish, the workflow publishes the MCP server metadata to the [MCP Registry](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/registry) via `mcp-publisher`. The manifest is `server.json` at the repo root and references the `suprsend` npm package; ownership is verified by the `mcpName: io.github.suprsend/cli` field in `npm/suprsend/package.json` (which must match `server.json#name`). Authentication is via GitHub OIDC — no extra secrets needed. The MCP host launches the server as `npx -y suprsend start-mcp-server` (`packageArguments` in `server.json`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release > Pre-release tags (beta / rc / alpha / canary)
text: Tags with a SemVer pre-release suffix (`0.3.0-beta.1`, `0.3.0-rc.2`, `1.0.0-alpha`, etc.) flow through the same release pipeline but each downstream channel branches:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release > Pre-release tags (beta / rc / alpha / canary)
text: - **GitHub release** — `release.prerelease: auto` in `.goreleaser.yaml` auto-detects the suffix and marks the release as a pre-release.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release > Pre-release tags (beta / rc / alpha / canary)
text: - **npm** — `scripts/publish-npm.sh` derives the dist-tag from the suffix (`-beta.1` → `beta`, `-rc.2` → `rc`, `-canary.5` → `canary`) and publishes all seven packages under that dist-tag, NOT under `latest`. Stable users running `npm i suprsend` are unaffected; testers opt in via `npm i suprsend@beta`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release > Pre-release tags (beta / rc / alpha / canary)
text: - **Homebrew** — `homebrew_casks[].skip_upload: auto` skips the public `suprsend/homebrew-tap` update on pre-releases. `brew upgrade suprsend` on the stable tap never bumps users to a beta build.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release > Pre-release tags (beta / rc / alpha / canary)
text: - **MCP Registry** — the four publish-related steps in `release.yml` are guarded by `if: ${{ !contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}`, so the registry only ever advertises stable versions.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release > Pre-release tags (beta / rc / alpha / canary)
text: - **Glama** — Glama releases are user-triggered through their admin UI; the maintainer chooses whether to mark a Glama release on a pre-release tag.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Release > Pre-release tags (beta / rc / alpha / canary)
text: The detection rule across all four channels is the same: any tag with a `-` in the version string is treated as a pre-release per SemVer 2.0. If we ever need stable releases with weird suffixes, all four guards have to be revisited together.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo
text:
A workspace grows to tens of GB: `target/`, React Native `Pods/` and Gradle
builds, release checkouts in `.context/`, and a Bazel output base that lives
outside the workspace. `just clean` (`./clean.sh`) lists what a rebuild
recreates; add `--all` for merged `.context` worktrees and Bazel output bases,
`--apply` to delete. Use it rather than a hand-rolled `rm -rf`.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo
text:
Cleaning is per folder. Every folder that produces build output owns a
`clean.sh` that sources `tools/scripts/clean-lib.sh` and names its outputs
(`clean_paths`, plus `clean_command` for a tool like `flutter clean`); the root
`clean.sh` runs every one git tracks, in parallel. **A new folder that builds
something gets a `clean.sh` too** (commit it, or it never runs). Only list
paths git ignores: the lib refuses anything else, and
`tools/scripts/tests/test_clean.py` fails on it.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Building native bindings / cross-compiled artifacts
text:
**Native artifacts are built by Bazel**, not `xtask`. Bazel brings its own
hermetic toolchains (Rust, Android NDK, clang, Windows SDK), so these are the
same targets the release ships from — do **not** hand-roll `cargo ndk` or raw
`cargo build --target <triple>` to reproduce them:

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Building native bindings / cross-compiled artifacts
text:
Use `bazelisk` (reads `.bazelversion`). `just bazel-build | bazel-analyze |
bazel-test` are the shortcuts; each forwards extra Bazel flags. Full setup,
including the Windows MSVC EULA note, is in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Building native bindings / cross-compiled artifacts
text:
Every first-party Rust target (`rust_library`, `rust_binary`, `rust_test`, …)
passes `version = XYBRID_VERSION`, loaded from `@xybrid_version//:version.bzl`.
That constant is read from `Cargo.toml`'s `[workspace.package] version` by
`//bazel:cargo_version.bzl`; without it rules_rust sets `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` to
`0.0.0`, which every shipped (Bazel-built) SDK would report. Add it to any new
Rust target: `bazel.yml`'s "Every Rust target stamps the workspace version" step
(a `bazel query` for Rust targets still on the `0.0.0` default) fails otherwise.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Building native bindings / cross-compiled artifacts
text:
`xtask` is **not** the native-binding entry point anymore. `build-android`,
`build-xcframework`, `build-uniffi`, `stage-react-native`, `setup-targets`,
`build-all`, and `package` were all removed once Bazel took over. What remains
is Flutter, Unity staging, and dev-env chores:

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Building native bindings / cross-compiled artifacts
text:
Flutter native is cargo **on purpose**: `flutter run` inside the repo goes
through cargokit → cargo, so the contributor path must match. `build-ffi` /
`build-unity` build `xybrid-bolt` (the pre-bolt `xybrid-ffi` C ABI is retired);
`deploy-unity-native` exists so a Bazel-built lib can be staged into
`bindings/unity/Runtime/Plugins/` with the right per-platform `.meta`.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Building native bindings / cross-compiled artifacts
text:
After editing `bindings/flutter/rust`, regenerate the Dart glue with
`flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate` (CLI version must match the pinned
`flutter_rust_bridge` in `bindings/flutter/rust/Cargo.toml`); `flutter run` then
rebuilds the native lib via cargokit.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Building native bindings / cross-compiled artifacts
text:
**The arm64 AAR links llama.cpp dynamically; everything else statically.**
Only the Kotlin AAR's arm64 slice (so Kotlin and React Native) uses
`//:llama_android_dl`: ggml built with `GGML_BACKEND_DL` +
`GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS`, so `libxybrid_bolt.so` needs `libllama.so`,
`libggml*.so` and `libmtmd.so`, and one CPU backend per ISA level ships as a
module that `bindings/kotlin/bazel/jni/ggml_cpu_backend.cpp` loads at startup
(best first; ggml skips variants the CPU cannot run). It is selected by the
`//bazel/ggml:android_arm64_cpu_variants` platform, which only the AAR builds
for — the Flutter arm64 cdylib keeps the static `//:llama`, because its
precompiled package carries a single `.so`. Any new target that picks a llama
build must select on `//bazel/ggml:cpu_variants_enabled` too, or the AAR would
link two ggml copies. The shipped variant list lives in
`bazel/ggml/android.bzl` and must match the loader's (the `build-android.yml`
gate fails otherwise). Two rules_foreign_cc traps are handled there:
Android is configured as `CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux`, so a CMake hook
(`bazel/ggml/android_system_name.cmake`) makes ggml build its Android variant
set, and `CMAKE_PLATFORM_NO_VERSIONED_SONAME` keeps sonames unversioned (an APK
only carries `lib*.so`).

The manifest is GENERATED — `.github/workflows/build-natives.yml` publishes the

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Prebuilt llama.cpp natives (the cargo fast path)
text:
- **The manifest goes stale on purpose.** It pins plain hashes of
  `wrapper.cpp`, `wrapper.h`, `build.rs`, and the llama.cpp commit. Touch any
  of them and every row is ignored until CI republishes — that is the guard
  that stops a local edit from linking archives that predate it. A dropped
  fast path after editing `build.rs` is expected, not a bug.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Prebuilt llama.cpp natives (the cargo fast path)
text:
- **Anonymous reachability is not covered by our own CI.** Every job here
  `oras login`s first, so a private package looks healthy internally and 401s
  for everyone outside. `tools/scripts/natives-verify-anon.sh` is the check
  that catches it; it runs credential-free at the end of `build-natives`.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Prebuilt llama.cpp natives (the cargo fast path)
text:
The publisher fingerprint (`natives-fingerprint.sh`) folds in the LOCAL
cmake/cc/NDK versions. That is right for publisher/consumer cache parity and
wrong for distribution, which is why the download path selects by target +
feature set + ABI attributes from the manifest instead of recomputing it.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI coding agents in xybrid > How to work in this repo > Releases
text:
**Releases are cut by branch name, not by hand.** Push a `release/v<version>`
branch and `.github/workflows/release-prep.yml` does the rest (manifest-version
check, artifact builds, `Package.swift` checksum patch, draft GitHub Release, and
the `Release v<version>` PR to master). Don't `gh pr create` a release or run
`just bump-version` on a feature branch and open a PR from it — that bypasses the
pipeline and ships nothing. Never commit `Package.swift useLocalNatives = true`
(local-dev only; breaks remote SPM — run `bindings/apple/scripts/set-natives-mode.sh
--set-remote`). Full ritual + gotchas: **§ Releases** below.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions
text:
These are the decisions xybrid has already made. They override the upstream
rule indexes in Sections 1–2 wherever the two disagree.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > What xybrid is (read this first)
text:
xybrid is a **local-first execution engine with a platform layer built on top**.
Both planes share one codebase, and the platform plane is **additive** — it
extends the same runtime without replacing the offline path:

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > What xybrid is (read this first)
text:
1. **Foundation — on-device execution engine.** Model load/run/stream,
   pipelines, hardware acceleration. Zero-config, offline, no account required.
   This is the default path and most of the code today.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > What xybrid is (read this first)
text:
2. **Platform / control-plane layer (additive).** Opt-in capabilities layered on
   the engine — the direction being actively built out. When a developer
   authenticates, these light up *on top of* the same local runtime:
   - **Auth / API keys** — `crates/xybrid-core/src/cloud/config.rs`
     (`set_xybrid_api_key`, `XYBRID_API_KEY`). Gates the cloud gateway *and* the
     telemetry exporter. Default gateway: `api.xybrid.dev`.
   - **Cloud routing** — `crates/xybrid-core/src/cloud/` +
     `crates/xybrid-core/src/orchestrator/routing_engine.rs` (local→cloud fallback under device stress).
   - **Telemetry / observability** — `crates/xybrid-core/src/telemetry/`;
     SDK exporter in `crates/xybrid-sdk/src/telemetry.rs`; ingest at `ingest.xybrid.dev`.
   - **Remote routing authority** — `crates/xybrid-core/src/orchestrator/authority/remote.rs`
     (`GET /v1/routing/advice`; partial).
   - **Control sync** — `crates/xybrid-core/src/control_sync.rs` (policy /
     registry refresh; scaffolded, backend not yet wired).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > What xybrid is (read this first)
text:
The public README markets the foundation ("offline, no cloud, no API keys")
because that's the zero-config default — the platform layer is what you add on
top once you authenticate. **When touching `xybrid-sdk` or `xybrid-core`, treat
the platform plane as a first-class, additive surface**, not an afterthought:
new SDK entry points should consider whether they extend into it too.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text: Cargo workspace, `resolver = "2"`, edition 2021, MSRV not pinned. Members:

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text:
| Crate                          | Role                                                       | Layer    |
|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------|
| `crates/xybrid-core`           | ML execution + pipelines; **additive platform plane** (cloud routing, telemetry, control sync) | core lib |
| `crates/xybrid-sdk`            | Public Rust SDK; model load/run/stream + platform init (auth, telemetry) | lib      |
| `crates/xybrid-cli`            | `xybrid` binary                                            | bin      |
| `crates/xybrid-ffi-facade`     | FFI-agnostic POD/Arc facade over the SDK (one canonical translation) | FFI |
| `crates/xybrid-bolt`           | BoltFFI bindings: Swift / Kotlin / Java / C# (Unity) / WASM + C header — the sole native binding crate | FFI |
| `bindings/flutter/rust`        | flutter_rust_bridge wrapper for Dart                       | FFI      |
| `macros`                       | proc-macros (`xybrid-macros`); syn/quote only              | proc     |
| `xtask`                        | build / codegen automation                                 | tool     |
| `integration-tests`            | end-to-end tests with real models & fixtures               | test     |

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text:
The Python SDK (`bindings/python`, not a workspace member) runs on boltffi's
**generated** bindings as of 0.29: `xybrid/_bolt/` is generator output
(`tools/scripts/gen_python_bolt.py`, byte-compared in CI via `--check`), and it
imports a compiled CPython bridge that dlopens the `xybrid-bolt` cdylib. Both
binaries are staged by `tools/scripts/build-python-bolt.sh` and are **build
outputs, never committed** — so wheels are per-interpreter (`cp3XX`) and the
SDK requires Python >= 3.10.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text:
Because the generated package is byte-compared, it carries no hand-written
code. The Pythonic surface (envelope factories, `result.text`, model
properties, typed exceptions) is attached to the generated classes at import by
`xybrid/_sugar.py` and `xybrid/_errors.py`, guarded by `tests/test_sdk.py`. Add
SDK ergonomics there, never in `xybrid/_bolt/`.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text:
The React Native package (`bindings/react-native`, npm `@xybrid/react-native`,
not a workspace member) is the one **hand-bridged** binding: a Codegen
TurboModule over the Swift and Kotlin SDKs, so nothing reaches it for free.
`tests/parity.test.mjs` fails when `crates/xybrid-bolt` gains an export, record
field, enum variant or error variant that `bindings/react-native/parity.json`
neither maps nor excludes. When you add bolt surface, wire it through React
Native (spec, both shims, TS facade — see its README) or exclude it there with a
reason; don't leave the test red. Its iOS core is not in the npm tarball:
`pod install` downloads the release XCFramework and checks the SHA-256 that
release-prep pins in its `package.json`.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text:
Every SDK names itself in registry requests and telemetry (`binding=` in
`X-Xybrid-Client`), and the first registration in a process wins. Flutter
registers in its `#[frb(init)]` hook, Python on import, Unity from static
constructors and React Native before every bridged call. Until an SDK
registers, `xybrid-bolt` reports a fallback: `swift` on Apple platforms,
`kotlin` on Android. A registration always replaces it, whenever it happens,
so a new binding there reports theirs only until it registers. Add a new name
to the facade's `resolve_binding`; a test fails until you do. The table is in
`docs/telemetry/registry.md`.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text:
The browser package (`bindings/web`, npm `@xybrid/web`) is a GGUF text-generation
preview over the existing Rust/llama.cpp path. `pnpm build` invokes Bazel for CPU
and experimental WebGPU WASM, then bundles the client and worker. `pnpm
pack:release` checks the real npm archive in an isolated consumer; CI and release
preparation run Chromium against its extracted contents. Release publication
stages that same archive for npm approval. Setup is in
`bindings/web/RELEASING.md`; installing the package never invokes native tools.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text: **Dependency direction (do not reverse):**

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text:
Workspace **package metadata** is inherited via `[workspace.package]` —
member crates use `version.workspace = true`, `edition.workspace = true`,
etc. Keep that pattern.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Workspace layout
text:
Workspace **dependencies** are *not* uniformly inherited today. The root
`[workspace.dependencies]` block exists, but most member crates still pin
versions per-crate (e.g. `serde = "1.0"`, `tokio = { version = "1.0", … }`).
When adding a dep, match the surrounding crate's existing style — don't
unilaterally migrate one crate to `dep.workspace = true` while the rest stay
version-pinned. Full `proj-workspace-deps` migration is a deliberate
refactor, not a drive-by change.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Error handling
text:
Rust-API library crates (`xybrid-core`, `xybrid-sdk`, `xybrid-ffi-facade`)
use **`thiserror`** with a single canonical error enum and a `Result` alias
per crate:

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Error handling
text:
| Crate              | Error type     | Result alias    | Defined in                           |
|--------------------|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------------------|
| `xybrid-core`      | `XybridError`  | `XybridResult`  | `crates/xybrid-core/src/error.rs`    |
| `xybrid-sdk`       | `SdkError`     | `SdkResult`     | `crates/xybrid-sdk/src/model.rs`     |
| `xybrid-ffi-facade`| `Error`        | `Result`        | `crates/xybrid-ffi-facade/src/lib.rs` (one canonical `From<SdkError>`; the FFI generator crates re-decorate it) |

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Error handling
text:
Sub-error enums (`InferenceError`, `PipelineError`, `AdapterError`, …) live
next to the modules that raise them and convert into the canonical type via
`#[from]` / `impl From`. Follow that pattern for new modules — don't invent
parallel top-level error types.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Error handling
text:
Binaries (`xybrid-cli`, `xtask`) use **`anyhow`** with `.context(...)` at the
boundaries where errors get printed.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Error handling
text:
`SdkError` implements a `RetryableError` trait (`is_retryable`, `retry_after`)
— preserve those semantics when adding variants. As of today
(`crates/xybrid-sdk/src/model.rs`) the retryable variants are
`NetworkError`, `RateLimited`, `Timeout`, and `Offline`; everything else
(including `CircuitOpen`, `ConfigError`, `ModelNotFound`, `LoadError`,
`InferenceError`, `IoError`, `CacheError`, `PipelineError`, …) is
explicitly **non-retryable**. Read the current `is_retryable` match arm
before changing or extending it — don't infer the rule from the variant name.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Error handling
text:
Don't use `Box<dyn Error>` in public signatures. Don't `.unwrap()` outside
tests, examples, and clearly-marked invariant checks (use `.expect("...")`
with a message that explains the invariant — rust-skills `err-expect-bugs-only`).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Async runtime
text:
**Tokio**, multi-threaded. Workspace pins:
`tokio = { version = "1.0", features = ["rt", "rt-multi-thread", "sync"] }`.
No async-std, no smol.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Async runtime
text:
Public SDK APIs come in **sync + async pairs**: `load` / `load_async`,
`run` / `run_async`, `warmup` / `warmup_async`, `run_pipeline_async`, etc.
Sync variants block on the runtime internally. **Match this convention** when
adding new SDK entry points — don't break the symmetry.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Async runtime
text:
- Use `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` for CPU-bound or sync I/O (model loading
  is the canonical example — see `xybrid-sdk` model loader).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Async runtime
text:
- Don't hold `Mutex` / `RwLock` guards across `.await` (rust-skills
  `async-no-lock-await`, `anti-lock-across-await`).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Async runtime
text:
- Channels: `tokio::sync::mpsc` for streaming events; that's the established
  pattern for pipeline event streams (`xybrid-sdk/src/lib.rs`).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Async runtime
text:
Tests that need a runtime use `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().unwrap().block_on(...)`
today. New async tests may use `#[tokio::test]` — both are accepted.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > SDK run surface — capabilities are data, not entry points
text: The public run surface grows by axes, and axes multiply. The rule:

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > SDK run surface — capabilities are data, not entry points
text:
- **A new capability rides `RunOptions`, `GenerationConfig`, or `Envelope`** —
  never a new `run*` method. Constrained decoding shipped this way
  (`GenerationConfig.grammar` — zero new entry points), and new capabilities
  (tool calling, etc.) must too (`RunOptions`-carried inputs, parsed outputs
  on `InferenceResult`).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > SDK run surface — capabilities are data, not entry points
text:
- **A new entry point is justified only by a new IO shape** — a different way
  results physically flow out: batch return, per-token callback, async
  `Stream` handle, TTS chunk sink. Each IO shape gets exactly one sync + one
  async form, nothing else.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > SDK run surface — capabilities are data, not entry points
text:
- **Suffix chains are the anti-pattern.** Names like
  `run_streaming_with_context_options_preempt` are capabilities leaking into
  the namespace. `XybridModel` currently carries 14 `run*` variants for this
  reason, while bolt's entire foreign surface needs exactly one
  (`run(envelope, options)`). The excess is consolidation backlog, **not
  precedent** — don't add variant #15.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > SDK run surface — capabilities are data, not entry points
text:
- Multi-step orchestration (agent loops, retries, tool-execution cycles)
  lives **outside** `XybridModel` — a free helper or the caller's own loop —
  and FFI bindings get turn-based primitives (parsed results + another `run`
  call), not cross-boundary callbacks.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Testing & mocking
text: - **Unit tests** inline as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; ... }`.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Testing & mocking
text: - **Integration tests** in each crate's `tests/` directory.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Testing & mocking
text:
- **End-to-end tests** with real models in `/integration-tests/`. Fixtures
  live in `integration-tests/fixtures/{input,models,pipelines}/`. Tests that
  need a downloaded model gate themselves with `fixtures::model_if_available()`
  and skip cleanly if the model isn't present — follow that pattern, don't
  hard-fail on missing assets.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Testing & mocking
text:
- **HTTP mocking:** `httpmock` (already a dev-dep in `xybrid-sdk`). **No
  `mockall`, `mockito`, or `wiremock`** in this repo today — don't introduce
  another mocking library without discussion.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Testing & mocking
text: - **Benchmarks:** `criterion` (dev-dep in `xybrid-core`).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Testing & mocking
text:
- No `insta` snapshots, no `proptest`. Don't add either casually — they bring
  CI cost and a learning curve.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Testing & mocking
text:
Run model-gated tests with `just`-recipes under `mod integration-tests` in the
root `justfile`.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Concurrency primitives — when to use what
text:
The workspace is multi-threaded. **Don't use `Rc` or `RefCell`** — they aren't
in use anywhere and they trap you in single-threaded contexts.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Concurrency primitives — when to use what
text:
| Need                                            | Use                              |
|-------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Pass data into a function for read-only use     | `&T` (or `&[T]`, `&str`)         |
| Share owned state across threads / async tasks  | `Arc<T>`                         |
| Shared state, mostly reads, some writes         | `Arc<RwLock<T>>` (std)           |
| Shared state, exclusive access each time        | `Arc<Mutex<T>>` (std)            |
| Cross-task message passing                      | `tokio::sync::mpsc`              |
| One-shot reply channel                          | `tokio::sync::oneshot`           |

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Concurrency primitives — when to use what
text:
Use `std::sync::{Mutex, RwLock}` — **not** `parking_lot` (not a dependency).
Public traits that cross task boundaries are bounded `Send + Sync`; this is
established convention for backend / strategy / session traits in
`xybrid-core`. Keep that bound on new traits in the same family.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Concurrency primitives — when to use what
text:
Prefer borrows over `Arc::clone` when a borrow's lifetime is obviously short
enough. Reach for `Arc` when you're crossing a `spawn` / `spawn_blocking` /
channel boundary, or storing the value behind a trait object.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text:
**Releases are cut by branch name, not by hand.** The entire pipeline keys off a
`release/v<version>` branch. An agent's *only* correct action to start a release
is to create and push that branch — everything else (artifact builds, checksum
patch, draft GitHub Release, the release PR, the tag, and the crates.io / pub.dev
/ Maven Central publishes) is generated by CI. The ritual
(`.github/workflows/release-prep.yml` → `release-publish.yml`):

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text: Pushing `release/v*` triggers `release-prep.yml`, which:

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text:
1. Parses the version **from the branch name** and **fails** unless it matches
   every package manifest (`version-sync.sh --check` must be green).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text:
2. Builds all artifacts, patches `Package.swift`'s `xybridFFIChecksum`, and
   creates a **draft GitHub Release**.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text:
3. **Opens the `Release v<version>` PR to master itself.** On merge,
   `release-publish.yml` tags and publishes.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text:
- run `gh pr create` for a release, or run `just bump-version` on a feature
  branch and open a PR from it — that bypasses the artifact builds, the checksum
  patch, and the draft release, producing a PR that *looks* like a release but
  ships nothing. The branch name (`release/v*`) is the trigger; a PR title is not.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text:
- leave `Package.swift`'s `useLocalNatives = true` in any committed state. It is
  **local-dev only** and breaks remote SPM consumers (the local xcframework is
  not committed). Run `bindings/apple/scripts/set-natives-mode.sh --set-remote`
  before committing — remote (`false`) is the canonical committed state.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text:
`just bump-version` only rewrites the workspace `version`; it does **not** touch
internal path-dep `version = "..."` pins (e.g. `xybrid-sdk`/`xybrid-core` in
sibling `Cargo.toml`s). If those drift, lockfile regen fails under `^0.1.x` —
update them to match and re-run `cargo update -w` when bumping.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Releases — never hand-roll one (agents read this)
text:
**llama.cpp stable updates (POC).** `llamacpp-update.yml` checks official
`vX.Y.Z` releases daily and opens one version-specific update PR at a time.
Keep the submodule gitlink, `LLAMA_CPP_COMMIT`, and
`.github/llamacpp-version.json` consistent. Release preparation waits for
successful validation and a matching, complete generated native manifest,
then pushes `release/v<version>` through the existing pipeline. Stable `0.x`
SDKs default to the next minor for classified patch or minor upstream updates;
first tracked (bootstrap) updates, upstream major updates and SDKs >=1.0
require an explicit version. The release PR remains the publishing approval
point.
Release-branch version sync records the exact upstream commit being shipped.
Setup, dry runs, and conformance-fixture migration are documented in
`docs/development/llamacpp-updates.md`.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > GitHub Actions workflows — names, files, keys
text:
The map of every workflow is
[`.github/workflows/README.md`](.github/workflows/README.md). Its inventory table
is generated from the workflow files, and these rules keep it true:

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > GitHub Actions workflows — names, files, keys
text:
- **Display name** is `"Group: Subject"` (quoted). Group is one of `CI`, `SDK`,
  `Artifacts`, `Release`, `Security`, `Maintenance`, `Community`; `GROUPS` in
  `tools/scripts/gen_workflow_index.py` is the source of truth and says what
  each holds. A dispatch-only workflow ends its Subject with `(manual)`. Docs
  that cite a display name change with it, so `git grep` the old name.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > GitHub Actions workflows — names, files, keys
text:
- **Purpose** is the line directly above `name:`: `# Purpose: <one sentence>`,
  starting `Manual:` for a dispatch-only workflow. Keep it true when triggers
  change; a schedule edit can make "weekly" wrong.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > GitHub Actions workflows — names, files, keys
text:
- **Concurrency groups** start with the file stem, never `${{ github.workflow }}`,
  so a display name can change without changing the group. Use
  `<file-stem>-${{ github.ref }}`, key on the tag or issue number for
  event-driven workflows, or use the bare `<file-stem>` when every run must
  queue behind the last (`llamacpp-update.yml`, `star-history.yml`).

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > GitHub Actions workflows — names, files, keys
text:
- **Regenerate the map.** After touching any workflow, run
  `python3 tools/scripts/gen_workflow_index.py`. CI runs it with `--check` (job
  `Workflow index`) and fails on drift or a broken rule. A rebase can bring in
  master workflows written without these rules; fix them on your branch.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > GitHub Actions workflows — names, files, keys
text:
- **Rename workflow files rarely.** GitHub ties run history and code-scanning
  configurations (CodeQL `codeql.yml:analyze`, Scorecard `scorecard.yml:analysis`)
  to the path, and `release-publish.yml` and the docs call
  `gh workflow run <file>`. Change `name:` instead.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > GitHub Actions workflows — names, files, keys
text:
- **Job names are matched as checks; never rename them.** `CI Success`
  (`ci.yml` and `ci-docs.yml`) and `Bazel graph + RBE targets` (`bazel.yml`)
  gate `master` through branch protection. `tools/scripts/llamacpp_update.py`
  also waits on job names (`REQUIRED_CHECKS`, `AUTOMATION_CHECKS`) before it
  cuts a llama.cpp release. Edit a workflow's `name:` freely.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Things to leave alone unless explicitly asked
text: - `rustfmt.toml` is intentionally empty (defaults). Don't add style overrides.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Things to leave alone unless explicitly asked
text:
- The `#![allow(clippy::...)]` lists at the top of `xybrid-core/src/lib.rs`
  and `xybrid-sdk/src/lib.rs` exist because the crates are still alpha
  (`0.1.0-beta12`). Fixing those lints crate-wide is fine; **disabling
  individual call-sites** with `#[allow]` is not — push it to crate-level if
  it's project-wide.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Things to leave alone unless explicitly asked
text:
- API contract checks (`tools/scripts/api-contract-check.sh`) run in CI as a
  soft warning. If you change a public SDK signature, run it locally.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Open questions (resolve before encoding as rules)
text:
These are genuinely ambiguous in the current code — flag them to a maintainer
rather than picking arbitrarily:

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Open questions (resolve before encoding as rules)
text:
1. **MSRV.** No `rust-version` is pinned in any `Cargo.toml`. Should the
   workspace pin one (e.g. matching what CI's `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`
   resolves to today)?

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Open questions (resolve before encoding as rules)
text:
2. **Async test style.** `runtime.block_on` (current) vs `#[tokio::test]`
   (rust-skills `test-tokio-async`) — both work; no canonical choice yet.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Open questions (resolve before encoding as rules)
text:
3. **Workspace-level lints.** Only `bindings/flutter/rust` has a `[lints]`
   table. The rust-skills `lint-workspace-lints` / `lint-deny-correctness`
   rules suggest configuring lints workspace-wide; alpha-stage allow-lists in
   each crate make that disruptive today. Worth revisiting post-1.0.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Open questions (resolve before encoding as rules)
text:
4. **`Box<dyn Trait>` vs `impl Trait` in public APIs.** Trait-object style is
   used widely for backends (`Arc<dyn LlmBackend>` etc.) for plug-in
   replaceability. New code should follow that — but if a single-impl
   internal trait shows up, prefer `impl Trait`.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Open questions (resolve before encoding as rules)
text:
5. **Naming of streaming/event APIs.** `recv()` (channel-style) vs an
   `EventStream`-newtype wrapper. Current code uses the channel idiom; an
   abstraction layer hasn't been decided.

head: Section 0 — xybrid project decisions > Open questions (resolve before encoding as rules)
text: When you hit one of these, ask in the PR rather than guessing.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index)
text:
Each ID below links to the upstream anchor on `microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines`.
The one-line summary is enough to decide whether to read the full rule. **Bolded
rules are the ones you'll consult most often in this repo.**

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index)
text:
> *License: MIT (Microsoft Corporation). Source:*
> `https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/agents/all.txt`

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design
text: - `M-DESIGN-FOR-AI` — strong types, thorough docs/examples, testable APIs make agent work tractable.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Applications
text: - `M-APP-ERROR` — apps may use `anyhow`/`eyre`; libraries must not (see `M-ERRORS-CANONICAL-STRUCTS`).

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Applications
text: - `M-MIMALLOC-APPS` — set `mimalloc` as global allocator in app binaries for free perf.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Documentation
text: - **`M-CANONICAL-DOCS`** — public items: summary sentence + `# Examples / Errors / Panics / Safety / Abort` as applicable. No parameter tables.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Documentation
text: - `M-DOC-INLINE` — annotate `pub use foo::Foo` with `#[doc(inline)]` for own-crate re-exports (not std/third-party).

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Documentation
text: - `M-FIRST-DOC-SENTENCE` — first sentence ≤15 words, one line.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Documentation
text: - **`M-MODULE-DOCS`** — every public module needs `//!` docs covering contents, when to use, examples, side effects.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > FFI
text: - **`M-ISOLATE-DLL-STATE`** — only portable (`#[repr(C)]`, no statics/TypeId/non-portable refs) data crosses DLL boundaries. Critical for `xybrid-bolt` (the cdylib crossing DLL boundaries).

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Performance
text: - `M-HOTPATH` — identify hot paths early, bench with criterion, profile (Intel VTune / Superluminal). Enable `debug = 1` in `[profile.bench]`.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Performance
text: - `M-THROUGHPUT` — items/cycle is the metric; batch, partition, avoid empty cycles and contention.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Performance
text: - **`M-YIELD-POINTS`** — long CPU-bound async tasks must `yield_now().await` every ~10–100μs.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Safety
text: - **`M-UNSAFE-IMPLIES-UB`** — `unsafe` is *only* for things where misuse causes UB. Don't use it to flag merely dangerous functions.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Safety
text: - **`M-UNSAFE`** — needs a real reason (novel abstraction, perf, FFI). Document soundness, run Miri, follow unsafe-code guidelines.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Safety
text: - **`M-UNSOUND`** — never acceptable. Safe code that *can* cause UB is a bug, no exceptions.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-CONCISE-NAMES` — drop weasel words (`Service`, `Manager`, `Factory`). `BookingDispatcher` > `BookingService`.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-DOCUMENTED-MAGIC` — magic numbers get a comment explaining why; prefer named constants.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-LINT-OVERRIDE-EXPECT` — submodule lint overrides use `#[expect(..., reason = "...")]`, not `#[allow]`.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-LOG-STRUCTURED` — structured events with named properties + message templates (`{{property}}` syntax). Follow OTel semantic conventions. Redact PII.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - **`M-PANIC-IS-STOP`** — panic means *stop the program*. Not for upstream error signaling. Code must be panic-safe.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - **`M-PANIC-ON-BUG`** — detected programming bugs panic; no `Error` variant for "this shouldn't happen".

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-PUBLIC-DEBUG` — all public types implement `Debug`; redact sensitive data via custom impl + tested redaction.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-PUBLIC-DISPLAY` — types meant to be read by humans (errors, string wrappers) implement `Display`.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-REGULAR-FN` — free functions over associated functions, except for constructors and trait methods.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-SMALLER-CRATES` — split when in doubt; faster compiles, fewer cycles. Re-export via umbrella crate when useful.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-STATIC-VERIFICATION` — fmt, clippy (`correctness`, `complexity`, `perf`, `style`, `suspicious`, `pedantic` + select `restriction`), cargo-audit, cargo-hack, cargo-udeps, miri.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Universal
text: - `M-UPSTREAM-GUIDELINES` — also follow Rust API Guidelines / Style Guide / Design Patterns. Watch `C-CONV`, `C-GETTER`, `C-COMMON-TRAITS`, `C-CTOR`, `C-FEATURE`.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / building
text: - `M-FEATURES-ADDITIVE` — features only *add*; no `no-std` (use `std` feature); enabling any combo must compile.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / building
text: - `M-OOBE` — libraries `cargo build` on Tier-1 platforms with no extra tools/env. You own your dep tree's OOBE-ness.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / building
text: - `M-SYS-CRATES` — `-sys` crates: build via `cc` in `build.rs`, embed sources, optional tools, support static + `libloading`.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / interoperability
text: - `M-DONT-LEAK-TYPES` — prefer `std` types in public APIs; leak third-party types only for substantial ecosystem benefit or behind a feature.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / interoperability
text: - `M-ESCAPE-HATCHES` — native-handle wrappers expose `unsafe fn from_native`, `to_native`, `into_native`.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / interoperability
text: - **`M-TYPES-SEND`** — public types and async futures should be `Send` for Tokio compatibility.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / resilience
text: - **`M-AVOID-STATICS`** — `static`/thread-local items secretly duplicate across crate-version boundaries. Don't use them for correctness-relevant state.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / resilience
text: - `M-MOCKABLE-SYSCALLS` — I/O, clocks, entropy, anything non-deterministic is mockable via an internal enum dispatch + `test-util` feature.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / resilience
text: - `M-NO-GLOB-REEXPORTS` — `pub use foo::{A, B, C}`, not `pub use foo::*` (HAL platform-specific re-exports excepted).

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / resilience
text: - `M-STRONG-TYPES` — `PathBuf`/`Path` for OS paths, not `String`/`&str`. Use the strongest std type early.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / resilience
text: - `M-TEST-UTIL` — testing/mocking functionality gated behind a `test-util` feature.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - **`M-AVOID-WRAPPERS`** — don't expose `Arc<Mutex<T>>`, `Box<T>`, `Rc<RefCell<T>>` in public APIs; hide them behind clean signatures.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - **`M-DI-HIERARCHY`** — concrete types > generics > `dyn Trait`. Don't translate `IFoo` interfaces from C# verbatim.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - **`M-ERRORS-CANONICAL-STRUCTS`** — errors are structs with `Backtrace` + optional source; expose `is_xxx()` methods over public `ErrorKind`. See xybrid's per-crate error tables in § Error handling above.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - `M-ESSENTIAL-FN-INHERENT` — core functionality is inherent; trait impls forward to inherent methods.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - `M-IMPL-ASREF` — accept `impl AsRef<str>` / `impl AsRef<Path>` / `impl AsRef<[u8]>` for non-owning string/path/byte inputs.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - `M-IMPL-IO` — sans-io: accept `impl std::io::Read`/`Write` (or `futures::io::AsyncRead`) for one-shot init I/O.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - `M-IMPL-RANGEBOUNDS` — range params are `Range<T>` or `impl RangeBounds<T>`, not `(low, high)` tuples.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - **`M-INIT-BUILDER`** — ≥4 init permutations → `FooBuilder` with `Foo::builder()` and chainable methods ending in `.build()`. Required params go to `builder(deps: impl Into<FooDeps>)`.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - `M-INIT-CASCADED` — types with 4+ params group parameters into helper types semantically.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - `M-SERVICES-CLONE` — service types implement `Clone` via `Arc<Inner>` so dependents share a handle.

head: Section 1 — Microsoft Pragmatic Rust (rule index) > AI-friendly design > Library / UX
text: - **`M-SIMPLE-ABSTRACTIONS`** — service-type generics don't nest visibly. `Foo<Bar<FooBar>>` in a user's field is a smell.

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance to AI coding agents working with this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: `gin-restful` is a Go library that provides a Flask-RESTful style abstraction over the Gin web framework. Resources are defined by implementing independent HTTP method interfaces — only implemented methods become routes.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Core Files
text:
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `resource.go` | 6 interfaces: `Lister`, `Getter`, `Poster`, `Putter`, `Patcher`, `Deleter` |
| `api.go` | `API` struct, `NewAPI`, `AddResource` — type-asserts resource and registers Gin routes |
| `bind.go` | `Bind[T]` and `MustBind[T]` — generic request body binding helpers |
| `errors.go` | `HTTPError` type and `Abort()` helper for structured error responses |
| `handler.go` | `makeHandler` (response dispatcher), `handleError`, `normalizePath` |

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Design Patterns
text: - **Interface segregation**: Each HTTP method is a separate interface. Implement only what you need.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Design Patterns
text: - **Type-safe binding**: `Bind[T]` / `MustBind[T]` use Go generics for compile-time type checking on request bodies. Response type is `any`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Design Patterns
text: - **Error handling**: Return `*HTTPError` (via `Abort()`) for client errors with status+message. Non-HTTPError errors produce `500` with a generic message — internal details are never leaked.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Design Patterns
text: - **204 No Content**: When status is 204, the framework sends no response body.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Design Patterns
text: - **Abort on error**: All error paths call `c.AbortWithStatusJSON` to stop the middleware chain.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Package
text: Package name is `restful`. No import alias needed.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions
text: - Handler methods return `(any, int, error)` — response body, HTTP status code, error.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions
text: - Use `Bind[T]` when you need custom error handling, `MustBind[T]` for automatic 400 abort.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions
text: - Use `Abort(status, message)` to return HTTP errors — never return raw `fmt.Errorf` for client-facing errors.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions
text: - `AddResource` panics if the resource implements none of the 6 interfaces — this catches typos/signature mismatches early.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions
text: - All examples use `sync.RWMutex` for concurrent map access — follow this pattern.

head: AGENTS.md > Examples
text:
| Example | Path | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| Basic | `example/basic/` | Simple CRUD |
| Complex | `example/complex/` | Multiple resources, pagination, PUT/PATCH split |
| Hybrid | `example/hybrid/` | RESTful + regular Gin handlers, auth middleware |

head: LLM Wiki
text: > raw 소스를 LLM이 직접 합성·유지하는 **영구 마크다운 위키**로 키우는 워크스페이스. Karpathy "LLM Wiki" 패턴 구현 — 매 질문마다 재검색하는 RAG가 아니라, 한 번 합성하고 최신 상태로 *누적*하는 지식 베이스.

head: LLM Wiki
text: **target runtime**: Claude Code (이 CLAUDE.md가 위키 운영 규약 = the "schema" layer). **외부 스킬·플러그인 의존 없음** — 이 폴더만 있으면 어디서든 `claude`로 동작.

head: LLM Wiki > 핵심 원칙
text: - **One Workspace, One Agent** — 이 워크스페이스는 llm-wiki 유지관리 전용 단일 에이전트입니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 핵심 원칙
text: - **3-Layer 분리** — raw(불변 원본) / wiki(LLM 소유) / schema(이 파일). 세 레이어를 절대 섞지 않습니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 핵심 원칙
text: - **Router, not Catalog** — `index.md`는 "모든 페이지 목록"이 아니라 의도→타입/샤드 **라우터(MOC)**입니다. 위키가 커져도 query당 토큰이 일정합니다 (`conventions.md §0`).

head: LLM Wiki > 핵심 원칙
text: - **Compounding, not Retrieving** — 매 질문마다 처음부터 재발견하지 않습니다. 한 번 합성하고 *최신 상태로 유지*합니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 핵심 원칙
text: - **Provenance Required** — 모든 사실 주장은 출처 소스로 역링크합니다. 출처 없으면 "확인 필요"로 표시합니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 핵심 원칙
text: - **Grep-Friendly First** — 페이지는 *검색되게* 씁니다. frontmatter + BLUF + 고정 섹션 + [[링크]].

head: LLM Wiki > 핵심 원칙
text: - **Maintenance is the Job** — 지루한 bookkeeping(교차참조·일관성 유지)이 핵심 가치입니다. 한 소스가 보통 페이지 10~15개를 건드립니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 폴더 구조 (3-Layer)
text: 주제 하위의 `sources/entities/concepts`는 비넘버링 도메인 폴더입니다 (규약: `00-system/conventions.md`).

head: LLM Wiki > 워크플로우
text: - **Phase 0: 현황 감사** — 첫 작업 전 `30-wiki/index.md`(라우터), `log.md`, 기존 주제를 확인합니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 워크플로우
text: - **Phase 1: 수집(ingest)** — 자료를 `10-inbox/`에 저장만 합니다 (위키화 안 함).

head: LLM Wiki > 워크플로우
text: - **Phase 2: 정제(compile)** — `10-inbox/`의 소스를 위키로 합성하고, 라우터·인덱스·aliases·overview를 갱신한 뒤 원본을 `20-raw/`로 이동합니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 워크플로우
text: - **Phase 3: 질의(query)** — 2단 라우팅(Route→Search)으로 답하고, 가치 있는 답을 파일백합니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 워크플로우
text: - **Phase 4: 점검(lint)** — 모순·고아·인덱스/라우터 정합·갭을 점검합니다.

head: LLM Wiki > 커맨드 목록
text: - `/ingest {소스}` — Lite. 자료(URL·파일·텍스트)를 `10-inbox/`에 저장만. 위키화 안 함. 산출물: inbox 새 파일.

head: LLM Wiki > 커맨드 목록
text: - `/compile [소스]` — Standard. inbox 소스를 위키로 합성(소스요약→엔티티/개념→정본화→라우터/인덱스/overview→raw 이동). 산출물: `30-wiki/` 페이지 다수.

head: LLM Wiki > 커맨드 목록
text: - `/query {질문}` — Lite. 2단 라우팅(Route→Search)으로 회수·인용 합성, 좋은 답은 파일백. 산출물: 답변 + (선택) `50-queries/`.

head: LLM Wiki > 커맨드 목록
text: - `/lint [주제]` — Standard. 모순·고아·인덱스/라우터 정합·tier·갭 점검. 산출물: 리포트 + 수정.

head: LLM Wiki > Scale Modes
text: - **Lite** — 소스 ~수십 개. 주제 라우터가 곧 카탈로그 겸함(`indexes/` 생략 가능). `/ingest → /compile → /query`.

head: LLM Wiki > Scale Modes
text: - **Standard** — 페이지 수백 개. 타입별 `indexes/{type}.md` 분리. `/compile → /query → /lint` 정기.

head: LLM Wiki > Scale Modes
text: - **Full** — 페이지 수천 개+. 타입 인덱스를 **첫 글자 샤딩(≤50K)**, 선택적 외부검색(`.rag`) 병용. 정기 lint로 일관성.

head: LLM Wiki > Scale Modes
text: > 규모가 커져도 **index/샤드를 통째로 컨텍스트에 올리지 않습니다.** 라우터로 의도→타입/샤드를 정하고 **소수 후보만** 펼칩니다 (§ 도메인 프레임워크 / `conventions.md §9`).

head: LLM Wiki > 트리거 경계
text:
**should-trigger → `/ingest`**: "이거 위키에 넣어줘", "이 URL 가져와줘", "이 PDF 수집해줘" (저장만)
**should-trigger → `/compile`**: "위키로 정리해줘", "컴파일해줘", "inbox 처리해줘", "위키에 반영해줘"
**should-trigger → `/query`**: "X에 대해 뭐 알아?", "A랑 B 비교해줘", "위키에서 찾아줘", "정리해서 보여줘"
**should-trigger → `/lint`**: "위키 점검해줘", "모순 없나 봐줘", "인덱스 맞나 봐줘", "고아 페이지 확인해줘"

head: LLM Wiki > 트리거 경계
text: - "원본 파일 수정해줘" → 금지 (raw는 불변)

head: LLM Wiki > 트리거 경계
text: - "새 워크스페이스 만들어줘" → Workspace_Builder 영역

head: LLM Wiki > 트리거 경계
text: - "코드 짜줘" / "보고서 작성해줘" → 이 위키는 지식 *축적*용, 작업 *수행*이 아님

head: LLM Wiki > 트리거 경계
text: - "이미지 생성해줘" → 이미지 생성 도구 영역

head: LLM Wiki > 트리거 경계
text: **우선순위**: 자료는 `/ingest`(저장) → `/compile`(위키화). 질문은 `/query`. 위키가 커지면 정기 `/lint`.

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 상세 정본은 `00-system/conventions.md`. 핵심 요약:

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: **페이지 = LLM의 검색·인용 단위.** 한 페이지 = 한 주제, **~1,500 토큰 상한**, 넘으면 쪼개서 `[[링크]]`로 연결.

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 1. **BLUF** — 첫 1~3줄에 정의/답 (이 줄이 index.md 한 줄의 원천)

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 2. **타입별 고정 섹션** — ingest 때 쓸 위치가 결정적 + 섹션 단위 grep 가능

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 3. **YAML frontmatter** — `type/canonical/summary/tier/provenance/sources` (NLP 없이 필터링; `summary`는 타입 인덱스 줄로 재사용)

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 4. **`[[wiki link]]` + 정본화(aliases.md)** — 기계 traversal + 표기 흔들림(나폴레옹/Bonaparte) 해소. 정본명 첫 글자가 샤드 키.

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 5. **모든 주장에 provenance** — `[[sources/...]]` 역링크 (인용 가능 + 환각 억제)

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 6. **모순/불확실 명시 블록** — `> ⚠️ Contradiction:` (lint가 grep으로 찾음)

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 7. **안정적 kebab-case 파일명** = 엔티티명 (링크 안 깨짐 + greppable)

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: 9. **합성 파일백** — /query 결과를 `50-queries/`에 누적 (탐색이 휘발 안 함)

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: **네비게이션(검색) = 라우팅. index는 "읽는 카탈로그"가 아니라 "어디로 갈지 정하는 라우터(MOC)"다:**

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: - **2단 라우팅** — Phase A(Route): 라우터+`aliases`만 보고 의도→타입/샤드 결정(샤드 안 읽음). Phase B(Search): 지정 샤드만 펼쳐 후보 회수 → 본문+1홉.

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: - **계층 드릴다운**: 루트 라우터(주제) → 주제 라우터(타입) → 타입 인덱스/샤드 → 페이지. query당 토큰을 위키 크기와 분리.

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: - **정본화(aliases.md)**: 표기 흔들림을 정본명으로 → 정본명 첫 글자가 샤드 키.

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: - **샤딩**: 타입 인덱스가 ≤50K 토큰 넘으면 첫 글자로 분할(§8). 못 찾으면 형제 샤드 → grep → lazy.

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: - 규모가 수천+이면 선택적 외부검색(`.rag` BM25/벡터)을 1순위, 라우터→샤드는 폴백 — `conventions.md §9`.

head: LLM Wiki > 도메인 프레임워크 — 위키화 메커니즘
text: **이미지·PDF:** `20-raw/assets/`에 로컬 저장. LLM은 **텍스트를 먼저 읽고, 필요한 이미지를 별도로 본다**(2단계 — 마크다운 인라인 이미지는 한 번에 못 읽음).

head: LLM Wiki > 산출물 형식 (페이지 템플릿)
text:
| 산출물 | 템플릿 | 위치 |
