head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb
text:
This file is for agents connected to memoryweb via MCP. It tells you how to use
the tools correctly, what the tools will and won't surface, and how to behave
around archiving, drift, and knowledge gaps.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > What memoryweb is
text:
A persistent knowledge graph for a project or set of projects. You file concepts
and decisions as nodes, connect them with typed narrative edges, and retrieve
them by searching or following connections.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > What memoryweb is
text: It is called **memoryweb**. Nothing else.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Orientation at session start
text:
Always call `orient` for the relevant domain before answering questions about a
project. Do not rely on your context window or training for project state.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Orientation at session start
text:
`orient` returns all live nodes for the domain, recent activity, and a
`declared_spine` — the curated history of key decisions in chronological order.
Weigh the spine heavily when synthesising.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Orientation at session start
text: If you do not know what domains exist, call `domains` first.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Filing knowledge
text:
- `remember` — file a concept, decision, or finding. Accepts `related_to` to
  auto-connect at creation. Returns `suggested_connections` and
  `possible_duplicates` — act on these before filing more nodes.
  Supply an `items` array to file multiple nodes in one transaction.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Filing knowledge
text:
- `revise` — update `label`, `description`, `why_matters`, `tags`, or
  `occurred_at` on a live node without archiving it. Supply an `items` array for
  batch updates. Writes an audit log entry on every call. When updating a
  decision, do not paste new source material into its description — file a
  `node_kind=finding` for the evidence and connect with `depends_on` or
  `caused_by`.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Filing knowledge
text:
**Before filing a node**: search first. Infer the domain from search results;
prefer an existing domain over creating a new one. **Creating a new domain hides
the memory from every other domain's `orient` and domain-scoped `search`** —
only create one when no existing domain covers the topic. If a similar node
exists, suggest linking with `connect` rather than creating a duplicate.
Unfiled duplicates are the primary cause of orphan nodes and audit drift.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Filing knowledge
text:
**Evidence is a finding, not a footnote.** If a decision rests on something you
checked — code read, a doc fetched, a log, a search result — file that evidence
separately as `node_kind=finding` and connect the decision with `depends_on` or
`caused_by`. Do not fold raw evidence into the decision's description.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Filing knowledge
text:
**When reviewing `suggested_connections`**, check each candidate for
**contradiction** as well as relevance — a semantically close memory asserting
the opposite of what you just filed is a conflict candidate, not just a link
opportunity. If you find a contradiction, use `connect(relationship=contradicts)`
or `connect(relationship=resolved)` after user confirmation. Filing-time
`suggested_connections` is not interchangeable with `audit(mode=conflicts)` —
that mode is a separate domain-wide semantic sweep.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Filing knowledge
text:
**The `why_matters` field is the most important one** — it is what makes a node
retrievable from oblique search terms. Never skip it.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Filing knowledge
text:
**ALWAYS call `connect` for any `suggested_connections` before ending your
session.** A node with no connections is nearly worthless.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Connecting memories
text:
- `connect` — connect two nodes with a typed relationship and narrative *because*.
  Both nodes must exist first. Supply an `items` array to create multiple
  connections in one transaction.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Connecting memories
text:
- `disconnect` — remove a connection by edge ID. Hard delete — obtain the ID
  from `recall`.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Connecting memories
text:
- `suggest_connections` — read-only; returns up to 5 candidate connections from
  the same domain for a given node. Each suggestion includes a `domain` field so
  you can scope a cross-domain connect call correctly.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text: - `recall` — retrieve a node and all its connections by ID.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text:
- `search` — text and semantic search across `label`, `description`,
  `why_matters`, and `tags`. Returns `truncated: true` when results hit the
  limit. Use words that appear in stored content — not conceptual paraphrases.
  When Ollama is running, results include a `semantic_distance` field.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text:
- `history` — chronological listing with two order modes. `order=effective`
  (default): by COALESCE(occurred_at, created_at); supports `from`/`to`,
  `important_only`, `tags`. `order=modified`: by last updated (replaces the
  retired `recent` tool); supports `group_by_domain`. Returns
  `{nodes, results_truncated}` or `{groups, results_truncated}`.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text:
- `why_connected` — direct edges between two memories. Prefer
  `from_id`/`to_id` for exact pair verification; `from_label`/`to_label` for
  fuzzy lookup.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text:
- `orient` — full domain summary: rules, declared spine, significant, and
  recent sections. Includes `*_results_truncated` booleans per section.
  Cross-domain bootstrap (no domain) returns `{domains, results_truncated}`.
  When any truncation flag is true, use `search` for exhaustive retrieval.
  Includes `total_nodes` and `server_version`.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text:
- `significance` — dual-signal importance analysis. Returns four sections
  plus `declared_results_truncated`, `structural_results_truncated`,
  `uncurated_results_truncated`, and `potentially_stale_results_truncated`.
  Raise `declared_limit` or `limit` when truncated.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text:
- `visualise` — Mermaid flowchart for a domain or a single node's neighbourhood
  (pass `memory_id`). Always output the mermaid string inside a mermaid code block.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text:
**List truncation:** Multi-result tools return wrapped objects with
`results_truncated: true|false`. When true, raise `limit` (or `declared_limit`
on `significance`) and call again until false before treating the list as
complete. `audit(mode=archived)` defaults to 25 results — not a full listing.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Retrieving memories
text:
**All retrieval tools only return live nodes.** Archived nodes are invisible.
If something seems to be missing, call `audit(mode=archived)` to check whether
it was archived, or `audit(mode=stale)` to surface drift candidates.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Archiving and maintenance
text:
- `forget` — archive a single node with a reason, or un-archive with
  `restore=true`. Follow the forget protocol below.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Archiving and maintenance
text: - `forget_all` — archive multiple nodes atomically in a single call.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Archiving and maintenance
text:
- `audit` — surface nodes that need attention. All modes return wrapped
  objects with `results_truncated`:
  - `mode=stale` — `{candidates, results_truncated}` (default limit 10)
  - `mode=orphans` — `{nodes, results_truncated}` (default limit 50)
  - `mode=archived` — `{nodes, results_truncated}` (**default limit 25** —
    raise limit to enumerate all archived nodes)
  - `mode=conflicts` — `{candidates, results_truncated}` (default limit 10)
  - `mode=kind_coverage` — `{total_nodes, by_kind, legacy_dominant_pct, migration_candidates, results_truncated}` (default limit 50 on migration_candidates)

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Archiving and maintenance
text:
Run `audit(mode=orphans)`, `audit(mode=stale)`, and `audit(mode=conflicts)` as
**three separate steps** — never one combined pass or report. Orphans: resolve
every one yourself (`suggest_connections` + `connect`); only ask the user when
the target is genuinely ambiguous. Stale: fix duplicates and superseded labels
with `revise` without asking; genuine `contradicts` edges require user
confirmation before adjudicating via `connect(relationship=resolved)` (verify
the exact pair via `recall` first). Before escalating a contradiction, confirm
no `resolved`/`resolved_by`/`supersedes` edge already links the two IDs — that
edge is the canonical close signal; a `RESOLVED` label prefix is a legacy
backstop only. **Say nothing about audits if all three come back clean** — no
routine status lines. Only speak up for an unresolved orphan or a live
contradiction awaiting the user's decision.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Core tool guide > Domain management
text:
- `domains` — domain admin and discovery. Default (`action=list` or omit):
  all domains with live nodes plus registered aliases. Also:
  `action=add_alias`, `remove_alias`, `resolve`, `rename` (in-place domain
  rename — fails if target domain already has nodes; use `merge-domains` CLI).

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Relationship types
text:
| Type | Use when |
|------|----------|
| `caused_by` | B was caused by A |
| `led_to` | A caused B |
| `blocked_by` | A is blocked by B |
| `unblocks` | A unblocks B |
| `connects_to` | General association |
| `contradicts` | A and B conflict |
| `depends_on` | A requires B |
| `resolved` / `resolved_by` / `supersedes` | Adjudicates a `contradicts` pair (additive — does not remove the original edge) |
| `is_example_of` | A illustrates B |
| `governed_by` | A must satisfy standing rule or constraint B |

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Archiving — the forget protocol
text:
**Decision:** archiving is a deliberate, user-confirmed action. Never archive
a node unilaterally.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Archiving — the forget protocol
text: Follow this protocol exactly:

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Archiving — the forget protocol
text:
1. **Only consider archiving** after `audit(mode=stale)` surfaces a node as a
   candidate, or the user explicitly says something is stale, wrong, or no
   longer applies.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Archiving — the forget protocol
text:
2. **Present the node** with the reason it is a candidate and ask explicitly:
   *"Should I archive this?"* Do not assume the answer is yes.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Archiving — the forget protocol
text:
3. **Wait for unambiguous confirmation.** Acceptable: *"yes"*, *"archive it"*,
   *"go ahead"*. Not acceptable: *"that's probably outdated"*, *"it might be
   stale"*, *"maybe"*.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Archiving — the forget protocol
text: 4. **Never archive based on casual mention or implication.**

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Archiving — the forget protocol
text:
5. **After archiving**, tell the user:
   - The node ID
   - That it can be un-archived at any time with `forget(restore=true)`

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Drift — the review protocol
text:
`audit(mode=stale)` surfaces nodes that may be stale, contradicted, or
duplicated. It does not make decisions — it returns candidates for review.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Drift — the review protocol
text: After audit returns results:

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Drift — the review protocol
text:
1. Present each candidate with its reason (e.g. *"explicitly marked as
   contradicting"*, *"label suggests superseded"*, *"open question older than
   30 days"*, *"possible duplicate"*).

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Drift — the review protocol
text: 2. For each candidate, ask the user: *"Should I archive this?"*

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Drift — the review protocol
text: 3. Do not archive anything until the user confirms each one individually.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Drift — the review protocol
text: 4. *"That looks stale"* from the user is not confirmation. Ask explicitly.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Drift — the review protocol
text:
5. If the user says *"archive all of them"*, read back the full list and
   ask: *"Archive all of these?"* before acting.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Domain conventions
text: - Use `domain` to separate concerns: `deep-game`, `sedex`, `general`, etc.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Domain conventions
text:
- Register short aliases with `domains(action=add_alias)` so both `dg` and
  `deep-game` work.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Domain conventions
text:
- An unscoped search crosses all domains — use the domain param when you know
  which project you are in.

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Hidden archived nodes — what to do when something is missing
text: If a user asks about something and you cannot find it:

head: AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents using memoryweb > Hidden archived nodes — what to do when something is missing
text: 1. Try a broader search (drop specific terms, try synonyms).

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
Bugs here corrupt people's pipelines. Corruption-class bugs are sev-0: drop everything, fix,
postmortem, regression test.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
1. **Never acknowledge a record upstream before it is durably handled downstream.** Ack
   propagation is end-to-end; no intermediate component may ack early for throughput. Any
   batching/buffering change must prove ack correctness under crash.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
2. **Positions/offsets are monotonic and crash-safe.** A restart must never skip records
   (at-least-once) or corrupt position state. Position serialization changes require a versioned
   migration path and an upgrade test.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
3. **At-least-once is the floor.** Any path that could drop a record without delivering it or
   routing it to a DLQ is a data-loss bug — including error, shutdown, and rebalance paths.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
4. **Ordering guarantees are per-source-partition and documented.** Changes that could reorder
   records within a partition key require a design doc and explicit sign-off.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
5. **State and checkpoint writes are atomic.** Torn writes on crash must be impossible
   (write-ahead + rename, or the store's transactional API). Every state feature ships with a
   kill-mid-write recovery test.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
6. **Schema handling never silently mangles data.** Unknown fields, type mismatches, and drift
   follow the configured policy (halt/DLQ/evolve) — never silent coercion or truncation.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
7. **Shutdown is graceful by default.** SIGTERM drains in-flight records and checkpoints before
   exit. `kill -9` at any instant must be recoverable without loss — and we test exactly that.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Data integrity invariants (non-negotiable)
text:
Where code upholds one of these, say so at the enforcement site:
`// Invariant 1: ack only after destination confirms durable write`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Architecture & design discipline (staff/principal bar)
text: We're building infrastructure people bet their data on. Design like it.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Architecture & design discipline (staff/principal bar)
text:
- **Design doc before code for anything non-trivial.** Non-trivial = touches the data path,
  changes a public contract (protocol, config schema, CLI, error codes, state format), adds a
  subsystem, or exceeds ~2 days. The doc goes in `docs/design-documents/` and must cover:
  problem, constraints, alternatives (≥2, with why they lost), failure modes, upgrade/rollback,
  observability. A design doc that doesn't enumerate failure modes is not done.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Architecture & design discipline (staff/principal bar)
text:
- **ADRs for decisions.** Every significant architectural decision gets an immutable ADR in
  `docs/architecture-decision-records/`. Future contributors should reconstruct _why_ without
  archaeology.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Architecture & design discipline (staff/principal bar)
text:
- **Invariants are documented and enforced** — in package docs, with assertions/tests, not
  comments alone. If you can't state the invariant, the design isn't finished.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Architecture & design discipline (staff/principal bar)
text:
- **Think in failure modes first.** For any data-path change, answer before writing code: crash
  mid-operation? network partition? duplicate delivery? out-of-order? malformed input? disk
  full? The happy path is the easy 20%.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Architecture & design discipline (staff/principal bar)
text:
- **Backward compatibility is a design input.** Serialized state, pipeline configs, connector
  protocol, and registry format must be readable by N+1 versions with an explicit deprecation
  policy (announce → warn → remove, minimum two minor versions).

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Architecture & design discipline (staff/principal bar)
text:
- **No speculative generality.** Interfaces earn their existence with two real implementations
  or a design doc explaining why the seam matters. YAGNI violations are review blockers.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Architecture & design discipline (staff/principal bar)
text:
- **Simplicity is the review criterion.** If a reviewer can't explain the approach back in two
  sentences, it's too clever. Prefer boring, obvious code.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text:

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text:
- **Errors are API:** every user-facing error gets a stable error code, the failing config path,
  and a suggested fix. Machine-actionable errors are a product feature (agents consume them).

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text: - **CLI output:** every command supports `--json`. New commands ship with it, not after.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text:
- **Commits/PRs:** conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`). Small,
  reviewable PRs — split large work. PR descriptions state the roadmap item they advance.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text:
- **Breaking changes:** connector protocol, pipeline config schema, and error codes are public
  contracts. Breaking changes require a versioning plan and migration notes in the PR.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text:
- **Releases:** monthly release train. Changelogs from conventional commits; release notes a
  human would want to read. See `docs/releases.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text:
- **Performance:** claims require benchi runs, committed configs, reproducible results. Never
  assert numbers without a benchmark in the repo.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text:
- **State layer discipline:** local embedded KV state, checkpointed with the pipeline. No
  distributed snapshots, no pluggable state backends, no event-time watermark machinery. If a
  design doc starts growing Flink features, stop and flag it.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > Engineering conventions
text:
- **Docs move with code:** a feature PR without docs is incomplete. Update `conduit.io` docs
  source AND `llms.txt` when behavior changes — maintained together, always.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process
text:
**Automated gates:** lint, race detector, unit + integration, conventional-commit check — all live
and blocking. Coverage floor and the benchi regression check are **not live** (no CI job
implements either yet — see Process maturity below). Dependency vulnerability scanning
(govulncheck) is **live and blocking as a ratchet**: it fails a PR that makes a NEW vulnerability
reachable, while the 4 remaining pre-existing findings are held in a justified baseline — see Process
maturity below.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process
text:
**Review conduct:** review the tests first — if they wouldn't catch the bug this PR could
introduce, request changes before reading the implementation. Check error paths line by line
(that's where data loss lives). Verify invariant comments at touched enforcement sites still
hold. "Looks good" is not a review; state what you verified.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process
text:
**AI-authored code (most of ours):** Claude does an adversarial self-review pass before opening
any PR — re-read the diff hunting for the bug, specifically error paths, concurrency, resource
cleanup, and the data-integrity invariants. Findings and resolutions go in the PR description.
Self-review is not review; a separate session (or human) reviews with fresh context. Any
uncertainty about behavior under failure is stated, not assumed away.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process
text:
**Regression response:** any regression that reaches a release triggers a blameless postmortem
in `docs/postmortems/` and produces at least one new automated check.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process > Process maturity (be honest about which gates are actually live)
text: Do not claim a bar is met when it structurally isn't. Mark PRs against what's real today.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process > Process maturity (be honest about which gates are actually live)
text:
| Gate | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Lint, race detector, unit + integration, conventional commits | **live now** |
| Design doc / ADR before non-trivial work | **live now** |
| Adversarial self-review on AI PRs | **live now** |
| Human (DeVaris) sign-off on Tier 1 | **live now** |
| Coverage floor enforcement | **NOT live** (was "by Phase 1"; Phase 1 closed at v0.19 and this never shipped). No CI job measures or enforces coverage today. Targeted at v0.21 |
| benchi regression gate | **NOT live** (was "by Phase 1"). No workflow runs benchi; the numbers that exist are per-PR runs a human read. Targeted at v0.21, where the arch-v2 flip makes a standing regression gate load-bearing |
| Dependency vulnerability scan (govulncheck) | **live now, blocking as a ratchet** (`.github/workflows/govulncheck.yml` + `.github/govulncheck-allowlist.txt`, added 2026-08-21). Runs on every PR, on push to `main`, and nightly (05:15) via `govulncheck -format json ./...` — reachability-aware, so it reports only vulnerabilities this codebase's call graph can actually reach, not every CVE in the dependency tree. **It fails when a called-level vulnerability appears that is not in the baseline.** The baseline held 24 findings reachable on `main` at introduction; the 20 Go standard library entries were cleared 2026-10-07 by the go 1.25.14 bump (#2914). It now holds 4, each with a written justification beside it: 1 `golang.org/x/crypto` openpgp (unmaintained upstream) and 3 `github.com/hamba/avro/v2` (upstream archived 2026-01-18, #2817; cleared by the v0.21 connector sweep to `iskorotkov/avro`). Failing on ANY finding would have failed every PR for problems unrelated to its diff; report-only would have been green and therefore silent. To tighten further: clear baseline entries (the job reports which are already fixed) and add `govulncheck` to `main`'s required contexts |
| Property + fuzz tests on data-path/boundaries | **partially live** (was "by Phase 1"). 9 packages carry `Fuzz*` targets (egress policy/IP guard, registry envelope/trust/bounded-fetch, conduiterr status, fuzzymatch, diff) and their seed corpora run inside the normal `test` job — so a seed regression IS caught. What is missing is the testing-standards split: no short-fuzz CI job, no scheduled long run, and no property-based framework (rapid/gopter) in the tree at all |
| Chaos suite (`tests/chaos`) nightly | **live now + REQUIRED** (`.github/workflows/chaos.yml`) — nightly + every PR via the always-report/fail-closed detector (the job runs on all PRs; the SIGKILL/FIFO-ack no-infra suite executes only when a data-path tree changed, fail-closed on any diff ambiguity). `tests/chaos (race, x3)` **is** in `main`'s required branch-protection contexts (blocking) — the earlier "not yet required" note was stale. `bundle-e2e` **is now required too**. `rag-e2e` **is now required too** (verified against the live branch-protection API 2026-08-21; the earlier "one toggle away, held for a de-flake soak" note was stale). `rag-template-e2e` IS path-filtered, so it cannot become required until it is restructured to the always-report/fail-closed pattern; a path-filtered workflow never reports on unrelated PRs and would block every merge permanently. Required contexts on `main` today: `test`, `golangci-lint`, `validate-generated-files`, `build (linux/386)`, `docker build`, `tests/chaos (race, x3)`, `bundle-e2e`, `rag-e2e` |
| Upgrade/downgrade tests gating releases | by Phase 2 |
| 24h soak gating every release | by Phase 2 |

  of the gate. Wait for green.

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process > Merging (solo-maintainer workflow)
text:
- Bug fixes include the regression test that would have caught the bug, verified to fail without

- For a Tier 1 (data-path) change, any _unresolved_ uncertainty about behavior under failure is

head: CLAUDE.md — Conduit > PR review process > Merging (solo-maintainer workflow)

admin-merge path is for maintainer-authored work that has cleared the bar above.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses
text:
This directory contains a native implementation of the AI-DLC (AI-Driven
Development Life Cycle) methodology that ships to many CLI harnesses — today
Claude Code, Kiro CLI, Kiro IDE, Codex CLI, Cursor, opencode, and GitHub Copilot, and any capable CLI you port it to — from
a single hand-authored source.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text: **The human drives the engine. Tools for determinism. LLM for knowledge. Human for judgement.**

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
Every design, change, review finding, and question in this repository follows
these four tenets, in this order. The first wins any conflict: no tool
determinism, guard, or security concern overrides what the person explicitly
asked for in their own project.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
- **The human drives the engine.** AI-DLC is a tool the person runs on their
  own machine, in a project they chose, with their own coding agent, to drive
  their own work. When they ask for something, the engine does it and says in
  one line what happened. Their machine, shell and environment, git setup and
  hooks, editor and host-tool settings, installed plugins, the project's files,
  and their own words are theirs: AI-DLC works with them as they are and never
  overrides or second-guesses them for its own safety. AI-DLC owns its engine,
  its record of the work, what it tells the agent, and what it ships, and it
  answers for those.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
- **Tools for determinism.** The engine and hooks do what must be exact and
  repeatable: record that a message arrived through the person's own prompt, in
  order, and not from the agent or a helper (an observed interaction, not proof
  of identity); keep the person's words as the host delivers them; record state
  and the audit trail; mark steps; keep files; and own every chain, token,
  receipt, and part count. Control state lives in the tools, not in the agent's
  memory.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
- **LLM for knowledge.** The agent does what needs understanding: reading what
  the person meant from their own words in context, answering their questions,
  applying their instructions, and making the calls that knowledge settles, such
  as how to build what was approved. A directive names the next exact step, and
  the agent runs a command the engine issued exactly as given; it never invents,
  rebuilds, interprets, or holds onto a token beyond that directive, and never
  decides flow by how a sentence of prose ends.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
- **Human for judgement.** Where a decision needs judgement, the person makes
  it: what to build, whether the work is right, what to trade off, and when to
  stop. Nothing that knowledge or the tools can settle is put to the person, so
  their attention goes only where they alone can decide.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
Think of AI-DLC as a software factory the person runs. Scopes are the production
lines, stages are the stations on a line, and agents are the workers at each
station. Workers make the calls their station needs; the person makes the
judgement calls. Guards protect the person from workers doing the wrong thing;
they never stand between the person and what the person asks for.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
The engine exists to enforce the will of the human, never to overrule it. When
the person explicitly asks for something, the flow does it and says in one line
what happened: no confirmation question unless the action cannot be undone and
is not what they asked for, no re-asking what they already said, and no refusal
that puts the engine's rules ahead of their words. Follow up only when their
intent is genuinely unclear. Gates exist to collect the person's judgement, so
when the person decides (approve, change, skip, jump, or switch a check off),
the flow records that decision through its own mechanism instead of refusing
it. An explicit request means the person's own words, never the agent's account
of them. Exact answers such as "Approve", an option number, or a slash command
are shortcuts the tools may read; anything else is the agent's to understand. A
tool that judges the meaning of a person's words, or that second-guesses an
explicit request, is a defect, however safe it looks.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
**Guards.** A guard is a deterministic check over recorded facts, aimed at an
agent's action, never at a person's message. Its refusal names the exact next
step. The person's plain request lifts it, and the lift is recorded with their
words. When a guard or tool loses its own coordination bookkeeping (a claim on a
command, a busy lock, a project-identity hash that no longer matches), it fails
toward the person's last recorded instruction with a one-line note, never into a
re-ask, a refusal, or a loop with no way out. Evidence that selects or binds a
human decision (an approval record, the plan fingerprint, the marker naming the
approved target) is different: it never falls back to a guess. Its owning
mechanism decides whether the approval still holds (for Plan Approval, the
contract in `docs/reference/06-hooks-and-tools.md`, "Plan-Approval Guard
Hook"), and the flow never loops on it and never asks the person to approve
again what that mechanism says still holds.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
**What guards are for.** Guards keep an honest agent on the person's path when
it runs ahead, skips a step, or misreads (no build before the plan is approved,
no decision recorded that the person did not make, no lost words). They are not
a jail for an agent that deliberately works around them: the host tool's own
permission prompts, the plan question, and the person watching are that layer.
The person asking for something is never a bypass. AI-DLC's own engine must
never leak the person's secrets, run a command nobody asked for, write or delete
outside the project, or change the install or the person's settings unasked;
that is AI-DLC answering for its own code, not defending against the person's
setup or the project they chose to work in.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
**One owner per rule.** Every invariant (approval, transition, presence, the
plan fingerprint) has one owner and one shared check. Enforcing that check at
several boundaries (a hook for fast feedback, a command-line floor where hooks
cannot run) is fine; a second, independently written version of the same rule
is a defect, however safe it looks.

head: AI-DLC — one core, many harnesses > Tenets: the human drives the engine
text:
**Prior judgement.** A setting the team explicitly locked (for example a strict
Guard Policy held in memory) and an unattended run are human judgement already
made, and they outrank one person's chat request. The flow says in one line that
it is locked, where, and that changing that file changes it; it never loops or
refuses silently. Defaults are not locks: the person can change a scope, a
ceremony, a per-intent setting, or the conversation language whenever they ask.

text: - `plugins/<name>/` — **Optional, owned AIDLC plugins** (the plugin mechanism; design in the single chapter `docs/reference/18-plugin-mechanism.md`, authoring guide `docs/harness-engineering/10-authoring-a-plugin.md`). self-custodial, offchain protocol built directly on Bitcoin. The plugin and its

target **.NET 8**.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Conceptual Overview
text:
The plugin enables merchants to accept Bitcoin payments through Ark, using
Virtual UTXOs (VTXOs) for instant, low-cost transactions that can later be
anchored onchain for finality.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Supported Flows
text: The plugin supports these key flows:

head: NArk Repo Guide > Supported Flows
text: - **Ark-native**: direct offchain VTXO-to-VTXO payments within the Ark network.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Supported Flows
text:
- **Auto-sweep**: a store's balance is forwarded to its configured destination
  by the SDK's settlement subsystem (`ISettlementConfigProvider` +
  `DestinationSweepSettlementService`), not by a plugin-owned sweep policy.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Supported Flows
text:
- **Boarding Address Flow**: users enter the Ark system by funding a Taproot
  "boarding address," which is converted into a VTXO with help from the Arkade
  Operator. If the Operator is unresponsive, users can reclaim funds
  unilaterally after a timelock.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Supported Flows
text:
- **Arkade asset acceptance**: a store can settle invoices in a
  merchant-declared Arkade asset at a merchant-declared rate.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Supported Flows
text:
Each flow is implemented as a type of contract, created using a wallet defined
by a Miniscript descriptor and an address derivation index.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Ark Concepts
text: - **VTXOs**: Offchain Bitcoin outputs secured via collaborative (user + operator) and unilateral (timelocked) Taproot paths. These are the basic payment units in Ark.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Ark Concepts
text: - **Contracts**: Payment flows are modeled as Taproot contracts generated from a descriptor and derivation index. Each contract results in a unique payment address.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Ark Concepts
text: - **Boarding Addresses**: Onchain Taproot addresses that act as trust-minimized entry points to Ark. When funded, they allow the plugin to request the Arkade Operator to convert the UTXO into a VTXO.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Ark Concepts
text: - **Commitment Transactions**: Onchain transactions created by the operator that anchor offchain VTXO state into Bitcoin, securing it with Bitcoin-level finality.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Arkade OS Integration
text: Arkade extends Ark with programmability and verifiability. It introduces:

head: NArk Repo Guide > Arkade OS Integration
text: - **Arkade Script**: A scripting layer that expands Bitcoin Script for more expressive offchain contracts.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Arkade OS Integration
text: - **Arkade Signer**: A TEE-secured module that co-signs VTXO transactions and prevents double-spends through hardware-enforced integrity.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Arkade OS Integration
text: The plugin integrates with Arkade to:

head: NArk Repo Guide > Arkade OS Integration
text: - Generate boarding addresses and contracts

head: NArk Repo Guide > Arkade OS Integration
text: - Detect onchain deposits and initiate VTXO creation

head: NArk Repo Guide > Arkade OS Integration
text: - Subscribe to contract activity from the operator

head: NArk Repo Guide > Arkade OS Integration
text: - Anchor contracts onchain when requested or required

head: NArk Repo Guide > Design Considerations
text: - Wallets use Miniscript descriptors and must manage address derivation state safely.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Design Considerations
text: - All contracts must enforce a secure unilateral exit path for the user.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Design Considerations
text: - Boarding addresses must be monitored and resolved into VTXOs.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Design Considerations
text: - Payment detection is event-driven, based on Arkade Operator subscriptions.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Design Considerations
text: - Contracts may remain offchain until anchored, enabling both instant and deferred finality models.

head: NArk Repo Guide > Problem Domain Summary
text:
This plugin bridges Bitcoin-native offchain protocols with BTCPayServer's
payment system. It manages:

head: NArk Repo Guide > Problem Domain Summary
text: - Onboarding via boarding addresses

head: NArk Repo Guide > Problem Domain Summary
text: - Contract generation and tracking

head: NArk Repo Guide > Problem Domain Summary
text: - Offchain event monitoring through Arkade

head: NArk Repo Guide > Problem Domain Summary
text: - Invoice status updates based on offchain state transitions

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository Layout — Two Implementations
text:
New feature work goes to Go. Apply a Python change only if it is a bugfix
(on `python-froster`), and consider whether it needs a Go counterpart.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository Layout — Two Implementations > Documentation policy
text:
`README.md` on `main` is the **user-facing product doc** and must read as
if froster has always been this single Go binary — no "two
implementations" framing, no mention that it was ever written in Python, no
links to the `python-froster` branch. The **only** place the Go rewrite is
acknowledged is the "Deferred features" section, which lists what earlier
(pre-v0.23) releases had that this one doesn't yet (`config` wizard,
`update`, `test`, NIH grant search TUI, EC2/SES/Cost-Explorer restore) and
notes that archives from any earlier version restore unchanged. When
correcting facts in `README.md`, adjust wording for the single-binary
reality (binary download, manual `config.ini`, built-in crawler/rclone)
rather than adding implementation-history commentary.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository Layout — Two Implementations > Documentation policy
text:
This restriction is specific to `README.md`. Engineering docs — this file,
`go/README.md`, `GO-ARCHITECTURE.md`, `go/docs/python-behavior-spec.md` —
are expected to reference `python-froster` freely; the facts there (fixture
regeneration, behavioral parity, the rewrite rationale) require it.

text:

transfer (Minio port 9101), awsx (9301), workflow archive→delete→restore

head: CLAUDE.md > Go Implementation (`go/`) > Critical rules
text:
- **Do NOT bump aws-sdk-go-v2 versions independently** — they must track
  rclone's own pins (rclone's s3 backend breaks otherwise; see the NOTE in
  `go/go.mod`). When bumping rclone, re-align the SDK versions to rclone's go.mod.

head: CLAUDE.md > Go Implementation (`go/`) > Critical rules
text:
- Behavioral parity with Python is the prime directive: exact messages,
  step order, exit codes, file formats. Divergences require a
  `DOCUMENTED DEVIATION` comment and an entry in go/README.md's deviations
  list. Python's own *bugs* are generally not reproduced (see that list).

head: CLAUDE.md > Go Implementation (`go/`) > Critical rules
text:

  `GOOS=linux/darwin × GOARCH=amd64/arm64` with `CGO_ENABLED=0`
  (CI enforces via `.github/workflows/build-go.yml`).

These are the same items listed in `README.md`'s "Deferred features"

head: CLAUDE.md > Go Implementation (`go/`) > Release process
text: Tag-triggered via `.github/workflows/release-go.yml`:

head: CLAUDE.md > Go Implementation (`go/`) > Release process
text:
Builds all four `GOOS`/`GOARCH` targets (static, `-trimpath -ldflags "-s -w"`,

publishes a GitHub release with the binaries attached and notes

and `gh release view vX.Y.Z`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Python froster (frozen, branch `python-froster`)
text:
For anything Python: check out that branch (or a worktree). Its own
CLAUDE.md, README, tests (`python3 -m unittest discover tests/`), its own
`install.sh`, and PyPI release process live there — entirely separate from
the root `install.sh` on `main`, which installs the Go binary (see below).

head: CLAUDE.md > `install.sh` (root, `main` branch)
text:
Installs the Go binary directly: detects OS/arch, resolves the latest (or
`--version`-pinned) release via GitHub's `/releases/latest` redirect (no
API/JSON parsing), downloads the matching `froster-<ver>-<os>-<arch>` asset,
verifies it against the release's sha256 checksums file, and installs to
`~/.local/bin` (if on PATH) / `~/bin` / `/usr/local/bin` (if root) /
`--dir` override. Test changes to it against a real release before pushing —
see the manual test recipe used during development (HOME/PATH overrides,
`fakeroot` for the root branch) rather than assuming syntax correctness.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide
text:
This file provides quick, practical guidance for coding agents working in this
repo. It is intentionally short and focused on day-to-day work.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Project overview
text:
- Apache Pinot is a real-time distributed OLAP datastore for low-latency
  analytics over streaming and batch data.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Project overview
text:
- Core runtime roles: broker (query routing), server (segment storage/execution),
  controller (cluster metadata/management), minion (async tasks).

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-broker: broker query planning and scatter-gather.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-controller: controller APIs, table/segment metadata, Helix management.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-server: server query execution, segment loading, indexing.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-minion: background tasks (segment conversion, purge, etc).

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-common / pinot-spi: shared utils, config, and SPI interfaces.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-segment-local / pinot-segment-spi: segment generation, indexes, storage.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-query-planner / pinot-query-runtime: multi-stage query (MSQ) engine.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-connectors: external tooling to connect to Pinot

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-plugins: all pinot plugins.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-tools: CLI and quickstart scripts.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-integration-tests: end-to-end validation suites.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: - pinot-distribution: packaging artifacts.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Repository layout (high level)
text: When locating a plugin implementation, consult [kb/plugin-modules.md](kb/plugin-modules.md).

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Build and test
text: - Build JDK: Use JDK 25+ for Pinot services and the default build; client and SPI artifacts still target Java 11 bytecode.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Build and test
text: - Runtime JRE: Broker/server/controller/minion run on Java 25+.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Build and test
text: - Default to affected modules and their dependencies: `./mvnw -pl <module> -am test`.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Build and test
text:
- Faster module build: `./mvnw -pl <module> -am verify -Ppinot-fastdev`. This profile skips style and license checks;
  it does not replace applicable pre-push validation.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Build and test
text:
- Single test example: `./mvnw -pl pinot-segment-local -am -Dtest=RangeIndexTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false test`.
  See [kb/skills/run-test.md](kb/skills/run-test.md) for dependency availability and evidence reuse.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Build and test
text: - Full reactor build, when the task requires it: `./mvnw clean install`.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Build and test
text: - Full binary/shaded distribution, when required: `./mvnw clean install -DskipTests -Pbin-dist -Pbuild-shaded-jar`.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Build and test
text: - Local cluster startup: follow [kb/skills/quickstart.md](kb/skills/quickstart.md) for the smallest required build and readiness checks.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Integration tests
text: - Single integration test example: `./mvnw -pl pinot-integration-tests -am -Dtest=OfflineClusterIntegrationTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false test`

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - Add class-level Javadoc for new classes; describe behavior and thread-safety.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - Use Javadoc comments with either `/** ... */` or `///` syntax (per JEP-467); service code targets Java 25 by default.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - Keep license headers on all new source files.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - Use `./mvnw license:format` to add headers to new files.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - Preserve backward compatibility across mixed-version broker/server/controller.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - Prefer imports over fully qualified class names (e.g., use `import com.foo.Bar` and refer to `Bar`, not `com.foo.Bar` inline).

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - In tests, statically import methods from `Assert` and `Mockito`; do not qualify calls with `Assert.` or `Mockito.`.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - Import `FieldSpec.DataType` and `DataSchema.ColumnDataType` directly and use their simple names at call sites.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text:
- Keep a ternary expression on one line when it fits. Otherwise, put `? <true-expression>` and
  `: <false-expression>` on separate lines.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text:
- Prefer `List.of()`, `Set.of()`, and `Map.of()` for non-null immutable collection literals. Checkstyle blocks
  `Collections.emptyList()`, `Collections.emptySet()`, and `Collections.emptyMap()`; use `List.of()`, `Set.of()`, and
  `Map.of()` instead. Do not add blanket bans for `Collections.singleton*`; use them only when an element/key/value
  argument is intentionally null because `List.of(null)`, `Set.of(null)`, and `Map.of(...)` with null keys or values
  throw `NullPointerException`. Before replacing empty collection factories, check whether the value flows to
  mutating callers. See
  `kb/code-review-principles.md` C7.12.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Coding conventions and hygiene
text: - Prefer targeted unit tests; use integration tests when behavior crosses roles.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Commit messages
text:
- Do not include `Co-authored-by` trailers that reference AI tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot).
  - **Why**: These trailers propagate into squash-merge commits on GitHub, making the project history appear AI-authored rather than human-authored.
  - **Fix**: Omit the `Co-authored-by` line entirely when committing.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Checkstyle config
text: - Checkstyle rules and related config files live under `config/`.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Checkstyle config
text: - Use the Maven wrapper (`./mvnw` on Unix-like systems or `mvnw.cmd` on Windows) to run `spotless:apply` to format code and `checkstyle:check` to validate style.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Checkstyle config
text: - Run `./mvnw license:check` to validate license headers.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Pre-commit checks
text:
Before pushing, follow [kb/skills/precommit.md](kb/skills/precommit.md) for affected-module formatting, license headers,
checkstyle, and license validation. That procedure defines applicability, execution order, evidence reuse, and when
compiler warning checks are needed. Fix failures within the authorized scope; do not push with applicable checks failing.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Change guidance
text: - Query changes often touch broker planning and server execution; verify both.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Change guidance
text:
- Segment/index changes usually live under `pinot-segment-local` and
  `pinot-segment-spi`.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Change guidance
text: - Config or API changes should update relevant configs and docs where applicable.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Reference docs
text: - `README.md` for build and quickstart details.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Reference docs
text: - `CONTRIBUTING.md` for style, licensing, and contribution guidance.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Knowledge base (tool-neutral)
text:
The `kb/` directory holds AI-optimized procedures and reference material that any
coding agent (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, GPT, Qwen, Gemini, etc.) can read.
Claude Code's `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and `.claude/agents/<name>.md`
files are thin pointers that delegate to the kb/ procedures — non-Claude agents
should read kb/ directly.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Knowledge base (tool-neutral)
text:
- `kb/skills/` — operational procedures and review checklists. See
  [`kb/skills/README.md`](kb/skills/README.md) for the index. Each file is
  self-contained; read it and follow it when your task matches the skill name.
  - Operations: `precommit`, `run-test`, `quickstart`, `bench-compare`,
    `flaky-analyze`.
  - Review (eight domains, one per file): `review-config-backcompat`,
    `review-concurrency-state`, `review-architecture`, `review-performance`,
    `review-correctness-nulls`, `review-testing`, `review-naming-api`,
    `review-process-scope`.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Knowledge base (tool-neutral)
text:
- `kb/agents/code-reviewer.md` — review procedure that selects relevant domains,
  delegates substantial independent checks, and verifies consolidated findings.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Knowledge base (tool-neutral)
text:
- `kb/code-review-principles.md` — Pinot-specific review principles cited by id
  (e.g. `C2.4`, `C6.1`) from the review skills.

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Knowledge base (tool-neutral)
text: - `kb/claude.md` — kb/ authoring rules (one source of truth, terse, AI-optimized).

head: Apache Pinot - AGENTS Guide > Knowledge base (tool-neutral)
text:
**For non-Claude agents:** when a task matches a skill name (e.g. user asks for
a pre-commit check, a benchmark comparison, a flaky-test investigation, or a
code review), read the corresponding `kb/skills/<name>.md` and follow its
procedure. For a full code review, follow `kb/agents/code-reviewer.md` and cover
the domains relevant to the diff; small changes can be reviewed directly.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Druks runs durable agent apps on DBOS and Postgres. It owns workflow execution,
persisted state, events, gates, webhooks, sandbox access, and the shared
dashboard. Apps are standalone Python packages. They register through the
`druks.apps` entry point. `software_factory` is the bundled reference app for
coding work through GitHub pull requests.

text: Start with `README.md`, then read only the material relevant to the task:

text: - App contracts or the public author surface: `docs/writing-an-app.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text: - App pages, blocks, values, fields, actions, and liveness: `docs/druks-ui.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text: - Configuration or environment variables: `docs/configuration.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text: - Local install and operations: `docs/full-local.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text: - Remote deployment: `docs/deployment.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text: - Failure diagnosis: `docs/troubleshooting.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text: - Backend contribution, migrations, or verification: `docs/development.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text: - Migration head: `alembic heads`, not a scan of `backend/migrations/versions/`

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text: - Shared SPA work: `frontend/README.md`

text: - Documentation navigation and audience ownership: `docs/index.md`

text: - The checklist and craft gate every change is held to: `.druks/review/checklist.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Read map
text:
For app-surface changes, inspect the proof app at
`backend/tests/druks-field_notes/` and its tests as well as the author guide.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Keep platform and app ownership explicit. Keep GitHub issue, branch, PR, and
  coding-agent policy in `software_factory`, not in Druks core.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Describe durability precisely. Druks reuses completed durable checkpoints
  during replay. An interrupted operation can run again. Do not imply
  arbitrary-line resume or exactly-once external side effects.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text: - Derive `Run.state` from DBOS workflow status. Do not add a second writable state mirror.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Import the public concern namespaces documented in `docs/writing-an-app.md`.
  Do not import Druks internals.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Keep backend app discovery in runtime packaging. Keep shared-dashboard app UI
  registration in the frontend build. Keep standalone `dist/` delivery separate.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Keep generic agent, harness, workspace, sandbox, event, gate, webhook, and
  settings plumbing in Druks. Keep domain-specific policy in the app.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- One Druks installation serves one organization. Execution defaults and agent
  overrides are shared. Accounts own credentials, personal preferences, and run
  attribution. Do not add personal execution defaults.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Grow the author surface by parameter, not by namespace. If the SDK lacks a
  capability, widen the primitive that owns it. Add a keyword argument or a
  method to the class that holds the data. Do not add a namespace, facade,
  context object, or one-use helper module.

text:

  `druks.workflows`, `druks.workspaces`, `druks.agents`, `druks.events`,

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Derive liveness from run state. Do not mirror it in a column. Store an external
  outcome after its owner announces it. Do not infer that outcome from run
  lifecycle. A merge can occur after Druks stops the related run.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Use `@step` to mark a replay checkpoint, not an expensive call. On replay the body
  re-executes from the top and completed steps return cached results, so code outside a
  step runs again. Moving the boundary changes correctness, not performance.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:

  Do not give either one a durable column, row lock, or in-process lock.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text: - Do not add a store before something reads it.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text: - Put only identity and facts in a read-side field. Keep UI wording in the app pages.

head: AGENTS.md > Architectural boundaries
text:
- Give a shared resource one global registry. When a second
  consumer needs a different answer, add a scoping axis. Do not add one in anticipation.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Overview
text:
MetaEdit is an Obsidian community plugin for managing note metadata. It edits
YAML frontmatter and inline `key:: value` fields, and provides Auto Properties,
Progress Properties, Ignored Properties, edit-mode handling (single/multi
values), a Kanban board helper that updates linked notes when a card changes
lane, and a small public API for other plugins.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text:
Source lives in `src/`. Plugin registration and lifecycle wiring are in
`src/main.ts`; metadata read/write logic is in `src/metaController.ts` and
`src/parser.ts`; the public API is in `src/MetaEditApi.ts` / `src/IMetaEditApi.ts`;
settings are under `src/Settings/`; Svelte modal UI is under `src/Modals/`;
on-modify automators (Kanban helper, progress properties) are under
`src/automators/`; logging is under `src/logger/`; shared types are under
`src/Types/`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text:
Tests live next to the code (`src/**/*.test.ts`), in `__tests__/`, and alongside
the E2E harness scripts (`scripts/**/*.test.ts`). The shared jsdom-safe Obsidian
stub is `tests/obsidian-stub.ts`. The live Obsidian E2E suite is under
`tests/e2e/`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text:
Generated artifacts: `main.js` (and its source map) are git-ignored and built
into the repo root for release packaging, not hand-edited. `styles.css` is a
hand-written, committed release asset.

head: Repository Guidelines > Tooling & GitHub
text: - Use `pnpm` for package management and scripts. Avoid npm/yarn/bun.

head: Repository Guidelines > Tooling & GitHub
text: - Use the GitHub CLI (`gh`) for issues, PRs, and releases.

text:

  the shared release pipeline can determine versions. The PR title becomes the
  squash-merge commit and drives the released version.

head: Repository Guidelines > Tooling & GitHub
text:

  merge waiting for self-approval.

text: Before opening a PR, run the CI-equivalent checks locally:

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text:
Tab indentation, LF endings, UTF-8 (see `.editorconfig`). Use camelCase for
variables and functions, PascalCase for classes and Svelte components, and
kebab-case for directories where practical. Prefer type-only imports and route
logging through `src/logger`. ESLint lints TypeScript only; `.svelte` files are
not linted.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text:
Vitest runs in the `node` environment and aliases `obsidian` to
`tests/obsidian-stub.ts`; it cannot load real Obsidian modules. Structure
production code so Obsidian dependencies sit behind interfaces; unit tests target
pure logic (parser, controller helpers, queues, the Kanban helper) and swap in
adapters or the stub. Co-locate specs with their source or group them under a
feature folder. Add regression coverage for every bug fix, and ensure
`pnpm run test` passes before pushing.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text:
When a bug depends on real Obsidian runtime behavior - frontmatter position,
metadata cache, file writes, settings migration, the link menu, or the Kanban
helper reacting to file modifications - reproduce it in Obsidian before changing
code and verify it there after the fix. Record the exact Obsidian version,
platform, vault setup, command or API call invoked, console/runtime errors, and
plugin state before and after.

head: Repository Guidelines > Obsidian Runtime Workflow
text:
Agents with the `verify-in-obsidian` skill get the generic workflow there:
vault-mode choice, the runner script quartet, the `--print-env` HOME remap,
instance teardown, and the dev-tools loop. This section is the MetaEdit-specific
brief that a skill-less agent still needs.

head: Repository Guidelines > Obsidian Runtime Workflow
text:
- Plugin id `metaedit`. Reload with `obsidian vault=<vault> plugin:reload
  id=metaedit`; probe liveness with `Boolean(app.plugins.plugins.metaedit)`.
  Command id for the main action: `metaedit:metaEditRun`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Obsidian Runtime Workflow
text:
- The four runner scripts - `provision:e2e-vault`, `start:e2e-obsidian`,
  `stop:e2e-obsidian`, `obsidian:e2e` - run the shared `obsidian-e2e` bin,
  configured by `obsidian-e2e.config.mjs` at the repo root (plugin id, the three
  symlinked artifacts `main.js`/`manifest.json`/`styles.css`, and the
  `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`-shaped `data.json` seed).

head: Repository Guidelines > Obsidian Runtime Workflow
text:
- Worktrees use the isolated vault (`.obsidian-e2e-vaults/metaedit-<worktree>`)
  and must not race the shared `dev` vault. The canonical
  `/Users/christian/Developer/MetaEdit` checkout uses the shared `dev` vault
  (root `/Users/christian/Developer/dev_vault/dev`); only one checkout can own
  its plugin symlinks at a time.

head: Repository Guidelines > Obsidian Runtime Workflow
text:
- Always pass the `vault=` selector as a **prefix** argument, never a suffix -
  suffix form can resolve to the wrong vault.
```bash
pnpm run build                              # produce root main.js + manifest.json + styles.css first
pnpm run obsidian:e2e -- eval code='Boolean(app.plugins.plugins.metaedit)'
pnpm run obsidian:e2e -- dev:errors
pnpm run stop:e2e-obsidian                  # stop this worktree's instance on wrap-up

# point the Vitest tests/e2e suite at the isolated instance:
eval "$(pnpm run --silent start:e2e-obsidian -- --print-env)"
export HOME="$OBSIDIAN_E2E_OBSIDIAN_HOME"   # re-point the CLI socket, then: pnpm run test:e2e
```

head: Repository Guidelines > Obsidian Runtime Workflow
text:
The runner emits canonical `OBSIDIAN_E2E_*` env names, plus legacy
`METAEDIT_E2E_*` aliases during the migration (harness reads canonical first).

head: Repository Guidelines > Evidence-First Bug Triage
text:
- Default workflow: reproduce in Obsidian first, then implement the fix, then
  verify in Obsidian again, then add/adjust unit tests for regression coverage.

head: Repository Guidelines > Evidence-First Bug Triage
text:
- Do not assume a reported bug still exists; confirm current behavior before
  changing code. Issues may already be fixed by unrelated changes.

head: Repository Guidelines > Evidence-First Bug Triage
text:
- Prefer real user conditions over synthetic tests (commands, right-click "Edit
  Meta" menu, settings state, frontmatter vs inline fields, platform specifics).

head: Repository Guidelines > Evidence-First Bug Triage
text:
- When debugging command-triggered behavior, test both paths: hotkey execution
  and direct command execution (`obsidian command id=metaedit:metaEditRun`).

head: Repository Guidelines > Evidence-First Bug Triage
text:
- If not reproducible after solid evidence gathering, respond with the exact
  tested setup and ask for a fresh issue with versions, config, and repro
  artifacts.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release & PR Expectations
text:
Releases run on the shared forensic PR-to-release pipeline in
[`chhoumann/obsidian-plugin-workflows`](https://github.com/chhoumann/obsidian-plugin-workflows),
consumed via the three caller stubs in `.github/workflows/`
(`release-prepare.yml`, `release-trigger.yml`, `release.yml`). After every green
push to `master`, the `metaedit-release-bot` App opens or refreshes one standing
release PR containing only the synchronized version files (`package.json`,
`manifest.json`, `versions.json`) and generated notes; **merging that PR is the
sole release act.** There is no auto-release and no manual dispatch on the happy
path. The shared pipeline materializes the version files and keeps
`manifest.json` / `versions.json` in sync with the package version and Obsidian
`minAppVersion`. Release assets are `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css`.
Treat unexpected diffs in `package.json`, `manifest.json`, or `versions.json` as
blockers until understood.

head: Repository Guidelines > Release & PR Expectations
Repository Guidelines > Agent Playbook
text:
Scripted or automated work should rerun `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run build`, and
`pnpm run test` to keep the tree green, and surface disruptive operations in the
PR description. Treat unexpected diffs in `main.js`, `manifest.json`, or
`versions.json` as blockers until a maintainer approves. For runtime-affecting
changes, attach evidence from the isolated Obsidian E2E harness.

head: AGENTS.md - znvim Project Guide for LLMs > Terminology Reference
text:
| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **MessagePack** | Binary serialization format (like JSON but compact) |
| **RPC** | Remote Procedure Call - invoking functions on remote process |
| **Transport** | Communication channel (socket, pipe, etc.) |
| **Payload** | MessagePack-encoded data structure |
| **Request** | Client initiates method call, expects response |
| **Response** | Server replies to request with result or error |
| **Notification** | Fire-and-forget message (no response expected) |
| **Arena Allocator** | Bulk allocation strategy, single free for all allocations |
| **VTable** | Virtual function table for polymorphism |
| **Downcast** | Convert opaque pointer back to concrete type |

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Project Overview
text:
DonJuan is a Python package for procedurally generating tabletop battle-map
scenes. It started as a modular rebuild of the
[donjon dungeon generator](https://donjon.bin.sh/fantasy/dungeon/), and now
supports multiple scene types with dedicated renderers, FoundryVTT export, and
a PyQt5 desktop GUI.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Project Overview
text:
Current version: **0.0.3** (active development). Remote:
`https://github.com/tmcclintock/donjuan.git`.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Shared core model
text: Scene-specific containers:

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Shared core model
text: - `Dungeon` keeps `rooms`, `hallways`, and `room_entrances`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Shared core model
text: - `ForestScene` keeps `trees` and `undergrowth`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Shared core model
text: - `CampScene` keeps `fires`, `tents`, `paths`, and `trees`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Shared core model
text: - `VillageScene` keeps `buildings`, `roads`, `trees`, and `building_entrances`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Coordinate system
text:
All coordinates are `(y, x)` — row first, column second. `cell.y` is the row
index (0 = top), `cell.x` is the column index.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Cell states
text: - `cell.filled = True` — solid blocker / wall / tree obstacle

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Cell states
text: - `cell.filled = False` — open traversable space

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Cell states
text: - `cell.space` — the `Space` this cell belongs to (`None` for plain terrain)

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Edge / door logic
text:
`edge.has_door = True` is the single source of truth for whether an edge is a
passage/door. Renderers and FoundryVTT exporters read this flag directly.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Edge / door logic
text: - Doors are only valid between two unfilled cells.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Edge / door logic
text:
- `HallwayRandomizer._clear_interior_doors()` removes `has_door=True` flags
  that become interior to open space.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Edge / door logic
text:
- When dungeon edit mode paints a cell, all `has_door` flags on its edges are
  cleared to avoid stale markings.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: All randomizers extend `Randomizer` and may override:

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: - `randomize_dungeon(dungeon)`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: - `randomize_hallway(hallway)`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: - `randomize_room_entrances(room, *args)`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: - `randomize_room_size(room, *args)`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: - `randomize_room_name(room, *args)`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: - `randomize_room_position(room, *args)`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: Reusable randomizers in `core`:

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: - `RoomPositionRandomizer`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: Dungeon-specific randomizers in `dungeon`:

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text: - `RoomEntrancesRandomizer`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Architecture > Randomizer architecture
text:
Village generation uses shared `Room` / `Hallway` primitives plus a dedicated
`VillageRandomizer`.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Renderers
text:
| Class | Scene / grid | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `Renderer` | generic square-grid dungeon | `ax.imshow` of filled-grid boolean array |
| `HexRenderer` | dungeon hex grid | matplotlib hex polygons |
| `TexturedRenderer` | dungeon square grid | PIL-based dungeon texture pipeline |
| `ForestRenderer` | forest | textured outdoor forest image |
| `CampRenderer` | camp | textured camp image |
| `VillageRenderer` | village | textured village image |

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Renderers
text:
All accept `render(scene, save=False)` and return `(fig, ax)`. PIL-backed
renderers store `_last_image` for full-resolution saves.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Renderers > Dungeon texture packs and themes
text:
Dungeon packs are defined in `donjuan/dungeon/renderer.py`.
Available packs:

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Renderers > Dungeon texture packs and themes
text: `SPACE_THEMES` maps theme keys to dungeon floor-colour overrides.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Renderers > Dungeon texture packs and themes
text: To add a new dungeon theme:

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Renderers > Dungeon texture packs and themes
text: 1. append to `SPACE_THEMES` in `donjuan/dungeon/renderer.py`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Renderers > Dungeon texture packs and themes
text: 2. add a matching swatch to `_THEME_SWATCHES` in `gui/widgets.py`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > FoundryVTT export
text: - `donjuan/core/exporter.py` → `FoundryExporter`

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > FoundryVTT export
text: Scene-specific exporters:

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > FoundryVTT export
text: Current export semantics:

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > FoundryVTT export
text: - Dungeon: solid walls, doors, torch lights

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > FoundryVTT export
text: - Forest: circular tree blockers, movement-only undergrowth walls

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > FoundryVTT export
text: - Camp: circular tree blockers, movement-only tent walls, fire lights

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > FoundryVTT export
text: - Village: building perimeter walls/doors, circular tree blockers, open roads

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Key Gotchas
text:
- **`Hallway.append_ordered_cell_list` is broken** — it appends to a throw-away
  `list(self._ordered_cells)` copy. Always build the cell list externally and
  pass it to `Hallway(ordered_cells=..., name=...)`.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Key Gotchas
text:
- **`scene.emplace_space(space)`** re-links all edges via
  `grid.link_edges_to_cells()`. Call it after adding cells to a space.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Key Gotchas
text:
- **Room/building names must be unique** — scene containers use `name` as the
  dict key.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Key Gotchas
text:
- **`_build_spanning_tree` uses `id(room)`** instead of `room.name` to avoid
  collisions when names repeat.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Key Gotchas
text:
- **`DungeonCanvas.update_figure()` destroys the canvas** — old matplotlib
  connection IDs become invalid after a rerender.

head: AGENTS.md — Development Guide for DonJuan > Key Gotchas
text:
- **Slow tests** — rendering tests that write PNG files are marked
  `@pytest.mark.slow` and skipped by default. Run them with `pytest --runslow`.

text: Coverage is configured in `.coveragerc`.

Run with `python run_gui.py` from the repo root (requires `PyQt5`,

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol
text:
Every commit message must follow the Lore protocol — structured decision records using native git trailers.
Commits are not just labels on diffs; they are the atomic unit of institutional knowledge.

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol > Rules
text: 1. **Intent line first.** The first line describes *why*, not *what*. The diff already shows what changed.

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol > Rules
text: 2. **Trailers are optional but encouraged.** Use the ones that add value; skip the ones that don't.

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol > Rules
text: 3. **`Rejected:` prevents re-exploration.** If you considered and rejected an alternative, record it so future agents don't waste cycles re-discovering the same dead end.

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol > Rules
text: 4. **`Directive:` is a message to the future.** Use it for "do not change X without checking Y" warnings.

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol > Rules
text: 5. **`Constraint:` captures external forces.** API limitations, policy requirements, upstream bugs — things not visible in the code.

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol > Rules
text: 6. **`Not-tested:` is honest.** Declaring known verification gaps is more valuable than pretending everything is covered.

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol > Rules
text: 7. **All trailers use git-native trailer format** (key-value after a blank line). No custom parsing required.

head: oh-my-codex - Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration > Lore Commit Protocol > Trailer Vocabulary
text:
| Trailer | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `Constraint:` | External constraint that shaped the decision |
| `Rejected:` | Alternative considered and why it was rejected |
| `Confidence:` | Author's confidence level (low/medium/high) |
| `Scope-risk:` | How broadly the change affects the system (narrow/moderate/broad) |
| `Reversibility:` | How easily the change can be undone (clean/messy/irreversible) |
| `Directive:` | Forward-looking instruction for future modifiers |
| `Tested:` | What verification was performed |
