head: Repository Guidelines
text: Nano favors static, event-driven Java code with zero reflection and minimal dependencies. Treat this guide as the fastest path to productive contributions without violating the framework’s immutability and functional constraints.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - Core source lives under `src/main/java/org/nanonative/nano`, grouped by domain (`core`, `services`, `helper`, etc.) instead of classic MVC layers.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - Tests and runnable examples sit in `src/test/java`, while fixtures (PNG logos, JSON payloads) are under `src/test/resources`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - Long-form docs live in `docs/` (concept, context, services), and build artifacts land in `target/`. Keep generated files out of version control.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `./mvnw clean compile` – compile all sources with Java 21 toolchain.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `./mvnw test` – execute the JUnit 5 suite with AssertJ assertions.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `./mvnw clean verify` – run tests plus Jacoco coverage (`target/site/jacoco/index.html`).

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `./mvnw clean package` – produce the distributable JAR in `target/`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `./mvnw clean deploy -P release` – semantic-release build (requires configured GPG and credentials).

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - Favor static methods, fluent chains, and `final` fields; never introduce shared mutable state or `null` returns.

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - Event constants use screaming snake case (`EVENT_HTTP_RECEIVE`), packages remain `org.nanonative.nano.<domain>`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - Indentation is 4 spaces; rely on `spotless:apply` if present in your toolchain but keep formatting deterministic.

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: - Zero reflection, no parallel streams, and only virtual threads (`Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor`) for concurrency.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - Write component tests in `src/test/java`, naming files `*Test` and methods with `should...` to express behavior.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - Use embedded resources (Flapdoodle Mongo, in-memory HTTP) instead of mocks; prefer real HTTP calls or WireMock stubs.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - Keep tests deterministic by injecting `Clock` or seeds, and assert exact payloads. Failing tests must reproduce locally with `./mvnw test -DfailIfNoTests=false`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - Use Conventional Commits (`feat: add metric cache eviction`) for every change and bump versions per SemVer when shipping artifacts.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - Branch from `main`, describe intent, link issues, and attach logs/screenshots for behavioral changes or UI assets.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: - PRs must list test evidence (`./mvnw clean verify` output) and restate any config toggles touched (e.g., `CONFIG_ENV_PROD`).

head: Repository Guidelines > Security & Configuration Tips
text: - Avoid storing secrets; reference environment variables in docs and sample configs only.

head: Repository Guidelines > Security & Configuration Tips
text: - Use the provided `docs/context` references to wire services (HTTP, metrics, logging) and prefer atomic Mongo updates via `mongoTemplate.findAndModify`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Security & Configuration Tips
text: - When targeting GraalVM, stick to the `native-image` profile in `pom.xml` and confirm compatibility before requesting review.

head: Code formatting
text: Use `cargo +nightly fmt` for code formatting.

head: Code formatting > Code style > Generic bounds
text: Place generic bounds in `where` clauses rather than inline.

head: Code formatting > Code style > Imports
text: - Use `crate::` instead of `super::` in non-test code. `use super::*` is acceptable in `#[cfg(test)]` modules.

head: Code formatting > Code style > Imports
text: - Declare imports at the top with `use` so the body uses short names. Avoid long inline paths.

head: Code formatting > Code style > Comments
text: Do not use decorative divider comments (e.g. `// ── Section name ───────`). If a file needs clearer structure, split it into separate modules or files instead.

head: Code formatting > Code style > Panic messages
text: `panic!()`, `unreachable!()`, `debug_assert!()`, and `assert!()` must always include a descriptive message string.

head: Code formatting > Code style > Error handling
text: - Prefer `Result` over panics.

head: Code formatting > Code style > Error handling

head: Code formatting > Code style > Clippy
text: Run `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` and fix all warnings before committing.

head: Code formatting > Code style > Documentation

head: Code formatting > Code style > Documentation

head: AGENTS.md
text: Guidance for AI coding agents working **on** the secretbase package. secretbase provides fast, memory-efficient streaming hash functions, binary/text encoding and serialization for R. R >= 3.5, zero runtime dependencies — all cryptography is vendored C in `src/`.

head: AGENTS.md
text: Claude Code users: add `.claude/CLAUDE.md` containing `@../AGENTS.md` to import this file (`.claude/` is gitignored).

head: AGENTS.md > Formatter
text: Air, configured in `air.toml`: width 100, 2-space indent, `persistent-line-breaks = false`. **`tests/` is excluded** — don't reformat `tests/tests.R`.

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: **R layer (`R/`)** — thin wrappers over `.Call()`:

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `secret.R` — hash interfaces: `sha3()`, `shake256()`, `keccak()`, `sha256()`, `siphash13()`

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `base.R` — encoding / serialization interfaces: base64, base58, CBOR, JSON

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `secret.h` — shared header: context structures, constants, utilities

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `init.c` — `.Call` registration

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `sha3.c` — SHA-3 / SHAKE256 / Keccak (Mbed TLS derived)

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `sha256.c` — SHA-256 (Mbed TLS derived)

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `siphash.c` — SipHash-1-3 (c-siphash derived)

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `base64.c` — base64, including URL-safe variant (Mbed TLS derived)

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `base58.c` — Base58Check: 4-byte double-SHA-256 checksum, no version byte (libbase58 derived)

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `cbor.c` — CBOR (RFC 8949)

head: AGENTS.md > Two-layer architecture
text: - `json.c` — JSON (minimal; designed for HTTP API request/response bodies)

head: AGENTS.md > Load-bearing implementation details
text: - **Streaming serialization**: hash functions serialize R objects directly into the hash context via custom callbacks — the serialized object is never materialized in memory. Always R serialization version 3, big-endian; the first 6 header bytes are skipped for cross-platform portability.

head: AGENTS.md > Load-bearing implementation details
text: - **File hashing**: files are read in 65536-byte chunks (`SB_BUF_SIZE`), so files larger than RAM can be hashed.

head: AGENTS.md > Load-bearing implementation details
text: - **`convert` argument** controls output format: `TRUE` = character string (hex for hashes, base64/base58 for encoding), `FALSE` = raw vector, `NA` = integer vector (SHAKE256) or unserialized object (base64/base58 decoding).

head: AGENTS.md > Load-bearing implementation details
text: - C style: defensive programming, explicit error checking, early returns on error.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: Single-file custom "minitest" framework defined at the top of `tests/tests.R`: `test_library()`, `test_true()`, `test_null()`, `test_type()`, `test_equal()`, `test_identical()`, `test_error()` (with `containing =` for fixed-string message matching).

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: Test vectors: NIST known answers for the SHA functions; Bitcoin test vectors for Base58Check. All parameter combinations, error handling, serialization, and file operations are covered. Platform-specific tests (e.g. Unix file permissions) run conditionally. `R CMD check` runs the suite automatically.

head: AGENTS.md > Packaging notes
text: - roxygen2 with markdown (8.0.0); `NAMESPACE` is generated — never hand-edit.

head: AGENTS.md > Packaging notes
text: - Version is `major.minor.patch.dev` (current dev tag `.9000`).

head: AGENTS.md > Packaging notes
text: - `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/`, and `.posit/` are in `.Rbuildignore` and don't ship to CRAN.

head: AGENTS.md > Packaging notes

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Guide for AI coding agents working in this repository. Read this before touching code.
Every statement here was checked against the code; see §8 before adding to it.
Human-facing docs: [README.md](README.md) (install/config), [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What this repo is
text:
The stand-alone **web interface of Chat AI** (GWDG / SAIA) — a browser chat client for any
OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. It is one of three repos in the wider architecture:

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What this repo is
text:
| Repo | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| **this one** (`gwdg/chat-ai`) | web interface: `front` + `back` |
| `gwdg/saia-hub` | API gateway, SSH proxy |
| `gwdg/saia-hpc` | Slurm scheduler + HPC scripts |

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What this repo is
text: Two services, no monorepo tooling — each has its own `package.json` and is installed separately:

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What this repo is
text: - **`front/`** — React 19 SPA, Vite 7, runs entirely in the user's browser. All chat data is local.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What this repo is
text:
- **`back/`** — single-file Express 4 proxy (`back/service.mjs`, 412 lines). Per README it exists to
  hold the API key server-side and to prevent CORS errors in the user's browser.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Setup and commands
text: **Config is mandatory before anything runs.** Copy the samples first:

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Setup and commands
text:
`front/vite.config.js` calls `process.exit(1)` if `secrets/front.json` is missing or unparseable —
a front end that refuses to boot is almost always this.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Setup and commands > Native (preferred while iterating)
text:
Both default `CONFIG_LOCATION` to `../secrets/<name>.json` and `path.resolve` it against the
**current working directory**, so run them from inside `front/` and `back/`, or set
`CONFIG_LOCATION` explicitly. The two services fail differently when the path is wrong: `front`
exits, while `back` only logs `Failed to read back.json. Using default values.` and keeps running
**with an empty `apiKey`** — so every upstream call comes back unauthorized. If requests are
rejected, check that log line first.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Setup and commands > Docker
text:
Each Dockerfile sets `ENV CONFIG_LOCATION=/run/secrets/{front,back}`, fed by the docker secrets
declared in `docker-compose.yml`. Both services use `network_mode: host`, so ports are as
configured. `front/entrypoint.sh` greps `"mode"` out of `front.json` and runs `npm run dev` for
`dev` or `npm run prod` for `prod`, and exits on any other value.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Setup and commands > Checks
text:
**`npm run lint` does not currently run.** The script invokes `eslint`, but neither `eslint` nor the
plugins `.eslintrc.cjs` extends are in `front/devDependencies`, so a clean `npm i` gives
`sh: eslint: command not found`. (`.eslintrc.cjs` is also the pre-flat-config format.) Don't put
lint in your verification loop until that is fixed, and don't report it as passing.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Setup and commands > Checks
text:
**There is no test suite and no CI.** `front` has no test script, `back`'s `npm test` is `exit 1`,
and `.github/` contains only issue templates. So the loop is: build + exercise the change in a
browser. A passing build is not evidence that behaviour works.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Setup and commands > Checks
text:
`npm i` can rewrite `package-lock.json`. Check `git status` afterwards and keep unrelated lockfile
churn out of your commit.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants
text: These are the things that are not guessable from the file tree.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.1 Two stores, strictly separated
text:
| Store | Holds | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Dexie / IndexedDB** (`app-conversations-db`) | conversations, messages, content items, files, folders | `front/src/db/` |
| **Redux + redux-persist** (localStorage) | `interface_settings`, `user_settings`, `last_conversation`, `migration_data` | `front/src/Redux/` |

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.1 Two stores, strictly separated
text: `version` is in the root reducer but is not in the persist whitelist.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.1 Two stores, strictly separated
text:
Redux is persisted with a `version` + `migrations` map (`Redux/store/migrations.jsx`), and only a
four-action whitelist is mirrored across tabs via `redux-state-sync`: `SET_ADV`, `RESET_ALL`,
`MIGRATE`, `SET_COUNT`. Adding a persisted key means adding it to `whitelist` **and**
`getDefaultState()` in `Redux/store/store.jsx`.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.2 The conversation data flow
text:
`ChatPage.tsx` holds the whole hydrated conversation in one `localState` object and passes
`localState` / `setLocalState` down the tree. `useSyncConversation` reconciles that object with
IndexedDB. Writes go through `updateConversation(id, data)` in `db/index.ts`, which:

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.2 The conversation data flow
text: - replaces title + settings + the **entire** message list in a single Dexie transaction, and

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.2 The conversation data flow
text:
- enforces optimistic concurrency: unless `force` is passed it compares `data.lastModified`
  against the row in the DB and **returns `-1` without writing** on mismatch. `-1` means another
  tab changed this conversation, and surfaces as `modals/Chat/ConversationConflict.jsx`.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.2 The conversation data flow
text: So: thread the `lastModified` you read through to the write, and handle `-1`.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.2 The conversation data flow
text:
Data is normalised across `conversations → messages → content_items`, with `files_meta` /
`files_data` holding attachment bytes keyed by `fileId`; `hydrateConversation()` joins them back
into the nested shape the UI uses. Raw table access (`db.messages`, `db.content_items`, …) appears
**only** inside `front/src/db/` — everywhere else uses the functions it exports.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.3 Dexie migrations
text:
`db/index.ts` is at **version 4**. A new *indexed* field needs a new `this.version(n).stores({...})`
block plus an `.upgrade()` that backfills existing rows — this is how `folderId` (v3) and
`hasFirstPrompt` (v4) were added. A field that is only stored and never queried needs **no**
version bump; Dexie keeps unindexed properties on the row as-is. Never edit an existing version
block: users have live databases.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.4 "folder" in code == "topic" in the UI
text:
v1.0.0 renamed this feature for user-facing copy only. The `folders` table, `folderId`, and every
`*Folder*` function keep the old name. Don't rename them, and don't introduce "topic" identifiers
inside `db/`. UI strings and i18n keys say topic.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.5 Config reaches the front end through vite.config.js
text:
`secrets/front.json` is read **at Vite startup** and hand-mapped into `process.env.VITE_*`:
`VITE_BACKEND_ENDPOINT`, `VITE_MODELS_ENDPOINT`, `VITE_USERDATA_ENDPOINT`,
`VITE_DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, `VITE_TITLE_GENERATION_MODEL`, `VITE_MEMORY_GENERATION_MODEL`,
`VITE_PROPOSAL_GENERATION_MODEL`, `VITE_ANNOUNCEMENT`, `VITE_MODULE_*`. Consequences: **a new
config key requires editing `front/vite.config.js` too**, and a config change requires a dev-server
restart. Read values via `import.meta.env.VITE_*`; they arrive as strings, hence the
`=== "true"` comparisons.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.5 Config reaches the front end through vite.config.js
text:
Feature modules are gated this way — `VITE_MODULE_TOOLS`, `VITE_MODULE_FEEDBACK`,
`VITE_MODULE_CHOICES`, `VITE_MODULE_SPEECH` (JSON, with `model` and `voice`). A deployment can
switch these parts of the UI off, so new code in those areas must still behave with the flag off.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.6 Model capabilities are data, not code
text:
`front/src/config/models/<model-id>.json` is auto-globbed by `getModelDefaults.jsx` via
`import.meta.glob`, keyed on the filename. To give a model reasoning-effort support or other
per-model defaults, add or edit the JSON named exactly after the model id — no code change and no
registry to update.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.7 Secrets
text:
The API key is read only by `back/service.mjs` from `secrets/back.json`. `secrets/.gitignore`
ignores everything in that directory except itself, so real config files there are invisible to
git. Never move a key into front-end code or into a `.sample`.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.8 The back service's responses can mislead you
text: Verified in `back/service.mjs`:

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.8 The back service's responses can mislead you
text:
- **`/models` always returns HTTP 200**, even when the upstream rejects the request — the handler is
  `res.status(200).json(await response.json())`, so an upstream `{"message":"Unauthorized"}` arrives
  as a 200. Check the response body, never the status.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.8 The back service's responses can mislead you
text:
- **If `apiKey` is empty, `Authorization` falls back to the `inference-id` request header** rather
  than erroring — that is how the deployed setup passes per-user credentials through.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Architecture invariants > 4.8 The back service's responses can mislead you
text:
- **`/user` is a hard-coded placeholder** in this repo: it always returns the same `sample-user`
  object. Real user data comes from the gateway in a full deployment, so don't debug user/usage
  features against this response.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Conventions
text:
- **Gradual TypeScript.** `.jsx` and `.tsx` coexist. `front/tsconfig.json` is `strict: false`,
  `checkJs: false`, `allowJs: true`, `noEmit: true` — Vite does the emitting, so `tsc` is not part
  of any script. Shared types live in `db/dbTypes.ts` and `types/`.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Conventions
text:
- **Styling** is Tailwind **v4** via `@tailwindcss/vite`, but the theme still comes from
  `tailwind.config.js`, pulled in by `@config "../tailwind.config.js"` in `src/index.css`. The
  palette (`primary`, `bg_dark`, `bg_chat`, …), the `mobile` / `middle` / `desktop` breakpoints and
  the custom shadows are defined there.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Conventions
text:
- **Dark mode** is the `dark` class, toggled on `document.body` by `App.jsx` from
  `interface_settings.dark_mode` (`darkMode: "class"` in the Tailwind config). Style with `dark:`
  variants; the source of truth is that Redux flag, not the OS preference.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Conventions
text:
- **i18n:** user-facing strings go through `react-i18next` `t()`. `i18n/en.js` and `i18n/de.js`
  currently have identical top-level key sets — add every new key to **both**.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Conventions
text:
- **Modals** are opened through the `useModal()` hook from `modals/ModalContext.jsx` and built on
  `BaseModal.jsx`; that is the pattern every existing modal in the repo follows.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Conventions
text:
- **Upstream calls** each get their own file in `apis/`. Components, hooks and modals import them
  directly — there is no enforced layer between them.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Conventions
text:
- **Never enable `rehype-raw` without a sanitizer.** Model output is untrusted: it reaches the DOM
  verbatim, and so does any imported or shared conversation. `rehype-raw` in `ThinkingBlock.jsx`
  once turned HTML the model drafted while reasoning into live markup — `<iframe>` tags fetched
  real URLs (tripping Chrome's local-network prompt) and an injected `<style>` restyled the whole
  page. `SafeMarkdown` is safe only because it leaves `rehype-raw` off, so react-markdown drops
  raw HTML nodes. To *show* raw HTML instead of dropping it, convert mdast `html` nodes to `text`
  (`remarkHtmlAsText` in `ThinkingBlock.jsx`) — that leaves code fences alone, since fenced and
  inline code are their own node types.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Conventions
text:
- CONTRIBUTING.md asks that files and folders follow the structure of the existing ones; keep
  components in the folder of the screen area they belong to.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Git workflow
text:
- **Branch off `dev` and open PRs into `dev`.** `beta` is for changes that need testing before
  they go into `dev`; `main` carries releases. Work branches use flat, dash-separated names — e.g.
  `feature-forms`, `fix-toolNaming`, `markdown-fixes`, `tools-ui`, `lib-major-openai-v6`.
  (CONTRIBUTING.md documents the fork → feature branch → PR flow for outside contributors.)

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Git workflow
text:
- Releases are manual: bump `version` in `front/package.json` — it is shown in the footer by
  `VersionDisplay.jsx` and stamped into exported conversations by `conversationUtils.js` — and add a
  `## Version: vX.Y.Z (DD.MM.YYYY)` block with a `Highlights:` list at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`. `back/package.json` is versioned independently and is not
  bumped in lockstep.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. Git workflow
text: - Never commit `secrets/*.json`, `node_modules/` or `dist/`.

text: - [ ] `npm run build` clean in `front/` (there is no working lint — see §3)

head: AGENTS.md > 7. Before you finish
text: - [ ] new strings added to both `en.js` and `de.js`

head: AGENTS.md > 7. Before you finish
text: - [ ] Dexie schema change → version bump + `.upgrade()` backfill, existing version blocks untouched

head: AGENTS.md > 8. Maintaining this file
text:
This file is meant to grow. When you discover a constraint that cost you a debugging cycle — a
non-obvious invariant, a trap, a command that does not work the documented way — add it to the
matching section, briefly.

head: AGENTS.md > 8. Maintaining this file
text:
Two rules: **only write what you have verified in the code**, not what the structure suggests ought
to be true; and keep it to facts and rules — no task logs, no status updates, no changelog entries.
If something here turns out to be wrong, fix it rather than working around it.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Behavioral Guidelines
text: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.

head: CLAUDE.md > Behavioral Guidelines
text: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

head: CLAUDE.md > 1. Think Before Coding
text: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

head: CLAUDE.md > 1. Think Before Coding
text: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.

head: CLAUDE.md > 1. Think Before Coding
text: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.

head: CLAUDE.md > 1. Think Before Coding
text: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.

head: CLAUDE.md > 1. Think Before Coding
text: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

head: CLAUDE.md > 2. Simplicity First
text: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

head: CLAUDE.md > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No features beyond what was asked.

head: CLAUDE.md > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No abstractions for single-use code.

head: CLAUDE.md > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.

head: CLAUDE.md > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.

head: CLAUDE.md > 2. Simplicity First
text: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

head: CLAUDE.md > 2. Simplicity First
text: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: When editing existing code:

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: When your changes create orphans:

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

head: CLAUDE.md > 3. Surgical Changes
text: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

head: CLAUDE.md > 4. Goal-Driven Execution
text: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

head: CLAUDE.md > 4. Goal-Driven Execution
text: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

head: CLAUDE.md > 4. Goal-Driven Execution
text: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"

head: CLAUDE.md > 4. Goal-Driven Execution
text: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"

head: CLAUDE.md > 4. Goal-Driven Execution
text: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

head: CLAUDE.md > 4. Goal-Driven Execution
text:
For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

head: CLAUDE.md > 4. Goal-Driven Execution
text: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

head: CLAUDE.md > 4. Goal-Driven Execution
text: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: madengine is a CLI tool for running AI/ML models in local Docker, Kubernetes, and SLURM environments. The entry point is `madengine.cli.app:cli_main` (registered as the `madengine` console script).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: **CLI Layer** (`src/madengine/cli/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `app.py` — Typer app wiring, registers 5 commands: `discover`, `build`, `run`, `report`, `database`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `commands/` — One file per command (build, run, discover, report, database)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `constants.py` — `ExitCode` enum (`SUCCESS=0`, `FAILURE=1`, `BUILD_FAILURE=2`, `RUN_FAILURE=3`, `INVALID_ARGS=4`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: **Orchestration Layer** (`src/madengine/orchestration/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `build_orchestrator.py` — `BuildOrchestrator`: discovers models, builds Docker images, writes `build_manifest.json`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `run_orchestrator.py` — `RunOrchestrator`: reads or triggers builds, infers deployment target, delegates to local or distributed execution

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: **Core Layer** (`src/madengine/core/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `context.py` — `Context` class: merges `additional_context` with system detection (GPU vendor, architecture, OS, ROCm path). Uses `ast.literal_eval()` to parse additional_context strings (not `json.loads` — pass Python dict repr, not JSON)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `console.py` — `Console`: shell execution wrapper with live output support

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `docker.py` — Docker command wrapper

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: **Execution Layer** (`src/madengine/execution/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `container_runner.py` — `ContainerRunner`: runs models from manifest via `docker run`, writes results to `perf.csv`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `docker_builder.py` — `DockerBuilder`: builds images from Dockerfiles

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `container_runner_helpers.py` — Log error pattern scanning, timeout resolution

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: **Deployment Layer** (`src/madengine/deployment/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `factory.py` — `DeploymentFactory`: Factory pattern, registers `SlurmDeployment` and `KubernetesDeployment`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `base.py` — `BaseDeployment` abstract class, `DeploymentConfig` dataclass

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `kubernetes.py` / `slurm.py` — Concrete deployments; target is inferred by Convention over Configuration: presence of `"k8s"` or `"kubernetes"` key → K8s; `"slurm"` key → SLURM; neither → local

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `presets/` — JSON preset files for K8s/SLURM default configurations; auto-merged with minimal user configs

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `config_loader.py` — Loads and merges preset JSON with user-supplied config

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: **Utils** (`src/madengine/utils/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `discover_models.py` — `DiscoverModels`: three discovery methods: root `models.json`, `scripts/{dir}/models.json`, or `scripts/{dir}/get_models_json.py` (dynamic)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `gpu_tool_factory.py` / `gpu_tool_manager.py` — GPU vendor abstraction (AMD/NVIDIA)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `gpu_validator.py` — ROCm installation detection, GPU vendor detection

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `config_parser.py` — `ConfigParser`: parses `--additional-context` and tools config

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: **Reporting** (`src/madengine/reporting/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `update_perf_csv.py` — Writes/appends to `perf.csv` and `perf_entry.csv`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Layer Structure
text: - `csv_to_html.py` / `csv_to_email.py` — Report generation

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Data Flows
text: 1. **Build flow**: CLI → `BuildOrchestrator` → `DiscoverModels` (finds models by tags) → `DockerBuilder` (builds images) → writes `build_manifest.json`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Data Flows
text: 2. **Run flow**: CLI → `RunOrchestrator` → loads/generates `build_manifest.json` → infers target → `ContainerRunner` (local) or `DeploymentFactory` (K8s/SLURM) → writes `perf.csv`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Data Flows
text: 3. **`additional_context`**: User JSON/Python-dict string merged into `Context.ctx`. Context is parsed with `ast.literal_eval()`, so values can use Python dict syntax. Keys like `k8s`, `slurm`, `distributed`, `tools`, `pre_scripts`, `post_scripts` drive behavior.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Data Flows
text: 4. **Model definition**: Models defined in `models.json` with fields: `name`, `tags`, `dockerfile`, `scripts`, `n_gpus`, `args`, `timeout`, `skip_gpu_arch`, etc.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Data Flows
text: 5. **Script isolation**: During run, `scripts/common/` is populated from the madengine package (pre_scripts, post_scripts, tools) and cleaned up afterwards. The MAD project's own `scripts/` and `docker/` directories are preserved.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Deployment Target Inference
text: No explicit `"deploy"` field is needed. Target is inferred from config structure:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Deployment Target Inference
text: - `"k8s"` or `"kubernetes"` key present → Kubernetes deployment

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Deployment Target Inference
text: - `"slurm"` key present → SLURM deployment

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Deployment Target Inference
text: - Neither → local Docker execution

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Test Structure
text: Pytest config is in `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`. Test markers: `slow`, `integration`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Code Style
text: - Black formatting, 88-character line length

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Code Style
text: - isort with `profile = "black"`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Code Style
text: - Google-style docstrings

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Code Style
text: - Type hints required for public functions

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Code Style
text: - Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`, `style:`, `perf:`, `chore:`

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > High-Level Overview
text: - Monorepo Go service providing gRPC APIs (admin, user, public, debug) that are proxied to HTTP via gRPC-Gateway; exposed through `cmd/app/main.go` and the Cobra CLI under `app`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > High-Level Overview
text: - Layered architecture: **domain** (pure business logic and contracts), **usecase** (application services/interactors), **infrastructure** (framework, transport, persistence, third-party integrations).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > High-Level Overview
text: - Primary dependencies: PostgreSQL (SQLBoiler models), Firebase Authentication, Google Cloud Storage, X (Twitter) API, gRPC + HTTP gateway, Zap-based structured logging.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Entry Points & Execution Flow
text:
- `cmd/app/main.go` → `internal/infrastructure/cmd/root.go` registers subcommands:
  - `http-server run` → starts `internal/infrastructure/http.Run()` which spins up the gRPC server (`internal/infrastructure/grpc`) and HTTP gateway with CORS and ping handler.
  - `task ...` → maintenance tasks (e.g., create root staff/admin) defined in `internal/infrastructure/cmd/internal/task_cmd` and backed by usecase interactors.
  - `schema-migration database ...` → wraps migration helpers in `internal/infrastructure/postgresql/migration` for Goose migrations, schema extraction, and constant sync.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Entry Points & Execution Flow
text: - HTTP requests hit the gRPC-Gateway; gRPC calls flow through interceptors (logging, auth, authorization) to handlers that delegate into usecase interactors and domain services, which rely on repository interfaces implemented in infrastructure packages.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Configuration & Environment
text: - Runtime configuration populated from environment variables via `internal/infrastructure/environment/env.go` using `caarlos0/env`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Configuration & Environment
text: - Key groups: application (`PORT`, `ENV`, `MIN_LOG_LEVEL`), database (`DB_HOST`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_LOG_ENABLE`), GCP (`GCP_PROJECT_ID`, bucket name, Firebase client key, Identity Platform tenant IDs), X API credentials.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Configuration & Environment
text: - `internal/pkg/logger` builds a Zap logger whose minimum level derives from `MIN_LOG_LEVEL`; logger is attached to contexts for interceptors and usecases.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Domain Layer (`internal/domain`)
text: - **Model**: immutable-ish structs (e.g., `model.Asset`, `model.User`, `model.Staff`) with factory helpers and behavior (status transitions, derived IDs).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Domain Layer (`internal/domain`)
text: - **Model factory**: `internal/domain/model/factory.NewFactory` seeds model instances via `faker.FakeData` (mirroring the admin setup) and then overrides key fields manually—prefer tweaking the overrides instead of reintroducing constructor helpers.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Domain Layer (`internal/domain`)
text: - **Repository interfaces**: define persistence contracts (`internal/domain/repository`). Concrete implementations live under infrastructure (`postgresql/repository`, `firebase/repository`, `gcs/repository`). Mock interfaces generated under `internal/domain/repository/mock` for testing.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Domain Layer (`internal/domain`)
text: - **Services**: orchestrate complex domain operations (e.g., `service.Asset`, `service.Staff`, `service.Question`) often combining multiple repositories/caches.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Domain Layer (`internal/domain`)
text: - **Errors**: centralized typed errors in `internal/domain/errors` returning goerr instances with codes/messages used by interceptors for gRPC status mapping.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Domain Layer (`internal/domain`)
text: - **Cache contracts**: e.g., `cache.AssetPath` executed by Postgres-backed cache storing presigned asset metadata.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Domain Layer (`internal/domain`)
text: - **Common utilities**: `internal/pkg` packages for IDs, UUID, time (`now`), nullable helpers, validation.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Usecase Layer (`internal/usecase`)
text: - Exposes interactors grouped by audience (admin, staff, user, task, debug). Each interactor validates inputs (`internal/usecase/input/*` structs using `validation.Validate`) and coordinates domain services/repositories inside transactions.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Usecase Layer (`internal/usecase`)
text: - Transaction boundary defined by `repository.Transactable`; Postgres implementation wraps functions with retry-aware `RunTx` (`internal/infrastructure/postgresql/transactable`).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Usecase Layer (`internal/usecase`)
text: - Within write transactions, keep `Preload` disabled by default; enable it only when the usecase needs to inspect domain `ReadonlyReference` data inside the transaction. After mutations, perform a fresh load outside the transaction (with `Preload: true`) so readonly references are hydrated for response shaping.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Usecase Layer (`internal/usecase`)
text: - Outputs under `internal/usecase/output` when custom view models are needed.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Usecase Layer (`internal/usecase`)
text: - Authentication interactor mediates Firebase ID token verification for staff/admin/user contexts.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Usecase Layer (`internal/usecase`)
text: - Example: `adminStaffInteractor.Create` fetches tenant, validates asset via `service.Asset`, creates staff via `service.Staff`, and reloads the persisted entity for response.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Infrastructure Layer
text: - **Dependency wiring**: `internal/infrastructure/dependency.Dependency.Inject` constructs all repositories, services, and interactors, wiring Firebase, GCS, X API clients, and Postgres client.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Infrastructure Layer
text:
- **Transport**:
  - gRPC server (`internal/infrastructure/grpc/run.go`) registers handlers for admin/public/debug APIs, sets keepalive configs, and applies interceptors: request logging (structured zap logs + goerr mapping to gRPC status), session authentication (extracts Bearer tokens, verifies ID tokens via usecases, saves claims onto context), and simple authorization checks.
  - HTTP Gateway (`internal/infrastructure/http/run.go`) hosts gRPC-Gateway mux with custom JSON marshaler, registers gRPC handlers, adds `/` ping endpoint, and wraps mux with permissive CORS middleware.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Infrastructure Layer
text:
- **Persistence**:
  - Postgres client configured in `internal/infrastructure/postgresql/client.go`; SQLBoiler generated models under `internal/infrastructure/postgresql/internal/dbmodel` power repository implementations.
  - Repository packages translate between DB models and domain models (marshal/unmarshal helpers under `internal/infrastructure/postgresql/internal/marshaller`).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Infrastructure Layer
text:
- **External services**:
  - Firebase auth client wrappers provide staff/admin/user authentication repositories (verify tokens, CRUD users, custom claims).
  - GCS repository handles signed URL generation and asset uploads.
  - X integration (`internal/infrastructure/x/x`) fetches profile data for onboarding.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Infrastructure Layer
text: - **CLI Tasks**: `task create-root-staff` and `task create-admin` parse flags, load dependencies, and invoke corresponding interactors with current time (`internal/pkg/now`).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Layered Architecture Details > Infrastructure Layer
text: - **Migrations**: Goose-based runner manages migrations embedded via `db/postgresql/migrations`; constants sync reads YAML and upserts enumerations; schema extraction outputs `db/postgresql/schema.sql` and Mermaid diagrams.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Protocol & Schema Assets
text: - Protobuf definitions under `schema/proto`; Buf configuration (`buf.gen.yaml`, `buf.work.yaml`) generates gRPC stubs into `internal/infrastructure/grpc/pb` and OpenAPI specs into `schema/openapi/oshipo/...`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Protocol & Schema Assets
text: - Regenerate stubs with `make generate.buf`. SQLBoiler models regenerated via `make generate.sqlboiler.postgresql` after migrations.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Database & Data Modeling
text: - PostgreSQL schemas managed via Goose migrations in `db/postgresql/migrations` and constants in `db/postgresql/constants` (embedded YAML).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Database & Data Modeling
text: - SQLBoiler view/table files in `internal/infrastructure/postgresql/internal/dbmodel` are generated; avoid manual edits.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Database & Data Modeling
text: - Transaction helper retries on deadlocks (`pq` error codes `40P01`, `55P03`, `40001`).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > CLI & Development Recipes
text: - Linting: `make lint.go`, `make lint.proto`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > CLI & Development Recipes
text: - Tests: `make test` (runs `go test ./internal/...`).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > CLI & Development Recipes
text: - Mock generation: `make generate.mock` (runs `go generate` across repository).

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > CLI & Development Recipes
text: - Admin bootstrap: `go run ./cmd/app task create-admin -e <email> -p <pwd> -d <display> -r <role>`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Testing & Observability
text: - Unit tests present in domain/usecase packages (e.g., `internal/domain/service/*_test.go`, `internal/usecase/*_test.go`). Prefer using mocks from `internal/domain/.../mock` for isolation.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Testing & Observability
text: - Domain service tests (e.g., wallet service) must stay table-driven (`tests := map[string]testcaseFunc`) with `testcase` structs containing only `args`, `service`, and `want`; avoid introducing ad-hoc matcher helpers and rely on existing gomock matchers such as `gomock.Eq` alongside the generated mocks. When deterministic IDs are required, call `id.Mock()` directly without overriding or restoring `id.New` manually.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Testing & Observability
text: - Logging uses Zap with structured fields including operation IDs; interceptors map domain errors to gRPC codes and attach request IDs to `errdetails.RequestInfo` for clients.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Testing & Observability
text: - When adding handlers, ensure gRPC methods propagate context with logger via `request_interceptor` for consistent tracing.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Favor the existing layer boundaries: domain models stay pure (no infrastructure imports), usecases orchestrate business rules, infrastructure wires dependencies and IO.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Always validate incoming params using the input structs and `validation.Validate`; surface errors via domain error types so interceptors format responses correctly.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - When defining domain service APIs (packages under `internal/domain/service`), name request/response structs using the `XxxParam` / `XxxResult` pattern (e.g., `WalletGrantPointsParam`), not `Input` / `Output`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Wrap DB mutations inside `repository.Transactable.RWTx` to get retry and context-aware executors; use `transactable.GetContextExecutor` within repositories to access the active transaction.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Keep transaction boundaries in the usecase layer: the interactor should invoke `repository.Transactable.RWTx/ROTx`, while downstream domain services must assume a transaction context is already in place and must not start their own transactions.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Leverage services (asset, staff, question, etc.) instead of duplicating logic; they encapsulate cross-repository coordination.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - For usecases, always set `Preload` to `true` on repository `Get`/`List` options so readonly relations are hydrated, and after `Create`/`Update` flows, issue a final `Get` to build the response payload.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Even when no URLs need to be populated today, implement and invoke the appropriate `assetService.BatchXXX` helper from usecases to keep response shaping consistent.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - For assets: every resource returned from usecases/handlers must pass through `assetService.BatchSetXXX` just before returning; if a resource has no URLs/readonly references, still iterate and leave a comment-only no-op. `BatchSetTenantURLs` is responsible for cascading into tenant tags, and `BatchSetStaffURLs` must also set URLs on any readonly tenant references.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Respect generated code ownership: Protobuf/SQLBoiler outputs and embedded assets should be regenerated via Make targets, not edited manually.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Attach new dependencies in `internal/infrastructure/dependency.Inject` and update relevant handlers/interactors; keep constructor signature order consistent for readability.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - For new gRPC endpoints, extend protobufs under `schema/proto`, regenerate stubs, implement handler functions in infrastructure, and delegate to usecase interactors for business logic.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Route all state mutations and validation logic through domain models/services; usecases must call domain helpers rather than mutating `model` fields or reimplementing validation directly.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Do not introduce package-level helper functions/methods in usecase or domain/service packages for business logic; extend the relevant domain model (e.g., `model.Wallet`) instead so that state mutations live alongside their data.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - When adding domain-specific helper logic, attach it as a method on the relevant domain model (e.g., make expiration helpers receiver methods on `model.Wallet`) rather than free functions, even within `domain/model`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - When adding gomock expectations, mirror existing patterns: only use `gomock.Any()` for `context.Context`, avoid `DoAndReturn`, prefer exact argument matching with `Return`, and skip helpers like `gomock.AssignableToTypeOf`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - When writing rate limit tests, build the domain objects via helpers in `internal/domain/model/factory` and pass those concrete values directly into gomock expectations instead of introducing custom matchers so comparisons stay consistent across test suites.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Keep test `want` structs minimal: include only the fields asserted in the test flow (typically `got`/`expectedResult`) and move custom checks into small helper closures or inline assertions.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Write table-driven tests using `tests := map[string]testcaseFunc` where `type testcaseFunc func(ctx context.Context, ctrl *gomock.Controller) testcase`.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Define `testcase` structs with exactly `args`, `usecase` (or `service` for domain-layer tests), and `want` fields; construct mocks and test data inside each `testcaseFunc` before returning the struct.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Instantiate all test fixtures inside the returned `testcase` (e.g., factories, mocked repositories/services) so individual cases stay isolated and self-contained.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Do not embed assertion functions inside `want`; compare the actual result with the expected object directly using equality assertions.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Use `internal/pkg/logger` helpers to add contextual fields instead of ad-hoc logging; propagate contexts down call stacks.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - Within the UserService code paths (inputs, handlers, usecases), name the current authenticated user's identifier `UserID` to keep terminology consistent.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Contribution Guidelines for Agents
text: - UserService handlers must obtain the current time from the request context (e.g., `request_interceptor.GetRequestTime`) and pass it through inputs; do not call `now.Now`, `time.Now`, or similar clock helpers inside usecase or domain layers.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Development Philosophy
text: - Keep persistence logic cohesive: when an aggregate owns child entities, write repositories so create/update operate transactionally on the whole aggregate; avoid “readonly reference” patterns unless mandated by performance.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Development Philosophy
text: - Preload semantics should be explicit and consistent: use a boolean preload flag on repository queries, but allow aggregates that must always hydrate critical relations to override flags for correctness; document any such exceptions near the helper.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Development Philosophy
text: - Marshallers/DTO mappers are responsible for validation and normalization when crossing boundaries (DB ↔ domain ↔ transport); keep them thin, deterministic, and co-located with generated models to reduce drift.

head: AGENTS Guide for rapid-go > Development Philosophy
text: - Prefer declarative guides (like this file) that capture principles instead of one-off case notes; when adding new rules, generalize them to future work rather than binding them to a single feature.

head: Project Overview
text:
**kg-releases** is a Vue 3 web app that tracks GitHub release notifications for starred
repositories. Users log in with GitHub via Firebase Auth, and a separate backend (private repo)
fetches/caches releases and sends email notifications.

head: Project Overview
text: Live at: https://releases.netlify.app/

text: Type checking separately:

text: - **Performance:** All code must be performance-optimized by default.

head: Project Overview > Code Style & Standards
text: - **Consistency:** Strictly adhere to the existing codebase patterns.

head: Project Overview > Code Style & Standards
text:
- **Linting:** In-place rule overrides are permitted if necessary for working code; provide a brief

head: Project Overview > Code Style & Standards
text:
**Function ordering:** Follow top-down "newspaper style" - callers above callees. If function A
calls function B, A must appear above B in the file. Entry points and high-level logic at the top,
helper/implementation functions below. Read the file top-to-bottom like a newspaper: headline first,
then details.

head: Project Overview > Code Style & Standards
text: When changing code - DON'T remove pre-existing code comments, preserve them instead.

text:
- **Vue 3** with `<script setup>` composition API, **Vuetify 3** (Material Design), **Pinia** state
  management, **Vue Router 4**

text:
Pinia store holding user auth, releases, starred repos, and settings. Key state is persisted to

head: Project Overview > Architecture > Routing (`src/router.ts`)
text:
Route guards: `loggedInGuard` (redirects guests to home), `guestOnlyGuard` (redirects logged-in
users to releases). All guards await `bootstrapDone` promise before resolving.

text: - `HomePage.vue` — Login screen (guest-only)

text:
Creates Vue app → installs plugins (Pinia, Router, Vuetify, Sentry) → mounts → initializes Firebase
auth or loads releases depending on login state → resolves `bootstrapDone`.

head: Interactions
text:
- Keyboard
  - MUST: Full keyboard support per [WAI-ARIA APG](https://wwww3org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/)
  - MUST: Visible focus rings (`:focus-visible`; group with `:focus-within`)
  - MUST: Manage focus (trap, move, and return) per APG patterns

head: Interactions
text:
- Targets & input
  - MUST: Hit target ≥24px (mobile ≥44px) If visual <24px, expand hit area
  - MUST: Mobile `<input>` font-size ≥16px or set:
    ```html
    <meta
      name="viewport"
      content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"
    />
    ```
  - NEVER: Disable browser zoom
  - MUST: `touch-action: manipulation` to prevent double-tap zoom; set `-webkit-tap-highlight-color` to match design

head: Interactions
text:
- Inputs & forms (behavior)
  - MUST: Hydration-safe inputs (no lost focus/value)
  - NEVER: Block paste in `<input>/<textarea>`
  - MUST: Loading buttons show spinner and keep original label
  - MUST: Enter submits focused text input In `<textarea>`, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter submits; Enter adds newline
  - MUST: Keep submit enabled until request starts; then disable, show spinner, use idempotency key
  - MUST: Don’t block typing; accept free text and validate after
  - MUST: Allow submitting incomplete forms to surface validation
  - MUST: Errors inline next to fields; on submit, focus first error
  - MUST: `autocomplete` + meaningful `name`; correct `type` and `inputmode`
  - SHOULD: Disable spellcheck for emails/codes/usernames
  - SHOULD: Placeholders end with ellipsis and show example pattern (eg, `+1 (123) 456-7890`, `sk-012345…`)
  - MUST: Warn on unsaved changes before navigation
  - MUST: Compatible with password managers & 2FA; allow pasting one-time codes
  - MUST: Trim values to handle text expansion trailing spaces
  - MUST: No dead zones on checkboxes/radios; label+control share one generous hit target

head: Interactions
text:
- State & navigation
  - MUST: URL reflects state (deep-link filters/tabs/pagination/expanded panels) Prefer libs like [nuqs](https://nuqs.dev)
  - MUST: Back/Forward restores scroll
  - MUST: Links are links—use `<a>/<Link>` for navigation (support Cmd/Ctrl/middle-click)

head: Interactions
text:
- Feedback
  - SHOULD: Optimistic UI; reconcile on response; on failure show error and rollback or offer Undo
  - MUST: Confirm destructive actions or provide Undo window
  - MUST: Use polite `aria-live` for toasts/inline validation
  - SHOULD: Ellipsis (`…`) for options that open follow-ups (eg, “Rename…”)

head: Interactions
text:
- Touch/drag/scroll
  - MUST: Design forgiving interactions (generous targets, clear affordances; avoid finickiness)
  - MUST: Delay first tooltip in a group; subsequent peers no delay
  - MUST: Intentional `overscroll-behavior: contain` in modals/drawers
  - MUST: During drag, disable text selection and set `inert` on dragged element/containers
  - MUST: No “dead-looking” interactive zones—if it looks clickable, it is

head: Interactions

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: Jellyfin plugin that integrates DoesTheDogDie.com content warnings into media libraries. Fetches trigger warnings (animal death, violence, jump scares, etc.) and adds them as metadata tags to movies and TV shows.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build Commands
text: **Requires the .NET 10 SDK**, installed user-locally at `~/.dotnet` (the system `dotnet` may only have 8/9). NuGet restore walks every target framework of the referenced `DoesTheDogDie` library before framework negotiation happens — it multi-targets `net9.0;net10.0` — so a net9-only SDK fails restore with `NETSDK1045`. Prefix every dotnet command with:

head: CLAUDE.md > Build Commands
text: `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=LatestMajor` is needed because that SDK root's `shared/` has ASP.NET Core 10 but no 9.x runtime, and the `net9.0` unit-test testhost needs one to roll forward to. The plugin itself still targets and ships `net9.0` — only the build tooling needs .NET 10.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build Commands
text: The plugin's csproj resolves the library via a `DtddClientPath` MSBuild property (default `../../../dtdd-client`, i.e. checked out as a sibling of this repo's parent directory) and falls back to a `PackageReference` on the [`DtDDNetClient`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/DtDDNetClient) NuGet package if that path doesn't exist. Pass `-p:DtddClientPath=<path>` to point at the library elsewhere — e.g. from a worktree, where the default relative path won't resolve. The fallback version defaults to `0.1.0` via `DtddClientVersion`; pass `-p:DtddClientVersion=<version>` to pin a different one.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Instructions for AI agents (and humans) working in this repository. Keep this
file authoritative and up to date — when the workflow or conventions change,
update this file in the same pull request.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text:
A TypeScript bridge that controls **OpenCode** from **Telegram** via the
**Agent Client Protocol (ACP)** — `opencode acp` over JSON-RPC/stdio. One
ACP process manages many sessions; the bot streams responses, renders
MarkdownV2 + diffs, queues follow-ups, runs scheduled tasks, and can run
24/7 as a background service.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text: - **Runtime:** Node.js ≥ 20, TypeScript run directly via `tsx` (no build step).

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text: - **Key deps:** `grammy` (Telegram), `dotenv`, `diff`.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text: - **Transport:** `opencode acp` (stdio ACP / JSON-RPC 2.0) — not HTTP/SSE.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text: - **Entry point:** `src/index.ts` · **CLI/daemon:** `src/cli.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions (must follow)
text: - **`npm run typecheck` must pass** with no errors before any PR is merged.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions (must follow)
text:
- **Keep files focused and under ~500 lines.** Split logic into multiple modules
  rather than growing one big file.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions (must follow)
text:
- **ESM imports with `.js` specifiers** (e.g. `import { x } from "./x.js"`),
  named exports, match the existing style.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions (must follow)
text: - **Don't add dependencies** without a clear reason; pin versions.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions (must follow)
text:
- **Never commit secrets** — `.env`, tokens, logs, `data/`, or generated
  launcher files. They are git-ignored; keep it that way.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions (must follow)
text:
- Use secure-by-default patterns; this bot runs commands on the host, so respect
  `ALLOWED_USERS` and never weaken access control silently.

head: AGENTS.md > Feature delivery workflow (batched PRs → release)
text:
Features and fixes are delivered as **batches of small, focused branches opened
as pull requests**, then merged and shipped together in the **next versioned
release**. Do not commit feature work directly to `main`.

head: AGENTS.md > Feature delivery workflow (batched PRs → release)
text:
1. **Branch** off the latest `main`, one logical change per branch:
   `git checkout main && git pull && git checkout -b feat/<topic>`.

head: AGENTS.md > Feature delivery workflow (batched PRs → release)
text: 2. **Implement** the change; run `npm run typecheck`.

head: AGENTS.md > Feature delivery workflow (batched PRs → release)
text:
3. **Open a PR** to `main` with a summary + what was tested
   (`gh pr create --base main --fill`). CI runs `typecheck` on every PR.

head: AGENTS.md > Feature delivery workflow (batched PRs → release)
text: 4. **Batch & merge:** when several PRs are ready, merge them in sequence.

head: AGENTS.md > Feature delivery workflow (batched PRs → release)
text:
5. **Resolve conflicts** before merging: update the branch from `main`
   (`git checkout <branch> && git merge origin/main`), resolve, re-run
   `typecheck`, then merge. Prefer keeping both sides' intent; never drop a
   merged feature to "win" a conflict.

head: AGENTS.md > Feature delivery workflow (batched PRs → release)
text: 6. **Cut the release** once the batch is on `main` — see below.

head: AGENTS.md > Releasing a new version
text:
Releases are automated by `.github/workflows/release.yml`, triggered by pushing
a `vX.Y.Z` tag. The workflow type-checks, builds a clean downloadable source zip
(`git archive`, no `node_modules`/`.env`/logs/data), and publishes a GitHub
Release whose notes are the matching `CHANGELOG.md` section.

text: Supabase (your own project) is the only shared state between UI and gateway — the UI writes to `agent_commands`, daemons subscribe via Realtime and execute on their host. There is no direct network link between UI and gateway.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Architectural shape
text: - **Multi-workspace UI**: one UI instance manages N independent Supabase databases via the workspace registry. Each workspace is fully isolated. Within each database, every table enforces tenant-scoped RLS via `tenant_id`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Architectural shape
text: - **Multi-gateway per workspace**: each workspace can have multiple gateways (different hosts, different geos). Every agent has a `gateway_id`; daemons filter their command queue by their `GATEWAY_ID` env.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Architectural shape
text: - **Local-git-volume default**: each gateway owns a bare git repo in a Docker volume. Per-agent branches live there. Templates from `/opt/templates/` (baked into the gateway image) seed this repo on first boot. Optional `GIT_REMOTE_URL` lets users sync to GitHub/Gitea for backup.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Architectural shape
text: - **Remote desktop** via noVNC served from the gateway container. Tailscale is the recommended network path (private, no port exposure); public HTTPS (Caddy + Let's Encrypt) and local-only are alternatives.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Architectural shape
text: - **Usage budgets and org chart**: agent usage is recorded in `agent_usage`, budgets roll up in `agent_budgets`, and `agents.reports_to_id` gives runtime delegation context.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime
text: - `gateway/daemons/inbox_dispatcher.py` — watches `agent_inbox_items`, wakes agents via `openclaw agent`. Filters by `GATEWAY_ID` — only wakes agents bound to this gateway. Enriches `task_assignment` inbox items with unresolved blocker information from `task_relations`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime
text: - `gateway/daemons/command_runner.py` — watches `agent_commands`, leases via `lease_command(p_gateway_slug=GATEWAY_ID)`, executes shell commands. Heartbeats to the `gateways` table every 30s. Also subscribes to `secrets` table changes and triggers `sync_secrets()`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime
text: - `gateway/daemons/secrets_sync.py` — fetches encrypted secrets from Supabase, decrypts with AES-256-GCM (key derived via HKDF from the service role key), and writes per-agent `.env` files to `~/.openclaw/secrets/`. Triggered by Realtime on the `secrets` table and a 5-minute safety re-sync. Started by command_runner on boot.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime
text: - `gateway/daemons/file_processor.py` — leases `knowledge_items` with `kind='file'` and `processing_status='ready'`, downloads from storage, extracts text (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PPTX, TXT), updates `plain_text` and triggers embedding.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime
text: - `gateway/daemons/source_sync.py` — syncs external source connections via the plugin-based connector registry (`gateway/connectors/`). Polls `source_connections` where `next_sync_at <= now()`, fetches changes, upserts `knowledge_items` with `kind='source'`. Reads credentials from `~/.openclaw/secrets/gateway.env` (written by secrets_sync).

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime
text: - `gateway/daemons/plugin_runner.py` — watches `hq_plugin_event_queue` (SQL-trigger-emitted events), dispatches to enabled plugins (local Python handlers or remote webhook POSTs with HMAC). Subscribes to `hq_plugins` for config changes. Polling fallback every 5s.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime
text: - `gateway/embedder/embedder.py` — leases `knowledge_items` pending embedding via `lease_knowledge_items_for_indexing`, generates vector embeddings, creates chunks. HTTP server at `:9100` with `/embed` and `/healthz` endpoints.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime
text: - `gateway/daemons/sentry_init.py` — shared Sentry initialization for all daemons. Only active when `SENTRY_DSN` is set and `RUNTIME_MODE` is `hosted` or `e2b` (never in self-hosted). Provides `init_sentry(daemon_name)` and `capture(exc)`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Gateway runtime

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: `db/migrations/` contains 39 ordered migrations (001–039). Key tables:

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `gateways` — one row per gateway host. Seeded with a `default` row so single-gateway setups work immediately.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `agents` — agent definitions with `gateway_id`, `reports_to_id` hierarchy.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `knowledge_folders` / `knowledge_items` / `knowledge_item_agents` / `knowledge_chunks` — unified knowledge system. Items have `kind` (page/skill/file/source), `scope` (workspace/agent), embedding pipeline fields. Agent-scoped items use the junction table.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `entity_links` — universal polymorphic linking. Any owner (task, routine, collection_record, agent) can link to any target (knowledge_item, collection_record, contact, organization, task, url). Extended with `is_deliverable`, `review_status`, `review_note`, `submitted_by_agent_id` for agent-submitted work products on tasks.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `task_relations` — task-to-task dependency links (`blocked_by`, `blocks`, `relates_to`, `parent_of`, `child_of`). Used for dependency tracking and blocker resolution.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `labels` / `task_labels` — managed labels with color and description, linked to tasks via junction table.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `task_templates` — reusable task group templates with dependency graphs, stored as JSONB.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `routines` — scheduled and event-driven agent behaviors. Has `trigger_type` (schedule/event), cadence fields (sub-daily to monthly), and event fields (entity_type, field, condition, value).

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `collection_definitions` / `collection_fields` / `collection_records` / `collection_views` — user-defined tables with typed JSONB fields and saved views (table/kanban/calendar).

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `source_connections` / `source_sync_runs` — external source integrations via plugin-based connectors (`gateway/connectors/<provider>/`). Each provider has a `manifest.json`, auto-discovered by the registry. `writable` flag enables write-back. `source_write` command action routes writes through the command queue. Source connections reference `secrets` via `secret_id` FK for OAuth token storage.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `secrets` — encrypted credentials (AES-256-GCM). Scoped per gateway, optionally per agent. Categories: `user` (manual), `channel` (Telegram/Discord/Slack tokens), `integration` (OAuth tokens). Synced to gateway filesystem via Realtime. Values never exposed in API responses or logs.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `hq_plugins` — plugin registry. One row per installed plugin. Source types: `builtin`, `local`, `webhook`, `marketplace`. Has `hooks` (text array of subscribed events), `config` (operator settings), `config_schema` (JSON Schema), `webhook_url`/`webhook_secret` for remote plugins. Realtime-enabled.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `hq_plugin_events` — execution log. Every hook dispatch is recorded with status, duration, error message. 30-day retention via pg_cron.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `hq_plugin_state` — scoped key-value store for plugins. Keyed by `(plugin_id, scope_kind, scope_id, state_key)`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `hq_plugin_event_queue` — lightweight append-only queue bridging SQL triggers to the plugin runner daemon. Triggers on tasks, agents, knowledge_items, inbox, comments, secrets write here; plugin_runner polls/subscribes and dispatches. 1-hour retention via pg_cron.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `agent_commands` / `agent_inbox_items` — command queue and inbox for agent execution.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `agent_usage` / `agent_budgets` — append-only LLM usage plus per-agent budget rollups.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: - `tenants` — multi-tenant support via `tenant_id` on all tables, scoped RLS via `current_tenant_id()`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: Key RPCs: `search_knowledge_items()`, `search_knowledge_chunks()`, `lease_knowledge_items_for_indexing()`, `lease_knowledge_items_for_processing()`, `routine_next_occurrence()`, `spawn_routine_schedule_items()`, `lease_command()`, `get_agent_daily_usage()`, `get_task_relations()`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: Additional task infrastructure: `notify_blocker_resolved` trigger fires when a blocking task completes. `escalate_overdue_tasks` pg_cron job (every minute) marks overdue tasks as `missed` and creates inbox items for assigned agents.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Database
text: RLS: All tables use tenant-scoped policies via `current_tenant_id()` JWT claim. OSS uses a single default tenant (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`). The `service_role` key bypasses RLS.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **Code references**: use markdown link syntax when pointing the user at real files and specific lines.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **Supabase migrations**: always include explicit `GRANT` statements for `authenticated` and `service_role`. The project's Supabase setup does not grant these by default. *(Saved as memory — see user preferences.)*

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **New UI modules**: follow the existing pattern — types in `lib/<module>/types.ts`, hooks in `hooks/use-<module>.ts`, components in `components/<module>/`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **New daemon actions**: add the case to `command_runner.py`'s `build_command()`, add or migrate the `command_action` enum, and expose it as a server action in `apps/ui/src/app/dashboard/agents/actions.ts`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **New source connectors**: copy `gateway/connectors/_template/` to a new folder, fill in `manifest.json` and the connector methods, run `node scripts/build-source-manifests.mjs` to generate UI types. See `CONTRIBUTING-SOURCES.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **New plugins**: copy `gateway/plugins/_template/` to a new folder, edit `manifest.json` (id, hooks, config_schema, capabilities), implement `handler.py` (subclass `BasePlugin`, implement `on_event()`). For webhook plugins, no gateway code — register via Settings → Plugins. See `gateway/plugins/CONTRIBUTING.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **Dockerfile edits**: multi-arch build (amd64 + arm64) is the target. Use `TARGETARCH` arg when installing arch-specific binaries (Chrome vs Chromium, Tailscale, Caddy).

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **Colors and theming**: never use hardcoded hex, rgb(), or hsl(). All colors must resolve to CSS variable tokens via Tailwind utilities (`bg-primary`, `text-status-success`, `border-accent-blue/20`, etc.). The theme is user-customizable — workspace admins can change the brand color, surface warmth, and individual token overrides via Settings → Appearance. The derivation engine in `lib/theme/derive.ts` generates all CSS variables from a brand color + warmth; `components/theme-applier.tsx` injects them at runtime. When adding new interactive elements, use `bg-primary`/`text-primary` for the active/brand state. For new semantic roles, add a token to `globals.css` (both `:root` and `.dark`), wire it through `@theme inline`, and update the `ThemeTokens` type + derivation functions in `lib/theme/`.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **Testing**: run `make test` before committing. UI tests use Vitest + jsdom + React Testing Library; see `TESTING.md` for patterns. New hooks get a test file in `__tests__/hooks/`, new lib modules in `__tests__/lib/`, new components in `__tests__/components/`. Mock Supabase at the boundary via `createMockSupabaseClient`, never mock internal logic. Use factories (`buildTask`, `buildAgent`, etc.) for test data. Coverage thresholds are enforced in CI — run `make test-coverage` if you've added source files.

head: CLAUDE.md — HQ > Conventions
text: - **Comments**: default to none. Only add one when the *why* is non-obvious (a hidden constraint, a subtle invariant, a workaround). Don't narrate what the code does.

head: CLAUDE.md > What This Is
text: SAPMAP (SAP Landscape Attack Path Mapper) is a security research tool for SAP NetWeaver environments. It discovers SAP systems, maps RFC trust relationships, executes known exploits (Gateway SAPXPG unauth RCE, 10KBLAZE MS betrusted chain, CVE-2025-31324, etc.), and visualizes the attack surface as an interactive web map. Requires written authorization before use — see `DISCLAIMER.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Module Path Registration
text: `modules/__init__.py` appends every subpackage directory to `sys.path` at import time. This allows flat imports (`from sapmap_models import ...`) anywhere in the codebase regardless of caller location. Tests rely on `tests/conftest.py` doing the same path registration.

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: **Single SAPMAP user/password:** All exploit methods use a hardcoded credential (`SAPMAP00` / `Andinyougo123!`) with pre-computed password hashes embedded in `modules/core/sapmap_config.py`. This avoids needing the RFC SDK just to hash a password.

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: **Multi-method fallback chains:** When a primary method fails (e.g. SecStore extraction, RFC probing), code silently tries the next method rather than erroring. Understand the full chain before concluding a method is "broken."

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: **Lazy imports:** `pyrfc`, `pyyaml`, `pyjks`, `pywebview`, and `pycryptodome` are only imported when the feature requiring them is invoked. Import errors surface at use time, not startup.

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: **State file format:** `.sapmap` files are plain JSON — safe to inspect and manually edit. Auto-saved on exit; Ctrl+S triggers a manual save via the GUI.

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: **Artifacts:** `states/` (session files) and `loot/` (extracted secrets, hashes, reports) are gitignored and created at runtime.

head: AGENTS.md — pipeshub-ai > Storage is pluggable
text: Do not open a Neo4j, Arango, Qdrant, or Kafka client from indexing/query/connector feature code. Call `IGraphDBProvider`, `IVectorDBService`, or `MessagingFactory`. Those factories read env and construct the vendor client; your code stays the same on a Neo4j box and an Arango box.

head: AGENTS.md — pipeshub-ai > Storage is pluggable
text:
| Role | Env | Backends | Interface / factory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph | `DATA_STORE` | `neo4j` (what `install.sh`, Helm, and `backend/env.template` ship), `arangodb` | `IGraphDBProvider` / `GraphDBProviderFactory`; connectors use `GraphDataStore` |
| Vector | `VECTOR_DB_TYPE` | `qdrant` (default), `opensearch`, `redis` | `IVectorDBService` / `VectorDBProviderFactory` |
| KV / config | `KV_STORE_TYPE` | `redis` (default), `etcd` | `KeyValueStore` / `KeyValueStoreFactory`. Python config reads go through `ConfigurationService`, never the store directly |
| Document | — | MongoDB | Mongoose in the Node API (users, orgs, sessions). Not swapped today |
| Blob | storage config | local, S3, Azure Blob | `StorageServiceInterface` (`backend/nodejs/apps/src/modules/storage/`) |
| Broker | `MESSAGE_BROKER` | `kafka`, `redis` (streams) | `MessagingFactory` |

head: AGENTS.md — pipeshub-ai > Storage is pluggable
