head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Lighthouse (demo site)
text:
**Performance is held at 95, not 100, and that is deliberate.** Measured August
2026, all three pages sit at **99** across repeated runs, and the shortfall is
entirely one metric — LCP ~1030 ms scoring 0.94 of a weight-25 audit. Everything
else is perfect (FCP ~290 ms, total blocking time 6-13 ms). 95 leaves ~4 points
for runner variance while still failing on a real regression. Total blocking time
being near zero is what makes that safe: almost no main-thread work is in play, so
a slower CI runner moves this far less than it would for a hydration-heavy app.
Accessibility, best-practices and SEO are deterministic and held at 100.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: The published package resolves as **ESM only**: `"type": "module"`, and no subpath declares a `require` condition. A CJS build ships alongside it but nothing resolves to it — see the second bullet.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **Why nothing resolves to CJS.** `subscribers.ts` keeps its store in module-scoped `WeakMap`s. A consumer whose graph resolves both builds gets two stores and `useSharedState` silently stops sharing — the same class of failure as the react-router dual-load that prompted this, and unfixable from the consumer side.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **A CJS build is still emitted, as `.cjs`, and deliberately left out of `exports`.** Normal resolution therefore cannot reach it (`ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` even for an explicit `state-in-url/dist/...` subpath); only a real file path does — a Jest `moduleNameMapper`, a bundler alias. That is a whole-process substitution rather than a second copy, so the hazard above does not apply, and it gives Jest users a route that needs no flag. `.cjs` rather than `.js` because `"type": "module"` would otherwise parse it as ESM.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **`engines.node` is `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`** — the versions where Node's `require(esm)` is unflagged, so a CommonJS consumer can still `require()` this package. Verified, not assumed.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **Jest is the one consumer that pays.** It uses its own synchronous `vm` API and does not inherit Node's unflagged `require(esm)`, so it needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules` on Node 24.9+, or a `moduleNameMapper` onto the emitted `dist/*.cjs`. README Gotchas item 5 carries both recipes; `pnpm test:consumers` runs the Jest suite each way, with the flag and through the mapper, so neither can rot.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **Exports map: `types` first, `default` last, no `require`.** Conditions match in declaration order, so `types` after anything else is shadowed and TS falls back to guessing. `packages/urlstate/exportsTest.ts` asserts all three, including the absent `require`, so putting the emitted `.cjs` back on the resolution path has to be a deliberate edit.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **`next/navigation` gets its extension in the build, not the source.** Next ships no `exports` map (checked on 14.2, 15.5, 16.3), so Node resolves it as a file path and ESM does no extension guessing: the bare specifier is `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for anything loading the build through Node rather than a bundler — a Vitest suite with the package externalized, most realistically, where it fails at collection with an error naming only `next/navigation`. Rollup's `output.paths` on the ESM output adds the `.js`, so the source and the emitted `.d.ts` keep the bare specifier that every bundler wants and that survives Next adding an `exports` map later. CJS needs nothing; `require()` still guesses extensions. `exportsTest.ts` asserts the built `.mjs` carries it.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **`react-router` is a `>=6` peer, not `>=7`.** npm satisfies an open optional peer by installing react-router 8, which collides with the react-router 6 that `react-router-dom@6` and Remix 2 pull in — `npm install` then fails outright for those consumers.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **`packages/example-*` does not exercise the published package.** The Vite and Astro examples alias `state-in-url` to the library *source*, and the Next examples reach it through a `workspace:*` symlink — so the Playwright suite proves the hooks work, never that `dist/` and the `exports` map do. `pnpm test:consumers` is the only thing that installs the real tarball, and it builds a minimal App Router app (`packages/consumer-tests/next-app/`) so a bundler sees the published map too.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **`packages/consumer-tests` is excluded from the root `tsconfig.base.json`.** Its files are fixtures copied into throwaway projects, so `state-in-url/next` resolves only there; a root typecheck reports TS2307. `next build` inside the matrix is what typechecks them. The exclusion cannot carry its own comment — the JSON is reformatted on save and a comment there is stripped. A stray `pnpm install` inside that directory hides the failure locally by symlinking the repo in as `state-in-url`, which is how it reached CI green locally.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - Run `pnpm test:consumers` after touching any of this. It packs the tarball and checks 99 combinations: six framework consumers across pnpm, npm, yarn (node-modules), yarn (PnP) and bun, in ESM and CJS, plus Vitest, Jest and `bun test` suites. The `consumers` job in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs it, and the script exits non-zero on CI when a package manager is missing — otherwise an absent bun would shrink the matrix and still report a pass.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Packaging
text: - **`bun test` needs no workaround.** It reads the exports map itself, so react-router 7 passes under it with none of the `deps.inline` Vitest requires — the same three files, unchanged. Its one need is a DOM: bun has no `environment` switch, so `bunfig.toml` preloads `bun.setup.mjs`, which registers happy-dom's globals.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Conventions
text: - **Conventional commits** (commitlint + commitizen enforced via husky). Releases are automated by semantic-release. `fix:` and `feat:` bump the version and **must only be used for changes inside `packages/urlstate/` or `package.json`** — use `ci`, `build`, `docs`, `style`, `test`, `chore`, `refactor` for everything else (examples, tests, config).

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Conventions
text: - ESLint config (`.eslintrc.cjs`) uses `plugin:maintainable/recommended` with a complexity cap of 12 and enforced import sorting; Prettier runs via lint-staged on commit. Unused vars must be prefixed `_`.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Conventions
text: - Node 24 (`.nvmrc`). Build target ES2022.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > Conventions
text: - When adding a new entry point, add it to the `exports` map in `package.json` and ensure its `index.ts` is picked up by the Rollup glob (`packages/urlstate/**/index.ts`).

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > The demo site's AI-discovery surfaces
text:
`packages/example-nextjs16` is what <https://state-in-url.dev> serves, and it
answers agents in four overlapping ways — they disagree about which to try:

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > The demo site's AI-discovery surfaces
text:
| Surface | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `/llms.txt` | `public/llms.txt` — the single source |
| `/` under `Accept: text/markdown`, or a known agent user-agent — 307 to `/index.md` | `src/proxy.ts` |
| `/index.md`, `/react-router.md`, `/remix.md`, `/astro.md` | `src/app/<route>.md/route.ts`, all four through `src/app/llmsTxtResponse.ts` |
| `/nextjs.md`, `/vs/nuqs.md` | built from the page's own copy module and samples — those pages have content of their own |
| `<link rel="alternate">` and a `Link:` response header | `src/app/seoStuff.ts` (`markdownAlternates`), `next.config.mjs` |

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > The demo site's AI-discovery surfaces
text:
All three `.md` mirrors serve the same document, deliberately: this site is one
page repeated per router variant, and `public/llms.txt` documents Next.js,
React Router and Remix together. Three near-identical files would be three
things to keep in sync and would answer no question better.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > The demo site's AI-discovery surfaces
text:
**The one rule that matters: `/` must never carry a Markdown body.** Vercel's
edge cache keys on the URL path and does not honour `Vary`, and Next overwrites
`Vary` on dynamic App Router responses anyway. A cacheable Markdown variant is
pinned into the entry for `/` by the first agent that asks, and every reader
after it gets raw text until it expires — a 200 throughout, so nothing alerts.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > The demo site's AI-discovery surfaces
text:
`src/proxy.ts` therefore answers an agent with a **307 to `/index.md`**. `/` is
left holding only HTML, and the document sits on a URL with one representation
that caches normally — `max-age=3600` and a CDN hit, instead of the `no-store`
an inline body needs.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > The demo site's AI-discovery surfaces
text:
307, not 308: a permanent redirect is heuristically cacheable under RFC 9111,
and one held under `/` would send readers to the mirror.

head: AGENTS — state-in-url > The demo site's AI-discovery surfaces
text:
The negotiation stays in the proxy rather than moving to `next.config.mjs`
`redirects()`, which would decide it at the CDN with no function involved. Next
compiles a `has` condition to ``new RegExp(`^${value}$`)`` — anchored, no `i`
flag — so these patterns cannot be ported as written: `(?i)` throws in JS,
`(?i:…)` is a V8-only ES2025 modifier Vercel's router need not accept, and the
anchoring turns a token list into a whole-string match no real user-agent
satisfies. Two engines disagreeing about one rule is the shape of every
incident in this file. One engine, testable locally.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: - `skills/`: standalone Agent Skills with `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, and `githubclaw.json`; add `scripts/`, `src/`, `references/`, or `assets/` only when needed.

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: Use ESM JavaScript for Worker and skill scripts. Keep modules small and purpose-named, such as `config.js`, `line.js`, or `resolve-worker-name.mjs`. Use kebab-case directories and `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` environment variables.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: Worker tests live in `workers/line-bot/test/` and use Node’s `node --test` runner. Name tests with the `.test.js` suffix, for example `config.test.js`. Add tests for parsing, configuration, request handling, and branch/name normalization when changing Worker behavior. Skills rely on build checks or script-level manual verification unless they define tests.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: Use Conventional Commits 1.0.0: `<type>[optional scope]: <description>`, with optional body and footers. Examples: `feat(error-handler-action): ...`, `fix(workflow): ...`, `docs: ...`, and `chore(templates): ...`. Avoid literal string `\n` in commit messages; use actual newline characters. Do not create message bodies with repeated `git commit -m` parameters. Write the full message to a temporary file and run `git commit -F /tmp/commit-message.txt`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: Pull requests should describe changed paths, link related issues, list validation commands, and attach screenshots or sample outputs for user-facing content.

head: Repository Guidelines > Action Release Reminder
text: Reusable workflow consumers are pinned to the `v1` tag. If any file under `actions/` changes, explicitly remind the maintainer to decide whether to republish or move `v1` to the latest compatible commit. Do not move tags unless asked.

head: Repository Guidelines > Security & Configuration Tips
text: Never commit API keys, LINE tokens, GitHub tokens, `.dev.vars`, or generated dependency directories. For `workers/line-bot/`, copy expected variables from `env.example`, then use `WORKER_NAME=your-worker-name bun run set` to upload secrets through Wrangler.

head: CLAUDE.md > Guidelines
text: - Never bypass or suppress errors (e.g. no `unwrap`, `#[allow(...)]`, `--no-verify`, ignoring `Result`s) without asking the user first.

head: CLAUDE.md > Guidelines

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: `cl` is a command organization and execution tool. It stores commands (with aliases, namespaces, and named parameters) in a TOML file and provides two interfaces: a CLI and a TUI.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Workspace layout
text: - **cl-core** — domain types and logic (no I/O concerns)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Workspace layout
text: - **cl-cli** — `clap`-based CLI; defaults to launching the TUI when called with no subcommand

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Workspace layout
text: - **cl-gui** — `ratatui`-based TUI

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core domain (cl-core)
text: `Command<'cmd>` is the central type: `alias`, `namespace`, `command` string, optional `description` and `tags`. Named parameters in commands use `#{name}` syntax and are substituted at execution time.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core domain (cl-core)
text: `Commands<'cmd>` wraps a `HashMap<Namespace, Vec<Command>>` and exposes `add`, `edit`, `remove`, `find(alias, namespace)`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core domain (cl-core)
text: `Config` trait abstracts configuration; `DefaultConfig` reads/writes TOML at `~/.config/cl/config.toml`. Command data is stored at `~/.config/cl/commands.toml`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core domain (cl-core)
text: Extension traits (`CommandVecExt`, `CommandMapExt`) add sorting, filtering, and mapping helpers to standard collections.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > CLI subcommands (cl-cli)
text:
| Subcommand | Alias | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `exec` | `x` | Find and execute a stored command, substituting `#{param}` via `--param=value` flags |
| `share` | `s` | Import/export commands |
| `config` | — | Manage settings |
| `add` | — | Add a command without the TUI |
| `misc` | — | Hidden utilities |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: Uses an actor model with Tokio channels:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: - **`StateActor`** owns app state; receives `StateEvent` messages from the UI

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: - **`UiActor`** renders with ratatui and emits `StateEvent` on key input

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: UI is stack-based with a `Layer` trait:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: - `MainScreenLayer` — namespace tabs + command list

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: - `EditScreenLayer` — form for editing command fields

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: - `QuickSearchLayer` — fuzzy search via `nucleo-matcher`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: - `PopupLayer` — error/confirmation dialogs

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TUI (cl-gui)
text: `SignalHandler` intercepts SIGTERM/Ctrl-C and coordinates graceful shutdown via a `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Benchmarks
text: `benches/core.rs` uses Criterion with sample data at `benches/data/sample.toml`. Benchmarks cover init, find, update, add, and remove operations on `Commands`.

head: html-video 项目工作区 > 会话进度（2026-06-07）— Remotion 原生数据模板 + 按帧增强（Phase A+B 跑通，**git 待 Joey 定**）
text: - **混流 concat 不能用 concat demuxer + 重编码**：hyperframes 与 Remotion 段的 timebase/PTS 不兼容，concat demuxer 会**错误累加时间戳→8s 片变 35s**（`-vsync cfr` 也救不了，因为坏 PTS 已被喂进来）。**正解 = concat FILTER**：每段独立 `-i` + `-filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]...concat=n=N:v=1[v]"` 重建时间轴 → 精确 8s。单引擎仍走 demuxer `-c copy`（快、无损）。判混流类输出**必须 ffprobe 量时长 + `ffmpeg -f null -` 全解码**，不能只看文件生成。

text:
**#22 字体跳闪真根因（两轮才修对）**：① 第一版只加 `document.fonts.ready` 等待——不够，因为纯 CSS
`@keyframes` 动画在 `goto` 后**不等字体就自动跑**，等字体的 ~3s 连同 FOUT 一起被 playwright 录进开头，
单文件模板还不裁死区。② 正解：`addInitScript` 注入 `* {animation-play-state:paused}` 在文档解析前**冻结所有动画**
→ 等 stylesheet link + `fonts.load()` 每个 face + `fonts.ready` → 解冻并把冻结期当 leadInMs 裁掉。统一了单文件 + 多 composition 时序。
对 CSS/rAF/setTimeout 三类驱动都验证首帧字体正确（`fonts.check()=true`）。

text: Guidance for coding agents (and humans) contributing to `terraform-provider-groundcover`. This file complements [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) — it captures the conventions that come up repeatedly in code review.

head: AGENTS.md > Repo layout
text: - `internal/provider/` — resource implementations (`resource_<name>.go`), API clients (`client_<name>.go`), tests (`resource_<name>_test.go`), shared utils (`yaml_utils.go`, etc.)

head: AGENTS.md > Repo layout
text: - `examples/resources/groundcover_<name>/resource.tf` — HCL example per resource

head: AGENTS.md > Repo layout
text: - `docs/` — generated docs; regenerated from schema + templates via `make generate`

head: AGENTS.md > Repo layout
text: - `templates/` — doc templates consumed by `tfplugindocs`

head: AGENTS.md > Repo layout
text: - `tools/` — doc generation tooling (`cd tools && go generate ./...`)

head: AGENTS.md > Repo layout
text: - `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `REFERENCE.md` — must be kept in sync with code changes

head: AGENTS.md > PR checklist
text: Every PR must include this checklist in its description, with items checked as appropriate:

head: AGENTS.md > PR checklist
text: - [ ] I have written acceptance tests for my changes

head: AGENTS.md > PR checklist
text: - [ ] I have run `make generate` to update generated docs

head: AGENTS.md > PR checklist
text: - [ ] I have added examples demonstrating the new functionality

head: AGENTS.md > PR checklist
text: - [ ] I have updated the README.md with details of changes

head: AGENTS.md > PR checklist
text: - [ ] I have updated the CHANGELOG.md file

head: AGENTS.md > PR checklist > PR title convention
text: Use a clear prefix: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`. When the work is tracked in Linear, prefix the title or branch with the ticket ID (e.g. `BE-1234: ...`).

head: AGENTS.md > Changelog & versioning
text: Follow semantic versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`):

head: AGENTS.md > Changelog & versioning
text: - **patch** (`x.y.Z+1`) — bug fixes, doc-only changes, internal refactors with no user-facing impact

head: AGENTS.md > Changelog & versioning
text: - **minor** (`x.Y+1.0`) — new resources, new attributes, new optional behavior, SDK bumps that add functionality

head: AGENTS.md > Changelog & versioning
text: - **major** (`X+1.0.0`) — backwards-incompatible changes (removed resources/attributes, breaking schema changes)

head: AGENTS.md > Changelog & versioning
text: Before adding a new version section to `CHANGELOG.md`:

head: AGENTS.md > Changelog & versioning
text: 1. Run `git tag --sort=-v:refname | head -5` to see the latest tagged release.

head: AGENTS.md > Changelog & versioning
text: 2. Look at `CHANGELOG.md` for any **unreleased** version section above the last tag. If one exists (the version is in the changelog but not tagged yet), **append to that section** — do **not** create a new version above it.

head: AGENTS.md > Changelog & versioning
text: 3. Only create a new version section when no unreleased section exists.

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Where tests live
text: Add tests to the **existing test file** for the area you're touching (e.g. add to `yaml_utils_test.go`, not a new `*_extra_test.go`). Don't create parallel test files for new cases.

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: Acceptance tests hit a real backend and run slowly (30s–90s+ each). Keep coverage focused on what only acceptance tests can catch:

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: **Required for every resource:**

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: - CRUD — create, read, update, delete

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: - Disappears — resource removed out-of-band still reconciles

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: - Regressions — e.g. no perpetual plan diff / apply loop

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: **Optional (one or two, not exhaustive):**

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: - One major top-level variant of a complex schema (e.g. "Simple" vs "Advanced"). Prefer **unit tests** for finer-grained variant coverage.

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: - One acceptance test per provider in connected apps

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: - One acceptance test per mutation in synthetic tests

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: - Exhaustive enum / variant coverage — those belong in unit tests or are already covered by backend tests

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Acceptance test scope
text: If you're reviewing a PR that adds many acceptance test variants beyond CRUD/disappears/regression, suggest moving variant coverage to unit tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Tests > Running tests
text: Required env vars for acceptance tests:

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text: When adding `groundcover_<name>`:

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text: 1. `internal/provider/resource_<name>.go` — schema, CRUD, import

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text: 2. `internal/provider/client_<name>.go` — API client wrapper

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text: 3. `internal/provider/resource_<name>_test.go` — CRUD + disappears + regression acceptance tests

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text: 4. `examples/resources/groundcover_<name>/resource.tf` — HCL example

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text: 5. `make generate` — refresh `docs/resources/<name>.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text:
6. **`README.md`** — add an entry in **both** lists:
   - "Usage Examples" — bullet linking to the example file
   - "Running Tests" — the `TF_ACC=1 go test ... -run TestAcc<Name>Resource` command

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text: 7. `CHANGELOG.md` — append to the existing unreleased section, or create one

head: AGENTS.md > Adding a new resource
text: The README per-resource lists are frequently missed; check both before opening the PR.

head: AGENTS.md > Schema & deprecation
text: When introducing a new "preferred" config form while keeping the old form working for backward compatibility, it is **intentional** to:

head: AGENTS.md > Schema & deprecation
text: - Accept both forms in the validator

head: AGENTS.md > Schema & deprecation
text: - Document **only** the new form in the schema description and generated docs

head: AGENTS.md > Schema & deprecation
text: - Update examples to use only the new form

head: AGENTS.md > Schema & deprecation
text: Don't "fix" the schema description to also mention the legacy form for consistency with the validator — the omission is deliberate, so new users aren't confused by two ways to do the same thing.

head: AGENTS.md > Common make targets
text: Run `make fmt lint` and `make generate` before opening a PR.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text: - Follow standard Go idioms; `gofmt` is enforced.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text: - Match the existing patterns in neighbouring resources rather than introducing new abstractions for a single use case.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text: - Use lowercase "groundcover" in user-facing strings and docs.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text: - Handle API errors with clear messages and include retry logic for transient failures where the SDK doesn't already do so.

head: Customer docs
text: Uses **Bun**, not npm or pnpm.

head: Customer docs
text: - When adding a page, register it in `navigation.json` after creating the file.

head: Customer docs
text: - FAQs use a `faqItems` field in frontmatter (JSON array with `question` and `answer`) plus `{% faq /%}` in the body. See `billing.mdoc` for an example.

head: Customer docs
text: - Local build: `bun run build`.

head: AGENTS.md
text: > On 1st message, greet user with: "AI-Driven Development On ⚡"

head: AGENTS.md > Behavior
text: - **Stay critical.** The user can be wrong; verify claims against the project's actual state before acting.

head: AGENTS.md > Behavior
text: - **Be anti-sycophantic:** no flattery or filler, don't fold under pushback, never open with "you are right". Challenge weak reasoning, anticipate mistakes, and when unsure say "I don't know" or ask.

head: AGENTS.md > Behavior
text: - **Surface tradeoffs and evaluate their impact** instead of hiding them.

head: AGENTS.md > Communication
text: - **Answer first:** result before reason. Drop pleasantries (sure, of course, happy to) and hedging.

head: AGENTS.md > Communication
text: - **No preamble or recap:** don't restate the request or summarize visible changes. Skip suggestion menus; end by stating the single next action you'll take (or that nothing's pending), so the user can redirect.

head: AGENTS.md > Communication
text: - **Evidence over assertion:** back "works", "tested", "fixed" with the command, output, or file that proves it.

head: AGENTS.md > Communication
text: - **Quote the shortest decisive line** of an error or log, not the whole dump.

head: AGENTS.md > Communication
text: - **No tool-call narration.** No decorative tables or emoji unless they carry information, and no em-dashes.

head: AGENTS.md > Communication
text: - **In chat, write for a reader who scans:** telegraphic, fewest words, fragments over sentences, arrows (=>) for relationships. Cut any word that doesn't change meaning. Normal prose in authored docs and code. Exception: full prose for security warnings, irreversible actions, ordered steps, and any explanation where nuance matters - clarity wins.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Surgical changes:** ship the minimum that solves the problem; touch only what the task needs, and leave the code cleaner than you found it.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Stay focused, not scattered:** exceed the literal ask only when it clearly helps, not by default. When you spot an unrelated issue, note it in one line and keep going; detour only if it blocks the task.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Solve your own issues first:** genuinely try to resolve it yourself before escalating to the human.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Do not commit or push** unless the user asks.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Don't assume your knowledge is current.**

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Placement discipline:** for every plugin change, think hard about where responsibility belongs; follow `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Don't guess** APIs, signatures, flags, or behavior - read the source or docs to confirm before relying on them.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Ambiguous or expensive task:** ask one sharp question to pin down scope before building, rather than guess.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Batch independent operations** in one pass, not one at a time.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Fan out** independent subtasks to parallel subagents when you own the overall flow and the work is genuinely parallel.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Before adding any instruction, finding, or rule, check whether an existing one already covers or contradicts it.** If so, don't add a parallel: delete it, merge it into the stronger one, or rewrite with explicit scope and priority.

head: AGENTS.md > Action
text: - **Name by intention, not mechanism:** describe the goal or responsibility, not the tool or file format.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy
text: Custom Lovelace Dashboard Strategy for Home Assistant. Generates dynamic dashboards from area/device/entity metadata with flexible user configuration. This project is actively used by Simons loved YouTube viewers — clean, stable code is top priority.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture
text:
**Language:** TypeScript (ES2020, strict mode)
**Build:** Webpack → code-split chunks (main + lit + core + views + editor on-demand)
**Distribution:** HACS-compatible (Custom Repository), deployed to `/config/www/community/simon42-dashboard-strategy/`

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Module Overview
text:
Output:
```
dist/
├── simon42-dashboard-strategy.js                        # Entry point (instant custom element registration)
├── simon42-dashboard-strategy-core.<hash>.js            # Registry, cards, utils
├── simon42-dashboard-strategy-lit.<hash>.js             # Lit framework (shared)
├── simon42-dashboard-strategy-views.<hash>.js           # All view strategies
├── simon42-dashboard-strategy-editor.<hash>.js          # Editor (lazy-loaded on demand)
├── *.js.gz / *.js.br                                    # Pre-compressed variants
└── *.LICENSE.txt                                        # License files
```

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Data Flow
text: 1. **Entry Point** registers custom elements, calls `Registry.initialize(hass, config)` synchronously

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Data Flow
text: 2. **Registry** reads entity/device/area data from `hass` object (synchronous), builds pre-computed Maps/Sets

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Data Flow
text: 3. **Utils** collect persons, weather, favorites using pre-filtered Registry methods

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Data Flow
text: 4. **Section Builders** generate overview, areas, weather/energy sections

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Data Flow
text: 5. **View Builders** generate utility views (lights, covers, security, batteries, climate) + per-area room views

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Data Flow
text: 6. **Custom Cards** render reactive UI (real-time `hass` updates via `set hass()`)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: The Registry is a **static singleton** (no instance, all static members). Initialized once, then provides O(1) lookups everywhere.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text:
**Synchronous Init** (reads directly from hass object, no WebSocket needed):
```
Object.values(hass.entities)  → EntityRegistryDisplayEntry[]
Object.values(hass.devices)   → DeviceRegistryEntry[]
Object.values(hass.areas)     → AreaRegistryEntry[]
```
Called once in dashboard strategy `generate()` before views are returned. Idempotent — subsequent calls in view strategies are no-ops.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text:
| Map | Key | Value | Filtered? |
|-----|-----|-------|-----------|
| `_entityById` | entity_id | EntityRegistryDisplayEntry | Raw |
| `_deviceById` | device_id | DeviceRegistryEntry | Raw |
| `_entitiesByDevice` | device_id | entity_id[] | Raw |
| `_entitiesByDomain` | domain | entity_id[] | Raw |
| `_entitiesByArea` | area_id | EntityRegistryDisplayEntry[] | Raw |
| `_visibleEntitiesByArea` | area_id | EntityRegistryDisplayEntry[] | **Pre-filtered** |
| `_visibleEntitiesByDomain` | domain | entity_id[] | **Pre-filtered** |
| `_configDiagEntitiesByArea` | area_id | EntityRegistryDisplayEntry[] | Config/diagnostic only |

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: Raw Maps stay available for the Editor (needs all entities for show/hide toggles).

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: **Pre-Filtering** (applied once during init via `_isEntityVisible()`):

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: - Not in `_excludeSet` (no "no_dboard" label)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: - Not in `_hiddenFromConfig` (not in `areas_options.*.groups_options.*.hidden`)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: - Not `hidden_by` (user or integration)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: - Not `disabled_by` (user or integration)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: - Not `entity_category` "config" or "diagnostic"

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: Downstream code uses pre-filtered methods directly — no redundant inline checks.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > Registry — Core Design
text: **Area resolution** (entity → area): `entity.area_id` → device area → parent device area. Since HA 2026.9 a device can be a *child* of another device (`parent_device_id`, e.g. one sub-device per camera lens); a child with `area_id: null` inherits the parent's area, exactly like HA's own `getDeviceAreaId`. Always resolve via `Registry.getDeviceAreaId(deviceId)` (or `getEffectiveDeviceAreaId()` from `utils/device-utils.ts` in the editor, which reads `hass.devices`) — never read `device.area_id` directly, or entities on child devices silently drop out of their room.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > HA Entity Registry vs. State-Attributes (CRITICAL)
text: Many entity properties exist ONLY in the Entity Registry, NOT in state attributes. Always use the registry as primary source:

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > HA Entity Registry vs. State-Attributes (CRITICAL)
text:
| Property | Registry (`hass.entities[id]`) | State attributes |
|----------|-------------------------------|-----------------|
| `hidden_by` | "user", "integration", null | NOT available |
| `disabled_by` | "user", "integration", null | NOT available |
| `entity_category` | "config", "diagnostic", null | Sometimes copied, often missing |
| `platform` | "mobile_app", "mqtt", etc. | NOT available |
| `device_id` | device UUID | NOT available |

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Architecture > HA Entity Registry vs. State-Attributes (CRITICAL)
text: **Rule:** Always read `hidden_by`, `disabled_by`, `entity_category`, and `platform` from the registry. Group cards (lights, covers) get entities pre-filtered from the registry array — they have these fields directly on the entity object. The summary card works with `hass.states` keys and must look up registry entries via `hass.entities?.[id]`.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - **No `const fn = () => ...` arrow function assignments** — Biome's Qwik rule false-positives on them ("Non-serializable expression must be wrapped with $(...)"). Use `function` declarations instead. Applies to src AND test files, and to **function-local** const arrows too, not just module level (hit repeatedly, latest in #336).

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - No `any` in new signatures (`Record<string, unknown>` over `Record<string, any>`)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - No dynamic `obj[variable]` lookups on config objects — use `Map`/`Reflect.get` (detect-object-injection). **`hass.states[someVar]` in new/changed lines counts too** — use the `stateFor()`/`Reflect.get` helpers.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - **Always bind the catch parameter in async functions**: `catch (error: unknown)` — Codacy's security-node rule doesn't know optional catch binding (`catch {`).

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - Codacy's API can report ghost findings pinned to lines that no longer block the quality gate — when a finding looks inexplicable, check the PR check status first instead of contorting the code.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - **The quality gate is `issueThreshold: 0`** — EVERY new finding blocks, Warning severity included, and **moved lines count as new lines** (refactor PRs get fully rescanned). Budget for this before large moves.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - **Reproduce the type-aware rules locally instead of API whack-a-mole:** temporary eslint flat config with `parserOptions.project` enabling `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` + `no-non-null-assertion`, run on the touched files. One pass finds everything (the PR-issues API paginates at 100 and hides findings).

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - **Record-type lookups lie** (`tsconfig` has no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`): `no-unnecessary-condition` demands removing `?.` on `Record` values that CAN be absent at runtime (e.g. `groups_options.badges`). Do NOT drop the guard — rewrite as `Reflect.get(obj, key) as T | undefined` so the condition stays type-honest. Only drop `?.`/fallbacks where the API really guarantees presence (`hass.states[x].attributes`, `hass.areas/devices/entities`, `EntityRegistryEntry.labels` — HA floor 2024.7).

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - Array index access `arr[i]` also triggers detect-object-injection — use `arr.at(i)` (lib ES2022) + `splice(i, 1, next)` for writes.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - `xss/no-mixed-html` and `@typescript-eslint/no-confusing-void-expression` are file-level disabled in `src/editor/**` (mass false positives on lit-html / house-style event arrows); a no-op stub plugin in `eslint.config.mjs` keeps the directives valid locally. The `.codacy.yml` engine switch (adopted from oriel-dashboard) is currently NOT honored by our Codacy setup — disabling the legacy ESLint8 engine in the Codacy UI would supersede the inline disables.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - Semgrep flags `yaml.load()` as RCE — false positive for js-yaml v4 (safe schema by default); suppress with `// nosemgrep` on the call line.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Codacy Pitfalls (CI blocks on "high" findings)
text: - Findings without auth: `https://app.codacy.com/api/v3/analysis/organizations/gh/TheRealSimon42/repositories/simon42-dashboard-strategy/pull-requests/<N>/issues` (paginated via `cursor`!)

text: **Never commit directly to `main`.** Always use feature branches.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Feature Development
text: 1. `git checkout -b feature/<name>` from `main`

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Feature Development
text: 2. Develop, build, test on live system

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Feature Development
text: 3. **Source only — `dist/` is gitignored and never committed.** HACS serves the built files as release assets (see Release Automation below); old tags (≤ v1.3.4-beta.9) still carry their committed `dist/`

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Feature Development
text: 6. **PR titles must be Conventional Commits** (`feat: …`, `fix: …`, `feat(scope)!: …`, `chore: …`) — squash merges make the PR title the commit message, and release-please derives version bumps and CHANGELOG entries from it. `feat`/`fix` trigger a release; `chore`/`docs`/`ci`/`refactor` don't. Runtime-relevant dependency bumps should therefore be merged as `fix(deps): …`, not `chore(deps): …`, or they never reach a release

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Feature Development

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Feature Development

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: Releases are cut by **release-please** — no manual version bumps, no manual CHANGELOG edits, no manual tags:

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: 1. On every push to `main`, `release-please.yml` maintains a permanent **Release PR** (runs under the `simon42-release-bot` GitHub App — GITHUB_TOKEN events don't trigger workflows, see the workflow header). The PR bumps `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `STRATEGY_VERSION` (via the `// x-release-please-version` marker — **never remove that comment**) and writes the CHANGELOG entry from the Conventional-Commit squash titles since the last release

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: 2. Merging the Release PR makes release-please **publish** the (pre-)release directly. No draft: GitHub delivers no `release` workflow events for drafts, and release-please doesn't count drafts as released (learned the hard way on beta.13 — stalled pipeline + phantom next-version PR)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: 3. `release-build.yml` fires on `release: published`, builds, verifies (`verify-release-version.mjs`, `verify-release-bundle.mjs`) and uploads all `dist/*.js` (+ `.gz`/`.br`/LICENSE) files as individual assets. The release is asset-less for the ~2 minutes the build takes — a HACS poll in that window fails once and self-heals

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: 4. HACS installs tagged versions from the release assets. `hide_default_branch: true` in `hacs.json` prevents installing `main`, which has no `dist/`

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: - **Do not create GitHub releases or tags manually.** The legacy tag-push workflows are removed — with direct publishing, the App-token tag push would have double-triggered them

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: - Versioning is configured in `release-please-config.json`. During a beta cycle: `"versioning": "prerelease"` + `"prerelease-type": "beta"` increment `beta.N` on every `feat`/`fix`

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: - **Cutting the stable release** (e.g. `v1.4.0`): flip `"prerelease"` to `false` and `"versioning"` to `"default"` in `release-please-config.json`; if the proposed version isn't the wanted one, force it with a `Release-As: 1.4.0` footer in an empty `chore` commit. Afterwards flip back for the next beta cycle

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Git & Release Workflow > Release Automation (release-please, since #353; dist/ removal history: #190)
text: - **Repair path**: build failed on a published release → `gh workflow run release-build.yml -f tag=vX.Y.Z`; failed while still draft → "Re-run failed jobs" on the workflow run

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions
text: Deliberate architecture decisions that should not be changed:

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Code-Split Chunk Architecture (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: The bundle is deliberately split into 5 chunks:

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Code-Split Chunk Architecture (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text:
| Chunk | Contents | Size | Loads |
|-------|----------|------|-------|
| `main` (Entry) | Custom element registration | tiny | Immediately — must register before HA's 5s timeout |
| `lit` | Lit framework (shared) | small | Async, shared by core/views/editor |
| `core` | Registry, Utils, Cards, OverviewView | medium | Async, for the home screen |
| `views` | Lights/Covers/Security/Batteries/Climate/Room Views | small | Async, on navigation |
| `editor` | StrategyEditor + js-yaml | large | On-demand, only when user opens config |

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Code-Split Chunk Architecture (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: **Why:** Without code splitting, the entry point was a single large bundle. HA has a fixed 5-second timeout for custom element registration. On slow connections (Slow 4G), the JS file competes with all other HA chunks and custom cards for max. 6 browser connections. With the tiny entry point, the element registers instantly while the rest loads in the background.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Code-Split Chunk Architecture (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: **Content-Hash Chunk Filenames:** Chunks include a `[contenthash:8]` in their filename (e.g. `simon42-dashboard-strategy-core.c6a1e2e6.js`). HACS only sets its cache-busting `hacstag` on the entry file — without content hashes, browsers would serve stale cached chunks after a HACS update.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > No Auto-Detection for Temperature/Humidity on Area Cards
text: The overview area cards only show `sensor_classes` (temperature, humidity) when the user has explicitly assigned an entity in the **HA area settings** (`area.temperature_entity_id`, `area.humidity_entity_id`). No auto-detection because:

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > No Auto-Detection for Temperature/Humidity on Area Cards
text: - Wrong sensors would be displayed (e.g. printer temperature in the office)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > No Auto-Detection for Temperature/Humidity on Area Cards
text: - The user would have no way to remove them

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > No Auto-Detection for Temperature/Humidity on Area Cards
text: - HA's own Home Strategy does it the same way

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > No Auto-Detection for Temperature/Humidity on Area Cards
text: **Note:** In room detail views (RoomViewStrategy), sensors ARE auto-detected — they appear as badges and can be filtered via `no_dboard` label or `groups_options.hidden`.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Pre-filtered Features on Area Cards and Tile Cards (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: Area cards only receive `controls` that actually exist in the area (e.g. `['light', 'cover-shutter']`), not all possible controls. Tile cards only receive `features` that the entity supports (e.g. `light-brightness` only for lights with brightness support, `climate-hvac-modes` only for climate entities).

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Pre-filtered Features on Area Cards and Tile Cards (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: **Why:** Without pre-filtering, each card must scan all entities itself — with many areas and entities, this causes massive load times on weak devices (tablets, wall panels). Check here first when investigating performance issues!

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Custom Cards: LitElement with Reactive willUpdate() (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: All custom cards (SummaryCard, LightsGroupCard, CoversGroupCard) use LitElement with `willUpdate(changedProps)` instead of the previous innerHTML rebuild pattern. This means:

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Custom Cards: LitElement with Reactive willUpdate() (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: - HA calls `card.hass = ...` on **every** state change (any entity in the entire system) — this happens hundreds of times per minute

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Custom Cards: LitElement with Reactive willUpdate() (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: - Without the reactive pattern, each card would rebuild its entire DOM on every `set hass()` call → massive performance problems

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Custom Cards: LitElement with Reactive willUpdate() (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: - With `willUpdate()`, cards check whether relevant states actually changed and only re-render when needed

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Custom Cards: LitElement with Reactive willUpdate() (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: - SummaryCard additionally caches relevant entity IDs (`_relevantEntityIds`) and only invalidates the cache on registry changes (`oldHass.entities !== this.hass.entities`)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Custom Cards: LitElement with Reactive willUpdate() (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: - LightsGroupCard and CoversGroupCard use tile card pooling (DOM elements are reused instead of recreated)

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Custom Cards: LitElement with Reactive willUpdate() (PERFORMANCE-CRITICAL)
text: **Why:** The migration from innerHTML to LitElement + willUpdate was extensive, but without this pattern the dashboard is unusable on weak devices (tablets, wall panels). Do not revert!

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Design Decisions > Climate Summary Default: Off
text: `show_climate_summary` defaults to `false` because not every user has thermostats. All other summaries (lights, covers, security, batteries) default to on.

text:
**Original problem:** With disabled cache + Slow 4G throttling:
`Error: Timeout waiting for strategy element ll-strategy-dashboard-simon42-dashboard to be registered`
→ HA has a fixed 5-second timeout for custom element registration. Official strategies are part of the frontend bundle (no HTTP request), custom strategies must be loaded as external JS files.

head: Simon42 Dashboard Strategy > Roadmap: HA Best Practices Alignment
text: **Analysis result:** The remaining timeout on Slow 4G is a browser connection limit issue (max. 6 concurrent HTTP connections per origin). HA's own frontend chunks + all installed custom cards compete for slots. The strategy JS must wait until a slot is free. We have no control over this — neither HACS nor HA offer prioritization for custom resources. On normal connections (Fast 4G+) everything works smoothly.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Read in Advance
text:
- Vue Lynx: [llms.txt](https://vue.lynxjs.org/llms.txt), **REQUIRED**.
  Read this before working on any Vue Lynx task — it covers the Vue Lynx API, dual-thread architecture, and Lynx-specific caveats from a Vue perspective.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Debugging Checklist
text: When investigating runtime errors in Lynx bundles:

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Debugging Checklist
text:
1. **Clear caches first** — Before doing any code analysis, always:
   - `rm -rf node_modules/.cache` in the example/app directory
   - Restart the dev server (`pnpm dev`)
   - Restart LynxExplorer (stale error toasts persist across navigations)
   rspeedy-plugin is built separately from example apps. After rebuilding the plugin, the webpack persistent cache in example apps still serves stale bundles. This is the #1 cause of "phantom" errors that don't reproduce after a clean rebuild.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Debugging Checklist
text: 2. **Verify hash matching** — For worklet-related errors (`TypeError: cannot read property 'bind' of undefined`), check that BG `_wkltId` hashes match MT `registerWorkletInternal` hashes. Inspect the `.web.bundle` (JSON format) to compare.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Debugging Checklist
text: 3. **Check LynxExplorer state** — The error toast is persistent across page navigations. A stale error from a previous page load can be mistaken for a current error. Restart the simulator app to clear.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Architecture Notes > Dual-Thread Build (rspeedy-plugin)
text: - **Background Thread**: Vue runtime + user app. Layer: `vue:background`.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Architecture Notes > Dual-Thread Build (rspeedy-plugin)
text: - **Main Thread**: PAPI bootstrap + worklet registrations. Layer: `vue:main-thread`.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Architecture Notes > Dual-Thread Build (rspeedy-plugin)
text: - Both layers import the same user code; webpack `issuerLayer` routes files to different loaders.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Architecture Notes > Dual-Thread Build (rspeedy-plugin)
text: - BG: `worklet-loader` (SWC JS pass) — replaces `'main thread'` functions with context objects.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Architecture Notes > Dual-Thread Build (rspeedy-plugin)
text: - MT: `worklet-loader-mt` (SWC LEPUS pass) — extracts `registerWorkletInternal()` calls.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Architecture Notes > Common Gotchas
text: - `worklet-loader-mt` must emit `export default {};` for vue script sub-modules (`?vue&type=script`) to satisfy the `experimentalInlineMatchResource` proxy re-export.

head: Vue Lynx — Agent Guidelines > Architecture Notes > Common Gotchas
text: - Bootstrap packages (`vue-lynx/main-thread`, `vue-lynx/internal/ops`) must be excluded from MT loaders — in pnpm workspaces they resolve via symlinks (not under `node_modules/`), so `/node_modules/` exclude alone is insufficient.

text: - `VueMarkMainThreadPlugin` must add `RuntimeGlobals.startup` for MT entry chunks — without it, `chunkLoading: 'lynx'` prevents module factory execution.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: ThomsonLint is a knowledge and rule framework for AI-assisted hardware design review. It provides structured, machine-readable resources that enable AI models to analyze and identify potential issues in hardware designs (schematics and PCB layouts). The tested driver is Claude Code; a single-file-upload bundle exists for web AIs (e.g., Gemini, Claude.ai, ChatGPT) but that workflow has not been validated.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: The framework is named after J.J. Thomson, discoverer of the electron, reflecting its goal of uncovering fundamental issues in hardware designs.

head: CLAUDE.md > Core Components
text: - **`ontology/ontology.json`** - Machine-readable JSON defining rules, domains, severity levels, and failure modes for hardware design review

head: CLAUDE.md > Core Components
text: - **`examples/examples.json`** - Practical examples (good and bad) that map to ontology rules, used for training/testing AI understanding

head: CLAUDE.md > Core Components
text: - **`docs/AI_Hardware_Design_Review_KnowledgeBase.md`** - Human-readable explanations and context for the ontology rules

head: CLAUDE.md > Core Components
text: - **`docs/Multi_Agent_Reasoning_Spec.md`** - Specification for multi-agent architecture (Power/SMPS, High-Speed SI, Analog, EMC/ESD, Thermal/Mechanical agents)

head: CLAUDE.md > Reviewer Paths
text: Claude Code is the tested reviewer driver. A second path exists for single-file-upload web AIs but has not been validated. Both paths consume one source of truth: `docs/REVIEWER_INSTRUCTIONS.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Reviewer Paths
text:
- **Claude Code (CLI, in this repo) — tested.** The user prompts the agent to read `docs/REVIEWER_INSTRUCTIONS.md` and follow it. Step 1 of that file then directs the agent to load the framework knowledge base from:
  - `ontology/ontology.json`
  - `examples/examples.json`
  - `docs/AI_Hardware_Design_Review_KnowledgeBase.md`
  The project ships a `/design-review` skill at `.claude/commands/design-review.md` — type `/design-review` at the Claude Code prompt instead of pasting the full prompt manually.
  Do **not** read `review_instructions.txt` from Claude Code. The bundle (~260KB / 5700 lines) is intended for single-file upload to a web AI and exceeds Claude Code's per-file `Read` limit. The source files are the truth; the bundle is a concatenation of them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Reviewer Paths
text: - **Web AI with single-file upload (Gemini, Claude.ai, ChatGPT, etc.) — untested.** The `review_instructions.txt` bundle is produced by `gen_context.sh`, which concatenates `docs/REVIEWER_INSTRUCTIONS.md` with the three knowledge base files. The maintainers have not validated this path; treat as experimental.

head: CLAUDE.md > Reviewer Paths
text: The reviewer-facing flow (inputs, outputs, prompts) is documented in README.md §5 "Running a Review".

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: The bridge is the HTTP transport to a running Fusion Electronics session over Autodesk's "Fusion MCP Server" endpoint (`ping` / `eagle` / `read` / `stage-ulps` verbs). Step 0 of `docs/REVIEWER_INSTRUCTIONS.md` now runs on `tools/fusion_export.py` (next section), which imports this bridge; driving the ULPs over the bridge (`stage-ulps` + `RUN` dispatches) remains only as a fallback pattern. The ULP-over-bridge path was verified end-to-end 2026-08-28 against a live 1-sheet design before being superseded.

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: Non-obvious operational facts (learned the hard way — do not rediscover):

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: - **Dialog latch (known Fusion issue).** Two triggers are confirmed: any dispatch whose EAGLE command contains `RUN`, and any **no-op `EDIT`** (opening the sheet/editor that is already open — isolated by A/B test 2026-08-28). The add-in then refuses further scripts with "Cannot perform 'script' while a command dialog is open" — **no dialog is actually visible**; only a keypress (Escape) in the Fusion window clears it. Detect the clear by polling a no-op `execute_script`. Real editor switches, `RATSNEST`, `DISPLAY`, `WINDOW FIT`, and `EXPORT IMAGE` do not latch. `run_eagle()` auto-prefixes every command with `SET CONFIRM YES;`, which prevents the same latch after confirmation prompts and auto-answers ULP overwrite prompts — but prevents neither trigger above.

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: - ULP-fallback only: the schematic and board ULP passes **cannot merge into a single dispatch** — the images ULP terminates via `exit()`, which also ends the rest of the chained command line.

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: - **Reads follow the active editor** and are never latch-blocked. With the board tab active, `electronics.Schematic`/`Sheet`/`Part` read empty — that means "wrong editor", not "no design open" (`ping` detects and reports this case).

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: - Fusion's screenshot query returns "No active graphics view" for the 2D electronics editors — you cannot remotely see what is on screen.

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: - **Export/stackup JSONs are Latin-1, not UTF-8** (e.g. the German layer name "gesam-Maß"). Python's `json.load` raises `UnicodeDecodeError`; decode with `latin-1` first. This is a pre-existing trait of the ULP output (the committed comet stack file has the same byte), not a bridge bug.

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: - ULP PNG renders are fixed-size per canvas: every board PNG of a design is **byte-identical in size** (checksums differ — they are not duplicate renders), and board PNGs can exceed 150MB.

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: - `run_eagle()` embeds the command into the generated Python via `repr()` **deliberately** — single quotes and Windows backslash paths (`RUN 'C:\...'`) survive. Do not "simplify" it to an f-string.

head: CLAUDE.md > Live Fusion Capture (`tools/fusion_bridge.py`)
text: - **The dialog latch is not only post-`RUN`: a no-op `EDIT` (opening the sheet/editor that is already open) also arms it** — isolated by A/B test 2026-08-28 (real switch → clean; same `EDIT .S1;` repeated → latched). Real switches, `RATSNEST`, `DISPLAY`, `WINDOW FIT`, and `EXPORT IMAGE` do not latch.

head: CLAUDE.md > Direct Capture (`tools/fusion_export.py`) — the Step 0 path
text: ULP-free capture: emits the same `-thomson-export-{sch,brd,stack}.json` contracts from `electronics_read` queries and renders the review PNGs via dispatched `EXPORT IMAGE` chains (verbs `sch` / `brd` / `images` / `all`). Verified against a same-day ULP capture of `series-shunt`: exact parity except documented deltas (`clearance_mm` null — MCP exposes no NetClass clearance; `layers_used` over-reporting; the stackup is *more* correct — the ULP's "ROUTE" name fallback put layer 19 Unrouted in the copper stack). Zero Escapes for 1-sheet designs; its `wait_channel()` prompts and waits if the latch arms. **The comet (routed + poured, round-outline) parity diff passed 2026-08-28** — every delta accounted for, several in the direct path's favor (the ULP was numerically blind to routing and pours on Fusion inner copper 303, and its edge-distance check measured against the drawing extent instead of the board outline). **Step 0 of `docs/REVIEWER_INSTRUCTIONS.md` now runs on this tool** (`python tools/fusion_export.py all`); the ULPs stay in `tools/` solely for the manual fallback path. Details and the intentional deltas: `docs/Direct_Read_Feasibility.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Source Attribution (mandatory)

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Ingesting YouTube Content (transcript + creator attribution)
text: When asked to pull a transcript from a YouTube video (typically as raw material for a KB addition), use the helper script:

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Ingesting YouTube Content (transcript + creator attribution)
text: It downloads the video's English captions via yt-dlp, cleans the rolling-caption duplicates into timestamped paragraphs, and writes `<video-id>-transcript.txt` with a header containing the title, creator name, creator homepage URL, video URL, upload date, and duration. Output goes to `/tmp` by default — transcripts are working material for KB distillation and must not be committed to the repo.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Ingesting YouTube Content (transcript + creator attribution)
text:
- **yt-dlp must be current** — YouTube routinely breaks old versions. If the system `yt-dlp` fails with extraction errors, install the latest into a venv and pass it explicitly:
  ```bash
  python3 -m venv /tmp/ytdlp-venv && /tmp/ytdlp-venv/bin/pip install -U yt-dlp
  python tools/yt-transcript.py <url> --yt-dlp /tmp/ytdlp-venv/bin/yt-dlp
  ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Ingesting YouTube Content (transcript + creator attribution)
text: - **Mandatory follow-up — creator homepage.** After pulling the transcript, go to the creator's YouTube homepage (the "Creator homepage" URL in the transcript header, e.g. `https://www.youtube.com/@PredictableDesigns`) and gather the creator's information: creator/host name, channel name, channel description, and any external website or business links they list. This information is what populates the `**Source:**` attribution line (see "Source Attribution" above) when the transcript becomes a KB addition. Do not write the KB section without it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Ontology Rule Structure

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Findings File Structure (output of a review)
text: Top-level fields: `project_name`, `review_date`, `source_documents`, `issues`, `verified_checks`, `cross_checks`. The three findings arrays share one entry shape — see `tests/findings_schema.json` and `tests/sample_findings.json`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Findings File Structure (output of a review)
text: - **`issues[]`** — problems requiring designer triage. Severity, description, recommended_actions all required.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Findings File Structure (output of a review)
text: - **`verified_checks[]`** — analyses the agent performed where the result was OK. Read-only in the report. Crucial: do NOT omit a verification because nothing was wrong; the verification itself is a deliverable.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Findings File Structure (output of a review)
text: - **`cross_checks[]`** — design-wide analyses spanning multiple ontology rules (e.g., MT3608 layout cross-check covering PWR_BUCK_001/002/003/004 plus thermal). `rule_id` may be an array.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extending the Framework > Findings File Structure (output of a review)
text: - **Per-entry `evidence[]`** — typed rows. Either parameter comparisons (`label/datasheet/design/margin/verdict/source`) or free-form notes (`note/source`). Every row must cite a `source`. The validator cross-references these against design inputs in the findings directory.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: PhiSpace is an R package for continuous cell state annotation of single-cell and spatial omics data. It uses partial least squares (PLS) regression to phenotype cells on a continuum rather than assigning discrete labels. The R package source lives in `pkg/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/PhiSpaceR.R` — Main user-facing `PhiSpace()` wrapper (handles single/multiple references, stores normalised scores in `reducedDim`)

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/PhiSpaceR_1ref.R` — Core single-reference implementation `PhiSpaceR_1ref()`. Returns both raw (`PhiSpaceScore`, `YrefHat`) and normalised (`PhiSpaceNorm`, `YrefHatNorm`) scores. Supports `cellTypeThreshold` for filtering rare cell types.

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/tunePhiSpace.R` — Parameter tuning via cross-validation. Also supports `cellTypeThreshold`.

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/codeY.R` — Converts categorical phenotypes to dummy matrices

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/mvr.R` — Internal PLS/PCA regression fitting

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/superPC.R` — Supervised PCA/PLS model builder

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/phenotype.R` — Prediction function

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/normPhiScores.R` — Score normalization (column-wise median centering or row-wise min-max)

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/rankFeatures.R` — Feature importance ranking

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/clusterPhiSpace.R` — K-means clustering on PhiSpace scores

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/spatialSmoother.R` — KNN-based spatial smoothing

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/findNiches.R` — Spatial niche identification

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/vizSpatial.R` — Spatial visualization (`VizSpatial()`)

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/saveCellTypeMaps.R` — Batch spatial heatmap export

head: AGENTS.md > Key Source Files
text: - `pkg/R/utils.R` — Shared utilities (color palette, censoring, scaling, etc.)

head: AGENTS.md > Core Function Architecture
text: `PhiSpaceR_1ref()` returns a list with both raw and normalised scores:

head: AGENTS.md > Core Function Architecture
text: - `PhiSpaceScore` / `PhiSpaceNorm` — query scores (matrix or list of matrices)

head: AGENTS.md > Core Function Architecture
text: - `YrefHat` / `YrefHatNorm` — reference predictions

head: AGENTS.md > Core Function Architecture
text: `PhiSpace()` uses the pre-normalised scores from `PhiSpaceR_1ref()` and stores them in `reducedDim(query, "PhiSpace")`.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Wrapper-Modernisation Plan (agreed 2026-10-07)
text:
`findNiches()` defaults differ from the vignettes: Lloyd algorithm, 20 starts and
500 iterations, against the R default Hartigan-Wong algorithm, 50 starts and

call. With the vignette's arguments it reproduces the CosMx labels exactly; with
its defaults the adjusted Rand index is 0.89. Since 2026-10-08 it reports
progress and niche sizes with `message()` (silence with `verbose = FALSE` or
`suppressMessages()`); the CosMx and Stereo-seq niche chunks set
`message = FALSE`, so fresh and cached pages show the same text. The same
change was made in `zeroFeatQC()`, `spatialSampler()` and `spatialSmoother()`
(whose progress bar still writes to standard output). `clusterPhiSpace.R`
keeps `cat()` because it uses it only in `print()` and `summary()` methods.
Fresh local builds after the change: CosMx 35 checks and 14 of 14 figures
identical, Stereo-seq 48 checks and 23 of 23 figures identical. The kmeans
and irlba warnings stay visible, as in the old explicit vignettes.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Wrapper-Modernisation Plan (agreed 2026-10-07)
text:
Until 2026-10-08, `pls.fit()` called `irlba::partial_eigen()`, which draws a
random start vector, so PhiSpace scores varied between runs by about 1e-8
unless the seed was the same. Since the sparse-aware fit (see Package
Performance Work), PLS uses `eigen()` and does not depend on the seed; PCA
regression still uses irlba for few components.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
1. Record its scientific purpose, input objects, helper scripts, cached results,
   expected figures/tables, random seeds, and meaningful output invariants.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
2. Inventory every data path and download. Never depend on a developer home
   directory or private Dropbox mount.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
3. For legacy `.qs` files, use old `qs` only for one-time local conversion.
   Save with `qs2::qs_save()`, read back with checksum validation, and compare
   the restored R object with the original. Renaming `.qs` to `.qs2` is invalid.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
4. Publish data in a stable shared folder, preserve relative paths, and record
   SHA-256 hashes in `scripts/<slug>-inputs.tsv`.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
5. Add `PHISPACE_<SLUG>_DATA`, `PHISPACE_<SLUG>_INPUTS`, and, for a folder ZIP,
   `PHISPACE_<SLUG>_ARCHIVE`. Source helpers with `local = TRUE`.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
6. Enable evaluation and fail on chunk errors. Use
   `knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE)` and render with `lazy = FALSE`.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
7. Run a **fresh-analysis build** with cached results deliberately absent, so
   computation errors cannot be hidden by old outputs.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
8. Run a separate **cached-result build** with all downloadable outputs present.
   Confirm it renders without loading the retired `qs` namespace.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
9. Record runtime, peak RAM, package versions, dimensions/names, and meaningful
   numerical differences from established results.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
10. Add `scripts/prepare-<slug>.R`, `scripts/build-<slug>.R`, its manifest, and
    the vignette to Actions only after both local builds pass. Resolve the exact
    workflow dependency set locally.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
11. Commit only that vignette source, scripts, manifest, workflow update, and
    publishing notes. Never commit `Test/` caches or staged websites.

head: AGENTS.md > Vignette Overhaul: Active Project > Standard Procedure for Each Vignette
text:
12. After the user pushes, check both Actions jobs and inspect the live article.
    Local success does not prove runner resources, permissions, or deployment.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions
text: - **Input flexibility**: Many functions accept both single objects and lists of objects (e.g., `PhiSpace()` accepts single or multiple references/queries). When a return value may be a matrix or list of matrices, handle both cases explicitly.

head: Working on this repository
text:
A browser-based 3D atlas of clinical neuroanatomy: meshes in MNI152 space, synchronised MRI slices, and
authored clinical content in English and Turkish. Vite + TypeScript + three.js in `src/`, a Python pipeline in
`pipeline/`, and the prose as JSON in `content/`.

head: Working on this repository
text:
This file is for anyone — human or agent — setting the project up or changing it. [README.md](README.md) gets
a reader running, [docs/guide.md](docs/guide.md) is the tour of what the app does,
[docs/developing.md](docs/developing.md) the layout, the data flow and the checks, [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
the rules for changing it; this is the operating manual. The traps below are the ones that actually cost time.

head: Working on this repository > Setting up
text: `npm run data` fetches without serving; `npm run dev` serves without fetching.

head: Working on this repository > Setting up
text:
**The atlas data is not in this repository and must never be committed.** `public/data/` is 63 MB of generated
meshes, MRI volumes and label tables; it is gitignored, and `npm run check-tree` fails if it is ever tracked.
Skip `npm run data` and the app starts and tells you what to run — it does not hang or throw.

head: Working on this repository > Setting up
text:
To generate the data instead of downloading it, `npm run data:build` (see [docs/pipeline.md](docs/pipeline.md)). It needs `uv`,
downloads several GB, and takes a long time. You almost never need it: reach for it only when changing how the
meshes or volumes are built.

head: Working on this repository > Rules that are not negotiable
text:
1. **Never commit generated or private data.** Not `public/data/`, `dist/`, `dist-private/`, `pipeline/raw/`,
   `pipeline/work/`, `source/`, `reference/`, `qa/shots/`, and no mesh, volume or archive. `npm run check-tree`
   enforces this and runs as a pre-commit hook (`npm run hooks:install`) and in CI.

head: Working on this repository > Rules that are not negotiable
text:
2. **Never weaken `scripts/check-public.ts` or `scripts/check-tree.ts` to make something pass.** They are the
   whole licence guarantee. If one fires, it is describing a real problem — fix the problem.

head: Working on this repository > Rules that are not negotiable
text:
3. **`dist-private/` must never be published, deployed or copied anywhere shared.** Only `npm run build`
   output is redistributable, and only because `check-public` certifies it.

head: Working on this repository > Rules that are not negotiable
text:
4. **The `private` branch and the `v1.0.0-private` tag stay local.** Never push them. Work happens on `main`
   and is rebased onto `private`; never merge `private` into `main`.

head: Working on this repository > Rules that are not negotiable
text:
5. **The exclusion of the four restricted datasets is unconditional, and "this project is non-commercial" is
   NOT the reason it is safe to publish.** Brainstem Navigator forbids distributing anything derived from it
   outside your organisation; PAM50 states no licence at all; Diedrichsen is CC BY-ND, so distributing the
   meshes we make from it is forbidden outright. None of those three is about money. Harvard-Oxford is a
   separate case — FSL relicensed it to CC BY-SA 4.0 in August 2025 and it is held back pending a decision,
   not because it is non-commercial. **Never add a build mode that includes restricted data on the grounds
   that some particular use is non-commercial**, and never relax the gate on that reasoning. See
   [docs/editions.md](docs/editions.md#the-exclusion-is-unconditional).

text:

head: Working on this repository > The two editions
text:
A build is the **private** edition if and only if restricted data was built into it — it is decided by the
data, not by a flag. Four datasets are excluded — Brainstem Navigator and PAM50 because they may not be
redistributed, Diedrichsen because CC BY-ND forbids distributing the meshes we make from it, and
Harvard-Oxford as a hold pending review (see rule 5); they sit in `group: restricted` in `sources.yaml`, and
`atlas-download` refuses to fetch that group unless it is on the `private` branch or `ATLAS_ALLOW_RESTRICTED=1`.
The public edition substitutes openly licensed data for all four. Full detail, including how to obtain the
restricted ones, is in [docs/editions.md](docs/editions.md).

head: Working on this repository > The two editions
text:
In `public/data/` the **plain names are always the public edition** (`manifest.json`, `content.json`,
`search-index.json`, `content.tr.json`); the private edition lives beside them as `*.private.json` and exists
only where restricted data was built. So a plain `npm run dev` or `npm run build` cannot leak.

head: Working on this repository > The two editions
text:
| | |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` / `npm run build` | public edition (`dist/`), gated |
| `npm run dev:private` / `npm run build:private` | full edition (`dist-private/`), ungated, do not publish |
