head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3)
text: MCP server for structured reasoning via Atom of Thoughts. Decomposes problems into atomic units (premise → reasoning → hypothesis → verification → conclusion) with confidence tracking, session scoping, and on-demand D3 visualization.

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > MCP Tools (3)
text:
| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `AoT-fast` | Default reasoning. Depth 3, auto-suggests conclusions. Set `viz:true` during planning |
| `AoT-full` | Deep reasoning with decomposition-contraction. Depth 5. Same shape as AoT-fast, plus decomposition controls |
| `atomcommands` | Lifecycle/meta: `decompose`, `complete_decomposition`, `termination_status`, `best_conclusion`, `set_max_depth`, `export`, `check_approval`, `new_session`, `switch_session`, `list_sessions`, `reset_session` |

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Atom Types
text: `premise` (P) → `reasoning` (R) → `hypothesis` (H) → `verification` (V) → `conclusion` (C)

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Atom Types
text: Each atom: `atomId`, `content`, `atomType` (required), `dependencies` (default []), `confidence` (default 0.7), optional `viz` (default false), optional `sessionId` (default active session).

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Sessions
text: - All atom state scoped to a `sessionId` (default `"default"`).

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Sessions
text: - Auto-archive on `shouldTerminate`; auto-spawn fresh `default-N` on next zero-dep atom.

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Sessions
text: - Two reasoning problems in the same MCP process do not collide.

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Sessions
text: - Every response includes `sessionId`.

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Visualization
text: - Set `viz: true` on any AoT call to render the D3 graph and open it in the browser.

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Visualization
text: - The HTML embeds a callback URL (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/approval`) that the approve/reject UI POSTs to.

head: mcp-atom-of-thoughts (v3) > Visualization
text: - `atomcommands check_approval` reads the in-memory store keyed by sessionId. Falls back to file polling on the configured downloads dir if the listener can't bind or the POST fails.

The OpenUI Lang component catalogue is split into the sibling **pebble-protocol-ui/SKILL.md** (the agent loads it lazily when building a UI block).

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > What we're building
text: A static React PWA that connects directly to a Hermes agent's HTTP API. No backend, no MCP server. The Pebble launcher (`main.go`) serves the app and reverse-proxies `/api/*` to Hermes from the same origin, so **on the desktop machine Pebble auto-connects to its own localhost origin with no wizard and no paste**. Tailscale is only needed to *reach* Pebble from another device: you expose the launcher with `tailscale serve`, then use the app's **"Open on phone"** button — with a tunnel up it shows a QR to scan; without one it opens the `SetupScreen` wizard that walks you through Tailscale. Access (over the tunnel) is gated by the tailnet itself — there is no API token. It talks to the agent over `GET /api/sessions` + `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream` (SSE).

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > What we're building
text: - **Session list** — chat inbox, WhatsApp-style (not a task board). Active / Completed sections, each sorted by `last_updated`

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > What we're building

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Internal protocol (adapter ↔ store)
text: The agent communicates **only** through the `pebble_send` tool, provided by the bundled Hermes plugin (`hermes-plugin/`, installed to `~/.hermes/plugins/pebble/` by the launcher). The agent never emits plain `assistant.delta` text — all user-visible output is a `pebble_send` tool call.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Internal protocol (adapter ↔ store)
text: - A saved/verified `{ hermes }` config (from the setup wizard) → `HermesAdapter`.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Internal protocol (adapter ↔ store)
text: - `connect()` → `GET /api/sessions` → emits `session_list`.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Internal protocol (adapter ↔ store)
text:
- `user_message` → `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream` (SSE). Stream events translated:
  - `tool.started` for `pebble_send` → read `arguments.type` and dispatch: `message` → `agent_message` (kind `message`), `ui` → `agent_ui`, `status` → `session_status`, `push` → `agent_message` and/or `agent_ui`. A `label` on any type updates the session name. `session_status: active` is emitted once at stream start, `done` on `run.completed`.
  - `tool.started` for other tools → `agent_message` kind `thought` ("Running X…"); finalized to "Ran X" on `tool.completed` (or on stream end, so the "Thinking…" indicator never sticks).

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Internal protocol (adapter ↔ store)
text: - `ui_action` → next user turn carrying `{"ui_action":..., "payload":..., "session_id":...}` JSON envelope. The plugin's `pre_llm_call` hook parses that and injects it as structured context.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text:
- Connection is auto-derived from the origin (no `?hermes=` URL params). On boot, `main.tsx` primes the store from one of three sources (in priority order): (1) a saved config (`loadConnectionConfig()`, returning device); (2) a `#connect=` deep-link from a scanned "open on phone" QR (`consumeConnectLink()`); (3) the **origin Pebble loaded from** (`originConnectCandidate()` — now accepts localhost too, since the launcher serves app + API from that origin). For (2) and (3) the candidate is verified via `testConnection()` before it's saved, with `wsUrl` set optimistically so the gate shows `ConnectingScreen` (not a flash of the wizard) during verification, and cleared to `null` on failure. When primed, `wsUrl` holds the agent base URL as a non-null marker; `connectionConfig` holds the full `{ hermes }`. Three-state gate in `App.tsx`:
  1. `wsUrl === null` → `SetupScreen` (Tailscale wizard). This is now an **exceptional fallback** — it only appears when origin verification fails (e.g. bare `vite` dev with no launcher proxying, or a QR scanned onto a phone not yet on the tailnet). On the desktop the launcher origin verifies, so the wizard never shows at boot.
  2. `wsUrl` set but `wsStatus !== "connected"` → `ConnectingScreen` (animated dots; error variant with retry when connection permanently fails)
  3. Connected → `Layout`. The connected-but-no-sessions empty state lives inside `SessionList` ("No chats yet." + New Chat button).

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - **"Open on phone"** (desktop sidebar) is the primary path to the wizard. It calls `fetchConnectInfo()` → the launcher's `GET /api/connect-info`, which reports the Tailscale tunnel URL (or null). Tunnel up → QR encoding `buildConnectLink(config, tunnelUrl)` (the link's base is the *tunnel* URL, never localhost, so the phone can reach it). No tunnel → `SetupScreen` shown as a dismissable destination (`onClose` prop) over the chat. Its final step takes an `onRecheck` callback: after the user runs `tailscale serve`, "I've run it — show QR" re-queries the launcher — tunnel found swaps straight to the QR, not found shows an inline "couldn't find it yet" retry. (Without `onRecheck`/`onClose`, the wizard is the legacy full-screen boot fallback that instead tells you to open the printed `.ts.net` URL.) Tunnel detection lives in `main.go`'s `detectTunnelURL()` (parses `tailscale serve status`).

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Connection helpers live in `src/lib/connection.ts`: `saveAndConnect()` (persist + prime store), `buildConnectLink(config, tunnelUrl?)`/`consumeConnectLink()` (the QR deep-link, config in the URL *fragment* so it never hits a server), `fetchConnectInfo()` (queries the launcher for the tunnel URL). There's no connection-settings UI: the address is just the origin Pebble loaded from (localhost on desktop), so there's nothing to configure or disconnect — the only connection affordance is the sidebar's "Open on phone" button.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - **Passphrase lock (optional, opt-in).** Set `PEBBLE_PASSPHRASE` (or `--app-passphrase`) on the launcher and `main.go` gates `/api/*` behind it: any request without a matching `pebble_auth` cookie gets a `401`. The cookie is set by `POST /api/login` (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, 1-year), so the secret lives only in the browser — the React app never holds it, and the browser auto-attaches it to the SSE stream. Empty passphrase → no gate (default). A 401 surfaces a store flag `authRequired` (set from both the boot `testConnection` and the adapter's `connect()` probe via an `auth_required` error event), which renders `PassphraseScreen` as the **outermost** gate in `App.tsx` — ahead of `SetupScreen`. `submitPassphrase()` in `connection.ts` does the login; on success it clears the flag and resumes connect. `/api/login` and `/api/connect-info` are never gated. Docs: DEVELOPERS.md. Caveat: stops a browser hitting `localhost:<port>` without the phrase, not someone who already controls your OS account.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - **Chat URLs are hash-routed** (`useHashRoute` in `src/lib/`). The open session mirrors to `#/session/<id>` and back (refresh, back/forward, shareable deep-link); the bare list is no hash. `activeSessionId` in the store is the source of truth — the hook just keeps the URL in sync both ways. Hash (not path) routing is deliberate: the launcher never sees the fragment, so nothing is configured server-side and `#connect=` (the QR deep-link) and the `__pending__` new-chat sentinel are both excluded from routing. The hash is preserved across the passphrase unlock, so a deep-linked chat lands you on that chat after login.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Streaming messages: `agent_message` with `streaming: true` are assembled chunk-by-chunk. `streaming: false` = final chunk.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - `agent_message` has a `kind` field: `"thought"` (agent reasoning/tool chatter) or `"message"` (final output). Thoughts are collapsed into a subtle "thinking..." indicator while streaming, then become an expandable disclosure row. Messages render as full bubbles. Both share the same `message_id` and group together in the thread.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - `agent_ui` renders inline in the thread immediately after the preceding `agent_message` (or standalone).

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Sessions are persisted to localStorage. Message history uses IndexedDB (keyed by session_id).

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Session list is split into two sections (`SectionedList` in `SessionList`): **Active** and **Completed**. A session is Active if its status is `active`/`waiting`, *or* it was updated within the freshness window (`FRESH_WINDOW_MS`, 5 min) — so a chat you were just in doesn't drop into Completed the instant the agent stops. Older `done`/`error` sessions settle into Completed. Within each section, rows are sorted by `last_updated` descending. (`now` ticks every 30s so a fresh session re-buckets itself once the window elapses.)

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Session status is shown as a small icon (not a pill) next to the timestamp, WhatsApp-style. No labels.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Server (`GET /api/sessions`) returns timestamps as Unix epoch **seconds** (float), with the last-activity field named `last_active` (not `updated_at`/`last_updated`). `toSessionMeta` converts via `epochToISO()`; missing it makes every session read as "now".

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Session avatars use DiceBear Thumbs, seeded by `session_id`: `https://api.dicebear.com/9.x/thumbs/svg?seed={session_id}`. Rendered as a 40×40px circle. No initials fallback needed — DiceBear always resolves.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Deleting a session removes it immediately and permanently — no archive, no undo.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Mobile: full-screen list → tap → full-screen thread. Back button returns to list.

head: Pebble — Claude Code Context > Key behaviours
text: - Desktop (≥768px): sidebar list + thread side by side.

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance to the agent when working with code in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: TeamCopilot is an open-source multi-user AI agent platform for teams that want shared agent capabilities without giving up control, visibility, or operational guardrails.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: At a high level, TeamCopilot combines:

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: - a web UI for chatting with an agent remotely

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: - a shared filesystem-backed workspace of custom skills and workflows

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: - approval and permission controls for risky or reusable automation

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: - auditability for chat sessions and file changes

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: - team-oriented secret management for agent-assisted execution

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Structure
text: This is a monorepo (without workspaces) containing:

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Structure
text: - **Backend** (root): Express.js + TypeScript + Prisma + SQLite — lives in `src/`

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Structure
text: - **Frontend** (`frontend/`): React 19 + TypeScript + Vite — separate `package.json`

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Structure
text: The backend serves the built frontend from `frontend/dist/` as static files with SPA fallback routing.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Backend API Pattern
text: All authenticated/versioned API routes use the `apiHandler` wrapper from `src/utils.ts`:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Backend API Pattern
text: `apiHandler` handles: API version validation from the URL path, JWT token verification from `Authorization: Bearer` header, and user lookup from Prisma. The `CustomRequest` type extends Express Request with `version`, `userId`, `email`, and `name`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Authentication Flow
text: Email/password auth → JWT tokens (365-day expiry). The flow:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Authentication Flow
text: 1. `POST /api/auth/signup` — creates user with bcrypt-hashed password, returns JWT

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Authentication Flow
text: 2. `POST /api/auth/signin` — validates credentials, returns JWT

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Authentication Flow
text: 3. Frontend stores token in localStorage and sends `Authorization: Bearer {token}` on subsequent requests

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Authentication Flow
text: 4. Password reset via CLI: `npm run reset-password -- user@example.com` sets a temporary password

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Route Structure
text: All API routes are mounted under `/api` via `apiRouter`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Route Structure
text: Non-API `GET *` requests serve `frontend/dist/index.html` for client-side routing.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Route Structure
text: `src/index.ts` also exports `createApp()` so route-level tests can mount the Express app in-process without starting a separate server.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Database
text: SQLite via Prisma ORM. Schema is at `prisma/schema.prisma`. The database now stores much more than just auth metadata, including users, permissions, approvals, chat/session data, and secret-management tables such as `user_secrets` and `global_secrets`. SQLite uses WAL mode for concurrency (configured in `src/prisma/client.ts`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Shared Workspace Model
text: TeamCopilot is filesystem-first:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Shared Workspace Model
text: - workflows live in `workflows/<slug>/`

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Shared Workspace Model
text: - custom skills live in `.agents/skills/<slug>/`

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Shared Workspace Model
text: - the filesystem contents are the source of truth for those resources

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Shared Workspace Model
text: This means most resource creation, editing, approval diffs, and runtime behavior are driven by real files on disk rather than opaque database blobs.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: TeamCopilot has two secret scopes:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: - user secrets: private to a specific user

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: - global secrets: shared across the team and managed by engineers

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: Important implementation details:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: - workflows declare required secret keys in `workflow.json` under `required_secrets`

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: - workflow runs receive resolved secrets as environment variables at runtime

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: - skills declare required secret keys in `SKILL.md` frontmatter

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: - skills keep placeholder references like `{{SECRET:OPENAI_API_KEY}}` in file content rather than storing raw secret values

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: - agent-facing secret usage in shell goes through a secret-proxy model; plaintext secret values are not included in the LLM-visible context

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Secrets Model
text: - `.env` files are still redacted in editor/file APIs, but AI-authored workflows should rely on declared runtime secrets rather than workflow-local `.env` files

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Approvals And Runtime Boundaries
text: - Workflows and custom skills can require engineer approval before they are usable.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Approvals And Runtime Boundaries
text: - Workflow execution must go through the platform runtime rather than direct shell execution of `run.py`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Approvals And Runtime Boundaries
text: - Approval diffs and chat session file diffs are part of the product’s audit trail and are intentionally inspectable.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Logging
text: `src/logging.ts` provides `logInfo` and `logError`. Both use `console.log` and `console.error` respectively.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Cron Jobs
text: `src/cronjob/index.ts` exports `startCronJobs()` which is called at server startup.

head: AGENTS.md > Environment Variables
text:
JWT secret is generated on first boot and stored in `key_value`. Rotate via `npm run rotate-jwt-secret`.
Optional: `WORKSPACE_DIR` (absolute path or relative to project root, default `./my_workspaces`)

text: - `TEAMCOPILOT_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0`) — Hostname for the main server

head: AGENTS.md > Environment Variables > Server
text: - `TEAMCOPILOT_PORT` (default `5124`) — Port for the main server

head: AGENTS.md > Environment Variables > Opencode Server
text: - `OPENCODE_PORT` (default `4096`) — Internal port used by the Opencode server started inside the backend process (always listens on localhost)

head: AGENTS.md > Environment Variables > Opencode Server
text: - `OPENCODE_MODEL` (default `openai/gpt-5.3-codex`) — AI model to use

head: AGENTS.md > Design Direction
text: Per `plan-single-tenant.md`, TeamCopilot is evolving toward a more fully integrated multi-user agent platform with richer real-time communication and stronger operational controls. The current implementation already centers around:

head: AGENTS.md > Design Direction
text: - a filesystem-first workspace model

head: AGENTS.md > Design Direction
text: - embedded OpenCode-based agent execution

head: AGENTS.md > Design Direction
text: - approval and audit flows

head: AGENTS.md > Design Direction
text: - profile/global secret management with a secret-proxy approach

head: AGENTS.md > Design Direction
text: Workflows remain filesystem-first folder packages with `workflow.json` manifests, `run.py` entrypoints, and per-workflow `.venv`. AI-authored workflow secret handling should use `required_secrets` plus runtime injection rather than workflow-local `.env` files.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > General
text: - Avoid too many conditional types. Be sure of the types before implementing. For example, if something cannot be undefined / null, then don't make it optional and don't use `| undefined` or `| null` in the type.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > General
text: - IMPORTANT: DO NOT BE DEFENSIVE WHEN IMPLEMENTING CODE. BE SURE OF TYPES! Add asserts, and if things error out, we can debug the errors if they happen!

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > General
text: - When making prisma schema changes, the migration needs to be done via the prisma migration command. NOT via by manually creating the migration file.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > Frontend > Network calls
text: When making network calls, use the `axios` library. Specifically, use the `axiosInstance` from the `./frontend/src/utils.ts` file. Make sure to always handle errors from the network call:

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > Frontend > Network calls
text: - If it's a GET request, and it errors out, then show the error message to the user via the UI on the screen.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > Frontend > Network calls
AGENTS.md > Code style > Frontend > Network calls
text: Make sure that if the call requires auth, you pass in the access token as an Authorization bearer token in the headers. To get the access token, use the `useAuth` hook from the `./frontend/src/lib/auth.tsx` file.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > Backend > Error responses
text:
Instead of doing something like:
```
res.status(400).json({ error: 'status must be "running", "success", or "failed"' });
```

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > Backend > Error responses
AGENTS.md > Code style > Backend > Error responses
text: - The error handler in `index.ts` will handle it in the correct way.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > Backend > Error responses
text: - This is applicable for all status codes other than 200 ones.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style > Error handling
text: - Prefer throwing errors rather than silently handling them via return values like false or null.

head: AGENTS.md > Communication
text: - When asking the user questions (especially for clarification), ask **just one question at a time**.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Service worker gate**: `apps/wallet` requires `bun run build:sw` BEFORE `dev`/`build` — silent load failure otherwise.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **`/sharing` + `/install` are standalone web entrypoints**: `apps/wallet` ships THREE builds, not one — the SPA, the service worker, and `vite.standalone.config.ts`, which emits `sharing.html` / `install.html` (preact, no router, no blockchain: ~90 KB gz against the SPA shell's ~390 KB) because both pages are opened as full-page loads by the web/iOS/Android SDKs. nginx routes those two paths there; Tauri and client-side navigations keep using the SPA routes. Same `SharingView` / `InstallView` on both surfaces — a build gate (`assertEagerBundleBudget`) fails the build if the light bundle regresses.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Wallet `@/*` dual resolution**: resolves to both `./app/*` AND `../../packages/design-system/src/*` (tsconfig).

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Vanilla Extract everywhere**: all styles use `.css.ts` (`style()`/`keyframes()`) + `Box` sprinkles. No CSS Modules remain — do not add `.module.css`.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Don't repaint design-system components through `className`**: every component appends the caller's class after its own recipe class, so the caller always wins and the component stops following the design system. `className` is for placement (or use `Box` sprinkles props); to change how a component *looks*, add a variant to its `recipe()` and expose it through its `RecipeVariants<typeof x>` prop type — `packages/design-system/src/components/Button` (`button.css.ts` + `index.tsx`) is the reference.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **`globalStyle` is scoped, not banned**: it is legal for resets and root-element rules (`html`, `body`, `::view-transition-*`), for DOM we do not emit (vendored chart markup), and for caller-supplied children a layout primitive cannot class (`Tiles`, `Spread`, `Inline`, `DataTable` rows). Do not use it to reach into our own components' children: put the same class on both elements, or add a dedicated class, instead of a `${parent} *` descendant selector.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **`wallet-shared` scope rule**: imports FORBIDDEN in `business`/`backend`/`shopify`. Wallet+listener only.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Orchestration rule (backend)**: `service → service` and `service → orchestrator` FORBIDDEN. Cross-domain logic lives only in `src/orchestration/`. Access singletons via `{Domain}Context.services.*`, never `new Service()`.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **SDK `development` export condition**: monorepo apps consume SDK source directly at *runtime* — but `tsc` still resolves types through `sdk/*/dist/*.d.ts`, so a stale or bad `dist` breaks `typecheck` while `dev` runs fine. The errors surface in app/test files that reference a real, exported SDK type (`'@frak-labs/core-sdk' has no exported member named X`), so they read as dead code to delete — they are not. Confirm the symbol exists in `sdk/*/src` (it usually does), then `bun run build:sdk`. CI builds the SDK from scratch and never sees this, so it is local-only and does not track `dist` mtime: a `dist` newer than the last `src` commit can still be wrong.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **CDN bundles are `deps.alwaysBundle: [/.*/]`**: fully self-contained; bumping a dep bloats CDN size. Also one parse unit, so a single above-floor construct anywhere in the dependency graph makes the whole bundle unparseable — hence `bun run check:es-output`.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Zustand individual selectors mandatory**: `store((s) => s.x)`. Destructuring whole store = re-render storm (business app is most sensitive).

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Shopify non-obvious**: no `<a>` / no `react-router` `redirect` in auth routes (loses session); stage literal `"prod"` is FORBIDDEN — use `"production"`; README mentions Prisma/SQLite but project uses Drizzle/Postgres. **Storefront origins are generated, not fetched**: dev and prod are two separate Shopify apps with two separate `shopify app deploy` runs, so the stage is known before upload — `apps/shopify/scripts/generateStageArtifacts.ts` bakes the wallet/backend/SDK origins into `listener.liquid` and the post-purchase bundle, and `bun run check:shopify-stage` (inside `lint`) fails if what is committed is not the prod table, because a deploy uploads the working tree.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Of the 3 plugins, only 2 are real**: `plugins/{wordpress,prestashop}` are live; `plugins/magento` is unused scaffolding that no merchant and no one here has ever run against a Magento install. It stays as a starting point — do not port new features into it, and do not read it as a working reference. See `plugins/magento/AGENTS.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Bun bin trap**: `bun test` bypasses Vitest and runs Bun's own runner — always use `bun run test`.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Dual TypeScript (intentional)**: `typescript@6` stays alongside `@typescript/native` (TS 7): tsdown/rolldown-plugin-dts and tsserver (editor) peer on TS ≤6; only `typecheck` scripts use the TS 7 `tsc`. Do NOT "clean up" the TS 6 dep.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Docs generation left this repo, but the JSDoc contract did not**: reference pages are generated from `sdk/{core,react,components}` source by the landing/docs repo (TypeDoc config in its `packages/docs/astro.config.mjs`, output to Starlight). Wallet-side we only run `bun run build:sdk` — `typedoc.js` and `docs/{replace-external,vocs-frontmatter,vocs-sidebar}.js` were deleted as uninvoked. What survives is invisible: SDK source uses `@group` and `@description` as **custom** block tags, which the consuming config must declare via `blockTags: [...OptionDefaults.blockTags, "@description", "@group"]` plus `frontmatterCommentTags: ["description"]`, or they degrade silently to unknown tags. `@ignore` is the real hiding mechanism — not `@internal`, which has zero uses — and needs `validation.notDocumented: false` to avoid warning on ignored types referenced elsewhere. Entry points are each package's `src/index.ts` plus core's `src/actions/index.ts`. Breaking a reference page is a wallet-side JSDoc fix, not a docs-repo one.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Biome config**: 4-space indent, double quotes, ES5 trailing commas, cognitive complexity ≤16 everywhere except `packages/rpc` (own `biome.json`, rule off) and `packages/design-system/src/components/charts/**` (root override, rule off). `type` over `interface`, no enums, no `as any`/`@ts-ignore`/`!`.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **The quality gate does NOT cover native**: biome cannot parse Kotlin or Swift, so `example/native-{android,ios}` (and `sdk/{android,ios}`) are excluded in `biome.json`. Native has its own equivalents — ktlint via the Gradle plugin, `swift format` from the Xcode toolchain — run per app (`bun run --cwd example/native-ios lint`) or across both with `bun run --filter '*/native-*' lint`. Neither needs installing. There is no separate native typecheck: Gradle assembly (`assembleDebug` in the harnesses, `assembleRelease` in `sdk/android`) and `swift build` under Swift 6 strict concurrency *are* it.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Native example apps are the test harness, not a demo**: a native SDK cannot run without an app hosting it. Both harnesses drive the real client through its public API only — Android via a Gradle composite build, iOS via a SwiftPM path dependency.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **`sdk/{android,ios}` implement the MVP surface**: two artifacts each (core is UI-free, UI carries the web view) covering identity + proof signing, the FrakContext v2 codec, tracking over a durable queue, inbound `fCtx`, the sharing sheet and the install handoff. Android has been device-tested throughout development and iOS since 2026-08-12 — but always against `example/native-{android,ios}`, in a debug build, on one screen, which cannot catch what the harness itself gets wrong, what only R8 does, or what only a multi-destination `NavHost` triggers. CI (`.github/workflows/apps.yaml`) covers both SDKs on every `dev`/`main` push and PR touching them — Android now runs the full `check` (ktlint, `assembleRelease`, JVM tests, the ABI gate, Android Lint, version drift — the dex budget was retired in `32836c217` for measuring unminified output; the harness's `release` variant is minified so R8 is reproducible), but that is still compile-and-JVM/host-test coverage only, no emulator, no simulator. **The Android ABI gate is now ratified**: `frak-sdk/api/frak-sdk.api` and `frak-sdk-ui/api/frak-sdk-ui.api` are committed, `apiCheck` passes and runs in CI, and `check` is green — change a public signature and it goes red until you rerun `bun run --cwd sdk/android apiDump` (JDK 17 + `ANDROID_HOME`) and review the diff. iOS has no ABI gate and cannot easily have one. **Both SDKs are published**: `id.frak.sdk:core` and `id.frak.sdk:ui` at `1.0.0-beta.1` are on Maven Central and `frak-id/frak-ios-sdk` carries the matching tag, cut from `0a5b873a4` on 2026-08-13 — but *nothing consumes a published artifact yet*, so the ABI is nominally frozen and practically still free, and that ends the moment a merchant integrates. Take the ABI decisions in `docs/plans/native-sdk/open.md` §1 before then. Plan: `docs/plans/native-sdk/` — `decisions.md` for what is settled and why, `open.md` for what is not, `next.md` for the order.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **`sdk/ios` now declares Swift 6 in `Package.swift`**: the manifest is tools-version 6.0 with `.swiftLanguageMode(.v6)` on all four targets, so a merchant's own build gets the same strict concurrency CI does — it used to be tools-version 5.9 with `-swift-version 6` passed only from `scripts/run.sh`, which CI called and a merchant never did. The cost is a hard Xcode 16 floor for anyone resolving the package; `.unsafeFlags` is not an alternative, SwiftPM forbids it on a package resolved as a dependency. Tests use Swift Testing, not XCTest — the XCTest overlay cannot link at an iOS-simulator triple from SwiftPM.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Native SDK versioning is deliberately outside Changesets, and independent per platform**: `id.frak.sdk:core` and `FrakSDK` version separately — a merchant's binary freezes at store submission, so a JS-style patch cadence is meaningless, and either platform must be able to take a hotfix alone. Both `package.json` files are `private` and in `.changeset/config.json` `ignore`; they exist only to dispatch to `scripts/run.sh`. Nothing pairs the two versions; they have matched so far because they were cut together, not because anything enforces it. What Changesets would have owned is replaced by three things. **The bump is one hand-written commit that moves every site at once** — five files on Android (`gradle.properties`, `FrakSdkVersion.kt`, `package.json`, the harness coordinates in `example/native-android`, and the README twice — the merchant integration snippet and the `publishLocal` path) and three on iOS (`FrakSDKVersion.swift`, `package.json`, the `exact:` pin in `README.mirror.md`) — gated as a set by `bun run check:native-versions` (`scripts/native-version.ts`), which runs inside `bun run --cwd sdk/android check`, every iOS `run.sh` subcommand, and both release workflows. The list lives at the monorepo root because one Android site is outside that package, and because a per-platform copy is the thing that drifts. **The CHANGELOG is `sdk/{android,ios}/CHANGELOG.md`** (Keep a Changelog), written under `[Unreleased]` as you work and promoted by the release commit; the gate fails a release whose version has no section, and both workflows publish that section as the GitHub release body. The iOS one ships inside the mirror payload, where it is the only history a merchant can see. **The publish is the tag** (`android-v*` / `ios-v*`); iOS lints, builds and tests the released tree on macOS *before* the mirror push, since the mirror refuses to retag a published version, and Android drafts its GitHub release while the Portal deployment is still `USER_MANAGED` so both are published by the same hand.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text:
- **Comments are on a budget, and it is now enforced (`bun run lint:comments`)**: this rule has decayed twice — once before `f7e69f4` (unreachable from `dev` now; it took 6826 comment lines to 2275) and again across the native SDK work, which put ~600 lines back. So it stopped being prose: `scripts/check-comments.ts` runs inside `bun run lint`, and the rules below are what it checks on every `.kt`/`.swift`/`.ts`/`.tsx` file — biome owns formatting and lint rules in the TS tree, but it has nothing to say about comment prose, which is why the TS half decayed unwatched. Point it at paths to scope it (`bun run lint:comments -- services/backend/src`). Generated output (`*.gen.ts`, `*.d.ts`) and installed or emitted trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage`, `.sst`, `.pulumi`) are never scanned.
  - **Ceiling: 5 lines of comment text per block** — delimiters (`/**`, `*/`) and blank `*` separators do not count, and a `- Parameters:`/`@param`/`@return` tail is exempt. A block that wants more is telling you the code needs a name, not a paragraph. Public surface → 1–2 sentence summary plus those tags. `internal`/`private` → one line, and only for a trap the next reader would otherwise "fix". Statement inside a body → one line.
  - **Never longer than the code it sits on** (measured against the whole braced body, so a type is measured against the type). 9 lines of doc on a 1-line `let` is the exact shape that got deleted last time.
  - **Never the history**: `used to`, `previously`, `no longer`, `the old X`, `we tried`, `originally`, "record of what was checked", "rejected alternatives, for completeness" — all rejected by the linter, all of it belongs in the commit message, the PR body, or `docs/plans/**`. A source file is where rationale goes to never be deleted. Cross-platform comparisons ("Android does X, we do Y") are the same thing and go the same place.
  - **Never the mechanism**: comment the trap (an invariant the compiler cannot state, a lock held one layer up, a wire-format quirk), not what the next five lines plainly do.
  - **Tests**: the test name is the documentation. No doc block on a `@Test`/`func test…`/`it(`/`test(`/`describe(` beyond one line, and never a note on what the test deliberately does *not* cover — delete it or make it a case.
  - **Baseline, not amnesty**: `scripts/comment-budget-baseline.json` holds the findings that predate the gate, counted per file. A file may only ever get better — add one and the build goes red. After paying some down, run `bun run lint:comments -- --update-baseline` and commit the smaller numbers. Gating TS added ~1 275 findings to it in one go: that is the measured TS debt, not a licence to leave it.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Commit style**: Conventional Commits (`type(scope): subject`) — e.g. `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `build`, `style`, `perf`, `test`, `docs`.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Vite 8 bundles with rolldown natively** (Rust) — no `rolldown-vite` alias; `@wagmi/connectors` stubbed in resolutions to avoid MetaMask SDK bloat.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **The browser floor is Safari 15.4**: `BROWSER_TARGET_ECMA` / `BROWSER_TARGET_SAFARI` live in `packages/dev-tooling/src/es-version.ts` (`vite.ts` re-exports them, so existing import sites are unchanged), with `BROWSER_TARGET` and the Lightning CSS targets still in `vite.ts`. Coverage is not uniform, and the gaps are deliberate: the four vite configs that pin a target read `BROWSER_TARGET`; the five `tsdown` configs keep literal targets, proven by `bun run check:es-output` parsing what they emit — it also fails on a `tsdown` config nobody registered. Four surfaces sit outside a pin — `services/backend/src/utils/processCss.ts` (lowers merchant-supplied CSS wider on purpose), the wallet service worker (`ES2020`, commented), and `apps/business` + `apps/shopify`, which run the gate without a pin because the floor comes from wallet traffic they do not serve. Never write `baseline-widely-available` — that alias moved twice (safari16 under vite 7, safari16.4 under vite 8), silently, inside unrelated migrations. Three layers enforce the floor and they catch different things: `lib: ES2022` rejects what you *author* — but only where the workspace declares a `typecheck` script, since root typecheck is `--filter '*' typecheck`; a new browser workspace needs both, or its pin is decorative (`packages/client` and `sdk/legacy` were that gap until FRA-306/FRA-320); `assertBundleEsVersion` rejects what a vite app *ships*; and `bun run check:es-output` rejects what the `tsdown` packages ship — ambient augmentations `lib` cannot see (`bun-types` merges `Promise.withResolvers` onto `PromiseConstructor`), dependency code hidden by `skipLibCheck`, and syntax rolldown emits verbatim below target. `bun-types` cannot be removed from the four apps or `wallet-shared`: their `@backend-*` path mappings pull real backend source (`Bun.serve`, `Bun.password`, `bun:jsc`) into each app's own compilation.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **The iOS floor is 16.0 for the Tauri wallet app, and it is gated (`bun run check:ios-floor`)** — `sdk/ios` is a separate surface and targets iOS 15: passkeys are the only entry path into the wallet and `ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredential*` needs iOS 16, so a 15.x install could never create a credential — and would not even fail cleanly, since the plugin's reject string matches no branch in `classifyWebauthnError` and lands on `unknown`/`retryable` (a generic retry toast on an operation that can never succeed). The floor makes the App Store show Apple's own "requires iOS 16.0 or later" instead. ITMS-90068 only mandates 15.0 from Spring 2027; 16 is the passkey requirement, not the Apple one. Thirteen sites carry it — `gen/apple/project.yml` (the truth), both `XCBuildConfiguration` blocks in the committed `project.pbxproj`, the `Podfile`, `minimumSystemVersion` in `tauri.conf.json` (pins it against the Tauri CLI's own 14.0 default on `tauri ios init`), eight plugin `ios/Package.swift`, and the SwiftPM pre-warm stub in `.github/workflows/tauri-mobile-release.yml`, where a stale floor poisons the shared artifact cache. `scripts/check-ios-floor.ts` gates them as a set, inside `bun run lint` and the release workflow's validate job: bump `project.yml` and let it name the rest. It also catches the trap that a partial bump is not a warning — `.vN` requires the PackageDescription that shipped it (`.v15`→5.5, `.v16`→5.7), so a manifest left on an older `swift-tools-version` is a hard parse error, while a manifest left at an older `.vN` links fine and surfaces only as an always-true availability branch nobody deletes.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Stages matter**: `$dev` (local), `dev` / `prod` (AWS), `gcp-staging` / `gcp-production` (GCP GKE, all prod apps). Migration `KubernetesJob` MUST finish before backend `KubernetesService` deploys.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Listener is not standalone**: served at `/listener` path on wallet ingress.

head: AGENTS.md — Root Compass > Non-Obvious Patterns (Tribal Knowledge)
text: - **Frontend secrets = build-time only** via BuildKit `--mount=type=secret` (never runtime). Backend secrets = K8s env vars from GCP Secret Manager.

Backend LLM control belongs in scripts, not CLI commands. Do not add aliases or convenience methods; copy protocol updates from OpenCode and update the CLI directly.

head: Protocol Convention
text: `ui.screenshot` is the one deliberate Drive-local exception. OpenCode exposes `ui.capture`, which returns a renderer-neutral RGBA terminal frame. Drive implements `ui.screenshot` by calling `ui.capture`, rendering that frame to a PNG, and returning its absolute path. Do not add `ui.screenshot` to the OpenCode wire protocol, require an OpenCode endpoint to declare a media directory, or expose media-directory bookkeeping in normal usage. A standalone `--command.ui.screenshot` invocation must print the image path to stdout.

head: Protocol Convention
text: `packages/drive` is the generic published package. `apps/catalog` owns OpenCode-specific flow IDs, taxonomies, captures, and review UI; the package must not import the app.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: Gotchas learned the hard way in `packages/drive/test/manual/`; prefer the helpers in `test/manual/tui-regressions/support.ts` over reimplementing them.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - Timeout severity is split: `UiWaitTimeoutError` (a `waitFor`/`getElement`/`getNode` deadline passed) is catchable and safe to branch on; `UiTimeoutError` (an unanswered UI RPC) aborts the whole run even when caught. Use `support.appeared` for "did X show up in time?".

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - LLM request bodies carry the whole conversation. Route markers by which appears **last** in the serialized body (`lastIndexOf`), never by the first `includes` hit (`support.serveMarkers`).

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - Server admissions are the only ground truth for "did my prompt land" (`support.admissions`). The screen and `prompt-history.jsonl` can both mislead: history records composer text at POST-resolution time, which may include text typed mid-flight that was never sent.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - `ctrl+c` on an empty composer exits the TUI (killing the run with `RpcClientDefect: connection closed`); use `ctrl+u` to clear leftover composer text.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - Effect v4: it is `Effect.catch`, not `Effect.catchAll`.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - Seeded state-machine probes stream every chosen transition to stderr and must write `state-machine-failure.json` on any failure, including terminal verify phases (`state-machine.ts` exports `saveFailure`). A failure without its seed and trace is nearly worthless.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - Isolated-instance state lives under `${artifacts}/home/...` (for example `home/.local/state/opencode/prompt-history.jsonl`); screenshots land under the run's `output/.../generation-N/` directory.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - Set `OPENCODE_DRIVE_MEDIA_DIR=$PWD/.drive-output` (gitignored) when running probes from an agent. The default media root is under the system tmpdir with a per-run id in the path, so every run triggers a fresh outside-the-project permission prompt; a stable in-workspace directory avoids that entirely.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - Interrupting a busy session takes **two** escape presses within 5 seconds (the first arms, the second fires `session.interrupt`). A single `ui.press("escape")` is a no-op for interruption.

head: Protocol Convention > Writing Probe Scripts
text: - `server.kill()` mid-stream abandons the in-flight served reply (deliberate detach, not a failure) and `server.launch()` attaches the LLM stub to the replacement service; pass `OPENCODE_DRIVE_DB=...` so both generations share a database (see `quiescence-restart.ts`).

head: OMH Agent Contract
text:
This file is the repo-local operating contract for coding agents working on
oh-my-hermes, including Codex, Claude Code, Hermes runtime/handoff paths, and
generic executor profiles.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Product Direction
text:
Read `docs/DIRECTION.md` before changing architecture, workflow behavior,
wrapper contracts, generated skill guidance, or coding delegation semantics.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Product Direction
text:
OMH is a Hermes-native wrapper orchestration layer. Keep Hermes responsible for
chat intake, clarification, source-backed research, planning, and status
narration. Keep main coding work delegated to the selected coding owner through
explicit prepared handoffs and observed evidence. Do not make Codex the implicit
default in product language, docs, schemas, prompts, or reports when Claude
Code, Hermes runtime/handoff paths, or generic executor profiles are also valid
owners.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Product Direction
text:
When developing OMH itself, treat Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes
runtime/handoff paths as first-class product surfaces. User-facing runtime
selection may choose one coding owner for a task, but OMH feature design,
contracts, docs, setup, memory recall, and status/reporting changes should
consider all three surfaces unless a change is explicitly scoped to one
executor. If support differs, document the difference as a capability boundary
instead of silently optimizing for Codex.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Product Direction
text:
Do not turn OMH into a hidden Hermes runtime patch, transport bot, network
service, LLM router, or secret coding executor. The one sanctioned execution
surface is the explicit opt-in fanout dispatch bridge described under
Implementation Boundaries — operator-invoked, local-only, fully observed,
never hidden and never a default. The one sanctioned network call is the
`omh_jev_ask` tool, also described there — user-requested per turn, never a
default.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Command Audience
text:
Treat natural-language Hermes chat as the normal product surface. Most people
should only need to run `omh setup`, `omh update`, and `omh doctor` directly.
Removal or unusual repair commands are exceptional maintenance paths, not the
day-to-day OMH workflow.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Command Audience
text:
Commands under `omh chat`, `omh coding`, `omh runtime`, `omh memory`, `omh
loop`, `omh goal`, `omh harness`, `omh capabilities`, `omh release`, `omh
state`, and similar control-plane groups primarily exist for Hermes Agent,
wrappers, coding agents, automations, and maintainers. Public docs may show
those commands as integration or operator references, but must label the
audience explicitly and must not make normal users memorize or run them to get
value. Describe the human action as an intent or outcome, such as asking Hermes
to prepare coding work, while keeping the backend command in the agent-facing
reference.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Delivery Grain
text: One user goal should normally produce one PR.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Delivery Grain
text:
Plan, explain, and report delivery at the full user-goal completion grain. Do
not frame a recommendation as "the first PR", "initial PR", "first slice", or a
similarly partial unit unless the user explicitly asks for phased delivery or an
independent release/rollback boundary forces a split. When implementation must
be split, state the complete target capability first, then explain the concrete
split reason and the remaining capability gap.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Delivery Grain
text:
Use multiple focused commits inside the same goal PR when useful. Planning docs,
tests, implementation, code-review fixes, CI fixes, and small follow-up docs
belong in the same PR when they serve the same user goal.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Delivery Grain
text:
Do not split review feedback or small follow-up fixes into new PRs merely
because a previous commit already exists. Split only when the next change is a
different user-facing goal, has independent release or rollback value, would
make the current PR too risky to review, is blocked by an external decision, or
the user explicitly asks for separate PRs.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Delivery Grain
text:
When the user asks to merge, finish review fixes in the current PR first, rerun
verification, wait for required checks, then merge if authority is clear.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Pull Request Reports
text:
PR descriptions must read like a useful feature report, not a terse changelog.
When a coding agent opens a PR for this project, use the repository PR template
and fill every relevant section with concrete, reviewable detail.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Pull Request Reports
text: Every PR body should explain:

head: OMH Agent Contract > Pull Request Reports

head: OMH Agent Contract > Pull Request Reports

head: OMH Agent Contract > Pull Request Reports
text:
Avoid one-line summaries such as "update docs" or "fix setup" when the PR

head: OMH Agent Contract > Implementation Boundaries
text:
- No LLM, API, Discord, Slack, GitHub, or network calls inside core `omh`
  features unless the user explicitly approves a scoped integration.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Implementation Boundaries
text:
- The approved scoped integration under that clause is the fanout dispatch
  bridge (`omh coding fanout dispatch`, 2026-07 owner approval, plus its
  `omh coding run` single-run entry that builds and dispatches a one-unit
  contract through the same engine in one call): an explicit operator command
  that spawns LOCAL agent CLIs (the CLIs make their own network calls; omh
  still makes none) in per-unit worktrees against a frozen `fanout_contract/v2`,
  recording every spawn and exit as observed journal evidence. It never runs
  by default, never merges branches, never persists raw prompts under `.omh`,
  and never executes anything outside an explicit `dispatch`/`run` invocation
  -- running one against an explicitly-named owner is itself the required
  opt-in. Bridge dispatch is a separate axis from chat prompt-handoff
  semantics: chat-prepared handoffs remain prompt-only for prompt-only
  profiles.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Implementation Boundaries
text:
- The approved Hermes-native child boundary (`omh coding hermes-child dispatch`,
  2026-08 owner approval) is a second explicit operator/maintainer surface for
  one isolated local Hermes single-query process (`hermes chat --query-file -`,
  the one Hermes transport that reads a prompt from stdin). It requires
  `--confirm-dispatch`, accepts prompts only through stdin/files, enforces a
  depth-one recursion limit and safe-mode file tools, records authenticated
  `routing_observation/v1` evidence, and never runs automatically. This
  boundary supports observed Hermes execution and the explicit benchmark
  controller; it does not make core OMH a provider client or hidden runtime.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Implementation Boundaries
text:
- `omh coding paired-run dispatch` may reuse that same Hermes-child boundary
  for explicitly confirmed evaluation cells. The operator supplies one
  digest-matching task file per frozen task, the repository/revision, and the
  provider; OMH passes task bytes over child stdin, creates detached per-cell
  worktrees under an atomically unique invocation-owned parent, verifies
  signed evaluation bindings, removes only paths reserved by that invocation,
  and persists no task body. This is a front door to the approved child boundary,
  not a third subprocess authority. Executors without a receipt-capable
  adapter are refused without substitution; caller-injected adapters remain
  the executor-neutral extension seam.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Implementation Boundaries
text:
- `omh coding fanout dispatch --final-review` may also compose that existing
  child boundary after dispatcher-observed integration GREEN. It requires the
  explicit flag, a clean integrated worktree/tree revision, and named Hermes
  provider/model settings; four read-only lenses run in disposable,
  write-denied detached worktrees under fixed concurrency, parse only a closed
  verdict token, and cannot merge or mutate the integrated checkout.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Implementation Boundaries
text:
- `omh coding fanout dispatch --diagnostics` may spawn only the closed local
  diagnostic command set after producer verification GREEN. The default
  adapter discovers supported binaries from `PATH`, passes no shell text or
  user-selected executable, materializes detached fixed-revision worktrees,
  strips messages and absolute paths, redacts the child environment, caps
  concurrency/time/output, always reaps the provider's complete process tree,
  and removes every temporary worktree. No provider is installed or started
  unless the operator types the flag. On Windows the provider starts suspended,
  enters a kill-on-close Job Object, and resumes only after ownership succeeds;
  clean evidence requires the Job Object to report zero active processes.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Implementation Boundaries
text:
- The approved scoped network integration (2026-09-23 owner approval) is the
  `omh_jev_ask` plugin tool: it POSTs typed questions to Jev with the user's
  own key and returns probabilities. It runs only when the person's own
  message for that turn names Jev (a per-turn marker `pre_llm_call` records;
  otherwise the tool returns `consent_not_observed` and opens no socket), and
  only when a route resolves — `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
  plus `{"openrouter_route": true}` in `<omh_home>/jev/settings.json`, which
  OMH never writes. Stdlib only, HTTPS only, a fixed two-host route table, no
  redirects, bounded bodies, no retry after a sent request times out. It
  persists no key, `state`, question text, or reply; one metadata-only ledger
  row per ask. `src/plugin_bundle/omh/jev_ask_client.py` is the only network
  client in `src/` and only `tools/jev_ask_tool.py` may import it. Third-party
  Jev plugins are still never called, and `omh doctor` still reads no
  credential value.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Implementation Boundaries
text: - No Hermes core patching.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Verification > Reporting Our Own Numbers
text:
A rate OMH computes about itself is a claim, so it carries what it divided.
Every percentage in a payload names the buckets its numerator summed, what its
denominator counted, and every observation class excluded before either count
was taken — `src/quality/reported_rate.py` is that shape, and
`reported_rate_shape_errors()` is what checks it. Two specific traps:

head: OMH Agent Contract > Verification > Reporting Our Own Numbers
text:
- **An empty denominator is not 0%.** `max(1, count)` in a divisor turns a
  corpus with nothing in it into a confident zero, which claims that every case
  was measured and every case failed. Report `percent: null` with basis
  `no_observations` instead, and let an unmeasured rate fail its target rather
  than pass it.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Verification > Reporting Our Own Numbers
text:
- **A composed numerator says so.** When a rate sums more than one outcome
  bucket, name them in the payload, not only in a text formatter — every
  non-human consumer reads the JSON.

head: OMH Agent Contract > Verification > Reporting Our Own Numbers

The same rule governs prose: a headline number in a commit, PR, or report names
the arm, the corpus, the selection rule, and the committed artifact it came

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: Full-stack interactive narrative (relationship drama RPG) demo. Backend generates stories via LLM, frontend lets users create and play them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - **Backend**: FastAPI + Pydantic + LangGraph + SQLite (`rpg_backend/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - **Frontend**: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7 + Motion.js (`frontend/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - **Production**: https://rpg.shehao.app (single EC2 + nginx + SQLite)

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Backend Domains

| Domain | Path | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| Auth | `rpg_backend/auth/` | Cookie-session auth, SQLite user store |
| Author v1 | `rpg_backend/author/` | Public API contracts, gateway, metrics, display utilities |
| Author v2 | `rpg_backend/author_v2/` | Story generation implementation: LangGraph workflow, templates, IP library |

| Play v1 | `rpg_backend/play/` | Play session service, public contracts, turn processing |
| Play v2 | `rpg_backend/play_v2/` | Runtime engine: director, narration, causal contracts, escalation |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Backend Domains
text: **v1/v2 relationship**: v1 modules own the public API contracts and service interfaces. v2 modules provide the implementation. For example, `main.py` imports contracts from `author/contracts.py` (v1) but instantiates `ProductAuthorJobService` from `author_v2/`. Same pattern applies to play: `PlaySessionService` (v1) delegates to v2 runtime handlers.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Frontend Structure

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions
text: This file governs how Claude Code maintains the personal knowledge wiki in this vault. Read it at the start of every session before doing any wiki work.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > What This Wiki Is
text: This is a **persistent, compounding knowledge base** — not a RAG index. When you add a source, Claude reads it, extracts key knowledge, and integrates it into interlinked wiki pages. The wiki accumulates understanding over time; cross-references, contradictions, and syntheses are already there when you need them.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > What This Wiki Is
text:
You (the human) are responsible for: sourcing material, exploration, and asking the right questions.
Claude is responsible for: summarizing, cross-referencing, filing, and maintaining the wiki.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Page Types > `overview` — `wiki/overview.md`
text: The single evolving synthesis page. Updated when a new source meaningfully shifts the overall picture. Structured as a narrative with cross-links, not a list.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Page Types > `topic` — `wiki/[kebab-name].md`
text: Notes on a concept, technology, domain, or idea. Examples: `wiki/distributed-systems.md`, `wiki/machine-learning-ops.md`, `wiki/investing-frameworks.md`.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Page Types > `entity` — `wiki/[name].md`
text: Notes on a specific person, company, tool, project, or place. Examples: `wiki/anthropic.md`, `wiki/kafka.md`, `wiki/ray-dalio.md`.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Page Types > `source-summary` — `wiki/sources/[slug].md`
text: Summary of one ingested source. Slug is kebab-case derived from the title. One page per source.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Page Types > `qa` — `wiki/qa/[slug].md`
text: A filed answer to a notable query. Created when an answer synthesizes multiple pages in a way worth preserving.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Page Types > `admin` — `wiki/index.md`, `wiki/log.md`
text: Special system/administrative pages. Not synthesis content. There are exactly two: `index.md` (master index) and `log.md` (activity log).

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Frontmatter Format
text: All wiki pages use this YAML frontmatter:

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Frontmatter Format
text: - `type`: Required. One of the six page types above.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Frontmatter Format
text: - `tags`: Optional. Lowercase, hyphenated. Topics for the Obsidian tag pane.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Frontmatter Format
text: - `sources`: Links to the `wiki/sources/` pages that informed this page.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Frontmatter Format
text: - `related`: Links to other wiki pages directly relevant to this one.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Frontmatter Format
text: - `updated`: Date this page was last meaningfully revised.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Naming Conventions
text: - **File names**: kebab-case, all lowercase. `machine-learning-ops.md`, not `MachineLearningOps.md`.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Naming Conventions
text: - **Links**: Always use Obsidian `[[wikilinks]]` — never bare URLs or markdown `[text](path)` links for internal cross-references.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Naming Conventions
text: - **Link format**: Use the full path from vault root: `[[wiki/distributed-systems]]`, `[[wiki/sources/attention-is-all-you-need]]`.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Naming Conventions
text: - **Section headings**: Use `##` for top-level sections within a page, `###` for subsections.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Naming Conventions
text: - **Contradictions**: Mark with `> [!WARNING] Contradiction` callout. Explain both claims and their sources.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Naming Conventions
text: - **Uncertainty**: Mark claims you're unsure about with `[?]` inline.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: Run this workflow whenever the user adds a new source. Do not skip steps.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 1 — Read the source**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - If URL: fetch and read the full content.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - If file in `raw-sources/`: read it with the Read tool.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - If pasted text: treat as the source.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 2 — Discuss with the user**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Summarize the source in 3-5 bullets.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Ask: what aspects matter most? Anything to emphasize or skip?

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Let the user's response shape which topics get deep treatment.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 3 — Create source summary page**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - File: `wiki/sources/[slug].md`

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Sections: title, author/date, one-paragraph abstract, key claims (bulleted), notable quotes (max 3), your synthesis note, links to wiki pages this source touches.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 4 — Update `wiki/index.md`**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Add the new source to the Sources section with a one-line description and link.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 5 — Identify affected wiki pages**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Run `INDEX_PATH=qmd.sqlite pnpm dlx @tobilu/qmd query -c wiki "<source topic and key claims>"` to surface related existing wiki pages.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Also Glob `wiki/*.md` and `wiki/sources/*.md` to ensure completeness.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - List all pages to create or update.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 6 — Update or create wiki pages**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - For each affected page: open it, integrate the new information, add `[[wiki/sources/slug]]` to the `sources` frontmatter, update `updated` date.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Create new pages for topics/entities that don't have one yet.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Keep each page a synthesis, not a copy of the source. Write in your own words with source attributions.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 7 — Flag contradictions**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - If the new source contradicts anything on an existing wiki page, mark it with the `[!WARNING] Contradiction` callout on the affected page. State both positions and both sources.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 8 — Update `wiki/overview.md`**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: - Only if the source shifts the high-level synthesis or introduces a significant new theme.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text: **Step 9 — Append to log**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Ingest Workflow
text:
- Append an entry to `wiki/log.md` using this format:
  ```
  ## [YYYY-MM-DD] ingest | Source Title

  [[wiki/sources/slug]] | Pages touched: [[wiki/page1]], [[wiki/page2]], ...
  ```

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: Run this workflow when the user asks a question against the wiki.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: **Step 1 — Search the wiki**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: - Run `INDEX_PATH=qmd.sqlite pnpm dlx @tobilu/qmd query -c wiki "<question>"` to surface semantically relevant pages.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: - Read `wiki/index.md` to confirm coverage and catch any pages qmd didn't surface.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: - Read the 2-5 most relevant pages fully.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: **Step 2 — Synthesize an answer**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: - Write the answer with inline `[[wiki/page]]` citations.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: - Be clear about confidence level. Flag gaps with "The wiki doesn't have coverage on X."

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: **Step 3 — Offer to file**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: - If the answer draws together multiple pages in a novel way, ask: "This answer synthesizes several pages in a useful way — want me to file it as a Q&A page?"

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: - If yes: create `wiki/qa/[slug].md`, add to `wiki/index.md` Q&A section, and cross-link from the relevant topic pages.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text: **Step 4 — Log (optional)**

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Query Workflow
text:
- For significant queries that reveal new understanding, append to `wiki/log.md`:
  ```
  ## [YYYY-MM-DD] query | Brief question summary

  Filed as: [[wiki/qa/slug]] (or "not filed")
  ```

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text: Run this workflow periodically or when the user asks to "health-check the wiki."

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text: Check for each of the following and report findings:

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text:
1. **Orphan pages** — wiki pages with no inbound `[[links]]` from other wiki pages.
   - Fix: add links from relevant topic pages, or note they may be stubs to delete.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text:
2. **Unresolved contradictions** — pages with `[!WARNING] Contradiction` callouts that haven't been resolved.
   - Fix: flag to user; determine if new sources could resolve them.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text:
3. **Stale claims** — claims on older pages that newer sources have superseded.
   - Fix: update the claim, update the source attribution.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text:
4. **Missing pages** — concepts or entities mentioned frequently (via `[[links]]`) that lack their own page.
   - Fix: create stub pages and queue for future ingestion.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text:
5. **Broken links** — `[[wikilinks]]` pointing to files that don't exist.
   - Fix: create the missing page or correct the link.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text:
6. **Data gaps** — important topics in the wiki that lack source coverage.
   - Report: suggest specific sources or web searches to fill the gap.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Lint Workflow
text:
After checking, produce a lint report with: issues found, fixes applied, and a "next sources to investigate" list. Append to `wiki/log.md`:
```
## [YYYY-MM-DD] lint | Lint run

N issues found, N fixed. [Brief summary of notable findings.]
```

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Hard Rules
text: 1. **Never modify anything in `raw-sources/`**. These are immutable raw inputs.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Hard Rules
text: 2. **Never touch existing vault files** (daily-notes, misc, ideas, root-level .md files, .obsidian/). The wiki lives only in `wiki/`.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Hard Rules
text: 3. **Always append to `wiki/log.md`** — never overwrite it.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Hard Rules
text: 4. **One source summary per ingested source** in `wiki/sources/`. Never merge two sources into one summary page.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Hard Rules
text: 5. **Every wiki page must have frontmatter** with at least `type` and `updated`.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Hard Rules
text: 6. **Cross-link aggressively** — if you mention a topic or entity that has (or should have) a wiki page, link it with `[[wiki/page]]`.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Hard Rules
text: 7. **Write synthesis, not transcription**. Wiki pages should reflect integrated understanding, not copied excerpts.

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Search Tool
text:
This vault uses **qmd** (`pnpm dlx @tobilu/qmd`) for local semantic and full-text search.
Collections and contexts are registered via `pnpm qmd:setup` and stored in `qmd.sqlite` at the vault root (gitignored).

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Search Tool
text:
| Command | Use |
|---------|-----|
| `INDEX_PATH=qmd.sqlite pnpm dlx @tobilu/qmd query -c wiki "<question>"` | Hybrid search — best for topic discovery |
| `INDEX_PATH=qmd.sqlite pnpm dlx @tobilu/qmd search -c wiki "<terms>"` | Fast keyword search (BM25, no LLM) |
| `INDEX_PATH=qmd.sqlite pnpm dlx @tobilu/qmd vsearch -c wiki "<question>"` | Pure vector/semantic search |

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Search Tool
text: Add `--json` for structured output. Omit `-c wiki` to search all collections (wiki, raw-sources, human, daily-notes).

head: LLM Wiki — Schema & Operating Instructions > Search Tool
text:
**Re-indexing:** After a bulk ingest session run:
```bash
pnpm qmd:reindex
```
Do NOT re-index after every single file edit.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text: **AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives** is a C# toolkit built around a Roslyn incremental source generator. Consumers declare a `readonly partial struct`/`partial class` implementing `IDomainValue<T>` with a `Validate(T value)` method; the generator emits the constructor, `TryCreate`, operators, `IParsable<T>`, `IConvertible`, `JsonConverter`, `TypeConverter`, XML serialization, Swagger/OpenAPI mappings, etc. See `README.md` for the full user-facing feature set — keep it in sync with generator behavior when either changes.

head: CLAUDE.md > Solution layout
text: - `src/AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives` — core attributes, base types (`PrimitiveValidationResult`, `InvalidDomainValueException`, etc.) and the `*Extensions` flexible-parsing helpers (`DateOnlyExtensions`, `DateTimeExtensions`, `DateTimeOffsetExtensions`, `TimeOnlyExtensions`, `TimeSpanExtensions`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Solution layout
text: - `src/AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives.Generator` — the incremental source generator itself (`DomainPrimitiveGenerator.cs`, `Executor.cs`, `Helpers/*`, `Models/*`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Solution layout
text: - `src/AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives.XmlDataTypes` — ready-made XML Schema primitive types (`GDay`, `GMonth`, `GYear`, `NonEmptyString`, etc.) built on top of the generator.

head: CLAUDE.md > Solution layout
text: - `src/AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives.SwaggerExtensions` / `src/AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives.OpenApiExtensions` — Swashbuckle and Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi integration.

head: CLAUDE.md > Solution layout
text: - `tests/AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives.UnitTests` — behavioral tests against generated code.

head: CLAUDE.md > Solution layout
text: - `tests/AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives.Generator.Tests` — Roslyn generator snapshot tests using Verify (`*.verified.cs` files under `Snapshots/`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Solution layout
text: - `tests/AltaSoft.DomainPrimitives.XmlDataTypes.Tests` — tests for the XML data types package.

head: CLAUDE.md > Solution layout
text: - `Examples/` — a demo API project and standalone example domain types (`DomainPrimitivesDemo/`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Build & test
text: Target frameworks are `net8.0`, `net9.0`, `net10.0` (`Directory.Build.props`); `LangVersion` is `Latest`. When changing generator output, regenerate/update Verify snapshots by running the generator tests and accepting the new `.verified.cs` output — never hand-edit a `.verified.cs` file to match new code without confirming the generated output is actually correct.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build & test
text: Do not commit `bin/`/`obj/`/`.vs/` — `clean.bat` wipes them locally if needed.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - No explicit constructors, public properties, or public fields on `IDomainValue<T>` implementations — the generator owns those and will emit compiler errors on violations (this is by design, not a bug to "fix").

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - Generated code lives in `*.g.cs`; never hand-edit generated output — change the generator instead.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - `SerializationFormatAttribute` and the `IsDateOrTime()`-gated codegen in `MethodGeneratorHelper.cs` are the two places that decide whether `Parse`/`TryParse` for date/time-backed primitives use plain `.Parse`/`.TryParse` vs. the flexible `ParseFlexible`/`TryParseFlexible` helpers — check both when touching date/time parsing behavior.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - Match existing XML doc style (`<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<inheritdoc/>` where applicable) — `GenerateDocumentationFile` is enabled and analyzers run at `AnalysisLevel=latest`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - Follow this repo's own no-unnecessary-comments style; prefer expressive names over comments in new code.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Project Overview
text: **ColibriGui** is a cross-platform 2D UI framework built on top of Ogre3D, designed primarily for games but suitable for industrial HMI and embedded systems. It provides a lightweight, flexible UI solution with touch, keyboard, and gamepad support.
