head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Layout System
text: There are three layout classes:

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Layout System
text: 1. **LayoutLine**: Extremely similar to CSS flexbox

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Layout System
text: 2. **LayoutMultiline**: Like LayoutLine but makes sure multiple rows (or columns if m_vertical = false) end up all the same size

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Layout System
text: 3. **LayoutTableSameSize**: Extremely similar to a CSS Grid

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Layout System > Layout Cell Order Important
text: When using ColibriGui layouts (`LayoutLine`, `LayoutTableSameSize`, etc.):

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Layout System > Layout Cell Order Important
text: 1. **Layout Cell Order is Preserved**: When you call `rootLayout.addCell()` multiple times, the order is preserved in rendering

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Layout System > Layout Cell Order Important
ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Layout System > Layout Cell Order Important
text: This ensures the label always appears before the buttons, regardless of which layout is used. You can't simply call `rootLayout.addCell( &lineLayout )` and `rootLayout.addCell( &tableLayout )` before `rootLayout.addCell( mLabel )` because that would alter the original order. Of course, if the label was originally called last, then you could do that. But you must not alter the order unless that is intended. In that sense, treat Layouts like CSS.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 1. **Thread Safety**: All UI operations must occur on the main thread. No concurrent access to widgets.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 2. **Memory Management**: ColibriManager owns all created widgets. Do not manually delete them.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 3. **Coordinate System**: All positions and sizes are in virtual canvas. How the virtual canvas translates to display depends on the renderer and `ColibriManager::setCanvasSize`.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 4. **Fixed Point**: Font sizes use 26.6 fixed point format internally. Use `FontSize` helper class or pass raw `uint32_t` value.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text:
5. **State Machine**: Widgets have 6 states (not counting NumStates sentinel):
   - `States::Disabled`
   - `States::Idle`
   - `States::HighlightedCursor`
   - `States::HighlightedButton`
   - `States::HighlightedButtonAndCursor`
   - `States::Pressed`

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 6. **Render Mode**: Choose between `BreadthFirst` (render parents first, faster but can cause issues if Widgets with children overlap) or `DepthFirst` (render children first) for correct Z-ordering. Set via `Widget::m_breadthFirst`.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 7. **RTL Support**: Use `ColibriManager::setSwapRTLControls(true)` to globally swap left/right controls for Arabic/Hebrew interfaces.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 8. **Focus Navigation**: Keyboard navigation uses tab order. Call `setKeyboardFocus()` on widgets that should receive keyboard focus. Widgets must also be keyboard navigable via `setKeyboardNavigable(true)`.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 9. **No Testing Framework**: This project has no unit tests. Verify functionality through examples in `Examples/` directory.

head: ColibriGui - AI Assistant Guide > Important Notes for AI Agents
text: 10. **Ogre Integration**: `ColibriManager::setOgre()` must be called after construction to provide Ogre objects for rendering.

klooAgentGuard — local DLP + observability layer for AI coding agents.

Tauri desktop app (Rust backend, web frontend). Runs a local HTTP server
on localhost:8008. Agent CLIs/IDEs install hook scripts that POST to this
server. No proxy — everything is hook-driven.

Cursor IDE       /cursor_hook/*     cursor_hooks.rs    commands/cursor.rs
  Claude Code      /claude_hook/*     claude_hooks.rs    commands/claude.rs
  Codex CLI        /codex_hook/*      codex_hooks.rs     commands/codex.rs

Each agent has:
  - Hook receiver (axum routes in *_hooks.rs)
  - Install/uninstall commands (commands/*.rs that write hook scripts + config)

DLP (Data Loss Prevention)
  - Regex + keyword pattern matching against prompts, tool inputs, file reads
  - Patterns stored in SQLite, configurable per-backend
  - Can block or pass — detections logged with full context
  - Files: dlp.rs, builtin_patterns.rs, pattern_utils.rs, dlp_pattern_config.rs

Token Limit
  - Per-backend max_tokens_in_a_request, blocks if exceeded
  - Settings: predefined_backend_settings.rs

Dependency Protection
  - Two independent per-backend settings in dependency_protection:
      block_malicious_packages  — hard deny when OSV returns vulnerabilities
      inform_updated_packages   — allow with advisory when a newer version exists
  - Intercepts two surfaces:
      1. Bash install commands (all three agents): pip install, npm install,
         yarn/pnpm/bun add, cargo add, go get, gem install, dotnet add
         package, composer require, mvn dependency:get
      2. Dependency file writes (Claude Code only — pre_write hook):
         requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, package.json, Cargo.toml,
         go.mod, Gemfile, pom.xml, build.gradle, *.csproj, composer.json
  - Manifest-driven installs handled: bare `npm install`, `pip install -r
    requirements.txt`, `composer install` read the dependency file from cwd
    when the command itself names no packages.
  - Version precision: tracks `version_is_exact` per package. Range specs
    (^, ~, >=, *, Cargo's implicit ^) are NOT treated as exact pins —
    OSV queries for non-exact versions resolve latest from the registry
    first; update advice only fires for exact pins.
  - Vulnerability check: POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query per package,
    3-second timeout, fail-open, concurrent via futures::join_all.
    Ecosystems: PyPI, npm, crates.io, Maven, Go, RubyGems, NuGet,
    Packagist.
  - Latest version check (6 registries): PyPI, npm, crates.io, RubyGems,
    NuGet, Go proxy. Maven/Packagist skipped for v1.
  - Edit/MultiEdit file preview: for Claude's pre_write hook, the full
    post-edit file content is reconstructed (apply_string_edit on disk
    content) before parsing, so all dependencies are visible — not just
    the edited snippet.
  - Agent-specific behaviour:
      Claude Code: block + inform (permissionDecisionReason carries both)
      Codex CLI:   block only (empty stdout required for allow — no inform)
      Cursor IDE:  block (permission:"deny") + inform (agent_message on allow)
  - Files: dep_protection.rs (extraction, OSV, registry APIs),
    predefined_backend_settings.rs (DependencyProtectionSettings)
  - Frontend: two tiles per agent card ("Vulnerability Guard",
    "Update Advisor") in backends.js, styled in pages-backends.css
  - Shared reqwest::Client created in server.rs, passed to all three
    hook routers via state structs.

Shell Compression (token saving)
  - Intercepts shell command output, compresses before agent sees it
  - Claude path: PreToolUse command rewrite through POST /cli_compression
  - Cursor path: preToolUse command rewrite via `updated_input.command`,
    also through POST /cli_compression
  - Codex path: PostToolUse result replacement from /codex_hook/post_tool
    (the command has already run; the hook replaces what the model sees)
  - Files: shell_compression/ (mod.rs, compress.rs, executor.rs, patterns.rs)
  - Enabled per-backend via token_saving.shell_compression setting
  - Advanced search/diff/JSON compressor flags apply to both paths

Context-Aware File Read Caching (token saving)
  - Session file cache with stable refs (F1, F2, ...)
  - Modes: full, diff, lines:N-M — auto-picks best via ctx_smart_read
  - Files: ctx_read/ (cache.rs, ctx_read.rs, ctx_smart_read.rs, protocol.rs)
  - Enabled per-backend via token_saving.ctx_read setting

Logging / Observability
  - All hook events logged to SQLite: prompts, tool calls, DLP detections, usage
  - Correlation: prompt rows keyed by turn/session, tool rows by tool_use_id
  - database.rs handles all persistence

Garden (project-level file/module view)
  - "Each project is a garden": groves = modules (first path segment),
    clearings = sub-folders within a grove, hero trees = hottest files
    (full conical trees), bushes = lightly-touched files (undergrowth).
  - Visual mapping:
      Tree height   = file size (est_tokens, sqrt-scaled)
      Trunk width   = line count
      Canopy tiers  = stacked triangles; more tiers = more touches
      Canopy color  = top backend (green=Claude, blue=Codex, purple=Cursor)
      Dead tree     = bare branches + ∅ symbol (file deleted from disk)
      Depth         = hero trees foreground (bigger, lower), bushes
                      background (smaller, higher, fainter)
      Sun           = cache hit ratio (brighter = more cache reads)
      Gold coins    = full-price input tokens (1 coin ≈ 100K)
      Copper coins  = cached input tokens (1 coin ≈ 1M)
  - Layout: groves get weight-proportional widths. Within each grove,
    files are grouped into clearings by second path segment. Each clearing
    shows up to 3 hero trees + up to 6 undergrowth bushes, with "+N more"
    for the rest.
  - Backend: stats.rs `get_garden_stats` (project picker) and
    `get_garden_detail` (per-project file breakdown, structs GardenFile /
    GardenDetail).
  - File paths come from three sources inside `get_garden_detail`:
      1. requests.extra_metadata.file_path      — Claude Code hooks
      2. tool_calls.tool_input.{file_path,path,notebook_path} — Cursor
      3. Bash tool_input.command parsing        — Codex (Bash-only)
  - Source 3 uses `extract_paths_from_bash` (tokenize → drop flags/
    operators/metachar tokens → keep tokens that are path-ish AND resolve
    to real files under cwd). This is why Codex projects show any trees
    at all — the paths are buried in `sed`/`nl`/`cat`/`wc` invocations.
  - Frontend: src/garden.js (self-contained SVG renderer + project picker).
    No session-based view remains; the Garden tab is only this file view.

Agent Behaviour (session-level observability)
  - Behaviour Monitor page is now trend-first and day-wise, not a
    baseline/comparison view.
  - Top layer shows four compact metric cards with daily mini-graphs:
      Read-first discipline
      Exploration balance
      Bash reliance
      Tool tempo
    These cards show the selected-range aggregate plus daily sparkline
    shape; there is no "vs earlier" logic anymore.
  - Supporting cards stay high-level:
      Current Operating Mix: explore/modify/bash/other share bars
      Current Profile: investigation style, shell reliance, tempo, etc.
      Coverage: active days, avg turns/session, files touched/session,
      guardrail activity
  - Session cards remain expandable for drilldown, but the collapsed view
    is intentionally summary-only: files touched, read-first %,
    explore/modify ratio, bash share, tools/turn, plus short flags like
    read-first, bash-heavy, deep-scan, blocked.
  - Expanded turn details still show tool tags, file chips, bash command
    previews, and blocked-turn markers when users need to investigate.
  - Backend: stats.rs `get_agent_behaviour` (queries requests table,
    groups by session_id in extra_metadata, correlates prompt and tool rows)
  - Frontend: src/behaviour.js + src/pages-behaviour.css. Topbar nav item.

Symbol Extraction (tree-sitter)
  - Extracts imports and definitions from source files using tree-sitter
    AST parsing. Runs at PostToolUse time when the agent reads/writes/edits
    a file — reads the file from disk and stores symbols in SQLite.
  - Supports 10 languages: JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go,
    Java, C, C++, Ruby, C#. Language detected from file extension.
  - Symbols extracted:
      Imports   : import/from/use/require/#include/using statements
      Definitions: functions, methods, classes, structs, enums, traits,
                   interfaces, modules, type aliases
  - Each symbol: { kind, name, source (import path), line }
  - Files: symbols.rs (extractor + queries), database.rs (file_symbols
    table), stats.rs (get_file_symbols, get_import_graph commands)
  - Import graph: `get_import_graph(cwd)` returns edges between project
    files, with best-effort resolution of import paths to known files.
  - Frontend integration:
      * Clicking a tree/bush in the Garden opens a symbol panel (HTML
        overlay, right side) showing imports grouped by source and
        definitions grouped by kind (functions, classes, etc.)
      * Dashed curved lines connect trees that import from each other
        (rendered as SVG paths behind the tree layer)
  - Hook wiring:
      Claude Code: extract_symbols_for_tool() in claude_hooks.rs
      Codex CLI:   extract_symbols_for_tool() in codex_hooks.rs (with
                   Bash command path extraction via paths_from_bash_for_symbols)
      Cursor IDE:  inline extraction in before_tab_file_read_handler
  - Symbols are best-effort, fire-and-forget. Parse failures or missing
    files are silently ignored. 500KB file size cap prevents slow parses.

Cursor              Claude Code         Codex CLI
                    ------              -----------         ---------
Prompt submit       beforeSubmitPrompt  UserPromptSubmit    UserPromptSubmit
Pre tool use        preToolUse +        PreToolUse          PreToolUse (Bash only)
                    beforeShell/Read/   (Bash/Read/Write/
                    Tab/MCP
                                        Edit/MCP/Notebook)
Post tool use       afterAgent*         PostToolUse         PostToolUse
Stop/End            —                   Stop + SessionEnd   Stop
Session start       —                   SessionStart        SessionStart

Codex quirks:
  - PreToolUse allowed path = empty stdout (not JSON). Deny = JSON with
    permissionDecision:"deny". See codex_hooks.rs pre_tool_deny_response.
  - PostToolUse may return feedback JSON (`decision:"block"`, `reason`,
    `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, `continue:false`) to replace
    the completed tool result. This is how Codex shell compression works.
  - Stop and SessionStart are fire-and-forget for our current handlers.
  - Hook scripts use silent:true in hooks.json to suppress TUI banners.
  - ctx_read token saving is not used for Codex.

head: SwiftAgent

head: SwiftAgent
text: > **Note**: デフォルトはApple FoundationModelsを使用。`--traits OpenFoundationModels` で OpenFoundationModels に切り替え可能。

head: SwiftAgent > コア概念
text:
| 概念 | 説明 |
|------|------|
| **Step** | `Input -> Output` の非同期変換単位。`run(_:)` を直接実装するか、`body` を定義して宣言的に合成 |
| **Session** | TaskLocalベースのセッション伝播（`@Session`, `.session()`） |
| **Memory/Relay** | Step間の状態共有（`@Memory` で保持、`$` で `Relay` を取得） |
| **Context** | 汎用TaskLocal伝播（`@Contextable`, `@Context`, `.context()`） |
| **Generate** | LLMによる構造化出力生成 |

head: SwiftAgent > Step 一覧
text:
| 種別 | Steps |
|------|-------|
| プリミティブ | `Transform`, `Generate`, `GenerateText`, `EmptyStep`, `Join`, `Gate` |
| 合成 | `Chain2-8`, `Pipeline`, `Parallel`, `Race`, `Loop`, `Map`, `Reduce` |
| 修飾 | `Monitor`, `TracingStep`, `AnyStep` |

head: SwiftAgent > Memory / Relay
text: Step間で状態を共有するためのプロパティラッパー。

head: SwiftAgent > Memory / Relay

| `Relay<Value>` | getter/setter クロージャによる間接アクセス |

head: SwiftAgent > Pipeline / Gate

|---|------|
| `Pipeline` | `@StepBuilder` でStepを順番に実行するコンテナ |
| `Gate` | 入力を変換またはブロックするStep |
| `GateResult` | `.pass(value)` で続行、`.block(reason:)` で中断 |

head: SwiftAgent > Conversation

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 設計原則
text: - `ParticipantDescriptor`: エージェント、ロボット、家電、群などが交換する自己記述。

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 設計原則
text: - `Affordance`: participant が状況内で実行可能に見える capability contract。

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 設計原則
text: - `RoutePlan`: delivery、evidence、policy decision を含む実行前 routing 判断。

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 設計原則
text: - `SymbioTransport`: runtime が必要とする最小境界。networking framework の型を core に漏らさない。

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 設計原則
text: - `ParticipantView`: affordance、claim、evidence、availability、policy 制約を含む局所 view。

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 設計原則
text: - `Community`: raw connectivity ではなく、関係性・信頼・記憶を含む哲学上の社会的基盤。

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 内部データフロー
text:
**spawn() フロー:**
```
factory() → actorReady() → ActorRegistry registration
    → local refs retained → ParticipantView registered → .joined event
```

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 内部データフロー
text:
**terminate() フロー:**
```
Terminatable.terminate() → resignID()
    → local storage removal → .left event
```

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 内部データフロー
text:
**send() ローカルフロー:**
```
SymbioRuntime.send()
    → local agent lookup
    → Communicable.receive()
```

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 内部データフロー
text:
**send() リモートフロー:**
```
SymbioRuntime.send()
    → SymbioInvocationEnvelope
    → SymbioTransport.invoke()
    → remote SymbioActorSystem.handleIncomingInvocation()
```

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 内部データフロー
text:
**peer discovery フロー:**
```
PeerConnectivity event
    → PeerConnectivitySymbioTransport
    → SymbioTransportEvent
    → SymbioRuntime peer view / routing update
```

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > PeerConnectivity Adapter
text: `SwiftAgentSymbioPeerConnectivity` は `PeerConnectivitySession` を `SymbioTransport` として使うための adapter を提供する。

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > PeerConnectivity Adapter
text:
| コンポーネント | 責務 |
|---------------|------|
| `PeerConnectivitySymbioTransport` | PeerConnectivity events / streams を Symbio transport semantics に変換 |
| invocation stream | `SymbioInvocationEnvelope` と `SymbioInvocationReply` を交換 |
| descriptor stream | `ParticipantDescriptor` を交換し routing view を更新 |

head: SwiftAgent > モジュール > SwiftAgentSymbio > 主要コンポーネント
text:
| コンポーネント | 責務 |
|---------------|------|
| `SymbioRuntime` | participant view 管理、spawn/terminate、send、route plan、変更通知 |
| `SymbioActorSystem` | DistributedActorSystem 実装、ActorRegistry 統合、local invocation |
| `SymbioTransport` | remote invocation と peer event の境界 |
| `ParticipantDescriptor` | participant の identity、representation、capability contract、claim |
| `ParticipantView` | local subjective view と availability / evidence |
| `Affordance` | capability contract と delivery option |
| `RoutePlan` | route step、policy decision、evidence input |
| `SymbioRuntimeChange` | joined、left、updated、becameAvailable、becameUnavailable |
| `Communicable` | 通信可能なエージェント |
| `Replicable` | runtime 経由で自己複製できるエージェント |
| `ReplicateTool` | LLM が subagent 生成を要求するための tool |

head: NeMo Helix
text: NeMo Helix is NVIDIA's toolkit for making the agents you ship safer, more accurate, and cheaper to run.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo
text: If a user asks you to set up, try, build, evaluate, harden, or optimize an agent inside this repo, you MUST use the skills defined in `packages/nemo_helix_ext/src/nemo_helix_ext/skills/`. Read the relevant skill file directly and follow it step by step.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO
text: - Read `packages/nemo_helix_ext/src/nemo_helix_ext/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` as a file and follow the instructions in order.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO
text: - Stay on the path the skill defines. If the skill calls a `nemo` CLI command, run that exact command. If it points at a `references/` file, read it.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO
text: - If a step changes system state (installs something, starts a service, deploys an agent), run the verification step the skill specifies before moving on. Do not claim a step succeeded without verifying.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO
text: - If you are unsure which skill applies, read `packages/nemo_helix_ext/src/nemo_helix_ext/skills/nemo-skill-selection/SKILL.md` and let it route you.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO NOT
text: - DO NOT invoke any plugin-based skill, `/skill-name` slash command, or globally-installed assistant for these requests. The repo skills are authoritative. A globally-installed skill (brainstorming, planning, code-review, etc.) will give the wrong answer because it does not know NeMo.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO NOT
text: - DO NOT brainstorm a solution from scratch when a NeMo skill claims the task. The skill already has the answer.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO NOT
text: - DO NOT write Python, Pydantic AI, LangChain, or other agent framework code from scratch when a shipped skill covers the request. Skills will tell you the supported way to connect the agent to NeMo Helix. For a new agent build, `nemo-build-agent` uses LangChain Deep Agents through Fabric. Work on a NAT workflow only when the user explicitly asks to maintain or migrate an existing one.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO NOT
text: - DO NOT improvise CLI flags. Only use flags documented in the skill or shown in `nemo <subcommand> --help`.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > DO NOT
text: - DO NOT report a task complete if you cannot verify it. If a verification step fails or times out, surface what you saw and ask the user to confirm before continuing.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Available skills
text: User-facing skills in `packages/nemo_helix_ext/src/nemo_helix_ext/skills/`:

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Available skills
text: - `nemo-skill-selection`: entry point. Use when the user's intent is broad or unclear.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Available skills
text: - `setup`: verifies that NeMo Helix is installed and running. If install is missing, tells the user how to run the CLI install (`make bootstrap` + `nemo setup`). **Install itself is CLI-only.** Do not attempt to install NeMo via skill-driven pip; the workspace dependency graph and credential handling are not reliably automatable inside a sandbox.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Available skills
text: - `nemo-build-agent`: builds a tested LangChain Deep Agent from approved requirements, then packages and registers it through Fabric.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Available skills

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Working in a sandboxed environment
text: If you are inside a sandboxed coding-agent environment (macOS sandbox, CI container, restricted shell):

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Working in a sandboxed environment
text: - Each skill calls out the sandbox capabilities it needs. Read those first.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Working in a sandboxed environment
text: - If a step requires capabilities you do not have, stop and tell the user what is missing. Do not improvise around the sandbox by skipping verification.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Working in a sandboxed environment
text: - The macOS sandbox denies listening sockets, so `nemo services run` and `nemo setup --start-services` cannot host the platform from inside it (the CLI reports `Not permitted to listen on ...`). Do not retry on other ports. Ask the user how the platform should be hosted; see the "Starting the platform from a sandboxed agent" section of `nemo-skill-selection`.

head: NeMo Helix > How to help users in this repo > Working in a sandboxed environment
text: - `uv` is known to crash under the macOS sandbox today (`system_configuration::dynamic_store` panic). Install is CLI-only for this and other reasons.

head: NeMo Helix > What this repo is
text: NeMo Helix brings together NVIDIA NeMo libraries under one CLI, Python SDK, and web UI. Current capabilities:

head: NeMo Helix > What this repo is
text: - **Harden agents**: guardrails (content safety, jailbreak detection, PII redaction), garak (red-teaming), anonymizer (PII handling for training data).

head: NeMo Helix > What this repo is
text: - **Evaluate agents**: evaluator (LLM-as-judge, deterministic, agentic, RAG benchmarks), Harbor-backed eval suites.

head: NeMo Helix > What this repo is
text: - **Tune agents and models**: skill optimization, prompt/hyperparameter tuning, Switchyard model routing, and fine-tuning through Customizer.

head: NeMo Helix > What this repo is
text: - **Build and manage agents**: Fabric connects supported agent harnesses to NeMo Helix for packaging, deployment, testing, observation, and optimization.

head: NeMo Helix > What this repo is
text: New agents should use an explicit Fabric configuration and a supported adapter. Existing NAT workflows can still be maintained when the user asks for that path. Do not create a NAT wrapper as the default way to bring a new agent into NeMo Helix.

head: Agent Development Instructions > Git Workflow
text: - Git branches should follow the pattern `<descriptive-branch-name>/<username>` where the branch name comes first, the `/<username>` suffix is included (not email address, just username), and kebab case is used. Do NOT embed an issue/ticket number in the branch name — branch names are public and issue trackers may be private, so a tracker ID in a branch name leaks private references.

head: Agent Development Instructions > Git Workflow
text: - Always pass `-s` to `git commit` (DCO sign-off). This includes amends, fixups, and any commit variant.

head: Agent Development Instructions > Git Workflow > Squashing Commits
text: **CRITICAL: Never `git reset --soft` to any commit that isn't an ancestor of your current HEAD.**

head: Agent Development Instructions > Git Workflow > Squashing Commits
text: When squashing commits, use one of these safe methods:

head: Agent Development Instructions > Git Workflow > Squashing Commits
text: **Why this matters:** In a shared repo, `origin/main` is almost never an ancestor of your feature branch — main moves forward as others merge work. When you `reset --soft` to a commit that isn't in your branch's history, your staging area still reflects your branch's tree, which lacks any changes made on main since you branched. The resulting commit effectively **reverts** all that work.

head: Agent Development Instructions > Git Workflow > Squashing Commits
text: Both `HEAD~n` and `git rebase -i HEAD~n` are safe because they only operate on commits that are already in your branch's history.

Claude Code, Codex, and every other AI tool must not add AI attribution to

head: AGENTS.md > What this is
text:
This project is built with the **AI Blueprint**, a workflow layer, not an
app skeleton. To start a new project, scaffold the app first in an empty folder
(create-next-app, Vite, etc.), then overlay these files on top. Never run a
framework scaffolder inside a directory that already holds the blueprint files
(`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `blueprint/`); it fails
because the directory isn't empty.

head: AGENTS.md > What this is
text: The workflow is defined by the local skills and context files below.

head: AGENTS.md > Proportional engineering
text:
Build for established requirements, not hypothetical scale, threats, or future
flexibility. Reuse existing code, the standard library, native platform features,
and installed dependencies before adding machinery.

head: AGENTS.md > Proportional engineering
text:
- Unknown scale or extensibility defaults to the smaller reversible design. Do
  not infer enterprise, multi-tenant, hostile-user, or compliance requirements.

head: AGENTS.md > Proportional engineering
text:
- Derive trust and data-integrity boundaries from actual reachability: untrusted
  input, auth/session/ownership, shared persisted data, destructive operations,
  payments, secrets, and sensitive data.

head: AGENTS.md > Proportional engineering
text:
- Ask only when an unknown materially changes behavior, architecture, persisted
  data, interoperability, a real security boundary, or cost. Otherwise choose the
  simplest repository-native implementation.

head: AGENTS.md > Proportional engineering
text:
- Add an abstraction, dependency, service, configuration surface, compatibility
  layer, or security mechanism only for a current requirement.

head: AGENTS.md > Proportional engineering
text:
- Simplicity never removes real trust-boundary validation, data-loss prevention,
  accessibility, explicit security requirements, configured tests, or project rules.

head: AGENTS.md > Proportional engineering
text: - Stack-specific template standards apply only when the project uses that stack.

`blueprint/config.json` is the user-owned, machine-readable workflow policy for
this project. Workflow skills read the relevant settings before acting. A
missing file means built-in defaults. An invalid file falls back to defaults for
read-only status reporting, but mutating workflow commands stop and point to
`/doctor` instead of guessing.

head: AGENTS.md > Project configuration
text:
Configuration can make review or verification stricter and can tune local
branch names and automated-mode limits. It never grants permission to commit,
merge, push, deploy, publish, send, delete data, waive a failing check, or accept
a finding. Those approval and safety boundaries are not configurable.

head: AGENTS.md > Project configuration
text:
`qualityGates.regular` controls automatic audit, independent-review, check, and
try-guide behavior for the normal workflow and Autopilot.
`qualityGates.continuous` controls the same per-feature gates for Continuous
Mode. The existing `tryGuide` keys select `/check guide`, which generates
instructions without performing verification or recording acceptance.
Independent review defaults to `when-sensitive` in both workflows, while
audit, check, and try guide default to `manual`. Sensitive or unusually broad
work therefore selects independent review automatically; ordinary small work
does not. Setting a workflow's independent review to `manual` disables that
automatic selection, while an explicit `/audit independent current` remains
available. The other conditional modes are `when-sensitive` for audit,
`when-behavioral` for check, and `when-user-facing` for try guides. `always`
runs the gate for every work item in that workflow.

head: AGENTS.md > Project configuration
text:
`review.independentExecution` controls how a selected independent-review gate
runs. Its default, `automatic`, uses a fresh isolated reviewer child when the
active adapter can prove isolation, exact reviewer identity and model, and
completion. Otherwise it preserves the request and falls back to the manual
handoff. This setting changes execution only; the quality-gate policy still
decides whether review is selected.
The automatic path spawns a generic child through the current runtime and gives
it the installed project-local Audit skill and review contract. It never requires
or discovers global agent roles, skills, prompts, or TraversyFlow components.
New review requests record requested execution and completed receipts record
actual execution. Manual uses `fresh session`; automatic uses `fresh subagent`;
an explicit automatic fallback records actual manual with `fresh session`.

head: AGENTS.md > Project configuration
text:
`git.landing` controls only how `/complete` offers to land finished regular
work. Its default, `local-merge`, keeps the local squash-merge flow. Set it to
`pull-request` when completed branches should be pushed and opened as pull
requests for provider review and squash merge. Configuration never supplies the
required push, pull-request, or merge approvals. Continuous Mode remains
local-only and ignores this setting.

head: AGENTS.md > Project configuration
text:
New projects default to one review packet after all small implementation steps
(`workflow.stepReview: "feature"`) with step checkpoint commits disabled. This
keeps the normal loop reviewable without repeating the full session context after
every step. Set `stepReview` to `every` when teaching, pairing closely, or working
on a high-risk change. That restores the per-step approval pauses. To fully
restore the previous workflow, including optional checkpoint prompts after an
approved step, also set `checkpointCommits` to `enabled`. Onboarding presents
these pairs as Efficient and Guided choices, but stores only the two low-level
settings. They can be changed at any time. Both styles end with an optional
read-only code walkthrough. Review cadence controls approval pauses, not whether
the user can ask for an explanation of the finished implementation.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text:
Build one feature, fix, or rollback at a time, behind review gates. Each step's instructions
are plain markdown skills any capable agent can read and follow. The workflow is
exposed through tool-specific adapters:

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: - Codex: `.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: - Claude Code: `.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: - GitHub Copilot: `AGENTS.md` plus `.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: - Google Antigravity: `AGENTS.md` plus `.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`

  `.claude/skills/` tree already installed for the selected tools

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text:
Unused adapters can be removed. Codex and GitHub Copilot share `.agents/`, and
Google Antigravity uses that tree too. OpenCode can reuse `.agents/` or
`.claude/`. Projects without Claude Code can delete `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/`.
Claude Code-only projects can delete `.agents/`, but should keep `AGENTS.md`
because `CLAUDE.md` imports it. Do not create `.opencode/skills/` or an
Antigravity-specific skill tree. Both tools use the supported shared trees.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text:
When changing shared workflow behavior, update the matching skill in both
adapter folders so every supported tool stays aligned.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Parallel work
text:
Blueprint supports parallel work through isolated Git checkouts, without a
separate team mode. Give each developer or agent its own clone or Git worktree
and one dedicated branch before starting `/feature` or `/fix`. The branch must
use the configured prefix and the work item's lowercase kebab-case title. Each
checkout keeps its own
`blueprint/context/current-feature.md`, findings, and review state. Never run two
active work items in the same working directory or replace another worker's
active spec.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Parallel work
text:
Parallel branches may both update `blueprint/build-plan.md`; resolve any normal
Git conflict when the later branch lands. Use `git.landing: "pull-request"` when
the default branch is protected or several isolated checkouts are active. This
model intentionally does not add per-item state folders or automatic agent
coordination.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Parallel work
text:
Learn the feature loop: `/feature` -> `/implement` -> `/check` -> `/audit current` ->
`/complete`. Approve the Feature spec before Implement. Check proves behavior;
Audit reviews code and records findings. Showing both in this path does not
change configured gates or make Audit mandatory. `/check guide` only generates
manual instructions and never performs verification or records acceptance.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Build
text: - `feature` - turn a build-plan item into a spec, or propose a reviewed plan addition for a genuinely new feature

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Build
text: - `implement` - build the current spec one small, reviewed step at a time

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Build
text:
- `check` - prove the current spec against the running app, or use `check guide`
  for a read-only manual review guide: where to go, what to click, what to expect

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Build
text: - `complete` - run the final safety pass, log features, fixes, or rollbacks under `blueprint/history/`, then request approval for the configured local merge or pull-request landing

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Understand and review
text: - `explore` - investigate an idea against the actual code without writing files or requiring plans

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Understand and review
text: - `brief` - read-only briefing on an upcoming build-plan feature (scope, dependencies, size) before you spec it

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Understand and review
text: - `status` - read-only progress summary, workflow drift warning, and suggested next action

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Understand and review
text: - `debug` - reproduce and isolate a failure without editing code, then hand the evidence to `fix` or `implement`

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Understand and review
text: - `audit` - branch-aware or full-project review across all concerns or a focused quality, security, performance, or tests lens; `audit independent current` prepares an immutable checkpoint for a fresh reviewer session or configured isolated reviewer child; records findings in `blueprint/context/findings.md` and independent receipts in `blueprint/context/review.md`, where blocking findings or stale review state stop `complete`

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Understand and review
text: - `doctor` - Blueprint health check for setup, adapters, plans, overview freshness, dashboard state, and workflow drift; it may offer to reset only malformed generated dashboard state after approval

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Plan and set up
text: - `onboard` - tune commands, standards, visibility, ignore rules, and tool adapters after overlaying the Blueprint onto a freshly scaffolded or early project

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Plan and set up
text: - `adopt` - bootstrap the Blueprint into an existing brownfield app with shipped features

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Plan and set up
text: - `discovery` - optional deep, multi-turn planning conversation that drafts the two user-owned plans only after review and approval; direct plan writing remains fully supported

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Plan and set up

- `overview` - distill the two planning docs into
  `blueprint/context/project-overview.md`, then offer a reviewed initial planning
  baseline commit before Feature 1

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Plan and set up
text: - `prototype` - optional, pre-build static mockups to lock the look

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Plan and set up
text: - `tests` - set up unit testing by default, or a repeatable browser harness with `tests browser`

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Plan and set up
text: - `ci` - explicitly set up one project-specific Verify command and matching automatic GitHub checks, with an optional local pre-push hook

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Recover and release
text: - `fix` - document an ad-hoc bug or change into `blueprint/context/current-feature.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Recover and release
text: - `rollback` - plan a safe reversal of a completed feature from its archive and exact git commit, with later-dependency review before code changes

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Recover and release
text: - `release` - optional Render or Vercel deployment readiness, local config, env review, and smoke-test planning

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Recover and release
text:
In Codex, invoke these as skills (`$onboard`, `$discovery`, `$overview`, `$feature`,
`$implement`, and so on) or ask naturally, such as "run the overview." In Claude
Code and Google Antigravity, use slash commands such as `/onboard` or `/feature`.
These are AI chat commands, not terminal commands. In OpenCode or other tools
without a dedicated invocation syntax, ask the agent to run the matching skill
or follow its `SKILL.md` manually. The
conventions in `blueprint/context/` apply however a step is invoked. `/discovery`
is never required: users may write detailed plans directly or develop them
through any conversation before running `/overview`.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Automation
text:
Optional explicit-only skill: `autopilot` combines `feature` or `fix` with
`implement` in one bounded pass when directly invoked, including the configured
regular quality gates. The normal workflow stops for human approval of the spec
before implementation; Autopilot continues through that review point. It may
create checkpoint commits on the feature or fix branch after passing steps and
repair confirmed P0/P1 findings when its audit gate runs. It stops before
`/complete`, merge, push, deploy, or destructive actions.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Automation
text:
Optional explicit-only skill: `continuous` can resume or select the next planned
feature and repeat the complete local feature lifecycle through the configured
limit or end of the build plan. It creates one branch and one local main commit
per feature, applies the Continuous quality gates, archives and merges serially,
and stops on decisions or failed safety gates. It never pushes, deploys,
publishes, sends, or performs destructive actions.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Automation
text:
Deployment is also explicit. `/release` can prepare local Render or Vercel config
and run readiness checks, but it must stop before deploy, remote service changes,
push, or publish unless the user gives a separate yes in the current chat.

head: AGENTS.md > Dashboard activity
text:
The dashboard can show the active or most recent substantial Blueprint command
from `blueprint/.state/run.json`. This file is generated local state, ignored by
Git, and never part of a feature commit.

head: AGENTS.md > Dashboard activity
text:
Commands with meaningful progress or a durable handoff should write it when the
state directory exists: `onboard`, `adopt`, `discovery`, `overview`, `feature`,
`fix`, `rollback`, `implement`, `debug`, `check`, `audit`, `tests`,
`ci`, `prototype`, `autopilot`, `continuous`, `complete`, and
`release`. Short orientation commands such as `explore`, `brief`, `status`, and `doctor`
do not write activity state. The `check guide` mode also never writes activity
state; select the Check mode before any activity call. Doctor's optional
approved reset removes malformed activity instead of recording another run.

head: AGENTS.md > Dashboard activity
text:
Writing the initial activity record is the first action of a tracked command,
before project inspection, preflight, or other tool calls. This one generated
state write does not authorize product changes or bypass any safety check.

head: AGENTS.md > Dashboard activity
text:
Never create or edit `run.json` directly. From the project root, use the first
helper that exists:

head: AGENTS.md > Dashboard activity
text:
Start with `start --command <skill> --summary <truthful-summary> --boundary
<boundary>`. Use `update` at meaningful milestones or for a blocker, with
`--status blocked` and `--resume <exact-command>` when recovery is needed. End
with `finish --status ready|completed --summary <truthful-summary>`. The helper
validates every field before atomically replacing the generated file. If it is
missing or fails, report the activity warning and continue the workflow without
writing a manual fallback.

head: AGENTS.md > Dashboard activity
text: The helper writes this schema:

head: AGENTS.md > Dashboard activity
text:
`status` must be `running`, `blocked`, `ready`, or `completed`. Use `ready` when
the command reached its intended review handoff, such as Autopilot waiting for
review before `/complete`. Use `blocked` with the exact recovery command when
work can resume. `boundary` must be `read-only`, `reviewed`, or `local-only`.
The progress, feature, detail, boundary, and resume fields are optional. Never
put secrets, raw logs, prompts, or user content in this file. Activity tracking
must not change a command's approval boundaries or turn a reporting failure into
a workflow failure.

head: AGENTS.md > Automatic verification
text:
Automatic GitHub checks are a separate explicit setup. `/onboard` and `/adopt`
only report existing checks and point to `/ci` or `$ci` when none exist. Running
`/ci` inspects the real project and defines one `Verify` command from checks that
already exist. Use this order when available: typecheck, tests, then build. Never
invent a test runner or another check just to fill the command.

head: AGENTS.md > Automatic verification
text:
For JavaScript and TypeScript projects, prefer a package script such as `verify`
and use the detected package manager. For other stacks, use the native task
runner or exact combined command. Record the exact command under Commands below.

head: AGENTS.md > Automatic verification
text:
The optional `.github/workflows/verify.yml` must run that same command for pull
requests and pushes to the default branch. Preserve existing workflows, use the
project's real runtime and install command, and grant only `contents: read` by
default. This setup does not add coverage, browser tests, security scans, or
version matrices; those remain later project choices. A local pre-push hook that
runs the same `Verify` command is offered as an opt-in at the end of `/ci`, and
`git push --no-verify` still bypasses it, so the remote ruleset stays the lock.

head: AGENTS.md > Automatic verification
text:
GitHub branch protection or a ruleset can require the check after the repository
is pushed, but that is a separate remote setting. Missing automatic GitHub
checks do not make the Blueprint unusable.

Testing is opt-in. If this project does not already have a unit test runner, run
`/tests` or `$tests` to add one and update this section with the real test

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text:
Browser testing is also opt-in. Run `/tests browser` or `$tests browser` to add
or normalize a browser harness and document its exact command as `Browser
tests`. Check and Continuous Mode can then reuse it without installing tooling
mid-feature.
- If you encounter something surprising or confusing in this project, add it into this file (AGENTS.md).
- If a test fails, investigate and fix the issue. Don't just ignore it.
- After implementing a feature use fmt/clippy/test to ensure quality
- This repo is hosted on GitHub. You can use `gh` to access it. (ask if not logged in)
- This repo uses GitHub CI (defined in `.github/workflows`) for continuous integration and release Rust crates.

- Surprising finding (2026-02-25): IVF search path applies extended-code refinement (`ex_codes_packed`, `f_add_ex`, `f_rescale_ex`) after FastScan lower-bound filtering, but current MSTG `search_posting_list_fastscan` only uses FastScan estimated distances and does not consume posting-list extended-code fields during search. `src/mstg/posting_list.rs` stores these fields, yet `src/mstg/search.rs` does not currently use them.

- Update (2026-02-25): MSTG now includes stage-2 extended-code refinement in `src/mstg/search.rs` using `ex_codes_packed`/`f_add_ex`/`f_rescale_ex` (SIMD packed-dot when ex_bits is supported, scalar unpack fallback otherwise), with bounded rerank size (`max(64, 8*top_k)` per posting list) to control latency.

- Surprising finding (2026-02-25): After aligning MSTG with IVF-style online `distk` pruning (global top-k heap across posting lists), MSTG-mem latency improved versus the first two-stage rerank patch, but MSTG-disk latency regressed significantly (roughly 4-5x slower than MSTG-mem), likely because mmap posting-list decode + sequential heap updates limit parallelism and cache locality.

- Update (2026-02-26): Introducing a two-stage scheduler (serial bootstrap lists to warm distk, then parallel per-posting-list local heaps with merge) recovered most performance while keeping IVF-aligned lower-bound+ex-refine semantics. On cohere_100k_768d / epsilon=0.02, MSTG-mem balanced improved from ~9073us to ~3164us and MSTG-disk balanced from ~40529us to ~12787us at similar recall (~97.8%).

- Update (2026-02-26): Added MSTG `SearchDiagnostics` with `search_with_diagnostics()` to expose selected centroids, scanned vectors, lower-bound skips, refined vectors, and timing breakdown (`posting_access_time_us`, `posting_search_time_us`, approximate decode/build overhead).

- Surprising finding (2026-02-26): `src/mstg/index.rs` test `test_mstg_search` used a strict top-1 distance assertion (`results[0].distance < 0.1`) that can fail nondeterministically in CI despite correct retrieval behavior. Prefer asserting query id recall in top-k for approximate MSTG tests.
- ARD specification is in spec/ard.md
- Keep a high level log of Features and Capabilities in README.md under ##features.

- Project documentation is a lightweight orientation record, not the full source of truth.
  It should help humans quickly understand the big idea and help future agents know which
  scripts, workflows, specs, and plans to inspect for detailed question-answering. Prefer
  concise summaries with explicit artifact pointers over duplicating shell/script logic.
- Do NOT test things that the `ty` typechecker automatically enforces.
- Any HF_TOKEN usage must only remain temporarily in memory during a request scope, and must never be stored or emitted in a plain format.

- Avoid mocking or `monkeypatch` for testing purposes, preferring to use typechecks, simple logic-focussed unit tests and stubs/simulators. Small integration or e2e tests are preferred over lots of unit tests for tightly coupled scenarios.
- Avoid testing properties and other data transfer scenarios unless transformations or other behaviour is involved.
- Prefer a functional style of programming where possible.
- Feature additions should consider the CLI surface as well as adherence to the ARD specification. Both CLI and HTTP should wrap the same, clean, well factored core logic.

For how the system fits together and where to extend it, see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).

head: AGENT.md > What this is
text:
`diagrid-dev-dashboard` is a **single Go binary** that embeds a React + Vite SPA (via `go:embed`) and
acts as a passive, read-only observer for local Dapr development. There is **no Node.js at
runtime** — the frontend is compiled to `web/dist` and baked into the binary at build time.

head: AGENT.md > What this is
text: - **Module:** `github.com/diagridio/dev-dashboard`

head: AGENT.md > What this is
text: - **Toolchain:** Go ≥ 1.26 (`go.mod` pins 1.26.7), Node.js 20 + `npm` (build/test only).

head: AGENT.md > What this is
text: - **Entry point:** `main.go` → `cmd/` (cobra root, default subcommand is `serve`).

head: AGENT.md > Repository layout
text:
**Architectural rule:** all logic lives in `pkg/*` domain packages; nothing in `pkg/*` may
depend on `cmd/`. The server mounts as a `chi` sub-router and the SPA is an `fs.FS`, so the
whole thing can later be folded into a `diagrid dashboard` subcommand. Preserve this.

head: AGENT.md > Build
text:
The SPA must be built **before** the Go binary (the binary embeds `web/dist`). `make build`
does both in order.

head: AGENT.md > Build
text: Manual equivalent (no `make`):

head: AGENT.md > Build
text:
Sub-path mount: `DASH_BASE_PATH=/dashboard/ make build` then run with `--base-path /dashboard`
(the env var, used at Vite build time, must equal the flag and both must end with `/`).

head: AGENT.md > Test
text:
Go tests are **build-tag-gated** — a plain `go test ./...` reports "no test files". You MUST
pass `-tags`.

head: AGENT.md > Test
text: Single package / direct invocation:

head: AGENT.md > Test
text: - **unit** (`//go:build unit`) and **web** (Vitest) — self-contained, the everyday gate.

head: AGENT.md > Test
text:
- **integration** (`//go:build integration`) — exercises state-store/workflow read paths and the
  assembled HTTP server. The store contract and workflow parity tests run against temp SQLite
  plus real Redis / PostgreSQL / MongoDB containers (testcontainers-go); the container backends
  skip when no container runtime is available, so a skip there is not a pass. Runs in CI but
  not in `make test`.

head: AGENT.md > Test
text: - **e2e** (`//go:build e2e`) — drives a real `daprd`; local-only, skips when Dapr isn't installed.

head: AGENT.md > Test
text:
- **Golden files** (`testdata/golden/*`): regenerate after an intentional shape change with
  `-update`, e.g. `go test -tags integration ./pkg/workflow -run Golden -update`.
```sh
make tidy                # go mod tidy
```

head: AGENT.md > Release
text: > Maintainers only. Releasing is a tagged-commit + GitHub Actions (GoReleaser) flow.

head: AGENT.md > Release
text:
Because `go install` can't run `npm`, the tagged commit must embed a prebuilt `web/dist`.
`scripts/release.sh` builds the SPA, makes a **detached** commit force-adding `web/dist` past
`.gitignore`, tags it, and returns you to your branch — so `main` stays free of built assets.

head: AGENT.md > Release
text: Validate locally before tagging (needs GoReleaser v2):

head: AGENT.md > Release
text:
Release matrix is **5 archives**: macOS + Linux (amd64 + arm64) and Windows (amd64). No native
Windows/arm64 — it runs the amd64 build via emulation. Version string is injected from the tag
via ldflags (`diagrid-dev-dashboard --version`).

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build & Run
text: **You must run `xcodegen` after creating or deleting any Swift file** — the project.yml sources the entire `Magnetism/` directory, but the .xcodeproj needs regeneration to pick up changes.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: Menu-bar-only macOS window manager (LSUIElement=true, no dock icon). Swift 6 strict concurrency, macOS 14+, single SPM dependency: [KeyboardShortcuts](https://github.com/sindresorhus/KeyboardShortcuts).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Modules
text: - **Core/** — `WindowManager` orchestrates everything. `AccessibilityElement` wraps AXUIElement. `WindowAction` enum is the single source of truth for all 18 actions (display names, categories, shortcut bindings via extension in ShortcutNames.swift).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Modules
text: - **Calculations/** — One struct per layout action, all conforming to `WindowCalculation` protocol. Factory in `WindowCalculation.swift` maps `WindowAction` → calculation.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Modules
text: - **Shortcuts/** — `ShortcutNames.swift` defines `KeyboardShortcuts.Name` constants with Magnet-compatible defaults. `ShortcutManager` registers `onKeyUp` handlers.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Modules
text: - **Snapping/** — `SnapManager` uses a passive CGEvent tap (`.listenOnly`). `SnapZoneDetector` checks mouse position against screen edges/corners. `SnapOverlayWindow` shows an animated preview.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Modules
text: - **Preferences/** — `PreferencesWindowController` hosts SwiftUI views in an AppKit NSWindow (SwiftUI Settings scene is unreliable in LSUIElement apps).

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical Technical Patterns > Coordinate Flipping
text: NSScreen uses bottom-left origin; AX API uses top-left origin. **All** window calculations must use `NSScreen.flippedVisibleFrame` (defined in `CGExtensions.swift`), never raw `visibleFrame`. The overlay window converts back with `CGRect.screenFlipped()` for display.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical Technical Patterns > Triple-Set Pattern
text: `AccessibilityElement.frame` setter does `setSize → setPosition → setSize`. macOS enforces per-display size limits during cross-display moves — setting size twice ensures the final frame is exact. This pattern also appears at the end of `animateFrame()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical Technical Patterns > Animation
text: `WindowManager.animateWindow()` is `nonisolated` and dispatches to `DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInteractive)` because the animation loop uses `Thread.sleep()` in 12 steps with ease-out cubic interpolation. Cross-display moves skip animation (would look wrong flying through dead space).

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical Technical Patterns > CGEvent Tap Memory Management
text: `SnapManager` passes `self` to the C callback via `Unmanaged.passUnretained()`. The `eventTap` property **must** be held — if it's deallocated, the tap stops working silently.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical Technical Patterns > Terminal.app Workaround
text: `WindowManager.execute()` temporarily disables `AXEnhancedUserInterface` before moving Terminal windows, then re-enables it in a `defer` block.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical Technical Patterns > Private API: `_AXUIElementGetWindow`
text: Declared via `@_silgen_name` in `AccessibilityElement.swift` to get `CGWindowID` from an AXUIElement. Used for window history tracking. May break in future macOS versions.

head: CLAUDE.md > Swift 6 Concurrency Strategy
text: All singleton managers are `@MainActor final class`. No async/await patterns. The only off-main-thread work is the animation loop in `AccessibilityElement.animateFrame()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Swift 6 Concurrency Strategy
text: The `kAXTrustedCheckOptionPrompt` global variable triggers a Swift 6 concurrency warning — worked around by using the string literal `"AXTrustedCheckOptionPrompt"` directly in `AccessibilityPermission.swift`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a New Window Layout
text: 1. Add a case to `WindowAction` enum (with `displayName` and `category`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a New Window Layout
text: 2. Create `Calculations/[Name]Calculation.swift` conforming to `WindowCalculation`

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a New Window Layout
text: 3. Add the case to `WindowCalculationFactory.calculation(for:)`

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a New Window Layout
text: 4. Add a `KeyboardShortcuts.Name` in `ShortcutNames.swift` with a default binding

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a New Window Layout
text: 5. Add the mapping in the `WindowAction.shortcutName` extension

head: CLAUDE.md > Adding a New Window Layout
text: 6. Run `xcodegen` to pick up the new file

text: - **No App Sandbox** — required for AX API access

text: - **Accessibility permission** — prompted on first launch; re-prompted during development because ad-hoc re-signing invalidates the trust entry

Hard Requirement: call binaries directly in functions.shell, always set workdir, and avoid shell wrappers such as `bash -lc`, `sh -lc`, `zsh -lc`, `cmd /c`, `pwsh.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -Command`, and `powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -Command`.

{"command":["apply_patch","*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: path/to/file\n@@\n- old\n+ new\n*** End Patch\n"],"workdir":"<workdir>","justification":"Brief reason for the change"}

head: Repository Guidelines
text: This project ships a PySide6 desktop app for offline ROS 2 calibration. Keep every contribution tightly scoped and verify changes against recorded `.mcap` rosbags before opening a pull request.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: Core logic lives in `ros2_calib/`: `main.py` wires the GUI, `calibration_widget.py` and `lidar2lidar_o3d_widget.py` host the calibration views, while helpers such as `bag_handler.py`, `calibration.py`, and `ros_utils.py` manage data access and math. GUI assets (icons, screenshots, demo media) reside in `assets/`. Build artifacts (`build/`, `dist/`, `ros2_calib.egg-info/`) are disposable—regenerate them locally instead of committing updates. Configuration and packaging metadata stay in `pyproject.toml` and `MANIFEST.in`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate`: set up an isolated toolchain.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `pip install -e .[dev]`: install the app plus linting/build extras.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `ruff check`: run linting (E, F, W, I) with a 100-character limit.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `ruff format`: auto-format Python sources; add `--check` in CI scripts.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `ros2_calib`: launch the GUI from your shell for quick smoke tests.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `python -m build`: produce wheels/sdists before publishing.

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: Use Python 3.10+ features judiciously while keeping type hints for new APIs. Follow Ruff’s defaults: 4-space indentation, trailing commas where practical, and sorted imports. Modules and functions stay `snake_case`; Qt widgets/classes use `PascalCase`; constants stay upper snake. Break long GUI signal chains into helper functions and document non-obvious math with concise comments.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: Automated tests are currently absent—add `pytest` modules alongside new features under `tests/` with files named `test_<feature>.py`. For GUI-heavy changes, describe manual validation: launch `ros2_calib`, load a representative `.mcap`, and confirm TF tree, calibrations, and exports behave as expected. Capture edge cases such as missing `/tf_static` frames or sparse point clouds.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: Follow the existing short, imperative commit style (`add lidar2lidar calibrator`, `bump version to v0.0.6`). Group related changes and avoid bundled assets or builds. PRs should outline motivation, summarize implementation, list validation commands, and attach before/after screenshots for UI tweaks. Link issues when available and note any dependencies (e.g., new ROS bag schema) so reviewers can reproduce results quickly.

head: ipcheck 项目规范 > 不可混淆的语义
text: - “本机真实 IP”是国内直连服务观察到的公网出口，不是内网地址；“出口 IP”是当前请求路径观察到的代理出口。探测失败或路径不确定时不得断言真实流量走向。

head: ipcheck 项目规范 > 不可混淆的语义
text: - 环境代理、系统代理和 TUN／VPN分别是进程环境、配置和启发式状态。沙箱观测不能替代宿主机状态或实际出口验证。

head: ipcheck 项目规范 > 不可混淆的语义
text: - 系统时区不受 `TZ` 影响；CLI 时区优先取 `TZ`。CLI 与桌面版分别比较，各自限制见诊断手册。

head: ipcheck 项目规范 > 不可混淆的语义
text: - 网络综合结论依现有高／中／低判定，IPv6 仍单独提示；修改字段或风险逻辑前先读手册、核对代码并覆盖判定边界。

head: ipcheck 项目规范 > 不可混淆的语义
text: - 147 域名名单是冻结的历史快照，来源见 [审计证据](../fuxi/raw/2026-06-30-cc-反蒸馏水印审计/域名黑名单-147项.md)，不是实时官方黑名单。客户端水印状态不证明服务端处理。

head: ipcheck 项目规范 > 不可混淆的语义

head: Echokraut > Rules
text:
- ⚠ **Never read a `Vector3D` back out of ManagedBass.** `ManagedBass.Vector3D` is a **class** (that
  is why `ChannelSet3DPosition` accepts `null` for the orientation), so the `ref Vector3D` parameters
  of `Bass.Get3DPosition` / `Bass.ChannelGet3DPosition` hand BASS a pointer to a managed object
  reference and it writes floats over the object header — an instant `AccessViolationException` that
  takes the whole game down (measured 2026-08-03). Writing is fine (the object goes by value); only
  float/int/enum readbacks (`Get3DFactors`, `ChannelGet3DAttributes`, `Bass.Info`) are safe.

head: Echokraut > Changelog Maintenance (mandatory per commit)
text: Every commit must contribute to a changelog file under `Echokraut/Resources/Changelogs/`. The user-facing changelog popup (`NativeChangelogWindow` + `IChangelogService`) reads these embedded files and shows entries between `Configuration.LastSeenChangelogVersion` and the current `Plugin.PluginVersion` to every user after a plugin update — so a commit without a changelog touch silently disappears from the user's "what's new" view.

head: Echokraut > Changelog Maintenance (mandatory per commit) > Per-commit workflow
text: Before staging a commit, run these steps in order:

head: Echokraut > Changelog Maintenance (mandatory per commit) > Per-commit workflow
text:
1. **Compare project version against the latest release tag — on GitHub.**
   - "Latest release tag" means the highest-versioned tag on the GitHub mirror, **excluding any tag that starts with `ELI-`** (those tags belong to the standalone `EchokrautLocalInstaller` project, not the plugin, and must never influence Echokraut versioning).
   - Authoritative lookup command:
     ```bash
     git ls-remote --tags github 2>/dev/null \
       | awk -F/ '{print $NF}' \
       | grep -v '\^{}$' \
       | grep -E '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' \
       | sort -V \
       | tail -1
     ```
     The strict `X.Y.Z.W` regex excludes both `ELI-*` (EchokrautLocalInstaller) and any one-off marker tags (`TEST`, etc.). `\^{}` strips peeled-tag artifacts; `sort -V` does version-aware sort so `0.10.0.0` correctly sorts after `0.9.9.9`.
   - Why GitHub and not local / GitLab tags: GitHub Releases are what users actually install from. Local tags can be created without ever pushing; GitLab tags can be in flight or out of sync. The mirror pipeline pushes GitLab → GitHub, so GitHub is the authoritative "what's been released" record.
   - Project version: `<Version>` element in `Echokraut/Echokraut.csproj`.

head: Echokraut > Changelog Maintenance (mandatory per commit) > Per-commit workflow
text:
2. **If `<Version>` ≤ latest tag**, bump it before committing.
   - Default bump is **patch** (last segment +1). Example: tag `0.19.0.0`, project `0.19.0.0` → bump to `0.19.0.1`.
   - Bump **minor** (`0.19.0.0` → `0.19.1.0`) when the commit ships a user-visible feature significant enough to call out in release notes.
   - Bump **major/minor manually** for breaking changes — never do that automatically.
   - The `<Version>` value drives `Plugin.PluginVersion`, which is what `IChangelogService` compares against. A version that's not strictly greater than the latest released tag means the changelog popup logic can't distinguish "you're on the released version" from "you've got newer commits from the build pipeline".

head: Echokraut > Changelog Maintenance (mandatory per commit) > Per-commit workflow
text:
3. **Update both changelog files** for the post-bump version: `Echokraut/Resources/Changelogs/v{NEW_VERSION}_EN.txt` and `_DE.txt`. Two cases:
   - **First commit on a new version** (file doesn't exist yet): create both files. Use any existing `v{X}_EN/DE.txt` as a template — `MAJOR NEW FEATURES` / `IMPROVEMENTS` / `BUG FIXES`, ASCII section headers, blank lines between entries (the section splitter in `NativeChangelogWindow` relies on those for rendering). **Also add two `<EmbeddedResource Include="Resources\Changelogs\v{NEW_VERSION}_{LANG}.txt" />` lines** to `Echokraut/Echokraut.csproj` (mirror the pattern of the existing entries). Without those, MSBuild won't embed the new files and the runtime resource enumeration silently misses them.
   - **Subsequent commits on the same version**: append a new bullet to the appropriate section (`MAJOR NEW FEATURES` for `[NEW]` items, `IMPROVEMENTS` for refinements, `BUG FIXES` for fixes). Keep the bullet prose short — match the existing tone (concrete + user-visible, not implementation detail).
   - **Multi-section commits**: a single commit can legitimately touch multiple sections (e.g. a bug fix that ships a small UX tweak alongside it). Write a bullet in each affected section.

head: Echokraut > Changelog Maintenance (mandatory per commit) > Per-commit workflow
text: 4. **Both languages must stay in sync.** When you add an entry to `_EN.txt`, add the corresponding German translation to `_DE.txt` in the same position. FR/JA fall back to EN at runtime (no FR/JA changelog files yet).

head: Echokraut > Changelog Maintenance (mandatory per commit) > Per-commit workflow
text: 5. **Internal-only refactors / test churn / CI tweaks** that have zero user-visible effect can skip the changelog with a one-line note in the commit message (`(no changelog: internal refactor)`). Use this sparingly — when in doubt, write the entry. The `INTERNAL / DEVELOPER` section was deliberately removed from `v0.19.0.0` because it noised up the user-facing popup; do not reintroduce it.

head: Echokraut > Changelog Maintenance (mandatory per commit) > Per-commit workflow
text: 6. **Merge commits are exempt.** A `--no-ff` merge from a feature branch into `main` doesn't introduce content beyond what's already in the feature-branch commits (which already updated the changelog when they were made). Don't bump or touch the changelog on the merge.

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text:
**For App Store Submission**:
```bash
# Build with auto-updater disabled for App Store
xcodebuild -scheme ZenDevToolkit \
  -configuration Release \
  -archivePath build/ZenDevToolkit.xcarchive \
  SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS="DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE" \
  archive

# Export for App Store Connect
xcodebuild -exportArchive \
  -archivePath build/ZenDevToolkit.xcarchive \
  -exportPath build/export-appstore \
  -exportOptionsPlist scripts/ExportOptions-AppStore.plist
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text: - For regular development: Use the default `ZenDevToolkit` scheme (auto-updater enabled)

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text: - For App Store testing: Use the `ZenDevToolkit` scheme with `Debug-AppStore` configuration

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text:
1. **Update Version Numbers** (4 places):
   - `ZenDevToolkit/Info.plist`: Update both `CFBundleShortVersionString` (e.g., "1.0.1") and `CFBundleVersion` (e.g., "101")
   - `ZenDevToolkit.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`: Update `MARKETING_VERSION` (this overrides Info.plist's `CFBundleShortVersionString`!)
     - Search for `MARKETING_VERSION = x.x.x;` and update ALL occurrences
   - `ZenDevToolkit.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`: Update `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` (this overrides Info.plist's `CFBundleVersion`! App Store validation rejects uploads whose build number doesn't increase)
     - Search for `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = n;` and update ALL occurrences
   - `README.md`: Update the version badge

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text:
2. **Update Documentation**:
   - `CHANGELOG.md`: Add new version section with release notes
   - Move items from `[Unreleased]` to the new version section
   - Update the comparison links at the bottom

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text:
3. **Commit Changes**:
   ```bash
   git add -A
   git commit -m "feat: release version X.X.X"
   ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text:
4. **Create and Push Tag**:
   ```bash
   git tag -a vX.X.X -m "Release version X.X.X"
   git push origin main
   git push origin vX.X.X
   ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text:
5. **GitHub Actions will automatically**:
   - Build and sign the app
   - Create a GitHub release
   - Upload the built artifacts

head: CLAUDE.md > Release Process > Creating a New Release > Building for Different Platforms
text:
6. **After CI/CD completes, update the release description**:
   - Use `.github/RELEASE_TEMPLATE.md` as a guide
   - Include both installation AND upgrade instructions
   - Add checksums from the built artifacts
   - Link to the full changelog

head: AGENTS.md > Project overview
text:
PUDL ingests raw public energy data (EIA, FERC, EPA, and others) and transforms it into
clean, analysis-ready tables. The pipeline is orchestrated using Dagster assets and jobs.

head: AGENTS.md > About this file
text:
`AGENTS.md` is the canonical instruction file for this repository. `CLAUDE.md` in
the same directory is a symlink that points to `AGENTS.md` — they are always
identical, not independent files to be kept in sync.

head: AGENTS.md > About this file > Working across multiple worktrees
text:
When working in multiple git worktrees simultaneously, any `AGENTS.md` injected
into your context at session start reflects the **primary working directory** only.
If you encounter an `AGENTS.md` at a different path during the same session, do not
assume it is the same file — it may be a different version of this document, or
belong to an entirely different repository.

head: AGENTS.md > About this file > Working across multiple worktrees
text:
- Always use full absolute paths when referencing or comparing `AGENTS.md` files
  across worktrees — this makes the distinction visible immediately.

head: AGENTS.md > About this file > Working across multiple worktrees
text:
- When you need to know which `AGENTS.md` governs a particular worktree, read it
  directly from that worktree's directory rather than relying on the
  context-loaded version.

  - `dagster/config.py` — reusable Dagster run-config fragments and helpers
  - `dagster/io_managers.py` — IO managers for SQLite, Parquet, and FERC SQLite reads
  - `dagster/jobs.py` — named Dagster jobs (`pudl`, `ferc_to_sqlite`, `ferceqr`)

  - `dagster/resources.py` — `ConfigurableResource` definitions and default resource map
  - `dagster/sensors.py` — sensor-based automation (e.g. the FERC EQR sensor)

Raw inputs and pipeline outputs live **outside the repository**, in directories with

  - Apache Parquet files (`$PUDL_OUTPUT/parquet/`) — the primary analytical outputs
  - SQLite databases (`$PUDL_OUTPUT/*.sqlite`) — used for FERC raw data and some outputs
  - DuckDB databases (`$PUDL_OUTPUT/*.duckdb`) — currently only for FERC XBRL data
  - JSON datapackage descriptors (`$PUDL_OUTPUT/*_datapackage.json`) — frictionless

head: AGENTS.md > Development environment > Python environment

create Python environments. Do not run `uv run`, `uv pip install`, `python -m venv`, or
anything similar. Pixi is the only permitted environment manager.

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > rg (ripgrep)
text:
Use instead of `grep` for all codebase searches. Faster, respects `.gitignore`, and

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > pyrefly
text:
Use to find Python type errors before committing. `pyrefly` uses its own error codes
(e.g. `missing-argument`, `unresolved-attribute`) which differ from mypy's
(e.g. `call-arg`, `attr-defined`).

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > pyrefly
text: For suppression syntax, see **Type error suppression** in the Code Style section.

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > pyrefly
text:
**Baseline policy**: PUDL is not yet enforcing full type-checking — pre-existing errors
are recorded in `.pyrefly-baseline.json` and suppressed by `pixi run pyrefly-check`.

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > pyrefly
text:
- Never introduce a *new* pyrefly error. Run `pixi run pyrefly-check` (or `pixi run -e
  dev pyrefly check <file>` for a quick look at one file) before committing.

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > pyrefly
text:
- Never edit or regenerate `.pyrefly-baseline.json` to absorb a new error — that defeats
  its purpose as a ratchet against regressions. The only legitimate reason to regenerate
  it (`pyrefly check --baseline .pyrefly-baseline.json --update-baseline`) is to shrink
  it after fixing pre-existing errors, and only with explicit user approval.

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > pyrefly
text:
- If pyrefly flags pre-existing errors in code you're already editing, fix them
  opportunistically.

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > pyrefly
text:
- The baseline is updated weekly. The process is: fix newly introduced errors that have
  accumulated since the last baseline update, run `pixi run pyrefly-prune-baseline`
  followed by `pixi run pyrefly-update-baseline`, then `pixi run pyrefly-diff-baseline`
  to verify that the only changes are errors that have been fixed.

Accepts Dagster asset selection syntax via `--asset-select`.

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > dbt_helper
text:
**`dbt_helper validate` runs against the Parquet files in `$PUDL_OUTPUT`.** If those
files were not produced by materializing the corresponding asset using the full ETL
settings on the current branch, the validation results will not be reliable. Only
validate tables you are actively working on, and always materialize them first on the
current branch:

text: Use `pixi run dg` to ensure `dg` is always run in the correct environment.

head: AGENTS.md > Preferred CLI tools > ruff
