head: AGENTS.md > Available skills
text:
Skills are defined in `skills-lock.json`. If not already installed, run
`pixi run install-skills`.

head: AGENTS.md > Available skills
text:
- **`dagster-expert`** — Dagster and `dg` CLI reference. Use when adding or modifying
  assets, resources, IO managers, jobs, sensors, or any other Dagster construct.

head: AGENTS.md > Available skills
text:
- **`datapackage`** -- Explains how to work with the Frictionless Datapackage
  metadata standard, which uses a `datapackage.json` descriptor to annotate a
  collection of data resources, including tabular data.

head: AGENTS.md > Available skills
text:
- **`pudl`** -- PUDL data and metadata reference, which extends the Frictionless
  Datapackage standard. Explains how to interpret PUDL metadata and how to
  query and safely use PUDL data, both local and remote.

head: AGENTS.md > Dagster architecture
text:
**Settings flow**: Always pass config via `dg launch --config dg_xxx.yml`. Never
hand-assemble `run_config` dicts. The YAML path is read by `GlobalDataConfigResource`,
which loads `GlobalDataConfig` and injects it into all assets and IO managers.

head: AGENTS.md > Dagster architecture
text:
**FERC SQLite provenance**: each FERC SQLite materialization records a fingerprint
(Zenodo DOIs, years of data processed) in Dagster asset metadata. Downstream IO managers
call `assert_ferc_sqlite_compatible()` before reading and raise a descriptive
`RuntimeError` if the stored fingerprint does not match the current run.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text:
Always include `--no-cov` when running pytest directly (not via a pixi task) to skip
coverage collection and avoid spurious failures.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text:
Tests are organized into four tiers under `tests/`, primarily distinguished by how long
they take to run and whether they depend on a full Dagster ETL build. A
`pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook in `tests/conftest.py` enforces this split
automatically: a test outside `tests/pipeline/`/`tests/validate/` that depends on the
ETL (via the `prebuilt_outputs` fixture, directly or transitively), or a test inside
either of those directories that doesn't, fails collection with a message telling you
where to move it.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing > Unit tests
text:
Unit tests live under `tests/unit/`, take up to 2 minutes, don't require any ETL
outputs, and run automatically via the pre-commit hook on every commit.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing > Integration tests
text:
Integration tests live under `tests/integration/` and test interactions between
different parts of the system, in some cases requiring network access (e.g. downloading
a small amount of data from Zenodo). They take a few minutes at most and also run in GitHub
Actions on every push.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing > Pipeline and data validation tests
text:
Pipeline tests (`tests/pipeline/`) run a Dagster-managed fast ETL using `dg_pytest.yml`
and then exercise code against those outputs — an end-to-end smoke test. Data validation
tests (`tests/validate/`) check the outputs of that ETL run (foreign key constraints and
the `dbt` data validation suite) and depend on the pipeline tests having already
produced outputs to check. Because the fast ETL takes ~45 minutes, both tiers only run
in the merge queue as a final check before a PR merges into `main` — **do not run these
interactively during development**, unless you pair them with `--live-pudl-output`
against outputs you already have locally.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing > Custom pytest flags
text:
- `--live-pudl-output` — skip the ETL prebuild and use existing local PUDL outputs.
  Useful for pipeline/validation tests when your change doesn't affect the ETL itself
  (e.g. analysis code or data validation). **Cannot be combined with unit and
  integration tests** in the same session; the suites require incompatible
  `$PUDL_OUTPUT` environment variable handling.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing > Custom pytest flags
text:
- `--temp-pudl-input` — download a fresh copy of raw inputs for this run only, instead
  of reusing the local datastore cache. Use when testing datastore functionality.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing > Custom pytest flags
text: - `--dg-config PATH` — override the default `dg_pytest.yml` with a custom Dagster config.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing > Fixture constraints
text:
Do not run tests that depend on `prebuilt_outputs`, `pudl_engine`, `ferc1_engine_dbf`,
`ferc1_engine_xbrl`, or `ferc714_engine_xbrl` fixtures during development — these
require a Dagster pipeline ETL build and belong under `tests/pipeline/` or
`tests/validate/`. Exception: with `--live-pudl-output`, these fixtures use existing
outputs and run quickly.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing > Test style
text: Use pytest-mock (`mocker`). Avoid `unittest` and `monkeypatch`.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text:
**Acronyms in compound class names**: In compound class names that contain multiple
acronyms, capitalize acronyms as words: e.g. `FercDbf`, `FercXbrl`.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text: **Line length**: limit lines to 88 characters. Do not artificially restrict to 80.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text:
**Type annotations**: add annotations wherever they aid readability or IDE
inference — function signatures are the highest-value target. Annotations on
internal variables are optional; add them only when the type is non-obvious.
Enforcement is currently light and experimental, so err on the side of annotating
rather than skipping.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text:
**Type error suppression**: suppress `pyrefly` errors with
`# type: ignore[specific-code]`, using pyrefly's own error codes (e.g.
`missing-argument`, `unresolved-attribute` — see the `pyrefly` entry in Preferred
CLI tools). Only fall back to a bare `# type: ignore` if pyrefly gives no error code to
target; a bare ignore also requires `# noqa: PGH003` to silence ruff's rule against
untargeted ignores:

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text: If the suppression is non-obvious, add a prose comment explaining why:

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text:
**Logging**: never use `print()` outside of CLI interfaces. Use Python's `logging`
module via the `pudl.logging_helpers` module. Obtain a logger at module level with
`logger = pudl.logging_helpers.get_logger(__name__)`. Never use old-style `%`
formatting or `str.format()` for log messages that include variable values. Instead
always use f-strings for log messages that need to include variable values:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns
text: - Data validation belongs in dbt, not in Dagster asset checks.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns
text:
- Sanity checks on data assumptions embedded within the `pudl.transform` modules
  should raise `AssertionError` loudly when assumptions are violated, rather than
  silently passing and causing downstream issues.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns
text: - Use existing utility functions in `pudl.helpers` before writing new ones.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns
text: - Raw data access must use the datastore pattern, not direct file I/O.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns
text:
- Use nullable pandas dtypes (`pd.Int64Dtype()`, `pd.StringDtype()`) to avoid
  generic `object` dtypes and mixed NULL values.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns
text:
- Parquet outputs use the compression codec and level set by
  `pudl.PARQUET_COMPRESSION` and `pudl.PARQUET_COMPRESSION_LEVEL` (zstd), and pyarrow
  dtypes. Never hardcode a codec or level where Parquet is written.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns
text: - For large datasets (>1GB), use polars or DuckDB to read data instead of pandas.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns > API compatibility and refactoring scope
text:
PUDL is an **application**, not a library. No external consumers depend on its internal
APIs. You do not need to maintain backwards-compatibility shims, deprecation warnings, or
gradual cut-overs when refactoring. A change is complete when every call-site and
reference inside the repository has been updated and the tests pass.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture and key patterns > API compatibility and refactoring scope
text:
**Excluded from scope**: the `devtools/` and `notebooks/` directories are informal,
untested, and already broken. Do not spend time updating them, and do not let broken
references there block a refactor.

head: AGENTS.md > Metadata system
text:
Metadata describing tables, columns, and data sources lives in `pudl.metadata`.
"Resources" are tables; "Fields" are columns. Metadata classes in
`pudl.metadata.classes` use Pydantic and mirror the frictionless datapackage standard.

head: AGENTS.md > PUDL developer reference docs
text:
The following files under `docs/dev/` and `docs/methodology/` cover
PUDL-specific concepts and conventions. **Read the relevant file before working
in that area** rather than guessing at conventions.

head: AGENTS.md > PUDL developer reference docs
text:
| File | When to read it |
| ---- | --------------- |
| `docs/dev/naming_conventions.rst` | Before naming any asset, table, column, variable, or code identifier — covers layer prefixes (`raw_`/`core_`/`out_`), table-type suffixes (`_assn`, `_ent`, `_scd`, etc.), and column-name patterns for IDs, codes, units, and flags |
| `docs/dev/metadata.rst` | Before adding or modifying a table, column, or data source — explains how Resources (tables) and Fields (columns) are defined, validated with Pandera, and wired into the frictionless datapackage |
| `docs/dev/data_guidelines.rst` | Before designing a new transformation — establishes what changes to raw data are acceptable, tidy-data requirements, unit conventions, and time-series completeness expectations |
| `docs/dev/existing_data_updates.rst` | When integrating a new year or version of an existing data source — step-by-step workflow covering file maps, extraction, transformation, schema updates, ID mapping, and validation |
| `docs/dev/datastore.rst` | When working with raw input data, the `pudl_datastore` CLI, or Zenodo DOI references in `zenodo_dois.yml` |
| `docs/dev/clone_ferc1.rst` | Before touching FERC extraction or the `ferc_to_sqlite` job — explains the DBF→SQLite and XBRL→SQLite conversion pipeline and the raw FERC asset group |
| `docs/dev/pudl_id_mapping.rst` | When working with cross-dataset entity resolution (`plant_id_pudl`, `utility_id_pudl`) or the manual ID mapping spreadsheet |
| `docs/methodology/entity_resolution.rst` | When working with `pudl.glue` or entity/SCD tables — explains how PUDL reconciles inconsistent plant and utility identities across EIA and FERC reporting |

compare the current branch against the branch it will merge into** (typically `main`,
but check the PR base branch) using `git diff <upstream>...HEAD` or

text:
Create a new branch and a matching worktree with the same name for each feature that

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow
text:
After editing files run `pixi run ruff check` and `pixi run ruff format` on the changed

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow
text:
Newly added functionality should be accompanied by unit tests and release notes. Include
both the issue number and PR number in release notes entries.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow
text:
Make focused commits composed of related changes. **When relocating code,
documentation, or any other text between modules, move it verbatim — never rewrite or
reinterpret it in the same step.** If the moved content also needs edits, make those as
a separate step with explicit user approval. When moving entire files, always use `git
mv` to preserve history. When moving blocks of code between files or within the same
file, first commit the verbatim move without changes, then make any necessary edits in a
subsequent commit.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow
text:
Write informative commit messages that summarize the changes and their motivation. Use
plaintext no more than 80 characters wide, with a short summary line (max 50 chars). For
significant changes, follow the first summary with a blank line and a more detailed
description. Do not add spurious or generated files to source control.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution workflow
text:
When you are ready to commit, run `pixi run prek-run` and fix all issues before
attempting to commit.  NEVER skip pre-commit hooks by using `--no-verify`. Fix the
underlying issue or ask for help — do not bypass the checks.

head: AGENTS.md > Sandbox safe execution
text:
**Shell autocorrect**: the `.pixi/` directory in the project root can trigger zsh's
command-line spelling correction, which suggests correcting `pixi` → `.pixi`. This
is always wrong, but the problem is zsh-specific — bash and fish don't correct
command names this way, so no guard is needed under those shells. Under zsh, use
the `nocorrect` precommand modifier, which disables correction for that single
command line only without mutating shell option state (unlike `unsetopt`, so it
won't trip sandbox checks that flag option-changing builtins). Guard on
`$ZSH_VERSION` so the same line works unchanged under bash:

head: AGENTS.md > Sandbox safe execution
text:
This is POSIX-style syntax, valid under both bash and zsh. Fish uses different
`if`/`end` syntax and isn't a supported shell for agent sandboxes, so it's out of
scope here — but fish doesn't have this autocorrect behavior in the first place.

head: AGENTS.md > Sandbox safe execution
text:
**Frozen execution**: use `pixi run --frozen` to prevent pixi from updating the
environment when running commands, avoiding unexpected dependency resolution:

head: AGENTS.md > Sandbox safe execution

head: AGENTS.md > Sandbox safe execution

head: Coding agent guide
text: 公共开发约定，不依赖本机技能或私有协作系统。修改前阅读 [README](README.md)、[架构](docs/cloud-agent-architecture.md) 和相关源码，检查 `git status --short`，保留他人改动。接业务先看 [业务复用指南](docs/business-reuse.md)，再看 [模块与适配器](docs/modules.md)。优先复用现有任务、确认、身份和投递机制；领域 SQL 与框架同库组合时使用宿主事务端口，不在业务中复制第二套通用状态机。

head: Coding agent guide > 边界与不变量
text: - `packages/` 不导入 `apps/`、`modules/`、`adapters/` 或模型 SDK；业务在模块，外部协议在适配器，通过 `apps/container.ts` 装配。默认集合在 `modules/catalog.ts`，Worker 不按业务名分支。

head: Coding agent guide > 边界与不变量
text: - `Module.next(input, steps)` 必须纯净：不访问网络、数据库、时钟或随机数。每个逻辑步骤 key 稳定，重试复用 `context.idempotencyKey`。

head: Coding agent guide > 边界与不变量
text: - 声明工具副作用；未知写入不能直接重发，`reconcilable_write` 必须实现 `reconcile`。确认绑定参数，拒绝、过期、改参不得被 retry 绕过。

head: Coding agent guide > 边界与不变量
text: - 身份、工作区和凭据来自可信服务端，不来自模型或客户端。角色不产生业务通配能力；授权变更须有版本检查、原因、幂等和审计。

head: Coding agent guide > 边界与不变量
text: - 旧租约或已取消任务不得提交结果；取消不撤销远端动作。模块通过 `validateContext` / `authorizeRead` 复核领域权限，核心不猜测步骤数据形状。

head: Coding agent guide > 边界与不变量
text: - 修改编排、协议、工具或授权语义时升级模块版本；迁移只能追加，不编辑已应用文件。模块为可信部署代码，不动态求值用户代码。

head: Coding agent guide > 边界与不变量
text: - 通用发行版不内置领域业务；新业务通过独立包和端口装配。架构测试夹具放在 `tests/fixtures/`，不得被生产入口导入；本地 `project/` 参考仓库不纳入 Git 或镜像。

head: Coding agent guide > 代码与文档
text: TypeScript 严格模式，不用显式 `any`；优先短函数和显式参数，复杂约束与并发逻辑用简洁中文注释。改动聚焦目标，配置、API 和文档与实际行为同步，说明错误及恢复语义。

head: Coding agent guide > 代码与文档
text: 不提交 `.env`、凭据、备份、本机协作资料；公开文档不引用私人路径或会话。不要打印完整连接串、降低隔离检查或清空用户数据库来通过测试。

head: Coding agent guide > 验证与交付
text: 环境准备见 [开发指南](docs/development.md)，按变更范围执行：

head: Coding agent guide > 验证与交付
text:
| 变更 | 验证 |
| --- | --- |
| 交付工具、发布或公开边界 | 另跑 `pnpm test:tooling`、`pnpm secrets:check`；候选包只从干净提交生成并校验 |
| 仅文档 | `pnpm docs:check`、`git diff --check` |
| 代码 | `pnpm format:check`、`pnpm check` |
| 页面 | 另跑 `pnpm test:browser`，检查桌面和手机截图 |
| 部署、迁移或授权存储 | 构建镜像，另跑 `pnpm test:compose` |
| SDK、公共 API、业务包 | 另跑 `pnpm sdk:verify`、`pnpm contracts:check`、`pnpm evaluate`；基线变更须解释兼容性 |
| 数据生命周期/联合恢复 | 另跑 `pnpm test:recovery`，只使用新建测试库 |
| 依赖 | `pnpm licenses:generate`、`pnpm licenses:check`，检查锁文件与许可 |

head: Coding agent guide > 验证与交付
text: 覆盖率仅统计 `packages/**`，不能当作整仓覆盖率。交付说明变化、实测结果和未验证范围。提交使用 `feat:` / `fix:` / `docs:` 等前缀，推送和发布须有维护者授权。

head: AGENTS.md
text: Operational guide for AI agents working in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Before Writing Code
text: - Write everything in English: code, comments, variable names, documentation.

head: AGENTS.md > Before Writing Code
text: - Do not implement code, schema, migration, script, configuration, or documentation changes unless the user explicitly authorizes implementation with "wdrażamy" or an equivalent clear instruction. Analysis, investigation, and recommendations do not authorize changes.

head: AGENTS.md > Before Writing Code
text: - Check `.ai/specs/` before coding any non-trivial feature.

head: AGENTS.md > Before Writing Code
text: - Skills are installed in `.claude/skills/` (Claude Code) and `.agents/skills/` (Codex). `.agents/skills/` is the local source of truth — edit a skill **only** there, then run `ags push-skill` to propagate it to the source repo (it also syncs the `.claude/skills/` copy). See Installing skills.

head: AGENTS.md > Before Writing Code
text: - Prefer minimal, focused changes. Do not refactor code outside the task scope.

head: AGENTS.md > Before Writing Code
text: - Do not run `yarn build` automatically after implementation. Run it only when the user explicitly asks.

head: AGENTS.md > Before Writing Code
text: - Comment and naming conventions are defined in the `code-style` skill. Load it before writing or reviewing TypeScript.

head: AGENTS.md > Task Router
text: Match the task to the table before starting. A single task often maps to multiple rows.

head: AGENTS.md > Task Router
text:
| Task | Action |
|---|---|
| Creating a new collection or extending the schema | Load skill `payload-build-collections` |
| Adding a custom admin view, tab, or field UI | Load skill `payload-build-modules` |
| Building a front-end component or page (`src/components`, `src/modules/*/components`, `(frontend)`) | Load skill `payload-frontend-build-components` |
| Debugging hooks, queries, access control, transactions | Load skill `payload` |

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- `src/modules/` is organized by business capability, not by Payload collection. A module
  is a vertical slice that may own domain rules, frontend components, server queries, and
  Payload Admin UI.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- Closely related concepts belong to areas inside one module. For example, `training`
  contains `exercises`, `plans`, and `logs`; do not create a separate top-level module for
  every table or entity.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- Keep `src/app/` thin: route files compose module entry points but do not own feature
  implementations. Modules must never import from `src/app/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- Keep Payload `CollectionConfig`, fields, hooks, access control, relationships, and
  indexes in `src/collections/`. Collections may import only client-safe domain APIs from
  modules, never module components, admin UI, or server entry points.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- Put domain-specific React components under `src/modules/<module>/components/`. Keep only
  domain-agnostic primitives in `src/components/ui/` and cross-module application UI in
  `src/components/common/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- Put server-side queries and use cases under an explicit `server/` entry point and add
  `import 'server-only'`. Do not re-export server code from a client-safe module barrel.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- Put Payload Admin implementations under `src/modules/<module>/admin/<feature>/`.
  Collection configuration must reference the exact component file and the import map
  must be regenerated after a path changes.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- Use `types.ts` only for types and interfaces, and `constants.ts` only for constants and
  declarative configuration. Name operation files after their responsibility; do not add
  generic `utils.ts`, `helpers.ts`, or `models.ts` files.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text:
- Code outside a domain area must use its public `index.ts`. Environment-specific APIs use
  explicit subpaths such as `@/modules/training/plans/server` or
  `@/modules/training/components/workout-plans`.

head: AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
AGENTS.md > Module Architecture
text: - Keep only business-agnostic technical functions and SDK clients in `src/lib/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Payload-Generated Types

head: AGENTS.md > Payload-Generated Types
text:
- A type declared in a module may use the same name as a generated Payload type. Types
  exported from different files do not conflict merely because their names match.

head: AGENTS.md > Payload-Generated Types
text:
- A naming conflict occurs only when two types with the same local name are imported
  into the same scope. Alias the imports when both representations are needed, for
  example `Workout as PayloadWorkout` and `Workout as PlanWorkout`.

head: AGENTS.md > Payload-Generated Types
text:
- Name module-owned types according to their domain role. Do not add prefixes or
  suffixes solely to avoid a same-name type exported by another module.

head: AGENTS.md > Database Migrations

head: AGENTS.md > Database Migrations
text: - Maintainers run `yarn payload migrate:create` and `yarn payload migrate` manually. Agents must not run either command.

head: AGENTS.md > Database Migrations
text: - Agents must never create migration files manually or edit Payload-generated migration files.

head: AGENTS.md > Database Migrations
text: - Keep Payload-generated schema migrations in their generated form. Do not add manual SQL or data updates to them.

head: AGENTS.md > Data Backfills
text: - Implement every data backfill as a separate, idempotent script through the Payload Local API.

head: AGENTS.md > Data Backfills
text: - Do not add data backfill SQL to Payload-generated schema migrations.

head: AGENTS.md > Data Backfills
text: - Maintainers run backfill scripts manually. Agents must not run them.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter
text:
VeraCite audits BibTeX/biblatex bibliographies to catch hallucinated, mangled, or
mis-identified citations before publication. `README.md` is for users,
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) is the mechanics for human contributors
(setup, workflow, tests, code style), and **this file is the *principles* — the
contract for changing the code** that every contributor, human or AI, should
follow. When a change conflicts with a principle here, the principle wins; if the
principle itself is wrong, change *it* first, in its own commit, with the reasoning.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Trust is the #1 priority
text:
One false positive on a clean entry makes the user distrust *all* output, so **a
false positive is the cardinal sin — prefer silence to a wrong flag**, tightening
a rule even at some cost to recall, never the reverse.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Trust is the #1 priority
text:
VeraCite is **read-only**: it flags, never edits. **Crossref (by DOI) is the
primary metadata resource**; arXiv/INSPIRE/OpenAlex/Open Library corroborate it.
A `suggested:` edit always conforms the bib *toward* that record, unless the
record is clearly broken.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Trust is the #1 priority
text:
A **VeraCite-side failure must never masquerade as a citation problem.** A
TRANSIENT error (rate-limit, 5xx, network drop) is the tool's hiccup, not a
defect in the entry — mark it retryable and re-run that phase on resume, rather
than reporting it as UNVERIFIED. A settled 404 ("no such record") is not retried.
A tail of entries silently going UNVERIFIED from one rate-limit is a trust
failure as real as a false positive.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Every message must suggest an action
text: - If a finding implies nothing to do, don't emit it — silence is the clean pass.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Every message must suggest an action
text:
- One finding per line, carrying a stable `category`, the offending line, and a
  structured `suggested` patch when one exists. When one fix resolves several
  findings, suppress the dependents (`SUPERSEDES`).

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Every message must suggest an action
text:
- **The per-record NDJSON is the single source of truth** — every output (the
  terminal report and `--json`) is a parse of it through one record builder and
  one renderer, never a recompute from live objects or a second formatting path.
  No aggregate is stored: summaries are re-derived from the records each run, so
  fresh and resumed runs take the identical path. A phase is marked done **only
  when it actually succeeded** — a transient or failed attempt leaves it undone
  so a later pass retries it. Each record stamps a `checksum` of its source text
  so an edited entry is recomputed from scratch on resume.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Every message must suggest an action
text:
- **Keep the NDJSON forward-compatible.** Tolerate a report a *future* version
  wrote: read with `.get`, treat unknown fields/records as opaque and preserve
  them verbatim rather than dropping them.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Severity means a specific kind of action
text:
| level | meaning | examples |
|-------|---------|----------|
| `[ERROR]` | a syntax error or clearly-broken citation — **must fix** | unbalanced braces, missing `=`, dead DOI, duplicate, id resolves to a different paper |
| `[WARN]` | a real data problem hurting accuracy — **investigate** | year/author/title/volume/pages/journal disagree with the record; sources conflict |
| `[note]` | stylistic or a completeness/portability nudge — usually no render effect | casing, dashes, brace-protection, an abbreviated given name, an invalid-for-biblatex field |

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Everything is a rule
text:
No guessing in the verification path — every finding is a comparison against an
authoritative record or a deterministic rule (`--llm` is the sole exception).

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Everything is a rule
text:
- A per-entry check is `@rule`; a whole-file check is `@file_rule`, both in
  [`rules.py`](veracite/rules.py).

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Everything is a rule
text:
- Every finding carries a stable `category` that sets its severity, group, and
  catalog text. Its metadata lives in [`report.py`](veracite/report.py) and
  [`config.py`](veracite/config.py); [`catalog.py`](veracite/catalog.py)
  introspects them to build `--list-rules`, so it cannot drift. Adding or
  changing a category touches all three — `test_catalog.py` catches a miss.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text:
A rule must be **principled** and **general enough** to catch a broad class,
narrow enough to **never fire on a valid entry**.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text: - Generalize to the underlying defect, not the one input that surfaced it.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text:
- Prefer structural signals (check digits, datamodel legality, brace/quote
  balance) over free-text heuristics, which are the likeliest to misfire.
  *Example:* a digit glued to a name looks like a stray year — but a digit
  inside TeX markup (`\hspace{0.167em}`) is not name content; fold markup out
  before scanning, don't pattern-match the raw text.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text:
- Fold away legitimate variation before comparing (name particles/suffixes,
  ISO-4 abbreviations, brace/quote wrapping, `--` vs `-`) — each unfolded thing
  is a false positive waiting. *Example:* arXiv's id lookup serves only the
  **latest** version's title, so a faithfully-cited v1 title can look like a
  mismatch; never conclude "this title exists nowhere" from a title-search index
  alone, since it too holds only the latest title.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text:
- Attach `suggested=` only when certain of the target; otherwise report the
  discrepancy without one. A *resolved but divergent* record is still
  uncertain — soften the claim rather than asserting a mismatch, since the link
  itself (or the record) may be the wrong one.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text:
- An offline guess the authoritative record later disproves must be
  **withdrawn, not shipped** — declare the supersession (`SUPERSEDES`) or
  `rep.withdraw()` it once the record contradicts it.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text:
- A style/`[note]` recommendation must be **grounded in a BibTeX/biblatex data
  standard**, never personal taste — if you can't name the standard it
  enforces, it isn't a rule.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text:
- A note that fires on (nearly) **every** entry is noise, not signal — scope it
  to the entries the standard actually targets. *Example:* `urldate` matters
  for a grey-web/`@online` source, not for a published article whose url is
  just its DOI/arXiv landing page.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Writing a rule that doesn't misfire
text:
- Check every proposed rule change against these principles before writing it —
  even when it comes from the user.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Self-improving by design
text:
VeraCite should **get more accurate after every stress test**: run it on a real
bibliography, hand-audit the output against the record, and feed each false
positive/negative back as a *generalized* rule plus tests. A durable principle
learned in one session belongs in this file so it is enforced in the next.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Self-improving by design
text: - Generalize, don't proliferate — ten symptoms of one gap is one rule change.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Self-improving by design
text: - A change must close a recall gap, never flip a clean entry into an error.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Self-improving by design
text:
- Never push a bad value — validate before suggesting, withhold mangled values,
  and cap weak-match confidence so it can't overwrite toward a wrong reference.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Self-improving by design
text: - Every cycle ships positive and negative tests for the class.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Known gaps / deferred (with constraints)
text:
- **`url` is not validated.** Checking a dead/wrong link would mean VeraCite
  fetching a URL from an untrusted `.bib` — an SSRF risk.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Before proposing a patch
text: 1. Reproduce and find the **true root cause** (not a diagnostic artifact).

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Before proposing a patch
text:
2. **Enumerate the candidate fixes** — what each catches, what it might miss,
   how it could falsely fire.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Before proposing a patch
text:
3. **Flag the best option with trade-offs, and wait** — don't reflexively edit
   beyond a trivial, obviously-correct change.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Before proposing a patch
text:
4. **Test the class, not the fixture** — including the look-alike valid inputs
   the rule must not flag (`synthesis` must not match a `thesis` rule).

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Commands
text:
`--key KEY` focuses the whole run on a single citation key — only that entry is
resolved and only its findings are reported. Use it to verify a specific record
after applying a suggested fix, without re-running the entire bibliography.

head: CLAUDE.md — the VeraCite contributor charter > Commands
text:
Integrity score and confidence are transparent deterministic formulas
([`verify.py`](veracite/verify.py)), not model outputs — keep them that way.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird
text: Songbird is a self-hosted real-time communication platform built as a Node.js/React monorepo.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Workspace Architecture
text: - **`client/`**: React 19 SPA (Vite, Tailwind CSS 4, Vitest + Playwright).

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Workspace Architecture
text: - **`server/`**: Node.js Express 5 backend (SSE realtime updates, in-memory SQLite via `sql.js`, Vitest + Supertest).

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Workspace Architecture
text: - **`docs/`**: Dual-language VitePress documentation (English & Persian/Farsi).

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Critical Architecture Quirks & Pitfalls
text: - **Design & Styling (`DESIGN.md`)**: Respect and follow [`DESIGN.md`](./DESIGN.md) for all frontend styling, UI component design, typography, color system, accessibility, and UI patterns.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Critical Architecture Quirks & Pitfalls
text: - **Node Requirement**: Requires Node `>=24.18.0` and npm `>=11.18.0`.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Critical Architecture Quirks & Pitfalls
text: - **Database (`server/db.js`)**: `sql.js` runs in-memory with debounced disk persistence (`DB_SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS`). All SQL queries **must** reside inside `server/db.js`. Never write inline SQL queries elsewhere.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Critical Architecture Quirks & Pitfalls
text: - **Server Test Isolation**: `server/db.js` and `server/index.js` initialize WASM and disk state on module load and **cannot** be imported in tests. Server API integration tests must use `makeApp` from `server/test/helpers/makeApp.js` to inject stubbed dependencies.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Critical Architecture Quirks & Pitfalls
text: - **Realtime SSE**: Real-time events are dispatched via `server/lib/sse.js` (`emitChatEvent`). API mutations must invoke SSE broadcast handlers to notify connected clients.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Critical Architecture Quirks & Pitfalls
text: - **Client Routing & API**: No React Router library. SPA navigation is managed manually in `client/src/App.jsx` via `window.history`. All client HTTP calls **must** use `apiFetch` in `client/src/api/chatApi.js` (`credentials: "include"`).

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Critical Architecture Quirks & Pitfalls
text: - **Documentation Updates**: Any update to documentation under `docs/` must update both English (`docs/*.md`) and Persian (`docs/fa/*.md`) documents, matching the structure in `docs/.vitepress/config.mjs`. Call the `documentor` subagent to update docs when you implant a new feature.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Development & Git Workflow
text: - **Git Execution**: **NEVER** run `git` commands automatically. Suggest a commit message in the format `type(scope): description` and let the user execute git operations.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Development & Git Workflow
text: - **Bug Fixing Workflow**: Do not guess or fix immediately upon a bug report. First write a test reproducing the issue under test scenarios, verify it catches the bug, then apply the fix.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Development & Git Workflow
text: - **Response Style**: Keep task completions concise. Do not generate unrequested markdown summary files.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > graphify
text: This project has a knowledge graph at graphify-out/ with god nodes, community structure, and cross-file relationships.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > graphify
text: When the user types `/graphify`, use the installed graphify skill or instructions before doing anything else.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > graphify
text: - For codebase questions, first run `graphify query "<question>"` when graphify-out/graph.json exists. Use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for focused concepts. These return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output. Always prefer graphify query commands over raw text grepping on graphify-out/.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > graphify
text: - Dirty graphify-out/ files are expected after hooks or incremental updates; dirty graph files are not a reason to skip graphify. Only skip graphify if the task is about stale or incorrect graph output, or the user explicitly says not to use it.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > graphify
text: - If graphify-out/wiki/index.md exists, use it for broad navigation instead of raw source browsing.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > graphify
text: - Read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context.

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > graphify
text: - After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).

head: Repository Guidelines: Songbird > Superpowers
text: When using superpowers skills, create the plans or specs docs under `.superpowers/docs`.

head: AGENTS.md
text: - To set up the development environment, make sure that a venv is created and the pre-commit and pre-push hooks are installed, see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

head: AGENTS.md
text: - The `floss/` folder has the main functionality, while `scripts/` has auxiliary plugins and scripts. Docs are in `doc/`.

head: AGENTS.md
text: - Result caching is on by default. When reproducing or diffing output across commits, disable it with `FLOSS_CACHE_ENABLE=0` (or `FLOSS_CACHE_DIR` to point it at a scratch dir) — otherwise a run may serve a cached document written by earlier code.

head: AGENTS.md
text: - All lints, formatters, and tests in `.github/workflows` **must** pass before making a PR. When applying linters or formatters locally, **ALWAYS use `pre-commit run <tool> --all-files`** (e.g., `pre-commit run black --all-files`). Do not run these tools directly (e.g., `black <file>`), as doing so bypasses `.pre-commit-config.yaml` rules (such as 120-character line lengths) and will ruin existing codebase formatting.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes
text:
Guia para qualquer agente (Claude e afins) trabalhando neste repositório. Leia antes de editar.
Documentação para humanos fica no [README](./README.md) e no [CONTRIBUTING](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > O projeto
text:
**Roadmap DSA** — o maior guia **visual e gratuito** de Algoritmos e Estruturas de Dados em
português, feito **pela comunidade Craft & Code Club**. Cada tópico tem: algoritmo rodando passo
a passo (visualizador), artigo, vídeo, problemas (LeetCode/GeeksforGeeks) e referências.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > O projeto
text: - Domínio: `https://dsa.craftcodeclub.io`. Repo: `craft-code-club/roadmap-dsa`.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > O projeto
text:
- Licença: **dupla**. Código sob **MIT** (open source, uso comercial permitido); conteúdo
  didático sob **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0**. A fronteira **não é por diretório** — ela atravessa
  arquivos: num visualizador, o componente é código e as strings didáticas (notas de passo,

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Stack e comandos
text: - **Next.js 16 (App Router) + React 19**, export estático (`output: "export"` → `out/`). Node 22+.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Stack e comandos
text: - Conteúdo em **MDX**. Partes interativas são ilhas `"use client"`; o resto é estático (SSG).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Stack e comandos
text:
- Deploy: **Cloudflare Pages via Wrangler** (ver seção Deploy e `.github/workflows/`).
```bash
npm run dev      # desenvolvimento
npm run build    # DEVE passar (gera ./out). 55+ páginas.
npm test         # Playwright (roda contra o ./out via python http.server). DEVE passar.
PORT=3101 npm test   # porta alternativa: obrigatório quando há mais de uma suíte na máquina
```

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Verificação (faça sempre)
text:
1. Depois de mudar código, rode `npm run build` **e** `npm test`. Os dois têm que passar.
   A suíte **não reusa** servidor que já esteja na porta: reusar fazia ela testar o `out/` de
   outro worktree (ou o dev server, que serve da fonte) e **passar verde com código quebrado**.
   Porta ocupada agora falha dizendo isso; use `PORT=<outra> npm test`.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Verificação (faça sempre)
text:
2. Para conferência visual, use o **`agent-browser`** (Vercel Labs CLI, instalado na máquina):
   - Servir o build: `python3 -m http.server 4321 --directory out` e abrir nele; ou usar o dev server.
   - Screenshot da página inteira: flag é **`--full`** (não `--full-page`).
   - Mobile: **`agent-browser set viewport 390 844`** (depois de `open`). Confira overflow com
     `document.body.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth`.
   - Overlay/modal (position:fixed): use screenshot de **viewport** (sem `--full`).
   - `find role button` não acha botões cujo nome começa com glifo (⤢). Clique via
     `agent-browser eval "document.querySelector('.classe').click()"`.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Verificação (faça sempre)
text:
3. Arquivos temporários (prints, GIFs, artefatos) vão para **`/screenshots/`** (está no
   `.gitignore`). Nunca commite esses arquivos.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **`content/fundamentos.ts` é a fonte única dos FUNDAMENTOS**, a sequência principal (dirige o
  menu lateral, o `/fundamentos/`, as tags e o SEO). `content/` fica na raiz, irmão de `src/`:
  `src/` é o código de estrutura, `content/` são os dados, artigos e visualizadores. Agrupamento
  estilo LeetCode (16 grupos): cada estrutura junto das técnicas que operam sobre ela; paradigmas
  (Recursão, Backtracking, Programação Dinâmica, Greedy Algorithms) como grupos próprios.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **`content/roadmaps/` é a casa dos roadmaps extras**, um arquivo por roadmap
  (`content/roadmaps/<slug>.ts`), com `index.ts` guardando o modelo, o registro e os derivados
  das três casas. **`content/avulsos.ts`** guarda os tópicos que se bastam numa página só.
  O índice é uma lista à mão porque o módulo é importado por componente de cliente (o `Shell`
  decide a barra lateral com ele) e código de cliente não tem `fs`; quem impede que ela envelheça
  é o teste `todo arquivo de content/roadmaps/ está registrado no índice`, que lê a pasta.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **Vocabulário, e ele importa:** *Fundamentos* é a sequência principal; *roadmap* é um percurso
  extra; *tópico* é uma página. "Trilha" e "curso" não existem mais no produto nem no código
  (só sobrou "Trilha de navegação", que é o nome do breadcrumb).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **A página canônica de um tópico é sempre `/topicos/<slug>/`**, venha ele de onde vier. Quem
  precisa de todos os tópicos do site (`generateStaticParams`, sitemap, guarda de datas) usa
  `SITE_TOPICS`; quem fala dos Fundamentos (progresso, barra lateral, números da home) usa
  `ALL_TOPICS`. Trocar um pelo outro não dá erro — dá número errado na home ou 404 num tópico.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **UM TÓPICO PODE ESTAR EM MAIS DE UM ROADMAP.** O grupo de um roadmap aceita um `Topic` escrito
  ali (ele é o DONO) ou uma `string` com o slug (ele só CITA). O dono decide a casca da página
  canônica e reivindica o slug; quem cita ganha o tópico na lista e uma URL própria
  (`/roadmaps/<r>/<topico>/`) com `canonical` de volta para `/topicos/<slug>/` e fora do sitemap.
  Exemplos vivos: `content/roadmaps/caminhos-minimos.ts` cita 6 tópicos e não tem nenhum
  próprio (todos são dos Fundamentos, em outra ordem); a Skip List não é citada por roadmap
  nenhum e por isso abre sem barra lateral.
  O **namespace é global e o build cobra**: slug de tópico, id de grupo, slug de roadmap, citação
  que resolve e tópico não repetido são conferidos no import de `content/roadmaps/index.ts`.
  Como escolher a casa de um tópico novo: ver a tabela em
  [README](./README.md#fundamentos-roadmap-ou-tópico-avulso-onde-o-tópico-mora).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **Identificadores em inglês; qualquer coisa que o aluno lê em português.** Vale para os
  campos do roadmap **e para o código dos visualizadores** (variáveis, tipos, props, funções).
  Comentários podem ser em português; nome de componente, o que fizer sentido. A fronteira que
  já mordeu: o código Python que aparece na tela, os rótulos das variáveis e as notas do passo a
  passo são **conteúdo didático**, mesmo dentro de uma string — renomear em lote traduz o
  identificador e estraga a aula junto ("O array precisa estar sorted"). Detalhes e o
  procedimento de conferência em [`content/visualizers/README.md`](content/visualizers/README.md) §0.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **O tópico não tem casa.** Cada um é uma pasta com **dois arquivos**:
  `content/topicos/<slug>/index.ts` (o dado: `topico`, o `sumario` do artigo e a `pratica`) e
  `content/topicos/<slug>/artigo.mdx` (o texto). Um terceiro arquivo ali reprova no teste: quando
  o peso obriga a separar, quem separa é o REGISTRO, não a pasta.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **Os roadmaps CITAM tópicos**, em `content/roadmaps/<slug>.ts`, por
  `topics: [{ topic: "hash-table" }]`. Um tópico pode ser citado por nenhum, por um ou por seis; o
  tópico não muda por isso e não sabe quem o cita. Os Fundamentos são um roadmap como os outros.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **Três registros à mão**, porque `content/topicos/index.ts` é importado por componente de
  cliente (a barra lateral) e cliente não tem `fs`:
  `content/topicos/index.ts` (os tópicos), `content/topicos/artigos.ts` (os `.mdx`) e
  `content/topicos/pratica.ts` (problemas e referências). Os dois últimos **só o servidor
  importa**, e é isso que mantém 2,1 MB de artigo e 64 KB de problema fora de toda página.
  Esqueceu de registrar? O arquivo fica na pasta e o site não o serve — quem cobra é
  `tests/roadmaps.spec.ts`, que lê o diretório e compara nos dois sentidos.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **Os TIPOS moram em `src/content/tipos.ts`**, não em `content/`. Na raiz, `content/` é só
  conteúdo; o modelo é código. Um tópico novo importa `Topic` de `@/content/tipos`.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- Campos do tópico: `name`, `group`, `level`, `description`, `youtube` (id), `article` (link do
  blog), `extraVideos`, `viz`, `noViz`, `status: "ready" | "soon"`. O `group` é o **assunto**
  ("Arrays e Strings"), não um endereço — quem dá endereço é o roadmap que cita. Dois tópicos com
  o mesmo assunto têm de escrevê-lo **igual**: duas grafias viram duas seções em `/topicos/` com o
  mesmo título e o mesmo `id` de âncora (já aconteceu, e a lista passou a duplicar linhas).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **"Em breve" é só para tópico vazio.** `isEmptyTopic()` (em `content/topicos/index.ts`) = `soon`
  sem `youtube`, `article` nem `viz`. **`extraVideos` NÃO entra na conta**, de propósito e com a
  razão escrita no código: são links para resoluções soltas de exercício, e um tópico que só tem
  isso continua sem aula, sem texto e sem visualização. (A doc já disse o contrário do código
  aqui; quem vale é o código.) Só os vazios levam o selo "em breve" no menu lateral e
  o `noindex`; quem já tem qualquer material aparece normal. Tópico que nunca vai ter visualizador
  recebe `noViz: true` e deixa de mostrar o aviso de "visualização em construção".

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **"NOVO" é tag manual, não data.** O selo do menu lateral vem de `isNew: true` no tópico. Quem
  publica um tópico põe a tag no mesmo PR **e tira a dos anteriores** — sem data, nada envelhece
  sozinho. Não derive o selo de outro campo (já foi `viz`, e virava "novo" permanente).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **Código no MDX: sempre com linguagem na cerca** (` ```python `). O Shiki roda no build (plugin
  rehype em `next.config.ts`) e o HTML já sai colorido: zero JS de highlight no cliente, SSG
  intacto. A cerca também alimenta o selo discreto de linguagem no canto do bloco, montado em
  `mdx-components.tsx` (mapa `LINGUAGENS`). Cerca **sem** linguagem fica sem cor e sem selo, o que
  é o certo para diagrama em ASCII e pseudo-fórmula. Linguagem nova precisa entrar em duas listas:
  `langs` (`next.config.ts`) e `LINGUAGENS` (`mdx-components.tsx`).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- Visualizadores ficam em `content/visualizers/` (ex.: `SlidingWindowVisualizer`,
  `TwoPointersVisualizer`), expostos em `mdx-components.tsx`. A lista de apoiadores fica em
  `src/app/apoie/apoiadores.ts` (página fixa, não é conteúdo de DSA).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **Vai mexer na casca de um visualizador (altura, expandido, teclado, foco, rolagem)?
  Leia [`content/visualizers/README.md`](content/visualizers/README.md) antes.** Ele é o
  contrato da casca adaptativa (`.viz-fit`): as três camadas (comprimir antes de esconder),
  a decisão por medição em vez de breakpoint, a API de CSS, o contrato de teclado e foco do
  painel expandido, e as armadilhas já medidas.
  A mecânica é um hook, **`src/lib/visualizer.tsx`** (`useVisualizer` + `VizHeader` e `VizFooter`): chame, espalhe as props e use os componentes prontos — não reescreva.
  Ele cobre o que TODO visualizador tem (caber na tela, painel, bloco que mostra e
  oculta, controles de reprodução) e nada do que cada um mostra. Uso de referência: `BigOCounterVisualizer.tsx`.
  **Não edite o bloco `viz-fit` do `globals.css` para acomodar um visualizador
  específico** — ele é compartilhado por todos.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text: - Alias: `@/*` → `src/*`, `@content/*` → `content/*`.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Modelo de conteúdo
text:
- **Adicionar tópico/visualizador:** ver README (seções "Como adicionar"). O padrão de
  visualizador é gerador puro de passos + casca compartilhada + botão Expandir.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Navegação e links
text:
- **`src/lib/links.ts` é ponto único.** Comunidade = `LINKS.site` (craftcodeclub.io); repo =
  `LINKS.github` (`craft-code-club/roadmap-dsa`); apoio = `LINKS.apoiar` (campanha na APOIA.se).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Navegação e links
text:
- **Discord tem duas portas, por design.** *Dentro do app*: `LINKS.discord`, convite direto, um
  clique só. *Fora do app* (README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, templates do `.github/`, qualquer
  `.md`): `https://craftcodeclub.io/join`, que é o ponto de rotação da comunidade. Nunca cole
  `discord.gg/<código>` cru em arquivo de documentação.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Navegação e links
text:
- Barra: **esquerda** = Início, Fundamentos, Roadmaps, Tópicos; **direita** = YouTube, Discord,
  Apoiar + menu `⋯`. O menu `⋯` tem: Sobre o projeto, Craft & Code Club, GitHub do projeto,
  Apoiadores e Parceiros — e, conforme a largura aperta, os itens que saíram da barra.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Navegação e links
text:
- **A barra encolhe em degraus, e a ordem é comprimir antes de esconder** (a mesma filosofia da
  casca dos visualizadores). São quatro, todos no `globals.css`: **1000px** comprime o respiro
  (é onde nasce a gaveta e ela rouba 42px); **940px** manda Início e YouTube para o `⋯`
  (`nav-hide-md` na barra, `only-mobile only-md` no menu); **760px** manda Fundamentos, Roadmaps
  e Tópicos (`nav-hide-sm` / `only-mobile`); **400px** comprime o que sobrou.
  Duas regras que não se negociam: **nada some da barra sem aparecer no `⋯`**, e **as peças da
  barra são rígidas** (sem `min-width: 0`, sem quebra de linha). A rigidez é de propósito: peça
  que encolhe em silêncio se sobrepõe sem estourar a página, e nenhuma medição de overflow pega
  isso — foi assim que a marca passou a quebrar em três linhas em 920px. Quem mede os quatro
  degraus é `tests/barra-do-topo-responsiva.spec.ts`, varrendo 1400 → 320px.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Navegação e links
text:
- **Um tópico tem DUAS URLs, e elas não competem.** `/topicos/<slug>/` é a **canônica**: quem chega
  pelo índice geral, sem percurso, e vê na barra os roadmaps que citam o tópico.
  `/roadmaps/<r>/<slug>/` é a mesma página dentro de um percurso: menu do roadmap, anterior/próximo,
  e as **citações do artigo reescritas** para o roadmap (`linkDentroDoRoadmap`), para o leitor não
  cair fora dele ao clicar numa referência. Toda cópia aponta `canonical` para a canônica e fica
  fora do sitemap.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Navegação e links
text:
- **A casca muda com a rota, e é o `Shell` que decide** (`layoutDaRota`): a barra do roadmap em
  `/roadmaps/<slug>/` e em tudo abaixo dele, a barra dos roadmaps-que-citam em `/topicos/<slug>/`,
  e **nenhuma barra** na vitrine `/roadmaps/`, no índice `/topicos/` e nos tópicos que ninguém cita. A ausência é a decisão,
  não um esquecimento: num tópico avulso a barra ao lado seria uma lista para lugar nenhum.
  ⚠️ O `layoutDaRota` casa o PRIMEIRO SEGMENTO da rota por string. Renomeou rota? Aquele `if` não
  quebra o build nem o tipo: ele silenciosamente devolve a casca padrão, e o roadmap inteiro passa
  a abrir com a barra dos Fundamentos. Mexeu no `Shell` ou numa rota? Rode
  `tests/roadmaps.spec.ts`, que é quem mede as cascas — foi ele que pegou exatamente isso.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Navegação e links
text:
- **Rota renomeada leva 301 no mesmo PR**, em `public/_redirects`: hoje `/topico/*` →
  `/topicos/*`, `/fundamentos/*` e `/roadmap*` → `/roadmaps/fundamentos/*`. E a rota de origem
  **não pode existir como arquivo no `out/`**, senão o Pages serve o arquivo e a regra nunca roda.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Navegação e links
text:
- Links **externos** mostram `↗` (classe `ext`; a regra CSS é `.topnav > a.ext` para não afetar o
  menu). Bolinhas de marca: Discord blurple, YouTube vermelho, Apoiar âmbar.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > SEO
text:
- `sitemap.ts`, `robots.ts` e `opengraph-image.tsx` existem. **Rotas de metadata precisam de
  `export const dynamic = "force-static"`** por causa do `output: "export"`.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > SEO
text:
- Tópicos realmente vazios (`soon` sem youtube, article nem viz) recebem `noindex`
  (ver `generateMetadata` em `topico/[slug]/page.tsx`). Ao ganhar conteúdo, saem do noindex sozinhos.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > SEO
text:
- **A mesma régua vale um nível acima:** a abertura de um roadmap sem NENHUM tópico com material
  também é `noindex` e fica fora do sitemap (`roadmapHasMaterial`). Ela continua no site (mapear
  o território vale para quem estuda), mas não pede lugar no índice.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > SEO
text:
- **`/roadmaps/<r>/<topico>/` serve o mesmo texto de `/topicos/<slug>/`**, então ela aponta
  `canonical` (e `og:url`) para a canônica, fica FORA do sitemap e não emite JSON-LD nenhum: quem
  declara o recurso é a canônica, e declarar de novo numa página que acabou de dizer "a principal
  é outra" é a mesma contradição do `noindex` com `LearningResource`.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > SEO
text:
- O rastro de navegação tem **quatro formas** (Fundamentos, roadmap, avulso, e o tópico dentro de
  um roadmap) e a página monta o array de migalhas UMA vez, usando-o nos links e no
  `BreadcrumbList`. Não recrie a decisão dentro do `jsonld.ts`: o teste "o rastro marcado é o
  rastro desenhado" existe por causa disso.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Responsividade
text:
- Nos grids que colapsam no mobile, use **`minmax(0, 1fr)`** (não `1fr` puro, que vira min-content
  e estoura a largura) e **`min-width: 0`** nos itens que precisam encolher (article, `.mdx-cartao`,
  `.prose-pre`). Já verificado: 0 overflow em 360/390/768px.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Deploy
text:
Site estático (`out/`) publicado no **Cloudflare Pages** via **Wrangler**. O deploy roda no CI
(`.github/workflows/cloudflare-pages-deploy.yml`) em push para `main`; PRs de forks não fazem
deploy, e todo PR precisa da aprovação de um mantenedor antes do merge. Deploy local:
`npx wrangler pages deploy out --project-name <nome>`. Não há `wrangler.toml`: o nome do projeto
vem de `--project-name` (no CI, do secret). Secrets: `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`,
`CLOUDFLARE_PROJECT_NAME` (e, para apoiadores, `APOIASE_KEY` / `APOIASE_SECRET` /
`APOIASE_CAMPAIGN`).

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Deploy
text:
**Credencial da APOIA.se: três nomes, e nenhum é intercambiável.** `APOIASE_KEY` vai no header
`x-api-key`, `APOIASE_SECRET` no `Authorization: Bearer` (é um JWT) e `APOIASE_CAMPAIGN` é o id da
campanha. Sem os dois primeiros, o muro de `/apoie` sai da lista de plano B de
`src/app/apoie/apoiadores.ts` **e o build avisa no log** — o `return` calado dessa mesma linha é o
que fez a página publicada mostrar 3 apoiadores com 5 apoios na campanha, por meses, sem nada
denunciar. A varredura que prova que credencial nenhuma chega ao `out/` é
`tests/segredo-nao-vai-para-o-cliente.spec.ts`; ela lê os 1.242 arquivos do build, HTML, chunks e
payload RSC, e entra com 0 ocorrência em 16 regras.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Analytics
text:
- **Google Analytics 4 é opt-in por ambiente.** `src/components/Analytics.tsx` só renderiza o
  `GoogleAnalytics` do `@next/third-parties` quando `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID` existe; sem a variável ele
  devolve `null` e nenhum byte do gtag.js é pedido. O workflow injeta o ID **só no build da `main`**
  (é uma *variable*, `vars.NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID`, não um secret: o ID sai no HTML de toda página).
  Preview de PR, build de fork e `npm run dev` ficam sem analytics — de propósito, para não sujar a
  propriedade nem medir o desenvolvedor.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Analytics
text:
- Não troque o componente do `@next/third-parties` por um `<script>` na mão: o snippet do Google é
  síncrono e bloqueia o parser; o componente usa `next/script` com `afterInteractive` e cuida da
  deduplicação entre navegações client-side do App Router.

head: CLAUDE.md — direções para agentes > Analytics
text:
- **Google Search Console: a verificação é por DNS**, propriedade de *domínio*, com TXT no
  Cloudflare — não depende de deploy nem de arquivo no `out/`. `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION`
  (que vira `metadata.verification.google` no layout) é o plano B para quem só tem propriedade de
  prefixo de URL. As duas variáveis estão documentadas no `.env.example`.

head: CLAUDE.md > What ATHENA is
text: ATHENA is a fully offline, privacy-first voice assistant (no cloud, telemetry, or API keys; zero runtime Python) that chains speech-to-text → LLM → text-to-speech entirely in C++ on a single consumer GPU plus large system RAM. The pipeline:

head: CLAUDE.md > What ATHENA is
text: - **STT + LLM**: `whisper-talk-llama` (a patched whisper.cpp `talk-llama`) captures the mic (SDL2), transcribes with Whisper `small.en`, and runs the **Qwen3.5-397B-A17B** MoE chat model *in-process* (its routed experts offloaded to system RAM via `--cpu-moe`). It also does Silero VAD, prosodic endpointing, emotion2vec emotion tagging, barge-in, and cross-session memory.

head: CLAUDE.md > What ATHENA is
text: - **TTS**: `talk-llama` streams generated assistant sentences to a trigger file; the `orpheus-speak` daemon reads them, asks a local `llama-server` (hosting the **Orpheus-3B** GGUF) for SNAC audio tokens over HTTP/SSE, decodes them to PCM with the **SNAC 24 kHz ONNX** vocoder, and plays via `aplay`.

head: CLAUDE.md > What ATHENA is
text: **Three processes run concurrently**, all started by `launch-athena-397b.sh`: `llama-server` (Orpheus TTS backend, port 8080), `orpheus-speak` (SNAC decoder/player), and `whisper-talk-llama` (STT+LLM, run in the foreground/blocking). `speak-daemon.sh` is **not** a launched process — it is only registered as `talk-llama`'s `-s` speak handler and stays dormant because the active path is `--stream-file` (see gotchas).

head: CLAUDE.md > What ATHENA is
text: > Two LLMs run at once. `llama-server` on :8080 serves **only** Orpheus TTS. The conversational Qwen model runs **inside** `whisper-talk-llama`, not over HTTP.

head: CLAUDE.md > Model file layout note
text: All model files live **flat in `models/`**, including the five Qwen shards (`Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-UD-Q3_K_XL-0000{1..5}-of-00005.gguf`). `launch-athena-397b.sh:29` previously pointed `QWEN_MODEL` at a nonexistent `models/QWEN-3.5-397B/` subdirectory, which made the preflight loop (`launch-athena-397b.sh:636-638`) abort every launch (see the failed run in `athena.log` at 2026-06-30 14:44:26). That path has been corrected to `models/Qwen3.5-...-00001-of-00005.gguf`; if you relocate the shards into a subdir, update `QWEN_MODEL` to match.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build commands
text: ATHENA actually depends on exactly two compiled binaries (`llama-server`, `whisper-talk-llama`) plus its own `orpheus-speak`. All the other `llama-*`/`whisper-*`/test binaries the CMake builds produce are unused byproducts.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build commands
text:
**1. llama.cpp** (produces `llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server`):
```bash
cd /home/user/ATHENA/llama.cpp
cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="120a;86" \
  -DGGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS=OFF -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON -DGGML_CUDA_F16=ON \
  -DGGML_SCHED_MAX_COPIES=1 -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DGGML_LTO=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_UI=OFF
cmake --build build -j 12
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Build commands
text:
**2. whisper.cpp with the custom talk-llama** (produces `whisper.cpp/build/bin/whisper-talk-llama`). The FIVE custom files MUST be copied in **before** configuring (see the `patches/talk-llama/` layout note above):
```bash
cd /home/user/ATHENA/whisper.cpp
cp ../patches/talk-llama/* examples/talk-llama/
cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="120a;86" \
  -DONNXRUNTIME_ROOT=/home/user/ATHENA/onnxruntime-linux-x64-gpu_cuda12-1.27.0 \
  -DGGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS=OFF -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON -DGGML_CUDA_F16=ON \
  -DGGML_SCHED_MAX_COPIES=1 -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DGGML_LTO=ON -DWHISPER_SDL2=ON \
  -DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j 12
```
`-DONNXRUNTIME_ROOT` enables emotion2vec (defines `ATHENA_EMOTION_ORT=1`); `-DWHISPER_SDL2=ON` enables mic capture. `whisper-talk-llama` bundles its **own** full copy of the llama sources (`examples/talk-llama/llama*.cpp`) — it does not link `libllama` or depend on the `llama.cpp/build` tree.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build commands
text:
**3. orpheus-speak** (produces `orpheus/build/orpheus-speak`):
```bash
cd /home/user/ATHENA/orpheus
cmake -B build -DONNXRUNTIME_ROOT=/home/user/ATHENA/onnxruntime-linux-x64-gpu_cuda12-1.27.0 \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
```
`-DONNXRUNTIME_ROOT` is mandatory (`CMakeLists.txt` FATAL_ERRORs without it). The ORT `.so` is resolved at runtime via a RUNPATH baked into the binary — moving/renaming the onnxruntime dir breaks the binary unless rebuilt. `cmake --install` is broken (the `install()` rule references a nonexistent `speak.sh`); the project is always run in-place from `build/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build commands
text: ONNX Runtime is **never built** — it is a prebuilt tarball extracted in place.

head: CLAUDE.md > Running ATHENA
text: The **desktop icon path differs materially** from a direct shell run: the `Athena 397B.desktop` Exec line is the **only** place `GGML_CUDA_NO_PINNED=1` and `ATHENA_MPS=1` are set. A direct `./launch-athena-397b.sh` gets neither (no MPS, pinned memory on).

head: CLAUDE.md > Running ATHENA
text: Inspecting individual pieces: the binaries can be run standalone, e.g. `orpheus/build/orpheus-speak --watch <trigger> --snac <snac.onnx> --play "aplay -q" --stream-tts -v`, or single-shot `orpheus-speak [opts] "text to speak"` (→ `/dev/shm/orpheus_tts.wav`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together)
text: Main flow (`launch-athena-397b.sh`, bottom of file): `setup_gpu_performance` → `start_mps` (must precede any GPU proc so all inherit `CUDA_MPS_*`) → `setup_system_performance` → `setup_audio` → preflight `check_file` for all binaries + models (incl. all 5 Qwen shards) → start GPU telemetry sampler → launch `llama-server` and poll `/health` → launch `orpheus-speak` → launch `whisper-talk-llama` in the **foreground** (blocking). `trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM` + `set -e -E` with an ERR trap.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together)
text:
**Process 1 — Orpheus TTS server** (PID_LLAMA):
```
stdbuf -oL -eL llama-server -m <orpheus GGUF> \
  -c 13824 -np 2 -ngl 99 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 \
  --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --cache-ram 0 -fa on -t 0
```
Readiness: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/health` (polled up to ~60 s; failure aborts launch). `-np 2` + continuous batching give parallel TTS slots (was `-np 4`; single-user needs no more, and it halves peak concurrent-decode / MPS stream count — CHANGES.MD §10). `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT` is **no longer set** (see gotchas).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together)
text:
**Process 2 — orpheus-speak** (PID_ORPHEUS):
```
orpheus-speak --watch <speak_tts.txt> --snac <snac24_dynamic_fp16.onnx> \
  --play "aplay -q" --stream-tts --diag -v --capture-dir <run_dir>/tts-capture
```
SNAC runs on CUDA device 0 (~1.7 GB VRAM; `--snac-cpu` forces CPU). `--diag` is omitted when `ATHENA_DIAG=0`; `--capture-dir` is omitted when `ATHENA_TTS_CAPTURE=0` (see *TTS garble-diagnosis capture* below).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together)
text:
**Process 3 — whisper-talk-llama** (foreground), pinned to cores 0-15:
```
taskset -c 0-15 whisper-talk-llama \
  -ml <Qwen shard 00001-of-00005> -mw <ggml-small.en.bin> \
  --ctx-size 80000 --mlock --no-mmap --cpu-moe -t 16 -ngl 99 -ctk bf16 -ctv bf16 -fa \
  --temp 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.00 --presence-penalty 1.5 --repeat-penalty 1.0 \
  --reasoning off -s <speak-daemon.sh> -sf <speakfile.temp> --stream-file <speak_tts.txt> \
  --barge-in --barge-rms 0.0020 --barge-ratio 1.5 --barge-ms 150 --barge-blackout-ms 200 \
  <memory args> -p Igor -bn Athena -mt 256 -vms 25000 \
  --vad-engine silero --vad-model <ggml-silero-v6.2.0.bin> --vad-last-ms 400 --vad-window-ms 700 \
  --endpoint --endpoint-short-ms 800 --endpoint-long-ms 800 --endpoint-f0-fall 60 \
  --endpoint-extend-ms 1200 --endpoint-f0-rise 50 --endpoint-energy-rise 0.5 \
  --endpoint-energy-decay 4.0 --silero-min-run-ms 100 --silero-debug -pe
```
Dense/attention layers on GPU (`-ngl 99`); routed MoE experts on CPU and page-locked in host RAM (`--cpu-moe --no-mmap --mlock`, ~161 GiB resident). Qwen KV must be **bf16** — a quantized KV degraded output. Memory args are added only when `MEMORY_DIR` is set: `--memory <dir> --memory-words 2048 --time-refresh-min 15`, plus a `--personality-reflect-every 1` (`launch-athena-397b.sh:777`) — the latter is a **temporary demo edit** (lowers the personality-revision threshold to 10 so one session can fire a revision); drop the flag to revert to default behavior.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together)
text: `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT` is **no longer set** on any process (CHANGES.MD §10 C1). It was previously an inline prefix on `llama-server` and `whisper-talk-llama`; it is an experimental multi-stream/buffer-reuse CUDA path with a known buffer-reuse race (the "unspecified launch failure" class) and no measurable benefit, so it was removed. Base CUDA graphs (`-DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON`) + kernel fusion stay on and self-disable at batch>1.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together) > Ports, sockets, and the TTS handoff protocol
text: The only TCP endpoint is `llama-server` on `127.0.0.1:8080` (`/health`, `/completion` SSE). `orpheus-speak`'s connection to :8080 is a **compiled-in default** (`--api http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion`), not passed by the launcher. The only other socket is the CUDA MPS control pipe `/tmp/nvidia-mps/control` (unrelated to TTS).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together) > Ports, sockets, and the TTS handoff protocol
text: The TTS handoff is **file-based** (regular files + atomic `mv` + inotify + a polling `.done` sentinel) — not a named pipe or socket. Files (launcher paths, all under `/home/user/ATHENA/`):

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together) > TTS garble-diagnosis capture
text:
`orpheus-speak` has built-in (pure-C++, no Python) instrumentation for root-causing the intermittent TTS **garble**. `ATHENA_TTS_CAPTURE` (**default 1**) makes the launcher pass `--capture-dir <run_dir>/tts-capture`, dumping per TTS session: `.tokens` (raw model output), `.codes` (parsed audio codes, re-decodable), `.wav` (live decoded audio), `.meta`. Each session writes a few MB of WAV — set `ATHENA_TTS_CAPTURE=0` to disable. Two offline subcommands (each runs and exits):
```bash
# re-decode captured codes with a contention-free CPU reference
orpheus-speak --snac <snac24_dynamic_fp16.onnx> --snac-cpu --decode-codes <sess>.codes   # → <sess>.codes.redecode.wav
# correlation/RMS verdict between two WAVs (clean ≈0.999 MATCH; garble craters it → MISMATCH)
orpheus-speak --compare-wav <sess>.wav <sess>.codes.redecode.wav
```
MATCH ⇒ the codes/model are the fault; MISMATCH ⇒ the on-GPU SNAC decode corrupted the audio under contention. (The 20260630-230402 run's audio was 100% clean — no garble recurred under MPS.) The end-of-run crash there was a **GPU/GSP fault**, not garble — see the GSP gotcha below. A watchdog/auto-restart supervisor was designed but deferred (CHANGES.MD §10); `talk-llama` now at least fails **safe** on a GPU loss (brain-resilience, below) rather than aborting.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together) > GPU / model assumptions
text: Target platform (baked into comments/values): **Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `6.17.0-1028-oem`) on a ThinkPad P16 Gen 3 — Intel Core Ultra 9 285HX (24 cores, no SMT), 192 GB DDR5-4000, single NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell Laptop 24 GB. VRAM is tight (~19 of 24 GB used). The 192 GB RAM requirement comes from the MoE experts living in host RAM under `--cpu-moe`. Qwen decode is bound by memory bandwidth (~6.4 tok/s), not GPU. Both CUDA builds target `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120a;86` (Blackwell sm_120a + Ampere).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (how the launcher wires it together) > Diagnostics
text: `ATHENA_DIAG=1` (default) creates `athena-diag/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>/` and spawns `athena-gpu-monitor.sh <run_dir> 1000` (1 Hz; §13a: each stream is now ONE persistent `nvidia-smi --loop-ms`, not a spawn-per-sample, to avoid UVM va-space churn) writing `gpu.csv`, `gpu-proc.log`, `gpu-throttle.log`, `xid.log`, `kmsg-full.log` (unfiltered kernel log — oops/panic backtraces, §11 F2), `power-state.log`; `llama-server` output → `orpheus-server.log`. A prior kernel panic is harvested into `athena-diag/crash-<ts>/` on the next launch. `ATHENA_DIAG=0` disables all of it (server output → `/dev/null`). Much of the GPU tuning and these knobs exist to chase a recurring NVIDIA **Xid 69** fault at the ~95 W power wall; `ATHENA_LOCK_MEMCLK`, `ATHENA_GPU_POWER_LIMIT`, `ATHENA_GPU_CLOCK_CAP`, `ATHENA_MPS` are off-by-default A/B levers. `demo-rec-start.sh`/`demo-rec-stop.sh` are an independent PulseAudio screen-recording tap, never invoked by the launcher.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (non-obvious)
text: - **Memory persistence requires a graceful spoken "Goodbye Athena".** That triggers a ~20-30 s Qwen memory-consolidation generation. **Ctrl+C does NOT write memory** (SIGTERM arrives first). Cleanup order is load-bearing: orpheus-speak and llama-server are killed first (5 s grace each), `talk-llama` **last** with a 60 s grace — a SIGKILL mid-decode under MPS (with ~161 GiB pinned host RAM) was observed to corrupt kernel page state.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (non-obvious)
text: - **`ATHENA_MPS=1` does not guarantee MPS actually engages.** `start_mps` (`launch-athena-397b.sh`) previously treated a merely *existing* `/tmp/nvidia-mps/control` pipe as "daemon already up" and returned without starting one — so a **stale** pipe left by a prior daemon that died without cleanup (a SIGKILLed `talk-llama`; the reuse path also "will NOT stop it on exit") made every subsequent launch silently run **without** MPS, the three GPU clients time-slicing one context. Both 2026-06-30 demo runs hit this despite the desktop icon setting `ATHENA_MPS=1`. Fixed (see `CHANGES.MD` §7): `start_mps` now liveness-probes the pipe (`get_default_active_thread_percentage | timeout 5 nvidia-cuda-mps-control`) and clears/rebuilds a stale one. **Diagnostic tell:** an **empty `mps-log/`** in the run's diag dir (and no `nvidia-cuda-mps-server` in `gpu-proc.log`) means MPS did **not** run — a daemon this launcher owns writes into `mps-log/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (non-obvious)
text: - **MPS needs `/usr/sbin` on PATH.** The MPS *server* (`nvidia-cuda-mps-server`) ships in `/usr/sbin`, which some shells/distros omit from the interactive user PATH — so the control daemon can't exec it and every server dies `exited with status 1` (empty `mps-log/server.log`), leaving clients with `MPS client failed to connect ...`; llama-server then falls back to CPU while orpheus-speak's SNAC CUDA-EP `CreateSession` fails. Fixed (see `CHANGES.MD` §9): `start_mps` prepends `/usr/sbin` to PATH, then **self-checks** that a server actually spawns (`start_server -uid $(id -u)` + `get_server_list`) and falls back to no-MPS if not. orpheus-speak also now retries SNAC on the **CPU EP** if the CUDA session fails (prints the real ORT error) instead of exiting. **Diagnostic tell:** `Server N exited with status 1` in `mps-log/control.log` = the server can't launch.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (non-obvious)
text: - **The five `patches/talk-llama/` files must be copied into `examples/talk-llama/` before `cmake` configure** (`cp patches/talk-llama/* whisper.cpp/examples/talk-llama/`). An upstream sync or `git checkout .` erases them; the patched CMakeLists is required even on current master (upstream's own drops the emotion2vec wiring, and ATHENA's pre-DSA one fails to link there).

Its `SPEAK_FILE`/`TRIGGER_FILE`/`DONE_FILE` vars must stay in sync with the launcher's (lines 87-89) — they previously omitted the `/ATHENA/` segment, which would have made the legacy `-s/-sf` path silently exit on a missing file; they have since been corrected to match, and its comment block refreshed from the old `QWEN-3.5-9B` example to the current 397B setup.

text: - ONNX Runtime GPU requires the **full cuDNN 9.x** (not JIT, which adds runtime latency); ensure `/etc/ld.so.conf` includes the ORT lib path + `sudo ldconfig`, or the CUDA EP is unavailable.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas (non-obvious)
text: - Qwen is a 5-shard split GGUF; the launcher passes only shard `00001-of-00005` to `-ml` and llama loads the rest, so a missing later shard fails minutes into load — preflight explicitly checks all 5.
