head: CLAUDE.md
text:
Agent instructions for ExFig - a CLI tool that exports colors, typography, icons, and images from Figma to iOS, Android,
and Flutter projects.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Context
text:
| Aspect          | Details                                                                                            |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Language        | Swift 6.3, macOS 13.0+                                                                             |
| Package Manager | Swift Package Manager                                                                              |
| CLI Framework   | swift-argument-parser                                                                              |
| Config Format   | PKL (Programmable, Scalable, Safe)                                                                 |
| Templates       | Jinja2 (swift-jinja)                                                                               |
| Required Env    | `FIGMA_PERSONAL_TOKEN`                                                                             |
| Tooling         | mise (`./bin/mise` self-contained), swiftly (Swift toolchain management via `.swift-version`)      |
| Platforms       | macOS 13+ (primary), Linux/Ubuntu 22.04, Windows (Swift 6.3) - see `.claude/rules/linux-compat.md` |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: Twelve modules in `Sources/`:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
| Module          | Purpose                                                   |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ExFigCLI`      | CLI commands, loaders, file I/O, terminal UI              |
| `ExFigCore`     | Domain models (Color, Image, TextStyle), processors       |
| `ExFigConfig`   | PKL config parsing, evaluation, type bridging             |
| `ExFig-iOS`     | iOS platform plugin (ColorsExporter, IconsExporter, etc.) |
| `ExFig-Android` | Android platform plugin                                   |
| `ExFig-Flutter` | Flutter platform plugin                                   |
| `ExFig-Web`     | Web platform plugin                                       |
| `XcodeExport`   | iOS export (.xcassets, Swift extensions)                  |
| `AndroidExport` | Android export (XML resources, Compose, Vector Drawables) |
| `FlutterExport` | Flutter export (Dart code, SVG/PNG assets)                |
| `WebExport`     | Web/React export (CSS variables, JSX icons)               |
| `JinjaSupport`  | Shared Jinja2 template rendering across Export modules    |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
**Data flow:** CLI -> PKL config parsing -> FigmaAPI fetch -> ExFigCore processing -> Platform plugin -> Export module -> File write
**Alt flows:** tokens (.tokens.json → TokensFileSource), penpot (PenpotAPI → Penpot*Source)
**MCP:** `exfig mcp` → StdioTransport → tool handlers. `OutputMode.mcp` routes all output to stderr.
**Batch mode:** Single `@TaskLocal` via `BatchSharedState` actor — see `ExFigCLI/CLAUDE.md`.
**Parallelism:** All exporters use `parallelMapEntries()` (max 5 concurrent) — see `ExFigCore/CLAUDE.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Conventions
text:
| Area            | Use                                   | Instead of                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| JSON parsing    | `JSONCodec` (swift-yyjson)            | `JSONDecoder`/`JSONEncoder`           |
| JSON DOM access | `JSONCodec.parseValue(from:)`         | `JSONSerialization` / `import YYJSON` |
| Terminal UI     | Noora (`NooraUI`, `TerminalText`)     | Rainbow color methods                 |
| Terminal output | `TerminalUI` facade                   | Direct `print()` calls                |
| README.md       | Keep compact (~80 lines, pain-driven) | Detailed docs (use CONFIG.md / DocC)  |

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Conventions
text:
**Documentation:** README is short. Detailed docs in DocC articles (`Sources/ExFigCLI/ExFig.docc/`).
`docs/` is DocC OUTPUT (gitignored) — never put source docs there.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: Enu is a 3D sandbox environment for creating and exploring voxel worlds using a Logo-inspired programming API. It's built with Nim and the Godot game engine (v3.5), enabling users to program interactive 3D environments using Nim scripts that run in the Nim VM.

head: CLAUDE.md > Voice of Official Content
text:
This applies to bots, signs, and narration in the levels *we* ship (the course,
tutorials, demos) — not to player projects, which have their own voice.

head: CLAUDE.md > Voice of Official Content
text:
The bots of Enu are **friendly, earnest, and — put kindly — not very bright.**
They mean well, they're glad you're here, and they get things charmingly wrong:
mangling a story they love, muddling their own plan, chasing a goal that makes
no sense, always with total sincerity. Write them that way on purpose.

head: CLAUDE.md > Voice of Official Content
text:
- **Confidently wrong beats blandly correct.** Let them misremember, over-explain,
  and contradict themselves between lines. An occasional flash of accidental
  insight is welcome; keep most of it fond and foolish.

head: CLAUDE.md > Voice of Official Content
text:
- **Vary the understanding a lot.** Across a bot's lines its grasp of the
  situation should swing wildly — that variance is the joke.

head: CLAUDE.md > Voice of Official Content
text:
- **Kind, never mean.** The player is the competent one; the bots are the
  endearing mess they're helping. The joke is never at the player's expense.

head: CLAUDE.md > Voice of Official Content
text:
- **Own the mistakes.** Non sequiturs and confident nonsense are the charm, not
  bugs to sand off.

head: CLAUDE.md > Voice of Official Content
text:
Why this is the house style, not an accident: it keeps the world warm and
low-stakes so a new player feels safe poking at things; increasingly these bots
will be driven by small local language models we shouldn't expect too much from,
so rather than hide the seams we lean into them; and, frankly, it makes us happy.
Overall theme: broken-but-well-intentioned robots and AI, helpful in spite of
themselves.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build Commands > Do it the normal way
text:
Prefer the standard, supported path over hand-wiring. Builds, submodules, setup,
and dependency management go through the built-in `nim`/`atlas` tasks (`nim
prereqs`, `nim build`, `nim import_assets`, `atlas install`, ...). Don't shell out
to `scons`, hand-`git clone` submodules, or symlink/copy prebuilt artifacts (the
Godot binary, `deps/`, `vmlib/stdlib`, `app/.import`, ...) from another checkout
to skip a step — those shortcuts drift from what real users and CI do, hide build
breakage, and entangle checkouts. Lock files are regenerated by their tool, never
edited by hand. Deviate only for a specific, stated reason, and prefer fixing the
task over working around it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Casing Conventions
text: This project follows Ruby-like casing conventions. Nim is style-insensitive for identifiers (ignoring case and underscores), so these are style guidelines rather than compiler requirements:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Casing Conventions
text: - **Types**: `UpperCamelCase` (e.g., `VoxelRenderer`, `GameState`, `Build`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Casing Conventions
text: - **Enum values**: `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` (e.g., `ERASER`, `BLUE`, `CODE_MODE`, `PLAYING`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Casing Conventions
text: - **Constants**: `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` (e.g., `CHUNK_DIM`, `ACTION_COLORS`, `IR_BLACK`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Casing Conventions
text: - **Everything else**: `snake_case` (procs, variables, fields, parameters, etc.)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Casing Conventions
text: - **Third-party identifiers starting with lowercase**: use `snake_case` (e.g., `writeVu64` → `write_vu64`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Casing Conventions
text: Only use `lowerCamelCase` when `snake_case` doesn't work, which should only happen with third-party macros that don't properly normalize identifiers.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Additional Coding Style Rules
text: 1. **Naming Conventions:** Never use `camelCase` for Nim code. Enu strictly uses `snake_case` for everything (variables, procs, types in some parts, but standard Nim types are strictly `PascalCase`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Additional Coding Style Rules
text: 2. **Exceptions:** Do not use `newException(ExceptionType, "msg")`. Use the helper method `ExceptionType.init("msg")` (e.g., `ValueError.init("Circular dependency detected")`).

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 1. Project Identity
text:
**Purpose**: A multilingual programming language where code can be written in any of 17 natural
languages. The long-term direction is a human-language-first semantic platform
for AI-native, multimodal, reactive, concurrent, and distributed programming.
The current repository implements a transitional compiler/runtime stack toward
that goal. Keywords, operators, and builtins are data-driven (JSON), not
hard-coded.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 2. Core Architecture > Key Design Principles
text:
- **Data-driven**: All language-specific knowledge lives in JSON under
  `multilingualprogramming/resources/usm/`. No language keywords are hard-coded in Python.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 2. Core Architecture > Key Design Principles
text:
- **Single AST**: All 17 language frontends produce the same AST node types
  (`multilingualprogramming/parser/ast_nodes.py`).

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 2. Core Architecture > Key Design Principles
text:
- **Semantic-core direction**: the parser output is increasingly bridged into a
  shared semantic IR so the project can grow beyond a historical
  parser-to-backend compiler shape into a fuller Core 1.0 language model.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 2. Core Architecture > Key Design Principles
text:
- **Dual backend**: Python backend (always available) + optional WAT/WASM backend
  (`wasmtime` optional dependency). Smart backend selector lives in
  `multilingualprogramming/runtime/backend_selector.py`.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 2. Core Architecture > Key Design Principles
text:
- **Surface normalization**: Alternate keyword forms (e.g., Spanish iterable-first, Japanese
  variants) are normalized by `multilingualprogramming/parser/surface_normalizer.py` before
  parsing.

text:
- **Strategic vision**: Multilingual 1.0 as a human-language-first semantic
  platform for AI, multimodal, reactive, concurrent, and distributed programs.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 4. Universal Semantic Model (USM) > `resources/usm/keywords.json`
text:
- Each concept can have **multiple keyword forms** per language (multi-word keywords as both

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 4. Universal Semantic Model (USM) > `resources/usm/keywords.json`
text:
- Keyword categories: compound statements (COND_IF, LOOP_WHILE, LOOP_FOR, FUNC_DEF, CLASS_DEF,
  TRY, MATCH, WITH), simple statements (LET, CONST, RETURN, YIELD, RAISE, IMPORT, PASS, BREAK,
  CONTINUE, DELETE, ASSERT, GLOBAL, NONLOCAL), callables (PRINT, INPUT), logical (AND, OR, NOT,
  NOT_IN, IN, IS, IS_NOT), type keywords (TYPE_INT, TYPE_FLOAT, TYPE_STR, TYPE_BOOL, TYPE_LIST,
  TYPE_DICT), boolean literals (TRUE, FALSE), and more.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 5. Pipeline Deep-Dive > Lexer (`lexer/lexer.py`)
text:
- **Greedy multi-word matching**: tries up to 3 consecutive tokens as a single keyword.
  Both space-separated (`"not in"`) and underscore-joined (`"not_in"`) forms are recognized.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 5. Pipeline Deep-Dive > Lexer (`lexer/lexer.py`)
text:
- **Unicode operators**: `×`, `÷`, `−`, `≠`, `≤`, `≥`, `→`, fullwidth brackets, CJK corner
  brackets `「」`, guillemets `«»`, smart quotes, etc.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 6. WAT / WASM Backend > WAT Generator (`codegen/wat_generator.py`)
text:
| Construct | WAT support |
|---|---|
| Variable declaration/assignment | ✓ |
| Arithmetic (+, -, *, /) | ✓ (f64) |
| Augmented assignment (+=, -=, *=, /=, //=, %=) | ✓ native f64 arithmetic |
| Augmented assignment (&=, \|=, ^=, <<=, >>=) | ✓ i32 round-trip |
| Augmented assignment (**=) | ✓ via `call $pow_f64` host import (`Math.pow` in JS) |
| Comparisons | ✓ |
| Boolean logic | ✓ |
| `if` / `elif` / `else` | ✓ |
| `while` loop | ✓ |
| `for` loop over `range()` | ✓ |
| `for` loop over list/tuple variable | ✓ index-based using linear-memory list header |
| Function definition | ✓ |
| `async def` / `await` | ✓ best-effort (`async def` = regular WAT func; `await` evaluates operand) |
| `return` | ✓ |
| Class definition (OOP) | ✓ (see §7) |
| Inheritance | ✓ (see §8) |
| `match`/`case` (numeric/boolean patterns) | ✓ lowered to WAT block + nested if |
| `match`/`case` (string patterns) | ✓ interned-offset `f64.eq` comparison (compile-time strings only) |
| `match`/`case` (`None` pattern) | ✓ `f64.eq` with `f64.const 0` |
| `match`/`case` (capture variable `case x:`) | ✓ binds subject to local, always matches |
| `match`/`case` (tuple/list literal patterns) | ✓ element-wise `f64.eq` + length check (list/tuple subject only) |
| `match`/`case` (class/complex patterns) | stub comment |
| `print` | ✓ (host import) |
| `abs` | ✓ native `f64.abs` |
| `min(a,b,…)` n-arg | ✓ chained `f64.min` |
| `max(a,b,…)` n-arg | ✓ chained `f64.max` |
| `len(str_literal)` / `len(str_var)` | ✓ compile-time byte length / parallel length local |
| `len(list_var)` / `len(tuple_var)` | ✓ loaded from list/tuple header in linear memory |
| List/tuple literal allocation | ✓ heap bump-allocator; layout = [len_f64, elem0, elem1, …] |
| `list[i]` / `tuple[i]` index read | ✓ `f64.load` at `base + 8 + i*8` |
| `try/except/finally` | ✓ numeric exception-code model: `raise` stores a non-zero f64 code; `except ExcType` matches that code; `except:` / `except Exception:` catch any non-zero code; `finally` runs unconditionally (emitted on both the unhandled path before `unreachable` and the normal/handled path after the handler block); `as e` binds the actual exception code |
| `with` statement | ✓ best-effort (body executed; `__enter__`/`__exit__` not callable from WAT) |
| Lambda expressions | ✓ lifted to WAT functions; stored as table index (f64); called via `call_indirect` |
| List/generator comprehension over `range` | ✓ lowered to WAT loop + f64 accumulator |
| List/generator comprehension over list variable | ✓ index-based loop + f64 accumulator |
| Other comprehensions | stub comment (dynamic collections not representable as f64) |
| String concatenation (`+`) | ✓ compile-time (both literals) → interned; runtime → `$__str_concat` heap helper |
| String indexing (`s[i]`) | ✓ `i32.load8_u` → char code as f64 |
| String slicing (`s[a:b]`) | ✓ `$__str_slice` heap copy helper |
| `async for` over `range()` / list var | ✓ best-effort (same lowering as sync `for`) |
| `async with` | ✓ best-effort (same lowering as sync `with`) |
| `async for` over other iterables | not supported |
| `input()` | ✓ reads a line from WASI fd 0 (stdin), strips trailing CR/LF, returns as f64 string pointer; `$__last_str_len` is set |
| `argc()` | ✓ builtin returning the WASI argument count as f64 |
| `argv(i)` | ✓ builtin returning the i-th WASI argument as f64 string pointer; `$__last_str_len` is set |
| DOM manipulation | ✓ conditional `"env"` host imports emitted when any DOM builtin is used; WAT wrapper functions for `dom_get`, `dom_text`, `dom_html`, `dom_value`, `dom_attr`, `dom_create`, `dom_append`, `dom_style`, `dom_remove`, `dom_class` |
| Source location comments | ✓ `;;  @line:col` WAT comment emitted at the top of each compiled statement when source position is available |

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 13. Known Issues & Gotchas > SemanticAnalyzer — Augmented Assignment on Undefined Variable
text:
Augmented assignment (`x += 1`) correctly reports `UNDEFINED_NAME` when the target variable has
not been previously defined. Plain assignment (`x = 1`) implicitly defines the variable (Python
semantics).

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 13. Known Issues & Gotchas > Lexer INDENT/DEDENT Inside Brackets
text:
The lexer emits INDENT and DEDENT tokens even inside bracket pairs (unlike CPython, which
suppresses them). Any parser method that handles multi-line constructs inside brackets
**must** call `_skip_bracket_newlines()` rather than `_skip_newlines()`.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 13. Known Issues & Gotchas > WAT `min`/`max` — n-arg Supported
text:
The WAT backend lowers `min(a, b, c, …)` and `max(a, b, c, …)` to chained `f64.min` /
`f64.max` for any number of arguments ≥ 1.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 13. Known Issues & Gotchas > `super()` in WAT — Guard Ordering
text:
The `super()` detection guard in `_gen_stmt()` and `_gen_expr()` **must run first** before
the generic CallExpr branch. If you add new statement/expression types, insert them after
the super() guard or ensure the guard still runs first.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 13. Known Issues & Gotchas > Concept Count in Tests
text:
`tests/keyword_registry_test.py` has a hardcoded assertion on the number of concepts (50).
When adding a new concept to `keywords.json`, **update this count** or the test will fail.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Agent Guide for `multilingual` > 13. Known Issues & Gotchas > WASM Execution Tests Requiring `rustc`
text:
2 tests in `WATInheritanceWasmExecutionTestSuite` are skipped because they require the
`rustc` compiler with the `wasm32` target installed. This is expected — they are marked as
skipped in the test report.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Critical Rules for Content
text: These rules MUST be followed when editing or creating skills:

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Critical Rules for Content
text: 1. **Slash commands are a subset of Skills** — never list them as a separate category. They are the same mechanism.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Critical Rules for Content
text: 2. **Three automation mechanisms only**: Hooks, Skills, Sub Agents. Agent Teams are NOT a fourth mechanism — they are architecturally distinct (separate full Claude instances) and always flagged as experimental.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Critical Rules for Content
text: 3. **Worktrees are an isolation layer**, not a coordination mechanism. They provide git-level isolation for parallel work.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Critical Rules for Content
text: 4. **Agent Teams are experimental** — always flag them with ⚠️ and note they may change.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Critical Rules for Content
text: 5. **The onboarding skill is interactive**, not a reference dump. It walks users through setup step by step. The ask skill answers questions by reading reference docs.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Critical Rules for Content
text: 6. **IKEA analogy**: Hooks = assembly events (they fire during the process), Skills = packages with instruction sheets (reusable, pre-written), Sub Agents = packages + a handyperson (delegate and they deliver).

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Critical Rules for Content
text: 7. **Difficulty tiers** — Every reference doc has a `> **Level: 🌱/🌿/🌳**` badge after the title. Sections that differ from the file's overall level get an emoji prefix on the `##` heading. Only tag sections that differ — don't repeat the file-level tag on every heading.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Versioning
text: The authoritative plugin version lives in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (`"version": "X.Y.Z"`). The `marketplace.json` plugin entry also has a `version` field — **`plugin.json` takes priority**, but keep both in sync to avoid confusion.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Versioning > Why bumping matters
text: Installed plugins are cached at `~/.claude/plugins/cache`. **Version is the cache key** — if you change code but don't bump the version, users won't see the update. Always bump the version when shipping changes.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Versioning > Semantic versioning
text:
| Change type | Bump | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Major** (X) | Breaking changes, structural redesigns | Removing a skill, renaming hook events, changing game-data schema incompatibly |
| **Minor** (Y) | New features, new reference docs, new hook behaviors | Adding a skill, adding a tracking category, new reference doc |
| **Patch** (Z) | Bug fixes, wording tweaks, small improvements | Fixing a regex in a hook script, typo in a reference doc, adjusting a case branch |

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Deployment

The docs website is served by **Cloudflare Pages** (native Git integration) on
`claude-code-guide.org` — Cloudflare clones the repo, runs the Jekyll build, and
serves the result. **There is no deploy workflow in the repo**; the Pages project
and custom domain are provisioned out-of-band (via the `cultureflare` CLI / its
`cf-pages-project-create.sh` + `cf-pages-domain-add.sh`).

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Deployment
text:
The build is **advanced-mode Pages**: a root `_worker.js` intercepts every
request to serve agent-readable markdown. The moving parts must stay in lockstep:

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Deployment
text:
- `_plugins/llm_markdown.rb` — at build time, writes a `.md` twin of every
  content page (and a concatenated `llms-full.txt`). Its `twin_relpath` path
  scheme is the source of truth.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Deployment
text:
- `_worker.js` — serves a page's `.md` twin on `Accept: text/markdown` or an
  explicit `.md` URL, and maps `/` → `/llms.txt`. Its `markdownTwin()` **must
  match** the plugin's `twin_relpath`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Deployment
text:
- `_includes/head_custom.html` — emits `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
  pointing at the same twin URL.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Deployment
text: - `_redirects` + `404.md` — catch-all that returns a real 404.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Deployment
text:
- `_config.yml` `include:` — force-copies the underscore-prefixed `_worker.js`
  and `_redirects` into the build root (Jekyll skips `_`-files otherwise).

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Deployment
text:
If you change the twin path scheme, change it in all three of `llm_markdown.rb`,
`_worker.js`, and `head_custom.html`.

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Git Workflow > After implementing a plan

head: CLAUDE.md — Agent Instructions > Git Workflow > After implementing a plan

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: Requires `uv` and GNU `make`. `make install` always uninstalls first, then installs editable with `GWKOKAB_DEV_BUILD=1`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: Note: `CONTRIBUTING.md` shows `pytest -n auto`, but `pytest-xdist` is not a declared dependency — drop `-n auto` unless you install it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs prek → tests (py3.11 & 3.13) → docs, with `JAX_ENABLE_X64=1`, `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu`, `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_force_host_platform_device_count=4`. CI installs with `uv sync --extra cpu --group dev --group test` and runs `uv run pytest tests`, not `make install`. `pyproject.toml` sets `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]`, so a new warning anywhere in the import chain fails tests; the test job has a 10-minute timeout, so keep new tests CPU-cheap.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - `src/gwkokab/` — the library: NumPyro/JAX population models, likelihoods, selection-function (Poisson mean) estimators, cosmology, parameter algebra.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - `src/gwkokab/analysis/` — the CLI drivers that assemble a full hierarchical inference run from JSON config, plus `inference_io` (Pydantic config parsing).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - `src/gwkokab_scripts/` — standalone post-hoc utility CLIs (plotting, HDF5 surgery, flowMC/NumPyro tuning helpers).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: Every user-facing entry point is a console script declared in `pyproject.toml`'s `[project.scripts]`; there is no `__main__`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The analysis matrix
text: An analysis is the product of three independent axes, composed by multiple inheritance:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The analysis matrix
text: 1. **Model family** (`analysis/<family>/`): `n_pls_m_gs`, `ecc_matters`, `multisource`, `subpopulation`. Each has a `common.py` defining `<Family>Core` with two key properties — `parameters` (the event coordinates read from data) and `model_parameters` (the flat list of population hyper-parameter names).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The analysis matrix
text: 2. **Data representation** (`analysis/core/`): `discrete_base.py` (per-event posterior samples, bucketed) or `analytical_gwalk_base.py` (per-event Gaussian summaries — mean/covariance — resampled). Selected by which module you run: `discrete_<family>` vs `analytical_gwalk_<family>`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The analysis matrix
text: 3. **Sampler backend** (`analysis/core/`): `flowMC_base.py` or `numpyro_base.py`. Chosen *at runtime* from `sampler_cfg.json`'s `sampler_name`, not by the entry point.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The analysis matrix
text: So `analysis/n_pls_m_gs/discrete.py` defines `NPowerlawMGaussianDiscreteAnalysis(NPowerlawMGaussianCore, DiscreteBase)` and then two trivial subclasses that mix in `FlowMCBase` or `NumpyroBase`. The sampler mixin supplies `driver()`; the data-representation base supplies `run()` and `read_data()`. `main()` picks the class after reading the sampler config.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The analysis matrix
text: Likelihoods are picked by `inference/factory.py::get_likelihood_fn(sampler_name, analysis_type)`, which maps the 2×2 to the four modules in `inference/`. Those wrap the pure math in `inference/poissonlikelihood_utils.py` (`discrete_poisson_likelihood_fn` / `analytical_gwalk_poisson_likelihood_fn`): the inhomogeneous-Poisson log-likelihood `-μ(Λ) + Σ_n log Σ_k [p(ω_k|Λ)/π_k]`, with optional variance tapering when `--variance-cut-threshold` is set.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The analysis matrix
text: `AnalysisBase.run()` sequence: `classify_model_parameters()` → `read_data()` → build the Poisson-mean estimator → build `logpdf` via `likelihood_fn` → `driver()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Priors: regex, aliases, constants, lazy
text: `prior_cfg.json` is **not** parameter-name-keyed; keys are regexes matched against `model_parameters` by `analysis/utils/regex.py::match_all`, then processed in `analysis/utils/priors.py::get_processed_priors`. A value can be:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Priors: regex, aliases, constants, lazy
text: - a dict with `"dist"` → an instantiated NumPyro/GWKokab prior (`{"dist": "Uniform", "low": 0.0, "high": 10.0}`),

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Priors: regex, aliases, constants, lazy
text: - a number → a **constant** (frozen with `lax.stop_gradient`, not sampled),

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Priors: regex, aliases, constants, lazy
text: - a string naming another parameter → an **alias** (tied parameter, shares one sampled dimension),

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Priors: regex, aliases, constants, lazy
text: - a dict whose *field values* are strings → a **lazy prior**: becomes a `jax.tree_util.Partial` plus a dependency map, so a prior's hyper-parameters are themselves sampled.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Priors: regex, aliases, constants, lazy
text: `analysis_base.py::_classify_model_parameters` splits these four kinds, topologically sorts lazy dependencies (cycle-checked), and builds either a `JointDistribution` or a `LazyJointDistribution` over the sorted variable names. Sampled dimensions are ordered by `sorted(variables.keys())` — that ordering is what `variables_index` in the output HDF5 records, and it is how chains map back to parameter names.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Priors: regex, aliases, constants, lazy
text: Hyper-parameter names follow `<name>_<component>_<index>`. The component tag is family-specific: `pl`/`g` (power-law, Gaussian) for `n_pls_m_gs` and `ecc_matters`; `spl`/`bpl`/`gpl`/`gg` for `multisource`; `spl`/`bpl`/`gpl` for `subpopulation`. So `alpha_pl_0`, `mmax_pl_1`, `spin_1z_loc_g_0`, `log_rate_2`. `analysis/utils/common.py::expand_arguments` generates the indexed forms.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Configuration I/O
text: Four JSON files, all Pydantic models with `extra="forbid"` (a typo raises `ValidationError` rather than being ignored) — see `analysis/core/inference_io/` and `docs/source/inference_io/`:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Configuration I/O
text:
| Flag | Model | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--data-loader-cfg` | `DiscretePELoader` / `AnalyticalGWalkPELoader` | which event files, how to undo the PE prior |
| `--prior-cfg` | (plain JSON, see above) | population priors |
| `--pmean-cfg` | `PoissonMeanEstimationLoader` | selection function; `estimator_type` ∈ `neural_vt`, `neural_pdet`, `injection`, `custom` |
| `--sampler-cfg` | `SamplerConfig` → `NumpyroGlobalConfig` \| `FlowMCGlobalConfig` | which sampler and all its knobs |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Configuration I/O
text: The `gwk_*_cfg_template` console scripts dump starter versions of these.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Configuration I/O
text: `--pmean-cfg`'s `estimator_type` is a Pydantic discriminator picking one loader in `inference_io/_poisson_mean.py`, whose `get_estimators()` calls into `poisson_mean/`: `neural_vt` → `poisson_mean_from_neural_vt`, `neural_pdet` → `poisson_mean_from_neural_pdet`, `injection` → `poisson_mean_from_sensitivity_injections` (with `far_cut`/`snr_cut`). `custom` loads `python_module_path` by file path and calls its `custom_poisson_mean_estimator(key, parameters, filename, **kwargs)`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Output
text: Everything lands in one HDF5 file named by `analysis/utils/literals.py` (`inference_data.hdf5`): `constants`, `variables_index`, `sampler_cfg/*`, `samples`, and `chains/chain_<n>`. Sampler configs round-trip (`write_to_hdf5` / `read_from_hdf5`), so post-hoc scripts reconstruct the run from the file alone. `gwk_report` executes `analysis/report/template_report.ipynb` through papermill to produce an HTML report.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Models
text: Models are NumPyro `Distribution` subclasses. Central abstraction is `models/utils/_scaledmixture.py::ScaledMixture` — a mixture whose components carry `log_scales` (log rates); the Poisson-mean estimators expect a `ScaledMixture` so rates and shapes are inferred jointly.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Models
text: Hybrid models (`models/hybrids/`) are built compositionally: `_ncombination.py` holds `create_*` factories (one per physical parameter block), which `_npowerlawmgaussian.py`, `_multisource.py`, `_subpopulation.py` combine into a per-component `JointDistribution` and then into a `ScaledMixture`. Adding a physical parameter to a family means touching four places: a `create_*` factory, the `_build_*_distributions` wiring, the family's `model_parameters`/`parameters` properties in `analysis/<family>/common.py`, and its `--add-*` CLI flag in `model_arg_parser`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Models
text: `models/constraints.py` and `models/transformations.py` add custom NumPyro constraints/transforms (mass sandwiches, ordered vectors, mass-coordinate changes) and register them with `biject_to` via `@_transform_to_*` dispatch.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Parameters and coordinate changes
text: `parameters.py` defines the `Parameters` str-enum (imported everywhere as `from gwkokab.parameters import Parameters as P`) and a `RelationMesh`: a rule graph over GW parameters (`(m1, m2) → chirp_mass`, `(chi1, cos_tilt_1) → spin_1z`, `z ↔ luminosity_distance`, …) with a `resolve()` that derives every reachable parameter from whatever is present. That is what backs the `--derive-parameters` flag on the synthetic-data CLIs. Pure formulas live in `utils/transformations.py`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Logging and errors
text: Uses `loguru`, configured in `analysis/utils/logger.py`; CLIs call `log_info(start=True)` before anything else. Raise the auto-logging exceptions from `utils/exceptions.py` (`LoggedValueError`, `LoggedKeyError`, `LoggedTypeError`, `LoggedUserWarning`, …) rather than bare built-ins — they log at error/warning level on construction, with loguru `{}`-style formatting args.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Logging and errors
text: Runtime env vars: `GWKOKAB_LOG_LEVEL` (default `TRACE`), `GWKOKAB_LOG_DIR` (`./logs`), `GWKOKAB_LOG_FILE`, `GWKOKAB_DEBUG` (adds source paths to log lines), `GWKOKAB_DEFAULT_COSMOLOGY` (default `Planck15`), `GWKOKAB_DEV_BUILD` (appends git hash to `__version__`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > End-to-end workflow
text: See `docs/source/examples/ecc_plus_spin/` for a complete worked run: `synthetic_events_<family>` (draw a population) → `synthetic_discrete_pe` or `synthetic_analytical_gwalk_pe` (add measurement error, write per-event files; the error models are `errors.py`'s `banana_error` / `truncated_normal_error` / `mock_spin_error`, wired per-parameter by `synthetic_pe.py::error_function_registry`) → `discrete_<family>` / `analytical_gwalk_<family>` (inference) → `gwk_report`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: `tests/` mirrors `src/` one-to-one (`tests/gwkokab/models/mass/test_models.py` ↔ `src/gwkokab/models/mass/_models.py`). Several packages carry same-named modules, so test basenames collide; `--import-mode=importlib` in `addopts` is what makes that legal — do not drop it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: `tests/conftest.py` calls `numpyro.enable_validation(False)` at import: NumPyro >= 0.22 validates distribution arguments by default, and with `filterwarnings = ["error"]` its out-of-support `log_prob` warning would fail every test that integrates over a grid or mixes components with different supports. Tests that check validation pass `validate_args=True` explicitly.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: Shared fixtures live in five conftests and are worth reusing before writing new setup:

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: - `tests/gwkokab/conftest.py` — `linear_model_file` (writes an HDF5 network that is exactly an affine map, so Poisson means have closed forms), `injections_file`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: - `models/conftest.py` — `pytree_roundtrip` (flatten/unflatten a distribution, i.e. what a `jit`/`vmap` boundary does), `trapz_1d`, `trapz_nd` (normalization checks).

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: - `models/hybrids/conftest.py` — `hyper_parameters`: feed it a family's `core.model_parameters` and get a physically sensible value for every name, keyed by *role* (the part before the component tag), so it stays valid as component counts change. Passing `core.model_parameters` also catches drift between the analysis layer and the model factory.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: - `inference/conftest.py` — `mixture`, `normal_mixture`, `estimator`, `model_factory` (recording doubles), `discrete_data`, `analytical_data`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: - `gwkokab_scripts/conftest.py` — `run_main(main, *argv)` drives a console script's `main()` through a fake `sys.argv`; `samples_file`/`compound_file` fabricate the two `inference_data.hdf5` layouts. Autouse fixtures force the `Agg` backend and isolate pyplot state.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing
text: Style is `pytest.mark.parametrize` plus plain asserts, with `chex` for array/shape assertions in the numerics-heavy files. Because warnings are errors, a dependency that warns at *import* must be pre-imported quietly in a conftest (see the `glasbey` note in `gwkokab_scripts/conftest.py`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - Every source file starts with `# Copyright 2023 The GWKokab Authors` and `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - `__init__.py` re-exports use the explicit `from .x import y as y` form (required for the strict re-export rules the docs/type-checkers rely on). Public modules are also re-exported as `from . import x as x`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - numpydoc-style docstrings; docformatter wraps at 88. Ruff: line length 88, double quotes, isort with `order-by-type = false`, `combine-as-imports`, two blank lines after imports.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - Test files must be named `test_*.py` (enforced by the `name-tests-test` hook).

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `build:`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text: - prek hooks also enforce: HTTPS-only URLs in markdown/yaml, no nested-bracket link pattern (the `no-bracket-links` hook in `prek.toml`), codespell, gitleaks, and JSON-schema validation of workflow/dependabot/readthedocs files.

text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: This is a TypeScript library that provides an easy API for making Server-Sent Events (SSE) requests using the Fetch API. It supports both browsers and Node.js (v18+) and outputs dual-format packages (CommonJS and ESM).

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Commands > Lint
text: While not defined in package.json scripts, ESLint is configured. The project uses:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Flow
text: 1. **Entry Point**: [src/index.ts](src/index.ts) exports the main API from `fetch.ts` and type definitions from `interface.ts`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Flow
text: 2. **Main API**: `fetchEventData()` in [src/fetch.ts](src/fetch.ts) handles the HTTP request and orchestrates SSE parsing

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Flow
text: 3. **Stream Processing**: [src/sse.ts](src/sse.ts) contains the core SSE parsing logic

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > SSE Parsing Pipeline
text: The library uses a two-stage parsing approach:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > SSE Parsing Pipeline
text:
1. **LineDecoder** ([src/sse.ts](src/sse.ts)):
   - Parses byte chunks into SSE line buffers
   - Handles all newline variants: `\n`, `\r`, `\r\n`
   - Maintains internal buffer for incomplete lines across chunks
   - Tracks field length (position of first colon) for each line
   - Critical detail: Handles the optional space character (ASCII 32) after the colon in SSE format

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > SSE Parsing Pipeline
text:
2. **MessageDecoder** ([src/sse.ts](src/sse.ts)):
   - Converts parsed lines into `ServerSentEvent` objects
   - Accumulates multi-line data fields
   - Emits complete events when encountering empty lines
   - Extracts `event` and `data` fields from SSE format

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Text Decoding
text: The library handles text decoding differently based on environment:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Text Decoding
text: - **Node.js**: Uses `Buffer.from(bytes).toString('utf-8')`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Text Decoding
text: - **Browser**: Uses `TextDecoder` API

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Text Decoding
text: - Both paths are in `MessageDecoder.decodeText()` ([src/sse.ts:84-116](src/sse.ts#L84-L116))

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: [src/utils.ts](src/utils.ts) provides `checkOk()` which:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: - Checks HTTP response status

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: - Extracts error messages from JSON or text responses

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Error Handling
text: - Throws descriptive errors with server-provided messages when available

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Implementation Details > SSE Format Parsing
text: The library correctly handles the SSE specification where field values can have an optional space after the colon:

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Implementation Details > SSE Format Parsing
text: - `data: value` (with space) → extracts "value"

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Implementation Details > SSE Format Parsing
text: - `data:value` (no space) → extracts "value"

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Implementation Details > SSE Format Parsing
text: This is handled in [src/sse.ts:69](src/sse.ts#L69) by checking if `line[filedLength + 1] === NewLineChars.Space`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Implementation Details > Streaming Architecture
text: - Uses `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` from Fetch API

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Implementation Details > Streaming Architecture
text: - Processes chunks incrementally without loading entire response into memory

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Implementation Details > Streaming Architecture
text: - `LineDecoder` maintains state across chunks to handle lines split across multiple reads

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Implementation Details > Request Body Handling
text: `fetchEventData()` automatically serializes plain objects to JSON while passing through other BodyInit types unchanged ([src/fetch.ts:16-20](src/fetch.ts#L16-L20)).

head: AGENTS.md
text: 本文档用于约束在本仓库中工作的 AI 编码代理。所有操作应以当前代码、构建配置和用户要求为准；`README.md` 与 `docs/` 用于补充背景。当文档与代码不一致时，先核对实际配置和实现，不要直接照搬历史结论。

head: AGENTS.md > 沟通与交付
text: - 始终使用简体中文沟通，包括回复、代码注释、文档和提交信息。

head: AGENTS.md > 沟通与交付
text: - 开始修改前先阅读相关实现、配置和设计文档，避免凭经验猜测 OpenHarmony 或平台 API。

head: AGENTS.md > 沟通与交付
text: - 只修改任务所需文件，保留用户已有的未提交改动，不清理或覆盖无关变更。

head: AGENTS.md > 沟通与交付
text: - 完成后说明修改内容、验证命令与验证结果；未执行的验证及原因也要明确说明。

head: AGENTS.md > 沟通与交付
text: - 未经用户明确要求，不提交、不推送、不发布、不部署，也不改签名材料和版本号。

head: AGENTS.md > 项目概览
text: 鸿镜（HongJing）是 OpenHarmony 设备投屏与 HDC 调试工具，由两个子工程组成：

head: AGENTS.md > 项目概览
text: 1. `scrcpy_server/`：运行在 OpenHarmony 设备上的系统 HAP。

head: AGENTS.md > 项目概览
text: 2. `scrcpy_client_flutter/`：运行在 macOS/Windows 上的 Flutter 桌面客户端，Linux 为后续目标。

head: AGENTS.md > 项目概览
text: 客户端通过系统或应用内置的 `hdc` 执行设备发现、安装、卸载、shell 和端口转发。投屏连接固定使用：

head: AGENTS.md > 项目概览
text: 视频流、心跳、设备状态和控制消息均复用该 TCP 通道，不增加设备 LAN 直连方案。

head: AGENTS.md > 目录与职责
text: 不要手工修改 `.dart_tool/`、`build/`、`Pods/`、`ephemeral/`、`.hvigor/` 等生成目录。

head: AGENTS.md > 不可擅自改变的架构决策
text: - HDC 通过 Dart `Process` 调用 CLI：优先应用内置二进制，其次系统 PATH/常见 SDK 路径。

head: AGENTS.md > 不可擅自改变的架构决策
text:
- 视频解码使用平台原生实现并通过 `MethodChannel('scrcpy/decoder')` 与 Flutter Texture 上屏：
  - macOS：VideoToolbox。
  - Windows：优先 D3D11 硬件路径，失败后使用 CPU 回退路径。
  - 不引入 `media_kit`、`fvp` 或 FFI FFmpeg 替代现有架构。

head: AGENTS.md > 不可擅自改变的架构决策
text: - 服务端 `module.json5` 的 `mainElement` 必须保持为 `ScrcpyService`。`EntryAbility` 只承担调试页或必要的授权入口，不承载核心服务逻辑。

head: AGENTS.md > 不可擅自改变的架构决策
text: - 服务自启和常驻以 `AppScope/app.json5` 的 `keepAlive` 为基础，不新增 BootReceiver、StaticSubscriber 或启动完成广播。

head: AGENTS.md > 不可擅自改变的架构决策
text: - 截屏和编码必须按客户端连接状态启停：无客户端时释放截屏、编码器和相关系统资源，重连后重新创建。

head: AGENTS.md > 不可擅自改变的架构决策
text: - macOS App Sandbox 当前关闭，以允许调用 `hdc` 和建立本地 TCP 连接；修改时必须同步检查 `DebugProfile.entitlements` 与 `Release.entitlements`。

head: AGENTS.md > 不可擅自改变的架构决策
text: - 当前真实 SDK 配置以 `scrcpy_server/build-profile.json5` 为准：`compileSdkVersion` 为 23，`compatibleSdkVersion` 为 15。`CLAUDE.md` 中的 API 20 是历史信息，除非用户明确要求降级，否则不要改回。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > 分层
text: - `ScrcpyService.ets`：管理服务生命周期、客户端 presence、采集启停、控制分发和后台任务。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > 分层
text: - `InputInjector.ets`：处理触摸、鼠标、键盘、音量和亮度等输入。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > 分层
text: - `Protocol.ets`：ArkTS 侧协议常量及编码；协议变更必须与 Dart/C++ 同步。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > 分层
text: - `AppListProvider.ets`：生成可卸载应用列表。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > 分层
text: - `ScreenCaptureEncoder.*`：OH_AVScreenCapture、H.264/RAW/JPEG 和背压控制。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > 分层
text: - `TcpServer.*`：监听 53535、连接管理、协议拆包与消息广播。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > 分层
text: - `napi_init.cpp` 与 `types/libscrcpy_capture/Index.d.ts`：NAPI 导出及 ArkTS 类型声明；改 native 导出时三处必须一致。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > ArkTS 约束
text: 修改 `.ets` 文件时遵守 ArkTS 严格语法：

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > ArkTS 约束
text: - 禁止 `any`、`unknown` 和无约束动态类型，变量与回调参数使用明确类型。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > ArkTS 约束
text: - 不使用内联对象类型；提取为命名 `interface` 或 `class`。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > ArkTS 约束
text: - 对象字面量必须有明确目标类型，并写完整字段名，不使用属性 shorthand。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > ArkTS 约束
text: - 避免直接 `for...of Map.values()`，优先使用 `.forEach`。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > ArkTS 约束
text: - 系统 API 的导入路径、类型字段和版本差异必须以当前 Full SDK 声明为准。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > ArkTS 约束
text: - 需要新增 OpenHarmony API 时，优先查当前 SDK 的真实 `.d.ts` 和官方文档。常用本机目录为 `~/Library/OpenHarmony/Sdk/<版本>/ets/api/`，不要假定固定为 API 20。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > Native 约束
text: - C++ 使用 C++17，目标 ABI 当前为 `arm64-v8a`。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > Native 约束
text: - 所有 native 资源遵循严格的创建/销毁配对，断开、失败和提前返回路径同样要释放。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > Native 约束
text: - `OH_AVScreenCapture` RAW 模式的 `AcquireVideoBuffer` 与 `ReleaseVideoBuffer` 必须一一配对；丢帧或跳过路径也不能省略。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > Native 约束
text: - H.264 帧编码完成后不要随意丢弃依赖帧。队列压力应优先使用现有暂停/恢复控制，让服务端在编码前背压。

head: AGENTS.md > 服务端开发规则 > Native 约束
text: - 修改 NAPI 接口时同步更新 C++ 注册、ArkTS `.d.ts` 和调用方。

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text: - 业务状态、连接生命周期和共享实例集中在 `lib/state/app_state.dart`。Widget 不自行创建新的 `HdcClient`、`StreamClient` 或 `VideoDecoder`。

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text: - `lib/hdc/` 统一封装 HDC 命令；UI 层不要直接调用 `Process.run`。

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text:
- `lib/net/protocol.dart` 是 Dart 侧协议真值之一。改包格式或 subtype 时同步检查：
  - `scrcpy_server/entry/src/main/ets/scrcpyservice/Protocol.ets`
  - `scrcpy_server/entry/src/main/cpp/TcpServer.*`
  - 所有发送、解析和状态处理调用点

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text: - TCP 使用大端序。帧头固定为 `type(4B) + length(4B) + payload`。

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text: - `StreamClient` 在 `connect` 和 `disconnect` 时都必须重置解析器，防止半包残留污染重连。

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text: - 触摸、鼠标和文本输入涉及渲染尺寸到设备尺寸的坐标转换；修改 UI 布局后必须验证横竖屏、缩放和留黑区域。

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text: - 修改 MethodChannel 方法、参数或返回值时，同步更新 Dart、Swift 和 Windows C++ 实现。

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text:
- Windows 两条纹理路径的像素约定不同：
  - PixelBuffer 路径按 RGBA。
  - D3D11 `DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM` 路径按 BGRA。
  不要混用通道顺序。

head: AGENTS.md > 客户端开发规则
text: - `third_party/xterm/` 是项目内嵌依赖，只有任务明确涉及终端内核时才修改。

head: SKILLS: > Temporary test data
text:
`test/_temp` is only for active test runs and unresolved failure diagnostics.
Remove each run's owned temporary data when it passes; remove obsolete failure
data after the issue is resolved. Preserve `.gdignore`. Do not retain successful
ad-hoc hosts or use `-KeepArtifacts` routinely. Export explicitly needed evidence
to `_exports/_validation` before cleanup. Tool downloads belong in `.cache`, not
`test/_temp`. Never delete another active run's data or unresolved evidence.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Is This Project?
text: `heatwave3` is an R package that detects marine heatwaves (MHWs) and cold-spells (MCS) directly on gridded NetCDF data using the Hobday et al. (2016, 2018) definition. All core algorithms (climatology, event detection, categorisation, block averages) are implemented in C++ with `std::thread` parallelism and direct libnetcdf I/O — no R NetCDF packages needed at runtime.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Is This Project?
text: This is a ground-up C++ reimplementation of [heatwaveR](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/), designed for gridded data rather than per-pixel time series.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C++ Core (`src/`)
text: All compute-intensive work is in C++ with Rcpp bindings:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C++ Core (`src/`)
text: - **`netcdf_io.cpp/h`** — Direct NetCDF-C I/O with spatial/temporal subsetting, CF time parsing, scale_factor/add_offset/_FillValue handling. Supports both NC_CHAR and NC_STRING attributes. Reorders data to pixel-major layout [pixel][time] for cache-friendly per-pixel processing. Reads and writes climatology, event, and SST NetCDF files.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C++ Core (`src/`)
text: - **`climatology.cpp/h`** — Full ts2clm algorithm: gap filling, NA interpolation, DOY assignment (non-leap years skip DOY 60), spread to DOY×year matrix, sliding-window percentile (Type-7 quantile matching R exactly), circular-padded rolling mean smoothing. `std::thread` parallelism over pixels with progress reporting.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C++ Core (`src/`)
text: - **`event_detect.cpp/h`** — Full detect_event algorithm: threshold exceedance, run-length encoding, duration filtering, gap joining, 19 event metric computations. Cold spell support (threshold inversion). Optional inline Hobday et al. (2018) category computation (I Moderate through IV Extreme) and season assignment. `std::thread` parallelism over pixels with progress reporting.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C++ Core (`src/`)
text: - **`blob_label.cpp`** — 3D connected-component labeling (union-find, 6-connectivity, optional dateline wrap). Ported from heatwaveR.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C++ Core (`src/`)
text: - **`blob_metrics.cpp`** — Per-(blob, day) spatial metric reduction. Ported from heatwaveR.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C++ Core (`src/`)
text: - **`heatwave3_init.cpp`** — Rcpp exports bridging C++ to R. Key exports: `hw3_compute_clim`, `hw3_detect_events` (with category/hemisphere and protoEvent/write_daily params), `hw3_read_sst`, `hw3_read_event_nc`, `hw3_read_clim_nc`, `hw3_read_daily_nc`, `hw3_category`, `hw3_block_average`, `hw3_read_metric_summary`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > C++ Core (`src/`)
text: - **`heatwave3_types.h`** — Core structs: `EventResult` (19 metrics + category + season), `EventData` (for reading event NetCDF), `SubsetSpec`, `ClimData`, `GridData`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: Function names are suffixed with `3` to avoid conflicts with heatwaveR:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: **Output naming.** `ts2clm3()`, `detect_event3()`, and `detect3()` take a single `name` (path stem) and derive output filenames: `<name>_clim.nc`, `<name>_events.nc`, `<name>_events_daily.nc`, `<name>_protoevents.nc`. They always write their native NetCDF and return the written path(s) invisibly; there is no `return_df`/`save_file`. To read a product into R or export it to CSV/RDS/Parquet, use `hw3_export()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`detect3()`** — **Primary entry point.** All-in-one: climatology + detection + optional inline categories. Returns the written paths invisibly.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`ts2clm3()`** — NetCDF → climatology NetCDF (seas + thresh per DOY per pixel) at `<name>_clim.nc`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`detect_event3()`** — SST + climatology → event NetCDF. `clim_file` defaults to `<name>_clim.nc`. Supports `category = TRUE` (inline categories) and `hemisphere = "south"/"north"`. Per-day output via `daily = c("none","also","only")` (writes `<name>_events_daily.nc` with temp/seas/thresh/intensity/event/event_no + daily category) and `protoEvent = TRUE` (writes `<name>_protoevents.nc` with the heatwaveR proto flags, instead of the event table). All per-day products are gridded `[lon, lat, time]`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`hw3_export()`** — Read/export hub: auto-detects the product (via `hw3_file_meta`), returns a long data.frame (whole or first `n` rows) or writes a flat `.csv`/`.rds`/`.parquet`. Reading is C++-backed.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`category3()`** — Reads pre-computed categories from event file, or computes from climatology file for older events. `hemisphere` parameter replaces deprecated `S`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`category_daily3()`** — Per-pixel daily MHW/MCS series for a date window, built in C++ from SST + clim + events (windowed SST hyperslab, no re-detection; event membership read from the events file). Returns the full daily grid with the same columns as the `daily="also"` product (`lon, lat, t, temp, seas, thresh, intensity, event, event_no, category`); `category` is set on event-member exceedance days and `NA` elsewhere, with `ice_thresh` for the cold-spell ice category. The MHW Tracker's `load_sub_cat_clim()` event-day subset is `subset(x, !is.na(category))`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`block_average3()`** — Yearly event metric aggregation (pure C++)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`exceedance3()`** — Static threshold exceedance

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`detect_blob3()`** — 4D spatially-connected blob detection

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`event_line3()`** — Per-pixel time series plot from NetCDF (C++ reader, no ncdf4)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`geom_flame3()`** / **`geom_lolli3()`** — ggplot2 custom geoms

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > R API (`R/`)
text: - **`plot_metric3()`** — Spatial map of event metrics (C++-backed aggregation via `hw3_read_metric_summary`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Data Flow
text:
Or all-in-one:
```
NetCDF (SST) → detect3(name="X", category=TRUE) → X_clim.nc + X_events.nc
hw3_export("X_events.nc") → data.frame  (or .csv/.rds/.parquet)
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 1. **Pixel-major memory layout**: SST data reordered to [pixel][time] for contiguous per-pixel time series access during the `std::thread` parallel loops.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 2. **Type-7 quantile**: Matches R's default `quantile()` exactly via linear interpolation.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 3. **CF ragged array**: Event NetCDF uses an `event` dimension with lon/lat coordinate variables — avoids wasteful padding to max_events.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 4. **No R NetCDF dependency at runtime**: Uses libnetcdf C API directly via `configure` script. All four functions that previously used ncdf4 (`category3`, `block_average3`, `plot_metric3`, `event_line3`) now use the C++ reader.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: 5. **Inline categories**: Category computation uses the same climatology data already loaded during detection — zero extra I/O.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build System
text: - `configure` — Finds libnetcdf via nc-config, pkg-config, or common paths. Adds rpath on macOS. No OpenMP probe (parallelism is `std::thread`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Build System
text: - `src/Makevars.in` — Template substituted by configure.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build System
text: - `src/Makevars` — Generated; links `-lnetcdf` + `-pthread` (for `std::thread`; no OpenMP runtime).

head: CLAUDE.md > Build System
text: - SystemRequirements: netcdf (>= 4.0), C++17

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > What is Pragma?
text:
Pragma is a **macOS + Linux + Windows desktop app** (Tauri v2) moving toward a
host-server + thin native-client architecture. The host runs persistent, worktree-scoped
terminal sessions through `pragma-server`; native clients connect over a local Unix
socket (on all three platforms), or over a bridge that presents a remote SSH host or a
WSL distribution as one. Plugins for opencode, Claude Code, and Cursor report status through
the `pragma-cli` helper.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > North star: clean, reusable, consistent
text:
The overriding priority is a **clean, reusable architecture** with **consistent rules
across TypeScript and Rust**. When you write code:

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > North star: clean, reusable, consistent
text:
- **Reuse before you write.** Search for an existing helper, component, or constant
  first. Lift duplicated logic into a shared location the moment it appears twice.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > North star: clean, reusable, consistent
text:
- **Do not be afraid to create a new package or directory.** If something is shared,
  or _could_ be shared, give it a home (`packages/*`). If a value is referenced in
  more than one place, it belongs in `@pragma-sh/constants`, not inline. Small,
  single-purpose packages are encouraged.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > North star: clean, reusable, consistent
text:
- **One source of truth.** Never copy a value across the TS/Rust boundary by hand —
  put it in `@pragma-sh/constants` (see `packages/constants/AGENTS.md`).

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > North star: clean, reusable, consistent
text:
- **Keep the two languages in lockstep.** The same concept should be named, layered,
  and error-handled the same way in TypeScript and Rust. See _Code standards_ below.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > North star: clean, reusable, consistent
text:
- **Suggest sweeping changes.** If you see a cleaner structure,
  propose and make it — restructuring for clarity is welcome, not discouraged.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > North star: clean, reusable, consistent
text:
- **Host-tool plugins stay out of core — ask first.** A host-tool plugin/agent package
  (`packages/*-plugin`, such as opencode/Claude/Cursor integrations) is
  **self-contained data plus its own bundled assets**. It must **not** add or modify code
  in pragma core (`apps/pragma`, including `src-tauri`), the server
  (`crates/pragma-server`), the UI, the CLI (`crates/pragma-cli`), or the SDK
  (`packages/sdk`) **without explicit owner permission**. A host-tool plugin installs
  itself through its host tool's own plugin mechanism, never through per-plugin Pragma
  code. Launchable Pragma agents are contributed through the `@pragma-sh/plugin`
  `defineAgent` API (or the built-in Pragma plugin), not per-tool JSON files copied by
  core. There are deliberately **no** per-tool core installers: the old
  `opencode_plugin.rs` / `claude_plugin.rs` installers were **removed**. The generic
  Pragma plugin runtime is the exception: infrastructure for `.pragma/config.json` plugins lives in
  `packages/plugin`, `apps/pragma/src/plugins`, and `apps/pragma/src-tauri/src/plugins.rs`.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > Keeping this guide current (self-improvement)
text:
- **Edit the relevant AGENTS.md in the same change that makes it outdated.** Add a
  package, move a file, change a command, bump a tool, adopt a new pattern → update the
  matching AGENTS.md (root and/or child) in the same commit. Because `CLAUDE.md` is a
  symlink to the root AGENTS.md, both humans and agents stay in sync automatically.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > Keeping this guide current (self-improvement)
text:
- **Mirror it in the skills.** Canonical user-facing skill sources live under `skills/`
  and are symlinked into `.agents/skills/` (which `.claude/skills` also exposes). Internal
  contributor skills live directly in `.agents/skills/`, so that directory contains both
  internal and user-facing skills. If you
  change a workflow here, update the relevant skill (`pragma-architecture`,
  `shared-constants`, `tauri-command`, `code-quality`, `jev`, `pragma`) too, and
  add a new skill when you add a substantial new workflow.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > Keeping this guide current (self-improvement)
text:
- **Ship the website with the feature.** A user-visible change is not done until
  `apps/www` matches it: add or update the `/docs` page (and its `meta.json` entry), the
  landing-page copy or bento card when the feature is worth announcing, and any page the
  change makes wrong — wiki, CLI, SDK, keybindings, disk layout. Same change, same commit,
  exactly like the AGENTS.md rule above. A feature nobody can read about does not exist.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > Keeping this guide current (self-improvement)
text:
- **When you discover something the hard way, write it down.** A non-obvious gotcha, a
  setup step, a "don't do X because Y" — capture it here (or in the relevant child
  AGENTS.md) so the next person (or agent) doesn't rediscover it.

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > Keeping this guide current (self-improvement)
text: - **Prefer fixing the guide over working around it.**

head: Pragma — Agent & Contributor Guide > Keeping this guide current (self-improvement)
text:
- **Keep it concise.** Prune advice that no longer applies. Length is not authority;
  accuracy is.
