head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- 内置的「打不开」提示图用 `ImageDatabase::isErrorTipsFrame` 认（比 `data` 指针，
  `getErrorTipsMat()` 返回的是母本的浅拷贝，所以指针相等就是它）。**别靠「尺寸 +
  左上角像素颜色」去猜**：一张正好 800x600、左上角又正好是主题背景色的真图会被误判，
  后果是悄悄跳过色彩管理、少画边框，而且没有任何迹象。源码检查里有一项盯着这个。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- 窗口行为测试里要「点图片外的空白处」，别写死坐标。窗口是满工作区的、图片居中缩放，
  左右留白和上下留白通常只有一边非零，写死的点会随图片长宽比落到画面上。从标题里读
  真实像素尺寸和缩放百分比算出画面范围，再挑确实在留白里的点。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项

  程序那边 `OpenClipboard` 一失败就什么都没写进去。用 `GetClipboardSequenceNumber`
  等版本号变化，再用带重试的 `OpenClipboard` 直读（`ClipboardText` / `ClipboardImageSize`）。
  PowerShell 7 也没有 `Get-Clipboard -Format Image`。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- 发布就是绿色版，**不做安装程序**。`packageRelease.ps1` 出三样：裸的
  `YeImageViewer.exe`、`...-portable.zip`（Windows 自带能解压）、`...-portable.7z`
  （最小）。压缩包里 exe 躺在根目录，不要再埋进 `x64\Release\`。
  曾经有个 7z SFX 一键安装器，已经删掉：SFX 的版本信息写着 `7z Setup SFX small`，
  Windows 的「程序兼容性助手」据此判定它是安装程序，而它退出时又不写卸载注册项，
  于是**每装一次就弹一次「可能未正确安装此程序」**。程序本来就是绿色单文件，
  装不装都一样。打包契约测试现在反过来禁止 SFX 回来。
  `installLocal.ps1` 保留——它是 PowerShell 脚本，不触发兼容性助手。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- 真窗口测试要在临时目录里跑自己那份 exe 和素材，**别直接用仓库里的**。
  旋转角度和每图缩放是持久化的（存在 exe 旁边的 `YeImageViewer.db` 里），直接跑的话
  每次起始状态都不一样：实测连跑六轮，起始缩放 17%/46%/9%，旋转顺时针90°/180°/
  逆时针90°/无。结果不可重现的测试没法用来判断「是不是真的坏了」，而且还会把旋转
  记录写进开发目录的配置、影响别的环节。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- EXIF 的摄影参数显示走 `ExifValueFormat.h`（有配套单元测试）：曝光时间 `1/60 s`、
  光圈 `f/8`、焦距 `89.9 mm`、曝光补偿 `+1/3 EV`、白平衡/测光/方向等枚举翻成词。
  认得的标签才翻，不认得的返回 `nullopt` 退回通用的「小数 (原始分数)」——厂商私有
  扩展按自己的表编号，照规范翻会翻出错的词，而错的词比一个数字更误导人。
  **方向（Orientation）千万别再从拼好的 EXIF 文本里扒。** 原先五处写的是
  `exifInfo.find("方向: ")` 再把紧跟的那个字符减 `'0'`，于是「把 1 翻成正常」
  这一个显示改动就能让所有带旋转标记的 JPEG 不再转正，界面毫无异样。现在
  `ExifParse::getExif` 用出参 `orientationOut` 直接带出原始数值。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- 信息面板分两套：带边框窗口下是紧凑卡片（只有基础 7 项），沉浸显示下才是完整面板

  `presentationMode ? Mode::Full : Mode::Compact`。完整面板的高度跟着窗口长
  （`ImageInfoPresentation::maxPanelHeight`），别再给它写死上限——写死 400 逻辑像素时，
  880 高的窗口里相机、光圈、快门全被压在视口外要滚好几次，而窗口还空着四百多像素。
  标签列宽要放得下四个汉字（`LOGICAL_COMPACT_LABEL_WIDTH`），48 的时候「文件大小」
  只显示出「文件大」。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- 「关于」页底下那行「♥ 觉得不错？赞赏一下作者~」点一下会把 hero 卡片翻到收款码那面
  （`SettingLayout::ABOUT_DONATE_*`，收起时只有那行小字是热区，展开时整张卡片都能点回去）。
  那行是分两段画的：红心一段、文字一段，不然上不了两个色；心形用裸的 U+2665，
  加上 U+FE0F 变体选择符是在要彩色 emoji，而这里是 GDI 单色绘制，要不到就画成豆腐块。
  两段颜色在 `SettingLayout.h`，各自压在卡片底色上的对比度由 `ContrastRatio.h`
  按 WCAG 公式算、单元测试盯着（正文 4.5:1，红心按图形算 3:1）。别直接套信息面板
  那套强调蓝——设置页的卡片底比面板底亮一截，同一个蓝摆过来只剩 4.48:1。
  收款码是 `YeImageViewer/file/donate-{alipay,wechat}.png`，从原始收款海报里裁出码本体

  它逐像素量静区够不够四个模块、显示尺寸下每个模块够不够四个像素。踩过一次——
  按 184 逻辑像素画时支付宝那个码（41 模块）每模块不到四个像素，边界糊成灰的，
  界面上看着是个正常二维码，扫码器就是不认，而且没有任何报错。

- README 的界面预览图别手工截——跑 `./tools/make-preview.ps1`。手工截的尺寸、背景、

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- 读屏幕像素的探针要先把被测窗口**置顶**（`SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST, SWP_NOMOVE|
  SWP_NOSIZE|SWP_NOACTIVATE)`），不然别的程序弹个窗口盖上来就把读数搅乱。
  「大图渐进加载探针」为此假失败过一次：报「预览与原图取景不一致」，而同一个构建
  单独连跑三轮漂移都只有 0.1；失败那轮有两帧亮度从 64 掉到 32、非暗像素从 66% 掉到
  20%——这台机器上有个 Shazao.MainWindow 一直排在 Z 序上面还在移动。
  置顶之后四轮读数完全一致（62.2 → 62.4）。
  别用「数一数 Z 序上面有几个窗口和它相交」来判遮挡：那个窗口多数时候并没有真画出来，
  读数照样平稳，照这个判定会把本来能跑的环节变成永远 SKIPPED，比假失败还糟。
  置顶只改 Z 序，解码时序和渲染路径都不受影响；置顶之后仍被盖才是真环境问题，记 SKIPPED。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text: - 查「打开一张图为什么慢」用 `YEIMAGEVIEWER_STARTUP_TRACE=<文件路径>` 环境变量（见 `StartupTrace.h`），会记下 CRT 静态初始化、建窗口、建 D3D 设备、解码、格式转换、色彩管理、首帧绘制各段的时刻。没设环境变量时一个字节都不写。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text: - 建 D3D 设备要七十多毫秒，建窗口只要五毫秒。图片解码在 `onWindowCreated()` 里就派出去了，和建设备并行跑；启动那一次的 `initOpenFile` 要传 `keepWarmCache = true`，否则 `imgDB.clear()` 会把在途的解码作废。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text:
- 别再去给 libpng 的去滤波写 SIMD。做过一轮完整的：libpng 自带的 SSE2 只覆盖 3 和 4 字节像素（`intel/intel_init.c` 里 `if (bpp == 3) ... else if (bpp == 4)`），16 位图是 6 或 8 字节像素，确实掉回标量。补齐 6/8 字节的 SSE2 实现之后，自检确认结果与规范逐字节一致，解码耗时却一点没变——A/B 各跑四轮：原版 1506/1513/1513/1523 ms，SIMD 版 1512/1524/1594/1608 ms。
  原因是这一步受内存带宽限制，不受计算限制：SIMD 版每行（9000 像素 × 6 字节）25.4 µs，期间读 row、读 prev、写 row 共 162 KB，折合 6.4 GB/s，正好顶在单线程内存带宽上。libpng 原本的标量实现早就撞在同一堵墙上了。
  顺带记两件事：量性能必须多跑几轮取中位数，这次先后被两个单次测量（1733、1646）误导过；另外别拿「按规范直写的参考实现」当标量基线去算加速比，libpng 自己那份优化过的 C 比参考实现快十倍。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text: - 色彩管理排在解码之后，直接顶在出图时间上：源和目标同色彩空间时整步跳过（绝大多数图都是这种情况），大图按行分块并行。改 `ColorManager::applyToMat` 之后要跑 `./x64/Release/YeImageViewer.exe --color-selftest <文件>`，它用生产代码验证恒等真被跳过、并行结果和串行逐字节相同。

head: AGENTS.md > 修改注意事项
text: - 主窗口渲染路径以 OpenCV `cv::Mat` 作为 CPU 画布，再交给 Direct3D 显示；避免在高频绘制路径中引入阻塞 I/O 或昂贵同步操作。

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance to Codex (Codex.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: AphexCMS is a Sanity-inspired, database-agnostic CMS built with SvelteKit V2 (Svelte 5). It uses a monorepo managed by pnpm workspaces and Turborepo.

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands
text: Standard scripts (`dev`, `build`, `format`, `lint`, `check`, `db:*`) are in the root and `apps/studio` `package.json` — read those rather than duplicating them here. A few non-obvious ones:

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands
text: - `pnpm test:package` — build + type-check `cms-core` (not just a test run).

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands
text: - `pnpm -F @aphexcms/studio test:local | test:http | test:graphql` — run only the Local API / HTTP / GraphQL suites (all suites: `test`).

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands
text: - `pnpm shadcn <component-name>` — add a shadcn-svelte component to `@aphexcms/ui`.

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands
text: - `./scripts/sync-template.sh [--apply]` — sync studio → template (dry run without `--apply`); see the `sync-template` skill.

head: AGENTS.md > Syncing studio → template → scaffolder
text: The studio → template → `create-aphex` sync workflow lives in the **`sync-template` skill** — invoke it when syncing `apps/studio` downstream to `templates/base`, cutting a template release, or editing the scaffolder.

head: AGENTS.md > Syncing studio → template → scaffolder
text: There is exactly one `aphex` binary, exposed by `@aphexcms/cms-core` (`packages/cms-core/src/cli/index.ts`): `aphex generate:types` and `aphex migrate`, both used by the templates. Scaffolding is `pnpm create aphex` (`packages/create-aphex`). The old `aphx` wrapper package was removed — it only spawned `npx create-aphex`, and having two near-identical command names caused more confusion than it saved typing.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **apps/studio** — Reference SvelteKit app (the actual CMS admin). Contains schema definitions, auth setup, DB/storage singletons, and API route re-exports.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **packages/cms-core** — Database-agnostic core engine. Contains admin UI components, route handlers, field validation, schema utilities, plugin system, and TypeScript types. Exports via `@aphexcms/cms-core`, `@aphexcms/cms-core/server`, `@aphexcms/cms-core/client`, `@aphexcms/cms-core/schema`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **packages/postgresql-adapter** — PostgreSQL implementation using Drizzle ORM. Also exports `/pglite` (embedded Postgres).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **packages/sqlite-adapter** — SQLite implementation via libsql (local `file:` databases and Turso). A first-class alternative to Postgres, not a reduced tier; both run the same cross-dialect conformance suite (`packages/sqlite-adapter/tests/conformance.spec.ts`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **packages/storage-s3** — S3-compatible storage adapter (R2, AWS S3, MinIO).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **packages/ui** — Shared shadcn-svelte component library (`@aphexcms/ui`). Components imported as `@aphexcms/ui/shadcn/<component>`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **packages/cli, packages/create-aphex** — CLI tooling for scaffolding.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **packages/nodemailer-adapter** — Nodemailer/SMTP email adapter (includes `createMailpitAdapter()` for local dev).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **packages/resend-adapter** — Resend API email adapter (production).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Monorepo Layout
text: - **templates/base** — Starter project template for new AphexCMS projects.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Ports & Adapters (Hexagonal):** `cms-core` defines interfaces (`DatabaseAdapter`, `StorageAdapter`, `AuthProvider`); separate packages provide implementations. This keeps the core database-agnostic.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Route Handler Re-exports:** API routes are defined in `cms-core/src/routes/` and re-exported in `apps/studio/src/routes/api/`. This avoids duplication while allowing customization.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Singleton DI via Config:** The app creates singleton adapters (DB, storage, auth) and passes them to `createCMSConfig()` in `aphex.config.ts`. The `createCMSHook()` in `hooks.server.ts` initializes the CMS engine and injects services into `event.locals.aphexCMS`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Schema System:** Content schemas are TypeScript objects defined in `apps/studio/src/lib/schemaTypes/`. Two types: `document` (top-level entities) and `object` (reusable nested structures). Field types: `string`, `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `slug`, `url`, `image`, `file`, `array`, `object`, `reference`, `date`, `datetime`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Reserved field names — the boot-time trap.** A document already has its own columns, and a schema field that shadows one is rejected when the engine initializes (`validateSchemaReferences`, `packages/cms-core/src/lib/schema-utils/validator.ts`): `id`, `type`, `status`, `organizationId`, `createdBy`, `updatedBy`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `publishedAt`, `draftData`, `publishedData`, `publishedHash`. The two that bite hardest, because they're the natural names:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **`type`** — the field a Payload-style variant picker wants (`hero.type`, `link.type`). Name it `variant`/`linkType`. The check walks nested `object` fields, not only top-level ones, so an inner `type` fails too.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **`publishedAt`** — don't declare one; the engine stamps it on first publish and it reads back as `_meta.publishedAt`. A query sorts on it directly (`sort: '-publishedAt'`), but **`orderings` may only name fields the schema declares**, so an ordering on `publishedAt` is a separate validation error.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: `describe_cms` on the MCP server returns the live list; `validate_schema` catches all of this before the file is written, which is much faster than finding out at boot.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Conditional fields (`hidden`) — an editor-experience feature, not a security one.** Any field may declare `hidden: ({ siblingData, documentData }) => boolean` to hide itself when it doesn't apply (a link's target document when the link is a custom URL, a hero's media when the hero is text only). Three things to know:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **Reach for `siblingData`**, not `documentData`. It's the object the field belongs to, so repeated array items each answer for themselves — with `documentData`, three link rows all follow the first row's value.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **Hidden fields are skipped by validation too** (both paths call `isFieldVisible` from `schema-utils`), so a required field on the inactive branch can't block a save with an error pointing at a control nobody can see. Keep genuine invariants in `validation` as well — the API is reachable without the admin.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **Hiding keeps the stored value**, so toggling a choice twice isn't destructive — which means a renderer must not read a field the editor can't see, or the page shows something with no control to change it.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: `hidden` is **not** access control: the value stays in the document, in API responses, and writable through the API. Use field-level `access` for that. Docs: `docs/aphex-docs/content/docs/schemas/conditional-fields.mdx`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: Two authoring styles, both valid:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - `const x: SchemaType = { ... }` — plain annotated object.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - `defineType({ ... })` — an **optional** wrapper (`@aphexcms/cms-core`) that captures the exact `fields` literal via a `const` type parameter, so lifecycle hooks get a `data` typed **by self-reflection from the schema's own fields** — no generated types, no casts. Backwards compatible: plain objects keep working; `defineType` only adds the typed-hook ergonomics. Inferred field values are `T | undefined` (a write may carry a subset).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Schema hooks & validation (transform vs reject vs react):** A schema may declare `hooks.beforeValidate: DocumentHook[]` — save-time functions that run on every write path (Local API `create`/`update`, including the admin UI) **before** field validation. Hooks are **transform-only**: normalize/derive input and return the new data (the one thing validation can't do — it judges, never mutates). Keep the three concerns separate:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **Transform** (normalize, slugify, stamp, default) → `hooks.beforeValidate`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **Reject** (required, format, cross-field invariants like "unique names") → `validation: (Rule) => Rule.custom(...)` — never a hook.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **React** (email, webhook, cache) → a domain-event consumer, out of band — never a hook.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: This bright line ("hooks transform, never react") is deliberate: it takes the one useful idea from Payload-style hooks while avoiding the mess of side-effects running inside the write path. Runner: `packages/cms-core/src/lib/local-api/hooks.ts`; types + `InferFields`/`FieldTSType`: `packages/cms-core/src/lib/types/schemas.ts`; helper: `packages/cms-core/src/lib/schema-utils/define-type.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Visual editing (`@aphexcms/visual-editing`) — preview is interactive, so every renderer owes the author a target.** `usePreview()` gives `live()`, `edit()`, `image()` and `encode()`. Four rules that are easy to get wrong and produce silent, preview-only breakage:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **A repeated block must reveal its own row**: spread `{...ve.edit({ field: 'layout', arrayIndex: index })}` onto its root element. Text carries stega markers and is clickable by itself, but only the text is — surrounding chrome, buttons and empty states are inert without an explicit target, and a block that ignores its `index` sends the author to the top of the array rather than to their block. Images _always_ need it: a string can carry stega inside itself, an image has no string to carry.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **`live()` merges rather than replaces.** It keeps underscore-prefixed keys (`_posts`, `_form`) that a `load` derived and the editor's document can't know about; authored fields still come from the editor, so clearing one still clears it.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **A block rendering a different document needs its own `live()`**, gated on type _and_ id (`ve.live(block._form, { type: 'form', id: block._form.id })`) — otherwise editing that document does nothing until a reload.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **Clean any value you branch on** (`stegaClean`): a stega-marked `'center'` or `'cta'` matches no `===` and the branch silently takes the wrong arm. Display strings keep their markers — that is what makes them clickable.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Block Content (Rich Text):** Rich text follows Sanity's Portable Text model — an array of blocks, not a standalone field type. Schema: `{ type: 'array', of: [{type: 'block'}, ...] }`. The `block` type is a built-in that activates the TipTap-based Portable Text editor. Configuration follows Sanity's conventions:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - `block` is never created manually — the editor manages text blocks automatically

text: - `image` is a built-in block type with asset browser integration (insert + replace)

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - Inline objects (`block.of`) render as chips within text; block-level types render as cards between paragraphs

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - Validation works via the standard `Rule` class since block content is a regular array

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - Stored as Portable Text JSON (spec: portabletext.org)

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - Serializer: `packages/cms-core/src/lib/components/admin/fields/richtext/portable-text-serializer.ts`

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - Editor: `packages/cms-core/src/lib/components/admin/fields/richtext/RichtextField.svelte`

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - `ArrayField.svelte` detects `{type: 'block'}` in `of` and delegates to `RichtextField`

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Document Workflow:** Draft/published model with hash-based change detection. Auto-save every 2 seconds. Publishing copies draft data to published data with a content hash. **Scheduled publish/unpublish**: `localAPI.collections.<type>.schedulePublish(ctx, id, runAt)` (and `scheduleUnpublish`) enqueue a durable job on the queue (below); the worker runs the actual publish at `runAt`, re-validating and emitting `document.published`. Permission is checked at schedule time. At most one pending schedule per document (rescheduling cancels the prior). Editor UI: `ScheduleDialog.svelte`; the pending schedule shows as a banner in `DocumentEditor.svelte`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Concurrency (compare-and-swap):** Every document write is guarded by a monotonic `revision` column on `cms_documents`, incremented on every draft write. A caller that read the document at revision N can pass `expectedRevision: N` to `updateDocDraft`/`publishDoc`/`unpublishDoc` (and `VersionService.restoreVersion`); a mismatch throws `RevisionConflictError` instead of silently overwriting a change made in between (a second tab, an AI agent, a concurrent request) — `expectedRevision` is optional everywhere, so omitting it preserves unconditional last-write-wins. Threaded end-to-end: adapter → `CollectionAPI` → zod request schemas (`expectedRevision` in, `revision` out via `_meta`) → HTTP routes (409 on conflict) → client (`api/documents.ts`) → `DocumentEditor.svelte`, which sends the revision it last read on every write and surfaces a 409 as "changed elsewhere, reload" rather than a generic error. **Non-obvious**: both `PostgreSQLAdapter`/`SQLiteAdapter` (`packages/{postgresql,sqlite}-adapter/src/index.ts`) wrap the document adapter with org-hierarchy fallback (retry against a child org if not found in the caller's org) — that wrapper must forward `expectedRevision` too, or CAS is silently a no-op end-to-end even though the inner adapter enforces it correctly. Proven cross-dialect by the `revision compare-and-swap` block in `packages/sqlite-adapter/tests/conformance.spec.ts` (run against both pglite and libsql). This is Milestone 1 of `references/content-copilot-phase-1-plan.md` — the concurrency-safety prerequisite for a future mutating content-copilot agent.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **API Contracts (Zod):** All cms-core API endpoints use zod as a single source of truth for request shapes. Schemas live in `packages/cms-core/src/lib/api/schemas/<resource>.ts` and are imported by both the route handler and the client (`packages/cms-core/src/lib/api/<resource>.ts`). Route handlers validate via `safeParse` and return `{ success: false, error, issues }` with status 400 on failure; clients consume `z.infer<>` request types so input shapes can't drift. For query strings use `Object.fromEntries(url.searchParams.entries())` + `z.coerce.number()`. Keep hand-written TS interfaces for **response** types (e.g. `Asset`, `Organization`) — zod `.passthrough()` adds an index signature that breaks strict assignment for callers. Studio routes import schemas via `@aphexcms/cms-core/api/schemas/<resource>` (the package's `./*` export wildcard). Skip schemas for GET-only endpoints and no-body POST/DELETE (publish, accept-invitation, etc).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Email System:** Ports & adapters pattern — `cms-core` defines the `EmailAdapter` interface (`send()`, optional `sendBatch()`), with Nodemailer and Resend implementations in separate packages. Email templates are Svelte 5 components using `better-svelte-email`, rendered server-side via a shared `Renderer` to email-safe HTML with Tailwind support. Templates live in each app at `src/lib/server/email/components/` (EmailLayout, PasswordReset, EmailVerification, Invitation). The renderer at `src/lib/server/email/renderer.ts` produces both HTML and plain text (`toPlainText()`). Three email types: password reset, email verification, and organization invitation. Dev uses Mailpit (localhost:1025, UI at localhost:8025); prod uses Resend. Emails are sent via Better Auth callbacks (auth flows) and fire-and-forget in route handlers (invitations). The adapter is injected via `createCMSConfig()` and available at `event.locals.aphexCMS.emailAdapter`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Event, Queue & Job System (the durable "react to facts" spine):** The leg the architecture reserved for reactions — the Codex rule is **hooks transform, events react** (a hook mutates input in the write path; a consumer reacts out of band). Four parts, all DB-backed and organization-scoped, defined as ports in `packages/cms-core/src/lib/db/interfaces/events.ts` and implemented by the relational adapters:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **`cms_domain_events`** — an **immutable, append-only** log of facts (`document.published`, …). Written via `appendEvent`, typically inside the same `withTransaction` as the state change that caused it (transactional outbox), so a fact never exists without its change nor is lost if the change committed.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **`cms_event_outbox`** — a **mutable worklist** written in that same transaction, mirroring each event. Claimed by **status** (`processed_at IS NULL`), never by log position — so a late-committing event with an early timestamp isn't skipped (the bug a cursor-scan over the log would have). `event_type`/`payload` are denormalized for join-free fan-out.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **`cms_jobs`** — a **work queue** with leases, exponential backoff + jitter, dead-lettering, and a unique `(org, idempotencyKey)`. Lifecycle: `pending → leased → completed/failed/cancelled`. A crashed worker's lease expires and the job is reclaimed. At-least-once, so **handlers must be idempotent**.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **The relay** (`jobs/relay.ts`) turns facts into work: drains the outbox, and for each **subscribed consumer** enqueues one delivery job, then marks the row processed. **No lease** — at-least-once relay + idempotent enqueue (key `evt:<eventId>:<consumerId>`) = exactly-once delivery per (event, consumer). A delivery **is a job** (reserved type `aphex/consumer:<id>`), so consumers inherit all the retry/backoff/dead-letter machinery — no separate deliveries table.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: Flow: `publish() → domain event + outbox row (one txn) → [worker tick] relay fans out → delivery job per consumer → runner invokes consumer → retry/dead-letter`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Running it — one seam, three modes.** `runJobsBatch(services, opts)` (`jobs/run-batch.ts`) is the single place the handler map is assembled (core built-ins → plugin `aphex/event/consumer` deliveries → plugin `aphex/job/handler` → app `config.jobs.handlers`, last wins) and one tick runs: **relay first, then execute** (so a just-published doc's consumers can fire the same tick). It's driven by the protected endpoint `POST /api/internal/workers/run`, gated by a shared secret (`config.jobs.workerSecret`; 404 when unset, so it's never an unauthenticated surface). Three ways to drive that endpoint: **platform cron** (hosted), the **self-hosted poll loop** (`apps/studio/scripts/worker.ts`, `pnpm -F @aphexcms/studio worker`), and (planned) an **embedded in-process loop** that calls `runJobsBatch` directly. The runner never loops itself — the caller sets cadence; each call is bounded by `config.jobs.batchSize`/`relayBatchSize`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Emitting & subscribing.** Events are typed via `defineEvent(type, zodSchema)` (`events/catalog.ts`); emitters `parse` the payload so a bad shape fails at the write site. Built-in `document.published` is emitted by the shared `emitDocumentPublished` helper (`events/emit.ts`) on **every** publish path — versioned or not, from the admin UI, Local API, REST, GraphQL, MCP, or a scheduled job — because all publishes bottom out at `collection-api`. Two plugin part kinds close the loop (`plugins/types.ts`):

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **`aphex/event/consumer`** — `{ id, events: [...], handler, maxAttempts? }`. React to an event durably. The handler gets `{ event, databaseAdapter, logger, settings }`, where `settings.get(pluginId)` returns the plugin's **decrypted** per-org settings (e.g. a webhook URL `secret`) — so a plugin that declares an `aphex/settings` part can read its own config inside a reaction. Throw to retry.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: - **`aphex/job/handler`** — `{ handlers: { <type>: JobHandler } }`. Register executors for jobs the plugin (or app) enqueues directly via `databaseAdapter.scheduleJob`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: A plugin that emits an event from a route, subscribes to it, and registers the handler is fully self-contained — **no wiring in the app's `aphex.config.ts`**. Example: `apps/studio/src/lib/plugins/notify-plugin.ts` (a Discord/Slack publish notifier). Keep event/job/consumer type strings package-namespaced to avoid collisions. **Do not** put side effects in schema hooks — that's what consumers are for.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Architecture Patterns
text: **Recurring work is a chain, not a cron row.** There is no recurring-job type: a repeating job reschedules _itself_, each tick's handler enqueuing the next before it returns (`scheduleNextTick(adapter, job, { intervalMs })`). A tick is an ordinary job, so it inherits leases, backoff, dead-lettering and the Activity view, and a chain switches itself off per environment by simply not rescheduling. Starting one is the part that's quiet to get wrong: use `ensureRecurringJob(adapter, { organizationId, type })`, which decides on **liveness** (`pending`/`leased`) and not an idempotency key. A keyed bootstrap looks right and fails later — the bootstrap job completes immediately, so every later arming call gets that finished row back and no-ops, meaning a chain that dies can never be revived while the arming call still reports success. Call `ensureRecurringJob` from any path that implies the feature is in use (a settings panel opening, a manual "sync now"); it never starts a second live chain and always revives a dead one. Relatedly, `scheduleJob`'s `idempotencyKey` returns the existing row _whatever its status_ — pass `resurrect: true` to re-arm a `failed`/`cancelled` one, but never on a hot read path, where a permanently broken job would be re-armed on every request (`requeueJob`, i.e. the Activity view's Retry, is the operator's route for that).

head: AGENTS.md > Code Conventions
text: - **Barrel files** (`index.ts`): keep them **super thin — re-exports only, no mixed concerns** — primarily to **keep bundle chunk sizes down.** Rollup's download unit is the chunk, not the symbol: when a barrel re-exports both light and heavy modules, importing _anything_ from it can pull the heavy modules into the same shared chunk, so every page that touches the barrel ships code it never uses (this is what forced the `@aphexcms/cms-core/client` → `/client/ui` split — a fat barrel dragged the TipTap/field-editor chunk onto every admin page). So: a barrel only re-exports from siblings (`export * from './x'`), never declares logic or implementations inline, and **groups by weight** — keep heavy, rarely-needed exports out of a barrel that light/hot paths import (give them their own narrow entrypoint). See `packages/cms-core/src/lib/schema-utils/index.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance to agentic coding tools when working with code in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: `tzf-rs` is a fast timezone finder library for Rust that converts longitude/latitude coordinates to timezone names. Since v2 it is protobuf-free: the data source is the TZF embedded binary format (`.tzb`) shipped by the `tzf-dist` crate, and the public surface is two finder types:

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: - **DefaultFinder**: Recommended. Expands `.tzb` geometry into geometry-rs polygons at load (~13 ms); `get_tz_name` answers from the FUZZY preindex tiles with exact point-in-polygon fallback; `get_tz_names` is always polygon-exact and lexicographically sorted.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: - **EmbeddedFinder**: Low-memory. Queries the `.tzb` bytes in place (~4 MB total, ~2 ms open); identical results, microsecond queries.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: The Go reference implementation of the format is `github.com/ringsaturn/tzf/v2/internal/embedbin`.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: MSRV is **1.88** (edition 2024 + let-chains), declared as `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml`.

head: AGENTS.md > Essential Commands
text:
**`--all-features` never builds this crate.** `bundled` and `full` are mutually
exclusive (`compile_error!` in `src/lib.rs`), and while the dev-form path
dependency is active cargo additionally refuses "depends on crate `tzf-dist`
multiple times with different names". Lint and test the two legs separately;
`make lint` and `make ci` already do.

head: AGENTS.md > Development data setup
text: Until tzf-dist publishes the `.tzb` artifact release, Cargo.toml carries a path dependency on a sibling `../tzf-dist` checkout (branch `v2-artifacts`). Fill it with real artifacts by running `scripts/build-tzf-dist-dev.sh` in a sibling `tzf` checkout (branch `embedded`), which builds the artifact set from upstream raw GeoJSON and installs it over tzf-dist's committed placeholders.

head: AGENTS.md > Development data setup
text:
Cargo.toml documents the publishable **release form** of those dependencies
next to the dev form; `release-runbook-v2.md` is the ordered switch-and-tag
procedure. `.github/workflows/rust.yml` and `deploy_doc.yml` detect which form
is active and skip the Go bootstrap automatically once the release form lands.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Architecture
text:
- `src/tzb/` — the `.tzb` reader, mirroring Go `internal/embedbin`:
  - `mod.rs`: constants, `Error`, BBox, CRC32 (slicing-by-8), zigzag-LEB128 cursor
  - `reader.rs`: open/validation, directory records, GRID candidates, in-place PIP query walk (spec §8)
  - `fuzzy.rs`: FUZZY section validation + in-place binary-search lookup
  - `expand.rs`: expansion loader (E profile → open rings), per-timezone expansion for GeoJSON
  - `raycast.rs`: segment raycast (port of geometry-rs/tidwall semantics; geometry-rs 0.5 keeps its raycast result fields private)
  - `tile.rs`: slippy-map tile math, bit-identical to Go `geom.TileID`

head: AGENTS.md > Code Architecture
text: - `src/finder.rs` — materialized polygon finder (geometry-rs `I32Polygon` + YStripes, always on), dense GRID index, FUZZY hash-map fast path, parallel item assembly

head: AGENTS.md > Code Architecture
text: - `src/lib.rs` — public API (`DefaultFinder`, `EmbeddedFinder`, `Error`, `deg2num`); both finders expose `get_tz_name`, `get_tz_names`, `timezonenames`, `data_version`, and under `export-geojson` `to_geojson`, `get_tz_geojson`, `to_preindex_geojson`, `get_tz_preindex_geojson`

head: AGENTS.md > Code Architecture
text: - `src/geojson.rs` — GeoJSON export types (feature `export-geojson`)

head: AGENTS.md > Code Architecture
text:
`src/lib.rs` also carries a `#[cfg(doctest)] ReadmeDoctests` item that runs
every Rust-tagged fenced block in README.md as a doctest under
`bundled,export-geojson`, so README samples cannot drift from the API.

head: AGENTS.md > Correctness invariants
text: - Rings from the loaders are **open**; geometry-rs stores rings **closed** — `close_ring` in `src/finder.rs` appends the closing vertex. Never feed open rings to `I32Polygon`.

head: AGENTS.md > Correctness invariants
text: - Boundary semantics: exterior rings allow on-edge containment, hole rings do not (`contains_point_allow_on_edge`); a border query belongs to every touching polygon.

head: AGENTS.md > Correctness invariants
text: - `tests/parity_test.rs` pins DefaultFinder ≡ EmbeddedFinder; cross-language parity with the Go v2 reference was verified over ~195k samples per artifact.

head: AGENTS.md > Correctness invariants
text: - tzf-rs consumes the `.tzb` (E) profile only; `.tzm` memory images are rejected with `Error::Profile`. The `.tzm` format serves the Go runtime's zero-copy ring aliasing, which geometry-rs's owned polygon storage cannot exploit (measured: ~3 ms faster open, more memory — dropped 2026-08-28).

head: AGENTS.md > Features
text: - `bundled` (default): lite `.tzb` via crates.io tzf-dist. Mutually exclusive with the `full` feature.

head: AGENTS.md > Features
text: - `export-geojson`: GeoJSON export methods.

head: AGENTS.md > Features
text: - `clap` (default): the `tzf` CLI binary.

head: AGENTS.md > Features
text:
- `full`: full-precision `.tzb` (~14 MB) and `DefaultFinder::new_full()`. **The
  data is git-only** — `full.tzb` exceeds the crates.io package limit, so the
  registry `tzf-dist` package excludes it *and* `src/full.rs`. Enabling `full`
  against the registry copy does not compile. Consumers need the tzf-dist git
  source: either take tzf-rs itself from git, or add `[patch.crates-io]` for
  `tzf-dist`. Both recipes are in README's "Setup 100% Accurate Lookup".
  Inside this repo `full` always works, because the manifest's own
  `tzf-dist-git` entry keeps the git (or path) source.

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance to AI Agents when working with this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Overview
text: A Mars source package providing composable creative writing agents and skills for Meridian and Claude Code. Also distributes Claude.ai skill uploads via GitHub Releases.

head: AGENTS.md > Key Distinctions
text: **`skills/` vs `cw/skills/`:** `skills/` is the Mars source: consumed by Claude Code projects via `mars add`. `cw/skills/` holds the Claude.ai / plugin distribution — genericized copies with Meridian-specific references removed. Edit `skills/` first, then resync `cw/` (see [Syncing the `cw/` distribution](#syncing-the-cw-distribution)). CI fails on drift, so this is not optional.

head: AGENTS.md > Key Distinctions
text: **Agents vs skills:** Agents are spawned as independent processes (orchestrators, writers, critics). Skills are reference material loaded into agent context (craft knowledge, patterns, conventions). See `agents/` and `skills/` directories.

head: AGENTS.md > Key Distinctions
text: **Destination sync:** Comes from the `writing-sync` Mars dependency (`haowjy/writing-sync`), not this repo. Do not vendor those skills here or add them to `cw/` / `GENERATED_SKILLS`.

head: AGENTS.md > Package Management
text: This repo is both a Mars source package (publishes agents/skills) and a Mars consumer (depends on `meridian-base`).

head: AGENTS.md > Package Management
text: Version lives in `mars.toml` under `[package]`. Tags trigger CI releases.

head: AGENTS.md > Package Management
text: **Version sync:** `mars version patch` bumps `mars.toml`. The sync script (`sync_cw_skills.py`) auto-syncs the version into both `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (`metadata.version`) and `cw/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (`version`), staging the files for the in-flight commit. This runs in all modes (check, lint, apply) so the pre-commit hook catches drift.

head: AGENTS.md > Package Management
text:
**Meridian session roots:** Meridian spawns resolve `MERIDIAN_TASK_DIR` for the
checkout where source work happens, but `MERIDIAN_PROJECT_DIR` stays anchored to
the session control root for state, profiles, and context. Nested
`meridian ...` commands use project-root resolution, so CWD alone may not target
this package. For package releases, pass the package root explicitly:

head: AGENTS.md > Package Management
text:
Use explicit `-C <package-root>` whenever running Meridian commands for this
package from an inherited Meridian environment. For task checkouts, prefer
`meridian -C "$MERIDIAN_TASK_DIR" ...`.

head: AGENTS.md > Syncing the `cw/` distribution
text: `cw/skills/` adapts `skills/` for harnesses without Meridian (Claude.ai uploads, the Claude Code plugin). Skills split two ways:

head: AGENTS.md > Syncing the `cw/` distribution
text: - **GENERATED** — selected skills copied from a temporary Mars consumer project's `.claude/skills/`. Mars performs Claude frontmatter/native lowering; the script filters the skills that belong in the cw distribution.

head: AGENTS.md > Syncing the `cw/` distribution
text:
- **MANUAL** — skills carrying cw-specific adaptations, cw-only behavior, or dependency changes not yet available through a released Mars dependency. Hand-maintained; the tool lints but never overwrites them.
```bash
python3 scripts/sync_cw_skills.py            # full check: Mars build + drift + lint
python3 scripts/sync_cw_skills.py --lint     # lint only (no Mars build); used by CI and pre-commit
python3 scripts/sync_cw_skills.py --apply    # build temp Mars consumer and refresh GENERATED components
python3 scripts/sync_cw_skills.py --list     # print the GENERATED/MANUAL classification
```

head: AGENTS.md > Syncing the `cw/` distribution
text: After editing a generated `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, run `--apply` so Mars lowers it into the cw distribution. Adapt MANUAL skills by hand, then run the check. The sync script builds a temporary Mars consumer and may need network access to resolve git dependency tags. CI fails on generated drift, leaked Meridian vocab in `cw/`, or dangling skill/agent references. cw frontmatter is Claude vocab (`name` + `description`, plus Claude-native flags such as `disable-model-invocation` when Mars lowers `model-invocable: false`) — never Mars `type`/`model-invocable`/`effort`.

head: AGENTS.md > Syncing the `cw/` distribution
text: **`creative-writing-muse`:** source lives in `skills/creative-writing-muse` and is generated into `cw/skills/creative-writing-muse`. It is a user-activated, single-agent muse mode for skills-only environments; the `muse` agents do not load it. The agents follow the Product Lead pattern directly: capture author intent, craft specialist prompts, route work, synthesize results, and speak back to the author.

head: AGENTS.md > Syncing the `cw/` distribution
text: **Plugin manifest:** `cw/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is required. Claude Code auto-discovers components without it, but the marketplace **add-from-GitHub** path (Cowork / claude.ai) validates the plugin and *rejects it* if the manifest is missing. `claude plugins validate .claude-plugin/marketplace.json` only checks the marketplace schema, not the plugin — so CI also runs `claude plugins validate cw`, which validates the manifest plus every agent/skill component file.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Patterns

head: AGENTS.md > Development
text: **Release flow:** Bump version in `mars.toml` → commit → tag `vX.Y.Z` → push tag → CI creates GitHub Release with `.skill` artifacts.

head: AGENTS.md > Development
text: **Pre-commit hook:** `.githooks/pre-commit` front-loads the distribution-breaking checks (cw skill sync + `claude plugins validate cw`) so they fire at commit time instead of only in CI. It's committed but not auto-installed — enable it once per clone:

head: AGENTS.md > Development
text: It blocks the commit on failure; bypass a single commit with `git commit --no-verify`. (Skips plugin validation if the `claude` CLI isn't on PATH.)

head: AGENTS.md > Development
text: **CI:** PRs run `mars check` + marketplace/plugin validation (`claude plugins validate`) + frontmatter validation + `sync_cw_skills.py` drift check + zip build. Tag pushes create releases.

head: Code style
text:
- IMPORTANT: Most code should carry zero comments, occasionally one. When something feels like it needs explaining, try better naming or structure.
  - Only comment on what the code can't show. For example, non-obvious constraints, subobtimal approaches, edge cases that are not covered, or links to external documentation or references.
  - Do not restate what the code does. Comments should express the why.

head: AGENTS.md > Mock Architecture
text: Mocks span two process boundaries — an **inner mock** in the app context and an **outer mock** in the test process. The inner mock (created via `@wdio/native-spy`) intercepts real API calls inside the app. The outer mock (vitest-compatible) is used for test assertions. Call data syncs one-way from inner to outer via `update()`, serialized as JSON across CDP/WebDriver boundaries. See `docs/architecture/mock-architecture.md` for details.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Standards > Comments

- Don't couple comments to details that drift without signal — specific
  version numbers, transient stack traces, "this used to do X". These rot
  silently as the environment changes. Keep the rationale, drop the
  citation: `// Forge silently broke packaging in a patch release` rather

  they're an active signal to update. `// Workaround for forge/forge#4219;
  drop once a fix lands` is useful even years later.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution
text:
Bengal builds the sites people read documentation on. Bugs here reach end users
through someone else's content: broken links, wrong code blocks, stale pages,
empty search indexes. Treat these as safety rules, not style preferences.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > North Star
text:
We make free-threaded Python worth deploying for content tooling. Bengal should
prove that a documentation generator can run on a pure-Python default path,
scale with cores on Python 3.14t, and require zero npm for normal site builds.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > North Star
text:
We favor readable Python, real parallelism, measurable performance, and
user-visible correctness. The public promise is visible in `README.md` and
`pyproject.toml`: Python 3.14+, pure-Python documentation generation,
incremental builds, AI-native outputs, validation, and extension points.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Non-Negotiables
text:
- **Pure Python default build path.** `README.md:9`, `README.md:11`, and
  `pyproject.toml:8` position Bengal around Python free-threading and zero npm.
  Normal site generation must not require npm, Node, or a JS toolchain. The
  optional assets pipeline is an explicit opt-in path and must stay documented as
  optional if it remains supported.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Non-Negotiables
text:
- **Python 3.14 is the floor.** `pyproject.toml:10`, `pyproject.toml:121`, and
  `pyproject.toml:276` set runtime, Ruff, and ty to Python 3.14.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Non-Negotiables
text:
- **Core is passive for new work.** `CONTRIBUTING.md:132` and `.importlinter:25`
  keep `bengal/core/` out of orchestration, server, rendering pipeline, and asset
  work. Do not add new core I/O or direct logging. Existing transitional debt in
  `bengal/core/asset/`, `bengal/core/resources/`, `bengal/core/theme/providers.py`,
  `bengal/core/output/`, and `bengal/core/page/page_core.py` is not precedent
  for new code.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Non-Negotiables
text:
- **Rendering owns presentation.** HTML, excerpts, TOCs, template URLs,
  shortcode/link extraction, page bundle views, and section URL ergonomics
  belong under `bengal/rendering/`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Non-Negotiables
text:
- **Pipeline records stay immutable.** `bengal/core/records.py:151`,
  `bengal/core/records.py:224`, and `bengal/core/records.py:245` define
  `ParsedPage`, `RenderedPage`, and `SourcePage` as frozen records. Do not add
  setters, plugin state, or late mutation.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Non-Negotiables
text:
- **Writes are atomic.** `CONTRIBUTING.md:144` names `atomic_write_text`,
  `atomic_write_bytes`, and `json_compat.dump` as the output/cache write path.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Non-Negotiables
text:
- **Sharp edges are bugs.** `pyproject.toml:147`, `pyproject.toml:176`, and
  `pyproject.toml:182` keep exception handling visible. No silent `except`, no
  casual `# type: ignore`, no vague flags, and no error that fails to say what
  to do next.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Non-Negotiables
Bengal Agent Constitution > Architecture Boundaries
text:
| Path | Steward / Contract |
|---|---|
| `bengal/core/` | Passive domain model, compatibility surfaces, import-linter core boundary |
| `bengal/core/page/` | `Page` compatibility surface and template-facing shims |
| `bengal/core/section/` | `Section` hierarchy surface and navigation compatibility |
| `bengal/core/site/` | `Site` coordinator, registries, services, and lifecycle compatibility |
| `bengal/rendering/` | Presentation, templates, URLs, excerpts, TOCs, shortcodes, links |
| `bengal/rendering/template_functions/` | Explicitly registered template globals, filters, and tests |
| `bengal/rendering/pipeline/` | Parse/render records, dependency capture, output handoffs |
| `bengal/orchestration/` | Build lifecycle, phase handoffs, scheduling, stats, site runner |
| `bengal/orchestration/build/` | Hardcoded build phases and plugin phase hook timing |
| `bengal/orchestration/incremental/` | Rebuild decisions, cache/provenance invalidation, warm-build parity |
| `bengal/build/` | Build contracts and provenance helpers; detector logic currently lives in orchestration/effects |
| `bengal/cache/` | Persistent cache stores, indexes, migration tolerance, atomic cache writes |
| `bengal/config/` | Config schema, loaders, env overrides, snapshots, validation |
| `bengal/cli/` | Milo command surface, terminal output, command registration |
| `bengal/server/` | Dev server, live reload, watcher, reactive preview, Pounce integration |
| `bengal/protocols/` | Public structural contracts for plugins, core, rendering, build hooks |
| `bengal/plugins/` | Entry-point discovery, plugin registry, hook application |
| `bengal/content/` | Content discovery, sources, notebook handling, versioning |
| `bengal/content_types/` | Section/content classification and generated strategy scaffolds |
| `bengal/parsing/` | Patitas-backed parsing, directives, roles, renderer integration |
| `bengal/autodoc/` | Python, CLI, and OpenAPI extraction plus virtual page models |
| `bengal/assets/` | Asset manifest, CSS directives, generated asset contracts |
| `bengal/themes/default/` | Default theme templates, CSS/JS, icons, swizzle contracts |
| `bengal/scaffolds/` | `bengal new ...` generated site/content/theme artifacts |
| `bengal/postprocess/` | Sitemap, feeds, search, llms.txt, redirects, output format artifacts |
| `bengal/health/` | Validators, reports, remediation, linkcheck, artifact checks |
| `bengal/snapshots/` | Frozen render-time site/page/section/template snapshots |
| `bengal/utils/` | Shared primitives, atomic I/O, paths, concurrency, observability |
| `bengal/audit/` | Generated artifact audit records and reviewer-facing checks |
| `site/` | Public docs source and dogfood site |
| `tests/` | Behavioral proof, fixtures, mocks, markers, regression memory |
| `benchmarks/` and `tests/performance/` | Performance evidence and regression budgets |
| `plan/` | RFCs, epics, deferred design evidence, not shipped behavior |
| `bengal-syntax-highlighter/` | VS Code grammar package; not part of the Python build path |

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Architecture Boundaries
text:
`Page`, `Section`, and `Site` are compatibility surfaces and coordinators, not
dumping grounds. Page template-facing properties may remain as shims, but should
delegate to rendering helpers. Section stays mixin-free. Site coordinates
registries, services, and orchestration. Protocols, plugins, and hook surfaces
are public contracts.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Governance Alignment
text:
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` records review routing. Bengal is solo-maintained, so a
  global `*` fallback plus area-specific lines all route to `@lbliii` (the owner
  who approves changes). Ownership of high-risk surfaces — public API/protocols/
  plugins, CLI and config, rendering/templates/themes, orchestration/cache/
  incremental/dev server, docs/site/scaffolds, and release/dependencies/
  workflows — is recorded explicitly rather than left implicit. Human approval
  routing is therefore `codeowners-routed` (last-match-wins). Some scoped
  `AGENTS.md` files in subdirectories may still describe the older
  `manual-confirmation-needed` state until they are swept separately.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Governance Alignment
text:
- Canonical public knowledge lives in `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
  `CHANGELOG.md`, `site/content/`, `tests/README.md`, and `.importlinter`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Governance Alignment
text:
- CI and release governance lives in `.github/workflows/`, `pyproject.toml`,
  `uv.lock`, and `.github/dependabot.yml`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Governance Alignment
text:
- Stewards advise. Humans approve public API, dependency, release, security,
  persistence, and user-facing contract changes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text: Check in before doing any of these:

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text:
- Changing public API, plugin protocols, hook signatures, `bengal.plugins`
  entry points, CLI flags/commands, config keys, release layout, or
  `BengalError` construction.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text:
- Adding a runtime dependency, build phase, persistence schema, migration,
  output format contract, security/auth behavior, or irreversible operation.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text: - Touching immutable pipeline records or adding mutation to pipeline stages.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text:
- Reintroducing core mixins or growing the empty mixin allow-list guarded by
  `tests/unit/core/test_no_core_mixins.py`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text:
- Hoisting a deferred import to module level. Run `check-cycles` or the
  import-linter equivalent first.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text:
- Changing concurrency, lifecycle, watcher, cache invalidation, or
  free-threaded shared state behavior.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text: - Chasing ty diagnostics below the current project floor without a scoped plan.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text:
- Reorganizing methods on `Site`, `Page`, or `Section` instead of deleting
  vestiges and migrating callers.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text: - Fixing a test/code disagreement without knowing which one is authoritative.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text:
- Guessing at an unreproduced bug. Ask for a minimal repro, ideally a
  `tests/roots/` fixture.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Stop And Ask
text: - Folding adjacent issues into a bug fix. Flag them as follow-up work.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - Adding npm or JS tooling to make the frontend path easier.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - Moving rendering behavior back into core.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - Rebuilding old forwarding layers around `Site`, `Page`, or `Section`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text:
- `try: ... except Exception: pass`; if swallowing is intentional, emit a
  diagnostic with what and why.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - `# type: ignore`, `noqa: S110`, or `noqa: S112` to clear noise.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - Defensive validation inside core instead of at boundaries.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - Direct `logger.X` inside `bengal/core/`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - Non-atomic output or cache writes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - Refactoring during a bug fix unless the refactor is the fix.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Anti-Patterns
text: - Treating `plan/` as shipped behavior or `site/public/` as authored docs.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text:
Read this root file plus the closest scoped `AGENTS.md` before editing a tree.
The root is the constitution, routing guide, and **steward** swarm protocol.
Backlog drive (`drive` / `board` / `claim`) lives in `plan/BACKLOG.md` — do not
embed the orchestrator here. Scoped files are domain stewards for concrete
trees, public contracts, product surfaces, safety boundaries, docs, tests,
examples, fixtures, and checks.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text: Every steward uses this operating model:

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text: - **Point Of View:** who or what the domain represents.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text: - **Protect:** invariants, contracts, quality bars, and failure modes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text: - **Contract Checklist:** local surfaces that must agree when the domain changes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text: - **Advocate:** features, fixes, and investments the domain should push for.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text: - **Own:** tests, docs, examples, fixtures, maintenance checks, and proof paths.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text:
- **Do Not** and **Serve Peers:** optional; include only when they carry
  non-obvious local guidance.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward System
text:
Stewards advise from their domain's interests; the implementing agent owns
synthesis, scope, and final implementation. Cross-boundary PRs include
`Steward Notes` naming each area and how its invariants were protected.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Contract Checklist
text:
- Identify every surface that should agree: CLI/API, programmatic use,
  protocols, schema/types, templates/UI, docs, examples, scaffolds, tests,
  benchmarks, changelog, and release smoke tests.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Contract Checklist
text:
- Every accepted finding must name required proof and collateral updates, or
  explicitly say `no collateral: <reason>`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Contract Checklist
text:
- Docs, examples, and scaffolds move in the same PR as user-facing behavior
  unless synthesis records why they are unaffected.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Contract Checklist
text:
- Contract-affecting PRs include a parity matrix when behavior spans multiple
  entrypoints.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Contract Checklist
text:
- Factual P0/P1 findings carry `machine-verified`,
  `manual-confirmation-needed`, or `not-machine-verifiable`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Signal Format
text:
Steward findings should be contract-oriented, evidence-backed, and
collateral-aware.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Signal Format
text:
- Evidence: `<source-file>:<line>` and, for content audits,
  `<source-file>:<line> -> <doc-file>:<line>`

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Signal Format
text:
- Verification Status: machine-verified / manual-confirmation-needed /
  not-machine-verifiable

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Convergence Rule
text:
Two or more independent stewards flagging the same accepted finding promotes it
to P0 unless the implementing agent disproves the factual basis with source
evidence. Convergence promotion applies to the same underlying contract break,
not merely similar wording.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text:
- Implementation review: `ask stewards`, `bugbash`, `review swarm`,
  `steward synthesis`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: - Content audit: `audit docs`, `content audit`, `accuracy pass`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text:
- Backlog burn-down: `drive`, `board`, `claim #N` — see `plan/BACKLOG.md`.
  Bare `swarm` is ambiguous; prefer `drive` for workers and `review swarm`
  for stewards.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: When delegation is available:

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: - Spawn independent steward agents for affected domains.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: - Each steward reads root plus its closest scoped `AGENTS.md`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: - Each steward advocates only for that domain's interests.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: - Each steward returns findings in the Steward Signal Format.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: - The implementing agent owns synthesis and final decisions.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: - Keep PR scope bounded to accepted findings and their proof/collateral.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text: - Defer unrelated suggestions to not-now/follow-up.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Swarms
text:
For backlog, roadmap, or prioritization work, consult all scoped stewards and
rank work by convergence, blast radius, dependency order, risk reduction,
reversibility, public contracts, free-threading, and user-visible correctness.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Saga Goals
text:
When tooling supports an active goal, use it as the runtime mission tracker for
a selected saga. Goals do not replace `plan/ROADMAP.md`, active plan files,
commits, changelog fragments, or final plan updates.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Saga Goals
text:
- Create a goal only after the saga is selected and the user explicitly asks to
  start a saga, start a goal, resume a goal, or make a named saga active.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Saga Goals
text:
- The goal objective should name the active plan slice, expected proof, commit
  discipline, and required plan/archive update.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Saga Goals
text:
- Do not create a goal for open-ended discovery. First answer "what should we
  work on next?" from `plan/BACKLOG.md` (`board`) plus `plan/ROADMAP.md` and
  steward consultation, then start the goal once the user accepts or asks to
  begin. For a long delegated burn-down, the user says `drive`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Saga Goals
text:
- Keep the goal active until the saga is genuinely closed: code/docs/tests or
  explicit no-impact notes are done, commits are scoped, proof is recorded, and
  planning state is refreshed.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Saga Goals
text:
- Mark a goal complete only when no required saga work remains. Mark it blocked
  only when the same blocker has repeated and no meaningful progress is
  possible without user input or external state.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Global Sweep On Accepted P0s
text:
Before closing an accepted P0, grep the relevant docs and code trees for the
same wrong claim or behavior. At minimum sweep `bengal/`, `site/content/`,
`README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `tests/`, and `plan/` unless
the finding is provably narrower. Record the command or mark why it is not
machine-verifiable.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Feedback Loop
text:
- **Steward miss:** when a bug escapes an applicable steward, update the
  checklist, a regression test, a docs/snippet check, a routing rule, or record
  why the miss should not become policy.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Feedback Loop
text:
- **Steward overreach:** when a steward repeatedly pulls unrelated work into
  PRs, narrow the checklist, split the steward, or move the concern to
  follow-up.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Feedback Loop
text: - Repeated high-quality findings should become checklist items.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Steward Feedback Loop
text: - Repeated noisy findings should be pruned or clarified.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Extension Routing
text:
- **Template function or filter:** add a module under
  `bengal/rendering/template_functions/` with `register(env, site)` and wire it
  in `register_all()`. No auto-discovery.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Extension Routing
text:
- **Content type strategy:** use `bengal new content-type <name>` or register a
  `ContentTypeStrategy` from `bengal/content_types/`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Extension Routing
text:
- **Plugin hook:** evolve `bengal/protocols/` and `bengal/plugins/` together,
  with contract tests and migration notes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Extension Routing
text:
- **CLI command:** add a Milo command under `bengal/cli/milo_commands/` and
  register it with `cli.lazy_command(...)` in `bengal/cli/milo_app.py`. Use
  annotated parameters, dict returns, and CLI render helpers.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Extension Routing
text:
- **Build phase:** stop and ask. Build phases are hardcoded in
  `bengal/orchestration/build/__init__.py`; behavior changes should usually use
  plugin hooks.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Free-Threading And Performance
text:
This applies when work touches parallel builds, watchers, caches, render
pipelines, global state, template caches, asset manifests, or hot paths.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Free-Threading And Performance
text:
- Prefer immutable records, snapshots, ContextVars, thread-local render
  pipelines, and leaf locks over shared mutable state.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Free-Threading And Performance
text:
- State which shared state, lock, snapshot, cache key, or hot path was
  considered.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Free-Threading And Performance
text:
- Performance claims need a benchmark, timing comparison, or explicit
  no-impact explanation.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Free-Threading And Performance
text:
- Relevant evidence includes `tests/test_thread_safety.py`,
  `tests/performance/`, `benchmarks/`, and `bengal/concurrency.py`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Public Contracts
text:
This applies to CLI flags, config keys, protocols, plugin hooks, template
globals, generated files, package metadata, output formats, docs snippets, and
scaffolds.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Public Contracts
text:
- Every public contract change needs tests plus docs/snippet/scaffold parity or
  a no-impact note.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Public Contracts
text:
- Avoid widening `SiteLike`, `PageLike`, `SectionLike`, or `Plugin` for one
  internal caller.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Public Contracts
text:
- Keep `bengal/__init__.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `bengal/protocols/`,
  `bengal/plugins/`, and generated reference docs in agreement.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Release And Dependency Risk
text:
This applies to `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.github/workflows/`,
`CHANGELOG.md`, `changelog.d/`, and package-data changes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Release And Dependency Risk
text:
- Fresh-wheel behavior matters as much as locked-repo behavior. The release
  workflow smoke-tests the built wheel against freshly resolved dependencies.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Release And Dependency Risk
text: - Package-data changes need source-tree and installed-wheel proof.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Release And Dependency Risk
text:
- User-facing changes under `bengal/` need a `changelog.d/` fragment unless a
  maintainer marks the change exempt.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Release And Dependency Risk
text:
- Changelog fragments and release pages are written for **third-party consumers**,
  not maintainers: no internal coinage (phase/sprint/saga/epic/plan-file/branch
  slug), no process narration, no contributor-only churn — translate mechanism to
  user-visible effect. Rules live in `docs/b-stack-changelog-strategy.md`; stewards
  in `changelog.d/AGENTS.md` and the "Release Pages" section of `site/AGENTS.md`;
  `poe changelog-lint` enforces the high-precision subset.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Documentation Accuracy
text:
This applies to README, site docs, generated reference docs, examples, snippets,
and migration notes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Documentation Accuracy
text: - Do not document aspirational behavior as shipped behavior.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Documentation Accuracy
text:
- Every command, config field, template function, and public API claim traces to
  source, generated help, schema, or a test.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Cross-Cutting: Documentation Accuracy
text:
- When a P0 content correction is accepted, run the Global Sweep before closing
  it.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns
text:
- **Fabricated CLI or config fields.** Verification: every flag traces to

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns
text:
- **Unverified finding regression.** Verification: every factual P0/P1 carries

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns
text:
- **Narrow-fix regression.** Verification: every accepted P0 closure runs the
  Global Sweep above.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns
text:
- **Dependency drift between lockfile and wheel.** Evidence:
  `CHANGELOG.md:52` and `.github/workflows/python-publish.yml:37`. Verification:

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns
text:
- **Kida strict-undefined template fallout.** Evidence: `CHANGELOG.md:31` and

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns

- **Stale CLI command shape.** Evidence: `CHANGELOG.md:65`. Verification:

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns
text:
- **Silent fallback or swallowed error.** Evidence: `CHANGELOG.md:67`,

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns
text:
- **Cache/provenance divergence and stale outputs.** Evidence:
  `CHANGELOG.md:95`, `CHANGELOG.md:127`, and incremental integration tests.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns
text:
- **Package data missing from wheels.** Evidence:
  `tests/unit/test_package_data.py:3`. Verification: package-data tests and

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Known Regression Patterns

text:
- `make test` passes, or the scoped equivalent is run with rationale. Hot-path

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text: - `make ty` or `uv run ty check bengal/` does not regress the diagnostic floor.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text:
- `ruff format` and `ruff check --fix` are clean, or formatting/lint gaps are

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text:
- Tests cover the interesting path, including failure paths and malformed input

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text: - Docs, examples, scaffolds, and templates are updated for user-facing changes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text:
- Free-threading, performance, or security-sensitive changes state what shared

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text:
- User-facing changes under `bengal/` include a `changelog.d/` fragment or an

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text: - Public API or plugin protocol changes include migration notes.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text:
- Errors use `BengalError` with useful `code`, `context`, `suggestion`, and

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text:
- Every accepted steward finding has test/docs/example/benchmark proof or an

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text: - Import-linter or cycle checks pass when imports move.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text: - PR description explains why. The diff explains what.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Done Criteria
text: Tests passing is not the same as done.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Review Notes
text: - One concern per PR unless a broad rename is the concern.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Review Notes
text:
- Commit style: `<scope>: <description>`, using scopes such as `core`,
  `orchestration`, `rendering`, `cache`, `cli`, `tests`, `docs`, `deps`, or
  `release`.

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Review Notes
text:
- Flag surprises: weird tests, unused public names, suppressions, dead code,
  changed allow-lists, stale docs, benchmark gaps, free-threading assumptions,

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > Review Notes

head: Bengal Agent Constitution > When This File Is Wrong

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
Work items live in `.work/todo.jsonl`. **Settings live in `.work/config.yml` — read that
file; do not infer settings from this document.** This file is policy only, which is why
`AGENTS.md` is a symlink to it: one policy, every harness. Do not add harness-specific
notes here.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **Every request that produces work is broken into worklog items FIRST.** Run
  `bin/worklog add` (see the work-track skill) before starting, and move items
  `in_progress` → `done` as the work happens — the UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks
  enforce this. Unrecorded work is invisible work.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **Exiting plan mode is not optional bookkeeping.** Every plan MUST end by running
  `worklog plan-capture`, which writes `docs/plans/<date>-<name>.md` and appends the
  plan's steps as work items. This is also enforced by a hook; if you find yourself
  ending a plan without it, that's a bug, not a shortcut. After capture, plans and
  their items are published (tickets + wiki) by a background subagent; implementation
  never waits on publishing.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **Plans are the permanent design record.** `docs/plans/` is where the *why* lives — it
  is the specification half of spec-driven development, checked into the repo and
  published to the wiki for exactly that reason. A plan is written once and never
  regenerated or rewritten. If the design changed, write a NEW plan with
  `supersedes: <slug>` in its front matter. Do not edit history: the record of why the
  first approach was abandoned is the most valuable thing in the file. When you need to
  know why a decision was made, read the plan, not the ticket.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **If you discover work mid-flight that wasn't in the plan** — a bug, a missing
  migration, a broken test — run `worklog add --unplanned --discovered-during <item>`
  BEFORE doing the work. Do not silently absorb it. Unplanned work that never gets
  recorded is why estimates never improve.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **When a plan is complete, run `worklog sync`.** This closes items, updates the
  ticketing system, regenerates the roadmap, and publishes. Partial failure is expected
  and fine — sync is best-effort by design and reports its drift.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **When asked for a status report**, run `worklog status --kind <daily|weekly|timecard>`.
  It writes `docs/status/<date>-<kind>.md`, commits, and publishes to the wiki. Never
  paste a status report into chat without writing the file — an unrecorded status report
  is a rumour.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **Status reports are frozen once published.** If last Tuesday's daily was wrong, write
  the correction into today's report. Do not regenerate an old one: someone read it and
  made a decision from it.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **Never hand-edit `docs/roadmap.md`.** It is generated and CI-checked. To change the
  roadmap, change the work items.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **Design docs and code walkthroughs are generated, never hand-edited.** The design-docs
  skill regenerates `docs/designs/` at release via background agents: the `current_*`
  pair is a sanctioned in-place rewrite (like `docs/roadmap.md`). A freeze is a short
  dated note (tag + git_hash + delta from the previous freeze), not a copy of the live
  pair. Existing full dated copies stay frozen. A hand-edit is either overwritten at
  the next release or corrupts a frozen record — fix the code or the skill instead.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **Tests must hold coverage.** CI enforces >=80% line coverage on `bin/*.py`; the
  target is 95%. New modules ship with tests, and a PR that drops coverage below the
  floor does not merge.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **PRs merge only when every quality gate is green.** Arm `gh pr merge --auto --merge`
  (or `/worklog:merge`) so GitHub merges when required checks pass; the poll loop is
  fallback. Pending means wait; failing means fix. Never `--admin`, never squash
  (ADR-0008), never bypass a gate, never merge blind.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **Never edit `.work/*.jsonl` with an editor or a shell redirect.** Use `worklog`. Every
  write must be a well-formed event terminated with a newline; a hand-edit that drops the
  trailing newline corrupts the next merge.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text:
- **One session per working directory.** Two assistant sessions sharing a checkout switch
  branches out from under each other mid-operation and independently "fix" the same
  problem in different ways. Give each session its own `git worktree`. `worklog` warns
  when it sees more than one session active here, but the warning is advisory and arrives
  after the fact — the worktree is the actual fix.

head: Acme Platform > Work tracking policy
text: <!-- worklog:taxonomy:start -->

head: Acme Platform > Work taxonomy
text: Every work item sits on four independent axes:

head: Acme Platform > Work taxonomy
text:
| Axis | Field | Values | Answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level | `level` | epic / story / task / subtask | size & place in the parent tree |
| Kind | `kind` | feature / bug / ops / triage | nature of the work |
| Milestone | `milestone` | free string (e.g. v0.6.0) or null | what ships together |
| Planned | `unplanned` + `discovered_during` | bool + ULID | deliberate vs discovered |
