head: AGENTS.md
text: Guidance for any AI agent working in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > What this is
text:
Cookie AutoDelete V3 — a **Manifest V3** browser extension (TypeScript + React +
Redux) that auto-deletes unwanted cookies and other site data. It's a MV3 fork of
the original Cookie AutoDelete. Ships one codebase to both **Chromium** (Chrome /
Edge / Brave / Vivaldi) and **Firefox**; the two differ only by a manifest patch
at build time.

head: AGENTS.md > Working agreements
text:
- **Never push to `main`.** Work on a branch and open a PR. `main` is protected and
  a push to it auto-publishes a release (see Release process).

head: AGENTS.md > Working agreements
text:
- **Every PR updates the release notes.** Add/extend an entry in
  `src/ui/settings/ReleaseNotes.json` under the version this PR ships in. That file
  feeds the "What's New" Welcome tab users see after an update.

head: AGENTS.md > Working agreements
text:
- **Code is self-explaining.** Prefer clear names over comments. Add a comment only
  when the *why* is non-obvious (e.g. an MV3 service-worker quirk, a
  cross-browser workaround) — the existing comments in `src/background/` are the
  bar to match, not to exceed.

head: AGENTS.md > Working agreements
text: - Run `npm run test-all` (tests + lint) before opening a PR. Lint is zero-warnings.

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text: Run a single test file / name:

head: AGENTS.md > Commands
text: Version bump (writes both `package.json` **and** `extension/manifest.json`):

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Two build targets, one source
text:
`extension/manifest.json` is authored as the Chromium MV3 manifest. At package time
`tools/buildFilesDev.js` clones it in memory and patches per target
(`chromePatchManifest` / `firefoxPatchManifest`): Firefox gets the
`contextualIdentities` permission + `browser_specific_settings` and its
`service_worker` entry is rewritten to `background.scripts`; Chromium gets those
stripped. The on-disk manifest is restored after each zip. **Don't hand-edit the
manifest per browser — change the patch functions.**

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Two build targets, one source
text:
`webext-browser` types + `webextension-polyfill` give one `browser.*` API across
both. MV3/Chrome-only surfaces absent from the Firefox type defs (e.g.
`runtime.onSuspend`) are reached through explicit casts — see the bottom of
`src/background/index.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Background service worker — `src/background/`
text: MV3 terminates the SW aggressively, which drives the design here:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Background service worker — `src/background/`
text:
- **`index.ts`** registers every event listener **synchronously at module top
  level** so Chrome wakes the SW on the event, then `await ready()` before touching
  the store. Registering listeners late (inside async init) means a cold wake
  misses the first message — that's why the redux-webext connect/message protocol
  is re-implemented inline here instead of via `createBackgroundStore`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Background service worker — `src/background/`
text:
- **`lifecycle.ts`** owns one-time init (`ready()` — idempotent, retryable),
  `getStore()`, and the **save debouncer**. State persists to
  `storage.local` (full state) and `storage.session` (the `cache` slice); a
  synchronous `flushSave()` on `runtime.onSuspend` guards against loss on
  termination.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Background service worker — `src/background/`
text: - **`whatsNew.ts`** opens the Welcome tab on version update (gated by a setting).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > State — `src/redux/`
text:
Redux + redux-thunk. `State.ts` / `Reducers.ts` / `Actions.ts`, with the shared
`State` / `Expression` / `Setting` shapes and the `SettingID`, `SiteDataType`,
`ListType` **const enums** declared globally in `src/typings/Global.d.ts` (no
import needed). The UI talks to the background store over **redux-webext**: the
popup/settings dispatch actions that the background applies to the single source
of truth, then pushes state back over the port.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Cleanup engine — `src/services/`
text:
`CleanupService.ts` is the core: decides what to delete on tab-close / domain-change
/ manual / startup, honouring the **whitelist / greylist** expression lists and
per-expression `cleanSiteData` flags. Cookies are removed via `chrome.cookies`
(partition-aware — supports CHIPS `partitionKey`); non-cookie site data goes through
`chrome.browsingData.remove*`, which is **host-scoped only, not partition-aware**.
That asymmetry is why cross-site partitioned entries get their cookies cleaned but
their cache/storage left alone — see `isCrossSitePartitioned` and the full rationale
in `docs/chrome-vs-extensions-api.md`. Other services: `TabEvents`, `CookieEvents`,
`AlarmScheduler`/`AlarmEvents`, `ContextMenuEvents`, `BrowserActionService` (icon),
`BrowserDetect`, `SettingService`, and `Libs.ts` (shared helpers: domain parsing,
`getSetting`, `cadLog`, CHIPS detection).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > UI — `src/ui/`
text:
Two independent React roots built as separate webpack entries: `popup/`
(per-site quick actions) and `settings/` (full options, expression tables, activity
log, Welcome/What's-New). `common_components/` is shared. Each entry ships as **one
self-contained bundle** (`splitChunks: false`) — MV3 SWs and `chrome-extension://`
pages can't reliably load webpack's async split chunks.

head: AGENTS.md > Release process
text:
`package.json` version is the **source of truth** (kept in sync with
`extension/manifest.json` by `tools/bumpVersion.js`). Pushing to `main`
(`.github/workflows/release-on-main.yml`) resolves that version and, **only if a
`v<version>` release doesn't already exist**, runs test → lint → build and publishes
a GitHub Release with the Chrome `.zip` + Firefox `.xpi`. So a release is cut by
merging a version bump to `main` — never by pushing directly.

head: AGENTS.md > Release process
text:
Before merging that version bump, also run `npm run test:e2e` locally — CI only
runs the mocked Jest suite, so the real-browser harness (see Tests below) is the
last check against actual cookie deletion before the release goes out.

head: AGENTS.md > Tests
text:
Jest + ts-jest. Tests live under `__tests__/` (currently the build tooling and
release workflows); setup in `__tests__/setup.js`, `testEnvironment: node`.

head: AGENTS.md > Tests
text:
`__tests__/e2e/` is a **local pre-release harness**, not part of `npm test`. It
loads the built extension into Playwright's Chromium, browses real sites, and
asserts against the real cookie jar — the one thing the mocked unit tests cannot
do. It needs network access and is excluded from Jest via
`testPathIgnorePatterns`. Run `npm run test:e2e` before cutting a release.

head: AGENTS.md > Tests
text:
Failures are prefixed to say who is at fault: `SETUP FAILED` (harness),
`PRECONDITION FAILED` (site or network), `CLEANUP FAILED` (a real CAD
regression). Only the last one should block a release.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Bug Fixes
text: Always reproduce a reported bug before changing code. Confirm the failure using the narrowest reliable reproduction and record the current behaviour so the fix can be verified against it. If reproduction is impossible because required data, credentials or services are unavailable, state that clearly before proceeding.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Bug Fixes
text: After fixing the bug, rerun the original reproduction as well as the regression test. Test externally visible behaviour and durable state rather than private implementation details. Prefer real models and database behaviour over mocks.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions
text: Start with the smallest correct change in the current owner. Before editing, identify the source of truth and the invariant being protected. Read [the architecture guide](ARCHITECTURE.md) when a change crosses subsystem boundaries.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Rails ownership ladder
text: Put behaviour in the narrowest layer that naturally owns it:

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Rails ownership ladder
text: 1. **Controller**: HTTP concerns, authentication, authorisation, strong parameters and response selection.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Rails ownership ladder
text: 2. **Model**: invariants, state transitions and behaviour owned by persisted data.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Rails ownership ladder
text: 3. **Scope or query object**: reusable data retrieval. Introduce a query object only when scopes stop composing clearly.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Rails ownership ladder
text: 4. **Job**: delayed or retryable execution. Jobs must be idempotent.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Rails ownership ladder
text: 5. **Service object**: an operation that genuinely coordinates multiple models, external systems or transaction boundaries.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Rails ownership ladder
text: 6. **Concern**: a cohesive capability, not a place to hide unrelated model or controller size.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Rails ownership ladder
text: Do not create a service object merely to make a controller or model shorter. Extract an operation only when it has a coherent responsibility that does not naturally belong to one model.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Use database constraints for integrity and model validations for useful feedback.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Put related writes in a transaction. Do not make network calls inside that transaction.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Enqueue external side effects after commit where practical.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Make GoodJob jobs safe to retry without duplicate records, notifications or state transitions.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Treat caches, dashboard rollups and summaries as derived data. Identify and update the source of truth rather than repairing derived output.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Check authorisation separately from authentication.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Use bang methods when failure must abort the operation.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Do not use callbacks for workflows spanning multiple models or external systems.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Rescue only errors the code can meaningfully handle and rescue the narrowest exception class possible. Log enough context and re-raise unexpected failures. Never report success after a partial write.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Check query count and eager loading when rendering collections.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Store timestamps in UTC. For calendar boundaries and presentation, use `Time.current` or `Date.current` inside the user's `Time.use_zone(user.timezone)` context. Background jobs that calculate user-local calendar boundaries must establish that context explicitly.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > Correctness rules
text: - Use `Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)` rather than wall-clock time to measure elapsed execution time.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: Zoom out only when there is evidence that the current ownership boundary prevents a correct implementation. Evidence includes:

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: - The same business rule must change in three or more places.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: - Two modules disagree about the source of truth.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: - A correct operation cannot be made atomic within the current boundary.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: - Callbacks, jobs or cache refreshes repeatedly compensate for unclear ownership.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: - A collection of booleans represents an undocumented state machine.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: - Retry, concurrency or ordering bugs recur because state is implicit.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: - A public contract repeatedly leaks internal implementation details.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: - Tests require extensive stubbing because responsibilities cannot be exercised independently.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: Do not re-architect merely because a class is long but cohesive, a method gained one branch, two snippets look similar, an abstraction feels inelegant or a hypothetical future caller might need flexibility. Do not add an abstraction with only one caller unless it creates a clear ownership boundary or protects a critical invariant.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: Use this escalation order:

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: 1. Fix the bug in the existing owner.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: 2. Strengthen the owner's invariant or API.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: 3. Remove proven duplication around that invariant.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: 4. Extract one coherent responsibility.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: 5. Rework the subsystem boundary only when the earlier steps cannot make it correct.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Engineering Decisions > When to zoom out
text: Before a broad redesign, state the invariant, why the current owner cannot protect it, the smallest viable new boundary, migration and rollback risks and how behaviour will be preserved. Get user agreement on the plan unless the redesign is required to resolve an active correctness or security issue.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Git Practices
text: - **NEVER commit `config/database.yml`** unless explicitly asked to - contains sensitive local/production database credentials

text: - Always use the GitHub PR template at `.github/pull_request_template.md` when creating a PR.

text: - Write PR titles and descriptions in British English.

text: - Never use Oxford commas.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **Naming**: snake_case files/methods/vars, PascalCase classes, 2-space indent

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **Controllers**: Inherit `ApplicationController`, use `before_action`, strong params with `.permit()`

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **Models**: Inherit `ApplicationRecord`; keep domain behaviour with the model that owns the data; use enums and composable scopes where they clarify the domain

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **Concerns**: Use concerns only for cohesive capabilities with a clear name, not as miscellaneous storage

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **Error Handling**: Rescue specific failures that can be handled meaningfully; log context and let unexpected failures surface

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **Imports**: Use `include` for concerns, `helper_method` for view access

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **API**: Namespace under `api/v1/`, structured JSON responses with status codes

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **Jobs**: GoodJob with 4 priority queues, inherit from `ApplicationJob`, concurrency control for cache jobs

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Code Style (rubocop-rails-omakase)
text: - **Auth**: `ensure_authenticated!` for APIs, token via `Authorization` header or `?api_key=`

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Svelte 5 Runes
text: Don't mirror Inertia props into local `$state` with a `$effect` that just copies them back **for read-only display values**. Props are already reactive — bind to `user.foo` directly (or pass it as `value={user.foo}`) instead of introducing a redundant `let foo = $state(user.foo)` + `$effect(() => { foo = user.foo })`. Only introduce local `$state` when you actually need state that diverges from the prop.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Svelte 5 Runes
text: **Exception — editable form state for Inertia forms.** When the user edits the value locally (`bind:value`, `bind:group`, `bind:checked`), you legitimately need local `$state`, *and* you need a `$effect` to re-sync from props after a server validation error. On 422, Rails re-renders the same component with updated `application`/`form` props; if you only initialize once (`let foo = $state(application.bar)` or `let foo = $state(untrack(() => application.bar))`), the form fields will not reflect server-normalized values on re-render. Keep the `$effect` here — this is the legitimate use case, not the anti-pattern.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Svelte 5 Runes
text: If `svelte-check` warns `state_referenced_locally` on a `$state(prop)` initializer that you genuinely want to read once (e.g. a tab-default chosen from a prop that never changes after mount), wrap the initializer in `untrack(() => ...)` from `svelte` to silence it. Do **not** use `untrack` to silence the warning on editable form fields — that hides a real bug; restore the `$effect` instead.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Svelte 5 Runes
text: For computed values derived from props (`const x = prop === "a" ? ... : ...`), use `$derived(...)` instead of a bare `const` — otherwise `state_referenced_locally` will fire and the value won't update if the prop changes.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Path helpers (js_from_routes)
text: We use [js_from_routes](https://js-from-routes.netlify.app) to generate TypeScript path helpers from Rails routes, instead of passing `*_path` strings down as Inertia props. **Don't pass paths as props** — derive them on the client.

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Path helpers (js_from_routes)
text:
- **Don't:**
  ```ruby
  render inertia: "Foo", props: { update_path: my_foo_update_path }
  ```
  ```svelte
  <Form action={update_path} method="patch">
  ```

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Path helpers (js_from_routes)
text:
- **Do:**
  ```ruby
  render inertia: "Foo", props: {}
  ```
  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { fooThings } from "../../api";
    const updatePath = fooThings.update.path();
  </script>
  <Form action={updatePath} method="patch">
  ```

head: AGENTS.md for Hackatime > Path helpers (js_from_routes) > Adding a new path helper
text: 1. Mark the route in `config/routes.rb`: add `export: true` to the route or `resources` call, or wrap a group in `defaults export: true do ... end`. Beware that js_from_routes derives helper names from sibling routes on the same controller, so adding or removing an exported route can rename existing helpers — check `svelte-check` after changing exports.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Repo Invariants
text: These are non-negotiable architectural truths:

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Repo Invariants
text: - **Nodes are thin** - Nodes are coordination shells, not business logic containers

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Repo Invariants
text: - **Handlers own logic** - Business logic lives in handlers, not nodes

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Repo Invariants
text: - **Reducers are pure** - `delta(state, event) -> (new_state, intents[])` with no I/O

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Repo Invariants
text: - **Orchestrators emit, never return** - ORCHESTRATOR nodes cannot return `result`

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Repo Invariants
text: - **Contracts are source of truth** - YAML contracts define behavior, not code

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Repo Invariants
text: - **Unidirectional flow** - EFFECT → COMPUTE → REDUCER → ORCHESTRATOR, never backwards

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Agent Behavioral Rules
text: - Never disable pre-commit hooks, CI checks, or type checkers to make code pass. Fix the code instead.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Agent Behavioral Rules
text: - Never write state files to `~/.claude/` — use the workspace-local `.onex_state/` directory.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Agent Behavioral Rules > Contract-first topic definitions
text:
This repo defines the contract framework that all ONEX nodes use. Kafka topic
declarations belong in contract YAML files (`event_bus.publish_topics` /
`subscribe_topics`), not hardcoded in application code. Enforced by
`validation/validator_hardcoded_topics.py` plus the `demo-path-topic-coherence`
CI gate (`onex-demo-path-topic-gate`), and by
`validators/contract_config_compliance.py` (bare env reads, bus-bypass imports,
missing contract config; CI job `contract-config-compliance`).

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Non-Goals
text: We explicitly do **NOT** optimize for:

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Non-Goals
text: - **Backwards compatibility for internal APIs** - Internal Python module paths may change without notice. The stable external surface is defined in the External SDK Surface section below.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Non-Goals
text: - **Convenience over correctness** - Contract violations fail loudly

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Non-Goals
text: - **Business logic in nodes** - Nodes coordinate; handlers compute

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Non-Goals
text: - **Dynamic runtime behavior** - All behavior must be contract-declared

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Non-Goals
text: - **Implicit state** - All state transitions are explicit and auditable

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Non-Goals
text: - **Tight coupling** - Protocol-based DI enforces loose coupling

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Quick Reference > Pre-push scope (2026-09-11)

Pre-push is policy, type and lint checks plus two named test exceptions —
**nine hooks**, none of which runs the suite. The governed impacted-test
selector was retired from this stage; hosted CI is the enforced merge gate and
runs the identical selection. Measured in-tree on 2026-09-11, `pytest tests/
--ignore=tests/integration` collects 45,136 tests on both sides with zero rows
in either difference, and neither side applies a marker expression, so no test
lost its only execution path.

The runtime publishes to the contract's declared `terminal_event` topic with

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Project Structure > File Naming Conventions
text:
Every directory under `src/omnibase_core/` requires a file-name prefix
(`models/` → `model_*`, `enums/` → `enum_*`, `nodes/` → `node_*`, ...). The
enforced map is `DIRECTORY_PREFIX_RULES` in
`src/omnibase_core/validation/checker_naming_convention.py` (CI job
`naming-conventions`) — read it there; a hand-copied table here drifted.
Traps: the rule keys on the FIRST directory after `omnibase_core/`
(`models/cli/model_cli.py` follows the `models` rule, not `cli`), and several
directories accept multiple prefixes (e.g. `pipeline/`, `types/`, `errors/`,
`validation/`, `runtime/`). Always allowed: `__init__.py`, `conftest.py`,
`py.typed`, and `_`-prefixed private modules.

| **Immutable value** | `ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid", from_attributes=True)` |

| **Contract/external** | `ConfigDict(extra="forbid", ...)` |

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Pydantic Model Standards
text:
**`extra="forbid"` is mandatory on EVERY model** — `extra="ignore"` and `extra="allow"` are
default-deny. Declaring nothing is not neutral: Pydantic's default for an undeclared `extra`
is `"ignore"`, so a model with no `model_config` is *already* silently dropping unknown
fields. Multiple live silent-data-loss incidents came from exactly that. Inheriting `forbid`
from a base counts — do not redundantly redeclare it. If a model must tolerate unknown input,
add an explicit typed passthrough field; do not loosen `extra`. Enforced by
`omnibase_core.validators.pydantic_extra_forbid` as a CI gate (inside the required Quality
Gate) and a pre-commit hook; the only suppression is an expiring, ticket-and-PR-keyed waiver
in `extra_forbid_waivers.yaml`.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Pydantic Model Standards
text: **`from_attributes=True`**: Required on frozen models for pytest-xdist compatibility.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Pydantic Model Standards
text: **Mutable defaults**: ALWAYS use `default_factory` — e.g. `items: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)`

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Pydantic Model Standards > Plan Contract Enforcement Fields
text: `ModelPlanContract` carries plan-level enforcement metadata for the plan → epic → tickets → PR → dogfood chain. When adding a new plan, set `epic_id` (Linear epic identifier), `plan_phases`, `success_criteria` (via `ModelDoDItem`), and `halt_conditions` at the top level — not in `context`. The existing `phase: EnumPlanPhase` lifecycle field is distinct from `plan_phases: list[str]` and must not be confused.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Pydantic Model Standards > Plan Contract Enforcement Fields
text: **See**: [Pydantic Best Practices](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/guides/onex-pydantic-best-practices.md)

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Code Quality
text: - **TODO policy**: `# TODO(TICKET-ID): ...` — a TODO without a Linear ticket is blocked by the agent-left-marker pre-commit hook.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Code Quality
text: - **Type ignores**: specific code + reason — `# type: ignore[arg-type]` with a `NOTE(TICKET-ID):` explanation; never bare `# type: ignore`.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Code Quality
text: - **Enum vs Literal**: Enums on external contract surfaces and cross-process boundaries; Literals allowed only in internal parsing glue.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Code Quality
text: - **Thread safety**: Do NOT share node instances across threads — nodes are single-request scoped; use thread-local instances. See [Threading Guide](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/guides/onex-threading.md).

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Common Pitfalls
text: - Always call `super().__init__(container)` in node constructors — skipping base-class init breaks DI.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Common Pitfalls
text: - Node `__init__` takes `ModelONEXContainer`, never `ModelContainer` (value wrapper).

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Common Pitfalls
text: - `ModelHandlerOutput.for_orchestrator(result=...)` raises — ORCHESTRATOR cannot return `result` (see Handler Output Constraints).

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Common Pitfalls
text: - Prefer type-based DI resolution (`container.get_service(ProtocolEventBus)`); string-based is the late-binding-plugin exception, not the default.

head: CLAUDE.md - Omnibase Core > Common Pitfalls
text: - Use `uv run` for all Python commands.

text: Lightfriend is a full-stack AI assistant SaaS with Rust on both backend (Axum web framework) and frontend (Yew WebAssembly framework). head: AGENTS.md > macOS Prerequisites
text:
`just dev-backend` auto-runs `just setup-mac` which installs the Homebrew
keg-only libs the backend links against (sqlite, openssl@3, libiconv,
postgresql@14). `brew install` is idempotent so this is fast after the
first run. Non-macOS hosts no-op out of setup.

head: AGENTS.md > macOS Prerequisites
text:
If a new crate ever pulls in a new dylib and boot fails with
`Library not loaded: @rpath/libX.dylib`:

head: AGENTS.md > macOS Prerequisites
text: 1. Find the missing lib: `brew --prefix <formula>`

head: AGENTS.md > macOS Prerequisites
text:
2. Add a `link-arg=-Wl,-rpath,<prefix>/lib` entry to
   `backend/.cargo/config.toml`

head: AGENTS.md > macOS Prerequisites
text: 3. Add the formula to the `brew install` list in the `setup-mac` recipe

head: AGENTS.md > macOS Prerequisites
text: 4. `touch backend/src/main.rs && cargo build` to relink

head: AGENTS.md > macOS Prerequisites
text:
Homebrew keg-only means the lib is NOT symlinked into `/opt/homebrew/lib`,
so the default rpath doesn't find it. `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` is stripped by
macOS SIP at runtime and does not work as a workaround; rpaths must be
baked at link time.

head: AGENTS.md > macOS Prerequisites
text:
To validate a prod-style build actually works, run `just build-local`.
That runs the same Docker/Linux build the deploy pipeline uses; macOS
dyld issues are irrelevant inside that container.

head: Project Overview
text: - Project name: BambooHR PHP SDK

head: Project Overview
text: - What it does: Official PHP SDK providing a type-safe, fluent interface to the BambooHR REST API with auto-generated client classes, fluent builder pattern, automatic token refresh, and retry logic

head: Project Overview
text: - Primary language: PHP 8.1+

head: Tech Stack
text: - Framework: Client SDK (no web framework); fluent builder pattern wrapping auto-generated OpenAPI client

head: Tech Stack
text: - HTTP client: Guzzle (PSR-18 compatible)

head: Tech Stack
text: - Linting: PHP CodeSniffer (`phpcs.xml`); Static analysis: PHPStan (`phpstan.neon`)

head: Tech Stack
text: - Code generation: OpenAPI Generator with custom Mustache templates in `templates-php/` (these templates inject retry logic, request ID tracking, OAuth middleware, etc. into the generated output)

head: File Structure
text: - Hand-written source: `lib/Client/` (auth, builder, middleware, logging, token management)

head: File Structure
text: - Auto-generated APIs: `lib/Api/` — do NOT edit directly

head: File Structure
text: - Auto-generated models: `lib/Model/` — do NOT edit directly

head: File Structure
text: - Shared helpers: `lib/ApiErrorHelper.php`, `lib/ApiHelper.php`, `lib/ApiException.php`, `lib/Exceptions/`

head: File Structure
text: - Tests: `test/` (auto-generated stubs — mostly ignored); hand-written tests alongside `lib/` if needed

head: File Structure
text: - Examples: `examples/` — progressive usage examples

head: File Structure
text: - Scripts: `scripts/` — post-generation scripts (`cleanup_obsolete_files.sh`, `update_error_docs.sh`, `classify_semver.sh`, etc.)

head: File Structure
text: - Config: `composer.json`, `phpcs.xml`, `phpstan.neon`, `phpunit.xml.dist`

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: The SDK is auto-generated from `specs/public.yaml` using OpenAPI Generator. `make generate` runs the generator then executes a series of post-generation shell scripts for cleanup, error doc generation, and obsolete file removal.

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: **Semver classification** (`scripts/classify_semver.sh`) — compares two OpenAPI specs using `oasdiff` and outputs a bump level (`major` / `minor` / `patch` / `none`). Used in the automated release pipeline (epic SPN-2923).

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: Classification rules (highest wins):

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: - `oasdiff breaking --fail-on ERR` exits 1 → **major**

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: - changelog level 3 (ERR) → **major** (safety net)

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: - changelog level 2 (WARN) → **minor**

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: - changelog level 1 (INFO) additive/unknown → **minor**; deprecations only → **patch**

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: - `--apply` bumps `composer.json` for all levels including major

head: SDK Generation Pipeline
text: `scripts/oasdiff-severity-levels.txt` suppresses scope-change noise (~34 false-positive entries on every diff). Do NOT add `#` comments to this file — oasdiff will reject it. See `scripts/README.md` for full research notes.

head: Conventions
text: - PascalCase for classes; camelCase for methods/properties; `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants

head: Conventions
text: - Namespace root: `BhrSdk`; hand-written client code lives under `BhrSdk\Client`

head: Conventions
text: - All hand-written code should pass PHPStan level 8 (`phpstan.neon`); auto-generated code is excluded

head: Conventions
text: - All public methods require type declarations; use `?Type` nullable syntax where appropriate

head: Conventions
text: - Exception variables: use descriptive names (e.g., `$authFailedException`), never `$e`

head: Constraints
text: - Most files in `lib/Api/` and `lib/Model/` are **auto-generated** — edits are lost on `make generate`

head: Constraints
text: - To preserve a file across regeneration, add it to `.openapi-generator-ignore`

head: Constraints

head: Common Patterns > API Access

head: Common Patterns > API Access
text:
The accessor list is **generated**, not hand-maintained: `scripts/sync_accessors.php`
rewrites the block between the `// --- BEGIN/END GENERATED ACCESSORS ---` markers in
`lib/Client/ApiClient.php` from the `lib/Api/*.php` entries in
`.openapi-generator/FILES`. It runs automatically at the end of `make generate`, so a
spec tag rename updates the client instead of breaking it.

head: Common Patterns > API Access
text: Run `make sync-accessors` after regenerating; `make check-accessors` fails if they drift.

head: Common Patterns > API Access
text:
**Anything hand-written must live outside the markers.** `manual()` is the example — it
sits below the END marker, and `ManualApi` is deliberately absent from the FILES
manifest (it survives regeneration), so the sync cannot touch it. This is also why the
sync reads the manifest rather than globbing `lib/Api/`, which would sweep `ManualApi`
in and clobber its hand-written accessor.

head: Common Patterns > Custom / Unsupported Endpoints
text: Use `$client->manual()` (returns `ManualApi`) to call endpoints not yet in the generated SDK. Inherits all SDK auth, retry, and logging behavior.

head: Common Patterns > Exception Handling
Common Patterns > Exception Handling
text:
Full hierarchy:
```
ApiException (base)
├── ClientException (4xx)
│   ├── BadRequestException (400)
│   ├── AuthenticationFailedException (401)
│   ├── PermissionDeniedException (403)
│   ├── ResourceNotFoundException (404)
│   ├── MethodNotAllowedException (405)
│   ├── ConflictException (409)
│   ├── PayloadTooLargeException (413)
│   ├── UnsupportedMediaTypeException (415)
│   ├── UnprocessableEntityException (422)
│   └── RateLimitExceededException (429)
└── ServerException (5xx)
    ├── InternalServerErrorException (500)
    ├── NotImplementedException (501)
    ├── BadGatewayException (502)
    ├── ServiceUnavailableException (503)
    └── GatewayTimeoutException (504)
```
