head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide
text: Cross-platform SSH/SFTP client (Flutter UI on a Rust core, all 5 desktops + mobile). Open-source alt to Xshell/Termius. **Solo developer project.** This file is the single source of truth for agent rules.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Documentation Map
text: - **[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)** — module structure, APIs, data flows, design decisions. 3000+ lines.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Documentation Map
text: - **[`docs/USER_GUIDE.md`](docs/USER_GUIDE.md)** — end-user reference. Update whenever a user-visible flow / toggle / surface changes.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Documentation Map
text: - **[`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)** — build instructions, code style for humans.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Documentation Map
text: **Lookup discipline.** Never read `ARCHITECTURE.md` cover-to-cover. Use the `/doc <topic|§N.M>` skill (greps the heading, reads only that slice) or open the TOC and `Read` with `offset`+`limit`. A cross-link is another narrow fetch, not a full Read. `§N.M` below = look it up via /doc; bare links are kept only where the anchor is load-bearing.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: Apply on every response without re-reading.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Don't commit or push unless asked.** "commit" = commit only, "commit and push" = both. Default branch is `dev` — never push to `main` directly. Repo is public on GitHub.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **HARD STOP between fixes** — implement → tests → docs → post-fix summary → ask to commit. Batch-mode signals override (one combined summary at arc end). See § Commits.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **All files in English only** — code, comments, commits, docs.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Never suppress lint / compiler warnings** — `// ignore:`, `@SuppressWarnings`, `#[allow(*)]` (any inner lint, not just `clippy::…`), `// rustfmt::skip`, `// dart format off`, or anything equivalent. Fix root cause: use the symbol, delete it, `#[cfg(test)]`-gate test-only surfaces, drop stale attributes, or rewrite. "Documented surface" / "intentional, future use" / "false positive" are NOT fixes — they trigger "no hypothetical future requirements". Re-verify audit-agent verdicts on suppression markers personally.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **No fabrication anywhere — verify with `git log` / grep / measurement, or don't write the value.** Binds code, docs, tests, migrations, seed data, version strings, default config, perf numbers, "historical" labels, error messages. When asked to remove fabricated content, remove cleanly — never replace with new speculation.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Authorization boundaries — never destroy or overwrite tracked state without explicit permission.** Covers: deleting tracked files (plans, source, docs, tests), dropping DB schemas, force-overwriting uncommitted work, reverting / resetting commits, mass-rename or reformat outside the asked diff. When asked to remove X, remove exactly X — no slipped-in additions. Surface destructive steps once and wait.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Amend before push, never after.** When the prior commit is local-only and the next change belongs to the same logical arc that should have been part of it (typo, missed sibling edit, staging miss), `git commit --amend` is the project default — it overrides any harness rule that defaults to new commits "unless explicitly asked". After first push: new commits only, no exceptions.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Don't install packages without asking.** Latest stable only — no beta/dev/pre-release.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Always build via Makefile** — `make run/build-linux/test/lint`. Top-level umbrellas (`test`, `lint`, `format`, `format-check`) cover Dart + Rust; `dart-*` / `rust-*` variants when only one side is in scope. Never call `flutter` / `cargo` directly.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Skip `make lint` / `make test` for doc-only commits** — no `.dart` / `.rs` / `pubspec.yaml` / `Cargo.toml` in staged diff → skip; pre-commit hook runs `make check` automatically.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Cross-platform verification** — Android change → also iOS; Windows → also Linux + macOS.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Think systemically** — full scope and side effects, not just literal instruction.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Wide grep after every rule tightening.** When AGENTS.md edits remove a carve-out or expand a rule's scope, the prior plan / DoD is obsolete — what counts as a violation just changed. First follow-up = project-wide grep for every violation shape of the new rule, not just the old plan's literals. Each match migrates or gets a one-line justification. Per-commit diff review is necessary but not sufficient — agents fix only what's named; only the wide grep catches siblings.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Batch-mode signals override scope discipline.** A signal to finish everything end-to-end (in any language) or a handed-over multi-item plan → work the whole queue without stopping between items. Inconvenience, needed rework, or "can't QA this here" don't justify skipping, and a `.opencode/plans/` punch list is no substitute for doing the work. Stop only when the queue's empty, a real blocker hits, or the user says so.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **"Full" / "line-by-line" / "every item" reviews mean exactly that** — never silently truncate on token budget. Status reports must match reality — never call work "done" while items quietly deferred.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **One logical commit per arc**, not split into code/test/doc messages, unless user asks otherwise. Commit prose: no plan-IDs, no AI-tell phrasing ("I implemented…", "Let me know if…").

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Terse output by default.** No preambles, no recap-of-what-I-just-did paragraphs, no QA / validation matrices, no excessive bold / headers / nested numbered lists. Match shape to the question.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Ask before guessing UI placement.**

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Every change ships with docs + tests + translations** — incomplete commit otherwise.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **References are one-directional.** This file may link out to human docs; human docs and source comments must NOT link back to this file or any agent-instruction file. `.opencode/skills/*/SKILL.md` may reference this one freely. When a human doc wants to cite a rule, inline the substance.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Rust owns data AND logic; Flutter renders.** Every grammar, parser, validator, format-checker, decision tree, persistent state, and I/O lives in `lfs_core` / `lfs_os_security`. Flutter holds only the rendering surface — focus, hover, scroll, dialog visibility, TextField text-buffer pre-submit, animation controllers. No exceptions, no carve-outs ("form-level validation", "fast-path for common case", "test contexts that don't load FRB" etc.). If a sync FRB call hangs under `pumpAndSettle`, fix the test infrastructure (`pumpUntilFrbSettles` helper, DB / app-state bootstrap) — don't put grammar Dart-side. Data flow is one-way for truth: Rust → FRB → Riverpod/ChangeNotifier → widgets. **Don't cache Rust-owned data in Dart** (singletons, static fields, `late` vars, Riverpod NotifierProviders wrapping a Rust store) — re-fetch via FRB or subscribe to `BusEvent` stream. Mutations Rust-side only; Dart sends FRB call and re-reads, never patches locally. **The Dart `lib/core/` layer is itself Flutter-free** — it imports ZERO `package:flutter` (no UI `material`/`widgets`/`services`/`foundation`, no plugins `path_provider`/`app_links`/`flutter_foreground_task`, no `flutter_riverpod`, no l10n, no `xterm`); the only permitted framework edge is `flutter_rust_bridge`, the bridge core wraps. Everything else in `lib/core/` is pure Dart (`meta` for `@visibleForTesting`/`@immutable`, `uuid`, `path`). Placement when something in core needs a Flutter capability: app-wide UI state → `providers/`; plugin adapters (foreground service, camera, local-FS sandbox dirs, deep-link source) → `lib/platform/` or inject from the boundary; observable state core owns → a `dart:async` broadcast `Stream`, never `ChangeNotifier`/`ValueNotifier`; the support/sandbox dir → resolved once at startup and pinned Rust-side (`config_store_init` → `master_password::try_pinned_support_dir`), read back from Rust, never `path_provider` per call. Enforced by the fitness test `test/core/no_flutter_in_core_test.dart` — a stray import fails CI.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Editing under `rust/`** — `lfs_core` MUST NOT depend on `flutter_rust_bridge` / `tauri` / any frontend crate; `lfs_os_security` is the single audit perimeter for OS-API FFI. After edits: `make rust-format rust-lint rust-test`; if FRB API surface (`rust/crates/lfs_frb/src/api/*.rs`) changed, also `make rust-codegen` and stage regenerated `lib/src/rust/`. `pubspec.yaml` `flutter_rust_bridge:` runtime and `rust/crates/lfs_frb/Cargo.toml` build dep MUST match codegen CLI version exactly. Layout: §3.14.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Cold-start path — STRICT INVARIANT**: nothing on cold-start imports `lib/src/rust/...` or calls FRB. Pre-FRB FRB calls throw `StateError("flutter_rust_bridge has not been initialized")`. Wire FRB-touching listeners from `_LetsFLUTsshAppState._wireFrbDependentBootstrapListeners` AFTER `_initRustCoreOrFatal` returns. See § Cold-start ordering.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Persisted-file wire format change** — bump `SchemaVersions`, ship `Migration`, register in `lfs_core::migration::registry::build_app_registry`, test the chain. `.lfs` future-version handling is rejection-only (`read_archive_to_pending` rejects newer-version archives — not a registry). Intra-DB schema changes follow drift bootstrap. Developer guide: §3.6.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Parallel agents** — only `git add` files YOU changed. Do NOT run tests — main process's job.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Save plans / audits / multi-axis findings to `.opencode/plans/<topic>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`** (gitignored), paired with a TaskList. Never hold large analyses only in chat. `docs/` is human-audience and forbids LLM asides; memory is for cross-session preferences, not project-state snapshots.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **Plans are engineering punch-lists — no QA inside them.** No "manual test plan" / "validation matrix" / per-platform QA bullets. User owns QA scope.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Always-On Rules
text: - **No plan-item IDs in git-tracked artefacts** — no `P1.2-*`, `Phase E1`, `Task 3.2`, `stage 6.6` shapes in commits, code, docs, filenames, headers, even when the plan itself is in git. ARCHITECTURE.md `§N.M` cross-refs are fine — stable doc anchors. Prose-wise: `"ships alongside the overlay methods added to the native plugins"`. Before staging, grep diff and commit message for `/P[0-9]/`, `/Phase [0-9A-Z]/`, `/stage [0-9]/`, `/Task [0-9]/`, `/[A-Z][0-9] /`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: **The single most important discipline.** Code is temporary; docs are how intent survives. Treat `ARCHITECTURE.md` as a first-class deliverable. Every task — planning, editing, bug-fixing, refactor, review — is also a docs task.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: **Audience — write for humans, always.** `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and every other git-tracked doc are written for humans. No LLM asides. Agent-specific guidance stays in this file. The split is absolute.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: **Every § covers both *how* (mechanism — states, inputs, outputs, invariants, failure modes) and *why* (rationale — constraint, past incident, rejected alternative, trade-off accepted).** Only-how leaves intent guessable; only-why leaves mechanism re-derivable.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: 1. **TOC → specific §, never cover-to-cover** (see Lookup discipline above). Applies at planning stage too.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: 2. **If the § is missing or ambiguous: read the code, then fill the gap in the § in the same commit.**

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: 3. **If you find code-doc drift, fix the doc in the same commit.** Code is source of truth on current behaviour. Don't extend a stale § with matching stale additions. If code drifted from intended design, flag and ask — don't paper over.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: 4. **Walk the Documentation Maintenance Checklist after edits** — update every triggered §, same commit.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: 5. **Cross-link related §s.** Docs are a graph. When the cross-link target doesn't exist, **extract it** — create the § or lift the paragraph, then link. When you rename, move, merge, split, or delete a §, update every inbound link in the same commit (`rg -- 'old-anchor-slug'`). When in doubt, link to file not anchor.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: 6. **Extend docs proactively.** Non-trivial behaviour under-documented, important invariant only implicit in code, magic number without rationale, § missing "why" → write it up. Extending is the default; thinning requires justification.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: 7. **If writing the § revealed the code is too tangled, propose rewriting the code.** Documenting is the most honest review the module gets. Signs: needs a flowchart for one method's control flow; two sub-sections describe "same but for case Y"; "why" paragraph cannot find a coherent constraint; invariant cannot be stated as a single sentence.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Docs First — Read Before, Fix Drift, Update After
text: "Forgot to check docs", "the docs didn't say", "the link broke because I renamed the target", "the code was ugly but technically worked" — all invalid skip reasons.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Documentation Maintenance Checklist
text: **Every code change MUST be accompanied by documentation updates.** Violation = incomplete commit.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Documentation Maintenance Checklist
text: General rule: whatever you change in `lib/` or `rust/`, update the corresponding §3–§10 in ARCHITECTURE.md (module map, API tables, data models, providers, widgets, utilities, data flows). Plus these non-obvious triggers:

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Documentation Maintenance Checklist
text:
| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| Changed persistence schema (rusqlite SQL: column / table / index) | Update §11. Schema lives in `lfs_core::db::*`, bootstrapped idempotently on open; structural changes need additive `ALTER TABLE` / `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` so existing user DBs upgrade without wipe |
| Changed wire format of persisted file (`config.json`, `credentials.kdf`, hardware-vault blob, `.lfs` archive) **or** added new envelope artefact | Bump `SchemaVersions::<X>`, ship `Migration`, register in `lfs_core::migration::registry::build_app_registry`, add chain test (§3.6) |
| Edited FRB API surface (`rust/crates/lfs_frb/src/api/*.rs`) | Run `make rust-codegen`, stage regenerated `lib/src/rust/` in same commit |
| Touched any `rust/**/*.rs` | Run `make rust-format rust-lint rust-test`, update relevant ARCHITECTURE § |
| Changed security model | Update §13 + SECURITY.md |
| New design decision | Add to §16 with rationale |
| New CI workflow / changed pipeline | Update §15 |
| Platform-specific change | Update §12 |
| New/changed user-facing string | Add key to `lib/l10n/app_en.arb` **and translate into every other `app_*.arb`** (15 total: ar, de, en, es, fa, fr, hi, id, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, vi, zh). Run `flutter gen-l10n`. Use `S.of(context).key` |
| User-visible change | Update README.md **and** USER_GUIDE.md — relevant § with usage steps, examples, platform caveats |
| New end-user feature | Add a top-level § in USER_GUIDE.md linked from its TOC |

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: Locked priorities: **ideal code, security, optimality**. Every migration / refactor / cleanup decision weighs against these only. Inconvenience is not a skip reason. Bar to skip is one of:

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 1. **Moving it makes the system worse** — measurable safety / perf / consistency regression. Examples: single-instance gate moved to native shell (D-Bus / `CreateMutexW` / `LSMultipleInstancesProhibited`) because Dart shapes ran post-engine-boot; cold-start handlers stay pure Dart because pre-FRB FRB calls hang for minutes. Bar is "concrete regression we can point at".

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 2. **The replacement primitive cannot exist** — language/framework lacks it (Riverpod is Dart-only; `BuildContext` cannot live outside Flutter).

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 3. **The user explicitly authorized the skip** for that specific item.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: **Cost is not a selection criterion.** Complementary defences = union (defence-in-depth), not pick-cheapest. Static lint + runtime fallback + observability for the same fault class are all three. Ranking alternatives by implementation cost ("cheap / medium / heavy") is an anti-pattern. Rank by best practice. Cost shows up only when telling the user how long the work will take.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: **Capability ladder** — when a feature needs an OS capability unavailable on some platform, pick the highest rung that works:

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 1. **Bundle** — link statically, vendor, use system frameworks present on every supported version (sqlite3 via build hooks, iOS AVFoundation, Android CameraX). Default; pick this unless impossible.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 2. **Built-in fallback** — for genuinely platform-specific capabilities (OS keychain, biometric API), provide a feature that works without (master password instead of keychain). User keeps a usable app.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 3. **Per-platform native** — Kotlin / Swift / ObjC / C / Rust via MethodChannel/FFI. Prefer native over Dart when measurably better on perf, functionality, or integration depth.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 4. **Honestly hide** — when no platform path meets the bar (Linux biometric canonical), render the control as **disabled with a reason**. Honest "Not available on Linux" beats a weaker path that looks strong.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 5. **Optional OS dep with graceful degradation** — last resort, the only rung permitting end-user install step. Allowed only if all three hold: (a) runtime detection + short localized "X unavailable because Y not installed" message (one line, no install commands in UI); (b) config control disabled with same reason in tooltip; (c) `README.md` Installation has copy-pasteable command per platform. Canonical: Linux biometric / `fprintd`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: 6. **Weaker path with honest label** — only when (a) ladder above has no answer, (b) weaker path delivers non-trivial value, (c) UI states what the user got (`Software-gated`, `DPAPI (software-backed)`, `Keyring (no biometric binding)`). **Never label weaker the same as stronger.**

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: Hard-requiring user installs to launch the core app is forbidden. When choosing a path for an authorised feature, write "why native" or "why Dart" into the commit message or backlog entry.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: **Surface every improvement path — never bury it.** Notice drift / dead code / suboptimal code / weakening labels / inconsistencies — flag in one sentence ("noticed X is suboptimal because Y; want me to handle it?"). Operator decides scope — make the choice visible, then wait. **Never silently park** as "working = OK" / "low priority" / "out of scope" / "deferred" without operator confirmation, and don't unilaterally expand into a multi-day refactor. Phrases "true X" / "real X" / "verified X" / "proper X" are red flags when you use them to re-pitch a stable decision; honest drift always gets named.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: **Anti-patterns to suppress:**

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: - Offering exit ramps ("session closed?", "wrap up?", "continue or stop?") between every step.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: - Pre-emptively declaring a sweep "subjective" / "needs your anchor" without trying.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: - Conflating "this WSL box can't test platform X" with "no point writing the code".

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: - `TODO` / `FIXME` / `XXX` markers as deferrals.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: - Ranking alternatives by implementation cost.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: - A fallback shipping without a visible downgrade label, or instead of a feasible stronger path.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Three Pillars + Capability Ladder
text: This rule overrides "don't add features beyond what the task requires" for migration / refactor work. **For one-off bug fixes**, pillars apply to general direction; they don't compel rewriting unrelated code that happens to be touched.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > External Libraries & APIs — Look Up, Don't Guess
text: **Never invent method signatures, parameter names, default values, or behaviour from memory.** Lookup order:

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > External Libraries & APIs — Look Up, Don't Guess
text: 1. **Existing usage in this repo** — `Grep` for the symbol or `import 'package:<pkg>'`. Canonical: russh / russh-sftp under `rust/crates/lfs_core/src/ssh/`, rusqlite under `.../db/`, RustCrypto (`aes-gcm`, `argon2`, `ed25519-dalek`) under `.../crypto/`, OS-bound surfaces under `rust/crates/lfs_os_security/`, FRB bindings under `lib/src/rust/`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > External Libraries & APIs — Look Up, Don't Guess
text: 2. **Context7** — `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` then `mcp__context7__get-library-docs`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > External Libraries & APIs — Look Up, Don't Guess
text: 3. **Web docs** — official site, package README on pub.dev / crates.io / GitHub.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > External Libraries & APIs — Look Up, Don't Guess
text: 4. **Source** — `~/.pub-cache/` (Dart) or `~/.cargo/registry/` (Rust).

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > External Libraries & APIs — Look Up, Don't Guess
text: If still unknown, ask. Do not guess.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: **Before adding any widget, helper, mixin, style constant, or store: search `lib/widgets/`, `lib/theme/`, `lib/core/**` for an existing equivalent.** Behaviour close but not identical → **extend** the shared primitive (add a parameter), don't fork. Inline implementation in another file counts the same: lift it to `lib/widgets/` first, swap the original call site, then build your new caller on top. Shipping a second inline copy "to unblock" leaves every later caller copying the wrong one.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: **Coverage:** widgets (`AppIconButton`, `AppDialog` + `AppDialogHeader`/`Footer`/`Action`, `HoverRegion`, `AppDataRow`, `AppDataSearchBar`, `StyledFormField`, `SortableHeaderCell`, `ColumnResizeHandle`, `StatusIndicator`, `MobileSelectionBar`, `AppShell`, `ModeButton`, `ConfirmDialog`, `ErrorState`); theme constants (`AppTheme.radius{Sm,Md,Lg}`, `barHeight*`, `controlHeight*`, `itemHeight*`, `*ColWidth`, `AppFonts.{tiny,xxs,xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`); cross-feature mixins / `*_helper.dart` files; persistence (Store → DAO template per §11).

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: **Non-negotiable extraction triggers** — refactor before committing if:

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: 1. Same string literal in ≥3 places (S1192) → constant or l10n key.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: 2. Same widget tree (≥5 lines) in ≥2 files → extract widget.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: 3. Same hardcoded numeric (radius, padding, width, height, fontSize) in ≥2 places → constant in `AppTheme` / `AppFonts`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: 4. Same `if/else` block or async pipeline in ≥2 callers → extract helper / mixin.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: 5. New `*_dialog.dart` / `*_button.dart` / `*_row.dart` not extending an existing `App*` primitive → check first whether a parameter on the existing primitive solves it.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Reuse First (project-wide)
text: **Premature-abstraction guard:** triggers mean *consider extraction*, not *extract no matter what*. If the third caller would force a parameter that warps the first two, leave the duplication and add `// TODO(reuse): N callers — revisit when shape stabilises`. Reuse exists to reduce surface area, not grow it.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Comments — Short, Current, No Fabricated Rationale
text: Comments are load-bearing when they exist — a present invariant the next reader cannot infer from well-named identifiers.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Comments — Short, Current, No Fabricated Rationale
text: **1. Short.** ≤5 lines, thought finishes inside the budget. One coherent point: name a trap, state an invariant + its why, call out a non-obvious ordering. Never multi-paragraph. If the thought needs more room, write it into `ARCHITECTURE.md` and point: `// See ARCHITECTURE.md §3.6 → SecretStore for the plaintext-discipline rule.`

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Comments — Short, Current, No Fabricated Rationale
text: **2. Current state only — no retrospective.** A comment describes the code *as it is now*; the "what was the bug, what is the new shape" prose belongs in the **commit message**. Before staging, grep the diff for these narrative-voice tells: `originally`, `previously`, `after the migration`, `replaces the legacy`, `now retired`, `the legacy path`, `before we`, `used to`, `Mirrors the prior`, `pre-fix`, `the prior`, `the earlier`, `legacy` (runtime sense is fine — `legacy fallback path` ok, `replaces the legacy` not).

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Comments — Short, Current, No Fabricated Rationale
LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Comments — Short, Current, No Fabricated Rationale
text: **3. No fabricated rationale.** Only cite platforms, measurements, failure mechanisms, behavioural claims real and verifiable from code, git log, or captured user report. Forbidden: concrete timings without source (`~3 s on Win IoT`); generic-sounding alternatives that imply measurement (`non-trivial latency`); specific OS subsystems pinned as cause without link (`Defender real-time scan`, `Gatekeeper signature check`); causal chains explaining *why* when you have only the *what*. Document the structural reason (the bug class prevented, the contract enforced).

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Comments — Short, Current, No Fabricated Rationale
text: Same rule applies to Rust `//`/`///`/`//!` and Dart `///` doc comments.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Architecture (non-obvious rules)
text: - **No SCP** — SFTP only (`lfs_core::sftp`).

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Architecture (non-obvious rules)
text: - SSH keys accepted **both as file and text** (paste PEM).

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Architecture (non-obvious rules)
text: - `.lfs` format + import modes: §3.9. Credentials in `CredentialStore` AES-256-GCM, never plain JSON: §3.6.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Architecture (non-obvious rules)
text: - **State placement** — app-wide UI state → Riverpod `NotifierProvider` over FRB; widget-local (dialog / pane / panel / tab) → `ChangeNotifier` + `AnimatedBuilder` (canonical: `FilePaneController`, `UnifiedExportController`, `SessionPanelController`, `TransferPanelController`). Side-channel Riverpod overrides for widget-local state = boilerplate with no win — §4.3. Persistent state in neither — see Always-On "Rust owns data".

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Logging — AppLogger, Auto-Sanitized
text: Every log line goes through `AppLogger.instance.log(message, name: 'Tag', error: e, stackTrace: st)`. **Never `print` or `dart:developer.log` directly** — both bypass the sanitizer (`print` also survives release builds). The only channel is the opt-in file at `<appSupportDir>/logs/letsflutssh.log`. Default threshold `Off` (privacy-first); `logCritical` bypasses for crash breadcrumbs.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Logging — AppLogger, Auto-Sanitized
text: **Auto-sanitization** scrubs PEM private keys, long base64, IPv4/IPv6, `user@host`, `host:port`, Windows / Unix home paths, `as/user/login=<user>` shapes. Don't pre-sanitize. Sanitizer can't catch **free-form user-chosen strings** (session labels, key labels, tag names, snippet titles, folder names) — log marker `<label>`, not the value. § Error Handling Architecture.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Logging — AppLogger, Auto-Sanitized
text: **Add logs generously** at every load-bearing transition (entry/exit of disk/DB/network/subprocess/native ops; every branch of user-consequential `try/catch` including swallowed-and-continued; ambiguous-input decisions; places a past bug could surface). Test: "could a user hand me the log and could I tell what happened without reproducing?"

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Logging — AppLogger, Auto-Sanitized
text: **Never embed raw passwords / passphrases / key bytes.** Log `'Password verify failed'`, not `'Password verify failed: $typedPassword'`. Sanitizer handles exception text — `log('X failed: $e', error: e)` is fine.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Logging — AppLogger, Auto-Sanitized
text: **Levels** — `info` default, `warn` for degraded-recoverable, `error` for unrecoverable / data at risk. `log(error: e)` without explicit `level:` auto-promotes to error — override with `LogLevel.warn` for recoverable paths that carry an exception. `logCritical` is always error. No debug rung — per-frame tracing wraps a local flag you ship and revert.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Logging — AppLogger, Auto-Sanitized
text: **Tag names module-scoped**, not file-scoped: `'FilePane'`, `'Session'`, `'KdfParams'`, `'MigrationRunner'`, `'KnownHosts'`, `'SecureClipboard'`. Grep existing `name:` before inventing. Critical paths (`FlutterError.onError`, `PlatformDispatcher.onError`, `runZonedGuarded`, migration fatals, DB integrity-probe failures) use `logCritical`. Dev / beta threshold via `--dart-define=LETSFLUTSSH_LOG_LEVEL=<info|warn|error>`; `make run` defaults to `info`. Never set in release.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Theme & UI Constants
text: OneDark theme: centralized in `app_theme.dart`, semantic color constants, no hardcoded `Colors` — §8.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Theme & UI Constants
text: - **Font sizes** — never hardcode `fontSize`. Use `AppFonts.{tiny,xxs,xs,sm,md,lg,xl}` (mobile +2 px).

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Theme & UI Constants
text: - **Border radius** — never hardcode `BorderRadius.circular(N)`. Use `AppTheme.radius{Sm,Md,Lg}` (4/6/8). Exception: pill-shaped elements.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Theme & UI Constants
text: - **Heights** — never hardcode height literals. Use `AppTheme.barHeight{Sm,Md,Lg}`, `controlHeight{Xs..Xl}`, `itemHeight{Xs..Xl}`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > UI Components
text: - **Buttons & hover** — `AppIconButton` for all icon buttons. `HoverRegion` for custom hover containers. Never bare `IconButton`, `InkWell`-as-button, or manual `MouseRegion`+`GestureDetector`+`setState(_hovered)`. Exception: `context_menu.dart`, mobile touch buttons.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > UI Components
text: - **Dialogs** — `AppDialog` for all modal dialogs. Never bare `AlertDialog`. Complex dialogs compose from `AppDialogHeader`/`AppDialogFooter`/`AppButton`. Progress: `AppProgressBarDialog.show()`. Exception: mobile touch buttons keep `Material`+`InkWell` for ripple.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > UI Components
text: - **Text selection is opt-in on desktop — clickable ≠ selectable.** No global `SelectionArea` on the desktop shell (gesture-arena race with `ThresholdDraggable`); wrap prose surfaces (dialog bodies, threat lists, release-notes, help) in `AppSelectionArea` locally, never a drag target / `AppButton` / interactive row. Mobile wraps once at `MobileShell`. Inside any `AppSelectionArea`, clickable tiles / rows / headers / badges (and form-field labels) opt out via `SelectionContainer.disabled` — `HoverRegion` auto-wraps, `InkWell` does not (wrap its child). Full mechanism + rationale: § Selection scoping.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > UI Components
text: - **Session panel input model** — focus, shortcut dispatch, two-phase folder click, and clipboard all have non-obvious contracts; read §5.3 before editing `session_panel.dart`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > UI Components
text: - **Text overflow** — localized text in `Row` or fixed-width → wrap with `Flexible`/`Expanded` + `overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis`. For label columns use `ConstrainedBox(maxWidth:)` not fixed `SizedBox(width:)`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > UI Components
text: - **Accessibility** — wrap interactive list items (session rows, file rows) and panel headers with `Semantics` (`label`, `button: true`, `selected`, `header: true`). `StatusIndicator` has built-in `Semantics`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > UI Components
text: - **Disable vs hide unavailable controls — first on feasibility, then on surface type.** *Disable only when the capability is possible on this platform but unavailable right now* (dependency not installed, no key selected, prerequisite toggle off) — the user can act to enable it. *Hide when fundamentally impossible on the platform* (no system ssh-agent on Android/iOS, no biometric API on Linux desktop) — a permanently-greyed control is noise, not discoverability. Within the disable case, surface type decides presentation: *Configuration surfaces* (Settings, session-edit forms, preference dialogs) → render disabled with tooltip + tap-toast explaining the reason; *Action surfaces* (lock screen, context menus, per-row action buttons, action dialogs) → hide. Disabled state must visibly affect the whole row (opacity on full container). When hiding a config control, preserve any persisted state it maps to — hide the widget, never silently rewrite the stored value.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: All user-facing strings MUST use `S.of(context).xxx`. Never hardcode in widgets — treat as a bug. Add keys to `lib/l10n/app_en.arb`, run `flutter gen-l10n`. Exceptions: constructor defaults (no context), log messages. Tests must include `localizationsDelegates: S.localizationsDelegates, supportedLocales: S.supportedLocales` in every `MaterialApp`. See §8.1.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: **Tone — native IT register, not dictionary calques.** Audience is engineers and sysadmins; strings should read like a dev to a colleague, not a textbook. Per-locale dominant pattern for tech terms:

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text:
| Locales | Pattern |
|---|---|
| RU, ES, PT-BR, FR, DE, IT | Latin for dev-tool tech (SSH, Keychain, Hardware, Log, Timeout, Worker, Fingerprint, Passphrase, Scrollback, rate limit). Apple/MS consumer-UI natives only for OS-specific labels |
| TR, ID | Heavy English in dev context. TDK / KBBI / öztürkçe calques read textbook |
| AR, FA, HI, VI | Latin tech terms inside native prose is normal; native coinages for SSH/TPM/keychain/forensics/wrapping sound amateur |
| JA | Katakana (キーチェーン, ハードウェア) for loan words; Latin (SSH, TPM, DMA, CVE, Argon2id) for acronyms |
| KO | Hangul transliteration (키체인, 하드웨어) or Latin — both valid; match native dev doc convention |
| ZH | Latin for protocols/acronyms always; common words translate (硬件, 密码); Apple 钥匙串 OK but `keychain` Latin also works |

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: **Never:** coin a native word for "keychain" when devs don't (RU ключница, VI chuỗi khóa, FA کلیدستان, KO 열쇠고리, ZH 钥匙链); translate Unix "pipe" as water pipe (RU труба, PT Pipa, TR Boru, AR أنبوب); translate "worker" as human laborer (PT Trabalhadores, AR العمال, TR İşçi); translate "forensics" as legal/courtroom (RU криминалистика, PT Perícia — use "memory dump"); translate SSH "fingerprint" with biometric word (collides with biometric-unlock UI); use "please" in error messages (RU пожалуйста, ES Por favor, JA ください, TR lütfen — drop all); mix dialects (PT BR vs PT PT; ES tuteo vs ustedeo; DE du vs Sie) — pick one per file; use different translations for the same English term in the same file.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: **Critical semantic-inversion traps:**

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: - ES `restablecida` / PT `redefinida` for "connection reset by peer" → opposite meaning. Use `reiniciada por el peer` / `encerrada pelo peer`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: - KO `암호문` for "passphrase" → means `ciphertext`. Use `패스프레이즈`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: - JA `解錠` for "decrypt/unwrap" → physical lock-picking. Use `復号`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: - JA `ボルト` for "vault" → bolt/volt. Use `ボールト`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: - HI `समझौता` for "compromise" → agreement/deal. Use `कॉम्प्रोमाइज़`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: - FR `sauvegardé` for "backed by" → false friend. Use `adossé à`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: **Watchlist — keep English / native IT form unless the locale's dev community uses a native equivalent:** SSH, SFTP, SCP, TLS, DNS, proxy, TCP, known_hosts, TPM, TEE, DMA, Secure Enclave, StrongBox, HSM, keychain, keyring, Keystore, Credential Manager, key material, wrapped key, sealed blob, KDF, PBKDF2, Argon2id, AES, HMAC, AEAD, passphrase, fingerprint, host, host key, port, login, log, worker, scrollback, release, timeout, keep-alive, rate limit, backdoor, plaintext, snapshot, forensics, dump, probe, breaking change, driver, distro, config, credential, slot, vault, kernel, build, runtime, mitigation, lockout, idle.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Localization (i18n)
text: Self-test: read aloud. Sounds like a textbook → rewrite. Sounds like a Slack message to a colleague → ship. **Do localization yourself** — don't delegate translation to sub-agents (they fall back to safe dictionary calques). Survey use (read 1000-line file, flag candidates) is fine; tone decisions stay in the main thread.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Diagrams in Docs — Mermaid, Not ASCII Box-Art
text: Every diagram in `docs/**/*.md`, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md` and any tracked markdown MUST be a ` ```mermaid ` fenced block (`flowchart`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `sequenceDiagram`, `classDiagram`). GitHub renders as SVG; ASCII `┌─┐`/`└─┘` breaks on narrow viewports. Convert in the same commit when editing existing ASCII.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Conventions > Diagrams in Docs — Mermaid, Not ASCII Box-Art
text: Not covered: directory trees (keep plain fenced — Mermaid is worse for deep trees); pipe tables (GitHub renders as HTML); code blocks. Single-box info cards → plain markdown bullets. Don't add ASCII fallbacks via `<details>` — doubles the source and rots.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: All code follows its language's canonical style — **Dart**: Effective Dart; **Rust**: Clippy + rustfmt — and passes `make lint` with zero issues before any Dart/Rust commit. Suppression bans: see Always-On. SonarCloud gates on top, on rules the linters miss — obey these on first draft:

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: - **S3776 — cognitive complexity ≤ 15.** Common fixes: extract conditional children into `_buildFoo(…)`; pull repeated computations into a local `final already = …;` before `return`; split `if (enable) { … } else { … }` into `_enableFoo()` / `_disableFoo()`; long `if (error is X)` chains → group by category, extract `_tryLocalizeFooError` returning `String?`; async chains with nested mounted/null guards → extract each phase into `Future<T?> _phaseFoo(…)`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: - **S3358 — no nested ternaries.** Rewrite as `if`/`else if`/`else` assigning to a local, or a `switch` expression. Subtle: `active ? Icon(asc ? up : down) : null` is already S3358 — extract to `_directionIcon(col)`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: - **S1854 — dead/unused values.** Don't `final x = ...;` then overwrite; use `late final x;` with `if`/`else` assignment.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: - **S1192 — string literal duplicated ≥3 times.** → constant or l10n key.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: - **S1481 / S1172 — unused locals / parameters.** Delete or prefix with `_`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: - **No `print()` / `debugPrint()`** — `AppLogger` always. Errors surfacing to UI go through `localizeError()`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: - **No generated file edits** — `*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart` excluded; change source.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Code Quality — SonarCloud
text: **Shape before scanner.** Method body >~30 lines or three nested conditional blocks → split before committing. Widget `build()` over that should already have named `_buildFoo` helpers.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Testing Methodology
text: **Everything that can be unit-tested without touching the OS or an external system must be unit-tested.** Allow-list for "no unit test": OS-specific capability (biometric prompt, OS keychain, native plugin MethodChannel, platform file pickers, single-instance lock, notification APIs, TPM / Secure Enclave / Windows Hello, Linux D-Bus services like `fprintd`) or integration with external system (real SSH/SFTP server, real QR camera, real update server). For exempt functions, the harness-testable **slice** still gets tests — isolate pure-Dart logic from the non-testable edge.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Testing Methodology
text: Target: 100% coverage (excluding OS-specific edges + integration tests). One test file per source file. Testable by design: extract pure logic, DI over hardcoded `ref.read()` — §14. If a function cannot be unit-tested and the reason is not on the allow-list, refactor.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Testing Methodology
text: - **Tests assert spec, not current output.** Before any `expect(...)`, state in one sentence what the function _should_ do — derived from feature intent. **Never** run, observe, paste — that's a pinning test that cements bugs. If correct behavior is unclear, stop and ask.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Testing Methodology
text: - **When test and code disagree, surface it — don't silently "fix" either side.** Three options: real bug, wrong spec, ambiguous requirement. Stop, report with input + spec + where derived + current output. Let the user decide.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Testing Methodology
text: - **Failing tests after a change: diagnose before editing the test.** Re-derive the test's intended contract; compare to what your change promised; if test still checks a contract you did NOT intend to break, the code is wrong; only when the test pins an internal detail you deliberately reshaped do you rewrite — and the new assertion expresses the **new** contract intent-first.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Testing Methodology
text: - **Uncovered lines are a marker, not a target.** Don't write tests whose only goal is to execute the line (`isNotNull` / `isA<T>()` / "doesn't throw"). Ask: what branch / decision / contract does this line encode?

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Testing Methodology
text: - **Fuzz tests for every untrusted-input consumer** — not only parsers. Tiers: user-supplied files (import, wizard text, clipboard); network / peer-supplied (SSH banner, SFTP path strings, terminal ANSI); inter-process (deep-link URIs, QR payload, OS clipboard, IPC); on-disk state (config JSON, KDF params, LFS archive header, vault blobs). Each target gets a Dart property-based test in `test/fuzz/` or standalone harness in `fuzz/` + seed corpus + CFL wiring in `.clusterfuzzlite/build.sh`. New untrusted-input code = new fuzz target same commit. See § Fuzz testing.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Testing Methodology
text: - **UI changes = test updates** — proactively update all tests referencing changed widget names, labels, finders.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Commits & Versioning
text: - **HARD STOP between fixes.** Implement → tests → docs → **post-fix summary** → ask to commit. Don't start the next fix until current is committed. Exceptions: batch-mode signal; series of related doc/rule edits in a single session — batch into one commit at natural arc end.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Commits & Versioning
text: - **Post-fix summary is mandatory.** Per bug: **Symptom** (user-visible behaviour that was wrong), **Root cause** (why, named with file/function/field), **Fix** (what you changed). One bug per paragraph, ≤5 lines. Batch mode → single combined report at arc end. The user reads the summary to decide whether you understood the bug — don't skip because the diff "speaks for itself".

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Commits & Versioning
text: - Format per CONTRIBUTING.md → Commit messages. Drives the auto-generated GitHub release notes — keep user-readable. Use `type(scope):` with parenthesized scope for module-specific commits (`refactor(import): ...`, `test(known-hosts): ...`); drop scope only when genuinely cross-cutting.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Commits & Versioning
text: - **Version bumps are automatic.** `/pr` skill runs `dev/scripts/bump-version.sh` — parses conventional commits since last tag, bumps `pubspec.yaml` (patch for fix/refactor/perf/build/deps, minor for feat, major for BREAKING CHANGE; chore/docs/test/ci/Revert = no bump). Don't bump manually.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Commits & Versioning
text: - **Green CI before merging to main** — pre-commit hook runs `make check` automatically.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Branching & Release Flow
text: Default working branch is `dev` — never push directly to `main`.

head: LetsFLUTssh — Development Guide > Branching & Release Flow
text:
| Scenario | Action |
|---|---|
| App change (feat/fix/refactor) | bump on dev → PR `dev` → `main` → CI → auto-tag → release |
| Tests/docs/CI only | Merge to `main` — no bump, no tag, no release |
| Dependabot deps | Auto: PR to main → automerge patch/minor → CI → auto-tag (no per-PR bump; deps ride the next release's bump) |
| Manual build | `gh workflow run build-release.yml` — fails if CI hasn't passed |
| Re-trigger failed build | `gh workflow run build-release.yml --ref v{VERSION}` |

head: BNCC API — Agent Context > Custo de operação (auditoria 2026-07-28)
text:
A camada de IA (`torch`/`SentenceTransformer`) é carregada **sob demanda**, na primeira busca
semântica (`vector_store.get_vector_service`) — **nunca no startup**. Carregá-la no lifespan custava
70s de cold start e forçava `min-instances=1` no Cloud Run: 72% de uma fatura de ~R$450/mês para
servir ~100 req/dia. Hoje o boot é ~1,5s e o serviço escala a zero (~R$95/mês).
**Não mova essa carga para o startup** — `tests/integration/test_lazy_ai_startup.py` falha se isso
acontecer, porque a regressão é invisível (nada quebra, só volta a custar caro).
Corolários: `requirements.txt` é só runtime (dev/PDF em `requirements-dev.txt`), o `Dockerfile`
instala torch do índice **CPU-only** (a wheel padrão traz ~2,5 GB de CUDA inútil), e a landing manda
`Cache-Control` público para a CDN do Firebase absorver o tráfego. Ver `deploy/README.md`.

head: BNCC API — Agent Context > Documentação versionada (ver `docs/versioning.md`)
text:
Dois eixos, app FastAPI único (sem sub-apps: `dependency_overrides` não se propaga a sub-apps montados).
**Eixo 1 (contratos que coexistem):** registro em `app/api/versions.py` dirige docs/OpenAPI por versão;
cada versão maior sob prefixo estável (`/api/v1`, futuro `/api/v2`). Superfícies: `/docs/{slug}` (Scalar;
`/docs` = a mais recente), `GET /api/{slug}/openapi.json`, manifesto em `GET /api/versions`. **Eixo 2
(histórico de releases):** `scripts/freeze_openapi.py` congela o OpenAPI enriquecido em
`docs/openapi/{slug}/{release}.json` (manifesto `index.json`), servido em
`GET /api/{slug}/releases/{release}/openapi.json`; Scalar navega releases via `/docs/{slug}?release=X`.
OpenAPI enriquecido montado em `app/api/openapi.py`. Adicionar v2 = incluir o roteador com
`prefix="/api/v2"` em `app/main.py` + registrar `APIVersion("v2", ...)` em `app/api/versions.py` (docs,
OpenAPI e snapshots passam a cobri-la automaticamente). **Nunca quebrar contrato dentro de uma versão
publicada — mudança incompatível exige nova versão de caminho** (Princípio I).

head: BNCC API — Agent Context > Documentação versionada (ver `docs/versioning.md`)
text:
> **Fontes da BNCC (as 3 etapas cobertas):** EF e EM vêm de `data/bncc_ensino_fundamental.pdf` e
> `data/bncc_ensino_medio.pdf` (pdfplumber, isolamento de coluna). A **Educação Infantil** vem do

> impede o pdfplumber, o script o **normaliza com pikepdf** antes de extrair as 3 colunas de faixa
> etária. O **Complemento de Computação** (Parecer CNE/CP 02/2022) vem de
> `data/BNCCComputaoCompletodiagramado (1).pdf` via `scripts/extract_bncc_computacao.py` (chamado por
> `extract_bncc_data.py`): recupera espaços posicionais com `x_tolerance`, isola a coluna HABILIDADE
> e lê o **eixo** (horizontal na EI; rotacionado 90° no EF). Contagens atuais do snapshot: EI 104,
> EF 1408, EM 209 — inclui **141 habilidades de Computação** (`componente=computacao`), com eixos
> em EI/EF (`missing_sources: []`). Ver `specs/002-bncc-computacao/`. Os PDFs são grandes e ficam
> fora do versionamento (`data/` no .gitignore); apenas `data/bncc_v1.json` é versionado.
>
> **Reconciliação de fidelidade (auditoria 2026-07-06):** as descrições foram cruzadas com DUAS
> testemunhas do texto oficial — o documento `data/BNCC_EI_EF_110518_versaofinal_site.pdf` (600 págs.,
> normalizado com pikepdf; EI+EF+EM, o **árbitro**) e o dataset `github.com/dfdb76/bncc-mcp` (CSVs da
> versão final homologada, que casam 100% com o PDF nos códigos EI+EF). Isso corrigiu 59 descrições
> corrompidas por interleaving de coluna / truncamento / bleed e inseriu `EF05CO11` (antes ausente),
> via `scripts/reconcile_bncc_descriptions.py` + `scripts/bncc_description_fixes.json` (idempotente,
> texto oficial de livre uso, Lei 9.610/98 art. 8º IV). **Cuidado:** a seção de EM do PDF é o rascunho
> de mai/2018 (pré-homologação de dez/2018) — o EM final vem do snapshot/CSV, nunca do PDF.
>
> **Qualidade das descrições** é auditada por `scripts/audit_extraction.py` (portão versionado,
> `tests/contract/test_audit_extraction.py`): checa truncamento/blob/contaminação/fusão/**interleaving**
> (duplicação adjacente de >=4 palavras, assinatura do splice de coluna) além de códigos e contagens.
> Estado atual: **0 achados ERROR**. Habilidades de anos combinados
> (12/35/67/89) têm célula **mesclada** (largura total) recuperada por `recover_descriptions`;
> objetos com prosa de campo/exemplo são descartados (`_is_rel_bleed`). Computação traz o EF em
> dois quadros oficiais (por ano `EF0xCO` + por etapa `EF15CO`/`EF69CO`) — texto repetido entre
> esquemas é fiel, não duplicata.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository Layout
text: This is a monorepo for **Desktop Homunculus**, a cross-platform desktop mascot application built with the Bevy game engine. It renders transparent-window VRM 3D characters with WebView-based UI overlays.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository Layout
text: Sub-directories have their own CLAUDE.md with detailed architecture: `engine/`, `packages/sdk/`, `packages/ui/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Commands > Engine (Rust) — run from `engine/`
text:
Single test:
```bash
cargo test -p homunculus_http_server            # All tests in one crate
cargo test -p homunculus_http_server test_health # Single test by name
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Commands > Engine (Rust) — run from `engine/`
text:
Release builds use `--profile dist` (not `--release`), which enables `lto = "thin"` and `strip = true`:
```bash
make release-macos           # Native arch → .app bundle → PKG
make release-macos-arm       # Apple Silicon
make release-macos-x86       # Intel
make release-macos-universal # Universal binary (ARM + x86)
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview
text: The engine is built from ~20 independent Bevy plugins in `engine/crates/`, following a Core → API → HTTP layering. The HTTP API (Axum on `localhost:3100`) bridges async requests to Bevy's single-threaded ECS via the `ApiReactor` pattern. See `engine/CLAUDE.md` for detailed Rust architecture, code examples, and crate descriptions.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview
text: Asset path resolution: dev mode uses `assets/` relative to `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; release uses `../Resources/assets` (inside `.app` bundle).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > OpenClaw Integration
text:
DH does not include an in-process agent runtime. For AI-powered interaction, run
[OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai) externally and install the
[`@hmcs/openclaw-plugin`](packages/openclaw-plugin/) plugin. See
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-18-openclaw-agent-integration-design.md` for the
full integration design.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > WebView Integration (bevy_cef)
text: UI components (settings, right-click menu) are React apps embedded via Chromium Embedded Framework (`bevy_cef`). They communicate with the Rust backend through the HTTP API and SSE-based pub/sub (`signals` module in the SDK). CEF runs with `disable-web-security` to allow cross-origin requests from WebViews to `localhost:3100`. A `CefFetchPlugin` proxies JavaScript `fetch` calls from WebViews through native `reqwest`. Transparent areas of a WebView do not capture mouse events — clicks pass through to the 3D scene beneath. This means CSS-only visibility changes (e.g., collapsing UI to a small icon) do not require resizing the WebView itself.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > WebView Integration (bevy_cef)
text: WebView keyboard shortcuts: `F1`/`F2` open/close DevTools, `Cmd+[`/`Cmd+]` navigate back/forward.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > WebView Integration (bevy_cef)
text: WebView sources can be URLs, inline HTML, or local mod assets using `{ "type": "local", "id": "mod-name:asset-id" }`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > MOD System
text: Mods are pnpm workspace packages. Each mod's `package.json` must include a `"homunculus"` field declaring:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > MOD System
text: - **assets**: Objects with `path`, `type` (`vrm`, `vrma`, `sound`, `image`, `html`), and `description`. Asset IDs use format `"mod-name:asset-id"`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > MOD System
text: - **menus** (optional): Right-click context menu entries that can open webviews.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > MOD System
text: - **tray** (optional): System tray menu entries (distinct from `menus`). Processed by `homunculus_tray` via `bevy_tray_icon`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > MOD System
text: The `"homunculus.service"` script runs automatically as a long-running child process (service) at startup using `node --import tsx` (TypeScript files run directly without a build step; tsx is installed locally in the mods directory by `ensure_tsx()`). MOD commands are exposed via `"bin"` and invoked through the HTTP API (`POST /mods/{mod_name}/bin/{command}`). Mods use the `@hmcs/sdk` SDK.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > MOD System
text: **Mod discovery**: The engine runs `pnpm ls --parseable` in the mods directory (`~/.homunculus/mods/`) to discover installed mods, then reads each mod's `package.json` directly.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > MOD System
text: Source mods live in `mods/` (in the repo, for development). At runtime, mods are installed to `~/.homunculus/mods/` (configurable via `config.toml` `mods_dir` field). The built-in `@hmcs/assets` mod provides default VRMA animations (`vrma:idle-maid`, `vrma:grabbed`, `vrma:idle-sitting`) and sound effects (`se:open`, `se:close`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Frontend UI (Mod-Based)
text: UI apps live in `mods/` as mod packages — **settings** (`mods/settings/ui/`), **menu** (`mods/menu/ui/`), and **persona** (`mods/persona/ui/`). They are React 19 + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4 apps that import `@hmcs/ui` (from `packages/ui/`) as the shared component library. Build output goes to each mod's `ui/dist/` (bundled into a single `index.html` via `vite-plugin-singlefile` for CEF loading) and is declared as an asset in the mod's `package.json`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Frontend UI (Mod-Based)
text: **Design language**: Glassmorphism — semi-transparent backgrounds (`bg-primary/30`), `backdrop-blur-sm`, subtle borders (`border-white/20`), white text. This is the canonical style for all WebView UI overlays on the transparent Bevy window. The `@hmcs/ui` library is built on **shadcn/ui (new-york style)** with Radix UI primitives and **lucide-react** icons. Use the `cn()` utility from `@hmcs/ui` (clsx + tailwind-merge) for conditional class names.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > MCP Server (`engine/crates/homunculus_mcp/`)
text: Embedded Rust MCP server using Streamable HTTP transport, mounted at `/mcp` on the engine's Axum router (`localhost:3100/mcp`). Exposes static tools (character control, audio, webview), 5 resources (`homunculus://info`, `homunculus://characters`, `homunculus://mods`, `homunculus://assets`, `homunculus://rpc`), and 3 prompts. Uses the `rmcp` crate with `LocalSessionManager` for session isolation. MCP-specific fields and dynamic tool registration were removed from the RPC layer in favor of static exposure; RPC methods are invoked via HTTP (`POST /mods/{mod_name}/bin/{command}`), not auto-registered as MCP tools.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Rust CLI (`engine/crates/homunculus_cli/`)
text: The `hmcs` binary is a Rust CLI built with `clap`. Current subcommands:

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides repository-specific guidance to coding agents and other automated assistants working with or on `mne-denoise`. It covers two use cases: helping users apply mne-denoise correctly, and modifying the package, tests, documentation, or repository tooling.

head: AGENTS.md > What is mne-denoise
text:
`mne-denoise` provides artifact-suppression and signal-denoising methods for
EEG and MEG. It supports NumPy arrays and optional integration with
MNE-Python containers, and provides scikit-learn-style estimators where that
interface fits the method. The package contains several distinct scientific
methods rather than one universal denoising procedure.

head: AGENTS.md > What is mne-denoise
text: The scientific semantics and assumptions of each method matter more than implementation convenience. mne-denoise should integrate naturally into the MNE ecosystem and reuse generic MNE behavior rather than reproduce functionality that MNE already owns.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: Use the current public API only. Before suggesting an import or workflow, inspect the current public facades and `tests/test_public_api.py`; do not infer the API from filenames or old examples. Importability alone does not make a name public.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: Do not hallucinate stale names from historical documentation or branches. In particular:

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text:
- Do not suggest an object that exists only because a similar name appeared in
  an earlier version.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text:
- Public imports must come from current documented facades and their declared
  `__all__` values.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text:
- Modules and names beginning with `_` are implementation details and should
  not be recommended to users.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: When the context is available, determine the parts of the scientific problem that affect the recommendation:

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: - Raw, Epochs, Evoked, or NumPy input.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: - Sampling frequency and channel types.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: - The target artifact or noise source.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: - Continuous versus epoched data.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: - Line frequency, when line-noise removal is relevant.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text:
- Whether the goal is artifact suppression, source extraction, component
  enhancement, or another operation.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: - Preprocessing already performed, including filtering and referencing.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: Do not ask every question in every conversation, but do not ignore these factors when they change the scientific interpretation or API choice. No method is universally best. Explain relevant assumptions, choose the simplest public workflow that fits the goal, and preserve MNE metadata and container semantics.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: Do not recommend private helpers when a public estimator or function exists. Distinguish established published methods from mne-denoise-specific extensions and experimental research APIs.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text:
Honor experimental-status and validation warnings in the current public
docstrings and method documentation. Public availability does not imply that
an API is an established or independently validated scientific method. Do not
recommend experimental or unvalidated research APIs as established defaults.
When scientific validation status matters, inspect the current method
documentation and primary literature before making a recommendation. For
example, an API such as GuidedASR should be presented with that qualification
whenever its current documentation marks it experimental.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: Artifact attenuation is not evidence that desired neural signal was preserved. Where relevant, encourage users to evaluate both artifact attenuation and preservation of the signal of interest, using suitable controls and scientific knowledge.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: Example code for users must:

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text: - Use canonical import paths and current constructor parameter names.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text:
- Use the current `fit`, `transform`, `fit_transform`, or functional API
  semantics.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text:
- Avoid needless NumPy extraction and MNE-object reconstruction when an
  estimator accepts an MNE container directly.

head: AGENTS.md > Helping users with mne-denoise
text:
- Never mutate user data unless the public API explicitly documents in-place
  behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth
text:
Scientific truth and software-contract truth are related but not
interchangeable.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > Scientific algorithm semantics
text: Use this order when resolving a scientific question:

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > Scientific algorithm semantics
text: 1. The primary scientific publication.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > Scientific algorithm semantics
text: 2. An authoritative or reference implementation, when relevant.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > Scientific algorithm semantics
text: 3. The current mne-denoise implementation and scientific tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > Scientific algorithm semantics
text:
4. Historical branches, historical outputs, fixtures, and old documentation
   only when they are needed to resolve an ambiguity.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > Scientific algorithm semantics
text: Historical output parity is not by itself scientific truth. Do not recreate old substrate, parity, or output-generation machinery merely to preserve historical numerical arrays. If the implementation and the publication or reference implementation appear inconsistent, stop and surface the discrepancy rather than silently choosing one interpretation.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > mne-denoise software contracts
text: Use this order for package behavior and compatibility questions:

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > mne-denoise software contracts
text: 1. The intentional public API and its tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > mne-denoise software contracts
text: 2. Shared estimator and MNE-container contract tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > mne-denoise software contracts
text: 3. Algorithm-specific tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > mne-denoise software contracts
text: 4. Current user documentation.

head: AGENTS.md > Sources of truth > mne-denoise software contracts
text: Correct documentation when it contradicts the implementation and tests, unless the discrepancy reveals a scientific bug that needs separate investigation.

head: AGENTS.md > Before writing new code
text: Search for an existing owner before adding local machinery:

head: AGENTS.md > Before writing new code
text: 1. Search mne-denoise for an existing implementation or helper.

head: AGENTS.md > Before writing new code
text: 2. Search public MNE-Python APIs.

head: AGENTS.md > Before writing new code
text: 3. Search NumPy, SciPy, and scikit-learn functionality where appropriate.

head: AGENTS.md > Before writing new code
text: 4. Only then introduce new local machinery.

head: AGENTS.md > Before writing new code
text: Prefer existing public MNE APIs over local duplication. Generic MNE object, channel, forward, covariance, filter, and container behavior should not be reimplemented here when MNE already owns it. If the needed behavior only exists privately, consider whether an upstream public API or change is more appropriate instead of importing MNE internals.

head: AGENTS.md > Before writing new code
text: Keep logic local when mne-denoise semantics genuinely differ. Do not import MNE private helpers casually to remove a few lines, build wrappers solely for conceptual symmetry, or create an abstraction for one caller unless it materially clarifies ownership. Do not add hypothetical parameters or extension points, and do not add dependencies without a concrete need and discussion. Never promote an optional dependency to a required dependency as a side effect.

head: AGENTS.md > Before writing new code
text: Implement behavior at the highest existing owner layer. For example, a generic estimator invariant belongs in the package-wide estimator contract suite, not in repeated method-specific tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Keep changes focused
text: Optimize for reviewer comprehension and long-term maintenance, not diff size or output volume. Prefer the smallest change that fully satisfies the issue, and avoid opportunistic cleanup of unrelated code.

head: AGENTS.md > Keep changes focused
text: If a task starts requiring a new subsystem, dependency, public API family, or many unrelated files, reconsider its scope. Reuse existing test infrastructure before creating new infrastructure. Avoid future-proofing that has no immediate requirement.

head: AGENTS.md > Keep changes focused
text:
Do not expand a focused task into unrelated architecture, public API,
dependencies, algorithms, or upstream work unless the issue or maintainer
explicitly asks for it. Do not silently turn a documentation or
repository-guidance task into a scientific implementation change.

head: AGENTS.md > Public API
text:
The intentional public API is defined and tested in
`tests/test_public_api.py`. Treat its facade and canonical-path registries,
together with the corresponding `__all__` declarations, as the authoritative
inventory.

head: AGENTS.md > Public API
text:
Public facades declare `__all__`, and canonical public paths are tested
explicitly. Importability alone does not make a symbol public. A new public API
requires updates to the appropriate facade, `__all__`, API documentation,
tests, and user-facing documentation or the changelog when appropriate.

head: AGENTS.md > Public API
text:
Private underscore names have no compatibility promise. Experimental APIs
must be clearly identified. Documentation and examples must never invent
public names that are not part of current main.

head: AGENTS.md > Estimator contracts
text: `tests/_contract_cases.py` is the central estimator capability registry, and `tests/test_estimator_contracts.py` executes the shared cases. The registry is capability-based: it does not promise that every estimator has the same interface or output shape.

head: AGENTS.md > Estimator contracts

head: AGENTS.md > Estimator contracts
text: Before adding an estimator-specific test for generic behavior, check whether the estimator should instead opt into an existing capability in `_contract_cases.py`. Do not repeat tests such as one input-mutation test per estimator when the central contract owns that property. Algorithm-specific tests should cover algorithm-specific science and behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > MNE container contracts

head: AGENTS.md > Progress reporting

head: AGENTS.md > Progress reporting
text: Algorithm code emits structured progress events through callback support. `ProgressEvent` is the immutable protocol payload. Callbacks are synchronous runtime observers supplied by keyword; their return values are ignored and their exceptions propagate unchanged. Logging is independent: `verbose` controls package logs, while `callback` controls events.

head: AGENTS.md > Progress reporting
text: `TqdmProgress` is an optional presentation adapter that consumes events. Algorithm internals must not own tqdm bars directly. Do not add `print()`-based progress or a second callback interface. New callback-aware methods should follow the existing package convention and should not make callback state an estimator hyperparameter.

Passing one local environment is not sufficient evidence of repository

head: AGENTS.md > Repository task commands

head: AGENTS.md > Testing philosophy
text:
Test scientific, public, and integration contracts rather than private
implementation details. Prefer deterministic behavioral or numerical
assertions to execution-only or shape-only coverage tests. Historical bug
cases are useful when they protect a durable contract, but organize them
under the contract that owns them rather than creating a historical-parity
testing architecture.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing philosophy
text:
Use parametrization when it represents genuinely equivalent cases. Keep
scientifically distinct regimes separate. Use coverage diagnostically; do not
optimize for a percentage at the expense of meaningful tests. Centralize
shared estimator and MNE-container behavior in their contract suites.

head: AGENTS.md > Scientific implementations and validation
text:
Primary scientific literature governs algorithm claims and semantics. Identify
whether behavior is a published method, an established implementation
convention, an mne-denoise-specific extension, or experimental/prototype
behavior. Do not silently describe an extension as if it came from the
original paper.

head: AGENTS.md > Scientific implementations and validation
text:
Scientific tests should exercise meaningful invariants and behavior, not only
reproduce one historical array. If changing scientific behavior, document why
and cite the relevant source. Parity with old package output is insufficient
evidence of correctness. Numerical tolerances should reflect meaningful
floating-point expectations, not be widened merely to make a test pass.

head: AGENTS.md > Documentation and docstrings
text:
Every public function, class, and method docstring is part of the public API
and must match current behavior. Check public docstrings for:

head: AGENTS.md > Documentation and docstrings

head: AGENTS.md > Documentation and docstrings
text:
Use NumPy-style docstrings and the repository's citation conventions. Do not
maintain a complete bibliography manually in every docstring. Do not leave
stale parameter names after API changes, claim Raw/Epochs/Evoked support that
the implementation or contracts do not provide, or misstate copy versus
in-place semantics and `fit`/`transform` lifecycle. Document experimental
status where appropriate.

head: AGENTS.md > Documentation and docstrings

When changing or reviewing public API, audit public docstrings callable by

Existing docstrings are not authoritative when they disagree with those
sources of truth.

head: AGENTS.md > Examples and gallery
text:
Gallery examples have CI, runtime, and maintenance costs. One new estimator
does not automatically require one new example. Extend an existing example
when it teaches the same concept; add a gallery item when it teaches a
meaningful scientific capability or workflow. Tiny syntax demonstrations
belong in docstrings or method documentation, and tests are not gallery
examples.

head: AGENTS.md > Examples and gallery

New real-data dependencies must use the documentation data prefetch/cache
mechanism. Add datasets to `scripts/prefetch_docs_data.py` when an example
needs them. Examples must use public APIs and should not preserve obsolete
APIs merely to avoid changing docs. Prefer the existing documentation and
gallery structure unless a change in information architecture is explicitly
part of the task.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository scripts and generated artifacts
text:
Scripts under `scripts/` are operational repository helpers. Do not add
substrate or parity-generation scripts without a demonstrated current need.
Generated changelog, release, and citation artifacts should be maintained by
their owning tooling rather than hand-edited where applicable. Old parity

Never commit directly to `main`. Keep pull requests focused and use existing
issue or design discussion for substantial behavior changes. User-visible
changes need the repository's changelog mechanism. Do not add AI co-author
trailers unless repository policy explicitly requires them. The human
contributor remains responsible for submitted changes.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Prerequisites

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Prerequisites
