head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Prerequisites > Eclipse source bundles (recommended)
text:
The `@source` axis needs source bundles to read Eclipse Platform/JDT API
source and javadoc. Without them,
`jdt q '"org.eclipse.core.runtime.CoreException" | @source'` returns
"Source not available". Install all Eclipse source bundles once
(Eclipse must NOT be running):

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Prerequisites > Eclipse source bundles (recommended)
text:
Adjust the update site URL to match your Eclipse version (e.g. `4.39`)
and paths to your Eclipse installation.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Environment check (REQUIRED)
text:
**Run at the start of every conversation, before any other work.
Subagents (Explore, Plan, etc.) skip this section — jdt is already
verified by the main agent.**

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Environment check (REQUIRED)
text:
1. `jdt setup --check` — verifies CLI, Node, Java, Maven, Eclipse, bridge.
   - `jdt: command not found` → `cd cli && npm install && npm link`
   - Plugin not installed → `jdt setup --eclipse <path>`
   - Eclipse not running → start it, re-run check

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Environment check (REQUIRED)
text:
2. `jdt status` — **workspace dashboard**. Shows git repos, open editors,
   compilation errors, running launches, test results, and project list
   in one call. This is your orientation command — run it first to
   understand what the developer is working on.
   - If `jdtbridge-verify` or `jdtbridge-package` are missing from
     launch configs, import them:
     ```bash
     jdt launch config --import launches/jdtbridge-verify.launch
     jdt launch config --import launches/jdtbridge-package.launch
     ```

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Environment check (REQUIRED)
text:
3. Verify `jdtbridge.target` exists in repo root (gitignored, per-developer).
   Without it, Tycho builds fail. If missing, create it pointing to the
   local Eclipse directory:
   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no"?>
   <?pde version="3.8"?>
   <target name="eclipse-local" sequenceNumber="1">
       <locations>
           <location path="/path/to/eclipse" type="Directory"/>
       </locations>
   </target>
   ```

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Use `jdt` for Java analysis
text:
**Prefer `jdt` over grep/glob for Java-specific queries.** Grep returns
string matches; `jdt` returns semantic results from Eclipse's compiler index.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Use `jdt` for Java analysis
text:
`jdt status` shows the full workspace state — including a `help` section
with the full command reference. `jdt help <command>` for detailed usage
of any command.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Use `jdt` for Java analysis > `jdt q` — graph query language
text:
`jdt q '<qlang-pipeline>'` evaluates a qlang pipeline against the
Eclipse semantic graph. The graph is navigated through operand axes
that consume a node-Map (skeleton or detail) OR a fqn string
from `pipeValue`. Output is qlang-literal; fqn strings in the result
are ready subjects for the next step.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Use `jdt` for Java analysis > `jdt q` — graph query language
text:
Full axis catalog, sugar conduits, and modifier syntax live in
`jdt help q` (runtime truth) and `docs/jdt-query-spec.md`.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Use `jdt` for Java analysis > FQN — member form
text: Every node carries one identifier field, `:fqn`. Per kind:

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Use `jdt` for Java analysis > FQN — member form
text:
A bare `pkg.Class#method` without parens is ambiguous when the
type has multiple overloads; the error descriptor carries
`:candidates` so the caller can pick and retry. Types can be
simple (`String`) or qualified (`java.lang.String`); generics
are stripped — `List<String>` matches `List`.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Use `jdt` for Java analysis > Pipeline composability
text:
All of the below return a single qlang-literal value — ready for
pipe-chaining with standard shell tools or further `jdt q` calls.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Use `jdt` for Java analysis > Subagents (Explore, Plan)
text:
Custom jdt-aware agents are installed in `.claude/agents/` by

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > `jdt build` vs full verify
text:
| | `jdt build` | `jdt launch run jdtbridge-package` | `jdt launch run jdtbridge-verify` |
|---|---|---|---|
| What | Eclipse clean+full build (or `--incremental`) | Tycho build, no tests | Tycho full build + tests |
| Speed | 3-10 seconds (incremental: 1-3s) | 30-40 seconds | ~5 minutes |
| Tests | No | No | Unit + integration |
| Output | Compiled classes in Eclipse | p2 site in `site/target/` | p2 site in `site/target/` |
| When | Quick iteration while coding | Before `jdt setup --skip-build` | Before commit |

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > `jdt build` vs full verify
text:
Console output is captured by Eclipse and available via `jdt launch logs`.
Use `-f` to stream live, or inspect afterwards with `--tail`. Example:
```bash
jdt launch run jdtbridge-verify           # launch (prints guide first time)
jdt launch logs jdtbridge-verify -f | tail -20  # wait + last 20 lines
jdt launch logs jdtbridge-verify --tail 30      # inspect after completion
```
For CI without local Eclipse: `mvn clean verify -Pci`.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Making changes
text: 1. **Create a branch** — never commit directly to master

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Making changes
text: 2. **Write code + tests** — every change needs tests

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Making changes
text:
3. **Build** — plugin first, tests second (default is clean build):
   ```bash
   jdt build --project io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge
   jdt build --project io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests
   jdt test run io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests --coverage -f
   ```

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Making changes
text:
4. **Full Tycho build** — `jdt launch run jdtbridge-verify` then
   `jdt launch logs jdtbridge-verify -f | tail -20` to wait

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Making changes
text: 5. **Install and verify live** — `jdt setup --skip-build`, then test

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Making changes
text:
6. **Check ALL docs** if CLI syntax or API changed:
   - `cli/src/cli.mjs` (`jdt help` output)
   - `cli/src/commands/*.mjs` (per-command help)
   - `README.md`, `cli/README.md`, `plugin/README.md`, this file

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Making changes
text: 7. **Commit → push → PR → squash merge → delete branch**

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Making changes

8. **After merge** — switch to master, pull, clean build:
   ```bash
   git checkout master && git pull
   jdt build --clean
   ```

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Pull requests
text:
Use `gh pr create` / `gh pr edit` / `gh pr merge`. **Always pass `--body`
via HEREDOC** to avoid shell escaping issues. Do NOT use markdown formatting
characters (`*`, `#`, `` ` ``) in `--body` — they break `gh` argument parsing.
Use plain text or `- [x]` checklists only.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Pull requests
text:
**Waiting for CI:** use `gh pr checks <N> --watch` — it blocks until
all checks complete, then exits with 0 (all pass) or 1 (failures).
Never use `sleep` loops to poll CI status.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Pull requests
text:
**Bot review comments.** After CI, automated reviewers
(`gemini-code-assist[bot]`, etc.) leave a review summary plus
line-level comments. `gemini-code-assist` first puts an 👀 reaction
on the PR description when it picks up the PR; the actual review
lands ~1–2 min later. Watch for both signals:

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Pull requests
text:
Every concrete bot finding must be resolved before merge — either
fix it in a follow-up commit, or reply on the comment with a clear
reason for rejection. Do not leave bot comments unanswered: the
human reviewer expects each one closed by the time they look.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Pull requests
text:
After replying, also **mark the conversation resolved** so the PR
page no longer shows it as outstanding. The REST comments API can
post replies; resolving the conversation is GraphQL-only:

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Important details
text:
- **Clean build after branch switch or merge.** `git checkout`, `git pull`,
  squash merge — all rewrite `.class` files that Eclipse's incremental
  builder may not invalidate. Run `jdt build --clean` to avoid phantom
  errors and stale bytecode. This also applies after `git pull` on master.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Important details
text:
- **New Java files invisible until build.** `jdt test run` says "Type not found"
  → run `jdt build` for the project first.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Important details
text:
- **Build order matters.** `plugin.tests` is a Fragment-Host of `plugin` —
  sees package-private members, but must build after plugin.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Important details
text:
- **`jdt setup --skip-build` restarts Eclipse.** Port changes. `jdt` commands
  auto-discover the new port, but raw `curl` URLs break.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Important details
text:
- **`jdt setup` without `--skip-build` runs Maven internally.**
  After a full build, always add `--skip-build` — never build twice.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Test infrastructure
text:
**Prefer Eclipse launch configurations over direct CLI commands.**
The developer works in Eclipse — launch configs give them history,
Console output, and a shared vocabulary between agent and IDE.
Use `jdt launch run` and `jdt test run` instead of `cd cli && npm test`
or `mvn verify`. When a launch config exists for the task, use it.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Test infrastructure
text:
If you must call `npm`/`mvn` directly (e.g. no matching launch config,
CI context, or specific flags not expressible via launch), explain why.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Test infrastructure
text:
- **CLI tests:** `jdt launch run npm-test -f` (preferred) or
  `cd cli && npm test` (fallback). Single file:
  `jdt launch run npm-test -f -- test/paths.test.mjs`

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Test infrastructure
text: - **Plugin unit tests:** `jdt test run io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests --coverage -f`

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Test infrastructure
text: - **Integration tests:** full Tycho build only (`jdt launch run jdtbridge-verify`) — use `@EnabledIfSystemProperty(named = "jdtbridge.integration-tests", matches = "true")`

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Test infrastructure
text:
- **Test fixture:** `TestFixture.java` creates a project with known classes —
  `test.model.Animal`, `Dog`, `Cat`, `test.edge.Calculator` (overloads),
  `Repository` (generics), `test.edge.Color` (enum), `test.edge.Marker`
  (annotation). Add new test types there.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running plugin tests
text:
**Prefer running individual test classes or methods**, not the full suite.
Full suite (832 plugin + 28 UI = 860 tests) takes ~2 minutes and runs
in a separate Eclipse runtime. Individual tests take 5-15 seconds.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running plugin tests
text:
**UI tests must run via the full suite**, not by class FQN.
`jdt test run <FQN>` against a class in `plugin.tests.ui` synthesises
a headless launch config — `PlatformUI.getWorkbench()` is null in
that runtime and the test hangs on the first `Display.syncExec`.
Use `jdt test run io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests.ui` so the
shared `*.tests.ui.launch` (workbench PDE) picks up the test.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running plugin tests
text:
Both suites use shared launch configs from `launches/`. If a config
is missing or broken, restore from the repo:
```bash
jdt launch config --delete "io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests"
jdt launch config --import launches/io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests.launch

jdt launch config --delete "io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests.ui"
jdt launch config --import launches/io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests.ui.launch
```

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running plugin tests
text:
- **Plugin tests run in a PDE test runtime** with workspace bundles
  (not the installed plugin). `jdt build` is enough — no `jdt setup`
  needed before running tests.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running plugin tests
text:
- **But `jdt setup` IS needed** to test live behavior (`jdt q` axes,
  `jdt launch`, `jdt open`, etc.) because those go through the
  installed plugin's HTTP server.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running plugin tests
text:
- **Build before testing:** `jdt build --project io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests`
  — otherwise new test classes won't be found.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running plugin tests
text:
- **TestFixture lifecycle:** each test class needs `@BeforeAll static void
  setUp() throws Exception { TestFixture.create(); }`. The fixture is
  idempotent but must be created before `JdtUtils.findType()` calls.
  If a `@Nested` class has `@AfterAll` with `TestFixture.destroy()`,
  subsequent nested classes in the same file won't find fixture types.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running plugin tests
text:
- **Check results:** `jdt test runs` shows all runs with relative time.
  `jdt test status <testRunId> -f` for details on failures.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Running CLI tests
text:
CLI tests mock the HTTP server — no Eclipse needed. They run on both
Windows and Linux (CI). Path conversion tests mock `process.platform`.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Plugin changes → live testing
text:
Plugin tests run in a PDE test runtime (workspace bundles) — `jdt build`
is enough. But live commands (`jdt q`, `jdt launch config --delete`,
`jdt refactor`, `jdt open`, `jdt test run`) go through the **installed**
plugin's HTTP server. After changing plugin code:

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Plugin changes → live testing
text: Only then will live commands use the new code.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Shared launch configurations
text:
`launches/` contains `.launch` files committed to the repo. Eclipse
auto-discovers them from the project directory. They are NOT in
workspace metadata — `jdt launch config --delete` does not touch them.
`--delete` only removes configs from
`<workspace>/.metadata/.plugins/org.eclipse.debug.core/.launches/`.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Shared launch configurations
text:
To add a new shared launch config: create `.launch` XML in `launches/`,
`jdt refresh` the project. Eclipse picks it up automatically.
Use `${system_path:node}`, `${workspace_loc:...}`, and
`${system_property:java.io.tmpdir}` variables for cross-platform
paths — no absolute paths in committed .launch files.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Shared launch configurations
text: Available launch configs in `launches/`:

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Shared launch configurations
text:
| File | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `jdtbridge-verify.launch` | Maven Build | `clean verify` — full Tycho build + tests |
| `jdtbridge-package.launch` | Maven Build | `clean package` — Tycho build, no tests |
| `npm-test.launch` | Program | CLI vitest suite |
| `io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests.launch` | JUnit Plug-in Test | Plugin tests (832 tests, headless PDE runtime) |
| `io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests.ui.launch` | JUnit Plug-in Test | UI tests (28 tests, workbench PDE runtime) |

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Shared launch configurations
text:
PDE test launch configs carry explicit bundle lists for the test
runtime. Key constraints for the UI config:

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Shared launch configurations
text:
- `org.eclipse.debug.ui`, `org.eclipse.eclemma.ui`,
  `org.eclipse.help.ui` must be `@default:false` (not auto-started) —
  their `start()` methods call `PlatformUI.getWorkbench()` which
  throws before the workbench is created.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Shared launch configurations
text:
- JUnit 5 bundles (`*5.14.3`, `*1.14.3`) are required alongside
  JUnit 6 — `TestFixture` creates projects with `JUNIT_CONTAINER/5`.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Development workflow > Shared launch configurations
text:
To restore a launch config from the repo:
```bash
jdt launch config --delete "io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests.ui"
jdt launch config --import launches/io.github.kaluchi.jdtbridge.tests.ui.launch
```

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Releasing
text:
Requires: clean working tree, master branch, tag must not exist.
CI deploys automatically: npm publish, p2 site, GitHub Release.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Releasing
text:
After CI creates the GitHub Release, replace the auto-generated body
with human-written release notes. Show the draft to the user for
approval before publishing. Use `gh release edit vX.Y.Z --notes "..."`.
See previous releases for style (feature paragraphs, not bullet lists
of commits).

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text:
Tests are code. Same quality bar as production — no fallbacks,
no dead branches, no defensive patterns "just in case."

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text:
**100% test-file coverage.** Every line and branch inside a test
file must be exercised. If JaCoCo shows a missed branch in your
test, you wrote a branching construct that doesn't belong there.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text:
**No branching in tests.** A test is a deterministic sequence:
set up → call → assert. No `if`, no `for` with filter predicates,
no `try/catch`, no `stream().filter().findFirst().orElseThrow()`.
Each of these creates branches JaCoCo must cover — and the
"other" branch is unreachable by design, tanking coverage.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text: - Direct index access (`entries[0]`) not loop + filter

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text: - Direct cast (`(IType) children[0]`) not `instanceof` scan

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text: - `JsonArray.contains(new JsonPrimitive("x"))` not loop + flag

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text: - `assertNotNull(x)` then use `x` — not `if (x != null)`

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text:
**No conditional test execution.** No `if (!available()) return`,
no `@EnabledIf`, no `Assumptions.assumeTrue`. A test either runs
its assertions or fails loud. If a test needs a runtime capability
(UI bundle, specific launch type), put it in the correct suite
from the start — `plugin.tests` (headless) vs `plugin.tests.ui`
(workbench).

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text:
**No null from test helpers.** A helper that looks something up
either finds it or throws `AssertionError`. Never return null
and check at the call site.

head: JDT Bridge — Agent Instructions > Test requirements
text:
**Shared infrastructure goes in `tests.support`.** TestFixture,
TestAwait, and any reusable lookup/factory helpers belong in the
`tests.support` module — not duplicated across test files.

head: AGENTS.md > 项目形态
text: AI Gate 是面向 Codex 工作流的本地优先路由层和桌面壳。最重要的边界是薄网关语义：保留上游协议语义，账号密钥留在本机，做不到的能力要明确不支持，不要伪造兼容。

head: AGENTS.md > 项目形态

head: AGENTS.md > 项目形态
text: - `frontend/`：Vite + React + Ant Design 桌面端/网页端 UI。

head: AGENTS.md > 项目形态
text: - `desktop/`：Tauri 桌面壳和桌面打包配置。

head: AGENTS.md > 项目形态

head: AGENTS.md > 项目形态

head: AGENTS.md > 项目形态

head: AGENTS.md > 项目形态

head: AGENTS.md > Harness-First 工作流
text: 每个改动都必须能被某种 harness 验证。harness 可以是单元测试、集成测试、shell 冒烟脚本、本地 dev server、Worker 命令、打包脚本，或带有具体输出的定向手工检查。

head: AGENTS.md > Harness-First 工作流
text: - 先识别能覆盖这个 bug 或回归的最小 harness。

head: AGENTS.md > Harness-First 工作流
text: - 保留已有用户改动，不要回退无关 dirty files。

head: AGENTS.md > Harness-First 工作流
text: - 优先使用现有 helper、路由模式、状态模型和测试工具。

head: AGENTS.md > Harness-First 工作流
text: - 行为变更尽量先新增或更新 harness，再改实现。

head: AGENTS.md > Harness-First 工作流
text: - 运行相关 harness，并在回复中写明具体命令。

head: AGENTS.md > Harness-First 工作流
text: - 如果 harness 无法运行，说明原因和仍未验证的风险。

head: AGENTS.md > Harness-First 工作流
text: - 没有看到真实输出前，不要声称修复完成、构建成功、发布成功或测试通过。

head: AGENTS.md > 验证矩阵
text: 先运行最窄的适用命令；如果改动影响共享行为，再扩大验证范围。

head: CLAUDE.md > Session State (2026-08-26) > `.env` handling — settled (updated 2026-08-28, #337)
text:
Zed classifies **every** env file as Shell Script: bare `.env` via the bash
grammar's `path_suffixes`, and `.env.*` variants via `"Shell Script": [".env.*"]`
in Zed's own `assets/settings/default.json`. The extension therefore attaches to
`.env` through the single `"Shell Script"` entry in `extension.toml`, and the LSP
dispatches env features on **filename**, not on Zed's language classification:
every env feature routes through one shared gate,
`env_key_locator::is_env_file_name` (and its path form `path_is_env_file`),
which matches `.env` exactly or a `.env.` variant prefix. The Salsa ingestion
in `execute_salsa_update` joined that gate last — it read `starts_with(".env")`
until #337, and so admitted `.envrc`, `.environment`, and `.env-backup` as
Laravel env sources. Startup registration is the one env path that does not
consult the gate, because it names its three files outright and classifies
nothing.

head: CLAUDE.md > Session State (2026-08-26) > `.env` handling — settled (updated 2026-08-28, #337)
text: Consequences, all verified against primary sources:

head: CLAUDE.md > Session State (2026-08-26) > `.env` handling — settled (updated 2026-08-28, #337)
text:
- **No language definition is shipped for `.env`, and none should be.** An
  extension language could tie-and-win bare `.env` (bash offers `".env"`), but
  the `.env.*` variants sit at the `UserConfigured` tier that only a user's own
  `file_types` can override. Shipping one would fix `.env` and leave
  `.env.local` shell-linted — a split worse than the uniform status quo.

head: CLAUDE.md > Session State (2026-08-26) > `.env` handling — settled (updated 2026-08-28, #337)
text:
- **`zarifpour/zed-env` is not recommended, and the `"env"` attach entry was
  dropped in v0.7.4 (#337).** Its `path_suffixes` are a bare `"env"` (loses the
  length tie to `".env"`), so it never claims the files it appears to; and its
  bare `"conf"` / `"example"` / `"local"` / `"test"` entries reclassify
  unrelated files project-wide (e.g. `laravel/sail`'s `supervisord.conf`).
  Because it never claims `.env`, the `"env"` attach entry never fired — it
  bought no capability, while reading to a registry reviewer as this extension
  claiming another extension's language. `extension.toml` now attaches to
  `"PHP"`, `"Blade"`, `"XML"` and `"Shell Script"` only, and its comment block
  carries the written justification for the `"Shell Script"` entry.

head: CLAUDE.md > Session State (2026-08-26) > `.env` handling — settled (updated 2026-08-28, #337)
text:
- **SC2034 noise is NOT silenced by this extension.** The
  `language_server_additional_workspace_configuration` hook that injected
  `--exclude=SC2034` into bash-language-server shipped in v0.7.2–v0.7.3 and was
  removed entirely in v0.7.4 (#337). It reconfigured a language server this
  extension neither provides nor owns, which Zed's publishing prerequisites
  forbid, and the registry rejected v0.7.3 over it
  (zed-industries/extensions#7370). `src/lib.rs` now writes workspace
  configuration for `laravel-lsp` and nothing else. The manual workarounds in
  `docs/environment.md` are the whole answer by design: document how, do not do
  it to the user's other servers.

head: Project conventions > Non-obvious invariants
text:
- `agent/channels/eve.ts` — the `auth:` array is an **ordered** chain
  (app session → internal run secret → Vercel OIDC → local-dev). The first
  entry that resolves wins, so reordering it changes which principal
  authenticates a request. Do not sort or "tidy" it. Since eve 0.30.0
  `localDev()` keys off the running process, not the request's Host — the
  loopback-Host hole it used to have is fixed upstream.

head: Project conventions > Non-obvious invariants
text:
- `lib/chat-events.ts` — eve's event payloads are not one discriminated union,
  so `eventType()` is the **only** place allowed to read `.type` off an opaque
  event. Everything else must go through the exported predicates.

head: Project conventions > Non-obvious invariants
text:
- `lib/lookout-schedule.ts` — the lookouts UI only ever emits two UTC cron
  shapes (`M H * * *` daily, `M H * * D` weekly) and the parser assumes it.
  Emitting any other cron shape from the UI will silently fail to schedule.

head: Project conventions > Non-obvious invariants
text:
- `agent/schedules/lookouts.ts` — scheduling is an in-database lease driven by a
  minute-tick eve schedule. There is no QStash / external queue; some stale
  comments elsewhere in the code still mention one.

head: Project conventions > Non-obvious invariants
text:
- `app/globals.css` imports `shadcn/tailwind.css`, which supplies the
  `data-open` / `data-closed` Tailwind variants the overlay animations depend
  on. Do not drop the `shadcn` dependency or that import.

head: Project conventions > Non-obvious invariants
text:
- `lib/models.ts` holds the featured picker list and `DEFAULT_CHAT_MODEL`; the
  live model is chosen per turn in `agent/agent.ts` from the user's picker
  choice and sent as-is; only its *context window* is looked up in the AI
  Gateway catalog. Changing one without the other desyncs context-window math.

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text:
Durations and easing curves are **not** hand-typed at call sites. The easing
tokens live in the `@theme inline` block in `app/globals.css` and are available
as Tailwind utilities:

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text:
| Token | Utility | Value | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ease-out-strong` | `ease-out-strong` | `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` | entering / exiting UI |
| `--ease-in-out-strong` | `ease-in-out-strong` | `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)` | on-screen movement |
| `--ease-drawer` | `ease-drawer` | `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` | iOS-like drawer / sheet curve |

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text:
They are named with a `-strong` suffix so they do not override Tailwind's
built-in `ease-out` / `ease-in-out` utilities app-wide; a site opts in
explicitly.

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text: - entering or exiting → `ease-out-strong`

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text: - moving or morphing on screen → `ease-in-out-strong`

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text: - hover / colour change → `ease`

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text: - constant motion (spinners, marquees) → `linear`

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text: Duration budget — pick the Tailwind `duration-*` class inside these ranges:

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text:
| Element | Duration |
|---|---|
| Button press feedback | 100–160ms |
| Tooltips, small popovers | 125–200ms |
| Dropdowns, selects | 150–250ms |
| Modals, drawers | 200–500ms |

head: Project conventions > Motion tokens
text:
Do not introduce a new hand-typed `ease-[cubic-bezier(...)]` in app code. If
none of the tokens fits, add a token rather than a one-off curve.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: **dep-scope** is a granular dependency analyzer for TypeScript/JavaScript projects. Unlike Knip or Depcheck (binary used/unused), it provides symbol-level analysis: which symbols from each dependency are used, usage percentages, native alternatives, duplicate detection, and peer dependency identification.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: **V2 feature**: `dep-scope migrate` generates LLM-ready markdown migration prompts for dependencies that can be removed. Run without arguments to auto-detect all candidates; pass a package name to target one. Prompts are context-aware (TypeScript target, framework, file locations) and ready to pipe into Claude Code.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: **e18e integration**: 169 packages from the [e18e module-replacements](https://e18e.dev) project are embedded statically in `src/rules/e18e-data.ts`. Any import from a recognized micro-utility or polyfill package (e.g. `has-flag`, `left-pad`, `array-includes`, `object-assign`) is automatically flagged as RECODE_NATIVE with the native replacement shown. Total packages with alternatives: 195.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Verdict System
text:
| Verdict       | Criteria |
|---------------|----------|
| KEEP          | Well-used, no alternatives needed |
| RECODE_NATIVE | < threshold symbols + native alternatives exist (built-in or e18e) |
| CONSOLIDATE   | Duplicate with another lib in same category |
| REMOVE        | Zero imports detected |
| PEER_DEP      | Required by other packages, redundant in package.json |
| INVESTIGATE   | Needs manual review (low usage, no alternatives) |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Verdict System
text: Threshold default: 5 symbols. Configurable via `-t` flag or config file.

text: When verdict is INVESTIGATE, `investigateReason` explains why:

|--------|---------|
| `LOW_SYMBOL_COUNT` | Only 1-2 symbols used |
| `SINGLE_FILE_USAGE` | Used in only 1 file |
| `LOW_FILE_SPREAD` | Used in 2-3 files (below fileCountThreshold) |
| `UNKNOWN_PACKAGE` | Unknown package, manual review needed |

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: This is **henry.ink** - a social annotation layer for the web. What if every webpage had marginalia for notes? Originally developed as a browser extension for the Community Archive hackathon, it has evolved into a web-first platform at henry.ink that works without any installation. The project maintains both the web application and the original browser extension (Chrome & Firefox) for integrated browsing experiences.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conceptual Overview
text: This project takes a "reverse Hypothesis" approach to web annotations. Instead of overlaying annotations on existing webpages (like traditional annotation tools), we recreate the webpage content within our own environment. This gives us full control over the UI, enabling seamless integration of comments with the original content - such as automatically highlighting annotated text. The goal is to create a unified reading experience where blog posts and their associated discussions from Bluesky, Are.na, and other sources feel naturally integrated rather than bolted on.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 1. Big Picture
text:
| Layer                          | What It Does                                                                       | Where To Learn More                                     |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **MCP Server**                 | Hosts “tools”, “resources”, and “prompts” that the client (human or LLM) can call. | MCP C# SDK README → *Getting Started (Server)* section. |
| **Refactoring Logic (Roslyn)** | Analysers, code‑fixes and syntax transforms that change or inspect code safely.    | Roslyn SDK quick‑starts and samples.                    |

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 1. Big Picture
text: MCP gives us the protocol surface; Roslyn gives us the ability to *understand* and *rewrite* C#; everything else is standard .NET hosting.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 2. Key MCP Concepts (30‑second refresher)
text:
| Concept                              | What It Represents                                                                | Typical Use in This Repo                    |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| **Tool** (`[McpServerTool]`)         | A *side‑effect‑free* operation that *returns* something (e.g., “Extract Method”). | Main refactoring entry‑points.              |
| **Resource** (`[McpServerResource]`) | Read‑only contextual data, addressable via URI templates.                         | Metrics, dependency graphs.                 |
| **Prompt** (`[McpServerPrompt]`)     | A templated `ChatMessage` that instructs an LLM.                                  | Enforce architectural or style constraints. |

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 2. Key MCP Concepts (30‑second refresher)
text: > **Tip:** One class → one concept. Mixing tools and resources in the same type hurts discoverability.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 3. Fast Path: Creating a New Refactoring Tool
text: 1. **Decorate** the class with `[McpServerToolType]` and the method with `[McpServerTool]`.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 3. Fast Path: Creating a New Refactoring Tool
text:
2. **Keep the surface minimal**
   * One or two domain parameters (string name, Location span, etc.).
   * Accept `CancellationToken` as last parameter.
   * Prefer returning *strongly‑typed* objects; strings are fine for simple success/error.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 3. Fast Path: Creating a New Refactoring Tool
text: 3. **Delegate to Roslyn helpers**—don’t re‑invent tree traversal.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 3. Fast Path: Creating a New Refactoring Tool
text: 4. **Add an Xunit test** beside the implementation; use the `AdhocWorkspace` pattern shown in the Roslyn samples.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 4. Roslyn SDK Best Practices
text: * **Immutable first** – every tree, compilation and symbol is immutable; create new trees instead of mutating existing ones.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 4. Roslyn SDK Best Practices
text: * **Cancellation everywhere** – pass the `CancellationToken` you receive to every Roslyn call to avoid UI freezes.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 4. Roslyn SDK Best Practices
text: * **Prefer `SyntaxGenerator` over manual trivia handling** for readability.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 4. Roslyn SDK Best Practices
text: * **Use *incremental* analyzers** (`IncrementalGenerator`, `IncrementalValuesProvider`) when performance matters.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 4. Roslyn SDK Best Practices
text: * **Unit‑test refactorings and analyzers** with the `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing` framework; follow the pattern in the “Write your first analyzer” tutorial.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 4. Roslyn SDK Best Practices
text:
* **Separate analysis from transformation**:
  * Use `SyntaxWalker` / analyzers to **find** code.
  * Use `SyntaxRewriter` or generators to **rewrite** the code.
  * This keeps diagnostics fast and only allocates when a fix is actually applied.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 4. Roslyn SDK Best Practices
text: * **Reuse Workspaces** – long‑lived `AdhocWorkspace` instances reuse metadata references and reduce allocations.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 4. Roslyn SDK Best Practices
text: * **Avoid `.Result`** – Roslyn APIs are async‑first; blocking can deadlock Visual Studio.

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 5. Error Handling (Thin Version)
text:
| Situation                                        | How To Respond                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Business rule violated (e.g., method name empty) | `return "Message…";`                                       |
| Protocol violation (e.g., JSON schema mismatch)  | `throw new McpException("…", McpErrorCode.InvalidParams);` |
| Unexpected failure                               | `throw new McpException("…", McpErrorCode.InternalError);` |

head: Refactoring MCP Server Contribution Guide > 5. Error Handling (Thin Version)
text: Keep messages actionable: *what happened*, *how to fix*.

text: - **Build before migrate**: `pnpm run build:server` is required before running any migration CLI commands. The server CLI entry (`src/cli.ts`) is compiled separately via `nest-cli.json` projects config.

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas
text: - **Single root `.env`**: The root `.env` (copied from root `.env.example`) is the only env file. The server and its CLI resolve it from the repo root regardless of CWD (see `packages/server/src/common/config/env.ts`). If a `packages/server/.env` exists it takes precedence over the root `.env`.

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas
text: - **Webapp env prefixes**: Only `VITE_`, `REACT_APP_`, and `PUBLIC_URL` env vars are exposed to the client (see `vite.config.ts`).

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas
text: - **Server path alias**: `@/*` maps to `packages/server/src/*` (both in `tsconfig.json` and Jest `moduleNameMapper`).

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas
text: - **Webapp path alias**: `@` maps to `packages/webapp/src` (Vite resolve alias).

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas

head: AGENTS.md > Key gotchas

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp
text: The full request/response cycle with case conversion at each layer:

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp
text: 1. **Server DB columns**: snake_case (MariaDB/Objection.js).

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp
text: 2. **Server DTOs** (`@ApiProperty`): camelCase — used for internal class-validator validation only.

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp
text:
3. **`SerializeInterceptor`** (global, `packages/server/src/common/interceptors/serialize.interceptor.ts`):
   - **Inbound**: converts request body/query from **snake_case → camelCase** so DTOs receive camelCase keys.
   - **Outbound**: converts response from **camelCase → snake_case** before sending to client.
   - **Net effect**: the API wire format is always **snake_case**.

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp
text: 4. **SDK request middleware** (`shared/sdk-ts/src/middleware/snake-case-request-middleware.ts`): enabled by default. Converts outgoing request body/query from camelCase → snake_case (to match what the server interceptor expects).

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp
text: 5. **SDK response middleware** (`shared/sdk-ts/src/middleware/camel-case-middleware.ts`): **disabled by default** (`disableCamelCaseTransform: true`). Converts snake_case → camelCase when opted in.

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp
text:
6. **Webapp consumption**:
   - **SDK fetcher path** (`useApiFetcher()` in `packages/webapp/src/hooks/useRequest.tsx`): most queries get **snake_case** data by default. Pass `{ enableCamelCaseTransform: true }` to get automatic camelCase.
   - **Legacy axios path** (`useApiRequest()`): no automatic transform. Use `transformToCamelCase()` / `transfromToSnakeCase()` from `@/utils` manually.

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp > Practical impact
text: - **When writing new query hooks**: use `useApiFetcher({ enableCamelCaseTransform: true })` and work with camelCase. Types from `@bigcapital/sdk-ts` are camelCase.

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp > Practical impact
text: - **When using legacy `apiRequest`**: responses are snake_case — call `transformToCamelCase(res.data)` before using.

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp > Practical impact
text: - **Database columns** are always snake_case. When adding migrations, use snake_case. When writing Objection.js models, map to camelCase properties.

head: AGENTS.md > Data flow: server → sdk-ts → webapp > Practical impact
text: - **New API endpoints**: define DTOs with camelCase `@ApiProperty` names. The `SerializeInterceptor` handles the rest.

text: Home-ops IaC repo — Kubernetes cluster managed with Flux CD, Talos Linux, and SOPS/Age encryption.

head: AGENTS.md > Project model
text: Claude works as the **medior developer** — it implements changes, validates them, and presents PRs for review. The human maintainer is the **senior** — reviews code, runs final checks, and merges approved PRs.

head: AGENTS.md > Project model
text: - AI **does**: write code, run validation, create commits via `but`, open PRs via GitHub MCP tools (`github_create_pull_request`), check konflate blast radius, report cautions.

head: AGENTS.md > Project model
text: - AI **does not**: merge PRs, push to `main` directly, approve its own changes, skip validation hooks, run auto-merge, or merge without explicit human approval.

head: AGENTS.md > Project model
text: - Every change goes through `pre-commit` and the full validation pipeline before a PR is opened.

head: AGENTS.md > Project model
text: - The PR description must follow the shape under "Creating PRs" below. The reviewer skims it before reading the diff, so short and specific beats complete.

head: AGENTS.md > Project model > When to create PRs
text: - **Task complete**: when a discrete set of related, validated changes is done — commit, push, and open a PR.

head: AGENTS.md > Project model > When to create PRs
text: - **Session end**: if there are uncommitted changes that pass validation, commit and open a PR before ending the session. Every session leaves a clean working tree or a ready-to-review PR.

head: AGENTS.md > Project model > When to create PRs
text: - **One concern per PR**: separate unrelated changes into their own PRs so each can be reviewed and merged independently.

head: AGENTS.md > Toolchain
text:
Every CLI this repo needs is pinned in `mise.toml` at the repo root — `talosctl`, `kubectl`, `flux`,
`talhelper`, `sops`, `helmfile`, `stern`, `yq`, `jq`, `just`, `fd`, `pre-commit`, plus `flate` and

head: AGENTS.md > Toolchain
text:
CI installs from the same `mise.toml` via `jdx/mise-action`, so local runs and the merge gate use
identical binaries. Do not install these tools by hand or with Homebrew — an unpinned copy on PATH
is exactly what made local validation diverge from CI before. `mise ls --current` shows what is
active.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs
text:
Use GitButler CLI (`but`) for all version control writes (commits, branches, pushes). Delegate VCS to the
gitbutler skill for command detail. Use GitHub MCP tools (`github_create_pull_request`,
`github_issue_write`, etc.) for all GitHub API operations. Never use `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`,
or `gh pr create` for write operations. Never force-push, never skip hooks.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Before committing
text: 1. Always run `pre-commit run --all-files` and fix any errors.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Before committing
text:
2. Run the full validation pipeline if Kubernetes manifests changed:
   - `just configure` → `just validate` → `just flate-test` → `python3 scripts/find_mistakes.py`

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Before committing
text: 3. Inspect the diff: `but diff` (selected dirty files/hunks), `but status` (commit/branch layout).

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Making commits
text: - Use `but commit -b <branch> -m "<msg>" <ids>` to create a branch and commit in one step.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Making commits
text: - Use file/hunk IDs from `but diff` — never stage blindly.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Making commits
text: - Write concise, imperative-mood commit messages matching the existing repo style.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs
text: 1. Push the branch with `but push <branch-name>`.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs
text: 2. Create the PR via MCP: `github_create_pull_request` with title, body (`head` branch, `base: "main"`, `owner: "axeII"`, `repo: "home-ops"`).

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs
text: 3. Write the body to the shape below.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs
text: 4. Present the PR URL to the human maintainer for review.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: Four headings, nothing else, whole body under 30 lines.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: - One line under a heading is the target. Use bullets only for genuinely separate items.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: - **What.** The resources or files that changed and the behaviour that changes with them. The reviewer has the diff, so do not restate it file by file.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: - **Why.** The problem this solves, in a sentence or two. Link the issue instead of retelling it.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: - **Risk.** Blast radius: namespaces touched, whether storage, networking or RBAC is involved, whether Flux restarts anything on reconcile. Konflate cautions go here. "None, docs only" is a complete answer.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: - **Validation.** Which steps ran and that they passed. Name the steps, do not paste their output. Paste output only for a failure you are shipping around on purpose.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: - Leave out session narrative, summary preambles, emoji headings, and tables of changed files.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: - Investigation notes, rejected alternatives, and long logs go in a PR comment or a linked issue, not in the body.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating PRs > PR body shape
text: - Run the `unslop` skill over the body before posting, if it is installed.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Review flow
text: - After pushing, check konflate for blast radius: `konflate_list_pull_requests` → `konflate_get_pr_summary(<number>)`.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Review flow
text: - Address any konflate cautions (data-loss, immutable-field, RBAC) before requesting review.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Review flow
text: - Wait for CI (flate, yayamlls) to pass.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Review flow
text: - Report the konflate summary and any cautions in the PR description so the human reviewer can assess risk.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Review flow
text: - **Never merge your own PRs.** The human maintainer reviews and merges approved PRs.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating issues
text: For bugs, tech debt, or tasks outside a PR workflow, create a GitHub issue. Use the `github` MCP server's structured tools for issue operations.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating issues

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating issues

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating issues
text: - Keep issues scoped to one concern. Reference related PRs/issues by number rather than summarizing them.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating issues > Issue body shape
text: Three headings, nothing else, whole body under 25 lines.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating issues > Issue body shape
text: - **What** is the observed problem, **Why** is what it costs or blocks, **What's needed** is the fix or the next step to find one.

head: AGENTS.md > Commits and PRs > Creating issues > Issue body shape
text: - Evidence gathered while investigating (logs, `kubectl` output, radar findings) goes in a follow-up comment, not the opening body. The body holds what a reader needs to decide whether to care.

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text: The `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yaml` workflow runs daily at 02:00 UTC and applies these rules:

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text:
| Category | Detection | Min age | Days | Konflate gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **patch / digest** | `type/patch`, `type/digest` | **2d** | any | no failures, no cautions |
| **minor** (release train) | `type/minor` | **3d** | **Fri–Sat** (Europe/Berlin) | no failures, no cautions |
| **major (ci/gh-action)** | `type/major` + `renovate/github-action` | **2d** | any | no failures (cautions allowed) |
| **major (other)** | `type/major`, not `renovate/github-action` | — | MANUAL | — |
| **critical infra** | `needs-review` label, or title/branch matches `ceph\|cilium\|flux\|dragonfly` | — | MANUAL | — |
| **area/talos** | `area/talos` label (`talos/**`) | — | MANUAL | — |

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text: - **Cluster quiet window:** Sun 00:00–05:00 UTC — no merges (Talos upgrade window).

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text: - **Sleep between merges:** 300 seconds to let Flux reconcile before the next merge.

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text: - Konflate re-render is triggered before each merge gate via `KONFLATE_PUSH_TOKEN`.

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text: - **Bulk merge** (`.github/workflows/bulk-merge-prs.yaml`) also excludes rook-ceph, `area/talos`, `type/major`, `type/minor`, and `hold`.

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text:
- **Defense in depth:** The `pr-classify` workflow applies `needs-review` and `risk/critical` labels to
  critical-infra PRs. Auto-merge hard-skips any PR with the `needs-review` label regardless of the
  title/branch regex — two independent detection layers must both fail for a critical upgrade to
  auto-merge.

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text:
- **Konflate** is reachable only from inside the home network (private IP). From GitHub Actions, the
  konflate gate is skipped — the auto-merge relies on label/age/day rules alone. `Konflate` as a
  required status check in branch protection won't work from outside the network.

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text: - **Konflate write-back** posts a summary PR comment + commit status after each render when reachable (inside the network).

head: AGENTS.md > Auto-merge policy
text: - **Setup:** add `KONFLATE_PUSH_TOKEN` (random 32-byte hex) to 1Password `konflate` item and as a GitHub Actions secret; confirm the GitHub App has `checks: write` + `pull-requests: write` permissions.

text:
| # | Rule name | Priority | Expression | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Block threats | 0 | `(cf.threat_score gt 40)` | Block |
| 2 | Allow github webhooks | 20 | `(http.request.uri.path contains "/hook") and (ip.src in {192.30.252.0/22, 185.199.108.0/22, 140.82.112.0/20, 143.55.64.0/20})` | Skip |
| 3 | Block bots | 10 | `(cf.client.bot)` | Block |
| 4 | Allow kromgo and konflate | 45 | `((http.host wildcard "kromgo.juno.moe*") or (http.host eq "konflate.juno.moe")) and (ip.geoip.country eq "US")` | Skip |
| 5 | Allow only home country | 5 | `(ip.geoip.country ne "CZ")` | Block |

head: AGENTS.md > Cloudflare WAF rules

head: AGENTS.md > Cloudflare WAF rules

head: AGENTS.md > Claude Code agents, skills, and commands > Agents (`.claude/agents/`)

head: AGENTS.md > Claude Code agents, skills, and commands > Agents (`.claude/agents/`)
text:
Delegate to these rather than doing cluster or log investigation inline: their output stays out of
the main context window.

head: AGENTS.md > Claude Code agents, skills, and commands > Agents (`.claude/agents/`)
text:
Two behaviours worth knowing, both observed directly rather than inferred (Claude Code
2.1.236, 2026-08-30 — re-check before relying on either if your build is much newer):

head: AGENTS.md > Claude Code agents, skills, and commands > Agents (`.claude/agents/`)
text:
- **Editing an agent file does not take effect until Claude Code restarts.** A `.claude/agents/*.md`
  edited mid-session keeps running with the definition loaded at startup — the agent will answer
  from its old instructions and give no indication they are stale. Restart before testing a change.

head: AGENTS.md > Claude Code agents, skills, and commands > Agents (`.claude/agents/`)
text:
- **Declared built-in tools can be silently dropped.** `cluster-radar` declares `Grep` and `Glob`

  (`grep -rn …`) so nothing breaks, but do not assume a declared built-in is present. MCP tools
  were unaffected.

text: Copilot CLI works in this repo too, sharing the same instructions and an equivalent set of agents.

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > What is shared automatically
text:
Copilot CLI discovers `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the repository root on its own, and supports
the same `@relative/path` include syntax, so `CLAUDE.md` → `@AGENTS.md` resolves there exactly as
it does in Claude Code. **This file is the single source of truth for both tools** — no
`.github/copilot-instructions.md` is needed, and adding one would only duplicate this.

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
The same three agents as `.claude/agents/`, in Copilot's schema — `cluster-radar`, `grafana-logs`,
and `ship`, with the same read-only and no-merge boundaries. Invoke one with:

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
Repository agents live in `.github/agents/`; user-level ones in `~/.copilot/agents/`, and a
user-level agent of the same name wins.

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text: **`.github/agents/*.agent.md` is generated — do not edit it.**

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
Copilot CLI *does* read `.claude/agents/*.md`, so symlinking the two directories — the usual advice
for sharing AI config — looks like it works. It does not, and it fails silently. Verified against
CLI v1.0.82:

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
| Agent file | `tools:` entry | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.claude/agents/probe.md` | `mcp__github__get_me` | **silently dropped**; agent had built-ins only |
| `.github/agents/probe.agent.md` | `github/get_me` | granted and invoked successfully |

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
This is deliberate on GitHub's part — the docs state that "all unrecognized tool names are ignored,
which allows product-specific tools to be specified in an agent profile without causing problems."
That tolerance is what makes sharing *instruction* files across tools work so well, and it is
exactly what makes sharing *agent* files dangerous: `cluster-radar` symlinked into Copilot would
load cleanly, report no error, and have zero radar tools.

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text: Two facts worth keeping in mind:

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
- `.github/agents/` **wins** over `.claude/agents/` on a name conflict, so the generated files are
  the ones in effect. Deleting them does not fall back gracefully — it silently strips every MCP
  tool from all three agents.

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
- Copilot ignores `model:` with a warning (`specifies model "inherit" which is not available`), so
  model selection cannot be shared either.

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
The bodies are identical, so `.claude/agents/` is the single source and the Copilot copies are
generated from it:

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > Agents (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
text:
The `sync-agents` pre-commit hook fails on any drift in either direction — an edit to a source
that was not regenerated, or a hand-edit to a generated file. If an agent gains a tool with no
Copilot equivalent, the script exits with the tool name rather than silently dropping it; add the
mapping to `BUILTINS` in the script.

head: AGENTS.md > GitHub Copilot CLI > MCP servers for Copilot
text:
Copilot CLI reads `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` — it does **not** auto-load a repo-level
`.github/mcp.json` (that path applies to other Copilot surfaces). `github-mcp-server` is built in,
so only `radar` and `grafana` need configuring, and both live in the user config because of the
Grafana token.

text:
`.github/mcp.json` is kept as the committed, secret-free definition of the radar server. Apply it
explicitly with:

layer in DeepAgentLabs. It helps teams understand what ran, what the model and
agent did, what context and tools were involved, what it cost, and whether the
system performed well over time.

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text:
Two phases, split by the merge to `main` — bumping happens before, and the
tag-driven release automation happens after.

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text:
**1. Pre-release (on the feature branch, before merge):** Bump version in
`pyproject.toml`, `src/agenticlens/__init__.py`, and `CHANGELOG.md` (a
dated release section under `[Unreleased]`). Commit as part of the
branch's normal history; goes in with the rest of the PR.

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text:
**2. Release (on `main`, once that branch has merged):** plain `git`, no
manual `gh release` step required.

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text: 1. Pull the merge commit on `main`.

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text:
2. Tag: create an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag pointing at the merge commit,
   using the `CHANGELOG.md` release section for that version as the tag
   message:
   `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -F <file-with-that-section> --cleanup=verbatim`.
   `--cleanup=verbatim` is required — git's default cleanup silently strips
   lines starting with `#`, which would eat the changelog's `###` headers.

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text: 3. Push the tag: `git push origin vX.Y.Z`.

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text:
That tag push is the release trigger. `release-pypi.yml` runs automatically
and does both of the following from the same tag:

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text: - publishes the package to PyPI using `PYPI_API_TOKEN`

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text: - creates the GitHub Release object for `vX.Y.Z`

head: AgenticLens Development Reference > Release
text:
The GitHub Release title is the tag name, and its body is copied from the
matching `CHANGELOG.md` section so the changelog, tag, PyPI release, and
GitHub Releases page stay aligned. (`release-testpypi.yml` is a separate,
manual `workflow_dispatch` staging flow — unaffected.)

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Engineering Rules

text: - Update documentation when behavior, workflow, architecture, or AI guidance changes.

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Engineering Rules
text: - Do not declare named functions inside other functions in Dart or Rust. Use private file-level helpers, private methods, or small private widgets/classes instead.

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Engineering Rules

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Engineering Rules

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Net Impact Discipline
text: - Before a non-trivial code change, evaluate the tradeoff: expected benefit, negative impact, complexity cost, regression risk, and simpler alternatives.

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Net Impact Discipline

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Net Impact Discipline

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Net Impact Discipline

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Net Impact Discipline

head: Genesix AI Agent Guidelines > Workflow > Validation Matrix
text:
| Change Surface | Must Inspect | Must Run | Should Run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dart/Flutter UI, state, repository, routing without generated output impact | Affected files and package versions if external APIs are involved; for Forui API questions, refreshed local Forui docs when network is available | `dart analyze` | `dart format .` |
| Localization ARB changes | Every `lib/l10n/*.arb` file for key parity and generated localization output impact | `flutter gen-l10n`, `dart analyze` | A focused key-parity check across all ARB files |
| Riverpod generators, Freezed models, JSON/build_runner annotations | Affected annotations, generated output impact, package versions | `dart run build_runner build -d`, `dart analyze` | `dart format .` |
| Rust changes without FFI signature impact | Affected modules and crate dependencies if relevant | `cd rust && cargo check` | `cd rust && cargo fmt` |
| Rust FFI signature or bridge contract changes | Rust API surface, generated bridge impact, Dart call sites | `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate`, `dart run build_runner build -d`, `cd rust && cargo check`, `dart analyze` | `cd rust && cargo fmt`, `dart format .` |
| Dependency version changes | Manifests, impacted docs, affected call sites; for Forui changes, run `dart run tool/sync_forui_docs.dart` and keep `.agents/references/forui/**` uncommitted | Relevant analyze/check/build command for impacted area | Formatting commands |
| Security-sensitive wallet changes | Trust boundaries, sensitive-data handling, lifecycle ordering, storage/signing/FFI/XSWD/logging impact | Relevant analyze/check/build command for impacted area, plus `wallet-security-review` | Focused tests or security review subagent when risk justifies it |
| AI guideline/docs-only changes | Instruction entrypoints and links | Markdown/readability review and stale-reference search | No Dart/Rust checks unless code changed |
