head: Agent Instructions
text:
Madolt is a magit-like Emacs interface for the Dolt version-controlled
database.  The **MVP is complete** -- all 9 source files and 9 test files
are implemented with 185 passing tests (~4,685 LOC total).

head: Agent Instructions
text:
See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for project overview, build/test
instructions, interactive QA testing guide, and technical notes.

head: Agent Instructions > Build & Test
text:
**During development, `make clean && make compile` is overkill** when
you've only changed a single file.  Instead, load the source `.el`
file directly into the running Emacs via `emacsclient --eval
'(load-file "path/to/file.el")'`.  This is much faster for iterating.
Save `make clean && make compile` for when you need to run tests
(which use compiled `.elc` files) or before committing.

head: Agent Instructions > Build & Test
text:
**`make test` is slow** (~8 minutes).  **NEVER run it in the foreground
or with a synchronous tool call** — it WILL time out or block.  Always
use a PTY session (`pty_spawn`) or pipe through tee in the background:
`make test 2>&1 | tee tmp/tests.log &` then check the log afterwards.
For targeted changes, prefer running individual module tests (e.g.
`make test-dolt`, `make test-log`, `make test-status`) which are much
faster.

head: Agent Instructions > Build & Test
text:
**Never block waiting for test suites to finish.**  Launch tests in a
PTY session with `notifyOnExit`, then **immediately** do interactive
QA testing via tmux while tests run in the background.  This
parallelizes the two required verification steps and avoids wasted
idle time.

head: Agent Instructions > Build & Test
text:
The Makefile assumes `straight.el` packages under `~/.emacs.d/straight/build/`.
Override with `STRAIGHT_DIR=/path/to/packages`.

head: Agent Instructions > Build & Test
text:
**Pre-existing test failures are NEVER acceptable to ignore.** If
failures are unrelated to ongoing work, create a bead to track them
(if not already tracked) and fix them at medium-high priority.  Never
dismiss failures as "pre-existing" without filing an issue.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux
text:
**Both automated AND interactive testing are required** when working on
UI changes. Run unit tests first (`make test`), then **ALWAYS** verify
interactively via tmux before considering the work complete. This is
**MANDATORY** — never skip interactive testing for any change that
affects buffer display, process output, keybindings, or user-facing
messages.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux
text: Use a **dedicated tmux session called `madolt-test`** for interactive testing. This session runs Emacs with madolt loaded in a controlled environment that can be inspected programmatically via `emacsclient`.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux
text: **CRITICAL RULES for tmux session management:**

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux
text: - **NEVER kill existing tmux sessions or windows.** Take great care to preserve any running sessions.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux
text: - **Session name is always `madolt-test`** -- do not use other names, and do not reuse session names belonging to other tools.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux
text: - **Do NOT use `tmux kill-session`, `tmux kill-window`, or `tmux kill-pane`** unless you are absolutely certain the target is a stale `madolt-test` session with no running process.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Setting up the test repo
text: Create a temporary dolt repo for interactive testing:

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Running Emacs in tmux
text:
**CRITICAL: Use a dedicated server name** to avoid conflicts with any
pre-existing Emacs server. NEVER kill an Emacs server you didn't start —
it may have unsaved work, open buffers, or running processes.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Inspecting state with emacsclient
text: **Always use `-s madolt`** to connect to the dedicated server:

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Inspecting state with emacsclient
text: Once Emacs is running with `server-start`, use `emacsclient --eval` to inspect and interact programmatically:

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Sending keys via tmux
text: For testing keybindings rather than Elisp functions, send keys directly:

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Important tmux notes
text: - **Window size**: tmux resizes to match the connecting client terminal, so `-x 120 -y 40` at creation doesn't persist. Use `tmux resize-window` to force a specific size.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Important tmux notes
text: - **Prefer emacsclient**: For inspecting buffer contents and evaluating Elisp, `emacsclient --eval` is far more reliable than capturing tmux pane output. Use tmux `send-keys` only when testing actual keybindings.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Important tmux notes
text:
- **Never use emacsclient to switch buffers or frames** when testing
  interactively via tmux.  `emacsclient --eval` runs in whatever
  frame/window Emacs happens to select, which may NOT be the one
  visible in the tmux pane.  Use `tmux send-keys` for all navigation
  (buffer switching, quitting, etc.) during interactive testing.
  Reserve `emacsclient` for read-only inspection (checking variable
  values, buffer contents) where the target buffer is specified
  explicitly via `with-current-buffer`.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Important tmux notes
text: - **Graceful shutdown**: Send `C-x C-c` to quit Emacs, or use `emacsclient --eval '(kill-emacs)'`. Never kill sessions/windows/panes violently.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Important tmux notes
text: - **PTY sessions**: Alternatively, use `pty_spawn` to run Emacs in a managed PTY session for automated testing within the agent environment. But this is far less preferable because it cannot easily be observed by the user during testing, so ask permission before using this fallback.

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Typical QA workflow
text: 1. Compile with `make clean && make compile`

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Typical QA workflow
text: 2. Set up or verify the test repo state in `tmp/test-dolt/`

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Typical QA workflow
text: 3. Launch Emacs in the `madolt-test` tmux session (or restart if already running)

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Typical QA workflow
text: 4. Use `emacsclient --eval` to inspect buffer contents and verify behavior

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Typical QA workflow
text: 5. Send keys via tmux to test keybindings

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Typical QA workflow
text: 6. Check for correct section rendering, staging/unstaging, diffs

head: Agent Instructions > Interactive QA Testing via tmux > Typical QA workflow
text: 7. When done: `emacsclient --eval '(kill-emacs)'` (leave the tmux session intact for next time)

head: Agent Instructions > Design Principles
text:
- **Copy magit wherever possible** -- keybindings, faces, buffer names,
  transient layouts, section types, and UX patterns should match magit's
  conventions unless Dolt requires a different approach.  When in doubt,
  check how magit does it and follow that design.

head: Agent Instructions > Design Principles
text:
- **Two-tier error reporting for SQL connections** -- user-facing
  messages should be concise and actionable (e.g. "SQL connection
  failed; using CLI").  Detailed diagnostics (stack traces, query
  text, connection parameters) go to the hidden ` *madolt-sql-log*`
  buffer.  Use `madolt-connection--log` for this: its first argument
  is the user message (shown in minibuffer), its optional second
  argument is the detail (logged only).  Never use `display-warning`
  for SQL connection issues.
  More broadly, errors from **background data collection** (status
  refresh, log refresh, refs refresh) should use this hidden log
  buffer — the user didn't explicitly ask for those commands, so
  noisy warnings are disruptive.  In contrast, errors from
  **user-initiated actions** (staging, unstaging, committing, merging,
  etc.) should appear in the process buffer (`$` to view) since the
  user explicitly triggered them and needs to see the outcome.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text:
- **Dual backend: CLI + SQL** -- madolt defaults to CLI (`dolt`
  subprocess) but supports opt-in SQL server routing via
  `madolt-use-sql-server`.  When enabled, queries are routed through
  a persistent MySQL-protocol connection to `dolt sql-server` for
  near-zero latency.  Falls back to CLI transparently on failure.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text:
- **SQL queries should never hang** -- if a SQL query to
  `dolt sql-server` appears to hang, the problem is almost certainly
  in how the query or connection is being used, NOT in the server
  being slow.  Common causes: `SET` commands produce no output in
  mysql batch mode (combine with a `SELECT` to get detectable
  output); stale data in `pending-output` from a prior query;
  `madolt-connection--output-complete-p` waiting for output that
  will never arrive.  Never increase timeouts as a workaround for
  hangs — find and fix the root cause.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text:
- **Dolt v1.82.x does NOT support `$EDITOR`-based commit messages.**
  All commits use `-m` flag via minibuffer input.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text:
- **Dolt does NOT support detached HEAD.** `dolt checkout <hash>`
  fails with "dolt does not support a detached head state".

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text: - **Dolt stages whole tables**, not hunks. No partial staging.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text:
- **`dolt commit --all`** only stages modified/deleted tables, NOT
  untracked. Use `--ALL` for that.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text:
- **Stale .elc files cause insidious test failures** -- always
  `make clean` before `make compile`.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text:
- **`magit-insert-section` with `(eval type)` needs DOUBLE parens:
  `((eval type))`**.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes
text:
- **`define-derived-mode` replaces the keymap variable** -- bindings
  must be added AFTER the mode definition using `keymap-set`.

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes > CLI-only operations (no SQL equivalent)
text:
These commands must always use the CLI backend, even when
`madolt-use-sql-server' is enabled:

head: Agent Instructions > Technical Notes > CLI-only operations (no SQL equivalent)
text:
| Operation | Why CLI-only |
|-----------|-------------|
| `dolt blame` | No SQL equivalent. Could theoretically use `dolt_history_<table>` but complex and low priority. |
| `dolt diff` (raw tabular mode) | Formatted `\| +\| <\| >\|` output is CLI-specific rendering. |
| `dolt diff -r json` | JSON diff output has no direct SQL equivalent; `dolt_diff_<table>` system tables have a different schema. |
| `dolt log --graph` | Graph rendering is CLI-specific; no SQL equivalent. |
| `dolt stash` | `DOLT_STASH()` exists but requires subcommand args; behavior differs from CLI. |

head: Overview
text: - This is a collection of RSS 2.0 feeds for AI news and blog sites which don't provide RSS feeds themselves.

head: Overview
text:
- Tech stack:
    - `uv` for project management - use it to manage packages and run commands in the project.
    - `scrapy` to scrape the sites.
    - `feedgen` to generate RSS feeds.
    - `dateparser` to parse dates.

head: Overview
text: - Document the feeds in a table in the README, giving the name (e.g. Anthropic News) and filename (e.g. `feeds/anthropic-news.xml`). Keep it sorted by name, except AI RSS Feeds News which stays at the top.

head: Overview
text: - The README should also document any commands `uv run ...` to generate feeds and instructions for adding new feeds.

head: Overview
text: - Refer to the README as well as this AGENTS file when you perform a task.

head: Overview > Scraping with scrapy
text: - Enable HTTP caching unconditionally. I will delete the cache now and then to keep things fresh.

head: Overview > Scraping with scrapy
text: - Use a single configurable spider class, with per-feed configuration in `feeds.toml`.

head: Overview > Scraping with scrapy
text:
- Each feed entry in TOML should define:
  - required fields like `feed_title`, `source_url`, `item_container_selector`, `item_title_selector`, and `item_link_selector`,
  - optional fields like `feed_link`, `feed_description`, and `language`,
  - fields like `item_container_selector` (CSS selector for the container for each item)
  - fields like `item_title_selector`, `item_link_selector` (CSS selectors for the title or link for a specific item, scoped to the container for the item, these can be scrapy's extended selectors with the suffixes like `::text` and `::attr(href)`)
  - other supported fields like `item_date_selector`, `item_description_selector`, `item_guid_is_permalink`, `min_item_count`, and `min_item_ratio_vs_previous`.

head: Overview > Scraping with scrapy
text: - These mostly default to `None` and if left as `None` then the corresponding field in the feed or item is not set.

head: Overview > Scraping with scrapy
text: - Be lenient in what selectors can return. For example `item_link_selector` can return either text (the URL) or an HTML node (in which case its `href` attr is taken).

head: Overview > Scraping with scrapy
text: - Don't follow any links (to articles or to later pages of links), just use the information on the source page.

head: Overview > Scraping with scrapy
text: - For pages backed by embedded JSON, use `format = "json"` instead of CSS selectors. This applies `item_container_selector` (a jq query) independently to every JSON blob found on the page — Next.js `__NEXT_DATA__`, Next.js Flight stream records, and JSON-LD `<script type="application/ld+json">` blocks — and unions the matches. Items are deduped by resolved link, keeping whichever record has the later date; when two sources report the same item with an equal date, whichever was scanned first wins, so put the richer source (e.g. JSON-LD, which often has descriptions) first if that matters. `item_title_selector` etc. are jq queries scoped to each item; use `//` to fall back across differently-shaped sources (e.g. `.title // .headline`, `.href // .url`, `.date // .datePublished`).

head: Overview > Taking snapshots
text: - Don't repeatedly curl a page when developing feeds - put a copy into `./snapshots` and refer to that.

head: Overview > Taking snapshots
text: - To refresh/create a snapshot directly, use e.g. `curl -f https://www.anthropic.com/news -o snapshots/anthropic-news.html`.

head: Overview > Taking snapshots
text: - If a new feed can't be scraped with the existing setup, suggest how to proceed and we can discuss before implementing new scraping methods.

head: Overview > Taking snapshots
text: - If the feed is backed by embedded JSON (Next.js `__NEXT_DATA__`/Flight data and/or JSON-LD), extract it like `uv run python extract_json.py snapshots/cohere-blog.html >snapshots/cohere-blog.json`. This uses the same blob-discovery logic as the spider (`iter_json_blobs` in `src/spiders/feed.py`), so it finds everything the `format = "json"` pipeline would.

head: Overview > Taking snapshots
text: - You can find where items are in an extracted JSON dump like `uv run python json_grep.py snapshots/cohere-blog.json "Part of the title"` if the user gives example titles (ask for some).

head: Overview > Feed generation
text: - Each site will correspond to one feed, e.g. the Anthropic News site will become a `anthropic-news.xml` feed.

head: Overview > Feed generation
text: - Generated using `uv run python generate_feeds.py`.

head: Overview > Feed generation
text: - Feeds are put into `./feeds`.

head: Overview > Feed generation
text: - Look at existing feeds (`feeds.toml`) for consistency.

head: Overview > Feed generation
text: - Use selectors that are likely to be stable over time.

head: Overview > Feed generation
text: - When you add a new feed, run `uv run python generate_opml.py` to regenerate the OPML list.

head: Overview > Feed generation
text: - Also add new feeds to the News section of the readme.

head: Overview > Broken feeds
text: - If a feed stops working, it can be marked `broken = true` in `feeds.toml`. This will stop a known problem from failing the whole run, and will flag when it starts working again.

head: Overview > Broken feeds
text:
- To fix a feed:
  - Grab a new snapshot (as above).
  - If it uses embedded JSON, extract the data (as above).
  - Read the existing feed in `feeds.toml`.
  - Compare it to the new snapshots and fix the feed.
  - Remove `broken = true`.

head: Overview > Broken feeds
text: - News pages sometimes have featured articles shown differently from the main list, ensure you get them all. It can help if the user supplies the titles for a selection of articles (featured and not), so you can find them more easily in the HTML.

head: Overview > Broken feeds
text: - Update the News section of the readme if a feed is marked broken or is fixed. If it's fixed the same day then skip.

head: Overview > News
text: - Keep the News section of the README and the hand-maintained `feeds/ai-rss-feeds-news.xml` feed in sync: every news line in the README gets a matching item in the feed, newest first. See "Maintain The News Feed" in the README for the item format.

head: Overview > News
text: - News covers user-visible changes to the collection: feeds added, removed, deprecated, renamed, broken or fixed (skip broken-then-fixed on the same day).

head: Overview > News
text: - Item titles are short: name the feed(s) if only one or two are affected, otherwise summarise (e.g. "Three feeds broken"). Put the detail in the description.

head: Overview > News
text: - `ai-rss-feeds-news.xml` is not in `feeds.toml` and isn't generated; `generate_opml.py` adds it to the top of the OPML.

head: Overview > Regeneration
text: - There is a github workflow (`.github/workflows/generate-feeds.yml`) that runs every 3 hours.

head: Overview > Regeneration
text: - Can also trigger it manually.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Rule zero: prove it works before opening the PR
text:
**Your job is to deliver code that is proven to work.** If you
have not proven the change works, it is not time to open the PR
yet. "It compiles", "type checks pass", and "the diff looks
right" are not proof. Proof is: the relevant tests run locally
and pass, the new behaviour is exercised by a test you added or
extended, and any user-visible path you touched has been
executed end-to-end. If you cannot run the suite in your
environment, say so explicitly in the PR body rather than
implying coverage you did not actually achieve. Opening a PR
that turns out not to work wastes the reviewer's time and is
the single fastest way to lose trust on this repo.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Rule zero: prove it works before opening the PR
text:
The rest of this document covers how to dress up that proven
change for review. None of it matters if rule zero is not met.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > What this project is
text:
`frozenlist` provides `FrozenList`, a list-like
`collections.abc.MutableSequence` that becomes immutable (and
hashable) once `freeze()` is called. It is a small, widely
deployed dependency of `aiohttp` and the rest of the
`aio-libs` stack, so it is performance sensitive. The
pure-Python implementation lives in `frozenlist/__init__.py`
and the Cythonized fast path lives in
`frozenlist/_frozenlist.pyx`; the package picks the compiled
class when the extension is importable and falls back to the
pure-Python `PyFrozenList` otherwise (or when the
`FROZENLIST_NO_EXTENSIONS` environment variable is set).

head: Notes for LLM contributors > What this project is
text:
| Path                          | What                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `frozenlist/__init__.py`      | pure-Python `FrozenList`, public API, extension loader |
| `frozenlist/__init__.pyi`     | type stubs for the public API                          |
| `frozenlist/_frozenlist.pyx`  | Cython `FrozenList` (hot path; ships in wheels)        |
| `tests/test_frozenlist.py`    | pytest suite (covers both implementations)             |
| `CHANGES/`                    | towncrier news fragments, one per PR                   |
| `docs/`                       | Sphinx docs source                                     |
| `packaging/pep517_backend/`   | in-tree PEP 517 backend that drives `cythonize`        |

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 3. Open the PR as a draft, and leave it that way
text:
Use `gh pr create --draft`. **Every LLM-authored submission
must be fully reviewed by a human before it is marked ready
out of draft, with no exceptions.** That review is the
responsibility of the person running the agent, not of the
project maintainers; do not shift the burden of reviewing LLM
work onto them. Maintainers do not look at drafts, so the
draft state is the agent's hand-off to the operator's review,
not a request for the project to review the code on the
operator's behalf. Do not mark the PR ready yourself, and do
not request reviewers from the agent session; the human who
reviewed the change and flipped it out of draft is the one who
routes it.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 4. Disclose the agent, do not advertise it
text:
Disclosure is required, advertising is not welcome. Put one
plain line at the bottom of the PR body naming the agent that
drafted the change, for example:

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 4. Disclose the agent, do not advertise it
text: That single line is enough. Beyond that:

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 4. Disclose the agent, do not advertise it
text:
- **No `Co-Authored-By:` trailers** for an LLM or any AI tool,
  in commits or in the PR body. Attribution goes to the human
  who reviewed the change.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 4. Disclose the agent, do not advertise it
text:
- **Agent output goes in a footer below the PR summary,
  ideally in a collapsed `<details>` block.** The aio-libs
  template sections (What / Are there changes in behavior /
  etc.) come first and read like a human wrote them. Anything
  the agent wants to surface for reviewers (scan results, test
  logs, branch hygiene notes, pipeline output) goes
  underneath that. A collapsed `<details>` block at the very
  bottom is the recommended shape; it keeps the summary
  readable while still letting a curious reviewer expand the
  agent's work:
  ```markdown
  <details>
  <summary>Agent run details (optional, for reviewers)</summary>

  Tests: <command and result>
  Lint: <command and result>
  </details>
  ```
  What is not OK is mixing this content into the template
  sections themselves, or pushing it above the human-readable
  summary so reviewers have to scroll past it. The shape and
  content of the footer is otherwise up to the agent.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 4. Disclose the agent, do not advertise it
text:
- No `🤖`, `✨`, `🚀` emoji decoration in commit messages, PR
  titles, PR bodies, or news fragments. Project style is
  plain prose.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 4. Disclose the agent, do not advertise it
text:
- Commit messages and PR prose should read as if a human
  contributor wrote them. Specifically:
  - **No em-dashes (`—`)** and no dashes used as sentence
    separators (`foo - bar`). Use a semicolon or a comma.
    This is the strongest tell for AI-generated prose in this
    project, and reviewers do read for it.
  - No "Let me", "I'll", or first-person narration of what
    the agent did. Describe the change, not the author.
  - No filler sections ("Overview", "Summary of changes",
    "Key takeaways") on top of the template. The template
    already has the right sections.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 5. Keep the PR body short
text:
A couple of sentences per template section is plenty. If the
change is non-obvious, a short reproducer or a paragraph on
root cause is welcome. Long, multi-section essays with bolded
sub-headings are not the style here.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 6. Commit hygiene
text:
- One logical change per PR. If a refactor and a bugfix are
  bundled together, split them.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 6. Commit hygiene
text:
- Pre-commit auto-fixes (`black`, `isort`, `yesqa`,
  trailing-whitespace, end-of-file-fixer, and friends) run on
  commit and rewrite files in place; when a hook rewrites a
  file the commit aborts, so re-stage and commit again. See
  [`.pre-commit-config.yaml`](.pre-commit-config.yaml) for
  the full list.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Pull request rules > 6. Commit hygiene
text:
- The repo does **not** use Conventional Commits as a CI
  gate. Match the existing landed subjects (short imperative
  or descriptive prose, optionally prefixed with `Build(deps):`
  for dependabot-style dependency bumps); do not force
  `feat:` / `fix:` prefixes onto every commit.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests
text:
Install dev deps, build the Cython extension in place, and run
the suite:

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests
text:
Other useful Makefile targets: `make vtest` is verbose,
`make cov` runs the tox-driven coverage matrix, `make cov-dev`
produces an HTML coverage report under `htmlcov/`, and
`make lint` runs `pre-commit` across the tree.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests
text:
To exercise the pure-Python `FrozenList` instead of the
Cython one, set `FROZENLIST_NO_EXTENSIONS=1` before invoking
pytest. The `tests/conftest.py` fixture already parametrises
most tests across both implementations, but new tests that
target behaviour shared by both should follow the same
pattern rather than hard-coding `from frozenlist import
FrozenList`.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests
text:
CI runs the full matrix across the supported Python versions
plus a wheel build via `cibuildwheel`. The minimum supported
Python is declared in `pyproject.toml`
(`requires-python = ">=3.10"`); do not use syntax or stdlib
features that postdate it.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests > Every line in a test must be covered
text:
The coverage gate applies to test code too, not just
`frozenlist/`. A test that contains a branch or statement the
suite never reaches will fail CI. This catches a class of
mistake agents make all the time: defensive `raise` inside a
monkeypatched stub, a cleanup branch behind
`if had_own_getstate:` that the happy path never enters, an
`else` arm guarding a condition that is always true under the
fixture. From the perspective of a unit suite all of those
lines are dead code, and the coverage report flags them the
same as dead code in `frozenlist/`.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests > Every line in a test must be covered
text: Design tests so every line runs:

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests > Every line in a test must be covered
text:
- Drive the fixture deterministically so both arms of any
  conditional are hit, or drop the conditional entirely and
  assert the single shape you actually set up.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests > Every line in a test must be covered
text:
- Do not add `raise TypeError("must not be invoked")` guards
  inside stubs the test installs; if the stub is never meant to
  fire, either omit it or assert at the call site that it did
  not. An unreachable `raise` is the most common form of this
  failure.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests > Every line in a test must be covered
text:
- Cleanup branches that only run when setup took a particular
  shape (`if had_own_getstate: ...` style restores) need a
  second test, or a parametrize, that exercises the other shape.
  If you cannot justify the second case, unconditionally restore
  instead.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests > Every line in a test must be covered
text:
- Prefer `monkeypatch` (which auto-reverts) over hand-rolled
  save/restore blocks; the auto-revert path has no untaken
  branch for coverage to flag.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Tests > Every line in a test must be covered
text:
See [aio-libs/yarl#1687](https://github.com/aio-libs/yarl/pull/1687)
for the canonical example: the test added an unreachable `raise`
inside a patched `__getstate__` and a conditional restore of the
original attribute, both of which CI rejected as uncovered.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Cython extension
text:
`frozenlist/_frozenlist.pyx` is the compiled implementation
and `frozenlist/__init__.py` carries the pure-Python
equivalent. They must stay behaviourally identical: any
change to one must land in the other in the same PR, and the
test suite exercises both paths (directly via the public
`FrozenList` import and via `PyFrozenList`). The Cython
module is marked `freethreading_compatible = True` and uses
an atomic `_frozen` flag; if you touch the freeze semantics,
keep both implementations in lockstep and update the tests
accordingly.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Cython extension
text:
Generated files (`frozenlist/_frozenlist.c`,
`frozenlist/_frozenlist.html`, the built `*.so`) are build
outputs; do not commit them. `make cythonize` regenerates the
`.c` sibling of the `.pyx` source during development; the
in-tree PEP 517 backend under `packaging/pep517_backend/`
handles the same step during a wheel build.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Documentation
text:
User-visible API changes need a docs update under `docs/`
(typically `docs/index.rst`, plus any narrative pages). The
docstring goes in the code; the prose context goes in the
Sphinx sources. `make doc` builds the docs locally;
`make doc-spelling` runs the spellcheck (extend
`docs/spelling_wordlist.txt` for legitimate new terms rather
than disabling the check).

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not open a PR for code you have not proven works (see
  _Rule zero_ at the top of this file). Run the relevant
  tests, cover the new behaviour with a test, exercise the
  user-visible path end-to-end, and say so honestly in the PR
  body if any of that was not possible in your environment.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not invent a `## What / ## Why / ## How / ## Testing` PR
  body; use the aio-libs template above.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not skip the `CHANGES/` fragment "because the change is
  small". Even a one-line bugfix needs one.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not add `Co-Authored-By` trailers for LLM tools, in
  either commits or the PR body.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not mix agent-generated scan output, test summaries, or
  pipeline reports into the template sections. Put them in a
  collapsed `<details>` footer below the PR summary instead.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not use em-dashes or sentence-separating dashes in PR
  prose or commit messages.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not commit Cython build artefacts
  (`frozenlist/_frozenlist.c`,
  `frozenlist/_frozenlist.html`, `*.so`) alongside source
  changes.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not leave unreachable lines in tests (defensive `raise`
  inside a stub the suite never invokes, cleanup branches that
  only run for a setup shape the test does not exercise). The
  coverage gate applies to test code; see _Every line in a test
  must be covered_ above.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not change one of the two `FrozenList` implementations
  (Cython or pure-Python) without making the matching change
  in the other and extending the tests so both paths are
  covered.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not mark the PR ready for review yourself; that is the
  call of the human running the agent, not the agent itself.
  Maintainers do not look at drafts, but that does not mean
  they should be doing your review; the operator is
  responsible for reviewing the LLM-authored change before
  flipping the PR out of draft.

head: Notes for LLM contributors > Things not to do
text:
- Do not request reviewers from the agent session; the human
  who flips the PR out of draft will route it.

head: Working in this repo
text:
Flux-managed k3s homelab. `k8s/bootstrap/` creates the umbrella Flux resources,
`k8s/platform/` contains infrastructure, and `k8s/apps/` contains workloads.
**Two directories per app, split by who owns them.** `k8s/namespaces/<app>/` is
platform-owned and holds what has to exist before the app can reconcile — the
`Namespace`, the `sync.yaml` that is its Kustomization, and a
`ClusterRoleBinding` where the app needs one. The `GitRepository` that
Kustomization reads and the `flux-reconciler` identity it applies as are not
files: Kyverno generates both from the Namespace's `flux.rbac.thaum.xyz/role`
label, through `generate-flux-reconciler`. `k8s/apps/<app>/` is what `sync.yaml`
reconciles, and is the tenant's. That directory line is the review boundary.

head: Working in this repo
text:
A platform component works the same way one level up: it is a directory listed
in `k8s/platform/<domain>/kustomization.yaml`, reconciled by the
`platform-<domain>` Kustomization declared in `k8s/bootstrap/` and living in the
`platform-<domain>` namespace.

head: Working in this repo
text:
**Which namespace a Kustomization object declares is what decides how much it may
do**, because kustomize-controller resolves `--default-service-account` in the
object's own namespace. One in its app's namespace is confined there; one in a
namespace whose `flux-reconciler` also holds a `ClusterRoleBinding` is not. Every
app Kustomization now lives in its own namespace — `k8s/flux/`, the `apps` and
`platform` umbrellas and the `flux-system` namespace itself are all gone.

head: Working in this repo
text:
**Nothing cluster-scoped may live under `k8s/apps/<app>/`** — that directory is
reconciled by the confined identity, so a `Namespace` or `PersistentVolume` there
fails to apply. Either put it in `k8s/namespaces/<app>/`, which the cluster-admin
`namespaces` Kustomization applies, or give that namespace a
`clusterrolebinding.yaml` so its own reconciler may apply it.

head: Working in this repo
text:
Nine namespaces take the second route, and the distinction matters when reading
one: that binding widens the reconciler back to cluster-admin, so the namespace
is confined by nothing. `dlna-local`, `paperless`, `photos`, `plex` and `vod-arr`
because their `PersistentVolumes` belong with the app rather than with the
namespace; `datalake-logs`, `datalake-metrics`, `grafana` and `homer` because
their charts install a `ClusterRole`, `ClusterRoleBinding` or CRD, and no
RoleBinding can confer a cluster-scoped object at any width of role. Each object
states its own reason.

head: Working in this repo
text:
The cost of the confinement is cross-namespace `dependsOn`:
`--no-cross-namespace-refs=true` forbids an app Kustomization naming a
`platform-<domain>` one, so there is no ordering edge from apps to platform, nor
between the domains. On a rebuild an app fails until what it needs exists, and
retries.

head: Working in this repo
text:
Moving one needs the target Namespace to carry `flux.rbac.thaum.xyz/role` first,
so that its `GitRepository` and `flux-reconciler` exist, and the move itself is
a delete-and-create — so the
outgoing object must be suspended **and** set `prune: false` in an earlier
commit, or deleting it garbage-collects the app it just handed over.

head: Working in this repo
text:
Changing anything Flux applies: see the `app-deployment` skill in
`.claude/skills/`. It covers proving the render, the rollout order and the traps
that have bitten. Editing `docs/`: see the `docs-authoring` skill there — which
section a page belongs in, what must be generated rather than typed, and how to
lint before pushing.

head: Working in this repo > Validation
text:
`make validate` also fails on deprecated Flux API versions. Note both scripts read
**git-tracked** files, so a new manifest is invisible until staged.

head: Working in this repo > Validation
text: Kubeconfig: `~/.kube/clusters/ankhmorpork`.

head: Working in this repo > Helm chart values
text:
Values live in `values.yaml`, fed in via `configMapGenerator` and `valuesFrom` —
not inline in `spec.values`. Renovate's `helm-values` manager reads `values.yaml`
but cannot see inside a HelmRelease.

head: Working in this repo > Helm chart values
text:
The generator keeps a stable name and carries
`reconcile.fluxcd.io/watch: Enabled`, set through `generatorOptions.labels`.
helm-controller watches labelled ConfigMaps referenced in `valuesFrom`, so a
values-only edit upgrades the release on the write instead of on its next
interval. A generator no HelmRelease reads does not get the label.

head: Working in this repo > Scripts in `hack/`
text:
Bash by default: a script that runs tools in sequence and checks exit codes is a
bash script. Use Python when it needs a data structure that outlives one pipeline
— grouping, joining or cross-referencing across files — or when it parses
something with no good CLI. Prefer the standard library; `yq -o=json` into `json`
beats adding a dependency.

head: Working in this repo > Scripts in `hack/`
text:
Never embed one language in another. No Python heredocs in bash, no
`subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", ...])` in Python: pick the language that fits and
write the whole script in it. And no wrapper scripts — the Makefile calls the
real script directly.

head: Working in this repo > Manifest layout and naming
text:
Keep one Kubernetes object per manifest file. Group distinct components under
their own directories and use type-based names inside them, such as
`operator/repository.yaml`, `operator/release.yaml`, `operator/values.yaml`, and
`gui/deployment.yaml`. If a flat directory genuinely needs qualified filenames,
put the object or artifact type first rather than the component name.

head: Working in this repo > Suspended components
text:
No Flux Kustomizations are declared suspended in Git. Check both the repository
and live Flux state before changing suspension, because live state can
temporarily diverge during maintenance.

head: Working in this repo > Postgres (CloudNativePG)
text:
Every database uses the `cnpg-database` chart from
`oci://ghcr.io/thaum-xyz/helm-charts`; `docs/reference/helm-releases.md` lists them.

head: Working in this repo > Postgres (CloudNativePG)
text:
Rendered names must match what's live — `postgres-rw` is hardcoded by consumers,
so the chart's fullname is the bare release name and `releaseName` is pinned.
Never copy `install.remediation` from another release: its strategy is *uninstall*,
which on an adopted Cluster deletes it and, through `ownerReferences`, its PVCs.

head: Working in this repo > Postgres (CloudNativePG)
text:
Backups: `barman_cloud_cloudnative_pg_io_*` metrics are the real signal.
`cnpg_collector_last_available_backup_timestamp` reads **0** for plugin-method
backups, so anything built on it is worthless.

head: Working in this repo > Observability
text:
Split by role, not by stack. `platform-observability` holds collectors and
exporters only — alloy, kube-prometheus-stack (with its own Prometheus and
Alertmanager disabled), blackbox-exporter, uptimerobot. The stores get their own
namespaces: `datalake-metrics` (Prometheus, Pyrra), `datalake-logs` (Loki),
`datalake-alerts` (Alertmanager, github-receiver), `grafana`.

head: Working in this repo > Observability
text:
Operator CRDs come from the `prometheus-operator-crds` HelmRelease in `k8s/crds/`,
applied by the `crds` Kustomization declared in `k8s/bootstrap/` because nearly
every component ships a ServiceMonitor or PrometheusRule. Only `platform-cluster`
dependsOn it, being the one domain in the same namespace; `--no-cross-namespace-refs`
forbids the other four, so a component whose CRDs are missing fails and retries.
The objects still render into `platform-observability`.

head: Working in this repo > Observability
text:
Rules live with whatever produces or remediates their signal, the way k8up,
cnpg and ups rules already do.

  `docs/evaluation_runbook.md` for the practical evaluate-build-viewer
  workflow and `docs/evaluation_policy.md` as the source of truth for
  prompt/runtime choices, embedding variant policy, and result coverage audits.

head: Repository Guidelines > Evaluation Execution
text:
- Prefer the attention implementation officially recommended by the evaluated
  model. Use explicit `--attn-implementation sdpa`, `--flash-attn2`, or
  `--attn-implementation flash_attention_2` when appropriate; leaving attention
  unspecified can make long benchmark runs substantially slower for some models.

head: Repository Guidelines > Evaluation Execution
text:
- Dense evaluation automatically includes full-dimension `int8,binary` and
  `rescore:int8,binary` variants unless `--no-default-embedding-variants` is
  used. When dense truncation dims are supplied with
  `--embedding-variant truncate:DIMS`, the CLI also expands them into standalone
  truncation plus truncation x quantized/rescore variants.

head: Repository Guidelines > Evaluation Execution
text:
- If a requested dense truncate dimension matches the encoded base embedding
  dimension, evaluation warns and skips that no-op truncate variant because it
  duplicates the original full-dimension result.

head: Repository Guidelines > Evaluation Execution
text:
- After benchmark runs, audit result coverage before reporting or rebuilding
  leaderboard comparisons. Confirm base task completeness and verify that every
  intended variant category exists for each model.

head: Repository Guidelines > Evaluation Execution
text:
- When comparing a new run against existing model data, prefer the cached remote
  DuckDB, such as
  `~/.cache/hakari-bench/duckdb/remote_latest_hakari_bench.duckdb` or the synced
  Hugging Face snapshot DuckDB, instead of reading raw result JSON or `.json.xz`
  files directly. Direct JSON reads are rarely needed for existing remote
  results and should be reserved for local run outputs or schema/debug work.

head: Repository Guidelines > Leaderboard Viewer
text:
- For leaderboard viewer design changes, read `@DESIGN.md` first and keep
  design-specific rules there.

head: Repository Guidelines > Leaderboard Viewer
text:
- Before and after implementing viewer or DuckDB-related changes, benchmark
  representative queries against a freshly updated latest remote DuckDB cache.
  Record comparable timings, preserve the established filter and calculation
  order, and do not accept material regressions in unrelated viewer paths.

head: Repository Guidelines > Leaderboard Viewer
text:
- When updating viewer UI design, check `@DESIGN.md` before editing and update
  it when the design direction, tokens, layout rules, or component behavior
  changes.

head: Repository Guidelines > Leaderboard Viewer
text:
- After changing the leaderboard viewer, install Playwright Chromium and run the
  browser test before considering the work complete. This is required for
  changes to viewer behavior, queries, URL/state restoration, filters, design,
  layout, interactive controls, generated HTML, CSS, or JavaScript:
  ```bash
  uv run --only-group viewer-browser-test playwright install chromium
  uv run --only-group viewer-browser-test pytest -q -m browser tests/test_viewer_browser.py
  ```
  `uv run tox -e browser` is the CI-style shortcut for the same workflow; it
  installs Chromium before running the browser test. Do not skip this validation
  merely because focused unit tests pass. If the browser test cannot run, report
  the reason explicitly and do not describe the viewer change as fully verified.

head: Repository Guidelines > Leaderboard Viewer
text:
- When updating the leaderboard viewer in this project, keep
  `docs/duckdb_schema.md` in sync. Update it when DuckDB schema, viewer queries,
  leaderboard semantics, score grouping, variant handling, or required columns
  change.

head: Repository Guidelines > Leaderboard Viewer
text:
- The served stylesheet `hakari_bench/viewer/assets/app.css` is a compiled,
  minified Tailwind output. Never hand-edit it. Edit the source
  `hakari_bench/viewer/assets/app.tailwind.css`, then rebuild and commit both:
  ```bash
  uv run python scripts/build_viewer_css.py            # rebuild app.css
  uv run python scripts/build_viewer_css.py --watch    # rebuild on change
  uv run python scripts/build_viewer_css.py --check     # verify in sync
  ```
  The build pins the Tailwind version for reproducible output and needs Node's
  `npx` on PATH. `uv run tox -e css` runs the `--check` in CI-style validation.
  New Tailwind utility classes used in viewer `.py`/`.js` only appear after a
  rebuild.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text:
- The default evaluation method is `evaluate dense`, loaded with
  `SentenceTransformer`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text:
- Supported evaluation method subcommands are `dense`, `sparse`, `reranker`,
  `late-interaction`, and `bm25`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text: - `sparse` uses SentenceTransformers `SparseEncoder`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text:
- `reranker` uses SentenceTransformers `CrossEncoder` and requires a candidate
  ranking such as `bm25`; `--rerank-top-k` limits the candidates to rerank.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text:
- `late-interaction` uses PyLate ColBERT and scores query/document token
  embeddings with exact MaxSim.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text:
- Default dtype is `bf16`. Keep `--dtype`, `--trust-remote-code`,
  `--flash-attn2`, `--attn-implementation`, `--device`,
  `--model-max-seq-length`, `--truncate-dim`,
  `--sparse-query-max-active-dims`, and `--sparse-document-max-active-dims`
  explicit CLI options.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text:
- If no attention implementation is specified for model evaluation, the CLI
  warns and delegates to the Transformers/model default. Treat that as a prompt
  to confirm the model's official recommendation before launching long runs.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text:
- Do not shorten model max sequence length for benchmark runs just to avoid
  slow execution or memory pressure. Use the model's default/configured maximum
  length unless the user explicitly requests a different value. If memory errors
  happen, first reduce batch size or adjust execution options; changing
  `--model-max-seq-length` makes results less comparable and must be called out
  clearly in the result metadata and summary.

head: Repository Guidelines > Model Loading
text:
- Prompt overrides are optional. If no prompt or prompt name is provided,
  preserve SentenceTransformers model prompt behavior.

head: Repository Guidelines > BM25 Behavior
text:
- BM25 evaluation supports two sources:
  - By default, read the selected dataset candidate subset
    (`--candidate-ranking`, default `bm25`) and use that ranking as the BM25
    baseline.
  - Use local `bm25s` computation only when explicitly requested with
    `--bm25-source computed`, or from `build-candidates bm25` when generating
    BM25 candidate subsets.

head: Repository Guidelines > BM25 Behavior
text:
- If the default dataset subset is unavailable, fail with an actionable error
  instead of silently recomputing BM25 locally.

head: Repository Guidelines > BM25 Behavior
text: - Local BM25 uses `bm25s` with the standard Okapi-style Robertson method.

head: Repository Guidelines > BM25 Behavior
text:
- If `--bm25-tokenizer` is omitted for local BM25, auto-select the tokenizer
  from task metadata first and then from 10 sampled queries detected with
  `fast-langdetect`. Tasks marked `category: code` use `regex`; natural
  language tasks use `wordseg`, `english_porter_stop`, Snowball `stemmer`,
  `whitespace`, or `regex` according to the tokenizer policy in
  `docs/create_nano_datasets.md` and task metadata.

head: Repository Guidelines > BM25 Behavior
text:
- Supported BM25 tokenizers are `regex`, `whitespace`, `transformer`, `stemmer`,
  `english_regex`, `english_porter`, `english_porter_stop`, and `wordseg`.

head: Repository Guidelines > BM25 Behavior
text:
- `wordseg` support is optional. Keep language-specific dependencies behind the
  `wordseg` extra and lazy-load them only when the tokenizer is selected.
  Current wordseg languages are `ja`, `zh`, `th`, `ko`, and `vi`.

head: Repository Guidelines > BM25 Behavior
text:
- Nano dataset BM25 candidate subsets used for top-100 reranking diagnostics
  should force qrels positives into the final top-k candidate list and record
  `candidate_coverage`. Query and relevant coverage should be 100% unless the
  dataset README and metadata explicitly document why that is impossible.

head: Repository Guidelines > BM25 Behavior
text:
- Persist the resolved BM25 source, backend, algorithm, tokenizer, and candidate
  subset metadata in result JSON under `config.bm25` and `model.bm25`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text:
- Per-task result files are written below:
```text
output/hakari-results/{model_id}/{huggingface_dataset_name}/{split_or_task}.json.xz
```

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text:
- Run-level summaries are derived from per-task result JSON when building the
  DuckDB database; do not write aggregate result files.

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text:
- `scripts/build_results_database_and_report.py` accepts repeated
  `--results-dir` options for merging multiple result roots. Treat the argument
  order as the merge priority: the first directory wins for duplicate
  `model_name`/task JSON, and later directories only fill missing results.
  Use `--overwrite-result-duplicates` when later directories should replace
  duplicate logical model-task rows from earlier directories.
  `model_name` comes from result JSON `model.id`; do not use `model_dir` as
  part of the logical model identity.

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text:
- DuckDB builds default to streaming result rows into DuckDB. Use
  `--materialize-results-in-python` only for the legacy materialized path or
  `--html-output` when a static HTML report is required.

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text:
- When rebuilding the canonical leaderboard DuckDB from the latest Hugging Face
  dataset results, use `scripts/sync_remote_results_and_rebuild.py` instead of
  pointing the builder at ad hoc local result directories. Prefer
  `--sync-backend xet` for the large Hugging Face results dataset; it keeps a
  git checkout under
  `~/.cache/hakari-bench/hf-datasets/hakari-bench__results__xet`, fetches with
  LFS smudge disabled, runs `git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD`, installs the local
  Git Xet transfer agent with `git xet install --local --path ...`, removes
  stale untracked files with `git clean -fdx`, and pulls only
  `hakari-results/**` LFS payloads. Existing local Git LFS/Xet cache objects
  should be reused. The rebuilt DuckDB should be written outside the checkout
  under `output/clean-hf-results-duckdb/{checkout-name}/hakari_bench.duckdb` so
  the cached Hugging Face results repo remains git-clean. The plain `git`
  backend remains available when Git Xet must not be installed. Use
  `--skip-git-sync` only when intentionally rebuilding from the existing local
  cache without cleaning or syncing.

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text:
- Use `--append-results-dir` when adding a separate root containing only new
  model-task JSON to an existing DuckDB. This mode is append-only and should
  reject duplicate result paths or duplicate logical model-task rows.
  If the target DuckDB is missing and no local base is supplied, append mode
  should download the configured latest remote DuckDB before adding results.
  Use `--append-base-duckdb` plus `--append-output-duckdb` when a new merged DB
  should be created from an existing base, and `--model-name-override` only when
  the append directory represents one logical model.

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text: - Existing result files should be skipped unless `--overwrite` is provided.

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text:
- Result JSON should preserve as much runtime detail as practical, including
  batch size, dtype, package versions, torch/CUDA info, prompts, total
  parameters, trainable parameters, embedding parameters, transformer/active
  parameters, evaluation timestamps, dataset load duration, and evaluation
  timing.

head: Repository Guidelines > Results and Metadata
text:
- Active parameters are currently computed as total parameters minus input
  embedding parameters when both counts are available.

head: Repository Guidelines > Dataset Configuration
text: - Add new datasets as YAML files under `config/datasets/`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Dataset Configuration
text: - Add grouped benchmark definitions under `config/dataset_collections/`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Dataset Configuration
text:
- Keep dataset specs generic enough to handle:
  - datasets split by task,
  - datasets not split by task,
  - collection-style benchmarks such as `MNanoBEIR`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Dataset Configuration
text:
- `MNanoBEIR` is defined as a built-in collection in
  `config/dataset_collections/mnanobeir.yaml`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Dataset Configuration
text:
- Keep the evaluation task count distinct from the leaderboard Overall count.
  A complete model evaluation runs and preserves 563 task results, including
  `NanoBEIR-en` as the English component of `MNanoBEIR`. The viewer excludes 13
  overlapping Nano task copies through `config/viewer/benchmarks.yaml`, so the
  Overall score is calculated from 550 tasks. The excluded results must remain
  in the results dataset; see `docs/benchmark_scope.md` for the rationale and
  exact task list.

head: Repository Guidelines > Dataset Configuration
text:
- Built-in dataset names should stay consistent across docs, configs, and tests:
  `NanoBEIR-en`, `MNanoBEIR`, `NanoMIRACL`, `NanoMLDR`, `NanoJMTEB`,
  `NanoRTEB`, `NanoMTEB`, `NanoCMTEB`, `NanoMMTEB`, `NanoFaMTEB`,
  `NanoRuMTEB`, `NanoVNMTEB`, `NanoMTEB-BR`, `NanoMTEB-Misc`, `NanoLongEmbed`, and
  `NanoCoIR`.

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance to coding agents collaborating on this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text:
Sandopolis is a portable and accurate multi-system Sega emulator for Genesis, Master System, Game Gear, and SG-1000, written in Zig (and C).
Priorities, in order:

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 1. Correct emulation behavior and compatibility.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 2. Clear timing and subsystem interactions.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 3. Maintainable boundaries between frontend and core emulation logic.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 4. Performance, but only after correctness is covered by tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Use English for code, comments, docs, and tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Prefer small, focused changes over broad rewrites.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Ensure the project is modular and components are decoupled with clean APIs and interfaces.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Keep emulator state instance-bound inside the existing structs (`Bus`, `Vdp`, `Io`, `Z80`, `Cpu`, and `AudioOutput`).

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Avoid introducing a new global mutable state.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Keep SDL/frontend logic in `src/main.zig` and `src/frontend/`; keep core emulation logic in `src/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text:
- Keep SDL3 portable in the build graph: use the Zig-native SDL3 build (`castholm/SDL`) plus `zsdl` bindings, and do not hard-code platform binary
  artifacts such as `lib/libSDL3.so` in `build.zig`.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Add comments only when they clarify non-obvious hardware behavior or timing.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Good: add a VDP timing helper inside `src/video/vdp.zig` with module-local tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Good: add a regression ROM boot assertion in `tests/regression_tests.zig`.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Bad: move emulator core behavior into `src/main.zig`.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Bad: add a new debug-only behavior path without tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Use Oxford commas in inline lists: "a, b, and c" not "a, b, c".

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Do not use em dashes. Restructure the sentence, or use a colon or semicolon instead.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Avoid colorful adjectives and adverbs. Write "TCP proxy" not "lightweight TCP proxy", "scoring components" not "transparent scoring components".

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Use noun phrases for checklist items, not imperative verbs. Write "redundant index detection" not "detect redundant indexes".

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text:
- Headings in Markdown files must be in the title case: "Build from Source" not "Build from source". Minor words (a, an, the, and, but, or, for, in,
  on, at, to, by, of) stay lowercase unless they are the first word.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/main.zig`: SDL frontend, event loop, rendering, audio device setup.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/api.zig`: API/doc entrypoint used for generated documentation.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/public/`: deliberate public API facade type (`Machine`) exposed from `src/api.zig`.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/testing/`: explicit testing facade used by non-unit suites that need lower-level control than `Machine` alone exposes.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/testing_root.zig`: root module used for internal testing facades that need broader access than `src/testing/` alone.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/bus/`: cartridge loading/persistence, memory map, open-bus behavior, Z80 arbitration, and VDP/audio timing coordination.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/scheduler/`: frame/master-clock scheduling.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/cpu/`: 68K/Z80 wrappers, runtime hooks, CPU-facing memory interface, and the local jgz80 bridge C code.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `src/audio/`: sample-based YM2612 FM synthesizer (`ym2612_sample.zig`, runtime), cycle-accurate Nuked OPN2 core (`ym2612.zig`, validation), SN76489
  PSG with bipolar output, blip-buffer band-limited resampler, board analog LPF, 3-band parametric equalizer, and the output mixing pipeline.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/input/`: controller I/O and configurable input mapping.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/recording/`: GIF animation recording with LZW compression and crash-safe output, WAV audio recording, and BMP screenshot capture.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/video/`: VDP and video timing/rendering logic.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `src/sms/`: Sega Master System and Game Gear emulation: VDP Mode 4, memory bus with Sega mapper, I/O port dispatch, Z80-based machine, PSG-only
  audio, GG 12-bit CRAM, and GG viewport cropping.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/frontend/`: SDL frontend helpers including config, UI state, save manager, menu, dialog, toast, and performance overlay logic.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/unit_test_root.zig`: internal test root that aggregates module-local unit tests for `zig build test-unit`.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/wasm.zig`: WebAssembly export layer wrapping the `SystemMachine` facade for browser deployment.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/wasm_stubs.c`: minimal C stubs (setjmp/longjmp and main) needed for WASM builds.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `src/libretro.zig`: Libretro core shared library wrapping the `SystemMachine` facade for RetroArch and other Libretro frontends; runs Genesis,
  SMS, Game Gear, and SG-1000 content.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/system.zig`: system type detection (Genesis, SMS, or Game Gear) from ROM headers and cartridge region codes.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `src/system_machine.zig`: `SystemMachine` tagged union abstracting Genesis and SMS/GG for all frontends, including unified input mapping and
  save-state serialization that dispatches on the state-buffer magic.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/rom_loader.zig`: ROM file loading with ZIP archive extraction (deflate and stored).

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/`: remaining core emulator modules (`machine.zig`, `cli.zig`, `performance_profile.zig`, `rom_metadata.zig`, `state_file.zig`, etc.).

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `tests/`: non-unit suites only:
    - `integration_tests.zig`
    - `regression_tests.zig`
    - `property_tests.zig`

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `tests/testroms/`: local (public-domain and community) ROMs for testing and hardware verification; see `tests/testroms/README.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `roms/`: local ROMs for manual testing only; this directory may be absent.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `tools/`: developer-only utilities that are not part of the shipped emulator runtime.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `external/`: optional checked-out third-party source trees used for developer tooling or reference comparison, not default runtime dependencies.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `web/`: browser frontend for the WebAssembly build (HTML, JavaScript, AudioWorklet, and WebXR theater scene). `web/fonts/`, `web/img/`, and
  `web/sandopolis.wasm` are generated by `make web` and gitignored.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `docs/assets/overlays/`: libretro common-overlays assets (Genesis button icons, CRT bezel) under CC BY 4.0; source of truth for
  `web/img/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `tmp/`: scratch/reference material only; do not treat it as the Sandopolis source, and it may be missing.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `build.zig.zon`: source dependencies only. Avoid adding checked-in platform binary packages when an upstream source dependency is available.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text: - Unit tests belong in the Zig module they exercise.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text: - `zig build test-unit` collects module-local unit tests through `src/unit_test_root.zig`.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text: - Integration, regression, and property-based tests belong in `tests/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text:
- Non-unit tests should use the public API from `src/api.zig`. If they need lower-level control than `Machine` exposes, add or extend the explicit
  `sandopolis.testing` facade instead of re-exporting raw core structs.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text: - `tests/integration_tests.zig` is for stable public-API and cross-module wiring coverage that is not tied to a specific bug history.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text: - `tests/regression_tests.zig` is for bug reproductions, timing regressions, and ROM-backed behavior checks.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text: - `tests/property_tests.zig` is for invariant-style and randomized coverage.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text: - ROM-dependent tests belong in `tests/regression_tests.zig`.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text:
- `tests/testroms/` contains community test ROMs for hardware verification. Use these for targeted regression tests against known hardware behavior.
  `roms/` is for local game ROMs used in manual testing only.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Layout Rules
text: - If you move code across modules, move or rewrite the unit tests with it.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text: - `Bus` is the central coordination point for memory, timing, Z80 arbitration, VDP progression, and audio timing.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text: - `scheduler/frame_scheduler.runMasterSlice()` is the authoritative scheduler path for frame execution.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text:
- Timing-sensitive changes must respect the interaction between:
    - `Bus.stepMaster()`
    - `scheduler/frame_scheduler.runMasterSlice()`
    - `Cpu.stepInstruction()`
    - `Vdp.progressTransfers()`
    - `AudioTiming.consumeMaster()` and `Z80.setAudioMasterOffset()` (audio event timestamps)

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text:
- The jgz80 C bridge (`src/cpu/jgz80_bridge.c`) owns the YM/PSG event ring buffers and register shadows. Audio event flow crosses a Zig/C boundary;
  changes to audio event capture or draining must account for both sides.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text:
- The PSG is reachable from both the Z80 (address `0x7F11`) and the M68K (VDP port `0xC00011`). Both paths must push timestamped events through the
  Z80 bridge.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text: - Keep frontend concerns separate from emulation concerns.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text:
- Frontends (`src/main.zig`, `src/wasm.zig`, and `src/libretro.zig`) must drive the emulator through the `SystemMachine` facade instead of
  switching on the system variant or reaching into `Machine`/`SmsMachine` internals. Add missing capabilities to the facade; use the
  `asGenesis()` escape hatch only for deliberately Genesis-only features.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text:
- The YM/PSG audio event types are owned by `src/audio/events.zig` as native extern structs; `src/cpu/z80.zig` casts them across the C boundary
  with comptime layout asserts against `jgz80_bridge.h`. Keep both sides in lockstep when changing event layouts.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text:
- `src/platform.zig` is the only place allowed to use `std.Io`, `std.fs`, or `std.process` directly. All other code must go through the `platform`
  module for file, directory, clock, env, args, and sleep operations. This contains standard-library churn between Zig versions to one file. When a
  Zig upgrade changes these APIs, update the wrapper bodies in `src/platform.zig` instead of spreading fixes across call sites.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text: - Preserve MIT-license boundaries. Treat external emulator repos and AGPL code as references unless licensing has been reviewed explicitly.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Constraints
text:
- `external/Nuked-OPN2` is an optional LGPL developer-reference dependency. Keep it isolated to the `compare-ym` tool and never make it part of the
  default `sandopolis`, `check`, `test`, or release build paths.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 1. Identify whether this is a timing, API, frontend, or docs change.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 2. Read the touched module and existing nearby tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: Implement using red-green TDD:

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 1. Write a failing test first that describes the expected behavior (red).

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 2. Run the test and verify it fails for the right reason.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 3. Write the smallest implementation that makes the test pass (green).

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 4. Refactor if needed while keeping tests green.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 5. Run the narrowest relevant test target while iterating (`zig build test-unit`, `zig build test-integration`, etc.).

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 6. Run `zig build check` and `zig build test`.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: 7. Update docs (`README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `src/api.zig` exports) if behavior or workflow changed.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: Additional validation when relevant:

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: - `zig build test-frontend` when touching frontend helper functions or UI state logic.

head: AGENTS.md > Workflow
text: - `zig build docs --prefix .` for docs/API/build-doc changes.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Project Overview
text: High-performance Go library for parsing EXIF metadata from JPEG, HEIC, AVIF, TIFF, DNG, CR2, CR3, CRW, NEF, ARW, RW2, and PNG. Targets parity with ExifTool as the reference implementation. Zero-allocation perceptual image hashing included.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Core Principles
text: - **Idiomatic Go** — Use `gofmt`/`goimports` style. No JavaScript, Java, or Python patterns (no classes, no getters/setters, no builder patterns, no fluent interfaces).

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Core Principles
text: - **Near-zero allocation** — Hot paths must avoid heap allocation. Use stack buffers (`[N]byte`), `sync.Pool`, and the `Acquire`/`Release` pattern. Always `b.ReportAllocs()` in benchmarks.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Core Principles
text: - **Functional options** — `ReaderOption func(*Reader)` pattern for optional config. Precompute lookup tables for option closures where possible.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Core Principles
text: - **Pooled resources** — Every pooled type has `Acquire*` / `Release*` functions. Always `defer Release*()` immediately after acquire.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Error Handling
text:
- **Sentinel errors**: Define in `var (...)` blocks using `errors.New` (stdlib), not `fmt.Errorf`:
  ```go
  var (
      ErrNoExif = meta.ErrNoExif
      ErrImageTypeNotFound = imagetype.ErrImageTypeNotFound
  )
  ```

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Error Handling
text: - **Error wrapping**: Use `github.com/pkg/errors.Wrapf(err, "message")` with lowercase message, no trailing punctuation.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Error Handling
text: - **Error comparison**: Always use `errors.Is(err, ErrNoExif)`, never `==`.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Error Handling
text: - **Graceful degradation**: Skip invalid tags rather than aborting. Log non-fatal issues at warn level.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Error Handling
text: - **Conditional logging**: Always check level before creating log event: `if r.warnEnabled() { ... }`.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: - Exported types: PascalCase (`IFD0Tag`, `ExifIFDTags`, `Reader`)

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: - Unexported: camelCase (`state`, `eofReader`, `loggerMixin`)

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: - Constants: PascalCase exported (`ImageJPEG`), camelCase unexported

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: - Receiver names: single letter (`r *Reader`, `s *state`)

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: - Avoid stutter: `exif.Exif` not `exif.ExifReader`

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Naming
text: - File names: short, single word where possible

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Zero-Alloc Hot Path Guidelines
text: 1. Prefer `[N]byte` arrays on stack over `make([]byte, N)`.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Zero-Alloc Hot Path Guidelines
text: 2. Use fixed-size tag queues (`[128]tag.Entry`) instead of dynamic slices.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Zero-Alloc Hot Path Guidelines
text: 3. Embedded values (≤4 bytes) read directly from IFD entry without allocation.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Zero-Alloc Hot Path Guidelines
text: 4. Returned byte slices reference parser buffers — document they are only valid until next read.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Zero-Alloc Hot Path Guidelines
text: 5. Use `sync.Pool` for everything: readers, states, bufio readers, pixel arrays.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Zero-Alloc Hot Path Guidelines
text: 6. Avoid `fmt.Sprintf` in hot paths; use structured slog fields.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Zero-Alloc Hot Path Guidelines
text: 7. Avoid `interface{}` allocations; use concrete types.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Zero-Alloc Hot Path Guidelines
text: 8. Use insertion sort for small fixed-size queues (avoids allocating `sort.Interface`).

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Code Generation
text: - `//go:generate msgp` for MessagePack serialization (`*_gen.go`)

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Code Generation
text: - `//go:generate stringer -type=TypeName` for enum string methods

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Code Generation

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Coding Conventions > Code Generation

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Testing > Benchmarks
text: - Every benchmark must call `b.ReportAllocs()` and `b.SetBytes(int64(len(data)))`.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Testing > Benchmarks
text: - Load file into `[]byte` with `os.ReadFile`, use `bytes.NewReader(data)`, call `r.Seek(0, 0)` between iterations.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Testing > Benchmarks
text: - Table-driven with `b.Run(name, ...)` sub-benchmarks.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Testing > Benchmarks
text: - Environment variable `IMAGEMETA_BENCH_IMAGE_DIR` overrides the benchmark image directory.

head: AGENTS.MD — imagemeta > Testing > Benchmarks
text: - Target: JPEG: ≤64 B/op, 2 allocs/op. CR2: ≤1600 B/op, ≤20 allocs/op. CR3: ≤3800 B/op, ≤22 allocs/op.

head: AGENTS.md > What this app is
text:
Reckoning is a self-hosted invoicing app for freelancers and small
agencies. Customers + projects + time tracking → invoices + offers
rendered as PDFs and emailed.

head: AGENTS.md > Stack > SPA conventions
text:
- **The API comes first, and its schema is the tests.** Declare an
  endpoint in a Minitest DSL spec under `test/integration/api/v1/`, then
  `RAILS_ENV=test rake openapi_ruby:generate` writes `swagger/v1/schema.yaml`
  and `pnpm run generate-api-client` turns it into the hooks under
  `app/frontend/services/api/`. A route and an action without a DSL
  declaration are unreachable from the SPA — that has bitten twice.

head: AGENTS.md > Stack > SPA conventions
text:
- **Rails owns a path or the SPA does.** `config/routes.rb` ends in a
  catch-all that hands every page load to the shell; the list of first
  path segments above it (`api`, `api-docs`, `backend`'s two mounts,
  `cable`, `rails`, `up`) is what the server keeps. A path that answers
  a non-page request — an export, a PDF — is declared before it.

head: AGENTS.md > Stack > SPA conventions
text:
- **A screen's state lives in the URL.** Filters, sorting and paging are
  query parameters, so a filtered list is a link someone can send.

head: AGENTS.md > Stack > SPA conventions
text:
- **Three test layers, and they do different jobs.** Vitest for a
  component's logic against a stubbed adapter, the Minitest DSL specs
  for the contract, Playwright for the flow through a real server. A
  screen port lands with all three.

head: AGENTS.md > Stack > SPA conventions
text:
- **Measure, do not guess, when porting a look.** The server-rendered
  stylesheet is still built: render the old markup against
  `application.css`, screenshot it, and match. Two bugs got through on a
  guess — a chart whose labels wrapped and a tab that had no card.

head: AGENTS.md > Essential commands > Setup
text:
No `.env` is needed. `.env.tpl` is committed and holds `op://` references
instead of secrets; `bin/op` resolves them at run time. Machine-specific
overrides (ports, `WORKTREE_SUFFIX`) go in `.env.local`, which is gitignored and
read after the template.

head: AGENTS.md > Essential commands > Development
text:
Anything needing dev secrets goes through `bin/op`. Commands that don't — tests,
linters, generators — can run directly.

head: AGENTS.md > Essential commands > Testing
text:
The CI runs tests sharded with `knapsack` (4 shards). To run a single
shard locally: `CI_NODE_TOTAL=4 CI_NODE_INDEX=0 bundle exec rake knapsack:minitest`.

head: AGENTS.md > Essential commands > Linting & static analysis (run after EVERY change)

head: AGENTS.md > Essential commands > Secrets (Kamal path)
text:
Every Kamal secret comes from the **`Reckoning` 1Password vault** via
`.kamal/secrets-common` and `.kamal/secrets.<destination>`. Those files hold
`op read` calls, not secret material, and are committed on purpose.

head: AGENTS.md > Essential commands > Secrets (Kamal path)
text: CI uses `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` instead of `OP_ACCOUNT`.

head: AGENTS.md > Essential commands > Secrets (Kamal path)
text:
- `RAILS_MASTER_KEY` decrypts `config/credentials/production.yml.enc`, which
  supplies `secret_key_base`, the devise secrets, mailer credentials **and the
  `active_record_encryption` keys**. A wrong key does not fail loudly — it makes
  every encrypted column read back as garbage.

head: AGENTS.md > Essential commands > Secrets (Kamal path)

  Postgres accessory credentials. They resolve over the Docker network
  (`reckoning-db`, `reckoning-redis`) because live is a single node with
  colocated datastores.
