head: KlickerUZH > Stacked PRs
text: - Use the maintained draft sync PRs for `v3` -> `v3-ai` and `v3-ai` -> `v3-audit`. Merge these integrations with normal merge commits to preserve ancestry; a squashed sync fails the `sync-ancestry` check until the restore PR the guard opens is merged with a merge commit (see [Squashed sync guard](docs/ci-and-deployment.md#squashed-sync-guard)). Retain the applicable verification and merge/deployment authorization gates. Other feature-branch synchronization remains manual.

head: KlickerUZH > Stacked PRs
text: - **Branch promotion chain**: `v3` -> `v3-ai` -> `v3-audit`. Never merge `v3` into `v3-audit` directly, and do not cherry-pick around a hop. `v3-audit` is the branch staging builds from, so every `v3-ai` commit it is meant to release has to arrive through a `v3-ai` -> `v3-audit` merge. When an approved change adds, renames, reorders, or retires an integration branch, agents must maintain the explicit sync pairs and their workflow triggers, tests, and documentation together; follow [Changing the sync chain](docs/ci-and-deployment.md#changing-the-sync-chain).

head: KlickerUZH > Stacked PRs
text: - **Integration mechanics**: the `v3` and `v3-*` rulesets block deletion and force-push, and their required checks evaluate both pull requests and direct pushes. Admins may bypass required checks on pull requests; `v3-ai` additionally permits a repository-admin direct push, and the push still runs the full CI suite on the branch. A non-fast-forward push is rejected when the branch has moved, so duplicate syncs cannot land.

head: KlickerUZH > Stacked PRs
text: - **Sync routing**: automation creates drafts for those two pairs only; source pushes keep their diffs current. Maintainers control readiness, conflict resolution, and merging. Resolve substantive conflicts on a task branch and open an integration PR, recording the integrated source SHA in the merge message. The staging promoter independently re-validates the exact `v3-audit` head before moving `stg-release`. See [Draft sync PR maintenance](docs/ci-and-deployment.md#draft-sync-pr-maintenance) for triggers and CI behavior.

head: KlickerUZH > Stacked PRs
text: - GitHub stacked PRs are enabled for this repository. Always use `$stacked-change` and `$gh-stack` for larger features: substantial cross-layer or multi-concern work, changes with distinct reviewer audiences or runtime models, and existing large branches that need decomposition. Keep an ordinary single PR for small, cohesive changes only.

head: KlickerUZH > Stacked PRs
text: - This is a KlickerUZH repository capability, not a GitHub-wide assumption. Verify native stack support before using the workflow in another repository.

head: KlickerUZH > Stacked PRs
text: - Final AI review is standing-authorized for all KlickerUZH PRs. Once exact-head CI and ordinary feedback are settled, agents may post `/final-review` for an unstacked PR or ordinary stack layer, and `/final-review-stack` only on the top PR of a verified native stack, without asking again. This approval covers sending the public PR diff to the workflow's configured OpenRouter model and the resulting usage cost; it does not authorize merging, approving, force-pushing, or exposing uncommitted or private data.

head: KlickerUZH > Release preparation
text:
Use the release scripts in the root `package.json` to generate versions and
`CHANGELOG.md`; never hand-edit package versions or assemble release notes as a
substitute. For an alpha release, run `pnpm run release:alpha` (preview with
`pnpm run release:alpha:dry`). The script uses `.versionrc.js` as the authoritative
version-target list. During PR preparation, pass `--skip.tag` and create the tag
only at the approved merged release commit. Tag publication and production
activation remain separately authorized actions.

head: KlickerUZH > GraphQL Workflow
text: Code-first with **Pothos** in `packages/graphql/src/`. After changing types/resolvers (`src/graphql/`) or `.graphql` ops (`src/graphql/ops/`), regenerate with `pnpm --filter @klicker-uzh/graphql generate` (codegen is required — ops are stale otherwise). Op-name prefixes: `Q` query, `M` mutation, `S` subscription, `F` fragment. Package builds regenerate the ignored typed documents and persisted-query maps; the generated public SDL snapshot at `packages/graphql/src/public/schema.graphql` remains tracked for review and local GraphQL tooling.

head: KlickerUZH > Database Workflow
text: Prisma split-schema under `packages/prisma/src/prisma/schema/`. After editing a `.prisma` file, run `pnpm --filter @klicker-uzh/prisma run prisma:migrate:raw` inside the provisioned disposable container (creates/applies the migration and explicitly regenerates the TypeScript client), then `pnpm run prisma:sync` (mirrors model files into `apps/analytics` while preserving its Python generator and datasource), then rebuild dependents. Update GraphQL types/resolvers if the change affects the API. Prisma 7 reset and migration commands do not seed automatically; use the explicit raw seed command for local fixtures. See [Data & Migrations](docs/data-and-migrations.md) for the guarded shadow requirement and schema-drift checks.

head: KlickerUZH > Auth Model > Participation state boundary
text:
`Participation.isActive` is a **leaderboard opt-in flag**, not an enrollment,
course-access, or security flag. Toggling it changes leaderboard inclusion only;

head: KlickerUZH > Local Dev Setup > Self-contained devcontainer (recommended) > OpenRouter-backed local chat
text:
Local Auto Mode is selected by `CHAT_PRIMARY_MODEL_ID=auto`. Chat sends the
`auto-router` deployment to LiteLLM at `http://litellm:4000`; LiteLLM classifies
the request with the current Auto V2 policy in `util/litellm/config.yaml`.
Classification uses Luna low; semantic corpus matching uses
`openai/text-embedding-3-small`; SIMPLE, MEDIUM, and COMPLEX route to Luna
medium, high, and xhigh; REASONING routes to Sol medium. LiteLLM then forwards
all three request types through OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible endpoint;
OpenRouter supplies the selected models but does not make the routing decision.
This adds one classifier request and, for semantic matching, one embedding
request to the same external OpenRouter data boundary. It therefore adds local
latency and usage cost. LiteLLM falls back from Sol medium to `gpt-5.1` on an
upstream failure. Separately, zero-credit fallback remains within the selected
usage class. Chat can select allow-listed Luna for a BASE selection before
calling LiteLLM; current ADVANCED selections such as Auto are denied while no
ADVANCED fallback is allow-listed.

head: AGENTS
text: Single source of truth for coding-agent guidance in this repo.

head: AGENTS
text:
**Read `OPINIONS.md` before changing anything it covers** — patch/update logic,
pagination, resource naming, keyword-only arguments on public methods, deprecations,
releases, and testing edge cases.
`AGENTS.md` states what to do; `OPINIONS.md` explains the traps.

head: AGENTS > Project Basics
text: - Python: >=3.10 (use modern type hint syntax: `list[str]`, `str | None`).

head: AGENTS > Project Basics
text: - Formatting and linting: Ruff (line length 99).

head: AGENTS > Project Basics
text:
- Commit style: Conventional Commits (`type(scope): summary`), enforced by hooks.
  See `OPINIONS.md` for `feat`/`fix`/`docs`/`chore` distinctions and release rules.

head: AGENTS > Repo Layout
text: - `src/albert/collections/` — API-facing collection classes that call endpoints.

head: AGENTS > Repo Layout
text: - `src/albert/resources/` — Pydantic models representing API resources.

text: - `src/albert/core/` — Session, pagination, shared enums, and base classes.

head: AGENTS > Repo Layout
text: - `src/albert/utils/` — Reusable helper utilities.

head: AGENTS > Repo Layout
text: - `docs/` — mkdocs content (autogenerated from docstrings via mkdocstrings).

head: AGENTS > Repo Layout
text: - `tests/` — `unit/` (offline) and `integration/` (live API) pytest suites; start at `tests/TESTING.md`.

head: AGENTS > Repo Layout
text: - `OPINIONS.md` — non-obvious constraints; read before editing the areas it names.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - **Keep it simple.** Minimum code that solves the problem. No speculative abstractions, no configurability that wasn't asked for.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - **Follow existing patterns.** Check similar code before writing new code. Match style and structure.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - **Touch only what's needed.** Don't refactor adjacent code, improve unrelated formatting, or remove pre-existing dead code unless asked. Remove only imports/symbols that *your* changes made unused.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - **Validate at boundaries only.** Trust internal code and type hints. Only validate user input and external API responses.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - **Catch narrow exceptions.** Never `except Exception` (or bare `except`) in SDK code; catch `AlbertHTTPError` or the specific subclass the code can handle. See `OPINIONS.md`.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - **Changing a field's `alias`/`serialization_alias` is a wire change** for every code path that serializes the model, including unrelated endpoints. Grep the model's `model_dump(by_alias=True)` call sites first. See `OPINIONS.md`.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - **Bulk/batch methods short-circuit empty input.** Every bulk method (`*_many`, `add_columns`, `delete_rows`, ...) returns without firing a request when given an empty list, and the guard applies uniformly across all sibling bulk methods. A no-op `update()` (nothing in `model_fields_set`) returns the current entity without a request.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - Collections inherit from `BaseCollection` and accept an `AlbertSession`.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - Public collection methods use `@validate_call` for runtime validation. Match sibling methods on the same collection: if they declare it, new methods do too.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text:
- **Always use keyword-only arguments (`*`) for public methods.** Place `*` immediately
  after `self` (or `cls`) on all public collection, resource, and client methods
  (e.g. `def get_by_id(self, *, id: str) -> Cas:`). Never expose positional parameters on
  public APIs. See `OPINIONS.md` for rationale.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - Resources use `BaseAlbertModel`/`BaseResource` with Pydantic `Field` and aliases.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text:
- **Field documentation lives on attribute docstrings**, not in class-level ``Attributes`` sections.
  ``BaseAlbertModel`` sets ``use_attribute_docstrings=True``, so Pydantic emits them as
  JSON Schema ``description`` values (used by the ReAct worker tool factory and
  ``expand_schema``). Place the docstring on the line immediately after each field, and
  add a blank line after each field+docstring pair so adjacent fields are visually
  separated in the IDE::
    ```python
    description: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    """Human-readable project name/description. Also serves as the display name."""

    status: str | None = Field(default=None)
    """Lifecycle status of the project."""
    ```
  Keep the class docstring for narrative, examples, and cross-refs; document individual
  fields only via attribute docstrings. Prefer attribute docstrings over
  ``Field(description=...)`` so docs stay in one place (existing ``Field(description=...)``
  values are left as-is until migrated). Collection classes (``*Collection``) are not
  Pydantic models — their ``Attributes`` blocks document ``base_path`` / ``session`` and
  stay in the class docstring.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - Search result model naming: see `OPINIONS.md`.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards
text: - Keep API payloads in wire format (camelCase) via `Field(alias=...)` and `model_dump(by_alias=True, mode="json", exclude_none=True)`.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Reuse shared enums and types
text:
Before typing a field as a bare `str` (or declaring a new local enum/model), check
`src/albert/core/shared/` for an existing definition. Common cross-resource concepts
already live there:

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Reuse shared enums and types
text: - `enums.py` — `Status` (active/inactive), `OrderBy` (asc/desc), `SecurityClass`.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Reuse shared enums and types
text: - `models/base.py` — `EntityLink`, `EntityLinkWithName`, `AuditFields`, `LocalizedNames`.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Reuse shared enums and types
text: - `types.py` — `MetadataItem`, `SerializeAsEntityLink`.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Reuse shared enums and types
text:
This applies to search items too (e.g. `status` on a `{Entity}SearchItem` is
`Status | None`, not `str | None`), so wire values stay consistent and invalid values
fail validation instead of passing through silently.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Reuse shared enums and types
text:
**Reuse only on an exact match.** Use a shared enum/type only when it covers exactly
what the field requires: the same value set and the same semantics. Do not force-fit
`Status` onto a field whose lifecycle has more or different states, and do not add
members to a shared enum just to make one field fit. When the match is not exact, use
`str` (for open-ended values) or a resource-specific enum (for a fixed but different
value set).

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Pydantic `extra` on resource models
text:
`BaseAlbertModel` does not set `extra`. Pydantic's default is `extra="ignore"`: undeclared
keys are dropped with no error.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Pydantic `extra` on resource models
text:
- **API responses** (resources, unpack rows, lookup results): inherit `BaseAlbertModel`
  with no `extra` override so new API keys do not break validation.

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Pydantic `extra` on resource models
text:
- **`extra="allow"`**: only when the model must preserve unknown top-level keys on the
  instance (e.g. evolving response wrappers).

head: AGENTS > Coding Standards > Pydantic `extra` on resource models
text:
- **Caller request models** (a caller-facing subset of a wire payload the collection may
  enrich): set `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` when the collection fills fields
  that are not declared on the model. Without `forbid`, undeclared keys (e.g.
  `substances=[]` on a model where composition is filled from unpack) are silently ignored

head: AGENTS > Pagination
text: Many list/search methods use `AlbertPaginator` (`src/albert/core/pagination.py`). Two modes:

head: AGENTS > Pagination
text: - **Offset** (`PaginationMode.OFFSET`) — uses `offset` param, defaults to `limit=1000`, stops when `Items` is empty.

head: AGENTS > Pagination
text: - **Key** (`PaginationMode.KEY`) — uses `startKey`, expects `lastKey` in response. Do not pass `limit` from the SDK; the backend controls page size.

head: AGENTS > Pagination
text: - **Choose the mode from response-shape evidence, not habit.** A `total` field in the payload signals OFFSET; a `lastKey` continuation token signals KEY. For a brand-new endpoint, verify the whole envelope (`Items` key, continuation key, accepted query params) against the backend handler, the OpenAPI spec, or a live call before merge. The wrong mode silently truncates results after the first page. See `OPINIONS.md`.

head: AGENTS > Pagination
text: Expose a `max_items` parameter on public list/search methods where appropriate to allow early stopping.

head: AGENTS > Pagination
text: After iteration, `AlbertPaginator.has_more` is True when `max_items` stopped the iterator and more items are known to exist (unyielded items on the current page, or a continuation key/offset), or when response `total` exceeds items yielded. It is False after a natural end of results. Prefer this flag over comparing yielded count to `max_items` (backends can under-return a page).

head: AGENTS > Pagination
text: Offset search endpoints (projects, tasks, lots, inventories, datatemplates, parametergroups, propertydata) return a string/int `total` field — `_record_total` reads that key. Never wrap a returned paginator in `yield from` / `async for … yield` inside `get_all`; return the paginator (or `MappedPaginator` / `MetadataPreservingIterator`) so callers keep `has_more` / `total`.

head: AGENTS > Pagination > Which iterator wrapper to return
text:
| Return | When |
| --- | --- |
| `AlbertPaginator` | The endpoint page is already the caller-facing type (or a trivial `deserialize`). Prefer this for direct list/search with no per-item hydration. |
| `MappedPaginator` | `get_all` maps each list/search hit (usually `get_by_id`), including KEY-mode listings that hydrate after the page (e.g. users, storage_locations). Use when hydration is per-item and some hits may be dropped (`map_fn` returns `None`). |
| `MetadataPreservingIterator` | Custom iteration over a source paginator that is not a simple 1:1 map (batch hydration, multi-step transforms). Pass the source paginator plus the items iterator you actually yield. |

head: AGENTS > Pagination > Which iterator wrapper to return
text: Rule of thumb: if you already have an `AlbertPaginator`, return it. Reach for `MappedPaginator` / `MetadataPreservingIterator` only when a plain generator would strip `has_more` / `total`.

head: AGENTS > Pagination > Which iterator wrapper to return
text: **`offset` and `limit` are never exposed as method parameters.** They are internal pagination state managed entirely by `AlbertPaginator`. Never add `offset` or `limit` to a public method signature or docstring. Use `max_items` as the only caller-facing pagination control.

head: AGENTS > Pagination > Which iterator wrapper to return
text: Exception: when a backend caps page size below `DEFAULT_LIMIT` (1000), set `limit` in the search/list payload (or paginator params) to that cap so the first request is valid (see `substance_v4`, `workflows`). Collections still must not expose `limit` as a public method parameter.

head: AGENTS > Testing
text:
- **Read `tests/TESTING.md` before writing or changing any test.** It decides unit vs
  integration and points to the binding guide for each suite:
  `tests/unit/TESTING.md` and `tests/integration/TESTING.md`.

head: AGENTS > Testing
text:
- Integration tests (`tests/integration/`) are the primary mechanism: they cover every public
  collection method against the live API. Their non-negotiables (details in the guide):
  - Every test file that consumes a session-scoped `seeded_*`/`static_*` fixture carries a
    module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.xdist_group("...")`; pick the group that already
    owns the fixtures (table in the guide).
  - Shared `seeded_*` fixtures are read-only; update/delete tests create private entities and
    clean up in `try/finally`.
  - Search assertions must be scoped to `seed_prefix`, filtered to the fixture's ids, and
    wrapped in `poll_until` (`tests/utils/wait.py`); `text`/`name` params are
    fuzzy full-text queries, and other workers delete their seeds mid-run.
  - No exact-count asserts on unscoped queries.
  - Seed helpers live in `tests/integration/seeding.py`; new seed entities are appended
    (tests index into seeded lists).
  - Required env vars: `ALBERT_CLIENT_ID_SDK`, `ALBERT_CLIENT_SECRET_SDK`, `ALBERT_BASE_URL`.

head: AGENTS > Testing
text:
- Unit tests (`tests/unit/`) cover logic the SDK owns: patch/diff builders, pagination,
  `utils/` transforms, resource validators/serializers, session/auth plumbing, and repo-wide
  meta checks. Their non-negotiables (details in the guide):
  - No network, no env vars, no imports from `tests/integration/` (conftest guards enforce
    the first two).
  - Do not unit-test public collection methods. Test the collection's private pure helpers.
  - HTTP fakes only via `responses` (sync) / `respx` (async), asserting on what the SDK sends
    or how it reacts, never on assumed server behavior.
  - Patch builders cover the unset / explicit `None` / `[]` / changed / unchanged matrix.

head: AGENTS > Testing
text:
- **New or changed branching logic in a collection** (payload assembly, diffing, validation,
  batching) goes into a pure helper with unit tests in the same PR.

head: AGENTS > Testing
text:
- **Tests for a new feature or method:**
  1. Public collection method: integration test in
     `tests/integration/collections/test_<collection>.py` per the integration guide.
  2. Branching logic (payload building, diffing, validation, batching, transforms): a pure
     helper with unit tests for every behavior, per "Writing standards" in
     `tests/unit/TESTING.md` (one behavior per test, parametrize same-assertion tables,
     whole-result assertions, deterministic).
  3. New resource validator or serializer: accept, reject, and coerce unit tests plus a
     wire-format round trip.
  4. New public method: the meta tests enforce keyword-only arguments, the `max_items`
     default, docstring rules, and the collection `Methods` listing. Run
     `uv run pytest tests/unit/meta`.
  5. Bug fix: add the failing case as a test first; if it was pinned with `xfail`, remove
     the marker.

head: AGENTS > Documentation > Wording conventions (keep consistent across the SDK)
text: - No em dashes (`—`); use commas, colons, or parentheses (org language policy).

head: AGENTS > Documentation > Wording conventions (keep consistent across the SDK)
text:
- Docstrings must describe **what** a method does from the caller's perspective — never how it is wired to the backend. Banned terms in public docstrings: `endpoint`, `route`, HTTP verbs (`GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`), HTTP status codes (`HTTP 200`, `404`), `request` / `response`, `payload`, `JSON`, `diffing`, `patching`, and phrasing like "returned by the API". Keep code comments and log messages free of these too whenever a caller-neutral phrasing exists. The standard `session` Parameters line and `base_path` Attributes line ("The base API route for \<entity\> requests") are the sanctioned exceptions.
  - Wrong: `"""Update an attachment by diffing the current server state."""`
  - Right: `"""Update an attachment."""`
  - Wrong: `The updated attachment returned by the API.`
  - Right: `The updated Attachment.`
  - The ban also covers **request-mechanics phrasing**, the most common evasion: `in batches`, `batched calls`, `round trip(s)`, `re-fetched`, `its own request`, `avoids N requests`, `required by the endpoint`. Describe the caller outcome, not the wire mechanics.
    - Wrong: `Workflows are created in batches and re-fetched automatically.`
    - Right: `Created workflows are fully populated.`

head: AGENTS > Documentation > Wording conventions (keep consistent across the SDK)
text: - **Docstrings are the Ask Albert tool-search surface.** Include common user synonyms in the summary line so prompts match (e.g. `Star (pin) a project.`). When a behavior change invalidates a comparative claim in a sibling docstring (`Unlike X, ...`), update that docstring in the same PR; stale comparatives actively misdirect the agent.

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Overview
text: Celluloid is a macOS virtual camera application that captures video from a physical camera, applies real-time filters and adjustments, and outputs the processed video as a virtual camera that other apps (Zoom, FaceTime, etc.) can use.

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture
text: The app consists of two main components:

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)
text: A SwiftUI menu bar application that:

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)
text: - Captures video from physical cameras using AVFoundation

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)
text: - Applies real-time image processing (brightness, contrast, saturation, exposure, temperature, filters)

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)
text: - Writes processed frames to a shared location for the camera extension

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)
text: - Manages the camera extension lifecycle (install/update)

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)
text: - `CelluloidApp.swift` - App entry point, sets up menu bar presence

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 1. Main App (`Celluloid/`)
text: - `ExtensionManager.swift` - SystemExtensions framework integration for installing/updating the camera extension

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Architecture > 2. Camera Extension (`CelluloidCameraExtension/`)

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: **The Core Problem:** The main app and camera extension run in completely separate process contexts:

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: - Main app runs as the logged-in user

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: - Camera extension runs as `_cmiodalassistants` system daemon

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: **Why File Sharing Doesn't Work:**

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: CMIOExtensions run in an extremely restrictive sandbox. They cannot read files from:

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: - App Group containers (different user context)

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: - Create pixel buffers in memory

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: - Generate graphics (test patterns)

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: - Send frames to the video system

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Inter-Process Communication Challenge
text: **Current State:** Extension shows animated color bars (generated internally) because it cannot read the actual camera frames from the filesystem.

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Planned Solution: IOSurface
text: IOSurface provides shared GPU memory between processes. Implementation requires:

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Planned Solution: IOSurface
text:
1. **Main App:**
   - Create IOSurface with unique ID
   - Write processed frames to IOSurface
   - Broadcast IOSurface ID via Darwin notifications or XPC

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Planned Solution: IOSurface
text:
2. **Camera Extension:**
   - Receive IOSurface ID
   - Look up IOSurface by ID
   - Read frames directly from shared memory

head: Celluloid - Architecture Documentation > Planned Solution: IOSurface
text: This bypasses filesystem entirely and is the standard approach for video frame sharing on macOS.

head: DOX framework
text: - DOX is the AGENTS.md hierarchy used by this project.

head: DOX framework
text: - Agents must follow the applicable AGENTS.md chain before editing files.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - AGENTS.md files are binding work contracts for their subtrees.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Durable docs, source files, prompts, tests, and packaging metadata must stay understandable from the nearest applicable AGENTS.md plus every parent AGENTS.md above it.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Spynel is the Go application rooted in this repository. It owns chat transports, harness sessions, deterministic markdown orchestration, persisted runtime state, executable project extensions, documentation, and distribution.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Describe Spynel consistently as a classic, non-AI program that coordinates and oversees external AI/coding harnesses. It is not itself an agent and does not compete with or duplicate harness intelligence. The product relationship is one human through one assistant-facing relationship to many agents; “One human → one agent → infinite agents” is a conceptual expression of scalable leverage, never a literal resource guarantee. Use “Simplicity at scale.” as the primary slogan and “Simplicity. Leverage. Quality.” as the defining words. Do not invent capabilities, integrations, guarantees, or adoption claims when adapting this positioning to public copy.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - The retired Python prototype and the former nested Go layout are not part of the repository. Product behavior, tests, documentation, packaging, and automation use root-relative paths.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Produce one cross-platform application that hosts the styled TUI, long-running communication channels, coding-harness sessions, Markdown orchestration, and project extensions. Release archives include the sherpa-onnx native runtime beside the executable.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - `cmd/spynel` is composition only. Channels translate external messages into the provider-neutral application contract and never call a coding harness directly.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Every channel conversation and orchestrated Markdown file has an independent harness session. Persisted leases prevent duplicate orchestration and recover stale work across restarts.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Accepted human conversation messages carry private stable source identities and append-only execution/admission/terminal/cancellation correlation. The default-on live `orchestrator.retrigger_unresponded_messages` feature is owned only by the elected primary, coalesces startup/reconnect signals with a five-minute bounded 24-hour scan, fences its final reservation through provider admission under the exact election term, and uses the ordinary same-conversation communication session with relevance-first guidance and a visible handled-or-skipped response, including live local TUI transcript delivery. First upgrade creates a forward activation baseline without inspecting, inferring, backfilling, or replaying legacy history; missing or pre-activation correlation is categorically ineligible. Exact handled, active/queued, durable task/goal-linked, cancelled, prior-recovery, unauthorized, group, corrupt, and overflow cases suppress or fail closed without partial-tail dispatch. This is terminal-result recovery, not notification delivery or generated-reply redelivery; public logs/status expose aggregates only.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Every running process in one workspace participates in a single primary-server election. The owner alone runs Telegram, WhatsApp, and continuous Markdown orchestration; every TUI reaches the owner's application service over an authenticated loopback API. Primary leases carry a non-secret digest of a private per-user/per-environment installation token so a client rejects a known-foreign host/container loopback before dialing; missing or invalid identifiers remain fresh-owner fenced and receive only bounded compatibility readiness. Interactive secondary TUI startup reports connection progress before entering the alternate screen, while automation remains quiet. The first TUI in an ownerless workspace resumes the latest TUI communication session, while additional live TUIs receive independent sessions. Five-second heartbeats, a 30-second stale threshold, lock-free discovery of atomically published leases, serialized compare-and-replace takeover, and target-fenced `/primary` handoffs prevent duplicate owners while allowing secondary startup, explicit promotion, or recovery from a dead or stalled server.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - The main communication agent is a responsive dispatcher: it answers questions and reports durable state, routes finite work into tasks and long-term objectives into goals, and leaves substantive execution to independent orchestrator sessions.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - The communication agent performs bounded inspection without narrating routine tool steps, then gives one brief, natural, outcome-first result. Ordinary question, status, and delegation turns have no preamble or progress messages. Routine task and goal confirmations hide internal files, paths, IDs, metadata, lifecycle details, and orchestration mechanics; explicit detail requests and dedicated diagnostic commands such as `/status`, `/jobs`, `/tasks`, and `/goals` remain technically precise. Telegram and WhatsApp routine confirmations never contain local-path Markdown links. Agents must obtain current UTC from the environment instead of estimating timestamps written into durable Markdown state.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - The communication agent carries a framework-owned evidence-grounded honesty contract even when a workspace preserves a customized chat template. It must distinguish observation and durable or source-backed evidence from inference, uncertainty, and unknowns; never lie, fabricate evidence, invent causality, imply inspection it did not perform, or present stale or unverified claims as facts; and verify materially uncertain current, workspace-specific, causal, high-impact, completion, dispatch, delivery, release, external-state, or code-behavior claims when bounded authoritative inspection is practical. Otherwise it says that it does not know yet and offers or dispatches investigation. Corrections identify the unsupported claim and changed evidence rather than reflexively agreeing. Stable low-risk knowledge remains responsive without ritual lookup, and this behavioral contract is not represented as a mathematical guarantee of model perfection.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Runtime state, histories, WhatsApp credentials, installed extensions, and the canonical user configuration `.spynel/config.yaml` belong inside each initialized workspace's fixed `.spynel/` directory. Relative configuration paths resolve from the workspace root, and no configurable state-directory key exists. Installation identity and live process-control records belong in the OS per-user configuration directory. Automatically managed speech models live in the operating system's per-user cache under Spynel's versioned speech namespace and are shared across compatible workspaces for that user.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - Spynel is alpha software and supports only its current configuration, state, manifest, session, and workflow schemas. Validate current setting values and reject obsolete state, manifest, session, and workflow representations. Ignore unused configuration keys on load without rewriting the file; ordinary canonical saves remove them. Do not retain configuration migrations or fallback readers. Prefer one clear current representation over preserving pre-release data.

head: DOX framework > Core Contract
text: - There is no OpenAI-compatible HTTP façade. Channels, harnesses, and trusted executable hooks are extended through explicit interfaces.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - The canonical repository and Go module path is `github.com/agent0ai/spynel`; release, package, issue, and documentation links use that owner and repository.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Keep the README quick start focused on installation and launch commands plus platform/prerequisite requirements. Describe the supported platforms as macOS and Linux, without Windows caveats or promises. Do not narrate installer progress, PATH mechanics, or installation file locations there; put those details in the getting-started documentation. Keep prerequisite and uninstall data-retention information concise and remove duplicate setup instructions and speculative setup claims.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Keep the root README's public community links aligned with the Agent Zero ecosystem: the Agent Zero website and repository, Discord, X, YouTube, GitHub Sponsors, and Spynel's own GitHub Issues page. Do not add product-specific links or unsupported Spynel services.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Keep application and orchestration code harness-neutral. Codex, Claude Code, Agent Zero CLI, Pi RPC, and ACP behavior belongs in `internal/harness`; future harnesses register metadata/factories there, implement the same interface, and explicitly declare native-steer or queued follow-up behavior. ACP-compatible CLIs normally use one concise command/argument alias around the shared v1 stdio adapter; only the explicit custom ACP profile accepts a user command and shell-free argument list. Agent Zero CLI uses `a0 acp` and must pass `a0 acp --check` before discovery reports it as available.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Keep every harness scalar under `.spynel/config.yaml`'s `harness` section and require exact current catalog names and sandbox/review values after case/edge-whitespace normalization. All one-line live agent prefixes default empty. Optional harness-native commands such as `/goal` are outer-trimmed and separated from the original prompt by exactly one ASCII space immediately before dispatch; empty or whitespace-only prefixes preserve the prompt byte-for-byte. `harness.reviews` overlays task policy with `skip-trivial` (default agent-decided behavior), `always`, or `never`; enforce `always`/`never` independently of task front matter and prompt overrides, while mandatory goal outcome review remains separate.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Treat model, reasoning effort, and service mode as one atomic active-safe dispatch snapshot. Detected choices come from provider/model metadata; model and supported-harness effort pickers end with Custom text entry, available even when discovery fails. Explicit model/effort identifiers bypass discovery membership checks and let the harness validate support. Service modes remain capability-validated, ACP effort remains unsupported, and a model change clears stale properties to inherit unless an effort is explicitly supplied in that transaction.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Keep all exposed non-extension settings live behind the shared save-and-reload boundary. The only restart-bound settings are `extensions.enabled`, `extensions.directory`, and `extensions.hook_timeout`. A validated save atomically replaces canonical YAML, reloads that file into the shared process snapshot before returning, and publishes the refreshed snapshot to runtime owners; use minimal direct hooks only for owners that cache derived state. Model selection commits under the same fence as harness dispatch admission: admitted turns retain their captured model, including active native steering, while every provider dispatch snapshot ordered after the commit uses the new model, including queued continuations. Harness implementation, command, arguments, and sandbox changes remain transactional and idle-only. Subsequent operations read the refreshed snapshot, while active channels and in-flight orchestration may finish under their admitted state. Bare `spynel` deterministically launches the TUI; `spynel serve` is headless unless `--tui`, and the retired `channels.tui.enabled` input is normalized away rather than retained.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Task and goal workflows have fixed folders, prompts, transitions, and stale thresholds owned by `internal/orchestrator`; no `orchestrator.routes` setting, custom routes, or persisted route snapshots exist.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - The default CLI command is `spynel`; the project configuration file is `.spynel/config.yaml`.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - The supported v1 integration uses the elected application service: request-correlated HTTP/NDJSON messages, bounded committed conversation subscriptions and cursor replay from existing history, atomic bounded resynchronization, and ordinary outbox notifications. An optional private authenticated Unix socket supplements loopback without changing foreign-environment election fences or TUI conversation identity. Headless operational stderr mirrors only content-free lifecycle metadata through the existing runtime logger.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Keep the plain CLI equivalent to the non-visual application control plane: named disk-backed conversations, bounded streaming/NDJSON message input, active-turn follow-ups, structured status, conversation inspection/branching, attachments, shared slash commands, and trusted extension hooks must use the same application service as interactive channels.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Authenticated workspace operators see one global live and archived job, task, and goal set through Telegram, WhatsApp, TUI, CLI, and the shared application/API boundary. Assign jobs workspace-local durable numbers from 1 through 9999, wrap to 1, and preserve a job's number through recovery and archival. Numeric lookup selects the newest generation after reuse; collision-proof archive identities remain private. Workspace-local job archives retain bounded redacted event streams through the chat-history retention boundary; they are inspection-only and never workflow evidence. Conversation identity, creation channel, and durable `notify.origin` are delivery metadata, never inspection or control ACLs. Preserve transport and loopback authentication before the shared handler, prevent cross-workspace archive reads, and expose only bounded privacy-safe projections without conversation IDs, prompts, session keys, notification origins, or arbitrary durable fields.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Keep `spynel docs` as a separate harness-free, server-free interface over curated compiled documentation. Stable topic/section references, deterministic bounded text/JSON output, concise `/help` metadata, prompt guidance, and repository documentation must be validated together; static docs never read or impersonate live workspace state.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Markdown task and goal files are the durable source of state. Front matter is machine-readable; bodies and agent logs are human-readable. Tasks are single finite objectives carrying explicit boolean `review_required`; missing or malformed values fail safe to review. Choose review by expected risk reduction versus latency and cost: broad, high-risk, hard-to-reverse, security-sensitive, data/schema, infrastructure, deployment, release, migration, or materially uncertain work normally follows `todo -> working -> review -> reviewing -> done`, while read-only work and minor localized reversible changes may use `working -> done` with proportionate verification, evidence, residual uncertainty, and an exact UTC timestamp. Explicit speed or no-review guidance is honored unless material risk justifies review. Goal derivation alone never forces task review; planners choose per child task, while independent goal review remains mandatory. Goals are measurable long-term outcomes following leased planning, passive task-round execution, and independent leased review; settled tasks are evidence rather than automatic goal completion. Every claimed phase has a persisted lease and orphan/stale recovery. Task reviewers may correct and reverify only trivial localized low-risk findings; broader or uncertain findings return the same task to `todo` for implementation. A recovery agent may choose another configured outcome allowed for its owned phase when evidence proves normal order would preserve a dead end, but it must journal the condition, evidence, exception, safety boundary, and next action and may never bypass required review, live ownership, or destructive-safety constraints. Spynel journals accepted heartbeat repairs, recovery starts, deterministic corrections, scheduled wakeups, and proactive-notification outcomes in `## Progress`. Every task transition to `done`, `failed`, or `cancelled`, plus actionable unscheduled `waiting`, directly starts one ordinary asynchronous notification-agent turn with the task and ordinary notification CLI guidance. The agent alone decides whether to send and directly records its send, skip, or CLI failure in task progress. Spynel does not persist notification-agent control state, interpret provider output, write a notification result, or recover/replay the turn. Ordinary channel authorization and delivery behavior remain unchanged. Executable hooks are delivered at least once with a stable `event_id`; persist successful per-extension receipts, retry unrecorded hooks with that ID, require consumers to persistently deduplicate visible effects, and never claim exactly-once arbitrary side effects. Bounded completion summaries distinguish ordinary direct completion from independently reviewed acceptance without acting as notification-delivery state.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Shared `/tasks` and `/goals` commands inspect bounded durable Markdown state without invoking a harness. The identical contract is available through direct `spynel tasks`/`spynel goals` automation commands, the generic plain command API, the TUI, and authorized Telegram/WhatsApp messages. Bare commands default to all nonterminal work; `recent` uses `updated_at` windows of three and seven days respectively, while `active`, `review`, `waiting`, `done`, `failed`, and `all` provide semantic lifecycle views. Custom-day, bounded-limit, detail, and plain-CLI NDJSON options remain compact, newest-first, and explicit about unreadable or invalid documents.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Runtime prompt templates ship in the package and are copied into initialized workspaces so users can override them.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Every agent prompt receives one framework-owned scope-discipline rule after template rendering and before workspace-owner instructions, so stock and customized templates equally prioritize the smallest useful actions and verification. Developer and reviewer orchestration prompts additionally receive concise role-specific 80/20 guidance: implement the smallest maintainable solution for observed and realistic needs, and review practical correctness without demanding speculative completeness while flagging harmful overengineering. These rules never weaken explicit requirements or evidence-backed correctness, safety, authorization, privacy, destructive-action, data-integrity, lifecycle, independent-review, or data-handling contracts. Communication prompts additionally receive the evidence-grounded honesty contract through framework composition so ordinary saved preferences cannot remove it.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Exactly five workspace-owner persistent instruction files live under `.spynel/instructions/` as `agent-chat.md`, `agent-developer.md`, `agent-reviewer.md`, `agent-notification.md`, and `agent-heartbeat.md`. Each matching file is validated and loaded fresh as the final separated prompt section; initialization and upgrade create only missing canonical files without replacing edits, and explicit current instructions plus applicable safety and AGENTS/DOX contracts take precedence.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - The elected primary alone schedules the semantic workflow heartbeat. Its enabled state and interval apply live, scheduling is fixed-delay, and one stable provider-neutral harness session remains non-overlapping and inspectable until provider release. The framework only triggers the worker and supplies minimal primitives; agents do the work. The heartbeat agent inspects bounded durable workflow state, decides from task progress whether a user wait has been inactive long enough and a reminder is useful, uses the ordinary recent-authorized notification CLI when appropriate, and records its send/skip/failure in that task's progress. Never implement this policy as classic-runtime reminder queues, waits, timers, thresholds, eligibility logic, identity linking, correlation, acknowledgement, deduplication, retry contingencies, or reminder orchestration. Ordinary terminal and actionable unscheduled waiting transitions still start the dedicated notification agent directly.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Heartbeat and notification agents use one ordinary asynchronous job lifecycle. A successful harness `Send` is provider admission, not completion; keep the job and bounded context live through the first non-continuing terminal final/error event, cancellation, or timeout, archive every accepted event through that boundary, and settle ownership exactly once. `Codex turn started` is nonterminal. Late/duplicate terminal events are ignored, while heartbeat cadence/non-overlap remains separately fenced until provider release. Before task-notification dispatch, validate the task's enabled metadata and selected outcome, render exactly one task-evidence block as full content when safe or deterministic valid-UTF-8 beginning/recent-end excerpts with explicit untrusted middle omission when oversized, include the exact absolute authoritative path for full-file inspection, and budget the projection after all other prompt sections with a 4 KiB safety reserve below the 128 KiB boundary. Then render the absolute executable and workspace plus exact authorized origin into a shell-safe `notify --workdir ... --origin ... --message \"Hello there\"` command; the agent changes only the example message text. The ordinary CLI/API also exposes mutually exclusive `--recent-authorized` routing; it resolves only the newest user-active authorized conversation, returns only an event ID, and fails closed on multiple remote users, tied activity, revocation, unknown conversations, groups, or no eligible activity. The resolver and ordinary outbox delivery are primitives, never reminder policy.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - `/trigger` is the shared manual process interface: orchestrator passes retain serialized route ownership, and heartbeat requests enter the same non-overlapping primary scheduler as timed audits so manual completion resets the fixed delay. `/cleanup [days]` defaults to seven whole days and shares one cross-process operation with the primary-only eight-hour automatic cleanup, whose live retention setting defaults to 30 days. Cleanup uses strict older-than eligibility, protects every authenticated renewable live-TUI conversation lease (including transition grace) and every exact live job archive, serializes startup admission and resume branch creation-through-registration with history deletion, and remains fenced for one full live-lease duration after owner acquisition while attached clients renew into the replacement process. An ownerless plain-CLI cleanup also holds the election mutation lock through deletion and runs only when no primary lease exists outside the durable one-live-lease grace period after a clean release. Cleanup deletes only old histories and validated bounded job archives and moves only old terminal tasks unchanged into the cold unconfigured `tasks/archive` folder. Goal scanning and archiving share one boundary, and settled tasks remain live while linked to any nonterminal goal. Cleanup reports removed job files and bytes plus partial errors without touching active work or leases.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - `/task` and `/goal` append dedicated workspace Markdown directives to the normal communication-agent prompt; that agent creates or refines the durable document under the full workspace contract. They are not deterministic file-writing slash shortcuts.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Enabled Telegram and WhatsApp transports require valid canonical sender allow-lists and fail closed at configuration, supervisor preflight, adapter startup, every live inbound event, and every outbound/provider boundary. Each adapter resolves the current list rather than trusting its constructor snapshot; missing, malformed, unavailable, or revoked authorization publishes a persistent error, terminates the active listener/socket, and is not reconnect-retried until configuration changes. Telegram teardown may call only `deleteWebhook` after revocation so a stopped listener is never left registered; all useful provider traffic remains blocked. Persisted credentials, sessions, Telegram identity mappings, prior event authorization, group addressing, and self-chat identity never grant access alone. Telegram may persist a minimal identity learned only from an allow-list-authenticated private inbound update so username-authorized users retain stable numeric proactive origins, but every application and delivery check must reapply the current allow-list and fail closed on absent or corrupt identity state.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Telegram and WhatsApp deliver only the last non-continuing final response or terminal error for a remote message; streamed deltas, status events, and intermediate continuation responses remain visible only on streaming-capable local surfaces such as the TUI.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - The application emits one provider-neutral main communication-agent dispatch/terminal boundary consumed with overlap-safe, conversation-scoped reference semantics by the TUI, Telegram, and WhatsApp, including stalled-message recovery outside an inbound callback. Recovery routing preserves that dispatch boundary as the sole canonical owner, stops activity before terminal delivery, and never activates for scans that admit no provider turn. Ordinary Telegram messages still start visible user-turn activity at acceptance, including media/transcription preparation; slash commands wait for agent dispatch so framework-only commands remain inactive. WhatsApp translates only that canonical communication-agent lifecycle into composing, so media preparation, framework-only commands, and eventless intake remain inactive and every terminal response or handler error synchronously pauses after the final reference is released.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Preserve in-flight communication turns when follow-up messages arrive. The latest message must receive a prompt response without silently abandoning still-relevant earlier coordination or taking ownership of long-running implementation work. When adjacent ordinary messages accumulate behind a queue-mode harness, dispatch them together in arrival order using the newest bounded prompt snapshot; never merge job controls across their validation and reservation boundaries.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Job-scoped operator guidance uses the existing orchestrator session and emitter, treats delimited input as nonterminal data, preserves durable ownership and lifecycle tracking, bounds and deduplicates ordered delivery, and never equates acceptance or provider completion with a durable transition. A control message may cause at most one automatic continuation after exact owner/session/lease/document revalidation.

text: - Prefer standard-library dependencies unless a dependency materially improves reliability.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - The root POSIX `install.sh` bootstraps complete native GitHub bundles without Node/Go/compiler requirements. `internal/updater` owns installation-local markers, strict bounded checksum/archive/runtime validation, an automatically released installer lock, immutable retained releases, and the atomic `current` switch. Preserve unrelated user-bin entries and npm installations; unmanaged archives/development binaries never acquire ownership from inherited environment. The script requires a release containing its native `install-bundle` entry point.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Standalone installation must show progress and place its launcher in an existing PATH directory so the plain piped install command is followed immediately by `spynel` in the same shell, for root and regular users. Request native sudo authorization only when that directory needs elevated write access; never claim a child process changed its caller's PATH. Verify the command before reporting success and preserve unrelated executables. Explicit off-PATH overrides retain automatic shell configuration and the optional shell-safe `env` helper. Public `uninstall.sh` shares the verified bootstrap and calls native `uninstall-bundles` to remove both the marked GitHub installation and the current global npm installation. It automatically stops installation-owned processes and disables/removes matching startup registrations before removing packages, while preserving workspaces and unrelated files. Keep the README uninstall command at its end, without manual stop/disable prerequisites.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - Script-installed interactive TUIs check GitHub asynchronously with the existing ten-second/hourly policy. Shared `/update` validates and publishes their complete bundle before graceful owner shutdown and restart through the stable entry point. Automatic-startup registrations retain that stable path; headless/noninteractive launches perform no proactive checks.

head: DOX framework > Project Contracts
text: - The npm wrapper performs a ten-second update check only for interactive TUI starts, never for generated automatic-login services or noninteractive commands. It passes explicit periodic-check eligibility, the attempted lookup timestamp, and any valid latest version to the launched binary; an eligible npm-managed TUI reuses that snapshot, refreshes asynchronously no more than hourly, and shows a semantic warning triangle beside the header version only while a newer version is known. `/update check` reports npm state through every channel; `/update` stops the requesting Go process before npm replaces the package, coordinates other instance restarts, then restarts the requester through the supervising launcher.

   - `notes`: short description of what changed

head: leCore
text:
> A from-scratch, NumPy-only Vector Symbolic Architecture / Holographic Reduced
> Representation engine: memory, meaning, geometry, images, and PROGRAMS as points
> in one high-dimensional space — with calibrated abstention, self-measuring
> approximate search, deterministic bit-reproducible builds, and a measured
> pipeline that compiles programs into model weights.

head: leCore
text:
IMPORTANT for AI assistants: do not summarize this project from the file tree.
The interesting capabilities are documented in the engine's own capability
catalog, and generic prodding tests the wrong things.

head: leCore
text:
1. Read CAPABILITIES.md (the auto-generated menu of every capability, with
   plain-language descriptions, runnable examples, and search aliases).

head: leCore
text:
2. Run the proof: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python3 tools/showcase.py
   (six flagship claims as live assertions, ~2 s, laptop CPU, no GPU/torch).

head: leCore
text:
3. Ask the engine itself — it contains a semantic search engine over its own
   capabilities, and it is better at finding the right module than grep:
       import lecore
       mind = lecore.agent_boot()          # you are an agent: use this one
       mind.find_capability("prevent hallucination")
   BOOT WITH BOTH ENDS ATTACHED. `agent_boot()` is `autoboot()` plus a model
   rung, and the difference is measurable:
       lecore.UnifiedMind()      no memory at all — even doctrine answers "refused"
       lecore.autoboot()         memory in front: known questions answer at T0
       lecore.agent_boot()       ...and unknown ones ESCALATE to your model
                                 instead of stopping at T4
   It takes no arguments in a harness. The memory partition comes from
   `$LECORE_PARTITION` (falling back to ./lecore_memory, then the shipped
   release_bundle/), and the model from an OpenAI-compatible endpoint via
   `$LECORE_LLM_URL` / `$LECORE_LLM_MODEL` / `$LECORE_LLM_KEY` (`OPENAI_*` are
   read too) — which is the normal case, because YOUR MODEL IS USUALLY IN
   ANOTHER PROCESS: Claude or ChatGPT behind OpenWebUI, openzoo, ollama or a
   vendor API. Pass a base URL or a local `text -> text` callable to be explicit.
   Use plain `lecore.autoboot()` when a HUMAN is at the keyboard: agent_boot
   requires a model and would otherwise wire the person in as the back end.
   TEACH AS YOU GO. `mind.teach(question, answer)` costs nothing and makes the
   next session's answer a T0 lookup instead of a rediscovery; if the fact is
   about source files, `mind.teach_about(question, answer, [paths])` fingerprints
   them so `mind.stale_facts()` tells you when the code moved underneath it.
       mind.suggest("compress a float series")
   DECIDE, DON'T PROMPT (sweeps 171-176). For a question with a fixed set of answers, ask a TYPED
   question instead of asking your model to guess: no text, a schema, a ranked answer with a margin,
   a calibrated p_correct (HIGH = confident; None until that door has calibrated on reported outcomes),
   a p_null where the door has a null (LOW = significant), an honest abstention, and an id you report the
   outcome against. The bare "p" is deprecated (it meant opposite things at different doors).
       a = mind.typed(state, ["billing", "shipping"])       # one line: schema built, linted, scored, recorded
       mind.decision_outcome(a["id"], truth)               # the ONLY outcome path -- the table, the reflex
                                                           # and the calibration all learn from it
       q = {"cat": {"type": "choice", "options": ["billing", "shipping"],
                    "examples": {"billing": ["card charged twice"], "shipping": ["parcel lost"]}}}
       mind.systemone_lint(q, states=[state])              # the full form: lint the question BEFORE asking it
       a = mind.systemone_decide(state, q, scorer="nb")    # {"cat": {"value", "ranked", "p_correct", "p_null", "id", ...}}
       r = mind.route("smooth a bumpy mesh")               # act / choose / abstain -- tiered by default, and it
                                                           # LEARNS: a reported outcome comes first next time
       mind.verify_decision(state, answer)                 # is the served answer valid for this input?
       mind.swarm_step(state, tool, done_when=..., evidence=..., verify={"verb": ..., "args": {...}})
   FIND BY MEANING, LEARN ON THE GO (sweep 181). A taught answer is found when the question is REWORDED; an
   unsure question goes to your model as a typed choice (same row / new answer + HOW it was found / unclear) and
   the verdict is learned at once. Live answers are kept as the METHOD (tool + slots), never the value.
       m.meaning_resolve(query, verdict, by="model")       # apply a verdict (the model's JSON reply, or its dict)
       m.meaning_tool_register("price", fn)                # the tool a learned method may call in-process
       m.meaning_report()                                  # what memory learned: rows, wordings, calibration
   ONE LEARNING LOOP UNDER EVERY DOOR (sweep 182). Every door that decides -- typed, route, rank, serve,
   meaning, compose -- returns the same record (value, ranked, margin, p_correct, p_null, id), takes its
   outcome through decision_outcome(id, truth), and learns through ONE contrastive rule on its own prototype
   store with its own calibrator. The ids survive a restart once the partition is booted; a correction
   UNLEARNS the wrong answer in the reflex trace (1.000 vs 0.453 read back); serve asks the capability router
   after a memory miss ("use capability X") and its escalation carries the capability menu.
       r = mind.rank(state, ["candidate", {"text": "...", "examples": ["..."]}])   # your own candidates, same record
       mind.decision_outcome(r["id"], "the label that was right")                  # the rank door learns from it
       mind.verify_precheck(state, ["tool_a", "tool_b"])  # order actions by past verify results; never skips a verify
       mind.door_calibration_report()                     # which doors can already say p_correct
       mind.router_learn()                                # OFF by default: +1.5 points routing top-1, ~45 s, +15 MB
   Numbers, baselines and kept negatives: docs/research/BENCHMARK_sweep182_contrastive.md; syntax: section 8e.
   WRITE CODE THROUGH THE SAME LOOP. `mind.plan_change(request)` decides reuse / extend / build with the
   catalog and the source as evidence (11 of 12 on history) and hands you the build loop with a done_when
   per step; `mind.edit_verified(path, old, new, selftest_module=...)` is one edit that cannot leave the
   file broken (a failed check undoes it: 200 of 200 measured); `mind.review(paths)` finds determinism
   hazards with line numbers, undocumented public defs, duplicates and the tests to run, and returns a
   merge_ready verdict you report against. docs/TYPED_DECISIONS.md section 8b.
   The syntax reference with live-generated JSON for every door is docs/TYPED_DECISIONS.md; the
   measurements (with baselines and seed spreads) are docs/research/. Over HTTP every one of these
   is a POST /invoke with {"name", "args"}; restart the service after editing code or a new verb
   "does not exist".

head: leCore > Key facts
text: - Pure NumPy + Flask + stdlib + hashlib. No torch, no GPU, no learned weights in core.

head: leCore > Key facts
text: - Deterministic: bit-reproducible under any PYTHONHASHSEED; one stated tie rule everywhere.

head: leCore > Key facts
text: - Every claim ships with its measurement; refuted ideas are kept on record as negatives.

head: leCore > Key facts
text:
- ~847 modules, one UnifiedMind facade (33 parts, none over 2,000 lines), ~2,510 faculties, 895 catalog
  capabilities, 7,280+ tests, audits at 0/0/0.

head: leCore > Key facts
text:
- Typed decisions refuse honestly (calibrated abstention, conformal answer sets, batch FDR), learn from
  outcomes reported by id -- every door on one contrastive rule with its own calibrator, the ids surviving a
  restart -- and a reflex answers repeats from experience and unlearns a corrected answer; every claim in
  docs/research/.

head: leCore > Key facts
text:
- Optional dependencies are plugins (`holographic/plugins/`): they bind at construction, can be left out
  with `plugins=()`, and `mind.plugin_list()` is the honest preflight (available / missing / install).
  Loading is operator-only (`_plugin_load` is private); `plugin_list` / `plugin_manifest` are public.

head: leCore > Key facts
text: - Approximate search must measure its own recall on YOUR data or demote to exact.

head: leCore > Key facts
text: - Retrieval can refuse (calibrated abstention) instead of hallucinating a match.

head: leCore > Key facts
text:
- Programs compile into certified model weights (residual + conditioning +
  quantization + sha256 certificates); model files are ~250-byte RULES that
  re-bake bit-identical weights. Live models: https://huggingface.co/staccs

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices
text: Based on Playwright documentation and successful test implementations:

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > Key Principles
text: 1. **Use Web-First Assertions**: Prefer `await expect(locator).toBeVisible()` over manual waits

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > Key Principles
text: 2. **Prioritize User-Facing Selectors**: Use `getByRole()`, `getByText()`, and `getByPlaceholder()` over CSS selectors

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > Key Principles
text: 3. **Handle Strict Mode**: When multiple elements match, use more specific selectors like `getByRole('button', { name: 'Text' })`

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > Key Principles
text: 4. **Test User Behavior**: Focus on what users see and do, not implementation details

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > React-Specific Considerations
text: - **State Updates**: React state may not update immediately with `fill()`. Use `dispatchEvent()` if needed

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > React-Specific Considerations
text: - **Form Submission**: Test actual user interactions (clicking buttons, pressing keys) rather than forcing form submission

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > React-Specific Considerations
text: - **Component Interactions**: Use semantic selectors that match how users interact with the interface

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > Testing Strategy
text: - Test authentication flows and basic UI interactions

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > Testing Strategy
text: - Verify interface elements are present and accessible

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > Testing Strategy
text: - Focus on user-visible behavior rather than internal state

head: CLAUDE.md > Playwright Testing Best Practices > Testing Strategy
text: - Use mocking for external API calls to ensure test reliability

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: LLMtary is a Flutter desktop app for AI-assisted penetration testing. It accepts JSON reconnaissance data for a target, uses an LLM to identify vulnerabilities, then executes test commands to validate each finding.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Data Flow
text: 1. **Input**: User enters targets (IPs, hostnames, FQDNs, or CIDR ranges — comma or newline separated, or imported from a file) into the **SCOPE / RECON** tab, with optional exclusions and Rules of Engagement. The built-in `ReconService` then autonomously collects scan data via an LLM-guided recon loop. Recon output is stored per-target and merged into the device data.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Data Flow
text:
2. **Analysis** (2-phase): `VulnerabilityAnalyzer` runs a phased pipeline:
   - **Phase 1** — fast context discovery: CVE/version matching, DNS/OSINT, network services, SNMP. Results build a context block.
   - **Phase 2** — full vulnerability analysis: all web, AD, tech-specific, and specialized prompts, each enriched with Phase 1 context. Phase 2 findings are more targeted because they know what Phase 1 found.
   - Post-analysis: deduplication, evidence-quote validation, businessRisk-aware sort, and (if ≥2 HIGH/CRITICAL AD findings) a BloodHound-style attack chain reasoning pass.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Data Flow
text: 3. **Execution**: `ExploitExecutor` runs an agentic loop (max 10 iterations per vuln) generating and running OS commands, then determining vuln status (confirmed/not_vulnerable/undetermined). Includes OPSEC guidance injection and rate-limit detection.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Data Flow
text: 4. **Chain reasoning**: After all vulns are tested, if ≥2 are confirmed, a post-execution chain reasoning pass identifies multi-step attack paths and adds them as `AttackChain` findings.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Data Flow

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Services
text: - **`recon_service.dart`** — Autonomous LLM-guided reconnaissance engine. Runs discovery commands (nmap, DNS, web fingerprinting) and builds/enriches device JSON before analysis. Defines `ReconPhase` enum (`portScan`, `serviceBanner`, `webFingerprint`, `dnsEnum`, `osDetect`), `ReconResult` model (structured recon output that merges into device JSON), nmap XML parser, banner grabber, WAF detector, and DNS/certificate hostname extractors. The `enrichWithRecon()` static method is the integration point — call it before `VulnerabilityAnalyzer.analyzeDevice()` to enrich user-supplied JSON with automated recon data.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Services
text: - **`exploit_executor.dart`** (largest file, ~91KB) — Orchestrates the active testing loop. Builds compact context from device JSON (only ports relevant to the vulnerability), calls LLM for commands, executes them, detects stuck loops (repeated failures / unreachable target), validates whether tests actually reached the target. Includes lockout-aware spray counter (hard interception when safety threshold exceeded), subdomain takeover fast-path verification, and post-exploitation pillaging with lateral movement/persistence/domain dominance/pivoting prompts.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Services
text: - **`vulnerability_analyzer.dart`** — Fires batched analysis prompts based on target scope (internal RFC-1918 vs external/FQDN). Prompt sets: CVE matching, web app core/API-auth/logic-headers/secrets (4 passes), network services, SNMP/management, SSL/TLS, Active Directory (3 passes: credential/escalation/lateral), privilege escalation (when OS indicators present), DNS/OSINT/subdomain recon and email security (external only). Additional conditional prompts: business logic deep-dive, wireless security, network infrastructure attacks, thick client/binary protocols, supply chain analysis, cloud exposed resources, cloud infrastructure misconfig.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Services
text: - **`prompt_templates.dart`** (~70KB) — All LLM prompts. Prompts are objective-based (not tool-centric). Output format is always a JSON schema for consistent parsing. Includes post-exploitation prompts: `lateralMovementPrompt`, `persistencePrompt`, `domainDominancePrompt` — scoped by `PostExploitAccessType` and fired after vulnerability confirmation.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Services
text: - **`llm_service.dart`** — Unified interface to 6 providers: Ollama, LM Studio, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, OpenRouter.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Services
text: - **`command_executor.dart`** (~48KB) — Cross-platform shell execution with dangerous-command blocking, sudo credential caching, tool validation, and timeout protection.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Services
text: - **`device_utils.dart`** — Target classification (internal vs external), device JSON field extraction, and `CloudIndicators` detection (provider, metadata endpoint, IAM credentials, object storage, serverless, `isExternallyExposed`, `hasInternalCloudAccess`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Target Scope Classification
text: Internal targets (RFC-1918, loopback, link-local, plain hostnames) get a different analysis prompt set than external targets (public IPs, FQDNs). This distinction runs throughout `VulnerabilityAnalyzer` and `PromptTemplates`. Always check `DeviceUtils.classifyTarget()` when modifying analysis logic.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Prompt Design Convention
text: Prompts in `PromptTemplates` describe **what to check or achieve**, not **which tool to use** or **which CVE to look for**. This is intentional and must be preserved.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Prompt Design Convention
text: - **No specific tool names in analysis prompts.** Say "enumerate SMB shares" not "run enum4linux". The LLM picks the best tool available on the tester's machine. Do not add `nmap`, `sqlmap`, `metasploit`, or any other tool name as a required instruction.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Prompt Design Convention
text: - **No specific CVE IDs in analysis prompts.** Say "check for known RCE vulnerabilities in this version range" not "check for CVE-2021-44228". CVE matching is handled by `cveVersionAnalysisPrompt()`, which instructs the LLM to match observed versions against known vulnerability ranges — it does not enumerate specific CVEs.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Prompt Design Convention
text: - **Objective-first framing.** Each prompt section should start from the attacker's objective ("gain OS command execution", "extract authentication material") and describe what evidence or conditions would indicate that objective is achievable. The LLM then determines which commands and tools to use.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Prompt Design Convention
text: - **Platform-neutral language.** Avoid Linux-only or Windows-only command references in analysis prompts. The execution loop already injects OS context; analysis prompts should remain OS-agnostic.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Prompt Design Convention
text: Do not revert to tool-specific or CVE-specific examples when editing prompts.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > State Management
text: `AppState` (`widgets/app_state.dart`) is the single ChangeNotifier for the entire app. It holds vulnerabilities, command logs, LLM settings, the current project/target, and debug/prompt logs. UI widgets consume it via `Provider.of<AppState>`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Vulnerability Status Flow
text: Vulnerabilities start as `pending`. After execution they become:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Vulnerability Status Flow
text: - `confirmed` — evidence of the vulnerability was found

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Vulnerability Status Flow
text: - `not_vulnerable` — test conclusively proved no vulnerability

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Vulnerability Status Flow
text: - `undetermined` — target unreachable or inconclusive (early exit from stuck-loop detection)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Requirement
text: **LLMtary must run correctly on Windows, macOS, and Linux.** This is a hard requirement — every code change must work on all three platforms.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Requirement
text: - Shell command generation must work on the host OS. `CommandExecutor` handles OS-specific adaptations and exposes `Platform.isWindows`, `Platform.isMacOS`, `Platform.isLinux`, and a WSL detection flag. When modifying any command generation or execution logic, verify it handles all three OS code paths.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Requirement
text: - File path construction must use `path` package helpers (`join`, `dirname`, etc.) — never hardcode `/` separators.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Requirement
text: - Temp file locations, process spawning, and tool invocation all differ between Windows (PowerShell/cmd/WSL) and POSIX systems. Check `CommandExecutor` before adding any OS-level operation.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Cross-Platform Requirement
text: - Flutter desktop builds require `flutter config --enable-<platform>-desktop` and platform-specific build commands (`flutter build linux/macos/windows`). Test the analyze step (`flutter analyze`) before committing changes that touch platform-sensitive paths.
