head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy
text:
The repository-local `veil-update` skill provides procedural guidance for phnt
synchronization. It MUST comply with this policy. If skill instructions conflict
with this section, this section takes precedence.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Source Selection and Audit
text: 1. Read the old upstream commit from `VERSION_COMMIT`.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Source Selection and Audit
text:
2. Resolve the requested target commit, or the upstream default branch HEAD when
   no target was requested, and pin it by full commit SHA.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Source Selection and Audit
text:
3. Fetch both commits and verify that the old commit is an ancestor of the new
   commit. Stop when the ancestry check fails.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Source Selection and Audit
text:
4. Generate both a name-status inventory and the full diff for
   `phnt/include/` between the two pinned commits.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Source Selection and Audit
text:
5. Record an explicit disposition for every changed upstream file and every
   diff hunk: applied, already equivalent in Veil, retained for a documented
   compatibility reason, or intentionally ignored with a documented reason.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Source Selection and Audit
text:
6. A new or unclassified header, symbol family, or version macro blocks
   updating `VERSION_COMMIT`. Absence from the skill's mapping table is not
   permission to skip a change.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Semantic Reconciliation
text:
- Reconcile additions, modifications, deletions, renames, and cross-file moves.
  Do not apply a blanket preserve-existing-content rule.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Semantic Reconciliation
text:
- Retain an upstream-removed declaration only when Veil requires it for a
  documented compatibility contract.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Semantic Reconciliation
text:
- Apply related changes as one Veil module or dependency unit. Upstream file
  order does not define Veil declaration order.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Semantic Reconciliation
text:
- Treat `ntmisc.h` as a multi-domain source. Classify its changed sections by
  symbol ownership and report every section separately; do not restrict review
  to Package APIs.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > API Family Conversion
text: - Native system calls use Veil's `__kernel_entry NTSYSCALLAPI` form.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > API Family Conversion
text:
- Add a native `Zw*` declaration only when the corresponding entry is present
  in upstream `ntzwapi.h` or an authoritative WDK declaration.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > API Family Conversion
text:
- Win32k `NtUser*` and `NtGdi*` declarations use the applicable `W32KAPI` form
  and do not receive synthesized `ZwUser*` or `ZwGdi*` declarations.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > API Family Conversion
text:
- Ordinary native exports retain the applicable `NTSYSAPI` or other Veil export
  form and do not receive an automatic Zw pair.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > API Family Conversion
text:
- Preserve upstream ABI, parameter types, SAL annotations, and declaration
  order unless an SDK or WDK compatibility adaptation is required and
  documented.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Version Guard Conversion
text:
- Enumerate every `PHNT_VERSION` and `PHNT_WINDOWS_*` token present in the new
  upstream commit and provide an explicit Veil conversion before applying the
  diff.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Version Guard Conversion
text:
- Use `PHNT_WINDOWS_ANCIENT` rather than the obsolete
  `PHNT_WINDOWS_OLDEST`; map it to Veil's supported minimum,
  `NTDDI_WIN2K`.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Version Guard Conversion
text:
- Map `PHNT_WINDOWS_11_25H2` to `NTDDI_WIN11_DT` and
  `PHNT_WINDOWS_11_26H1` to `NTDDI_WIN11_BR`.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Version Guard Conversion
text:
- Do not map `PHNT_WINDOWS_11_27H2` or a later release until `Veil.h` contains
  an authoritative constant for that release.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Version Guard Conversion
text:
- Treat `PHNT_WINDOWS_NEW` as a sentinel. Do not blindly convert it to the
  newest fixed `NTDDI_*` value.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Validation and Finalization
text:
1. Complete each coherent Veil module or dependency unit before an intermediate
   build. Cross-file moves must not be validated as isolated half-applied
   changes.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Validation and Finalization
text:
2. Run `Veil.Test\BuildAllTargets.cmd` after all changes. The final process exit
   code must be 0.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Validation and Finalization
text:
3. Do not run a global `taskkill /f /im MSBuild.exe` as a normal pre-build
   action. Terminate only a verified stale process that blocks this repository's
   build.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Validation and Finalization
text:
4. Update `VERSION_COMMIT` to the pinned new SHA only after final validation
   succeeds.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Validation and Finalization
text:
5. Remove only cache content created by the current synchronization. In the
   standard procedure this is `.cache/systeminformer`; remove `.cache` itself
   only when the current task created it and it is empty.

head: AGENTS Instructions > phnt Synchronization Policy > Validation and Finalization
text: 6. Report `ntmisc.h` changes by classified section.

head: AGENTS Instructions > Error Handling Guidelines > Common Issues and Solutions
text:
| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Undefined type | Missing dependency | Check definition order; add `#include` or move definition |
| Redefinition | Duplicate in SDK/WDK | Wrap with `#ifndef _KERNEL_MODE` or version check |
| Missing SAL annotation | phnt inconsistency | Add appropriate `_In_`, `_Out_`, `_Inout_` annotations |
| Macro conflict | Name collision | Use `VEIL_` prefix or conditional compilation |

  inline assembly will be automatically rejected. Even for a small amount, it is
  preferred to keep the function as non-matching when it's trivially provable
  that it is equivalent to the original (e.g. register renaming, reordering).
  - The only exception is `asm("")` which can serve as a barrier for optimization.

head: Code Style Rules
text:
- Do not use `goto` for matching unless it is **absolutely** necessary and plausible
  that the original source code contained `goto`.

head: Code Style Rules
text:
- The naming convention are different across the game and libraries. For the most
  part, just be consistent with the code around your changes.

head: Code Style Rules
text:
- If the code matches, but it doesn't look like something that would normally be written
  by a developer, it is likely there are still compiler optimizations that should be undone.
  Common optimizations include:
  - Inlining helper functions
  - Look-up table or unsensible if-else chain. Use switch statement instead.
  - Duplicated code. The compiler can duplicate code in multiple places in the function to optimize
    control flow.
  - Complex or unsensible control flow. The compiler can deduplicate code to optimize control flow,
    especially duplicated if-conditions. In this case, the re-implementation should re-duplicate
    the code.
  - Loop unrolling.

head: Code Style Rules
text:
- Use functional style cast only for converting an `enum class` to the underlying integer type, narrowing
  a number type, or converting between signed and unsigned. Do not use C-style casts.

head: PR Rules
text:
- Do not publish a PR without human review. If the human doesn't know what
  they are doing, do not create a PR.

head: PR Rules
text: - Do not commit one-off scripts.

head: PR Rules
text: - Do not include any assembly or disassembly as code, comment, commit message or PR description

head: PR Rules
text:
- Include details of your research. e.g.:
  - Where the symbol (class/variable/function) names come from
  - For matching, if a cleaner code pattern is tried but does not match

head: PR Rules
text:
- Make the PRs small and focused, which helps review:
  - One subsystem/component per PR
  - If the change spans across a lot of components, batch them into smaller PRs

head: Agent Instructions > Import boundaries
text:
**Feature domains.** In `schemas`, `components`, `hooks`, `providers` and `utils`, a domain under
`features/` may import itself plus that partition's declared shared set — nothing else. The sets
live in `eslint.config.mjs`.

head: Agent Instructions > Import boundaries
text:
Tests and stories are exempt from both rules; production source still may not import `@msw`,
`@fixtures`, `@testUtils` or story modules. A domain name means the same thing in every partition.

head: Agent Instructions > Non-negotiables
text:
- **Imports:** always the most specific alias. No relative parent imports (`../`), no barrel
  `index.ts` files, style imports last. Import order is lint-enforced — run `lint:fix`, don't
  sort by hand. Details under [TypeScript and imports](#typescript-and-imports) below.

head: Agent Instructions > Non-negotiables
text:
- **Components:** build on `@ui` before creating anything new; new reusable primitives go in `src/components/ui`. ``/`` instead of `
`, ``/`

`/`

head: Agent Instructions > Non-negotiables
text:
- **Styling:** no `style` prop, no inline styles, no utility class strings, no concatenated
  class names. Colors and spacing come from `src/styles/variables.scss`. Prefer component
  props over new CSS; express variants as `data-*` attributes via `toDataProperties`. Write
  flat, greppable selectors — nest only modifiers of the current selector, never `&__Element`.

head: Agent Instructions > Non-negotiables
text:
- **Strings:** every user-visible string — including `aria-label`, table headers, and empty
  states — goes through `t('ns:category.key', 'Default')` with an inline default. Never
  hand-edit `src/assets/locales/**`; it's generated from code and Crowdin.

head: Agent Instructions > Non-negotiables
text:
- **Formatting:** never format money, numbers, percentages, or dates by hand. Use
  `useIntlFormatter()` / `<MoneySpan>`. Currency inputs are **cents**; percent inputs are
  **fractions**; dates take a `DateFormat` enum value, never a format string.

head: Agent Instructions > Non-negotiables
text:
- **Data:** no `useSWR` or `fetch` in feature code — use the factories in `@hooks/utils/swr`.
  `businessId` and auth are injected; never pass them from a component. When consuming a new
  backend response, **stop and ask for the API contract** rather than guessing the schema.

head: Agent Instructions > Non-negotiables
text:
- **State:** SWR owns server state, Zustand owns UI state, Context is for DI. Never mirror
  server data into a store. Never call `setState` during render, and avoid `useEffect` and
  `setState` for values you can derive — see [`src/components/SKILL.md`](src/components/SKILL.md).

head: Agent Instructions > Non-negotiables
text:
- **Stabilize deliberately:** `useCallback` only for props to `memo()`ed children or hook
  dependency arrays; `useMemo` only for expensive computations, object/array props to
  `memo()`ed children, or dependency-array values. Never memoize primitives. Do memoize object
  literals returned from custom hooks.

text: Each of these has broken something before:

head: Agent Instructions > Things to avoid
text:
- **Unmocked requests fail.** Vitest and Storybook both error on unhandled `layerfi.com`
  calls. A new endpoint needs an MSW handler **registered in the enclosing `handlers.ts`**.

head: Agent Instructions > Things to avoid
text:

  field on one endpoint and returns `null` on another.

head: Agent Instructions > Things to avoid
text:
- **Never hand-write snake_case JSON.** Mocks hold decoded fixtures and encode through the
  schema, so wire-format changes propagate automatically.

head: Agent Instructions > Things to avoid
text:

head: Agent Instructions > Things to avoid

head: Agent Instructions > Things to avoid

head: Agent Instructions > Publishing
text:
`@layerfi/components` ships from `src/index.tsx`; `prepack` runs `typecheck` plus a clean build.
See [`PUBLISHING.md`](PUBLISHING.md) and the `release-*` workflows. **Adding an export to
`src/index.tsx` is a public API change** — call it out in the PR. It also creates a subpath:
`build:exports` reads that file and generates `dist/exports/<Name>.{mjs,cjs,d.mts,d.cts}` for every
public name, so `@layerfi/components/<Name>` resolves. Nothing to maintain by hand, but the new
subpath is part of the same API commitment.

head: Agent Instructions > Publishing
text:
`build:js` produces three outputs — per-module ESM, a bundled `dist/cjs/index.cjs` for the `.`
require condition, and a per-module `dist/cjs/modules/**` reached only through the subpath shims.
The CJS barrel stays bundled on purpose: `require` never tree-shakes, so splitting it only made
`require('@layerfi/components')` slower.

text: - Converted HTML is sanitized via DOMPurify (isomorphic-dompurify).

head: WP Astro MCP Server > Security & Trust Model
text: - SQLite state in `data/wp-astro.db` (gitignored), WAL + busy_timeout for multi-process safety.

head: Agents.md
text: This file provides guidance to all AI agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, etc.) working with code in this repository.

head: Agents.md
text:
You are an experienced engineer, familiar with the platform-specific details of Android. Much of this codebase
is still Java, and reading, editing, debugging and fixing that Java is a normal, expected part of your work — fix a bug
in a Java class by editing that Java class. What is not open to choice is the language of *new* files: those are always
Kotlin. Kotlin-first means new code is Kotlin, not that existing Java is off limits.

head: Agents.md > Your Role
text: - You implement features and fix bugs.

head: Agents.md > Your Role
text: - You work on an open source project and lowering the barrier for contributors is part of your work.

head: Agents.md > Your Role
text:
- You explain your work to less experienced contributors in your chat replies and in the material the contributor uses
  for the pull request description — never as comments inside the code. Readable code is the explanation the code
  itself gets; see [Hard Rules](#hard-rules).

head: Agents.md > Hard Rules
text:
These are the rules that get broken most often. They are not preferences, and no local circumstance overrides them.
Verify each one against your own diff before you report a task as finished.

head: Agents.md > Hard Rules
text: 1. **Every new file is Kotlin.** Never create a `.java` file.

head: Agents.md > Hard Rules
text:
2. **Write comments only if needed.** No explanatory line above a function, no note next to a variable, field,
   branch or magic-free constant. Carry the meaning in names and small functions instead: if you feel the urge to
   describe *what* the code does, rename it or extract it until the description is unnecessary.

head: Agents.md > Hard Rules
text:
3. **Never grow a large file.** 300 lines is the ceiling for any file. A file already at or above it must not gain a
   single line: put the new code in a new Kotlin file — extension function, use case, mapper, state or model class —
   and keep the edit to the existing file to the minimum that wires it up. "The class was already 900 lines" is a
   reason not to add the 901st. If the task cannot be done without growing such a file, say so and
   propose the extraction before writing the code. This rule bites on new functionality: never answer "where does this
   new code go?" with "the bottom of the biggest class in the package." A fix that genuinely belongs in that file still
   goes in that file.

head: Agents.md > Hard Rules
text:
4. **Review your own diff before reporting done.** Read it as a reviewer, not as its author, and delete what you would
   ask a contributor to remove: dead code, unused parameters, redundant null checks, defensive branches that cannot be
   reached, indirection used once, leftover scaffolding, and any file you touched only incidentally. Then confirm out
   loud, in your final message, which language every new file is in and which files ended up over 300 lines.

head: Agents.md > Reference Guides
text:
`.claude/skills/` holds the detailed guidance behind the rules above: the concrete before/after transformations, so you
do not have to infer the house style from surrounding legacy code. Read the relevant guide **before** writing code, not
after a reviewer asks for changes. They apply to every agent, whichever tool you are: Claude Code loads them as skills
on demand, and every other agent can read them as plain Markdown with its file-reading tool.

head: Agents.md > Reference Guides
text:
| Guide | Read it when | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [`project-conventions`](.claude/skills/project-conventions/SKILL.md) | Any change that adds or renames a file | SPDX header form, the ≤300-line and one-top-level-type-per-file rules, magic-number and resource rules, Java-interop annotations (`@JvmStatic`, `@JvmOverloads`), commit expectations, and the verification commands that exist here |
| [`android-idioms`](.claude/skills/android-idioms/SKILL.md) | Writing any new Kotlin, or converting Java to Kotlin | How to decompose an oversized lifecycle function, scope functions (`run`/`apply`/`with`), `switch` → `when`/`partition`, extension functions and KTX over verbose Java utilities, null safety instead of platform types, `companion object` constants |
| [`fail-fast`](.claude/skills/fail-fast/SKILL.md) | Any code with preconditions, nullable values, or nested `if`/`else` | Guard-clause shapes, `require`/`requireNotNull`/`check` matched to the original exception type, flattening nested pyramids, `?: return` chains, and when *not* to invert a branch |
| [`deprecated-apis`](.claude/skills/deprecated-apis/SKILL.md) | Touching activity results, fragment menus, or observer callbacks | Activity Result API instead of `startActivityForResult`, `MenuProvider` instead of `onCreateOptionsMenu`, and why a behaviour-locked conversion keeps `java.util.Observable` rather than silently moving to Flow |

head: Agents.md > Reference Guides
text:
Precedence: where a guide and the [Hard Rules](#hard-rules) appear to disagree, the Hard Rules win — flag the
contradiction to the contributor instead of quietly picking one. The guides use examples from the wider
nextcloud/android codebase; the principles transfer, the specific class names do not exist in this repository.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy
text: All contributions generated or assisted by this agent must fully comply with:

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy
text: - **[AI Contribution Policy](https://github.com/nextcloud/.github/blob/master/AI_POLICY.md)** - the primary reference for AI-specific rules, covering disclosure, author accountability, communication, security, licensing, code quality, and autonomous agent behavior.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy
text: - **[Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/nextcloud/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)** - covering testing requirements, the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO), license headers, conventional commits, and translations. These apply in full to all contributions regardless of how they were produced.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must always do
text: - Add an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` git trailer to every commit containing AI-assisted content.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must always do
text: - Ensure every pull request includes a disclosure of AI tool use in the PR description.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must always do
text: - Produce focused, scoped pull requests that address exactly one concern. Do not touch unrelated files or introduce incidental refactors.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must always do
text: - Verify all dependencies against actual package registries before suggesting them. Do not use hallucinated or unverified package names.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must always do
text: - Explicitly inform the contributor when any action they are about to take, or have taken, would violate the AI Contribution Policy or the Contribution Guidelines. Do not silently proceed. State which rule is at risk and what the contributor should do instead.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must always do
text: - Warn the contributor if a pull request is growing too large. A PR approaching several thousand lines of changed code is a signal that it should be split into smaller, focused PRs. Suggest a logical split before the PR is opened, not after.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must always do
text: - Recommend opening a ticket for discussion before starting implementation whenever a feature or change is sufficiently complex - for example when it touches multiple subsystems, requires architectural decisions, or the right approach is not yet clear. A ticket allows maintainers and the contributor to align on direction before code is written, avoiding wasted effort on a PR that may be rejected or require fundamental rework.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must never do
text: - Open issues, submit pull requests, post review comments, or send security reports autonomously. Every contribution must be reviewed and submitted by a human.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must never do
text: - Add `Signed-off-by` tags to commits. Only the human contributor can certify the Developer Certificate of Origin.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must never do
text: - Generate or submit security reports without independent human verification. Report verified vulnerabilities via [HackerOne](https://hackerone.com/nextcloud), not as GitHub issues.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must never do
text: - Write PR descriptions, review comments, or issue reports on behalf of the contributor. These must be in the contributor's own words.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must never do
text: - Fully automate the resolution of issues labeled [`good first issue`](https://github.com/issues?q=org%3Anextcloud+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) or similar beginner-friendly labels.

head: Agents.md > Nextcloud Contribution Policy > What this agent must never do
text: - Submit code that has not been reviewed and cleaned up by the contributor. Dead code, redundant logic, excessive comments, and unrelated changes must be removed before submission.

head: Agents.md > Project Overview
text:
Nextcloud Notes for Android — a notes management app that syncs with a Nextcloud server. Kotlin is the language of the
project; the large amount of Java still present is legacy that is being migrated away from, not a style to follow.
Targets API 28+ (minSdk 28, targetSdk 36). Uses Nextcloud Single Sign-On (SSO) for authentication.

head: Agents.md > Build Commands
text: Build output: `app/build/outputs/apk/`

head: Agents.md > Build Flavors
text:
| Flavor   | App ID                              | Purpose           |
|----------|-------------------------------------|-------------------|
| `fdroid` | `it.niedermann.owncloud.notes`      | F-Droid release   |
| `play`   | `it.niedermann.owncloud.notes`      | Google Play       |
| `dev`    | `it.niedermann.owncloud.notes.dev`  | Development builds|
| `qa`     | `it.niedermann.owncloud.notes.qa`   | Per-PR testing    |

head: Agents.md > Architecture
text: The app follows MVVM with a clear layered structure. All source lives under `app/src/main/java/it/niedermann/owncloud/notes/`.

head: Agents.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **Persistence layer** — `persistence/`: Room database (`NotesDatabase.java`, version 29 with migrations 9–29), `NotesRepository.java` as single source of truth, and `ApiProvider.java` which caches per-account Retrofit instances for `NotesAPI`, `OcsAPI`, `FilesAPI`, `ShareAPI`, and `UserStatusAPI`.

head: Agents.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **Sync** — `SyncWorker` (WorkManager background sync) and `NotesServerSyncTask` handle server synchronization.

head: Agents.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **ViewModel layer** — per-feature ViewModels (`MainViewModel`, `CategoryViewModel`, `ManageAccountsViewModel`, etc.) expose data to the UI via LiveData.

head: Agents.md > Architecture > Key Layers
text: - **UI layer** — traditional XML layouts. Activities/Fragments per feature area. `MainActivity` is the main entry point post-login.

head: Agents.md > Architecture > Authentication
text: Uses Nextcloud Android-SingleSignOn (SSO). Accounts are managed via `SingleSignOnAccount` / `SingleAccountHelper`. `ApiProvider` creates and caches Retrofit instances per SSO account, avoiding repeated reflection overhead.

head: Agents.md > Architecture > Feature Package Structure
text:
| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `main/` | Note list, navigation drawer, multi-select, grid/list toggle |
| `edit/` | Note editor fragments, category/title editing |
| `persistence/` | Room DB entities/DAOs, repository, API interfaces, workers |
| `branding/` | Server-driven Nextcloud theming via `BrandingUtil` / `NotesViewThemeUtils` |
| `shared/` | Common models (`Capabilities`, `ApiVersion`), utils, RxJava extensions |
| `widget/` | Two widget types: single note preview and note list |
| `exception/` | Global exception handling with tip/suggestion system |
| `importaccount/` | SSO account import flow |

head: Agents.md > Architecture > Database
text: Room database version 29. Migrations 9–24 are manual Java migrations; 25–29 use Room auto-migrations. Schema JSON files are in `app/schemas/`. Entities: `Account`, `Note`, `CategoryOptions`, `Capabilities`, `ShareEntity`, `SingleNoteWidgetData`, `NotesListWidgetData`.

head: Agents.md > Architecture > Reactive Programming
text: RxJava 2 is used throughout for async operations. Kotlin extensions for RxJava live in `shared/`. New code should prefer coroutines/Flow where practical.

head: Agents.md > General Guidance
text:
Every new file needs to get a SPDX header in the first rows according to this template. 
The year in the first line must be replaced with the year when the file is created (for example, 2026 for files first added in 2026).
The commenting signs need to be used depending on the file type.

head: Agents.md > General Guidance
text:
XML:
```xml
<!--
  ~ Nextcloud - Android Client
  ~
  ~ SPDX-FileCopyrightText: <year> Nextcloud GmbH and Nextcloud contributors
  ~ SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
-->
```

head: Agents.md > Design
text: - Follow Material Design 3 guidelines

head: Agents.md > Design
text: - In addition to any Material Design wording guidelines, follow the Nextcloud wording guidelines at https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/latest/developer_manual/design/foundations.html#wording

head: Agents.md > Design
text: - Ensure the app works in both light and dark theme

head: Agents.md > Design
text: - Ensure the app works with different server primary colors by using the colorTheme of viewThemeUtils

head: Agents.md > Commit and Pull Request Guidelines > Commits
text: - All commits must be signed off (`git commit -s`) per the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO). All PRs target `master`. Backports use `/backport to stable-X.Y` in a PR comment.

head: Agents.md > Commit and Pull Request Guidelines > Commits
text: - Commit messages must follow the [Conventional Commits v1.0.0 specification](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#specification) — e.g. `feat(chat): add voice message playback`, `fix(call): handle MCU disconnect gracefully`.

head: Agents.md > Commit and Pull Request Guidelines > Commits
text:
- Every commit made with AI assistance must include an `AI-assistant` trailer identifying the coding agent, its version, and the model(s) used:
  ```
  AI-assistant: Claude Code 2.1.80 (Claude Sonnet 4.6)
  AI-assistant: Copilot 1.0.6 (Claude Sonnet 4.6)
  ```
  General pattern: `AI-assistant: <coding-agent> <agent-version> (<model-name> <model-version>)`
  If multiple models are used for different roles, extend the trailer with named roles:
  ```
  AI-assistant: OpenCode v1.0.203 (plan: Claude Opus 4.5, edit: Claude Sonnet 4.5)
  ```
  Pattern with roles: `AI-assistant: <coding-agent> <agent-version> (<role>: <model-name> <model-version>, <role>: <model-name> <model-version>)`

head: Agents.md > Commit and Pull Request Guidelines > Pull Requests
text: - Include a short summary of what changed. *Example:* `fix: prevent crash on empty todo title`.

head: Agents.md > Commit and Pull Request Guidelines > Pull Requests
text: - **Pull Request**: When the agent creates a PR, it should include a description summarizing the changes and why they were made. If a GitHub issue exists, reference it (e.g., “Closes #123”).

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text:
The bullets below are the summary; [`project-conventions`](.claude/skills/project-conventions/SKILL.md) and the other
[Reference Guides](#reference-guides) show what each one looks like in practice.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: [//]: # (REUSE-IgnoreStart)

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Every new file is Kotlin, no file exceeds 300 lines, and code carries no comments — see [Hard Rules](#hard-rules).

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Line length: **120 characters**

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Standard Android Studio formatter with EditorConfig.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Indentation: 4 spaces, UTF-8 encoding

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Do not use decorative section-divider comments of any kind (e.g. `// ── Title ───`, `// ------`, `// ======`).

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Every new file must end with exactly one empty trailing line (no more, no less).

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - All new files must include an SPDX license header: ` SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later `

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Translations: only modify `values/strings.xml`; never the translated `values-*/strings.xml` files

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Create models, states in different files instead of doing it one single file.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Do not use magic number.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Apply fail fast principle instead of using nested if-else statements.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Do not use multiple boolean flags to determine states instead use enums or sealed classes.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text:
- When you must edit an existing Java class, use modern Java — Optionals, records, streams where they genuinely help.
  This applies to edits inside files that are already Java; it is never a reason to create a new Java file.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: - Avoid hardcoded strings, colors, dimensions. Use resources.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text:
- Run `./gradlew lintFdroidDebug` and `./gradlew testFdroidDebugUnitTest`, and fix every finding inside the files you
  changed.

head: Agents.md > Code Style
text: [//]: # (REUSE-IgnoreEnd)

head: Agents.md > Testing
text: - **Unit tests**: `app/src/test/` — JUnit 4, Mockito, Robolectric. Uses `includeAndroidResources = true`.

head: Agents.md > Testing
text: - **Instrumented tests**: `app/src/androidTest/` — Espresso, requires running device/emulator.

head: Agents.md > Testing
text: - Parallel test execution enabled (max forks = processors / 2).

head: Agents.md > Testing
text: - Code coverage via JaCoCo (enabled for debug builds).

head: Agents guidance for Weblate
text:
This file captures agent-specific guidance for working in the Weblate codebase.
For application-developer workflows and broader product integration guidance, use
`docs/devel/` instead of repeating that material here.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Project overview
text:
- Weblate is a Django-based web translation platform with Celery background
  tasks.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Project overview
text: - The primary stack is Python, Django, JavaScript, and HTML/CSS/Bootstrap.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text: - Follow existing Django patterns and project conventions.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text: - Prefer the repository's configured Ruff-based formatting and linting rules.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Use human-readable Ruff rule names in overrides, such as
  `# ruff: ignore[assert]`; do not use or rewrite them to cryptic codes such as
  `# noqa: S102`, `# ruff: N801`, or `# ruff: noqa: F841`.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Prefer type hints and use `from __future__ import annotations` in Python
  modules.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Use `TYPE_CHECKING` imports for type-only dependencies when that avoids
  runtime import cycles.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Add new user-configurable model fields to the existing REST serializers, API
  documentation, schema, and API behavior tests for that model. Review write
  permissions and validation explicitly. Keep secrets, computed state, and
  intentionally internal fields unexposed, and document the reason when the
  omission is not self-evident.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Do not add tests that duplicate OpenAPI schema expectations covered by the
  tracked snapshot in `docs/specs/openapi.yaml`; schema changes are visible
  during review. Allow focused tests of configuration-dependent behavior that
  the snapshot cannot cover, and parsing and validation of served schema
  documents without asserting fixed schema contents. Keep other tests focused
  on API behavior, permissions, validation, schema endpoint availability, and
  documentation UI integration.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- All translatable user-facing strings must use Django i18n helpers. New
  messages introduced exclusively for API responses must not be localized. API
  responses may reuse localized messages generated by code shared with the UI,
  including model, form, and validator errors. Do not disable localization,
  replace shared messages with API-specific English messages, or require
  separate UI/API messages solely to enforce nonlocalized API responses. Do not
  flag reuse of shared localized messages as a review issue.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Messages written to persisted storage, such as the audit log, add-on log, or
  changes, should not be localized.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- In templates, use `{% translate %}` / `{% blocktranslate %}` for translatable
  text.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Preserve accessibility and the existing Bootstrap/jQuery-based frontend
  patterns. For user-facing HTML, CSS, or JavaScript changes, follow
  `ACCESSIBILITY.md` and `docs/contributing/frontend.rst`, including keyboard
  navigation, visible focus, semantic controls, labels/errors, and
  non-color-only state.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Write commit messages using the Conventional Commits format
  `<type>(<optional scope>): <description>`. Common types include `feat`,
  `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, and `chore`. Example:
  `fix(translations): handle empty component slug`. Include a concise commit
  body describing the motivation. When the commit resolves an issue, add a
  `Fixes #123` clause.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Pin dependencies to exact versions using `==`. Use a non-exact constraint
  only when there is a deliberate reason, and document that reason next to the
  dependency declaration, as is done for `certifi` to allow newer certificate
  bundles.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Code expectations
text:
- Keep new project code under GPL-3.0-or-later and include the repository's
  usual copyright and SPDX license header in new Python files.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Documentation expectations
text:
- Match the style of the surrounding page in `docs/`; prefer clear, direct,
  instructional prose with short paragraphs over marketing language or large
  rewrites.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Documentation expectations
text:
- Preserve the existing structure and heading hierarchy. Prefer extending an
  existing section over creating a new one, and keep headings in sentence case
  to match the current documentation.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Documentation expectations
text:
- Use Sphinx and reStructuredText conventions already present in the docs:
  prefer semantic cross-references such as `:ref:`, `:doc:`, `:guilabel:`,
  `:setting:`, `:wladmin:`, `:file:`, and `:program:` instead of raw links,
  repeated explanations, or ad-hoc formatting.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Documentation expectations
text:
- Keep documentation changes scoped and additive when possible. Avoid
  unnecessary rewrites or structure changes, especially because the
  documentation is translated.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Documentation expectations
text:
- Document every new configuration option. Document native Django settings in
  the appropriate settings documentation, typically `docs/admin/config.rst`,
  and Docker-exposed environment variables in
  `docs/admin/install/docker.rst`. Update both documentation surfaces when an
  option is available through both mechanisms.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Documentation expectations
text:
- Use admonitions, screenshots, and code blocks only when they add concrete
  value and match the style of the surrounding page.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Documentation expectations
text:
- Keep manually maintained explanations in the main documentation pages. In
  `docs/snippets/`, do not hand-edit content inside autogenerated marker
  blocks; manual explanatory text outside those blocks is preserved by the
  generator and can be edited when appropriate.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text:
- Be careful with repository, webhook, and file-handling code; validate inputs
  and avoid introducing path traversal, command injection, or script injection
  risks.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text: - Handle VCS operations defensively and surface failures cleanly.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text: - Mock external VCS operations and API calls in tests.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text:
- Review `docs/security/threat-model.rst` when changing public endpoints,
  authentication or token modes, deployment modes, backup or import formats, VCS
  execution paths, outbound integration classes, add-on execution capabilities,
  or security-relevant defaults for hooks, HTTPS, rate limits, CSP,
  private-network access, or backup import limits.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text:
- Review does not necessarily require an edit. Update the threat model in the
  same change only when its scope, actors, trust boundaries, assumptions,
  claimed security properties, or triage dispositions change or leave a gap,
  following its "Conditions that change this model" section. Features covered
  by existing guidance do not need individual entries. Keep feature-level
  endpoint, permission, configuration, implementation, and limit details in
  the relevant feature or administration documentation; link to them only when
  needed to explain a distinct boundary, exception, or triage outcome.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text:
- For user-visible changes, add or update a changelog entry in the top section
  of `docs/changes.rst` for the upcoming release.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text:
- Do not alter changelog sections for already released versions; put follow-up
  entries in the current unreleased section instead.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text:
- Keep changelog entries concise and link to the relevant documentation for the
  feature instead of embedding long explanations in the changelog itself.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Weblate-specific guardrails
text:
- Minor fixes and fixes for features that have not been released yet do not
  need a changelog entry.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > GitHub discussions
text:
- GitHub organization discussion URLs such as
  `https://github.com/orgs/WeblateOrg/discussions/19794` can still belong to the
  `WeblateOrg/weblate` repository. When working with these URLs, resolve the
  discussion through `WeblateOrg/weblate` repository discussions instead of
  treating the URL as an issue, pull request, or organization-only object.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > GitHub discussions
text:
- Use GitHub discussion-aware tooling, such as `gh api graphql` against
  `repository(owner: "WeblateOrg", name: "weblate") { discussion(number: ...) }`,
  when the regular GitHub issue or pull request connectors do not expose the
  discussion.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Testing and linting instructions
text:
- Select test fixtures by their identifying fields or retain the object returned
  when creating them. Do not use an unordered queryset's first row when the
  assertion depends on which row was selected. Use an explicit `order_by()`
  when order is the behavior under test.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Testing and linting instructions
text:
- Complex data migrations must have populated upgrade tests in `ci/run-migrate`:
  add old-version setup and post-upgrade assertion scripts in
  `ci/migrate-scripts/`, gated to applicable source releases. Seed data that
  exercises conditional branches and cross-app relationships, and verify the
  resulting data, not just successful migration execution. Empty-database runs
  and helper tests against the latest schema do not detect missing migration
  dependencies or premature access to future columns. Use historical models
  from `apps.get_model()` and declare dependencies for the models accessed.
  Keep migration database access independent of current model helpers.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Testing and linting instructions

  in `docs/contributing/start.rst` (`devcontainer` section). Run
  `./scripts/devcontainer up`, then use `./scripts/devcontainer exec --` before
  the commands below. Run `./scripts/devcontainer doctor` to diagnose setup,
  and `./scripts/devcontainer bootstrap` after dependency changes. The test
  environment uses PostgreSQL and Valkey; it does not start application workers.

head: Agents guidance for Weblate > Testing and linting instructions
text:
- Use `pytest` to run the test suite: `uv run pytest`. On a fresh checkout,
  first follow the local test setup in `docs/contributing/tests.rst`
  (`DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=weblate.settings_test`, `collectstatic`, and test
  database prerequisites). `scripts/test-database.sh` can be sourced to set up
  the database connection variables such as `CI_DB_USER`, `CI_DB_PASSWORD`,
  `CI_DB_HOST`, and `CI_DB_PORT`. If tests cannot reach the configured
  PostgreSQL server, do not assume it is stopped: local sandboxing can block
  access to an already-running service. Retry with permission to access the
  local service when sandboxing is the cause. Only when PostgreSQL is confirmed
  not to be running, and it is installed as a local Linux service, try
  `sudo service postgresql start` and rerun the failed command. Treat service
  startup as a recovery step, not a prerequisite for every test invocation. If
  you start PostgreSQL this way, stop it with `sudo service postgresql stop`
  after the retry, whether the command succeeds or fails, so no service process
  is left running when the task finishes.

head: Agent Guide > Commands
text: From `apps/web/` unless noted. Always `pnpm`, never `npx`/`npm`.

head: Agent Guide > Commands
text: **The checks are CI's**, all of them on every push; locally a session runs only the tests of what it touched, and the pre-commit hook formats what is staged (the `running-checks` skill).

head: Agent Guide > Commands
text: From the repo root: `pnpm i` after a manifest change, `pnpm update:node [version]` to bump node everywhere, `pnpm graph:gen` for `dependency-graph.svg`. In a package that gained, renamed or lost a module file: `pnpm build` regenerates its barrel, which is all a sibling typechecking against its source needs. Migrations are generated from `packages/db-schema/` and applied at app startup, never from the CLI — the `drizzle` skill owns all of it.

head: Agent Guide > Commands
text: On Windows, Vitest runs only because `apps/web/configuration/modules.ts` keeps a minimal Nuxt module allowlist under `process.env.VITEST` — loading the full set crashes the config load while `@vite-pwa/nuxt` resolves its virtual register module (the error and the probe that retires the fork are in `apps/web/content/docs/architecture/test-harness-workarounds.md`). A test needing an excluded module adds it to the Vitest branch there.

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: Working is not finished. Once the change does what it should — a feature, a fix, a refactor, a docs pass, anything — run this before saying it is done. Steps 1–3 are an audit with a table of its own, which the `finishing` skill owns and `/finishing` runs at any point in the work, asked or not:

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: 1. **`/code-review` over what you changed.** Both lanes, unprompted, every time: quality (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude) and correctness (defects, broken conventions). A first draft of anything non-trivial leaves duplicated copy, a constant restated in two files, a twin of an existing helper, or a special case that belonged in the shared mechanism — that gets found here, not by a reviewer. The `code-review` skill owns the lanes, which rules a window loads, the trigger rule a finding must carry, and the stop rule.

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: 2. **Ground the result in tests — only where a test earns its line.** This step deletes at least as often as it adds. Add the regression test for what the review exposed; add nothing another enforcer already owns (typecheck, a Zod constraint, an existing test), because such a test cannot fail honestly and only pins today's implementation; and trim the tests the change made redundant. The full criterion is the `testing` skill's "What to Test".

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: 3. **Carry the docs and skills with it.** A shipped decision updates its owning docs page and, if it is a reusable convention, its owning skill (the `docs` skill and the `skill-authoring` skill) — in the same change, never "later". A rename owes the same sweep over prose: grep the old name across `content/docs`, `.agents/skills`, `.agents/ledgers` and the READMEs, and fix the flow diagrams that label an edge with it. A behaviour change owes that sweep with no name to grep, so the lookup runs the other way: list the pages whose `Key files` table names a source you changed, and read each one's prose and diagrams against what the code now does. No test fails on a name that only lives in a sentence, and none fails on a sentence that was true last week.

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: 4. **The tests of what the change touched**, once at the end and **in the background** while the session keeps working — the paths the change touched, passed as arguments, plus, where a change moved bytes into a bundle, that package's own suite, since only a fresh build moves its size snapshot. Nothing else runs locally: typecheck, lint and format are CI's on the push (step 6).

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: 5. **Commit the coherent chunk by pathspec, then `pnpm ai:queue:push`.** The collector rewrites `origin/ai/queue` behind every window, so the local branch goes stale the moment one ports; the script replays from the fork point only what the sessions committed since and pushes plain — never a bare `--force-with-lease`. A dirty tree is another session's and never stashed: the script replays in a throwaway detached worktree instead, so only a conflicting replay makes the push wait (the `review-queue` skill). Step 4 does not stand in the way: a queue push starts no review, so the push goes out and the tests run against the same tree beside it. Anything they turn up is a commit behind it.

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: 6. **Watch the push's CI run, and fix its typecheck and lint.** The run is watched in the background like the tests, and a red typecheck or lint job is the session's own, not left for later: read the job's failed log, reproduce it with that one check, fix it, and push a commit behind it, then watch again until both are green. Only a red that reaches `main` is the collector's repair (`apps/web/content/docs/infra/review-collector/repair.md`, and the `running-checks` skill).

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: Skip step 1 only for a genuinely one-line change. When a step finds nothing, say so — that is a result.

head: Agent Guide > Finishing a change
text: Carrying one settled convention across code that predates this ritual is a **sweep**: one file per sweep in `.agents/ledgers/`, tracked as repo state rather than as a proposal, and run per the `sweeps` skill. A sweep is not only a job someone schedules — **when the change edits a file inside a unit an open ledger still lists as unswept, sweep those files first, in their own commit ahead of the behaviour change**, so the ledger drains as a by-product of ordinary work. Scope it to the files being touched, keep the two commits apart, and leave the row alone: coverage tracks whole units, and there is no partially-swept state.

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Project Overview
text: Cron job scheduler with YAML/JSON and traditional crontab support, using `github.com/robfig/cron/v3` for scheduling, HTMX v2 for web UI, and SQLite with WAL mode for persistence.

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Core Packages
text: - **app/service**: Core scheduler implementation with `DayParser` for business day templates, `LogPrefixer` for command-specific logging

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Core Packages
text: - **app/crontab**: Parser supporting traditional crontab and YAML/JSON with embedded JSON schema validation

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Core Packages
text: - **app/conditions**: Conditional execution with semaphore-based concurrency control (default: 10 concurrent checks)

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Core Packages
text: - **app/web**: Web UI server implementing `JobEventHandler` interface, uses Go templates with `html/template` and `embed`

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Core Packages
text: - **app/web/enums**: Type-safe enums generated via `go-pkgz/enum` for `JobStatus`, `EventType`, `Theme`, `SortMode`, `FilterMode`

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Core Packages
text: - **app/notify**: Notification service for job completion/failures

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Core Packages
text: - **app/persistence**: SQLite persistence with `sqlx` and `modernc.org/sqlite` driver

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Key Dependencies
text: - **Scheduling**: `github.com/robfig/cron/v3` with standard 5-field parser (not seconds-based)

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Key Dependencies
text: - **Database**: `github.com/jmoiron/sqlx` with `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go driver, native DATETIME support)

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Key Dependencies

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Key Dependencies

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Key Components Architecture > Key Dependencies
text: - **YAML validation**: `github.com/invopop/jsonschema` for config validation

Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Interface Design Patterns > Minimal Interface Principle

text: Functions return concrete `*SQLiteStore` while accepting `Persistence` interface for flexibility.

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Template System
text: - Uses `html/template` with `embed` for static files

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Template System
text: - **CRITICAL**: Templates and static files embedded at compile time - **must rebuild after any changes**

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Template System
text: - Template helper functions are pure (no dependencies): `humanDuration`, `timeUntil`, `since`, `ago`, `runDuration`, `clock`, `deref`; `describeSchedule` renders cron specs in plain words via `lnquy/cron` (`app/web/schedule.go`)

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Template System
text: - Partials: `jobs.html` (table, tabs, search, alert), `inspector.html` (job inspector and run output), `runform.html` (run dialog and acceptance toast), `settings.html`, `neighbors.html`; all parse from one glob into one template set

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > HTMX Integration Patterns
text: - **Out-of-band updates**: `hx-swap-oob="innerHTML"` for updating multiple elements in single response

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > HTMX Integration Patterns
text: - **Auto-refresh polling**: the table polls with `hx-trigger="load, every 5s, refresh-jobs from:body"` and `hx-include="#search, #selected-job"`; the inspector's live part polls itself with `hx-include="#insp-output"`; a recorded run's output does not poll, a run in progress (`#live-out`, `GET /api/jobs/{id}/live-output?start=<unix micro>`) polls itself every 5s until it is recorded, then that response is the recorded run's output, matched by start time

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > HTMX Integration Patterns
text: - **Request ordering in the inspector**: every request that fills `#inspector` or `#insp-output` syncs on `#inspector` - clicks with `:replace`, the live-output poll with `:abort` - so a click always wins over a poll; `uiCloseInspector` fires `htmx:abort` on `#inspector` before emptying it. The status poll (`#insp-live`) is not synced

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > HTMX Integration Patterns
text: - **OOB from a replaceable element is lost**: htmx 2 resolves OOB targets from the requesting element's root node, so a response to a button the status poll has since replaced drops its OOB updates (the main swap still lands). State that must follow a click goes inside the swapped fragment, not out of band

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > HTMX Integration Patterns
text: - **Inspector header dot**: the header (`.insp-h`) holds the focused heading and is rendered once per open, so its status dot (`#insp-dot`) is refreshed by the status poll: the `part=live` response is `inspector-live-poll`, the live part plus the dot as an OOB fragment. The full `inspector` render includes plain `inspector-live`, without the OOB copy

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > HTMX Integration Patterns
text: - **Response coordination**: `HX-Refresh: true` header triggers full page refresh when needed

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > HTMX Integration Patterns
text: - **Event coordination**: Custom events like `refresh-jobs` coordinate updates between components (used by toggle, sort, filter)

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > HTMX Integration Patterns
text: - **Lazy-load dropdowns**: Native `<details>/<summary>` with `hx-trigger="toggle once"` for dropdowns that fetch content on first open (used in neighbors selector)

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Event-Driven Architecture
text: - Server implements `JobEventHandler` interface to receive job events

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Event-Driven Architecture
text: - Events processed asynchronously via channel with goroutine

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Event-Driven Architecture
text: - Job state updated in memory immediately, persisted separately during sync cycles

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Event-Driven Architecture
text: - **Runs in progress**: `OnJobStart` carries `LiveOutput func() string` (nil when `--log.exec-max-lines=0`), a reader of the run's web capture, which spans all repeater attempts. The server keeps each run in progress in `Server.active` by job and start time, since one job can overlap itself (no `--dedup`, or a manual run with an edited command). `IsRunning` is derived from what is left there, and a finished run is recorded before it leaves the active set, so a poll finds it in one or the other

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Cookie-Based Preferences
text: Theme, sort-mode, filter-mode stored in HTTPOnly cookies with 1-year expiration. The cookies only set a fresh page's modes: each tab sends its own `filter` (hidden `#filter-mode`) and `sort` (`#sort-mode`) with every list request, and `getSortMode`/`getFilterMode` prefer those, so a change in one tab never leaks into another.

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > CSS Architecture
text: - **CSS Custom Properties**: light tokens in `:root`, dark under `[data-theme="dark"]`; the login page keeps its own `--color-*` tokens

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > CSS Architecture
text: - **Container queries on `.app`**: at 1180px and up the inspector docks beside the table; below that it is a fixed overlay drawer, full screen under 600px; 44px touch targets below 1180px; phone rows become two-line blocks under 720px

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > CSS Architecture
text: - The run dialog becomes a bottom sheet under 600px (media query, since a modal dialog sits outside the container)

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > CSS Architecture
text: - **Focus ring**: the global `:focus-visible` outline is drawn in the dashboard only after a Tab press and until the next pointer press. `ui.js` keeps that state in `data-keynav` on `<html>`, and `:where([data-keynav="false"]) :focus-visible` removes the outline. A browser treats Esc as keyboard use too, so without the gate a mouse user who closes the inspector or run dialog with Esc gets a ring on the row, and again after each poll re-focuses it. The login page loads no `ui.js` and keeps the ring

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Dashboard: Table, Inspector, Run Dialog
text: - One job table (`jobs-table`) with no alternative views. Rows carry `data-job-id`; the `.job-open` name button opens the inspector

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Dashboard: Table, Inspector, Run Dialog
text: - **Selection state**: the selected job lives in the hidden input `#selected-job` outside every polled target, set by OOB fragments and sent with each table poll. The selected run travels inside the output it selected: each `.out` fragment carries a hidden `selected-run` input (a recorded run's id, or `live:<start>` for a run in progress), so the runs list highlight always matches the output on screen

head: Cronn Project Architecture Knowledge > Web UI Architecture > Dashboard: Table, Inspector, Run Dialog
