head: AirwayLab
text: Open-core sleep/airway analysis tool for CPAP/BiPAP users. Parses ResMed SD card data (EDF format), runs four independent analysis engines entirely in the browser, and provides AI-powered therapy insights via Claude Haiku.

head: AirwayLab > Stack
text: Next.js 14 (App Router) · TypeScript (strict) · Tailwind CSS 3.4 · shadcn/ui with @base-ui/react · Recharts 3.8 · Supabase (EU region, RLS always on) · Vercel · Anthropic Claude Haiku · Vitest · Web Workers

head: AirwayLab > Privacy Architecture
text: AirwayLab has a two-tier architecture:

head: AirwayLab > Privacy Architecture
text: **Tier 1 — Browser-only (default):** All core analysis runs client-side in a Web Worker. EDF files are parsed, flow data extracted, and all four engines execute without any network request. Results persist in localStorage (`airwaylab_` prefix, 30-day expiry, 4MB cap). No data leaves the browser. Ever.

head: AirwayLab > Privacy Architecture
text: **Tier 2 — Server-enhanced (opt-in):** Users can explicitly opt in to features that require server communication: AI-powered insights (sends metrics, never raw waveforms), data contribution (anonymised aggregate metrics to Supabase), and premium features behind the `ailab-beta-2026` gate. Every server interaction requires informed, affirmative consent.

head: AirwayLab > Privacy Architecture
text: The distinction matters for every feature decision: if it touches user health data and doesn't have explicit consent, it must stay in Tier 1.

head: AirwayLab > Build & Verify
text: Always run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` before considering work done.

head: AirwayLab > Directory Structure
text: **⚠️ PROTECTED modules** (`lib/parsers/`, `lib/analyzers/`, `workers/`): These contain clinically validated algorithms. String changes (comments, logs) are fine, but never modify logic without explicit discussion and clinical understanding.

head: AirwayLab > Analysis Engines > Glasgow Index (`lib/analyzers/glasgow-index.ts`)
text: Ported from DaveSkvn/GlasgowIndex (GPL-3.0). Scores inspiratory flow shapes on 9 components (0–1 each): skew, spike, flatTop, topHeavy, multiPeak, noPause, inspirRate, multiBreath, variableAmp. Overall score = sum of all 9 components, range 0–9. Pipeline: findMins → findInspirations → calcCycleBasedIndicators → inspirationAmplitude → prepIndices. Multi-session nights use duration-weighted averaging.

head: AirwayLab > Analysis Engines > WAT — Wobble Analysis Tool (`lib/analyzers/wat-engine.ts`)
text: Three metrics: FL Score (inspiratory flatness, 0–100, higher = worse), Regularity (Sample Entropy on minute ventilation, higher = more irregular), Periodicity Index (FFT power in 0.01–0.03 Hz band, detects periodic breathing at 30–100s cycles). Includes a Cooley-Tukey radix-2 FFT implementation.

head: AirwayLab > Analysis Engines > NED — Negative Effort Dependence (`lib/analyzers/ned-engine.ts`)
text: Per-breath analysis: NED = (Qpeak − Qmid) / Qpeak × 100, Flatness Index = mean/peak, Tpeak/Ti ratio, M-shape detection (valley < 80% Qpeak in middle 50% of inspiration). RERA detection: runs of 3–15 breaths with progressive FL features evaluated by NED slope, recovery breath, and sigh detection. Estimated Arousal Index (EAI): respiratory rate + tidal volume spikes vs 120s rolling baseline. Night summary includes H1/H2 split and combined FL percentage.

head: AirwayLab > Analysis Engines > Oximetry Pipeline (`lib/analyzers/oximetry-engine.ts`)
text: 17-metric framework from Viatom/Checkme O2 Max CSV data. Cleaning pipeline: buffer zone trimming (15min start, 5min end), motion filter, invalid sample removal, SpO2 range validation (50–100), HR double-tracking correction. Metrics: ODI-3/ODI-4 (2min rolling baseline), HR Clinical surges (30s baseline, 8/10/12/15 bpm thresholds), HR Rolling Mean surges (5min baseline, 5s sustain), coupled events (ODI + HR within ±30s), desaturation time, summary stats, H1/H2 splits.

head: AirwayLab > Component Patterns
text: - **Server Components by default.** Only add `'use client'` when state, effects, or browser APIs are needed.

head: AirwayLab > Component Patterns
text: - **shadcn/ui with @base-ui/react** — NOT Radix primitives. Check `components/ui/` for available primitives.

head: AirwayLab > Component Patterns
text: - **Dashboard tabs** use the shared `Tabs` component. Each tab receives `NightResult` data and renders independently.

head: AirwayLab > Component Patterns
text: - **Metric cards** use `MetricCard` with traffic light colours from `thresholds.ts`.

head: AirwayLab > Component Patterns
text: - **Charts** use Recharts 3.8. All chart components include an "airwaylab.app" watermark.

head: AirwayLab > Component Patterns
text: - **Auth state** flows through `AuthProvider` (context) → `useAuth()` hook. Feature gating via `canAccess()` and the `ailab-beta-2026` gate.

head: AirwayLab > Component Patterns
text: - **Insights** are generated by `generateInsights()` — rule-based, 6 categories (glasgow, wat, ned, oximetry, therapy, trend), 4 types (positive, warning, actionable, info), sorted by priority, capped at 6 per night.

head: AirwayLab > Component Patterns
text: - **Threshold system**: `THRESHOLDS` defines green/amber/red boundaries per metric. `getTrafficLight(value, threshold)` returns the colour tier. All threshold colours use Tailwind classes (`text-emerald-500`, `text-amber-500`, `text-red-500`).

head: AirwayLab > Testing Conventions
text: - **Framework:** Vitest 4.0 with jsdom environment and `@testing-library/jest-dom` matchers.

head: AirwayLab > Testing Conventions
text: - **Location:** `__tests__/*.test.ts(x)` — flat directory, one file per module.

head: AirwayLab > Testing Conventions
text: - **Naming:** `{module-name}.test.ts` matching the source file name.

head: AirwayLab > Testing Conventions
text: - **Pattern:** Each test file creates synthetic data via helper functions (e.g., `makeSineWave`, `makeFlatToppedWave`) rather than using fixture files. This keeps tests self-contained and fast.

head: AirwayLab > Testing Conventions
text: - **What's tested:** All four analysis engines, insights generator, export functions, persistence, thresholds, upload validation, metric explanations. Focus is on value ranges, boundary conditions, and comparative behaviour (e.g., "flow-limited data scores higher than normal").

head: AirwayLab > Testing Conventions
text: - **Path alias:** Tests use `@/` imports resolved to project root.

head: AirwayLab > Testing Conventions
text: - **Run:** `npm test` (single run) or `npx vitest` (watch mode).

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 1. **Privacy-first with opt-in sharing.** Core analysis is browser-only. Server features require explicit consent. This is a non-negotiable architectural constraint, not a preference.

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 2. **Two-tier architecture.** Free tier (Tier 1) is complete — all engines, insights, exports, persistence. Premium tier (Tier 2) adds AI-powered analysis behind the `ailab-beta-2026` feature gate. Premium funds development; it does not gate essential analysis.

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 3. **Tiered models, cost-constrained.** Community insights use Claude Haiku; premium uses Claude Sonnet 4.6 for higher-quality analysis (`app/api/ai-insights/route.ts`). Cost constraint for a side project with a 2hr/week maintenance budget. Do not change models without discussion.

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 4. **localStorage persistence.** Results persist for 30 days under `airwaylab_results` key with a 4MB cap. Bulk data (per-breath arrays) is stripped before serialisation. Date objects are restored on load. Migration guards handle schema evolution (e.g., `estimatedArousalIndex` added in v0.6.0).

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 5. **Web Workers for analysis.** The analysis worker (`workers/analysis-worker.ts`) runs all parsing and engine computation off the main thread. It yields control periodically (every 25 EDF files parsed, every 10 nights analysed) to prevent browser lockup on large SD cards.

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 6. **EDF parsing quirks.** ResMed EDF files use 2-digit years (year < 85 → 2000s, else 1900s). BRP.edf files contain flow waveforms. STR.edf contains machine settings. Identification.tgt contains device model. Sampling rates vary by device (typically 25 Hz for AirSense 10).

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 7. **Supabase EU region.** GDPR requirement. RLS must be enabled on every table before use. Auth is Supabase Auth only — no OAuth/social login.

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 8. **Open-core model (GPL-3.0).** The Glasgow Index engine is ported from DaveSkvn/GlasgowIndex (GPL-3.0), which requires the entire project to be GPL-3.0. This aligns with the mission: open data, open code, verifiable trust.

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 9. **Dark-default theme with light option.** Dark is the default clinical aesthetic. A light theme is available via Settings > Display Preferences for accessibility. Both themes use HSL CSS variables defined in `globals.css` (`:root` for dark, `[data-theme="light"]` for light) and referenced in `tailwind.config.ts`. Preference persists in `airwaylab_theme` localStorage key.

head: AirwayLab > Key Design Decisions
text: 10. **Rule-based insights before AI.** The insight generator (`lib/insights.ts`) uses deterministic rules and clinical thresholds, not ML. AI insights (Claude Haiku) are an optional enhancement, not a replacement.

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - TypeScript strict — no `any`, no `@ts-ignore` unless documented why

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Server Components by default, `'use client'` only when state/effects are needed

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Zod for all external data validation (API inputs, file uploads, env vars)

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Named exports — default exports only for page/layout components (Next.js requirement)

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Tailwind only — no CSS modules, no styled-components, no inline styles

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Branch per feature (`feat/`, `fix/`, `chore/`), never commit directly to main

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - `airwaylab_` prefix for all localStorage keys

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Plus Jakarta Sans (body) + JetBrains Mono (code/data)

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Error messages: never expose raw errors to users; map to user-friendly text

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - **Every catch block must have visible error handling.** Enforced by `airwaylab/no-silent-catch` ESLint rule (`scripts/eslint-rules/no-silent-catch.mjs`). Catches must include Sentry reporting, user-visible error state (setState), re-throw, or a documented `eslint-disable-next-line` with justification. Console-only catches and empty `.catch(() => {})` handlers are flagged as errors. Fire-and-forget patterns (IDB cleanup, non-critical side effects) require an inline comment explaining why silence is safe.

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Medical compliance: all AI-generated insights must include "discuss with your clinician" language

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Legal pages: Privacy Policy (`/privacy`), Terms of Service (`/terms`), Accessibility (`/accessibility`), Contact (`/contact`) — keep updated when data flows change

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Every page that collects or displays health data must include the medical disclaimer component

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Every server feature that sends data externally must have an explicit consent step — no implicit consent via feature gates alone

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Every new API route must log the action type + user ID (anonymised if unauthenticated) for audit purposes

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Account deletion requests must be fulfillable within 30 days — any new data store must have a documented deletion path

head: AirwayLab > Conventions
text: - Any new third-party integration must be added to the Privacy Policy's processor list before deployment

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow
text: **This workflow is mandatory.** The root failure mode: AI-generated code passes automated checks but introduces subtle UI, integration, and logic bugs that compound across features. The fix is friction between "code generated" and "code in production."

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Pipeline
text: `spec → build → test → review → verify (human) → merge → post-deploy check`

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Pipeline
text: Full process details live in the internal pipeline prompts (`prompts/spec.md`, `prompts/build.md`), kept local and out of this public repo. This section defines the rules; the prompts define the how.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Scope Gates
text:
| Tier | When | Process | Examples |
|------|------|---------|----------|
| **Full spec** | New features, engine changes, API routes, privacy/consent, protected modules | `prompts/spec.md` → `prompts/build.md` (all agents) | New analysis metric, AI insights flow, auth changes, data contribution |
| **Light spec** | UI changes, refactors, significant bug fixes | Write the step template (files, tests, manual QA). Review + all 5 checks + preview verification. | Dashboard layout change, component refactor, broken loading state |
| **No spec** | Near-zero regression risk | Standard PR with all 5 checks. Quick visual check on preview. | Blog posts, copy changes, dependency bumps, CSS-only tweaks, docs |
| **Batch fixes** | Known issues with clear scope from audits/issues | Validate findings against codebase, implement directly, pipeline, PR. No architecture design. Skip feature-dev. | Zod validation gaps, missing rate limiters, dep cleanup, test gaps |

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Scope Gates
text: When in doubt, use the tier above. **Do not use `/feature-dev` for batch fixes.** Feature-dev's 7-phase workflow (explore, architecture, clarify) is designed for new features with unknown scope. For audit findings and known fixes: validate, implement, ship.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 1. **Spec before build.** Full-tier changes start with `prompts/spec.md`. Specs are saved to `specs/` as persistent files.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 2. **One concern per PR, max 400 lines.** No bundling unrelated changes.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 3. **Tests ship with the code.** No separate "test:" PRs.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 4. **All 5 checks must pass before PR:** `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npm run lint` + `npm test` + `npm run build` + `npx playwright test` (for UI changes).

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 5. **Human QA before merge.** Demian verifies Vercel preview deploy. ALL manual QA boxes must be checked. Partial pass = no merge.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 6. **One step at a time.** Do not start the next spec step until the current PR is merged and verified in production.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 7. **Protected module changes are isolated.** Own PR, never bundled with other changes.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 8. **Max 3 feature PRs per day.** Ship, verify, observe.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 9. **Fix-on-fix = red flag.** Stop. Revert if merged. Re-spec the area.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Shipping Rules
text: 10. **Bundle size budget.** Flag any PR increasing bundle >10KB. LCP must stay under 2s.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Remote/Headless Session Handoff
text: Remote Claude sessions (launched via `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` or background tasks) MUST follow this protocol:

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Remote/Headless Session Handoff
text: 1. **Output = GitHub issue, not PR.** Create an issue with findings, not a docs PR or implementation. Findings go stale; issues are actionable.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Remote/Headless Session Handoff
text: 2. **Never implement fixes.** The remote session lacks interactive context to make design decisions. It discovers; a human-supervised session implements.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Remote/Headless Session Handoff
text: 3. **Validate before reporting.** Check the current codebase state before claiming something is missing. `Glob` + `Grep` first.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Remote/Headless Session Handoff
text: 4. **One branch, no uncommitted work.** If any code was written during exploration, either commit it on a clearly-named branch or discard it. Never leave uncommitted changes for another session to inherit.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: 1. **Assess severity.** Core analysis broken → revert immediately. Cosmetic/secondary → hotfix branch.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: 2. **Revert first, investigate second.** `git revert <commit> && git push`.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: 3. **Hotfix via light spec.** Review + all 5 checks + preview verification. No shortcuts.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: 4. **Post-incident note** on the PR: what broke, why, what the spec/review missed.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: **Database rollback is different, code revert alone is not enough.**

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: - **Migrations are additive and forward-only.** Never write a destructive down-migration to roll back. If a migration is wrong, the fix is a new forward migration, not editing or deleting the applied one. Merged `supabase/migrations/` files are immutable.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: - **Code vs schema order.** Because migrations are additive-first (schema lands before the code that needs it), a bad CODE deploy reverts cleanly with `git revert` while the harmless extra schema stays. A bad MIGRATION needs a forward corrective migration, applied and real-path-verified via the `awl-migration` skill before the corrective code merges.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: - **Destructive change (drop/rename/backfill).** Stop and escalate. Not revertible by `git revert`. Recover from a backup or point-in-time restore (verify which is enabled for the project) against a fresh branch DB, verify, then cut over. Never run a destructive statement on prod without a tested restore path.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: - **Verify the real path, not HTTP 200.** Confirm recovery through the real consumer path (a real event reaching terminal good state), per `scripts/awl-smoke.sh --confirmed` and the `verify-real-path-post-deploy` lesson.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Rollback Protocol
text: - **Ownership and rehearsal.** Demian owns the rollback decision. Rehearse the restore-to-branch path once on a non-incident day so it is not first attempted under fire.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Post-Deploy Verification
text: After merge, "verified" means ALL of these:

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Post-Deploy Verification
text: 1. **Smoke test** — Upload SD card data on airwaylab.app. Full pipeline: upload → parse → analyze → all dashboard tabs.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Post-Deploy Verification
text: 2. **Feature check** — The specific feature from the QA checklist works on production.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Post-Deploy Verification
text: 3. **Regression spot-check** — 2-3 adjacent features that share components or state.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Post-Deploy Verification
text: 4. **Console check** — DevTools shows no new errors or warnings.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Post-Deploy Verification
text: 5. **Mobile check** — Changed area renders correctly on mobile viewport.

head: AirwayLab > Development Workflow > Post-Deploy Verification
text: 6. **Sentry watch** — Monitor for 5 minutes immediately. Check again 24 hours later.

head: AirwayLab > Migration Numbering Convention
text: Migration files in `supabase/migrations/` are numbered sequentially. Collisions cause silent data loss or failed deployments.

head: AirwayLab > Migration Numbering Convention
text: 1. **Always read `NEXT_MIGRATION` first.** Before writing any new migration file, read `supabase/migrations/NEXT_MIGRATION` to get the next available number.

head: AirwayLab > Migration Numbering Convention
text: 2. **Increment `NEXT_MIGRATION` in the same commit.** Any PR that adds a migration file must also update `NEXT_MIGRATION` to the subsequent number in the same commit.

head: AirwayLab > Migration Numbering Convention
text:
3. **Reserve numbers with stub files for manual prod changes.** If a migration is applied directly to prod (e.g. a hotfix), immediately commit a stub file:
   ```
   supabase/migrations/{N}_manually_applied.sql
   ```
   with this header:
   ```sql
   -- Applied manually to prod on YYYY-MM-DD. Do not re-run.
   ```
   This reserves the number in the repo so future PRs cannot reuse it. Increment `NEXT_MIGRATION` in the same commit.

head: AirwayLab > Migration Numbering Convention
text: 4. **Never reuse or skip numbers.** Migration numbers are permanent. Gaps are acceptable; collisions are not.

head: AirwayLab > Migration Numbering Convention
text: **Before opening a migration PR:** verify that your file's number matches `NEXT_MIGRATION`. If another PR has already claimed that number, bump your number and update `NEXT_MIGRATION` again.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never send health data without consent.** No analytics on waveform data, no silent uploads, no background syncing. If data leaves the browser, the user must have opted in.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never exceed the 4MB localStorage cap.** Strip bulk data (per-breath arrays, raw waveforms) before persisting. Pre-flight size check in `persistence.ts`.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never modify engine logic without clinical understanding.** The engines implement published respiratory analysis methodologies. A "refactoring" that changes threshold values or algorithm steps can produce clinically incorrect results.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never modify, rescale, or transform Glasgow scores.** The Glasgow component scores (0–1 per component, 0–9 overall) are clinically validated metrics from the Glasgow Index methodology. Visualisation code must adapt the chart scale to fit the data — never change the data to fit the chart. This applies to all presentation layers (charts, tooltips, exports, reports).

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never create API routes without auth middleware.** Every `app/api/` route must validate authentication.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never use `console.log` in production.** Use `console.error` with structured context for debugging; these flow to Vercel logs + Sentry.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never hardcode secrets.** Use `process.env` with Zod validation. Add new vars to `.env.example`.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never install dependencies without discussion.** Each dependency is maintenance cost against the 2hr/week budget.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never use `any` or `@ts-ignore`.** If TypeScript complains, the types are wrong — fix them.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never present analysis as medical advice.** Always include "discuss with your clinician" language. This is a consumer health tool, not a medical device.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never deploy a new third-party data integration without updating the Privacy Policy.** The processor table in `/privacy` must reflect all services that receive user data.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never store health data server-side without documenting retention period and deletion mechanism.** Every table with health-related data must have a documented retention schedule and a path to deletion for DSAR requests.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never add automated decision-making (AI/ML) features without an explicit user consent step.** GDPR requires informed consent for automated processing of health data. Use the `AIConsentModal` pattern or similar.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never remove or weaken medical disclaimers from any output.** All exports (CSV, JSON, PDF, forum), reports, AI insights, and chart images must include the standard disclaimer language.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never merge without Vercel preview verification.** Passing CI is necessary but not sufficient. Demian must verify the preview deploy before merge.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never bundle unrelated changes in one PR.** Each PR addresses exactly one concern. A feature + unrelated e2e tests = two PRs. A bug fix + a refactor = two PRs.

head: AirwayLab > Anti-Patterns
text: - **Never ship more than 3 feature PRs in a single session.** If bugs compound across features, the cost of debugging exceeds the value of shipping fast.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **Flat directory structure.** There is no `src/` directory. `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `workers/` are at the project root.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **EDF date parsing.** 2-digit years: < 85 → 2000s, ≥ 85 → 1900s. Date format is `dd.MM.yy`.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **Float32Array vs number[].** Flow data uses `Float32Array` for memory efficiency. These are not serialisable to JSON — `persistence.ts` strips them before saving.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **Duration-weighted averaging.** Glasgow Index uses duration-weighted averaging across sessions within a night. Don't simple-average multi-session results.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **H1/H2 split.** NED and Oximetry results include first-half / second-half comparisons. The split point is the midpoint of the concatenated data, not midnight.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **Sampling rate varies.** Don't hardcode 25 Hz. Use the rate from the parsed EDF header.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **Oximetry is optional.** `NightResult.oximetry` can be `null`. Always null-check before rendering oximetry metrics.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **Duplicate files.** The repo contains macOS-created duplicates (e.g., "file 2.tsx"). These should be cleaned up when encountered but are not functional files.

head: AirwayLab > Common Gotchas
text: - **Feature gate check.** Premium features use `canAccess('ai_insights', tier)` — always check before exposing premium functionality.

       encoded_url = quote(original_url, safe='')

           f"&awinaffid={AFFILIATE_CONFIG['publisher_id']}"

text: Custom CSI escape sequences with `<` prefix to avoid conflicts with standard xterm.js sequences. These are used both by key handlers (sent to `terminal.write`) and directly testable via `XTermElement.write()`:

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > TypeScript Component Details > `xterm-console-mixin.ts` — Console feature
text:
| Sequence | Param | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `\x1b[<H` | — | Cursor home: moves to start of logical line, then forward past prompt |
| `\x1b[<E` | — | Cursor end: moves to end of logical (possibly wrapped) line |
| `\x1b[<L` | n (default 1) | Cursor backward wrapped: moves left n chars, crossing line boundaries |
| `\x1b[<R` | n (default 1) | Cursor forward wrapped: moves right n chars, crossing line boundaries |
| `\x1b[<B` | — | Backspace (wrapped): moves back then deletes char, handles wrapped lines |
| `\x1b[<D` | n (default 1) | Delete n chars (wrapped): shifts remaining chars left across wrapped lines |
| `\x1b[<K` | 0/1/2 | Erase in logical line (extends standard erase-in-line across wrapped rows) |
| `\x1b[<N` | — | Linefeed/Enter: fires `line` DOM event with current line text |

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > Key Internal Details
text: - **Initialization sequence:** `XTermBase` constructor → appends light-DOM `<div slot="terminal-container">` → client `_slotchange()` fires in `requestAnimationFrame` → `terminal.open(div)` → fires `terminal-initialized` → server drains `deferredCommands`.

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > Key Internal Details
text: - **Deferred commands vs. return values:** All `void` JS calls made before `terminal-initialized` are buffered in `deferredCommands` and replayed. Any call returning a `CompletableFuture` before initialization throws `IllegalStateException` immediately.

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > Key Internal Details
text: - **Custom CSI prefix `<`:** The console mixin uses the `<` intermediate byte (`0x3C`) in CSI sequences to namespace all its operations. Standard xterm.js sequences never use this prefix, so there is no conflict.

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > Key Internal Details
text: - **`_onData` Enter routing:** The LitElement `_onData` handler replaces `\r` with `\x1b[<N\n` before writing to the terminal. This routes the Enter key through the console mixin's CSI handler, which reads `currentLine` and fires the `line` DOM event.

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > Key Internal Details
text: - **Vaadin version compatibility in `ClientTerminalAddon`:** `encodeWithTypeInfo` is resolved at runtime via `MethodHandle` lookup — uses `com.vaadin.flow.internal.JsonCodec` (Vaadin ≤24) or `com.vaadin.flow.internal.JacksonCodec` (Vaadin ≥25). Never hard-code this path.

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > Key Internal Details
text: - **GraalVM native image:** `src/main/resources/META-INF/native-image/…/proxy-config.json` and `reflect-config.json` are pre-configured for the dynamic proxy (`XTermBase` static initializer) and field reflection (`TerminalTheme.asJsonObject()`).

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > Key Internal Details
text: - **`Position.advance()` mutates:** The `Position` helper class's `advance()` method modifies the instance in place and returns `this`. Use `plus()` to get a new instance without mutation.

head: XTerm Console Addon — Claude Guide > Key Internal Details
text: - **`TerminalHistory` is not a `TerminalAddon`:** It does not extend `TerminalAddon` and is not registered via `registerServerSideAddon`. It is attached to the component via `ComponentUtil.setData`. Only one instance per terminal is allowed.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox
text: Cross-platform native sandbox for running arbitrary commands in isolated environments.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox
text:
| Platform | Isolation engine | Root | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Linux (`ch`)** | Cloud Hypervisor micro-VM (KVM) + virtiofsd + smoltcp netstack | not required (kvm group) | Preferred when `/dev/kvm` + `/dev/vhost-vsock` + `cloud-hypervisor` binary available |
| **Linux (`bwrap`)** | bubblewrap (user namespaces) + smoltcp netstack | not required | Auto-fallback; ~50 ms start, no VM |
| **macOS** | Apple Virtualization.framework → Linux micro-VM + smoltcp netstack | not required | ~2 s cold |
| **Windows** | Hyper-V HCS → Linux micro-VM + smoltcp netstack via SYSTEM service | one-time install | ~600 ms |

head: tokimo-package-sandbox
text: All backends present the same `Sandbox` handle with identical semantics: configure → create → start → spawn shells → stop. A single init binary (`tokimo-sandbox-init`) runs as PID 1 (or PID 2 inside bwrap) in every sandbox, speaking the same wire protocol regardless of transport. Networking is unified: every backend uses the same smoltcp userspace netstack for `AllowAll`.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox
text: **Linux backend selection** (`SANDBOX_BACKEND` env):

head: tokimo-package-sandbox
text:
| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| (unset) / `auto` | Probe `ch` first; fall back to `bwrap` if unavailable |
| `ch` | Force Cloud Hypervisor; fail if unavailable |
| `bwrap` | Force bubblewrap; fail if unavailable |
| `disabled` | Refuse to construct any backend |

head: tokimo-package-sandbox
text: `Sandbox::active_backend()` returns the concrete backend chosen at runtime.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Public API
text: A single [`Sandbox`](src/api/mod.rs) handle exposes a command-style RPC interface (~30 methods). Backed by a per-platform [`SandboxBackend`](src/api/backend.rs) trait implementation:

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Public API
text: Key types exported from `src/lib.rs`: `Sandbox`, `SandboxBackend`, `ConfigureParams`, `ShellOpts`, `Mount`, `NetworkPolicy`, `Event`, `JobId`, `HostExecCtx`, `HostExecAction`, `HostExecCallback`, `SessionSummary`, `SessionDetails`, `PortForwardSpec`, `Error`, `Result`, `SandboxBackendKind`, `ActiveBackend`, `FontDir`.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — two backends, one API
text: The Linux platform layer probes for Cloud Hypervisor at `Sandbox::connect()` time and picks the strongest backend that works on the host. CH is preferred (real KVM isolation, full kernel boundary, identical posture to macOS/Windows); bwrap is the fallback (no VM, fastest startup, works without `/dev/kvm`).

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — two backends, one API
text: Both backends share **everything except the isolation primitive**: the same `tokimo-sandbox-init` PID 1 binary, the same `FuseHost` + `tokimo-sandbox-fuse` FUSE infrastructure, the same smoltcp netstack, the same protocol frames. Only the transport wiring differs (SEQPACKET socketpairs vs. hybrid-vsock UDS sidecars).

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — Cloud Hypervisor (`ch` backend)
text: - **No daemon, no service, no root.** Each `Sandbox` owns its own `cloud-hypervisor` + `virtiofsd` process group.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — Cloud Hypervisor (`ch` backend)
text: - **Same packaged kernel + initrd + rootfs** as macOS/Windows (`vm-kernel-*` + `vm-rootfs-*` tag artifacts).

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — Cloud Hypervisor (`ch` backend)
text: - **vsock transport** uses CH's *hybrid-vsock* — host plays vsock by listening on per-port UDS files instead of `/dev/vhost-vsock`. All channels (init, netstack, FUSE, console) are guest-initiated.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — Cloud Hypervisor (`ch` backend)
text: - **File sharing** ConfigureParams mounts use `virtiofsd`. Runtime `add_mount` still uses FUSE-over-vsock through the same `FuseHost` as other backends.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — Cloud Hypervisor (`ch` backend)
text: - **Networking:** `AllowAll` uses the same smoltcp userspace netstack. `Blocked` omits the network device.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — Cloud Hypervisor (`ch` backend)
text: - **PTY:** Master fd stays in guest; init bridges I/O through protocol events over vsock.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — bubblewrap (`bwrap` backend)
text: - **No daemon, no service, no root.** Each `Sandbox` owns its own bwrap+init pair.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — bubblewrap (`bwrap` backend)
text: - **Packaged rootfs.** `/usr /bin /sbin /lib /lib64 /etc/passwd /etc/group` come from `.vm/base/rootfs/` (same artifact as macOS/Windows). Only network/DNS/CA config is bound from the host.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — bubblewrap (`bwrap` backend)
text: - **Networking:** Both `AllowAll` and `Blocked` use `--unshare-net` with a fresh netns. `AllowAll` layers smoltcp on top via TAP (`tk0`), bridged to host through STREAM socketpair. `Blocked` gets only `lo`.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — bubblewrap (`bwrap` backend)
text: - **File sharing:** All mounts use **FUSE-over-socketpair** — same `FuseHost` + `tokimo-sandbox-fuse` as macOS/Windows. Each mount gets an `AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM` socketpair; host end served by `FuseHost`, guest end passed to `tokimo-sandbox-fuse` via `--transport unix-fd`.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Linux — bubblewrap (`bwrap` backend)
text: - **PTY:** Master fd transferred to host via `SCM_RIGHTS` for direct I/O.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > macOS — Virtualization.framework
text: - **No service, no root.** Library-only; each `Sandbox` boots its own VM.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > macOS — Virtualization.framework
text: - **Shared filesystem:** All mounts use **FUSE-over-vsock** — host runs in-process `FuseHost` on vsock port 5555, each mount spawns a `tokimo-sandbox-fuse` child in guest that connects back via vsock. Same infrastructure as Linux and Windows.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > macOS — Virtualization.framework
text: - **Networking:** `AllowAll` uses host-side **smoltcp userspace netstack**. `Blocked` omits the network device.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > macOS — Virtualization.framework
text: - **PTY:** Master fd stays in guest; init bridges I/O through protocol events over vsock.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Windows — Hyper-V HCS
text: - **SYSTEM service** manages VMs on behalf of unprivileged users. One-time install via `sudo ... --install` or MSIX.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Windows — Hyper-V HCS
text: - **Per-session isolation:** Each session gets a unique VHDX clone and HvSocket service GUID, supporting concurrent sessions.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Windows — Hyper-V HCS
text: - **Networking:** `AllowAll` uses the same **smoltcp userspace netstack** as macOS. `Blocked` sets `tokimo.net=blocked` in kernel cmdline.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Architecture > Windows — Hyper-V HCS
text: - **PTY:** Same as macOS — master in guest, I/O bridged through protocol.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Userspace network stack
text: All backends use the same **smoltcp-based L3/L4 proxy** (`src/net/netstack/`) for `NetworkPolicy::AllowAll`. One unified netstack, one interception point, regardless of platform or Linux backend choice.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Userspace network stack
text: - **Dual-stack IPv4/IPv6** with extension header walking (HopByHop, Route, Opts, Frag)

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Userspace network stack
tokimo-package-sandbox > Userspace network stack
text: - **3 threads:** RX reader (transport → smoltcp), main poll loop, TX writer (smoltcp → transport)

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Userspace network stack
text: - **120 s idle timeout** per flow

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared init binary (`tokimo-sandbox-init`)
text: A single Rust binary that runs as PID 1 (or PID 2 in bwrap) inside **every** sandbox on **every** platform. Auto-detects its transport at startup:

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared init binary (`tokimo-sandbox-init`)
text:
| Transport | Used by | PTY mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `SOCK_SEQPACKET` (inherited fd) | Linux bwrap | `SCM_RIGHTS` fd transfer |
| VSOCK stream (guest connects) | Linux ch (hybrid-vsock) | Protocol bridge (Stdout/Write events) |
| VSOCK stream (guest listens) | macOS VZ | Protocol bridge (Stdout/Write events) |
| VSOCK stream (guest connects) | Windows HCS | Protocol bridge (Stdout/Write events) |

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared init binary (`tokimo-sandbox-init`)
text: Capabilities: `Pipes` and `Pty` stdio modes, `Resize`, `Signal`, `Killpg`, `OpenShell`, `MountFuse`/`UnmountFuse` (FUSE-over-vsock/socketpair).

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared init binary (`tokimo-sandbox-init`)
text: The host-side client is `src/init/client/` — generic over transport (`TransportSend`/`TransportRecv` traits). Each platform backend instantiates it with the appropriate transport (SEQPACKET for bwrap, VSOCKET for ch/macOS, pipe tunnel for Windows).

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared FUSE infrastructure (`FuseHost` + `tokimo-sandbox-fuse`)
text: All three platforms use the same FUSE-over-stream architecture for dynamic file sharing:

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared FUSE infrastructure (`FuseHost` + `tokimo-sandbox-fuse`)
text: - **Host side** (`src/vfs/host/`): `FuseHost` accepts connections, dispatches FUSE ops to a `VfsBackend` implementation, writes responses. One `FuseHost` per sandbox session.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared FUSE infrastructure (`FuseHost` + `tokimo-sandbox-fuse`)
text: - **Guest side** (`tokimo-sandbox-fuse` binary): one process per mount. Connects to host (vsock or unix-fd), performs VFS Hello handshake, mounts a FUSE filesystem at the target path, translates kernel FUSE ops into wire `Req`s.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared FUSE infrastructure (`FuseHost` + `tokimo-sandbox-fuse`)
text: - **VFS protocol** (`src/vfs/protocol/`): postcard-encoded frames over length-prefixed stream. ~35 ops covering the full FUSE op table.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Shared FUSE infrastructure (`FuseHost` + `tokimo-sandbox-fuse`)
text: - **Built-in backends** (`src/vfs/impls/`): `LocalDirVfs` (host directory passthrough), `MemFsVfs` (in-memory, for tests).

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Host-Exec Bridge
text: Lets guest commands transparently invoke a host-side callback. The guest stub `tokimo-host-exec` is hardlinked under `/run/tokimo/host-bridge/<name>`. When executed inside the sandbox, it connects to the host (vsock or Unix socket), sends a `Spawn` with argv/env/cwd, and the host runs a user-registered callback or host-side process, pumping stdin/stdout/stderr bidirectionally.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Host-Exec Bridge
text: - Host side: `src/host_exec/` — `HostExecBridge` with protocol state machine (Hello → Spawn → callback → RunOnHost/Reject).

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Host-Exec Bridge
text: - Guest side: `src/bin/tokimo-host-exec/` — connect + Hello + Spawn + pump.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Host-Exec Bridge
text: - Protocol: `src/host_exec/protocol/` — postcard-based framing, version 1.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > Windows VM artifacts
text: Windows requires three files (`vmlinuz`, `initrd.img`, `rootfs.vhdx`) in `<repo>/.vm/base/`. Built and published in-repo by `.github/workflows/vm.yml` under two independent tag namespaces: `vm-kernel-*` (vmlinuz + initrd, ships with each host crate version; the four guest binaries `tokimo-sandbox-init` / `tokimo-sandbox-fuse` / `tokimo-tun-pump` / `tokimo-host-exec` are baked into the initrd's `/bin/` and bind-mounted at runtime to `/run/tokimo/bin/` inside the rootfs) and `vm-rootfs-*` (pure Debian rootfs, no tokimo binaries, rarely rebuilt). See `packaging/vm-base/README.md` for the build pipeline. Download via:

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > HvSocket concurrency — critical design note
text: Each session allocates a **unique vsock port** via `vmconfig::alloc_session_init_port()`, which encodes into a unique HvSocket service GUID (`{port:08X}-FACB-11E6-BD58-64006A7986D3`). This is required because:

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > HvSocket concurrency — critical design note
text: 1. Hyper-V requires `(VmId, ServiceId)` to be unique for host-side listeners.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > HvSocket concurrency — critical design note
text: 2. The parent partition **must** use `HV_GUID_WILDCARD` as the listener VmId — binding a specific child's RuntimeId returns `WSAEACCES (10013)`.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > HvSocket concurrency — critical design note
text: 3. Two wildcard listeners on the same ServiceId → `WSAEADDRINUSE (10048)`.

head: tokimo-package-sandbox > HvSocket concurrency — critical design note
text: Therefore, the **only** way to run concurrent sessions is one `ServiceId` per session. Service GUIDs are registered via the HCS `ServiceTable` in the VM config JSON (no `HKLM` registry writes needed). The vsock port is passed to the guest kernel as `tokimo.init_port=<port>` on the cmdline.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Windsurf, etc.) working
**on** the Agent Kernel codebase itself. If you're building an agent *with* Agent Kernel, see
the [README](README.md) and [kernel.yaala.ai/docs](https://kernel.yaala.ai/docs) instead — this
file is for contributors to this repo.

head: AGENTS.md > Two skill sets — don't confuse them
text: This repo ships two unrelated sets of "skills," named similarly but serving opposite audiences:

text:
| Skill set | Location | Audience | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Dev skills** | [.agents/skills/ak-dev-*](.agents/skills/) | You, working on this repo | Architecture, testing conventions, code quality, and step-by-step guides for adding a new framework adapter / guardrail / knowledge base / messaging integration / tracing provider / multimodal storage / sandbox provider / queue transport to Agent Kernel core |
| **Bundled skills** | [ak-py/src/agentkernel/skills/](ak-py/src/agentkernel/skills/) (`ak-init`, `ak-build`, `ak-add-capabilities`, `ak-add-integration`, `ak-cloud-deploy`, `ak-test`) | End users of the `agentkernel` PyPI package | Shipped *inside* the package so a downstream developer's coding assistant can scaffold and extend agents built *with* Agent Kernel |

head: AGENTS.md > Two skill sets — don't confuse them
text:
If a task is about changing Agent Kernel's own source, use the dev skills under `.agents/skills/`.
Never edit the bundled skills to document a dev-only workflow, and never edit the dev skills to
change end-user-facing scaffolding behavior — read the description in each `SKILL.md` before
editing either.

head: AGENTS.md > Two skill sets — don't confuse them
text:
**Before non-trivial changes to core**, load `.agents/skills/ak-dev-architecture` — it covers
`Session`, `Agent`, `Runner`, `Module`, `Runtime`, `AgentService`, `ChatService` (and which layer
each surface calls), `AKConfig`, hooks, tools, multimodal, conversation threads, and the ECS
containerized deployment classes in depth. Don't re-derive this from
scratch by grepping; the skill is maintained precisely so agents don't have to.

head: AGENTS.md > Repo map
text:
The **core never depends on** `framework/`, `integration/`, `deployment/`, or `api/`. If a change
to `core/` requires importing something from those, that's a design smell — stop and reconsider,
or check with the maintainer.

head: AGENTS.md > Adapter architecture — stay unopinionated
text:
Every integration point (framework adapter, guardrail provider, knowledge base backend, session
store, messaging integration, tracing provider) is a **thin adapter behind a stable core
interface**, not a rewrite or reinterpretation of the underlying tool. The core abstraction
(`Agent`, `Runner`, `Module`, `Tool`, `KnowledgeBase`, `SessionStore`, `BaseTrace`, ...) defines the
minimal contract; the adapter's job is to wrap the native object/API as-is and translate at the
boundary — nothing more.

head: AGENTS.md > Adapter architecture — stay unopinionated
text: When adding or touching an adapter:

head: AGENTS.md > Adapter architecture — stay unopinionated
text:
- **Wrap, don't abstract over.** Expose the native framework/service object with minimal
  reshaping. Don't invent a new intermediate abstraction "for consistency" across adapters —
  each adapter can look different internally if that's what its underlying tool naturally wants;
  forcing uniformity across adapters is itself an opinion the architecture avoids.

head: AGENTS.md > Adapter architecture — stay unopinionated
text:
- **No feature-forcing.** Don't require a capability the underlying framework/service doesn't
  natively support (e.g. don't invent a fake token stream when the SDK has no streaming API —
  raise `NotImplementedError` until a real mapping exists). CrewAI and smolagents *do* stream in
  their SDKs; their AK adapters still raise because that wiring is not implemented yet — same
  `NotImplementedError` shape, different reason.

head: AGENTS.md > Adapter architecture — stay unopinionated
text:
- **No hidden defaults that change behavior.** Config-driven, explicit choices (`AKConfig`) beat
  adapter-internal heuristics. If an adapter needs a default, make it the same default the native
  tool itself would use.

head: AGENTS.md > Adapter architecture — stay unopinionated
text:
- **Consistent shape, not consistent opinion.** New adapters should match the *structural* pattern
  of existing ones in the same category (see `.agents/skills/ak-dev-new-*` for the exact
  per-category steps) so they're predictable to find and register — but that's about
  discoverability, not about making every backend behave identically.

head: AGENTS.md > Adapter architecture — stay unopinionated
text:
This is why the core/adapter boundary above is a hard rule, not a style preference: the moment
`core/` starts depending on a specific framework or service, the framework/service's opinions leak
into code every adapter has to live with.

head: AGENTS.md > House patterns for new features
text:
Three rules shape every new feature; `ak-dev-write-spec` designs against them and `ak-dev-review-pr`
reviews against them (full detail in the "House Patterns for New Features" section of
`.agents/skills/ak-dev-architecture`):

head: AGENTS.md > House patterns for new features
text:
- **Pluggable by default.** Any touchpoint with an external system, backend, or provider is an ABC
  plus thin adapters behind a factory in the `core/util/factory.py` shape (built-ins via `if/elif`
  real imports, `require_extra` for optional SDKs, a dotted-path bring-your-own branch), even when
  only one backend ships in the first PR.

head: AGENTS.md > House patterns for new features
text:
- **Reuse existing configuration; add knobs only when nothing existing expresses them.** Reuse whole
  `AKConfig` models where the shape exists (`_QueuesConfig` serves both `execution.queues` and
  `sandbox.broker.queue`), subclass to change defaults only, and let already-configured components
  enable a feature implicitly where that applies instead of adding `enabled`/`type` fields. Every new
  field needs a reason, a reader, a description, and a default that keeps existing YAML and `AK_*` env
  vars valid.

head: AGENTS.md > House patterns for new features
text:
- **Classes, not scripts.** Feature logic lives in classes with one responsibility each (ABC,
  backends, `*Factory`, `*Manager`/`*Handler`/`*Runner`, Pydantic models), state on instances.
  Module-level functions are reserved for small stateless shared utilities and the tool functions the
  tool builders bind.

head: AGENTS.md > House patterns for new features
text:
When documentation changes, the React landing and features pages hold hard-coded inventories of
frameworks, integrations, providers, deployment targets, and capabilities; update them alongside
`docs/docs/`. On the landing page they live in `docs/src/components/IntegrationsMarquee/data.tsx`,
`ArchitectureOverview/data.tsx`, and `FeatureExplorer/data.tsx`; on the features page in
`docs/src/pages/features.tsx` (see `ak-dev-sync-docs-from-branch`, *Docs-Site Landing and Features
Pages*, for the change-type to entry mapping).

head: AGENTS.md > Setup, build, lint, test

head: AGENTS.md > Setup, build, lint, test
text:
- Formatting is black + isort at **line length 150** (`ak-py/pyproject.toml`), not black's
  default of 88 — don't "fix" long lines that are within the configured limit.

head: AGENTS.md > Setup, build, lint, test
text:
- `make lint-check-all` is the exact command `code-quality.yml` runs in CI — run it before
  considering a change to `ak-py/` or `examples/` done.

head: AGENTS.md > Setup, build, lint, test
text:
For anything test-related beyond the basic `pytest` invocation (async fixtures, mocking
frameworks/session stores, the built-in fuzzy/semantic Test framework), load
`.agents/skills/ak-dev-testing-conventions` rather than guessing pytest patterns from scratch.

head: AGENTS.md > Setup, build, lint, test
text:
**Local `pytest` runs will show failures that aren't your fault.** Some tests are e2e and call
real services — `test.yaml` injects `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `WALLED_API_KEY`, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, and
similar secrets in CI, and those tests are skipped entirely for fork PRs that lack them. There's
no `.env.example` or pytest marker separating these from pure unit tests yet, so if you run the
suite locally without those keys set, expect some failures unrelated to your change — check
whether a failing test needs a credential you don't have before assuming you broke something.

head: AGENTS.md > Searching this repo
text:
`examples/*/.venv/` directories are gitignored, but may be present on disk (e.g. after running examples) — each can be 500MB–900MB of
vendored framework packages (openai-agents, google-adk, langgraph, ...). A broad `grep`/`find`/`rg`
without excluding `.venv` will return matches from inside vendored dependencies, not this repo's
code, and can burn a large chunk of context doing it. Scope searches to `ak-py/src`, `ak-py/tests`,
or a specific `examples/<dir>` subpath rather than `examples/` wholesale, or explicitly exclude
`.venv` (most search tools respect `.gitignore` by default — confirm yours does before trusting a
repo-wide search).

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **Commits & PRs**: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) is canonical for commit message format
  (Conventional Commits) and the PR checklist — don't restate it here; follow that file, and check
  recent `git log` for real examples of it in practice.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **New integrations** (framework adapter, guardrail provider, knowledge base, messaging
  platform, multimodal storage, tracing provider) each have a dedicated step-by-step dev skill
  under `.agents/skills/ak-dev-new-*` — use the matching one instead of improvising the wiring,
  since factory registration and export conventions are easy to get subtly wrong by copying the
  wrong existing adapter.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions
text:
- **Docs sync**: if your change alters implemented behavior, `.agents/skills/ak-dev-sync-docs-from-branch`
  and `ak-dev-sync-skills-from-branch` describe how root docs, `ak-py` docs, and the bundled
  skills get kept in sync with code — this repo has automation (`auto-sync-skills-docs.yaml`) that
  expects docs/skills to track implementation, not drift.

head: AGENTS.md > Terraform (`ak-deployment/`)
text:
These modules provision real cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure/GCP). Editing `.tf` files is fine;
**never run `terraform apply`, `terraform destroy`, or anything that touches real state/backends**
without explicit, in-the-moment user approval — this is the one part of the repo where an agent
action can have an irreversible effect outside the repo itself. `terraform plan` (read-only) is
safe to run to sanity-check a change.

head: AGENTS.md > Working with git in this repo
text:
- Never commit without telling the user first and getting confirmation — this repo's owner has
  asked to always be told before a commit runs.

head: AGENTS.md > Working with git in this repo
text: - Don't push, force-push, or open PRs unless explicitly asked.

head: AGENTS.md > Working with git in this repo
text: - Never edit files under `docs/versioned_docs/` — those are frozen snapshots of past releases.

head: AGENTS.md
text: Repository guide for AI coding agents.

head: AGENTS.md > Project In One Minute
text: UModel is an open-source object graph semantic layer for observability and operations data.

head: AGENTS.md > Project In One Minute
text: It turns model definitions, runtime entities, telemetry links, and topology relations into a workspace-scoped graph that humans and agents can inspect through one local service.

head: AGENTS.md > Project In One Minute
text: 1. Model packs define the vocabulary: `EntitySet`, `DataSet`, `Link`, `Storage`, relation semantics.

head: AGENTS.md > Project In One Minute
text: 2. EntityStore writes runtime entity and relation records.

head: AGENTS.md > Project In One Minute
text: 3. GraphStore providers persist model graph and runtime graph data.

head: AGENTS.md > Project In One Minute
text: 4. Query Service is the single read path through `.umodel`, `.entity`, and `.topo`.

head: AGENTS.md > Project In One Minute
text: 5. REST, CLI, Web UI, SDKs, AgentGateway, and MCP expose the same public contracts.

head: AGENTS.md > Project In One Minute
text: Do not describe UModel as an MVP, skeleton, prototype, toy, or internal demo.

head: DevSpace
text: DevSpace is a local development execution layer for MCP hosts such as ChatGPT and Claude. It gives a remote host workspace-scoped tools for reading, editing, searching, running commands, managing Git worktrees, reviewing changes, and coordinating bounded subagents on the user's machine.

head: DevSpace
text: Pi's SDK currently provides mature local coding primitives. DevSpace wraps those primitives in a Streamable HTTP MCP server and adds the product-specific boundaries around them: approved roots, workspace state, instructions, process sessions, worktrees, artifacts, review checkpoints, widgets, and subagent execution.

head: DevSpace
text: DevSpace owns tooling mechanics. The model receives only meaningful and actionable choices. The user sees outcomes. Tool defination should not leak internal implementation or it shoudn't be giving unwanted options to model to choose from if tooling can handle this.

head: DevSpace > Product model
text: These ideas should stay true as the project evolves:

head: DevSpace > Product model
text: 1. **The host is the orchestrator.** DevSpace exposes clear capabilities and execution state. It should not hide the workflow inside an opaque, uninspectable agent loop.

head: DevSpace > Product model
text: 2. **Everything happens in a workspace.** A workspace represents one local project directory or worktree plus the instructions and state accumulated while operating in it.

head: DevSpace > Product model
text: 3. **Local authority stays explicit.** DevSpace runs with access to the user's machine. Roots, paths, commands, processes, credentials, and destructive operations must be treated as product boundaries.

head: DevSpace > Product model
text: 4. **Subagents are bounded workers.** A subagent should have an explicit task, profile, working context, lifecycle, and result that the host can inspect and coordinate.

head: DevSpace > Product model
text: 5. **Adapters stay at the edges.** Pi, MCP hosts, and model providers each have their own terminology and capabilities. Provider-specific behavior should not become the core domain model.

head: DevSpace > Product model
text: 6. **Prefer composable primitives.** Build a small set of reliable operations that can be combined into larger workflows instead of baking every workflow into the server.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Host** — the MCP client presenting the agent experience and coordinating work.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Server** — the local DevSpace MCP server.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Workspace** — one opened directory or worktree and its accumulated instruction context.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **`workspace_id`** — the opaque handle returned by `open_workspace` and reused for calls in that workspace.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Allowed root** — a configured filesystem boundary within which a workspace may be opened. It is not itself necessarily a workspace.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Checkout mode** — operating on an existing checkout supplied by the user.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Worktree mode** — operating in an isolated Git worktree.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Tool surface** — the tools exposed by a configured mode, such as minimal, full, or Codex-compatible.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Process session** — a long-running command tracked for later input, output, or termination.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Instruction file** — an `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` discovered while navigating a workspace.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Subagent** — a bounded model invocation delegated and coordinated by the host.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Agent profile** — the model, provider, tools, and instructions used for a subagent.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Artifact** — an output surfaced for the host or user to inspect.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Review checkpoint** — stored state representing a coherent set of changes.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: - **Widget** — host-rendered UI/Cards attached to an MCP response.

head: DevSpace > Glossary
text: Use these terms precisely. In particular, do not use workspace, allowed root, checkout, and worktree interchangeably.

head: DevSpace > Security boundaries
text: Filesystem tools enforce approved-root containment. Shell commands run with the local user's authority and are not a general sandbox. Never imply that shell execution is contained merely because file tools are contained.

head: DevSpace > Security boundaries
text: Resolve and validate paths before destructive actions. Do not broaden an allowed root, delete application state, expose a credential, or replace an existing process as a convenient fix.

head: DevSpace > Security boundaries
text: Keep tunnel ownership and credentials with the user. DevSpace may operate through a user-controlled tunnel, but it does not own tunnel lifecycle or configuration.

head: DevSpace > Diagnose the correct layer
text: A failure may belong to the host, MCP transport, DevSpace, a Pi adapter, a provider, a model, a tool implementation, or the target project. Preserve the original error and identify the failing boundary before changing code.

head: DevSpace > Diagnose the correct layer
text: An adapter exception is not evidence that a model failed. A successful command is not evidence that a GUI opened, a host refreshed, or a user-visible workflow succeeded.

head: DevSpace > Diagnose the correct layer
text: Do not expand DevSpace's responsibility while fixing a local symptom. Host UI, provider model naming, tunnel management, and duplicated review experiences require an explicit product decision.

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: Determine how the user will consume the change and verify that path. Behavior may differ between:

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: - the source checkout and the packaged `npm`/`npx` installation;

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: - a direct terminal client and a real MCP host;

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: - a fresh process and a server or host that needs restarting;

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: - checkout mode and worktree mode;

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: - Linux, macOS, and Windows Bash environments;

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: - minimal, full, and Codex-compatible tool surfaces;

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: - widgets enabled, disabled, or limited to change review.

head: DevSpace > Verify the real path
text: State clearly when only a narrower proxy was verified. For model-facing schemas, inspect what the host receives. For UI and artifacts, inspect the rendered result rather than inferring success from the producing command.

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: When changing a cross-cutting concept, check every surface it actually reaches:

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - MCP schema, handler, description, and response;

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - workspace lifecycle and instruction loading;

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - allowed-root and path-containment behavior;

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - checkout and worktree modes;

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - process and subagent lifecycle;

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - tool-surface filtering;

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - widgets, artifacts, and review checkpoints;

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - persistence and migrations;

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: - packaged entry points, documentation, and examples.

head: DevSpace > Trace affected contracts
text: This is a map, not a requirement to touch every surface on every change. Avoid both incomplete contracts and speculative edits.

head: DevSpace > Pull requests
text: Only create or update a PR when explicitly asked, and read `CONTRIBUTING.md` first. Keep a PR focused on one coherent concern and use a conventional title such as `fix:`, `feat:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, or `chore:`.

head: DevSpace > Pull requests
text: Write the body as a few natural paragraphs explaining the problem and solution. Include verification, risk, or migration context only when it helps the reviewer. Avoid generated boilerplate, commit inventories, file-by-file narration, generic checklists, and mandatory `Testing` sections.

head: DevSpace > Pull requests
text: For UI changes, include before/after images and a short interaction video when behavior changes. Inspect the final diff before filing. When available, use the `file-pr` workflow to file the PR and `babysit-pr` to monitor CI and reviews.

head: DevSpace > Where code lives
text: - `src/server.ts` — MCP server setup, tool registration, and response wiring.

head: DevSpace > Where code lives
text: - `src/workspaces.ts` — workspace lifecycle, instructions, skills, and profiles.

head: DevSpace > Where code lives
text: - `src/roots.ts` — allowed roots and path containment.

head: DevSpace > Where code lives

head: AGENTS.md
text:
`CLAUDE.md` is the canonical agent guide for this repo — read it first, along
with the per-subsystem `pagespeed/*/CLAUDE.md` files (apache, nginx, envoy, iis,
kernel, system) and `html/CLAUDE.md`. This file only restates the facts agents
most often miss; it does not duplicate `CLAUDE.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text: - **Default branch is `master`, not `main`.** Branch from and target `master`.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text:
- **This build box holds many clones/worktrees.** Run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
  before editing; never edit sibling clones or vendored copies.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text:
- **Two source trees.** Rewriter filters + `RewriteDriver`/`RewriteOptions` live
  under `net/instaweb/` (not `pagespeed/`). See "Two Source Trees" in `CLAUDE.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text:
- **Builds and tests run inside the Docker dev container.** The host toolchain is
  too old: `docker compose up -d && docker compose exec dev bash`.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text:
- **Preferred Bazel config is `--config=clang-libstdcxx13`** (Clang + GCC 13
  libstdc++). C++ unit tests need the test_env quartet:
  `--test_env=REDIS_HOST=redis --test_env=REDIS_PORT=6379`
  `--test_env=MEMCACHED_HOST=memcached --test_env=MEMCACHED_PORT=11211`.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text:
- **Match CI locally before pushing:** `tools/format.sh` (the single entry point —
  resolves clang-format **20.x** itself, so it matches CI even if your local
  clang-format is a newer major) and `tools/tidyup.sh` (clang-tidy-20).
  `tools/install-hooks.sh` also wires a `pre-push` gate. See "Linting &
  Formatting" in `CLAUDE.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text:
- **Two name-colliding factory files:** the live IIS factory is
  `pagespeed/iis/iis_rewrite_driver_factory.cpp`; `pagespeed/windows/iis_rewrite_driver_factory.cc`
  is build-inert (`tags = ["manual"]`). See "IIS Platform Internals" in `CLAUDE.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text:
- **Customer-facing 1.1 docs live in `pagespeed-optimizer/website/src/content/docs-1.1/`**,
  not in this repo's `docs/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Must-not-miss facts
text:
- **A PR touching `pagespeed/`, `net/` or `install/` must carry a release note**
  — a blocking check (`release-note-guard` in the maintainer CI). Add an entry to `RELEASE_NOTES.md` (top,
  in-development section) *or* `CHANGELOG.md` (`## [Unreleased]`); either one is
  enough. Tests, `BUILD` files and `*.md` do not trigger it; `pagespeed/iis/` does.
  If nothing observable changed, waive it with a reason (≥12 chars) in a commit
  message or the PR body: `Release-Note: none - <why this is invisible to users>`.
  Check first: `bash tools/ci/check_release_note.sh --base origin/master --head HEAD`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: SiYuan Database Properties Panel is a plugin for SiYuan Note that displays database row attributes directly on pages created from database rows.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Entry Point & Plugin Lifecycle
text: - `src/index.ts` - Main plugin class extending SiYuan's `Plugin`. Handles lifecycle, settings, and protyle event listeners (LOADED_PROTYLE_STATIC, SWITCH_PROTYLE, WS_MAIN). Manages multiple Vue app instances via `createApp()` (one per block in a `Map<string, App>`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Component Hierarchy
text:
- `PluginPanel.vue` — Root component. Provides context via `provide()` (ProtyleKey, BlockIDKey, RefreshCallbackKey). Conditionally renders one of two panel variants based on the `allowEditing` prop:
  - `AttributeViewPanel.vue` — Read-only custom rendering (when `allowEditing` is false). Uses `AttributeViewValue.vue` and `ValueTypes/*` renderers.
  - `AttributeViewPanelNative.vue` — Native SiYuan editing via `protyle.renderAVAttribute()` (when `allowEditing` is true).
  - Both panels use `LayoutTabBar.vue` for tab switching.

| Component | Choice | Why |

| Config | serde_json | Human-readable config |

head: AGENTS.md — Feedo Development Guide > Key Design Decisions > Why `~/.config/feedo` everywhere?

head: AGENTS.md — Feedo Development Guide > Key Design Decisions > Why no database?
text: JSON config is human-editable, version-controllable, and simple. SQLite can come later if needed.

head: AGENTS.md — Feedo Development Guide > Key Design Decisions > Why async for feeds?
text: Fetching 50 feeds sequentially = 50× latency. Async lets us fetch in parallel without blocking the UI.

head: AGENTS.md — Feedo Development Guide > Key Design Decisions > Why ratatui over other TUI libs?
text: Active maintenance, good docs, immediate mode rendering fits our architecture.

head: AGENTS.md — Feedo Development Guide > Key Design Decisions > Why ratatui-themes?
text: Shared theme definitions with Hazelnut for consistent look across projects.

head: AGENTS.md — Feedo Development Guide > Key Design Decisions > Why encrypted credential storage?
text: Secure storage of sync service passwords without requiring OS keychain (works on all platforms).

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Product purpose
text: Loupe is a native macOS accessibility utility for inspecting and annotating interface elements. Changes must remain dependable in the real app, where macOS Accessibility permission, overlay behavior, signing, and coordinate conversion all affect what the user experiences.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Project boundaries
text: - Open and build `Loupe.xcworkspace`; do not substitute the `.xcodeproj`.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Project boundaries
text: - Keep the app shell in `Loupe/` and feature implementation in `LoupePackage/Sources/LoupeFeature/` consistent with the existing workspace and Swift package boundary.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Project boundaries
text: - Types consumed by the app target must remain accessible across that package boundary (mark them `public`, with a `public init()`).

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Project boundaries
text: - Accessibility coordinates use a top-left origin while AppKit screen coordinates use a bottom-left origin. Preserve and verify the existing conversion whenever selection, positioning, or overlays are involved.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Project boundaries
text: - Package dependencies belong in `LoupePackage/Package.swift`; build settings belong in the XCConfig files in `Config/` (Shared, Debug, Release, Tests) unless the established project structure requires otherwise.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Working agreements
text: - Inspect Git status before working. Preserve unrelated changes and untracked build output; do not clean, delete, pull, or rewrite repository state unless asked.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Working agreements
text: - Treat signing, entitlements, App Sandbox, Accessibility permission, window level, and overlay event handling as sensitive boundaries. Inspect their current behavior before changing them, and do not broaden permissions merely to make a test pass.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Working agreements
text: - Keep the experience native and accessible. Avoid changes that interfere with other apps, trap input, or leave overlays active unexpectedly.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Working agreements
text: - Do not confuse a successful build with successful accessibility behavior. Permission prompts, first-run state, multi-display coordinates, and the actual overlay must be checked when relevant.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Working agreements
text: - Do not turn conversational promises into standing instructions or memory automatically. Propose additions to this file and make them only when the user approves.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Verification and handoff
text: Choose verification for the affected behavior. Documentation-only changes do not require a build or launch. Changes to selection, overlays, coordinates, permissions, or interaction require relevant real-app checks as well as appropriate automated checks.

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Verification and handoff
text: - Build: `xcodebuild -workspace Loupe.xcworkspace -scheme Loupe -configuration Debug build`

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Verification and handoff

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Verification and handoff

head: Loupe Project Instructions > Verification and handoff
