head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: This is a Swift 6.3 parser/compiler/runtime for ARO (Action Result Object), a DSL for expressing business features as Action-Result-Object statements.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: An ARO application is a **directory** containing `.aro` files:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: For larger applications, use the `sources/` subdirectory convention:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: - All `.aro` files in the directory **and subdirectories** are automatically discovered and parsed

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: - Files can be in root, `sources/`, or any subdirectory to any depth

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: - No imports needed - all feature sets are globally visible within the application

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: - Exactly ONE `Application-Start` feature set per application (error if 0 or multiple)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: - At most ONE `Application-End: Success` and ONE `Application-End: Error` (both optional)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: - Feature sets are triggered by **events**, not direct calls

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text: - **Contract-First HTTP**: `openapi.yaml` is required for HTTP server (no contract = no server)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Application Structure
text:
**A directory of applications is not an application.** `aro run`, `aro build` and
`aro check` all refuse a path holding several `Application-Start` feature sets in
different subdirectories, and name one to point at instead. `aro check --recursive`
checks each of them separately — without it, every `.aro` file under the path is
pooled into one pseudo-application, so sibling applications appear to share feature
sets and entry points (GitLab #824).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Importing another application (ARO-0005 §3)
text:
No imports are needed *within* an application. `import` is for pulling in a
**separate** application's feature sets, and it is the one place a path appears in
ARO source:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Importing another application (ARO-0005 §3)
text:
The path is relative to the importing file's directory, and every feature set,
type and published variable of the imported application becomes visible — so
`Examples/ModulesExample/Combined` serves the routes whose handlers live in
`ModuleA` and `ModuleB`. Remove the two lines and startup fails with "Missing
ARO feature set handlers".

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Importing another application (ARO-0005 §3)
text:
It is resolved by `Application.resolveImports`; there are no visibility modifiers
and no partial imports.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Compilation Pipeline
text: - **Lexer** (`Lexer.swift`): Tokenizes source, recognizing articles (a/an/the), prepositions, and compound identifiers

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Compilation Pipeline
text: - **Parser** (`Parser.swift`): Recursive descent parser producing AST

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Compilation Pipeline
text: - **SemanticAnalyzer** (`SemanticAnalyzer.swift`): Builds symbol tables and performs data flow analysis

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Compilation Pipeline
text: - **Compiler** (`Compiler.swift`): Orchestrates the pipeline, entry point is `Compiler.compile(source)`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Runtime Execution
text: - **ApplicationLoader**: Discovers and compiles all `.aro` files in directory

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Runtime Execution
text: - **ExecutionEngine** (`Core/ExecutionEngine.swift`): Orchestrates program execution

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Runtime Execution
text: - **EventBus** (`Events/EventBus.swift`): Routes events to matching feature sets

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Runtime Execution
text: - **FeatureSetExecutor** (`Core/FeatureSetExecutor.swift`): Executes feature sets when triggered

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Runtime Execution
text: - **ActionRegistry** (`Actions/ActionRegistry.swift`): Maps verbs to implementations

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Event-Driven Feature Sets
text: Feature sets are triggered by events based on their **business activity**:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Event-Driven Feature Sets
text:
| Business Activity Pattern | Triggered By |
|---------------------------|--------------|
| `operationId` (e.g., `listUsers`) | HTTP route match via OpenAPI contract |
| `{EventName} Handler` | Custom domain events |
| `{repository-name} Observer` | Repository changes (store/update/delete) |
| `File Event Handler` | File system events |
| `Socket Event Handler` | Socket events |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contract-First HTTP APIs
text: ARO uses **contract-first** API development. HTTP routes are defined in `openapi.yaml`, and feature sets are named after `operationId` values.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contract-First HTTP APIs
text:
**Without openapi.yaml**: HTTP server does NOT start, no port is opened.
**With openapi.yaml**: HTTP server is enabled and routes are handled.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contract-First HTTP APIs
text:
Example:
```yaml
# openapi.yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: User API
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /users:
    get:
      operationId: listUsers    # Feature set name
    post:
      operationId: createUser
  /users/{id}:
    get:
      operationId: getUser
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contract-First HTTP APIs
text: **Path Parameters**: Extracted from URL and available via `pathParameters`:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contract-First HTTP APIs
text: - `Extract the <id> from the <pathParameters: id>.`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contract-First HTTP APIs
text: **Request Body**: Typed according to OpenAPI schema:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Contract-First HTTP APIs
text: - `Extract the <data> from the <request: body>.`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Happy Case
text:
Code contains only the happy case. Errors are handled by the runtime, which
reconstructs the failed statement with its values:
`Cannot retrieve the user from the user-repository where id = 530`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Happy Case
text:
**A `Retrieve` that matches nothing is not one of those errors.** It binds an
empty list (`ExtractAction.swift:860`); with a `where` clause matching exactly
one row it binds that record rather than a one-element list. The only throw on
that path is a repository that does not exist. Guard on the result — the
statement does not fail for you (GitLab #835).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Happy Case
text: Do not use it for production code, it is terribly insecure.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Caller-Scoped Repositories (ARO-0094)
text:
A repository is application-scoped unless it says otherwise, which is what every
repository was and still is by default. `Declare` says otherwise:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Caller-Scoped Repositories (ARO-0094)
text:
Handlers do not restate it: `Store the <item> into the <cart-repository>.` is
the same statement over HTTP, WebSocket and TCP, and writes to the calling
caller's partition. `session` is an identity (authenticated, survives
reconnects, revocable); `connection` is a transport lifetime that identifies
nobody — a TCP peer gets the second until `Attach the <session> to the
<connection>.` promotes it. **Promotion is irreversible within a connection.**

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Caller-Scoped Repositories (ARO-0094)
text:
A caller-scoped repository that cannot resolve its caller **throws** — never the
application-wide repository, never an empty one. `aro check` reports the
statically visible cases (a session repository in `Application-Start` or a file
handler, a connection repository on an HTTP route, conflicting declarations).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Caller-Scoped Repositories (ARO-0094)
text:
The scope value is a **string**: `{ scope: session }` is a variable reference
and fails. `Declare` and `Attach` are in `ActionRoleCatalog.mustRunForEffect`
because their argument is an expression, and the executor's expression fast path
would otherwise bind the value and never run the action.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Caller-Scoped Repositories (ARO-0094)
text:
Sessions are the runtime's: minting (256-bit CSPRNG id, HMAC-signed cookie,
`HttpOnly`/`Secure`/`SameSite`), validating on every request, refreshing
`last-seen`, rotating on `Attach`, and evicting on disconnect and expiry.
Everything after that is ordinary ARO against the application-scoped
`sessions-repository` and `connections-repository`, so logout is a `Delete`.
`Configure the <session: secure> with false.` is how a laptop opts out of the
TLS requirement. The cookie is declared in `openapi.yaml` as
`securitySchemes: { type: apiKey, in: cookie }`; a cookie scheme is satisfied by
a *validated session*, not by the cookie's presence.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text: - `Program` → `FeatureSet[]` → `Statement[]` (either `AROStatement` or `PublishStatement`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text: - `AROStatement`: `Action [the] <Result> preposition [the] <Object>` (articles optional)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text: - `SymbolTable`: Immutable, `Sendable` symbol storage per feature set

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text: - `GlobalSymbolRegistry`: Cross-feature-set symbol access for published variables

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text:
- `FeatureGraph` / `FeatureGraphDiff`: The application as nodes (feature sets)
  and wires (events, `Application.<Name>` calls, repository observers), and the
  comparison of two revisions of it. Derived statically with the runtime's own
  matching rules, so `aro diff --graph` and SOLARO's review sheet show the same
  graph the EventBus will wire up (GitLab #443).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text: - `ActionImplementation`: Protocol for action implementations

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text: - `ResultDescriptor` / `ObjectDescriptor`: Statement metadata for actions

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text: - `ExecutionContext`: Runtime context protocol

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Types
text: - `RuntimeEvent`: Protocol for events

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Action Semantic Roles
text:
Five roles, classified by data flow direction. `aro actions` prints the live
table and ARO-0004 §11 is generated from it — prefer either over this summary:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Action Semantic Roles
text: - **REQUEST** (Extract, Parse, Retrieve, Fetch, Probe, Pull, Clone): External → Internal

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Action Semantic Roles
text: - **OWN** (Compute, Validate, Compare, Create, Transform, Stage, Checkout): Internal → Internal

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Action Semantic Roles
text: - **RESPONSE** (Return, Throw, **Store, Log, Send, Write**, Render): Internal → External

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Action Semantic Roles
text: - **EXPORT** (Publish, Emit, Deliver, Commit, Push, Tag, Schedule): Makes symbols globally accessible or exports data

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Action Semantic Roles
text: - **SERVER** (Start, Stop, Listen, Connect, Close, WaitForEvents): Service lifecycle

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Action Semantic Roles
text:
`Store`, `Log`, `Send` and `Write` read as exports and declare `.response`. That
is a known, deliberate inconsistency (GitLab #480, ARO-0004 §2.4), not a typo to
fix here — roles drive data-flow analysis, so changing one changes behaviour.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Action Semantic Roles
text:
The five bullets are hand-picked but not hand-trusted: every name in them is
checked against the runtime by `python3 Scripts/generate-action-reference.py
--check`, which CI runs, so this summary cannot drift from the registry the way
it had (GitLab #846). Add a name only if the runtime agrees it has that role.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Statement Execution (ARO-0088)
text:
Statements start in source order; the program waits for one at the **first read
of its result**. Independent statements therefore overlap: two 2-second requests
in one feature set take ~2.1s interpreted (~2.8s compiled), not 4.2s.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Statement Execution (ARO-0088)
text:
Effects (`Log`, `Store`, `Emit`, `Send`, `Publish`, `Return`, …) never defer —
they run at their own statement and force what they read first, so observable
output stays in source order. `Emit` does not wait for its handlers; `Deliver`
is the same statement awaited, for when the next statement depends on what a
handler did (ARO-0088 §7, GitLab #905). Shutdown drains the cascade either
way. Deferral is an allowlist of value-producing verbs
(`LazyActionPolicy.deferrableVerbs`); `Sleep` is deliberately excluded because
the delay *is* the effect.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Statement Execution (ARO-0088)
text:
Mechanics: a deferred action returns an `AROFuture` running on
`ActionTaskExecutor` (GCD's elastic queue, so blocked forcers can't starve the
work that would unblock them). Each statement gets its own scope for framework
variables (`_with_`, `_literal_`, …) — otherwise a deferred action would read
the next statement's modifiers. Feature-set exit forces whatever is outstanding,
so a failure nobody read is still reported, attributed to the statement that
caused it. Slow-force warnings fire after `ARO_FORCE_WARN_SECONDS` (default 5s).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Statement Execution (ARO-0088)
text:
Streams pipeline the same way: the producer runs ahead of the consumer by
`ARO_STREAM_PREFETCH` elements (default 2) through a bounded channel.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Statement Execution (ARO-0088)
text:
`ARO_NO_DEFER=1` disables deferral entirely — the fastest way to find out
whether a suspected bug is order-related.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Bodies (ARO-0090)
text:
**Streams don't have a size. Values do.** A feature set that only *moves* its
request body — `Write … to the <file: …>`, `Send`, `Return`, `Emit`, `for each`
— never builds it in memory, so its size is bounded by the sink and no limit
applies. A feature set that *reads* it — a field access, `Compute`, `Store`,
`Log`, or a `when` guard — turns it into a value, and that is what is bounded.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Bodies (ARO-0090)
text: The limit is declared per route in the contract and defaults to 1 MB:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Bodies (ARO-0090)
text:
`Configure the <http-server: max-body> with "1MB".` (or `ARO_MAX_BODY`) sets the
default; the route's own declaration wins. A body over the limit is answered
`413` before it is read — from `Content-Length` at the request head where the
client declared one, incrementally otherwise.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Request Bodies (ARO-0090)
text:
Which of the two a route is, is computed from the source before the server
binds a port (`BodyMaterializationAnalyzer`, verb table in
`StreamConsumptionPolicy`), so `aro check` reports it per route. Anything the
analysis cannot see through — a plugin action, an unknown verb — counts as
reading. A body arrives once and can be consumed once. `Emit`/`Publish` of a
body *anchors* it: drained to a temp file a chunk at a time so handlers that
outlive the request can each read it, deleted when the last reference goes.
Folding qualifiers (`sha256`, `length`, `lines`) consume the body chunk by
chunk, so hashing a 4 GB upload costs a chunk too — and hashes the upload's
bytes rather than a rendering of its parsed form. `aro run` and `aro build`
agree: the analysis is baked into the binary at build time, and the compiled
server enforces the same limits and streams the same bodies.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > User-Defined Actions (ARO-0081)
text:
A feature set whose business activity is `Action` becomes callable
application-wide as `Application.<Name>`. Use this instead of writing a
plugin or hopping through the event bus when you want reusable inline
logic.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > User-Defined Actions (ARO-0081)
text:
`takes <name>` is sugar for a single positional argument extracted as
`input.<name>`. Without `takes`, callers pass an object literal via `with`.
The return value follows the standard Return action shape; the caller pulls
named fields off it the same way they would for any other record.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > User-Defined Actions (ARO-0081)
text:
**Recursion has no depth limit** (ARO-0081 §9). A call in tail position — the
final statement is an unguarded `Return … with <r>.` forwarding the call's
result untouched — reuses its frame, so depth costs nothing. Any other
recursion keeps its frames on the heap and is bounded by memory. A callee sees
its own bindings and application-level ones, never the caller's locals, so
lookup cost doesn't grow with depth. `aro check` warns when every path through
an action reaches a call before a `Return` (direct or mutual cycle), and a
runaway recursion stops at `ARO_MAX_CALL_DEPTH` (default 50 000, `0` disables)
with an error naming the call chain instead of an OOM kill.

| Type | Language | Interface |

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Directory Structure
text:
**`Plugins/` is the only plugin directory** (GitLab #848). A lowercase
`plugins/` is still read, with a deprecation warning, and will stop being read.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Directory Structure
text:
The two were never interchangeable, which is why this is worth a paragraph.
They used to be handled by two different loaders: `loadManagedPlugins` read
`Plugins/` and required one subdirectory per plugin with a `plugin.yaml` — the
layout `aro add` installs and `aro new plugin` scaffolds — while `loadPlugins`
read lowercase `plugins/` and took loose `.swift` files, prebuilt libraries and
bare Swift packages with no manifest. On macOS and Windows those are the same
directory, so both loaders walked it and one of them succeeded; on Linux they
are two, and only the matching one ran. A project therefore loaded a different
set of plugins depending on the developer's filesystem.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Directory Structure
text:
One directory is resolved now, and every layout above is loaded from it. Use

| Language | Registration Pattern |
|----------|---------------------|

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > C ABI Interface
text: Underlying all plugins is a C-compatible ABI. The SDKs generate these exports automatically:

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Qualifiers
text: Plugins can register custom qualifiers that transform values. Qualifiers work on types like List, String, Int, etc.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Qualifiers
text: Plugin qualifiers are **namespaced** via the `handler:` field in `plugin.yaml`. Access them as `<value: handler.qualifier>`:

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Qualifiers
text:
**Declaring the namespace handle in plugin.yaml:**
```yaml
name: plugin-collection
version: 1.0.0
handle: Collections        # root-level PascalCase handle (canonical, GitLab #95)
provides:
  - type: swift-plugin
    path: Sources/
    handler: collections   # legacy fallback — use root-level handle: instead
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Qualifiers
text: The root-level `handle:` field (PascalCase) is the canonical way to declare the namespace.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Qualifiers
text: - Qualifiers are accessed as `handle.qualifier` (e.g., `Collections.pick-random`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Qualifiers
text: - Actions are invoked as `Handle.Verb` (e.g., `Markdown.ToHTML`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Qualifiers
text:

  warning — including when a root-level `handle:` is also present, which it did
  not before (GitLab #825). If the two name different namespaces, the root-level
  one wins and the warning says so.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Plugin Qualifiers

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Python plugins in a standalone binary (GitLab #856)
text:
`aro build --static` promises one file you can copy, and a Python plugin
ordinarily breaks that: the binary needs an interpreter, a `libpython`, and the
standard library, all resolved from the machine that built it. So the build
declines rather than producing something that looks standalone and dies on the
target machine.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Python plugins in a standalone binary (GitLab #856)
text:
Point `ARO_STATIC_PYTHON` at a CPython distribution that can be embedded and it
builds instead, carrying the interpreter and the parts of the standard library a
program actually needs:

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Python plugins in a standalone binary (GitLab #856)
text:
The distribution needs a **real** static `libpython<version>.a` and its stdlib —
a python-build-standalone download, or CPython configured `--disable-shared`. A
stock python.org or Homebrew install will not do, and the reason is worth
knowing: they ship a file *named* `libpython3.x.a` that is a symlink to the
dynamic library, so a naive check finds a static archive that is not one. The
build reads the file's magic (`!<arch>`) rather than trusting its name.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Python plugins in a standalone binary (GitLab #856)
text:
What travels: 615 files and about 35 MB, measured against CPython 3.12. What
does not: CPython's own test suite, `idlelib` and `tkinter`, `__pycache__`, and
`site-packages` — the last deliberately, since copying whatever is installed on
the build machine is how a binary acquires dependencies nobody declared. A
plugin's own requirements are added explicitly instead.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Python plugins in a standalone binary (GitLab #856)
text:
The stdlib lands beside the executable as `aro-python<version>/`, not in a temp
directory: `/tmp` is frequently mounted `noexec`, which the stdlib's C
extensions cannot survive.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Python plugins in a standalone binary (GitLab #856)
text:
A plugin needing a **native** wheel still cannot be embedded — those are
compiled extensions that no amount of static linking folds in — so the refusal
path remains for them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Binary Mode Support
text:
Plugins work in both interpreter (`aro run`) and compiled binary (`aro build`) modes,
but the two link modes bundle them differently — and the choice is resolved once, in
`BuildCommand`, before plugins are compiled, so the plugin stage knows which build it
is in (GitLab #815).

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Binary Mode Support
text:
**`--static` (the default) bakes native plugins in.** A Swift package plugin is built
with `swift build -c release` if nothing built it already, C sources are compiled, and
a Rust crate gets a `staticlib`; the resulting `.o` files are linked INTO the binary
with their symbols renamed `aro_static_<plugin>__<symbol>` so several can coexist
(`Linker.swift`). No `dlopen` at run time.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Binary Mode Support
text:
**`--dynamic` ships the plugin's shared library beside the binary** and loads it at
startup the way the interpreter does. Nothing is baked in, and no object files are
needed.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Binary Mode Support
text:
**Python plugins cannot be made standalone** (GitLab #608). They need a CPython
interpreter and its standard library at run time, and the build resolves both from the
*build* machine — an absolute path to a framework or `libpython`, plus that machine's
`sys.prefix`. So `aro build --static` refuses one, naming the plugin and the exact
Python installation it would have depended on; `--dynamic` builds it with a warning
saying the same, because that mode never promised a single file.
`ARO_ALLOW_EMBEDDED_PYTHON=1` builds anyway, for people who build on the machine that
will run it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Plugin System > Binary Mode Support
text:
Whether a compiled binary may `dlopen` a plugin at all is recorded at link time —
the generated `main` calls `aro_set_build_link_mode`, and `DynamicLoading` answers
from that rather than probing the loader, which answers a different question
(GitLab #618).

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax
text:
<!-- aro-check: skip — the shape of a feature set, with placeholder names -->
```aro
(Feature Name: Business Activity) {
    Require the <token> from the <environment>.
    Extract the <result: qualifier> from the <source: qualifier>.
    Compute the <output> for the <input>.
    Return an <OK: status> for a <valid: result>.
    Publish as <alias> <output>.
}
```

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Statements that are not actions
text:
Four forms are part of the grammar rather than the action registry, so they have
no role, no prepositions, and no entry in `aro actions` — which explains them
instead of reporting "no action named" (GitLab #828):

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Statements that are not actions
text:
| Form | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `Publish as <alias> <variable> [when <cond>].` | Makes a variable visible to other feature sets in the same business activity; a false guard leaves the name unpublished (GitLab #830) |
| `Require the <name> from the <source>.` | Declares an external dependency (below) |
| `match <noun> { case <pattern> { … } otherwise { … } }` | Branches on a value; the first matching case wins |
| `Break.` | Leaves the innermost loop |

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Statements that are not actions
text:
**`Require`** names something the feature set expects to be there, and the source
decides who provides it:

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Statements that are not actions
text:
`framework` is a no-op that documents the dependency. `environment` binds the
variable of that name, and reading it when the variable is unset fails the
statement in the usual way. Any other source names a feature set, and `aro check`
warns when nothing publishes that symbol — the one case where the warning is the
point. The source name is a single identifier, so a multi-word feature set cannot
be named here.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Statements that are not actions
text:
Application lifecycle handlers:
```aro
(* Entry point - exactly one per application *)
(Application-Start: My App) {
    Log "Starting..." to the <console>.
    Start the <http-server> with <contract>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <startup>.
}

(* Exit handler for graceful shutdown - optional, at most one *)
(Application-End: Success) {
    Log "Shutting down..." to the <console>.
    Stop the <http-server> with <application>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <shutdown>.
}

(* Exit handler for errors/crashes - optional, at most one *)
(Application-End: Error) {
    Extract the <error> from the <shutdown: error>.
    Log <error> to the <console>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <error-handling>.
}
```

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text: The Compute action transforms data using built-in operations:

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
| Operation | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `length` / `count` | Count elements | `Compute the <len: length> from <text>.` |
| `uppercase` | Convert to UPPERCASE | `Compute the <upper: uppercase> from <text>.` |
| `lowercase` | Convert to lowercase | `Compute the <lower: lowercase> from <text>.` |
| `hash` | Compute hash value | `Compute the <hash: hash> from <password>.` |
| `trim` | Strip surrounding whitespace | `Compute the <clean: trim> from <field>.` |
| `replace` | Substring replacement | `Compute the <out: replace> from <t> with { find: "-", replace: "_" }.` |
| `html-escape` | Escape `& < > " '` for HTML | `Compute the <safe: html-escape> from <input>.` |
| `url-encode` / `url-decode` | Percent-encode a query value | `Compute the <enc: url-encode> from <query>.` |
| `url-resolve` | Resolve a relative URL against a base | `Compute the <abs: url-resolve> from <href> with { base: <page> }.` |
| `url-defragment` / `url-normalize` | Strip `#frag`; one spelling per address | `Compute the <clean: url-defragment> from <link>.` |
| `url-parts` | scheme, host, port, path, query, fragment | `Compute the <p: url-parts> from <link>.` |
| `base64-encode` / `base64-decode` | Standard Base64 | `Compute the <b64: base64-encode> from <creds>.` |
| `base64url-encode` / `base64url-decode` | URL-safe Base64 (JWTs) | `Compute the <tok: base64url-encode> from <payload>.` |
| `json-escape` | Escape for a JSON string literal | `Compute the <esc: json-escape> from <text>.` |
| `lines` | Split text into a list of lines | `Compute the <ls: lines> from <content>.` |
| `join` | Join a collection into a string | `Compute the <csv: join> from <items> with { separator: ", " }.` |
| `sum` | Total of a numeric collection | `Compute the <total: sum> from <amounts>.` |
| `avg` / `average` | Arithmetic mean | `Compute the <mean: avg> from <scores>.` |
| `unique` | Remove duplicates, first wins | `Compute the <tags: unique> from <all>.` |
| `random` | Random element, or Int below a bound | `Compute the <pick: random> from <options>.` |
| `sha256` | SHA-256 hex digest (alias of `hash`) | `Compute the <d: sha256> from <payload>.` |
| `basename` / `dirname` | Path head and tail | `Compute the <n: basename> from <path>.` |
| `extension` / `stem` | Type and name, no dot | `Compute the <e: extension> from <path>.` |
| `absolute` | Resolve `.`/`..` against the working directory | `Compute the <a: absolute> from <path>.` |
| `path-join` | Join with exactly one separator | `Compute the <p: path-join> from <dir> with <name>.` |
| `captures` | First regex match, as a record of its groups | `Compute the <p: captures> from <line> by /(?<k>\w+)=(?<v>.*)/.` |
| `all-captures` | Every match, as a list of those records | `Compute the <ps: all-captures> from <line> by /…/.` |
| `symmetric-difference` | Elements in exactly one of the two | `Compute the <changed: symmetric-difference> from <before> with <after>.` |
| `fixed` | Round to N decimal places (`with { places: N }`, 2 by default) | `Compute the <total: fixed> from <raw>.` |
| Arithmetic | +, -, *, /, % | `Compute the <total> from <price> * <qty>.` |

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
**Money is a result type, not a qualifier.** `as Currency` (and `as Decimal`,
the same format) is exact base-10 arithmetic, so `3 * 2.40` is `7.20` where
`Float` says `7.199999999999999`. `Decimal` used to be a silent alias for
`Float` — the word that promises exactness delivering binary floating point —
and is not any more (GitLab #906). The scale comes from the operands rather
than being invented: `+`/`-`/`%` take the wider, `*` adds the two and drops
trailing zeros back to the wider. Division cannot be exact, so the rule is
stated: six places, half-up, then trimmed the same way — six is four more than
any circulating currency's minor unit, so an intermediate division never
decides the cents. Exactness is **contagious**, which is the point: a statement
reading an exact amount stays exact without the annotation, so an amount is
computed once and every aggregate downstream agrees about it. `Currency`
carries **no currency code** — it is a precision format, and the code lives in
ARO-0014's `Money` schema (`{ amount, currency }`), which composes with it. An
amount is a number in every sink (JSON, CSV, YAML, HTTP bodies) at its own
scale, in both execution modes. `fixed` keeps its job — settling a
*presentation* scale — and on an exact amount it rescales rather than repairs.
`round`/`rounded`/`precision` still redirect to `fixed`;
`money`/`currency`/`decimal`/`exact` redirect to `as Currency`.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
Encoding qualifiers are specified in `Proposals/ARO-0019-standard-library.md` §3.1,
collection/text qualifiers in §3.2. A template whose path ends `.html` or `.htm`
escapes what it prints; `.tpl`, `.txt` and `.md` do not, so a `.tpl` emitting HTML
still needs `html-escape` (GitLab #476, `TemplateEscaping.forTemplate`). Both output
forms escape on the same rule — `Print <x> to the <template>.` and the `{{ <x> }}`
shorthand (GitLab #560) — and each opts out its own way: `<template: raw>` for
Print, the `| raw` filter for the shorthand. Escaping runs after the filters, so
`{{ <body> | markdown | raw }}` is how markup-emitting filters stay markup. Do not
hand-escape into an escaping template, or the reader sees `&lt;`.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
**The qualifier namespace is closed** (§3.3, GitLab #486). A Compute qualifier must
resolve to a built-in, a plugin qualifier (`handle.qualifier`), a chain (`a|b`), or a
date offset (`-7d`); anything else is an error naming the closest match. It
used to return the input unchanged, so an invented qualifier compiled, passed
`aro check`, exited `[OK]`, and printed the wrong value. Counting lines is
`lines` then `length` — `lines` already drops the trailing newline's phantom
element. Run `aro actions --qualifiers` for the live set.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
`aro check` rejects unknown qualifiers too (GitLab #465), so a green check means
the qualifier exists. The names live in `ComputeQualifierCatalog` (AROParser,
because the check path never loads the runtime) and a runtime test asserts they
match `ComputeAction.builtInQualifiers` — add a qualifier to one and the suite
fails until you add it to the other. Namespaced names and chains are accepted at
check time and resolved at run time, since `aro check` does not load plugins.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
Two forms are commonly mistaken for qualifiers, and the diagnostic names both:
sorting/reversing/element access are actions (`Sort the <s> for the <x>.`,
`Reverse the <r> for the <x>.`, `Extract the <f: first> from the <x>.`), and a
result *type* uses `as` (`Compute the <n> as Float from <s>.`) because the
qualifier slot selects an operation.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
**`Map` takes a field name, not a value.** `Map the <ns> from the <us> with name.`
and `Map the <ns: name> from the <us>.` are the same statement. There is no
per-element binding, so `with <item> * 0.9` has nothing to range over — it used
to parse and die on `Undefined variable: item`, and `with 3` was discarded
silently; both are check-time errors now. Use `for each` to compute per element.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
**Path qualifiers are pure functions** (ARO-0036 §9, GitLab #861) — none of
them touches the filesystem. `extension` has no dot, a dotfile is a name rather
than an extension, `dirname` of a bare filename is `"."`, and `path-join` uses
exactly one separator. **An absolute right-hand component does not reset the
path**: `path-join` of `/uploads` and `/etc/passwd` is `/uploads/etc/passwd`,
deliberately unlike Python, because the call it exists for is joining a trusted
directory to an untrusted name.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
`Configure the <mode> for the <file: "./run.sh"> with { permissions: "755" }.`
sets permissions and binds `{ path, permissions, octal, previous }`; octal and
the symbolic form `Stat` prints are both accepted, so a mode read off one file
applies to another. `Touch the <m> for the <file: p>.` creates or stamps.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
**Regex capture groups** (ARO-0037 §7): the pattern comes from the same
`by /pattern/flags` clause `Split` uses. `captures` binds the first match's
groups — named ones under their names, numbered ones under `"1"`, `"2"`, …, and
the whole match under `match`; `all-captures` binds a list of those records. **A
non-match binds an empty record (or empty list), it does not fail** — the same
call ARO makes for a `Retrieve` that matches nothing. A group that took part in
no match is absent rather than empty.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Computations
text:
**`subset of` is an operator, not a qualifier** (ARO-0042 §3.6, GitLab #864),
and it works in `where` as well as `when` (GitLab #894) — filtering is the side
it is most useful on.
It answers a question rather than producing a collection, so it sits with `in`,
`contains` and `matches`: `Return an <OK: status> for the <request> when
<required-roles> subset of <user-roles>.` Set semantics — a duplicate on the
left does not make a new member — and the empty set is a subset of everything.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Condition operators
text:
`when` and `where` take the same operator set (ARO-0001, ARO-0018 §2.1) — they
had diverged, so a predicate that could filter a collection could not guard a
statement (GitLab #830):

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Condition operators
text:
| Operator | Example |
|----------|---------|
| `in` / `not in` | `when <tag> not in <banned>` |
| `starts with` / `ends with` | `when <path> starts with "/api"` |
| `contains` | `when <name> contains "test"` |
| `matches` | `when <name> matches "^a.c"` |
| `before` / `after` | `when <deadline> before <now>` |
| `subset of` | `where <roles> subset of <granted>` |

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Condition operators
text:
The affix operators are **literal** — that is the point of having them, since
`matches "^a.c"` also accepts `axc`. `starts` and `ends` are not reserved: only
a following `with`, in operator position, makes them operators, so `<starts>`
and `<end-date>` stay usable as names. `not` alone is still the unary negation.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Absent values
text: `Extract … default <value>` supplies a value when the source is not there:

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Absent values
text:
Only an **unset** variable takes the default. `PORT=` is a value somebody wrote
and wins — the same rule the `default` operator follows for `false`, `0` and
`""` (GitLab #547). Without the clause an unset variable still binds `""`.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > HTTP status names
text:
`HTTPStatusCatalog` (AROParser) is the single source for
`Return a <Name: status>` — read by the interpreter, the compiled binary and
`aro check`. It used to be two hard-coded switches that disagreed (twelve names
vs five) and **both fell through to 200**, so `<TooManyRequests: status>` was a
200 with a rate-limit body (GitLab #830). Case and separators do not
distinguish names. A misspelling within a typo's distance of a real name is a
check warning; a genuine domain status (`<PendingVerification: status>`,
ARO-0002 §7) is a deliberate 200 and stays silent.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > HTTP status names
text: **Qualifier-as-Name Syntax**: When you need multiple results of the same operation, use the qualifier to specify the operation while the base becomes the variable name:

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > HTTP status names
text:
`Compare` takes both operands as inputs and binds a fresh result
(GitLab #469) — `<result: matches>` is the boolean, `<result: result>`
is `equal` / `less` / `greater`. The older two-operand spelling
(`Compare the <a> against the <b>.`) tried to rebind its own first
operand and could never run under immutability.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > HTTP status names
text: See `Proposals/ARO-0001-language-fundamentals.md` for the full specification.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Positional Command-Line Arguments (ARO-0047)
text:
`Application-Start` declares the positionals it reads with the `takes` clause
ARO-0081 already uses for user-defined actions, so `./crawler https://example.com 3`
works rather than only `./crawler --url … --depth …` (GitLab #857):

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Positional Command-Line Arguments (ARO-0047)
text:
A declared name is read exactly like a flag, and a flag of the same name wins.
`--` ends flag parsing. The one trap predates positionals: `--key value`
consumes the token after it, so `--verbose https://x` binds `verbose` to the
URL — write `--verbose=true`, or `--`, to mean two things.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Application-Wide Limits (ARO-0088 §10a)
text:
`with <concurrency: N>` bounds one loop; these bound the application (GitLab
#862). Work **queues** at a ceiling, it never fails.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Application-Wide Limits (ARO-0088 §10a)
text:
Several settings for one category go in **one object** — two statements naming
the same category rebind an immutable binding. A ceiling and a rate are
different limits and both apply: one request at a time still exceeds a
per-minute quota.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Application-Wide Limits (ARO-0088 §10a)
text:
The ceiling counts units of work that are not already running inside one — every
triggered feature set and every `parallel for each` iteration. Work started
beneath a slot-holder runs under that slot, which is what makes the ceiling
deadlock-free; the exception is the fire-and-forget event path, where nobody
awaits the handler, so it takes a slot of its own. `ARO_CONCURRENCY`,
`ARO_HTTP_CONCURRENCY` and `ARO_HTTP_RATE` set the same three.

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Long-Running Applications
text: For applications that need to stay alive and process events (servers, file watchers, etc.), use the `Keepalive` action:

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Long-Running Applications
text: - Blocks execution until a shutdown signal is received (SIGINT/SIGTERM)

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Long-Running Applications
text: - Allows the event loop to process incoming events

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Long-Running Applications
text: - Enables graceful shutdown with Ctrl+C

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Git Actions (ARO-0080)
text: Native version control via libgit2. The bare `<git>` system object discovers the enclosing repository upward from the current working directory (like the `git` CLI); use `<git: "/path">` for an explicit repository (opened as given, no discovery).

head: CLAUDE.md > ARO Syntax > Git Actions (ARO-0080)

head: CLAUDE.md > Language Proposals
text:
Proposal identifiers are unique and every `ARO-NNNN` reference must resolve —
enforced by `Scripts/check-proposals.py`, which runs in CI. When citing a GitLab
issue in code or docs, write `GitLab #<number>` — never the `ARO-` prefix, which
reads as a proposal reference. Eight such mistakes had accumulated in `Sources/`
before the check existed (GitLab #481).

head: CLAUDE.md > Concurrency
text: All core types (`SymbolTable`, `Token`, AST nodes, `ActionImplementation`) are `Sendable` for Swift 6.3 concurrency safety.

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling
text: The codebase follows these conventions:

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > throws vs Optional
text: - **Boundaries** (parser entry points, action `execute()`, public API): Use `throws` with descriptive errors

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > throws vs Optional
text: - **Internal lookups** (symbol table, registry queries): Return `Optional` — callers decide whether absence is an error

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > throws vs Optional
text: - **SymbolTable**: Use `lookup()` for optional access, `lookupWithContext()` when a missing symbol is a hard error (it throws `SymbolLookupError` with scope chain context)

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > Parser errors
text: - Use `expect(_:message:)` for single-token expectations

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > Parser errors
text: - Use `expectPreposition(_:message:)` for preposition tokens

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > Parser errors
text: - Use `expectIdentifier(message:)` for identifier-like tokens

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > Parser errors
text: - Direct `throw ParserError.unexpectedToken(...)` is reserved for multi-token or complex pattern checks where the helpers don't apply

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > Silent fallbacks (`try?`)
text: - Never use `try?` without documenting **why** the fallback is acceptable

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > Silent fallbacks (`try?`)
text: - When a `try?` fallback indicates data loss (e.g., returning `"[]"` for a failed array serialization), log a warning to stderr: `FileHandle.standardError.write(Data("[Component] Warning: ...\n".utf8))`

head: CLAUDE.md > Error Handling > Silent fallbacks (`try?`)
text: - `try?` is acceptable for truly optional operations (e.g., best-effort cleanup in `deinit`, optional file deletion)

head: CLAUDE.md > Git Commits
text: When creating git commits, do NOT include the Claude Code signature or co-author attribution in commit messages.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом
text:
Свой VPN целиком: протокол VP1, нода, панель, клиенты под Windows и Android.
Две аудитории: тот, кто раздаёт или продаёт доступ, и тот, кто просто
подключается, — и клиенты делаются для второго не меньше, чем панель для
первого. Один автор, публичный репозиторий, разработка до стабильной 1.0.
Текущая версия разработки указана в VERSION; критерии готовности — в
docs/development-plan.md. Публикация 1.x отложена до их выполнения.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом
text:
Читай этот файл целиком перед первой правкой. Он не про стиль кода — он про то,
почему проект написан так, а не иначе.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Язык
text:
Всё на русском: комментарии, имена в интерфейсе, сообщения об ошибках,
сообщения коммитов, документация. Имена идентификаторов — английские.
Сообщения об ошибках — с маленькой буквы, без точки, как принято в Go.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Главные запреты
text:
1. **Своих криптопримитивов нет и не будет.** X25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305,
   BLAKE2s через `github.com/flynn/noise`. Ничего самодельного в криптографии.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Главные запреты
text:
2. **Нарисованная кнопка — это обещание.** Не добавляй в интерфейс элемент,
   за которым нет действия. Если экран из макета содержит кнопку, которой
   нечем работать, — кнопку не переносим, а в сообщении коммита пишем, что
   не перенесли и почему.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Главные запреты
text:
3. **`Prologue = "veil/vp1"` в `internal/vp1/handshake.go` не трогать.** Это
   строка на проводе, по сути версия протокола: изменение молча ломает
   совместимость со всеми установленными клиентами. Переименование проекта
   сюда не распространяется.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Главные запреты
text:
4. **Миграционный код в `scripts/install-panel.sh` не чистить.** Он про чужие
   старые установки под именем veil и обязан остаться.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Главные запреты
text:
5. **Нода не знает лишнего.** Нет имён покупателей, списка других нод или
   журнала «кто куда ходил». Для перезапуска без панели разрешён только
   зашифрованный снимок ключей доступа, лимитов и расхода. Срок — 24 часа
   с последней успешной синхронизации; перезапуск его не продлевает.
   Явное отключение ноды и отзыв токена имеют приоритет над снимком.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Главные запреты
text:
6. **Секреты не попадают в историю.** `.gitignore` перечисляет ключи, базы,
   учёт трафика, keystore. Не добавляй файлы в обход него.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Комментарии
text:
Комментарий объясняет **зачем**, а не что. Так написан весь проект —
не ломай интонацию:

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Комментарии
text:
У каждого нетривиального решения в комментарии стоит причина и цена
альтернативы. Комментарий вида «увеличиваем счётчик» не нужен.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Сообщения коммитов
text:
Заголовок — законченное утверждение на русском, о поведении, а не о коде:
«Клиент замечает смерть ноды по трафику, а не по расписанию», а не «фикс
failover».

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Сообщения коммитов
text:
Тело — коротко. Несколько строк: что было не так и что стало. Если решение
неочевидное — одна фраза почему. Не пересказ диффа и не отчёт о проделанной
работе: подробности живут в коде и комментариях, а в истории им тесно.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Сообщения коммитов
text:
Никаких подписей инструмента: ни `Co-Authored-By`, ни «Generated with …».
Автор у проекта один, и в истории он один.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Сообщения коммитов
text:
**Коммитим прямо в main.** Ветка и PR — только для большой правки, которую
надо обсудить до слияния. На каждую мелочь PR не заводим: владелец не хочет
нажимать кнопку слияния по десять раз в день.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Тесты
text:
Тест проверяет обещание, а не реализацию: «повтор оплаты не выдаёт второй
доступ», «каждый элемент, который ищет код, есть в разметке». Имя теста —
предложение. Если правка чинит баг — сначала тест, который на этом баге
краснеет.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Карта проекта
text:
| Где | Что |
|---|---|
| `internal/vp1/` | протокол: хендшейк, кадры, добивка. Самое опасное место |
| `internal/transport/` | камуфляж: uTLS, REALITY, WebSocket, QUIC |
| `internal/inbound/` | VLESS и Trojan рядом с VP1 — путь миграции с чужих панелей |
| `internal/panel/` | панель: `store.go` (SQLite), `api.go` (маршруты `/api/v1`), `web/index.html` |
| `internal/client/` | ядро клиента: подписка, замер нод, переезд на живую |
| `cmd/marvia-node`, `cmd/marvia-panel` | то, что стоит на серверах продавца |
| `cmd/marvia-windows/` | клиент ПК: Go + WebView2, интерфейс в `ui/app.html` |
| `android/`, `mobile/` | Android-приложение и Go-мост под gomobile |
| `docs/` | `protocol.md`, `architecture.md`, `guide.md`, `bot.md` |

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Документация — часть правки
text:
Правка, меняющая поведение, обновляет соответствующий документ той же правкой.
В README есть таблица «что уже работает» и абзац «чего пока нет» — они должны
оставаться правдой. Честность списка «чего нет» — часть продукта: она же
единственная защита от продажи несуществующего.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Чего проект не делает (и предлагать не надо)
text:
Панель на телефоне. Свой платёжный шлюз. Хостинг нод за продавца.
Причины — в конце README, они продуманы.

head: Marvia — правила работы с проектом > Правовая рамка
text:
В текстах проекта — техническое описание возможностей и ограничений.
Не выдаём новость о законопроекте за действующий закон и не обещаем
отсутствие правовых рисков. Нормы, сроки и круг лиц проверяем по официальному
тексту на дату ответа; пересказ СМИ отдельно помечаем как пересказ.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Architecture Overview
text: A **Foundation Project** is structured to separate shared infrastructure from application logic:

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 1. Foundation Dependency Boundary
text: **NEVER** import or alias raw source files from `foundation/*/ts/src` or internal Go packages.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 1. Foundation Dependency Boundary
text: - **Frontend**: Consume foundation logic via package boundaries: `@ovasabi/runtime-transport`, `@ovasabi/frontend-kit`, `@ovasabi/ui-minimal`.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 1. Foundation Dependency Boundary
text: - **Backend**: Use the `server-kit` module exports.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 2. Correlation ID Propagation
text: Every mutating command MUST carry a `correlationId`. Trace it through all workers, events, and logs.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 3. Event Contract Lifecycle
text: All domain events follow `<domain>:<action>:<state>` pattern:

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 3. Event Contract Lifecycle
text: - `:requested` - Command received, validation passed

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 3. Event Contract Lifecycle
text: - `:success` - Operation completed

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 3. Event Contract Lifecycle
text: - `:failed` - Operation failed with reason

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 4. Tenant Isolation
text: Never trust client-supplied `organization_id`. Always derive from authenticated context via `auth.OrgIDFromContext(ctx)`.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 5. Error Handling
text: Use the foundation error taxonomy (`foundation/server-kit/go/errors`). Never panic in request handlers.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 6. Bounded Operations
text: All loops, retries, and external calls MUST have explicit bounds (timeouts, max attempts).

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 7. Just-in-Time Context Retrieval (Context Budgets)
text: To avoid context window overload, do NOT read all documentation files in bulk. Always start by reading `docs/foundation/foundation_glossary.md` to get the high-level concept index. Only load specific documentation files (like `transfer_lane.md` or `hermes_projection.md`) on-demand when modifying files that touch those specific domains.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 8. Scaffold Ownership Verification
text: Before editing any file in the workspace, you MUST cross-reference `templates/scaffold.manifest.tsv` to check its sync mode. If a file is marked `overwrite` or `force`, it is owned by the Foundation core and must not be edited in project space, as local edits will be wiped on the next fleet update.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 9. Evidence & Validation Tiers
text: Apply the appropriate severity validation tier to prevent over-engineering:

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 9. Evidence & Validation Tiers
text: - **Tier 1 (Core & Critical)**: Touches money/currency math (`money/`), authentication, authorization (`auth/`, `policy/`), database schema/isolation, or WASM memory buffers. Requires full benchmarks, specs, regression tests, or formal proofs.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 9. Evidence & Validation Tiers
text: - **Tier 2 (Domain & Logic)**: Touches domain services, workers, or API handlers. Requires standard unit tests and static lints.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 9. Evidence & Validation Tiers
text: - **Tier 3 (Presentation & Copy)**: Touches CSS layout styles, copywriting, translation tokens, or non-functional UI code. Requires local lint verification only.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 10. Database vs Compute Separation (Wrong Lane Prevention)
text: **NEVER** perform CPU-bound cryptographic operations (for example, `bcrypt`, `pgcrypto` hashing like `crypt` or `gen_salt`), complex validations, regex parsing on unindexed text columns, or heavy mathematical loops inside SQL queries. Keep the database (PostgreSQL) focused on durable truth, constraints, and relational integrity. Perform compute tasks in the application layer (Go, Rust, TypeScript) to scale compute horizontally and protect the connection pool from timeout exhaustion.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 11. Simplified Technical English (STE) Documentation Standard
text: All documentation and code comments must follow the ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English standard as adapted in `docs/ste_documentation_practices.md`. Key constraints:

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 11. Simplified Technical English (STE) Documentation Standard
text: - Procedural sentences and code comments: maximum 20 words.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 11. Simplified Technical English (STE) Documentation Standard
text: - Descriptive sentences: maximum 25 words.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 11. Simplified Technical English (STE) Documentation Standard
text: - Noun clusters: maximum 3 words.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 11. Simplified Technical English (STE) Documentation Standard
text: - No contractions (`don't` → `do not`), no phrasal verbs (`set up` → `configure`), no Latin abbreviations (`e.g.` → `for example`).

head: Foundation Intelligence > Critical Rules (Mandatory) > 11. Simplified Technical English (STE) Documentation Standard
text: - Safety alerts must use `WARNING` (data loss, security), `CAUTION` (bugs, performance), or `NOTE` (information only).

head: Foundation Intelligence > Go SIMD Posture
text: Go 1.26 includes experimental `simd/archsimd` support behind `GOEXPERIMENT=simd`. Treat this as a measured, architecture-specific optimization lane:

head: Foundation Intelligence > Go SIMD Posture
text: - Do not expose `archsimd` vector types in public APIs.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Go SIMD Posture
text: - Keep scalar Go and Rust/WASM/FFI fallbacks for every SIMD path.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Go SIMD Posture
text: - Use only for bounded, benchmark-proven loops over contiguous numeric or byte data.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Go SIMD Posture
text: - Keep it out of tenant/auth/orchestration code and request handlers unless a benchmark proves the boundary cost is worth it.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Go SIMD Posture
text: - Gate CI/build use explicitly with `GOEXPERIMENT=simd`; ordinary builds must remain portable.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Frontend & High-Performance > Transport Layer
text: Use `@ovasabi/runtime-transport` for all backend communication. It handles binary envelopes, WebSocket routing, and automatic request deduplication.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Frontend & High-Performance > UI Primitives (`ui-minimal`)
text: Check `foundation/ui-minimal` before creating local components. Use `MinimalButton`, `MinimalInput`, `MinimalAppShell`, and related primitives. App-level components should be thin wrappers.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Frontend & High-Performance > Runtime SDK (`runtime-sdk`)
text: The bridge for Rust/WASM execution. It uses a 4KB control-buffer contract for high-performance communication between the JS event loop and the WASM guest.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Communicative Connections
text: The Foundation modules are linked through a unified "Nervous System":

head: Foundation Intelligence > Communicative Connections
text: 1. **Envelopes**: Every message (HTTP, WS, Redis) is wrapped in a `RuntimeEnvelope` (`runtime-transport`).

head: Foundation Intelligence > Communicative Connections
text: 2. **Resilience Runtime**: The `server-kit/go/resilience` module coordinates health, circuits, and degradation across all backend modules.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Communicative Connections
text: 3. **WASM Kernel**: `runtime-sdk` provides the 4KB high-speed buffer for JS/Rust communication.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Communicative Connections
text: 4. **Config Sync**: `config-contracts` ensures frontend and backend use the same validated schema.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Gotchas and Anti-Patterns
text: 1. **Don't ignore context deadlines**: Always pass `ctx` to DB and external calls.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Gotchas and Anti-Patterns
text: 2. **Don't use MutationObserver for business state**: Use Zustand stores.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Gotchas and Anti-Patterns
text: 3. **Don't store secrets in frontend**: Use environment-injected config or secure storage.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Gotchas and Anti-Patterns
text: 4. **Don't skip error wrapping**: Use `errors.Wrap(err, "context")` to preserve stack traces.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Gotchas and Anti-Patterns
text: 5. **Don't put regex escapes in `grep -F` patterns**: `-F` matches backslashes literally, so gates silently never fire. Enforced by `tooling/scripts/check_managed_patches.sh` (CP-38).

head: Foundation Intelligence > Gotchas and Anti-Patterns
text: 6. **Don't add a cache layer without measured layering evidence**: benchmark the existing lane with `b.ReportAllocs`, pin a `testing.AllocsPerRun` budget guard, and prove the new layer is faster before placing it in front (see `docs/database_practices.md`).

head: Foundation Intelligence > Testing Requirements
text: - **Unit tests**: ≥95% statement coverage (`go test -cover`) for new/changed production code; legacy modules must improve toward 95% when touched and cannot regress without an approved exception. Enforced by `make check-coverage-ratchet` against per-package floors in `tooling/coverage_baseline.psv`.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Testing Requirements
text: - **Integration**: Mandatory for event contracts and critical flows.

head: Foundation Intelligence > Testing Requirements
text: - **E2E**: Required for auth guards and core user journeys.

head: Agent Instructions > Project Overview
text: This repository ships one npm package:

head: Agent Instructions > Project Overview
text: - **`wp-astrojs-integration`** (`src/`) — Astro loaders, Astro actions, auth bridge, catalog virtual modules, and components built on top of the published `fluent-wp-client` package

head: Agent Instructions > Project Overview
text: - The package also exposes `wp-astrojs-integration/integration`, an Astro integration that can fetch and cache a WordPress discovery catalog for catalog-aware helpers.

head: Agent Instructions > Architecture Priorities
text: - Treat `WordPressClient` from `fluent-wp-client` as the core integration layer. Add or harden client-backed behavior before introducing higher-level loaders, bridges, or actions that depend on it.

head: Agent Instructions > Architecture Priorities
text: - Build loaders, actions, and helpers on top of proven published client primitives.

head: Agent Instructions > Architecture Priorities
text: - The package is aligned to `fluent-wp-client` `^3.0.1`; loader payloads for post/page resources must remain plain serializable objects (no legacy helper methods on `entry.data`).

head: Agent Instructions > Architecture Priorities
text: - Keep the package aligned with WordPress' extensibility model. Default to generic resource-oriented patterns that work for core entities, custom post types, custom taxonomies, plugin endpoints, and custom auth flows.

head: Agent Instructions > Architecture Priorities
text: - Prefer Standard Schema-compatible validators for client response validation interfaces so consumers can use Zod or any other compliant schema library.

head: Agent Instructions > Architecture Priorities
text: - Validate and require only the minimum data needed for a feature to work.

head: Agent Instructions > Architecture Priorities
text: - Avoid hard-coding assumptions that only fit default posts/pages.

head: Agent Instructions > Architecture Priorities > Astro Actions Imports
text:
- All Astro Actions imports **must** use the public `astro:actions` virtual module.
  Never import from internal paths like `astro/actions/runtime/server.js` or `astro/actions/runtime/entrypoints/server.js`.
  The virtual module is resolved for `tsc` via the type declarations configured in `src/env.d.ts`.

text: - **Integration tests only** — no unit tests. Every test runs against a real WordPress instance.

head: Agent Instructions > Testing > Philosophy

head: Agent Instructions > Testing > Philosophy
text: - Prioritize Astro integration behavior (loader contracts, action schema/auth wiring, and error mapping). Avoid extensive re-validation of low-level REST semantics already covered by `fluent-wp-client`.

head: AGENTS.md
text: Guidance for AI coding agents working in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text:
**MDBX Navigator** is a read-only web UI for browsing the contents of a
[libmdbx](https://github.com/erthink/libmdbx) key-value database, in the spirit
of the table browsers that exist for SQL databases. It is split into two parts
that ship as a **single binary**:

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text:
- A **Go backend** that opens an `mdbx.dat` file from the local filesystem
  (read-only, exclusive mode) and exposes the raw KV data over a small REST API.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text:
- A **React Router 7 / React frontend** (SPA, framework mode) that consumes
  those APIs and renders a read-only browser. In production the built frontend
  is embedded into the Go binary via `go:embed` and served by the same process;
  during development it can be run separately against the backend.

head: AGENTS.md > What this project is
text:
Everything the UI shows is raw bytes rendered as `0x…` hex strings — there is no
schema interpretation of keys/values.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Toolchain
text:
- **Go** 1.26.x with **CGO enabled** — `mdbx-go` is a cgo binding, so a working
  C toolchain is required and `CGO_ENABLED=1` must be set. Pure-Go cross
  compilation will not work. (The `go` directive in `go.mod` is `1.26.4`.)

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Toolchain
text: - **Node** 24.16.0 (pinned in `web/.nvmrc`; run `nvm install` inside `web/`).

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Toolchain
text:
- **pnpm** is the package manager (not npm). Install it standalone or via
  `corepack enable`. The frontend has a committed `web/pnpm-lock.yaml`.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Toolchain
text: - **goreleaser** for producing the embedded single-binary build.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Full binary (frontend embedded)
text:
> Important: the Go build embeds `web/build/client` via `//go:embed all:build/client`.
> A plain `go build ./...` **fails** unless that directory exists. Build the
> frontend first (`pnpm --dir web run build`) or use goreleaser, which does it
> for you.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Run
text: - `--data` (required) — path to the `mdbx.dat` file.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Run
text: - `--host` (default `127.0.0.1`) — bind address.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Run
text: - `--port` (default `56516`) — bind port.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Run
text:
- `--lengthcap` (default `32`) — max value length (bytes) returned in list
  results before truncation; full values come from the `/value` endpoint.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Run
text:
The DB is opened **read-only in exclusive mode** with `OptMaxDB = 1000`. The app
is browse-only by design — do not add write paths. The UI is served at
`http://127.0.0.1:56516/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Run
text:
> Exclusive mode means the open **fails if another process already holds the
> file** (e.g. a running Erigon node). Stop the writer first, or point `--data`
> at a copy/snapshot. Real Erigon chaindata has ~100+ tables, many with
> `entries=0` — that is normal, and `forward`/`backward`/`search` on an empty
> table just return `[]`.

head: AGENTS.md > Build, run, and dev workflows > Frontend-only dev loop (inside `web/`)
text:
> Some native packages run install scripts that pnpm blocks by default. They are
> explicitly allowed in `web/pnpm-workspace.yaml` under `allowBuilds`: `esbuild`
> (Vite's platform binary), `@tailwindcss/oxide` (Tailwind v4's engine), and
> `unrs-resolver` (the resolver behind `eslint-import-resolver-typescript`).
> Without those entries, `pnpm install` / `pnpm run build` fail their dependency
> check.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions & gotchas
text:
- **Hex everywhere.** Keys and values cross the API boundary as `0x`-prefixed
  hex strings. Backend encodes with `encoding/hex`; the frontend parses/formats
  with `ethers` `hexlify`/`isHexString`. Search keys may be an odd number of hex
  nibbles — `table_search.go` right-pads with a `0` to byte-align.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions & gotchas
text:
- **dupsort tables.** Duplicate keys are addressed by a `dupIdx` ordinal. Cursor
  helpers (`readForward`/`readBackward`) track `dupIdx` as they walk, and several
  handlers advance the cursor `dupIdx` times to reach a specific duplicate. Keep
  this in mind when touching cursor logic — forward and backward index
  bookkeeping are mirror images and easy to get subtly wrong.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions & gotchas
text:
- **Opening DBIs (`mdbx.DBAccede`).** Tables are opened for reading with the
  `mdbx.DBAccede` flag (`txn.OpenDBI(name, mdbx.DBAccede, …)` /
  `OpenDBISimple(name, mdbx.DBAccede)`), **not** `0`. libmdbx persists a table's
  flags (e.g. `DupSort`), and (since the mdbx-go v0.40 bump) opening an existing
  dupsort table with `0` fails with `MDBX_INCOMPATIBLE`. `DBAccede` means "adopt
  the flags the DB was created with", so dupsort tables get their dupsort cursor
  semantics. Do not revert these to `0`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions & gotchas
text:
- **Pagination.** Loaders fetch `pageSize + 1` (or `+2` when resuming from a
  cursor position) rows on purpose, to detect whether a next page exists without
  a separate count. See `web/app/routes/*` and `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` in `types.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions & gotchas
text:
- **Frontend is SPA-only.** React Router runs with `ssr: false` (set in
  `react-router.config.ts`); routes use `clientLoader` (not server `loader`) and
  there is no Node server in production — the Go binary serves the static client
  build and the API. The build still does a one-shot server pass to prerender
  `index.html`, which is why `@react-router/node` and `isbot` are runtime
  `dependencies` (not devDependencies).

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions & gotchas
text:
- **`BACKEND_URL` is hardcoded** to `http://127.0.0.1:56516/api` in
  `web/app/types.ts`. If you change the default port/host, or run the UI against
  a remote backend, this constant must change too. CORS on the backend currently
  allows all origins for `GET`.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions & gotchas
text:
- **Read-only contract.** The backend only registers `GET` routes and opens the
  env read-only. Preserve this — no mutation endpoints, no write transactions.

head: AGENTS.md > Conventions & gotchas
text:
- **No test suite yet.** There are currently no Go or frontend tests. If you add
  logic worth covering (cursor traversal / dupsort / pagination are the prime
  candidates), add tests alongside it.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text:
- **Go:** standard `gofmt`; run `go vet ./...` before finishing. Handlers live on
  the `routes.Backend` receiver; keep mdbx access inside `Env.View(...)` closures
  and always `defer cursor.Close()` / `defer Env.CloseDBI(...)`.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style
text:
- **TypeScript/React:** Prettier (config in `web/.prettierrc.json`, with the
  Tailwind plugin) + ESLint flat config (`web/eslint.config.mjs`). Use the `~/*`
  import alias for `web/app/*` (resolved natively by Vite + tsconfig `paths`).
  Styling is Tailwind v4 utility classes; theme overrides live in
  `app/tailwind.css` via `@theme` (there is no `tailwind.config.ts`).

text: - README.md — user-facing install/build/run notes.

bioparco is a public collection of cute Compose Desktop experiments. The Italian name is
the joke: specimens gathered like a bioparco, each in its own enclosure.

Sebastiano Poggi (`rock3r`) is the owner. The showcase is a Jewel Desktop app that routes
into the specimens. Each specimen is a top-level Gradle submodule with its own README.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > TDD Where It Fits
text:
Physics, hit-testing, keyboard maps, and other plain Kotlin behaviour: write the failing
test first, prove it red, then make the minimum production change.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > TDD Where It Fits
text:
Visual motion and spring feel are the specimen. Do not invent unit tests that freeze
animation constants unless the change is actually about those numbers.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > Worktree Policy
text:
Before writing tracked files from a clean `main` checkout, check whether isolation already
exists. If you are already inside a worktree or already on a non-main branch, keep working
there. Otherwise prefer a worktree so the main checkout stays clean.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > Worktree Policy
text: Plans belong in `.plans/` at the repo root, which should stay gitignored.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > Worktree Policy
text: Use the local `using-git-worktree` skill when setting up an isolated workspace.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > Every Specimen Shows Its Animation
text:
Each specimen shows its animated WebP preview and links its MP4 in **two** places: its entry
in the root README and its own `README.md`, under `## Recording`. Both use the stable URLs
`https://static.sebastiano.dev/stable/bioparco/<specimen>.webp` and `.mp4`, which the `recordings` CI job overwrites on every run, so the
READMEs never go stale. Never link one-off uploads, `raw.githubusercontent.com` or GitHub
release downloads. Tune a preview in `recordings/previews/previews.tsv`. See
[docs/RECORDING.md](docs/RECORDING.md).

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > Every Specimen Shows Its Animation
text:
`ReadmeMediaTest` in `:recordings` enforces this as part of `./gradlew check`, so a new
specimen cannot land without its preview.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > Pre-push checklist
text:
`./gradlew :recordings:recordSpecimens` is **not** part of `check`. The recordings
come from the `recordings` CI job on `v*` tags (`xvfb-run`; a push to `main` is a
backup feed). The same job publishes the README media: see
[docs/RECORDING.md](docs/RECORDING.md). Local regeneration is optional.

head: AGENTS.md > Non-Negotiables > Pre-push checklist
