head: Megaplan
text: > **Before you invoke megaplan, run the `megaplan-prep` skill.** It's the front door for every run: it sizes the work (one plan vs. an epic), shapes the brief, and picks the profile (intelligence tier), robustness level, and thinking depth. Do not run `<launcher> init` without it.

head: Megaplan
text: **Scope:** This skill covers tooling — how to invoke and drive megaplan. For the decisions that come *before* invocation (scoping, brief, profile, robustness, depth), consult the **megaplan-prep** skill. If anything here contradicts megaplan-prep on decision-making content, megaplan-prep wins.

head: Megaplan
text:
Route every step through the Arnold CLI's Megaplan subcommands. Never call agents directly.
Before the first CLI call, resolve a working launcher and reuse it for the whole run. Do not assume the removed `megaplan` entrypoint is on `PATH`; command presence alone is not enough. Prove the launcher works by successfully running a harmless CLI call with it first. In the instructions below, treat `<launcher>` as that verified command.
Launcher resolution order:

head: Megaplan
text: 1. Try `python -m arnold_pipelines.megaplan config show`.

head: Megaplan
text: 2. If that fails, try `./.venv/bin/python -m arnold_pipelines.megaplan config show`.

head: Megaplan
text: 3. If that fails, try `uv run python -m arnold_pipelines.megaplan config show`.

head: Megaplan
text: 4. If those fail, stop and report that the Arnold Megaplan module launcher is unavailable.

head: Megaplan
text: 5. Do not use the removed `megaplan` module or console entrypoint; the repo-root `megaplan.py` file is a clean-break guard.

head: Megaplan > Triage
text: Decision-making (scoping, profile, robustness, depth, brief structure) lives in the **megaplan-prep** skill — consult it before running `<launcher> init`. **Always run megaplan, even for tiny work** — `bare` robustness is the floor, never skip the harness. The few seconds of overhead pay back in the captured brief, plan, and outcome record.

head: Megaplan > Modes
text: Megaplan has two output modes, picked with `--mode` at `init`:

head: Megaplan > Modes
text: - **`--mode code`** (default): the run produces a code diff. Execute workers emit per-task file changes. Use for features, refactors, bug fixes, migrations — anything whose deliverable is source code.

head: Megaplan > Modes
text: - **`--mode metaplan`** (alias: `--mode doc`): the run produces a single document artifact at `--output <relative/path>` (e.g. `docs/design.md`). The prep, execute, and review phases use authoring-specific prompts; the execute schema uses `sections_written` instead of file changes; auditing reasons about section delivery. Use for design docs, architecture specs, research notes, RFCs, proposals, post-mortems, migration plans — anything whose deliverable is prose, not code. This is the "design-first / preplan" workflow; `prep` is the visible repository-investigation *phase* inside every run (both modes have it), not a separate mode.

head: Megaplan > Modes
text: `--from-doc <relative/path>` works with either mode. The path must be relative to `--project-dir`, must stay inside that directory, and must point to an existing file. When present, `init` imports any `## Settled Decisions` section from that prior doc artifact and stores the source path for later planning and execution context.

head: Megaplan > Modes
text: All other flags (`--robustness`, `--auto-approve`, `--phase-model`, subagent mode, overrides, step editing) behave identically in both modes. The workflow phases are the same: `prep → plan → critique → gate → revise → finalize → execute → review`.

head: Megaplan > Modes
text: A common pattern is two runs: first `--mode metaplan` to produce a rigorous design document, then `--mode code --from-doc docs/design.md` on a new idea that references that document to implement it.

head: Megaplan > Modes
text: **`--mode` and `--output` go together.** `init` rejects `--output` without `--mode metaplan` (error `invalid_args`), and rejects `--mode metaplan` without `--output`. Don't try to pass one without the other.

head: Megaplan > Working tree default
text: Default to building on top of any existing uncommitted changes in the working tree, not stashing or resetting them. The plan author should treat the dirty tree as in-progress context the new work composes with. Only deviate when the existing changes directly contradict what the new plan needs to do — and then flag the conflict explicitly rather than silently overwriting.

head: Megaplan > Start
text:
Run `<launcher> config show` before `init`. If `raw_config.execution.auto_approve` is explicitly present, do not ask the execution-mode question and honor that configured override, including configured `false`. If that raw key is absent, ask execution mode (auto-approve or review) before `init`. In the same config check, respect `execution.robustness` as a settable override when it is configured; otherwise pick robustness yourself per the **megaplan-prep** skill.
```bash
<launcher> init --project-dir "$PROJECT_DIR" [--auto-approve] [--robustness bare|light|full|thorough|extreme] [--mode code|metaplan] [--output docs/foo.md] [--from-doc docs/prior.md] [--north-star path/to/NORTHSTAR.md] "$IDEA"
```
Legacy robustness names (`tiny|standard|robust|superrobust`) are still accepted on the CLI and in stored config — they map to `bare|full|thorough|extreme` respectively — but new plans should use the canonical names.
For metaplan-mode runs, pass `--mode metaplan --output <relative/path>` (the path is where the final document artifact is written, relative to the project dir). Everything else is identical to code mode.
Pass `--from-doc <relative/path>` when the new run should inherit decisions from a prior doc artifact. The path must be relative to the project dir, must exist as a file, and can be used with either `--mode code` or `--mode metaplan`. When the source doc contains a `## Settled Decisions` section, megaplan imports those decisions and automatically promotes them into success criteria for the new plan: `load_bearing: true` decisions become `must` criteria and `load_bearing: false` decisions become `info` criteria.

head: Megaplan > Start
text: Pass `--north-star <path>` when the plan needs durable end-state intent beyond the local brief. `init` snapshots the UTF-8 markdown/text file into the plan under `anchors/north_star/plan.md`; later source edits do not affect the active plan. First iteration supports only the `north_star` anchor type. Decision-heavy prompts get full `## Anchor Context: North Star` blocks; review-family prompts get short `## Anchor Check: North Star` reminders; execution and feedback prompts get no anchor context.

head: Megaplan > Settled Decisions Section Format
text: When authoring a doc artifact that makes design decisions, use either of these canonical markdown shapes (the parser accepts both):

head: Megaplan > Settled Decisions Section Format
text:
Bold-dash inline shape (preferred for short decisions):
```md
## Settled Decisions

- **SD-001** \u2014 Keep the current storage model. _load_bearing: true_
  Rationale: External integrations depend on it.
- **SD-002** \u2014 Default model is claude-sonnet-4-6. _load_bearing: false_
  Rationale: Balance of speed and capability.
```

head: Megaplan > Settled Decisions Section Format
text:
YAML-ish shape (preferred when decisions need more fields):
```md
## Settled Decisions
- id: SD-001
  load_bearing: true
  decision: Keep the current storage model
  rationale: External integrations depend on it.
```
Use one list item per decision. Keep the `SD-NNN` convention (`SD-` prefix plus a number), store `load_bearing` as `true` or `false`, and indent continuation lines by two spaces beneath the list-item marker.
Report the plan name, execution mode, robustness, mode (and `--output` path when metaplan mode), current state, and next step.

head: Megaplan > Workflow
text: Run the loop in this order:

head: Megaplan > Workflow
text: 5. `revise` when gate recommends iteration

head: Megaplan > Workflow
text:
8. `review`
Use `next_step` and `valid_next` for CLI routing. After `gate`, follow `orchestrator_guidance` instead of manually interpreting gate signals. When a response includes `next_step_runtime`, use its `duration_hint` and `recommended_next_check_seconds` to calibrate timing.
At `--robustness bare`, the loop is: `plan` → `finalize` → `execute`. There is no prep, no critique, no gate, and no review.
At `--robustness light`, the loop is: `plan` → `critique` → `revise` → `finalize` → `execute`. There is no prep, no gate, and no review.
At `--robustness full`, the loop is: `prep` → `plan` → `critique` → `gate` → ...
At `--robustness thorough`, the loop is also `prep` → `plan` → `critique` → `gate` → ... but uses 8 critique checks instead of 4 and enables parallel critique.
At `--robustness extreme`, the loop is the same as thorough but also enables parallel review.

head: Megaplan > Step Rules
text: - `plan`: inspect the repository first; produce the plan plus `questions`, `assumptions`, and `success_criteria`. Each criterion is `{"criterion": "...", "priority": "must|should|info"}`. `must` = hard gate (reviewer blocks), `should` = quality target (reviewer flags but doesn't block), `info` = human reference (reviewer skips).

head: Megaplan > Step Rules
text: - `prep`: make repository investigation explicit before planning. Respect `skip: true` when the task is already concrete enough.

head: Megaplan > Step Rules
text: - `critique`: surface concrete flags with concern, evidence, category, and severity; reuse open flag IDs; call out scope creep. Also validate that success criteria priorities are well-calibrated — `must` criteria should be verifiable yes/no, subjective goals should be `should`.

head: Megaplan > Step Rules
text: - `gate`: read the response, warnings, and `orchestrator_guidance`. (Skipped at light robustness.)

head: Megaplan > Step Rules
text: - `revise`: show the delta, flags addressed, and flags remaining. At light robustness, routes to `finalize`; otherwise loops back through `critique` and `gate`.

head: Megaplan > Step Rules
text: - `review`: judge success against the success criteria and the user's intent, not plan elegance. Only block on `must` criteria failures. `should` failures are flagged but don't require rework. `info` criteria are waived.

head: Megaplan > Gate Principle
text:
The gate response tells the orchestrator what to do next. Follow `orchestrator_guidance` unless you have a concrete reason to disagree after investigating the repository or plan artifacts yourself.
Investigate before disagreeing: read the current plan and critique artifacts, check the project code to verify whether a flagged issue is real, or use `<launcher> status --plan <name>` / `<launcher> audit --plan <name>`.
If you disagree with the guidance, explain why briefly and use an override. Do not manually reinterpret score trajectory, flag quality, or loop state when the gate already did that work for you.

head: Megaplan > Execute
text: - After a successful gate, run `<launcher> finalize` to produce the execution-ready briefing document.

head: Megaplan > Execute
text: - In auto-approve mode, run `<launcher> execute --confirm-destructive` after finalize.

head: Megaplan > Execute
text:
- In review mode, pause at the finalize-to-execute checkpoint and wait for explicit approval before running:
```bash
<launcher> execute --confirm-destructive --user-approved
```

head: Megaplan > Long-Running Execution
text:
For plans with multiple batches, use per-batch mode to drive execution incrementally:
```bash
<launcher> execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch 1
<launcher> execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch 2
# ... continue until all batches complete
```
Between batches, poll progress:
```bash
<launcher> progress --plan <name>
```
Use `<launcher> status --plan <name>` for the full plan state, including active-step timing and any `next_step_runtime` guidance from the latest response.
Per-batch mode uses global batch numbering (1-indexed, computed from ALL tasks). Each `--batch N` call:

head: Megaplan > Long-Running Execution
text: - Validates that batches 1..N-1 are complete

head: Megaplan > Long-Running Execution
text: - Executes only batch N's tasks

head: Megaplan > Long-Running Execution
text: - Writes `execution_batch_N.json` as evidence

head: Megaplan > Long-Running Execution
text:
- On the final batch, produces aggregate `execution.json` and transitions to `executed`
Timeout recovery: re-run the same `--batch N`. The harness checks prerequisite completion and merges only untracked tasks.
Note: `progress` shows completed state only (between-batch granularity). With per-batch mode, each batch is a separate CLI call, so the orchestrator has full visibility.

head: Megaplan > Overrides
text: - `<launcher> override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."`

head: Megaplan > Overrides
text: - `<launcher> override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."`

head: Megaplan > Overrides
text: - `<launcher> override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]`

head: Megaplan > Overrides
text:
- `<launcher> override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."`
`force-proceed` is available from `critiqued` (routes to finalize, not execute). `replan` is available from `gated`, `finalized`, or `critiqued`. `add-note` is safe from any active state.

head: Megaplan > Replan
text:
Use `replan` when the orchestrator itself needs to edit the plan directly instead of asking the revise worker to do it.
```bash
<launcher> override replan --plan <name> --reason "expanding scope" --note "Also clean up the display layer"
```
After `replan`, read the returned plan file, edit it directly, then run `<launcher> critique`.

head: Megaplan > Step Editing
text:
Use `step` when you need to insert, remove, or reorder step sections (`## Step N:` or `### Step N:`) without hand-editing the markdown.
```bash
<launcher> step add --plan <name> --after S3 "Add regression coverage for the parser"
<launcher> step remove --plan <name> S4
<launcher> step move --plan <name> S4 --after S2
```
Each edit writes a new same-iteration plan artifact, preserves the latest plan meta questions/success criteria/assumptions, and resets the plan to `planned` so it re-enters critique.

head: Megaplan > Sessions And Autonomy
text: - Agents default to persistent sessions.

head: Megaplan > Sessions And Autonomy

head: Megaplan > Sessions And Autonomy
text: - `--ephemeral`: one-off call with no saved session.

head: Megaplan > Sessions And Autonomy
text: - `--persist`: explicit persistent mode.

head: Megaplan > Sessions And Autonomy
text: - Keep moving and show results at each step.

head: Megaplan > Sessions And Autonomy

head: Megaplan > Configuration
text:
View current defaults with `<launcher> config show`. Override with `<launcher> config set <key> <value>`. Reset with `<launcher> config reset`.
When routing or behavior depends on config, check `<launcher> config show` and respect user overrides instead of assuming defaults.
Settable execution keys: `execution.auto_approve`, `execution.robustness`.

head: Megaplan > Profiles
text:
A profile is a named preset that maps each workflow phase to an agent/model spec. Pass `--profile <name>` to any command that accepts `--phase-model` (`init`, `loop-init`, `tiebreaker`, etc.) to apply the preset.
See **megaplan-prep** for profile selection. Inspect available profiles with `<launcher> config profiles list`.
Resolution order, later overrides earlier within the same name: built-in (`megaplan/profiles/*.toml`) → user (`~/.config/megaplan/profiles.toml`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/megaplan/profiles.toml`) → project (`<project_dir>/.megaplan/profiles.toml`).
Inspect with `<launcher> config profiles list` and `<launcher> config profiles show <name>`.
File format: TOML with a `[profiles.<name>]` table. Keys are phase names (`plan`, `prep`, `critique`, `revise`, `gate`, `finalize`, `execute`, `loop_plan`, `loop_execute`, `review`, `tiebreaker_researcher`, `tiebreaker_challenger`); values are agent specs like `"claude"`, `"codex"`, `"omp:fireworks/kimi-k2p6"`, `"omp:zai/glm-5.2"`. Example:
```toml
[profiles.my-mix]
plan     = "claude"
critique = "codex"
execute  = "omp:fireworks/kimi-k2p6"
review   = "codex"
```
`--phase-model` overrides on the CLI stack on top of any profile.

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: Phase spec values can also be **TOML string arrays** to declare an ordered fallback chain. The first element is the selected spec; subsequent elements are only tried when the preceding spec fails with a retryable availability or infrastructure error and the next spec crosses a provider-family boundary. Example:

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: **This is the only v1 entry point for fallback chains.** Comma-separated strings, CLI fallback-list flags, and YAML chain editing syntax are not supported in v1 and are deferred to later versions.

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: Internally, multi-spec phase values are persisted in `state.json` using the compact `__fallback_json__:<json-array>` encoding. This encoding is an implementation detail of the persistence bridge — you never write it by hand. The harness decodes it transparently; every downstream consumer sees the selected spec (first element) as the legacy scalar value.

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: **Fallback advancement rules (v1):**

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: - **Allowed:** Fallback advances to the next spec only on retryable **availability** or **infrastructure** failures (connection errors, timeouts, crashes, service unavailable, internal errors).

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: - **Blocked:** Fallback does **not** advance for malformed output, schema failures, test/evidence failures, blocked results, gate/review rejection, semantic failures, auth errors, quota exhaustion, rate limits, bad requests, unsupported models, or context-window errors.

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: - **Cross-provider requirement:** The next spec must belong to a different provider family than the failing spec (e.g., `claude` → `codex`, or `omp:deepseek` → `omp:fireworks`). Same-provider advancement is rejected.

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: - **execute / loop_execute:** Fallback chains are preserved in state but advancement beyond the first spec is **blocked** in v1 — the harness raises `ExecuteFallbackUnsafe` if a retryable failure would trigger a second attempt. This protects against duplicate side effects (file mutations, checkpoints, merges).

head: Megaplan > Profiles > Fallback chains (v1)
text: When an explicit fallback chain is configured for a phase, ambient runtime fallback (e.g., automatic provider retry) is **suppressed** — only the declared chain controls advancement.

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: See the **bakeoff** skill for methodology and the **megaplan-prep** skill for when bake-offs earn their cost. This section covers the CLI mechanics once you've decided to run one.

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text:
`<launcher> bakeoff run` runs the same idea through multiple profiles concurrently, each in its own git worktree, each driven autonomously by `<launcher> auto`. Use it when the user wants to compare profiles head-to-head on the same task (e.g., "run this with kimi and the default profile side-by-side").
Supports `--mode code` (default) and `--mode doc` / `--mode metaplan` (alias). For doc-mode bake-offs, `--output <relative/path>` is required and is threaded into each profile's `<launcher> init`; merge brings the chosen profile's doc artifact back to main instead of applying a code patch. Joke mode is not yet supported.
Requires a clean main worktree by default — pass `--allow-dirty` when there are unrelated uncommitted changes you want to keep on main. Those changes stay on main and are NOT copied into the worktrees, since worktrees branch off the current commit's SHA.
The idea must be a file (`--idea-file <path>`), not an inline string. Write the idea to a file first.
Bakeoff is inherently autonomous (it spawns `<launcher> auto`), so the execution-mode question doesn't apply to bakeoff runs. `--robustness` is forwarded to each profile's `init`. When a project-layer `.megaplan/profiles.toml` exists, it's automatically copied into each worktree so project-only profiles resolve.
Lifecycle:

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: - `<launcher> bakeoff run --idea-file <path> --profiles <p1> <p2> [--mode code|doc|metaplan] [--output <relative/path>] [--exp-id <id>] [--detach] [--robustness <level>] [--allow-dirty]` — kicks off N concurrent profile runs. Without `--detach` it streams a live status table every 5s and blocks until all profiles finish; with `--detach` it returns immediately and the user polls via `status`. `--output` is required with `--mode doc|metaplan` and rejected with `--mode code`.

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: - `<launcher> bakeoff status [--exp <id>]` — current state of each profile (running / completed / crashed).

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: - `<launcher> bakeoff tail [--exp <id>]` — tail the per-profile auto logs.

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: - `<launcher> bakeoff compare --exp <id> [--judge <model>]` — collect metrics across profiles; with `--judge`, an LLM judge ranks the outputs.

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: - `<launcher> bakeoff pick --exp <id> --profile <name> --rationale "..."` — record the human-selected winner.

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: - `<launcher> bakeoff merge --exp <id>` — merge the chosen profile's worktree back to main.

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: - `<launcher> bakeoff resume --exp <id>` — resume unfinished profile runs.

head: Megaplan > Bakeoff
text: - `<launcher> bakeoff abandon --exp <id>` — discard worktrees but keep audit data.

head: Megaplan > Cloud Mode
text: `<launcher> cloud` runs a plan inside a provider-managed container with a persistent workspace volume, so the run survives the user's terminal session. Suggest it for long-running plans that would outlast a local session, multi-repo work, or when the user wants an isolated persistent sandbox. The supported remote path is `provider: ssh` against the Hetzner agentbox; `provider: local` remains for local iteration and CI smoke tests.

head: Megaplan > Cloud Mode
text: Quick subcommand reference: `init`, `build`, `deploy`, `chain`, `status`, `attach`, `logs`, `exec`, `resume`, `down`, `destroy`. Typical flow: `<launcher> cloud init` → edit `cloud.yaml` → export secrets → `<launcher> cloud deploy` → `<launcher> cloud chain <chain.yaml>`.

head: Megaplan > Cloud Mode
text: For the full reference — `cloud.yaml` fields, the `extra_repos[]` + `chain_session` multi-tenancy model, the operator loop, and the gotchas that wedge fresh runs (committed `chain_state.json`, profile-alias gap, secret-upload behavior, "internal_error" masking credit failures) — see the **megaplan-cloud** skill. Read it before launching the first cloud chain in a new project; the gotchas section will save hours.

head: Megaplan > Tickets
text: `<launcher> ticket new` creates a repo-scoped issue ticket. Use it when:

head: Megaplan > Tickets
text: - During epic/plan work you notice an out-of-scope problem, bug, or rough edge

head: Megaplan > Tickets
text: - A user explicitly asks you to capture something for later attention

head: Megaplan > Tickets
text: - You want to log an observation that doesn't block the current task but should be tracked

head: Megaplan > Tickets
text: The command prints only a ULID to stdout on success. Tickets live as `.megaplan/tickets/{ulid}-{slug}.md` files and are auto-discovered by the planner for future epics. Link them to epics with `<launcher> ticket link <ticket> <epic> --resolves` so they auto-address when the epic completes.

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text:
`<launcher> brief` creates canonical source artifacts for work you intend to run.
Use it when:

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text: - You are turning an idea into a durable single-plan input

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text: - You are scaffolding an epic's `chain.yaml` and milestone idea files

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text: - You want the source document committed before `<launcher> init` snapshots it into plan state

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text:
Briefs live as committed files under `.megaplan/initiatives/{slug}/`. Single-plan
ideas live at `.megaplan/initiatives/{slug}/briefs/{slug}.md`; epics live at
`.megaplan/initiatives/{epic-slug}/chain.yaml` with milestone briefs under the
initiative's `briefs/` directory. This is ticket-like in storage and ergonomics, but not in lifecycle:
briefs feed `<launcher> init` / `<launcher> chain start`; tickets are open problem
notes that can be discovered, linked, and auto-addressed by epics.

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text:
Briefs and tickets share the local artifact substrate: common `.megaplan/<kind>/`
path handling, slug normalization, optional frontmatter parsing, keyword
filtering, and snippets. Use `<launcher> brief list`, `<launcher> brief show`, and
`<launcher> brief search` for the brief side of that common read surface.

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text:
For epics, `<launcher> brief epic` also scaffolds `NORTHSTAR.md` beside
`chain.yaml` and declares it through `anchors.north_star`. Edit it before
`chain start`. Chain runs require this top-level North Star by default. Use it
for the durable destination and milestone briefs for local scope. Opt out only
with `--no-require-anchor --missing-anchor-ack "<reason>"` or matching
`driver.require_anchor: false` plus `driver.missing_anchor_ack` in the spec.

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text:
`<launcher> init --idea-file <path>` reads the file and snapshots its text; it does
not move arbitrary files into the retired `.megaplan/briefs/` tree. If the idea file is a markdown
artifact with YAML frontmatter, `init` snapshots only the markdown body. Use
`<launcher> brief new --init` to create the canonical source file first and then
initialize from it.

head: Megaplan > Briefs
text: Inspect captured anchors with:

head: Megaplan > Feedback
text: See **megaplan-prep** for when to add the feedback phase (`--with-feedback`). This section covers the CLI mechanics once you've decided to use it.

head: Megaplan > Feedback
text: `<launcher> feedback --plan <name>` scaffolds a `feedback.md` file in the plan directory and opens it in `$EDITOR` (or `$VISUAL`). The file has one section per workflow stage — `prep`, `plan`, `critique`, `revise`, `gate`, `tiebreaker`, `finalize`, `execute`, `review` — plus an `Overall` section. Each section has a `rating:` (integer 0–10) and a free-form `comment:` field; leave any field blank to skip it.

head: Megaplan > Feedback
text: This is **user feedback**, owned by the human after a run finishes — megaplan only scaffolds the template and parses it back on load, it never overwrites edits. Old plans without a `feedback.md` simply have no feedback attached; running `<launcher> feedback --plan <name>` on an older plan scaffolds the template on demand (backwards compatible).

head: Megaplan > Feedback
text: Use `<launcher> feedback show --plan <name>` to print the parsed summary, and `--no-edit` to just scaffold the template and print the path without launching an editor. Parsed feedback is exposed on the in-memory `Plan` record as `Plan.feedback` (a dict shaped `{"overall": {...}, "stages": {stage: {...}}}`), so downstream tooling can read it the same way as any other artifact. When `--actor`/`MEGAPLAN_ACTOR_ID` is set, parsed feedback is also written to the `plans.feedback` jsonb column so the DB and file backends stay in sync.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Filling feedback with subagents
text: Recommended process when an agent (rather than the human) is producing the initial assessment:

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Filling feedback with subagents
text: 1. **Scaffold**: run `<launcher> feedback --plan <name> --no-edit` to create the empty `feedback.md`. Note the plan directory it prints — that is where the per-stage artifacts live (`plan_v*.md`, `critique*.json`, `gate.json`, `tiebreaker_*.json`, `finalize.json`, `execution*.json`, `review.json`, etc.).

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Filling feedback with subagents
text: 2. **Per-stage assessment**: dispatch one read-only subagent per stage that actually ran (skip stages with no artifacts). Brief each subagent narrowly — give it the plan idea, the stage name, and the artifact filenames for that stage only. Ask it to return a 0–10 rating plus a 1–3 sentence comment grounded in what the artifacts show (what worked, what was weak, what was missed). Run these in parallel; they have no dependencies on each other.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Filling feedback with subagents
text: 3. **Synthesize Overall**: after the per-stage results come back, *you* (the orchestrating agent, not a subagent) read the per-stage ratings and comments together with the final outcome (`final.md`, `review.json`, any `latest_failure`) and decide an Overall rating and comment. The Overall is a judgment call about whether the run delivered the goal, not an average of stage ratings.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Filling feedback with subagents
text: 4. **Write**: edit `feedback.md` with the ratings and comments. Leave a stage blank if it didn't run or you can't form a defensible opinion — empty is better than guessed. Run `<launcher> feedback show --plan <name>` to confirm the parser picked everything up.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Filling feedback with subagents
text: Keep comments grounded in specific artifact evidence ("critique flagged X but reviewer didn't catch the regression in Y") rather than vibes. The point of feedback is signal for future runs, not a participation score.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: `<launcher> feedback search` queries every plan with non-empty feedback across both backends — local `feedback.md` files in this project tree plus, when an actor is configured, the `plans.feedback` jsonb column in the DB. Duplicates between backends are de-duped by (plan name, project_dir). Use this to answer "which profile actually scored well on this repo?" or "where did the executor get a 6 or below?". Filters:

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: - `--profile <substr>` — substring match on the plan's profile (e.g. `--profile claude` matches `all-claude`, `claude-led`, etc.).

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: - `--repo <substr>` — substring match on the plan's `project_dir` / repo path.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: - `--min-rating N` / `--max-rating N` — bounds on the Overall rating.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: - `--stage <name>` — only plans that recorded a rating for that stage (`plan`, `critique`, `execute`, …).

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: - `--has-comment` — only plans whose Overall comment is non-empty.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: - `--all` — scan every megaplan project root on this machine, not just the current tree.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: - `--json` — emit raw rows instead of a table.

head: Megaplan > Feedback > Searching feedback across plans
text: Default output is a compact table (plan, profile, overall rating, backend, repo, plus the first line of the Overall comment). Combine with `<launcher> feedback show --plan <name>` to drill into a specific match.

head: Megaplan > Observability
text: Plans started after this layer landed write an append-only `events.ndjson` event journal to their plan dir. Four CLI surfaces read from it; reach for them whenever a run is in flight or you need to reconstruct what happened. See the **megaplan-observe** skill for the full failure-mode catalog and worked invocation chains.

head: Megaplan > Observability
text: - `<launcher> introspect --plan <name>` — single structured-JSON snapshot. Always check this first when something looks stuck; the `active_phase.liveness` enum (`progressing | quiet | stalled | timeout-imminent`) and `block_details.recoverable_via` together tell you whether to wait, intervene, or override. Also surfaces `outstanding_flags_count`, useful when a plan is sitting on unresolved critique signals.

head: Megaplan > Observability
text:
- ` trace --plan [--follow] [--format json|pretty|narrative] [--phase

] [--since ]` — stream events. `narrative` format is the agent-facing affordance; `--follow` tails as the plan progresses; `--phase` and `--since` filter. Prints `trace: no events.ndjson for plan ` cleanly when a plan predates the journal.

head: Megaplan > Observability
text: - `<launcher> doctor [--plan <name> | --repo]` — diagnostic. `--repo` catches rubric/binary drift (skill profile names vs `profiles list`) and editable-install dirtiness *before* `<launcher> init`, so reach for it after a branch switch / pull / fresh checkout. `--plan` reports lock, phase liveness, LLM liveness, cost-vs-cap, orphan subprocesses, and outstanding flags.

head: Megaplan > Observability
text: - `<launcher> record-tag --plan <name> --tag <name> --note "..."` — annotate a moment in the journal so later trace/introspect calls can find it. All three args are required.

head: Megaplan > Observability
text: Stale-timestamp inference, opaque blocked state, and "model thinking vs TCP wedged" are the three confusions this layer is designed to kill — if you find yourself running `lsof`, `ps`, or doing manual `ls -lat` time math on a plan dir, you should be running `introspect` or `trace` instead.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants
text:
AI-assisted contributions are welcome, but the bar is the same as for any other code: a change must be simple, readable, tested, and explainable by the person who opens the pull request.
This file tells an AI assistant — and its human — how to produce a change that fits Redocly CLI and survives review.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants
text:
It is the single source of truth for AI tools, read from the repository root — directly or through a tool-specific pointer file.
The detailed operating rules live in [`.claude/rules/`](./.claude/rules), and the sections below link to them for the full depth.
For full development setup, the complete test command reference, and the release flow, see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > How we work
text:
- Write the simplest code that solves the problem and matches the surrounding file.
  Don't add wrappers, layers, or abstractions for something used in one place.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > How we work

  If you can't say why a line is there, remove it.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > How we work

- Push back when something looks wrong.
  A good contribution argues for the better solution instead of agreeing with every instruction.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > How we work

- Base changes on what the code and configuration actually do, not on assumptions.
  Read the relevant file before you change it.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > How we work

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > How we work

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Build System
text:
`packages/core`, `packages/respect-core`, `packages/reunite-integration`, and `packages/client-generator` are compiled by TypeScript (`tsc -b tsconfig.build.json`).
`packages/cli` is bundled by esbuild (`packages/cli/scripts/build.mjs`) — it produces `lib/index.js` (entry chunk, ~450 kB) and lazy chunks under `lib/chunks/` (redoc + react, loaded only when `build-docs` runs).
The root `npm run compile` runs both steps: tsc for the compiled packages, then the esbuild bundle for the CLI.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Build System
text: The published CLI package ships from a staged `.publish/` directory (created by `packages/cli/scripts/prepare-publish-dir.mjs`) with a hand-crafted `package.json` that has zero runtime dependencies — everything is bundled.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Respect the architecture: Walker, Visitors, Nodes
text:
Every traversal of an API description in this repository — linting, bundling, decorating, and the CLI commands that read a description — rests on one pattern: the **Walker** traverses the parsed API description, resolves `$ref`s, and calls **Visitors** — objects keyed by **Node** type — through their `enter` / `leave` / `skip` hooks at every node.
Every rule, decorator, and preprocessor is a visitor.
Write new ones as visitors: a visitor already hands you the typed node, so reach for it before a regular expression or manual drilling into the document object.
A regex belongs only where a visitor cannot get you the value, such as the text inside one string.
What each `enter` / `leave` / `skip` hook receives and when it runs, the fields of the `ctx` object, and a worked rule are in [`.claude/rules/walker-visitors-nodes.md`](./.claude/rules/walker-visitors-nodes.md).

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Testing
text:
- **Compile before testing.** Unit tests import from `lib/` (compiled output), not `src/` — run `npm run compile` after every change.
  Do not work around the compile step with aliases, `tsconfig` changes, or a separate test suite for one package.
  The slow `client-generators` e2e suite is the one exception.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Testing
text:
- Cover the feature or fix with one focused test, not a pile of redundant ones.
  A single clear test that exercises the behavior is enough.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Testing
text:
- Rule unit tests parse a YAML document, run `lintDocument`, and assert with `toMatchInlineSnapshot` so the whole output stays visible.
  Generate or update snapshots as part of the change.
  When the rule must report no problems, assert `toEqual([])`.

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Testing

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Testing

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Testing

head: Contributing to Redocly CLI with AI assistants > Testing

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Purpose (one line)
text: Heimdall is a **trust-verified, self-healing knowledge layer for AI coding agents**: it watches what an agent does, keeps a semantic-memory graph fresh across every project, and labels every search hit with a trust verdict (STRONG / WEAK / STALE) so an agent never acts on a dead path or a hallucinated match. It is the code behind the "kb_search before implementing" hard gate and the `~/knowledge-base`/Graft machinery the harness rules reference.

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Purpose (one line)
text: The vendor repo lives at `/Users/arihantdeva/Repos/heimdall`; **live runtime state lives OUTSIDE the repo** under `~/.heimdall/` (journal, lock, hint queue, config) and `~/.graft/` (backend daemon + its sqlite DB), plus the `~/knowledge-base/` TSV/telemetry/stale logs. The repo is the engine; the home-dir files are the data.

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Structure map
text:
| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `bin/heimdall.js` | npm CLI entrypoint — thin dispatch to `bin/lib/cli-main.mjs` |
| `bin/lib/cli-main.mjs` | CLI dispatch + `init`/`insert`/`hint`/`verify`/`depth` implementations |
| `bin/heimdall-reconciler.mjs` | the **single writer** daemon: watch + hint ingest + drain + periodic audit |
| `bin/lib/journal.mjs` | authoritative index: sqlite (`node:sqlite`) — paths, owned nodes/edges, pending edges, dedup queue, generations |
| `bin/lib/reconcile.mjs` | level-triggered convergence: read disk, make graph match; `audit()` = drift detector |
| `bin/lib/extract.mjs` | desired state per file: hash + L0-L3 node/edge extraction, node-id namespacing, tree-sitter bridge |
| `bin/lib/heimdall_extract.py` | Python bridge: calls graphify per-language extractors directly (never `graphify.extract()`) |
| `bin/lib/depth.mjs` | depth ladder (path/file/symbol/graph), capability probe, config, root matching |
| `bin/lib/lock.mjs` | O_EXCL single-writer lock with stale-PID reclamation |
| `bin/lib/hints.mjs` | the only channel a non-writer may use: append "look at this path" lines |
| `bin/lib/sink.mjs` | projection targets: `MemorySink` (tests) and `GraftSink` (graft CLI) |
| `bin/lib/adapters.mjs` | `heimdall init --harness X` config writers (pi, claude-code, codex, cursor, opencode, gemini-cli, deepseek) |
| `bin/kb-search.sh` | ranked search: graft retrieve + verify + graft explore walk |
| `bin/kb_search_verify.py` | path extraction for stale-node rehoming (`extract_paths`); the retired CLI/verdict path is gone |
| `bin/kb-stale-scan.py` | full-graph stale sweep: rehome via `kb-rehome.sh` or log+delete |
| `bin/kb-rehome.sh` | deterministic rehome of a stale node (bounded basename search) |
| `bin/kb-health.sh` | `heimdall doctor`: daemon up, CLI responsive, search smoke, inventory freshness |
| `bin/kb-rebuild.sh` | full graph rebuild: backup → wipe → parallel restore → re-seed → prune → verify |
| `bin/seed-graft.sh` | load `~/knowledge-base/.inventory.tsv` into Graft (idempotent) |
| `bin/sync-edits.sh` | one-shot bootstrap: replay Pi session edit logs (write/edit/hashline_edit) as hints |
| `bin/telemetry.sh` | `collect`/`view`/`usage` — nodes/day, sync age, kb_* tool-call counts |
| `extensions/kb-tools.ts` | Pi extension: exposes `kb_search`/`kb_insert`/`kb_sync` agent tools |
| `extensions/kb-autosync.ts` | Pi extension: hook that appends path hints (never writes the graph) |
| `extensions/kb-orient.ts` | Pi extension: injects prior-work hits into the first user prompt of a session |
| `extensions/kb-search-guard.ts` | Pi extension: warns/escalates/blocks only on UNscoped discovery chains; agent-callable `kb_guard_pause` suspends enforcement 1–20 turns |
| `extensions/lib/kb-guard-core.mjs` | pure guard state machine (testable without the Pi runtime) |
| `vendor/graphify/` | vendored graphify v0.3.17 (MIT) — per-repo code-graph extractors (tree-sitter) |
| `vendor/graft/` | vendored Graft source (Apache 2.0) — backend daemon; **not prebuilt**, build from source |
| `config/heimdall.yaml.example` | example backend config → copy to `~/.graft/config.yaml` |
| `launchd/com.heimdall.backend.plist.example` | launchd template for `graftd` |
| `docs/adapters.md` | what each `heimdall init --harness X` installs |
| `docs/heimdall_compare.{dot,png}` | graphify vs Graft vs Heimdall positioning diagram |
| `types/pi-coding-agent.d.ts` | minimal type stub of the Pi host API so extensions typecheck standalone |
| `tests/*.test.mjs` | node:test suites (44 tests) |
| `.pi-subagents/` | subagent run artifacts (input/output/transcripts/meta) — gitignored, historical record |

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > How to run / test
text: Tests are property-based against invariants (convergence, idempotency, single-writer, ownership, order-independence, ABA guard), not call sequences. The concurrency tests are the point. The L3 end-to-end test self-skips when tree-sitter is absent. The `kb-verify.test.mjs` suite uses a `selftest:` node-id mode that reads file content straight from disk, so verdicts are testable **without a graft daemon**.

text: Dev-dependency note: `@types/node`, `typebox`, `typescript` are dev-only (the extensions import `typebox`); runtime deps are **zero** (Node built-ins only).

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - **Single writer everywhere.** Every graph/journal mutation goes through `Lock` (O_EXCL create + liveness check, stale-PID reclamation). Hooks/scripts may only emit **hints** (`hints.mjs` / `kb-autosync.ts`), which are advisory prompts, never descriptions of what changed. If you add a writer, route it through the lock and reconcile path — the codebase treats any second writer as a bug by design.

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - **Journal is authoritative; the sink (graft graph) is a rebuildable projection.** Sink writes happen BEFORE the journal commit (crash between → path stays dirty → redone; reverse order could mark clean an unprojected path).

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - **Reconcile is idempotent by construction**: desired state = pure function of (bytes, depth). Content hash is the change oracle; generation counter is the ABA guard (a stale commit is rejected, not merged).

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - **Exact ownership**: nodes/edges/pending belong to exactly one path; a commit deletes and re-inserts all of that path's rows in one transaction. Cross-file edges to not-yet-indexed symbols park as pending edges resolved from either side (order independence).

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - **Bound parameters only** for sqlite — the old hand-rolled LIKE escaping (`likeEsc`, python `escape`) was a recurring correctness bug; never build SQL by string concat here.

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - **Skip rules live in exactly one place**: `skipPath()` in `bin/lib/reconcile.mjs` (mirrored conceptually in `kb-autosync.ts`). If you touch skip rules, update both.

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - **Never PATH-resolve graft** in scripts: `GRAFT` env or `~/.local/bin/graft` absolute path only (supply-chain guard: a shadowed binary could delete memory nodes from inside a search). Keep it.

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - **Bridge calls graphify's per-language extractors directly**, never `graphify.extract()` — that would litter `graphify-out/cache/` next to every indexed file and add a second cache that can disagree with reality.

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed
text: - Node ids are namespaced by path hash (`nodeIdFor`) because graphify derives ids from file stem (every `index.ts` would collide).

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Conventions observed

text: 2. **Live state is in `~/.heimdall/` and `~/.graft/`, not in the repo.** `journal.db`, `reconciler.lock`, `hints.jsonl`, `~/.heimdall/config.json`, `~/.graft/config.yaml`, `~/.graft/profiles/default/graft.db`. Touching these outside the lock/reconcile machinery can corrupt a running system. Tests deliberately sandbox into temp dirs.

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Gotchas / warnings
text: 3. **The L3 test self-skips without tree-sitter** (silent green on a box that cannot do L3). If you see "L3: ... skipped", the machine cannot index symbols — not a code failure. `python3` on this machine is 3.9.6; the bridge needs a `tree_sitter`-capable python (see `pythonWithTreeSitter` candidates, `HEIMDALL_PYTHON` env).

head: AGENTS.md — Heimdall (working guide for AI agents) > Gotchas / warnings
text: 4. **`heimdall doctor`/`search` need the graft daemon running** (launchd `com.graft.daemon`, config `~/.graft/config.yaml` from `config/heimdall.yaml.example`). head: CLAUDE.md > What is vue-formify
text: A lightweight (~4kb gzipped) type-safe form management library for Vue 3. It provides automatic form value collection, schema validation (Zod, Valibot, ArkType via StandardSchemaV1), nested object/array support, and third-party UI component integration.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: CI runs `oxl:lint` and `vitest` on PRs to main.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core pattern: Generic factory components
text: Components (`Form`, `Field`, `FieldArray`, `Error`) are factory functions that accept a generic type parameter and return typed `defineComponent` results. This enables full TypeScript generics propagation from `useForm<T>()` through to component props (e.g., `name` autocompletes all valid nested paths of `T`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`composable/useForm.ts`** — Primary public API. `useForm<T>(options?)` returns typed component instances (`Form`, `Field`, `FieldArray`, `Error`) plus imperative methods (`handleSubmit`, `setError`, `resetForm`, etc.).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`composable/useInput.ts`** — Internal composable shared by Field/FieldArray. Manages per-field reactive state (value, error, dirty, touched, valid) in the store.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`components/Form.ts`** — Form component factory. Manages form store, provides context via `provide/inject`, handles submit validation.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`components/Field.ts`** — Field component factory. Renders `<input>` or custom component via `as` prop or slot. Delegates to `useInput()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`components/FieldArray.ts`** — Dynamic array field management. Slot exposes `{ fields, add, remove, error }`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`components/Error.ts`** — Error display component. Uses `errorFor` prop to bind to a named field.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`utils/store.ts`** — Singleton reactive store (`Record<string, FormStore>`) keyed by form UID.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`utils/validator.ts`** — Runs StandardSchemaV1-compliant validators and maps issues to field errors.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`utils/types.ts`** — All TypeScript types including `StandardSchemaV1`, `GetKeys<T>` (deep path autocomplete), `FormType`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`utils/utils.ts`** — Path parsing (dot/bracket notation), `mergeDeep`, `EventEmitter`, `flattenObject`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Source layout (`src/`)
text: - **`main.ts`** — Public entry point exporting `useForm`, `useInput`, `FormType`, `InputProps`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key concepts
text: - **Field paths**: Fields use dot-notation (`user.email`) and bracket notation (`users[0].name`) for nested/array values. The `GetKeys<T>` type generates all valid paths for autocomplete.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key concepts
text: - **Validation modes**: `'onSubmit'` (default) validates on submit; `'onChange'` validates live using `EventEmitter` for cross-component coordination.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key concepts
text: - **Store structure**: Field values are stored internally as `{ value, error, isDirty, isTouched, isValid, ignore }` objects and flattened when surfaced to the user.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key concepts
text: - **StandardSchemaV1**: Vendor-neutral validation interface — any schema library implementing `~standard.validate()` works without adapters.

text: **asv-mavlink** is a .NET MAVLink library targeting `net10.0`. It provides protocol parsing/serialization, generated MAVLink packet models, client/server microservices, device abstractions, and tools for working with MAVLink-compatible vehicles and payloads such as PX4, ArduPilot, ADS-B, SDR, GBS, RSGA, radio, FTP, missions, parameters, diagnostics, and related ASV extensions.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Protocol Layer
text: - `Dialects` contains MAVLink XML dialect definitions used by the generator.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Protocol Layer
text: - `Features` contains protocol pipeline features such as wrapping, filtering, and ID mapping.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Protocol Layer
text: - `IPayload`, `MavlinkMessage`, and `MavlinkV2Message` are central serialization abstractions.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Protocol Layer
text: Packet serialization is span-based and allocation-conscious. Preserve field order, sizes, CRC behavior, sequence handling, signatures, and MAVLink wire compatibility.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Generated Messages
text: Most files in `src/Asv.Mavlink/Protocol/Messages` are generated from XML dialects using `Asv.Mavlink.Shell`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Generated Messages
text: Prefer changing XML dialects, generator models, or Liquid templates instead of hand-editing generated packet files. If a generated file must be edited temporarily, document why and expect it to be overwritten by regeneration.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Microservices
text: Microservices live under `src/Asv.Mavlink/Microservices`. They expose typed client/server behavior over MAVLink packets: heartbeat, command, params, params-ext, missions, FTP, logging, mode, GNSS, ADS-B, SDR, GBS, radio, chart, diagnostic, audio, and ASV-specific extensions.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Microservices
text: Use R3 observables and reactive properties consistently. Prefer typed packet filters and existing `InternalSend`, `InternalCall`, and `InternalFilter` patterns instead of ad hoc message routing.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Devices
text: Device abstractions live under `src/Asv.Mavlink/Devices`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Devices
text: - Client devices model discovered MAVLink systems and compose microservice clients.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Devices
text: - Server devices expose local MAVLink services.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Devices
text: - Factories identify PX4, ArduPilot, generic, ADS-B, radio, SDR, GBS, RFSA, RSGA, and other supported device types.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Devices
text: Keep device discovery, identity, heartbeat handling, and component IDs explicit. Do not hide target system/component assumptions in helper code.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > CLI
text: CLI commands live under `src/Asv.Mavlink.Shell`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > CLI
text: The shell is built with ConsoleAppFramework and uses Spectre.Console for interactive output. Keep command options stable, documented, and script-friendly. Existing commands include packet generation, MAVLink monitor, proxy, FTP tree/browser/server, packet viewer, devices info, diagnostics, SDR export, and serialization benchmarks.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Storage and File Systems
text: Use the existing `Asv.Store` and System.IO.Abstractions patterns for file-backed behavior. Tests should avoid real file-system coupling unless explicitly validating integration behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Quality
text: - Nullable reference types are enabled (`<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`).

head: AGENTS.md > Code Quality
text: - `<LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>` is used; modern C# features are acceptable when they keep code clear.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Quality
text: - `Asv.Mavlink` allows unsafe blocks; use them only where protocol performance or binary interop justifies it.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Quality
text: - Generated `.Designer.cs` files and generated protocol messages should not be reformatted manually.

head: AGENTS.md > Code Quality
text: - Keep public APIs stable and explicit; this package is published to NuGet.

head: AGENTS.md > MAVLink Guidelines
text: - Treat MAVLink wire compatibility as a public contract.

head: AGENTS.md > MAVLink Guidelines
text: - Preserve little-endian binary layout, array lengths, extension-field behavior, truncation rules, CRC extra values, and MAVLink v2 signing semantics.

head: AGENTS.md > MAVLink Guidelines
text: - Prefer typed packet classes and payload objects over raw byte manipulation outside parser/serializer internals.

head: AGENTS.md > MAVLink Guidelines
text: - Use `MavlinkIdentity` and target system/component IDs deliberately in clients, servers, and tests.

head: AGENTS.md > MAVLink Guidelines
text: - For request/response flows, respect cancellation tokens, timeouts, retries, and existing `InternalCall` conventions.

head: AGENTS.md > MAVLink Guidelines
text: - Avoid blocking calls in packet-processing paths; use async APIs and observables consistently.

head: AGENTS.md > Naming Conventions
text: - MAVLink packet classes: `FooPacket`

head: AGENTS.md > Naming Conventions
text: - MAVLink payload classes: `FooPayload`

head: AGENTS.md > Naming Conventions
text: - Client microservices: `FooClient` / `IFooClient`

head: AGENTS.md > Naming Conventions
text: - Server microservices: `FooServer` / `IFooServer`

head: AGENTS.md > Naming Conventions
text: - Extended services: `FooClientEx` / `FooServerEx` where the existing convention already uses `Ex`

head: AGENTS.md > Naming Conventions
text: - Resource files: `RS.resx`, `RS.Designer.cs`, and domain-specific `.resx` files such as `ParamsDesc.resx`

head: AGENTS.md > Comments and Documentation
text: - Write code comments, XML docs, Markdown, and README content in English unless editing localized resource files.

head: AGENTS.md > Comments and Documentation
text: - Use clear English names for types, members, variables, files, modules, and public APIs.

head: AGENTS.md > Comments and Documentation
text: - Keep MAVLink terminology consistent with upstream MAVLink specs and ASV dialect XML files.

head: AGENTS.md > Comments and Documentation
text: - Add comments only when they explain intent, constraints, protocol quirks, compatibility requirements, assumptions, tradeoffs, or non-obvious behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Comments and Documentation
text: - Keep comments concise and up to date; remove or update them when the code changes.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Principles
text: - Follow SOLID principles. Each class/service should have a single, well-defined responsibility.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Principles
text: - Prefer composition over inheritance unless inheritance is clearly justified by existing protocol or device patterns.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Principles
text: - Keep protocol parsing, microservice behavior, device composition, CLI presentation, and storage concerns separated.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Principles
text: - Depend on abstractions at I/O boundaries to preserve testability.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Principles
text: - Keep public APIs explicit, stable, and easy to understand.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Principles
text: - Eliminate duplicated logic through extraction rather than copying.

head: AGENTS.md > Design Principles
text: - Avoid god objects, hidden side effects, unclear ownership, and implicit global protocol state.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Guidelines
text: **Think before coding:** State assumptions explicitly. If multiple interpretations exist, present them rather than picking silently. If something is unclear, ask before implementing. If a simpler approach exists, say so; push back when warranted.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Guidelines
text: **Simplicity first:** Write the minimum code that solves the problem. No speculative features, no abstractions for single-use code, no "flexibility" that was not requested, no error handling for impossible scenarios.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Guidelines
text: **Surgical changes:** Touch only what the task requires. Do not improve adjacent code, comments, or formatting. Match existing style. If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it; do not delete it. Remove only imports, variables, or functions that your changes made unused.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Guidelines
text: **Goal-driven execution:** For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan with verifiable steps before starting. Define success criteria and loop until the change is verified, for example by adding or running focused tests for protocol, serialization, and microservice changes.

head: astrcodey 编码规范
text:
> 适用对象:所有在本仓库工作的 AI agent(Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等)与人类贡献者。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 内置插件
text: 内置插件只能依赖插件系统,不能依赖项目的其他内容。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > DTO 规则
text: 只有数据跨边界时才创建 DTO(HTTP 请求/响应、SSE 载荷、前端契约、插件/MCP 边界、版本化持久化格式)。不要为内部函数调用创建 DTO;新增结构前先检查现有契约是否已满足。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 映射规则
text: - 需要上下文的转换用显式映射函数;明显、无损的转换才用 `From`。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 映射规则
text: - 不要为「未来可能用」添加 `Option<T>` 字段(可留 TODO 注释)。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 映射规则
text: - `serde(rename_all = "camelCase")` 只用于 protocol/wire 类型和 LLM tool call 参数类型。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > Rust 实现
text: - 函数直白,优先清晰的领域命名,不滥用 `utils`/`helper`/`manager`。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > Rust 实现
text: - 避免过宽的 `pub`,避免不必要的 `clone`/`unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > Rust 实现
text: - 不要在 `.await` 时持有锁;不要启动无生命周期、无错误处理、无 tracing 的后台任务。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > Rust 实现
text: - 优先直接编写本地代码;仅当逻辑被复用,或提取能实质性澄清一个重要流程时,才抽辅助函数。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 最小改动
text: - 只解决所提出的问题;不添加推测性功能、可配置性或相邻改进。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 最小改动
text: - 优先编辑现有代码,而不是重写文件或重塑无关逻辑。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 最小改动
text: - 修复 bug 或处理 review 意见时,保持既有控制流和逻辑结构,尤其是初始化、并发、元数据等敏感路径。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 最小改动
text: - 可以提及无关问题,但不要把它作为当前任务的一部分去解决。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 注释
text: - 注释用于阐明不明显的意图和不变式,不要用来弥补代码的不清晰。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 注释
text: - 不要写解释下一行功能、重述签名、描述刚做的改动的注释——这些属于 PR 描述。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 注释
text: - 必需的不变式注释(如锁的获取顺序、`SAFETY` 解包理由、`#[allow(dead_code)]` 的原因)只陈述不变式,不叙述。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 先重用,再写新代码
text: 写新代码前,先查找现有实现,在现有基础上扩展而不是重复编写:

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 先重用,再写新代码
text: - **共享原语**:不要创建无明确领域归属的 `support`/`utils` 桶。产品级默认目录在 `astrcode-core::config::defaults`(进程级路径原语实体在 `astrcode-paths`,由 defaults re-export);扩展可用的路径、frontmatter、shell 与 discovery 能力在 `astrcode-core`(SDK 保留 re-export);S5R 子进程运行时(peer 状态机与 I/O driver)在 `astrcode-s5r-runtime`,host 与 worker 共同依赖,不属于 SDK 作者面;工作区沙箱、展示格式化、哈希和运行时策略留在所属 crate,日志在 `astrcode-log`。写新函数前先按语义在 `crates/<owner>/src` 与调用方中搜索签名。重新实现工作区已有的原语,或手写 `std`/`tokio` 已提供的功能,属于 review 意见而非风格偏好。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 先重用,再写新代码
text: - **语义匹配而非名称匹配**:采用一个函数前,确认它的归一化、错误类型、超时/重试行为是否适用于调用点。语义不同时,新建一个名称更明确的函数,并在注释里指出被放弃的近似函数。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 先重用,再写新代码
text: - **常量与固定标记**:协议标签、错误标识、事件名称、命令标签等,先找语义相同的现有常量/枚举复用。确属新值时,在相关逻辑附近定义本地常量,不要把字面量散落各处;修改既有行为时,命名与格式要与既有常量一致。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 先重用,再写新代码
text: - **测试脚手架**:复用 `crates/*/tests/fixtures`、`crates/astrcode-protocol/fixtures` 等现有 fixtures,而非新写 setup。写测试前先 `rg -l '<fn-under-test>' <crate>/src <crate>/tests`。新测试必须能暴露现有测试未覆盖的失败模式。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 仅写必要代码
text: 新增的文件、类型、分支、注释都是需要证明其合理性的成本,而非进步:

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 仅写必要代码
text: - **在信任边界验证**:外部输入、从磁盘读入的字节、RPC 载荷、配置——在边界校验后即信任类型,不要重复检查类型系统或已校验的上游层已经保证的内容;保证不明显时用 `file:line` 注明校验位置。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 仅写必要代码
text: - **跨边界值要重复校验**:跨越持久化、RPC、版本边界的值永远无法被对端代码保证(对端可能更旧或有缺陷,磁盘字节可能损坏),因此在执行破坏性操作(删除、覆盖)前要立即重新校验。删除既有保护属于行为变更,需对抗性 review,不是清理。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 仅写必要代码
text: - **每个新分支都要有可命名的触发器**:一个具体的输入、状态或故障条件。无法命名触发条件就不要写该分支;确实不可触发就把它编码进类型,否则返回有类型的内部错误。`debug_assert!` 仅可用于从未跨磁盘/RPC/配置边界的纯内部运算,绝不能作为解码后或外部数据的唯一保护。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 仅写必要代码
text: - **不要用默认值掩盖数据损坏**:在某个值必须存在的地方(如必须存在的元数据)不要用 `unwrap_or_default()`,那会把损坏转成错误结果;应返回有类型的错误,显式表达失败而非隐式成功。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 仅写必要代码
text: - **错误上下文只加一次,加在可操作的层级**:每一层重新包装等价上下文是噪音;把易错链展开成嵌套 `match`(本可用 `?` 或组合子)同样不可取。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 测试
text: - 只写必要的测试。集成测试放 `tests/`,单元测试写在模块下方。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 验证
text: 优先最小相关检查:`cargo fmt --check` → `cargo test -p <crate> <test_name>` → `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`。然后再跑 `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --all-features`。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 验证
text: 大范围改动:`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --all-features`。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 验证
text: - 普通代码改动:至少跑 `cargo fmt --check`、相关 crate/test 的最小测试、相关 crate 的 clippy。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 验证
text: - 大范围/跨 crate/并发/协议/持久化/发布相关改动:跑完整 `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --all-features`。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 验证
text: - push、创建 PR、合并 PR、发 release 前:必须先确认本地或 CI 的对应验证已通过;若只是等 CI,也要明确说明哪些检查仍在跑。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 验证
text: - 若因环境缺失、耗时不可接受、用户明确要求跳过等原因无法执行验证,必须在回复中写清楚未跑哪些命令、原因和剩余风险。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 验证
text: - 不要把「能编译/能合并」当作验收;需根据改动性质补必要的行为测试或手动验收说明。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 回复要求
text: - **下一步建议**:基于当前改动,接下来最值得做的事(按优先级排列);若无则说无。两种情况都需说明原因。

head: astrcodey 编码规范 > 回复要求
text: - **剩余风险**:当前改动中已知或潜在的隐患、未覆盖的边界情况;若无则说无。

head: Spawned - Project Context
text: Rust actor framework inspired by Erlang OTP. Provides `Actor` trait (similar to GenServer) that separates concurrency logic from business logic.

head: Spawned - Project Context > Two Execution Modes
text: - **tasks**: Async/await with tokio. Use `spawned_rt::tasks` and `spawned_concurrency::tasks`

head: Spawned - Project Context > Two Execution Modes
text: - **threads**: Blocking, no async. Use `spawned_rt::threads` and `spawned_concurrency::threads`

head: Spawned - Project Context > Two Execution Modes
text: Both provide identical Actor API. The `tasks` module has `Backend` enum: `Async`, `Blocking`, `Thread`.

head: Spawned - Project Context > Key Types
text:
| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `Actor` | Trait for stateful message handlers |
| `Handler<M>` | One impl per message type (RPITIT, not object-safe) |
| `ActorRef<A>` | External handle to communicate with a running actor |
| `Context<A>` | Handler-side handle (passed to handlers) |
| `Response<T>` | Unified request-response wrapper (tasks: `.await`, threads: `.unwrap()`) |
| `Recipient<M>` | Type-erased per-message reference (`Arc<dyn Receiver<M>>`) |
| `CancellationToken` | Signal cancellation to timers/actors |
| `TimerHandle` | Handle for `send_after`/`send_interval` |

head: Spawned - Project Context > Actor Lifecycle
text: 1. `started(&mut self, ctx: &Context<Self>)` - Setup before message loop

head: Spawned - Project Context > Actor Lifecycle
text: 2. `Handler<M>::handle(&mut self, msg: M, ctx: &Context<Self>)` - Process messages

head: Spawned - Project Context > Actor Lifecycle
text: 3. `stopped(&mut self, ctx: &Context<Self>)` - Cleanup after stop

head: Spawned - Project Context > Conventions
text: - Use `tracing` for logging (not `println!`)

head: Spawned - Project Context > Conventions
text: - Prefer `&self` over `&mut self` for thread-safe methods

head: Spawned - Project Context > Conventions
text: - Handle poisoned mutexes with `unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())`

head: Spawned - Project Context > Conventions

head: CLAUDE.md > Task Runner (mise)
text: All tasks are defined in `.mise.toml`. Run `mise tasks` to see available commands. Most-used: `mise run nix:switch` (build + activate), `mise run nix:check` (flake check). Full task table: [docs/reference/mise-tasks.md](docs/reference/mise-tasks.md).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview
text: **Hybrid approach**: Nix manages packages/versions (reproducibility), symlinks manage native config files per tool (flexibility) — configs are never converted to Nix expressions. Neovim uses dpp.vim with modular TOML files (one TOML per concern: `dpp.toml`, `dpp_lazy.toml`, `ddc_settings.toml`, `lsp_settings.toml`, etc.) whose load list and lazy grouping live in `dpp/config.ts`; dpp.vim and denops.vim themselves come from the Nix store and `init.lua` only bootstraps them — see `docs/reference/neovim-config.md`. CI/CD is a hybrid Docker + Nix pipeline (`changes` → (`build-image` ∥ `check`) → `verify-docker`; `changes` detects docs-only diffs so the downstream jobs skip) to work around GitHub Actions' disk limits.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview
text: Full design rationale: [docs/explanation/architecture.md](docs/explanation/architecture.md). CI/CD details: [docs/reference/ci-cd-pipeline.md](docs/reference/ci-cd-pipeline.md), evolution/lessons learned: [docs/explanation/cicd-evolution.md](docs/explanation/cicd-evolution.md).

head: CLAUDE.md > Repository Structure
text: `.config/` holds native per-tool configs (bash, fish, git, tmux, nvim, hypr, waybar, alacritty), symlinked in by Nix. `flake.nix` + `home.nix` + `nix/modules/*.nix` define the Nix side. `.mise.toml` defines task runner commands. `llm/` holds AI context/personality files.

head: s3p — notes for Claude
text: Source is CaffeineScript (`.caf`). Build compiles to `build/`. Tests run from `build/` via Jest.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > Workflow
text: - `npm run build` — compile `source/**.caf` → `build/**.js`. Errors from CaffeineScript are clear; read the caret location.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > Workflow
text: - `npm test` — Jest against `build/`. Needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules` (wired in) for AWS SDK v3 dynamic imports.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > Workflow
text: - `npm run test:coverage` — same + coverage report.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > Workflow
text: - MinIO: `docker compose up -d`. Integration tests require env: `S3_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9000 AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=testAccessKey AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=testSecretKey AWS_REGION=us-east-1`. Without `S3_ENDPOINT`, integration tests auto-skip.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > Workflow
text: - Test scenarios share `source/test/MinioTestHelper.caf` — use `setupTestScenario` which handles bucket cleanup in `afterAll`.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CLI → API
text: Every CLI command has `--api-example` that prints the equivalent `require('s3p').xxx({...})` call. Use this to understand how to drive the API from tests.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CaffeineScript gotchas (things I've hit)
text: **Skim this before writing `.caf` — the parser is strict about layout.**

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CaffeineScript gotchas (things I've hit) > Chained method calls
text:
- Multi-line: leading dot on each continuation line.
  ```
  foo
  .replace a, b
  .replace c, d
  ```

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CaffeineScript gotchas (things I've hit) > Chained method calls
text:
- One line: all but the last call need explicit parens.
  ```
  foo.replace(a, b).replace c, d
  ```

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CaffeineScript gotchas (things I've hit) > Chained method calls
text: - WRONG: `foo.replace a, b .replace c, d` — parser chokes mid-line.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CaffeineScript gotchas (things I've hit) > `describe.skip` is not a thing here
text: Gate integration tests with `if endpoint` wrapping the whole `describe` block; in the `else`, register a `test "skipped"` so Jest sees the file as a test file.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CaffeineScript gotchas (things I've hit) > Smart import
text: `import &@aws-sdk/client-s3` auto-resolves any later-referenced unassigned names (`S3Client`, `PutObjectCommand`, `ListObjectsV2Command`, etc.) to properties of that module. No need to destructure up front.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CaffeineScript gotchas (things I've hit) > Everything returns a value
text: Functions return the last expression. The last statement in a file is auto-exported. Useful, but means stray expressions at the end of a function become its return value.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > CaffeineScript gotchas (things I've hit) > Scopes
text: `if` / `unless` do NOT create a new scope. Functions, classes, comprehensions, and `while`/`until` do. Variables are auto-let at the topmost scope where they're assigned.

head: s3p — notes for Claude > Known existing-code pitfalls
text: - `normalizeOptions` in `S3Comprehensions.caf` strips `returning:` from options without mapping it to `returnValue`. Callers must use `returnValue:` directly (see `S3P.list` fix).

head: s3p — notes for Claude > Known existing-code pitfalls
text: - `syncObject` in `S3.caf` calls `@copyObject` which doesn't exist — probably should be `@copy`. Not exercised by tests; the higher-level `S3P.sync` flow doesn't go through `syncObject`.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: Logstash is a server-side data processing pipeline that ingests data from multiple sources, transforms it, and sends it to various destinations. It's part of the Elastic Stack and is a **hybrid Java/Ruby application** using JRuby.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview > JRuby and versions
text: - The JRuby version is defined in **`versions.yml`** (repo root). The project uses **vendored JRuby only** — no external Ruby, rvm, or rbenv is required; Gradle installs JRuby into `vendor/jruby` via the bootstrap task.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview > JRuby and versions
text: - The gem path includes a Ruby compatibility version segment (e.g. `vendor/bundle/jruby/X.Y.0`). It is intentionally hardcoded in Gradle (`rubyUtils.gradle`), shell scripts (`bin/logstash.lib.sh`), and Java test helpers (e.g. `RubyEnvTestCase`). To find the current value, grep for `vendor/bundle/jruby/` in `bin/logstash.lib.sh`. Do not treat it as a bug or "dynamicize" it when working on the codebase.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview > Single source of truth for versions
text: - **`versions.yml`** in the repository root is the single source of truth for Logstash version, JRuby version, bundled JDK, Jackson, and related coordinates. Gradle loads it in `settings.gradle`; the `logstash-core` and `logstash-core-plugin-api` gemspecs copy from it. When in doubt about a version, check or update `versions.yml`.

head: AGENTS.md > Build Commands
text: Run all build and test commands from the **repository root** (where `gradlew` and `versions.yml` live), unless a specific task or doc says otherwise.

head: AGENTS.md > Build Commands
text: All commands require a JDK that meets the `sourceCompatibility` defined in `build.gradle` (currently 17+). JDK 21 is preferred and is the version bundled for distribution (see `bundled_jdk` in `versions.yml`). Ruby tests run via vendored JRuby — no external Ruby, rvm, or rbenv needed.

head: AGENTS.md > Build Commands
text: Use Gradle tasks as the normal entry points from the repo root. Rake and bundle are used as leaf tools where the existing Gradle tasks or scripts already wire them up.

head: AGENTS.md > Build Commands
text: **Build performance (CI):** For faster `installDefaultGems`, use `JARS_SKIP=true`; required jars are already vendored or in JRuby stdlib.

head: AGENTS.md > Running Tests
text: **Test layout:** Unit specs live under **`spec/`** (root) and **`logstash-core/spec/`**. Integration and acceptance tests live under **`qa/`** (e.g. **`qa/integration`** for integration tests). Use the commands below from the repo root; the single-integration-test example uses a path under `qa/integration`.

head: AGENTS.md > Running Tests
text: **Test task structure:** There are two separate Gradle test tasks: `javaTests` (pure Java unit tests) and `rubyTests` (Ruby specs **and** Java tests that depend on Ruby infrastructure). The top-level `test` task excludes all classes itself and simply delegates to both, so `./gradlew test --tests ...` will silently match nothing. Always apply `--tests` to `javaTests` or `rubyTests` directly.

head: AGENTS.md > Running Tests
text: **`javaTests` vs `rubyTests` split:** Several Java test classes are excluded from `javaTests` and included in `rubyTests` because they load Ruby code at runtime. The exclude/include lists are in `logstash-core/build.gradle`. If `--tests` returns "No tests found for given includes", the class is likely in the other task. Examples of Java tests that live in `rubyTests`:

head: AGENTS.md > Running Tests
text: - `OutputDelegatorTest`, `JavaCodecDelegatorTest` — test delegators that wrap Ruby plugin instances

head: AGENTS.md > Running Tests
text: - `ConfigCompilerTest`, `CompiledPipelineTest`, `EventConditionTest` — test config compilation which invokes the Ruby parser

head: AGENTS.md > Running Tests
text:
- `PluginFactoryExtTest` — tests Ruby plugin instantiation
```bash
# All unit tests (Java + Ruby)
./gradlew test

# All Java tests (pure Java, no Ruby dependency)
./gradlew :logstash-core:javaTests

# Single Java test class
./gradlew :logstash-core:javaTests --tests org.logstash.TimestampTest

# Single Java test method
./gradlew :logstash-core:javaTests --tests org.logstash.TimestampTest.testEpochMillis

# Java tests by pattern
./gradlew :logstash-core:javaTests --tests "org.logstash.settings.*"

# WRONG — will silently run nothing because `test` excludes all classes:
# ./gradlew :logstash-core:test --tests org.logstash.TimestampTest

# Java test that depends on Ruby — must use rubyTests, not javaTests:
./gradlew :logstash-core:rubyTests --tests org.logstash.config.ir.compiler.OutputDelegatorTest

# All Ruby tests (core) — also runs the Ruby-dependent Java tests listed above
./gradlew :logstash-core:rubyTests

# Single Ruby spec file
SPEC_OPTS="-fd -P logstash-core/spec/logstash/agent_spec.rb" \
  ./gradlew :logstash-core:rubyTests --tests org.logstash.RSpecTests

# All integration tests
./gradlew runIntegrationTests

# Single integration test
./gradlew runIntegrationTests -PrubyIntegrationSpecs=specs/slowlog_spec.rb

# All X-Pack Ruby tests
./gradlew :logstash-xpack:rubyTests

# Single X-Pack Ruby test
SPEC_OPTS="-fd -P spec/config_management/elasticsearch_source_spec.rb" \
  ./gradlew :logstash-xpack:rubyTests --rerun-tasks

# Single Ruby test for core or X-Pack (fast, direct JRuby)
bin/rspec logstash-core/spec/logstash/some_spec.rb
bin/rspec x-pack/spec/config_management/elasticsearch_source_spec.rb
```
