head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The daemon must fit one MTU (500 bytes).** `Snapshot.encoded` shrinks `n` (cards) — body,
  then title, then drop cards — and never touches `s` (sessions). Cards dropped for any reason
  (2-card cap or MTU) are counted into the separate `m` key.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **Encode with `sortedKeys` always.** Otherwise the "did it change?" comparison is always
  true and the board gets written every second.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **Every pose stays ≥ 5 s (`Timings.minPose`).** Poses skipped during that hold are dropped,
  never queued — a queue makes the mascot narrate an ever-later past.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **`--hook` must always exit 0**, daemon running or not. A broken hook breaks the user's
  session, which is far worse than a frozen screen.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **Unknown ≠ zero** in the usage panel: `-1` means unknown, `0` is a real value. Within one
  window (same `resets_at`) the percentage only increases, so a lower value is stale — never
  overwrite a newer one. Foreign keys in the shared cache file (`PROFILE_NAME`, `COST_*`)
  must survive.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The LAN counter only ever goes up.** A repeated nonce in GCM destroys the confidentiality
  of both frames that used it, so `LanSealer` increments before sealing and the board rejects
  anything not strictly greater than what it has already accepted. The board tells the Mac
  where to continue from when it accepts the connection — neither side stores a counter file.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The `sessionKey` is a full-account credential.** File only (`~/.tamaclaude/session-key`,
  mode 600), never argv, never env, never logged, re-read every poll. Not the Keychain: the
  adhoc signature changes cdhash on every build, so the item would prompt on every upgrade.
  The Finnhub key (`~/.tamaclaude/finnhub-key`) follows the same rule through `SecretFile`
  even though it is a smaller credential — a rule with an exception is a rule nobody
  remembers which file it applies to. It rides in a query string, so a quote URL is itself a
  secret: log it through `StocksSource.describe` or not at all.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **`-v` and `-psn_*` are not modes.** LaunchServices appends `-psn_0_12345`; an app that
  rejects unknown args dies on double-click.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **`PageKind` is a three-way contract**: `Pages.swift`, `firmware/main/ct_pages.h`, and
  `tools/gen/pages.py`. The raw values travel on the wire, so reordering one side silently
  changes what every frame means. `tamatest` reads the real header to check.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The weather strip is five columns on all three sides.** `[weather] fc_cols` sizes the C
  arrays and `WeatherFrame.hourLimit` caps what the Mac sends; a sixth hour on the wire is
  bytes the board drops. `tamatest` reads `layout.h` to check, as it does for `PageKind`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The 24h shape is 16 levels wide on all three sides.** `[crypto] spark_cols` sizes the C
  array, `CryptoFrame.sparkPoints` caps what the Mac sends, and a 17th point is bytes the board
  drops — same shape as the weather strip, and `tamatest` reads `layout.h` to check. **The
  stocks page draws a day-range band in that same box instead**: Finnhub's free tier has no
  history endpoint to plot, but every `/quote` carries today's `h`/`l`, so the box answers a
  different question — where the price stands in today's swing, not how it got there. It ships
  as one `"r"` key for the hero row only, and it is the first thing the squeeze drops.
  Everything else on the two pages stays pixel for pixel identical, because the user swipes
  between them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **A sparkline's baseline is its first point**, which is the 24h open. That is what makes the
  last bar agree with the printed percentage by construction rather than by luck, and it is why
  `fold` must keep both ends (`gen/trend.py` ↔ `ct_trend.c` ↔ `CryptoSource.spark`, all three
  using integer half-up rounding — Python's `round()` goes to even and would drift alone).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **One frame per page, and each must fit `Wire.maxPayload` alone** (ADR-0003). A frame is a
  mascot `Snapshot` exactly when it has **no** `g` key; a frame with `pl` is page settings.
  `{"g":N,"x":1}` retires a page the user turned off — not sending it is not enough (ADR-0002).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The screen jumps back to the mascot on an event *id*, not on a state.** `Snapshot.attention`
  (`"a"`) counts sessions *entering* a needs-human state; the board jumps only when that number
  goes up. Deciding from the state itself yanks the screen back every snapshot for as long as a
  permission prompt sits unanswered, and never jumps for the second session that asks while the
  first is still waiting.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The top bar belongs to every page, and never repeats what a page already shows bigger.**
  It lives outside every page root (`ct_topbar.c` ↔ `gen/topbar.py`), built last so LVGL keeps
  it on top. The mascot page answers `ct_ui_shows_clock`/`ct_ui_shows_usage` for itself — the
  rule is in the bar, the fact is in the page. Get that backwards and the idle screen shows the
  same clock twice.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The footer belongs to every page too, but unevenly — and that split is the rule.**
  Its band, age line, and mini mascot are for the four data pages (`ct_footer.c` ↔
  `gen/footer.py`, built before the age label and the mini so both sit *on* the band and the
  mascot straddles its top rule). Its **page pips are for all five**, mascot page included:
  swiping is the device's only input and an affordance present on four screens out of five
  teaches nobody. The pips count only pages `in_rotation` — a pip for a page a swipe skips is
  a promise the board does not keep — and the current pip doubles as the rotation clock, so
  "which page" and "how long until it moves on its own" are one object, not two rows.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **Page frames carry a data *age*, not a timestamp**, and the board counts on from there.
  A re-read with identical figures is still sent (the age is the difference); an age that is
  merely ticking is not a change.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **LVGL's 48 KB pool is the budget that runs out first, and it fails as a hang, not an
  error.** `CONFIG_LV_MEM_SIZE_KILOBYTES` is separate from the ESP heap (which has ~110 KB
  free); building the five pages already spends ~88% of it, and the remainder is what draw
  tasks and layers are allocated from *while rendering*. Exhaust it and `lv_draw_dispatch`
  spins waiting for a unit that never frees: `lv_timer_handler` never returns, the task
  watchdog fires every 5 s, and the only symptom is a frozen screen — nothing points at
  memory. So **draw composite graphics in one custom-draw object per page, not one widget per
  shape** (`ct_mini`, `ct_footer`, and the weather scene all do this); nine widgets per page
  was enough to wedge the board. `main.c` prints `lv_mem` beside `heap` once a minute.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Invariants worth knowing before you touch things
text:
- **The `VisualState` enum is a contract with the firmware.** Adding or reordering it means
  changing `ct_model.c`/`ct_mascot.c` too. `tamatest` guards this.

head: CLAUDE.md > The second path (LAN)
text:
When BLE has been quiet for 10 s the daemon opens a TCP connection to the board on
port 7333 and sends the same snapshot, sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key it pushed
over the config characteristic. The board finds nothing on its own and **never talks to
claude.ai** — the `sessionKey` stays on the Mac. The reasons are in `LanFrame.swift`,
`LanTransport.swift` and `ct_lan.c`; the frame layout must match `ct_lan.c` byte for byte.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text:
- Comments and design docs are in **Thai**; identifiers, commands, and error strings stay in
  English. Existing comments explain *why*, often citing what was tried and rejected — match
  that density rather than describing what the code does.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text:
- Commit subjects are lowercase imperative with a conventional prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`) and
  read as a sentence about the visible effect, e.g. `feat: give the sky half the screen and
  cap cards at two`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions
text:
- The board font has no em dash — anything crossing BLE goes through `Text.swift` first.
  Thai does cross, but only shaped: `Text.fit` picks the glyph variants (ADR-0008), and it is
  the only door, so nothing else may hand a raw Thai string to the wire.

head: CLAUDE.md > Agent skills > Issue tracker
text:
Issues live as GitHub issues in `thaitop/tamaclaude`, managed with the `gh` CLI. External PRs
are not a triage surface. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Agent skills > Triage labels
text:
The five canonical roles use their default label strings (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`,
`ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`). See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Agent skills > Domain docs
text: Single-context: `CONTEXT.md` + `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance
text: This repository uses **Belayin' Pin Bob** for workflow orchestration through Claude skills and subagents. Skills invoke specialized subagents, pass state through `.bob/` artifacts, and enforce quality gates automatically.

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > What Bob Provides
text: Bob installs workflow skills and specialized subagents to `~/.claude/`:

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > What Bob Provides
text: 1. **Workflow Skills** - User-invocable workflows (`/bob:work`, `/bob:explore`)

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > What Bob Provides
text: 2. **Subagent Orchestration** - Specialized agents for each workflow phase

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > What Bob Provides
text: 3. **State Management** - Persistent workflow artifacts in `.bob/state/` directory

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > What Bob Provides
text: 4. **Git Worktrees** - Isolated development environments

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > Available Workflows > /bob:work — Concurrent Agent Team Workflow
text: Multiple coder and reviewer teammates work in parallel. Requires `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`.

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > Available Workflows > /bob:explore — Team-Based Exploration with Adversarial Challenge
text: Concurrent specialist agents for codebase exploration. No code changes.

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > Available Workflows > /bob:audit — Spec Audit
text: Verify code satisfies stated invariants in spec-driven modules. Read-only — reports drift but doesn't fix it.

head: Belayin' Pin Bob - Agent Guidance > Loop-Back Rules
text:
| Trigger | Route to | Reason |
|---------|----------|--------|
| CRITICAL/HIGH review issues | BRAINSTORM | Re-think the approach |
| MEDIUM/LOW review issues | EXECUTE | Targeted fixes |
| Test failures | EXECUTE | Fix the code |

head: Cross-version compatibility
text:
For every feature or behavioral change, explicitly consider backward and
forward compatibility between versions that users may run at the same time.
Identify all independently released producers and consumers—including store
apps, extensions, desktop/mobile apps, controllers, installers, update feeds,
and services—and do not assume their deployments are atomic or ordered.

head: Cross-version compatibility
text:
When a change affects a shared protocol, API, persisted data, configuration,
artifact, or update path:

head: Cross-version compatibility
text:
- Prefer additive changes, capability negotiation, and overlapping supported
  version ranges over an exact-version cutover.

head: Cross-version compatibility
text:
- Plan a rollout in which old/new and new/old component combinations continue
  to interoperate throughout store review, staged rollout, and delayed updates.

head: Cross-version compatibility
text:
- Add cross-version tests for each supported pairing, and make release checks
  reject a new artifact when it has no compatibility overlap with a counterpart
  that users can still receive or run.

head: Cross-version compatibility
text:
- Document the compatibility window, rollout order, fallback/error behavior,
  and eventual removal plan for legacy support in the owning topic or tactical
  document.

head: Cross-version compatibility
text:
Do not intentionally strand a supported released component or require users to
update independently distributed components in lockstep unless the maintainer
has explicitly accepted the incompatibility and its user-visible consequences.

Focused, living records of continuing concerns live under

iOS runtime, release/signing, or legacy migration behavior, read the
corresponding topic document. Update it when work changes the current state,

[`docs/tactical/`](docs/tactical/README.md). Tactical filenames use
zero-padded numeric prefixes such as `000-topic.md`, `001-next-topic.md`.
Completed tacticals remain as execution records; continuing guidance belongs

head: Cross-version compatibility > Documentation roles
text:
Architecture and research documents own durable system shape, product history,
or external facts. They must not silently override a newer accepted decision in
a topic document. Mark historical proposals explicitly and link to the current
topic.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: crune is a static web dashboard that visualizes Claude Code session logs. It consists of two parts:

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: 1. **Data pipeline** (`scripts/analyze-sessions.ts` + `scripts/knowledge-graph-builder.ts`): Reads JSONL session files, extracts structured data, builds a semantic knowledge graph, and outputs JSON files to `public/data/sessions/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: 2. **Frontend** (`src/`): React SPA that loads the generated JSON and renders three views --- Overview, Session Playback, and Knowledge Graph.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - **No routing library** --- `App.tsx` manages view state via `useState<ViewMode>` (overview | playback | knowledge)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - **No state management library** --- Data flows through props from `App.tsx` down. Each view fetches its own data via custom hooks (`useSessionIndex`, `useSessionDetail`, `useSessionOverview`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - **Plain CSS** --- Each component has a co-located `.css` file. Global CSS variables are in `src/index.css` (colors, fonts, shadows)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - **Session playback** opens as a right-side drawer overlay, not a separate route

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: - UI text is in Japanese (commit `abc92e1`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: - Color variables have semantic roles: `--accent` (amber, interactive), `--brand` (amber, logo only — unified with accent), `--success/warning/danger` (status), `--chart-1..6` (data visualization)

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: - Tool call display logic is centralized in `ToolCallBlock.tsx` with per-tool rendering (Bash, Edit, Write, Read, Grep, Glob, Agent)

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Conventions
text: - Expand/collapse pattern: `useState(false)` + conditional render (no animation), see `SubagentBranch.tsx`

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text: `analyze-sessions.ts` reads from `~/.claude/projects/` by default. Override with `--sessions-dir` and `--output-dir` flags.

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text: Before analysis, `/insights` is automatically executed via `claude -p` to refresh facets data in `~/.claude/usage-data/facets/`. Use `--skip-facets` to skip this step.

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text:
Output structure:
```
public/data/sessions/
  index.json              # All sessions (sorted by createdAt desc)
  overview.json           # Cross-session stats + knowledge graph + tacit knowledge
  detail/{sessionId}.json # Individual session turns, subagents, linked plan
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text: The knowledge graph builder (`knowledge-graph-builder.ts`) uses a multi-signal embedding approach:

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text: - Text TF-IDF (weight 0.50) + Tool-IDF (weight 0.25) + structural features (weight 0.25), concatenated with sqrt-weighting

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text: - Truncated SVD via Gram matrix power iteration (k = min(80, max(20, m/4)))

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text: - Agglomerative clustering (average linkage) with elbow-detected threshold + oversized cluster splitting + **facets-based narrow cluster merging**

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text: - Louvain community detection -> Brandes betweenness centrality

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details
text: - See [docs/knowledge-graph-algorithm.md](docs/knowledge-graph-algorithm.md) for full details

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details > /insights Integration
text: The pipeline reads `/insights` facets data (`~/.claude/usage-data/facets/`) to improve accuracy:

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details > /insights Integration
text: - **Topic labels**: Uses `underlying_goal` from facets instead of TF-IDF keywords when available

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details > /insights Integration
text: - **Narrow cluster merging**: Merges small clusters (≤2 sessions) that share normalized goal categories

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details > /insights Integration
text: - **Reusability scoring**: Adds `successRate` and `helpfulness` signals (weight 0.10 each) derived from `outcome` and `claude_helpfulness`

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details > /insights Integration
text: - **Synthesis prompt enrichment**: Includes goals, friction details, and success rate in the LLM synthesis prompt

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details > /insights Integration
text: - **Session list**: Shows `brief_summary` from facets instead of raw first user prompt

head: CLAUDE.md > Data Pipeline Details > /insights Integration
text: Facets reader (`scripts/knowledge-graph/facets-reader.ts`) normalizes 50+ raw goal categories into ~10 canonical categories (feature, bugfix, refactoring, documentation, review, testing, ci, git_ops, setup, other).

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis
text: The pipeline detects recurring workflow patterns and generates reusable Claude Code skill definitions using LLM synthesis via `claude -p`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: `analyze-sessions` automatically synthesizes the top skill candidates during data generation:

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: - `--synthesize-model <model>` --- Use a specific Claude model (e.g. `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: - `--synthesize-count <n>` --- Number of top candidates to synthesize (default: 5)

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: - `--skip-synthesize` --- Skip LLM synthesis for faster builds

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: - `--facets-dir <path>` --- Custom facets directory (default: `~/.claude/usage-data/facets`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: - `--skip-facets` --- Skip `/insights` refresh and facets integration

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: - `--use-human-feedback` --- Fold playback feedback (issue #24) into synthesis + reusability scoring (default OFF for A/B)

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: - `--feedback-file <path>` --- Custom feedback file (default `public/data/feedback.json`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: Pre-synthesized results are stored in `overview.json` as `synthesizedMarkdown` on each `SkillCandidate` and displayed immediately in the Knowledge Graph UI. Synthesis output is post-processed by `stripSynthesisPreamble()` to remove any LLM preamble before the YAML frontmatter.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Pre-synthesis (build time)
text: Synthesis calls use `--no-session-persistence` to prevent creating spurious JSONL session files.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > On-demand re-synthesis
text: The UI provides a "再合成" button for on-demand re-synthesis with full graph context (connected topics, community, centrality). This requires the local skill server:

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > On-demand re-synthesis
text: The skill server (`scripts/skill-server.ts`) accepts POST requests at `/api/synthesize` and calls `claude -p` with the enriched prompt including graph context.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > On-demand re-synthesis
text: **Synthesis jobs are global** (`SkillSynthesisProvider`, `src/hooks/`): each `useSkillSynthesis(key)` reads/triggers a job keyed by a stable id (topic id, or an `adhoc:<sorted topic ids>` slice id). The fetch lives in the provider, so a synthesis **keeps running in the background and its result persists** when you change filters, switch tabs, or deselect a node — coming back to the same key shows the running/finished job. (Earlier the state was component-local and was lost on unmount.)

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: After a candidate is synthesized, `analyze-sessions` evaluates the generated SKILL.md via `scripts/skill-evaluator.ts` and persists the result onto `SkillCandidate.evaluation` (serialized into `overview.json`). Evaluation is gated behind synthesis **success** so heuristic `skillMarkdown` is never scored.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: Three layers (`evaluateSkill`):

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: 1. **Structural validation** --- deterministic zod-backed YAML frontmatter checks (name kebab-case, description length, body present). Always runs locally.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: 2. **LLM rubric** --- `claude -p` scores the skill 0-100 across nameQuality / descriptionTriggering / instructionsConcrete / noPreambleNoise (25 each). Runs unless `--skip-eval`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: 3. **Smoke firing** --- stubbed (deferred to a follow-up issue); always reports `skipped: true`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: `overallScore` = 50 for structural pass + scaled rubric (0-50). `toSkillEvaluation()` strips the raw LLM response and intermediate parse before persistence.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: Flags (next to the `--synthesize-*` flags, eval defaults **ON**):

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: - `--skip-eval` --- Skip the LLM rubric (structural-only).

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: - `--eval-model <model>` --- Claude model for rubric scoring (e.g. `haiku`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: - `--eval-threshold <n>` --- Soft threshold (default 60). When `overallScore < n`, the pipeline runs **exactly one** bounded re-synthesis retry and keeps the higher-scoring attempt. The candidate is never dropped; low scores are flagged in the UI. `--eval-threshold 0` disables retries. The retry decision is the pure function `shouldRetrySynthesis(score, threshold)`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Skill Synthesis > Skill Evaluation (issue #20)
text: **UI badge**: When `candidate.evaluation` exists, `KnowledgeNodeDetail` and `TacitKnowledgeView` render a compact評価バッジ --- 構造 OK/NG, スコア NN/100, optional rubric内訳, and 改善ヒント list. Pass/borderline/fail tone uses `--success`/`--warning`/`--danger` (pass ≥70, borderline ≥50, fail otherwise or structural NG).

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: A chunk-level dense vector index for retrieval, alongside (not replacing) the whole-session embedding path in `scripts/knowledge-graph/`. PoC findings + Go/Hold/Pivot recommendation are in [docs/rag-poc.md](docs/rag-poc.md) (issue #35).

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: Modules (`scripts/knowledge-graph/`):

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: - `embedder.ts` --- `EmbeddingBackend` interface (injectable; tests use a deterministic fake, no network), turn-level chunk extraction (`extractChunks`: `userPrompt + assistantTexts + tool names` per turn), int8 `quantize`/`dequantize` (L2-normalized components → `[-127,127]`, scale `1/127`, bounded round-trip error), and `embedSessions` orchestration.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: - `embedding-io.ts` --- `writeEmbeddingIndex`/`readEmbeddingIndex` (`public/data/embeddings/index.bin` row-major int8 + `meta.json`) and `createTransformersBackend` (lazy-loaded Transformers.js, `Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`, 384-dim, mean pooling + normalize). Kept separate so tests never import `@huggingface/transformers`.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: - `retriever.ts` --- hybrid `createRetriever`/`createRetrieverFromIndex`: dense cosine (dequantized) + sparse BM25 (reuses `buildBm25`), per-query min-max normalized, blended `alpha*dense + (1-alpha)*bm25` (default `alpha=0.6`), with a per-session diversification cap (default 2). `retrieve(query, k, opts)` returns `RetrievedChunk[]`.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: Flags on `analyze-sessions` (default **OFF**, promotion gated on the PoC):

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: - `--embed` --- run the embedder over analyzed sessions and write `public/data/embeddings/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: - `--embed-model <id>` --- override the default model.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in)
text: PoC harness: `npx tsx scripts/rag-poc.ts` (measures footprint / throughput / latency + A/B; `--fake` forces the no-network backend).

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Retrieval-enriched synthesis (issue #33, opt-in)
text: `--retrieval-context` (on both `analyze-sessions` and the `crune` CLI, default **OFF** for clean A/B) swaps the loosely-related cluster-blob "examples" slot (Representative User Prompts + Enriched Tool Patterns) for a **Retrieved Relevant Moments** section built from the hybrid retriever's top-k turn snippets (k=8). The rest of the synthesis prompt (frontmatter ask, topic info, graph position, human-flagged moments, heuristic reference) is unchanged.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Retrieval-enriched synthesis (issue #33, opt-in)
text: - **Query** per candidate: `buildRetrievalQuery(candidate, topic)` = topic label + top keywords + truncated heuristic `skillMarkdown` (600 chars). Pure/testable.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Retrieval-enriched synthesis (issue #33, opt-in)
text: - **Section**: `buildRetrievedMomentsSection(chunks)` renders `[sessionId#turnIndex] (score: N.NNN) snippet`; `SynthesisRequest.retrievedContext?: RetrievedChunk[]` threads it into `buildSynthesisPrompt`. When present and non-empty, the blob slots are suppressed and a numbered task rule grounds the skill in the retrieved moments.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Retrieval-enriched synthesis (issue #33, opt-in)
text: - **Retriever wiring** (`buildSynthesisRetriever`, shared via `scripts/knowledge-graph/synthesis-retriever.ts`): reuse the EmbedResult from `--embed` if it ran this run → else read an on-disk index at `public/data/embeddings/` → else embed fresh in-memory via `createTransformersBackend` + `embedSessions`. Index reuse is gated on per-chunk `sessionId`/`turnIndex` identity (`chunksAlign`), not just count, so a stale index can't ground synthesis on unrelated sessions. BM25 text is re-derived with `extractChunks` (same chunk order as the index). On any failure (no index, no backend) it logs a warning and returns `null` so synthesis FALLS BACK to the cluster blob (never crashes).

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Retrieval-enriched synthesis (issue #33, opt-in)
text: - **Preview A/B** (`crune --preview --retrieval-context`): the synthesis loop prints `Context strategy: retrieval (N moments)` vs `cluster blob` per candidate so a human can compare side by side.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Retrieval-enriched synthesis (issue #33, opt-in)
text: - **Measurement**: the #20 evaluator path (`overallScore`) is unchanged — run `--retrieval-context` vs without and compare `SkillCandidate.evaluation.overallScore` to A/B synthesis quality. Tests inject a fake `EmbeddingBackend`/in-memory retriever; the `claude -p` call stays behind the `synthesizeWithClaude` seam (never invoked in tests).

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Semantic Search UI (issue #34)
text: The chunk index powers a UI semantic search and a "似た瞬間" bookmark affordance, served by the skill-server.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Semantic Search UI (issue #34)
text: - **Endpoint**: `POST /api/retrieve` (`scripts/skill-server.ts`, proxied by `vite.config.ts`). Body `{ query, k? }` → `{ results: RetrievedChunk[] }`. The on-disk index is resolved lazily by `createLazyRetrieverProvider` (`scripts/retrieve-service.ts`); a **successful** retriever is memoized ONCE and reused (the model is never reloaded per request), while negative resolutions are NOT cached so a server started before `--embed` ran recovers once the index appears — no restart. The provider builds the embedding backend from the loaded index's own `meta.model`/`meta.dim` (via an injected `BackendFactory`) so query vectors always match the chunk vectors even when the index was embedded with `--embed-model`. Resolution distinguishes an ABSENT index (**400** `{error:'no embedding index; run analyze-sessions --embed'}`) from a CORRUPT/unreadable one (**503**, logged via `console.error`), so the UI degrades gracefully without telling the user to re-run a command that won't help. The pure `handleRetrieveRequest` is unit-tested with an injected `RetrieverResolution`.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Semantic Search UI (issue #34)
text: - **BM25 fallback**: `meta.json` persists only the short snippet, so BM25 runs over snippets as a documented degraded fallback; dense cosine (alpha=0.6) remains the primary signal.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Semantic Search UI (issue #34)
text: - **Hook**: `src/hooks/useSemanticSearch.ts` — debounced (`SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`) best-effort POST; pure `mapRetrieveResponse(ok, body, status)` maps the HTTP status (503 → "モデル準備中", 404 → "検索未対応", else generic) and pure `runSearchRequest` encapsulates the stale-response guard — both tested without a DOM.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Semantic Search UI (issue #34)
text: - **UI**: `SemanticSearch` bar on the Overview dashboard (`src/components/search/`); clicking a result opens the playback drawer at the matched turn via an optional `turnIndex` on `onSessionSelect` (App → `SessionPlayback initialTurnIndex`). On a bookmarked turn, `FeedbackCluster` shows a 🔍 "このブックマークに似た瞬間" popover (`SimilarMoments`) that searches with the turn's text and deep-links similar moments.

head: CLAUDE.md > RAG Embedding Pipeline (issue #32, opt-in) > Semantic Search UI (issue #34)
text: - **Static-deploy note**: in-browser retrieval (loading the ~93KB quantized index + a WASM embedder) is a viable follow-up; the current PoC routes through the local server.

head: claude-share
text: Single npm package (`@0xpv/claude-share`) exposing two binaries: `claude-share` (sharer) and `claude-connect` (receiver). Source lives in `claude-share/src/` and `claude-connect/src/` respectively; both compile into their own `dist/` via the root `package.json`.

head: claude-share > Dev commands
text: Build: `bun run build` (compiles both via bun build). Lint: `bun run lint`.

head: claude-share > Architecture
text: **Single public port** (default 2586): `port/detector.ts` sniffs first bytes — `CONNECT` goes to MITM proxy, TLS ClientHello (`0x16`) is terminated and piped to the Hono API on `PORT+1`, plain HTTP is piped to the Hono API on `PORT+1` (localhost-only). Bore tunnels PORT.

head: claude-share > Architecture
text: **MITM proxy** (`proxy/mitm.ts`): intercepts TLS only for `INTERCEPT_DOMAINS` (`api.anthropic.com`, `platform.anthropic.com`, `platform.claude.com`, `mcp-proxy.anthropic.com`). All other CONNECT requests are transparent TCP-piped — never touch the cert or plaintext.

head: claude-share > Architecture
text: **Token injection**: sharer's OAuth token is read from macOS Keychain at startup and injected per-request inside the MITM. Never written to disk, never sent to receiver.

head: claude-share > Architecture
text: **Pairing**: connect URL format is `http://<host>/connect/<pairingCode>`. The pairingCode is `base58(32-byte session key)` — it's also the private decryption key. Only the first 5 chars are sent over HTTP for session lookup; the receiver decrypts the response blob locally using the full key from the URL.

head: claude-share > Architecture
text: **Session key lifecycle**: `session.key` (32 bytes) → `session.pairingCode` (base58). Pressing `n` in TUI calls `regeneratePairingCode()` which zeroes nothing but replaces key+code and clears `pairingAttempts`. `destroySession()` zeroes the key.

head: claude-share > Security constraints — do not break
text: - Never log or transmit the full pairingCode over HTTP (it's the private key)

head: claude-share > Security constraints — do not break
text: - Only send `pairingCode.slice(0, 5)` in the `/pair` POST body

head: claude-share > Security constraints — do not break
text: - `INTERCEPT_DOMAINS` must stay minimal — non-Anthropic traffic must bypass the MITM

head: claude-share > Security constraints — do not break
text: - Blocked on `api.anthropic.com`: `/v1/files`, `/v1/fine_tuning`, `/v1/assistants`

head: claude-share > Security constraints — do not break
text: - Rate limit: 5 attempts per known IP, 20 for `"unknown"` (bore doesn't forward real IPs)

head: claude-share > Receiver saved state
text:
`~/.claude-share/connections/<machineId>.json` — pruned on startup if `sharedUntil` is past.  
`~/.claude-share/config.json` — device name.

head: claude-share > Known quirks
text: - `ensureBore()` must run **before** any `p.intro()`/`p.select()` calls. clack's `p.confirm()` tears down stdin in a way ink can't recover from if it runs after other prompts.

head: claude-share > Known quirks
text: - `--share <url>` and `--share=<url>` are both supported in the receiver.

head: claude-share > Known quirks
text: - bore doesn't set `x-forwarded-for`, so all bore requests arrive as `ip = "unknown"`.

text: Config Sync synchronizes configurations and policies from a source of truth (Git repository, OCI image, or Helm chart) to a Kubernetes cluster, ensuring consistency at scale. text:

   ```yaml
   ---

   ---
   ```


text: - 所有 Rust 结构需要带给 ts 侧的都使用 `ts-rs` crate 自动生成类型定义，生成位置为 `src-tauri/bindings`。ts 侧引用 bindings 时一般使用 `import { type xxx } from '@bindings/xxx'`。

head: 项目规范
text: - 所有 tauri 暴露给 ts 侧的 API 都放在 `src-tauri/src/bindings.rs` 内，该文件内不写复杂逻辑。

head: 项目规范

head: 项目规范
text: Rust 端可能 emit 的 tauri 事件如下：

head: 项目规范
text:
| key                    | value           | description                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| game://exit/{game_id}  | GameExitPayload | 游戏退出时触发（`{ success: bool, session_secs: u64 }`，session_secs 为本次会话秒数） |
| game://spawn/{game_id} | ()              | 游戏启动时触发                                                                        |
| config://updated       | Config          | Rust 侧更新配置时触发                                                                 |
| sync://failed          | String          | 与远端交互（上传/下载，存档/配置）失败时触发，value 为错误信息                        |

head: 项目规范

head: 项目规范 > 写入配置
text: TS 侧一般可以用 `const { config, actions } = useConfig()` 获取配置与操作配置，参考 `src/store/index.tsx`。

head: 项目规范 > 写入配置
text:
- Rust 侧的 Config 及其子结构使用 struct-patch 的魔改版本生成关联的 patch struct，并将类型暴露给前端。前端更新配置时构建一个 patch 并通过 IPC 传给后端，后端 apply。目的：减小 IPC payload，并且减少竞态条件（Rust 侧和 TS 侧同时写配置）的互相覆盖。核心：`src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs`（`Config`/`Game` 的 `#[patch]` proc macro），`bindings.rs` 的 `patch_config` 命令。
  - struct-patch 魔改：1. 支持细粒度 list 操作（原库只能整个 list 替换） 2. ListPatchOp derive `ts_rs::TS`，下游零注解获得 bindings
  - Rust 侧更新配置 emit 到前端仍然全量传。
  - 竞态条件极少的小结构体不再细粒度 derive Patch，是 patch 收益与配置复杂性的权衡。例：SettingsPatch/PluginMetadatasPatch 为 `Option<T>` 整体替换

head: 项目规范 > 写入配置
text: - Config 延迟落盘：防抖合并写盘，避免前端响应式频繁触发磁盘写入。核心：`src-tauri/src/utils/persist.rs`（`ThrottledWriter`），`src-tauri/src/db/saver.rs`（`ConfigSaver`，60s 间隔）。

head: 项目规范 > 变量机制
text: 由于软件设计就是默认多设备运行，因此采用变量机制来管理不同设备上的差异点，例如存档路径、游戏路径等。使用时一般调用 `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs` 中的 `Config::resolve_var`。前端使用时需要 invoke rust 的 `resolve_var` binding。

head: 项目规范 > 插件的设计
text: 这里的插件指的并非用户自行编写和安装的插件，而是开发者预定义的一系列功能，用户可以自行将其应用到游戏上，并且修改插件相关配置以实现自定义游戏附加功能的效果。

head: 项目规范 > 插件的设计
text: 插件拥有两种数据，一种是元数据，每个插件只会有一份元数据。元数据又分为两部分：

head: 项目规范 > 插件的设计
text: - **插件基本信息**：插件的 id、名称、版本号、作者、描述、外部链接等

head: 项目规范 > 插件的设计
text: - **插件元配置**：插件的唯一配置项，例如是否全局启用，默认为新增游戏启用，插件配置添加到新游戏上的默认值等。

head: 项目规范 > 插件的设计
text: 另一种是**插件配置**，同一个插件添加到不同的游戏上，可以为每个游戏分别编辑配置，以此决定插件对该游戏的影响。

head: 项目规范 > 插件的设计
text: - Rust 侧的插件定义在 `src-tauri/src/plugin`。TS 侧，所有插件在 `src/pages/Plugin/index.tsx` 统一管理；每个插件的具体配置在 `src/pages/Plugin/plugins`。

head: 项目规范 > 游戏启动
text: - `src-tauri/src/exec/mod.rs` 里大量使用了 Arc 以减少 clone 开销，提升性能。

head: 项目规范 > 游戏启动
text: - 对于提供了 current_dir 但是没有配置的插件，默认使用游戏 exe 所在目录作为 current_dir。

head: 项目规范 > 游戏启动
text: - `src-tauri/src/plugin/transaction.rs` 引入事务回滚机制，避免某阶段失败导致插件的影响（文件、注册表）残留。

head: 项目规范 > 游玩时长
text: 除了每个游戏有一个总游玩时长以外，还记录了每个游戏的每日游玩时长，并以 d3.js 联动图表形式展示在统计页面，参考 `src/pages/Statistics/*`。

head: 项目规范 > 图片下载优化
text: backon 指数退避重试；并发控制，同 URI 保证只 fetch 一次；4xx 拥有失败缓存，不重试，且区分 404 与 429 的缓存过期时长。核心：`src-tauri/src/http/image.rs`（重试/单飞去重），`src-tauri/src/http/dead_url.rs`（死 URL 缓存）。死 URL 缓存复用 `utils::persist::ThrottledWriter` 延迟落盘，避免频繁写 SSD。

text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: This is a DuckDB extension called `adbc` that integrates Arrow ADBC (Arrow Database Connectivity) with DuckDB. It's built using the DuckDB extension template. Familiarize yourself with the ADBC interface.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: There is a checkout of a similar project under ./odbc-scanner which is the ODBC scanner for DuckDB extension. This adbc extension is modeled after that extension but uses the ADBC interface instead.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: There is also a checkout of the Airport DuckDB extension under ./airport. The Airport extension integrates DuckDB with Apache Arrow Flight and demonstrates C++ code that can read Arrow record batches and return them to DuckDB. The docs are under ./airport/docs/README.md, but you're mostly interested in airport_take_flight.cpp.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: There is also a checkout of the DuckDB postgresql extension under ./duckdb-postgres.  The postgresql extension integrates DuckDB with psotgres and demonstrates C++ code that can interact with the foreign postgresql tables.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions
text: The extension provides the following functions:

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting
text: There are no connection handles. Connect with `ATTACH '<uri>' AS <alias> (TYPE adbc, driver '...')` and pass the alias (a VARCHAR) as the first argument of every `adbc_*` function; disconnect with `DETACH`. `GetAttachedConnection` (`src/adbc_connection.cpp`) resolves the alias: an unknown or non-ADBC name fails at bind. Inside an explicit `BEGIN … COMMIT`, writes (`adbc_execute`, `adbc_insert`) use the attachment's transaction write connection, and reads use it too once the transaction has written; otherwise both use the catalog's own connection in autocommit (so session state like temp tables carries across calls; two simultaneous alias reads in one query conflict). Writes to a READ_ONLY attachment are rejected.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting
text:
- **ATTACH options** (see Storage Extension below for more):
  - `driver` - Driver name, path to shared library, or path to manifest file (.toml). Not required when a connection profile is supplied (via `profile` or a `profile://` URI), since the profile provides the driver.
  - `entrypoint` - Custom entry point function name
  - `profile` - Name of a connection profile to resolve (see Connection Profiles). Equivalent to a `profile://<name>` path.
  - `search_paths` - Additional paths to search for driver manifests *and* connection profiles (colon-separated on Unix, semicolon on Windows)
  - `use_manifests` - Enable/disable manifest search (default: 'true'). Set to 'false' to only use direct library paths.
  - `secret` - Name of a DuckDB secret to use for connection parameters
  - Other options are passed directly to the ADBC driver

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text: The extension supports DuckDB secrets for storing connection credentials. Secrets are automatically looked up based on the `uri` option (scope matching) or can be explicitly referenced by name.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text:
**Creating a secret:**
```sql
CREATE SECRET my_postgres (
    TYPE adbc,
    SCOPE 'postgresql://myhost:5432',
    driver 'postgresql',
    uri 'postgresql://myhost:5432/mydb',
    username 'user',
    password 'secret'
);
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text: - `driver` - ADBC driver name or path

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text: - `uri` - Connection URI passed to the driver

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text: - `username` - Database username

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text: - `password` - Database password (automatically redacted in logs)

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text: - `database` - Database name (no driver accepts it as an option; it is folded into an empty `scheme://` URI path)

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text: `username` / `password` / `database` are sent as driver options first; if the driver rejects one (NOT_IMPLEMENTED, as PostgreSQL and SQLite do — they accept only `uri`) and the URI is `scheme://…` without userinfo, `CreateConnectionFromOptions` retries once with them percent-encoded into the URI (`FoldCredentialsIntoUri` in `src/adbc_connection.cpp`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support
text: - `entrypoint` - Custom driver entry point

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Secrets Support

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Driver Manifest Support

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text: The extension supports [ADBC connection profiles](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/format/connection_profiles.html) — named TOML files that bundle a driver name plus a set of connection options, so credentials and endpoints do not need to be hardcoded in SQL. Profile resolution is handled natively by the ADBC driver manager (arrow-adbc 23+).

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text: A profile is referenced by a `profile://<name>` URI or by the `profile` option, and the driver manager loads `<name>.toml` from the standard profile search paths:

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text: 1. Paths passed via the `search_paths` option

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text: 1. Paths passed via the `search_paths` option

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text: 2. `ADBC_PROFILE_PATH` environment variable (semicolon-separated)

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text: 3. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ADBC\Profiles`

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text: A `profile://<name>` with a `.toml` extension or absolute path is loaded directly; otherwise `<name>.toml` is searched for in the directories above.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text:
**Profile file format** (`mydb.toml`):
```toml
profile_version = 1
driver = "sqlite"

[Options]
uri = ":memory:"
# Values support environment-variable interpolation:
# password = "{{ env_var(MYDB_PASSWORD) }}"
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
text: Options explicitly passed to `ATTACH` take precedence over those from the profile. Use `adbc_profiles()` to list discoverable profiles.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Connecting > Connection Profiles
CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Transaction Control
text: Use DuckDB's `BEGIN` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK`. Inside a transaction, `adbc_execute` and `adbc_insert` commit or roll back together with writes made through the attached catalog (`INSERT INTO db.t …`), and reads see the transaction's uncommitted writes. A driver that cannot disable autocommit (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) fails the first write in an explicit transaction; outside one, `AdbcTransaction::GetWriteConnection` lets catalog writes run in the driver's autocommit, without per-statement atomicity.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Query Execution
text:
Binding must not execute user SQL. `adbc_scan` uses ADBC `ExecuteSchema`, or an
explicit `columns := {'name': 'TYPE'}` declaration when metadata is unavailable
(including SQLite). `adbc_scan_table` uses `GetTableSchema`. Runtime result types
are checked before reading values. See [docs/runtime-commands.md](docs/runtime-commands.md).

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Query Execution
text: - `adbc_scan(database, query, [params := row(...)], [batch_size := N])` - Execute a SELECT query and return results as a table. Supports parameterized queries via the optional `params` named parameter. The optional `batch_size` parameter hints to the driver how many rows to return per batch (default: driver-specific, typically 2048). This is a best-effort hint that may be ignored by drivers that don't support it.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Query Execution
text: - `adbc_scan_table(database, table_name, [catalog := ...], [schema := ...], [batch_size := N])` - Scan an entire table by name and return all rows. Supports optional `catalog` and `schema` parameters for fully qualified table names. Supports projection pushdown (only requested columns are fetched), filter pushdown (WHERE clauses are pushed to the remote database with parameter binding), cardinality estimation, progress reporting, and column-level statistics for query optimization (distinct count, null count, min/max when available from the driver via `AdbcConnectionGetStatistics`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Query Execution
text: - `CALL adbc_execute(database, query)` - Execute DDL/DML statements (CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) at runtime. Returns affected row count, or NULL when unknown. No scalar form is registered.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Query Execution
text: - `adbc_insert(database, table_name, <table>, [mode := ...], [max_batches := ...], [options := ...])` - Bulk insert data from a subquery. Modes: 'create', 'append', 'replace', 'create_append'. `options` is a STRUCT or MAP of driver-specific statement options (e.g. `{'adbc.ingest.temporary': 'true'}`), applied after the target table and mode.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Catalog Functions
text: - `adbc_info(database)` - Returns driver/database information (vendor name, version, etc.).

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Catalog Functions
text: - `adbc_tables(database)` - Returns list of tables in the database.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Catalog Functions
text: - `adbc_table_types(database)` - Returns supported table types (e.g., "table", "view").

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Catalog Functions
text: - `adbc_columns(database, [table_name := ...])` - Returns column metadata (name, type, ordinal position, nullability).

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Catalog Functions
text: - `adbc_schema(database, table_name)` - Returns the Arrow schema for a specific table (field names, Arrow types, nullability).

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Catalog Functions
text: - `adbc_profiles([search_paths := ...])` - Lists discoverable ADBC connection profiles from the standard search paths (plus any directories in the optional `search_paths` parameter). Returns one row per `*.toml` profile found: `name`, `driver`, `path`, `source` ('additional' | 'env' | 'user'), and `profile_version`. Requires no driver or connection.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Storage Extension (ATTACH)
text: The extension also provides a storage extension that allows attaching ADBC data sources as DuckDB databases. This enables querying remote tables using standard SQL syntax without explicit function calls.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Storage Extension (ATTACH)
text: - `driver` (required) - Driver name, path to shared library, or manifest name

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Storage Extension (ATTACH)
text: - `entrypoint` - Custom entry point function name

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Storage Extension (ATTACH)
text: - `search_paths` - Additional paths to search for driver manifests

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Storage Extension (ATTACH)
text: - `use_manifests` - Enable/disable manifest search (default: 'true')

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Storage Extension (ATTACH)
text: - `batch_size` - Hint for number of rows per batch when scanning tables (default: driver-specific). Larger batch sizes can reduce network round-trips for remote databases.

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Storage Extension (ATTACH)
text: - `default_schema` - Schema that unqualified names (`db.table`, `USE db`) resolve to. When omitted, `AdbcCatalog::GetDefaultSchema` resolves it on first use: the connection's `adbc.connection.db_schema` if the catalog lists that schema, else the only schema listed, else `main`. Catalog writes pass their schema as `adbc.ingest.target_db_schema` (`main` is the placeholder for drivers without schemas and is not passed).

head: CLAUDE.md > Extension Functions > Storage Extension (ATTACH)
text: - Other options are passed directly to the ADBC driver (e.g., `username`, `password`)

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Architecture
text: - `EndpointSecurity/` — translates Endpoint Security C events → domain types (`ESInboundAdapter`, `ESProcessRecord`, `MutePath`)

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Architecture
text: - `XPC/` — IPC boundary with the GUI app (`XPCServer`, `ConnectionValidator`, `EventBroadcaster`, `ProcessEnumerator`, `NSXPCConnection+AuditToken`)

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Architecture
text: - `Database/` — SQLite persistence (`Database`, `DatabaseMigrations`)

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Architecture
text: - `Policy/` — policy loading, signing, and state management (`PolicyRepository`, `PolicySigner`, `ManagedPolicyLoader`, `ManagedAllowlistLoader`)

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Architecture
text: - `Filter/` — filter orchestration and output (`FilterInteractor`, `AuditLogger`, `TTYNotifier`)

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Architecture
text: **Rule**: domain code never imports `EndpointSecurity`, `AppKit`, `SwiftUI`, `SQLite`, or any other infrastructure framework. Adapters own those imports.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Build and Test
text: Tests live in `Tests/` and use the Swift Testing framework (`@Suite`, `@Test`, `#expect`).

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > New code — TDD
text: Write the test first. Red → Green → Refactor. Keep the cycle short: one failing assertion at a time.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > Existing untested code — Feathers approach
text: 1. **Characterise before changing.** Write a test that pins the current behaviour exactly, even if that behaviour looks wrong. Do not change any logic yet; only add the test.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > Existing untested code — Feathers approach
text: 2. **Introduce a seam.** Extract an interface or closure parameter so the behaviour under test can be driven without real I/O. Prefer the simplest seam: a `@Sendable` closure injected at the call site beats a full protocol when only one behaviour varies.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > Existing untested code — Feathers approach
text: 3. **Narrow the scope.** Test the smallest unit that isolates the logic you need to change, using a fake collaborator (named `Fake…`, never `Mock…`).

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > Existing untested code — Feathers approach
text: 4. **Change under the safety net.** Modify the logic only once a characterisation test is green. Keep commits atomic: characterisation test → logic change → refactoring, each as its own commit.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > Existing untested code — Feathers approach
text: 5. **Do not retrofit tests onto integration boundaries.** Adapter code that calls OS APIs belongs behind a protocol seam so the domain logic can be tested without it.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > What to test
text: - Domain logic (policy evaluation, path matching, allowlist resolution) must be fully covered.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > What to test
text: - Adapters are tested at integration or system level when practical, not unit-level.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > What to test
text: - Do not test Swift language mechanics or framework plumbing.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Testing Strategy > Test structure
text: Fake collaborators are private nested structs/classes inside the test file. They implement only the protocol methods exercised by the test.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Naming
text: - Names describe intent at the call site, not the implementation.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Naming
text: - No abbreviations. No generic placeholders (`data`, `temp`, `value`, `result`, `info`).

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Naming
text: - Prefer nouns for types, verb phrases for methods that perform work.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Control flow
text: - Guard clauses first; exit early; reduce nesting.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Control flow
text: - No `else` after a `return`, `throw`, or `continue` — extract a method instead.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Control flow
text: - Ternaries on one line only; never nested.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Control flow
text: - Complex boolean logic lives in a clearly named computed property or method.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Methods
text: - Single responsibility. If you need to describe a method with "and", split it.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Methods
text: - Short parameter lists; group related parameters into a dedicated type.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Methods
text: - No side effects in computed properties.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Collections
text: - Never return or pass `nil` for a collection; return an empty collection.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Collections
text: - Iterate directly; no `if !collection.isEmpty { for … }` guard before a loop.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Immutability
text: - `let` for everything that does not change after initialisation.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Immutability
text: - Prefer value types (`struct`, `enum`) for domain models.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Enums over booleans
text: - Replace flag parameters and boolean return values with enums that name the cases explicitly.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Enums over booleans
text: - Pattern-match on enum cases; never inspect `.rawValue` to drive logic.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Errors and assertions
text: - Catch specific error types; never catch the root `Error` and swallow it.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Errors and assertions
text: - Do not return invented defaults to paper over failures — surface the error.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Errors and assertions
text: - Use `guard`/`precondition`/`fatalError` to enforce invariants that must always hold.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Errors and assertions
text: - Only add a guard if the condition is actually reachable.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Concurrency
text: - Mark shared mutable state with `OSAllocatedUnfairLock`; avoid `@MainActor` in domain code.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Concurrency
text: - Ancestry lookups are lazy: pass `@Sendable () async -> [AncestorInfo]` closures and call them only when a rule demands ancestry data.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Miscellaneous
text: - Named constants or enums; no magic numbers or strings.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Miscellaneous
text: - String interpolation, not concatenation or `String(format:…)`.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Miscellaneous
text: - Deserialise structured data into typed models; no raw dictionary key access.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Miscellaneous
text: - No fallback defaults unless the requirement explicitly calls for one; extra branches hide intent.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Swift Conventions > Miscellaneous
text: - Update every call site when changing an interface; no backwards-compatibility shims or deprecated aliases.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Protocol placement
text: A protocol lives in the same folder as the type(s) that take it as a constructor parameter — the *users* of the abstraction, not the implementors. This keeps the dependency arrow pointing inward: the consumer defines what it needs, and implementors reach in to satisfy it.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Protocol placement
text: The only exception is when the protocol must be visible to both binary targets (clearancekit app and opfilter system extension). In that case `Shared/` is the right home, because it is compiled into both binaries.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Protocol placement
text: - `PolicyDatabaseProtocol` lives in `opfilter/Policy/` alongside `PolicyRepository`, which takes it in its `init`. ✓

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Protocol placement
text: - A protocol consumed only by `opfilter/Filter/` types belongs in `opfilter/Filter/`, even if its concrete implementation lives in `Shared/`. The conformance (`extension ConcreteType: TheProtocol`) is declared in a file within `opfilter/Filter/`, keeping `Shared/` free of the dependency.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Preset and rule UUIDs
text: Every `FAARule` and `AppPreset` requires a stable UUID that must never change after the rule ships — the database signing system uses it as a key.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Preset and rule UUIDs
text: **Always generate new UUIDs with `uuidgen`:**

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Preset and rule UUIDs
text: Never hand-craft UUID strings.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Comments
text: Code should explain itself through precise naming and small, focused units. Comments are not a substitute for clarity.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Comments
text: **Write a comment only when:**

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Comments
text: - The code is correct but the reason it is written that way is non-obvious (e.g. a workaround for a known OS bug with a reference).

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Comments
text: - A performance-sensitive section explains *why* a specific algorithm was chosen and what the measured trade-off is.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Comments
text: - Comments that restate what the code does (`// Increment counter`).

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Comments
text: - TODO/FIXME left for future readers without a linked issue.

head: ClearanceKit — Developer Guide > Comments
text: - Doc-comment boilerplate on every declaration.

text:
| 问题 | 原因 | 解决方案 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI 卡死 | 同步命令执行耗时操作 | 改为 `async fn` 或将任务移到 `spawn_blocking` |
| IPC 数据过大 | 单次 invoke 超过 10MB | 使用 `Channel` 分块传输 |
| 跨窗口状态不同步 | 使用 store 而非 Tauri 事件 | 改用 `emit` + `listen` |
| 类型不同步 | 前端类型未更新 | 确保 `build.rs` 正确配置，运行 `cargo build` |
| 内存泄漏 | 循环引用或未清理的监听器 | useEffect 返回清理函数 |
| 窗口闪烁 | 未配置合适的 `decorations` | 设置 `decorations: false` + 自定义标题栏 |

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text: **Always use the Component-Based Broadcasting Pattern (like Paper model):**

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text:
1. **Create ViewComponents for rendering** instead of partials:
```ruby
module ModelName
  class ItemComponent < ApplicationComponent
    def initialize(model:, view_type: :default)
      @model = model
      @view_type = view_type
    end
    
    private
    
    def loading?
      # Define loading state logic
    end
  end
end
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text:
2. **Model handles broadcasting via callbacks**:
```ruby
class Model < ApplicationRecord
  after_create_commit :broadcast_prepend
  after_update_commit :broadcast_replace
  after_destroy_commit :broadcast_remove
  
  private
  
  def broadcast_prepend
    broadcast_prepend_to(
      "user_#{user_id}_channel",
      target: "dom_target", 
      renderable: ModelName::ItemComponent.new(model: self)
    )
  end
  
  def broadcast_replace
    broadcast_replace_to(
      "user_#{user_id}_channel",
      target: "model_#{id}",
      renderable: ModelName::ItemComponent.new(model: self)
    )
  end
end
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text:
3. **Background jobs just update and save** - no manual broadcasting:
```ruby
class UpdateModelJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(model_id)
    model = Model.find(model_id)
    model.update!(attributes)  # Triggers broadcasts automatically via callbacks
  end
end
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text:
4. **Controllers stay simple** - no manual Turbo Stream responses:
```ruby
def create
  @model = current_user.models.build(params)
  if @model.save
    redirect_to models_path  # Model broadcasts automatically
  else
    render :new
  end
end
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text:
5. **Views use components with collections**: ```erb <%= turbo_stream_from "user_#{current_user.id}_channel" %>
<%= render ModelName::ItemComponent.with_collection(@models, view_type: :table) %>
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text: **ViewComponent Best Practices:**

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text: - Use `with_collection` for rendering multiple components instead of manual iteration

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text: - Add `with_collection_parameter` when component name doesn't match the parameter name

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Real-time Updates & Turbo Streams Best Practices
text:
- Use Ruby hash shorthand when variable names match parameter names
```ruby
# Component must declare collection parameter when name doesn't match
module SavedHongBaos
  class ItemComponent < ApplicationComponent
    with_collection_parameter :saved_hong_bao  # Required since component is "ItemComponent" not "SavedHongBaoComponent"
    
    def initialize(saved_hong_bao:, view_type: :table)
      @saved_hong_bao = saved_hong_bao
      @view_type = view_type
    end
  end
end
```
```erb
# ❌ BAD - Manual iteration
<% @models.each do |model| %>
  <%= render ModelName::ItemComponent.new(model: model, view_type: :card) %>
<% end %>

# ✅ GOOD - Collection rendering
<%= render ModelName::ItemComponent.with_collection(@models, view_type: :card) %>

# ✅ GOOD - Hash shorthand when names match
<%= render Papers::ItemComponent.new(paper:, layout:) %>
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Common Issues & Solutions > Nested Forms Problem
text: When a form doesn't submit (particularly Save/Submit buttons don't trigger any action):

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Common Issues & Solutions > Nested Forms Problem
text: 1. **Check for nested forms** - HTML doesn't allow `<form>` elements inside other `<form>` elements

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Common Issues & Solutions > Nested Forms Problem
text: 2. **Common cause**: Using `button_to` inside a `form_with` creates nested forms

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Common Issues & Solutions > Nested Forms Problem
text:
3. **Solution**: Use external form pattern with `form` attribute:
```erb
<!-- Button inside main form references external form -->
<%= tag.button '',
    type: :submit,
    form: "external_form_id",
    data: { turbo_confirm: "Confirm?" },
    class: "btn" do %>
  Icon/Text
<% end %>

<!-- External form placed outside main form -->
<%= form_with(model: @model,
    url: some_path(@model),
    method: :delete,
    id: "external_form_id") %>
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Conventions > Common Issues & Solutions > Nested Forms Problem
text: This pattern maintains semantic HTML (buttons for actions) while avoiding invalid nested forms.

head: CLAUDE.md > Blog Post Writing Style Guide
text: When writing blog posts for Hong₿ao (in `app/content/pages/blog/`), use Marc Lou's conversational, vulnerability-focused style:

head: CLAUDE.md > Blog Post Writing Style Guide > Core Writing Principles
text:
1. **Personal & Vulnerable**: Start with real personal failures or struggles, not abstract advice
   - ❌ "Many people find Bitcoin confusing"
   - ✅ "After 8 years of failed orange-pill attempts, I finally figured it out"

head: CLAUDE.md > Blog Post Writing Style Guide > Core Writing Principles
text:
2. **Conversational Tone**: Write like you're talking to a friend over coffee
   - Use contractions (don't, won't, it's)
   - Short, punchy sentences mixed with longer ones
   - Direct questions to the reader
   - Real dialogue when appropriate

head: CLAUDE.md > Blog Post Writing Style Guide > Core Writing Principles
text:
3. **Hook with Relatability**: Open with universal experiences
   - ✅ "Every Christmas, same story."
   - ✅ "So... how's Bitcoin doing?" (actual dialogue they've heard)

head: CLAUDE.md > Blog Post Writing Style Guide > Core Writing Principles
text:
4. **Show Don't Tell**: Use specific examples and personal anecdotes
   - ❌ "People don't understand Bitcoin"
   - ✅ "I used to launch into passionate explanations about monetary policy. Watch their eyes glaze over in real-time."

head: CLAUDE.md > Blog Post Writing Style Guide > Core Writing Principles
text:
5. **Direct & Actionable**: Give clear takeaways without fluff
   - Use bold for key insights: **Stop lecturing. Start gifting.**
   - Bullet points for quick scanning
   - Clear section headers that tell a story

head: CLAUDE.md > Blog Post Writing Style Guide > Core Writing Principles
text:
6. **Avoid**:
   - Academic or overly technical language
   - Excessive praise or superlatives
   - Corporate speak or marketing jargon
   - Emojis (unless explicitly requested)
   - Long theoretical explanations

head: CLAUDE.md > Blog Post Writing Style Guide > Introduction Formula
text: 1. **Hook** - Universal situation or problem (1-2 lines)

head: CLAUDE.md
text: It is deliberately a **trunk**: the commands, the architecture, the invariants that must survive even if you never follow a pointer, and a map of the deeper docs. Each subsystem's rulings live in a doc next to its code -- read the mapped doc BEFORE editing that subsystem. Those docs are not optional background: nearly every paragraph in them is a "this looks wrong, here is why it is deliberate, do not revert it", and losing one causes a real regression.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text: `system.prepare()` must be called before `system.build_model()` in any script or test.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code style
text: Use plain ASCII in new code, comments, docstrings, and documentation -- avoid unicode punctuation and symbols. Use `->` not `→`, `--` or `-` not `—`/`–`, `...` not `…`, `sigma`/`Delta`/`chi2` not `σ`/`Δ`/`χ²`, `+/-` not `±`, `~` or `approx` not `≈`, `x` not `×`. Plain ASCII decorative separators (e.g. `# ---`) are fine; avoid box-drawing characters (`─` etc.) for these. This is a convention for new/edited content only -- do not go out of your way to rewrite unrelated existing unicode.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code style
text: Public files never point into a developer's private notes. For provenance cite the public PR or issue that landed the work (e.g. "(#353)"); if a reader genuinely needs a measurement, table or rationale, put it in a public doc (the subsystem's `.md`, or a new file under `docs/`) and point there.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: EXOZIPPy is a component-agnostic wrapper around PyMC. A user writes two YAML files — a system config (`*.yaml`) and a parameter override file (`*.params.yaml`) — and calls `exozippy <config.yaml>`. The high-level flow in `run.py` is:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: All component-specific logic is handled within the components. The higher level codes (run, config, system, etc) rely solely on the generic component blueprint, not specific implementations.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The seven lifecycle stages
text: `System.prepare()` drives stages 1-4; `System.build_model()` drives stages 5-7.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The seven lifecycle stages
text:
| Stage | Method | What happens |
|-------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | `comp.load_data(system)` | File I/O; push data-derived hints to ConfigManager |
| 2 | `comp.build_maps()` | Build integer index arrays (`*_map`) linking children to parents |
| 3 | `comp.register_parameters(system)` | Declare `comp.manifest`; push component-level hints |
| 4 | `config_manager.finalize_user_params()` | Symbolic relaxation engine resolves all initvals/scales |
| 5 | `comp.build_tensor_maps()` | Auto-convert `*_map` numpy arrays → PyTensor int32 variables |
| 6 | `comp.add_parameter(model, name, system)` | Materialize PyMC nodes in topological order |
| 7 | `comp.build_likelihood(model, system)` | Add `pm.Normal`/`pm.Potential` observational constraints |

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > The seven lifecycle stages
text: The component contract -- the four standard files per component, the auto-discovering factory, the manifest vocabulary and the build order -- is in `src/exozippy/components/components.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Invariants
text: - `system.prepare()` must be called before `system.build_model()` (above), and the plain-ASCII rule (above) governs everything anyone writes.

head: CLAUDE.md > Invariants
text: - **Never write into `config_manager.user_params` from a component.** `setdefault` there looks like it preserves user precedence, and does -- but the entry then *is* a user entry as far as everything downstream can tell: the provenance ledger, `export_solution`, `initval_source`, `probe_derivable`'s flat, `resolve`'s `user_modified`/`user_prior_modified` flags (the `*` in run.py's startup table) and the GUI all report a value the user never wrote. It also has a second effect nobody intends: `finalize_user_params` registers every unmapped `user_params` key as a **leaf symbol** in the relaxation engine, so an injected `star.av` became an engine symbol with its own ledger row, its own default-armor value and its own inject-back initval, for a parameter instance that does not exist -- the "orphaned 2-part rows" `export_solution` filters out by hand. Both remaining injections (the SED grid bounds; `AstrometryInstrument`'s `sigma: 0` pin on a `fluxfrac` the SED supplies) were removed in 2026-08 with **bit-identical start logp on all ten shipped examples** that exercise either component. Neither was ever a candidate for `add_hint`: a hint is a *ranked start value*, one scalar feeding `initval`, whereas `lower`/`upper`/`sigma` never enter the provenance ledger at all -- which is also why the fix carries no rank. Tests: `tests/test_component_override_channel.py`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Invariants
text: - **There are TWO conversion factors in the codebase and they are RECIPROCALS.** `Parameter._get_conversion_factors` (parameter.py) is the **internal -> user** multiplier; `ConfigManager.get_conversion_factor` (config.py, via the `unit_conversion` helper) is the **user -> internal** one. So `* factor` means opposite things in the two modules, and confusing them is silent -- `outputs/ledger.py` divided where it had to multiply and reported **every** converted parameter in `<prefix>_results.csv`, the rejected-seeds text and the rejected-modes LaTeX table wrong by `factor**2` (`examples/hd80606`'s planet mass: 1.45e-06 jupiterMass for a start of 1.596; `examples/GaiaBH1`'s `star.ra`: 0.0799 deg for 262.171). Nothing outside `Parameter` may reach for a factor: call `to_internal(val, index=None)` / `from_internal(val, index=None)` and the direction is in the name.

head: CLAUDE.md > Invariants
text: - **Never compose branch log-densities with `pt.where`** (the JAX where-trap): `where`'s VJP multiplies the unselected branch by zero, and `0 * NaN` or `0 * inf` poisons the gradient of the whole expression on every backend, while the C backend's finite dlogp hides it. Combine branch logps with `pt.logaddexp`, keep a floor on a radicand rather than on the result -- **and that floor must be STRICTLY POSITIVE**, because `pt.maximum(x, 0.0)` has zero gradient on the clamped side while `sqrt'(0)` is infinite, so flooring a radicand *at zero* rebuilds the very `0 * inf` this rule exists to prevent (`ECC_FLOOR`/`CHORD_RADICAND_FLOOR` in `components/orbit/physics.py` are the two worked examples; the second cost 46% of a shipped parameterization's support and froze chains at the denormal step size for a whole run, reviews 1.8.2 and 1.8.5) -- and use the soft-bound helpers in `src/exozippy/potentials.py` for a penalty that needs a gradient pointing back. A soft bound cannot rescue a NaN elsewhere in the sum: one NaN poisons the whole gradient vector, so the hard shield being finite is a *precondition* for the soft one doing anything. Likewise assemble a mixed value vector with `pt.set_subtensor`, not `pt.where`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Invariants
text: - **No fallbacks for internal invariants.** A code path that notices a malformed, missing or mis-shaped value the codebase ITSELF produced -- a `.get(key, default)` on an internal dict whose key must exist, a `getattr(obj, name, None)` on an internal object, an `isinstance` coercion, `np.broadcast_to` / `atleast_1d` / `nan_to_num` on an internal channel, a bare `except Exception` that logs and proceeds, a second-chance lookup under an alternate spelling -- and then repairs it and continues is not robustness. It masks an upstream bookkeeping bug and turns a loud failure into a silently wrong number, table or plot (the ob09020 start plot showed a stale q for weeks behind exactly such a path). Get the bookkeeping right at the source, and where the seam is reached anyway RAISE, naming the offender (the parameter, component, key or file). The only fallbacks that stay are the ones that sanitize UNAMBIGUOUS user input as a quality-of-life measure -- a scalar broadcast in a params file, a `~` in a path, an optional block that is legitimately absent -- and those translate to the one strict internal spelling immediately at the boundary, per the ONE-SPELLING rule in `config.md`. User-facing names are CASE-SENSITIVE and are never case-folded (filter names, magnitude systems -- SDSS g is not Gaia G; JDE 2026-10-01): a case variant raises, and may suggest the right spelling but never accepts it. Before writing a fallback ask: can a correct upstream ever produce this input? If not, raise. JDE ruling 2026-09-25 (#342).

head: CLAUDE.md — DataPurge Project Instructions > Project Overview
text:
DataPurge is an open-source tool that helps people exercise their privacy rights
by automating data broker opt-out requests. It's a static site deployed on
Cloudflare Pages — all PII stays in the user's browser.

head: CLAUDE.md — DataPurge Project Instructions > Architecture
text:
The web UI is a vanilla JS single-page app (ES modules, no framework, no build tooling).
A Python `build.py` script exports broker YAMLs and templates into JSON for the frontend.

head: CLAUDE.md — DataPurge Project Instructions > Key Design Principles
