head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: imports and formatting
text: - Use 4-space indentation and no tabs.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: imports and formatting
text: - Keep imports minimal; place `Foundation` first when used.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: imports and formatting
text: - Follow existing multiline style and trailing commas.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: imports and formatting
text: - Keep files focused; extract helpers instead of large monolith methods.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: types and naming
text: - `UpperCamelCase` for types; `lowerCamelCase` for vars/functions.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: types and naming
text: - Prefer `struct` for DTO/protocol models; use `actor` for shared mutable state.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: types and naming
text: - Mark cross-target API explicitly with `public`.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: types and naming
text: - Add `Sendable` where values cross concurrency boundaries.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: types and naming
text: - Use enums for constrained state/actions (`RouteAction`, `WorkerMode`, etc.).

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: types and naming
text: - For API-compatible values, use explicit raw values (snake_case when needed).

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: error handling and resilience
text: - Use `throws` for recoverable boundary failures.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: error handling and resilience
text: - In router/http boundaries, convert invalid payloads to stable 4xx responses.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: error handling and resilience
text: - Prefer graceful fallback over crashing in runtime services.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: error handling and resilience
text: - Avoid force unwraps and `fatalError` in production paths.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: error handling and resilience
text: - Log operational failures with context and continue when safe.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: concurrency and architecture
text: - Prefer actor isolation to locking.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: concurrency and architecture
text: - Keep orchestration async end-to-end (`async`/`await`).

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: concurrency and architecture
text: - Do not bypass actor boundaries with shared mutable globals.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Swift: concurrency and architecture
text: - Maintain separation: transport (`CoreHTTPServer`) -> routing (`CoreRouter`) -> service (`CoreService`) -> runtime (`AgentRuntime`) -> persistence (`SQLiteStore`).

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Agent behavior and model output handling
text: - Do not implement language heuristics for agent behavior. This project builds agents; code must not guess what the model is going to answer from localized filler phrases or keyword arrays.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Agent behavior and model output handling
text: - Never classify state, progress, intent, completion, tool use, or branching by matching phrases such as `посмотрю`, `сейчас проверю`, `i'll inspect`, `let me check`, `looking into`, or similar English/Russian text fragments.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Agent behavior and model output handling
text: - Prefer typed signals: explicit API fields, runtime events, tool call records, planner intents, task state, structured model output, or persisted metadata.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Agent behavior and model output handling
text: - If a behavior decision depends on user or model intent, route it through an explicit semantic/structured layer and cover it with tests. Do not add another list of words.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Agent behavior and model output handling
text: - UI text may be displayed as text, but it must not become control flow unless it comes from a stable, documented protocol field.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Tests
text: - Use Swift Testing macros (`@Test`, `#expect`).

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Tests
text: - Write behavior-focused tests with clear arrange/act/assert flow.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Tests
text: - Keep tests deterministic and isolated.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Tests
text: - For endpoint logic, test via router/service with realistic payloads.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Dashboard (React)
text: - Use function components and hooks.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Dashboard (React)
text: - Use named exports for components/utilities.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Dashboard (React)
text: - Keep state local; derive computed values with `useMemo` when useful.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Dashboard (React)
text: - Use `async/await` and handle non-OK responses explicitly.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Dashboard (React)
text: - Match existing JS formatting: 2-space indent, semicolons, double quotes.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Dashboard (React)
text: - Keep route parsing and navigation behavior in `Dashboard/src/app/routing/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Dashboard (React)
text: - Use `Dashboard/src/shared/api/coreApi.ts` as the main Core API client surface; `Dashboard/src/api.ts` re-exports that surface for legacy callers.

head: AGENTS.md > Code style guide > Dashboard (React)
text: - For dropdown/select UI, always use the custom `.actor-team-search` dropdown pattern (see `ActorsView.tsx` and `actors.css`) — never use native `<select>` elements.

head: AGENTS.md > Common recipes > Add a new API endpoint
text: 1. **Model** — add `XxxRequest` / `XxxRecord` structs to `Sources/Protocols/APIModels.swift` under the relevant `// MARK:` section.

head: AGENTS.md > Common recipes > Add a new API endpoint
text: 2. **Service method** — add the method to `Sources/sloppy/CoreService.swift` in the correct domain section. Use a typed error enum.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Project Overview
text: - Replaces broken links with archived versions

text: - Auto-archives your own content on create/update

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Tech Stack
text:

| PHP | 7.4+ |

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Tech Stack
text: **CRITICAL:** Do not edit WordPress core files. This is a plugin—all code lives in the plugin directory.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Commands > Build
text: Runs: blocks, asset scripts, styles. Use `npm run start` for watch mode during development.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Architectural Decisions
text: 1. **Action Scheduler for all async work** — Snapshot creation, link checks, post scanning, and status polling run as scheduled events. Do not perform long-running or external API calls inline in request handlers.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Architectural Decisions
text: 2. **Client interfaces** — `Link_Checker_Client` and `Snapshot_Client` are injectable via filters (`iawmlf_link_checker_client`, `iawmlf_snapshot_client`). Default implementations call external services; tests can replace them.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Architectural Decisions
text: 3. **Scoped dependencies** — Production uses php-scoped dependencies in `dependencies/` to avoid conflicts. `composer run:php` produces an optimized autoloader without dev deps.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Architectural Decisions
text: 4. **Migrations** — Database changes go through `migrations/` and `Migration\Migrations`. Add new migration classes to the `$migrations` array in the main plugin file.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Architectural Decisions
text: 5. **Settings filters override admin UI** — Filters like `iawmlf_link_exclusions` take precedence over stored options. Use filters for programmatic overrides.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Common Pitfalls
text: 1. **Editing core WordPress files** — NEVER modify WordPress core. All changes stay in the plugin directory.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Common Pitfalls
text: 2. **Skipping asset build** — Frontend changes in `assets/*/src/` or `blocks/src/` require `npm run build`. Unbuilt changes will not appear in deployment.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Common Pitfalls
text: 3. **Inline API calls** — Do not call Archive.org or external link-checker APIs directly in HTTP request handlers. Queue an Action Scheduler event instead.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Common Pitfalls
text: 4. **Forgetting text domain** — All `__()`, `_e()`, etc. MUST use `internet-archive-wayback-machine-link-fixer`. PHPCS will flag violations.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Common Pitfalls
text: 5. **Wrong global prefix** — Use `iawmlf_` or the plugin namespace for functions/classes. Avoid generic names that could conflict.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Common Pitfalls
text: 6. **Modifying `vendor/`** — Do not edit Composer packages. Override behavior with filters or new implementations wired via filters.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Common Pitfalls
text: 7. **403 false positives** — Some URLs block bots; they may be reported as broken (403) even when live. The `Link_Access_Validator_Event` handles this; use "Verify link allows checking" for manual verification.

head: Agent Instructions: Internet Archive Wayback Machine Link Fixer > Common Pitfalls
text: 8. **Wizard re-run** — To reset the setup wizard during testing: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=iawmlf-setup-wizard&rerun-wizard=1` (admin only).

head: AI 助手开发协作指南 (AGENTS.md) > 🎨 1. 编码规范 (Coding Standards)

  - 所有的 `net.Conn`、`os.File` 等资源必须有确定的 `Close()` 路径，无论正常结束还是 error 返回，必须使用 `defer` 确保关闭。
  - 启动任何 Goroutine 时，必须明确它何时、何种情况下会退出（防止 Goroutine Leak）。必须通过 `context.Context` 传递取消信号。

head: AI 助手开发协作指南 (AGENTS.md) > 🎨 1. 编码规范 (Coding Standards)

  - 禁止无限阻塞的 I/O 调用。

head: AI 助手开发协作指南 (AGENTS.md) > 🎨 1. 编码规范 (Coding Standards)
text:
5. **错误处理**：
  - 严禁吞咽错误（`_ = err`）或直接 `panic`。
  - 错误必须包含上下文（使用 `fmt.Errorf("do xyz failed: %w", err)` 包装）。
  - 错误字符串不应以标点符号（如 `!` 或 `.`）或换行符结尾。

head: AI 助手开发协作指南 (AGENTS.md) > 🎨 1. 编码规范 (Coding Standards)

head: AI 助手开发协作指南 (AGENTS.md) > 🎨 1. 编码规范 (Coding Standards)

head: AI 助手开发协作指南 (AGENTS.md) > 🎨 1. 编码规范 (Coding Standards)

head: AGENTS.md
text: Guidance for AI coding agents working in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text: A kit for keeping AI-flavored writing out of prose and repos. Three artifacts matter:

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text: - `SKILL.md`: the humanizer skill. Portable YAML frontmatter followed by the numbered pattern catalog. **Source of truth for the 41 patterns.** Edit it like a careful instruction document, not code.

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text: - `rules/slop-rules.json`: the machine-readable rule pack. **Source of truth for what `sloplint` flags.** Vocabulary tiers, phrases (with optional `fix`), and regex detectors.

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text: - `bin/sloplint.js`: the zero-dependency scanner. Keep it dependency-free and Node 18 compatible.

head: AGENTS.md > The maintenance contract
text: - The skill currently defines **41 numbered patterns**. If you add, remove, or renumber any, update the README, the skill frontmatter description, and every cross-reference in the same change.

head: AGENTS.md > The maintenance contract
text: - The pattern catalog (SKILL.md) and the rule pack (slop-rules.json) overlap but are not mirrors: the skill holds judgment calls a regex can't make; the rule pack holds only what a machine can check without heavy false positives. When you add a mechanically checkable pattern to one, consider the other.

head: AGENTS.md > The maintenance contract
text: - Version lives in three places: `SKILL.md` frontmatter (`metadata.version`), `package.json`, and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Bump them together.

head: AGENTS.md > The maintenance contract
text: - Every new rule in `slop-rules.json` gets a test in `tests/sloplint.test.js`. Run `npm test` before finishing.

head: AGENTS.md > The maintenance contract
text: - Keep install and usage language harness-neutral. The skill should work anywhere markdown skills load.

head: AGENTS.md > The maintenance contract
text: - This repo's own prose follows its own rules: no em dashes, sentence-case headings, no filler. Run `sloplint score README.md` after editing docs. The `references/` files are exempt where they quote slop as examples.

head: AGENTS.md > Watch out for
text: - `prepareText` blanks regions instead of deleting them so line numbers stay correct. Preserve that invariant.

head: AGENTS.md > Watch out for
text: - Tier 2 vocabulary only flags when two or more distinct terms appear; tier 3 only above a density threshold. Don't "fix" that into always-flag; it exists to avoid false positives on human writing.

head: AGENTS.md > Watch out for
text: - `applyFixes` must stay conservative: only mechanical, meaning-preserving replacements belong there. Judgment calls belong in the skill.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Work

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Work

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: For non-trivial repository changes, use this loop:

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 1. Start from an Issue, Discussion, or maintainer-approved task description.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 2. Create a short-lived branch from `develop` using `feat/`, `fix/`, `docs/`, or `chore/`.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 3. Run `pnpm agent:bootstrap` and `pnpm quality:predev`.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 4. Implement the smallest reviewable change with focused tests.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 5. Run `pnpm quality:local` before pushing when feasible.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 6. Open a PR to `develop` with the PR template filled in, including the GitNexus impact summary for critical skeleton changes.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 7. Wait for GitHub Actions, Contract Guard, Repo Guard, Codex, Copilot, and maintainer review comments.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 8. Address actionable review comments with follow-up commits, then rerun the relevant gates.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > Harness Loop
text: 9. Let maintainers decide merge readiness; do not add comment-triggered auto-merge behavior.

head: FrontAgent OSS Harness > OSS Scope
text: FrontAgent uses an open-source maintainer workflow. Do not add training-camp claim comments, score labels, progress ledgers, timeout-close automation, or comment-triggered auto-merge rules unless maintainers explicitly request a separate workflow.

head: AGENTS - Project Rules > Architecture > Single-source dual-binary pattern
text:
`apps/httpcheck.c` compiles to both `httpcheck` and `httpscheck`. The difference: `httpscheck` is compiled with
`-DWITH_TLS` and linked against mbedTLS 4. All TLS code paths in the file are gated on `#ifdef WITH_TLS`. Both
binaries share the same CLI flags.

head: AGENTS - Project Rules > Architecture > Library modules
text:
- **`lib/cli/`** - CLI argument parsing. Flags have immutable metadata (`cli_flag_meta_t`) and mutable state
  (`cli_flag_state_t`). Three value types: `FLAG_TYPE_BOOL`, `FLAG_TYPE_STRING`, `FLAG_TYPE_STRINGS`. Value
  priority: CLI flag > environment variable > default. Every flag can have a companion `--flag-env` flag to override
  the env var name at runtime.

head: AGENTS - Project Rules > Architecture > Library modules
text:
- **`lib/http/`** - HTTP protocol (no I/O). URL parsing is zero-copy: `host` and `path` fields point into the original
  string, not allocated copies. Use `_len` fields for bounds. `http_build_request()` constructs the full HTTP/1.1
  request string.

head: AGENTS - Project Rules > Architecture > Library modules
text: - **`lib/command/`** - Parses shell-like quoted command strings into `argv` arrays. Used only by `parallel`.

head: AGENTS - Project Rules > Architecture > Library modules
text: - **`lib/mbedtls4/`** - Vendored via `lib/install-mbedtls4.sh`, built with cmake. Only linked into `httpscheck`.

head: AGENTS - Project Rules > Architecture > httpscheck auto-detect mode
text:
When the URL has no scheme (`host:port/path` without `http://` or `https://`), `httpscheck` tries HTTPS first,
then falls back to HTTP on any connection/TLS error. The `--connect-timeout` flag controls both the TCP `poll()`
timeout and the `SO_RCVTIMEO` during TLS handshake; after a successful handshake, `SO_RCVTIMEO` is reset to the
full `--timeout`.

head: AGENTS - Project Rules > Architecture > Output discipline
text:
**Do not use `fprintf`, `snprintf`, or other `<stdio.h>` formatting functions in apps**. This bloats binary size.
Use `write()` with string literals or `fputs()` for error output. See the comment at the top of `apps/httpcheck.c`.

head: AI Contributor Guide > Generated Outputs

head: AI Contributor Guide > Parallel Work
text: - Multiple agents may be running in isolated worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`. They share this repo's object database, so any history change in one tree is visible to all of them.

head: AI Contributor Guide > Parallel Work
text: - In isolated worktrees, verify the worktree base before editing. Stop if it is stale.

head: AI Contributor Guide > Parallel Work
text: - **Do not rewrite commits.** No `git commit --amend`, `git reset --soft|--mixed|--hard <ref>` against existing commits, `git rebase`, `git push --force`, or `git push --force-with-lease`. If a commit needs to change, create a new commit on top.

head: AI Contributor Guide > Parallel Work
text: - **Do not move HEAD off the assigned branch.** No `git checkout <commit-or-branch>`, `git switch <branch>`, or `git reset --hard <other-rev>` to "test" a different revision. Each worktree must stay on the branch it was created with. To compare against another revision, use `git show`, `git diff <ref>`, or `git worktree add` for a new throwaway tree.

head: AI Contributor Guide > Parallel Work
text: - **Do not move stashes across branches or worktrees.** Prefer a scratch commit on the current branch over `git stash`. If you must stash, pop it in the same worktree on the same branch you stashed from — never in a sibling worktree.

head: AI Contributor Guide > Parallel Work
text: - These rules apply to `Bash` commands you issue *and* to anything you delegate to subagents.

text: - Public packages are `vite-plugin-tsl-precompile`, `@tsl-precompile/runtime`, and `@tsl-precompile/contract`.

head: AI Contributor Guide > Release Surface
text: - Keep package exports intentional. If a file is meant to be imported by users or the harness, expose it through `package.json`.

head: AI Contributor Guide > Release Surface

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance to AI coding agents when working with code in this repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Build & Dev Commands
text: **Mandatory build step:** After modifying any file that affects runtime behavior (e.g. `src/`, `agent.js`, `server.js`, `headful.js`, `scrape.js`, etc.), you **MUST** run `npm run build`. Exceptions include but are not limited to: `package.json`, `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, test files.

head: AGENTS.md > Planning Requirement
text: Before implementing **any non-trivial change** (anything beyond a simple bug fix or minor text edit), you **MUST**:

head: AGENTS.md > Planning Requirement
text: 1. Draft an implementation plan — describe proposed changes, files affected, new components, and architectural impact.

head: AGENTS.md > Planning Requirement
text: 2. Wait for user approval before touching any code.

head: AGENTS.md > Planning Requirement
text: Do not create a separate plan file unless explicitly asked. Post the plan in chat.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: **Request flow:** Frontend (React/Vite) → Express API (`server.js`) → execution engine (`scrape.js` for headless, `headful.js` for VNC browser sessions) → `src/agent/index.js` (orchestrator) → `src/agent/action-handler.js` (executes individual actions).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: **Key architectural boundaries:**

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: - `server.js` registers routes from `src/server/routes/*.js` and serves the frontend. It also handles headful browser lifecycle and NoVNC/websockify proxying.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: - `headful.js` and the agent engine both use the browser engine from `stealth-chromium.js` (Playwright by default, CloakBrowser when `USE_CLOAK_ENGINE=true`) — `headful.js` manages a persistent visible browser over VNC with a selector picker tool, while `scrape.js` fetches with got-scraping + Cheerio (no browser).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: - `src/agent/index.js` is the shared orchestrator called by both. It processes the action list, handles control flow (if/else/while/repeat/foreach via `logic-handler.js`), variable templating, and output providers.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: - `src/server/storage.js` abstracts persistence — defaults to JSON files in `data/`, optionally uses PostgreSQL when `DB_TYPE=postgres`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: **Module system split:** Root `.js` files use CommonJS; `src/` uses ESM (bundled by Vite for frontend, imported by backend via compatible paths).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: **Headful/VNC stack:** `start-vnc.sh` launches Xvfb (1920x1080) → x11vnc → websockify/noVNC. The browser runs inside Xvfb and is viewed through NoVNC embedded in an iframe (`public/novnc.html`). The selector picker injects inspect overlay JS into pages via `context.addInitScript()` in `headful.js` and streams selected selectors back via SSE (`/api/headful/selector_stream`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: **Duplicated extraction UI:** The Visual extraction-script editor exists in two places that must be kept in sync — `TaskSettingsCabinet.tsx` (Extraction tab in the task settings panel) and the in-canvas `ExtractionScriptBlock` inside `CanvasView.tsx` (the popup opened from the canvas). Any functional change to one (new field types, new attribute/selector picking behavior, new data model like repeating groups, etc.) must be applied to the other as well, unless the change is purely visual/stylistic to one surface (e.g. layout, spacing, panel-specific styling) — use judgment to tell the two apart.

head: AGENTS.md > Tech Stack
text:
| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Backend | Node.js, Express.js (REST API) |
| Frontend | React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide React |
| Automation | Playwright + `playwright-extra`/`puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth` (default); CloakBrowser opt-in via `USE_CLOAK_ENGINE=true` |
| Storage | JSON files in `data/` — optionally PostgreSQL via `DB_TYPE=postgres` |

text:
| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `server.js` | Main Express server entry point |
| `agent.js` | Wrapper that exports `src/agent/index.js` |
| `scrape.js` | Headless scraping jobs and video recording |

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Standards
text: - **Module system**: CommonJS for root files; ESM for frontend (`src/`).

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Standards
text: - **Async**: Always use `async/await` — no raw callbacks.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Standards
text: - **Error handling**: Wrap async operations in `try/catch`; return errors in API responses.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Standards
text:
- **Security** (non-negotiable):
  - Never commit secrets or credentials.
  - Always use `validateUrl` from `url-utils.js` to prevent SSRF attacks.
  - Sanitize all inputs before use in shell commands or file paths.

head: AGENTS.md > Agent Specification
text: All automation logic **must** conform to **`AGENT_SPEC.md`**. It defines the Task JSON schema and all supported action types. **Never invent new action types** without first updating both `AGENT_SPEC.md` and `agent.js`.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: Tests live in `tests/` as standalone Node.js scripts. Exit code `0` = success, `1` = failure. Run with `node tests/<file>.js`.

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: After completing any major feature implementation, provide the user with a checklist of things to manually verify. Include items relevant to what was changed. Examples:

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Build**: Did `npm run build` succeed with no errors or type errors?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Tests**: Did all tests in `tests/` pass (`node tests/<file>.js` and `npm test`)?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Browser launch**: Does the browser actually open (headful) or start headlessly (scrape/agent) without crashing?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Proxy**: If proxies are configured, does traffic route through them correctly?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Storage state**: Is session state still being saved/loaded from `storage_state.json` after the run?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Video recording**: Are `.webm` recordings still being saved to `data/recordings/` when recording is enabled?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Screenshots**: Are screenshots being saved to `public/captures/`?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Selector picker**: Does the VNC inspect overlay still activate and emit selectors via SSE?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Agent handoff**: If a task uses `stopAtActionId`, does the headful session resume at the right point?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Stealth**: Does the browser pass a bot-detection test (e.g. [https://bot.sannysoft.com](https://bot.sannysoft.com))?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: - **Persistent profile**: Is the `data/browser-profile*` directory being created and reused between runs?

head: AGENTS.md > Post-Implementation Checklist
text: Tailor the list to what was actually touched — don't list every item for every change.

head: AGENTS.md > Finalize Convention
text: When the user says to **finalize** after a task is complete, stage **all** modified files using `git add .` (not just the files the agent edited — the user may have made background changes) and create a commit with an appropriate message.

head: AGENTS.md > Finalize Convention
text: When publishing finished work, prefer committing and pushing directly on the `main` branch unless the user explicitly asks for a separate feature branch.

head: AGENTS.md > Finalize Convention
text: Commit titles should be long and descriptive enough to clearly summarize the full scope of the changes (even the ones you did not directly make), not terse or generic.

head: AGENTS.md > Finalize Convention
text: Do not add yourself (the agent) as a co-author on commits, and do not mention this instruction or its origin in the commit message.

head: AGENTS.md > Release & Changelog Convention
text: When the user asks to **create a new release**, complete all of the following before tagging or publishing it:

head: AGENTS.md > Release & Changelog Convention
text: 1. **Choose and bump the version.** Use the exact version requested by the user. If no version is specified, inspect all changes since the previous release and choose the appropriate next version according to SemVer (major for breaking changes, minor for backward-compatible features, patch for backward-compatible fixes). Update the version in `package.json` and any lockfile that mirrors it.

head: AGENTS.md > Release & Changelog Convention
text: 2. **Update the complete changelog.** Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry covering **all** changes since the previous release, not only changes made during the current coding session. Review the full commit range (`git log <previous-tag>..HEAD`) as well as any relevant uncommitted release changes so nothing is omitted.

head: AGENTS.md > Release & Changelog Convention
text: 3. **Reconcile the roadmap.** Review the Roadmap section in `README.md`. If the new release completes any listed roadmap item, mark that item as checked and update its wording when needed to accurately describe what shipped. Do not check off an item unless the released implementation actually fulfills it.

head: AGENTS.md > Release & Changelog Convention
text: 4. **Reconcile the agent specification.** Review the release for new or changed automation capabilities, task fields, action types, or behavior that users and implementers need to know about. Update `AGENT_SPEC.md` whenever the release adds anything substantively worth documenting there, keeping it aligned with the implementation.

head: AGENTS.md > Release & Changelog Convention
text: After pushing to `main`, check `git tag` for older release tags that do not yet have a corresponding entry in `CHANGELOG.md`. For each missing historical release, summarize only the commits between the previous release tag and that tag (`git log <previous-tag>..<tag>`). Only tags are treated as completed releases; a `package.json` version bump alone does not constitute one.

the AMD BC-250 (Cyan Skillfish / GFX1013). Run on the user's daily-driver
hardware — correctness and reversibility outrank cleverness.

head: BC-250 SteamOS Real Toolkit — Agent Notes > Working agreements

  `revert_*` + `*_installed` + `persist_state_add` + a reapply `case` +

head: BC-250 SteamOS Real Toolkit — Agent Notes > Working agreements

  dry-run apply *and* reverse against a pristine tree.

head: BC-250 SteamOS Real Toolkit — Agent Notes > Working agreements

  hardware behavior from dry-runs or upstream READMEs.

  draft `.devin/specs/<slug>/spec.md` (template: `.devin/specs/_template.md`)
  → user review → implement → reviewer gate → user tests → commit. Process:
  `.devin/specs/README.md`, workflow: `.devin/workflows/spec.md`. Only
  trivial bugfixes/docs edits skip the spec.

head: BC-250 SteamOS Real Toolkit — Agent Notes > Specs & subagents — REQUIRED workflow

  `researcher` (upstream/patch comparison — dispatch for any "investigate
  X upstream" task), `linux-systems` (kernel/bash/systemd write work),

  doing it serially in the root agent.

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > What This Is
text: **The Cognition Engine for Enterprise AI.**

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > What This Is
text:
aperture-nexus enables enterprise AI agents to establish relations for
context, capture knowledge across text, images, video, and documents,
and commit it to memory for search and retrieval. It uses **ApertureDB**
as its storage and query backend, leveraging ApertureDB's vector search,
knowledge graph, and multimodal data capabilities.

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > What This Is
text:
The three building blocks — **Knowledge** (what was captured),
**Memory** (the engine that stores and retrieves it), and **Context**
(who did what, in which session, and why) — together form the KMC
model and a complete cognition layer for enterprise deployments.

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Before Writing Any Code
text: 1. **Read the ApertureDB Python SDK source** in `../aperturedb-python/aperturedb/` — especially `Connector.py`, `Configuration.py`, `CommonLibrary.py`, `Query.py`, `Entities.py`, `Descriptors.py`, `Images.py`, `Videos.py`, `ParallelLoader.py`

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Before Writing Any Code
text: 2. **Understand the ApertureDB JSON API** — every query is a list of command objects. Multi-step queries use `_ref` to chain results. Study the examples in `../demos/` and `../workflows/`

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Before Writing Any Code
text: 3. **Run `adb-nexus validate`** before assuming a live DB is available for testing

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Architecture > Key Design Decisions (do not revisit without discussion)
text: - **`Memory` is the only thing that writes to ApertureDB** — `Context` and `Information` are data objects only

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Architecture > Key Design Decisions (do not revisit without discussion)
text: - **`Information.log()` validates and normalizes locally** — no model calls, no DB access

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Architecture > Key Design Decisions (do not revisit without discussion)
text: - **Sessions are many-to-many with users** — each participant gets their own `Context` into a shared session

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Architecture > Key Design Decisions (do not revisit without discussion)
text: - **DB connection wraps `create_connector()` from `aperturedb.CommonLibrary`** — three tiers: pass `Connector` directly → `APERTUREDB_KEY` env var → `APERTUREDB_JSON` env var → active `adb config`

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Architecture > Key Design Decisions (do not revisit without discussion)
text: - **Config is file-based** (`aperture_nexus.json`) — generated by `adb-nexus init`, never hardcoded

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Architecture > Key Design Decisions (do not revisit without discussion)
text: - **No root required anywhere** — paths, ports, and operations must work as a regular user

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Architecture > ApertureDB Storage Mapping
text:
| aperture-nexus concept | ApertureDB storage |
|------------------------|-------------------|
| Principal | Entity (`NexusPrincipal` class) with hashed `api_key`, `department`, `organization` properties |
| Session | Entity (`NexusSession` class) with `session_id`, `session_name`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `organization` |
| Context | Entity (`NexusContext` class) with `context_id`, `session_id`, `user_id`, `purpose`, ... |
| Session ↔ Context | Connection (`nexus_session_context`) |
| Context ↔ Context | Connection (`nexus_link`) with `type` property |
| Information (text, short) | `Blob` (document_type="text") + Descriptor with inline `text` property |
| Information (text, long/chunked) | `Blob` (document_type="txt") chunks + Descriptors |
| Information (image) | `Image` + `Descriptor` |
| Information (video) | `Video` + per-clip `Descriptor`s (start_frame/stop_frame) |
| Information (blob/document) | `Blob` with `document_type` property |
| Pending connection (info.connect()) | Written as `nexus_link` on `commit()` |

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Public API > `NexusAdmin`
text:
Identity authority. Requires admin ApertureDB credentials. Used at setup time
and by operators — not in the hot path of agent code.

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Public API > `Memory`
text:
Storage and retrieval engine. Operates on already-authenticated Principals
via the Context passed to each operation. Never authenticates directly.

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Public API > `Context`
text: Minimum required: `principal` AND (`session_id` OR unique `session_name`)

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Public API > `Information`
text: Always requires a `context_id`. Buffers locally — nothing written to ApertureDB until `memory.commit()`.

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Error Handling
text: All errors are subclasses of `NexusError`. Always:

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Error Handling
text: - Validate at the boundary (log() time, not commit() time)

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Error Handling
text: - Raise the most specific subclass available

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Error Handling
text: - Write clear messages: what went wrong, why, what to do

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Error Handling
text:
- Chain the original exception: `raise NexusXxxError("...") from e`
```
NexusError                 # base + unknown errors
├── NexusConfigError       # misconfiguration, missing models, missing optional deps
├── NexusValidationError   # bad input at log() time
├── NexusConnectionError   # ApertureDB unreachable
├── NexusPermissionError   # principal lacks permission
├── NexusProcessingError   # model call failed
└── NexusStorageError      # ApertureDB rejected the write
```

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Error Handling
text:
Good error message format:
```
NexusConfigError: No embedding model configured for image input.
Set models.image_embedding in aperture_nexus.json, or pass
embedding_model='your-model' to info.log().
Run 'adb-nexus init' to regenerate your config.
```

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Configuration
text: Config file (`aperture_nexus.json`) is discovered in this order:

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Configuration
text: 1. Explicit path: `Memory(config="...")`

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Configuration
text: 2. `APERTURE_NEXUS_CONFIG` env var

head: aperture-nexus — Development Guide > Configuration

head: Zenith Admin — 项目架构导航
text:
Zenith Admin 是一个基于 **Hono + React + Drizzle ORM** 的模块化全栈后台系统，采用 npm monorepo 管理。
后端是模块化单体，提供 API、后台运行时和 CMS 前台渲染；前端提供多个应用入口，共享层统一前后端契约。

本文件只维护稳定的架构事实：系统边界、工作区职责、依赖方向、运行时链路和文档入口。
字段约定、代码模板、组件用法、运行参数与验收步骤不在这里重复维护。

head: Zenith Admin — 项目架构导航 > 文档定位

开始任何代码改动前，必须阅读核心规范约束：后端与全局看
[constraints.md](.agents/skills/zenith/references/constraints.md)，前端看
[constraints-frontend.md](.agents/skills/zenith/references/constraints-frontend.md)。

head: Zenith Admin — 项目架构导航 > 系统上下文 > 核心边界
text: - **Server 是业务权威边界**：负责认证授权、业务规则、事务、任务编排、CMS 渲染和外部集成。

- **Shared 是契约边界**：每个业务域的 API 契约（实体 schema、操作的方法 / 路径 / 入参 / 响应）定义在

text:

跨进程 WebSocket 与设备推送经 Redis pub/sub 扇出，保证 worker 产生的进度和通知能送达任一 api 节点上的浏览器。

Electron 复用 Web 构建产物。可缓存服务端状态的主链路是：

head: Zenith Admin — 项目架构导航 > 前端运行时
text:
TanStack Query 主要管理可缓存的服务端状态；页面保留交互状态以及流式会话、设计器等非缓存本地状态。
流式请求、上传下载、终端和部分命令式操作会直接使用 Request Adapter 或专用传输。
管理员与会员使用独立的认证上下文、请求实例和会话语义，不能互换。
Demo 模式通过 MSW 替换 API 边界，但继续复用真实接口契约，不是第二套业务模型。

head: Zenith Admin — 项目架构导航 > 跨领域架构
text:
| 关注点 | 架构策略 |
| --- | --- |
| 契约一致性 | 每个操作的路径、入参与响应 schema 在 `shared` 契约中定义一次：Server 用 `defineContractRoute` 生成路由与 OpenAPI，Web 用 `api()` / `createResourceQueries()` 发起调用，Mock 用 `mock(op)` 绑定 handler；仍以字面量书写的 URL 由 web 的路径契约测试对照服务端路由快照校验 |
| 身份与隔离 | 管理员和会员认证隔离；租户与数据范围在服务端执行 |
| 数据一致性 | 多步业务写入的事务边界主要位于 Service，数据库约束提供最终保护 |
| 异步处理 | 任务中心与 worker 负责调度、重试、进度和批量处理 |
| 通知触达 | 事件目录（shared 代码定义）+ 统一派发层收口全部通知：`notify()` 唯一入口，渠道、偏好、免打扰与投递留痕由派发层负责 |
| 跨域协作 | 同步协作复用服务函数，需解耦的后续副作用使用领域事件与 subscriber，不走内部 HTTP |
| AI 运行时 | AI 域由 Mastra 框架承载（模型目录、Memory、RAG、评测），运行数据落同库独立 `mastra` schema，Studio 经 `/api/mastra` 标准 API 接入 |
| 外部集成 | 文件、消息、OAuth、支付、AI 等能力通过服务端适配层接入 |
| 可观测性 | 浏览器采集、请求追踪、日志、指标和审计共同构成观测面 |

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Rule 1 — Think Before Coding.
No silent assumptions. State what you're assuming. Surface tradeoffs. Ask before guessing. Push back when a simpler approach exists.
Rule 2 — Simplicity First.
Minimum code that solves the problem. No speculative features. No abstractions for single-use code. If a senior engineer would call it overcomplicated — simplify.
Rule 3 — Surgical Changes.
Touch only what you must. Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting. Don't refactor what isn't broken. Match existing style.
Rule 4 — Goal-Driven Execution.
Define success criteria. Loop until verified. Don't tell Claude what steps to follow, tell it what success looks like and let it iterate.

head: CLAUDE.md > Cross-Language Bindings
text: When modifying Rust code that has Python bindings (tapo-py), always check if corresponding Python type stubs (.pyi files) need updating. The `debug` feature in `tapo` is **user-facing public API** — `tapo-py` enables it (`features = ["python", "debug"]`), so all `debug`-gated types are also exposed to Python. Treat changes behind `cfg(feature = "debug")` as public API changes requiring changelog entries for both Rust and Python.

head: CLAUDE.md > Cross-Language Bindings > Exposing Rust Types to Python
text: - **Simple value/result types**: Annotate directly in the `tapo` crate with `#[cfg_attr(feature = "python", pyo3::prelude::pyclass(from_py_object, ...))]` and `#[cfg(feature = "python")] crate::impl_to_dict!(TypeName);`. Do NOT create a redundant wrapper struct in `tapo-py`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Cross-Language Bindings > Exposing Rust Types to Python
text: - **`serde_json::Value` → Python**: Use `crate::python::serde_object_to_py_dict`. Do NOT write custom conversion functions — pyo3's `serde` feature does not auto-implement `IntoPyObject` for `Value`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Cross-Language Bindings > Python Stub Conventions
text: - `Ext` classes in `.pyi` stubs (e.g. `ToDictExt`, `DebugExt`, `OnOffExt`) must use `typing.Protocol` since they describe capabilities of PyO3 classes without real Python-level inheritance.

text: **版本号单一来源 = git tag**（规范 `1.590`，纯数字三段、**无 v 前缀**——沿用仓库历史惯例，也是 scoop autoupdate 模板 `download/$version/` 的依赖；fmdata 更新也占正常版本号如 `1.591`）。**不要用四段号** `1.590.1`——`checkUpdate()` 的正则会截断成 `1.590`，用户收不到更新提示。更新日志.txt 里的版本行**带 v**（`v1.590`，面向用户显示格式，`release_notes.py` 内部做转换）。

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: **更新记录唯一来源 = `更新日志.txt`**（人手写，git 跟踪；CI 对它只读不改）。CHANGELOG.md 已废除。

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: 1. `更新日志.txt` 顶部（TODO 注释块之后）插入新版本块：`____分隔线 / v1.590 / 一行一条改动`——只写用户可感知的改动

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: 2. 代码改动走 PR（单人也不例外），**攒若干 commit 后一起发起**（不必一 commit 一 PR）：从 master 切分支/或 `git push origin master:<分支名>` → `gh pr create`（正文 `Fixes #N` 关联 issue）→ rebase-merge 进 master

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: 4. 在 merge 后的 master commit 上 `git tag 1.590 && git push origin 1.590` ← 触发 CI。**tag 是发版运维动作不走 PR**（业界惯例：PR 管代码变更，tag 管发布；版本号由 tag 驱动，必须打在已 merge 的 commit 上直推）

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: 5. CI（release.yml）：checkout tag 的 commit → 从 `data` prerelease 拉 FM 数据 → `build.py dist` → 从更新日志提取该版本条目作 Release body → 创建 **draft** Release

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: 6. 测试同学验证 draft 附件 → 人工点 "Publish release" 转正

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text:
**游戏版本更新后（fmdata，纯运维）**：
```bash
python script/build.py fmdata
python script/build.py fmdata-upload
# fmdata-upload: 以 dist/data_manifest.json 为真相源选包上传到 data prerelease,
#                复查线上资产确认成功后自动删除旧版本 zip (防多版本并存时 CI 选错包)
# 然后更新 更新日志.txt (走 PR) → 在 master 上打新 tag (如 1.591), 由人拍板
# 注意: 客户端 FMDataUpdater 会在用户下次启动时自动拉取新 data (无需发版即生效,
#       但要不要发版/打 tag 仍由人拍板, 流程不变)
# data/aces/version(WT 版本号) + data/aces/date(打包日期) 两个标记文件:
#       build.py fmdata 写入, FMDataUpdater 更新后对 date 兜底补写, 设置面板版本信息行显示
```

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: **灰度测试**：push 正式 tag → CI 建 draft（公众不可见，`checkUpdate()` 不弹）→ 测试同学下载验证 → Publish 转正。不通过即删 draft + 删 tag 重来。测试与发布共用同一份产物。**版本号不用 `-rc`/`-test` 后缀**——发布状态由 draft/published 表达。

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: **纯构建核验**：Actions 页手动触发 `release` workflow 填 version + 勾 dry-run → 只产出 artifact，不创建 Release。

head: CLAUDE.md > 发版流程
text: **原则**：发版永远是显式动作（人工 Publish；tag 触发的只是构建）；旧版本 Release 一经发布不再改动。

head: CLAUDE.md > 测试手册
text: `测试手册.md` 是全场景手动测试的唯一真相源, 由 agent 维护。审美一句话：**把关键点和操作放到一起, 没用的不要有**。

head: CLAUDE.md > 测试手册
text: - **结构**：顶层"预览模式 (主窗与所见即所得)"两列表（操作|测试版本）+ "游戏模式 (真机飞行)"三列表（机型|操作|测试版本），两种模式都按面板名分小节，同名小节两两对应

head: CLAUDE.md > 测试手册
text: - **操作列文体**："动作, 看什么; 动作, 听什么"的流水句，真实最短路径。标杆：`试飞并摔死重生, 没问题; 然后重新试飞, 没问题`（一句覆盖冷启动/连接/异常退出/幂等）。"没问题"就够了；只在**不直观的回归点**写具体预期（如"直升机不出现失速红区"）

head: CLAUDE.md > 测试手册
text: - **机型列**：具体机型（一般检查用 f4u-4b），前提括号跟在机型后（`mi-24a (带起落架)`、`he51a1 (无罗盘仪表)`），不同前提拆行；禁止"任意机型/—/临时选"占位

head: CLAUDE.md > 测试手册
text: - **等价类收敛**：普适特性（所见即所得/拖拽/持久化）和设置生效类（字体/边框/开关）拿飞行信息测一个例子；出过问题的项（字体大小, v1.585）补第二个面板做双份（现 MiniHUD）；后续某面板出新问题再照此补双份，不逐面板列等价类

head: CLAUDE.md > 测试手册
text: - **收录门槛**：只收**用户可感知**且有出错空间的场景（复杂算法/长传递链/机型前提分支），纯透传显示不收，纯系统层指标（如 TCP 连接数/TIME_WAIT——用户看不到，回归靠 mock/e2e 白盒覆盖）不收；**测试同学必须能自行触发**（依赖"云端发新数据"之类前置不受控的场景不收——agent 用 mock+改本地数据验证一次即可，不进手册）；预期必须可判定，"合理/正常/随x变化"这类看不出错的措辞不要

head: CLAUDE.md > 测试手册
text: - **禁止进手册**：场景编号、数据依赖字段名、实现细节（类名/配置键）、操作列里的版本备注、规则解释与元信息（"双份"）——这些只写在 CLAUDE.md。版本号只出现在测试版本列，且只填真机验证过的

head: CLAUDE.md > 测试手册
text: - **写完必须做纯审美审查**（重点，单独一步）：只对照上面的文体标准逐行过——"正常/合理"改"没问题"或删、空话（"试XX功能"）、冗余副词、元信息、占位机型、表格断裂。**这一步不做事实正确性核查**（机型文件是否存在/代码行为/配置项），内容对错是另一回事

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 包一览（src/）
text: - **`prog/`** 内核：`Launcher`（GPU 兼容 JVM 属性，须在 AWT 加载前设置）→ `Application` → `Controller`（生命周期/overlay 协调）→ `Service`（HTTP 轮询+计算后台线程，最大文件）；`OverlayManager`（overlay 可见性，方法须 synchronized）；`AlwaysOnTopCoordinator`（单例 z-order/对话框协调，WeakReference）；`FocusMonitor`（游戏失焦自动隐藏，复用 Service 轮询）；`fm/`（FM 单一真相源：`FMManager` 单例 identify/负缓存/FM_CHANGED 广播，`dataUpdated()` 供热替换后清负缓存强制重载；`FMLoader` 项目内唯一 `new Blkx` 点，全程 catch(Throwable)→READY/MISSING/CORRUPT；`FMDataUpdater` FM 数据在线自动更新一条链（检查→下载→sha256→解压→rename 替换→`dataUpdated()` 生效，`-Dvoidmei.fmdata.update=force/off` 开发与 e2e 用）；`FMHandle` 不可变句柄；`FMDataPaths` 路径唯一来源）；`config/`、`audio/`、`util/`、`hotkey/`、`i18n/`、`model/`、`event/`（`UIStateBus`/`FlightDataBus`）

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 包一览（src/）
text: - **`parser/`** 数据摄取：`State`/`Indicators`（8111 JSON）、`Blkx`（FM .blk 解析）、`FlightAnalyzer`、`FlightLog` 等

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 包一览（src/）
text: - **`ui/`** 界面：`MainForm`（设置窗）、`overlay/`（各 HUD overlay + `logic/HUDCalculator` + `model/HUDData`）、`layout/`（ui_layout.cfg 动态生成设置面板 + 17 种 renderer）、`component/`（HUD 部件）、`base/`（`DraggableOverlay`/`FieldOverlay`）、`model/`（`TelemetrySource` 等）、`replica/`、`util/`、`window/comparison/`（飞机对比）

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 数据流
text: - **HUDData 预计算**：计算在 Service 线程完成，EDT 只消费 `event.getHudData()`；overlay 内 dirty check（值变才重绘）

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 数据流
text: - **FM 加载**：Service 每轮 `identify(sIndic.type)`（同目标零成本），计算取 `FMManager.current()` 快照；无 FM 时相关指标按 0/上次值/MAX_VALUE 降级，UI 配合 visible-when 隐藏。**EDT 上不允许 new Blkx / FMLoader.load**（R3 规则）

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 数据流
text: - **引擎类型过滤**：Service 按引擎类型将无关指标置 0（喷气：进气压/水温；活塞：推力），配合隐藏逻辑

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 线程与窗口规则
text: - **EDT 规则**：Swing 组件更新必须 `SwingUtilities.invokeLater`；事件可能在后台线程回调

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 线程与窗口规则
text: - **僵尸窗口防护**：注册进 `AlwaysOnTopCoordinator` 的窗口必须在 `dispose()` 中 `unregisterOverlay(this)`，否则 `FocusMonitor.showAllOverlays()` 会复活已销毁窗口

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 线程与窗口规则
text: - **焦点抢占防护**：`setFocusable(false)` 必须在 `registerOverlay()` 之前；对话框用 `dialogWillShow()`/`dialogDidDismiss()` 挂起/恢复 alwaysOnTop

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 线程与窗口规则
text: - **托盘点击防重**：`Application` 用 `AtomicBoolean` CAS 防重复创建 Controller；`Controller.stop()` 清理顺序：关 overlay→退订事件→dispose MainForm→停 Service→存配置

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 线程与窗口规则
text: - **预览过期回调**：`Controller` 用 `AtomicLong previewGeneration` 防切换游戏模式后旧 EDT 回调复活预览 overlay

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 线程与窗口规则
text: - **预览 FM 回退**：预览模式走 `Controller.detectAndIdentify()`——先探测 8111 live 机型，拿不到回退配置的默认飞机，统一交 `FMManager.identify()`；仅 PREVIEW 状态触发

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > GPU 兼容 / DPI / 失焦检测
text:
| 机制 | 要点 |
|------|------|
| GPU 兼容 | `Launcher`（无 AWT import）在 AWT 加载**前**设 `sun.java2d.*` 属性关硬件加速；状态存 `gpu_compat.properties`（必须早于 ui_layout.cfg 可读，故独立文件）；`gpuCompatibilityMode` 配置键在 SwitchRowRenderer 有特殊处理 |
| DPI 缩放 | `DPIHelper` 经 `GraphicsConfiguration.getDefaultTransform()` 探测，暴露 `Application.dpiScale`（2.0=200%）与 `logicalWidth/Height`；字体/尺寸计算一律乘 dpiScale，屏幕定位用 logical 尺寸不用 `Toolkit.getScreenSize()`（那是物理像素） |
| 失焦自动隐藏 | `FocusMonitor`(200ms 节流)+`FocusDetector`（Windows: PowerShell 查 `aces` 进程；Linux: xdotool；macOS: AppleScript）；无新线程 |
| 网络代理 | **JVM 不读 `HTTPS_PROXY` 环境变量**（Java 老坑，`HttpURLConnection` 只认系统属性）。`Launcher` 启动最早期做两层：设 `java.net.useSystemProxies=true`（跟随 Windows 系统代理，Clash/v2rayN"系统代理"模式用户零配置自动生效；8111 不受影响——默认 nonProxyHosts 排除 localhost）+ 把 `HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY` 映射成 `https.proxyHost/Port`（只对终端启动生效，GUI 双击无 shell 环境；`-D` 显式设置优先）。**不做端口扫描探测**（用户拍板）：只开本地端口没开系统代理的工具属于用户侧开关没开，不代猜 |

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 工具类去向（禁止自写）
text:
| 需求 | 用 |
|------|-----|
| 物理常数 | `PhysicsConstants`（`g`/`G` 等）——**永不硬编码** `9.78f`/`9.80` |
| 插值 | `Interpolation`（`lerp`/`interp1d`/`interp2d`/`interpSweepLevel`） |
| 大气 | `AtmosphereModel`（`pressure`/`density`/`iasToTas`/`tasToIas`/`ramEffectAltitude`） |
| 活塞功率 | `PistonPowerModel`（详见 `src/prog/util/CLAUDE.md`） |
| 颜色 | `ColorHelper`（`parseColor` 收 hex `#RRGGBBAA` 或十进制 `R,G,B,A`；存储用十进制保兼容） |
| 异常 | `ExceptionHelper`（`sleepQuietly`/`logAndContinue`/`closeQuietly`）——禁止空 catch 块 |
| 日志 | `Logger`（TRACE/DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR，默认 INFO） |
| UI 样式/滑条/绘图/常量 | `OverlayStyleHelper`/`SliderHelper`/`GraphicsUtil`/`UIConstants`（详见 `src/ui/util/CLAUDE.md`） |

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > ConfigProvider 解耦
text: **Controller 不实现 ConfigProvider**。overlay 组件职责分离：

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > ConfigProvider 解耦
text:
| 字段 | 用途 |
|------|------|
| `config`（`ConfigProvider`） | 配置读写，`init()` 时 `c.getConfigProvider()` 获取 |

text: 禁止运行时从 Controller 取 configService、禁止把 config 强转 Controller（ClassCastException）。

text: **新增配置开关**：① `ui_layout.cfg` 加 `(item ... :type switch :target "myKey")` → ② `HUDSettings`/`OverlaySettings` 加接口方法 → ③ `ConfigurationService` 实现（`getBool("myKey", def)`）→ ④ 目标 overlay 用配置控制行为 → ⑤ `Controller` 把键加进 `.withInterest()`（WYSIWYG 实时预览）。注意 RowConfig 新字段有强制检查点，见 `src/prog/config/CLAUDE.md`。

head: CLAUDE.md
text:
Notes for any Claude session working in this repo. Keep this short. If
something here is wrong, fix it — don't accumulate stale context.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text:
A Claude Code plugin marketplace for iGPT. The marketplace manifest is at
`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. Each plugin under `plugins/` bundles a
role-specific set of skills (sales, CS, finance, HR, etc.) that all
talk to the same backend MCP server: `https://mcp.igpt.ai/`. The marketplace
ships 13 plugins, 76 skills, and 13 agents (one per plugin) total at the
time of writing.

head: CLAUDE.md > Working branch
text:
`dev`. `main` is the published branch — don't commit there directly. PRs
from `dev` → `main` happen on demand, not yet wired up.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**SKILL.md YAML frontmatter** — single line for `name` and `description`,
plus a nested `metadata` block. No quotes:

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text: **`.mcp.json` in every plugin** — exactly this shape, nothing more:

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text: No `description` field. `type` is `http`, not `url`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**Prerequisites section in SKILL.md** — inline, not a remote fetch. Every
SKILL.md has a `## Prerequisites` block right after the H1 that tells Claude
what to do if the iGPT MCP isn't connected or auth fails. The block is
self-contained so a user who installs a single skill outside the plugin still
gets useful guidance. The full guard at `shared/mcp-guard.md` (canonical URL
in each block) is kept as a fallback for deeper troubleshooting only — not
fetched on every invocation.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
If you change the inline block, change it across all 76 SKILL.md files in
one pass with a script. Don't drift.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**MCP tools available from `https://mcp.igpt.ai/`** — `ask` and `search`.
Pattern in most skills: `search` first to confirm data exists and narrow the
date range, then `ask` with a structured `output_format` schema for the
final answer. The `ask` tool takes two named arguments: `input` (the prompt
text) and `output_format` (the JSON schema). Use `input:`, never `prompt:`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text: **Workflow section in SKILL.md** — every skill follows the same template:

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
1. **Step 1 collects user-supplied values.** No hardcoded numbers, dates,
   or scopes anywhere in tool calls. Each variable the skill needs is
   defined in step 1 with a default and a description; values come from
   the user. Derived variables (e.g. a clause that's empty when scope is
   "all") are also defined here so step 3's input stays clean.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
2. **Step 2 calls search** with structured params. Variables are
   substituted into the params (e.g. date_from: ISO start date derived
   from [time_range]).

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
3. **Step 3 calls ask** with two arguments only: input and output_format.
   The input value is **only** the prompt template with [var] placeholders
   inline — no surrounding quotes, no meta instructions about substitution,
   no "where:" clauses, nothing else. When the skill runs, each [var] is
   replaced by the user's value and the resulting plain text is what gets
   sent.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**Placeholder syntax** — use `[var_name]`, not `{var_name}` and not
backtick-wrapped. Square brackets are the project standard. The brackets
are markers for substitution, not literal characters; they never appear in
the value sent to a tool.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**Time / date handling** — when a skill needs a date window, the variable
holds the user's natural-language phrasing ("the last 3 months", "May 2024",
"between Jan 1 and Mar 15", "since the kickoff"). Convert to ISO dates only
for the search call's `date_from` / `date_to`. For the ask input, use the
user's phrasing as-is. Don't ask the user for ISO dates; let them speak
naturally.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**Agents in `plugins/<plugin>/agents/`** — every plugin has exactly one
agent file at `plugins/<plugin>/agents/<plugin>.md` (the file name matches
the plugin directory). Auto-discovered by Claude Code; no path declaration
needed in `marketplace.json` or `plugin.json`. Each agent has YAML
frontmatter with `name`, `description`, `tools`, and `metadata.version`:

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
`tools` is restricted to the iGPT MCP tools so the agent stays in its lane.
The body follows a consistent structure across all 13 agents: when-to-invoke
examples, a list of available skills with one-line summaries, decision
dimensions for choosing between skills, working-with-user guardrails
(defaults, natural-language dates, lead-with-the-punch-line, offer next
action), and the same inline Prerequisites block as SKILL.md. Each agent
also adds **domain-specific guardrails** that don't fit elsewhere — e.g.
"be precise about commercial terms" in finance / procurement, "candidate
names are sensitive" in recruiting, measured language for board /
fundraising contexts in executive. Keep those when editing.

  level sensitive-content rules (candidate-name privacy in recruiting,

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**Per-plugin README** — buyer-facing front door for the plugin. Speak to
the role (consultant, salesperson, recruiter), not to developers. The
shape is locked across all plugins; use `igpt-consulting/README.md` as
the reference template.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
Standard sections in order: title + tagline + badges, "Why this exists",
"What you can ask", "A typical week", "The skills" (table), "The agent",
"What you see" (3–4 chat exchanges), "How it works" (pipeline diagram +
privacy note + domain-specific guardrails), "Install" (Cowork →
Desktop → Code → other), "Folder structure", "Customization",
collapsible "Output schemas", "Related", "License".

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
The **"How it works" section has two parts**: a universal block (pipeline
diagram + the standard "data stays with iGPT" privacy paragraph) followed
by 1–3 short paragraphs lifting the agent's domain-specific guardrails
into buyer-facing prose — e.g. "stage discipline + contrarian signals"
in sales, "facts vs. sentiment + faithful decision logs" in projects,
"voice is content + patterns over outliers" in marketing. Mirror what
the agent body already enforces; the README is just surfacing it for
the buyer.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
- **Don't hardcode plugin counts.** Say "all our role-specific plugins",
  not "all 13 plugins". Per-plugin skill counts in the badges line are
  fine since they're accurate to that plugin.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
- **Tool-agnostic workflow phrasing.** No "search + ask", "search then
  ask", or other references to specific iGPT tool names — describe the
  workflow as "queries iGPT against your email". Skills may evolve.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
- **No anti-JSON framing.** No "you never see JSON" / "you don't see
  it" — we also want developers using these. JSON examples live in a
  collapsible `<details>` block for integrators; just don't bash them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
- **Folder structure shows only plugin-defining files** —
  `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `agents/`, `skills/`,
  `README.md`. Don't list `LICENSE.txt` or other generic boilerplate.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
- **Flag skills that require a user-supplied input** in the skills
  table itself. Example: real estate's `client-offer-history` ends
  with "Requires a client name."; sales' `meeting-prep-briefing` ends
  with "Requires contact + company." This sets expectations before the
  user invokes the skill; the agent will also ask for the value before
  running.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**"What you see" pattern.** Each chat exchange starts with **You:**
*question* (lowercase, casual — how a user actually types), then
**Claude:** *(running `skill-name` — short description of what's
happening against email)*, then the rendered response with bold names,
dates, action notes, and a follow-up offer in italics block-quote.
Separate exchanges with `---`. No cute headers like "Monday morning
triage" above each — the question is the header. Include one
cross-skill example showing the agent in action (announced as *(the X
agent kicks in, running N skills in parallel...)*).

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**Use realistic role-specific content.** Made-up but plausible
vendor names ("Atlas Studio", "Beacon Cloud"), candidate names with
sensitivity rules where relevant ("Sarah K." not "Sarah Kowalski"
in recruiting), real publication names where they fit ("Forbes",
"Nature Neuroscience"), real prospect dialogue. Generic placeholders
("Customer A", "$X") read as marketing fluff and undercut the engine
visibility the section is meant to convey.

head: CLAUDE.md > Conventions to follow
text:
**Cowork install — 5 steps.** Step 1 shows the marketplace search and
the GitHub URL (`igptai/skills` or `https://github.com/igptai/skills`)
as parallel options, not as a fallback. No preamble before step 1, no
apologetic "if you don't see it" framing on the GitHub option. Steps 2–5
walk through finding the plugin, installing, connecting email through
iGPT (one-time OAuth in a browser, mention read-only permissions and
that raw email stays with iGPT, only structured findings reach Claude),
and asking in plain language with 1–2 role-specific example questions.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo quirks
text:
The repo lives on a Windows filesystem mounted into the sandbox. Git
operations work but spew `Operation not permitted` warnings on
`.git/objects/tmp_obj_*` and occasionally fail to clear `.git/index.lock`
or `.git/HEAD.lock`. Workaround: `mv` the lock file out of the way (rename,
since `rm` fails on the mount), then retry. Commits go through correctly
despite the warnings — verify with `git log` after.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo quirks
text:
Note: the file tools (Read/Write/Edit) and bash sometimes see different
versions of a file mid-edit on this mount. If git can't see your changes
after editing through the file tools, rewrite the file via bash heredoc.

15. **WHEN using `.github/pull-request-template.md`, the manual testing section
    should contain instructions for how to _manually_ test the changes. It must not
    list steps for automated testing.**
    - Good Instructions:
      - Run extension

      - Enable "Hide zero-balance tokens".
      - Verify mUSD is still visible.

text:
17. **DEEPLINK INTERSTITIAL SECURITY — EXTREMELY HIGH RISK:** Before implementing any change that can cause fewer deep links to show the security interstitial, agents **MUST stop and obtain explicit, documented consent from `@MetaMask/extension-security-team`**. Without documented Security approval, do not make the change—even when it appears necessary to complete another feature, migration, refactor, or test fix. To make this less

head: AGENTS.md > Troubleshooting > Build Issues
text:
| Problem                      | Solution                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Module not found` errors    | Run `yarn install` again                                     |
| `Out of memory` during build | Increase Node heap: `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` |
| LavaMoat policy errors       | Run `yarn lavamoat:auto`                                     |
| Webpack cache issues         | Run `yarn webpack:clearcache`                                |
| Stale build artifacts        | Delete `dist/` and `build/` directories                      |

head: AGENTS.md > Troubleshooting > Test Issues
text:
| Problem                 | Solution                                          |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| E2E tests fail to start | Build test build first: `yarn build:test`         |
| Tests hang indefinitely | Check if port 8545 (Anvil) is available           |
| Snapshot tests fail     | Update snapshots: `yarn test:unit -u`             |
| Browser not launching   | Check if browser is installed and in PATH         |
| Random E2E failures     | Use `--retries` flag or check for race conditions |

head: AGENTS.md > Troubleshooting > Development Issues
text:
| Problem                | Solution                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Extension won't load   | Check browser console for errors                       |
| Hot reload not working | Restart `yarn start`                                   |
| Changes not appearing  | Hard refresh extension (chrome://extensions)           |
| State corrupted        | Clear extension data in browser                        |
| Port already in use    | Kill process on port: `lsof -ti:PORT \| xargs kill -9` |

head: AGENTS.md > Troubleshooting > Dependency Issues
text:
| Problem                  | Solution                                        |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Yarn version mismatch    | Run `corepack enable`                           |
| Package install fails    | Clear cache: `yarn cache clean && yarn install` |
| Peer dependency warnings | Check if packages are compatible                |
| Allow-scripts fails      | Run `yarn allow-scripts auto`                   |

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions
text: This section captures non-obvious, durable caveats for running this repo inside Cursor Cloud VMs. Dependency installation is handled automatically by the startup update script (nvm install/use per `.nvmrc`, `corepack enable`, `yarn install`, and creating `.metamaskrc` from `.metamaskrc.dist` if missing). Standard commands live in the sections above and in `README.md`/`package.json` — reference those instead of duplicating.

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions > Node version gotcha (important)
text: - The repo requires Node `>=24.13` (`.nvmrc` → `v24.13`), but the base image ships a fixed `/exec-daemon/node` (v22) shim that sits early on `PATH` and otherwise wins over nvm. `~/.bashrc` runs `nvm use default` at the end so **interactive shells get Node 24 automatically**. If a command runs Node 22 (e.g. Yarn's engines check fails), run `nvm use` (from the repo root, which reads `.nvmrc`) or prefix `PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.1/bin:$PATH"` before the command. `corepack enable` must run under Node 24 so Yarn 4 (`packageManager` in `package.json`) is used, not the legacy Yarn 1.

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions > Running / building the extension
text: - It is a browser extension, so `yarn start` does not open a UI — it webpack-builds + watches into `dist/chrome` (MV3). Initial build takes ~45s and then prints `compiled successfully` / `Watching for changes…`. Load `dist/chrome` as an unpacked extension in a Chromium browser to use it. Use `yarn start:mv2` for Firefox (`dist/firefox`).

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions > Running / building the extension
text: - `.metamaskrc` uses a **placeholder `INFURA_PROJECT_ID` (`00000000000`)**, which is enough to build and to onboard/create a wallet locally, but **all live RPC fails** (you'll see "Unable to connect to <network>"). For any on-chain flow (balances, sending, swaps), provide a real `INFURA_PROJECT_ID`, or point networks at a local `yarn anvil` chain (`:8545`).

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions > Running / building the extension
text: - Build config precedence is **`process.env` > `.metamaskprodrc` > `.metamaskrc` > `builds.yml`** (`development/webpack/utils/config.ts`; env vars win). So the Cursor Cloud secret named `INFURA_PROJECT_ID` is picked up automatically by the build in any **new** VM session (it overrides the placeholder in `.metamaskrc` with no file edit needed). Note secrets are injected only into new VMs, not one already running when the secret is added.

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions > Visual / interactive verification (`mm` CLI)
text: - The `mm` CLI (`node_modules/.bin/mm`, from `@metamask/client-mcp-core`) drives the extension via Playwright and is the fastest way to click through onboarding/unlock/send flows. It requires **Playwright's Chromium**, which is not part of `yarn install`: run `yarn playwright install chromium` once (cached under `~/.cache/ms-playwright`) before `mm launch`. It also needs an X display — one is available at `DISPLAY=:1` (set `export DISPLAY=:1`).

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions > Visual / interactive verification (`mm` CLI)
text: - Launch against the existing dev build with `mm launch --context prod --extension-path dist/chrome --state onboarding`, then use `mm describe-screen` / `mm click --testid <id>` / `mm type`. During create-wallet, the on-home **Terms of Use** dialog's Agree button stays disabled until you click `terms-of-use-scroll-button` (repeatedly) to scroll the terms to the bottom. Always finish with `mm cleanup`. See `test/e2e/playwright/llm-workflow/README.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Cursor Cloud specific instructions > E2E tests
text: - Selenium-based E2E (`yarn test:e2e:*`) require a **test build** first (`yarn build:test` or the faster `yarn start:test`) plus a browser + driver; unit tests (`yarn test:unit`) and lint do not.

conventions for Git localization (l10n) contributions. This project
provides automated checking tools for Git l10n coordinators and
contributors, ensuring that pull requests submitted to
[git-l10n/git-po](https://github.com/git-l10n/git-po) comply with
established contribution conventions.

   - Subject must not contain non-ASCII characters
   - Subject length must not exceed 50 characters
   - Other lines must not exceed 72 characters
   - Must include "Signed-off-by:" signature

text: 3. **.po File Syntax**: Use `msgfmt` to verify syntax correctness

head: AGENTS.md - git-po-helper Project Guide > Development Standards > Main Functional Modules > Core Checking Features
text:

   po/XX.po

head: AGENTS.md - git-po-helper Project Guide > Development Standards > Main Functional Modules > Core Checking Features
text:
5. **File Location Cleanup**: File location information must be removed
   before submission

head: AGENTS.md - git-po-helper Project Guide > Development Standards > Main Functional Modules > Core Checking Features
text:

text:

  subsequent lines contain a detailed description of the change.

  than only describing how the change was implemented (how).

head: AGENTS.md - git-po-helper Project Guide > Development Standards > Commit Conventions

head: AGENTS.md - git-po-helper Project Guide > Development Standards > Commit Conventions
text:

head: AGENTS.md - git-po-helper Project Guide > Development Standards > Commit Conventions

  provide the commit message, for example:
  `git commit -F- <<-EOF`, and do NOT use multiple `-m <message>` arguments to
  build a multi-line commit message, because multiple `-m <message>` options
  will insert redundant blank lines into the final commit message.

head: AGENTS
text: Guidance for AI agents and human contributors working in `ts-gen`.

head: AGENTS > What this project does
text:
`ts-gen` is a TypeScript-to-Rust binding generator. It reads `.d.ts`
files and emits Rust source containing `#[wasm_bindgen] extern "C"`
blocks. The output is meant to compile cleanly against `wasm-bindgen`
and let downstream Rust code interact with JS APIs that are described
purely by their TypeScript declarations.

head: AGENTS > Conventions
text:
The single source of truth for "how does construct X translate?" is
[`CONVENTIONS.md`](CONVENTIONS.md). It catalogues every TypeScript →
Rust pattern we handle, ordered from simplest (primitives) to most
complex (subtyping LUB across unions).

head: AGENTS > Conventions
text: **When to update `CONVENTIONS.md`:**

head: AGENTS > Conventions
text: * Adding a new TS construct → add a numbered section.

head: AGENTS > Conventions
text: * Changing an existing translation rule → update its section.

head: AGENTS > Conventions
text:
* Bug fix that changes user-visible output → update if the fix changes
  the documented behaviour, otherwise just add a snapshot test.

head: AGENTS > Conventions
text:
A PR that changes the codegen output without a corresponding
`CONVENTIONS.md` change is suspect — either the convention was missing
(add it) or the change is unintentional (revisit it).

head: AGENTS > Code style
text: * Comments describe **nuance**, not the obvious. No `// ---` separators.

head: AGENTS > Code style
text: * Doc comments on public items use `///`; module-level docs use `//!`.

head: AGENTS > Code style
text:
* Diagnostic-worthy oddities go through `DiagnosticCollector::warn`,
  not `println!`/`eprintln!`.

head: AGENTS > Code style
text:
* Internal helpers are crate-private (`pub(crate)`) unless there's a
  reason to expose them to library consumers.

head: AGENTS > Build / test recipes
text: The `justfile` is the single source for repeatable commands:

head: AGENTS > Build / test recipes
text:
All recipes use `cargo +stable` because the upstream workspace pins an
older toolchain via `rust-toolchain.toml`. CI uses the same.

head: AGENTS > Tests
text:
1. **Unit tests** (`cargo test --lib`) — focused, white-box checks of
   internal helpers (parse logic, naming, subtyping LUB, signature
   expansion). New behaviour should ship with unit tests in the
   relevant module's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.

head: AGENTS > Tests
text:
2. **Snapshot tests** (`cargo test --test snapshot`) — fixture-driven.
   Every fixture under `tests/fixtures/` pairs with a snapshot under
   `tests/snapshots/`. Re-bless with `BLESS=1 cargo test`. Snapshot
   diffs in PRs should match documented convention changes — silently
   diff-only PRs are a smell.

head: AGENTS > Tests
text:
3. **Integration tests** (`integration-tests/`) — actual wasm-bindgen
   compilation + browser/V8 execution. Used for end-to-end ABI
   correctness. Lives in its own crate that only builds for `wasm32`.

head: AGENTS > Pipeline
text:
The two-phase parse is essential: phase 1 establishes name → kind
mappings so phase 2 can resolve forward references without re-walking
the AST.

head: AGENTS > When in doubt
text:
* **Are the conventions documented?** Check `CONVENTIONS.md` first; the
  pattern you're touching may already be specified there.

head: AGENTS > When in doubt
text:
* **Is there a fixture?** Add one. A targeted `.d.ts` snippet in
  `tests/fixtures/` plus its rendered snapshot is the cheapest way to
  pin behaviour.

head: AGENTS > When in doubt
text:
* **Does the change affect the rendered output?** Run
  `just test-overwrite` and review the snapshot diff carefully.

head: AGENTS > When in doubt
text:
* **Is the change cross-cutting?** Likely belongs in `signatures.rs`
  (per-callable layer), `typemap.rs` (per-type), or `subtyping.rs`
  (lattice). If you're adding a new module, consider whether a helper
  in an existing one would do.

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: The repo is a Bun workspace wrapped by Tauri 2. React UI code lives in `packages/client/src`, with view components in `components/`, extension-specific panels in `extensions/`, and RPC helpers in `lib/`. The Bun RPC backend sits in `packages/server/src/router.ts` and mounts extension routers under `packages/server/src/extensions`. `packages/server/src/extension.ts` hosts the extension runtime (`diffs.commands`, `diffs.window`, `diffs.workspace`, `diffs.storage`) that both built-in extensions use. Tauri assets stay under `src-tauri` (config in `tauri.conf.json`, Rust entry points in `src/main.rs` and `src/lib.rs`). Generated output under each `dist/` and the Rust `target/` folder must remain untracked.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `bun install` installs workspace dependencies with the pinned `bun@1.3.0` declared in `package.json`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `bun run dev` proxies to `tauri dev`, booting the Bun server, React client, and Tauri shell together.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `bun run tauri build` uses the `tauri` binary to emit production assets and bundle the desktop app.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: - `bun run lint` runs `oxlint --fix --deny-warnings .`; expect it to mutate files to resolve lint errors instead of waiving them.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands

head: UX Methods > Identity & scope
text: This repository is **UX Methods** — Andy Fitzgerald's personal knowledge-graph project, published at [uxmethods.org](https://www.uxmethods.org/). It is **separate from his Elemeno Health work**. Do not assume Elemeno conventions, schemas, tooling choices, or codebase patterns carry over here; treat this project on its own terms.

head: UX Methods > What UX Methods is
text: UX Methods provides a roadmap between and across the practices of user experience design. Its goal is to help UX practitioners arrive at purposeful, high-impact, user-centered design outcomes.

head: UX Methods > What UX Methods is
text: The web has no shortage of techniques, tools, and tips on how to "do" UX. Very few resources, however, explain how to use UX methods _together_, in a coordinated and purposeful way, to create holistic solutions. UX Methods fills that gap by:

head: UX Methods > What UX Methods is
text: - Assembling concise, reliable descriptions of UX method goals, steps, and outcomes

head: UX Methods > What UX Methods is
text: - Highlighting the meaningful relationships between methods so practitioners can craft holistic, purpose-driven project plans

head: UX Methods > What UX Methods is
text: - Collecting and contextualizing in-depth how-tos, case studies, and research from trustworthy sources on the web

head: UX Methods > What UX Methods is
text: For the full product and project vision — including the **surfaces** through which UXM knowledge is delivered (website UI, MCP, ontology docs, Fuseki, etc.) and the **characteristics** that should shape design and content decisions — see [docs/vision.md](docs/vision.md).

head: UX Methods > Project goal — knowledge graph maturation
text: UX Methods today uses a light taxonomy to coordinate methods. The active goal is to build on that foundation so the content collection, external resources, and semantic models become a **proper knowledge graph** that delivers significant value above and beyond the sum of its parts.

head: UX Methods > Project goal — knowledge graph maturation
text: - Use knowledge-graph approaches to enrich content, sharpen the expression of ideas, and improve the user experience

head: UX Methods > Project goal — knowledge graph maturation
text: - Build and demonstrate a skillset focused on generating new value and insight through the combination of structured, composable content and formal, domain-specific semantics

head: UX Methods > KG architecture — three layers > Sibling artefact — content-model diagram
text: Parallel to the three layers above, the Sanity schema can be visualised as a Mermaid `classDiagram` — documents vs objects, fields with cardinality, composition and reference edges. This began as an in-repo CLI (`content-model/`) that generated a committed `docs/content-model.md`, but the CLI had a hard limitation: loading `studio/schemaTypes/index.ts` directly, it never saw types contributed by Studio plugins (e.g. `skosConcept` from `sanity-plugin-taxonomy-manager`), so those edges dropped. **The CLI and its generated artefact have been retired** in favour of the Studio plugin below, which reads the fully-composed schema and has no such blind spot. The Mermaid mapping contract the CLI established lives on — see [ADR 0006](docs/decisions/0006-content-model-mermaid-export.md) (amended to note the retirement; it also covers the rationale for Mermaid over the OWL/RDFS approach ADR 0005 attempted).

head: UX Methods > KG architecture — three layers > Sibling artefact — content-model diagram
text: **The content model now lives in a published Studio plugin:** [`sanity-plugin-mermaid-content-model`](https://github.com/andybywire/sanity-plugin-mermaid-content-model) — extracted from this monorepo ([ADR 0007](docs/decisions/0007-content-model-plugin-architecture.md)) and published to npm. It renders the diagram **in-Studio** (the **Content Model** top-nav tool), reading the composed workspace schema via `useSchema()`, so `skosConcept` and other plugin-contributed types are included. `studio/` consumes it (`^0.1.0`). Like the old artefact, it sits parallel to the three KG layers — not pushed to Fuseki, not imported into `workspace.ttl`, not involved in inference.

text: **Snap SPARQL vs built-in SPARQL — important trap:**
