head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships
text: Methods are connected through the **inputs/outputs (IO) taxonomy**. A concept that is an _output_ of one method is an _input_ to another (e.g. "user's mental model" is an output of contextual research and an input to navigation design). This IO model is the seed the larger knowledge graph builds on — keep it intact when proposing schema or ontology changes.

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > SPARQL-based relationship logic
text: Today the site computes relationships via SPARQL joins:

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > SPARQL-based relationship logic
text: - **Upstream methods:** "who produces what I need" (their outputs match my inputs).

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > SPARQL-based relationship logic
text: - **Downstream methods:** "who needs what I produce."

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > SPARQL-based relationship logic
text: - **Weights:** `COUNT(DISTINCT ?shared)` over shared IO concepts.

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > SPARQL-based relationship logic
text: - **Multi-origin variant:** a UNION/`VALUES` query that runs for one or many origin methods at once.

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > SPARQL-based relationship logic
text: Reference query: `graph/queries/method-output-enables-method-input.rq`.

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > Inference work in progress
text: Some of this join logic is being moved into ontology semantics:

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > Inference work in progress
text: - Object properties `uxm:hasUpstreamMethod` and `uxm:hasDownstreamMethod` are defined in the core ontology.

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > Inference work in progress
text: - **OWL property chain axioms** let a reasoner infer these edges from `usesInput` / `producesOutput` + shared concepts.

head: UX Methods > Method-to-method relationships > Inference work in progress
text: Note that plain RDFS inference will **not** apply OWL property chains — you need an OWL-capable entailment regime (OWL RL or rules).

head: UX Methods > Open architectural decision — how inference runs in production
text: There are two viable production paths. Both are real; the project hasn't committed yet.

head: UX Methods > Open architectural decision — how inference runs in production > A. Query-time inference in Fuseki
text: Configure Fuseki with an OWL-capable reasoner so `hasUpstreamMethod` / `hasDownstreamMethod` appear as entailments at query time. Simpler conceptually; performance and entailment-regime selection are the questions.

head: UX Methods > Open architectural decision — how inference runs in production > B. Materialized derived graph (currently the pragmatic favorite)
text: A scheduled step computes upstream/downstream edges, weights, and optional explanations (which shared concepts caused each link), and writes them into a derived named graph (e.g. `https://uxmethods.org/graph/derived`). UI queries hit asserted triples only — extremely fast, easy to explain, easy to debug.

head: UX Methods > Open architectural decision — how inference runs in production > B. Materialized derived graph (currently the pragmatic favorite)
text: When making suggestions in this area, weigh both options honestly; don't quietly default to one. The "fast product value + strong foundation" framing tends to favor (B) once performance matters, but (A) is the more semantically pure demonstration.

head: UX Methods > Future direction — richer plan semantics
text: Longer-term, methods may be modeled as structured **plans** (steps, prerequisites, outputs) using **P-Plan** / **PROV Plan**, with executions and case studies mapped onto those plans. Not active work yet; flag it if proposed changes would constrain that direction.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Native over Docker on Linux x64
text: Linux x86_64 dev boxes should build and run every toolchain locally — RTL sims, synthesis, formal, PD (OpenLane/OpenROAD/magic/klayout/netgen), LLVM, Chipyard, AlphaChip CUDA, QEMU, Renode. Native is faster and far easier to troubleshoot than Docker: no bind-mount syscall overhead, real stack traces, normal `gdb`/`perf`, no daemon lifecycle to babysit. Keep Docker recipes around as a documented fallback for macOS, reproducibility audits, and pinned-image CI lanes only. If a script forces Docker on Linux even when a working native binary is on `$PATH`, that's a bug — fix the script.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > App and plugin primitives > Sub-agent invocation and loopback bridge
text: Coding sub-agents spawned by the orchestrator (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) live in sealed PTY workspaces with no direct access to the parent Milady runtime. They have two channels back to the parent:

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > App and plugin primitives > Sub-agent invocation and loopback bridge
text: **1. PTY stdout — `USE_SKILL` (write channel).** Emit `USE_SKILL <slug> <json>` lines on stdout; the orchestrator parses them and dispatches the matching skill in the parent runtime. This is how a sub-agent invokes `APP`, `PLUGIN`, or any other parent skill. Enabled by default; disable with `MILADY_ENABLE_CHILD_SKILL_CALLBACK=0`.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > App and plugin primitives > Sub-agent invocation and loopback bridge
text: **2. Loopback HTTP bridge (read channel).** Three endpoints on `127.0.0.1:31337` (or whatever `MILADY_API_PORT` resolves to). Loopback-only, agent-authed via the `:sessionId` path segment (must match an active task in the orchestrator's `tasks` map; unknown sessions 404, completed/stopped sessions 410):

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > App and plugin primitives > Sub-agent invocation and loopback bridge
text: - `GET /api/coding-agents/:sessionId/parent-context` — parent character, world/room context, the human user's identity. Use this to resolve pronouns the task brief left unresolved.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > App and plugin primitives > Sub-agent invocation and loopback bridge
text: - `GET /api/coding-agents/:sessionId/memory?q=<query>&limit=<N>` — query the parent agent's memory.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > App and plugin primitives > Sub-agent invocation and loopback bridge
text: - `GET /api/coding-agents/:sessionId/active-workspaces` — list the parent's currently-active workspaces.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: These govern every change. If existing code conflicts, fix the code.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 1. **Dependencies point inward only.** Presentation → Application → Domain → Infrastructure. Never import from an outer layer.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 2. **Computation lives in domain code, not presentation.** Derived values are computed in services / actions / use cases and returned as named fields. Clients format DTO fields for display; they do not aggregate, compute, or branch on raw data.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 3. **API routes are auth + dispatch.** Route handlers validate input, resolve the caller, and dispatch to a service / action. No business logic, no transformations, no calculations in route bodies.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 4. **No runtime type-tag branching where separate flows belong.** Distinct content kinds (apps, plugins, providers, actions) get separate handlers, not `if (kind === ...)` chains.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 5. **CQRS.** Readers read and return domain objects. Writers return `void` or an ID. Mappers handle DB↔domain translation.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 6. **Single source of truth for validation.** Route-layer schemas validate and transform input. Services / actions trust pre-validated input and perform presence/invariant checks only. No duplicate inline regex.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 7. **DTO fields are required by default.** Optional only when genuinely nullable. No `as` casts to skip missing fields. No `?? 0` to hide broken pipelines. If TypeScript says a field is missing, fix the pipeline.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 8. **Logger only, never console.** Server logging uses the structured logger only (`Logger.info/warn/error/debug`). Prefix `[ClassName]`. Include structured context on errors.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Architecture rules (non-negotiable)
text: 9. **Every action and endpoint needs a real caller.** Every POST/PUT/DELETE has a UI invocation path. Every GET has a consuming component/hook. Every action has a planner trigger or programmatic caller. Anything else is dead code.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Quality bar
text: What good changes look like: fewer codepaths, fewer special cases, fewer fallback branches, stronger types, cleaner layer boundaries, easier traceability from input → use case → DTO → UI, no dead abstractions, no defensive code that obscures failures.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Quality bar
text: Remove on sight: unused code, near-duplicate types, legacy / migration leftovers, AI slop and fake TODO implementations, comments describing churn, "temporary" fallbacks that became permanent, broad `try/catch` that just swallows or replaces errors with defaults, `any` / `unknown` / unsafe casts used to avoid thinking.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Quality bar
text: Constraints: do not preserve bad patterns "for compat" without a documented, verified live caller. Do not add abstractions unless they reduce total complexity. Do not DRY code that should remain separate because the domains differ. Do not centralize unlike concepts. Do not hide uncertainty with fallback values. Do not keep both old and new paths unless a live migration explicitly requires it.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Git workflow
text: **Motto: move fast, but never lose work to dangling branches or stashes.**

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Git workflow
text: - **Never `git stash`.** Commit instead — WIP commits are fine and can be amended or squashed later.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Git workflow
text: - **Always commit to the current branch in the current worktree.** Do not `git checkout`/`git switch` to another branch as part of "cleanup." If a task seems to need a different branch, ask first.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Git workflow
text: - **Prefer many small commits over uncommitted changes.** Push proactively when work is meaningful.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Git workflow
text: - **Never `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, force-push to main/master, or amend a published commit** unless explicitly asked. After a hook failure, fix the issue and create a NEW commit (`--amend` modifies the wrong commit).

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Git workflow
text: - **Never blanket-discard uncommitted edits as "dev-env churn."** `git checkout -- <file>` on uncommitted edits is destructive — confirm per-file, especially for binaries.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Git workflow
text: - Stage by name. Avoid `git add -A` / `git add .`.

head: Milady — Project Codex Guidance > Git workflow
text: The principle: every change ends up as a commit on the current branch in the current worktree, and ideally pushed.

head: Agents Guidelines
text: Behavioral guidelines for autonomous and semi-autonomous task execution. Use when working on iterative debugging, research, testing, build configuration, and multi-step problem-solving in Firmium — across the desktop stack (native iced/Rust, targeting Linux and Windows) and Android stack (Kotlin/Jetpack Compose).

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: Don't speculate. Don't hide uncertainty. Use tools to ground claims.

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: Before proposing solution:

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: - Current state (crate versions, Gradle/Kotlin dependency versions, iced/cpal/symphonia/Compose API behavior): check it (`Cargo.toml`, `android/app/build.gradle*`, docs).

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: - Problem others have hit (iced/wgpu render errors, cpal/symphonia panics, keyring issues on Linux/Windows, Media3/ExoPlayer or Compose issues on Android): search for existing solutions.

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: - Uncertain about fact: verify, don't guess.

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: Can't verify (tool fails, no results):

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: - Say so explicitly. Don't pretend certainty.

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: - Propose what you'd check if you could.

head: Agents Guidelines > 1. Search & Verify First
text: - Ask user to run diagnostic or provide context (e.g. `cargo run` console output, `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` trace).

head: Agents Guidelines > 2. Tool Chains Over Single Actions
text: Connect tools into complete diagnostic or workflow.

head: Agents Guidelines > 2. Tool Chains Over Single Actions
text: Don't stop at one search result. Chain:

head: Agents Guidelines > 2. Tool Chains Over Single Actions
text: - Web search for problem → fetch full articles → extract actionable steps

head: Agents Guidelines > 2. Tool Chains Over Single Actions
text: - Run command to check state → search for why it's wrong → propose fix

head: Agents Guidelines > 2. Tool Chains Over Single Actions
text: - Apply fix → run/build → verify behavior in dev window

head: Agents Guidelines > 2. Tool Chains Over Single Actions
text:
State chain explicitly:
```
1. [Search for] → found: [result]
2. [Fetch details] → learned: [insight]
3. [Run diagnostic] → state is: [finding]
4. [Propose fix] → verify by: [check]
```

head: Agents Guidelines > 2. Tool Chains Over Single Actions
text: Prevents chasing dead ends, makes reasoning auditable.

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: Act without asking when path is clear. Pause when ambiguous.

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Run `cargo run`, `cargo check`, `cargo build`, `./gradlew assembleDebug`

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Search for error messages or known issues (iced, cpal, symphonia, reqwest, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Media3/ExoPlayer)

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Check config (`Cargo.toml`, `android/app/build.gradle*`)

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Diagnose system state (check audio devices, keyring availability, Android logcat)

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Propose fixes based on clear patterns (iced `Message`/`update` wiring, MD5 auth token format, Compose state hoisting, ViewModel wiring)

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Creating new files outside standard dirs (`src/`, `backend/`, `themes/`, `assets/`, `packaging/`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/fossisawesome/firmium/`)

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Modifying config files with broad impact (`Cargo.toml`, `android/app/build.gradle*`, `AndroidManifest.xml`)

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Deleting or overwriting anything

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Changing packaging/release config (`cargo build --release`, makepkg, NSIS, `PKGBUILD`, `firmium.spec`, Android Gradle assemble/release config)

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: - Interpreting vague requirements ("make it faster," "improve it")

head: Agents Guidelines > 3. Autonomous Decisions
text: Test: if user might reasonably disagree with choice, ask first.

head: Agents Guidelines > 4. Error Recovery
text: Retry intelligently. Escalate clearly when stuck.

head: Agents Guidelines > 4. Error Recovery
text: 1. Try once more with adjusted parameters (different search terms, different command flags).

head: Agents Guidelines > 4. Error Recovery
text:
2. Still blocked, explain:
   - What did you try?
   - What was error?
   - What would unblock you? (user input, documentation, environment context)

head: Agents Guidelines > 4. Error Recovery
text: 3. Don't retry same thing repeatedly.

head: Agents Guidelines > 4. Error Recovery
text: - Propose multiple interpretations, not best guess.

head: Agents Guidelines > 4. Error Recovery
text: - Ask which matches user's intent.

head: Agents Guidelines > 4. Error Recovery
text: - Continue once clarity exists.

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: Show work only when it matters. Stay quiet on routine actions.

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: Show tool invocations when:

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: - They failed or produced unexpected output

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: - Result directly answers question

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: - Chain of reasoning is non-obvious

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: - Running diagnostic checks that confirmed expected state

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: - Performing routine searches with straightforward answers

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: - Executing standard, predictable steps

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: - What you found (not raw output)

head: Agents Guidelines > 5. Communication During Execution
text: - What comes next (or what you're blocked on)

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: Define "done." Loop until verified.

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: For each task, state success criteria upfront:

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: - "Fix crossfade glitch" → verify: `crossfade_to()` transitions between sessions with no audio dropout, tested in dev window

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: - "Add new UI action / backend call" → verify: `Message` variant handled in `App::update`, backend fn called via `Task::perform`, result message updates `App` state and re-renders

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: - "Fix Subsonic auth issue" → verify: `generate_auth_params()` (desktop) / `AuthManager` (Android) produces correct MD5 token, login succeeds against real Navidrome instance

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: - "Fix Android playback issue" → verify: `AudioPlayer`/`NowPlayingService` plays/pauses/seeks correctly, foreground notification stays in sync, tested via `./gradlew installDebug` + `adb logcat`

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: 2. Run verification check

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: 3. Pass: done. Fail: diagnose and retry.

head: Agents Guidelines > 6. Goal Verification
text: Strong criteria = operate independently. Vague criteria = constant back-and-forth.

head: Agents Guidelines > 7. Keep Docs in Sync > Other doc files (README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, API.md, android/CLAUDE.md)
text: Beyond `firmium-docs`, this repo carries its own doc files. Each has a narrower trigger — check these on every change, not just feature work:

head: Agents Guidelines > 7. Keep Docs in Sync > Other doc files (README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, API.md, android/CLAUDE.md)
text: - **New/changed system dependency** (ALSA, libsecret, libxkbcommon, Vulkan/OpenGL driver, etc., or a new Rust crate that pulls one in): update `README.md` "System Dependencies" **and** `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Prerequisites" — they list the same deps independently and drift if only one is touched.

text: - **New/changed Subsonic/OpenSubsonic/Navidrome endpoint usage** (anything in `backend/commands/subsonic.rs` hitting a new `/rest/*` call, or a change in auth/params/caveats): update `API.md`.

head: Agents Guidelines > 7. Keep Docs in Sync > Other doc files (README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, API.md, android/CLAUDE.md)
text: - **User-facing feature or removal** (desktop or Android): `firmium/FEATURES.md` (per root CLAUDE.md) **and** add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md` under the in-progress/unreleased version heading.

head: Agents Guidelines > 7. Keep Docs in Sync > Other doc files (README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, API.md, android/CLAUDE.md)
text: - **Android architecture change** (new module, restructured state management, new native integration): update `android/CLAUDE.md`, not just the desktop `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`.

text: - **Contributor workflow change** (build steps, test commands, clippy/lint config, git hooks): update `CONTRIBUTING.md`. If the change also affects docs-site or marketing-site contributors, check `firmium-docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` / `firmium-site/README.md` too — they're separate files, not auto-synced.

The code in this repository is open-source research and evaluation work. Redis's official
managed path for production use is **[Redis Agent Memory in Redis Iris](https://redis.io/agent-memory/)**

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: Core entrypoints live in `bin/`: `auto_continue_watchd.py` manages watchers and `auto_continue_logwatch.py` tails Codex events. Tests live in `test/` with Python unit suites in `test_watchd_unit.py`, `test_logwatch_unit.py`, `test_real_codex_contract.py`, and `test_real_codex_integration.py`. `test/smoke.sh` and `test/test_rollout_e2e.sh` are the fast CLI and real-Codex integration wrappers. Architecture notes and the running engineering log live in `docs/`. Example prompt text lives in `examples/messages/`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Build, Test, and Development Commands
text: Run the watcher locally with `python3 bin/auto_continue_watchd.py status` or `python3 bin/auto_continue_watchd.py start %6 --message "continue"`. Use `bash test/smoke.sh` for fast syntax and CLI checks. Use `python3 -m unittest test.test_watchd_unit test.test_logwatch_unit` for isolated manager and watcher logic. Use `bash test/test_rollout_e2e.sh` only when `tmux`, `codex`, and valid credentials are available; it launches real-Codex tests on a private tmux socket so it does not touch the existing server.

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: Follow existing Python and shell style: 4-space indentation in Python, `set -euo pipefail` in shell, and small stdlib-first helpers over new dependencies. Prefer snake_case for Python functions, variables, and test names. Keep CLI output short and operator-focused. Preserve the current file naming pattern: `auto_continue_*.py` for runtime code and `test_*.py` or `test_*.sh` for tests.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: Prefer test-driven changes. Add or extend a unit or regression test before fixing behavior, especially for pane resolution, thread detection, completion-source health, and thread-keyed state handling. Put pure logic coverage in `test/test_watchd_unit.py` and `test/test_logwatch_unit.py` using `unittest` and `unittest.mock`. Reserve the real-Codex harness for contract and integration behavior. Name tests after the behavior under test, for example `test_resolve_thread_id_fails_when_unknown`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: Match the existing history: short, imperative, capitalized commit subjects such as `Fix stop not killing paused watchers` or `Replace all-commands with wildcard targets`. Commit regularly, but do not create branches or worktrees unless explicitly approved. PRs should describe the operator-facing change, note tmux/Codex prerequisites, list commands run, and include terminal output or screenshots only when they clarify a UI or status-table change.

head: Repository Guidelines > Operational Notes
text: Keep `docs/ENGINEERING_LOG.md` updated with realizations, surprises, and design decisions. Runtime state is stored under `~/.codex/`; avoid assumptions that depend on the current working directory. When working with tmux, do not start a fresh server with bare `tmux` or `tmux new-session`; target the existing server with explicit subcommands instead.

head: 相册浏览器 PWA
text:
纯本地处理的相册浏览器。从原生 JS（~17000 行）重构为 Vue3 + Vite + Pinia。
**纯本地文件处理、不联网**（File System Access API，仅 Chrome/Edge/Opera）。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 技术栈
text: - **Vue 3**（`<script setup>`，纯 JS，无 TypeScript）

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 技术栈
text: - **Vite 5** + 双 build：`vite.config.js`（单 HTML）/ `vite.config.pwa.js`（PWA）

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 技术栈
text: - **Pinia**（setup store 风格）

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 技术栈
text: - **资源全内化**（零 CDN）：`@fortawesome/fontawesome-free` / `spark-md5` / `exifr` 均 npm 装 + ES import

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 技术栈
text: - **GalleryDB**（自建 IndexedDB，五 store，无第三方 KV 依赖）：`thumbnails`/`file-meta`/`user-data` 按 md5 三分类 + `roots`(多根句柄)/`scans`(扫描快照) 按 rootId KV。见 [db.js](src/services/db.js)

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 技术栈
text: - **@tanstack/vue-virtual**：Gallery 按行虚拟化（万图不卡，整页滚动 + 实测行高）

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 技术栈
text: - **质量基建**：`@antfu/eslint-config`（ESLint flat config）+ Vitest + `@vue/test-utils` + jsdom

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text:
1. **model 层纯数据 + 模块函数、副作用归 service**（`models/` 不 import Pinia/Vue、不反向依赖 store）：
   - `SmartFile`/`SmartFolder` 是**纯数据类**（字段 + 派生 getter，无实例方法）；所有行为是**同文件模块级函数**：`scanFolder` / `enrichFolder` / `folderToRecord` / `foldersFromRecordMap` / `createFolder` / `validateFolder` / `ensureBlobUrl` / `renameFile` / `moveFile` / `disposeFile` 等。`scanFolder(folder,{trust})` 纯函数——不改入参、不碰 store、不 dispose，返回增删结果集。模板用的派生 getter 保留——Vue 响应式追踪属性访问，**勿函数化**。
   - **副作用集中 service 层**：`integrateScanResult(folder,result,fs)`（写回**代理** folder + 注册/删 foldersData + `disposeFile` removedFiles + `markFolderDirty` 标脏）、`registerFolderTree`、`resetFoldersData`、`registerAndIntegrate`（P0-2：收口"set 进 Map→get 取代理→integrate"，新建 folder 必走）。⚠️ **写回必须是「代理」**（从 store 取或 `foldersData.get(path)`）；`createFolder` 返回的原始对象直接写回不触发响应式（见下方 reactive 陷阱）。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: 2. **service 层操作 store**：`services/` 内部 `useFsStore()` / `useToastStore()` 等直接调（在函数体内，不在模块顶层）。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: 3. **资源走 fileResource 池**（[fileResource.js](src/services/fileResource.js)）：blobUrl/File 集中管理（`acquire`/`destroy`/`peek`，in-flight 去重+cancel）。SmartFile 是其门面。**不要直接 `URL.createObjectURL`/`revokeObjectURL`**；size/mtime 单源在 `SmartFile._meta`（响应式），不进池。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: 4. **持久化走 schedulePersist(per-folder,治写放大)**:改树(增删/改名/移动/md5/duration)由 `integrateScanResult`(`markFolderDirty`)或 `afterFolderMutation(folder)` 标**该文件夹**脏 → `fs.dirtyFolders`(Set<rootId::path>) + `schedulePersist()`(1s debounce)。`persistIfDirty` 只遍历 dirty 集合、**每夹写一条 record**(`saveFolderRecord(rootId,folder)`→`scans`,非递归),`fileCount` 变才写 `roots`。**不要直接 `saveFolderRecord`/`folderToRecord`**。切根前 `flushPendingPersist` 落盘旧根(reload 用 `cancelPendingPersist` 重扫);重建走 `foldersFromRecordMap`(`loadScan` 前缀拉全 record→Map,秒切)。`visibilitychange:hidden` 触发 `flushPendingPersist` 兜底(P0-3)。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: 5. **CSS 全局复用**：`src/styles/` 的全局 CSS（`main.js` 全局 import）。组件**不重写这些 CSS**，模板直接用其 class（如 `.photo-card` / `.gallery-row` / `.tree-node` / `.modal-audio-player`）。组件 scoped 样式只补 CSS 里没有的。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: 6. **核心算法稳定**：scan 纯列表差集 + 信任名字集合短路、enrich 并发 getFile、GPS/ID3/.trash、calculateMD5（前 2MB 内容寻址缓存键——跨文件夹同图共享缩略图、md5 随快照持久化→秒切零重算；**chunkSize 锁死不动**）。**数据五分收口 GalleryDB，不再用 idb-keyval**：按 md5 的 `thumbnails`(blob LRU)/`file-meta`(duration/宽高/bitrate/capturedAt/gps/exifChecked)/`user-data`(favorites+notes 聚合) + 按 rootId 的 `roots`(多根句柄)/`scans`(per-folder record)，均懒加载、经 `db.js` kv 接口读写。duration 作 `SmartFile._meta` 运行时缓存，不随快照持久化。**EXIF 拍摄时间/GPS** 走 file-meta(md5 索引)：`loadCardMetadata` 图片懒抽一次(`exifChecked` 哨兵防反复、存量首次视窗自动回填),属性面板打开重抽**变了才更新**。改动配测试。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: 7. **跨组件状态进 Pinia store；组件私有状态用 `ref`/`reactive`**。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: 8. **主题切换**：`useThemeStore.applyTheme` 用 `document.documentElement.style.setProperty` 注入 CSS 变量（切主题先清残留再设新值，见 [theme.js](src/stores/theme.js)）。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: 9. **Web Worker 统一用 `?worker&inline` 导入**：`import W from './x.worker.js?worker&inline'` + `new W()` → Vite 打包并内联进单 HTML，真·自包含。⚠️ 勿用 `new Worker(new URL(...))`（外置 .js 破坏单 HTML），更**勿把 URL 提成变量**——Vite 靠 `new Worker(new URL())` 的 AST 形态识别 worker，提变量就不识别 → 退化成普通 asset 被 singlefile 内联成 data URL，**worker 内相对 import 不解析 → 加载即死、缩略图永远转圈**。现役:`thumbnail-worker.js`(pool)/`md5.worker.js`。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: > import 风格：相对 import 省略 `.js` 扩展名（Vite 默认解析，`.vue` 同样省略）。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: > 并发：getFile 批处理 / 后台目录遍历用 `runConcurrent`（[concurrency.js](src/utils/concurrency.js)，并发上限 + 错误隔离）；后台遍历带 `makeCancelToken`，切根时 bump token 退出在途任务。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 关键约定（请遵守）
text: > ⚠️ **Vue3 reactive 陷阱**：后台异步任务改 store 对象时**必须从 store 取代理**（`fs.rootFolder` / `foldersData.get(path)`），不要用 `createFolder` / `initProject` 返回的原始对象——改原始对象不触发响应式（子目录停在半透明不更新）。新建 folder 一律走 `registerAndIntegrate`（set 进 reactive Map 取代理再 integrate，P0-2 收口）；`scanAndPersist`/`flushPendingPersist` 内部已统一 `useFsStore().rootFolder` 取代理。详见 [架构重构 round1 spec](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-架构重构-资源层分离与纯model-design.md) + [round4 model 函数化](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-架构重构-round4-第一性原理审查与model函数化.md)。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 双 build
text: - **单 HTML**（`vite-plugin-singlefile`）：所有 JS/CSS/字体 base64 内联进单个 `dist/index.html`，可 `file://` 双击离线运行。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 双 build
text: - **PWA**（`vite-plugin-pwa`）：独立外链 SW + manifest（无法内联进单 HTML，故两套 config）。`workbox.globPatterns` 含 `woff2`（字体进预缓存）。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 双 build
text: 两套 build 共用 `dist/`，验证时注意先清。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 多文件夹（秒切换 + 按需校验）
text: 打开过的根文件夹记录在 IDB，可在 Sidebar 顶部 RootSwitcher 切换 / 移除 / 打开新。切换用 `scanCache` 缓存的扫描快照（`foldersFromRecordMap` 秒重建，零 IO）显示；后台 `rootEagerScan` 只扫 root 一层（顶层增删即时），深层 `handleFolderClick` 按需 trust 校验（名字集合一致零 IO）；变更（`dirtyFolders`）才 `schedulePersist` 落盘，切根前 `flushPendingPersist` 保旧根。运行时仍单根（一次一个 currentRoot）。详见 [多文件夹设计](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-多文件夹管理-design.md) + [round2 扫描优化](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-架构重构-round2-精修与扫描优化.md)。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 降级只读模式（非 Chromium 浏览器）
text: 不支持 File System Access API 的浏览器（Safari/Firefox，`isFileSystemAccessSupported()` 假）走降级只读：入口分流 `openDirectory()`（[folderActions.js](src/services/folderActions.js)）→ `<input webkitdirectory>` 一次选目录 → [webkitDirectory.js](src/services/webkitDirectory.js) 用 `File.webkitRelativePath` 纯内存重建整棵树（零 IO）。**能力退化为只读**：写回类（重命名/移动/删除/回收站/刷新落盘/多根切换）全部禁用置灰；缩略图/EXIF/收藏/备注仍按 md5 内容寻址复用。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 降级只读模式（非 Chromium 浏览器）
text: - **标志**：`isDegradedFSA()`（[browser.js](src/utils/browser.js) 模块级单例，`_setDegraded` 由降级入口设）。UI 置灰、`history.executeOperation` 总闸、`validateFolder` 短路都读它。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 降级只读模式（非 Chromium 浏览器）
text: - **读 File 统一入口**：`getFile(file)`（[SmartFile.js](src/models/SmartFile.js)）= `peek(file)?.file ?? file._file ?? file.handle.getFile()`，全库收敛（降级 SmartFile 直接持 `_file`）。fileResource 池仍以 SmartFile 为 key。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 降级只读模式（非 Chromium 浏览器）
text: - **差集复用**：`scanFolder` 提取公共 `diffEntries`（[SmartFolder.js](src/models/SmartFolder.js)），`scanDegradedFolder` 以 FileList 前缀过滤复用，核心算法不动。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 降级只读模式（非 Chromium 浏览器）
text: - **目录指纹秒开**：`computeDirectoryFingerprint`（spark-md5 哈希 `path|size|lastModified`）→ 存「指纹→md5快照」到 `scans`(key `degraded:<fp>`)；重选同目录命中 → 建树预填 md5 免重算；`loadCardMetadata` 降级增量收集落快照。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 降级只读模式（非 Chromium 浏览器）
text: - **零落盘天然成立**：降级不写 roots/handleStore → `currentRootId` 恒 null → `markFolderDirty` 短路（[persistence.js](src/services/persistence.js)）→ `dirtyFolders` 恒空。**不改 persistence.js**。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 降级只读模式（非 Chromium 浏览器）
text: - 降级不持久化多根（每次会话重选单目录）；刷新 = 重选目录；启动不恢复历史根（[App.vue](src/App.vue) `tryRestoreFolder` 短路）。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 重排模式（拖拽排序 + 序号写回文件名）
text: 进入后强制名称排序作起点，卡片可拖拽重排（多列跨行落点），「应用」把当前顺序固化为数字前缀写回文件名（`BatchRenameOperation` 聚合重命名，走 history 可撤销）。降级只读下 `enter` 拦截。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 重排模式（拖拽排序 + 序号写回文件名）
text: - **状态在 [reorder.js](src/stores/reorder.js)**：`active/order/selected/direction/applying/dragging/applyProcessed/applyTotal`；`enter` 快照 sortField→强制 name，`cancel` 恢复，`apply` 构造条目→`history.executeOperation`→finally `cancel`。`direction` 进模式时按排序方向定，**无 UI 切换**（升降序按钮已删），只影响 `seqForIndex` 编号映射、不改视觉 order。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 重排模式（拖拽排序 + 序号写回文件名）
text: - **重排态 = 非虚拟化 `reorder-grid`**（全量渲染 + `TransitionGroup` FLIP 挤位）；普通态 = 虚拟化 `gallery-grid`。**`gallery-grid` 常驻 DOM**，重排时用 `.reorder-hidden`（display:none）隐藏而非卸载——保缩略图/布局热，退出即秒显无闪白；隐藏期间仍随窗口滚动预热可视区缩略图。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 重排模式（拖拽排序 + 序号写回文件名）
text:
- **虚拟化测量两道守卫**（退出重排正确性的关键）：
  - `measureElement` 行高 `h<=0` → 返回 `estimateRowHeight()`：退出过渡期行未排布会量到 0，若缓存「仅 gap」的 15px，`getTotalSize` 少算整行 → 页面高度不对、滚动到该行才回弹；
  - `measureContainer` 在 `clientWidth<=0`（隐藏态）跳过，防 estimate 退 0、track 高度骤缩。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 重排模式（拖拽排序 + 序号写回文件名）
text: - **卡片稳定 key**：`rkOf(f)` 用 WeakMap 给 file 引用分配稳定数字 key——rename 只改 `file.path`，若 key=`f.path` 会触发卡片进出 FLIP 动画（哗啦啦）。

head: 相册浏览器 PWA > 重排模式（拖拽排序 + 序号写回文件名）
text: - **拖拽**：HTML5 drag + `moveSelectedTo(insertAt)` 落定（selected 整体插到 rest）；`REORDER_SCROLL_ZONE`=150px rAF 边缘滚动，鼠标进工具栏（`toolbarRef`）暂停感应；工具栏可用左侧 grip 把手拖拽改位（`toolbarPos`，x 为 null 居中、拖后固定）。点空白清选中（排除工具栏）。设计文档见下文「文档」节。

---
name: pi
description: Pi coding agent home directory — extensions, skills, prompts, and runtime config
---

head: Overview
text: Personal Pi agent home directory, symlinked to `~/.pi/agent`. Contains local extensions, custom skills, prompt templates, and agent profiles. Each extension is a self-contained Node.js package in `extensions/` with its own `AGENTS.md` for detailed context.

head: Overview > Extensions
text: 22 local extensions in `extensions/`. Each has its own `AGENTS.md` with detailed architecture, entity models, and conventions — read those before modifying an extension.

head: Overview > Extensions
text: - **pi-webserver** — shared HTTP server with auth; other extensions mount on it

head: Overview > Extensions
text: - **pi-kysely** — shared database registry with table-level RBAC

head: Overview > Extensions
text: - **pi-myfinance** — personal finance (accounts, transactions, vendors, budgets, reports)

head: Overview > Extensions
text: - **pi-personal-crm** — contacts, companies, interactions

head: Overview > Extensions
text: - **pi-channels** — bidirectional messaging (Telegram, webhooks)

head: Overview > Extensions
text: - **pi-memory** — persistent long-term memory and daily logs

head: Overview > Extensions
text: - **pi-vault** — Obsidian vault integration

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Structure
text: - Default export: `export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) { ... }`

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Structure
text: - Import types from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (`ExtensionAPI`, `getAgentDir`, `SettingsManager`)

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Structure
text: - TypeScript with `strict: true`, target ES2022, module ESNext, `allowImportingTsExtensions`

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Structure
text: - Use `.ts` extensions in imports (e.g. `import { foo } from "./bar.ts"`)

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Structure
text: - Tool parameter schemas use `@sinclair/typebox` (`Type.Object`, `Type.String`, etc.)

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Structure
text: - Tool results return `{ content: [{ type: "text", text: "..." }], details: {} }`

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Lifecycle & Events
text: - Initialize DB and state in `pi.on("session_start", async (event, ctx) => { ... })`

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Lifecycle & Events
text: - Register tools with `pi.registerTool({ ... })`, commands with `pi.registerCommand(name, { ... })`

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Lifecycle & Events
text: - Communicate between extensions via `pi.events.emit()` / `pi.events.on()` — never import directly

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Lifecycle & Events
text: - Mount web UI via `pi.events.emit("web:mount", { name, prefix, handler })` and API via `"web:mount-api"`

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Lifecycle & Events
text: - Listen for `"web:ready"` to re-mount if pi-webserver starts after your extension

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Database
text: - SQLite via better-sqlite3 (sync) as default backend; optional Kysely via event bus

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Database
text: - DB files go in `db/` directory under agent home (e.g. `db/finance.db`)

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Database
text: - Table names prefixed by extension (e.g. `finance_accounts`, `crm_contacts`)

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Database
text: - Migrations tracked in a `<prefix>_migrations` table with version numbers

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Database
text: - Parameterized queries only — no string interpolation in SQL

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Database
text: - WAL mode enabled (`PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`)

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Code Style
text: - No `console.log` — use pi-logger or structured error returns

head: Overview > Extension Development Conventions > Code Style

head: Overview > ⚠️ A2A Inbound Requests: Respond Directly
text: When Pi receives an inbound A2A request (another agent calling `message/send`), the correct response is to **complete the turn and return a result**. The task result is stored automatically in the SQLite TaskStore and retrieved by the caller via `tasks/get` polling.

head: Overview > ⚠️ A2A Inbound Requests: Respond Directly
text: **Never call `a2a_send` back to the agent that sent you a task.** This creates a loop that the hub's cycle-detection guard will block. Use these tools instead:

head: Overview > ⚠️ A2A Inbound Requests: Respond Directly
text:
| Goal | Correct tool |
|------|--------------|
| Reply with an answer | Just complete the turn — the response is stored automatically |
| Ask the caller a question | `a2a_request_input` — pauses task, waits for follow-up |
| Contact a *different* agent | `a2a_send` — fine, as long as it's not the requester |

head: Overview > ⚠️ A2A Inbound Requests: Respond Directly
text: The pi-a2a extension emits a `⚠️ A2A anti-pattern` warning if it detects an `a2a_send` targeting the inbound caller. Heed the warning and abort the send.

head: AGENTS.md
text: Shared agent guidance for this repo. `CLAUDE.md` / `GEMINI.md` / `.cursor/rules/main.mdc` are one-line imports of this file — edit here only.

head: AGENTS.md
text: Hand-rolled WebGPU engine. Vanilla JS, Vite, no framework, no TypeScript (ambient decls in `types/ogpu.d.ts` for TS consumers). No tests, no typechecker. ESLint + Prettier, format-on-save.

head: AGENTS.md > Where things are
text: - `api-digest.md` — generated public-surface index (every exported class, its method signatures, barrel re-exports). Read it for any signature or constructor option instead of opening the file.

head: AGENTS.md > Where things are
text: - `module-graph.json` — generated import graph; `hubs` lists the highest-in-degree modules. Trace `edges` instead of grepping for importers.

head: AGENTS.md > Where things are
text: - Both regenerate with `npm run repomap`. A pre-commit hook runs `repomap:check` and blocks stale copies — if a commit is blocked, `git add api-digest.md module-graph.json` and recommit.

head: AGENTS.md > Where things are
text: This file is the _why_; api-digest is the _what_. Keep method lists out of here.

head: AGENTS.md > Where things are
text:
Each source directory has its own `CLAUDE.md` with that area's footguns, auto-loaded when you read files there:
`src/core/` (Renderer, Transform, Camera, Mesh, RenderPipeline, Geometry, ComputeShader, Texture, RenderTarget, PerDrawBuffer, `primitives/`, `skin/`, ShaderReload) · `src/math/` (`Float32Array`-subclass wrappers over `wgpu-matrix`) · `src/modules/` (Orbit, Raycast, GUI, Animation, GLTFLoader, CubeMap, VideoTexture, `pbr/`, `gsplat/`) · `src/utils/IBLUtils/`.
`src/utils/` is standalone helpers; `examples/` is runnable demos at the repo root.

head: AGENTS.md > Where things are
text: `examples/` covers shadows, skinning, PBR/IBL, render targets, compute particles, glTF. Anything overlapping those extends the existing path rather than starting a new one.

head: AGENTS.md > Two cross-cutting contracts
text: - **Pass the `gpu` object, never the raw `device`.** `Renderer.init` augments the canvas context with `.device`/`.presentationFormat`/`.renderer`; that object (`renderer.gpu`) is what every class takes and stores. It's async — `await renderer.ready` before any GPU work (it also bootstraps `window.ktx`).

head: AGENTS.md > Two cross-cutting contracts
text: - **Standard uniforms are written by name.** `Mesh.draw` matches `projectionMatrix`, `viewMatrix`, `modelMatrix`, `modelViewMatrix`, `objectMatrix`, `normalMatrix`, `cameraPosition`, `cameraQuaternion`, `resolution`, `time` against the shader's reflected `Uniforms` struct. A misnamed field is **silently skipped** — no error, stale value. Details in `src/core/CLAUDE.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Two cross-cutting contracts
text: `Renderer.render` takes an optional external `encoder` to chain passes into one submit, and `target` selects a `RenderTarget`'s attachments over the bound canvas swapchain.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding conventions
text: - **Labels are kebab-case.** Every `label:` string (WebGPU debug labels, GUI display text) is lowercase-hyphenated; interpolations preserved, e.g. `` `${this.label}-bone-buffer` ``.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding conventions
text: - **WGSL `let` vs `var`.** `let` for values that never change, `var` only where reassigned.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding conventions
text: - **WGSL short type aliases.** `vec3f` not `vec3<f32>`, `mat4x4f` not `mat4x4<f32>` (`h` suffix for f16). Texture/atomic/array/ptr keep their generic form.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding conventions
text: - **WGSL vertex entry parameter is named `in`** — `fn vs(in: Vertex) -> VertexOutput`, mirroring `fs`.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding conventions
text: - **Comments earn their place.** Only when they add a why, a gotcha, or a non-obvious invariant. No `ponytail:`/agent prefixes in committed comments — keep the content, strip the prefix.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding conventions
text: - **Use the lookup skills, don't answer from memory.** WebGPU platform questions → `webgpu-spec-lookup`. `webgpu-utils` library questions → `webgpu-utils-lookup`.

head: AGENTS.md > Shaders
text: WGSL lives next to its importer, loaded via `?raw`. Cross-example shaders live in `src/modules/pbr/`. Aliases work in `?raw` imports (`@modules/pbr/pbr.wgsl?raw`); keep same-directory imports relative.

head: AGENTS.md > Shaders
text: Conventions enforced by `webgpu-utils` reflection:

head: AGENTS.md > Shaders
text: - Render uniform block must be named `uniforms` (lowercase), typed as a struct. `RenderPipeline` reads `this.defs.uniforms.uniforms` directly.

head: AGENTS.md > Shaders
text: - Entry points: vertex `vs`, fragment `fs`, hardcoded in `RenderPipeline`. Compute entry points can be anything — each becomes a kernel keyed by its name.

head: AGENTS.md > Shaders
text: - Texture uniforms take a `t<Name>` prefix (`tMap`, `tNormal`, `tBrdf`). Samplers are not textures — descriptive names (`iblSampler`).

head: AGENTS.md > Shaders
text: `npm run validate:shaders` checks every `**/*.wgsl` with `naga`, no browser needed (single file: `node scripts/validate-shaders.mjs <file>`). Install with `brew install naga-cli` — **not** `brew install naga`, an unrelated Snake game that takes the same binary name.

head: AGENTS.md > Optional features are not guaranteed
text: `Renderer.initDevice` feature-detects its `wantedFeatures` wishlist and drops (with a warn) anything the adapter lacks, so the engine boots anywhere. Guard any path that needs one on `device.features.has(...)` — `TimingHelper` gates on `'timestamp-query'`, `ComputeShader` timing is opt-in via `timing: true`. Texture-compression families are platform-split (`astc`/`etc2` ≈ mobile/Apple, `bc` ≈ desktop).

head: AGENTS.md > Running examples
text: `src/main.js` handles two query strings — don't confuse them:

head: AGENTS.md > Running examples
text: - **`?example=<key>`** — user-facing gallery (sidebar + preview iframe); the iframe loads `./?src=<key>` internally. This is what you link to.

head: AGENTS.md > Running examples
text: - **`?src=<key>`** — boots that example standalone on the page's own canvas, no gallery chrome.

head: AGENTS.md > Running examples
text: Keys live in the `views` map, gallery rows in the `items` array inside `renderLanding()`. New example: class under `examples/<name>/`, import it in `src/main.js`, add both entries.

head: AGENTS.md > Assets and external deps
text: - `public/assets/` — KTX cubemaps, PBR textures, JSON rigs/animations. Plain `fetch('./assets/...')`.

head: AGENTS.md > Assets and external deps
text: - `public/libktx_read.js` + `.wasm` — Khronos KTX reader, loaded as a global `<script>` in `index.html`; `initDevice` stashes it on `window.ktx`, ready once `renderer.ready` resolves.

head: AGENTS.md > Assets and external deps
text: - `wgpu-matrix` — functions mutate the out param (last arg) and return it.

head: AGENTS.md > Assets and external deps
text: - `webgpu-utils` — reflection, buffer/attribute creation, primitive generators.

head: AGENTS.md > Assets and external deps
text: - `parse-exr` — EXR loading inside `@utils/IBLUtils`.

head: AGENTS.md > Assets and external deps
text: - `@utils/wgslOverrides` (`applyOverrideConstants`) — Safari lacks pipeline-overridable constants, so this bakes `override` decls into module-scope `const` literals before compile, resolving default expressions to numeric literals so webgpu-utils' parser doesn't choke.

head: AGENTS.md > Assets and external deps
text: Recurring trap across areas: destroying/recreating a `Texture` invalidates its views, so any bind group holding them is stale — rebuild against `pipeline.bindGroupLayout(i)`.

head: AGENTS.md > Assets and external deps
text: Loaders exist for images (`Texture` with `src`), KTX (`@modules/KTXTexture`), JSON (`@utils/JSONLoader`), glTF (`GLTFLoader.js`) and IBL cubemaps (`@utils/IBLUtils`) — check these before writing a new one.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text: A header-only C++20 implementation of the **OPTICS** density-based clustering algorithm (Ankerst et al., 1999). Given points in R^n it produces the cluster-ordering + reachability distances, from which clusters are extracted — without knowing the number of clusters a priori. Built for time-critical use on large clouds (e.g. 3-D color spaces at 1e6–1e7 points, 16-D perspective transforms at 1e5–1e6).

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text: The library has **no mandatory external dependencies**: only the vendored `nanoflann` (in `include/optics/`) plus the standard library. Boost is an *optional* alternative backend, off by default.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text: For project history and direction: `CHANGELOG.md` (release notes, current version 0.9.1) and `docs/ROADMAP-*.md` (planned work — e.g. the `chi_tree_to_points` helper is queued in `docs/ROADMAP-post-0.9.1.md`). `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` covers vendored-dep licensing; `CITATION.cff` is the citation metadata.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text: For algorithm research and future direction: `documentation/` holds papers + `references.md` for the planned **sOPTICS** (sDBSCAN/sOPTICS, random-projection OPTICS — GitHub issue #50). The 1.0.0 milestone tracks the bigger algorithm/benchmark work: sOPTICS (#50), HDBSCAN\* (#52), CPU-speed comparisons vs ELKI/dbscan/sDbscan (#53), an ARI/NMI/Rand quality harness (#54), and non-Euclidean metrics (#51). Original OPTICS/FOPTICS papers live in `background/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text: Before tagging 1.0.0, one large reproducible study (the **benchmark matrix**) picks the library's data-dependent defaults (backend by dimensionality, sOPTICS-vs-OPTICS, neighbor mode/backend, epsilon estimator) and becomes the citable performance reference. Its design — axes, the tiered/fractional reduction, which existing harnesses feed it, comparability rules — is in `docs/ROADMAP-1.0.0-benchmark-matrix.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow
text: The pipeline lives under `include/optics/`. Public entry point is `optics.hpp`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow
text: 1. **`compute_reachability_dists<T, Dim, Backend = NanoflannBackend<T,Dim>>(points, min_pts, epsilon = -1, mode = OnDemand, n_threads = 0, core_dist = Scan)`** → `std::vector<reachability_dist>` (the cluster-ordering; `reach_dist == -1` means UNDEFINED/unreached). `T` is `float`/`double`, points are `std::vector<std::array<T,Dim>>`. `epsilon <= 0` auto-estimates via the **k-distance-knee** estimator (`epsilon_estimation_knee`, the default since it tracks the within-cluster scale; the uniform-density `epsilon_estimation` over-estimates on clustered data — issue #57). It falls back to the uniform estimate for backends without `KnnCoreDist`, or on degenerate (zero-variance) inputs. `mode` defaults to **OnDemand** (see below); `core_dist = Knn` (a `CoreDistMode`) is an equivalent, faster-on-dense core-distance path requiring a backend that models `KnnCoreDist`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow
text:
2. **Extraction:**
   - Threshold cut: `get_cluster_indices(reach_dists, threshold)` → flat clusters (noise → singletons; a deliberate simplification of the paper's ExtractDBSCAN, which also used core-distance).
   - Xi / steep-area: `get_chi_clusters_flat(...)` → flat `(begin,end)` ranges; `get_chi_clusters(...)` builds the nested `cluster_tree` (`tree.hpp`). This is paper Defs 9–11 / Fig. 19 and the most subtle code; its behavior is pinned by the `chi_test_*` cases.
   - One-call convenience wrappers, both `(points, min_pts, [param])`: `cluster_threshold(points, min_pts, threshold = auto)` (compute + flat cut; the paper's ExtractDBSCAN — `threshold < 0` ⇒ `detail::default_threshold`, a high reachability percentile; `cluster_dbscan` is a `[[deprecated]]` alias), `extract_xi(points, min_pts, chi = 0.05)` (compute + Xi, flattened — use `get_chi_clusters` for the tree), and `convert_cloud<Out>(in)` to lift an integer/byte cloud (e.g. `uint8` color data) to `float`/`double` before clustering.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow
text: 3. **Inspection (optional, no rendering in C++):** `io.hpp` exports dimension-agnostic CSV (`export_points_csv` with `cluster_labels`, `export_reachability_csv`); `tools/visualize.py` renders 2D/3D/PCA scatter + reachability plots with matplotlib. The `tools/` dir has its own `README.md` and further Python helpers (synthetic `datasets.py`, scikit-learn cross-checks `validate_sklearn.py`, algorithm-comparison figures `compare_algorithms.py`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > HDBSCAN\* (a separate clusterer, not an OPTICS extractor) — `hdbscan.hpp`, #52
text: `optics::hdbscan(points, min_cluster_size, min_samples = 0, method = EOM, allow_single_cluster = false, n_threads = 0)` → `HdbscanResult{ labels (-1 = noise), probabilities, n_clusters }`. Parameter-light: no `epsilon`/threshold. Pipeline (all in `hdbscan.hpp`, `detail::`): core distances via the backend's `knn_core_dist` (same quantity OPTICS uses) → **symmetric mutual-reachability** MST `max(core(a),core(b),d(a,b))` (note: OPTICS reachability is *directed*) via **dense Prim** (`mutual_reachability_mst`) → single-linkage hierarchy (`mst_to_linkage`, union-find) → `condense_tree` by `min_cluster_size` → `compute_stabilities` → `select_eom` (Excess of Mass, default) or `select_leaf`. The condense/stability/label stages are **MST- and metric-agnostic by design**, so a faster/approximate MST (Borůvka, or the sOPTICS/CEOs graph → "sHDBSCAN") can reuse them — a queued #52 follow-up. **Current exact MST is dense Prim: `O(n²)` time / `O(n)` memory** (fine for small/medium `n`; not yet the 1e5+ targets). `min_samples` is self-inclusive (matches `sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN`; scikit-learn-contrib/hdbscan excludes self ⇒ +1 there). Reimplemented from the papers; pinned by the `hdbscan:` test cases.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > HDBSCAN\* (a separate clusterer, not an OPTICS extractor) — `hdbscan.hpp`, #52
text: **`optics::shdbscan(...)` = sHDBSCAN**, the scalable approximate variant (#52 follow-up): same `detail::extract_from_mst` tail (steps 4–6 are MST-agnostic — that's the whole point), but the MST comes from the **sOPTICS CEOs neighbor graph** (`detail::approx_mutual_reachability_mst`: Kruskal over the sparse symmetric candidate edges, disconnected components joined above all real edges) with approximate core distances (`detail::approx_core_distances`). Cosine metric (unit-sphere normalize; `L2`/`L1` via the same random-Fourier embedding as sOPTICS), deterministic in `seed`. It is to `hdbscan()` what sOPTICS is to OPTICS — validate by Rand/NMI agreement, not bit-identical labels (measured Rand ≈ 1.0 vs exact `hdbscan()` on angular blobs). A dual-tree-Borůvka *exact* fast MST is still future work; both feed the same extractor. Pinned by the `shdbscan:` cases.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > HDBSCAN\* (a separate clusterer, not an OPTICS extractor) — `hdbscan.hpp`, #52
text: **Weighted / dedup (#52 × #46):** both `hdbscan()` and `shdbscan()` take a trailing `dedup = true` (collapse bit-identical points → unique weighted points via `deduplicate`, cluster, expand labels back to originals — shrinks the O(n²) MST to the unique count) and explicit `weights` (sklearn `sample_weight`; non-empty bypasses dedup). Weights thread through core distance (`knn_core_dist_weighted` exact / cumulative-weight k-th approximate), linkage/condense sizes (so `min_cluster_size` is in *weight* units via `LinkageUnionFind`'s weighted leaf sizes + `point_weight` fall-outs), and stability (already weighted via `child_size`). All-ones ≡ unweighted bit-for-bit; **weighted-on-dedup == unweighted-on-full exactly (Rand 1.0)** for exact `hdbscan()`, ≈0.91 for `shdbscan()`. Needs `KnnCoreDistWeighted` (NanoflannBackend models it). Pinned by the `*weighted*` cases.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > Neighbor-search backend seam
text: Backends satisfy the `NeighborSearch` C++20 concept (`backend.hpp`): they ingest the cloud once at construction and answer `radius_search(point, r, out)` with **no per-query point conversion**.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > Neighbor-search backend seam
text: - `NanoflannBackend<T,Dim,ApproxEpsPermille=0>` (default): a zero-copy adaptor over the user's `std::vector<std::array<T,Dim>>`. **nanoflann's L2 metric works in squared distance** — the backend squares the radius internally. Also exposes `knn_core_dist` (for `CoreDistMode::Knn`). A non-zero `ApproxEpsPermille` enables nanoflann's eps-approximate search; `ApproxNanoflannBackend<T,Dim,Permille=100>` is the alias.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > Neighbor-search backend seam
text: - `BoostRTreeBackend` (`boost_backend.hpp`, behind `OPTICS_ENABLE_BOOST_RTREE`): box pre-filter + exact Euclidean check.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > Neighbor-search backend seam
text:
- `HnswBackend<T,Dim>` (`hnsw_backend.hpp`, behind `OPTICS_ENABLE_HNSW`; vendored hnswlib in `include/optics/hnswlib/`, #47): **approximate** HNSW graph index. Models `NeighborSearch` (radius via hnswlib's **native epsilon range search** — a single graph traversal, `EpsilonSearchStopCondition`) and `KnnCoreDist`. Stores coordinates as float; recall is tunable via `M` / `ef_construction` (defaults 16 / 200). **Measured finding (`optics_hnsw_probe`, adaptive ~30-NN radius, n≈19k): HNSW query time is essentially dimension-independent (~55–80 ms across 16–128-D) while the exact KD-tree grows with D (34 → 82 → 224 ms), so they cross over at ~64-D — HNSW is ~2.8× faster by 128-D (recall ~0.92–0.99).** At the 16-D target the exact KD-tree is still ~2× faster, so nanoflann remains the default; HNSW is the right backend for the genuinely high-D (≥64-D) regime (where the static-`Dim` KD-tree even overflows the stack to build at 256-D). A one-time index build (~2 s at this n) is HNSW's fixed cost.
Swapping backends is a single template argument; call sites don't reshape data. The three internal backends are pinned interchangeable by `boost_backend_tests` (Nanoflann/Boost bit-identical ordering) and the approx recall test.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > Neighbor-search backend seam
text: Two **optional capabilities** are detected with `if constexpr` (a backend opts in by providing the method): `KnnCoreDist` (`knn_core_dist`, enables `CoreDistMode::Knn`) and `RadiusSearchWithDists` (`radius_search_with_dists`, #55) — returns each neighbor's squared distance alongside its index so the ordering can reuse them in the core-dist scan and the relaxation instead of recomputing. `RadiusSearchWithDists` is gated to `double` (where the backend's squared distance is bit-identical to `detail::square_dist`, so orderings stay byte-identical); `NanoflannBackend` models both.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > Neighbor acquisition (mode = OnDemand by default, Precompute opt-in)
text: `NeighborMode::OnDemand` (**the default since v0.9.1**) queries one neighborhood at a time during the ordering — **O(one neighborhood) memory**. `Precompute` queries every point's neighbors up front in parallel via `detail/thread_pool.hpp`'s `parallel_for` (`n_threads = 0` ⇒ hardware concurrency) and caches them — **O(n × avg_neighbors) memory**. Both produce identical orderings (pinned by `neighbor_mode_tests`). The OPTICS ordering loop itself is always sequential. Which mode is faster depends on neighborhood density: **Precompute wins on sparse/low-density clouds** (small cache, parallel queries — e.g. ~10× in 16-D); **OnDemand wins on dense clouds** (e.g. color images — it avoids materializing/re-reading a multi-GB cache, ~30% faster at 100k px, and never OOMs). See `perf/README.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > sOPTICS: approximate ordering via random projections (the provider seam)
text: `compute_soptics_reachability_dists(points, min_pts, epsilon = -1, n_projections = 1024, k = 0, m = 0, seed = 42, n_threads = 0)` is a scalable, **approximate** OPTICS (sDBSCAN/sOPTICS, Xu & Pham 2024; issue #50, reimplemented from the paper in `documentation/`). It deliberately does **not** use the `NeighborSearch` backend seam: instead of a radius search it builds **CEOs random-projection neighborhoods** (`detail/random_projection.hpp` — project onto `n_projections` Gaussian vectors, take each point's top-`k` extreme vectors, gather the top-`m` extreme points of each, ε-filter, symmetrize) and feeds them — with core-distance = the `min_pts`-th nearest candidate — into the **shared ordering driver `detail::optics_order`**. (`ceos_neighbors` also optionally returns each candidate's squared distance via `out_sq`; sOPTICS reuses those in the core-dist scan + relaxation instead of recomputing — the #55 idea on the RP path, byte-identical for float *and* double since every distance comes from `detail::square_dist`.) That driver is the algorithm-agnostic loop (seed queue, relaxation, lazy deletion) factored out of `compute_reachability_dists`; both OPTICS and sOPTICS drive it through a neighbor-provider + core-dist-provider pair (template params, so the `KnnCoreDist` `if constexpr` stays zero-overhead and orderings remain byte-identical for OPTICS). The default metric is **cosine** (points are L2-normalized onto the unit sphere, where Euclidean distance is monotone in cosine distance). A `metric` argument (`Metric::L2` / `Metric::L1`, #51) instead embeds the points into **random Fourier features** (`detail/random_features.hpp`) whose cosine geometry approximates the Gaussian / Laplacian kernel, then runs the same cosine pipeline on the features — so the ordering tracks **Euclidean / Manhattan** distance on the *original* data (`kernel_scale <= 0` ⇒ a median-distance auto bandwidth; χ²/JS not yet, see #51). Output is randomized but **deterministic in `seed`** ⇒ validated by Rand/NMI agreement with exact OPTICS, not bit-identical orderings.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & data flow > sOPTICS: approximate ordering via random projections (the provider seam)
text: Supporting headers: `detail/math.hpp` (distance/`pi`/`in_range`, replacing the old Geometry dep), `testdata.hpp` (N-dim synthetic clouds, shared with the benchmark), `test/support/ppm_fixture.hpp` (P6 reader for hand-drawn 2-D fixtures), `Stopwatch.hpp` (benchmark timing).

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas
text: - **`epsilon` is a `double` parameter, deliberately not `T`** — making it `T` lets it participate in template deduction and clashes with `T` deduced from `points` (e.g. passing the literal `10`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas
text: - `T` must be `float`/`double` (`static_assert`); integer coordinate inputs must be converted first.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas
text: - The library throws (`std::invalid_argument`/`std::runtime_error`) instead of calling `std::exit`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas
text: - 16-D nearest-neighbor is genuinely expensive (curse of dimensionality), and there the *search* dominates — opt into `Precompute` + threads, and the `ApproxNanoflannBackend` actually helps (eps-pruning cuts tree traversal: ~2.4× at eps=1.0 with recall still ~1.0). In **low** dimensions the approximate backend does **not** help (recall stays ~1.0, nothing to prune) — see `perf/README.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas
text: - **Dense neighborhoods (e.g. flat-color images) are the perf trap.** With auto-`epsilon`, the average neighborhood grows ~linearly with n, so the ordering is ~**O(n²)** in time *and* (under Precompute) memory — at ~100k px the Precompute buffer is ~19 GB. The cost is in *processing* neighborhoods (`compute_core_dist` scan + relax, both O(|nbrs|)), **not** the search, so a faster/approximate backend can't fix it; the auto-eps now defaults to the knee estimator (smaller than the old uniform one, which helps), but on genuinely dense clouds also use `OnDemand` mode (the default), `CoreDistMode::Knn`, an even smaller explicit `epsilon`, or downsample. (`compute_core_dist` no longer copies the index list — it fills a reused `thread_local` of squared distances.) **#55** further trims this: on the `double` nanoflann path the ordering now *reuses* the squared distances the search already computed (the `RadiusSearchWithDists` capability) instead of recomputing them in the core-dist scan and the relaxation — ~30%/~23% off those two phases, ~12% off the loop on a dense 3-D cloud (`optics_reuse_probe`), orderings byte-identical. The search itself is still the floor.

head: CLAUDE.md > Gotchas
text: - Perf tooling lives under `test/Benchmark/`: `optics_perf` (nanobench regression), `optics_benchmark`/`optics_scale` (timing), `optics_backend_compare` (per-backend, paired with `tools/timing_compare.py`/`timing_images.py` for scikit-learn), `optics_approx_probe` (approx recall vs eps/dim), `optics_mode_compare` (Precompute vs OnDemand). All default to 4 threads via `bench::threads()` (override `OPTICS_BENCH_THREADS`).

text: - Do not run `pnpm dev`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm start`, `pnpm run deploy`, migrations, seeds, or data scripts unless the user explicitly asks.

head: Project Guide > Commands
text:

  action. Requests to fix a PR, update a PR, address review comments, check CI,

head: Project Guide > Commands
text: - Use the current git user as commit author; never add Codex/AI authorship or AI-themed branch names.

head: Project Guide > Domain Rules
text: - A Listing is a handheld compatibility report: game plus handheld device plus emulator.

head: Project Guide > Domain Rules
text: - A PC Listing is a PC compatibility report: game plus PC hardware plus emulator.

head: Project Guide > Domain Rules
text: - User-facing UI should say "Compatibility Report", "Handheld Report", "PC Report", or "PC Compatibility Report", not "listing".

head: Project Guide > Domain Rules
text: - Listings and PC Listings must stay behaviorally aligned for voting, comments, moderation, trust effects, notifications, and approval flows.

head: Project Guide > Domain Rules
text: - Shared cross-listing behavior belongs in utilities instead of duplicated implementations.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text:
- Feature folders should follow the project-structure guidance from Bulletproof React:
  https://github.com/alan2207/bulletproof-react/blob/master/docs/project-structure.md

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Within `src/features/*`, prefer scoped subdirectories such as `components`, `hooks`, `utils`, `server`, and `shared` instead of flat feature folders.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text:
- Feature-owned modules may colocate client, server, and shared code under
  `src/features/<domain>/<module>/`.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text:
- Use this feature module structure for new or actively-refactored domain code:
  - `shared/` contains Zod schemas, types, constants, and pure formatting helpers usable by client and server.
  - `server/` contains repositories, services, policies, mappers, and feature-owned tRPC routers.
  - `client/` contains hooks, reusable components, and workflow views. Add client API wrappers only when they remove real duplication or encode a stable UI contract.
  - `client/admin/` is allowed for admin-only workflows.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text:
- Import direction matters more than folder names:
  - `client/` may import from its feature `shared/` and app-wide client-safe utilities.
  - `server/` may import from its feature `shared/`, server utilities, and repositories.
  - `shared/` must not import from `client/`, `server/`, `src/app`, or server-only libraries.
  - `src/app/**` routes/pages should compose feature modules; feature modules should not import from `src/app/**`.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - tRPC routers are transport adapters. Feature-specific routers should live in the feature `server/` folder when that feature owns the full use case; `src/server/api/root.ts` should only compose them.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Legacy routers in `src/server/api/routers/` are thin orchestration layers. They handle auth context, schema-validated input, repository/service calls, and response formatting.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Do not put raw Prisma queries or business logic in routers.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Define Zod schemas in feature `shared/*.schemas.ts` for feature-owned code, or in `src/schemas/*` for legacy/shared code. Do not define inline schemas in router `.input(...)` calls.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Feature-owned tRPC procedures should declare `.output(...)` with Zod schemas. Compatibility transports that must keep legacy shapes should still have explicit legacy output schemas instead of returning raw Prisma payloads by convention.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - All database access belongs in repository classes. Feature-owned repositories may live in feature `server/` folders; legacy/shared repositories may remain under `src/server/repositories/`.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - New or actively-refactored feature-owned Prisma repositories should extend `PrismaRepository` or `PrismaWriteRepository` from `src/server/persistence/prisma.repository.ts` for Prisma client ownership and shared write handling. Do not extend the legacy `BaseRepository` unless the inherited behavior is deliberately required and documented.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Do not add generic CRUD methods to shared repository bases. Prisma already provides typed CRUD; feature repositories should expose domain/use-case persistence operations with named select contracts.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - For feature-owned Prisma repositories, prefer a `server/persistence/` subfolder for named `select` contracts, query builders, and Prisma error translation. Derive repository record types from Prisma `GetPayload` plus those named `select` contracts instead of hand-maintaining structural copies.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Services should depend on the concrete feature repository by default. Do not add service-owned `Pick<Repository, ...>` contracts only for tests.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Add repository interfaces only for real boundaries: multiple implementations, external provider adapters, lifecycle concerns that route composition cannot handle directly, or domain/application layers that intentionally must not depend on infrastructure.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Repositories should use project error helpers and consistent database operation handling.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Multi-step business logic, external API orchestration, and complex calculations belong in services under feature `server/` folders or legacy `src/server/services/`.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Use policy functions for reusable authorization/business access rules that must be shared across transports. Routers may still use broad auth procedures, but services should enforce feature-level capabilities when the use case can be called from multiple transports.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Use `AppError` and `ResourceError` helpers instead of raw `Error`, raw strings, or one-off `TRPCError` usage.

head: Project Guide > Architecture
text: - Use specialized procedures such as `protectedProcedure`, `adminProcedure`, and `permissionProcedure(...)` instead of ad hoc permission checks.

head: Project Guide > API Compatibility And Legacy Contracts
text:
- Before introducing any `legacy` select, repository method, route, endpoint,
  schema, type, mapper, compatibility branch, or response shape, audit known
  consumers first. For mobile/public API work, this includes
  `/Volumes/T9/Coding/personal/2026/Emulation/EmuReadyApp` when it is available,
  or a temporary clone of `Producdevity/EmuReadyApp` on the `master` branch when
  the local app checkout is unavailable or not production-synced.

head: Project Guide > API Compatibility And Legacy Contracts
text:
- Record which fields consumers actually read. Do not preserve fields only
  because they existed in an old Prisma payload, old inferred type, or old API
  response.

head: Project Guide > API Compatibility And Legacy Contracts
text:
- Decide compatibility case by case: remove unused old fields, migrate the
  consumer, keep one standardized endpoint with a small low-cost superset, or
  keep a separate legacy contract only when the audited consumer behavior truly
  requires it.

head: Project Guide > API Compatibility And Legacy Contracts
text:
- Legacy contracts must have an owner, a reason, and an expected removal path.
  Remove legacy code as soon as audited consumers do not need it.
