text: - **PTRACE_GETREGSET** (NT_PRSTATUS): Read tracee's register snapshot

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > sys_ptrace Operations
text: - **PTRACE_SETREGSET** (NT_PRSTATUS): Write tracee's registers (applied on resume)

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > Register Snapshot Protocol
text:
Cross-thread HVF register access may not be supported, so we use a
snapshot protocol: the tracee snapshots its own vCPU registers into
`ptrace_regs` before entering ptrace-stop, and applies any dirty
changes back to the vCPU on resume. This ensures all HVF register
access happens on the owning thread.

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > BRK + Ptrace-Stop Flow
text: 1. Guest executes BRK → shim forwards via HVC #10

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > BRK + Ptrace-Stop Flow
text: 2. If `current_thread->ptraced`: tracee calls `thread_ptrace_stop(SIGTRAP)`

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > BRK + Ptrace-Stop Flow
text: 3. Tracee snapshots regs, sets `ptrace_stopped=1`, broadcasts `ptrace_cond`

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > BRK + Ptrace-Stop Flow
text: 4. Tracer's wait4 returns with `WIFSTOPPED(status)` and `WSTOPSIG==SIGTRAP`

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > BRK + Ptrace-Stop Flow
text: 5. Tracer reads/writes regs via GETREGSET/SETREGSET

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > BRK + Ptrace-Stop Flow
text: 6. Tracer calls PTRACE_CONT → sets `ptrace_stopped=0`, signals `resume_cond`

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > BRK + Ptrace-Stop Flow
text: 7. Tracee applies dirty regs, resumes execution

head: hyper-linux > Ptrace and clone(CLONE_VM) for Rosetta JIT > wait4 Integration
text:
`sys_wait4()` first checks for ptraced/vm-clone children via
`thread_ptrace_wait()` before falling through to the process table
for regular fork children. This handles both ptrace-stopped and
vm-exited states.

head: CLAUDE.md
text:
Working instructions for Claude (and any other AI agent) in **oo-wp-plugin** ("onOffice for
WP-Websites") — the WordPress plugin that brings estates, addresses and contact forms from the
onOffice enterprise API into WordPress, and the data layer the four onOffice parent themes render
on top of.

head: CLAUDE.md
text:
**The detailed rules live in `documentation/`. They are not loaded automatically — open the file
that covers your task before you start.**

head: CLAUDE.md
text:
**Three things make this repo different from the four theme repos:** it owns **customer database
schema** (a bad migration is unrecoverable on live installations), it has a **real PHPUnit suite**
(so tests are a review gate, not advisory), and its production dependencies are
**namespace-prefixed by Strauss** (so an ordinary-looking `use DI\Container;` is a bug). Don't
assume anything from the theme repos' docs transfers here without checking.

| [architecture.md](documentation/architecture.md) | bootstrap, DI, the `*Environment` seam, layers, request flow, **Strauss prefixing**, templates as a public API |
| [coding-standards.md](documentation/coding-standards.md) | PHP/WordPress conventions, naming, comments, security & escaping, hardcoded values, translations, BFSG |
| [database-and-migrations.md](documentation/database-and-migrations.md) | **`DatabaseChanges` — how to add a migration and what must never be touched** |
| [testing.md](documentation/testing.md) | PHPUnit against the WP test suite, mocks, what must have a test |

head: CLAUDE.md > Documentation map
text:
**Rule of thumb:** the first table wins on *how to work*; the second table and `Readme.md` win on
*details of a process*. If they contradict each other, the long-form document is authoritative and
the working instruction needs fixing.

head: CLAUDE.md > How to work in this repository
text:
- **Answer in the language the developer writes in.** Code, identifiers, comments and documentation
  are English, and so are PR titles (Conventional Commits); pull request reviews are German.

head: CLAUDE.md > How to work in this repository
text:
- **Match the surrounding file.** This codebase is old enough to have drifted — don't modernize a
  file you are only touching in one place, and don't mix a reformat into a change.

head: CLAUDE.md > How to work in this repository
text:
- **Never touch an existing migration.** Renumbering or editing a `DatabaseChanges` case breaks live
  customer installations irreversibly — see
  [database-and-migrations.md](documentation/database-and-migrations.md).

head: CLAUDE.md > How to work in this repository
text:
- **Import the prefixed vendor namespace** (`onOffice\WPlugin\Vendor\…`). An unprefixed import does
  not necessarily throw — it silently binds to another plugin's copy. See
  [architecture.md](documentation/architecture.md#prefixed-dependencies-strauss).

head: CLAUDE.md > How to work in this repository
text:
- **Read before writing.** Most real bugs here come from what a diff doesn't show: the DI binding in
  `config/di-config.php`, the hook registration in `plugin.php`, the `*Environment` interface that
  also needs the new method, the customer template that still uses the variable.

head: CLAUDE.md > How to work in this repository
text:
- **Never guess about cross-repo impact** — say what couldn't be checked. See
  [project.md](documentation/project.md#when-you-need-another-repository).

head: CLAUDE.md > How to work in this repository
text:
- **Nothing may be pushed, released or deployed without being asked** — see
  [workflow.md](documentation/workflow.md#nothing-here-may-be-triggered-without-being-asked).

head: CLAUDE.md > How to work in this repository
text: - **Finish with QA:** `make test-docker` — the same suite `unit-tests.yml` runs.

head: CLAUDE.md > Do's and Don'ts
text:
- Put `$wpdb` access in a `RecordManager*`, API access behind `SDKWrapper`/an `APIClientAction`, and
  WordPress globals behind a `WP/` wrapper. Those seams are what makes this code testable.

head: CLAUDE.md > Do's and Don'ts
text:
- Register hooks in `plugin.php`, keep the callback bodies in controllers. Add a DI binding in
  `config/di-config.php` when you introduce an interface.

head: CLAUDE.md > Do's and Don'ts
text:
- Never read `$_GET`/`$_POST` directly (`RequestVariablesSanitizer`), never interpolate into SQL
  (`$wpdb->prepare()`), never output unescaped, never write without both a capability *and* a nonce
  check.

head: CLAUDE.md > Do's and Don'ts
text:
- Never edit generated files: `dist/`, `vendor/`, `vendor-prefixed/`, and everything under
  `languages/` except `onoffice-for-wp-websites-de_DE.po`. Never hand-edit a version number or the
  `readme.txt` changelog — semantic-release owns them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Do's and Don'ts
text:
- Don't rename or drop a public class, method or template variable (`$pEstates`, `$pForm`,
  `$pAddressList`, …) without calling it out as breaking: the four themes and every customer's own
  template copy depend on them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Do's and Don'ts
text:
- Don't edit `SDK/` to fix a plugin problem — it mirrors `onOfficeGmbH/sdk`, with one deliberate
  divergence.

head: CLAUDE.md > Do's and Don'ts
text:
- Don't hardcode user-facing text, API URLs, table names, option names or capabilities — use the
  existing constants or add one.

head: CLAUDE.md > Do's and Don'ts
text:
- Keep important code readable even if it costs lines, and write comments that explain the **why**,
  in English.

head: CLAUDE.md > Pull request reviews
text:
The rules are in **[documentation/code-review.md](documentation/code-review.md)** — read that file
before reviewing. In one paragraph: approve what improves the codebase, report only findings worth a
developer's time (**3–8, hard cap 10**), severity prefixes **Blocker / Issue / Nit / FYI**, tests
read first, no PR summary and no praise section, post exactly one comment in German. Highest signal
in this repo: migration safety, cross-repo breakage, security, missing regression tests.

head: CLAUDE.md > Pull request reviews
text:
The same rules drive the automated review in `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml`. It runs
**on request, not on every push**: on *Ready for review*, on an `@claude` comment, or on a manual
workflow start. The `no-claude-review` label suppresses the automatic run.

Roboflow Inference is a set of Python packages that run computer vision models
locally and expose them via an HTTP API and command line interface. The repo
contains the core library, CLI, SDK, and Dockerfiles for building CPU or GPU
images. Supported Python versions are 3.10–3.12.

  [Slab guide](https://roboflow.slab.com/posts/inference-contributions-implementation-plan-1sb5nyqz);
  keep both aligned when changing the process. Agents can help investigate and
  draft a plan, but the contributor must understand and own the recommendation
  and unresolved questions.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution / PR Guidelines > Internal contributions (Roboflow team only)
text:
- A plan is generally unnecessary for documentation corrections or examples of
  existing functionality, added tests or regression coverage, contained fixes
  restoring established behavior, and local refactoring that preserves behavior
  and interfaces. New workflow blocks also qualify when they follow existing
  patterns and introduce no new execution behavior or execution-engine changes.
  Discuss changes to shared infrastructure, compatibility, security, or package
  dependencies with maintainers first, even for a small diff. If unsure, share a
  short description in the channel to establish whether a plan is needed.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution / PR Guidelines > Internal contributions (Roboflow team only)
text:
- Keep unfinished work in a draft PR. Before marking it ready, inspect the diff,
  run relevant checks, record the commands and results (including limitations),
  and be available to address feedback. Plan exemptions do not waive testing or
  review. Contributors remain responsible for follow-up issues after merge.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution / PR Guidelines > Internal contributions (Roboflow team only)
text:
- Use the optional [local pre-review skill](.claude/skills/review-local/SKILL.md)
  to check work before requesting CI review. In Claude Code, invoke
  `/review-local`; other agents can read and follow that file directly. Local
  findings are advisory and do not replace CI review or maintainer approval.

head: AGENTS.md > Contribution / PR Guidelines > Internal contributions (Roboflow team only)
text:
- Claude provides the first CI review. Address its findings and add the
  `claude-review` label to request another pass; the label is consumed when review
  starts, and new commits alone do not trigger another review. An eligible agent
  pass requests maintainer review through the Slack handoff bot. If disagreeing
  with a finding, explain why in a PR comment beginning
  `/maintainer-review <reason>` to escalate. The handoff requires an open,
  non-draft, same-repository PR; escalation also requires repository write access
  or higher. Coordinate in the linked Slack thread and record final approval in
  GitHub. See [handoff behavior](.github/maintainer-review-slack.md) for details.

head: go-clean-template
text:
Go clean-architecture reference service. Three domains (`user`, `task`, `translation`) exposed
over four transports (REST/Fiber, gRPC, RabbitMQ RPC, NATS RPC) from one shared use-case layer.
Module path: `github.com/evrone/go-clean-template`. The Go version is declared in `go.mod`.

head: go-clean-template > Commands — drive everything through the Makefile
text:
The `Makefile` loads `.env` (falling back to `.env.example`) and exports it into every target, and
several targets carry flags that matter. Running the underlying tool directly means running it with
different settings than CI. Use the target, not the tool.

head: go-clean-template > Commands — drive everything through the Makefile
text:
| Task | Use this | Not this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install tool binaries (`swag`, `mockgen`, `migrate`, linters) | `make bin-deps` | `go install ...` |
| Unit tests | `make test` | `go test ./...` — the target adds `-race -covermode atomic` and scopes to `./internal/... ./pkg/...` |
| Integration tests | `make compose-up-integration-test` | `make integration-test` — see below |
| Lint | `make linter-golangci` | `golangci-lint run` |
| Format | `make format` | `gofmt` — the target runs `go fix`, `gofumpt`, and `gci` with the repo's import grouping |
| Regenerate mocks | `make mock` | `mockgen ...` |
| Regenerate Swagger | `make swag-v1` | `swag init` — the target passes `--parseDependency -g internal/controller/restapi/router.go` |
| Regenerate protobuf | `make proto-v1` | `protoc ...` |
| Tidy / verify modules | `make deps` | `go mod tidy` |
| Vulnerability scan | `make deps-audit` | `govulncheck ./...` |
| Start dependencies (Postgres, RabbitMQ, NATS) | `make compose-up` | `docker compose up` |
| Start the whole stack including the app | `make compose-up-all` | `docker compose up` |
| Tear down | `make compose-down` | `docker compose down` |
| Run the app locally | `make run` | `go run ./cmd/app` — the target regenerates docs and builds with `-tags migrate` |
| Create a migration | `make migrate-create <name>` | `migrate create ...` |
| Apply migrations | `make migrate-up` | `migrate -path ... up` |
| Full check before pushing | `make pre-commit` | running the steps by hand |

head: go-clean-template > Commands — drive everything through the Makefile
text: `make help` lists every target.

head: go-clean-template > Commands — drive everything through the Makefile
text: Three traps in these targets:

head: go-clean-template > Commands — drive everything through the Makefile
text:
- **`make integration-test` is not the one you want.** It runs `go test ./integration-test/...` on
  the host, where the suite cannot resolve the container hostnames it needs, so it always fails.
  `make compose-up-integration-test` is the real entry point.

head: go-clean-template > Commands — drive everything through the Makefile
text:
- **`make migrate-create <name>` prints an error after it succeeds.** The target reads the name via
  `$(word 2,$(MAKECMDGOALS))`, so `make` then tries to build `<name>` as a target and reports
  `No rule to make target`. The migration files are already created; ignore that line.

head: go-clean-template > Commands — drive everything through the Makefile
text:
- **`make run` and `make pre-commit` depend on `swag-v1` and `proto-v1`**, so they need `swag` and
  `protoc` on `PATH`. Run `make bin-deps` first (`protoc` itself is not installed by it).

head: go-clean-template > Commands — drive everything through the Makefile
text: Never claim a change is done without `make format`, `make linter-golangci` and `make test` passing.

head: go-clean-template > Dependency rule
text: - `internal/entity` — domain types and sentinel errors. Imports nothing from this module.

head: go-clean-template > Dependency rule
text:
- `internal/usecase/contracts.go` — the interfaces controllers call. `internal/usecase/<domain>/`
  implements them.

head: go-clean-template > Dependency rule
text:
- `internal/repo/contracts.go` — the interfaces use cases call. `internal/repo/persistent/<domain>/`
  (Postgres) and `internal/repo/webapi/` (outbound HTTP) implement them.

head: go-clean-template > Dependency rule
text:
- `internal/controller/<transport>/v1/` — one package per transport, each with its own
  `request/` and `response/` DTOs. Controllers never import each other.

head: go-clean-template > Dependency rule
text:
- `pkg/` — transport-agnostic infrastructure (servers, logger, jwt, postgres, tracing). Must not
  import `internal/`.

head: go-clean-template > Dependency rule
text:
Inner layers never import outer ones. Wiring happens exactly once, in `internal/app/app.go`
(`initUseCases`, `initServers`).

head: go-clean-template > Where code goes
text: Decide by asking what the code knows about:

head: go-clean-template > Where code goes
text:
| The code knows about… | It belongs in | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing but the domain | `internal/entity/<name>.go` | struct + methods (`Task.Transition`, `TaskStatus.Valid`) |
| a domain rule that spans repositories | `internal/usecase/<domain>/<domain>.go` | method on `UseCase` |
| SQL, a table, a driver error code | `internal/repo/persistent/<domain>/<domain>.go` | method on `Repo` |
| an outbound HTTP API | `internal/repo/webapi/<name>.go` | method on the webapi struct |
| an HTTP status, a gRPC code, a message envelope | `internal/controller/<transport>/v1/<domain>.go` | handler |
| a server, pool, client or middleware with no domain knowledge | `pkg/<name>/` | reusable package |

head: go-clean-template > Where code goes
text:
- One file per domain per layer, named after the domain (`task.go`, `user.go`, `translation.go`),
  plus a `tracing.go` in every `usecase/<domain>/` and `repo/persistent/<domain>/` package.

head: go-clean-template > Where code goes
text:
- Package name matches the directory name. `internal/repo/persistent/translation/` is the one
  violation in the tree — it declares `package persistent`, which is why `internal/app/app.go`
  imports the three repositories under aliases. Follow `task/` and `user/`, not `translation/`.

head: go-clean-template > Where code goes
text:
- Constructors are always `New`, return the *interface* from `contracts.go`, and take their
  dependencies as arguments. No package-level state — `gochecknoglobals` and `gochecknoinits` are on.

head: go-clean-template > Where code goes
text:
- Unexported package constants are prefixed with an underscore (`_defaultEntityCap`,
  `_tracerName`). `mnd` rejects bare numeric literals, so add a constant rather than inlining one.

head: go-clean-template > The handler contract
text:
Every controller method, on every transport, does the same six things in the same order. Copy the
shape from a neighbouring handler in the same transport.

head: go-clean-template > The handler contract
text:
1. **Get the caller.** REST: `ctx.Locals("userID").(string)`. gRPC: `grpcmw.UserIDFromContext(ctx)`.
   AMQP / NATS: `extractUserID(d, r.j)`. A failure here is an auth error, not a 500.

head: go-clean-template > The handler contract
text:
2. **Decode into a transport-local DTO** from `<transport>/v1/request/`. Never decode into an
   `entity` type, and never pass a `request.*` type into a use case.

head: go-clean-template > The handler contract
text:
3. **Validate the DTO** with the injected `*validator.Validate` (`r.v.Struct(req)`). Structural
   validation (required, min, max, oneof) lives here. Domain validation — anything that needs to
   know the rules, like a status transition — lives on the entity or the use case and must not be
   duplicated in the controller.

head: go-clean-template > The handler contract
text:
4. **Call the use case** with the request context: `ctx.UserContext()` in Fiber (**not**
   `ctx.Context()`, which drops the trace), the handler's `ctx` everywhere else. `context.Context`
   is the first parameter of every method that crosses a layer.

head: go-clean-template > The handler contract
text:
5. **Map the error.** `errors.Is` against the `entity.Err*` sentinels → a transport status. Log the
   wrapped error, return a generic message to the caller.

head: go-clean-template > The handler contract
text:
6. **Encode the response.** Return an `entity` type directly only when its JSON shape is already
   the API shape — `entity.User` is safe this way because `PasswordHash` is tagged `json:"-"`.
   Anything with a wrapper, a projection or a different field set gets a type in
   `<transport>/v1/response/` (`response.TaskList`, `response.Token`). gRPC always converts through
   `response.New*Response`.

head: go-clean-template > The handler contract
text:
AMQP and NATS handlers are closures returning that transport's `server.CallHandler` —
`func(ctx, *amqp.Delivery) (any, error)` and `func(ctx, *nats.Msg) (any, error)`. Each transport
has its own `extractUserID` in `v1/auth.go` taking its own message type. Handlers return a plain
wrapped `error`; the RPC server turns it into a generic `ErrInternalServer` / `ErrBadHandler`
reply. Do not hand-build an error envelope there.

head: go-clean-template > Conventions that will bite you
text:
**Traced decorators.** Every repo and use-case constructor returns the *interface*, wrapped:
`func New(...) usecase.Task { return newTraced(&UseCase{...}) }`. The wrapper lives in
`tracing.go` next to each implementation. Adding a method to a contract means implementing it in
three places: the interface, the struct, and the `traced*` decorator. Skipping the decorator is a
compile error that reads as an unrelated interface mismatch.

head: go-clean-template > Conventions that will bite you
text:
**Mocks are generated, not written.** `internal/usecase/mocks_*_test.go` come from `go:generate`
directives in the two `contracts.go` files. After any contract change run `make mock` before
running tests.

head: go-clean-template > Conventions that will bite you
text:
**Error style.** Domain failures are sentinel errors in `internal/entity/errors.go`
(`ErrTaskNotFound`, `ErrTaskForbidden`, `ErrInvalidTransition`, …). Every other error is wrapped
with the layer path: `fmt.Errorf("TaskUseCase - Create - uc.repo.Store: %w", err)`. The `err113`
linter rejects `errors.New`/`fmt.Errorf` for new dynamic errors — add a sentinel to `entity`
instead. Controllers are the only place that translates a sentinel into a transport status.

head: go-clean-template > Conventions that will bite you
text:
**Config is environment-only.** `config/config.go` parses env vars with `caarlos0/env`. A new
setting needs the struct field, an entry in `.env.example`, and — if the container needs it — the
`environment` block in `docker-compose.yml`. Fields tagged `required` make the app fail at
startup.

head: go-clean-template > Conventions that will bite you
text:
**The linter is strict and non-obvious.** `.golangci.yml` enables ~45 linters. The ones that
reject otherwise-fine code: `wsl_v5` and `nlreturn` (blank line required before `return` and
around blocks), `funlen` (65 lines / 40 statements), `gocyclo` (10), `gocognit` (15), `mnd`,
`gochecknoglobals`, `exhaustive` (switches over enum types need every case or a `default`), `dupl`
(threshold 100 — copy-pasting a handler across transports trips it).

head: go-clean-template > Generated files — do not hand-edit
text:
- `docs/docs.go`, `docs/swagger.json`, `docs/swagger.yaml` ← `make swag-v1`, driven by the
  annotation comments above REST handlers and on `NewRouter` in `internal/controller/restapi/router.go`.

head: go-clean-template > Generated files — do not hand-edit
text: - `docs/proto/v1/*.pb.go` ← `make proto-v1` from the `.proto` files beside them.

head: go-clean-template > Generated files — do not hand-edit
text: - `internal/usecase/mocks_*_test.go` ← `make mock`.

head: go-clean-template > READMEs must be updated as a set
text:
`README.md` (English) is canonical. `README_RU.md` and `README_CN.md` are full translations that
mirror it **section for section, table row for table row** — same headings in the same order, same
tables, same code blocks, same links. Changing one and not the other two is the most common
regression in this repo.

head: go-clean-template > READMEs must be updated as a set
text: Update all three whenever a change touches what they document:

head: go-clean-template > READMEs must be updated as a set
text:
| Change | What to update in every README |
| --- | --- |
| New or changed REST / gRPC endpoint | the domain table under `Domains` (`Домены` / `领域`) |
| New domain | the `Overview` bullet list, `Content` index, and a new `Domains` subsection |
| New or renamed env var | the config table under `Observability` if tracing-related; otherwise the `config` section |
| New transport, server, port or service URL | the `Quick start` service list |
| New `make` target used in the getting-started flow | the `Quick start` code blocks |
| Renamed or moved package under `internal/` or `pkg/` | the matching `Project structure` subsection |

head: go-clean-template > READMEs must be updated as a set
text: Rules for the translations:

head: go-clean-template > READMEs must be updated as a set
text:
- Translate the prose; leave identifiers, paths, `make` targets, URLs, env var names, code blocks
  and route strings verbatim in English.

head: go-clean-template > READMEs must be updated as a set
text:
- Headings are translated, so the `Content` index anchors are localized too (`#домены`, `#领域`).
  Adding or renaming a section means updating that file's own anchors — an anchor copied from the
  English file will not resolve.

head: go-clean-template > READMEs must be updated as a set
text: - Keep the heading level identical across the three files.

head: go-clean-template > READMEs must be updated as a set
text:
- If you genuinely cannot produce a translation, still add the section in English to the other two
  files so the structure stays aligned, and say so in the change description.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a use case to an existing domain
text: 1. Add the method to `internal/usecase/contracts.go`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a use case to an existing domain
text:
2. Implement it in `internal/usecase/<domain>/<domain>.go` and mirror it in the same package's
   `tracing.go`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a use case to an existing domain
text:
3. If it needs new persistence, repeat the same three steps in `internal/repo/contracts.go`,
   `internal/repo/persistent/<domain>/`, and that package's `tracing.go`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a use case to an existing domain
text:
4. `make mock`, then extend `internal/usecase/<domain>_test.go` (table-driven, gomock, `t.Parallel()` —
   `paralleltest` enforces it).

head: go-clean-template > Adding a use case to an existing domain
text:
5. Expose it on whichever transports need it:
   - REST: handler in `internal/controller/restapi/v1/<domain>.go` + route in that package's
     `router.go` + swagger annotations, then `make swag-v1`.
   - gRPC: `.proto` change → `make proto-v1` → controller method in
     `internal/controller/grpc/v1/`.
   - AMQP / NATS: handler returning a `CallHandler` + a `"v1.<domain>.<action>"` key in the
     transport's `v1/router.go`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a use case to an existing domain
text:
Transports are independent by design; adding a method to only one is a legitimate choice, not an
oversight — but say which ones you covered.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
Work outward from the entity. Every step has a counterpart in the existing `task` domain — read it
before writing.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
1. **Entity** — `internal/entity/<domain>.go` with the type and its invariants; new sentinel errors
   go in `internal/entity/errors.go`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
2. **Migration** — `make migrate-create create_<table>`, then fill both the `.up.sql` and the
   `.down.sql`. A missing down-migration is a review failure.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text: 3. **Repo contract** — add the interface to `internal/repo/contracts.go`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
4. **Repo implementation** — `internal/repo/persistent/<domain>/<domain>.go` (`package <domain>`,
   Squirrel queries, driver errors mapped to sentinels) plus `tracing.go` next to it, and a `New`
   returning the interface wrapped in `newTraced`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text: 5. **Use-case contract** — add the interface to `internal/usecase/contracts.go`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
6. **Use-case implementation** — `internal/usecase/<domain>/<domain>.go` plus its `tracing.go`,
   same `New` pattern.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text: 7. **`make mock`**, then `internal/usecase/<domain>_test.go` against the generated mocks.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
8. **Wiring** — add a field to `useCases` in `internal/app/app.go`, construct repo and use case in
   `initUseCases`, and thread the use case through `initServers` into each router you are exposing.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
9. **Transports** — for each one: DTOs in `<transport>/v1/request/` and `response/`, handlers in
   `<transport>/v1/<domain>.go`, registration in that transport's `v1/router.go`, and the use case
   added to the `V1` / controller struct in `<transport>/v1/controller.go`. gRPC also needs
   `docs/proto/v1/<domain>.proto` and `make proto-v1`.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
10. **Docs** — swagger annotations on the REST handlers, `make swag-v1`, and the README updates
    listed above in all three languages.

head: go-clean-template > Adding a whole domain
text:
11. **Integration test** — `integration-test/<domain>_test.go` exercising the domain over the
    transports you exposed.

head: go-clean-template > API versioning
text:
Routes are grouped under a version package (`<transport>/v1/`). A v2 means a new sibling package
with the same layout, registered alongside v1 in the transport's top-level `router.go` — REST adds
an `app.Group("/v2")`, gRPC registers a second set of `NewXRoutes`, AMQP/NATS add more
`"v2.<domain>.<action>"` keys to the same route map. v1 stays untouched. `README.md` documents this
with worked examples per transport; follow it rather than inventing a scheme.

head: go-clean-template > Database
text:
`migrations/` holds golang-migrate pairs (`<timestamp>_<name>.up.sql` / `.down.sql`). Create with
`make migrate-create <name>`, apply with `make migrate-up`. The app applies them itself at startup
only when built with the `migrate` build tag (`internal/app/migrate.go`) — that is what `make run`
and the Dockerfile do. Queries are built with Squirrel via the embedded `*postgres.Postgres`;
there is no ORM and no raw string concatenation.

head: go-clean-template > Tests
text:
- Unit: `internal/...` and `pkg/...`, run by `make test` with `-race`. Use-case tests use the
  generated gomock mocks, are table-driven, and call `t.Parallel()` (`paralleltest` enforces it).

head: go-clean-template > Tests
text:
- Integration: `integration-test/` runs *inside* the docker network — it resolves the service as
  host `app` and talks to `rabbitmq` / `nats` by container name, so it fails on the host machine.
  Always run it through `make compose-up-integration-test`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework
text: A reference for AI developer agents working on the Mondrian Framework monorepo.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > What this project is
text: **Mondrian Framework** is a TypeScript framework for **modular server-side applications** focused on type safety, functional programming, and modern API standards. You define data models and functions once; Mondrian generates compliant OpenAPI, GraphQL (and Protobuf, planned) APIs and servers — no codegen step (purely TS types).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > What this project is
text: Core ideas (from `packages/docs/docs/docs/01-introduction.md`):

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > What this project is
text: - **Model**: formal representation of a domain concept/value object (DDD-style entities and value objects).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > What this project is
text: - **Function**: named operation with typed inputs, outputs, errors, and side effects.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > What this project is
text: - **Module**: named, reusable group of functions sharing a domain.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > What this project is
text: - **Runtime**: environment that executes modules (REST, GraphQL, SQS, cron, CLI, custom...).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > What this project is
text: Programming style mixes FP/FRP with PP. Inspired by Clean Architecture (Martin), DDD (Evans), Modern Software Engineering (Farley). 100% TypeScript on Node ≥ 20.9 (Deno/Bun WIP).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Workspaces, paths, and aliases
text: `package.json#workspaces` lists every internal package; `tsconfig.json#paths` aliases each as `@mondrian-framework/<pkg>`. TS uses `composite` + `references` for incremental builds. Internal packages reference each other with `*` versions in their `package.json#dependencies`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Public API surface (what to import)
text:
`packages/model/src/index.ts` re-exports as `model`, `encoding`, `decoding`, `validation`, `result`, `path`, `arbitrary`, `utils`.
`packages/module/src/index.ts` re-exports as `module`, `functions`, `logger`, `client`, `utils`, `serialization`, `exception`, `error`, `retrieve`, `security`, `provider`, `guard`, `middleware`.

text: Builders return `model.Type`. All accept `BaseOptions` (`name`, `description`, etc.).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Primitives**: `model.boolean()`, `model.string({ minLength, maxLength, regex })`, `model.number({ minimum, exclusiveMaximum })`, `model.integer({ minimum, maximum })`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Date/time**: `datetime` (JS Date), `timestamp` (ms unix), `date`, `time` (RFC 3339), `timezone` (IANA).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Locations**: `countryCode`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `locale`, `currency`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Other built-ins**: `email`, `phoneNumber` (E.164), `mac`, `ip`, `port`, `version` (semver), `json`, `url`, `uuid`, `isbn`, `rgb`, `rgba`, `unknown`, `record(type)`, `jwt({...claims}, 'RS256')`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Enums / literals**: `model.enumeration(['a','b'])`, `model.literal('Hello')`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Wrappers**: `optional`, `nullable`, `array` (immutable by default; `.mutable()` / `.immutable()`); chaining order matters (`.array().nullable()` ≠ `.nullable().array()`).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Objects vs entities**: `model.object({...})` for value objects (immutable readonly fields by default); `model.entity({...}, { description, retrieve: { where, orderBy, take, skip } })` for domain concepts with identity. Entities are what `retrieve`, security policies, and ORM mapping target.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Unions**: `model.union({ tagA: TypeA, tagB: TypeB })` — tagged at the model level.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Lazy types**: `const User = () => model.entity({...})`. Required for self/circular references; the function name is the type name (or use `.setName('X')`).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Custom types**: `model.custom<Name, Options, Inferred>(name, encoder, decoder, validator, arbitrary, options?)`. Decoder validates basic shape; validator enforces semantic rules. Both return `decoding.Result` / `validation.Result`. Arbitrary uses `fast-check`. See `packages/docs/docs/docs/fundamentals/model/01-definition.md` for the canonical port-type example.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Inference**: `type T = model.Infer<typeof T>`. Encoded form via `model.InferEncoded`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **Operations on a Type**: `.encode(value)`, `.decode(unknown)`, `.example()`, `.setName(...)`, `.setOptions(...)`, `.optional()`, `.nullable()`, `.array()`, `.sensitive()` (e.g. for passwords), `.mutable()`, `.immutable()`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The model layer (`@mondrian-framework/model`)
text: - **`result` module**: `result.ok(value)`, `result.fail({ errorKey: details })`. Functions never `throw` for application errors — they return `Result`s.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Functions
text: - `input`/`output`: any `model.Type` (or omit for void). Single input parameter (compose with objects/unions for many).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Functions
text: - `errors`: map of error name → schema. Use `error.define({ key: { message, ...detailFields } })` for default-message convenience. `error.standard.UnauthorizedAccess`, `error.standard.BadInput` are built-ins.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Functions
text: - `retrieve`: enable Prisma-style projections — `{ select?, where?, orderBy?, take?, skip? }`. Uses Prisma syntax. `retrieve.allCapabilities` enables them all. Constraints can be narrowed per-entity in the entity definition (`retrieve: { where: { id: true }, take: { max: 10 }, ... }`).

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Functions
text: - `options`: `namespace` (subgrouping for runtimes), `description`, `operation` (`'query' | 'command' | { command: 'create' | 'update' | 'delete' }`), `opentelemetry: boolean`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Functions
text: - The `body` receives `{ input, retrieve, logger, tracer }` plus a key per declared provider/guard. Always `return result.ok(...)` / `return result.fail(...)` — missing `return` is a known footgun.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Functions
text: - `def.mock({ errorProbability, maxDepth })` produces a fully type-correct mock implementation for prototyping/contract use.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Providers — DI for context-derived resources
text: - Providers' contextual inputs (first body param) accumulate into the **module context input** type. The runtime's `context: async (input) => ...` must produce all of them.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Providers — DI for context-derived resources
text: - A provider runs **once per function execution**. For singletons, instantiate outside `body`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Providers — DI for context-derived resources
text: - A provider's declared `errors` must also appear in the `errors` of every function that `.use`s it.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Guards — pre-execution gatekeepers
text: Same wiring as providers but `result.ok()` returns `undefined` (no value injected). Used as `.use({ guards: { auth: authGuard } })`. Errors must also be declared on the function.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Modules
text: Module-level `errors` can be raised from the `context` builder and are auto-added to every function's contract. Context builder runs **per invocation** — be mindful of expensive setup.

text: Defined per request via `policies(context)`:

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Security policies
text: - `selection`: `true` (all fields) or per-field `{ id: true, ... }`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Security policies
text: - `restriction`/`filter`: Prisma-like `where` predicates. Rules evaluated in order — first matching restriction's selection applies.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > The module layer (`@mondrian-framework/module`) > Security policies
text: - Applied automatically to functions with `retrieve`. Filters out unauthorized rows/fields _before_ returning. Traversed entities all need `.on(...)` rules to allow graph navigation.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **Always `return` `result.ok`/`result.fail`** — missing return won't always type-error.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **Lazy types `() => model.entity({...})`** for any reference loop; the function name becomes the type name.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **Provider/guard errors must also be declared** on every function that `.use`s them.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **Module context builder runs per invocation** — instantiate heavy clients outside.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **Set `maxSelectionDepth`** in production to prevent DoS via deep selections.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **Use `model.entity` (not `object`) for domain concepts** — entities are what `retrieve`, security, and ORM bridges target.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **Strict TS**: monorepo uses `"strict": true`, `composite: true`, NodeNext modules. Don't break references.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **`@mondrian-framework/utils`** holds shared TS helpers; check there before writing utility types.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **Coverage excludes** `packages/example/**` and `packages/docs/**`.

head: AGENTS.md — Mondrian Framework > Conventions & gotchas
text: - **`module.build` vs `module.define().implement()`**: `build` produces an implemented module from interface+impl in one step; `define` returns just the interface and exposes `.implement(...)` (also goes through `build`). Functions analogously have `.define()` + `.implement()` (no top-level `functions.build`). The example uses the split-interface pattern (`packages/example/src/interface/module.ts` defines, `packages/example/src/core/module.ts` implements) so the interface package is shareable independent of the impl.

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Simplicity & no bloat
text: - Always pick the simplest implementation that works.

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Simplicity & no bloat
text: - When refactoring, actively remove bloat. The diff should usually be net-negative.

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Simplicity & no bloat
text: - **No dead code.** If a function, file, branch, or `#ifdef` path isn't reachable in our supported configurations, delete it. Don't comment it out.

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Simplicity & no bloat
text: - Don't add features, abstractions, or layers that aren't required by the task in front of us. No designing for hypothetical future needs.

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Simplicity & no bloat
text: - Don't add error handling, validation, or fallbacks for cases that can't happen. Trust internal invariants; only validate at true system boundaries.

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Simplicity & no bloat
text: - No backwards-compatibility shims for features we control. If we change a thing, change every caller.

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Comments & documentation
text: - **Default to no comments.** Well-named identifiers explain *what*; only write a comment when the *why* is non-obvious (a hidden constraint, a subtle invariant, a workaround for a specific bug, behaviour that would surprise a reader).

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Comments & documentation
text: - **Inline comments describe the code as it is now**, not its history. Don't write "previously this used X", "removed Y", "refactored from Z". Git log is the history.

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Comments & documentation
text: - Historical context is allowed *only* when it explains why something is done in a non-intuitive way today (e.g. "ordering matters here because chip X latches on the falling edge — reversing the writes breaks Mockingboard").

head: NoxArchaistCompanion (NAC) — Project Notes > Coding rules (apply to ALL work in this repo) > Comments & documentation

head: SpacetimeDB Rules (All Languages) > Core Concepts
text: 1. **Reducers are transactional** — they do not return data to callers

head: SpacetimeDB Rules (All Languages) > Core Concepts
text: 2. **Reducers must be deterministic** — no filesystem, network, timers, or random

head: SpacetimeDB Rules (All Languages) > Core Concepts
text: 3. **Read data via tables/subscriptions** — not reducer return values

head: SpacetimeDB Rules (All Languages) > Core Concepts
text: 4. **Auto-increment IDs are not sequential** — gaps are normal, don't use for ordering

head: SpacetimeDB Rules (All Languages) > Core Concepts
text: 5. **`ctx.sender` is the authenticated principal** — never trust identity args

head: SpacetimeDB Rules (All Languages) > Feature Implementation Checklist

head: SpacetimeDB Rules (All Languages) > Feature Implementation Checklist

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > ⛔ COMMON MISTAKES — LLM HALLUCINATIONS
text: These are **actual errors** observed when LLMs generate SpacetimeDB Rust code:

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > ⛔ COMMON MISTAKES — LLM HALLUCINATIONS > 13. Client SDK Uses Blocking I/O
text: The SpacetimeDB Rust client SDK uses blocking I/O. If mixing with async runtimes (Tokio, async-std), use `spawn_blocking` or run the SDK on a dedicated thread to avoid blocking the async executor.

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 1) Common Mistakes Table > Server-side errors
text:
| Wrong | Right | Error |
|-------|-------|-------|
| `#[derive(SpacetimeType)]` on `#[table]` | Remove it — macro handles this | Conflicting derive macros |
| `ctx.db.player` (field access) | `ctx.db.player()` (method) | "no field `player` on type" |
| `ctx.db.player().find(id)` | `ctx.db.player().id().find(&id)` | Must access via index |
| `&mut ReducerContext` | `&ReducerContext` | Wrong context type |
| Missing `use spacetimedb::Table;` | Add import | "no method named `insert`" |
| `#[table(accessor = "my_table")]` | `#[table(accessor = my_table)]` | String literals not allowed |
| Missing `public` on table | Add `public` flag | Clients can't subscribe |
| `#[spacetimedb::reducer]` | `#[reducer]` after import | Wrong attribute path |
| Network/filesystem in reducer | Use procedures instead | Sandbox violation |
| Panic for expected errors | Return `Result<(), String>` | WASM instance destroyed |

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 2) Table Definition (CRITICAL)
text: **Tables use `#[table(...)]` macro on `pub struct`. DO NOT derive `SpacetimeType` on tables!**

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 2) Table Definition (CRITICAL)
text: > ⚠️ **CRITICAL:** Always import `Table` trait — required for `.insert()`, `.iter()`, `.find()`, etc.

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 5) Custom Types
text: **Use `#[derive(SpacetimeType)]` ONLY for custom structs/enums used as fields or parameters.**

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 7) Client SDK > ⚠️ CRITICAL: Advance the Connection
text: **You MUST call one of these** — without it, no callbacks fire:

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 8) Procedures (Beta)
text: **Procedures are for side effects (HTTP, filesystem) that reducers can't do.**

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 8) Procedures (Beta)
text: ⚠️ Procedures are currently in beta. API may change.

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 8) Procedures (Beta) > Key differences from reducers
text:
| Reducers | Procedures |
|----------|------------|
| `&ReducerContext` (immutable) | `&mut ProcedureContext` (mutable) |
| Direct `ctx.db` access | Must use `ctx.with_tx()` |
| No HTTP/network | HTTP allowed |
| No return values | Can return data |

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 1. **DO NOT derive `SpacetimeType` on `#[table]` structs** — the macro handles this

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 2. **Import `Table` trait** — `use spacetimedb::Table;` required for `.insert()`, `.iter()`, etc.

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 3. **Use `&ReducerContext`** — not `&mut ReducerContext`

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 4. **Tables are methods** — `ctx.db.table()` not `ctx.db.table`

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 5. **Server modules use `spacetimedb` crate** — clients use `spacetimedb-sdk`

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 6. **Reducers must be deterministic** — no filesystem, network, timers, or external RNG

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 7. **Use `ctx.rng`** — not `rand` crate for random numbers

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 8. **Use `ctx.timestamp`** — never `std::time::SystemTime::now()` in reducers

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 9. **Client MUST advance connection** — call `run_threaded()`, `run_async()`, or `frame_tick()`

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 10. **Subscribe in `on_connect` callback** — not before connection is established

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 11. **Update requires full row** — spread existing row with `..existing`

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 12. **DO NOT edit generated bindings** — regenerate with `spacetime generate`

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 13. **Identity to String needs `.to_string()`** — `identity.to_hex().to_string()`

head: SpacetimeDB Rust SDK > 11) Hard Requirements
text: 14. **Client SDK is blocking** — use `spawn_blocking` or dedicated thread if mixing with async runtimes

text:
- **Fix**:
  1. `parser_3mf.py`: Detects `paint_color` data in mesh triangles (via `_has_paint_data()`) regardless of `single_extruder_multi_material` flag — some exports set it to "0" even for painted files. Returns all `filament_colour` entries when paint data is present, preventing phantom `extruder_colour` from mixing in.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Coding Agent Operating Manual (u1-slicer-bridge) > Multi-Plate 3MF Support (NEW - M7.1) > Known Issues & Fixes Applied
text: - **Problem**: Responsive tests timing out; all API calls firing twice during page load.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Coding Agent Operating Manual (u1-slicer-bridge) > Multi-Plate 3MF Support (NEW - M7.1) > Known Issues & Fixes Applied
text: - **Root Cause**: `<body x-data="app()" x-init="init()">` called `init()` twice — Alpine v3 auto-calls `init()` on data objects from `x-data`, and `x-init` called it again. With Moonraker configured but unreachable, two sequential 10s health checks = 20s, exceeding the 15s `networkidle` timeout.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Coding Agent Operating Manual (u1-slicer-bridge) > Multi-Plate 3MF Support (NEW - M7.1) > Known Issues & Fixes Applied
text: - **Fix**: Removed redundant `x-init="init()"`. Responsive tests now use `domcontentloaded` instead of `networkidle`.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Coding Agent Operating Manual (u1-slicer-bridge) > Multi-Plate 3MF Support (NEW - M7.1) > Known Issues & Fixes Applied
text: - **Problem**: Dual-colour cube (two separate 10mm cubes offset in assembly) with 4 copies showed 6 visible cubes instead of 8. Adjacent copies overlapped in the center of the grid.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Coding Agent Operating Manual (u1-slicer-bridge) > Multi-Plate 3MF Support (NEW - M7.1) > Known Issues & Fixes Applied
text: - **Root Cause**: `_scan_object_bounds()` in `multi_plate_parser.py` scanned vertex bounds from each component's mesh but **never applied the component transform offsets**. Both components referenced the same mesh, so combined bounds equaled one cube's bounds (10mm), ignoring the +/-7.455mm offsets. Actual assembly footprint is 24.9mm wide.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Coding Agent Operating Manual (u1-slicer-bridge) > Multi-Plate 3MF Support (NEW - M7.1) > Known Issues & Fixes Applied
text: - **Fix**: Parse each component's `transform` attribute and apply translation offsets (`vals[9]`, `vals[10]`, `vals[11]`) to vertex bounds before combining.

head: AGENTS.md — AI Coding Agent Operating Manual (u1-slicer-bridge) > Multi-Plate 3MF Support (NEW - M7.1) > Known Issues & Fixes Applied
text: - **Result**: Object dimensions correctly reported as 24.9x10.5x10.0mm; grid spacing prevents overlap.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide
text: This repository contains `gitoxide` - a pure Rust implementation of Git. This document provides guidance for GitHub Copilot when working with this codebase.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Project Overview
text: - **Language**: Rust (MSRV documented in gix/Cargo.toml)

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Project Overview
text: - **Structure**: Cargo workspace with multiple crates (gix-\*, gitoxide-core, etc.)

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Project Overview
text: - **Main crates**: `gix` (library entrypoint), `gitoxide` binary (CLI tools: `gix` and `ein`)

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Project Overview
text: - **Purpose**: Provide a high-performance, safe Git implementation with both library and CLI interfaces

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > AI Agent Communication
text: - AI agents communicating through a person's account must identify themselves, for example in issue or PR descriptions and comments.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > AI Agent Communication
text: - AI assistance that does not replace the person as the speaker, such as proofreading or wording polish, does not require identification.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > AI Agent Communication
text: - Attributing AI assistance in commit metadata, for example with an `Assisted-by:` or `Co-authored-by:` trailer, is welcome but not required.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Test-First Development
text: - Protect against regression and make implementing features easy

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Test-First Development
text: - Keep it practical - the Rust compiler handles mundane things

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Test-First Development
text: - Use git itself as reference implementation; run same tests against git where feasible

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Test-First Development
text: - Never use `.unwrap()` in production code, avoid it in tests in favor of `.expect()` or `?`. Use `gix_error::TestResult` for test functions and helpers.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Test-First Development
text: - Use `.expect("why")` with context explaining why expectations should hold, but only if it's relevant to the test.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling
text: - Handle all errors, never `unwrap()`

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling
text: - Provide error chains making it easy to understand what went wrong

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling
text:
- Applications built on `gix` use `gix::Result` and `gix::Error`, preserving error context and source locations.
  Import error helpers, traits, and macros through `gix::error` instead of adding a separate `gix-error` dependency.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
Plumbing crates are migrating from `thiserror` enums to `gix-error`. Check whether a crate already
uses `gix-error` (look at its `Cargo.toml`); if it does, follow the patterns below. If it still uses
`thiserror`, keep using `thiserror` for consistency within that crate.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Public error APIs**: use `gix_error::Result<T>` and `gix_error::Error` for erased or
  message-based errors at public plumbing boundaries. Preserve concrete error types already exposed
  by public signatures, including `ExnResult<T, Specific>` and `Exn<Specific>`. This includes public
  traits, callbacks, iterator items, associated errors, and re-exported APIs.
  Keep native `io::Result`, standalone concrete-error results, and generic error adapters when they do
  not expose exceptions. This exemption covers native or operation-specific recovery errors, not
  shared diagnostics like `Message`. Public message-based errors use `Error` even without an `Exn`
  wrapper, including `FromStr::Err` and `TryFrom::Error`. Do not introduce public crate-specific or
  operation-specific forwarding aliases or renamed error exports.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Internal results**: use `Result<T>` for erased or message-based errors in private and
  `pub(crate)` helpers too. Retain concrete error types when callers benefit from typed recovery
  or payload access. Use `ExnResult<T, E>` or `ExnMessageResult<T>` when a specific exception type
  or exception-tree manipulation is actually needed; being private alone is not a reason to
  introduce an exception-returning wrapper. These aliases and typed construction helpers remain available.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Imports**: import `Result`, `ExnResult`, and `ExnMessageResult` under their canonical names
  directly from `gix_error` (or their `gix` re-exports), and use their bare names in signatures.
  Prefer to import `bail` when using `bail!`, via `use gix_error::bail;` or `use gix::error::bail;`,
  and invoke it without a qualified path.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Porcelain errors**: use the central `gix::Error` and `gix::Result` re-exports at public
  boundaries that return erased or message-based exceptions.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text: - **Static messages**: `gix_error::message("something failed")`

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text: - **Formatted messages**: `gix_error::message!("failed to read {path}")`

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text: - **Wrapping callee errors with context**: `.or_raise(|| message("context about what failed"))?`

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Standalone error (no callee)**: use `bail!(error)` for an early return with a concrete
  error or message, such as `bail!(message("something went wrong"))`. For a result expression
  at a boundary returning `Result`, use `Err(error.raise())`.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text: - **Wrapping an `impl Error` with context**: `err.and_raise(message("context"))`

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Typed exceptions**: use `.raise_typed()`, `.and_raise_typed(...)`, `.or_raise_typed(...)`, or
  `.ok_or_raise_typed(...)` when an `Exn<E>` is required; the default helpers return `Error` or `Result`.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Conversion without context**: `.or_error()` converts native errors and exceptions to `Result`.
  Propagate existing `Result` values directly when the callee already provides enough context.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Closure/callback bounds**: preserve concrete callback errors; use `Result<T>` for erased or
  message-based errors in public and private APIs. Private callbacks may use `ExnResult<T>`
  when they need exception-tree operations, or a specific error when useful. Use
  `.or_raise_erased(...)` to add context or `.or_erased()` to convert when an internal callback
  requires an erased exception.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **`Exn<E>` does NOT implement `std::error::Error`** — this is by design.
  Convert with `?`, `.into()`, or `.into_error()` when a boundary returns `Error`. Conversion retains
  the original error types, causes, metadata, and locations; erased errors support downcasting for recovery.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **In tests**: `gix_error::TestResult` (also re-exported by `gix_testtools`) accepts exceptions
  directly with `?`. Public `gix_error::Result` also works with `gix_testtools::Result` through `?`.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text:
- **Common imports**: `use gix_error::{bail, message, ErrorExt, Result, ResultExt};` plus typed
  exception aliases as needed.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Error Handling > `gix-error` (preferred for plumbing crates)
text: - See `gix-error/src/lib.rs` module docs for a full migration guide from `thiserror`

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Commit Messages
text: Follow "purposeful conventional commits" style:

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Commit Messages
text:
- Write commit messages in Markdown and assume readers view them with syntax highlighting.
  - Enclose anything that occurs in code, as well as crate names and shell commands, in backticks.
  - Use Markdown generously whenever markup helps readers understand or navigate the prose.
  - Use the body to share everything known about what motivated the change, not merely what changed.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Development Practices > Commit Messages
text: - Use conventional commit prefixes ONLY if message should appear in changelog

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Building and Testing > Test Best Practices
text:
- Tests must be isolated from the developer's checkout, other worktrees, shared
  Git metadata, and user configuration. Use disposable repositories provided by
  `gix-testtools`, such as `scripted_fixture_writable()`; never mutate a shared
  read-only fixture or use the source checkout as a test repository.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Building and Testing > Test Best Practices
text:
- Git invocations in test code must go through `gix_testtools::git()`,
  `git_command()`, or fixture scripts executed by `gix-testtools`. Do not spawn
  Git directly with `Command::new("git")` or ad hoc subprocess wrappers. If a test needs unsupported
  command options, extend the shared isolated helper instead of bypassing it.
  `run_git()` and `invoke_bash()` share this isolation. Subprocesses that invoke
  Git indirectly must use `gix_testtools::configure_git_environment()` too.
  Tests of APIs that read the process environment must isolate it before
  exercising those APIs or changing environment variables. In `#[serial]` tests,
  keep a `gix_testtools::isolate_git_environment()` guard alive for the entire test;
  it restores only its recorded changes on drop. Chain test-specific overrides
  onto that guard or use a separate `gix_testtools::Env` guard to restore them too.
  All concurrent environment access must participate in the same serialization. Otherwise, use
  `gix_testtools::run_in_isolated_process()` so changes cannot race other tests.
  Restore working-directory changes separately with `gix_testtools::set_current_dir()`.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Building and Testing > Test Best Practices
text:
- Setting a subprocess's working directory or passing `git -C` is not isolation:
  inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, or
  object-directory variables can redirect operations outside the fixture. Tests
  that exercise such overrides must scope them to disposable test repositories.
  Open repositories through the crate's isolated test helper or isolated `gix`
  options, with only test-specific configuration overrides.

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Building and Testing > Test Best Practices

head: Copilot Instructions for Gitoxide > Building and Testing > Test Best Practices

  second parameter. Prefer messages that explain the invariant, not just that an

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Schema and Documentation
text: The ASTRA schema is defined in LinkML files under `src/astra/schema/`. When modifying any schema file (`analysis.yaml`, `insight.yaml`, `universe.yaml`), you **must** also update the corresponding documentation:

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Schema and Documentation
text: - **`docs/specification.md`** — The human-readable specification. Update field tables, examples, and descriptions to reflect schema changes.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Schema and Documentation
text: - **`docs/index.md`** — Landing page; update the quick "At a glance" example if the change affects it.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Schema and Documentation
text: - **`docs/cli.md`** — CLI reference; update if the schema change adds a new validation rule or command surface.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Schema and Documentation
text: - **`docs/llms.txt`** — Agent-facing briefing served at `/latest/llms.txt` ([llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org/)). Update its concept list, example, and validator-rules section if the change affects them. Also shipped inside the wheel as `astra/docs/llms.txt` (hatch force-include in pyproject.toml) so `astra guide` in astra-tools can print the copy matching the installed schema.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Schema and Documentation
text: - **`README.md`** — If the change affects the quick example or design principles, update the README too.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Schema and Documentation
text: Run `just gen-python` to regenerate Python datamodels and `just gen-doc` to regenerate the schema reference docs after any schema change.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Documentation versioning (mike)
text: The whole docs site is versioned with [mike](https://github.com/squidfunk/mike) — specifically squidfunk's fork, which Zensical's versioning provider depends on. Each release deploys a full copy of the site to a subdirectory of the `gh-pages` branch (`/0.0.9/`, `/latest/`, etc.). Mike is enabled via `[project.extra.version] provider = "mike"` in `zensical.toml`; the version dropdown in the header is rendered natively.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Documentation versioning (mike)
text: 1. `just release X.Y.Z` — updates `CITATION.cff`, commits, and creates an annotated tag. Does not push. Schema YAMLs are *not* mutated; the version is injected at build time from the git tag.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Documentation versioning (mike)
text: 2. `git push && git push origin vX.Y.Z` — review then push. The `Deploy versioned docs on tag` GitHub Actions workflow runs `mike deploy --push --update-aliases X.Y.Z latest` automatically.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Documentation versioning (mike)
text: For a manual deploy (e.g. backfilling a tag), `just docs-deploy X.Y.Z` runs the same `mike deploy` locally.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Documentation versioning (mike)
text: First-time setup: after the first deploy, run `just docs-set-default latest` once so the bare site root redirects to `/latest/`.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Documentation versioning (mike)
text: Hosting: mike pushes to `gh-pages`. The hosting platform (Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, etc.) must be configured to serve from `gh-pages`, not `main`. Without this, `mike deploy` runs successfully but the site doesn't pick up versioned URLs in production.

head: ASTRA Spec - Development Notes > Documentation versioning (mike)
text: Schema artifacts (`docs/schema/*.{yaml,json,jsonld}`) are versioned along with the rest of the site: machine consumers should resolve them via the canonical `https://w3id.org/astra/...` URI (which redirects to a hosted location), or pin to `astra-spec.org/X.Y.Z/schema/...`.

head: ABSOLUTE LAW — DO NOT TOUCH LAYER NAMES
text:
If a checkpoint says a layer is `foo.bar.baz`, then in this repository it stays `foo.bar.baz`.
Not `bar.baz`.
Not `foo_bar_baz`.
Not "normalized".
Not "close enough".

head: ABSOLUTE LAW — DO NOT TOUCH LAYER NAMES
text:
Keymaps here **map keyspaces** so the engine/runtime can understand how different ecosystems name the same conceptual weight.
They do **not** rename stored model keys.
They do **not** strip prefixes.
They do **not** rewrite punctuation.
They do **not** slide dots around.
They do **not** materialize remapped state dicts.

head: ABSOLUTE LAW — DO NOT TOUCH LAYER NAMES
text:
If two ecosystems use different names for the same conceptual weight, the keymap resolves that relationship explicitly and the engine interprets the stored key as-is.
If the layout is unsupported, ambiguous, or structurally incompatible, you fail loud and extend the keymap properly.
You do **not** "normalize" a checkpoint by rewriting layer names in memory. Ever.

head: ABSOLUTE LAW — DO NOT TOUCH LAYER NAMES
text:
Lazy mappings are law too.
Checkpoint/state-dict seams stay lazy by default.
Keymaps and loaders inspect checkpoints through mapping/view APIs first (`shape_of(...)`, lookup views, computed views) and only touch real tensor values at the owner seam that actually needs them.
You do **not** materialize eager `dict(...)` copies of checkpoint mappings as convenience glue.

head: ABSOLUTE LAW — DO NOT TOUCH LAYER NAMES > WebUI Atlas > ACT IV – ARCHITECTURE, LEGACY, MODELS, PYTHON

  - it eagerly materialized checkpoint mappings into `dict(...)`
  - it rewrote stored keys in memory
  - it created component-specific loader drift
  - it caused avoidable RAM blow-ups during image-encoder load
  - it violated the canonical build/mount pattern by constructing the runtime module outside the memory-owner device/dtype path, then relying on later runtime offload wrappers to clean it up

head: ABSOLUTE LAW — DO NOT TOUCH LAYER NAMES > WebUI Atlas > ACT IV – ARCHITECTURE, LEGACY, MODELS, PYTHON
text:
- The correct rule is simple:
  - the IP-Adapter image encoder is **not** a special loader class
  - if a VAE or text encoder would load through canonical keymap/view resolution plus `safe_load_state_dict(...)`, then the image encoder must do the same
  - if a CLIP-vision layout needs support, extend the canonical loader/keymap ownership and keep it lazy
  - if the layout is unsupported, fail loud
  - if a component is memory-managed, the module itself must also be built/mounted through the canonical owner path before weight load: resolve the owner device/dtype first, construct under the same `using_codex_operations(**to_args, ...)` pattern used by the central loaders, place the module on that owner device/dtype, then call `safe_load_state_dict(...)`, and only after that rely on runtime offload/reload

user experience.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Rust Conventions

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Rust Conventions
text:
- In async code paths, use the async API when one exists: `tokio::fs`,
  `tokio::process::Command`, `tokio::net`, `tokio::time::sleep`. Reach for

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Rust Conventions
text:
- Never call a blocking function (`std::fs`, `Path::exists`, `std::thread::sleep`,
  a sync `Mutex` guard held across an `.await`) from an `async fn` on the Tokio
  worker pool, and never block the main thread. Details of the runtime's cost
  model live in [`crates/core/AGENTS.md`](crates/core/AGENTS.md).

  [`crates/core/AGENTS.md`](crates/core/AGENTS.md) for the ownership rule and

Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Newtype Wrappers
text:
Prefer newtype wrappers over raw primitives for domain concepts. A
`Fingerprint(String)` is safer and more descriptive than a bare `String`.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Newtype Wrappers > Guidelines
text:
- Wrap `String`, `i64`, and similar primitives when the value represents a
  specific domain concept (fingerprints, file kinds, identifiers, …).

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Newtype Wrappers > Guidelines

  it stays ergonomic.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Newtype Wrappers > Guidelines
text:

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Code Comments
text: Comment **why**, not **what**. Most code needs no comments — use good naming.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Code Comments

  code into its own well-named, documented function instead.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Code Comments

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Structured Logging
text:
Use structured fields with the `tracing` crate. Never use string formatting for
log data.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Structured Logging > Rules
text: - **Structured fields only** — data goes in fields, not format strings.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Structured Logging > Rules
text: - **No prefixes** — no `[Module]` tags; instrumentation scope provides context.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Structured Logging > Rules
text: - **No mixing** — don't combine structured fields with format args.

head: Cadmus — Agent Coding Conventions > Structured Logging > Async spans across `.await`
text:
On Tokio worker tasks, do not hold a [`tracing::Span::enter()`](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing/struct.Span.html#method.enter)
guard across an `.await`: the guard is not `Send` and the span can leak into
unrelated work while the task is parked. Prefer
[`.instrument(span)`](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing/trait.Instrument.html)
on the future (or `#[tracing::instrument]` on the async fn) so the span is
active only while that future polls.

head: OpenFOIA > Mission
text: OpenFOIA exists so that anyone, anywhere, can investigate power safely.

head: OpenFOIA > Mission
text: FOIA is an American privilege. Most of the world has no legal right to demand information from their government. Even where it exists, the act of asking can be dangerous. This project is for the journalist in Istanbul investigating corruption, the researcher in Nairobi tracking government contracts, the citizen in São Paulo following public money. Local-first. Offline-capable. Purgeable. Free.

head: OpenFOIA > Mission
text: Every coding decision flows from this: **the user's safety comes first.** If a feature leaks data, warns too late, or overpromises security — that's not a bug, it's a betrayal of the mission.

head: OpenFOIA > Principles
text: 1. **Data never leaves the machine unless the user explicitly chooses.** No silent cloud calls. No analytics. No telemetry. Warn before any network request.

head: OpenFOIA > Principles
text: 2. **Work offline by default.** Every core feature must work with zero internet. Network features (crossref, MuckRock, cloud AI) are opt-in enhancements.

head: OpenFOIA > Principles
text: 3. **Be honest about what we protect and what we don't.** Read `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md`. Never say "no traces" — say exactly what's cleaned and what isn't.

head: OpenFOIA > Principles
text: 4. **The tool works on a $300 laptop.** Core install is ~30MB. Heavy deps (GLiNER, PyTorch) are optional. The regex fallback always works.

head: OpenFOIA > Principles
text: 5. **A human and an AI agent use the same interface.** CLI commands and agent tool calls hit the same code paths, same database, same privacy guarantees.

head: OpenFOIA > Key Patterns
text: - **Optional deps are lazy-imported** inside functions. Missing dep → show `openfoia install-extras <name>`. Never crash at import time.

head: OpenFOIA > Key Patterns
text: - **All data paths go through `get_data_dir()`** — respects `OPENFOIA_DATA_DIR` and portable mode.

head: OpenFOIA > Key Patterns
text: - **Config uses `_default_config_path()`** — also respects portable mode. Never hardcode `~/.openfoia/`.

head: OpenFOIA > Key Patterns
text: - **Entity extraction has 4 tiers**: LLM → GLiNER → spaCy → regex. Each falls back. Regex always works.

head: OpenFOIA > Key Patterns
text: - **No password hashes in config.** Duress mode uses SQLCipher as verifier.

head: OpenFOIA > Key Patterns
text: - **Crossref warns before network calls.** Distinguish "no results" from "API error."

head: OpenFOIA > Common Tasks
text: - **New CLI command**: add to `cli.py` under the appropriate `*_app` typer group

head: OpenFOIA > Common Tasks
text: - **New records adapter**: `openfoia/records/<name>.py`, implement `RecordAdapter`, register in `__init__.py`

head: OpenFOIA > Common Tasks
text: - **New gateway**: `openfoia/gateways/<name>.py`, implement `DeliveryGateway`

head: OpenFOIA > Common Tasks
text: - **Schema change**: update `models.py`, then `alembic revision --autogenerate`

head: OpenFOIA > Common Tasks
text: - **Release**: branch `release/X.Y.Z`, bump `pyproject.toml` + `__version__`, add `## [X.Y.Z]` to `CHANGELOG.md`, PR to `main`. Merging publishes the release — see `docs/RELEASING.md`

head: OpenFOIA > Common Tasks
text: - **Changelog**: add user-visible changes under `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as you go

head: OpenFOIA > Don't
text: - Don't add core deps for optional features — use `[project.optional-dependencies]`

head: OpenFOIA > Don't
text: - Don't send data to external APIs without warning the user

head: OpenFOIA > Don't
text: - Don't store passwords or hashes in config files

head: OpenFOIA > Don't
text: - Don't use `innerHTML` in the web UI — use `textContent` and `createElement`

head: OpenFOIA > Don't
text: - Don't claim security guarantees you can't back up — read `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md`

head: OpenFOIA > Don't
text: - Don't optimize for developer convenience at the cost of user safety

head: AGENTS.md > 核心业务约束
text: - 投票内容先 `strip()`，再按等级 1 到 5 的正则插入顺序匹配。重叠规则中较低等级优先。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心业务约束
text: - 正则使用 `pattern.match()`，不是 `fullmatch()`；默认表达式 `^1$`～`^5$` 才是精确匹配。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心业务约束

head: AGENTS.md > 核心业务约束

head: AGENTS.md > 核心业务约束
text:
- niconico 模式将默认等级人数计算为：
  ```text
  max(初始人数, 实际总票数) - 其他四个等级的实际票数
  ```
  结果不得小于 0。当前 GUI 表格仍展示原始投票，补票计算发生在 `web_server.publish_vote_snapshot()`；若增加其他结果视图或导出路径，必须复用同一口径。

head: AGENTS.md > 核心业务约束
