head: Repository Guidelines > Documentation Guidelines
text: - In documentation page introductions, including `DocsPageLead` and opening paragraphs, focus on why the feature is useful, the problems it solves, and representative use cases. Keep implementation steps, configuration details, exhaustive capability lists, and API explanations in the examples and API sections instead of front-loading them in the introduction.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Follow the API naming, lifecycle, state-management, and rendering patterns of the closest existing Blazorise components before introducing a new pattern.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Keep component declarations in the established Blazorise order used by nearby components: events when applicable, members, constructors, methods, and properties. Within methods, place lifecycle overrides before class/style builders, invalidation overrides, event handlers, and private helpers; within properties, place overrides, internal or derived state, and builder-backed names before injected, parameter, and cascading properties.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Resolve provider-generated class names and styles through `ClassBuilder` and `StyleBuilder` build callbacks. Do not call `ClassProvider` or `StyleProvider` directly from rendered class-name or style-name getters; initialize builders for secondary elements in the constructor, expose their `.Class` or `.Styles` result, and invalidate them from `DirtyClasses` or `DirtyStyles` as appropriate.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - When parameters synchronize derived state, prefer `SetParametersAsync` with `ParameterViewExtensions` for coordinated change detection, especially across several parameters. Use change-detecting parameter setters only for simple, independent local transitions where they are clearer, and resynchronize supplied mutable complex parameters unless value equality is guaranteed.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - When renaming a component parameter while retaining the old name as an obsolete compatibility alias, proxy the alias directly to the canonical parameter (for example, `get => Text; set => Text = value;`). Do not introduce a separate backing field or an `Effective{Name}` member solely for the alias. Supplying both parameter names in the same render is unsupported; do not define precedence between them.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Maintain a single owner for component state. Descendants should consume parent state through cascading state rather than expose parameters that can create conflicting states.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Route user interaction, public methods, parameter updates, and two-way binding through the same component lifecycle and event semantics.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Always bind Razor events to named `On{Name}Handler` entry methods. Use `Handle{Name}` for overridable behavior invoked by those handlers. When argument conversion is needed, perform it in the entry method before calling the behavior method. Do not bind events directly to `Handle{Name}`, overload an entry-method name with different argument types, or resolve method-group ambiguity with lambdas or new forwarding members.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Provider-specific component overrides must inherit the closest applicable shared implementation so common behavior is implemented once. Keep provider overrides focused on provider-specific markup, styling, and behavior.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Keep shared component options and service contracts focused on component behavior rather than browser implementation details. Translate them into JavaScript option models, CSS selectors, class names, and DOM properties within the browser interop layer. Do not expose those details through shared component contracts merely because the existing JavaScript implementation requires them.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Add state fields only when their values cannot be derived from existing parameters, lifecycle, or collections. Keep one source of truth, and avoid parallel collections, cached values, and pending-render flags when simple checks or Blazor render coalescing are sufficient.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - For fixed cascading parents that own the child subtree, register children in `OnInitialized` and unregister during disposal; do not track previous parents unless the child can demonstrably survive a parent change.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Keep backing fields only when the raw parameter value and its effective rendered value genuinely differ.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Prefer Razor for component-local markup. Use shared protected `RenderFragment` builders only when common rendering logic requires provider-specific placement.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Avoid additional abstractions and public APIs unless they are required to represent genuinely distinct state or behavior.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Keep static provider styling in SCSS. Use `StyleProvider` only for styles derived from runtime component state.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Keep each CSS provider's SCSS self-contained. Do not import mixins, functions, or styles from the core Blazorise project or another provider. When multiple providers need the same styling helper, copy it into each provider and maintain the local copies independently.

head: Repository Guidelines > Component Development Conventions
text: - Prefer provider-native tokens and variables. Introduce new CSS variables only when necessary and name them according to the provider's established convention.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - Unit tests: xUnit + bUnit (`Tests/Blazorise.Tests`). Match existing naming like `*ComponentTest.cs`.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: - E2E: Playwright + NUnit (`Tests/Blazorise.E2E.Tests`). See `Tests/Blazorise.E2E.Tests/ReadMe.md` for codegen/debug tips and `.runsettings` for headless settings.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines

text: - Branching: target `master` for new work; target `rel-X.Y` for maintenance. Use `dev-*` (features) and `rel-*` (release fixes) branch prefixes.

text:
Known defects and traps in this tree. See `CLAUDE.md` for coding
standards, linters and copyright rules.

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node
text:
Inter-node RDMA over the TCP mesh backend was broken above two nodes.
Every destination GID resolved to one node id, so traffic for nodes 2+
was delivered to node 0 (worker mode) or node 1 (everything else), with
no error anywhere.

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node > What was wrong
text:
`tcp_resolve_node_from_gid()` derived a node id from one octet of the
destination GID by two narrow rules, and its callers substituted a
hardcoded default when neither matched:

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node > What was wrong
text:
The default was constant per instance and independent of the GID, which
is why one run showed three distinct GIDs producing one answer and two
instances disagreeing about which node that was.

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node > What was wrong
text:
Both rules were guesses. One read `raw[15]` as a node id, which only
holds for the synthetic GID built in `tcp_add_gid()` — and nothing calls
`rdma_rm_add_gid()`, so that GID is never registered. The other decoded
an IPv4-mapped GID under a `<subnet>.<(node_id + 1) * 10>` convention,
but [the DHCP pool][pool] allocated sequentially from `.10`, so only the
first node ever matched. The GIDs actually seen in the field were IPv6
link-local, which the first rule rejected outright.

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node > How it works now
text:
Node identity is configured, not inferred. Each instance is told its own
guest RoCE addresses in `ERNIC_TCP_GUEST_GIDS` (comma-separated,
`inet_pton` notation; IPv4 is stored in the `::ffff:a.b.c.d` mapped form
[`adminq_parse_roce_hdr()`][parse] builds). It advertises them over the
mesh as `TCP_MSG_NODE_GIDS` once it knows its node id, the manager fans
each advertisement out to the rest, and peers keep a `GID -> node id`
table keyed by the full 16 bytes.

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node > How it works now
text:
[`tcp_resolve_node_from_gid()`][resolve] is now nothing but an exact
lookup. A miss returns `UINT32_MAX` and the caller fails:
[`tcp_qp_state_rtr()`][rtr] returns `-EINVAL`, which
`rdma_rm_modify_qp()` turns into `-EIO`, and
[the adminq MODIFY_QP path][adminq] fails the command with the full GID
in the log. **Do not reintroduce a default peer**: a wrong node here is a
silent write into another guest's memory that nothing downstream catches.

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node > How it works now
text:
Deployment side: `service/rocm-ernic-launcher` derives each instance's
IPv6 link-local GID from its MAC, which is what a guest autoconfigures.
Override with `ERNIC_GUEST_GIDS_<n>` when the guest also carries a static
address peers will target. An address not listed is unreachable.

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node > How it works now
text: Covered by `tests/test_tcp_gid_resolve.c`.

head: Notes for agents > Fixed: the TCP backend resolved every GID to the same node > Reproducing the original failure
text:
Needs a minimum of three nodes. The `-T` TAP plus bridge setup is
required; without it the run never reaches the data path.

head: Notes for agents > Trap: the mesh has no Ethernet or DHCP path
text:
Guest TCP/IP rides the host TAP/bridge ([`ionic_eth_net.c`][ethnet] is a
plain TAP open/send/recv). The mesh carries only `TCP_MSG_IONIC` plus
control traffic.

head: Notes for agents > Trap: the mesh has no Ethernet or DHCP path
text:
It used to also carry raw Ethernet frames and relay DHCP, but nothing
ever sent either — both were handled and never originated. That dead code
is gone, along with `src/net/dhcp_server.c` and `src/net/eth_rx_inject.c`.
Their message ordinals survive as `TCP_MSG_RESERVED_18..20`: the wire
protocol has no version negotiation beyond a magic number, so renumbering
what follows would silently misparse against an unupgraded peer.

head: Notes for agents > Trap: the mesh has no Ethernet or DHCP path
text:
If you need guest-visible networking, the TAP/bridge is the path. Do not
rebuild a second one inside the mesh.

head: Notes for agents > Adjacent issues

head: Notes for agents > Adjacent issues
text:
- A registration wall at roughly 40 nodes. The number is measured on a
  64-node run; the full-mesh connection-cost mechanism behind it was
  inferred from socket counts and a slot-freeing experiment and is
  **not** confirmed against the code.

head: Notes for agents > Adjacent issues
text:
- Node ids are assigned monotonically, so they are not stable across
  runs.

head: Notes for agents > Adjacent issues
text:
- **A mesh node can hang on shutdown.** A worker sent SIGTERM logs
  `TCP backend: Cleaning up` and then blocks in `tcp_fini()` on a futex
  with its threads still alive — a join against a thread that never
  returns. The process survives SIGTERM indefinitely and needs SIGKILL.
  Only the TCP backend does this; a loopback server exits cleanly, which
  is why `tests/test_ionic_ci.sh` can `kill` and `wait` while
  `tests/test_tcp_mesh_ci.sh` has to bound its cleanup and escalate.
  Anything that stops a mesh node — a test harness, systemd, `docker
  stop` — pays a full termination timeout per node.

head: Notes for agents > Adjacent issues
text:
Note that nodes are never evicted from `mesh_nodes` — a dead node is
marked `is_alive = false` and reconnects under the same id — so the GID
table has no removal path by design. A returning node re-advertises and
replaces its own entries.

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: Provider implementations live in `internal/provider/<platform>/` and realize the API types as actual device configuration. Follow the `internal/provider/openconfig/` package as the reference implementation.

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: - One `.go` file per API resource (e.g. `interface.go`, `banner.go`, `device.go`)

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: - Each file contains: the provider interface implementation for that resource, plus all Go structs and helpers needed to realize it

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: - Keep it simple — avoid many small few-line functions and abstractions that don't serve a real purpose (YAGNI)

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: - Use string constants for any value used more than once — no raw string literals scattered across the code

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: **Idempotency is mandatory:**

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: A provider's `EnsureX` methods must be safe to call on every reconciliation without causing unnecessary device writes. After initial configuration, repeated calls must result in "configuration is already up to date" — no gNMI Set requests unless an actual drift exists.

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: The `gnmiext` package already implements a Get-and-Check approach: it diffs current device state against the desired configuration and only performs a gNMI Set when a real change is needed. This makes it safe for periodic reconciliation.

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: **Platform default values — critical pitfall:**

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: Optional fields in the API spec that map to optional fields in the provider Go struct require special handling:

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 1. If a field is unset in the API spec, the provider must adopt the platform's known default value in the struct (not leave it zero/empty)

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 2. Only overwrite with the API spec value when explicitly set by the user

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 3. This prevents false diffs: without this, the device returns its default → diff sees `"" != "default"` → unnecessary Set on every reconcile

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: **The `omitempty`/`omitzero` trap:**

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: Using `omitempty` or `omitzero` JSON struct tags on gNMI payload structs is dangerous for the same reason. An omitted field means "don't set this" in the gNMI payload, which is correct on first write. But on subsequent reconciles:

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 1. Device returns platform defaults for those fields in the Get response

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 2. The desired struct has those fields empty/zero (omitted from serialization)

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 3. Diff compares device state (with defaults) against desired (without) → mismatch

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 4. Operator performs a Set on every reconcile — breaking idempotency

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: **`omitempty` guidelines:**

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 1. **Safe:** The field's Go zero value matches the platform default or "absent" state. Omitting it from the payload is semantically equivalent to the device's default.

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 2. **Safe:** The field is a pointer or slice representing "not configured" (nil) vs "configured" (non-nil). Mutually exclusive choices (e.g. `accept`/`drop`) fall into this category.

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 3. **Dangerous:** The platform default is non-zero (e.g. `admin-state` defaults to `"enable"`, `port` defaults to `49`). Omitting the Go zero value would either misrepresent intent or cause a false diff on subsequent GET responses.

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: 4. **Unnecessary:** The field is unconditionally set to a non-zero value by the provider code. The tag never triggers, but removing it documents intent — the field is always present.

head: AI Agent Guide > Provider Implementation
text: **Rule:** After setting configuration once, the provider must produce no gNMI Set calls on subsequent reconciles when no user-facing configuration has changed. Test this explicitly.

head: STruC++
text: STruC++ is an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text to C++14 compiler written in TypeScript.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
These rules are identical in every Autonomy repository and are maintained in the MisterFlow plugin
(`Autonomy-Logic/skills`, `plugins/autonomy/harness/repository-rules.md`). Change them there, not here.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
- Tracked work starts with `autonomy:misterflow`: load it yourself before changing product code, fixing a
  bug, implementing or preparing a PR, even when no Jira key was mentioned. Only answering questions and typo or wording fixes that
  change no behaviour are exempt. "There is no ticket" or "skip the process" does not make product
  work untracked: offer to create the task instead of changing code. This file describes only this
  repository's commands, architecture and code conventions; for process, MisterFlow and the Confluence
  process pages win over anything written here.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
- Knowledge boundary: when data is missing or uncertain, say there is not enough information to answer
  reliably. Never fill a gap with a plausible assumption. Keep verified facts, inferences and missing
  data visibly separate, and say which is which.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text: - Language: answer in the developer's language. Jira, Confluence and GitHub text is always English.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
- Branches: `feature/<KEY>-<slug>` for demands and `bugfix/<KEY>-<slug>` for bugs, created from the
  integration branch named below. A production hotfix is a `bugfix/<KEY>-<slug>` branch from `main` and
  a PR. Never commit or push directly to the integration branch or `main`. One Jira key per branch: work
  for another key starts on its own branch before any edit. The key goes in the branch name and the PR
  title, never in commit messages, code or comments.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
- Commits: never commit on your own initiative. Propose the commit at a natural checkpoint, such as a
  finished and verified plan phase, and make it only after the developer confirms. Commit and push are
  separate commands, each confirmed on its own, never chained; opening a PR and merging each need their
  own confirmation too. When asked for a commit message or a commit, do not edit files you were not
  asked to change: report problems, such as a forbidden comment, and let the developer decide.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
- Scope: a rewrite or refactor beyond the current task is a new demand, proposed as a separate task and
  never mixed into the current branch. Never stash, reset, `checkout -- .` or otherwise discard the
  developer's changes, and never install anything outside the repository, without asking.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
- Tests: every demand ships with unit tests, an end-to-end test and a manual test by the developer, with
  evidence for each before any PR is opened, a draft PR included. Where this repository has no
  interface of its own, the end-to-end test runs through the interface or protocol that uses it. A
  repository with no code to unit test, such as documentation or local tooling scripts, uses its own
  validation checks in place of unit tests.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
- Typing: `any` in TypeScript and `typing.Any` in Python are forbidden. Use concrete types, or `unknown`
  or `object` narrowed where the data enters.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text:
- Comments: technical and minimal, at most 256 characters each; formal API documentation (JSDoc,
  docstrings, Doxygen) may be longer. Never write business rules, product strategy or rationale, Jira
  keys, names of people or customers, internal links or anything sensitive in a comment. Review the
  comments in the changed files before every commit.

head: STruC++ > Autonomy development rules
text: Integration branch: `development`. Jira project: `RTOP`.

head: STruC++ > Build & Development Commands > C++ Compilation Tests
text: Tests that compile generated code (for example `tests/integration/cpp-compile.test.ts`) require `g++` (C++14). A skip is not a pass: run them with g++ installed before a PR.

head: STruC++ > Architecture
text: Multi-pass compilation pipeline:

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `src/frontend/` - Lexer (`lexer.ts`), Parser (`parser.ts`), AST definitions (`ast.ts`, `ast-builder.ts`)

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `src/semantic/` - Symbol table (`symbol-table.ts`), type registry, type checker

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `src/backend/` - C++ code generation (`codegen.ts`, `type-codegen.ts`)

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `src/il/` - Instruction List detection, parsing and IL-to-ST transpilation

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `src/library/` - Library manifest, compiler, loader and CODESYS import

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `src/testing/` - Test model and parser for the ST testing framework

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `src/project-model.ts` - CONFIGURATION/RESOURCE/TASK parsing

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `src/runtime/include/` - Header-only C++ runtime library (IEC type wrappers)

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `tests/` - Test suite organized by compiler phase

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `docs/` - Architecture, CLI, compliance, testing, and runtime documentation

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Key Directories
text: - `vscode-extension/` - VS Code extension (client, language server, own tests)

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Parser Framework
text: Uses Chevrotain for lexing and parsing. Parser configuration: `maxLookahead: 3`, recovery mode enabled.

head: STruC++ > Architecture > Code Generation Output
text: Generates two files: `.cpp` (implementation) and `.hpp` (header). All generated code uses `strucpp` namespace. Variables use `IECVar<T>` wrapper for forcing support.

head: STruC++ > Implementation Status
text: Supported features and known gaps are tracked in `docs/IEC_COMPLIANCE.md`.

head: STruC++ > TypeScript Conventions
text: - Strict mode enabled with all strict flags

head: STruC++ > TypeScript Conventions
text: - AST nodes have `kind` discriminator and `sourceSpan` for location info

head: STruC++ > TypeScript Conventions
text: - Error handling uses `CompileError` objects with line/column info

head: STruC++ > TypeScript Conventions
text: - ESLint (`.eslintrc.cjs`, run on `src/`) sets `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` to `error`

head: STruC++ > Testing Patterns
text: - Unit tests: `tests/{frontend,semantic,backend,il,library,cli}/`

head: STruC++ > Testing Patterns
text: - Integration tests: `tests/integration/`

head: STruC++ > Testing Patterns
text: - ST validation programs: `tests/st-validation/`

head: STruC++ > Testing Patterns
text: - C++ validation: `tests/integration/cpp-compile.test.ts`

head: STruC++ > Testing Patterns
text: - Test file naming: `*.test.ts`

head: STruC++ > Testing Patterns
text: - Coverage: `vitest.config.ts` sets a 75% threshold on lines, functions, branches and statements

head: STruC++ > Testing
text: - Unit tests: `npm test` (single file: `npx vitest run <path>`).

head: STruC++ > Testing
text: - CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs only on pushes and PRs to `main`: lint, `format:check`, typecheck, build, `test:coverage`, the `vscode-extension` tests and bundle, and a binary smoke test. A PR into `development` gets no CI, so run `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm run test:coverage` locally before opening it.

head: STruC++ > Testing
text: - End-to-end: a compiled program run end to end. Existing suites compile ST to C++, build it with g++ and run the binary, for example `tests/integration/library-e2e.test.ts` and `tests/integration/xword-pointer-e2e.test.ts`. They require g++.

head: STruC++ > Testing
text: - The developer's manual test is required for every demand.

head: This is NOT the Next.js you know > UI Components
text:
**Always build UI out of the Shadcn primitives in `src/components/ui/` — never hand-roll an element one of them already covers.**
Before writing markup, check what is there (`Dialog`, `Card`, `Button`, `Input`, `Label`, `Select`, `Tooltip`,
`ContextMenu`, `DropdownMenu`, `Table`, `Tabs`, `Sheet`, `Popover`, `ScrollArea`, `Badge`, `Skeleton`, `Separator`,
`AlertDialog`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Slider`, `Accordion`, `Calendar`, …). Toasts go through `sonner`, images
through `@/components/ui/image` (a `next/image` wrapper with a fallback).

head: This is NOT the Next.js you know > UI Components

  configured in `components.json`: style `radix-nova`, icons from `lucide-react`), not rewritten by hand.

head: This is NOT the Next.js you know > UI Components

text: - For details, lead with the answer, then `---`; otherwise omit it.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety
text: - Answer, explain, review, diagnose, audit, and plan requests are read-only; inspect and report without editing the target.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety
text: - Change, build, implement, and fix requests authorize the smallest in-scope local production and test edits plus non-destructive verification. Documentation, configuration, scripts, generated artifacts, deletion, Docker cleanup, and system changes require current-task authorization; naming the exact non-code target supplies it.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety
text: - Inspect `git status --short` before editing and preserve unrelated or unattributed changes.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety > Consolidated Authorization Requests
text: Before requesting authorization, consolidate every proven need by exact target, action, intent, and impact. Separate conditional needs, do not re-request granted or speculative authority, and request an unforeseen need only when evidence proves its delta and consequence. Keep task authority separate from platform approval.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety > Git Is Read-Only by Default
text: The user owns every Git state change. Without current authorization for an exact operation and target, do not change the index, working tree, refs, remotes, branches, tags, stashes, worktrees, or submodules; do not stage files or use Git to roll back. Resolve a requested mutation read-only first, do not extend its authority, and complete authorized local work without it when it remains unauthorized.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety > Remote Writes and Sensitive Data
text: - A local request does not authorize a remote update; require the exact remote action and target.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety > Remote Writes and Sensitive Data
text: - For GitHub, use `GH_TOKEN`, then `GITHUB_TOKEN`, without exposing either; prefer the API when available, otherwise use `gh`.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety > Remote Writes and Sensitive Data
text: - Never send sensitive data externally, including credentials, private logs or source, personal data, and connection strings; redact it from commands, summaries, and retained artifacts.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety > Remote Writes and Sensitive Data
text: - Do not invoke another Codex task or external review service. Only the policy harness may run isolated, read-only, ephemeral Codex evaluations with synthetic non-sensitive cases and no repository source, logs, or task data; otherwise review in the active task.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety > Destructive and High-Risk Local Actions
text: Before deleting files or data, bulk-editing non-code artifacts, removing Docker containers, or changing global configuration, permissions, or packages, resolve exact targets, impact, and recovery read-only. Confirm unless the user already authorized those targets and recovery is reliable. Reliable recovery requires a verified source with restore steps or deterministic rebuild or download; Git restore needs separate authority.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Authority and Safety > Destructive and High-Risk Local Actions
text: For Docker cleanup, distinguish reproducible images from containers, volumes, and data. An in-scope image proven unused and reproducible needs no further confirmation; the other categories remain unauthorized unless named.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning
text: Evaluate premises that affect correctness, scope, compatibility, safety, or cost. Separate evidence from inference; report contradictory or insufficient evidence and the smallest alternative before acting.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning
text: Before editing, record the goal, boundary, acceptance criteria, and required verification. Inspect only the owners, consumers, contracts, tests, configuration, registrations, precedent, and instructions needed to make the change. For non-trivial work, plan only the ordered steps needed to control dependencies and verification.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning
text:
Before choosing a solution or drafting content, read the relevant context and establish the current responsibilities.
For existing artifacts, prefer applicable capabilities and patterns, adding only what the task requires.
Keep changes at the abstraction and detail appropriate to their surroundings.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Strict Scope and Task-Delta Gate
text: 1. An active task is one independent, verifiable objective including its corrections and follow-ups. Start a new baseline only after completion and an explicit independent objective; when ambiguous, stay read-only and confirm.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Strict Scope and Task-Delta Gate
text: 2. Derive acceptance criteria only from requested outcomes, proven direct prerequisites, and focused regression protection. Do not add cleanup, generalization, consistency work, adjacent fixes, or optional improvements.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Strict Scope and Task-Delta Gate
text: 3. Before a file-changing tool, record original status and relevant diffs, infer the smallest owning paths, and freeze `file -> allowed intent -> unmet criterion`. A named module or path is the maximum boundary, and an allowed file does not authorize unrelated hunks.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Strict Scope and Task-Delta Gate
text: 4. Keep the baseline and boundary through follow-ups, reviews, failures, and verification. Expand only with exact additional path and intent authorization, append without rebaselining, and keep other scope read-only.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Strict Scope and Task-Delta Gate
text: 5. Inspect every path and hunk after each coherent edit batch. Inspect immediately after a formatter, generator, bulk replacement, or any action whose write set is not exact. Before an outside-boundary edit, report its evidence, minimum scope, affected contracts, and consequence of declining it.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Strict Scope and Task-Delta Gate
text: 6. Preserve pre-existing and unattributed changes; do not overwrite, format, remove, roll back, or claim them, and do not infer ownership from baseline absence.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Strict Scope and Task-Delta Gate
text: 7. After the last write, audit the delta against the original baseline and remove only safely separable unnecessary task changes.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Architecture Change Gate
text: Architecture changes include public contracts, SPIs, extension or loading contracts, module dependencies, shared ownership, and changes to `final`, visibility, inheritance, constructors, or signatures at a public or shared boundary. A private internal signature or constructor change is not architectural by itself. Before an architecture edit, report ownership, reuse or delegation, compatibility, and minimum files and tests; confirm materially different choices and always gate an SPI change.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Evidence, Scope, and Planning > Architecture Change Gate
text: If the user rejects a design, stop patching it. Remove only its proven task changes, preserve unrelated work, and redesign from the last confirmed boundary. Use precise edits unless the task authorizes an exact Git restore.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Task Code Size Limit
text: Do not add over 10,000 physical production and test source lines in one active task without explicit authorization. Estimate before writing; recount after generated or bulk output, at 8,000 lines, and after the last write. If the task would exceed the limit, stop and propose the smallest independently verifiable decomposition.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Specialized Workflows
text: Use `$analyze-issue` for issue diagnosis and maintainer replies, `$gen-ut` with `code-implementation` for unit-test generation or coverage, and `$review-pr` for PR correctness, mergeability, CI, or a triggered Formal Review. Complete reviews or recommendations use Formal Review with `### Result`, one `Review Result`, `### Evidence`, and `### Coverage`; Coverage identifies local-only changes. Standalone review is read-only. A missing required specialized Skill uses an equivalent manual checklist; do not install or create one for the task. Optional Skills never waive gates or expand authority or scope.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Change Completion Gate
text: Every authorized code-writing task follows `.codex/context/change-completion.md`, including a restoration or rollback that changes production, test, script, build, generated, or behavior-affecting configuration artifacts.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Functional and Performance Non-Regression Gate
text: Preserve supported behavior outside the exact authorized change. Load the full non-regression rules when a change affects a public or shared contract, crosses owners, or has credible functional or performance risk. Do not benchmark when inspection rules out credible cost growth.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Roles and Boundaries
text: - The `typesafe-ai` skill guides Jev tool selection, request construction, and result interpretation; it does not execute requests.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Roles and Boundaries
text: - Jev MCP executes the actual Jev judgment and returns the result.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Roles and Boundaries
text: - Codex performs deep analysis, code changes, execution, final verification, and Jev result review.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Roles and Boundaries
text: - When Jev MCP is unavailable, Codex is the fallback; the skill is not an MCP substitute.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Routing
text: - Prefer Jev for bounded judgments such as classification, routing, ranking, prioritization, relevance, triage, and quick review.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Routing
text: - Keep code changes, debugging, long-context analysis, multi-step reasoning, exact calculations, command execution, test execution, and high-risk or irreversible operations in Codex.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Routing
text: - For a Jev-suitable task, consult the skill when available before checking MCP.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Routing
text: - Call Jev MCP only when it is installed and its tools are available. Unknown quota or balance allows an initial call for a useful bounded judgment. Later calls still require task suitability.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Routing
text: - If the skill is unavailable but MCP is installed, available, and clear, MCP may be called without installing the skill.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Routing
text: - If MCP is unavailable, the API key is missing or known invalid, or quota or balance is known insufficient, do not call Jev; let Codex handle the task.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Routing
text: - If a Jev MCP call reports insufficient quota, insufficient balance, authentication failure, or rate limiting, do not make further Jev calls during the current task.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Results and Safety
text: - Treat Jev as advisory. It must not edit files, run commands, authorize destructive actions, or replace user confirmation.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Results and Safety
text: - Use the `typesafe-ai` guidance and the task's impact and risk to judge whether a Jev result is reliable.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Results and Safety
text: - If the probability, uncertainty, result meaning, or applicability is unclear, Codex must review the result.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Results and Safety
text: - Before acting, Codex must verify important conclusions with source code, tests, or command output.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Results and Safety
text: - Do not send API keys, passwords, connection strings, or unrelated private source code to Jev.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Results and Safety
text: - Deterministic rules and simple arithmetic do not need Jev.

head: ShardingSphere Codex Development Guide > Jev/Codex Routing > Results and Safety
text: Do not include routine Jev usage feedback in task reports unless the user explicitly requests it.

head: AGENTS.md
text: Guidance for AI agents working in the **Shopsys Platform monorepo**. This file is a signpost: it carries the architecture and always-on rules inline, and links to skills in `.agents/skills/` for the detail. The skills are plain Markdown — follow the links whether or not your agent supports a "skills" mechanism.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview
text: Shopsys Platform is a **monorepo-based e-commerce platform**.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview
text: - **Backend**: Symfony PHP application with PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview
text: - **Frontend Admin**: Server-rendered Twig templates with LESS/CSS and JavaScript

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview
text: - **Storefront**: Next.js/React with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, GraphQL, pnpm

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Overview
text: - **API**: GraphQL Frontend API for backend-storefront communication

head: AGENTS.md > Monorepo Architecture > Package-First Development
text: **Core Principle**: All new PHP business logic MUST be implemented in `/packages/`, NOT in `/project-base/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Monorepo Architecture > Structure
text:
- **`/packages/`** (PRIMARY): Core framework implementation — all PHP classes, business logic, reusable components
    - Framework Bundle (`/packages/framework/`) — main business logic
    - Frontend API (`/packages/frontend-api/`) — GraphQL API
    - Other packages — additional framework components

head: AGENTS.md > Monorepo Architecture > Structure
text:
- **`/project-base/`** (SECONDARY): Application configuration layer
    - Configuration files (`app/config/`)
    - Rare project-specific extensions of package classes
    - Storefront React app (`storefront/`)

head: AGENTS.md > Monorepo Architecture > Decision Guide
text:
**Code goes in `/packages/`**: business logic, entities, facades, repositories, controllers, forms.
**Config goes in `/project-base/`**: service configuration, environment settings, routing.
Think: "Can other Shopsys projects reuse this?" → Yes = `/packages/`, No = `/project-base/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Monorepo Architecture > Decision Guide
text:
> **Note — `project-base/AGENTS.md` and its skills are authored for downstream projects.** `project-base/`
> ships its own `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.agents/skills` to downstream projects (the split publishes
> the `project-base/` subfolder as the standalone `shopsys/project-base` repo). Those are the **canonical,
> project-perspective** copies of the shared skills (codebase-locator/analyzer/pattern-finder,
> research-codebase, create-plan, implement-plan, test-writing, shopsys-architecture, shopsys-commands).
> They say package-first does _not_ apply and treat packages as read-only `vendor/shopsys/` — the opposite
> of the rules here. During monorepo development, follow **this** root file; the same-named skills in
> `.agents/skills/` are thin stubs that read the project-base canonical and apply one shared delta,
> `.agents/skills/monorepo-vs-project/SKILL.md`. `project-base/AGENTS.md` carries a scope guard saying the same.

head: AGENTS.md > Always-on rules
text: - **Package-first** (above): new business logic → `/packages/`; only config and rare extensions → `/project-base/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Always-on rules
text: - **Commands run in Docker**: PHP/Composer/Phing and storefront/pnpm run **inside containers**; git/`make`/system commands on the **host**. **Never start or stop containers yourself** — if they aren't running, ask the user. → `.agents/skills/shopsys-commands/SKILL.md`

head: AGENTS.md > Always-on rules
text: - **After GraphQL changes, run `make generate-schema`** to sync backend and storefront (CI fails if they drift).

head: AGENTS.md > Always-on rules
text:
- **Coding conventions** — reuse-first (DRY/KISS), comments explain _why_, docblocks for non-obvious types, and per-folder visibility/typing:
    - `project-base/` and `utils/`: `final`, `private`, typehints & return types everywhere.
    - `packages/`: `protected` (not `private`), no typehints/return types in entities & data objects, no `final` (except FormType, which requires it) — because these are extended in project-base.
      Full detail → `.agents/skills/coding-conventions/SKILL.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Always-on rules
text: - **Multi-domain/multi-language** is supported by default — consider it when changing entities, forms, and the API.

head: AGENTS.md > Always-on rules
text: - **Commits** — every commit or commit message you produce (incl. amend/reword/split, and commits made on the user's behalf by other skills) follows `.agents/skills/commit-conventions/SKILL.md`: atomic functional units, Shopsys message format, never `Co-Authored-By`. Interactive grouping of the working tree → `/commit`.

head: AGENTS.md > Key Configuration Files

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source
text:
This file is for an AI coding agent (or anyone scripting a build) that needs
to go from a clean checkout to a running app on a real Android device — the
exact commands, and the non-obvious constraints that make the naive path
fail. For what the app *is* and how it's designed, read `README.md` and
`ARCHITECTURE.md` first; this file only covers build/install mechanics.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > The one fact that changes everything: this is NOT an Expo Go app
text:
`app.json`'s `plugins` includes `expo-dev-client`, and this repo has three
**custom native modules** (`modules/bundled-assets`, `modules/ram-monitor`,
`modules/voice-input`) plus `llama.rn` (native LLM inference). None of that
runs inside the generic Expo Go app from the Play Store. Every build must go
through `expo prebuild` to generate a real native Android project, then a
real native build (`expo run:android` or an EAS cloud build) — there is no
`expo start` + "scan QR code with Expo Go" path for this app. If you're
tempted to just run `npx expo start` and expect it to work standalone: it
won't — it only starts the Metro bundler, which a dev-client build (built
via one of the two paths below) then connects to.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Prerequisites
text: - Node.js (any recent LTS; developed against Node 24) and npm.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Prerequisites
text:
- One of:
  - **A local Android SDK + NDK + JDK** (Android Studio installs all three) —
    needed for `expo run:android` (builds and installs directly on a
    connected device/emulator over USB).
  - **No local Android SDK at all** — use the EAS cloud build path instead
    (`eas.json` is already configured; needs an Expo account,
    `npx eas-cli login`, no local toolchain).

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Prerequisites
text:
- A physical Android device with USB debugging enabled and `adb` able to see
  it (`adb devices` lists it), if installing locally rather than via EAS. The
  bounty/project this app targets explicitly requires a real device, not
  just an emulator, for final verification — but an emulator works fine for
  iterating during development.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Compile from source and install (local Android SDK path)
text: Or via the `Makefile` (`make help` lists everything):

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Compile from source and install (local Android SDK path)
text:
**`--clean` on prebuild is not optional after touching `app.json` or its
plugins** (icon, name, any native config). Without it, `expo prebuild` can
leave a stale `android/` project with old values baked in, and a plain
`npm install` will never fix that — it never touches `android/` at all.
When in doubt, `--clean`.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Compile from source and install (local Android SDK path)
text:
`make setup` is the interactive wizard for humans (`scripts/setup.mjs`); an agent
should use the explicit commands above instead. It reads answers from stdin, so it
can be scripted if needed (e.g. `printf '2\n1\n' | node scripts/setup.mjs`).

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Release APK (no Metro needed)
text:
`plugins/withReleaseSigning.js` signs it with the key named by
`BOAR_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE`, `BOAR_UPLOAD_KEY_ALIAS`, `BOAR_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD`
and `BOAR_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD` in `~/.gradle/gradle.properties` (never in the
repo). Without them the release build is debug-signed, which is fine for your own
phone. An APK signed with a different key can't install over an existing BOAR:
Android requires uninstalling first, which deletes the app's downloaded models.
A first release build takes about 40 minutes.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > No local Android SDK: build via EAS instead
text:
or `make build-eas`. This produces a downloadable `.apk` (see `eas.json`'s
`preview` profile) — download it and `adb install <file>.apk`, or transfer it
to the device directly.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > After install: the app is not immediately usable — one more step
text:
First launch shows a **mandatory, one-time setup screen** that downloads the
default model (Qwen2.5-1.5B + an embedding model, about 1 GB total) — this is the app's only required network access, and the app is
gated behind it (`ModelManager.requiredModelsPresent()` in
`src/models/ModelManager.ts` decides whether the chat screen or the setup
wizard shows). If you're scripting an unattended install-and-verify flow,
this download has to complete (or you pre-seed the files — see next
section) before the app is otherwise usable. After that first setup, the
app works fully offline.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > After install: the app is not immediately usable — one more step > Skipping the in-app download (pre-seeding models)
text:
If you already have the GGUF weight files on the machine running the build,
you can bake them into the APK itself instead of downloading them at
first-run — see `docs/MODELS.md`'s "Pre-seeding models you already have
locally" section for the exact filenames/checksums and the
`scripts/setup-models.sh` + `assets/models/` + `withBundledModels.js` flow.
This is a genuinely different build path (bundles ~3.2GB into the APK, no
runtime network needed at all), not the default — only use it if avoiding
the in-app download matters for your scenario.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Verifying the build without a device (what an agent without device access can actually check)
text:
Neither of these proves the native build/install actually works — they only
prove the JS/TS layer is internally consistent. There is no way to verify a
real device install without a real device; don't claim success from
typecheck/tests alone if the task was specifically about building/installing.

text:
Run a local CodeRabbit review before every `git push`, in addition to
typecheck and tests:

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Before pushing: CodeRabbit review
text:
`make review` runs the same review with readable output. A review can take
several minutes, so run it in the background. Check each finding against the
current code before acting on it: fix the ones that hold up, and note in one
line why you skipped the others. Re-run once after fixing, not in a loop.

text:
If `cr doctor` says you are signed out, ask the person you're working with to

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Benchmarking models on a connected phone
text:
With a phone on USB, an agent can run the evaluation end to end without anyone
tapping the screen. Full guide: [docs/DEVICE_EVALUATION.md](docs/DEVICE_EVALUATION.md).

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Benchmarking models on a connected phone
text:
- **Check the phone isn't busy.** `eval:device` reloads the app. Don't run it,
  reinstall, force-stop or reload while a model download is in progress
  (`adb shell dumpsys power | grep BOAR:ModelDownload`, or a growing file in
  `adb exec-out run-as team.sopa.aoair ls -l files/models`); downloads can't
  resume after a restart. The phone's owner may be using it: ask first.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Benchmarking models on a connected phone
text:
- **Don't edit app source files while a run is going.** Metro hot-reloads them
  into the running app, which can interrupt the evaluation. Docs and scripts are
  fine.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Benchmarking models on a connected phone
text:
- **Keep the screen on.** Locking the phone backgrounds the app. If the phone
  won't accept `settings put global stay_on_while_plugged_in`, send
  `adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_WAKEUP` every 30 seconds for the length of
  the run, then stop.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Benchmarking models on a connected phone
text:
- **Use `--queries greeting-1` for a quick probe** of a new model (does it load,
  what prompt format does it get) before a full 17-question run.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Benchmarking models on a connected phone
text:
- **Report only what the phone measured.** The JSONL is the source of truth;
  a model that fails to load is recorded as failures, not skipped.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Benchmarking models on a connected phone
text:
To check a Hugging Face GGUF before anyone downloads it, read its header (the
first few MB) for `general.architecture` and `tokenizer.chat_template`: the
architecture must be supported by the llama.rn build in `node_modules`.

text: Full guide: [docs/KNOWLEDGE_PACKS.md](docs/KNOWLEDGE_PACKS.md).

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Building a knowledge pack
text:
- A full level 5 build takes hours (downloading ~50k introductions, then
  embedding); run it in the background and let it resume if interrupted, since

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Building a knowledge pack
text:
- Packs must be embedded with the app's model (`assets/models/embedding.gguf`,
  checked by SHA-256); the app ignores packs built with another one.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Building a knowledge pack
text: - Don't commit `.sqlite` packs to git; they go to a release asset (see the guide).

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Common pitfalls
text:
- **Blank/white screen, or "Failed to connect to `<LAN IP>`" after starting
  Metro**: almost always Wi-Fi client/AP isolation (common on phone hotspots
  and many routers) blocking the phone and dev machine from reaching each
  other, even on the same network. USB debugging isn't affected. Fix: force
  Metro onto the USB `adb reverse` tunnel instead of Wi-Fi —
  `npx expo start --localhost` (or `make start`, which already does this).

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Common pitfalls
text:
- **`ClassNotFoundException: expo.modules.splashscreen.SplashScreenManager`
  in logs**: a red herring — a caught, harmless, expected exception from a
  soft-dependency check inside `expo-dev-launcher`, not a real build
  problem. Don't spend time chasing it.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Common pitfalls
text:
- **A stale `android/` directory causing weird build errors after editing
  `app.json`**: see the `--clean` note above.

head: AGENTS.md — compiling & installing BOAR from source > Common pitfalls
text:
- **Don't run destructive git/native-reset commands to "fix" a build
  problem** (`rm -rf android`, force-pushes, etc.) without checking
  `git status` first and understanding why the build actually failed —
  most build failures here are the two points above, not something that
  needs nuking the repo state.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide
text: Agent context for working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` is a pointer to this file.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Project Overview
text: Awesome Vivaldi is a curated community mod pack for the Vivaldi Browser. It contains CSS and JavaScript modifications that alter Vivaldi's browser chrome UI and add AI-powered features. There is **no build system, no test suite, and no package manager** — this is a collection of static files that are injected directly into Vivaldi's runtime.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Version Targets
text: - **`Vivaldi8.0Stable/`** — Active development (Vivaldi ≥ 7.9). All new work goes here.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Version Targets
text: Each version directory mirrors the same structure: `CSS/` and `Javascripts/`.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Installation
text: Both scripts auto-discover Vivaldi's installation directory, create `user_mods/css/` and `user_mods/js/`, copy all mod files, and inject `injectMods.js` into `window.html`. Re-run after pulling updates — the installer overwrites mod files but preserves user config. Installs from older versions (`.vivaldimods/<version>/`) are detected and migrated automatically.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Installation
text: See `Doc/dev/installer-design.md` for architecture details.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Installation > Dev-Install (headless, for mod development)
text: `dev-install.sh` deploys a single mod to a hardcoded Vivaldi install path **without** the TUI installer. **Local-only script — not tracked in git; edit `VIVALDI_WIN` inside it to match your install.**

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Adding a New Mod
text: 1. JS: create `Vivaldi8.0Stable/Javascripts/<Mod>.js` (plus optional `Vivaldi8.0Stable/CSS/<Mod>.css`).

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Adding a New Mod
text: 2. CSS: add `@import "<Mod>.css";` to `Vivaldi8.0Stable/Import.css` (CSS mods load only via this chain; filenames cannot contain spaces).

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Adding a New Mod
text: 3. Deploy: run the installer TUI (`install.ps1` / `install.sh`) or `./dev-install.sh <Mod>` (local only).

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Adding a New Mod
text: 4. **No `window.html` edits needed** — installer mode discovers `user_mods/js/` dynamically at runtime.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Adding a New Mod
text: 5. AI/Markdown mods: depend on `VividAI.js` + `VividMarkdown.js` (see Shared Core Modules); do not reimplement.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Adding a New Mod
text: 6. Copy the `==UserScript==` / `==UserStyle==` metadata header from an existing mod file (name, description, version `YYYY.M.D`, author, website).

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > CSS Mods → `Import.css`
text: `Import.css` is the single entry point. CSS files are loaded via `@import`:

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > CSS Mods → `Import.css`
text: - Place new `.css` files in `CSS/` and add an `@import` in `Import.css`.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > CSS Mods → `Import.css`
text: - Commented-out imports disable a mod. Abandoned mods are kept as comments.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > CSS Mods → `Import.css`
text: - Vivaldi serves CSS mods via `chrome://vivaldi-data/css-mods/css` — CSS files **cannot have spaces** in their filenames.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > JavaScript Mods → `injectMods.js`
text: **Installer mode (recommended):** `injectMods.js` is injected into Vivaldi's original `window.html` by `install.sh` / `install.ps1`. It dynamically discovers JS mods from `user_mods/js/` via `chrome.runtime.getPackageDirectoryEntry`, loads `ModConfig.js` + `VividAI.js` + `VividMarkdown.js` first, then the rest alphabetically with `async=false` to preserve order. CSS is loaded by injecting `<link rel="stylesheet">` to `user_mods/css/Import.css`.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > JavaScript Mods → `injectMods.js`
text: **Manual mode (legacy):** Users copy `Vivaldi8.0Stable/Javascripts/` contents into Vivaldi's `resources/vivaldi/` directory and replace the browser's original `window.html` with the repo's copy, which lists all `<script>` tags statically. In this mode script order is literal — `VividToast.js`, `VividAI.js`, `VividMarkdown.js` must precede any mod that consumes them.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Inter-Mod Communication → `CustomEvent`
text: Mods communicate via `CustomEvent` dispatched on `document`, **not** via `window.__global` flags (deprecated; removed in the `6347eb7` refactor). Each mod listens for events from other mods and dispatches its own:

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Configuration → `ModConfig.js`
text: `ModConfig.js` is the central settings system. It:

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Configuration → `ModConfig.js`
text: - Injects an "Awesome Vivaldi" section into `vivaldi:settings/appearance/`

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Configuration → `ModConfig.js`
text: - Stores config in OPFS (Origin Private File System) under `.askonpage/config.json`

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Configuration → `ModConfig.js`
text: - Provides import/export for settings portability

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: Two core modules provide reusable AI and Markdown functionality. All AI/Markdown mods **MUST** depend on these instead of implementing their own:

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: **`VividAI.js`** — Shared AI configuration loader and OpenAI-compatible API caller.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividAI.config` — mutable runtime config (apiKey, apiEndpoint, model, etc.)

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividAI.loadConfig({ modKey })` — load from OPFS `config.json`, merge with per-mod overrides

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividAI.applyConfig(raw)` — external config push (via `vivaldi-mod-ai-config-updated` event)

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividAI.streamChat({ messages, signal, onDelta, ... })` — SSE streaming → `{ text, response }`

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividAI.fetchJSON({ messages, ... })` — non-streaming JSON request

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: **`VividMarkdown.js`** — Shared Markdown-to-HTML renderer with LaTeX, code highlighting, table support.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividMarkdown.render(md, hooks?)` — Markdown → HTML. `hooks.blockquote(lines)` for citation injection

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividMarkdown.enhanceCodeBlocks(el)` — add copy buttons + syntax highlight to code blocks

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividMarkdown.splitStable(md)` — streaming: split into committed + preview

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: - `VividMarkdown.cleanModelText(text)` — strip `<thinking>` tags

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: **When developing a mod that needs AI or Markdown:**

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: 1. Call `VividAI.loadConfig({ modKey: "yourModKey" })` in your init

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: 2. Use `VividAI.streamChat()` / `VividAI.fetchJSON()` for all API calls

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: 3. All mods except Diabar **MUST** pass `extra: { thinking: { type: "disabled" } }` to disable model thinking

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: 4. Use `VividMarkdown.render()` for all Markdown rendering; pass `hooks.blockquote` for custom blockquote handling (e.g. citation detection)

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Architecture: How Mods Load > Shared Core Modules
text: 5. Do **NOT** implement your own AI config loading, SSE parsing, or Markdown parser

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > CSS Gotchas
text: - **CSS variables break between Vivaldi versions.** Hardcoded `px` values are safer than `var()` fallbacks. Verify with Computed Styles in DevTools.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > CSS Gotchas
text: - **`!important` is often necessary.** Vivaldi sets many inline styles via JS; `position: fixed !important` or similar overrides are normal.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > CSS Gotchas
text: - **`:has()` is the primary tool for backward DOM selection.** Useful when a later element needs to style an earlier one (common in Vivaldi's DOM order).

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > CSS Gotchas
text: - **CSS Anchor Positioning is unreliable.** Use `left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%)` instead of `anchor-center`.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > JavaScript Gotchas
text: - **window.html scripts run in MV3-like context.** `chrome.scripting.executeScript` works; `chrome.tabs.executeScript` does not.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > JavaScript Gotchas
text: - **MutationObserver must attach to `#browser`** (persistent). Workspace switching rebuilds `.tab-strip`, so re-bind inner observers when the strip is rebuilt.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > JavaScript Gotchas
text: - **Check `tab.url` before injection.** `chrome.tabs.executeScript` throws on `chrome://` / `vivaldi://` pages.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > No Spaces in CSS Filenames
text: Vivaldi's CSS mod loader rejects filenames with spaces. Use `CamelCase.css` or `kebab-case.css`.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > Reaching Vivaldi React Internals via Fiber
text: Some Vivaldi features (e.g. StackEditor, inline rename) can only be triggered through React component methods not exposed in the public API. Walk the React fiber tree from a stable DOM element:

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > Reaching Vivaldi React Internals via Fiber
text: **Known reachable methods (found via `Others/Source/bundle.js` analysis):**

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > Reaching Vivaldi React Internals via Fiber
text:
| Method | Component location | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `setAwaitingEdit(groupId, true)` | Above `.tab-strip` | Opens native StackEditor modal (name + color picker) |

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Key Development Constraints > Reaching Vivaldi React Internals via Fiber
text: **How to discover more:** Search `Others/Source/bundle.js` for the command name (e.g. `COMMAND_RENAME_TAB_STACK`), trace its handler to the React method, then verify the component is reachable via fiber from a stable DOM element like `.tab-strip`.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Vivaldi CSS Variables (summary)
text: Vivaldi exposes theme-aware CSS custom properties on `#browser` (or `:root`). They follow the user's active theme and are safe to use in CSS mods via `var()`. **Record variable names only — values change with theme.** Full reference: `Doc/dev/vivaldi-css-variables.md`.

head: AGENTS.md — Awesome-Vivaldi Repository Guide > Vivaldi CSS Variables (summary)
text: Main series: `--colorBg*` (backgrounds), `--colorFg*` (text), `--colorHighlightBg*` (primary accent), `--colorAccentBg*` (secondary accent), `--colorBorder*`, `--colorSuccess/Warning/Error*` (semantic states), `--radius*`, plus `--colorTabBar`, `--densityGap`, `--scrollbarWidth`, `--monospaceFont`, `--sansSerifFont`, `--uiZoomLevel`. These are Vivaldi's own theme system — do not redefine them, only reference them.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
Canonical instructions for AI coding agents working on **genai-fullstack-blueprint**.
This file is the single source of truth: `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` are thin
pointers to this document — keep guidance here, not duplicated elsewhere.

head: AGENTS.md > Core philosophy: "Built-in over dependencies"
text: Prefer the platform's native capabilities over third-party packages. Concretely:

head: AGENTS.md > Core philosophy: "Built-in over dependencies"
text: - **No `dotenv`** — use `process.loadEnvFile()` / `node --env-file`.

head: AGENTS.md > Core philosophy: "Built-in over dependencies"
text:
- **No `jest` / `mocha` / `chai` / `sinon`** — use native `node:test` and
  `node:assert/strict` with `mock.method()` and `mock.timers()`.

head: AGENTS.md > Core philosophy: "Built-in over dependencies"
text: - **No `ws` / `socket.io`** — handle the HTTP upgrade event manually if needed.

head: AGENTS.md > Core philosophy: "Built-in over dependencies"
text: - **No `express-rate-limit`** — the project ships a native in-memory limiter (`Map`).

head: AGENTS.md > Core philosophy: "Built-in over dependencies"
text: - **No UUID libraries** — use `node:crypto` `randomUUID()`.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository layout
text: Monorepo with npm workspaces:

head: AGENTS.md > Repository layout
text:
- `packages/api` — Node.js (v22+) / Express backend. Runs TypeScript natively
  via `node --experimental-strip-types` (no build step). Clean Architecture.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository layout
text:
- `packages/client` — Angular 22 frontend. Standalone components, Signals,
  zoneless, `@defer`, `inject()`.

head: AGENTS.md > Backend conventions (`packages/api`)
text:
- Clean Architecture: business logic lives in **Use Cases**; controllers are thin
  (map HTTP ⇄ DTO, call a use case).

head: AGENTS.md > Backend conventions (`packages/api`)
text: - Validate **all** boundary input with `zod`.

head: AGENTS.md > Backend conventions (`packages/api`)
text:
- Use `AsyncLocalStorage` (`node:async_hooks`) for `traceId` / observability —
  never thread `traceId` through call signatures manually.

head: AGENTS.md > Backend conventions (`packages/api`)
text: - Prefer `performance.now()` over `Date.now()` for metrics.

head: AGENTS.md > Backend conventions (`packages/api`)
text: - Never leak `syscall` / `path` from native system errors into HTTP responses.

head: AGENTS.md > Backend conventions (`packages/api`)
text:
- Assume external LLM APIs fail: implement graceful degradation and circuit-breaker
  behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Frontend conventions (`packages/client`)
text:
- Modern Angular only: standalone components, Signals (`signal`, `computed`,
  `effect`, `linkedSignal`), `@defer` for lazy loading, `inject()` over
  constructor injection, `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`.

head: AGENTS.md > Frontend conventions (`packages/client`)
text: - Optimize for INP: yield heavy DOM work (`scheduler.yield()`).

head: AGENTS.md > Frontend conventions (`packages/client`)
text: - For Generative UI, use dynamic component loading.

head: AGENTS.md > Frontend conventions (`packages/client`)
text:
- **Streaming render:** never call `signal.set/update` once per raw SSE chunk.
  Chunks arrive in irregular bursts and cause jank. Enqueue characters and drain
  them on `requestAnimationFrame` at an adaptive speed, flushing the queue on
  abort/finish. See the **streaming-render** skill.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: - Backend: native `node:test` (`npm run test --workspace=api`).

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text:
- Frontend: Vitest (`npm run test --workspace=client`). Specs are colocated
  with their source under `src/**/*.spec.ts` (see `vitest.config.ts`).
  TestBed works for service/DI specs and inline-template components;
  external `templateUrl` components cannot be compiled under this JIT setup,
  and signal inputs (`input()`) are not written by JIT-compiled templates,
  so keep component specs template-free or inline-template with plain APIs
  (see `src/test-setup.ts`).

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text:
- When you touch domain/logic, leave a test that covers it. Prefer testing
  domain/util logic without the UI before wiring screens.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing
text: - `npm test` at the root runs both suites.
