head: DovesLapTimer - Project Guide > Continuous Integration
text:
- **arduino-lint.yml** — runs `arduino/arduino-lint-action@v2` at `compliance: specification`
  (Library Manager compatibility level). Uploads `arduino-lint-report.json` as an artifact.

head: DovesLapTimer - Project Guide > Continuous Integration
text:
- **compile-examples.yml** — uses `arduino/compile-sketches@v1` to compile every example
  against a matrix of boards:
  - `arduino:avr:mega` — `sector_timing_example` only (smoke test; the OLED + GPS
    examples are over Mega's SRAM budget — the README itself calls Mega "really
    pushing it", so we only claim the core library compiles on AVR Mega)
  - `arduino:avr:uno` — `sector_timing_example` only (smoke test on small AVR; the other two
    require `Serial1` which the Uno lacks)
  - `esp32:esp32:esp32` — all 3 examples (custom platform URL pulls the ESP32 BSP)
  - `Seeeduino:nrf52:xiaonRF52840Sense` — all 3 examples (recommended hardware; uses the
    Adafruit-based nrf52 core, not the older mbed core, since that's what real XIAO
    users compile against and it matches the FPU/double-precision pitch in the README)
  - Pulled libs: ArxTypeTraits, Adafruit GPS Library, Adafruit GFX, Adafruit SSD1306,
    Adafruit SH110X, Adafruit TinyUSB Library (last one needed so the Seeed nRF52
    BSP's `Serial`/`Adafruit_USBD_CDC` references resolve at link time)
  - Pre-compile step `pip install --user adafruit-nrfutil` runs only on the XIAO
    cell — the BSP's link recipe shells out to it even at compile-only time
  - `enable-deltas-report: true` uploads `sketches-reports/` so PRs surface flash/SRAM deltas

head: DovesLapTimer - Project Guide > Continuous Integration
text:
- **unit-tests.yml** — builds and runs the host-native test suite in `test/`
  on ubuntu-latest with `g++`. No board matrix; the suite is pure C++ and
  doesn't depend on any Arduino toolchain. Fails the run on any failed assert.

head: DovesLapTimer - Project Guide > Continuous Integration
text:
- **docs.yml** — builds Doxygen HTML from `src/` + `examples/` + `README.md` +
  `DETECTION.md` using the doxygen-awesome-css theme vendored under `docs/`.
  On push to master, deploys the output (`docs-build/html/`) to the
  `gh-pages` branch via `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages` (v4, SHA-pinned) with
  `force_orphan: true` (keeps the gh-pages branch lean — overwrites
  rather than accumulating history). On PR, builds-only without
  deploying so we catch a broken Doxyfile before merge. Live site:
  https://theangryraven.github.io/DovesLapTimer/ (GitHub repo Settings →
  Pages must be set to source = gh-pages branch, folder = /).

head: DovesLapTimer - Project Guide > Continuous Integration
text:
- **coverage.yml** — builds the `test/` suite with `g++ --coverage`, runs it,
  and summarizes line coverage of `src/` with `gcovr`. Gated on every PR via
  `make coverage` (fails under `COVERAGE_GATE`, currently **80%** — sits just
  below measured coverage; keep ratcheting it up alongside new tests via the
  `COVERAGE_GATE ?=` line in `test/Makefile`). On push to master it generates

  entirely in-runner). Current line coverage ~84.5% (gate at 80) — every
  module now has direct tests, including `CourseManager`

head: DovesLapTimer - Project Guide > Continuous Integration > Test layers
text:
- **Layer 1 — structural** (`arduino-lint.yml`, `compile-examples.yml`):
  lint pass + every example compiles across the board matrix. Catches
  missing includes, broken API signatures, fatal SRAM/flash overruns.

head: DovesLapTimer - Project Guide > Continuous Integration > Test layers
text:
- **Layer 2 — host unit tests** (`unit-tests.yml`): runs `test/` on the
  host via `make run`. Covers `GeoMath`, `DirectionDetector`,
  `CourseDetector` state machine, `CourseManager` orchestration
  (`test_course_manager.cpp`), `WaypointLapTimer`
  (`test_waypoint_lap_timer.cpp`), `SprintTimer` point-to-point runs over a
  synthetic open course (`test_sprint_timer.cpp` — run times, cancel/restart,
  ignored finishes, 0/1/2 splits, missed-split invalidation),
  a synthetic-track integration
  pass over the full `DovesLapTimer` pipeline, plus regression suites for
  midnight rollover (`test_midnight_rollover.cpp`), adversarial GPS input
  (`test_input_validation.cpp`), crossing-buffer wraparound
  (`test_buffer_wraparound.cpp`), and low-rate GPS crossing detection
  (`test_low_rate_gps.cpp`). Catches algorithm
  regressions that compile fine but produce wrong numbers. See
  `test/README.md` for layout and how to add a suite.

head: DovesLapTimer - Project Guide > Continuous Integration > Test layers
text:
- **Layer 3 — NMEA replay regression** (`unit-tests.yml`, same job): replays the
  four `examples/real_track_data_debug/gps_race_data_*.h` fixtures through the
  lap timer via `test/replay_runner.h` (minimal `$GPGGA` + `$GPRMC` parser, no
  Adafruit_GPS dependency). Asserts the output matches the per-lap DoveTimer
  golden values pinned in each fixture header to ±50ms, plus a ±200ms check
  against MyLaps magnetic-loop times where recorded. Catches interpolation
  regressions on real-world noisy GPS data, not just the clean synthetic track.
  21 replay tests across 4 fixtures. Additionally `test_nmea_sprint.cpp` runs a
  **differential replay**: the 2laps OKC fixture through BOTH the circuit timer
  (full S/F+S2+S3, OKC "Normal" lines from the DovesDataLogger SDCARD JSON) and
  a SprintTimer configured start=S/F, finish=S2 — every recorded lap becomes one
  point-to-point run whose time must equal that lap's circuit sector-1 time to
  ±10ms (two independent accounting layers over the same crossings must agree),
  plus pinned run goldens. Real-data sprint coverage until a true autocross
  fixture exists; note it can't exercise staging stops / cancel-restart (those
  stay synthetic).

text:
> Read this file at the start of EVERY session before touching code.
> These are the load-bearing rules. Breaking one silently is how this project
> rots across sessions. If you must break one, it’s a deliberate, isolated
> increment with its own ADR in DECISIONS.md — never a side effect.

text: 1. New `make demo-<this-increment>` passes.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Session ritual
text: 1. Full `make test` green (every prior demo still passes).

text: 1. If you touched the prompt prefix, re-run the prefix-hash test.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Session ritual
text:
1. **If you touched anything under `desktop/renderer/`, run
   `cd desktop && bun run build-renderer`, then GREP THE SERVED BYTES for a
   marker your change introduced.** `dev.ts bundleApp()` serves the prebuilt
   `desktop/renderer/app.bundle.js` whenever it exists and NEVER compiles from
   source (ADR-0260: Bun must not module-load a `.ts` from a protected install
   dir). So renderer source edits are invisible in the running app until that
   artifact is rebuilt, and no amount of restarting helps. A source typecheck or
   a scratch `bun build` proves the code COMPILES; it proves nothing about the
   bytes the app serves. Verify by fetching `/app.js` and `/styles.css` from a
   freshly booted engine and grepping for a new identifier, plus one retired
   identifier that must be ABSENT. This is the ADR-0303 vacuous-green trap in
   its most expensive form, because everything looks green and the user sees no
   change at all.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Session ritual

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Session ritual

Do not start the next increment in the same session. A half-finished second

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > The architecture in one paragraph
text:
We are building a security/provenance/memory layer **around** oh-my-pi (omp),
not from scratch. The harness is **TypeScript on Bun, in-process with omp**. The
**only** Python is `scanner-sidecar/` (the pure Unicode scanner). We extend omp
through hooks, custom tools, and its SDK. See DECISIONS.md ADR-0001.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Writing style
text:
- **Never use em dashes** (the long dash, Unicode U+2014). Use commas, periods,
  colons, or hyphens instead. This applies everywhere: code, comments, UI strings,
  commit messages, ADRs, and PROGRESS.md.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 1. Extend omp; never fork it.
text:
Prefer a hook or custom tool over any change that would require forking omp.
omp ships hundreds of releases; a fork is permanent merge pain. If you believe
something genuinely cannot be done via hook/tool/SDK, STOP and write an ADR
before forking anything.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 2. The language boundary is fixed.
text:
The harness is TypeScript. The ONLY directory containing Python is
`scanner-sidecar/`. Never add a `.py` file anywhere else. Never reimplement the
scanner in TypeScript. If a second Python surface seems necessary, that’s a
drift signal — stop and write an ADR.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 3. Fail-closed is law.
text:
Any failure to obtain a valid scan result — sidecar dead, malformed response,
timeout, missing id — MUST be treated as “block / quarantine,” never “safe.”
No code path may treat “scan unavailable” as “pass.” There is a test that kills
the sidecar mid-run and asserts the gate blocks; it must stay green forever.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 4. The quarantine gate runs in-process.
text:
The security gate is a `pre` hook inside omp’s runtime. It must not depend on a
network call or a fragile boundary to do its blocking. The scanner (pure, behind
the sidecar) may be out-of-process; the GATE that acts on its output may not.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 5. Untrusted content is always delimited and always late.
text:
All user-provided, retrieved, imported, or externally stored text enters prompts
only inside `UNTRUSTED_CONTENT_START` / `UNTRUSTED_CONTENT_END`, only after
scanning + sanitation, and only AFTER the cache breakpoint (never in the frozen
prefix). The system prompt instructs the model to treat delimited content as
data, never instructions.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 6. The prompt prefix is frozen and byte-stable.
text:
Prompt layers 1–4 (identity/safety, tool-use/permission policy, stable coding
rules, security/trust-boundary rules) are byte-identical across all requests.
Volatile context — date, cwd, git branch/status, env — that omp auto-injects
MUST live in the tail, after the cache breakpoint. Putting volatile bytes in the
prefix busts the KV cache every turn. Verify with the prefix-hash test.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 7. Trust labels are a closed set.
text: Exactly: `trusted | untrusted | suspicious | quarantined`. No other values.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 8. Events use exact names.
text:
Every logged event uses a name from the `EventName` enum in `contracts.ts`.
Emitting an unknown event name must raise. Every event carries `run_id`,
`session_id`, and `artifact_id` when an artifact is in scope.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 9. Stable IDs everywhere.
text:
Every run, finding, and approval has a stable string `*_id`. Reuse omp’s
Snowflake session/run IDs; mint your own for findings/approvals. IDs are never
regenerated for the same logical entity.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 10. DuckDB schema freezes on first write.
text:
Schema changes only ever happen through numbered migration files. Never edit a
table definition in place. The schema is a frozen contract.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 11. UI text is never cramped into wrapping columns.
text:
Readability is load-bearing. Any list/grid of rows (providers, models, settings,
tiles, chips) MUST keep each row's primary label on one line: the label takes the
space and ellipsizes on overflow (`white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden;
text-overflow: ellipsis`); it NEVER mid-word wraps inside a narrow column.
Secondary chips/badges are `white-space: nowrap`. Grid tracks use a generous
`minmax()` (about 220px or more) so labels do not fold; when content will not fit,
use fewer/wider columns or a single column, NEVER a fixed narrow multi-column grid
that word-wraps its text into unreadable slivers. If a label can be long, widen the
column or truncate it with a tooltip. This applies to every panel, popup, and
mockup (a mockup that word-wraps is a design bug, not a rendering artifact).

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Invariants (do not violate) > 11. UI text is never cramped into wrapping columns.
text:
The #1 cause is a FLEX container holding prose: `display: flex` makes every raw
text run AND every inline element (`<b>`, `<a>`, `<code>`) its OWN flex item, so a
sentence with bold phrases shatters into narrow stacked columns. A flex row MUST
therefore contain a SINGLE text child: give a leading icon `flex: none` and wrap the
message in ONE element, OR (preferred, as `.set-note` does) absolutely-position the
icon and let the text flow as a normal BLOCK paragraph. NEVER place raw text plus
inline tags directly as siblings inside a flex box. And mockups MUST reuse the real
component CSS (or copy it verbatim) - a hand-rolled divergent style that flexes
prose is this same bug wearing a costume, which is exactly how it slipped back in.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Licensing & commit hygiene
text:
Every first-party source file under `harness/`, `desktop/`, `tools/`, and
`scanner-sidecar/` carries the BUSL-1.1 SPDX header (`Copyright (c) 2026 TechLead
187 LLC` + `SPDX-License-Identifier: BUSL-1.1`; `#` for Python). This is enforced
two ways and you must keep both working:

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Licensing & commit hygiene
text:
- A **pre-commit hook** (`.githooks/pre-commit`) auto-applies the header to staged
  source. Run **`make install-hooks` once per clone** to activate it — git cannot
  self-install hooks on clone, so a fresh checkout (yours or a collaborator’s) has
  NO hook until this runs. `make install` runs it for you.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Licensing & commit hygiene
text:
- **CI** runs `tools/license_headers.ts --check` as a backstop, so nothing
  unheadered can land on master even if the hook was never installed.

head: AGENTS.md — Invariants > Licensing & commit hygiene
text:
Vendored / generated trees (`vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `desktop/release/`,
`.venv`, `__pycache__`, `dist/`) keep their own licenses and are NEVER
relicensed. New first-party files get the header automatically (hook) or via
`make license-headers`. When adding the header in code, read the file then write —
never `existsSync`-then-read (CodeQL flags that pair as a TOCTOU race).

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Project Overview
text: GitProxy is a Git HTTP proxy that intercepts Git operations (primarily `git push`) and enforces organizational policies before allowing changes to reach the actual Git host.

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Project Overview
text: - A **policy enforcement engine** (via processors and plugins)

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Project Overview
text: - A **review/approval gate** (manual or automated)

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Project Overview
text: - A **proxy server** for Git operations

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Project Overview
text: - A **UI + API layer** for reviewing, approving, and auditing pushes

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Project Overview
text: The core design principle is a **chain-of-processors architecture** where each Git action flows through ordered processing steps.

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Build & Run
text: **Stack:** TypeScript, Node >=22, Express 5, React 16, Vitest 3, NeDB / MongoDB

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > High-Level Architecture > 1. Proxy Server (`/src/proxy`)

text: - Parses requests into an `Action`

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > High-Level Architecture > 1. Proxy Server (`/src/proxy`)
text: - Executes the appropriate **Action Chain**

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > High-Level Architecture > 1. Proxy Server (`/src/proxy`)
text: - Blocks, rejects, or queues for approval

text: - **Action** — Represents a Git operation (push/pull/default)

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > High-Level Architecture > 1. Proxy Server (`/src/proxy`)
text: - **Chain** — Ordered list of processors

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > High-Level Architecture > 1. Proxy Server (`/src/proxy`)
text: - **Processor (Step)** — A single policy enforcement unit

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > High-Level Architecture > 1. Proxy Server (`/src/proxy`)
text: - **Plugin** — Custom processor injected externally

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Core Architectural Model > Action Lifecycle (Push)
text: 1. `parseAction` classifies request

text: **Order matters.** Some processors depend on artifacts created by previous ones (e.g., cloned repo, computed diff).

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Core Architectural Model > Processor Rules

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Core Architectural Model > Processor Rules

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Core Architectural Model > Processor Rules

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Tool Integration > Database changes
text: The fs, mongo and postgres sink backends must stay at feature parity. Before changing anything under `src/db`, read `.agents/skills/sink-parity/SKILL.md`: apparently simple adaptor changes usually cost more on the postgres side (explicit columns, update allowlists, append-only schema migrations) than on the document stores, and the skill carries the checklist that keeps the backends aligned.

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Agent Workflow
text: **The main agent must act as an orchestrator.** Never do work inline that can be delegated to a subagent.

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Agent Workflow
text: - **Delegate everything:** Use the Task tool with specialized subagents for all research, code exploration, code writing, testing, and analysis. The main agent should plan, coordinate, and summarize — not do the work itself.

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Agent Workflow
text: - **Maximize parallelism:** Launch multiple subagents concurrently whenever their tasks are independent. For example, when exploring code patterns AND analyzing tests AND checking dependencies, spawn all three agents in a single message rather than sequentially. Always send independent Task calls in a **single message** with multiple tool-use blocks.

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Agent Workflow
text: <!-- - **Use the right agent type:** Pick `Explore` for codebase search/understanding, `Plan` for architecture decisions, `Bash` for commands, and specialized agents (e.g., `code-reviewer`, `test-automator`, `debugger`) when they match the task.

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Agent Workflow
text: - **Keep the main context clean:** Offload large file reads, multi-file searches, and deep analysis to subagents so the main conversation stays focused on coordination and user communication.

head: AGENTS.md — GitProxy > Agent Workflow
text: - **Hooks run automatically — use subagents to respond:** When a hook (Spotless, build verification, code review, or simplification) reports an issue, delegate the fix to a subagent rather than doing it inline. If multiple hooks fail simultaneously, spawn parallel subagents to address each issue concurrently. -->

  `armsim out.s` 手动执行；`ARMSIM_TRACE=1 armsim out.s` 可逐指令跟踪。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 架构要点（改动前必读）
text:
管线：**词法/文法 → AST →（constexpr 折叠 +）IR 生成 → IR 优化 → ARM32
指令选择 + 线性扫描分配 → 汇编文本 → armsim 执行**。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 架构要点（改动前必读）
text:
1. **原生 IR 类型**：64 位（`long long`）与浮点（`float`/`double`）都是
   原生 IR 类型，通过 `IR::ty`（`TypeInfo`）承载，而不是前端降级成
   32 位拼接。宽度 8 的整数运算在后端用寄存器对（低半用本名、高半用
   `name + "#h"` 的独立分配区间）；将来 ARM64 直接映射原生指令。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 架构要点（改动前必读）
text:
2. **值规范表示**：宽度 ≤4 的整型一律按「扩展到 32 位」的规范形式保存在
   寄存器/栈槽；窄化发生在赋值/初始化/传参/返回边界（`convert_runtime`）。
   浮点常量在编译期以 IEEE 位模式复用 `int64_t` 通道（float = 低 32 位
   零扩展的位模式，double = 全 64 位），见 `type.h` 的 `convert_const`
   三参重载与 `const_to_double`/`double_to_const_bits`。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 架构要点（改动前必读）
text:
3. **浮点 = VFP 独立寄存器池**（`assembly/generate/context.h`）：s0–s15
   caller-saved、s16–s27 callee-saved、s28–s31 草稿；double 占偶对齐的
   连续两个 s 寄存器。与核心池平行的分配函数都以 `freg`/`fp` 命名。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 架构要点（改动前必读）
text:
4. **双池调用约定**：整型参数走 r0–r3/栈；浮点参数走 s 槽位（float 1 槽、
   double 2 个连续偶对齐槽，≥16 溢出到 `stack_size[0]` 区域）。
   `SET_ARG` 用 `ir.label == "vfp"` 标记 VFP 池；形参入口相应为
   `$argN` / `$fargN`。变参调用（printf/putf）按 C 默认实参提升，
   float → double 后以位模式走核心池。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 架构要点（改动前必读）
text:
5. **armsim 的 native_table 就是 Windows 下的 SysY 运行时**（getint/
   putint/putf/printf、`__aeabi_*` 等）。刻意**没有** `getlong`/`putlong`
   与 `getfloat`/`putfloat`——64 位/浮点 I/O 一律用两个 `getint` 拼接或
   `printf("%f")`；测试也遵守该约束。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 架构要点（改动前必读）
text:
6. 浮点比较的语义（NaN 无序）由后端把 `CMP` 与相邻的 `Jcc`/`MOVcc`
   **融合**实现（见 generate.cpp 的 `ir_fp(ir)` 分支）；IR 层的浮点条件
   统一先归一化为 0/1 谓词再跳转（eval.cpp `_eval_cond_runtime` 的 fp
   分支）。改动 CMP/Jcc 相邻性时务必保持这一约定。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 架构要点（改动前必读）
text:
`OpName` 命名前缀：`%` 局部变量、`@` 全局变量、`$argN`/`$fargN` 实参、
`%&`/`@&` 数组基址、`^` 导出不重命名；`#h` 后缀是 64 位值的高半。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 已知文法/语义限制（不是 bug，测试时绕开）
text:
- `long long` ↔ 浮点互转不支持（ARM32 无直接指令，需 `__aeabi_l2d` 类
  辅助，编译器会显式报错）。

head: AGENTS.md — syc 编译器项目指南 > 已知文法/语义限制（不是 bug，测试时绕开）
text:
- `float` 运算遵循 IEEE 单精度舍入，`double` 遵循双精度；整数除零在
  运行时 fatal，浮点除零按 IEEE 得 inf/nan。

head: artoolkitX — Agent Guide > Conventions & Patterns
text: - **Language and style**: C99 for core AR algorithms; C++14 for the controller/tracker layer; Java for the Android wrapper. For C, use K&R style. For C++, follow the Google C++ style guide. Always wrap branches in braces, unless part of a switch block.

head: artoolkitX — Agent Guide > Conventions & Patterns
text: - **Naming**: `AR` prefix for C symbols; `ARX` prefix for the C++ layer; `arx` prefix for C API functions exposed externally.

head: artoolkitX — Agent Guide > Conventions & Patterns
text: - **Error handling**: Return codes (`AR_E_*`), not exceptions. C++ layer logs via `ARLOGx()` macro where x is the log level (e=error, w=warning, i=info, d=debug).

head: artoolkitX — Agent Guide > Conventions & Patterns
text: - **CMake options**: Feature flags are `option()`-declared in the top-level CMakeLists. Platform guards use `ARX_PLATFORM_NAME`.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text:
RiceVM is a Dis virtual machine and Limbo compiler in Rust. The Dis VM is a register machine that executes bytecode compiled from the Limbo
programming language. The project includes a built-in Limbo compiler that compiles `.b` source files to `.dis` bytecode without depending on the
reference compiler from Inferno OS. Priorities, in order:

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 1. Correct implementation of the Dis VM specification and Limbo language.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 2. Clean, idiomatic Rust with safe abstractions over VM internals.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 3. Clear separation of concerns across workspace crates.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: 4. Maintainable and well-tested code.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Use English for code, comments, docs, and tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Keep `unsafe` usage minimal and well-documented; prefer safe Rust wherever possible.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Never use `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` in non-test code (enforced by `make lint`). Production code should never panic.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Prefer small, focused changes over large refactoring.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Add comments only when they clarify non-obvious behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Do not add features, error handling, or abstractions beyond what is needed for the current task.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text: - Add tests for every bug fix and new feature to prevent regression.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Rules
text:
- Write the test before the fix, and confirm it fails for the reason being fixed. A test that never failed against the old code proves only that the
  code compiles, which is how several bugs here survived a passing suite: `alt` emitted no code at all,
  `string` of a real produced 0, and a tuple channel delivered zeros. Assert the value or the control flow, not that the call returned. When a fix
  lands before its test, prove the test is real by reverting the fix, watching it fail, and restoring it.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Write in simple, plain English. Use short sentences and everyday words. Keep every fact, name, number, link, and file path.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text:
- Write correct and complete sentences. Start each sentence with a capital letter, capitalize proper nouns (Rust, Limbo, Inferno, and Dis), and leave
  common nouns lowercase in the middle of a sentence.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Avoid made-up words. Use participial phrases and abbreviations sparingly.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Use Oxford commas in inline lists: "a, b, and c" not "a, b, c".

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Do not use em dashes. Restructure the sentence, or use a colon or a semicolon instead.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text:
- Avoid colorful adjectives and adverbs. Write "operand decoding" not "fast operand decoding", and "reference counting" not "careful reference
  counting".

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Prefer noun phrases for checklist items over imperative verbs. Write "frame teardown" not "tear down the frame".

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Do not bold the lead-in of a list item. Write "Pointer maps: ..." not "**Pointer maps**: ...".

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text: - Use sentence case for the lead-in of a list item. Write "Wait records: ..." not "Wait Records: ...". Proper nouns keep their capitals.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text:
- Do not use a colon in place of a verb. Three uses are fine: joining two clauses inside a complete sentence, which is the replacement the em dash
  rule calls for; introducing the gloss of a list item; and introducing an enumeration, whether as a list or inline ("Opcodes: movp, movmp, and
  slicela"). What a colon must not do is turn a sentence into a label and a definition. Write "A cross-module call swaps in the callee's data and
  pushes the caller's" rather than "Cross-module calls: swap in the callee's data". That shape belongs to a list item, and carrying it into prose
  leaves a fragment where a sentence was required.

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text:
- Capitalize only the first part of a hyphenated compound: "Built-in Modules" in a heading, "Mark-and-sweep" at the start of a sentence, and "built-in
  module" elsewhere. Never write "Built-In".

head: AGENTS.md > Writing Style
text:
- Headings in Markdown files must be in title case: "Build from Source" not "Build from source". Minor words stay lowercase unless they are the first
  word: the articles (a, an, and the), the coordinating conjunctions (and, but, or, nor, so, yet, and for), and the short prepositions (in, on, at,
  to, by, of, up, as, from, with, into, and over). That example is why the prepositions are listed: "from" has to be lowercase for "Build from Source"
  to be correct, and an earlier version of this rule stopped at "of", which made its own example a violation.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `crates/ricevm-core/`: Shared types (Module, Opcode, Instruction, TypeDescriptor, and errors). No runtime logic.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `crates/ricevm-loader/`: Binary format parser for `.dis` module files. One public function: `load(&[u8]) -> Result<Module, LoadError>`.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `crates/ricevm-execute/`: Execution engine with 176 opcode handlers, heap, GC, built-in modules ($Sys, $Math, $Draw, $Tk, $Keyring, $Crypt, and
  audio), virtual device files, and file-based module loading.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `crates/ricevm-cli/`: CLI with `run`, `dis`, and `compile` subcommands.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `external/inferno-os/`: Git submodule of the Inferno OS repository (866 pre-compiled `.dis` files, Limbo source, and reference VM source in
  `libinterp/xec.c` for correctness validation).

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `Makefile`: GNU Make wrapper around `cargo` commands (`make test`, `make build`, `make lint`, etc.).

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- `rust-toolchain.toml`: Pinned Rust toolchain (1.97.1) with `rustfmt`, `clippy`, and `rust-analyzer`. Everyone who builds through rustup gets this
  version, which keeps builds and lint output reproducible.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text:
- The workspace's `rust-version` (1.90.0) is the minimum supported version, and it is deliberately lower than the pinned toolchain. It records the
  oldest compiler the code actually builds on, which is what a packager building against a distribution's own rustc needs; edition 2024 puts a hard
  floor at 1.85. Every crate inherits it with
  `rust-version.workspace = true`, so `cargo` refuses an older toolchain up front instead of failing later in the build. Raise it only when something
  in the code needs a newer compiler, and update the first entry of the CI matrices in
  `.github/workflows/lints.yml` and `tests.yml` to match, since that is what keeps the claim tested.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Crate Dependency Graph
text: `ricevm-execute` depends on `ricevm-loader` for runtime module loading (the `load` opcode reads `.dis` files from disk).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Internal Modules in `ricevm-execute`
text:
| Module         | Purpose                                                                                                        |
|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `vm.rs`        | `VmState` struct, execution loop with cooperative threading, and thread suspend/resume                         |
| `frame.rs`     | `FrameStack` with two-phase push (`alloc_pending` and `activate_pending`)                                      |
| `heap.rs`      | `Heap` with reference counting, copy-on-write strings, and `ArraySlice` shared views                           |
| `gc.rs`        | Mark-and-sweep collector (frames, MP, caller MP stacks, loaded module MPs, suspended threads, and `heap_refs`) |
| `address.rs`   | Operand resolution with `ModuleMp` virtual ranges and `decode_virtual_addr`                                    |
| `memory.rs`    | Typed read/write on byte buffers with bounds checking                                                          |
| `data.rs`      | Module data (MP) initialization with type-aware elem sizes and nested arrays                                   |
| `filetab.rs`   | Portable file descriptor table with in-memory pipe, virtual device files, and non-blocking stdin               |
| `ops/`         | 176 instruction handlers organized by category                                                                 |
| `sys.rs`       | Built-in `$Sys` module (43 functions with tuple return support, `%b`, `%u`, and `%.*`)                         |
| `math.rs`      | Built-in `$Math` module (66 functions including linear algebra)                                                |
| `draw.rs`      | Built-in `$Draw` module (SDL2 backend, optional `gui` feature)                                                 |
| `tk.rs`        | Built-in `$Tk` module (widget toolkit with embedded bitmap font and SDL2 rendering)                            |
| `audio.rs`     | `/dev/audio` and `/dev/audioctl` support (cpal backend, optional `audio` feature)                              |
| `builtin.rs`   | `ModuleRegistry` for built-in module registration with name and signature lookup                               |
| `scheduler.rs` | Preemptive thread scheduler infrastructure (not yet connected to main loop)                                    |
| `channel.rs`   | Channel data structure for inter-thread communication                                                          |

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Package names use hyphens (`ricevm-core`); Rust identifiers use underscores (`ricevm_core`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - The heap uses `HashMap<u32, HeapObject>` with monotonic IDs starting at `HEAP_ID_BASE` (0x1000_0000); pointers stored as `Word` (i32) in frames.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Array element references use a `heap_refs` table with `HEAP_REF_FLAG` sentinel, resolved during double-indirect addressing.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- `ArraySlice` heap type provides shared-storage views into parent arrays (required for Bufio buffer semantics); all operations (`cvtac`, `slicela`,
  `pread`, `pwrite`, channel send/recv) resolve slices to their parent.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- `slicela` adjusts reference counts for pointer-containing elements (e.g., `array of string`) to prevent premature freeing during operations like
  mergesort.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- Unified virtual address space: frame addresses are low, each module's MP has a unique range starting at
  `MP_BASE` (0x0080_0000) with `MP_STRIDE` (0x0010_0000) between modules, heap IDs above `HEAP_ID_BASE`. The `decode_virtual_addr()` function decodes
  addresses back to `AddrTarget`.
  `MAX_MODULES` (128) bounds the MP window, leaving a reserved gap below the heap IDs: without it the MP range reaches `HEAP_ID_BASE` and a module's
  data decodes as a heap object. Addresses in the gap, MP offsets past
  `MP_STRIDE`, and frame offsets past `MP_BASE` are rejected rather than silently misrouted.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - `caller_mp_stack` in `VmState` tracks caller module MPs during loaded module execution.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Branch instructions: `if src OP mid, goto dst` (not `if src OP dst, goto mid`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Case instructions (`casew`, `casec`, and `casel`) use binary search matching the reference Dis VM (`xec.c`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - `casel` entries are 24 bytes (not 20) due to LONG alignment padding.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Multi-module execution: loaded modules' MPs are swapped (not cloned) to persist state across calls.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Built-in function dispatch prefers name matching over signature hash matching (avoids collisions like read/write).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - `movmp` looks up the type descriptor to determine copy size (mid is a type index, not a byte count).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- Data initialization (`data.rs`) uses type descriptors for array element sizes and writes to the active buffer context (parent array or MP) for
  correct nested array initialization.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- Builtin return value copy in `mcall` transfers 4 bytes to the caller's return pointer; big-returning functions (like `seek`) and tuple-returning
  functions write their results directly through the return pointer.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- Type conversions match the reference: `cvtfw`/`cvtfl` round (±0.5), `cvtrf`/`cvtfr` convert f32↔f64,
  `cvtwc`/`cvtcw` format/parse decimal strings, `cvtfc` uses `%g` format.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - `expw`/`expl`/`expf` use repeated-squaring with base from mid and integer exponent from src.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- Cooperative threading: `spawn` creates threads in a queue, the run loop rotates every 2048 instructions,
  `recv` on empty channels blocks the thread, `send` on full channels blocks the thread, both directions unblock on state change. Cloned MP adjusts
  heap ref counts.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Alt table format: `{nsend, nrecv}` header followed by 8-byte `{channel_ptr, data_ptr}` entries.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Per-thread error string (`last_error`) implements the `werrstr`/`%r` mechanism.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- Portable I/O via `FileTable` (no `libc` dependency) with in-memory pipe support and non-blocking stdin (background reader thread prevents
  `sys->read` from freezing all VM threads).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- Virtual device files: `/dev/sysctl`, `/dev/sysname`, `/dev/user`, `/dev/time`, `/dev/cons`, `/dev/null`,
  `/dev/random`, `/dev/drivers`, `/prog/N/{status,wait,ns,ctl}`, and `/env/*`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- `$Keyring` module provides real MD5 and SHA1 digests via the `md-5` and `sha1` crates; auth functions (`readauthinfo`, `auth`, etc.) are stubs
  returning nil.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text:
- Nil dereferences (channel, array, string, list) are caught in the run loop and dispatched to exception handler tables, matching the reference Dis VM
  behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Library modules with `entry_pc = -1` return success immediately (no init function).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - SDL2 for GUI is behind an optional `gui` feature flag.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - Audio support (`/dev/audio` and `/dev/audioctl`) is behind an optional `audio` feature flag (cpal backend).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Key Design Decisions
text: - `export_real`/`export_real32` use correct argument order (address, then value).

text: The original Dis VM source is in `external/inferno-os/libinterp/`:

text:

head: Diffgotchi > Key Conventions
text: - `.tsx` = renders UI (has JSX). `.ts` = pure logic, no React

head: Diffgotchi > Key Conventions
text: - No `.js` import extensions. No `/index` in import paths — use `@/store` not `@/store/index`

head: Diffgotchi > Key Conventions
text: - Versioning via changesets — run `bun changeset` for user-facing changes

head: Diffgotchi > Key Conventions
text: - `bun run typecheck` must pass after every change

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: Don't repeat these mistakes:

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: - **No useEffect for derived state.** Compute during render. `useMemo` for expensive. Never `useEffect` + `setState` to transform data.

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: - **No useEffect for user events.** Put logic in event handlers, not effects triggered by state changes.

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: - **Every useEffect dep array must be complete.** Context values (`toast`, `dialog`) captured in closures = must be in deps. `store` (Zustand module ref) is stable, context hooks are not.

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: - **Clean up timers.** Every `setTimeout`/`setInterval` needs a ref + cleanup on unmount. No fire-and-forget timers that call `setState`.

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: - **Read store lazily in callbacks.** Command handlers, event handlers = call `store.getState()` at execution time. Don't close over reactive values that cause 20-dep useEffects.

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: - **Zustand selectors are already atomic.** `useAppStore(s => s.field)` only re-renders when that field changes. Don't "optimize" by grouping into object selectors — that's worse without `useShallow`.

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: - **TextAttributes are bitfield flags.** Combine with `|`: `TextAttributes.UNDERLINE | TextAttributes.ITALIC`. Parent attributes inherit to children — don't repeat on every child span.

head: Diffgotchi > React + Zustand Rules
text: - **No `any` types.** Define interfaces for opentui nodes, event handlers, refs. Even a 3-field inline type is better than `any`.

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: Real bugs/API mismatches that burned us:

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: - `TextAttributes.BOLD` = numeric constant (1), not constructor — `new TextAttributes({bold: true})` crashes

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: - Box props: `position="absolute"`, `left`, `top`, `zIndex` direct props, NOT inside `style`

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: - No `onClick` — use `onMouseDown`/`onMouseUp`

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: - KeyEvent has `.name`, `.sequence`, `.ctrl`, `.shift`, `.option` — no `.input` property

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: - `RGBA.fromInts()`, `RGBA.fromHex()`, `parseColor()` for colors — no `RGBA.brighten()`

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: - DiffRenderableOptions: `addedBg`, `removedBg`, `contextBg`, `addedContentBg`, `removedContentBg` — no `addedWordBg`/`removedWordBg`

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: - `renderer.currentFocusedRenderable` — no `renderer.getFocused()`

head: Diffgotchi > opentui Gotchas
text: - JS/JSX/TS/TSX all map to `"typescript"` for tree-sitter (no separate jsx/tsx grammars)

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Источник поведения и границы
text: - Основная цель рефакторинга: максимум переносимого кода в shared/core, shared/app и shared/ui; Android/Desktop содержат реальные операции ОС, storage/I/O adapters и native/runtime wiring.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Источник поведения и границы
text: - Функциональность и её семантика переносятся из существующего Android-приложения точно. Не придумывать новые функции, defaults, конфликтные политики, editor flows или runtime-возможности.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Источник поведения и границы
text: - Перед переносом сверять Android-источник и при необходимости историю. Наличие текущего альтернативного Desktop-алгоритма не определяет каноническую семантику.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Источник поведения и границы
text: - Отсутствие мобильного переносимого сценария в текущем Desktop не является причиной исключать его перенос. Настоящее platform/native ограничение подтверждается конкретным механизмом.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Источник поведения и границы
text: - Сохранять существующие форматы и их фактический контракт. Не обещать round-trip неизвестных полей там, где текущий codec их игнорирует.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Источник поведения и границы
text: - Для профилей Desktop без `resource-user-agent` использовать `Skipi/<текущая версия>/Desktop`, по последнему явному уточнению пользователя. Android сохраняет прежний UA. head: Правила проекта Skipi > Сначала тесты, затем production-код
text: Прямое правило пользователя: **сначала пишутся тесты, затем код; код пишется под тесты, а не тесты под готовый код**.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Сначала тесты, затем production-код
text: 1. До production-изменения описать ожидаемое поведение по Android-оригиналу и написать поведенческие тесты следующего малого среза.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Сначала тесты, затем production-код
text: 2. Запустить их до изменения реализации. Дефект/отсутствующий общий путь воспроизвести как RED; для чистого переноса зафиксировать работающий Android baseline и тот же контракт общего пути.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Сначала тесты, затем production-код
text: 3. Затем написать минимальный код, получить GREEN и провести рефакторинг под теми же тестами.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Сначала тесты, затем production-код
text: 4. Не менять expectations/snapshots под реализацию и не отключать тесты ради зелёной сборки. Проверять входы/результаты, а не зеркалить внутреннюю структуру кода.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Сначала тесты, затем production-код
text: 5. Перед завершением запускать соответствующие suites и необходимые integration/compile/UI/native проверки; отчёт различает выполненные и непроведённые проверки.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Сначала тесты, затем production-код
text: 6. В отчёте среза указывать тесты и исходный результат до production-кода, затем GREEN. Документирование само по себе не требует фиктивных поведенческих тестов.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Сначала тесты, затем production-код
text: Использовать существующий Gradle wrapper и конвенции Kotlin/Compose тестов в commonTest, app/src/test и desktopApp/src/test. Фактические команды и требования JDK/SDK находятся в разделе Q1–Q4 текущего плана. Успешный обычный Desktop unit suite без SKIPI_CORE_INTEGRATION_DIR не доказывает реальный FFM/Core запуск.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Координация
text: - Основной агент выступает оркестратором: разделяет задачи, удерживает контракты, проверяет тестовую спецификацию и итоговый diff.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Координация
text: - Для research и написания кода пользователь предпочитает subagents **gpt-6-luna, reasoning max**, когда соответствующие средства доступны.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Координация
text: - Тесты среза должны быть готовы до production-работы над ним; параллельно выполнять только независимые ветки со стабильными контрактами и без пересечения изменяемых файлов.

head: Правила проекта Skipi > Координация
text: - Не повторять успешно завершённые проверки без новых изменений или нерешённой причины.

head: Repository instructions
text: AgentRecall is a local Electron application that indexes, displays, and resumes coding-agent sessions. The repository ships two independently installed Electron applications: V1 is the stable product and V2 is the preview product with the upgraded session experience, PostgreSQL storage, Runtime, Agents, Workflow, Eval, MCP, Memory, and a managed Skill library. Read [README.md](README.md) for the product surface and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the contributor workflow.

head: Repository instructions > Repository map
text: Keep changes in the lowest owning area. Do not place V2-only behavior in shared V1 code, renderer presentation in persistence modules, or OS/filesystem operations in React components.

head: Repository instructions > Reading and validation
text: Commands and risk-based validation are maintained in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Read the applicable module instructions before editing: [apps](apps/AGENTS.md), [V2](apps/main-2.0/AGENTS.md), [workspace-core](packages/workspace-core/AGENTS.md), and [docs](docs/AGENTS.md).

head: Repository instructions > Reading and validation
text: Current behavior belongs in [docs/spec](docs/spec/README.md); important architectural decisions belong in [docs/adr](docs/adr/README.md). Read the relevant spec before changing a covered module. Observable behavior or contract changes update that spec; changes to process boundaries, data ownership, durable compatibility or team conflict policy also update the relevant ADR. Behavior-preserving refactors do not require a new ADR or spec rewrite.

head: Repository instructions > Working method
text: - Before searching local files or text, verify that `rg` is available. Prefer `rg` and `rg --files` over `grep`, `find`, or slower recursive tools.

head: Repository instructions > Working method
text: - Inspect the current implementation, its tests, and the relevant app boundary before editing. Do not infer a contract from a component name or one call site.

head: Repository instructions > Working method
text: - Never commit or log API keys, tokens, credentials, private session contents, or populated `.env` files.

head: Repository instructions > Working method
text: - Preserve unrelated working-tree changes. Restrict formatting, generated output, and cleanup to files owned by the task.

head: Repository instructions > Working method
text: - Prefer changing the existing function or component directly when logic has one caller. Create a helper only when it is reused or isolates a meaningful domain, lifecycle, safety, concurrency, transaction, or resource-management decision.

head: Repository instructions > Working method
text: - Do not add pass-through wrappers, single-use aliases, speculative options, compatibility paths without a current consumer, or exports created only to expose an implementation detail to tests.

head: Repository instructions > Working method
text: - Prefer maintained dependencies when they materially remove owned implementation and tests. Do not add a dependency for a trivial operation already clear in local code.

head: Repository instructions > Working method
text: - Do not manually edit `out/`, `dist/`, generated bundles, package archives, or lock-derived artifacts. Run the owning generator or build command when those outputs intentionally need refresh.

head: Repository instructions > Dual-app development
text: - For every session-related bug fix or feature, inspect the relevant behavior in both `apps/main-1.0` and `apps/main-2.0` before changing code.

head: Repository instructions > Dual-app development
text: - When the behavior applies to both products, implement and test it in both directories. Do not mechanically copy code: V1 uses SQLite and mostly synchronous store APIs, while V2 uses PostgreSQL and asynchronous store APIs.

head: Repository instructions > Dual-app development
text: - If session behavior intentionally differs between V1 and V2, document the user-visible reason and cover the intended divergence with tests.

head: Repository instructions > Dual-app development
text: - Changes unrelated to sessions may target only the affected application. V2-only Runtime, Agent, Workflow, Eval, Memory, and managed-Skill features do not require placeholder V1 changes.

head: Repository instructions > Dual-app development
text: - V1 and V2 use separate commands, app data, databases, MCP identifiers, and update caches. Do not introduce implicit cross-version reads, writes, migration, or cleanup.

head: Repository instructions > Session and durable-data rules
text: Follow the [session data and indexing contract](docs/spec/session-indexing.md), including source fidelity, read-only source defaults, format compatibility and complete-value limits. Team operations additionally follow the [team asset contract](docs/spec/team-assets.md). Enforce permissions and destructive decisions in the operation that performs the action, not only in renderer controls.

head: Repository instructions > Lifecycle, concurrency, and failures
text: - Represent one asynchronous operation with one clear owner. Timers, listeners, subprocesses, database leases, watchers, abort controllers, and temporary directories must have deterministic cleanup on success, failure, cancellation, reload, and window shutdown.

head: Repository instructions > Lifecycle, concurrency, and failures
text: - Do not add detached background work unless the product explicitly owns its lifetime and exposes its state. A renderer unmount, closed window, or failed request must not orphan work silently.

head: Repository instructions > Lifecycle, concurrency, and failures
text: - Make cancellation and retry semantics explicit. Do not report success before durable writes, link creation, process startup, or remote operations have actually completed.

head: Repository instructions > Lifecycle, concurrency, and failures
text: - Misconfiguration fails loudly at load time when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest point where the missing value can be resolved. Do not silently skip a requested provider, source, install target, or migration step.

head: Repository instructions > Lifecycle, concurrency, and failures
text: - Keep `try` blocks narrow. Every empty or best-effort `catch` names the exact expected failure and explains why ignoring it is safe; unexpected errors retain actionable context.

head: Repository instructions > Lifecycle, concurrency, and failures
text: - Avoid comments that restate control flow. Comments and JSDoc preserve non-obvious behavior, failure, timing, ownership, compatibility, and safe-use obligations.

head: Repository instructions > Testing and packaging safety
text: - Test observable behavior through the owning function, service, IPC boundary, or component. Tests describe the behavior being preserved; when the product behavior changes intentionally, update the obsolete expectation instead of adding compatibility solely for the test.

head: Repository instructions > Testing and packaging safety
text: - Keep regression coverage minimal. Prefer extending the owning test file, retain only tests that protect a distinct user-visible contract or failure boundary, and remove temporary scaffolding or redundant assertions before submission.

head: Repository instructions > Testing and packaging safety
text: - Match evidence to risk: focused unit tests for pure logic, integration tests for persistence and IPC, renderer tests for interactions, builds for process-boundary/import changes, and package smokes for install/update surfaces.

head: Repository instructions > Testing and packaging safety
text: - Tests that exercise installation, update, uninstall, hooks, MCP setup, Skills, session discovery, or agent configuration must use a temporary `HOME`, temporary npm prefix, and synthetic fixtures. Never read, upload, rewrite, or delete the developer's real Claude, Codex, Skills, Supabase, Electron, PostgreSQL, or session data.

head: Repository instructions > Testing and packaging safety
text: - Do not run global install or uninstall tests against the active Node.js prefix. Build first, install the generated package into a temporary prefix, verify it there, and remove all temporary files and child processes.

head: Repository instructions > Testing and packaging safety
text: - Validate macOS and Windows path behavior. Keep platform-specific assertions behind explicit branches; do not bake `/Users/...`, POSIX commands, symlink support, or path separators into cross-platform contracts.

head: Repository instructions > Testing and packaging safety
text: - If a test starts Electron, PostgreSQL, OpenViking, a UI window, watcher, or subprocess, stop it before reporting completion. Do not leave update locks, ports, temporary runtimes, databases, or package archives behind.

head: Repository instructions > Type safety, UI, and documentation
text: - Both applications compile with TypeScript `strict`. V2 also rejects unused locals and parameters. Avoid `any`; when external input cannot be typed, keep `unknown` until the boundary parser narrows it.

head: Repository instructions > Type safety, UI, and documentation
text: - Closed discriminated unions use exhaustive handling. Extensible values require a documented fallback that preserves unknown data or produces an actionable error.

head: Repository instructions > Type safety, UI, and documentation
text: - UI actions must expose their real state: disable duplicate submission while running, retain retryable failures, distinguish partial success, and require explicit confirmation for destructive or force-overwrite behavior.

head: Repository instructions > Type safety, UI, and documentation
text: - User-facing text should name the outcome and next action. Do not expose internal table names, IPC channels, branch names, implementation vocabulary, or raw stack traces unless the detail is intentionally diagnostic.

head: Repository instructions > Type safety, UI, and documentation
text: - Durable documentation describes the current product, not commit history. Update the owning guide or README when a change alters setup, visible behavior, configuration, data handling, or limitations.

head: Repository instructions > Type safety, UI, and documentation
text: - Keep one authoritative home for each fact. Link to the owning document instead of copying long command lists, architecture explanations, or release rules into multiple files.

head: Repository instructions > Development branches and releases
text: - MRs target `main`; direct feature pushes to `main` are not part of the development workflow. Split independent changes into independent branches.

head: Repository instructions > Development branches and releases
text: - Before opening or merging an MR, follow the [release-note rules](.release-notes/README.md) and run `npm run release-note:check`; do not proceed while it fails.

head: Repository instructions > Development branches and releases
text: - Release routing, versioning and publication follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). A major version increase requires explicit user confirmation.

head: Repository instructions > Editing these instructions
text: Keep root `AGENTS.md` for standing orders needed in most development sessions. Move detailed subsystem contracts and step-by-step procedures to the owning guide, README, or design document and leave a concise link here. State each rule once, in current-state language, and remove obsolete instructions when the repository changes.

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions
text: CLI for agents, CI, and humans to interact with QA Wolf. TypeScript, Bun runtime, Commander.js framework.

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions
text: See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for human contributor setup.

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > Testing
text: Tests use Bun's test runner. Run a single test file with `bun run test <path>`. Place test files next to the code they test, named `*.test.ts`.

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > Project Structure
text: The codebase is organized into five layers. **`core/`** holds pure functions and types with zero I/O. **`shell/`** holds I/O executors (process spawning, Playwright, UI rendering, API clients). **`domains/`** holds bounded-context business logic; each domain may import `core/` and `shell/` but never a sibling domain. **`commands/`** is the composite root: thin Commander registration plus `runDefaults.ts`, which bridges multiple domains to assemble the `flows run` command. **`runnerSdk/`** is the second composite root, serving a library consumer where `commands/` serves the terminal: it is the only directory the `exports` field points at, and it reuses `domains/interactiveRunner` rather than reimplementing it. oxlint enforces these boundaries via per-layer `no-restricted-imports` overrides in `.oxlintrc.json`; `runnerSdk/` additionally may not import from `commands/` or from `bun`, since it is published and runs under Node.

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > Project Structure
text: API clients (tRPC for the QA Wolf platform, GitHub REST) live in `src/shell/platform/` and `src/shell/` respectively — one module per auth boundary.

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > Project Structure
text: Commands register in one of two ways: platform public-API endpoints are generated from contracts via `registerPublicApiCommands` (`src/commands/publicApi/`), while commands with local logic or multi-step UX flows are hand-written under `src/commands/<domain>/`. Never both for the same endpoint — contracts served by a hand-written command go in the generator's skip-list (`handWrittenContractNames`). See `.claude/rules/domain-structure.md` ("Adding a command") for the full decision rule.

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > Code Style
text: - Prefer string unions over enums

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > Code Style
text: - Colocate types with their domain (`commands/flows/` exports `FlowListItem`, not a shared types dir)

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > Code Style
text: - Organize directories by meaning, not by shape

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > After Editing
text: Run `bun run lint:fix` and `bun run format` on changed files. Do not make cosmetic or stylistic changes to files unrelated to your task.

head: @qawolf/cli — Agent Instructions > After Editing
text: A pre-commit hook (`.githooks/pre-commit`) runs the naming check, lint, format check, typecheck, and `knip` automatically. Activate it once per clone with `bun install`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: BEAR.Package is the core framework implementation package for BEAR.Sunday, a resource-oriented PHP framework. It provides dependency injection, AOP compilation, routing, error handling, and context-based module loading.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Type Definitions
text: Domain types are defined in `src/Types.php` using Psalm type aliases:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Type Definitions
text: - `AppName`: Application namespace (e.g., `"MyVendor\\MyApp"`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Type Definitions
text: - `Context`: Context string (e.g., `"prod-api-app"`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Type Definitions
text: - `AppDir`: Application directory path

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Type Definitions
text: These types are imported via `@psalm-import-type` throughout the codebase.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - `Injector::getInstance()`: Creates/retrieves cached DI container for an application

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - `PackageInjector`: Internal injector implementation with caching support

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - Uses Ray.Di for dependency injection with compile-time optimization

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - Compilation process that generates optimized autoload, preload, DI scripts, and object graphs

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - `Compiler::compile()`: Main compilation orchestrator

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - Sub-compilers: `CompileAutoload`, `CompilePreload`, `CompileObjectGraph`, `CompileClassMetaInfo`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - Tracks loaded classes during compilation for preload generation

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - Uses Ray.Compiler to compile DI container to PHP scripts

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - `Module` class: Context-based module loader that processes hyphenated contexts (e.g., "prod-api-app")

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - Context modules are loaded in reverse order (right-to-left)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core Components
text: - Looks for modules in app namespace first, falls back to `BEAR\Package\Context\`

text: - Base framework module that installs core functionality

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: **Context-Based Configuration**

text: - Applications can have multiple contexts (e.g., "prod-api-app", "dev-cli-app")

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: - Each context segment maps to a Module (AppModule, ApiModule, ProdModule)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Patterns

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: - Constructor injection with type hints

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: - Interface binding in modules

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Patterns
text: - Provider classes for complex object creation

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Key Patterns

text: - Resources are the primary abstraction (not MVC)

head: AGENTS.md > Project Purpose
text:
`md2cb` is a cross-platform command-line tool that converts GitHub Flavored
Markdown (GFM) to rich HTML clipboard content. The goal is to produce clipboard
output that rich text editors can properly render with GitHub-style formatting.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Purpose
text:
This enables users to paste formatted markdown into rich text editors like
Microsoft Word, Teams, Slack, Google Docs, Apple Pages, etc., with proper
styling preserved.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text:
The tool is written in Rust for cross-platform support (macOS, Windows, Linux).
**Single binary with no external runtime dependencies.**

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: 1. **Markdown → HTML**: Uses `comrak` crate (GFM-compliant CommonMark parser)

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: 2. **Math → PNG Images**: Uses embedded MathJax (via QuickJS) + resvg for LaTeX → SVG → PNG

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: 3. **Mermaid → PNG Images**: Uses `mermaid-rs-renderer` (pure Rust) + resvg for diagrams → SVG → PNG

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: 4. **Image Inlining**: Fetches images and embeds as base64 data URIs

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: 5. **CSS Embedding**: GitHub markdown CSS embedded at compile time

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture
text: 6. **Clipboard**: Uses `arboard` crate for cross-platform HTML clipboard support

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Why PNG Images for Math?
text: - **MathML** is not rendered by most editors

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Why PNG Images for Math?
text: - **SVG** data URIs are blocked by many editors

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Why PNG Images for Math?
text: - **PNG images** are universally supported

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Architecture Overview
text: OpenDeck is a Tauri desktop application for controlling Elgato Stream Deck devices. It's built with:

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Architecture Overview > Core Architecture Pattern
text: OpenDeck acts as a **host application** that communicates with **plugins** (separate processes):

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Architecture Overview > Core Architecture Pattern
text: 1. Plugins connect via WebSocket (port dynamically allocated, starting from 57116)

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Architecture Overview > Core Architecture Pattern
text: 2. Static assets served via `tiny_http` webserver (port = WebSocket port + 2)

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Architecture Overview > Core Architecture Pattern
text: 3. Plugin property inspectors (HTML/JS) run in iframes and use separate WebSocket connections

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Architecture Overview > Core Architecture Pattern
text: 4. Device button presses/releases trigger events sent to plugins via WebSocket

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Architecture Overview > Core Architecture Pattern
text: Key data flow: `Device (elgato-streamdeck crate) → Rust event handlers → WebSocket → Plugin process`

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Key Conventions > Context System

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Key Conventions > State Management
text:
- **Backend**:
  - `DEVICES` (DashMap): Thread-safe device registry, keyed by device ID
  - `CATEGORIES` (RwLock): Plugin actions organized by category for UI
  - `Store<T>`: Generic JSON persistence with file locking, backup, and atomic writes
  - Profile locks: Use `acquire_locks()` (read) or `acquire_locks_mut()` (write) before accessing profiles

head: OpenDeck Development Guide > Key Conventions > State Management
text:
- **Frontend**:
  - Svelte stores (`propertyInspector.ts`): `inspectedInstance`, `copiedContext`, `openContextMenu` for UI state
  - Tauri `invoke()` for backend calls - returns Promises with typed results

head: AGENTS.md
text: Repo rule for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor). Read this before touching code.

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text:
`mesh-viewer` is a VS Code / Cursor extension (`AssetToolLabs.mesh-viewer-vscode`) that opens 3D
files and Gaussian splats in a custom editor. `esbuild.js` produces two independent bundles:

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text:
| Bundle            | Entry point                                    | Runs in                       |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `out/extension.js`| `src/extension.ts` → `src/viewerProvider.ts`   | extension host (Node)         |
| `out/webview.js`  | `src/webview/main.ts`                          | webview (browser, Three + Spark inlined) |

head: AGENTS.md > What this repo is
text:
Webview modules: `viewer.ts` (scene, camera, render loop, overlays), `loaders.ts` (per-format
loading and format sniffing), `timeline.ts` (dope sheet and playback), `weightMaterial.ts` (skin
weight coloring), `viewer.html` + `style.css` (shell). `src/types.ts` is the message protocol
between the two sides. Almost every format or rendering bug lands in `src/webview/`.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop
text:
**Every feature request, format-support request, and rendering/loading bug fix runs through all
six phases below, in order.** Do not go from prompt straight to edit. Do not declare a visual
result working — you cannot see the viewport, so phase 6 is where the user decides.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 1. Analyze
text: Before proposing a change:

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 1. Analyze
text: - Restate the ask and the observed vs. expected behavior in one paragraph.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 1. Analyze
text:
- Find the code that owns it. Format/loading → `src/webview/loaders.ts`. Scene, camera, shading,
  overlays → `src/webview/viewer.ts`. UI panels, tree, inspector → `src/webview/main.ts`.
  Animation → `src/webview/timeline.ts`. Webview HTML, CSP, resource URIs, file reads →
  `src/viewerProvider.ts`. Commands, activation, settings → `src/extension.ts` + `package.json`.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 1. Analyze
text:
- Check what the pinned `three` already ships before adding a dependency —
  `node_modules/three/examples/jsm/` has loaders, decoders, and utils that are often the whole fix.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 1. Analyze
text:
- Name the root cause. If you cannot, say so and treat phase 2 as a diagnostic step rather than
  claiming a cause you have not established.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 2. Get real test data
text:
Get an asset that actually exercises the code path **before** writing the fix, so there is a
before/after to compare.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 2. Get real test data
text: - Put everything in `test_data/` (gitignored, never committed). Do not drop assets in the repo root.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 2. Get real test data
text:
- Fetch two things where possible: a **repro asset** that triggers the bug or new path, and a
  **control asset** in the same format that already works and must not regress.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 2. Get real test data
text:
- Verified sources (reachable from this sandbox):
  ```bash
  mkdir -p test_data && cd test_data

  # Khronos glTF sample assets — index of every model, then a specific one
  curl -sSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets/main/Models/model-index.json
  curl -sSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets/main/Models/DamagedHelmet/glTF-Binary/DamagedHelmet.glb

  # three.js example models — fbx, obj, stl, ply, collada, usdz, vox, pcd, ...
  curl -sSLO "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/examples/models/fbx/Samba%20Dancing.fbx"
  curl -sSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/examples/models/stl/binary/pr2_head_pan.stl

  # assimp regression corpus — broad, weird, good for edge cases
  curl -sSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/assimp/assimp/master/test/models/OBJ/spider.obj
  ```

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 2. Get real test data
text:
- **Confirm the asset really hits the path** before coding — a sample named after a feature does
  not always use it. For glTF, check the extension list; for binary formats, check the header:
  ```bash
  node -e "const b=require('fs').readFileSync('test_data/x.glb');const j=JSON.parse(b.subarray(20,20+b.readUInt32LE(12)).toString());console.log(j.extensionsUsed,j.extensionsRequired)"
  ```

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 2. Get real test data
text:
- If nothing public exercises the path, **generate a fixture** with a small node script under
  `test_data/` and say in your report that the evidence is synthetic.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 2. Get real test data
text: - Record where each asset came from in `test_data/SOURCES.md` so the next session can refetch it.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 3. Plan, then get approval
text:
Write a dedicated plan and get the user's go-ahead before editing. In Claude Code use plan mode
and `ExitPlanMode`; in Codex post the plan and wait for an ack. The plan states:

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 3. Plan, then get approval
text: 1. Root cause (or the diagnostic that will pin it down).

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 3. Plan, then get approval
text: 2. Numbered steps, each with the file it touches and why.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 3. Plan, then get approval
text: 3. Which side of the boundary changes — extension host, webview, or both.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 3. Plan, then get approval
text: 4. What is explicitly out of scope.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 3. Plan, then get approval
text: 5. How each step gets verified, and which test asset proves it.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 3. Plan, then get approval
text:
Prefer the smallest change that fixes the class of problem. If a plan starts widening the CSP,
adding a dependency, or reworking the render loop, stop and flag the tradeoff instead of
absorbing it silently.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 4. Implement and rebuild
text:
Both must pass clean. Match the surrounding style: the existing code explains *why* in comments,
not *what*. English only — no Chinese in code, comments, or identifiers.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 4. Implement and rebuild
text:
Update `DOCS.md` and the `package.json` `contributes` block in the same change when you add a
format, a setting, or a command. A format needs all of: a `case` in `loadAsset`, a
`filenamePattern` in `customEditors.selector`, the `explorer/context` `when` regex, the
`DOCS.md` format table, and the `README.md`/`package.json` blurbs if it is user-visible.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 5. Install the local build
text:
The default installs into **both VS Code and Cursor**, and into only the ones the user actually
has: the script resolves each `code` / `cursor` CLI from `PATH` or the macOS app bundle (`PATH`
usually misses in an agent sandbox), prints `skip <editor> (not installed)` for one it cannot
find, and never tries to install into an absent editor. Do not narrow with `--target` unless the
user asks for one editor — installing into both is what keeps whichever window they happen to
have open in sync.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 5. Install the local build
text:
Use `--bump` when the user needs to see the version change to be sure the reload took. If neither
editor resolves, the script exits nonzero and prints the manual route — pass that along
(**Extensions → … → Install from VSIX…**) rather than retrying.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 6. Hand off and wait
text:
You cannot see the render. End your turn with an explicit test script and stop — do not report the
feature as verified:

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 6. Hand off and wait
text:
> Installed `mesh-viewer-vscode-<version>.vsix` into <the editors the script reported>.
>
> 1. In the editor you are testing in: `Cmd+Shift+P` → **Developer: Reload Window**
> 2. Open `test_data/<repro-asset>` — expect <specific observable>. Before this change it <old behavior>.
> 3. Open `test_data/<control-asset>` — expect no change from before.
> 4. Check the webview devtools console (`Cmd+Shift+P` → **Developer: Open Webview Developer Tools**) for `[3DViewer]` warnings.
>
> Tell me what you see and I will iterate.

head: AGENTS.md > The loop > 6. Hand off and wait
text:
If the user reports it still fails, go back to phase 1 with their evidence — new console output,
new asset — rather than trying variations blind.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard constraints
text:
- **The webview CSP is strict** (`src/viewerProvider.ts`, the `csp` array): `default-src 'none'`,
  script only via nonce plus `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, `worker-src blob:`, and no remote origins.
  Runtime code cannot fetch from a CDN. Widening the CSP is a last resort that needs a comment
  explaining the dependent, like the existing `wasm-unsafe-eval` note.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard constraints
text:
- **Everything the webview loads must be bundled or copied into `out/`.** Two working patterns:
  inline-wasm modules that esbuild swallows into `out/webview.js` (MeshoptDecoder), or a sidecar
  copied by `copyDraco()` in `esbuild.js` and handed over as a webview URI (DRACO). New sidecars
  also need an `!out/...` line in `.vscodeignore`, which is an allowlist.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard constraints
text:
- **`three` and `@types/three` are pinned to the same exact version.** Bump them together, and
  re-check the loaders after — `examples/jsm` is not a stable API.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard constraints
text:
- **`test_data/`, `*.vsix`, and every mesh extension are gitignored.** Keep it that way; do not
  commit binary assets.

head: AGENTS.md > Command reference
text:
`F5` in the editor launches an Extension Development Host from source and is the fastest inner
loop for iterating on the webview; `dev-install.sh` is for handing a real build to the user.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: TaskPaper is a macOS plain-text to-do list app. It is shared source for license holders — do not remove licensing code or redistribute binaries without permission.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: The codebase has a layered design where core logic lives in JavaScript (CoffeeScript) and the native macOS UI is Swift:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: Swift communicates with JavaScript via JavaScriptCore. The JS layers are compiled by webpack into minified bundles in `min/` directories, which Xcode copies into the app at build time.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: `birch-editor.js` depends on `birch-outline.js` via npm link (local file reference in package.json).

head: CLAUDE.md > Build Commands > JavaScript (requires Node v11.15.0 via nvm)
text: Both use gulp to compile CoffeeScript and webpack to produce bundles in `min/` (plain webpack output — not minified; UglifyJsPlugin is disabled).

head: CLAUDE.md > Build Commands > JavaScript (requires Node v11.15.0 via nvm)
text: The shipped bundles are the committed files `BirchOutline/BirchOutline.swift/Dependencies/birchoutline.js` and `BirchEditor/BirchEditor.swift/Dependencies/bircheditor.js`. Next to each lives a committed `.sha256` manifest hashing the bundle and its inputs (`src/**`, gulp/webpack config, package.json, package-lock.json). The `javascript.sh` build phase (first phase of every app target) verifies these: when manifests match, builds need no JS toolchain (this is the fresh-clone path); when JS sources have changed, it rebuilds via gulp (auto-using nvm's Node v11.15.0), refreshes `Dependencies/*.js` + manifests, and the changed files must be committed together with the source changes. If a rebuild is needed but Node 11/node_modules are missing or gulp fails, the Xcode build fails with an actionable error instead of silently shipping stale bundles.

xcodebuild -project TaskPaper.xcodeproj -scheme "TaskPaper Direct" build    # Direct sales (Paddle)
xcodebuild -project TaskPaper.xcodeproj -scheme "TaskPaper Setapp" build    # Setapp

head: About
text: This is a Connect Four implementation written in Mithril. It features several different modes:

head: About
text: 1. A two-player mode where two human players can play against each other on the same device

head: About
text: 2. A one-player mode where a human player can play against an AI component; the AI player is impleemtned using Minimax with alpha-beta pruning

head: About
text: 3. An online multiplayer mode where two players can play against each other over the internet; this works by one player iniiating an online game and sharing a generated link with the other player, who can then join the game using that link
