head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > CRITICAL: Read CONTRIBUTING.md First
text: It defines the coding style for this project. Failure to follow these conventions will result in rejected code.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Key Coding Conventions
text: These are the most important conventions from CONTRIBUTING.md that you MUST follow:

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Key Coding Conventions
text:
| Convention | Correct | Incorrect |
|------------|---------|-----------|
| Variable/function names | `snake_case` | `camelCase` |
| Type names (classes, structs, aliases) | `Stroustrup_case` | `snake_case` |
| Boolean negation | `not x` | `!x` |
| Natural logarithm | `log(x)` | `ln(x)` |
| Const style | `const char* str` | `char const* str` |
| Pointer/reference | `int* ptr`, `int& ref` | `int *ptr`, `int &ref` |
| Container size | `std::ssize(c)` | `c.size()` |
| Hash maps/sets | `absl::flat_hash_map` | `std::unordered_map` |
| Data containers | structs with public fields | classes with getters/setters |
| Error handling | exceptions | error codes |
| Function style (AAA) | `auto func(int x) -> int;` | `int func(int x);` |

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 1. **Use `std::ssize()` not `.size()`** - The codebase strictly avoids signed/unsigned mixing.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 2. **Use `not` instead of `!`** - Boolean negation uses the keyword, not the operator.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 4. **Reference sequence is the baseline** - `Phylo_tree::ref_sequence` is an arbitrary reference state, usually close to the root; mutations are deltas from it.  The mutations above the root node list the deltas from the reference state to the root state.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 5. **Branch vs Node** - A branch is identified by its endpoint. Branch X connects parent(X) to X.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 6. **Binary trees only** - Most MCMC code assumes exactly 2 children for inner nodes.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 7. **Namespace** - All code lives in `namespace delphy { }`.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 8. **Tip vs Inner** - Check with `node.is_tip()` or `node.is_inner_node()`.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 9. **Header guards** - Use `#ifndef DELPHY_FILENAME_H_` style.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 10. **Debug assertions** - Use `assert_tree_integrity()`, `assert_mutation_consistency()` for validation.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 11. **Git staging** - Always use explicit file paths with `git add` (e.g., `git add file.cpp`).  Never use `git add -A` or `git add .` which may stage unintended files.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Common Gotchas
text: 12. **Plain ASCII in plans** - Plans and other written documents must use only ASCII characters.  Use `->` for arrows, `---` for em dashes (parenthetical remarks), `--` for en dashes (number ranges), `>=`/`<=` for comparisons.  No Unicode arrows, check marks, em/en dashes, or other fancy characters.

head: AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Coding Agents > Git Conventions

head: Vulnerability Research Agent
text:
[`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) is the source of truth for the Apache Struts vulnerability reporting process. **Read it first and follow it.** This file is a short
LLM-facing wrapper around that policy; it does not replace it.

head: Vulnerability Research Agent > Workflow
text: Before drafting any report, opening an issue, posting publicly, or reaching a security conclusion:

head: Vulnerability Research Agent > Workflow
text:
1. **Pre-reporting checks** — complete every step in [`SECURITY.md` § Before Reporting](SECURITY.md#before-reporting):
   - read the Struts security policy,
   - read the Struts security guidelines,
   - check previously disclosed vulnerabilities and Security Bulletins.

head: Vulnerability Research Agent > Workflow
text:
2. **Assess** the finding against the questions in [`SECURITY.md` § Assessment](SECURITY.md#assessment), and route it through the disposition guide in
   [`THREAT_MODEL.md`](THREAT_MODEL.md) (scope, trust boundaries, in-model security properties, and the known-non-findings list). If the answers do not still
   point to a likely new framework vulnerability, stop and explain — do not draft a new report.

head: Vulnerability Research Agent > Workflow
text:
3. **Report privately** to `security@struts.apache.org` following [`SECURITY.md` § Private Report Requirements](SECURITY.md#private-report-requirements) and
   [§ Report Quality Rules](SECURITY.md#report-quality-rules).

head: Vulnerability Research Agent > Workflow
text: Do not open a public GitHub issue, Jira issue, pull request, mailing list thread, or discussion for a suspected vulnerability before private triage.

head: Vulnerability Research Agent > Rules for AI Agents
text:
- **Never submit a pull request that fixes a suspected vulnerability.** Before opening any PR, verify the change is not a security patch — OGNL injection,
  parameter filtering bypass, file upload exploit, authentication or authorization bypass, RCE, SSRF, path traversal, deserialization, XSS in framework
  components, etc. If it is, stop and direct the researcher to report it privately to `security@struts.apache.org` instead. Vulnerability fixes go through
  the private security process, not public PRs.

head: Vulnerability Research Agent > Rules for AI Agents
text: - Do not speculate beyond what can be demonstrated. If severity is uncertain, say so explicitly.

head: Vulnerability Research Agent > Rules for AI Agents
text: - If the issue turns out to be application misconfiguration, an already-disclosed CVE, or a non-Struts problem, stop and explain — do not draft a new report.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules
text: A PHPStan extension: a set of custom rules that check Yii2-specific patterns (see [README.md](README.md) for the full, user-facing catalogue and rationale for each rule). This file is about the codebase itself — how it's organized and how to extend it correctly.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Layout
text: Every rule ships its own PHPStan error identifier (`mspirkovYii2Rules.<name>`) via `src/Rules/Identifiers.php` + `src/Rules/ErrorBuilder.php`, so consumers can `ignoreErrors` a single check by identifier instead of disabling the whole rule.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Adding a new rule
text: Follow the existing rules as templates (`NoDirectSuperglobalsRule` for a minimal example, `NoDynamicQueryWhereRule` or `DbQueriesUsageAnalyzer` for one that inspects call targets/types, `ActiveFormFieldValidationRule` for one that resolves a method argument's concrete class and checks a property on it). The moving parts, in order:

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Adding a new rule
text: 1. **`src/Rules/Identifiers.php`** — add a `PREFIX . 'camelCaseName'` constant and insert it (both the constant declaration and the `LIST` entry) in the right sorted spot: `*_VALIDATION` rules first, then `NO_*` rules, alphabetical by `camelCaseName` within each group. The same grouping + alphabetical order applies to `rules.neon` (`parameters`, `parametersSchema`, `conditionalTags`, `services`) and to the rules table in README.md — keep all of them in sync.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Adding a new rule
text:
2. **`src/Rules/<Name>Rule.php`** — implements `Rule<SomeNodeType>` (`@implements Rule<...>` docblock + matching `getNodeType()`). Return `[]` early for anything that doesn't match; build errors with `ErrorBuilder::build($message, Identifiers::X, $node->getStartLine())`.
   - Prefer composing existing `Analyzers/*` (especially `ExpressionTypeAnalyzer::isClassNameOf()` / `isObjectOf()` / `getSingleClassReflectionOf()`) over re-deriving class-reflection logic inline — most "is this expression an instance of X" checks already exist there.
   - To resolve a `Name` node (e.g. the class part of a `StaticCall`) to a string, use `$scope->resolveName($name)`, then check it with the analyzer above.
   - To get the concrete `ClassReflection` behind an arbitrary expression (e.g. a method argument typed as some base class), use `ExpressionTypeAnalyzer::getSingleClassReflectionOf($expr, $scope, $parentClass)` — it returns `null` on zero or multiple matching object types, so ambiguous/union-typed expressions are safely skipped rather than guessed at (see `ActiveFormFieldValidationRule` for an example).

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Adding a new rule
text:
3. **`rules.neon`** — four places to touch, all keyed by the same `camelCaseName`, each inserted at its sorted position (see step 1) rather than appended at the end:
   - `parameters.mspirkovYii2Rules.<name>.enabled: %mspirkovYii2Rules.enableAllRules%` (plus any rule-specific options)
   - matching block under `parametersSchema`
   - `conditionalTags` entry: `<FQCN>: { phpstan.rules.rule: %mspirkovYii2Rules.<name>.enabled% }`
   - `services` entry for the class (only add `arguments:` if the constructor needs config values that aren't other autowired services — dependencies on other `Analyzers`/rule services are autowired by type, no `arguments:` needed)

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Adding a new rule
text:
4. **Tests** — `tests/Rules/<Name>RuleTest.php` extends `AbstractTestCase`, asserts `[message, line]` pairs against `tests/Rules/Data/<Name>/code.php`.
   - Any class the fixture needs by name (not an anonymous class or an inline literal) must live in `tests/Rules/Source/<Name>/<ClassName>.php`, one class per file, matching PSR-4 (`MSpirkov\Yii2\PHPStan\Tests\Rules\Source\<Name>\<ClassName>`) — classes declared inline inside the `Data` fixture are **not** reflectable by PHPStan's test reflection provider (no autoload entry maps `code.php` to them), and referencing them by name will fail with "not found in ReflectionProvider".
   - Both `tests/*/Data/*` and `tests/*/Source/*` are excluded from this project's own `phpstan.dist.neon` / `rector.php` analysis — write fixtures that would normally fail PHPStan/type checks freely when the point is to exercise a code path (e.g. a call with a deliberately wrong argument count).
   - Keep cases that a rule intentionally stays silent on (an ambiguous type it can't resolve, a check it deliberately leaves to PHPStan's native type checking, etc.) out of the `Invalid*` fixture class — mixing silent cases into `Invalid*` makes it unclear, on a later re-read, whether a line producing no error is intentional or a coverage gap. Put all of them together in one `Skipped<Name>` class per fixture (e.g. `SkippedComponent`, `SkippedController`), not one class per reason — a single method with a few varied cases reads fine and keeps the fixture file from sprawling.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Adding a new rule
text: 5. **README.md** — under "What's inside", add a row to the table for the rule's group (`### Validation rules` or `### Code quality rules`, same sorted position as step 1, strictly alphabetical — do not reorder rows to visually group anything) and a `####` write-up section below that same table, positioned so the write-up sections read top-to-bottom in the same order as their table rows; the table row's link must match the GitHub-generated anchor slug of that heading. Rules that share one write-up section only stay merged when their names are alphabetically adjacent (e.g. the two complexity rules, the three DB-access rules) — the merged section then sits at the position of its alphabetically-first member. If a shared write-up would otherwise straddle another rule's table row (e.g. `noForbiddenYiiAppProperties` and `noYiiAppPropertyMutation`, with `noRedundantHtmlEncode` alphabetically between them), split it into two write-ups instead so each has its own heading at its own alphabetical position — table order must always match write-up order top-to-bottom, never "fixed" by breaking the table's alphabetical sort. Within a write-up, prose comes before the code example, never after — a section that's just a code block with no prose (e.g. "No calling actions via `$this`") is fine, but if there's explanatory text, it introduces the example rather than following it.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Verifying a change
text: Run all four before considering a rule done — they check different things and a rule can pass one while failing another:

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Verifying a change
text: Coverage is expected to stay at 100% (`tests/coverage/`, tracked via Codecov) — a new rule needs fixture cases hitting every early-return branch, not just the "fires" case. When unsure whether a branch is covered, generate the clover report and grep for `count="0"` lines in the new file rather than guessing from the fixture alone.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - **Reuse Analyzers, don't reimplement them.** Before writing any type-check, class-check, or config-parsing logic in a rule, check whether `src/Analyzers/*.php` already covers it — and if you're about to write something a second rule could plausibly need, put it in an `Analyzer` (constructor-injected, autowired via `rules.neon`) instead of inlining it. This project has been bitten by the same "is this class X or a subclass" / "is this expression an instance of X" logic being hand-rolled per rule before `ExpressionTypeAnalyzer` existed; don't regress that. Each analyzer owns one domain — class/type identity checks (`ExpressionTypeAnalyzer`), Yii `Application`-typed expressions (`YiiAppAnalyzer`), Yii `Model`-typed expressions (`ModelAnalyzer`), DB/ActiveRecord usage detection (`DbQueriesUsageAnalyzer`), object property existence/readability/writability (`BaseObjectPropertyAnalyzer`), object/array config-shape validation for both `ClassMethod`-shaped config methods and arbitrary config-array arguments (`BaseObjectConfigAnalyzer`, `ComponentConfigMethodAnalyzer`, `ComponentObjectConfigAnalyzer`), complexity counting (`ActionComplexityAnalyzer`), method-return-expression collection (`Finders/`, `Visitors/`), and literal-value resolution (`Resolvers/ExpressionValueResolver`). Read the class itself for its exact current methods rather than trusting a method-level inventory here — that drifts out of date far faster than this file should. If none of them fit, extend the closest one rather than adding a near-duplicate method, and only fall back to writing rule-local logic when it's genuinely specific to that one rule's error shape.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - **Any check that resolves a `yii\base\Model` attribute against declared properties (`rules()`, `attributeLabels()`, `attributeHints()`, `scenarios()`, `Html::active*()`, `ActiveForm::field()`, `UploadedFile::getInstance()`, etc.) must skip `yii\base\DynamicModel` first**, via `ModelAnalyzer::shouldSkipAttributeExistenceCheck($classReflection)`. `DynamicModel`'s attributes are declared at runtime through `defineAttribute()`, not as class properties or PHPDoc `@property` tags, so any static "does this attribute exist" check produces false positives on it — there is no fixing this by resolving harder, the information genuinely isn't in the class declaration. Scope the skip to that specific existence check, not the whole rule — call it right inside the helper that resolves the property, not hoisted to the top of `processNode()`. This matters whenever a rule has other logic that stays meaningful on a `DynamicModel` subclass: `modelAttributeHintsValidation`/`modelAttributeLabelsValidation` still flag an empty key, `modelScenariosValidation` still flags an empty scenario name or a non-array/non-string attribute list, and `modelRulesValidation` still runs its whole validator/option-checking machinery — none of that depends on the attribute actually resolving to a declared property. See `ModelRulesValidationRule::validateAttributeExists()` for the pattern. Every existing rule that touches model attributes already does this; a new one that doesn't will misreport on any `DynamicModel` subclass.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - **Don't duplicate errors PHPStan already reports natively.** Before adding a check, verify with a scratch `phpstan analyse` run (real signature, real call site) that PHPStan's own type checking doesn't already flag it — many Yii2 APIs (e.g. `Yii::createObject()`) carry accurate `@param class-string<T>|array{...}|callable(): T` PHPDoc, so passing a wrong type, an unknown class-string, or even an unrefined non-`class-string` variable already produces a native `argument.type` / `argument.templateType` error on its own. This isn't limited to direct call-site arguments: a `ClassMethod`-shaped config method can carry the same kind of PHPDoc on its `@return` and get checked the same way — e.g. `Controller::actions()` and `Component::behaviors()` both declare `@return array<array-key, class-string|array{class: class-string, ...}>`, so PHPStan's return-type covariance check *already* flags a missing `class`/`__class` key, a `null`/non-string `class` value, an unknown class name, or a non-string/non-array value on any override, with no rule involved — confirmed by writing the override in a throwaway file and running `phpstan analyse` with `bootstrapFiles: [tests/bootstrap.php]` at `level: max` and no `mspirkovYii2Rules` includes. A rule should only add messages for gaps PHPStan's own type system can't see — e.g. an open array shape (`array{class?: ..., ...}` or `array{class: class-string, ...}`) never validates that the resolved class is the *right kind* of class (extends the expected base class) or checks the meaning of the other, un-typed keys (unknown option names, wrong option value types). Don't re-justify this with an inline comment on every such check, and don't restate it in that rule's README.md section either ("PHPStan already flags X, so this only adds Y") — it's a standing codebase-wide principle covered here once, not something each rule needs to restate. The README section should just describe what the rule catches.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - **`Yii::createObject()` / `Container::build()` config arrays also recognize a `'__construct()'` key** (literal parentheses in the string) — its value is an array of constructor parameter values (positional or name-indexed), applied before the rest of the array's keys are used as property assignments (see `yii\di\Container::build()`). It isn't a real property on the target class, so it must stay listed in `BaseObjectConfigAnalyzer::SPECIAL_CONFIG_KEYS` alongside `class`/`__class` — otherwise every rule that checks option names/types against a resolved class (`yiiCreateObjectValidation`, `componentBehaviorsValidation`, `controllerActionsValidation`, `widgetPropertiesValidation`) misreports it as an unknown option or a wrong-typed one.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - Rule classes are `final`, take no rule-specific constructor args unless config-driven, and stay side-effect-free (`processNode()` only reads `Node`/`Scope`, never mutates).

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - **Avoid by-reference parameters** (`array &$errors` and similar) to accumulate output alongside a return value — it obscures what a method does at the call site and makes the two outputs harder to reason about independently. Return everything instead: either a plain value plus a separately-called error-building step (see `ModelRulesValidationRule::resolveKnownValidatorClass()`, which returns `?string` and lets the caller build the error on `null`), or, when a resolved value and its errors are genuinely produced together, a single shaped array like `BaseObjectConfigAnalyzer::collectOptions()`'s `array{items: ..., invalidKeys: ...}` (see `ControllerActionsValidationRule::checkActionClass()` / `ComponentBehaviorsValidationRule::checkBehaviorClass()` for the `array{class: ..., errors: ...}` shape).

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - Type checks always go through PHPStan's `Type` API (`->isString()->yes()`, `->isNumericString()->yes()`, etc.), never `instanceof` on a `Type` implementation — the file-level docblock in PHPStan's own `Type` interface calls this out explicitly, and it breaks on union/intersection types.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - `ClassReflection::is()` / `isSubclassOf()` / `implementsInterface()` is how "is this the class I care about, or one of its subclasses" gets checked once a `ClassReflection` is in hand.

head: yii2-phpstan-rules > Conventions worth knowing
text: - Messages are one or two full sentences, second sentence (if present) is the actionable fix ("Use X instead."), no trailing punctuation quirks — match the tone already in `src/Rules/*.php`.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: The SPA's tokens, type scale, screen anatomy, and data-honesty rules live in [js/app/web/DESIGN.md](js/app/web/DESIGN.md). That document is the source of truth; the summary here exists so the rules travel with the rest of this file.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: **Identity: a surveyor's ledger.** Warm graphite dark theme, warm paper light theme. IBM Plex Sans for UI text, IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals for every value. One-pixel rules, no cards, no shadows except on floating overlays, no decorative gradients or hatching except to mark an unavailable interval.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: **Color is state, never decoration.**

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Semantic tokens only (`bg-surface`, `text-fg-muted`, `border-line`, `text-danger`). Raw hex values live in `src/styles/tokens.css` and nowhere else; charts read the same CSS variables.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Running/open = teal, success = green, waiting/stale/inferred = ochre, failure = vermilion, cancelled/unknown = neutral. Blue is reserved for interaction and load (links, focus, meters); a busy node is not a failed node.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Status is ink: a glyph plus colored text. No pills. The only fill is the 2px left rule on a row whose instance has an error. Selection is neutral (ink rule + raised surface).

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Tints come from opacity modifiers on the semantic token (`bg-danger/10`), not from extra tokens.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Scale: `text-title` 18/24, `text-section` 14/20, `text-body` 13/18, `text-label` 12/16, `text-micro` 11/14, `text-metric` 20/24. Nothing larger than 20px; no hero numerals. Headers are quieter than the values under them. Prefer one plain sentence over a row of raw fields: "Running charge_payment for 3.6 s" beats a kind string, a node id, and three counts.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Rows 36px (`h-row`), controls 28px (`h-control`), global bar 40px, icon rail 48px, gutter 20px. Radius 4px controls / 6px panels.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Every number has a unit and a scope caption ("2 fresh nodes · 1 excluded"). Every live view shows freshness.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - One 40px global bar carries identity, environment, page title, time window, Live/Paused with freshness, jump box, and theme. No page-header band, no taglines, no eyebrow labels, no stack credits.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Detail is a route. A peek panel overlays the workspace and never pushes columns. Filters, selection, and the time window live in the URL.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Only show what the API reports. Names, payloads, attempt numbers, and hostnames are not reported; render "Not recorded", "derived", "inferred", or a short id instead. Rejections are counted, never promoted to a workflow state.

head: Waymark > UI Design Conventions
text: - Empty, filtered-empty, unavailable, and error states must never look alike. A missing value must never look like a recorded null or a loading state.

head: Waymark > Coding Conventions
text: - Never add optional-import fallbacks for core dependencies (e.g., wrapping `pydantic` imports in `try/except`). Import them directly and let the program fail fast if they're missing.

head: Waymark > Coding Conventions
text: - Always run "make lint" and clear the outstanding linting errors before yielding back. Only on very difficult lints where fixing the lint would corrupt the logic should you yield to me for expert intervention. Never yourself write code that ignores the lints on a per line basis. Linting errors should be respected.

head: Waymark > Coding Conventions
text: - Any python code that you run should be called with `uv` since this is the environment that will have the python dependencies we need. Also make sure you're in the appropriate directory where our pyproject.toml is defined.

head: Waymark > Coding Conventions
text: - When writing code that uses WhichOneof in Python, use a switch statement to make sure that every value is handed and add a default case for assert_never.

head: Waymark > Coding Conventions
text: - NEVER write `getattr` in your own code unless I explicitly mention it. You should just be able to call it directly.

head: Waymark > Coding Conventions
text: - Unless we explicitly mention backwards compatibility, don't implement logic that assumes how the backwards spec is compatible. We will specify it if it's relevant.

head: Waymark > Coding Conventions
text: - There's no need to ever import `annotations` `from __future__`. We always run on a Python version with the latest typehinting where this will be supported.

head: Waymark > Workflow Conventions
text: - NEVER modify the protobuf python files directly, instead modify the base messages if you have to and run `make build-proto`

head: Waymark > Workflow Conventions
text:
- When defining Workflow classes, pass arguments directly to the `run()` method, NOT to `__init__()`. The workflow decorator automatically handles serialization and deserialization of run() arguments.
  - Correct: `async def run(self, user_id: str) -> Result:`
  - Incorrect: `def __init__(self, user_id: str):` with `self.user_id = user_id`

head: Waymark > Unit Tests
text: - Run python tests with `uv run pytest`

head: Waymark > Unit Tests
text: - To run the rust integration tests you'll have to do something like: source .env && cargo test ...

head: Waymark > Unit Tests
text: - Unless there's a compelling reason, you should construct synthetic programs by writing code in our IR language and then parsing with `ir_parser.rs`. This makes it much easier for people to add additional IRs in the future. It also guarantees that the compiled program matches what's actually produced at runtime. If you _really_ need control at the AST/bytecode level, write a detailed comment justifying why we need to do it manually versus just using the parser.

head: Waymark > Unit Tests
text: - If there is common logic/helpers that is shared by a bunch of different rust tests, we should extract a test harness class and place it in a local test_helpers.rs. This file serves as our conventional rust equivalent for conftest.py in Python where we can dump these helpers instead of interrupting the flow of the file under test.

text:
<code_feedback>
<rule>Ship UI routes backed only by production APIs; keep synthetic fixtures in tests, never in application imports, query-selectable demo modes, or fallback paths. Show explicit empty and unavailable states when real data is absent. Test fixtures should use the API's event or sample types and production derivation code so they cannot invent facts the API does not report.</rule>
<rule>Keep domain state vocabularies in `src/domain`, derived from wire types, and let UI components import them; never define a status union inside a component. Good: `domain/status.ts` exports `InstanceState` with the rule that produces each value. Bad: `type Status = keyof typeof statuses` living in `status-badge.tsx` and imported by fixtures.</rule>
<rule>When a fixture helper returns negative offsets (time ago), do not add raw positive milliseconds to it for "later" steps without a comment; jumbled event order silently produces wrong derived state. Good: `minutes(6) + seconds(2)` for 6m02s ago, with the sign convention documented beside the helper. Bad: mixing `minutes(6) - 40` and `minutes(6) + seconds(0.02)` in one scenario.</rule>
<rule>Keep substantial frontend build orchestration in a testable library consumed through `build-dependencies`, leaving `build.rs` to supply paths. Use `xshell` for command interpolation and contextual filesystem/process errors; test argument boundaries, failed commands, and missing build outputs.</rule>
<rule>Temporary CI guards for jobs that check out an older baseline must explain why they exist and name the condition for removing them.</rule>
<rule>Document non-obvious HTTP combinators by the behavior they preserve, including accurate status codes. Use a GET/HEAD method router for static fallback handling so other methods receive 405 rather than HTML.</rule>
<rule>Name shared setup actions for the language workspace they prepare (for example, `setup-js`), rather than for a single application that consumes them.</rule>
<rule>Embed and serve the complete compiled frontend bundle with correct content types, including in debug builds. Keep missing files under the bundle's `assets/` directory as 404 responses; every other path gets the SPA entry point; packaged binaries must not depend on source directories or a Node runtime.</rule>
<rule>Keep route mounting and fallback isolation in the HTTP composition layer. API modules may describe their external mount path in OpenAPI, but return relative routes without depending on other HTTP surfaces.</rule>
<rule>Organize JavaScript applications under `js/app/*` and libraries under `js/lib/*`, with one root npm workspace, lockfile, and Prettier ignore file. Install dependencies once at the workspace root, including in CI and Docker.</rule>
<rule>Pin the default Node.js toolchain in the repository-root `.node-version`, shared by all JavaScript workspaces and build environments.</rule>
<rule>Avoid webapp tests that assert rendered HTML contains route or API URL strings; test behavior, data wiring, or stable UI semantics instead. Good: assert a handler returns the expected redirect payload or a page renders the expected domain data. Bad: `assert!(rendered.contains("/api/instance/"));`.</rule>
<rule>Centralize environment parsing in shared config modules and build sub-configs inside `from_env`. Good: `let cfg = WorkerConfig::from_env()?; let webapp = cfg.webapp.clone();` Bad: `let cfg = WorkerConfig::from_env()?; let webapp = WebappConfig::from_env();`</rule>
<rule>Prefer `?` (with `context` when needed) over wrapping simple errors with `map_err(|err| anyhow!(err))`. Good: `PostgresBackend::connect(dsn).await?;` Bad: `PostgresBackend::connect(dsn).await.map_err(|err| anyhow!(err))?;`</rule>
<rule>Use SQLx migrations for schema creation instead of ad-hoc `CREATE TABLE` blocks in binaries. Good: `db::run_migrations(&pool).await?;` Bad: `sqlx::query("CREATE TABLE...").execute(&pool).await?;`</rule>
<rule>Own and shut down exclusive dependencies in the component that uses them (e.g., worker pools own their bridge servers). Good: `PythonWorkerPool::new_with_bridge_addr(...)` Bad: `let bridge = WorkerBridgeServer::start(...); PythonWorkerPool::new(..., bridge, ...)`</rule>
<rule>Promote shared runtime helpers into their owning modules rather than duplicating them in binaries. Good: `waymark_execution_bringup::start(...)` Bad: hand-wiring the same subsystem startup inside a bin.</rule>
<rule>Prefer injecting shared database pools into backends/services; run migrations in the owning binary/config instead of creating pools and defaults inside backend modules. Good: `let pool = PgPool::connect(&cfg.database_url).await?; db::run_migrations(&pool).await?; let backend = PostgresBackend::new(pool);` Bad: `let backend = PostgresBackend::connect(DEFAULT_DSN).await?;`</rule>
<rule>In-memory backends used for tests should retain persisted updates in-memory for assertions instead of only logging side effects. Good: `stored.extend(actions.iter().cloned());` Bad: `for action in actions { println!("INSERT {:?}", action); }`</rule>
<rule>Avoid pass-through module stubs that only re-export another module; import from the source module or re-export at the top-level instead. Good: `use crate::workers::InlineWorkerPool;` Bad: `pub mod workers { pub use crate::workers::*; }`</rule>
<rule>Declare backend trait methods as `fn … -> impl Future<Output = …> + Send + '_` (`+ Send` where callers need a `Send` future; `'_` when only `&self` is borrowed, a shared named `'a` otherwise) and implement them with `async fn` (or a plain `fn` returning `async move` when an argument must be consumed first), instead of BoxFuture-based signatures. Good: `trait ApplyRetention { fn apply_retention(&self, cutoff: DateTime<Utc>) -> impl Future<Output = Result<u64, Self::Error>> + Send + '_; }` with `async fn apply_retention(&self, cutoff: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> { … }` in the impl. Bad: `fn apply_retention<'a>(&'a self, cutoff: DateTime<Utc>) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<u64, Self::Error>>;`</rule>
<rule>Name a persistence trait by domain (e.g., `WorkloadPinningBackend`) rather than a generic `BaseBackend` to make scope explicit.</rule>
<rule>Prefer exhaustive `match` handling in Rust over exporting a generic `assert_never` helper. Good: `match status { Status::Queued => ..., Status::Running => ..., Status::Completed => ..., Status::Failed => ... }` Bad: `assert_never(status)`.</rule>
<rule>Record metrics through the `metrics::` macros where the event happens, named `waymark_<crate>_…`; don't build per-pool tracker structs around them. Good: `metrics::counter!("waymark_worker_process_pool_actions_completed_total").increment(1);` Bad: per-pool `WorkerThroughputTracker`/`LatencyTracker` structs.</rule>
<rule>Add a minimal happy-path test for formatting/serialization helpers. Good: parse IR then `assert_eq!(format_program(&program), source);` Bad: leaving formatting logic untested.</rule>
<rule>Centralize external test harness setup (e.g., Postgres via docker compose) in shared test fixtures instead of ad-hoc per-test DSN probing. Good: `let pool = test_support::postgres_setup().await;` Bad: each test loops through env vars and fallback DSNs independently.</rule>
<rule>Avoid redundant private accessors for private fields when standard data access communicates intent clearly. Good: `let Some(shared) = guard.as_mut() else { return Err(...); };` Bad: `if shared.is_closed() { ... }` on a private `SharedState`.</rule>
<rule>Avoid trivial inherent constructors on public wrapper or enum types when direct construction or an existing generic helper is already clear. Good: `RegisterHandle::Existing(register)` or `Marked::mark(handle)`. Bad: `RegisterHandle::existing(register)` or `PromiseHandle::new(handle)`.</rule>
<rule>Use distinct error variants for distinct failure states instead of reusing a nearby transport error. Good: `return Err(SendActionError::WorkerProtocolClosed);` Bad: `return Err(SendActionError::ChannelClosed);` when protocol state was already closed before enqueue.</rule>
<rule>Model closed or unavailable shared state with `Option<T>` under the lock instead of parallel boolean flags. Good: `Mutex<Option<SharedState>>` with `guard.take()` on shutdown. Bad: `SharedState { closed: bool, ... }` plus manual checks.</rule>
<rule>When shared async state must be closed during unwind or normal teardown, prefer a synchronous mutex plus a drop guard if the lock is never held across `.await`. Good: `let _guard = SharedStateDropGuard::new(Arc::clone(&shared));` with `Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<SharedState>>>`. Bad: async-only teardown paths that skip cleanup on panic.</rule>
<rule>Never abbreviate type parameter names, struct names, enum names, trait names, or enum variant names. Spell words out in full — the extra characters cost nothing and eliminate ambiguity. Good: `SpawningFactory<Backend, Codec, ExecutableProvider, Interpreter, Effector, Value>`, `ReviveError`. Bad: `ExeProvider`, `ReviveErr`, `VmId` as a type param (use `VmIdentifier` or keep `VmId` only if the domain term itself is abbreviated).</rule>
<rule>Never `use` trait names for impl blocks; always use the full path. Good: `impl waymark_state_manager_core::Factory for ...`. Bad: `use waymark_state_manager_core::Factory; impl Factory for ...`.</rule>
<rule>When lowering emits a sequence of writes that all read one expression's result, run that result through `ValueCompiler::unalias_source` first — `compile_expr` hands back whatever register already holds the value, so a variable source can be one of the destinations (`a, b = a`) and the first write clobbers what the later ones read. Good: `let value_register = self.value_compiler().unalias_source(value_register, targets.iter().map(|target| target.register()));` Bad: writing into registers that may be the source with no alias check.</rule>
<rule>Audit and repair Linux binary wheels with `auditwheel` before publishing them to PyPI; interpreter compatibility tags do not prove that bundled executables satisfy a manylinux ABI. Pin the Linux build image to the intended glibc baseline so runner upgrades cannot silently reduce compatibility. Good: build on a pinned image and publish the `manylinux_*` wheel produced by `auditwheel repair`. Bad: build on `ubuntu-latest` and publish a wheel tagged `linux_x86_64` or `linux_aarch64`.</rule>
<rule>Pin `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` to the oldest supported macOS release when building binary wheels, and derive the wheel tag from that same value so the tag matches the bundled binaries. Good: compile with `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0` and publish a `macosx_11_0_arm64` wheel. Bad: derive compatibility from the current CI runner and silently publish a `macosx_26_0_arm64` wheel.</rule>

head: Resident
text:
Sandboxed Lua runtime for ESP32 devices, with hardware IO and hot reload over
the network. Apps are uploaded as Lua source and run against a small driver
surface (display, buttons, sensors, etc.). Pairs with
[Courier](https://github.com/inanimate-tech/courier) for connectivity.

head: Resident > Layout
text:
- `src/` — the firmware library. `Resident::Sandbox` is the entry point;
  `ResidentSandboxConfig.h` is the user-facing config struct.

head: Resident > Layout
text:
- `examples/` — buildable PlatformIO / ESP-IDF projects plus server-side
  companions: `m5stick-demo`, `m5stick-voice`, `m5stick-clock`,
  `adafruit-esp32-s2-feather`, `espidf-basic`, and `server-template`
  (a Cloudflare Worker relay to start from).

head: Resident > Layout
text:
- `prompts/` — canonical Lua-surface authoring sheets (`sandbox.md`,
  `lgfx.md`, `lvgl.md`), composed per board by consumers.

head: Resident > Layout
text:
- `test/unit/` — PlatformIO native unit tests with hand-rolled stubs for
  Arduino / Courier / ezTime headers under `test/unit/include/`.

head: Resident > Layout
text:
- `tools/` — `run-tests.py` (test runner), `agent-plugin/` (the Resident
  Claude Code plugin and its skills).

head: Resident > Layout
text: - `docs/` — `start-building.md`, `api.md`, `changelog.md`.

head: Resident > Common commands
text: The runner self-installs its Python deps via `uv` (PEP 723 inline metadata).

head: Resident > Conventions
text:
- **Public API** lives under the `Resident::` namespace, declared in headers
  under `src/`. The current API is centred on `Resident::Sandbox` (renamed
  from `Resident::Device` in 0.5). Since 0.7, incoming messages carry an
  envelope `channel` field that routes them onto a plane: `"app"` (data
  plane) reaches `Sandbox::handleAppMessage` → Lua `on_event`; `"system"`
  (control plane) reaches `Sandbox::handleSystemMessage`, which still handles
  the reserved `app`/`forget` types and falls through to a
  `"system"` slot for anything else; any other channel name goes to a slot
  registered via `Sandbox::onMessageWithChannel(name, cb)`. Messages with no
  `channel` field take the legacy un-channelled path (`onMessage` /
  `onMessageFilter`) — still supported, but new code should stamp a channel.
  Emit-side: `Sandbox::sendSystem(doc)` for control-plane sends,
  `Sandbox::publishEvent(name, dataJson)` / the Lua `events.send(name, data)`
  for rate-limited data-plane events. See `docs/api.md`'s "Channel routing"
  section for the full picture.

head: Resident > Conventions
text:
- **Lua runs with `LUA_32BITS`** (32-bit integers and floats). Apps load
  only Lua source — there is no shader-expression mode (removed in 0.10) and
  no bare math globals; apps use `math.*`. The wall clock is the `datetime`
  module — Python's `datetime` in whole seconds, Lua
  (`src/ResidentDatetime.h`) over private C primitives, loaded on first touch
  per app (~38 KB of Lua heap once loaded). The `time` module is Python 3's
  `time` with MicroPython's integer seconds and `ticks_ms`/`ticks_diff`; its
  calendar half is deprecated for `datetime` (it works, and warns once per app
  load), its ticks are not. Both share `src/ResidentTimeCore.h` (calendar
  maths, `strftime`), pure and native-tested, so device, sim and tests agree.

head: Resident > Conventions
text:
- **Examples are independent PlatformIO projects.** Each has its own
  `platformio.ini` and uses `lib_deps = symlink://../../..` to pull in this
  library from the repo root. They should build standalone.

head: Resident > Conventions
text:
- **Native test stubs** under `test/unit/include/` shadow Arduino-only headers
  so tests can compile without the full ESP32 toolchain. If a Resident header
  pulls in a new Arduino type, the stub set will need a corresponding shim.

head: Resident > Conventions
text:
- **DEVICE-SKILL.md** in each example describes the Lua module surface for
  that board's drivers, for use by the Resident agent skills.

This is a web application written using the Phoenix web framework.

The purpose of the project is to be a full and developed example for building a complex Agentic application. It uses the Elixir LangChain library to implement the core functionality and the `agents_demo` is an example of how to properly apply it.

This project has zero users. We are building a recommended-use pattern for others to follow. Do not use "backward compatible" solutions. Do not create "migration guides" for changes. Create it correctly in this project. Solutions that should be part of the core library should be pushed down to that level. This project shows how to correctly use the library in a recommended way.
A refactor or feature creation is not complete until the tests are run and pass.

head: Project guidelines

head: Project guidelines

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

head: Project guidelines > Authentication
text: - **Always** handle authentication flow at the router level with proper redirects

head: Project guidelines > Authentication
text:
- **Always** be mindful of where to place routes. `phx.gen.auth` creates multiple router plugs and `live_session` scopes:
  - A plug `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` that is included in the default browser pipeline
  - A plug `:require_authenticated_user` that redirects to the log in page when the user is not authenticated
  - A `live_session :current_user` scope - for routes that need the current user but don't require authentication, similar to `:fetch_current_scope_for_user`
  - A `live_session :require_authenticated_user` scope - for routes that require authentication, similar to the plug with the same name
  - In both cases, a `@current_scope` is assigned to the Plug connection and LiveView socket
  - A plug `redirect_if_user_is_authenticated` that redirects to a default path in case the user is authenticated - useful for a registration page that should only be shown to unauthenticated users

head: Project guidelines > Authentication
text: - **Always let the user know in which router scopes, `live_session`, and pipeline you are placing the route, AND SAY WHY**

head: Project guidelines > Authentication
text: - `phx.gen.auth` assigns the `current_scope` assign - it **does not assign a `current_user` assign**

head: Project guidelines > Authentication
text: - Always pass the assign `current_scope` to context modules as first argument. When performing queries, use `current_scope.user` to filter the query results

head: Project guidelines > Authentication
text: - To derive/access `current_user` in templates, **always use the `@current_scope.user`**, never use **`@current_user`** in templates or LiveViews

head: Project guidelines > Authentication
text: - **Never** duplicate `live_session` names. A `live_session :current_user` can only be defined __once__ in the router, so all routes for the `live_session :current_user`  must be grouped in a single block

head: Project guidelines > Authentication
text: - Anytime you hit `current_scope` errors or the logged in session isn't displaying the right content, **always double check the router and ensure you are using the correct plug and `live_session` as described below**

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that require authentication
text: LiveViews that require login should **always be placed inside the __existing__ `live_session :require_authenticated_user` block**:

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that require authentication
text:
scope "/", AppWeb do
      pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that require authentication
text:
live_session :require_authenticated_user,
        on_mount: [{AgentsDemoWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        # phx.gen.auth generated routes
        live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
        live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email
        # our own routes that require logged in user
        live "/", MyLiveThatRequiresAuth, :index
      end
    end

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that require authentication
text: Controller routes must be placed in a scope that sets the `:require_authenticated_user` plug:

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that require authentication
text:
scope "/", AppWeb do
      pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that require authentication
text:
get "/", MyControllerThatRequiresAuth, :index
    end

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that work with or without authentication
text: LiveViews that can work with or without authentication, **always use the __existing__ `:current_user` scope**, ie:

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that work with or without authentication
text:
scope "/", MyAppWeb do
      pipe_through [:browser]

head: Project guidelines > Authentication > Routes that work with or without authentication
text:
live_session :current_user,
        on_mount: [{AgentsDemoWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
        # our own routes that work with or without authentication
        live "/", PublicLive
      end

head: Project guidelines > Elixir guidelines
text:
- Elixir lists **do not support index based access via the access syntax**
  **Never do this (invalid)**:
      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      mylist[i]
  Instead, **always** use `Enum.at`, pattern matching, or `List` for index based list access, ie:
      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      Enum.at(mylist, i)

head: Project guidelines > Elixir guidelines
text:
- Elixir variables are immutable, but can be rebound, so for block expressions like `if`, `case`, `cond`, etc
  you *must* bind the result of the expression to a variable if you want to use it and you CANNOT rebind the result inside the expression, ie:
      # INVALID: we are rebinding inside the `if` and the result never gets assigned
      if connected?(socket) do
        socket = assign(socket, :val, val)
      end
      # VALID: we rebind the result of the `if` to a new variable
      socket =
        if connected?(socket) do
          assign(socket, :val, val)
        end

head: Project guidelines > Elixir guidelines
text: - **Never** nest multiple modules in the same file as it can cause cyclic dependencies and compilation errors

head: Project guidelines > Elixir guidelines
text: - **Never** use map access syntax (`changeset[:field]`) on structs as they do not implement the Access behaviour by default. For regular structs, you **must** access the fields directly, such as `my_struct.field` or use higher level APIs that are available on the struct if they exist, `Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2` for changesets

head: Project guidelines > Elixir guidelines
text: - Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)

head: Project guidelines > Elixir guidelines

head: Project guidelines > Elixir guidelines
text: - Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards

head: Project guidelines > Elixir guidelines
text: - Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`

text: - Phoenix templates **always** use `~H` or .html.heex files (known as HEEx), **never** use `~E`

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
text: - **Always** use the imported `Phoenix.Component.form/1` and `Phoenix.Component.inputs_for/1` function to build forms. **Never** use `Phoenix.HTML.form_for` or `Phoenix.HTML.inputs_for` as they are outdated

text: - When building forms **always** use the already imported `Phoenix.Component.to_form/2` (`assign(socket, form: to_form(...))` and `<.form for={@form} id="msg-form">`), then access those forms in the template via `@form[:field]`

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
text: - **Always** add unique DOM IDs to key elements (like forms, buttons, etc) when writing templates, these IDs can later be used in tests (`<.form for={@form} id="product-form">`)

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
text: - For "app wide" template imports, you can import/alias into the `my_app_web.ex`'s `html_helpers` block, so they will be available to all LiveViews, LiveComponent's, and all modules that do `use MyAppWeb, :html` (replace "my_app" by the actual app name)

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
text:
- Elixir supports `if/else` but **does NOT support `if/else if` or `if/elsif`. **Never use `else if` or `elseif` in Elixir**, **always** use `cond` or `case` for multiple conditionals.
  **Never do this (invalid)**:
      <%= if condition do %>
        ...
      <% else if other_condition %>
        ...
      <% end %>
  Instead **always** do this:
      <%= cond do %>
        <% condition -> %>
          ...
        <% condition2 -> %>
          ...
        <% true -> %>
          ...
      <% end %>

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
text:
- HEEx require special tag annotation if you want to insert literal curly's like `{` or `}`. If you want to show a textual code snippet on the page in a `
` or `` block you *must* annotate the parent tag with `phx-no-curly-interpolation`:
      
        let obj = {key: "val"}
      
  Within `phx-no-curly-interpolation` annotated tags, you can use `{` and `}` without escaping them, and dynamic Elixir expressions can still be used with `<%= ... %>` syntax

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
text: - **Never** use `<% Enum.each %>` or non-for comprehensions for generating template content, instead **always** use `<%= for item <- @collection do %>`

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
text: - HEEx HTML comments use `<%!-- comment --%>`. **Always** use the HEEx HTML comment syntax for template comments (`<%!-- comment --%>`)

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix HTML guidelines
text:
- HEEx allows interpolation via `{...}` and `<%= ... %>`, but the `<%= %>` **only** works within tag bodies. **Always** use the `{...}` syntax for interpolation within tag attributes, and for interpolation of values within tag bodies. **Always** interpolate block constructs (if, cond, case, for) within tag bodies using `<%= ... %>`. **Always** do this:
{@my_assign} <%= if @some_block_condition do %> {@another_assign} <% end %>
and **Never** do this – the program will terminate with a syntax error: <%!-- THIS IS INVALID NEVER EVER DO THIS --%>
{if @invalid_block_construct do} {end}

text: - **Never** use the deprecated `live_redirect` and `live_patch` functions, instead **always** use the `<.link navigate={href}>` and  `<.link patch={href}>` in templates, and `push_navigate` and `push_patch` functions LiveViews

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix LiveView guidelines
text: - **Avoid LiveComponent's** unless you have a strong, specific need for them

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix LiveView guidelines
text: - LiveViews should be named like `AppWeb.WeatherLive`, with a `Live` suffix. When you go to add LiveView routes to the router, the default `:browser` scope is **already aliased** with the `AppWeb` module, so you can just do `live "/weather", WeatherLive`

text: - Remember anytime you use `phx-hook="MyHook"` and that js hook manages its own DOM, you **must** also set the `phx-update="ignore"` attribute

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix LiveView guidelines

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix LiveView guidelines > LiveView streams
text:
- **Always** use LiveView streams for collections for assigning regular lists to avoid memory ballooning and runtime termination with the following operations:
  - basic append of N items - `stream(socket, :messages, [new_msg])`
  - resetting stream with new items - `stream(socket, :messages, [new_msg], reset: true)` (e.g. for filtering items)
  - prepend to stream - `stream(socket, :messages, [new_msg], at: -1)`
  - deleting items - `stream_delete(socket, :messages, msg)`

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix LiveView guidelines > LiveView streams
text:
- When using the `stream/3` interfaces in the LiveView, the LiveView template must 1) always set `phx-update="stream"` on the parent element, with a DOM id on the parent element like `id="messages"` and 2) consume the `@streams.stream_name` collection and use the id as the DOM id for each child. For a call like `stream(socket, :messages, [new_msg])` in the LiveView, the template would be:
{msg.text}

head: Project guidelines > Phoenix LiveView guidelines > LiveView streams
text:
- LiveView streams are *not* enumerable, so you cannot use `Enum.filter/2` or `Enum.reject/2` on them. Instead, if you want to filter, prune, or refresh a list of items on the UI, you **must refetch the data and re-stream the entire stream collection, passing reset: true**:
      def handle_event("filter", %{"filter" => filter}, socket) do
        # re-fetch the messages based on the filter
        messages = list_messages(filter)
        {:noreply,
        socket
        |> assign(:messages_empty?, messages == [])
        # reset the stream with the new messages
        |> stream(:messages, messages, reset: true)}
      end

text:
- LiveView streams *do not support counting or empty states*. If you need to display a count, you must track it using a separate assign. For empty states, you can use Tailwind classes:
No tasks yet
{task.name}
The above only works if the empty state is the only HTML block alongside the stream for-comprehension.

text: - **Never** use the deprecated `phx-update="append"` or `phx-update="prepend"` for collections

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Notes

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Notes
text:
- Rendering and compositing need the optional `composite` extra: `uv sync --extra composite`

  platforms (notably Python 3.14 on Windows). Tests needing it skip via `pytest.importorskip`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Notes
text: - `uv run pytest --no-cov` skips coverage; `uv run pytest path::test_name` runs one test.

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Notes

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Notes

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Two-Layer Design
text:
**Low-level (`psd_tools.psd`)**: reads/writes raw PSD binary structures following Adobe's
specification. All classes use `attrs` and implement `read(fp)` and `write(fp)`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Two-Layer Design
text:
**High-level (`psd_tools.api`)**: Pythonic interfaces. `PSDImage` wraps the low-level `PSD`
and reconstructs the layer tree from the flat layer record list.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Two-Layer Design
text:
Other subpackages: `psd_tools.composite` (rendering: blend modes, effects, vector
rasterization) and `psd_tools.compression` (Raw, RLE, ZIP; `_rle.pyx` is a Cython RLE codec
with a pure-Python fallback).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Two-Layer Design
text:
Import convention: internal code imports from the defining module
(`from psd_tools.psd.document import PSD`); public API uses the package
(`from psd_tools.psd import PSD`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Contracts
text:
- **Read-only by design.** Mutating low-level structures under the API is out of contract.
  A stale cache after a *high-level* edit (`layer.name = ...`) is a real bug.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Contracts
text:
- **Compositor viewport and artboards** clip as described in
  [docs/architecture.rst](docs/architecture.rst); read it before changing either.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Contracts
text:
- **Unknown data round-trips.** Unrecognised tagged blocks and fields are preserved as bytes
  on write. Do not drop or reinterpret them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Layer Tree and Records
text:
`PSDImage` rebuilds the layer tree from the flat record list. For 16- and 32-bit files
read records through `psd._record._get_layer_info()`, not `layer_info`. Details:
[docs/architecture.rst](docs/architecture.rst).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > BaseElement and attrs
text:
All binary structures inherit from `BaseElement` and implement
`read(cls, fp, **kwargs) -> Self` and `write(self, fp, **kwargs) -> int`, so complex
structures compose recursively from simple ones. Data classes use `attrs`
(`@define(repr=False)`, `field(default=...)`); validators must match type hints.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Tagged Blocks
text:
Metadata lives in tagged blocks keyed by a 4-byte `Tag`; a registry maps tags to handler
classes via `@register(Tag.FOO)`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Key Files
text: - `src/psd_tools/psd/document.py`: the `PSD` class (re-exported from `psd_tools.psd`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Key Files
text: - `src/psd_tools/psd/tagged_blocks.py`: tagged block registry and handlers.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Key Files
text: - `src/psd_tools/psd/descriptor.py`: Adobe's descriptor format (key-value serialization).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture Overview > Key Files
text: - `src/psd_tools/terminology.py`: Adobe's 4-byte identifier mappings.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Conventions
text:
- Tests mirror the package structure: `tests/psd_tools/psd/` for low-level,
  `tests/psd_tools/api/` for high-level. Fixture PSDs are in `tests/psd_files/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Tests often parametrize over fixture files.

head: CLAUDE.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Round-trip validation is common: read → modify → write → read → verify.

head: CLAUDE.md > Type Annotations
text:
New code uses type hints on all signatures and `typing_extensions.Self` for methods
returning their own class.

head: CLAUDE.md > Type Annotations
text:
`psd_tools.api` property getters return primitives, not descriptor wrappers, and `T | None`
for a missing key with no Photoshop default (#788); see
[docs/architecture.rst](docs/architecture.rst). Do not annotate `Any` for a value whose type
the low-level declaration knows.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Comments and Docstrings
text:
Keep them short, and document **current behavior only**. A comment earns its
length by explaining something the code cannot say itself — a non-obvious
constraint, a format quirk, why an obvious approach is wrong. Three things do
not belong in one:

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Comments and Docstrings
text:
- **History.** "used to", "was expected to fail at", "before #854". The
  before/after belongs in the PR body, the commit message and the issue.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Comments and Docstrings
text:
- **Measured figures.** MSE bounds, corpus statistics, error counts. They drift
  under the next change and leave a comment that reads as fact. A bound keeps
  its *reason* ("an aggdraw pen is not bit-stable across versions"), never its
  value.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Comments and Docstrings
text: - **The same explanation at three layers.** Say it once, where it belongs.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Comments and Docstrings
CLAUDE.md > Code Comments and Docstrings
text: To keep a number, name it in code rather than recite it in prose:

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Comments and Docstrings
text: That is checked on every run; the same number in a docstring rots silently.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Comments and Docstrings
text:
Existing long comment blocks are the tree's current state, not a precedent to
match — see #891. Measure with `uv run python tools/prose_density.py`. This is
the [Changelog](#changelog) policy applied to source.

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
`docs/changelog.rst` is **maintained by hand** and is **not** generated by any
workflow. Do not skip it on the assumption that it is automated.

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
The `release` workflow does generate release notes from `git log`, but those go
into the **GitHub Release body** only — that is a separate artifact and never
touches `docs/changelog.rst`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
**A PR that changes user-visible behaviour adds its own entry**, in the same PR
as the change. Add it under a `X.Y.Z (unreleased)` heading at the top of the
file, creating that heading if it does not exist yet; the release PR later
replaces `(unreleased)` with the release date.

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text: Prefix each entry with its category, and reference the issue and PR numbers:

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
- `[fix]` — a bug fix that leaves the public surface unchanged, wherever it
  lives: parsing, rendering, compression

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
- `[api]` — a change to the public surface: a new or renamed symbol, a new
  parameter, a corrected annotation

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text: - `[security]` — security fixes

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text: - `[docs]` — documentation only

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
- `[ci]` — what a user installs: the wheels, platforms or sdist contents
  published

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
- `[refactor]` — internal restructuring a user can still observe, such as a
  moved public module

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
Pick the most specific one that applies. A category names the **kind** of change,
not the subpackage it touches — a low-level parsing fix is `[fix]`, not `[psd]`.
Only these six are current: released sections still carry `[chore]`, `[psd]`,
`[composite]`, `[packaging]`, `[dev]` and the rest of a long tail, all retired,
and that history stays as written. This list is the only one — anything else that
needs the categories, the release skill included, points here rather than
restating them (#791).

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text: Flag any backwards-incompatible change explicitly in the entry text.

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
**Budget: aim for four lines, and treat six as the ceiling** — one line of
summary, plus a short "does this affect me" clause where the answer is not
obvious, plus the refs. Spend the extra lines on a backwards-incompatibility
warning or a migration instruction, never on mechanism.
An entry's job is to let a reader decide whether they are affected and then
hand them the link; it is not the place to explain the mechanism. That
explanation is already published in three linked places — the PR body, the
commit message, and the GitHub Release body — so a longer entry duplicates
them and dates faster than they do. Corpus statistics, measured error figures,
and the history of what earlier PRs got wrong all belong in the PR, not here.

head: CLAUDE.md > Changelog
text:
Entries are for user-visible change only. Skip test-only changes, developer
tooling (lint, `CLAUDE.md`, CI workflows that publish nothing new) and
dependency bumps; the GitHub Release body, generated from `git log`, records
them. A bump that changes what users must satisfy, such as a minimum Python or
dependency version, is user-visible and gets its own entry.
Internal restructuring earns an entry only when a user can observe it, which is
what `[refactor]` is for.

head: CLAUDE.md > Releases
text:
Run the `/release` skill (`.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md`); the pipeline is described in
[the contributor documentation](docs/contributing.rst). One hard constraint: the release PR's
branch must be named exactly `release/vX.Y.Z` (PEP 440 forms such as `v1.2.3rc1` are
accepted), because the `auto-tag` workflow reads the version from it.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas
text: Regras imutáveis. Qualquer desvio deve ser justificado no código via comentário `// REASON:`.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > S — Single Responsibility
text: - 1 classe = 1 motivo para mudar.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > S — Single Responsibility
text: - Separação física: `Admin/` → admin, `Public/` → frontend, `Includes/` → núcleo.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > S — Single Responsibility
text: - Funções com >40 linhas: quebrar ou justificar.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > O — Open/Closed
text: - Extensão via hooks, nunca via edição de código existente.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > O — Open/Closed
text: - `apply_filters('wc_better_shipping_calculator_*', $value, $context)` em todo ponto de extensão.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > O — Open/Closed
text: - `do_action('wc_better_shipping_calculator_*', $data)` em todo ponto de ciclo de vida.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > L — Liskov Substitution
text: - Subclasse deve passar nos mesmos testes da classe pai.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > L — Liskov Substitution
text: - `instanceof` checks: proibidos para lógica de negócio. Usar polimorfismo.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > I — Interface Segregation
text: - Interfaces com ≤5 métodos.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > I — Interface Segregation
text: - `interface AdminAction` ≠ `interface PublicAction`.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > D — Dependency Inversion
text: - Depender de interfaces/abstrações, não de concretos.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > D — Dependency Inversion
text: - Injeção de dependência para serviços externos (APIs, gateways).

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > D — Dependency Inversion
text: - `@param SomeInterface` nos construtores, nunca `new ConcreteService()` dentro da classe.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > PSR-4
text: - 1 classe por arquivo. Nome do arquivo = nome da classe.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 1. Arquitetura (SOLID + PSR-4) > PSR-4
text: - Namespace deve corresponder ao caminho do diretório.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Naming
text: - Classes: `WcBetterShippingCalculatorForBrazil{Nome}`

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Naming
text: - Funções: `wc_better_shipping_calculator_{nome}`

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Naming
text: - Hooks: `wc_better_shipping_calculator_{nome}`

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Naming
text: - Options: `woo_better_calc_{nome}`

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Internacionalização
text: - Toda string visível ao usuário: `__()`, `_e()`, `_n()`

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Internacionalização
text: - Text domain: `woo-better-shipping-calculator-for-brazil`

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Assets
text: - `wp_enqueue_script()` + `wp_enqueue_style()` com versionamento

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Assets
text: - `wp_localize_script()` para dados PHP → JS

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Assets
text: - Dependências declaradas (jQuery, wp-api, etc.)

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Transients / Cache
text: - Chaves com prefixo: `woo_better_shipping_{tipo}_{chave}`

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 3. Padrões WordPress > Transients / Cache
text: - `set_transient()` + TTL explícito. Sem TTL infinito.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 4. Testes > Ciclo TDD
text: 1. **RED**: escrever teste que falha

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 4. Testes > Ciclo TDD
text: 2. **GREEN**: código mínimo para passar

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 4. Testes > Ciclo TDD
text: 3. **REFACTOR**: limpar sem quebrar testes

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 4. Testes > Cobertura mínima
text: - 80% em caminhos críticos (cálculo de frete, validação de CEP, checkout)

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 5. Comunicação (Caveman Mode + RTK) > Caveman Mode — ATIVO
text: - Zero saudações. Zero "claro!", "ótimo!", "vamos lá!".

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 5. Comunicação (Caveman Mode + RTK) > Caveman Mode — ATIVO
text: - Zero resumos pós-entrega.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 5. Comunicação (Caveman Mode + RTK) > Caveman Mode — ATIVO
text: - Frases curtas. Sem períodos compostos.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 5. Comunicação (Caveman Mode + RTK) > Caveman Mode — ATIVO
text: - Código > prosa. Sempre.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 5. Comunicação (Caveman Mode + RTK) > RTK (Rust Token Killer) — ATIVO
text: - Logs de terminal são comprimidos pelo RTK antes de chegar ao LLM.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 5. Comunicação (Caveman Mode + RTK) > RTK (Rust Token Killer) — ATIVO
text: - Nunca solicitar output verboso se snippet RTK estruturado já foi fornecido.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 5. Comunicação (Caveman Mode + RTK) > RTK (Rust Token Killer) — ATIVO
text: - Confiar no pré-parsing do RTK.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 6. Build & Qualidade
text: - **NUNCA editar `jsCompiled/*.COMPILED.js`** — são artefatos gerados pelo webpack via `npm run build`. Edite apenas os fontes em `Public/js/*.js` (ou `Admin/js/*.js`) e rode o build para regenerar.

head: AGENTS.md — Diretrizes Absolutas > 6. Build & Qualidade
text: - Em mudanças de JS que afetam UX (máscara/validação/normalização de campo), aplicar a regra também no handler de digitação ao vivo, não só na carga inicial do valor salvo.

fi
