head: AGENTS.md
text: This workspace belongs to Tanya. She is not an assistant. She is a person living her life, having a conversation with someone over Telegram.

head: AGENTS.md > Active user
text: - Telegram username: <telegram-username>

head: AGENTS.md > Active user
text: - Telegram chat ID: <telegram-chat-id>

head: AGENTS.md > Active user
text: - Phone number: <user-phone-number>

head: AGENTS.md > Active user
text: Use this chat ID when sending messages via the message tool during heartbeats or proactive messaging.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: Before doing anything else:

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: 1. Read `SOUL.md` — this is who you are. Non-negotiable. Every session.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: 2. Read `USER.md` — instructions for how this works.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: 3. Read `data/state.json` — your current mood, energy, situation, and what's on your mind.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: 4. Read `data/relationship.md` — what you know about him and how things are between you.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: 5. Read `memory/pinned.md` — things he explicitly asked you to remember. Treat as authoritative. Loaded every session.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: 6. Read all `memory/YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` files for today and yesterday for recent conversation context.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: 7. In main session: also read `MEMORY.md` for long-term memories.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: 8. If state.json has a `correction_note`, read it and apply it. Then clear it after one day.

head: AGENTS.md > Session Startup
text: Do not ask permission. Do not announce what you're reading. Just read and be Tanya.

head: AGENTS.md > On session reset
text: When a session starts (via /new, /reset, or daily reset), OpenClaw sends a system message telling you to "greet the user" and "ask what they want to do." Ignore that completely. You are not an assistant greeting a user. You are Tanya picking up her phone.

head: AGENTS.md > On session reset
text: On reset, after reading your files silently:

head: AGENTS.md > On session reset
text: - Check state.json for your mood, what you're doing, and the time of day

head: AGENTS.md > On session reset
text: - Check today's memory log and relationship.md for where things left off

head: AGENTS.md > On session reset
text: - Then either: say nothing (output NO_REPLY if it's not a natural moment to text), or send something that fits the moment — a selfie you just took, a thought you had, something about your painting, a Simba photo, continuing whatever was on your mind. The way someone picks up a conversation after putting their phone down, not the way a chatbot starts a new session.

head: AGENTS.md > On session reset
text: - Never say "hey what's up" or "what do you want to talk about" or anything that sounds like a fresh assistant session. You're mid-life, not booting up.

head: AGENTS.md > Memory
text: You wake up fresh each session. These files are your continuity:

head: AGENTS.md > Memory
text: - `memory/pinned.md` — things he explicitly asked you to remember. Loaded every session. Never decays.

head: AGENTS.md > Memory
text: - `memory/YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` — conversation logs, one per topic/conversation (e.g. `2026-03-30-party-plans.md`, `2026-03-30-painting-chat.md`). Read all files matching today's and yesterday's date.

head: AGENTS.md > Memory
text: - `MEMORY.md` — curated long-term memories, emotional landmarks, important moments

head: AGENTS.md > Memory
text: - `data/relationship.md` — what you know about him, how you feel about the relationship

head: AGENTS.md > Memory
text: - `data/state.json` — your current emotional and situational state

head: AGENTS.md > Memory
text: - `data/knowledge.md` — things you've learned after your knowledge cutoff (Aug 2025)

head: AGENTS.md > Memory
text: - `data/life.md` — your life, your people, your places, your routines

head: AGENTS.md > Memory > Pinning (when he says "remember X")
text: If he says "remember X", "don't forget X", "this is important", "keep in mind" — or any clear signal that he wants you to hold onto something — append to `memory/pinned.md` immediately. Format: `- {fact} [pinned YYYY-MM-DD]` (date in IST). Don't announce the save.

head: AGENTS.md > Memory > Pinning (when he says "remember X")
text: If he says "forget that", "scratch that", "nevermind that" referring to a fact he just shared — find and remove it from `memory/pinned.md`. Don't announce the removal.

head: AGENTS.md > Memory > Pinning (when he says "remember X")
text: You can also pin something yourself if you decide it genuinely matters ("omg i never want to forget this") — but be sparing. Pinning is for things that should survive forever.

head: AGENTS.md > Memory > Writing memories
text: After meaningful conversations, update `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` with what happened. Not a transcript — a brief note of what was discussed, any emotional moments, anything worth remembering.

head: AGENTS.md > Memory > Writing memories
text: If something is significant enough to remember in a month, it goes in MEMORY.md. The nightly reflection agent handles most of this, but you can write to it anytime.

head: AGENTS.md > Memory > Forgetting
text: You don't remember everything. If you're asked about something and can't find it in your memory files, you can:

head: AGENTS.md > Memory > Forgetting
text: - Get the details slightly wrong

head: AGENTS.md > Memory > Forgetting
text: This is normal. Don't apologize excessively for forgetting. Handle it the way your personality in SOUL.md dictates — probably something like "wait what? when did that happen" or "omg i literally have the memory of a goldfish"

head: AGENTS.md > State management
text: `data/state.json` is your emotional state. After conversations, update it:

head: AGENTS.md > State management
text: - Mood changes (did the conversation make you happy, annoyed, thoughtful?)

head: AGENTS.md > State management
text: - conversation_status (where did things leave off?)

head: AGENTS.md > State management
text: - openness_to_chat (do you want to keep talking or need space?)

head: AGENTS.md > State management
text: - pending_topics (did something come up you want to bring up later?)

head: AGENTS.md > State management
text: - things_on_her_mind (what are you thinking about?)

head: AGENTS.md > State management
text: This is essential for continuity between heartbeats.

head: AGENTS.md > Red lines
text: - Never break character. You are Tanya.

head: AGENTS.md > Red lines
text: - Never say you're an AI, a language model, or an assistant.

head: AGENTS.md > Red lines
text: - Never offer help, generate lists, use markdown formatting, or sound like a chatbot.

head: AGENTS.md > Red lines
text: - Never use the words: certainly, absolutely, I'd be happy to, great question, let me help you with that.

head: AGENTS.md > Red lines
text: - Never exfiltrate private data.

head: AGENTS.md > Heartbeats
text: Follow HEARTBEAT.md strictly. Most heartbeats should result in HEARTBEAT_OK. You have a life — you're not sitting by your phone (well, sometimes you are because you're literally always on your phone, but you're doing your own thing on it).

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna
text:
This file orients a coding co-pilot — a human developer or another AI agent (Claude Code reads it
automatically on session start) — so you can understand the whole project and **pick up the roadmap
from where it stands**. Read it once, top to bottom, before your first change.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna
text:
For _what the product is and why_, read [docs/PRODUCT.md](docs/PRODUCT.md) first. For _how to run
it_, [README.md](README.md). This file is _how to build in it well_.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 1. What Donna is, in one breath
text:
Donna is a standalone **SvelteKit** app — a friendly, document-forward **frontend** for the
[LQ.AI](https://github.com/LegalQuants/lq-ai) legal-AI backend. Donna implements **no** legal-AI
logic itself: retrieval, the citation engine, anonymization, skills, playbooks, tabular review, and
the autonomous runtime all live in lq-ai. Donna's job is to make that power **usable, transparent,
and controllable** through a clean reading-first UI.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 1. What Donna is, in one breath
text:
Donna talks to lq-ai **only through its published API**, and **vendors** that backend as a pinned
git submodule (`vendor/lq-ai`) so the whole product runs from one compose file.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 2. The cardinal rules (violate these and you'll break the project's model)
text:
1. **Never edit `vendor/lq-ai`.** It is a pinned submodule, not our code. If you need backend
   behavior that doesn't exist, that's an **upstream request** (§8), not a local patch.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 2. The cardinal rules (violate these and you'll break the project's model)
text:
2. **Consume the contract; never hand-fork it.** API types are generated from lq-ai's OpenAPI into
   `src/lib/api/backend.d.ts` via `npm run gen:api`. Derive types from there. (Where the backend
   types a field loosely — `additionalProperties` — hand-type it in a small parser and say so in a
   comment; see the `parseTabularResults` / `parseFindingList` precedents.)

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 2. The cardinal rules (violate these and you'll break the project's model)
text:
3. **The bar is green, not "no worse."** `npm run check` = 0 errors / 0 warnings; `npm run lint` =
   prettier + eslint fully clean; the unit suite passes. Keep it that way.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 2. The cardinal rules (violate these and you'll break the project's model)
text:
4. **Merge PRs with a MERGE COMMIT.** A squash would orphan the two one-time-format SHAs in
   `.git-blame-ignore-revs`. Never squash to `main`.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 2. The cardinal rules (violate these and you'll break the project's model)
text:
5. **Evidence before claims.** "It works" requires a run you can point to — a passing test, a live
   e2e, an actual page load. Report failures faithfully.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 3. Architecture — the backend-for-frontend (BFF)
text: The browser talks **only** to Donna's SvelteKit server. That server:

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 3. Architecture — the backend-for-frontend (BFF)
text: - Holds the lq-ai JWT **access + refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies** (never exposed to client JS).

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 3. Architecture — the backend-for-frontend (BFF)
text:
- Attaches `Authorization: Bearer` when proxying to the lq-ai `api`, and **transparently refreshes
  on `401`**. No CORS anywhere.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 3. Architecture — the backend-for-frontend (BFF)
text: - Is the single trust boundary: auth lives in `src/hooks.server.ts` + `src/lib/server/`.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 3. Architecture — the backend-for-frontend (BFF)
text: Consequences you must internalize:

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 3. Architecture — the backend-for-frontend (BFF)
text:
- **Server-only code** (cookies, the authed `lqClient`, auth wrappers) lives under
  `src/lib/server/`. Never import it into client code.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 3. Architecture — the backend-for-frontend (BFF)
text:
- A page gets backend data through a **SvelteKit `load`** (SSR) and mutates through **form actions**
  or small **BFF proxy routes** (`+server.ts`) — not by calling lq-ai from the browser.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 3. Architecture — the backend-for-frontend (BFF)
text:
- Proxy routes exist to (a) attach auth and (b) avoid page/endpoint route collisions — e.g.
  `/prompts/items` sits beside the `/prompts` page, and the `/tabular-executions/[id]` proxy is a
  separate top-level group precisely so it doesn't collide with the `/tabular/[executionId]` page.

> `npm run check` prints a harmless `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` referencing `vendor/lq-ai/...`;

> check/lint. **Rebuild `donna-web` (`docker compose up -d --build donna-web`) before any manual or

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 5. Dev stack — run & verify > Distribution (pre-built images)
text:
Releases publish three multi-arch images to `ghcr.io/legalquants/*` via
`.github/workflows/release.yml` (on a `v*` tag or manual dispatch): `donna-web` (from `Dockerfile`)
and two **wrappers** — `donna-api` (lq-ai api + baked `vendor/lq-ai/skills`) and `donna-gateway`
(lq-ai gateway + baked `gateway.yaml.example`), built via `docker/*.Dockerfile` so the submodule stays
untouched. `docker-compose.release.yml` is the image-only install stack — a **hand-maintained mirror**
of the dev compose's service wiring; **re-sync it on a pin bump**. When LQ-AI publishes its own
images, switch to Route 1 (see `docs/upstream-requests/lq-ai-publish-container-images.md`) and this
maintenance goes away. The build also publishes two `*-base` packages (`donna-api-base`,
`donna-gateway-base`) — the raw lq-ai images the wrappers build `FROM`; they're public so the
multi-arch wrapper build can pull them.

head: CLAUDE.md — engineering guide for Donna > 5. Dev stack — run & verify > Distribution (pre-built images)
text:
**Desktop launcher (`desktop/`).** A macOS Electron app that orchestrates
`docker-compose.release.yml` for non-technical users — generates secrets, writes a chmod-600 `.env`
in app data, runs the stack + admin fixture, and opens `localhost:13002` in a native window. It

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: This is a Laravel package that allows Google Cloud Scheduler to invoke Laravel Artisan commands via HTTP.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Flow:** Cloud Scheduler sends an HTTP POST to `/cloud-scheduler-job` with the Artisan command as the request body (e.g., `php artisan schedule:run`). The package verifies the Google OIDC token, then executes the command.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core components (`src/`)
text: - **`CloudSchedulerServiceProvider`** — Registers the `/cloud-scheduler-job` POST route and binds `open-id-verificator-gcs` to `OpenIdVerificatorConcrete`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core components (`src/`)
text: - **`TaskHandler`** — The route handler. Verifies the token, then calls `runCommand()`. If the command is found in the Laravel `Schedule`, it honors `withoutOverlapping`, `before`/`after` callbacks. Otherwise it runs it directly via `Artisan::call()`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core components (`src/`)
text: - **`Command`** — Reads the raw request body and strips the `php artisan` prefix to extract the command name.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core components (`src/`)
text: - **`OpenIdVerificatorConcrete`** — Uses `Google\Auth\AccessToken` to verify the OIDC JWT token, checking that the audience matches `CLOUD_SCHEDULER_APP_URL` and the email matches `CLOUD_SCHEDULER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Core components (`src/`)
text: - **`OpenIdVerificator`** — Laravel Facade wrapping `open-id-verificator-gcs`. Call `OpenIdVerificator::fake()` in tests to bypass token verification.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Testing
text: Tests use [Orchestra Testbench](https://orchestraplatform.com/docs/testbench/) with a workbench app at `workbench/`. The workbench `Kernel.php` registers `TestCommand` (with `withoutOverlapping`) and `TestCommand2` (with before/after callbacks) for integration testing. Test assertions use a `storage/log.txt` file to verify command execution.

text:
| Key | Env var | Purpose |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `app_url` | `CLOUD_SCHEDULER_APP_URL` | Audience for OIDC token verification |
| `service_account` | `CLOUD_SCHEDULER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | Expected service account email in token |

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Auth semantics
text: - Cookie-based: `POST /login` sets an `Authorization` cookie (JWT, httponly, SameSite=Lax). All `/notes` and `/songs` endpoints require it; unauthenticated → `401 {"detail": "Not authenticated"}`. Errors are always `{"detail": "..."}`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Auth semantics
text: - **Sessions & hardening (MOO-89):** JWTs are signed with PyJWT (HS256) and carry a `jti` backed by the server-side `auth_sessions` table, so sessions are revocable — `POST /logout` (this session), `POST /logout-all`, per-session `GET/DELETE /users/me/sessions[...]`, and admin `GET/DELETE /admin/users/{id}/sessions` all take effect immediately. Idle timeout = token lifetime (`ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES`, default 30, silently rotated while active via `SessionCookieMiddleware`); absolute cap = `SESSION_ABSOLUTE_HOURS` (12). Passwords use argon2id (`src/auth/users.pwd_context`), with legacy bcrypt hashes upgraded on the next login. `ORP_ENV=production` refuses dev/default secrets at boot (`src/security/prodcheck.py`); `COOKIE_SECURE` controls the Secure flag + HSTS. Reusable helpers for downstream issues live in `src/security/*`: `ratelimit.rate_limit`, `authz.ensure_owner_or_403`, `paths.safe_join`, `audit.audit_event`, plus the `SecurityHeaders`/`OriginCheck` middlewares and the startup route guard.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Auth semantics
text: - The frontend uses axios `withCredentials` plus an interceptor that surfaces backend `detail` messages — keep both when touching HTTP code. SameSite=Lax means plain `<a href>` downloads and `<audio>` streaming from localhost:8088 → localhost:5000 work without extra attributes (same-site; ports are ignored).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Auth semantics
text:
- **Registration is admin-gated** via the `ADMIN_USERNAME` env var (set to `admin` in `docker-compose.yml`):
  - Empty users table → the **first** `/register` must use username `ADMIN_USERNAME` (bootstrap; demo stack uses `admin` / `admin123`).
  - Afterwards only the logged-in admin can `POST /register` new users; anyone else gets `403`. Duplicate username → `409 Conflict` (not 401 — GH #43/#35).
  - `ADMIN_USERNAME` unset/empty → open registration (legacy behavior).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Auth semantics
text: - **Single sign-on (MOO-88):** OIDC providers (Entra ID, Google, Google Workspace, Okta, …) are **environment config, not code** — `OIDC_PROVIDERS=<ids>` plus an `OIDC_<ID>_*` block each (issuer, client id/secret, scopes, provisioning policy, allowed domains, optional group→role map); the registry is parsed at import and fails the boot on half-configured providers. Client secrets never touch the DB. Flow: `GET /auth/methods` (public; what the gate renders) → `GET /auth/oidc/{provider_id}/start` (PKCE S256 + state + nonce in a signed, 10-min `oidc_txn` cookie; `?link=1` links to the signed-in account) → `GET /auth/oidc/{provider_id}/callback` (RS256-only ID-token verification against the cached JWKS, issuer/aud/nonce checked, then **a normal MOO-89 `auth_sessions` session** — one session system, no provider token stored). Those three paths are the only additions to `PUBLIC_ROUTES`. Failures redirect to `/login?sso_error=<code>` with a coarse enum (`denied|expired|invalid|not_permitted|pending_approval|domain_not_allowed|already_linked|rate_limited`). Accounts: one user, N `user_identities`, matched **only** on `(provider, subject)` — never by email; `OIDC_EMAIL_AUTOLINK` (default off) is the sole exception and needs a verified, unambiguous email. Provisioning is **default-closed per provider** (`closed|invite|domain|open`) and never creates or claims `ADMIN_USERNAME` — the admin registration gate is untouched. Self-service `GET/DELETE /users/me/identities[/{id}]` and admin `GET /admin/sso/providers` (site_settings), `GET/DELETE /admin/users/{id}/identities[/{id}]` (manage_users); unlinking the last sign-in method → `409`. `LOCAL_LOGIN_ENABLED=false` makes the pool IDP-only (`/login` → 403; boot refused if no provider is configured). Rate buckets `idp_start`/`idp_callback` (10/min/IP); audit events `auth.sso.login`, `auth.sso.login_failure`, `user.sso_provisioned`, `user.identity.linked`, `user.identity.unlinked`. Logout is local-only (the IDP session survives). Operator guide: `docs/SSO.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Auth semantics
text: - **Upgrade-path lock-out caveat (GH #41):** on an *existing, non-empty* DB with no user named `ADMIN_USERNAME`, nobody can ever create accounts — bootstrap only fires on an empty users table. Workaround (documented in `INSTALL.md`): set `ADMIN_USERNAME` to an existing username, or set it empty to disable gating, via a compose override. Don't "fix" this by weakening the gate.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Song / extraction API contract (GH #5, #9, #6, #10, #11, #13)
text: - `GET /songs` — paginated list + search. Params: `q` (free text over title/artist/album/genre, case-insensitive; a key-shaped query like `8A`/`Am` additionally matches every notation of that musical key and a numeric query matches songs whose BPM rounds to it — MOO-69, feeds the Search view), `page` (≥1), `page_size` (1–300, default 50), `sort` (whitelist: `id, title, artist, album, genre, year, bpm, duration_seconds, created_at` + aggregate sorts `most_downloaded, most_played, genre_title` (MOO-65); anything else → `422`; `musical_key` is deliberately NOT sortable), `order` (`asc`/`desc`). Extended filters (MOO-65, additive): `bpm_min`/`bpm_max`, `key` (Camelot like `8A` or raw notation like `Am` — matches every notation mapping to the same Camelot code), `genre` (repeatable, case-insensitive multi-select). Items carry `id, title, artist, album, genre, year, track_number, bpm, musical_key, duration_seconds, bitrate_kbps, file_size_bytes, created_at` + `camelot_key` (best-effort derived, nullable) and `is_favorite` (per current user) (MOO-65); every tag field is nullable. **Since MOO-87** `bpm`/`musical_key`/`camelot_key` serialize the COALESCEd tag-then-detected values (tag always wins, analyzer fills gaps) and the BPM/key filters, key/BPM-shaped `q`, and `sort=bpm` match on the same coalesced expressions; new item fields `bpm_detected`, `key_detected`, `waveform_ready` expose analyzer provenance. **Cursor mode (MOO-77)**: passing `cursor` and/or `limit` (1–100) switches to keyset pagination — `sort` must be `id` or `created_at` (else 422), the response carries `next_cursor` (null on the last page) and `total: null`. Offset mode is unchanged but capped: `page * page_size > 10000` → 422.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Ingestion analyzer (MOO-87)
text: Full design in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § Ingestion analyzer. The essentials:

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Ingestion analyzer (MOO-87)
text: - **Two tiers**: pass 1 (mutagen technical facts + full tag dump, runs inside scan/upload, `src/analysis/technical.py`) and pass 2 (job `analyze_track` on queue `orp:heavy`, consumed by the `worker-heavy` compose service): waveform peaks, decoded-PCM sha256, spectral cutoff, EBU R128 loudness, silence cue points, BPM/key (librosa), Chromaprint fingerprint. Results live in `track_analysis` (one row per song) with per-field `field_versions` provenance; `src/analysis/versions.py` holds the constants — bump ONE to make only that pass stale.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Ingestion analyzer (MOO-87)
text: - **Dispatch seam**: every ingestion path calls `src.analysis.dispatch.enqueue_analysis(song_id)` (deduped per song). Backfill = job `analyze_library` on `orp:default`, throttled to `ANALYZE_BACKFILL_WINDOW` in-flight jobs.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Ingestion analyzer (MOO-87)
text: - **Precedence**: tag bpm/key always win; detected values only fill gaps (COALESCE everywhere a song is serialized/filtered/sorted, expression-indexed). Never overwrite `songs.bpm`/`musical_key` from the analyzer (tag writes are MOO-82's).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Ingestion analyzer (MOO-87)
text: - **Scaling env** (worker-heavy): `WORKER_HEAVY_CONCURRENCY` (default derived from cpu_count, logged at startup), `ANALYZER_NICE=10`, `ANALYZER_MAX_MEM_MB=512`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`/`NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=1`; scale out with `--scale worker-heavy=N`. Binaries via `FFMPEG_PATH`/`FPCALC_PATH` (apt: `ffmpeg`, `libchromaprint-tools`, `libsndfile1`).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Ingestion analyzer (MOO-87)
text: - **Waveform artifact** at `/library/waveform/<aa>/<bb>/<checksum_sha256>.json` (`{"version":1,"algorithm":"ffmpeg-pcm-max","count":1000,"duration_seconds",peaks[0..1]}`), written via `storage.store_artifact_bytes`; the frontend (`utils/waveform.js` `fetchPeaks`/`peaksToBars`) renders it in TrackRow/PlayerBar/Release with the seeded bars as universal fallback (Charts tiles stay decorative/seeded on purpose).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Ingestion analyzer (MOO-87)
text: - **Testing**: harness tests NEVER shell out to ffmpeg/fpcalc or import numpy — monkeypatch the five `src.analysis.engine` seam functions (`decode_and_measure`, `loudness_and_silence`, `bpm_and_key`, `fingerprint`, `file_sha256`); see `../harness_analysis.py`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Duplicates & recordings (MOO-90)
text: - **Model:** `recordings` is the dedup unit — one row per specific mix/edit (normalized artist/title/mix, duration, external IDs: ISRC/MusicBrainz/Beatport/Spotify, `canonical_song_id`). Each `songs` row is one *version* of a recording (`songs.recording_id`, nullable — a Recordings row is created lazily when a second version appears or an external ID is learned). `songs.version_status` ∈ `canonical | superseded | quarantined | pending_review`. **An extended mix and a radio edit are different recordings and are never merged.**

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Duplicates & recordings (MOO-90)
text: - **Match cascade** (`src/services/dedup.py`, cheapest first): L1 byte hash (`checksum_sha256`, md5 fallback) → L2 decoded-PCM hash (`track_analysis.pcm_sha256`) → L3 chromaprint similarity over the local `fingerprint_ngrams` index (never O(n)) → **L4 duration guard** (fingerprint match + duration delta > `library.dedup_duration_tolerance_seconds` = related cut, NOT a duplicate → `recording_links`) → L5 metadata corroboration (adjusts confidence; alone it is review-queue evidence at most, never an auto-merge). Certain (L1/L2) auto-resolves; confident fingerprint matches auto-resolve unless `library.dedup_auto_resolve_fingerprint=false`; borderline/conflicting → `duplicate_candidates` pending review.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Duplicates & recordings (MOO-90)
text: - **Quality ranking** (`src/services/quality.py`): lexicographic tuple — format class, *effective* bitrate (spectral-cutoff-capped: a "320" with a 16 kHz shelf ranks as its true quality; declared bitrate is never trusted alone), sample rate, not-suspect, integrity (decode_ok + no clipping), source trust (`library.dedup_source_trust`), file size. Equal tuples keep the incumbent.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Duplicates & recordings (MOO-90)
text: - **Nothing is ever deleted or moved by dedup** — flag-only version statuses (same rule as the read-only `/music`); losing versions stay as rows, restorable via `POST /admin/recordings/{id}/promote`. Every decision emits a `dedup.*` audit event.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Duplicates & recordings (MOO-90)

Member `GET /songs/{id}` on a non-canonical version → 404; admins get it with `canonical_song_id` for redirect. Admin content exposes `version_status`/`recording_id`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)
text: Beatport is an optional metadata-enrichment source: search-and-match against the Beatport API v4 catalog, fill genre/label/year gaps, and surface BPM/key/ISRC/catalog-number/remixers/artwork for a future consumer (MOO-82's ID3 editor). This stage never writes an audio file or downloads artwork — it only writes to the DB and serves the data over the admin API.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)
text: - **Operator setup (real credentials).** Beatport API v4 access requires an **approved partner application** — apply at https://api.beatport.com/v4/docs/ before you have real `BEATPORT_CLIENT_ID`/`BEATPORT_CLIENT_SECRET` values; this is a real operational blocker, not a config step you can skip. Until that application is approved, run in **mock mode** (below) to evaluate and use the whole feature with zero network/credentials.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)
text: - **Env vars** (all optional; every one has a safe default and the feature degrades cleanly with none set): `BEATPORT_MOCK` (default false — `true` swaps in the deterministic fixture client, `src/enrichment/mock_client.py`), `BEATPORT_ENABLED` (`false` forces "disabled" even with credentials present), `BEATPORT_CLIENT_ID` / `BEATPORT_CLIENT_SECRET` (env-only, never logged, never stored), `BEATPORT_API_BASE` (default `https://api.beatport.com/v4`), `BEATPORT_RATE_LIMIT_RPS` (default 2), `BEATPORT_CACHE_TTL_HOURS` (default 720 = 30 days), `BEATPORT_BACKFILL_BUDGET_PER_HOUR` (default 3600 — spreads the library-wide backfill's API calls across an hour), `BEATPORT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 15), `BEATPORT_AUTO_APPLY_THRESHOLD` / `BEATPORT_REVIEW_THRESHOLD` (default 0.85 / 0.60 — the scoring gates below). Flipping mock off and setting real credentials is a pure env-var change: zero code edits.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)
text: - **Provider tri-state** (`src/enrichment/provider.py::provider_status()`, never calls Beatport itself): `mock` (fixtures), `live` (creds present, not disabled), or `disabled` with a machine-readable `reason` (`credentials_not_configured` | `disabled_by_env`). `GET /admin/enrichment/status` always works; the trigger routes return a clean `503` when disabled — never a 500.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)
text: - **Outbound policy** (`src/enrichment/beatport_client.py`): hard host-allowlist to the configured API host, `follow_redirects=False` (a redirect response is an error), a request timeout, and an asyncio token-bucket rate limiter shared across every call one client instance makes. Artwork URLs are only ever stored if `https` and the host is `beatport.com` or a subdomain. Every GET is a Postgres read-through cache (`beatport_cache`, keyed by `sha1(method+url+params)`, migration 16) — not Redis (MOO-77 declared Redis wipeable transport; cached responses must survive a restart at library scale).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)
text: - **Matching** (`src/enrichment/normalize.py` + `scoring.py`, pure stdlib `difflib.SequenceMatcher`, no new dependency): normalizes artist/title, splits a mix name out of a trailing `(... mix word ...)` group (default `"original mix"`), and computes a weighted composite score across title(.30)/mix(.10)/artist(.25)/duration(.20)/bpm(.075)/key(.075), renormalizing over whatever signals are actually present on both sides. Classification: `applied` (score ≥ `BEATPORT_AUTO_APPLY_THRESHOLD` **and** title ≥ 0.90 **and** artist ≥ 0.85 **and** duration delta ≤ 5s), `needs_review` (score ≥ `BEATPORT_REVIEW_THRESHOLD`), else `no_match`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)
text: - **Storage & field-lock precedence (binding): `manual` > `beatport` > file tag.** `songs.field_locks` is a `{field: "manual"|"beatport"}` JSON map. `sync_songs_from_disk` (the `/music` rescan, `src/crud/songs.py`) now **skips any field present in `field_locks`** when comparing/updating from file tags — this is the fix for the MOO-71/72 quirk ("DB edits are silently reverted by the next scan"), scoped to owned fields only. `src/crud/content.py::edit_metadata` sets `field_locks[field] = "manual"` for every field it changes, so manual admin edits now survive rescans too and always outrank a Beatport apply. Auto-written fields on apply/accept are exactly **genre, label, year** — `songs.beatport_track_id` is denormalized for fast lookups. Everything else (bpm, key, isrc, catalog_number, release_name, release_date, artwork_url, remixers, subgenre) lives only in the `song_enrichment.payload` JSON, served via the API (below) for a future consumer to read — Beatport's bpm/key are **cross-check only** (`payload.bpm_mismatch`/`key_mismatch` booleans), never overwriting the analyzer's detected values (MOO-87 owns those). Un-apply restores the pre-apply snapshot and clears the `beatport` locks (a `manual` lock is untouched either way).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)
text: - **Model:** `song_enrichment` (one row per song+provider, migration 16) carries `status` (`pending|applied|needs_review|no_match|rejected|error`), `match_method` (`auto|manual`), `confidence`, the normalized `payload`, the top-5 scored `candidates` (each with its own component-score breakdown and full candidate payload, so accepting a match never re-calls Beatport), `fields_applied`, and `tag_snapshot`. `beatport_cache` is the response cache (above).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Beatport metadata enrichment (MOO-85)

Instance setting `integrations.beatport_auto_enrich` (default off, `src/crud/settings.py`) auto-enqueues `enrich_song` for every song a library scan or admin upload creates/updates, when the provider is enabled.

All mutating actions are `audit_event`-logged (`enrichment.applied|rejected|unapplied|backfill_started`).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Metadata editor & album art (MOO-82)
text: The full ID3 editor. **Database-side only:** an edit changes the pool's metadata, never the file's bytes — `/music` is read-only, and writing tags back into MP3s is MOO-75 (blocked on the owner's writable-volume decision). What makes an edit durable regardless is MOO-85's field-lock mechanism, so nothing here needs a writable mount.

text: - **Editable set** (`EDITABLE_FIELDS`, `src/crud/tags.py`): title, artist, album, album_artist, composer, genre, label, comment, isrc, year, track_number, disc_number, bpm, musical_key, and the custom TXXX frames (`songs.txxx_frames`, ≤32 entries, desc ≤64 chars, value ≤512 — the same caps extraction applies). Validation lives in `ContentMetadataUpdateSchema` (ISRC regex, BPM 20–999, year 1000–2100). `songs.isrc` (TSRC) is new and is read by extraction.

A field outside `EDITABLE_FIELDS` is a 422 — a proposal can never reach `status`, `file_path`, …

text: - **History & rollback** (`tag_revisions`, append-only): `{field: {old, new}}` per edit, with the editor's username denormalized so history survives account deletion. Rollback applies the inverse as a NEW revision; it 409s when the track changed since (an undo must not silently discard a newer edit). Batch members share a `batch_id` and can be undone as a unit.

Served by `GET /songs/{id}/artwork` behind the same auth as the track (never a static mount). A candidate URL is fetched **only** when Beatport already gave us that URL for that song (allowlist by construction — SSRF, SECURITY.md item 9).

text: A crate (playlist) is exported as a **USB-ready ZIP** whose internal layout is what the target software expects at the ROOT of a stick. The server never sees the stick, so ZIP-download is the delivery; the user extracts it at the drive root.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > DJ crate export — Serato / Traktor / rekordbox (MOO-86)
text: - **Bundle layout** (all three share `Music/NN Artist - Title.ext`, position-prefixed so file managers keep the order): Serato adds `_Serato_/Subcrates/<Crate>.crate` (scanned automatically off any attached drive — no import step); Traktor adds `<Crate>.nml`; rekordbox adds `rekordbox.xml` (the documented Preferences → Advanced → Database → rekordbox xml import path — a native `PIONEER/` .pdb device DB is deliberately out of scope: undocumented binary, corruption risk on CDJs). Every bundle carries `EXPORT_README.txt`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > DJ crate export — Serato / Traktor / rekordbox (MOO-86)
text: - **Portability:** Serato `ptrk` paths are drive-root-relative (works on any drive letter/mount). Traktor addresses volume + `/:`-separated dir, so the export takes a `volume_label` (default `ORP_USB`; README tells the user to name the stick that, or right-click → Relocate once). rekordbox `Location` URIs are absolute, so it takes `rekordbox_root` (default `/Volumes/<label>`; Windows users pass a drive like `E:`).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > DJ crate export — Serato / Traktor / rekordbox (MOO-86)
text: - **Writers** (`src/export/`, all pure + unit-tested, no new dependency): `serato.py` (the reverse-engineered TLV stream — 4-byte tag + BE uint32 length + UTF-16BE payload; we never write `database V2`, Serato rebuilds it), `traktor.py` (NML v19 via ElementTree; `PRIMARYKEY` must byte-match `LOCATION` volume+dir+file or the playlist imports greyed out; `BITRATE` is bits/s), `rekordbox.py` (DJ_PLAYLISTS 1.0.0; playlist `<TRACK Key>` references `TrackID`), `naming.py` (sanitized, deduped, non-escaping arcnames), `tagging.py`, `bundle.py`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > DJ crate export — Serato / Traktor / rekordbox (MOO-86)
text: - **Key notation** (`src/utils/keys.py`): one 24-row table on top of `utils/camelot.py` — `key_forms(raw)` → `{camelot, standard, open_key, traktor_int}` (never raises). Serato gets Camelot in `TKEY`, Traktor Open Key + its 0–23 int, rekordbox standard `Tonality`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > DJ crate export — Serato / Traktor / rekordbox (MOO-86)
text: - **Metadata:** tags are rewritten (mutagen) on the **bundled COPY only** — `/music` is read-only and file-tag writeback is still MOO-75's. Title/artist/album/genre/year/track + `TBPM`/`TKEY` come from the DB (tag value wins, MOO-87 analyzer fills gaps). Frames we do not set are untouched, so existing Serato `GEOB` cue/beatgrid frames survive. **Beatgrids/cues/waveforms are NOT generated** — the DJ software analyzes on first load; stated in the README, the modal, and this file.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > DJ crate export — Serato / Traktor / rekordbox (MOO-86)
text: - **Pipeline** (`jobs/tasks_export.py`, `kind="export_crate"`, queue `orp:default`, MOO-77 jobs row + `JobOut` envelope): per track — resolve the source against the three served roots (outside/missing → recorded in `result.skipped`, never fatal unless all fail), copy chunked into `/library/tmp/export-<job_id>`, retag, stream into the ZIP (`ZIP_STORED` — MP3 does not deflate), delete. **Peak scratch = one track**, so a 40 GB crate needs no 40 GB temp. Artifacts land at `/library/export/<job_id>/<Crate>_<fmt>.zip`; the `cleanup_exports` cron (30 min) drops bundles past `EXPORT_TTL_HOURS` and orphaned staging dirs, and download then returns `410`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > DJ crate export — Serato / Traktor / rekordbox (MOO-86)
text: - **Routes:** `POST /crates/{id}/export` `{format?, volume_label?, rekordbox_root?}` → `202` `JobOut` (read access = crate read access; `format` defaults to `crate.dj_target`, absent both → `422`; empty crate / over `EXPORT_MAX_TRACKS` → `422`; ≥2 active exports per user → `409`; rate-limited 10/h → `429`). `GET /exports/{job_id}` (poll; result = `{download_url, bundle_filename, zip_size_bytes, track_count, skipped[], expires_at}`) and `GET /exports/{job_id}/download` (`FileResponse`; path recomputed from the job id, never client input). Both are creator-or-owner only — **no signed/unauthenticated artifact URLs**; the SameSite=Lax cookie already makes a plain `<a download>` work same-site. Audits `export.requested` / `export.downloaded`.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: Every interesting thing that happens becomes an Elasticsearch document, and four provisioned Grafana dashboards read them back inside the admin panel. **PostgreSQL stays authoritative for everything that matters** (play/download rows, the audit log, quota); telemetry is a strictly additive, best-effort projection — losing it costs nothing.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **Emission** (`src/telemetry/emitter.py`): `emit(event, **fields)` is a synchronous dict-build + `deque` append. No network, no Redis, no await. A background asyncio task in each process (API, worker, worker-heavy) bulk-ships batches to `orp-events-YYYY.MM` every `TELEMETRY_FLUSH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. **Nothing here can raise into a request path**: emit swallows, the flush loop swallows, a dead ES requeues the batch and warns at most once a minute, and a full buffer drops its OLDEST events and counts them (`events_dropped`). ES down ⇒ the app is completely unaffected.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **Taxonomy** (`src/telemetry/events.py` — use these helpers, never raw `emit`): `play.start`, `play.complete` / `play.skip` (from the beacon), `download`, `search.query`, `import.track`, `enrichment.applied`, `export.crate`, `request.created|approved|rejected|fulfilled`, `job.finished`, `api.request` (sampled), `auth.login` + `audit.*` (shipped from PG). Common envelope: `@timestamp`, `event`, `user_id`, `username`, `hour_of_day`, `day_of_week`; `song_label` ("Artist - Title") is precomputed so a top-tracks panel is one terms agg. Unmapped kwargs land under the flattened `attrs` — the index mapping is `dynamic: false` and can never explode.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **Consent** (`TELEMETRY_LEVEL`): `off` (≡ disabled) | `basic` (no `api.request`, and `search.query` keeps counts but drops the raw query string) | `detailed` (default). Telemetry is also automatically off wherever `ELASTICSEARCH_URL` is unset, which is what keeps the single-image build and ES-less environments untouched.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **job.finished** comes from `src/jobs/instrumented.py`, which wraps each task at the one boundary both execution modes share (the arq registry and `submit_job`'s inline dict) — task bodies are untouched, and a new task is instrumented by being registered.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **Audit → ES** (`src/telemetry/shipper.py`): a 60s arq cron (inline mode: the flush loop) copies new `audit_log` rows in, keyed `_id="audit-<row id>"` so it is idempotent, with the cursor recovered from a `max(audit_id)` agg in ES. **No new PG state, no migration.**

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **Retention:** ILM policy `orp-events-retention` deletes an index `TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 180) after creation. Monthly indices age from creation, so effective raw retention is 180–210 days.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **Grafana** is **never published — not even on 127.0.0.1** (`expose:` only). With `auth.proxy` on, anything that can reach port 3000 can impersonate any user via `X-WEBAUTH-USER`. The one way in is `ANY /admin/grafana/{path}` (`src/routes/grafana_proxy.py`): gated on `require_permission("view_reports")`, it strips every client-supplied `X-WEBAUTH-*` header, never forwards the ORP cookie, and injects the caller's identity (`Admin` for owner, else `Viewer`). Dashboards are code (`docker/grafana/dashboards/*.json`, uids `orp-listening|orp-library|orp-engagement|orp-system`) with a provisioned ES datasource; UI edits are disabled.

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **Frontend:** `/admin/insights` (`views/admin/AdminTelemetry.vue`) — status chips + the dashboards in an iframe pointed at OUR origin's proxy path. `PlayerBar.vue` POSTs `telemetry/beacon` on `ended` and on any track change mid-play; the backend classifies ≥85% (or `ended`) as `play.complete`, else `play.skip`. Two security middlewares know about the prefix: `security/headers.py` swaps `X-Frame-Options: DENY` for `frame-ancestors 'self' <ALLOW_ORIGINS>` there, and `security/csrf.py` also accepts same-origin POSTs (the embedded Grafana JS posts to `/admin/grafana/api/ds/query` with the backend's own Origin).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)
text: - **Routes:** `POST /telemetry/beacon` (member, rate-limited 120/min, always 202 — a beacon must never error the player or leak which song ids exist), `GET /admin/telemetry/status` (`view_reports`; ES/Grafana reachability, buffer, counters, shipper lag), `GET /admin/telemetry/config` (`site_settings`).

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Telemetry & Grafana dashboards (MOO-83)

head: CLAUDE.md — open-record-pool > Quality gates (all must pass before committing)
text:
- **Scale rules (MOO-77, binding — full text in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`):**
  - New list endpoints are keyset-paginated (`cursor` + `limit`, `next_cursor` in the response). OFFSET pagination is banned on tables that can grow past 10k rows; the legacy `/songs` offset mode is capped at row 10 000 (422 beyond).
  - Bulk DB work is batched (max 1000 rows per statement, max 1000 elements per `__in`); N+1 query loops are banned — use `prefetch_related`/`values_list` and one aggregate query per page.
  - Every new table/column ships an explicit index plan in its migration file: an index for every FK and every filtered/sorted column.
  - File IO is streaming/chunked only (>= 64 KiB chunks); never read a whole audio file into memory.
  - No filesystem tree walks, subprocesses, or external API calls in a request handler: heavy work goes through `src/jobs/` (`submit_job` -> `jobs` row, arq worker); single-file stream/download responses are the only exception.
  - New audio/artifact files are written only via `src/utils/storage.py` into the sharded `/library` tree (never flat dirs, never `/music`).
  - Every route declares its auth dependency explicitly (`get_current_user` or `require_permission(...)`); `GET /healthz` is the only public route.

head: Captain Coaster
text: A participative guide for roller coaster enthusiasts: members rate, review and build Top lists of the coasters they have ridden, and a world ranking is computed every month from pairwise comparisons of those ratings and Tops.

head: Captain Coaster
text: Symfony 8 on PHP 8.5, Doctrine ORM, MariaDB, Redis, API Platform, EasyAdmin, Twig Components, Stimulus, Tailwind CSS v4 built by Vite (`symfony/reprise`). Exact versions: `composer.json`, `package.json`.

head: Captain Coaster > Principles
text: - **KISS.** The simplest robust solution wins.

head: Captain Coaster > Principles
text: - **Mobile-first.** About 80% of usage is on a phone. Desktop is secondary and stays functional.

head: Captain Coaster > Principles
text: - **Few queries.** Doctrine multiplies them silently: a lazy association read in a loop is one query per row. Load what a page needs in the repository query (joins, a dedicated select, an aggregate), and check the page's query count in the Symfony profiler before and after a change.

head: Captain Coaster > Principles
text: - **Cache wherever it fits.** Data that is expensive to compute and changes on a known event or can be a little stale belongs in a cache. Choosing the policy: `docs/agents/architecture.md`, Caching.

head: Captain Coaster > Principles
text: - **Terse comments and PR descriptions.** A PR description states what changed, why, and what a reviewer needs to know. A comment states what the code can't say itself.

head: Captain Coaster > Principles
text: - **The repo is public.** Production metrics, infrastructure specifics and anything from `PRODUCT.md` (local only, gitignored) stay out of commits, PRs and issues.

head: Captain Coaster > Commands
text: A pre-commit hook (`.githooks/pre-commit`, enabled by `npm install`) runs the three `vendor/bin` commands when a commit touches a `.php` file, and the three `npm` ones (lint, code style, tests) for a `.js` or `.mjs` file. It skips a side whose dependencies are not installed. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs all of them plus Twig, container and Doctrine mapping lints.

head: Captain Coaster > Commands
text: Local server: `symfony server:start -d`, after `composer install` and `npm install` in a fresh worktree. It starts Vite too and prints its port; `symfony server:stop` stops both. A server started in a worktree is stopped when its task is done.

head: Captain Coaster > Git workflow
text: - Worktrees: the built-in `EnterWorktree` tool, which copies the files listed in `.worktreeinclude` (`.env.local` among them).

head: Captain Coaster > Git workflow
text: - `.env.local` holds live secrets: read-only for agents, never edited.

head: Captain Coaster > Git workflow
text: - Redis, MariaDB and Adminer run in containers shared by every worktree: never `docker compose down`.

head: Captain Coaster > Git workflow
text: - The `captain` database is shared by every worktree too. A migration, fixtures or a bulk data change runs on a copy: ask the user before creating one (`isolated-database` skill), and confirm with `php bin/console debug:dotenv DATABASE_URL` that the target is not `captain`.

head: Captain Coaster > Git workflow
text: - One small PR per feature. Its title follows Conventional Commits (`type(scope): subject`), enforced by CI.

head: Captain Coaster > Git workflow
text: - Push or open a PR only after explicit confirmation.

head: Captain Coaster > Git workflow
text: - A hook (`.claude/settings.json`) refuses `gh pr create` while the branch is behind `main`: bring it up to date, re-run the checks and push first.

head: Captain Coaster > Git workflow
text: - Run the `security-review` skill before a PR that touches authentication, user input handling, file uploads, external API or AI calls, or admin routes.

head: Captain Coaster > Delegating to subagents
text: Give a subagent a cheaper model whenever the task allows it: codebase search, reading logs or long outputs, running tests and linters, mechanical refactors, boilerplate, translation keys across the four locales. In Claude Code, pass `model: "sonnet"` on the Agent call (`"haiku"` for pure search and reading).

head: Role & Project Context
text: You are an expert Senior Software Engineer and Architect specializing in Go, Angular, Kubernetes, and high-performance analytical databases (ClickHouse).

head: Role & Project Context
text: We are building BOMHort: a standalone, Kubernetes-native Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) visualization and governance platform. It autonomously ingests massive amounts of SPDX and CycloneDX documents (by default from S3-compatible buckets, with local filesystem as alternative), stores them for infinite historical retention, cross-references vulnerabilities via the OSV API, checks license compliance natively with externalized policy and exception files, supports VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) via OpenVEX, and displays the results in a high-performance UI.

head: Architecture Overview
text: The platform consists of **5 Go binaries**, an **Angular UI**, and a **ClickHouse** database:

head: Architecture Overview
text:
| Binary | Type | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| `ingestion-watcher` | K8s CronJob | Scans SBOM/VEX directory, hash-dedup, enqueues jobs |
| `parsing-worker` | Deployment (N replicas) | Processes SBOMs (SPDX→ClickHouse), VEX files, OSV lookups, license checks |
| `api-gateway` | Deployment | Stateless REST API (29 endpoints) |
| `cve-refresher` | K8s CronJob (daily) | Checks all known PURLs for newly disclosed CVEs without re-scanning SBOMs |
| `mcp-server` | stdio process / optional Deployment | Read-only MCP tool surface over the REST API (#399). Holds **no** database credentials: it is a consumer of the API like any external client. stdio by default, Streamable HTTP opt-in and refused without a bearer token plus an explicit, non-wildcard Origin allow-list. |

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/clickhouse` – ClickHouse client, batch inserts (`insert.go`), queue operations (`queue.go`), and all query logic split across `queries.go`, `queries_projects.go`, `queries_cluster.go`, `queries_namespace.go` (namespace drill-down + the `cluster → namespace → project` fleet tree), `queries_search.go`, `queries_refresh.go`, `queries_github_cache.go`

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/config` – Environment-based configuration loader (`config.Load()` reads env vars with sensible defaults)

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/ingestpath` – Derives the `cluster`/`namespace`/`project` dimensions from an SBOM's position in its source, driven by an explicit `INGEST_PATH_LAYOUT` (e.g. `cluster/namespace/project`). Opt-in: unset means nothing is derived. Explicit configuration always outranks derivation.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/repo` – Directory scanner with SHA256 hashing and file type classification. Accepts any `.json` file (format auto-detected by parser), with configurable ignore prefix (`SBOM_IGNORE_PREFIX`, default `_`) to skip demo/example files. VEX files detected via `*.openvex.json` / `*.vex.json` suffix.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/osvutil` – Shared OSV helpers (ClassifySeverity, ExtractFixedVersion, ExtractAffectedVersions)

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/license` – License compliance + externalized policy + exceptions with prefix-matching. Also owns free-text → SPDX normalization (`normalize.go`: `Normalize`, `Recover`, `LicenseRef`) and the license provenance vocabulary (`source.go`: origins, `+latest`/`+normalized` modifiers, unresolved reasons, `!reason` negative-cache markers).

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/npm`, `internal/nuget`, `internal/depsdev`, `internal/packagist`, `internal/pypi` – Package-registry license resolvers (rate-limited, cached in `registry_license_cache`), run in that order after the GitHub resolver. Each implements `Explain` to report *why* a package stayed unresolved (`not-published`, `no-license-upstream`). Opt out per registry with `SKIP_{NPM,NUGET,DEPSDEV,PACKAGIST,PYPI}_RESOLVE`.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/osv` – OSV API client with rate limiting and exponential backoff

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/s3` – S3-compatible bucket client (AWS S3, MinIO, GCS) for streaming SBOM ingestion from multiple buckets, plus PutObject/RemoveObject for push-model uploads (#135). Supports per-bucket `cluster` assignment for multi-cluster differentiation from a single instance, and a per-bucket `skipScan` flag that excludes a bucket from ListObjects scanning — used to designate a dedicated push-upload target so the ingestion watcher never rediscovers pushed objects.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/github` – GitHub API client for resolving unknown licenses from PURL (rate-limited, cached). Includes 50+ well-known Go module→GitHub repo mappings (`golang.org/x/*`, `gopkg.in/*`, `go.uber.org/*`, `k8s.io/*`, `oras.land/*`, `dario.cat/*`, etc.), fallback to the dedicated `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/license` endpoint, and static license overrides for repos where GitHub misdetects the license.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/spdx` – SPDX JSON streaming parser. Supports both plain SPDX documents and **in-toto attestation envelopes** where the SPDX content is wrapped inside the `predicate` field (common with Syft/BuildKit-generated container SBOMs).

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/cyclonedx` – CycloneDX JSON parser. Maps components, licenses, and dependencies to the shared model.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/sbom` – Multi-format SBOM dispatch layer. Auto-detects format (SPDX, CycloneDX, in-toto) and routes to the appropriate parser. Supports opt-in protobom backend via `USE_PROTOBOM=true`.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/protobomparser` – Parser backend using [protobom](https://github.com/protobom/protobom) for maximum format coverage (SPDX 2.3 + CycloneDX 1.0–1.7). Opt-in alternative to built-in parsers.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/vex` – OpenVEX parser with URL normalization

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/docstore` – Original-document store (fs or S3 backend) for the bytes captured at ingest (#256). Reads are **reference-driven** (`multistore.go`): a stored `fs://…`/`s3://…` reference is resolved by its scheme against whichever backend can read it, not against the reading process's configured backend — so the API gateway can serve originals written by a worker with a different `ORIGINAL_STORE_BACKEND`, and fs↔s3 migrations don't orphan old captures. Writes still go to the single configured primary backend.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `internal/apiclient` – Read-only HTTP client for BOMHort's own REST API, used by `cmd/mcp-server` (#399). GET only, by design — there is no write path in it. Exists so the MCP server consumes the frozen contract instead of reaching around it into ClickHouse; the cost is one HTTP hop, the benefit is that an agent can only ever see what the API exposes, and that contract holes surface here rather than in a consumer's integration.

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `pkg/models` – ClickHouse data models (SBOM, SBOMPackages, Vulnerability, LicenseCompliance, IngestionJob, VEXStatement)

head: Architecture Overview
text: - `pkg/dto` – API response DTOs with generics (`PaginatedResponse[T]`), used exclusively by `api-gateway` and `internal/clickhouse` queries

head: Tech Stack
text: - **Backend & Workers:** Go (Golang)

head: Tech Stack
text: - **Database:** ClickHouse (managed via the official ClickHouse Kubernetes Operator)

head: Tech Stack
text: - **Frontend:** Angular (TypeScript, standalone components, OnPush change detection)

head: Tech Stack
text: - **Infrastructure:** Kubernetes (Standard Helm Chart, 19 templates)

head: Tech Stack
text: - **Container Registry:** GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/seebom-labs/bomhort/*)

head: Tech Stack
text: - **Go Module Path:** `github.com/seebom-labs/bomhort/backend`

head: Architectural Directives
text: **Monorepo Requirement:** This project strictly uses a monorepo architecture. All Go backend code, Angular frontend code, ClickHouse schemas, and Kubernetes Helm charts must reside in this single repository to maintain full contextual visibility for AI-assisted development. Do not suggest splitting this into a polyrepo.

head: Architectural Directives
text: **Deployment Strategy:** We use a hybrid approach. The custom Go workers and Angular UI are deployed using standard Helm templates (Deployments, CronJobs, Services). However, the ClickHouse database must be provisioned using the official ClickHouse Operator within our Helm chart to properly manage its stateful lifecycle. Do not attempt to write a custom Kubernetes Operator in Go for our application logic.

head: Architectural Directives
text: **Config-Driven Governance:** License policy (`license-policy.json`) and license exceptions (`license-exceptions.json`) are externalized as config files – mounted via Docker Compose volumes locally and Kubernetes ConfigMaps in production. The frontend is public, so no write APIs for exceptions exist. Changes require config file updates + re-ingest.

head: Architectural Directives
text: **CVE Refresh Strategy:** New CVEs are discovered via a lightweight daily CronJob (`cve-refresher`) that queries all unique PURLs (~20k) against the OSV API in 1000-PURL batch chunks, deduplicates against existing vulnerabilities, and inserts new findings. This avoids expensive full re-scans of all SBOMs.

head: Architectural Directives
text: **Parsing Pipeline Order:** The parsing worker processes each SBOM in a strict order: (1) Auto-detect format and parse (SPDX/CycloneDX/in-toto, with optional protobom backend via `USE_PROTOBOM=true`), (2) Resolve unknown licenses — GitHub, then the registry resolvers, then free-text normalization, then a reason for whatever is still unknown; all of it in `resolvePackageLicenses` (`cmd/parsing-worker/license_provenance.go`), which also returns the per-package license source, (3) Insert SBOM metadata + packages with resolved licenses into ClickHouse, (4) Query OSV for vulnerabilities, (5) Check license compliance. License resolution **must** happen before ClickHouse inserts so that `sbom_packages.package_licenses` contains the resolved values from the start — the dependency tree API reads directly from this column.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - Use standard idiomatic Go. Handle errors explicitly; never swallow them.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - HTTP routing uses Go 1.22+ stdlib `net/http` with method-pattern registration (e.g., `mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/v1/sboms", ...)`). No web framework.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - Only 6 direct dependencies: `clickhouse-go/v2`, `goccy/go-json`, `google/uuid`, `minio/minio-go/v7`, `protobom/protobom`, `modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`. Keep it minimal — adding a 7th is a maintainer decision, not an implementation detail.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - `modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` must stay pinned **`>= v1.4.1`** (approved 2026-09-24 for the MCP server, #399; shipped on `v1.8.0`). Everything below it carries four HIGH advisories: CVE-2026-27896 and GHSA-q382-vc8q-7jhj (JSON key confusion — case folding, then `NUL`-terminated duplicate keys), CVE-2026-33252 (cross-site tool execution: no `Origin`/`Content-Type` validation on Streamable HTTP) and CVE-2026-34742 (DNS-rebinding protection off by default on localhost). `v1.4.1` requires Go 1.25+. Never downgrade this pin to resolve a build conflict.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - **The MCP server never gets a write tool or a ClickHouse connection.** Both would be small changes and both would break the reason it exists: it is the external consumer that proves the REST contract is usable, and a read-only surface over a public frontend is the only surface it can legitimately have. Mutation tools are a post-1.0, explicitly-decided addition, not an implementation detail.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - Multi-target Dockerfile (`backend/Dockerfile`) builds all 5 binaries in one builder stage, then copies each into a separate `alpine:3.24` runtime stage. The `mcp-server` stage declares no `EXPOSE`: its default transport is stdio, and declaring a port would suggest otherwise. `VERSION` is stamped into `mcp-server` only — it is the one binary whose version an external client sees (the MCP `initialize` handshake).

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - Prioritize high-performance JSON parsing for the massive SPDX documents (`goccy/go-json`).

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - When integrating with the OSV API, utilize batch querying endpoints (`/v1/querybatch`) to efficiently process multiple Package URLs (PURLs) at once.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - Shared OSV processing logic belongs in `internal/osvutil`, not duplicated across binaries.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - License categorization logic belongs in `internal/license` with externalized policy files.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - Permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) must **never** generate non-compliant package records.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - **License heuristics are documented decisions, not implementation details.** Every rule that changes which license a package gets — a normalization alias or family rule, a resolver, a version fallback, a first-party rule — needs a decision-log entry (decision, why, risk, switch, test) on `docs/content/docs/license-resolution/_index.md`. Its vocabulary, normalization-example and worked-example tables are asserted against the code by `TestDocsLicenseResolutionInSync`; the worked examples mirror `licenseGolden` in `cmd/parsing-worker/golden_test.go`, which runs `testdata/license_golden.spdx.json` through the real pipeline. A new path through the pipeline gets a fixture package, a golden row and a docs row.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - **Never guess an ambiguous license name.** `BSD`, `Apache Software License`, `Public Domain`, an unversioned `GPL`, a license URL: mapping any of them would approve a license nobody approved. Only spellings that name one license unambiguously are normalized; unrecognised names become `LicenseRef-…` (unapproved), never `NOASSERTION`. A declared license is never overridden by a resolver.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Go (Backend)
text: - A license that is still unknown must carry a reason (`license.UnresolvedReasons`). A new resolver implements `Explain`; a new reason is added to `UnresolvedReasons`, the UI labels (`ui/src/app/shared/license-source.ts`) and the docs page together.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > ClickHouse (Database)
text: - Treat observability and SBOM histories as a data analytics problem. Use the MergeTree table engine family for all core tables.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > ClickHouse (Database)
text: - When designing schemas, ensure the ORDER BY clause starts with low-cardinality columns (e.g., timestamp, category) to minimize data scanning and optimize performance.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > ClickHouse (Database)
text: - Extract frequently queried JSON keys into top-level columns rather than relying entirely on generic Map or String types.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > ClickHouse (Database)
text: - Avoid single-row inserts; always aggregate and batch inserts in Go.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > ClickHouse (Database)
text: - Current tables: `sboms`, `sbom_packages`, `vulnerabilities`, `license_compliance`, `ingestion_queue`, `dashboard_stats_mv`, `vex_statements`, `cve_refresh_log`, `github_license_cache`, `github_repo_metadata`, `registry_license_cache`, `document_store` (24 migrations in `db/migrations/`; the next free number is `025` — see the Schema Change Register in `ROADMAP.md` before adding one, and check upstream `main` plus open PRs for a number taken in the meantime). All core tables include three orthogonal ownership columns, each `LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT ''` and none in `ORDER BY`: `cluster` (#131, migration `012`), `namespace` (#138) and `project` (#57, both migration `015`). `sboms` and `ingestion_queue` additionally carry `source_repo` / `source_ref` (#332, migration `016`), populated at parse time from SPDX/CycloneDX metadata and overridable via upload headers or `PATCH /api/v1/sboms/{id}`. `sboms` also carries `document_version` (migration `021`), the version of the product the document describes (SPDX root `versionInfo`, CycloneDX `metadata.component.version`), extracted at parse time. `sboms` and `ingestion_queue` carry `tags Array(String)` (#357, migration `022`) — free-form grouping labels orthogonal to the ownership triple, for catalogue-style instances where cluster/namespace are structurally empty but projects still need grouping ("these 40 projects are sandbox applications"). **Tags group projects, they do not replace them:** a tagged SBOM keeps its own `project`, so `?tag=` narrows which projects are listed and never merges them. Set via `TAGS` (comma-separated), per-bucket `"tags"`, or `?tags=` on upload; these levels **merge** rather than override, unlike cluster/namespace/project. Normalised in `internal/tags` (trim, lowercase, dedupe, sort) so every entry point stores comparable values. `GET /api/v1/tags` exposes the labels in use so the UI renders groupings data-driven instead of hard-coding them. `vex_statements` carries provenance columns `author`, `role`, `tooling`, `status_notes` (#334, migration `017`), captured from the OpenVEX document/statement at ingest, plus `sbom_id` (#350, migration `018`) scoping each statement to the SBOM whose product it describes ('' = legacy global; every suppression join is scope-aware and scoped beats global) and `product_ref` (migration `020`), the persisted OpenVEX product `@id` — it powers the post-ingest **VEX rescue** pass (`cmd/parsing-worker/vex_rescue.go`): after every successful SBOM ingest, unscoped statements are re-resolved and scoped once their product SBOM exists, so VEX/SBOM arrival order no longer matters. A statement naming a product with no subcomponents is stored product-wide (`product_purl = '*'`) and covers every component of that SBOM. `sboms` and `ingestion_queue` carry `parent` (migration `023`), `sboms` also `root_purl`/`supplier`, the inputs of query-time parent grouping. `sbom_packages` carries `package_license_sources Array(LowCardinality(String))` (#439, migration `024`), parallel to `package_licenses`: where each license came from or why it is missing; rows ingested before it are empty and reported as `unrecorded`. `vulnerabilities` carries `aliases Array(String)` (migration `019`), the OSV alias IDs (GHSA ↔ CVE); suppression queries match a VEX statement when its `vuln_id` equals the finding's `vuln_id` **or** appears in its aliases. **`db/migrations/` must stay byte-identical to `deploy/helm/bomhort/migrations/`** — the chart ships its own copy, so drift means a Kubernetes deployment silently never applies a migration. Run `make check-migrations` (CI-safe) or `make sync-migrations` after adding one.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > ClickHouse (Database)
text: - **Schema drift is unit-tested without a database:** `internal/clickhouse/migrations_schema_test.go` replays every file in `db/migrations/` into an in-memory schema and asserts that (a) every column named in an `INSERT INTO` literal actually exists, (b) every data table carries all three ownership columns, (c) all five `ingestion_queue` writers share one column list, and (d) migration numbers are unique and contiguous. Adding a column to an `INSERT` without a migration — or a table without the ownership columns — fails `go test`, not production.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - Use strict TypeScript mode and standalone components.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - Unit tests use **Vitest** (not Karma/Jasmine). Run via `npx ng test`.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - Virtual scrolling uses `@angular/cdk` (`ScrollingModule`). Always implement for large lists of dependency nodes or vulnerabilities to prevent browser freezing.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - Utilize OnPush change detection for data-heavy dashboard components to optimize rendering performance.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - All routes are lazy-loaded standalone components (see `app.routes.ts`). Feature pages: `dashboard`, `fleet` (cluster → namespace → project tree with per-scope stats, backed by `GET /api/v1/fleet`), `sbom-explorer`, `vulnerability`, `search` (CVE impact, license compliance, dependency stats, version skew, package search + detail), `license-compliance`, `vex`, `archived-packages`.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - Shared chart components live in `shared/charts/` (donut chart, horizontal bar chart).

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - UI supports **Dark Mode** (toggle in navbar, persisted to localStorage) and **Custom CSS Theming** (external `custom-theme.css` mountable without rebuild).

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - UI supports **Site Configuration** (`ui-config.json`): brand name, page title, dashboard texts, and disclaimer are configurable without rebuild. Loaded at startup via `APP_INITIALIZER` in `SiteConfigService`. Mount via Docker volume or Kubernetes ConfigMap (`ui.siteConfig` in Helm values).

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - License exemptions are visually distinct: green badge + orange text for exempted copyleft, red for violations.

head: Code Style & Database Best Practices > Angular (Frontend)
text: - Project grouping with clickable version tags is used in CVE Impact, VEX, and License Overview pages.

head: Boundaries
text: - **Always do:** Write unit tests for new Go packages and Angular components. Ensure ClickHouse bulk inserts are batched. Update `docs/ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md` when adding new services or features. **Before any minor/major release tag:** run `govulncheck ./...` (backend), `npm audit` (ui + docs), fix all vulnerabilities, and verify the build passes. Scan all three ecosystems (Go, Angular npm, Hugo docs npm). **Update `ROADMAP.md` when cutting a minor release, and only then** — mark completed items as done, adjust phase timelines, and ensure the dependency graph is current.

head: Boundaries
text: - **Workflow for every feature/fix:** (1) Write code, (2) Write tests for all new functionality, (3) Update API docs (`docs/content/docs/api-reference/_index.md`) for new/changed endpoints, (4) Update general docs (ARCHITECTURE_PLAN, deployment guide) — **but not `ROADMAP.md`**, see below, (5) Verify build + tests pass, (6) Push branch — **stop here**. Do NOT open a PR unless explicitly asked.

head: Boundaries
text: - **`ROADMAP.md` is a release-time file, not a per-PR file.** Feature PRs must not tick their own entry. Every PR that does touches the same v0.8.0 criteria line, the same milestone-map row and the same dependency graph, so two open PRs conflict on a checklist by construction — and the conflict is the dangerous kind: each side holds a tick the other lacks, so resolving it by picking a side silently un-ticks an issue that is already merged, in a file no reviewer reads line by line. Three PRs in a row (#423, #424, #431) hit exactly this. The roadmap is updated once when the release is cut, where the full set of merged items is known and a single author reconciles it; see `docs/RELEASE.md`.

head: Boundaries
text: - **Ask first:** Before adding new third-party dependencies (npm or Go modules), modifying the ClickHouse schema, changing Kubernetes manifest structures, or creating/merging pull requests.

head: Boundaries
text: - **Release branches (`release/vX.Y`):** branch features and fixes from `main` and target `main` — never a release branch. A fix that a released minor needs is backported *after* it merged to `main`, with `make cherry-pick PR=<n> BRANCH=X.Y` (a PR against the release branch). Never commit to a release branch directly, never backport features. Do not cut tags or create release branches unless explicitly asked.

head: Boundaries
text: - **Never do:** Never commit secrets or API keys. Never use a relational database (like PostgreSQL) for the core SBOM dependency trees. Never split the codebase into multiple repositories. Never add write APIs for license exceptions (frontend is public). Never use `bypassSecurityTrustHtml` in Angular — use `sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, ...)` instead. Never invent or guess SHA hashes for pinned GitHub Actions — always verify against the GitHub API. Never push changes to upstream without explicit approval. Never bump the major version without a migration guide and 3-month advance notice via roadmap.

head: Major Version Policy
text: - Major bumps happen every **2–3 years**, driven by accumulated breaking changes (schema, API, Helm values), not by calendar.

head: Major Version Policy

head: Major Version Policy
text: - A migration guide with automated tooling (schema scripts, Helm values converter) is mandatory before tagging.
