head: Security Hardening > API Gateway (`cmd/api-gateway/main.go`)
text: - **Security headers** are set via `securityHeadersMiddleware`: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`.

head: Security Hardening > API Gateway (`cmd/api-gateway/main.go`)
text: - **CORS** is configurable via `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env var (default `*` for dev, restrict in production). `GET` and `OPTIONS` are allowed on every endpoint; `POST` is additionally advertised only for `/api/v1/sboms/upload` (checked by path in `corsMiddleware`, not applied globally).

head: Security Hardening > API Gateway (`cmd/api-gateway/main.go`)
text: - **Rate limiting** via `rateLimitMiddleware`: 100 requests per 10s per IP, with background cleanup to prevent memory leaks.

head: Security Hardening > API Gateway (`cmd/api-gateway/main.go`)
text: - **Authentication** via `authMiddleware` (opt-in, default off). Set `AUTH_ENABLED=true` plus either `SERVICE_TOKEN` (shared secret for upstream proxies, accepted as `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-Service-Token`) and/or `API_KEYS` (comma-separated list, accepted as `X-API-Key`). Uses `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` to prevent timing attacks. Public paths (`/healthz`, `/livez`, `/readyz`) and `OPTIONS` preflight always bypass auth. `POST /api/v1/sboms/upload` (#135) additionally self-enforces `AUTH_ENABLED=true` inside `uploadHandler` itself — a write endpoint being open by default is a materially different risk than the read-only default, so it doesn't rely solely on the global opt-in.

head: Security Hardening > API Gateway (`cmd/api-gateway/main.go`)
text: - **Input validation**: All UUID path parameters (`sbomID`) are validated against `uuidPattern` regex. Vulnerability IDs (`vulnID`) are validated against `vulnIDPattern`. Query parameters that reach a query are whitelisted to known values; pagination parameters are parsed as integers and clamped.

head: Security Hardening > API Gateway (`cmd/api-gateway/main.go`)
text: - **Pagination bounds**: `clampPageSize()` enforces max 500 items per page to prevent abusive queries.

head: Security Hardening > API Gateway (`cmd/api-gateway/main.go`)
text: - **Log injection prevention**: `sanitizeLogParam()` strips newlines/control characters and truncates to 200 chars before logging user-supplied values.

head: Security Hardening > API Gateway (`cmd/api-gateway/main.go`)
text: - **No SQL injection risk**: All ClickHouse queries use parameterized queries (`?` placeholders), never string interpolation with user input.

head: Security Hardening > Nginx (`ui/nginx.conf`)
text: - Security headers: `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy` (strict `default-src 'self'`), `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`.

head: Security Hardening > Nginx (`ui/nginx.conf`)
text: - `server_tokens off` hides nginx version.

head: Security Hardening > Angular (Frontend)
text: - **Never bypass Angular sanitization** — use `DomSanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, ...)` which strips `<script>`, event handlers, and other dangerous HTML while preserving safe formatting (`<strong>`, `<a>`, `<em>`, `<code>`).

head: Security Hardening > Angular (Frontend)
text: - Dashboard description and disclaimer use safe sanitization, not `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`.

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **Signed Releases**: All container images are signed with [cosign](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign) (keyless/OIDC via Fulcio) and attested with SLSA provenance (`actions/attest-build-provenance`) in `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **Pinned Dependencies**: All GitHub Actions **and reusable workflows** (e.g. `cncf/prow-github-actions/.github/workflows/prow.yml`) are pinned by full commit SHA (not tags), with the tag as a `# vX.Y.Z` comment. When adding or updating a pinned action, **always verify the SHA against the GitHub API** (e.g., `gh api repos/{owner}/{action}/git/refs/tags/{version}`; for an annotated tag, dereference `git/tags/{sha}` to the commit) before committing — never invent or guess SHA hashes. External downloads (e.g., Hugo in `deploy-docs.yml`) include SHA256 checksum verification.

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **Token Permissions**: Every workflow declares top-level `permissions:` read-only (`contents: read` or `read-all`); write scopes go on the job that needs them. A single top-level `contents`/`actions` write drops Scorecard's Token-Permissions check to 0 — that is what happened with `prow.yml`. `deploy/helm/tests/test_workflow_security.py` enforces both rules in CI.

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **Vulnerabilities**: An advisory that cannot be fixed and provably does not affect BOMHort is ignored in `backend/osv-scanner.toml` (read by osv-scanner and Scorecard) with a reproducible reason and an `ignoreUntil` date — never without both.

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **Branch Protection**: Repository rulesets, not classic protection, are the source of truth (Scorecard can read rulesets without an admin token). *Release and Main* covers `main` + `release/**`: PR, required checks incl. `prow/lgtm`, up-to-date branch, one human approving review covering the latest push. *Release tags* makes `v*` tags immutable. Approvers use GitHub's Approve review, which Prow counts as `/approve` (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge gate").

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **Fuzzing**: Native Go fuzz tests exist for SPDX and VEX parsers (`internal/spdx/fuzz_test.go`, `internal/vex/fuzz_test.go`). The `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml` workflow runs them weekly and on PRs touching `backend/`.

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **SAST**: CodeQL runs on every push/PR for Go and TypeScript (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`).

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **Scorecard**: The `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml` workflow runs the OpenSSF Scorecard weekly and publishes results as SARIF to GitHub Security tab.

head: Security Hardening > Supply Chain Security (OpenSSF Scorecard)
text: - **Dependency Updates**: Dependabot covers `gomod`, `npm`, `github-actions`, and `docs` (`.github/dependabot.yml`).

head: Working in this repository
text:
OnCo is a public, cited knowledge graph of oncology: about 19,000 records in `src/data`, rendered as a static
Next.js export. Readers are patients and the people caring for them. Every claim carries a source, and a page
that is confidently wrong is the worst thing this project can ship.

head: Working in this repository
text:
This file is short on purpose: it is read at the start of every session, so it holds only what is costly to
learn the hard way and cannot be a test. Everything else is enforced or written down elsewhere, linked below.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text:
- **Never invent a fact, a figure, a citation or a date.** If a source cannot be reached, say so on the page. A
  named gap is worth more than a plausible number. Tools that summarise a page can fabricate: a fetch of a
  ministry page produced "universal health insurance since 1961" from a page containing neither the year nor the
  phrase. Verify anything load-bearing against the raw text.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text:
- **Never cite an identifier you remember. Resolve it first.** This is the commonest real error, and it is not
  invention: a DOI or PubMed id recalled from training is usually a real paper, just the wrong one. Caught in two
  rounds: an id for a surveillance-imaging trial that resolved to a cancer-anorexia editorial, one for a Hodgkin
  late-effects cohort that resolved to IBIS-II, one for a retinal-imaging study, `10.1038/ng.621` used for the
  lymphoma EZH2 paper when it is the myeloid one, and wrong ids for BELINDA and ECHELON-3. Resolve every DOI
  through Crossref or Europe PMC and read the abstract before you use a figure from it.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text: - **Never alter a quotation to make it kinder or shorter.** Quoted abstracts keep their authors' words.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text:
- **Never put a secret in the repository**, in a commit message, or in a chat. There are none here and there
  should continue to be none; `gitleaks` runs on every ship and a commit subject is republished publicly by
  `scripts/provenance.ts`, so write commit messages as if they were a page, because they become one.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text: - **Never copy patient data, or anything from a private project, into this repository.**

head: Working in this repository > Never
text:
- **Keep review screenshots and recordings out of the repository.** Capture them in a temporary directory
  outside the checkout and attach or link them in the pull request, including matching before/after views
  when reviewing a visual change. Product image assets belong in the repository; review artifacts do not.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text:
- **Never run `vercel link` or edit `.vercel/`.** The project is already linked; relinking can point a deploy at
  the wrong project.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text:
- **Never edit files in the main checkout while a ship is running**, and never run gates or a second build during
  one. `scripts/ship.sh` sweeps the working tree into its commit, and the upload packs `public/` while the API
  build clears part of it: doing both at once killed a deploy that had reported success.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text:
- **Never ship a change to the product without the owner's say-so.** `scripts/ship.sh` classifies the diff and
  refuses if it touches anything that decides what a page shows, in what order, or what it is called. Data ships
  on its own; the product waits. Send it with `scripts/propose-product-change.sh` and it appears at `/admin/`
  with a preview. `docs/PRODUCT-APPROVAL.md` is the rule and `scripts/change-class.ts` is where the line is
  drawn. Do not set `ONCO_PRODUCT_APPROVED` on your own judgement, however obviously good the change looks.

head: Working in this repository > Never
text:
- **Never lower a floor or raise a budget to make a test pass.** Fix the corpus, the ranking or the page. If the
  measure itself is wrong, change what it counts and say why in the comment; that has been the right answer four
  times and the wrong one never.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **An agent works in its own git worktree and never touches another.** Do not copy `node_modules` into one: that
  reached 37 GB across worktrees and filled the disk mid-run. Symlink it, or run the gates from the main checkout.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text: - **Check the branch you are on before you report it.** Agents have misreported their own branch three times.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **Exit code 0 is not a commit and "UPLOADED" is not live.** Read the log, check `git log`, and confirm the page
  serves 200 before saying it shipped.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **Verify on the rendered page, not only in the test.** Reading the live page has caught a gendered pronoun, a
  name printed twice in one sentence, and a budget measuring a quarter of what the reader downloads.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **Show side-by-side screenshots when opening a product PR.** Capture the same page, viewport and scroll
  position with and without the feature, and put the labelled comparison in the PR description.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **A fragment in a pattern needs word boundaries.** `imid` matched inside `pyrimidine` and put a myeloma drug's
  blood-clot warning on every fluoropyrimidine page, including one about a skin cream. Six review passes missed it.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **A full-suite failure under load is usually the machine.** Five whole-page render files (`nested-anchors`,
  `mechanics`, `record-fold`, `record-top`, `EntityDetail`) time out on their own 120-second guard when other
  worktrees are building, and pass alone. Re-run the file before reporting it, and use `SLOW_TEST_MS`, which is
  the env var the chain already sets for this. Do not change a test to make it green.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **Never resolve a contributor's pull request by union.** `scripts/resolve-additive.py` keeps both sides,
  which is right for an append-only log or a registry line and wrong for an object literal where both sides
  rewrote the same record: on 7 October eleven overlapping pull requests were batch-merged that way and it
  produced TypeScript that would not parse, with two broken files committed before anyone noticed. Merge them
  one at a time and read each hunk. Where an earlier pull request already corrected a record, keep that
  version; where arrays differ, union the arrays so nothing the contributor wrote is lost.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **The two registry files conflict on every parallel round, and one resolver gets it wrong.**
  `src/data/spikes/index.ts` resolves by union with `scripts/resolve-spike-registry.py`.
  `scripts/spike-sources.ts` holds its map on one very long line, and `scripts/resolve-additive.py` keeps both
  sides of it rather than merging them, which TypeScript rejects as duplicate keys. Merge that line by hand,
  union the entries, and then run `scripts/audit.test.ts`: it is the only thing that notices a lost entry. On
  2 October a hand-merge silently dropped seven files and that test was what caught it.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **Supplement the record that exists; do not write a second one.** `SpikeSupplement` in
  `src/data/spikes/index.ts` attaches fields to a record another file owns, and the build fails if it names an
  id that does not exist. It is reachable only from a `Spike`, which needs a `cancerId`; for a record with no
  cancer, add to the owning file's own array instead.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **A question-shaped record name competes with the benchmark questions.** Ask's lexical index scores on
  `name`, so a record called "... and what happened to the survivorship care plan" outranked the right answer
  for the benchmark question "What happened to tazemetostat in 2026?" and dropped extractive recall below its
  floor. Renaming the record fixed it. Name a record for its subject, not as a question.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **`SCHEMATIC_ALIAS` resolves one hop only.** Aliasing a new technology to an id that is itself an alias
  leaves it on a generic drawing. `src/data/animated-wave8.test.ts` is what catches it; point at the drawing.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **Grade what is unproven rather than leaving it out.** Where something is widely sold and has no evidence,
  `src/data/complementary.ts` has the model: a tag `evidence:<grade>` from strong to harm, a number only where
  the source states one. A reader who finds nothing here finds the seller's own page instead.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text: - **Read the smallest page in a round, not the flagship.** That is where a wrongly matched card is visible.

head: Working in this repository > Rules a test cannot catch
text:
- **Prefer the record that already exists.** A paper is its DOI and its PubMed id; a trial is its registry id. If
  the corpus holds one, supplement it. `npm run dedupe` surveys duplicates before you write.

text: Prose drifts; these do not. Read them rather than a description of them.

- `scripts/resolve-spike-registry.py`, `scripts/resolve-additive.py` — the two merge conflicts every parallel

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file is the canonical contributor guide for this repository.

head: AGENTS.md
text: If another assistant-specific file exists, it should defer to this document for repo workflow, quality gates, and architecture constraints.

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: Keep this Electron video app production-ready while preserving:

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: - clear module boundaries

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: - stable user-facing behavior

head: AGENTS.md > Mission
text: Do not optimize for "quickly making tests pass." Optimize for making the codebase more robust.

head: AGENTS.md > Required Workflow
text: For any non-trivial change, follow this order:

head: AGENTS.md > Required Workflow
text: 1. Identify the affected feature and expected behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Required Workflow
text: 2. Define or update acceptance criteria before implementation.

head: AGENTS.md > Required Workflow
text: 3. Add or update tests first for the intended behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Required Workflow
text: 4. Implement the code change.

head: AGENTS.md > Required Workflow
text: 5. Run the full verification suite.

head: AGENTS.md > Required Workflow
text: 6. Fix code defects if tests fail. Do not weaken assertions unless the product requirement itself changed.

head: AGENTS.md > Change Policy
text: - Prefer small, isolated changes over broad rewrites.

head: AGENTS.md > Change Policy
text: - Preserve behavior unless the task explicitly changes product behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Change Policy
text: - Do not introduce duplicate business logic across renderer and main.

head: AGENTS.md > Change Policy
text: - Shared normalization/domain logic belongs in `src/shared/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Change Policy
text: - Main-process business logic belongs in `src/main/services/`, not in IPC registration or app bootstrap.

head: AGENTS.md > Change Policy
text: - Renderer feature logic belongs in `src/renderer/features/`, not inline in `src/index.html`.

head: AGENTS.md > Change Policy
text: - `src/preload.ts` should remain a narrow bridge and not gain business logic.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text: Current intended structure:

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text:
- `src/main/`
  - Electron runtime bootstrapping, IPC registration, services, infra

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text:
- `src/shared/`
  - domain rules, normalization, data-shape helpers shared across layers

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text:
- `src/renderer/`
  - renderer entrypoint and feature utilities

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text:
- `tests/unit/`
  - pure logic and isolated helper tests

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text:
- `tests/integration/`
  - service/integration tests with controlled fakes

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text:
- `tests/e2e/`
  - Electron smoke and workflow checks

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text: - Put pure data logic in a testable module first.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text: - Keep side effects at the edges.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text: - Inject dependencies where practical for testability.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture Guardrails
text: - Favor explicit validation and errors over silent fallback when data is invalid.

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: Always define expected behavior and acceptance criteria before implementing. Treat "what behavior changed?" as a required design question before coding.

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: How to prove the behavior depends on the layer — apply tests-first where it earns its keep, and be honest where it cannot:

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: - Pure logic and main-process services (`src/shared/**`, `src/main/services/**`): write the proving unit/integration tests first. These paths test cheaply against temp directories and fakes, and this is where tests-first pays off most.

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: - Filesystem, IPC, or service coordination: add integration tests alongside the change.

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: - OS-, device-, or `MediaRecorder`-level behavior (real disk-full, device disconnect, app quit ordering, capture edge cases): unit tests with fakes are NOT sufficient proof. Add e2e/smoke coverage where feasible, and document explicit manual verification steps for what automation cannot reach. Never claim durability or capture reliability is proven from helper-only tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: - Renderer UI glue (banners, overlays, status text): prefer behavior-level e2e/smoke checks or documented manual verification over brittle DOM-assertion unit tests written first. Extract decision logic into a pure helper and unit test that instead.

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: For every user-visible behavior change, add at least one proving test that would fail without the change — at the most honest layer available, not merely the most convenient one.

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: Minimum expectation by change type:

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: - Pure helper/domain change: unit tests

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: - Main-process service or IPC change: unit + integration tests

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: - Renderer feature change: utility tests and, if behaviorally important, e2e or smoke coverage

head: AGENTS.md > Test-First Requirements
text: - Release/build/packaging change: verification via packaging smoke and relevant CI updates

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text: Do not chase 100% coverage as a vanity target. Protect confidence instead.

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text: Coverage priorities by layer:

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text:
- `src/shared/**`
  - target very high coverage
  - new logic should normally ship with direct unit coverage

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text:
- pure modules in `src/main/services/**`
  - target high coverage
  - normalization, parsing, validation, section math, FPS selection, ffmpeg filter builders should be directly tested

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text:
- orchestration-heavy main-process code
  - combine unit coverage with integration coverage
  - do not rely on line coverage alone

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text:
- renderer runtime glue
  - prefer behavior tests and smoke/e2e coverage over brittle implementation-detail tests

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text: Use this rule when changing code:

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text: - if logic moved or behavior changed, coverage for that area should stay the same or improve

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text: - if an agent adds a new branch/edge case, it should usually add a test for that branch

head: AGENTS.md > Coverage Policy
text: - do not lower confidence in a critical path while keeping the global coverage number flat

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Rules
text: - Never "fix" a test by removing meaningful assertions just to get green CI.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Rules
text: - If a test reveals a bug, fix the underlying code.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Rules
text: - Prefer deterministic tests using mocks, fakes, fixtures, and temp directories.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Rules
text: - Avoid live external dependencies in tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Rules
text: - Keep tests readable and behavior-focused.

text: Use pnpm only in this repo.

head: AGENTS.md > Required Commands
text: - `pnpm run build:styles`

head: AGENTS.md > Required Commands
text: - `pnpm run package:smoke`

head: AGENTS.md > Required Commands

head: AGENTS.md > Learned User Preferences

head: AGENTS.md > Learned User Preferences
text: - Prefer resilient recording stop/finalize behavior: if one recorder (e.g. camera) fails during finalize, do not wedge the whole flow; allow partial success where possible and surface a clear error instead of hanging.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned User Preferences
text: - When judging recording reliability, do not treat helper-only unit tests as sufficient proof for real `MediaRecorder`, device, or OS-level capture edge cases.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned User Preferences
text: - Treat recording durability as non-negotiable: an app crash, quit, or finalize failure must not lose captured bytes, and recovery must still surface whatever was saved.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned User Preferences
text: - Treat original recordings as immutable: editing and Transcribe & Cut may change timeline metadata and source ranges, but must never overwrite, delete, or corrupt source media.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned User Preferences
text: - Keep automatic cutting conservative: Transcribe & Cut only removes silence, never speech. Bad-take removal is a separate, explicitly user-invoked button whose removals stay visible in the transcript panel with one-click Restore — because it is manual and reversible it may be more assertive (restart-cluster detection on cutoff markers, rephrase/stutter tolerant), but it must stay deterministic and must preserve ordinary full repeats without cutoff evidence, different continuations, short lists, and far-apart retries.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned User Preferences
text: - Recurring regressions (camera/audio sync drift, export/playback stutter on long or multi-section timelines) deserve root-cause investigation with end-to-end proving tests over surface-level fixes; these categories have regressed repeatedly across sessions and helper-only tests have missed them.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Editor PiP and overlay positions are authored in a fixed 1920×1080 space; when export resolution is above 1080p (derived from source, capped at 2560×1440), scale PiP and overlay geometry proportionally so placement matches preview instead of reusing literal 1080p pixel offsets on a larger frame.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Same-screen system audio may require Electron display-media loopback (`getDisplayMedia` with main-process coordination); external capture-device paths are not a substitute for all desktop/window sources.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Multi-section ffmpeg export accumulates A/V drift from two distinct sources: (1) per-section `fps` normalization rounds each video to the nearest frame boundary while paired audio keeps the exact source duration — clamp with `trim=duration=<exact>,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS` after the `fps` filter (or apply `fps` once after concat) so per-section video matches paired audio length before concat; (2) screen and camera MediaRecorders start emitting at slightly different wall-clock epochs and camera WebM is VFR with no seekable index, so trims driven by a single shared timeline offset cut the two files at non-matching moments — persist per-file start epochs at record time and apply per-file offsets during ffmpeg trim.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Export graphs must stay bounded because dense camera-overlay keyframes can exceed ffmpeg parser limits; for QuickTime-compatible H.264 screen exports, use yuv420p with a compatible profile/level and avoid unnecessary output resolution.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - `@electron/packager` dependency pruning can miss transitive packages under `pnpm`’s symlinked `node_modules` layout (fresh CI installs surface this); the packaging smoke harness avoids relying on that prune path.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Transcription is on-demand, not part of recording: stopping puts a full-length section on the timeline, and "Transcribe & Cut" later batch-transcribes via ElevenLabs Scribe word timestamps, replaces that take's sections with silence-cut ones as one undo step, and stores the spoken word tokens on the take (`transcriptSegments`). Bad-take removal is the separate "Remove Bad Takes" button: it runs the union of the conservative exact-prefix detector, a restart-cluster detector (cutoff markers `--`/`...`, ≥4 shared opening tokens with stutters collapsed, ≥60% token overlap, retry hops ≤4s; the retry opening is matched at every word position inside a cut-off unit with the rightmost match winning, so a good section ending that flows into a flubbed next-section start loses only the flubbed tail, and chained part-good/part-bad units each serve as the previous flub's retry), and an optional main-process LLM pass (`OPENAI_API_KEY`; sentence chunks in, strictly validated chunk indices out, times always resolved from our own word boundaries, final chunk never removable, graceful fallback without the key), then subtracts the ranges surgically so silence cuts and manual edits survive. Removed takes are never persisted — the transcript panel derives them as stored-words-not-covered-by-sections, which keeps undo/redo consistent and powers per-take Restore. Media remains immutable, and failure/no-speech/mid-flight edits leave the timeline unchanged with visible status.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - `src/renderer/styles/main.css` is Tailwind build output (`build:styles`, minified); full `check` rebuilds styles via nested steps, so tracking a non-matching formatted copy causes perpetual diffs—prefer generating locally and not treating it as hand-edited source.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Recording durability depends on streaming `MediaRecorder` chunks directly to disk via IPC temp `.part` files (renamed on finalize) instead of buffering in the renderer; screen and camera are independent recorder pipelines, so stop/save/finalize must tolerate one failing without blocking the other, and recovery normalization must require the screen file but tolerate a missing camera file so a partial failure does not discard an otherwise-recoverable take. Partial WebM files report `duration=Infinity`; resolve real duration by seeking a probe `<video>` element to `1e101` so the browser computes duration from the seekable range, and tolerate unreadable probes without wedging the whole recovery flow.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Premiere FCP7 xmeml constraints: emit Basic Motion `<center>` in media-frame units (`canvasOffsetPx / mediaDim`), not sequence units. The camera clip ships uncropped (Basic Motion + Opacity only): the square PiP crop and corner rounding are applied by the user in Premiere via a Film Impact "Rounded Crop" (`AE.Impact_Crop_FX`) effect preset, because xmeml cannot carry third-party effects (Premiere's own FCP XML exporter reports them "not translated"). Historical lessons if in-XML cropping is ever re-attempted: stock `Crop` must be `<effecttype>filter</effecttype>` + `<effectcategory>Matte</effectcategory>` (mis-classifying it makes Premiere silently drop it); rounded corners via travel mattes were reverted — travel-matte modes are dropped, Track Matte Key cannot use disabled/underlying tracks, and PNG/small-video Motion geometry imports differently from full-resolution video.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - `flushScheduledProjectSave()` runs when switching away from or closing a project and writes the in-memory project state back to `project.json`, overwriting any external edits made to the file while the app was running; edit `project.json` externally only with the app fully quit.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Editor playback must never track timeline sections by object identity: section arrays get wholesale-replaced (Transcribe & Cut, undo/redo restore copies), and an identity `indexOf` on a stale reference returned -1 so playback silently jumped to `sections[0]` and replayed old content. The draw-loop advance decision lives in `renderer/features/timeline/playback-advance.ts` — id-based lookup, geometry read from the current array, and a `stale` result that forces a re-resolve instead of guessing. Route future playback-advance changes through that module and its tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Learned Workspace Facts
text: - Editor responsiveness relies on invalidation-only paused drawing, frame-driven playback, a lazy active/next-take media pool, throttled scrub seeks with an exact release seek, release-only full trim DOM rebuilds, and cached/capped waveform envelopes with canonical-audio fallback and visible loading/error/no-audio states. Preserve these policies through the focused timeline helper modules and tests rather than reintroducing eager decoders, continuous paused compositing, or unbounded waveform scans.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: Frame has two halves that share one Z3-backed separation-logic core:

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: 1. **Solver** (`frame/core`, `encoding`, `checking`, ... below): a separation logic entailment checker for `P |- Q`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: 2. **Security agent** (`frame/sil`, see "Security Scanner" below): tree-sitter frontends for Python, Java, JS/TS, C/C++ and C# lower source to SIL, a taint/heap analysis finds vulnerabilities, Z3 checks path feasibility, and an optional LLM layer adds detection, triage, exploitation (`frame exploit`) and fixing (`frame fix`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - Core separation logic: empty heap (`emp`), points-to (`x |-> y`), separating conjunction (`*`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - Pure formulas: equality, boolean logic, arithmetic

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - Inductive predicates: lists, trees, custom data structures

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - Frame reasoning with automatic inference

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text: - Symbolic findings and LLM findings are tiered separately (`source_var` = `llm_detect` / `llm_verified`); never merge the tiers.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text: - **Two argparse parsers exist**: `frame/cli.py` (the `frame` entrypoint) and `frame/sil/cli.py` (`python -m frame.sil.cli`). `cmd_scan` lives in `sil/cli.py`, but any new `scan` flag must be added to BOTH parsers (tests/test_cli_frame_entrypoint_excludes.py exists because this bit us).

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text: - Suppression/config precedence: CLI flags > config file > built-in defaults. `--min-severity` and `--fail-on` default to `None` in argparse so the config file can supply them; resolve in `cmd_scan`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text: - Suppressed findings are kept on `ScanResult.suppressed` (reported as `summary.suppressed`), never silently dropped. Repo-scale LLM findings are merged after per-file suppression and are not currently subject to inline markers.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text:
- **Frontend conventions that bit us** (each was a silent recall or precision bug):
  - Code that is not inside a function must still be lowered. JS module scope becomes a synthetic `<module>` procedure; string-literal class fields / object properties become `<clinit>` / `<literal-properties>` procedures (`frontends/_literal_fields.py`). These carry only `Assign`s of literals, so they add no taint sources or sinks.
  - Spec sink-kind strings must go through `instructions.resolve_sink_kind` (aliases such as `path` -> `filesystem`, `redos` -> `regex`). Every frontend does; a hand-rolled `if kind in SinkKind else SQL_QUERY` fallback used to report any unrecognised kind (a tainted `setHeader`, a tainted regex) as SQL injection. A new spec sink kind must be a `SinkKind` value or an alias -- `tests/test_sink_kind_resolution.py` fails otherwise.
  - Path conditions are joined disjunctively in **every** language, and the walk does not follow an edge the solver proves infeasible (`_edge_feasible`). Without that pruning a provably dead path can be the first to reach a join and the feasible one is never analysed (salt `archive.py`); see `tests/test_join_path_conditions.py`.
  - `ProcSpec.is_source` taints only the call's *return value*. C input functions that fill a buffer or out-parameter (`fgets`, `scanf`, `read`, `recv`) use `taint_out_args` (set in `c_specs.py`).
  - C vs C++ matter: `Program.language` is `"c"` or `"cpp"`. A bare variable argument can only be an out-parameter in C++ (reference binding); in C it is a by-value read (see `_arg_may_define`).
  - **C/C++ path facts are decided by the SL/Z3 checker, never by name sets.** The path condition is a list of pure formulas: branch guards (`_feasibility_guard`), `x == rhs` for assignments (`_assignment_fact`), with writes, stores through pointers and calls havocking what they may change (`_advance_path_facts`). Joins keep `shared & (rest1 | rest2)` (`_join_path_conditions`). CWE-476 is `pc |- p == nil` (`_provably_null`), decided after a dedicated path-fact fixpoint (`_path_fact_fixpoint`) because the main walk does not re-analyse a node when only its path condition changes. Do not add per-pointer flag sets; add facts.
  - CWE-457 uses the same machinery: "x has no value yet" is the ghost fact `x#uninit == 1` (set by a bare declaration, cleared by anything `_uninit_inits` counts as a write), and a read is reported only if `pc & x#uninit == 1` is satisfiable (`_maybe_uninitialized`). The walk's reaching-definition set only nominates candidates.
  - A write or a call **forgets atoms, not facts** (`_forget`): only the atoms about the changed names become unknown (true where positive, false under a negation), so a disjunction keeps what it says about other variables. An oversized join first forgets volatile atoms (fields, globals, call results; see `_is_stable_name`) before falling back to the shared facts. For C, guard formulas use real arithmetic over the variables with casts stripped (`_exp_to_formula`), never an opaque name like `"(n % 4)"`.
  - **The C frontend must lower every write and every jump**, or the path facts describe paths that do not exist: `break`/`continue` are real edges (`_translate_jump`, with a `for` update node as the `continue` target; a `break` inside the sequentially-lowered `switch` stays a no-op); `#if`/`#ifdef` inside a function body becomes an unguarded branch per arm (`#if 0` arms are dead; no `#else` means an empty arm); comma expressions and nested `x++`/`--x` are lowered (postfix through a `$` temporary); `x += e` is `x = x + e`; an assignment inside a condition is an `Assign` in the node that evaluates it (loop conditions in the loop head). Function-like macros `#define`d in the file are recorded on `Program.function_macros` and may write their arguments.
  - The scanner's `_verify_check` runs the incorrectness checker (`pc * null_deref(p)` -> witness). It used to raise on every call (stale `VulnType` names) so nothing was verified; `tests/test_c_null_path_facts.py` pins it.
  - C analyzers are a mix of structural passes (translator, SIL-based) and older line-based regexes (`interprocedural_analyzer.py`). Test C snippets one statement per line; a one-line function defeats the line-based ones and hides real behaviour.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text:
- **A spec name is not always the whole story** (`tests/test_sink_receiver_precision.py`):
  - Frontends and `Program.get_spec` suffix-match member chains (`models.sequelize.query` -> `query`). A global function spec (`setTimeout`, `eval`, bare `exec`/`execSync`/`spawn`) sets `ProcSpec.global_only`: a member call matches only on `window`/`global`/`globalThis` or a receiver the file never declares (`_may_be_global`), so `req.setTimeout(ms, cb)` and `re.exec(s)` are not sinks.
  - JS module bindings (`const cp = require('child_process')`, `import {exec as run} from ...`) rename calls after the module in `_get_call_name` (`cp.exec` -> `child_process.exec`, `run` -> `child_process.exec`), so module-qualified specs match whatever the local name is.
  - A guessed receiver type (`Program.get_spec`'s common-prefix list) never yields a taint-free usage sink or an `exact_class` spec. Credential-named variables whose head noun is metadata (`secretKeyAlgorithm`) are not secrets (`_METADATA_HEADS`). Python-only idioms (pathlib `/`) are gated on `program.language`.
  - A sink that installs a callback (`setHostnameVerifier`) sets `permissive_callback_arg`: it fires only when the callback provably accepts everything (all returns `true`, or a documented-permissive library object, also through a non-reassigned local/field).
  - Java `catch` clauses are branches after the try body (`_translate_handlers`), not code that always runs, and `throw` is a value-less `Return`. Sequential handlers made a rethrowing catch end every path and a helper "return" its exception.
  - XXE: `secure_parsers` holds parsers hardened by `setFeature`/`setAttribute`/`setEntityResolver` (`_track_xml_hardening`), products of a hardened factory, and results of a same-class helper whose every non-null return is hardened (summarised in a pre-pass). Joins intersect it and `_states_equal` compares it. `TaintSink.receiver` carries the parser to the sink.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text: - **Java specs match by declared type** (`tests/test_java_declared_types.py`): many keys are written against a conventional variable name (`documentBuilder.parse`, `jdbcTemplate.query`). The frontend records each name's declared type (fields, params, locals, for-each/resource/catch vars; `var` from `new T()` or `JAVA_FACTORY_RETURN_TYPES`; a name declared with two types is unknown) and sets `Call.receiver_type`; `typed_spec_lookup` (used by the frontend and `Program.spec_for_call`) tries `type_spec_receivers(T)` (`T`, decapitalised `T`, `JAVA_TYPE_RECEIVERS` aliases) before names. An `exact_class` spec (`Random.*`) needs the runtime class (`Call.receiver_exact`: `new T()`, never reassigned) because a value declared `Random` may be a SecureRandom; a taint-free name-only sink is not applied to a receiver whose type is known. Session/request `getAttribute` is server state, not a source.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text:
- **Same-named procedures are all kept** (`tests/test_overloaded_procedures.py`): `Program.add_procedure` names the 2nd, 3rd... `name#2`, `name#3` (overloads, Python property setters, C `#ifdef` arms) instead of replacing the first, and records `overload_arities`; use `Procedure.simple_name` and `accepts_arity(n)` for arity-only languages.
  - Java calls resolve by type (`Program.resolve_java_call`): the frontend types each argument (`_arg_type`: literals, primitives/arrays/fields, numeric promotion, casts, `new`, own-method return types, String methods) and each parameter (`_static_type`, type variables unknown); `java_convertible` says yes/no/maybe (widening, boxing, final JDK types, the in-file hierarchy `Program.class_supertypes`). An exact match wins; otherwise a single non-rejected candidate wins only in a class with no supertypes (`Procedure.class_open`), since an inherited overload could be more specific. Anything else resolves to nothing -- never guess.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text: - **JS NoSQL sinks are database-handle methods** (`ProcSpec.db_method`, `db_method_applies`): they need a receiver (`RECEIVER_UNKNOWN` marks a chained call's), and do not apply when the frontend's `_receiver_kind` knows the receiver is something else -- an array/string/regex/object/function literal, `new X()`, a value from a Node core module or an in-memory utility library (`crypto.createHash(...)`), an array/string method result, an object-literal property, or a call whose first argument is a function literal. Unknown receivers (a model imported from `./models/user`) still match.

head: CLAUDE.md > Security Scanner (`frame/sil`)
text: - Java lowers a call in a `return` expression as `tmp = call; return tmp`, and hoists an argument that is a taint-source call (`parse(req.getInputStream())` -> `$a = req.getInputStream(); parse($a)`), so specs and ordinary propagation apply. An unqualified / `this.` call to a method the class declares resolves to that procedure (`receiver_type` = the class), never to a same-named library spec, and `spec_for_call` returns None for it so default argument->result propagation still applies (returning the procedure's empty ProcSpec silently disabled it and cost ~20 points of OWASP recall).

text: - **Validate Java spec/frontend changes on OWASP BenchmarkJava** (2740 labelled cases): the per-file CWE set should not change unless intended. Corpus scans alone missed regressions it caught.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (solver) > Key Design Decisions
text: **Theoretical Foundation**: Frame implements separation logic (Reynolds & O'Hearn, 2002) using SMT-based reasoning with Z3. The core technique is the heap-as-array encoding (Piskac, Wies, Zufferey, 2013), which reduces separation logic entailments to first-order logic queries. See README.md "Theoretical Foundations" section for detailed references and comparison with other solvers (Sleek, Cyclist, Grasshopper, SPEN).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (solver) > Key Design Decisions
text: **Heap Representation**: Heap is a Z3 array `heap: Loc -> Val`. Domain is tracked as a set of locations. Disjointness enforced by ensuring domains don't overlap in separating conjunction.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (solver) > Key Design Decisions
text: **Predicate Unfolding**: Bounded unfolding (default depth 3) to maintain decidability. Deeper unfolding increases completeness but may hit recursion limits or timeouts. Adaptive unfolding adjusts depth based on formula size.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (solver) > Key Design Decisions
text: **Predicate Folding**: Goal-directed folding prioritizes proposals that match the consequent (inspired by Cyclist's cyclic proof techniques but adapted for SMT). Blind folding provides a fallback for general synthesis.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (solver) > Key Design Decisions
text: **Lemma Library**: Pattern-based lemma application (similar to Sleek's strategy) handles common entailments without Z3 queries. Proven lemmas for transitivity, reflexivity, and construction patterns.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (solver) > Key Design Decisions
text: **Soundness**: All predicates validated for strict positivity (no negation), free variables properly bound, and arity consistency. Parser bug fixed in commit d239d01 - critical fix for storing body text correctly.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture (solver) > Key Design Decisions
text: **Performance**: Fast paths for reflexivity (<1ms), syntactic checks before Z3. Average 5ms per check on test suite.

head: CLAUDE.md > Critical Implementation Notes > Parser Bug Fix (d239d01)
text: The parser had a critical bug where it was storing the Formula object instead of the body text when parsing SMT2 predicates. This caused recursive predicate definitions to fail. Always store `body_text` as string, not Formula object.

head: AGENTS.md
text: This file provides guidance for AI coding agents working on the Alby Lightning Browser Extension repository.

head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: Alby Lightning Browser Extension — a WebExtension (Chrome MV3, Firefox/Opera MV2) that brings Bitcoin Lightning Network payments and Nostr signing to the browser. It implements the **WebLN**, **Nostr (NIP-07)**, **WebBTC**, and **Liquid** provider APIs by injecting them into web pages and routing requests through a background script that talks to a configurable Lightning backend (LND, LNbits, LNC, LNDhub, NWC, Alby account, Eclair, Galoy, plus native-companion variants for Tor).

head: AGENTS.md > Tech Stack
text: - **Build:** Webpack 5 + SWC, separate builds per target browser (`dist/<env>/<browser>`)

head: AGENTS.md > Tech Stack
text: - **Frontend (UI surfaces):** React 19, React Router v6, TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS 3, i18next, Zustand, axios

head: AGENTS.md > Tech Stack
text: - **Storage:** `browser.storage` (settings/state) + Dexie/IndexedDB (allowances, payments, permissions, blocklist) via `db.ts`

head: AGENTS.md > Tech Stack
text: - **Crypto:** `@noble/*`, `@scure/*`, `bitcoinjs-lib`, `liquidjs-lib`, `nostr-tools`, `crypto-js` (legacy)

head: AGENTS.md > Tech Stack
text: - **Testing:** Jest (unit, via `@swc/jest`). The Playwright e2e suite under `tests/e2e/` is currently broken and unmaintained — rely on Jest only.

head: AGENTS.md > Tech Stack
text: - **Manifest:** Single `src/manifest.json` with `__chrome__` / `__firefox__` / `__opera__` prefixes resolved by `wext-manifest-loader` at build time

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands > Development
text: Load `dist/development/<browser>` as an unpacked / temporary extension. See `doc/SETUP.md` for browser-specific load instructions and `doc/SETUP_ANDROID.md` for Firefox Android.

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands > Build / Package
text: `manifest.json` ships with version `0.0.0`; the webpack loader rewrites it from `package.json` at build time.

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands > Lint, Format, Type-check
text: ESLint, Prettier, and `tsc --noEmit` are enforced on staged files via Husky + lint-staged. Commit messages are validated by commitlint (Conventional Commits).

head: AGENTS.md > Common Commands > Testing
text: The Playwright `yarn test:e2e` / `yarn test` scripts still exist in `package.json` but the e2e suite is broken and not maintained — do not rely on them. Add new tests as Jest unit tests (colocated `*.test.ts` next to source, or under `tests/unit/`).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Three execution contexts
text: The extension code is split across three runtime contexts that **cannot share modules or memory directly** — they communicate only via `browser.runtime.sendMessage` and `window.postMessage`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Three execution contexts
text: 1. **Background script** (`src/extension/background-script/`) — long-lived (MV2) / service-worker-like (MV3) singleton. Owns the unlocked wallet state, IndexedDB, the connector instance, and is the **only** place that touches the Lightning backend or private keys.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Three execution contexts
text: 2. **Content scripts** (`src/extension/content-script/*.js`) — injected into every page. They inject the corresponding inpage script (`inpage-script/`) into the page's main world and proxy messages between page ↔ background. There is one content script per provider (`webln.js`, `alby.js`, `nostr.js`, `liquid.js`, `webbtc.js`) plus `onstart.ts` and `context-menu.ts`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Three execution contexts
text:
3. **UI surfaces** (`src/app/router/`) — separate React apps bundled as different webpack entries:
   - `popup` — the toolbar popup
   - `prompt` — modal window opened by the background script for user confirmation (payment, signMessage, permission, etc.)
   - `options` — full-page settings
   - `welcome` — onboarding flow

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Three execution contexts
text: Each surface lives under `src/app/router/<Name>/index.tsx` and is referenced from `webpack.config.js` `entry:` and from `static/views/*.html`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Provider APIs (injected into web pages)
text: Inpage providers live in `src/extension/providers/<api>/index.ts`. Each method calls `this.execute(actionName, args)` which `postMessage`s to its content-script bridge; the bridge forwards to `router.ts` and the response comes back the same way (see [postMessage.ts](src/extension/providers/postMessage.ts) and [providerBase.ts](src/extension/providers/providerBase.ts)). All methods require `enable()` to have resolved first; `providerBase` enforces this. Public docs: <https://guides.getalby.com/developer-guide/developer-guide/alby-browser-extension-apis>.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Provider APIs (injected into web pages)
text: **`window.webln`** — [providers/webln/index.ts](src/extension/providers/webln/index.ts) (WebLN spec)

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Provider APIs (injected into web pages)
text:
| Method                                             | Purpose                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

text: All providers also inherit `enable()` / `isEnabled()` / `on()` / `off()` from [providerBase.ts](src/extension/providers/providerBase.ts). To add a new method: add it to the inpage provider, register a corresponding action in [router.ts](src/extension/background-script/router.ts), implement the handler under [actions/](src/extension/background-script/actions/), define the message type in [src/types.ts](src/types.ts), and (for WebLN-like flows) extend [connector.interface.ts](src/extension/background-script/connectors/connector.interface.ts) on every connector.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Request flow (the critical path)
text: `router.ts` is the central map from string action name → handler. Adding a new RPC means registering it there and exposing it via `src/common/lib/api.ts` (the typed client used by React UI and content scripts).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Connectors
text: `src/extension/background-script/connectors/connector.interface.ts` is the abstraction every Lightning backend implements (`getInfo`, `sendPayment`, `keysend`, `makeInvoice`, `signMessage`, etc.). Adding/modifying a method here means updating **every** connector implementation (`alby`, `lnd`, `lnc`, `lnbits`, `lndhub`, `nwc`, `eclair`, `galoy`, and the `native*` companion-app variants). The `Native.ts` base class handles the native-messaging transport used for Tor proxying via the [alby-companion-rs](https://github.com/getAlby/alby-companion-rs) host app.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > State & persistence
text: - **`state.ts`** (Zustand-style store in background) — unlocked wallet state, current account, current connector instance, password. Rehydrated from `browser.storage` on startup; the password lives in memory only.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > State & persistence
text: - **`db.ts`** (Dexie / IndexedDB) — allowances, payments, permissions, blocklist. The UI reads via the typed `request()` API and never imports `db.ts` directly.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > State & persistence
text: - **`browser.storage.local`** — settings, account metadata (with the connector config encrypted by the unlock password).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > State & persistence
text: - **Migrations:** [src/extension/background-script/migrations/index.ts](src/extension/background-script/migrations/index.ts) — a single object keyed by migration name. Each key runs once on startup; the executed names are tracked in `state.migrations`. Add a new key for a new migration; never rename or remove an existing one.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Domain concepts
text: These are the user-visible behaviors backed by [`db.ts`](src/extension/background-script/db.ts). An agent touching auth/payment flows must understand which one applies — they are distinct mechanisms, not synonyms.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Domain concepts
text: - **Allowance** (`db.allowances`) — a per-host **payment budget** (`totalBudget` / `remainingBudget`, in sats). When a site has an allowance, `webln.sendPayment` / `keysend` debit it silently up to `remainingBudget`; over-budget or expired allowances fall back to a Prompt. Allowances also flag `lnurlAuth` (auto-login allowed) and `enabledFor` (the WebLN method scopes). Created via the Prompt's "remember" option.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Domain concepts
text: - **Permission** (`db.permissions`) — a per-host, per-method **auto-approve flag** independent of any budget. Keyed by `(accountId, host, method)` where `method` is one of `PermissionMethodNostr` (`nostr/signMessage`, `nostr/signSchnorr`, `nostr/getPublicKey`, `nostr/encrypt`, `nostr/decrypt`), `PermissionMethodBitcoin` (`bitcoin/getAddress`), or `PermissionMethodLiquid` (`liquid/getAddress`). `blocked: true` means "always deny without prompting." Managed via `addPermissionFor` / `hasPermissionFor` / `isPermissionBlocked` in [permissions/](src/extension/background-script/permissions/).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Domain concepts
text: - **Blocklist** (`db.blocklist`) — a site the user has fully suppressed; the inpage providers should not be active there. Distinct from blocked Permission rows (which gate specific methods).

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Domain concepts
text: - **Payment** (`db.payments`) — a local audit log of every sent payment (`preimage`, `paymentHash`, `host`, `allowanceId`, fees). Read-only history; the UI lists this in account detail.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Domain concepts
text: - **Account encryption** — every `account.config` (connector creds: macaroons, NWC URIs, mnemonics, …) is encrypted with the user's unlock password before being written to `browser.storage`. The decrypted config is held only on `state.connector` while the wallet is unlocked. **Never persist a connector config in plaintext, and never log it.**

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Domain concepts
text: - **Onboarding (Welcome flow)** — each backend has a dedicated connect screen under [src/app/screens/connectors/Connect<Backend>/](src/app/screens/connectors/). Adding a new connector means: (a) implement the class under `background-script/connectors/`, (b) add the `Connect<Name>` screen, (c) register the route in [src/app/router/connectorRoutes.tsx](src/app/router/connectorRoutes.tsx), (d) translate the labels.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Domain concepts
text: - **LNURL flows** — handled in [actions/lnurl/](src/extension/background-script/actions/lnurl/): `auth` (LUD-04 login, optionally via mnemonic-derived linking key per LUD-05), `pay` (LUD-06 pay-to-LN-address), `withdraw` (LUD-03), `channel` (LUD-07). These run in the background script, open a Prompt, then call the active connector.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Path aliases
text: `tsconfig.json` defines `~/* → src/*`, `@components/* → src/app/components/*`, `@screens/* → src/app/screens/*`. Prefer these over deep relative imports.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Manifest variants
text: `src/manifest.json` uses `__chrome__`, `__firefox__`, `__opera__`, and `__chrome|firefox__` key prefixes. `wext-manifest-loader` strips the prefixes for the active `TARGET_BROWSER` at build time. Chrome ships as MV3 (service worker, `host_permissions`); Firefox/Opera ship as MV2 (background page, combined `permissions`). When adding a permission or background entry, set both variants.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Conventions
text: - **TypeScript strict mode** — no `any`. New code is `.ts/.tsx`; pre-existing `.js` content scripts and inpage scripts may stay JS.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Conventions
text: - **i18n:** All user-facing strings go through `react-i18next`. Translations live in `src/i18n/locales/<lang>/translation.json`. Use `snake_case` keys, nest by screen/component, only indent when there's more than one attribute (`title` / `label`). See `doc/CONTRIBUTION.md` for full rules — translations are managed via Weblate, so structure matters.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Conventions
text: - **HTTP:** Use `axios` (not `fetch`) — this is an explicit project preference.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Conventions
text: - **Commits:** Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`) — enforced by commitlint. Same prefixes for branch names (`feat/...`).

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Conventions
text: - **No sensitive data in logs.** The background script's console is shared; never log seeds, mnemonics, macaroons, NWC URLs, or unlock passwords.

head: AGENTS.md > Coding Conventions
text: - **Prompt windows are user-facing.** Any new action that requires confirmation should open a Prompt route under `src/app/router/Prompt` and resolve via the message returned from it.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: UnrealBridge is a TCP bridge between external tools (Claude Code) and Unreal Engine 5.3+ (verified clean BuildPlugin against 5.3.2 / 5.4.4 / 5.5.4 / 5.6.1 / 5.7.1 / 5.8.0 via `tools/build_matrix.py`; some libraries are gated to 5.7+ and a few inline shims handle 5.3 and 5.8 — see `docs/version-compatibility.md`). UE 5.2 and earlier are not supported. It consists of:

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - A UE Editor plugin (`Plugin/UnrealBridge/`) that runs a TCP server inside the editor

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - A Python CLI client (`.claude/skills/unreal-bridge/scripts/bridge.py`) used by the `unreal-bridge` skill

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: - API reference docs and helper scripts for querying/manipulating UE assets via Python

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Commands
text:
**Sync plugin and matching skills to a UE project:**
```bash
sync_project.bat D:\Path\To\YourProject
```
Mirrors `Plugin/UnrealBridge/` plus `.claude/skills/unreal-bridge/` into the target project's plugin, `.agents`, and `.claude` destinations. Local plugin build outputs are retained. `sync_plugin.bat` is a legacy command-name alias with the same project-root argument.

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Commands
text:
**Test bridge connection:**
```bash
python .claude/skills/unreal-bridge/scripts/bridge.py ping
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Commands
text:
**Execute Python in UE:**
```bash
python .claude/skills/unreal-bridge/scripts/bridge.py exec "print('hello')"
python .claude/skills/unreal-bridge/scripts/bridge.py exec-file script.py
```

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text: Length-prefixed JSON over TCP on an OS-assigned port (default bind `127.0.0.1`, port auto-allocated at startup). Clients find the editor via the UDP discovery service (host-local by default; see next section) — port 9876 is no longer hardcoded on the TCP data channel.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text: - Request: `[4 bytes big-endian length][JSON: {"id":"...", "command":"exact_exec", "expected":{"protocol_version":2,"instance_id":"...","pid":...,"project_path":"..."}, "request":{"script":"...","timeout":30}, "token":"..." (optional)}]`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text: - Response: `[4 bytes big-endian length][JSON: {"id":"...", "success":bool, "output":"...", "error":"...", "protocol_version":2, "instance_id":"...", "pid":..., "project_path":"..."}]`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text: - Token auth: required when the server binds non-loopback. The token is written to `<Project>/Saved/UnrealBridge/token.txt`; clients read it and add `"token":"<value>"` to every request. Constant-time compared on the server.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text: - Every request uses an `exact_*` command with frozen discovery identity. Payload fields live under `request`, so a legacy server cannot mistake `exact_exec` for an ordinary script request. The production dispatcher rejects missing/malformed identity, request objects, and unknown/legacy commands before any command body, work admission, or GameThread dispatch; the client rejects response identity drift. `project_path` is one wire-canonical string and must match discovery/startup output exactly on every OS.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text: - Client response frames are bounded to `MAX_RESPONSE_FRAME_BYTES` (10 MiB), must be non-empty, valid UTF-8, and decode to a JSON object before identity fields are read.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text:
- Special exact commands (handled inline on the worker thread, bypass the Python exec queue):
  - `exact_ping` → `pong` (TCP-only liveness)
  - `exact_editor_status` → cached Engine/Slate tick ages, readiness, staleness and modal-attention summary (no fresh GameThread dispatch)
  - `exact_gamethread_ping` → `alive`/`unresponsive` + `latency_ms` (GT liveness)
  - `exact_debug_resume` → unsticks a paused BP breakpoint via `FKismetDebugUtilities::RequestAbortingExecution`
  - `exact_modal_status` → structured active-Slate-modal snapshot (title, body, buttons, redacted inputs, checkboxes)
  - `exact_modal_action` → guarded click/input/checkbox action; rejects stale snapshots

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text:
`bridge.py exec*` automatically calls `modal_status` after an exec timeout and
adds `blocked_by_modal` plus the snapshot to its response. It never selects an
action automatically. The caller must read the dialog semantics and act with
the returned `snapshot_id`; this prevents both blind confirmation and a stale
action landing on a different dialog.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > TCP Protocol
text:
Exec and modal GameThread work share a cancellable lifecycle. If the server-side
deadline expires while work is still queued, the response reports `cancelled before execution`
and a later ticker/task-graph consumer cannot run the body. If the GameThread already claimed
the work, it is not safely retractable; the response reports `already started and outcome is unknown`
instead of claiming a successful cancellation. Shutdown first closes a shared admission gate,
uses the same queued cancellation path, and drains tracked worker/GameThread closures before
module unload; each result/event therefore has exactly one terminal publisher.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Discovery Protocol
text: UDP discovery defaults to a host-local multicast probe on `239.255.42.99:9876` with TTL 0 plus a parallel loopback probe to `127.0.0.1:9876`. Both carry the same request id and responses are de-duplicated by Server-start UUID. `--discovery-scope=lan` (or `UNREAL_BRIDGE_DISCOVERY_SCOPE=lan`) explicitly opts into one-hop multicast with TTL 1; loopback remains as a fallback. Multiple editors can bind via `SO_REUSEADDR`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Discovery Protocol
text: - Probe (client → group): `{"v":2, "type":"probe", "request_id":"<uuid>", "filter":{"project":"<name|path|*>"}}`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Discovery Protocol
text: - Response (server → probe source, unicast): `{"v":2, "protocol_version":2, "type":"response", "request_id":"<uuid>", "instance_id":"<uuid>", "pid":..., "project":"...", "project_path":"...", "engine_version":"...", "tcp_bind":"...", "tcp_port":..., "token_fingerprint":"<sha1(token)[:16]>", "capabilities":["exact_exec",...]}`. The six pre-existing exact commands are the minimum required capability set; `exact_editor_status` is an advertised optional capability required only by the status command, and unique forward-compatible extras are allowed.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Discovery Protocol
text: - Client loop: resolve scope (`CLI > UNREAL_BRIDGE_DISCOVERY_SCOPE > local`) → send the same probe to TTL-scoped multicast + loopback → collect for `--discovery-timeout` ms (default 800) → tolerate Windows UDP reset notifications and discard each malformed/incomplete/legacy datagram without aborting collection → de-duplicate by instance UUID → filter by `--project=...` → freeze identity → connect TCP. The discovery group must be an IPv4 multicast address. A wildcard advertised bind resolves to that response's source IP. Empty `token_fingerprint` means no token required. Direct unicast mode requires the inseparable `--endpoint`, `--instance-id`, `--expected-pid`, and `--expected-project-path` tuple, copied verbatim from discovery/startup output.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Server configuration (CLI / env / editor ini)
text: Priority CLI > env > `EditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini [UnrealBridge]` > default.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > Server configuration (CLI / env / editor ini)
text:
| CLI | Env | INI key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-UnrealBridgeBind=` | `UNREAL_BRIDGE_BIND` | `Bind` | `127.0.0.1` | Interface to bind TCP to |
| `-UnrealBridgePort=` | `UNREAL_BRIDGE_PORT` | `Port` | `0` | TCP port — `0` = OS-assigned ephemeral |
| `-UnrealBridgeToken=` | `UNREAL_BRIDGE_TOKEN` | `Token` | *(empty)* | Required when bind is not loopback |
| `-UnrealBridgeDiscoveryGroup=` | `UNREAL_BRIDGE_DISCOVERY_GROUP` | `DiscoveryGroup` | `239.255.42.99:9876` | Multicast group + port |
| `-UnrealBridgeDiscoveryEnabled=` | `UNREAL_BRIDGE_DISCOVERY` | `DiscoveryEnabled` | `1` | `0` = disable discovery responder |
| `-UnrealBridgeNoDiscovery` *(flag)* | — | — | — | Shorthand for `DiscoveryEnabled=0` |

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Workflow
text: Edit C++ source in `Plugin/UnrealBridge/Source/`. Two canonical loops, picked by whether the edit touches reflection metadata:

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Workflow > Hot reload (editor stays up) — body-only edits
text: Syncs plugin source then triggers Live Coding via the bridge. Works when the edit only changed function bodies (no new `UFUNCTION` / `UCLASS` / `UPROPERTY` / `USTRUCT` members). LC patches the running editor in place — PIE, open assets, viewport camera all survive. Takes ~10–60s depending on how many TUs changed. On `Status="Failure"` the script tails recent `LogLiveCoding` entries; the actual MSVC error text only lives in the external LiveCodingConsole GUI window (see `bridge-editor-api.md` Live Coding section).

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Workflow > Full rebuild + relaunch — any reflection change
text: Quits the editor → runs the version-locked plugin + skill sync → runs the target project's `Build.bat` → launches the editor detached → polls `bridge.py ping` until ready. Use when adding/removing `UFUNCTION` / `UCLASS` / `UPROPERTY`, changing struct layouts, or recovering from a failed LC compile. Build.bat's stdout captures full compiler output (this is the only way to surface MSVC errors when hot reload reports Failure). Takes ~2–5 minutes.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
ArchLang: a declarative language (`.arch`) that compiles to SVG floor plans. TypeScript, Node 18+,
npm-workspaces monorepo; the core (repo root, `@chanmeng666/archlang`) also runs in the browser.
Code and tests are the documentation; this file holds only what they cannot say.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- `compile()` is pure, sync, deterministic: no I/O, time, randomness or Node APIs in `src/` outside
  `src/cli.ts`+`src/cli/`; environment via the `World` seam; numbers via `src/num-format.ts`; never
  mutate the memoised parse-stage `PlanNode` (clone). Zero runtime deps.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text: - User-source errors are returned as a `Diagnostic` (byte `span` + catalogued `E_*`/`W_*`), never thrown.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- `compile()` is bounded: every input returns within the step budget and the drawing budget. Charge
  new evaluator work to the step meter BEFORE allocating (`MAX_EVAL_STEPS`, `E_STEP_LIMIT`,
  `src/expr.ts`); budgets are counts, never time. Every coordinate/length stays within
  `MODEL_RANGE_MM` (`src/num-format.ts`, `E_OUT_OF_RANGE`).

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- New element = one `src/elements/` module registered in `defs.ts`, no switch; it declares
  `drawCost` (an upper bound on what it draws) and `bounds()`/`measures()` covering every coordinate
  and length it draws. New fixture category = a `FIXTURE_FAMILIES` row + a `CATALOG` entry; a drawn
  symbol ignores its `label`.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- Never hand-edit `dist/` or a generated file; run `gen:*`. Drift-green proves reproducibility, not
  correctness: derive generator templates from the source of truth, never retype.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text: - A derived position comes from the shape, never its bounding box or centroid.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- Every new language form ships a byte-identity law pinned by test (SHA-256 of SVG + `describe()` +
  `lint()` over the examples). Never bless a golden to green a suite.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text: - Heights draw nothing; `--view` measures nothing (`describe()`/`lint()` never learn it).

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- A drawing change never moves `describe()`/`lint()` over the corpus; a glyph never gains
  handedness and a loss is allow-listed (`test/glyph-chirality.test.ts`).

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text: - `npm run check` does not typecheck `test/`; `typecheck:all` does.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- A clean auto-merge of a MOVED function another branch MODIFIED is not evidence: diff the moved
  body, run both branches' fixtures together.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- Releases are tokenless OIDC (`v*` tag); never an npm token, never automate npmjs account/2FA.
  Pushing `main` deploys the sites. Before a tag: `/release-check`.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- Eval: T3 live run declined forever; `eval:live` is paid, owner-only; holdout never published;
  dataset canary never regenerated.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text: - Sites are light-only (no dark mode); `brand/archlang-logo-master.svg` is byte-sacred.

head: AGENTS.md > Hard rules
text:
- No secrets in this public repo. Versions come from npm/tags/`gh release`, never a doc; release
  narrative lives only in `CHANGELOG.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Overview
text: DPTLib is a platform-independent C99 library (base, databases, datastruct, framebuf, geom, io, text, utils, wuss modules) shared across the author's projects (PrivateEye, MotionMasks, etc). Targets desktop (Linux/macOS/Windows) and RISC OS (via GCCSDK).

text: - `BUILD_TESTS=YES` — build the `DPTLibTest` self-test executable.

head: CLAUDE.md > Build

head: CLAUDE.md > Build
text: Requires libpng (`find_package(PNG)` on non-RISC OS). On RISC OS the build fetches and patches zlib/libpng itself via `FetchContent` (see `cmake/*.patch`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Module layout.** Each module lives in two places that must be kept in sync:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - `include/<area>/<module>.h` — the public API, always wrapped in `extern "C"`, documented with Doxygen `\file`/`\param`/`\return` comments.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - `libraries/<area>/<module>/` — implementation `.c` files (often one function per file, e.g. `libraries/datastruct/vector/{create,destroy,insert,...}.c`), plus a private `impl.h` defining the opaque struct behind the public typedef and any internal-only declarations.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: New source/header files must be added by hand to the relevant `set(..._SOURCES ...)` list and, for public headers, to `PUBLIC_HEADERS`, in `CMakeLists.txt` — there is no globbing.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Error handling.** No exceptions; functions return `result_t` (`include/base/result.h`). Each module reserves a `result_BASE_<MODULE>` offset block and defines its own `result_<MODULE>_*` codes starting from that base. Common generic codes (`result_OK`, `result_OOM`, `result_BAD_ARG`, etc.) live at `result_BASE_GENERIC`. Callers typically check `rc != result_OK` and propagate.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Debug/logging.** `include/base/debug.h` provides `logf_info/warning/error/fatal/abort`, plus `check(err)` (log-and-`goto failure`) and `sentinel` (unreachable-code marker), both of which are compiled out entirely when `NDEBUG` is set — don't rely on their side effects in release builds.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Test structure.** There is a single test binary (`DPTLibTest`, from `apps/test/main.c`) that dispatches to per-module `<module>_test(resources)` functions declared centrally in `include/test/all-tests.h`. Tests return `result_TEST_PASSED`/`result_TEST_FAILED` (`result_BASE_TEST`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **Notable sub-libraries with their own docs** (`docs/*.md`): `io/stream` (chainable byte-stream sources/transforms, PackBits and move-to-front compression), `framebuf/bmfont` (proportional bitmap fonts loaded from specially-formatted PNGs), `framebuf/composite` (Porter-Duff compositing on RGBA/BGRA bitmaps), `wuss` (minimal window manager: creation, z-ordering, mouse routing, dirty-region redraw, client-delegated content).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: **RISC OS.** `TARGET_RISCOS` (set by an external toolchain file) switches CMake to fetch/build zlib+libpng from source, link OSLib from `$GCCSDK_INSTALL_ENV`, and applies `riscos_set_flags()`. `pngusr-ro.dfa`/`pngusr-rw.dfa` select libpng's build config depending on `DPTLIB_IMAGES_READ_ONLY`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code style
text: - C99, `-Wall -Wextra -pedantic`. Allman brace style, 2-space indentation, tabs converted to spaces (see `.astylerc`/`.editorconfig` — astyle is the formatter of record).

head: CLAUDE.md > Code style
text: - Declare variables at the top of each scope (pre-C99 style is followed throughout, even though the standard is C99), ordered by first use.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code style
text: - File header comment format: `/* filename.c -- one-line description */`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code style
text: - Section breaks within files use `/* ----- ... ----- */` rule comments.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code style
text: - Public API docs use Doxygen (`\file`, `\param`, `\return`); a `Doxyfile` exists for generating them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Commit messages
text: Use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/): `<type>[optional scope]: <description>`, e.g. `fix(pickle): handle zero-length blobs`. Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `ci`, `build`. Add a `!` before the colon (or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer) for breaking changes.
