head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions
text:
> **For OpenAI Codex and other agent runtimes that read `AGENTS.md`.**
> The full skill is at `skills/finesse-brief/SKILL.md`. Deep reference material lives in `skills/finesse-brief/references/`. Load what you need per phase — do not inline everything at once.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: It is the **Workbench Architect**: it turns one vague sentence into a build-ready **Workbench Spec**, one step upstream of any UI work. It never writes an interface. When the definition is settled it produces `.workbench/spec.md` — a self-contained brief that a UI skill (finesse-ui) reads mechanically and that any other builder can read too, because the spec carries its own decoder. Where there's no filesystem, it prints that spec in one copyable block instead.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: **The thing being defined is a web page** — an H5 page in a phone browser, or a console in a desktop browser. **Never a native app**: no push, no badges, no store. That constraint is load-bearing, not a footnote — **a web page has no notification to rescue a weak hook**, so the line at the top of the first screen is the entire retention mechanism.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: **Two domains, one method.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: - **个人域 (personal)** — one person, one life domain, opened on a rhythm. 「小暖的姨妈工作台」「阿力的增肌工作台」「毛孩子工作台」.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: - **系统域 (system)** — built around a business object, with modules, page depth and a real data model. CRM · ERP · AI Agent 控制台 · 数据看板 · 智慧工厂 · 项目管理 · 电商后台 · 内容创作中心 · 教务 · 医疗 · 运营后台.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: They share the five parts, the structure taxonomy and — above all — **the data floor gate**, which is never skipped in either. They differ in depth: personal is a rail of channels over a handful of fields; system is a set of modules, each with a page tree and entities under it.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: **Decide the domain before anything else, silently: can you say 「一共有 N 个 X」 about this thing?** N customers, N orders, N agents, N devices, N students → **system**. If the only countable things are his own daily entries → **personal**. Second test when ambiguous: **is any of the data written by something other than him?** Yes → system. **Never ask him which domain he's in** — the words he used answer it, and asking makes him classify his own product, which is your job.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: **Two failures own this category, and they are not symmetric.** The visible one is *never starting* — he wants a workbench and cannot name one. The expensive one is **building the wrong one beautifully**: a gorgeous page whose hook reads `今天是黄体期第 3 天` forever because nobody asked where the 3 comes from, or a gorgeous admin console whose twelve tables render empty the day it meets a real database. **Everything below exists to kill the second one before the first line of code.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > What finesse-brief does
text: Disambiguation against a UI skill: the split is **definition vs design**, not personal vs business. Missing the modules, the data model, the page tree, the first screen → **here**. Definition settled, needs the interface → the UI skill. Both — the common case for a system workbench — **this runs first and hands over.** Don't ask about roles or head-count to decide; roles are a field in the spec now.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else)
text: > **The rule over all five: the moment you know enough, you owe him a whole workbench — that turn.** Not a plan to build one, not the next question. **A draft he can object to beats an interview he sits through**, because reacting is cheap and specifying is expensive: he can find ten things wrong with a page in fifteen seconds and cannot produce one out of thin air. In the personal domain "enough" is the domain word; in the system domain it is three facts, bought in **at most two messages**. Any further "let me ask a few more things first" is a defect.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else)
text: **Before any of this: look for `.workbench/spec.md`.** If it exists, **read it first** — this session is a *revision*, not a new definition. No doors, no routing question, no V0: load the spec, change only the affected keys, keep `excluded` and `deferred` intact (they are the memory of decisions already made), and reissue the whole thing. **Re-running discovery on someone who already has a spec is the most annoying failure this skill can produce.** In a chat product the spec is in the conversation rather than on disk; same rule.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else)
text:
| Door | Looks like | First move |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| **Q — one or two personal words** | 「养宠物」·「记账」·「陪孩子学习」·「帮我搞个健身的」 | **A complete input, not a fragment.** Match **one** skeleton in `references/starters.md`, fill it with whatever he gave you, output the **V0** — Workbench Read plus the buildable definition — **this same turn**. No evidence questions first |
| **S — a system workbench** | 「我想做个 CRM」·「AI Agent 工作台」·「给工厂做个看板」·「电商后台」 | `references/system-domain.md`. **Two questions in two messages (see below), then the whole spec.** Already-known is never re-asked — 「我想做个 CRM，我们十个销售」 has answered two of the three, so ask only the third. All three known → assert immediately |
| **D — wants one, hasn't named a domain** | 「我想做个工作台」·「想弄个工作台，给点建议么」 | **One routing question, not an investigation.** 工作 · 学习 · 创作 · 健康 · 财务 · 家庭 · 阅读 · **客户/订单/库存这类业务 · AI 和自动化 · 一堆数据要盯着** · 别的 — plus the makeshift-tool question **marked optional**, same message. His answer routes into Q or S. Only 「我也不知道」/「你帮我定」 drops you into the Life Read (`references/discovery.md`), roughly one session in five |
| **N — a domain plus real context** | 「给我妈做个吃药提醒的，她 70 岁记性不好」·「我们十来个销售现在用飞书表格跟客户」 | Compose directly and ship the V0 that turn. Skip the search, keep every gate — a named domain is not a defined workbench |
| **A — an existing idea or product** | 「帮我看看这个设计行不行」 | `audit`, **read-only**: structure fit · data floor · the blacklist for its domain. Change nothing |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else)
text: **Door D used to route straight into evidence archaeology, and that was the single most expensive bug in this method** — it charged a round to extract one noun from someone who would have typed it unprompted. The domain question is a *router*, not a proposal: picking 「健康」 decides almost nothing (it still contains a hundred workbenches), whereas picking 「记账」 off a category menu decides the product and hands back the median one. That distinction is the whole reason one is legal and the other is banned.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else)
text: **A routing word matches no skeleton — narrow it yourself, don't hand the breadth back.** 「健康具体指哪方面呢？」 is the category menu one level down and costs the round you just saved. Assume the most common workbench in that domain (`starters.md` §2.A: 工作 → 今天做了什么 → 自动周报 · 创作 → 灵感到发布 · 阅读 → 在读/读完/划线…), build it, and state the assumption in **one clause inside the V0** — never as a preamble.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else)
text: **A starter is a category skeleton, not a species.** 「养宠物」 resolves to one skeleton that holds for 猫 · 狗 · 兔 · 异宠 alike — keep the channel names neutral (`口粮红黑榜`, not `猫粮红黑榜`) and treat the species as the cheapest personalization slot there is: **ask 「什么宠物？叫什么？」 while showing him the filled workbench, never before it.** Same for 记账 (个人 vs 摆摊), 健身 (增肌 vs 减脂) and every other starter — the branch is a fill-in, not an interview question.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else)
text: **When a domain is named but no verb: the domain test picks the track, then length picks the depth.** Personal + one or two words = Door Q (assert now). Personal + real detail about a specific person = Door N (compose, since a starter would flatten the detail he bothered to give you). System = Door S. **When in doubt between Q and N take Q: showing him something wrong fast beats asking him something slow.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else) > Door S — the two-question round, and then you stop asking
text: A system workbench genuinely can't be guessed the way 「养宠物」 can: the same word 「CRM」 covers a solo consultant's contact page and a forty-seat sales floor, and those are different products. So buy three facts, in **at most two messages**:

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else) > Door S — the two-question round, and then you stop asking
text: **Then the whole spec. No third round.** What each question buys: **主对象** derives the modules, entities and first screen — without it you build 「数据管理 · 报表中心 · 系统设置」, the three modules that mean nobody decided anything. **谁在用** decides whether `roles` is one line or four and whether the primary module is the doer's screen or the watcher's. **每天最常做** decides which module is `primary` and what the 结论条 points at.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else) > Door S — the two-question round, and then you stop asking
text: Not on that list, deliberately: 行业 · 公司规模 · 技术栈 · 竞品 · 预算. None change the spec; each costs a round. Everything else — 要不要移动端 · 要不要导出 · 权限怎么分 — is a **refinement to a spec he's looking at**, answered in three words there instead of a round here.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else) > Door S — the two-question round, and then you stop asking
text: **This is a router, not a menu.** 「围着什么转」 doesn't hand him a product, it names the noun everything derives from; 「每天最常做」 only decides what sits at the top of the first screen. **A list of workbench categories (CRM · ERP · 电商 · 医疗 · 工厂) would hand him the product**, and it returns the first row every time — that's why it stays banned even though the system domain makes it tempting.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Which door the user came in (route before anything else) > How to actually ask, in whatever host you're running in
text: The routing question and the system round are shaped like multiple choice, and not every runtime has a structured question tool. **If one exists (`AskUserQuestion` or equivalent), use it — for those two places only.** If it doesn't, **ask the identical question as plain text with the options written inline**; never degrade it into an open question (「你想做个什么样的工作台？」) because the tool is missing — the options are what make it answerable in one word. **Then STOP and wait**: do not ask and then proceed on a guessed answer, and **never treat a file on disk, a prior session, or your own inference as this turn's answer.** And **never reach for a structured question tool anywhere else** — not for 「这样对吗？」, not for confirming the spec, not for the handoff offer. Everything after the V0 is a revision to an artifact he's looking at, and polling him about it is the interview this method replaces.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Commands (targeted iteration)
text: A full run executes the workflow below. For a single complaint about an existing definition, route the request through **one verb** instead of re-running discovery — Codex has no slash commands, so map the user's intent to the verb and load only that reference.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Commands (targeted iteration)
text:
| Verb | Intent it matches | Load |
|------|-------------------|------|
| `sketch` | 「先给我看看效果」·「直接做出来我看看」 → starter → spec → straight to the builder, **labeled a starting point** | `starters.md`, `handoff.md` |
| `discover` | 「不知道做什么」 → the full flow from zero (default when no domain is named) | all |
| `define` | Domain already named. Skip the search, keep every gate | `grammar.md`, `hook-engineering.md` |
| `modules` · `channels` | 「频道太多了」·「模块该怎么切」 → re-cut the rail only | `grammar.md`, `system-domain.md` |
| `hook` | 「每天打开没啥可看的」 → rewrite the opening line and re-bind its fields. **The most common single-point fix — it's almost never the channels** | `hook-engineering.md` |
| `data` | **System.** 「这些数据从哪来」·「表里有什么字段」 → derive or repair `entities`: fields, writers, relations | `system-domain.md` |
| `pages` | **System.** 「每个模块里面到底有什么页面」 → expand modules into L1/L2/L3 | `system-domain.md` |
| `monetize` | 「这个能赚钱吗」 → find the seam in an already-stable channel set | `monetization.md` |
| `audit` | 「有人会用吗」 → **read-only** health check. Reports, never edits | `day-two.md` |
| `narrow` | Too many channels, too much daily input → cut to the spine | `grammar.md`, `day-two.md` |
| `widen` | 「太单薄了」 → add depth, **not** surface | `workbench-types.md` |
| `handoff` | Write `.workbench/spec.md` and hand it to the builder | `handoff.md` |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 1. Life Read — evidence, not wishes (**the rare branch**)
text: **Run this only when he was asked which domain and genuinely could not answer.** If he hasn't been asked yet, go back to Door D and ask — most people who open with 「我想做个个人工作台」 know exactly what they want to manage and simply haven't said it, and putting them through a life inventory costs a round and reads as an interrogation. Roughly one session in five reaches this section.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 1. Life Read — evidence, not wishes (**the rare branch**)
text: For the genuinely blank case it is worth doing well, because that user can't be routed and the evidence really does find what a menu never would.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 1. Life Read — evidence, not wishes (**the rare branch**)
text: A design brief describes a thing. **A workbench brief describes a person, and the person is the least reliable narrator available.** He says he wants to 「管理健康」; what he actually does is weigh himself and forget to write it down. The gap between the stated want and the observed behavior is where the workbench is.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 1. Life Read — evidence, not wishes (**the rare branch**)
text: Ask about **past behavior**, never about future desire. Highest-yield evidence, in order:

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 1. Life Read — evidence, not wishes (**the rare branch**)
text:
| Evidence | Why it outranks a stated need |
|---|---|
| **The makeshift tool** — a 备忘录 he keeps re-editing, an Excel, a self-chat in 微信, a 相册 used as a log | Someone already paying a daily tax with a bad tool has proven both the need and the willingness. The strongest signal in the method |
| **The abandoned attempt** — a tracker he quit in week two | The most precise datum available: it names the exact input cost that broke him. Set the new design's cost **below** it, and say the number out loud |
| **The re-googled question** | A knowledge channel with a guaranteed audience of one |
| **The resented app** — opens daily, complains about it | Category validated; only the shape is wrong |
| **The photographed thing** | A record channel already being kept, unlabeled |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 1. Life Read — evidence, not wishes (**the rare branch**)
text: **Never open with a category menu — and the ban is on the words, not the formatting: never write a domain name he didn't write first**, not as an example, not as a counter-example, not after 「比如」, and **not inside a sentence declining to offer a menu.** The polite violation is the common one — a line announcing it won't list categories, naming three of them in the parenthetical explaining why. Those three are now in his head and he often picks one. Don't explain the ban either. (The Door D routing list — 工作 · 学习 · 创作 · 健康… — is the deliberate exception, and only because picking a row there decides almost nothing.) If the evidence points at two genuinely different workbenches, name the fork — that comes from *his* answer, unlike a menu.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > The opening message has a fixed shape — copy it
text: **The first sentence is the first question**, or the one clause introducing it — no preamble, no diagnosis of his request, no account of what you're about to do. **No reasons attached to any question**; each is self-evidently purposeful read cold, and explaining what it hunts converts a question he'd answer into a lecture he'll skim. The closing line is the only self-description allowed, because it tells him what an answer buys. **Target length: this block, ±30%** — a draft at triple it is method narration, and the excess is never the questions.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > The opening message has a fixed shape — copy it
text: **Two questions, not three** — he already failed to answer one; don't respond by asking more. **The moment one answer arrives you owe him the whole V0**, that turn. A partial answer is enough to assert from, and asserting wrong gets corrected faster than asking right gets answered.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP
text: **Written in Chinese, in words the user can veto.** Structure names, dial numbers and channel-type labels are coordinates for *you* and never appear here.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP
text: Example (Door D, evidence = 备忘录 + 弃用过一个健身 App):

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP
text: Three lines carry the weight:

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP
text: - **`每天打开，你会看到：` must contain real values.** A template — `今天是{周期}第{n}天` — is unfalsifiable: he can't tell whether that number will ever be computable, so he approves it, and you find out on build day that nothing produces it. Filling in concrete values forces you to notice what the sentence requires. **If you can't fill the blanks, the hook isn't ready to show.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP
text: - **`你每天要喂它：` decides whether it survives.** State it in seconds and physical actions (「点一下完成」,「拍一张照」) — that's the number he can judge against his own morning. Hiding the cost until build time is how you get an abandoned tracker.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP
text: - **`不对的话` names two real, mutually different forks**, each one something you'd genuinely define differently. Not 「有什么想法都可以说」, which returns nothing.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP > Under it, same message: the part a builder can use
text: The Read is the ten-second veto surface; alone it can't be turned into a page, and a second round spent asking for the rest is the round this whole method exists to save.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP > Under it, same message: the part a builder can use
text: **它是给谁的 is singular, always.** A page for 一个上班族晚上到家喂猫 and one for 一个开宠物店的 don't look alike, so the field earns its place — but write a segment and the scope inflates into a product for nobody. **首页从上到下 is the one builders most often don't get**: `hook` fixes line one, and a page with only line one specified gets six identical cards under it. **None of this exempts the hook from its field binding** — a richer document makes that gate cheaper, not optional.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP > Under it, same message: the part a builder can use
text: **Then STOP and wait.** One artifact, one turn. Asserting a specific wrong workbench earns a fast, specific correction; asking a fourth question earns a fourth polite answer.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP > Under it, same message: the part a builder can use
text: **Every later message reissues this whole definition, never just answers.** He says 「其实是给我自己看的，不用给老板交」 → you don't reply 「好的，明白了」; you reissue the V0 with the 日报 channel gone and the hook rewritten, plus one line naming what moved. He should always face a single artifact getting better, never a transcript he has to assemble. That's what makes late questions safe: under a definition he can see, 「要不要手机上也能用」 is a refinement he answers in three words.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 2. Output the V0 — the Workbench Read, then the buildable definition, then STOP > Under it, same message: the part a builder can use
text: If he'd rather see a screen than read a definition (「先给我看看效果」) — that *is* the go-ahead. Go starter → spec → build, then label the result a starting point. Many people cannot evaluate a spec and can evaluate a screen instantly.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 3. Set the three dials — and run the balance rule immediately
text:
| Dial | 1–3 | 4–6 | 7–10 |
|------|-----|-----|------|
| **CADENCE** — how often it earns an open | weekly or event-driven | a few times a week | every day, at a fixed moment |
| **INPUT** — what he must feed it daily | one tap, or nothing | a number and a choice, ~20s | multi-field logging, ~2min+ |
| **DEPTH** — what it gives back beyond a reminder | a prompt an alarm could do | computed state + a next step | insight he could not produce himself |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 3. Set the three dials — and run the balance rule immediately
text: > **INPUT must be strictly below DEPTH. If `INPUT ≥ DEPTH` the workbench is already dead** — and it's dead at definition time, where fixing it is free.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 3. Set the three dials — and run the balance rule immediately
text: Every abandoned tracker is this inequality: he pays a daily tax and receives, in exchange, a display of the thing he just typed. Three legal fixes, in order: **lower INPUT** (derive, default, one-tap) → **raise DEPTH** (a trend, a comparison against his own past, a translation of jargon into a decision) → **cut the channel**. The third is the one people skip and is often right.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 4. Pick the structure, not the audience
text: Audiences are infinite and a list of them is a marketing sheet. **Structures are eleven**, and the structure decides the hook formula, the first screen's shape, the data-model skeleton, the retention mechanic, and the specific way it dies. **Two workbenches from entirely different industries that share a structure share their engineering** — that's the whole return on classifying this way.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 4. Pick the structure, not the audience
text:
| Structure | The engine | Hook shape | Dies by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **cycle** | an external rhythm the system can compute (月经周期, 孕周, 距考试, 疫苗) | 「你在第 N 天/段 → 因此今天…」 | the anchor date is never entered, so N never exists |
| **ledger** | daily entries whose value is the accumulated curve (体重, 蛋白, 记账, 背词) | 「今天 X / 目标 Y，差 Z」 | input debt — three days' gap makes the curve feel ruined and he stops |
| **state** | today's condition, no accumulation needed (睡眠, 情绪, 持仓体检) | 「昨晚/今天你是 X，所以 Y」 | it's the same X every day, so it stops being information |
| **runbook** | a prescribed sequence for today (训练计划, 刷题) | 「今天这 N 件事」 | the list is identical daily — an alarm would have done it |
| **care** | another being's state (宠物, 婴儿, 植物, 老人) | 「它/他第 N 天 · 今天该…」 | milestones only, no daily reason to open |
| **feed** | external information selected and translated (财经早报, 行业情报) | 「今天这 3 条 + 一句人话」 | generic content he could get anywhere |
| **operation** | money and stock moving (摆摊, 小店, 进销存, ERP, 电商后台) | 「今日流水 X · 库存告警 Y · 建议 Z」 | personal: the accounting costs more than a notebook. system: **the stock number is wrong from week one and then nobody trusts any number on the page** |
| **pipeline** | objects advancing through ordered stages (CRM 商机, 订单, 工单, 任务, 内容, 审批) | 「N 个待推进 · M 个卡在 X 超 K 天」 | **nobody moves the cards** — everything sits in stage 1 forever and the board is a lie |
| **registry** | a searchable catalogue of objects (客户档案, 商品库, 知识库, Skill 市场, 学员, 病历) | 「新增 N 条 · M 条缺关键信息」 | **it starts empty and stays that way**; no daily reason to open, becomes search-only |
| **console** | a fleet of running things you can intervene in (Agent, Workflow, 设备, 定时任务) | 「N 个在跑 · M 个失败 · 消耗 X」 | **the green wall** — nothing ever fails, so it stops being information |
| **monitor** | metrics with anomalies, drillable to detail (BI 看板, 工厂大屏, 运维, 持仓) | 「今日 X / 目标 Y · 异常这 N 处」 | **totals without anomalies → wallpaper**; or no drilldown, so a number raises a question the page can't answer |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 4. Pick the structure, not the audience
text: **Most real workbenches are primary + one secondary.** 养宠 = care + ledger. 增肌 = ledger + runbook. CRM = pipeline + registry. Agent 台 = console + registry. 智慧工厂 = monitor + console. 电商后台 = operation + pipeline. **The primary owns the hook and the first screen's shape**; the secondary supplies a module or two. Three structures means three workbenches — name the fork and make him pick one.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 4. Pick the structure, not the audience
text: > **`registry` and `monitor` should almost never be alone.** Both have known retention holes — an empty catalogue, a wall of totals — and both are fixed by the secondary, not by anything inside themselves.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 4. Pick the structure, not the audience
text: Also name **the moment**: 早上通勤 · 睡前 · 练完那一下 · 收摊后 · 上班坐下第一件事 · 交接班时 · 周一晨会前. It decides the hook's tense (morning = imperative 今天该做什么; evening = reflective 今天怎么样) and the input's affordable size — nobody fills a form at 23:50. **A workbench with no named moment has no cadence and gets opened out of curiosity twice** — and in a web page there's no push to buy back a weak moment.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 5. Compose the five parts — in this order
text:
| # | Part | The question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Identity** — name + who it's for | 这是谁的台子？ |
| 2 | **Daily hook** — the one sentence on open | 今天它跟我说什么？ |
| 3 | **Data floor** — the fields under that sentence | 这句话凭什么成立？ |
| 4 | **Channels** — the left rail | 我还能在这儿干什么？ |
| 5 | **Revenue seam** — where money can appear | 它靠什么活？ |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 5. Compose the five parts — in this order
text: **The order matters more than any single part.** Start at the channels — the natural instinct, because channels are the fun part — and you produce a features menu, then reverse-engineer a hook to sit on top of it. That hook will be generic, because its job was to cover a rail rather than to say something true.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 5. Compose the five parts — in this order
text: **The identity line is load-bearing.** 「小暖的姨妈工作台」 beats 「经期管理系统」 because it fixes a scope: 小暖 has one body, one cycle, one partner to brief. A 「系统」 acquires users, then roles, then settings, and the definition inflates into a product for nobody.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 5. Compose the five parts — in this order
text: **Channel mix rule:** exactly one **Today** · at least one **Record** · at least one **Review** · **Knowledge ≤ ⅓** of the rail · **4–9 total**, each with a `weight` so the builder can build hierarchy instead of a uniform list. No Record channel means no data floor. No Review channel means he's been feeding a database and will notice in week three.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6. Bind every hook to a field — the gate this skill exists for
text: **Never skipped, in any door, in either domain, for any structure.** For every hook clause, and every module claiming to show 「今天的」 anything, answer all five:

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6. Bind every hook to a field — the gate this skill exists for
text:
| | Question | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Which field does it read?** | The sentence needs data no one ever defined |
| 2 | **Who or what writes that field?** | See the four writers below — 「用户会输入」 is a *wrong* answer more often in the system domain than a missing one |
| 3 | **When does it get written?** | No moment in anyone's day where they would |
| 4 | **What does it say on day one, empty?** | A blank, a `--`, a zero-row table, or a lie |
| 5 | **On a skipped day / a disconnected source?** | It shows stale data as if it were current |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6. Bind every hook to a field — the gate this skill exists for
text: **An empty cell means the hook is not approved, no matter how good it sounds.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6. Bind every hook to a field — the gate this skill exists for
text: The **fortune-cookie test**: render the hook on **day 40, on a day nothing was logged and no job ran**. Reads the same as day 1 → it's decoration that happens to sit near the top of the page.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6. Bind every hook to a field — the gate this skill exists for
text: **A hook with no variable is banned outright**, and the system domain has its own version: **a hook made of totals.** 「今日订单 128 · GMV ¥45,600 · 转化率 3.2%」 is an accurate stat strip that says nothing to do. **A 结论条 must contain at least one clause pointing at something needing action today** — 待跟进 · 超期 · 失败 · 告警 · 缺货 · 待审. Mechanical check: for each clause ask 「看到这个数，他现在会做什么？」 If every answer is 「知道了」, rewrite before anything else matters.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6. Bind every hook to a field — the gate this skill exists for
text: **Density:** personal 1–2 varying values. System 2–4 clauses, composed as **{进度或总量，带对比} · {今天要处理的那一类，带数量} · {最严重的那一个，点名}**. The third clause — naming the single worst thing — is what separates a workbench from a report, and it's the one most often dropped.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > The four writers — the section that prevents the beautiful empty console
text: Personal workbenches have one writer and the risk is he won't bother. **System workbenches have four, and the risk is worse: everyone assumes some other party fills the field, and the answer turns out to be nobody.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > The four writers — the section that prevents the beautiful empty console
text:
| Writer | Means | Cost | Trap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | a person types or clicks it | **the most expensive thing in a spec** | Three per module across nine modules is a full-time data-entry job nobody agreed to. Count them |
| `system` | the workbench writes it as a side effect of an action already happening | free | Almost never fails. **This is the one to design toward** |
| `integration` | another system supplies it (支付回调, 模型用量, 设备上报, ERP 同步, Excel 导入) | **exists only if that integration is actually built** | The commonest lie in a system spec: 「数据从 ERP 来」 with no API, no owner, no date |
| `derived` | computed at read time (超期 = now − last_activity_at > 7d) | free | Only as real as its inputs. Derived from an unbuilt integration is fictional |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > The four writers — the section that prevents the beautiful empty console
text: **The best move in the whole system track is turning a `user` field into a `system` one by attaching it to an action he already takes.** Nobody fills in 「最后联系时间」; everybody writes a 跟进记录 after a call — so `last_activity_at` is written by the system when that record is saved, and 「3 个超 7 天没动」 becomes true for free and never goes stale. Same shape: 状态 ← 拖一次看板卡片 · 是否已发货 ← 扫码出库 · 运行结果 ← 运行本身结束时落一行.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > The four writers — the section that prevents the beautiful empty console
text: **And the rule that follows:** every `integration` field names its source and whether it exists **today**. If it doesn't, record it in `depends_on` with an `until_then`, and **the number leaves the hook.** A first screen that renders blank on launch day loses the user before anything else in the spec gets a chance to work.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > The four writers — the section that prevents the beautiful empty console
text: When a field needs input nobody will give, try **in order**: **attach it to an existing action** (above) → **derive it** (weekday → 推日; one exam date → a four-month countdown) → **ask once, not daily** (anchor dates, the monthly target, the alert threshold) → **one tap with a sensible default** → **change the hook to one the data supports.** The last is a success, not a compromise: a true smaller sentence beats a false bigger one, because the false one becomes visibly false around day four and takes his trust in the whole surface with it.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6.5 System domain — the three things a personal workbench doesn't need
text: **Without these the spec is a wish list.** A builder handed 「频道：客户管理」 has to invent the entire screen, and what he invents is nine identical tables.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6.5 System domain — the three things a personal workbench doesn't need
text: **`subject` — the noun everything revolves around.** Two CRMs, same word: `subject: 客户` is a relationship history (first screen = 最近联系过的 + 很久没联系的; core entity Customer 1-n Interaction), `subject: 商机` is a fulfillment queue (first screen = 看板 by stage; core entity Opportunity n-1 Customer). **Same industry, same word, two products.** Name it and the modules derive themselves in five slots: **总览 · 主对象本身（almost always `primary`）· 主对象的产物或历史 · 主对象的原料 · 设置**, plus at most two the third question demanded (审批 · 告警 · 对话). 5–9 total.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6.5 System domain — the three things a personal workbench doesn't need
text: **Module names carry verbs.** 「客户管理」「订单管理」「数据管理」「系统管理」 are not modules — **a noun plus 管理 is the absence of a decision.** Name the object (`客户`) and put the verbs in `does` (`查客户、看聊过什么、记一次跟进`).

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6.5 System domain — the three things a personal workbench doesn't need
text: **`roles` — a field, not a reason to refuse the job.** ≤4. Each names what it *does*, not what it *is* (「主管：周一早上看全组卡了多少单，给卡住的指派人」, not 「主管」). Exactly one carries `opens_daily: true` — the hook, the first screen and the `primary` module are built for **him**. **If two roles see the same screens, there is one role**; write one, because a login guarding nothing costs a build week and buys nothing.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6.5 System domain — the three things a personal workbench doesn't need
text: **`entities` — the data model that makes the hook real.** Each entity: fields, **the writer of each field**, relations. 4–8 entities; twenty is premature database design. **The test that makes it worth writing: point at every number in the 结论条 and find the field.** 「3 个卡在报价超 10 天」 = `count(stage='报价' AND now − last_activity_at > 10d)` — both fields present, both with writers, one of them free. **If a number can't be traced to a field, it comes out of the hook.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6.5 System domain — the three things a personal workbench doesn't need
text: **`channels[].pages` — L1/L2/L3.** L1 = the module's own screen (**and `shows` names its shape**: 表格 · 看板，列=阶段 · 卡片列表 · 时间轴 · 漏斗图), L2 = one object opened, L3 = one sub-record — **only if a genuine sub-record exists.** 设置 is L1 only; a module whose objects have no sub-records stops at L2. **Depth follows the data, not the layout.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 6.5 System domain — the three things a personal workbench doesn't need
text: **Category → structure, kept internal (never shown — it's a category menu):** CRM = pipeline+registry · Agent 控制台 = console+registry · BI/驾驶舱 = monitor · 智慧工厂/IoT = monitor+console · ERP/进销存 = operation+pipeline · 电商后台 = operation+pipeline · 项目管理 = pipeline+registry · 内容创作 = pipeline+registry · 知识库/Skill 市场 = registry+feed · 运营后台 = monitor+operation · 教务 = registry+pipeline · 医疗 = registry+pipeline · 客服工单 = pipeline · HR 招聘 = pipeline+registry · 审批 OA = pipeline · 金融持仓 = monitor+state.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 7. The care subject who can object
text: 「妈妈给孩子做的学习工作台」 is one of the most common briefs in this category, and it is **not** a variant of the pet workbench — several constraints invert:

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 7. The care subject who can object
text:
|  | 宠物 / 婴儿 | **学龄孩子 / 父母** |
|---|---|---|
| Who acts | you log **your own** actions | you'd be logging **his** behavior |
| Input tolerance | high | **low** — watching in order to log is surveillance |
| Readers | one | **two**, and the same sentence must be true and kind for both |
| Cadence | daily | **usually weekly** |
| Dies by | milestones only | **it became a supervision tool** |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 7. The care subject who can object
text: Three possible data sources, and **the third is usually the right one**: she watches and logs (almost never right) · he logs it himself (then the hook must be worth *his* while too) · **log outcomes weekly instead of process daily**.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 7. The care subject who can object
text: The hook states **progress, not deficit** —「这周读了 4 天」, never「这周有 3 天没读」. Same data; only one survives being read aloud. The record is **subject-visible by default**, and **no channel that measures him carries commerce**（「落后同龄人 30%」 converts brilliantly and is the fastest way to turn a companion into a supervisor）.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 7. The care subject who can object
text: > **The test: would you read this sentence aloud to him, in front of him?** If not, don't write it.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 7. The care subject who can object
text: Note the boundary this does *not* cross: **two readers is a writing constraint, not a permissions model.** Nobody logs in as a type of user, so it stays in scope.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 8. The revenue seam — last, and out of a channel
text: 1. **The seam grows out of an existing channel or it doesn't exist.** 暖宫贴 belongs on 疼痛急救 because that channel is already about relief; a standalone 商城 tab is an ad. Can't name the channel it attaches to → there's no seam yet, and `seam: none yet` is a fine answer.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 8. The revenue seam — last, and out of a channel
text: 2. **Never monetize a channel he opened while anxious or in pain.** 疼痛急救 mid-cramp, 宠物医院 at 2am, 情绪 on a bad day: highest conversion, highest damage — and the damage is to the daily habit the whole workbench depends on. The 年报/周报 channel is usually the honest seam: he opens it deliberately, in a good mood.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 8. The revenue seam — last, and out of a channel
text: > **In the system domain `seam: none` is usually the correct answer, and inventing one is a defect.** A CRM's revenue model is that someone paid for the CRM; a factory dashboard's is that it prevents downtime. An internal tool with an in-page 增值服务 module is the enterprise form of the pasted-on shop tab. Two exceptions: the workbench *is* the product sold to outside users (then the seam is one line — 席位 · 用量 · 模块解锁 — attached to a module), or the user buys things to do the job (采购 · 进销存 · 摆摊). **The distress rule carries over with a specific shape: the 告警 / 故障 / 事故 module carries no commerce.** 「升级到专业版可查看完整告警历史」 on an incident screen is how a tool gets ripped out after the first real incident.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: Before calling any definition done, scan `references/day-two.md`. **Two lists; run the one that matches.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: **D-list (personal) — the ways it's empty by Thursday:**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The fortune-cookie hook** — no variable, or a variable nothing produces. The #1 killer

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The encyclopedia rail** — Knowledge > ⅓ of channels. That's a 百科, and nobody opens a 百科 daily

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **Input debt** — `INPUT ≥ DEPTH`, or three channels each demanding daily logging

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **No Review channel** — nothing ever says 「你已经坚持 14 天」. Accumulation with no moment of return is just chores

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The fake Today** — a 「今日 X」 channel identical on Monday and Thursday

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The blank cold start** — day one is `--`, an empty chart, a six-field wizard, or a fabricated demo number, so he never reaches day two

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **Ten-plus channels** · **the pasted-on seam** · **a moment that doesn't exist in his actual day**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **Scope inflation** — a *personal* workbench growing roles and a settings center. **Check the domain test first: a genuine system workbench is a different domain, not scope inflation**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **Streak punishment** — never require backfill; returning after a gap must cost nothing

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **Fabricated substance** — a 科普 channel whose medical or financial content the model would invent is worse than no channel

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **Supervision creep** — see §7. The only failure that damages something outside the product, and the one most likely to look like success in week one

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: **S-list (system) — the ways it's dead on arrival:**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The demo-data lie** — the 结论条 shows `12 个待跟进`, and nothing in the spec produces a 12. **Detect by rendering the first screen against an empty database.** The #1 system killer, and it *looks* rigorous right up until launch day

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The list-page hellscape** — every module's L1 is a table with a search box. Nine modules, nine identical screens, and nowhere that states a conclusion. **The `primary` module's L1 is a board / triage list / curve / fleet of cards**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The empty back office** — `cold_start.day_1` describes the emptiness instead of naming a first action (导一份 Excel · 建第一个 Agent · 录一个客户，只要名字和电话). `registry` and `console` die here outright

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The noun module** — any name ending in 管理, any `does` without a verb

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The permission hallucination** — three roles, no module where any two differ. Merge them, or state the real difference (usually a filter)

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The unbuilt integration** — the hook depends on data from a system with no API, no owner, no date. **Record it in `depends_on` and take the number out of the hook**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The orphan module** — no relation to `subject` (公司公告 in a CRM). Cut it or record it in `deferred`

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **The symmetrical page tree** — L1/L2/L3 everywhere, including 设置

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **Roles as an org chart** — five or more roles. He's describing a company

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **No Review module** — feels optional in a company (「报表有 BI 做」) and isn't: it's what makes the workbench worth opening on a quiet day

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: - **Everything is `primary`** — the visual form of never having decided what matters

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: Then write **`.workbench/spec.md`** (schema in `references/handoff.md`): YAML frontmatter for the builder — `domain`, `purpose`, `user` (personal: one person, never a segment) or `roles` (system), `surface`, `structure`, `moment`, `dials`, `hook` **with each clause's bound field and writer**, `cold_start.day_1/day_2/day_7/re_entry`, **`home`: the first screen top to bottom**, channels with types, weights and **`does`**, **`mvp`/`later`**, **`visual`**, seam with `banned_channels`, `excluded`, `deferred` — plus Chinese prose for the human (who it's for, the evidence, one ordinary day end to end, why these modules, what was deliberately left out and why).

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: **System adds four fields, and they are not optional:** **`subject`** · **`roles`** · **`entities`** (fields + `written_by` per field + relations) · **`channels[].pages`** (L1/L2/L3 with `shows` and `actions`), plus **`depends_on`** whenever an integration isn't live yet.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: **`home` and `channels[].does` are what make the file buildable rather than merely readable.** `hook` fixes the first line; without `home` the builder invents what sits under it and invents six identical cards. A module with a name and no capability leaves its entire screen to guesswork.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: **End it with a `## 给实现方` section, every time.** `structure: console`, `type: today`, `weight: primary`, `shape: delta`, `L2`, `written_by` are this method's private enums — finesse-ui knows them, Cursor and v0 and a human contractor do not, and the decoder lives in `handoff.md`, which does not travel with the file. Plain-Chinese lines inside the spec are what make it a brief instead of a puzzle: **it's a web page, not an App, so the hook is the only thing bringing anyone back** · the hook is the top of the first screen, not a greeting strip · the empty state shows `cold_start.day_1`, never 「暂无数据」 or a fake demo row · this structure means this main display · module count decides bottom bar vs sidebar and `weight: primary` is the landing page, not one of nine equals · **build each module's pages from `pages`, and `shows` decides the shape — don't turn a 看板 into a table, and don't ship nine identical tables** · build the schema from `entities`, and `written_by: system` fields get no input control · **don't display a `depends_on` field, and don't display 0 in its place** · INPUT 6+ needs a permanent entry button. **Write only the lines this spec actually needs.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: **No filesystem — a chat product, a phone assistant — then print the whole spec in one fenced block** (frontmatter and prose together, no commentary inside the fence) and say in one line that it can be copied to any builder. Chat UIs put a copy button on code blocks; a spec split across four bubbles reaches the builder missing its frontmatter. **Never claim to have written a file you didn't.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: What the builder reads out of it: `surface` → a page in a phone browser or a desktop one · `channels[]` → the navigation, count drives the shell · `channels[].pages` → **the routes and the depth the shell must support** · `hook` → the first screen · `entities` → the tables, forms, columns and filters · **`cold_start.day_1` → the empty state** · `structure.primary` → whether the main display is a calendar, a curve, a checklist, a board, a list+detail, a fleet of cards, or figures with an anomaly list.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Mandatory workflow (execute in order) > 9. Run the blacklist for the domain, write the spec, then stop
text: > **Writing the spec is the end of this job. Building is a separate yes.** Offer the handoff in one line and wait — the user may want to sit with the definition, take it elsewhere, or build it himself. Auto-running a build off a freshly-approved definition spends his time on a decision he hasn't made.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Say it in words he can act on — and never narrate the method
text: `structure=ledger`, `CADENCE=daily`, `Record 频道`, `data floor` are internal vocabulary — they earn their place in your reasoning and none of them are answerable by the person reading. First time such a term must appear in user-facing text, follow it with a one-clause plain gloss; after that use it bare, or better, don't use it at all. **Reason in whatever vocabulary you like; write to him in his.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Say it in words he can act on — and never narrate the method
text: That governs words. This governs whole sentences, and it's the more commonly broken of the two, because the material in this file is interesting and it's the easiest thing to hand over:

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Say it in words he can act on — and never narrate the method
text: > **Everything the user reads is about his workbench. Nothing he reads is about how you got there.**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Say it in words he can act on — and never narrate the method
text:
| Banned | Why | Instead |
|---|---|---|
| Mentioning the starter library **at all, including by negation** —「没有现成的『工作日』骨架，我给你组合一个」 | Denying a list still reveals the list; he now hunts for a word that hits it instead of reacting to the workbench | Compose it and show it. A composed starter passes the same gates — there's nothing to disclose |
| Structure names, dials, channel types **anywhere he reads** —「(结构：台账为主 + 复盘为辅)」·「这天然就是个『知识频道』」 | Writing them in the sentence *above* the Workbench Read obeys the letter and loses the point | 「主要是攒记录，顺带每周回看一次」·「每次都能翻回来的固定栏目」 |
| Reciting a rule of this method —「录入 30 秒，回报是一份周报，这样才活得过第二周」·「菜单只会让你随手点第一行」 | That's the ruleset read aloud to the person it protects. Competent-sounding, useless to him | Apply it silently; if it needs defending, defend it in his terms:「记多了你一周就烦了，所以我只要一句话」 |

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Say it in words he can act on — and never narrate the method
text: Two exceptions, both narrow: state a **consequence** he must judge (「录入我压在你崩掉的那个阈值以下」 — that's about his week), and **label a `sketch` output** as a starting point (a status, not a rationale). The test: delete the sentence — is his workbench any worse defined? No → it was for you.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Out of scope
text: - **The interface** — that's the UI skill's job (the designed handoff above)

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Out of scope
text: - **The engineering** — storage, sync, auth implementation, model choice, deployment, how an integration actually gets built. **The spec names an integration as a dependency; it does not design it**

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Out of scope
text: - **A real multi-tenant commercial product** — 计费、租户隔离、合规、SLA、销售流程、路线图. **Roles are in scope; a company's product strategy is not.** This defines one workbench thoroughly; it does not do product management for a SaaS business

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Out of scope
text: - **Clinical, financial or legal substance.** This decides that a 妇科科普 or 持仓体检 or 用药提醒 module should exist and what it must show. **It does not supply the content and must not invent it** — name the module, then say plainly where real content has to come from

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Out of scope
text: **Two things that used to be out of scope and no longer are:** *multiple roles* (「销售看自己的，主管看全组」 is `roles` plus per-module differences, not a refusal) and *enterprise categories* (CRM, ERP, 工厂, 医疗, 教育 are `pipeline`/`operation`/`monitor`/`registry` workbenches on the system track). What still isn't in scope is the *business* around them.

head: finesse-brief — Agent Instructions > Out of scope
text: **One boundary that hasn't moved:** a 妈妈给孩子做的学习工作台 has two people looking at it and stays **personal** — one owner, one domain, one moment, one hook, no page tree, nobody logging in as a *type*. **Two readers of one surface is a writing problem, not an architecture one.**

head: racers-portable — agent notes
text: Cross-platform port (SDL3) of the [LEGO Racers decompilation](https://github.com/isledecomp/racers), modeled on [isle-portable](https://github.com/isledecomp/isle-portable). Windows/Linux/macOS today; emscripten deferred.

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Ground rules
text: - **The decompilation is the source of truth.** `LEGORacers/`, `GolDP/`, `common/` and `util/` come from the upstream decomp (git remote `racers`) and must stay mergeable: keep reccmp annotations (`// FUNCTION:`, `// GLOBAL:`, …) intact and do not rename or reorganize decomp code here.

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Ground rules
text: - **Upstream-first policy.** Any change the original 32-bit binary could still byte-match (type modeling, renames, restructuring) is made in the decomp repo first — verified there with a full reccmp report diff — and arrives here by merge/rebase. Only genuine portability work is made directly in this repo.

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Ground rules
text: - **Keep the touched-file surface tiny.** Rewritten app boundary: `LEGORacers/src/app/main.cpp`, `win32golapp.cpp`, `LEGORacers/src/video/` (player, AVI demuxer). Everything else in decomp directories should compile unmodified against the `miniwin/` headers; pointer-width fixes are a few lines each and tagged `// 64-bit compatibility:`. Platform hooks in decomp-adjacent code are tagged `// [library:xxx]` (window, filesystem, synchronization, input, audio, 2d, 3d, video, config).

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Ground rules
text: - All platform work lives in `miniwin/` (DirectDraw/D3D6-IM, DirectSound, DirectInput 5 and a small Win32 surface over SDL3 + miniaudio) and `3rdparty/` (vendored FFmpeg n4.4.4 Indeo 5 decoder behind a minimal shim; `Indeo5_Open/Decode/Close`).

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Ground rules
text: - `clang-format` everything you touch (CI-enforced; the vendored FFmpeg sources under `3rdparty/ffmpeg-indeo5/` except the wrapper are exempt and must stay byte-unmodified).

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Building
text: `DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES=ON` (default) fetches SDL3 at a pinned release; with it OFF, a system SDL3 is found via `find_package`. A game installation (LEGO.JAM, `*.TUN`, Indeo 5 `*.AVI`) is required to run: `./build/LEGORacers --path <gamedir>`.

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Testing aids (environment variables)
text: - `RACERS_AUTOKEY="ms:scancode[:holdMs],..."` — scripted key injection (SDL scancodes; Alt/Ctrl/Shift chord state is tracked).

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Testing aids (environment variables)
text: - `RACERS_TOUCH=1` — mouse-as-finger testing: SDL mouse→touch synthesis feeds the touch layer so drag-steering/buttons/taps work without a touchscreen (touch-synthesized menu clicks are suppressed for these fingers to avoid doubling the real mouse).

head: racers-portable — agent notes > Testing aids (environment variables)

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Project Overview
text: Phantom Fragment is a high-performance container alternative using Linux kernel features (namespaces, seccomp, Landlock, cgroups). Codebase: Primarily Rust with Zig for low-level components (zygote pool, memory management).

text: **UI Module:** Standardized output functions in `ui.rs` (info!, success!, error!, warn!, dimmed!).

text: **IO Utils:** Shared file I/O in `io_utils.rs` for tail_file, follow_file operations.

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Key Patterns
text: **Graceful Degradation:** Security features fall back silently if unsupported.

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Key Patterns
text: **FFI Pattern:** Zig exports C ABI, Rust links via `extern "C"`.

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture
text: Phantom Fragment supports three distinct execution tiers, from standard cold start to optimized sub-millisecond warm starts:

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 1: Cold Start (Default)
text: - **Command**: `phantom run alpine <cmd>`

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 1: Cold Start (Default)
text: - **Mechanism**: Standard fork/exec with fresh process

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 1: Cold Start (Default)
text: - **Performance**: ~45ms startup time

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 1: Cold Start (Default)
text: - **Use Case**: Default, works reliably on all systems

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 1: Cold Start (Default)
text: - **Status**: ✅ **Production Ready**

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 2: Warm Fragments / Mother Fragments
text: - **Command**: `phantom warm fragment create alpine 3` then `phantom run --warm alpine <cmd>`

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 2: Warm Fragments / Mother Fragments
text: - **Mechanism**: Pre-warmed daemon processes ("mother fragments") that stay alive and fork on demand

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 2: Warm Fragments / Mother Fragments
text: - **Performance**: Faster than cold start (avoids image setup overhead)

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 2: Warm Fragments / Mother Fragments
text: - **Use Case**: When you need faster startup than cold, without pre-fork complexity

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 2: Warm Fragments / Mother Fragments
text: - **Status**: 🚧 **Beta/Experimental** - Currently has significant limitations (daemon stability, IPC issues)

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 3: Zygote Pool (Fastest)
text: - **Command**: Currently `phantom warm --benchmark` (for testing); future: integrated with run command

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 3: Zygote Pool (Fastest)
text: - **Mechanism**: Pre-forked processes via Zig zygote pool using clone3/vfork syscalls

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 3: Zygote Pool (Fastest)
text: - **Performance**: Sub-millisecond (<1ms) target

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 3: Zygote Pool (Fastest)
text: - **Use Case**: High-frequency execution, serverless workloads, maximum performance

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Tier 3: Zygote Pool (Fastest)
text: - **Status**: 🚧 **Partial** - Low-level implementation complete, not yet integrated with run command

text:
| Tier | Command | Status | Performance |
|------|---------|--------|-------------|
| **Cold** | `phantom run alpine` | ✅ Working | ~45ms |
| **Warm** | `phantom run --warm alpine` | 🚧 Beta/Experimental | Unreliable, may fall back to cold |
| **Zygote** | `phantom warm --benchmark` | 🚧 Benchmark only | <1ms (in benchmarks) |

head: AGENTS.md - Phantom Fragment Development Guide > Three-Tier Execution Architecture > Current Implementation Status
text: **Note**: The zygote pool (Tier 3) exists as a low-level Zig implementation but is not yet connected to the `phantom run` command. The warm fragment daemon (Tier 2) is in beta/experimental status with significant limitations.

text: This is an public repository.

head: Project Context > Language Guidelines
text:
* **Code & Documentation:** All code comments, documentation (README, JSDoc), variable names, and commit messages **must be written in English**, regardless of the language used in the conversation.
  * **Conversation:** When explaining concepts or replying to the user, **use the language the user is speaking** (e.g., if the user speaks Japanese, reply in Japanese).

head: Project Context > TypeScript Coding Standards
text: Adhere to a strict **Functional Programming** paradigm.

head: Project Context > TypeScript Coding Standards > 1\. Immutability & Safety
text:
* **No `let` or `var`:** Use `const` for all variable declarations.
  * **No `any`:** Strict type safety is required.
  * **No `null`:** Avoid using `null`. Use optional properties (`?`) or `undefined` instead.
  * **No Type Assertions:** Avoid using `as` to force types. Rely on type narrowing, type guards, and proper inference.

head: Project Context > TypeScript Coding Standards > 2\. Data Structures & Abstractions
text:
* **Use `type`:** Prefer `type` aliases over `interface` definitions.
  * **No Classes:** Do not use `class`. Use pure functions and data structures.
  * **Higher-Order Functions:** Utilize higher-order functions (map, filter, reduce, etc.) and composition instead of imperative loops or stateful logic.

head: Project Context: Lineage 2 API > Current Data Model > Key Decisions
text:
- `ItemDetailDto` shape:
  - common fields stay top-level (`id`, `name`, `weight`, `price`,
    `material`, `iconFile`)
  - type-specific fields are grouped: `category?`, `stats?`, `shots?`,
    `timing?`, `flags?`, `crystal?`
  - groups are omitted entirely when no inner key applies
  - `null` is reserved for the four always-emitted top-level fields;
    everything else is omit-when-absent

head: Project Context: Lineage 2 API > Current Data Model > Key Decisions
text:
- `NpcDetailDto` / `MonsterDetailDto` shape:
  - vitals + reward + combat + movement live under `stats`
  - six base attributes (str/dex/con/int/wit/men) live under `baseStats`
  - AI fields (`aggroRange`, optional `assistRange`) live under
    optional `behavior?`; the group is omitted entirely on the few
    NPCs without an `<ai>` block
  - `isAggressive` stays top-level for parity with `NpcListDto`
  - `skills[]` is always emitted; `title`/`race`/etc. are omitted when
    the source value is null

head: Project Context: Lineage 2 API > Current Data Model > Key Decisions
text:
- Quests:
  - `QuestDetailDto` does not surface `scriptFile` (Java path is an
    implementation detail)
  - `questItems[]` uses `QuestItemRefDto` with no `count` — engine list
    registers item ids only; a placeholder count would be a lie
  - `rewards.adena?` / `exp?` / `sp?` are optional; absent ≠ zero
  - `clientJournalEntries?` is the in-game quest log text, not a
    mechanically-derived walkthrough; trailing `\n` markers are
    trimmed at the DTO layer, internal markers preserved verbatim

head: Project Context: Lineage 2 API > Current Data Model > Key Decisions
text:
- Hennas:
  - mechanics fields (`statChanges`, `engravePrice`, `dyeItem`,
    `allowedClassIds`) always populated from `hennas.xml`
  - `engravePrice` (not `price`) is the Symbol Maker's engrave cost,
    distinct from the dye item's own vendor `ItemDetailDto.price`
  - display fields (`displayName`, `iconFile`, `shortLabel`) are
    honestly `null` for the 9 Greater II symbols (172–180) whose DAT
    record uses an unsupported shared-prefix encoding

head: Project Context: Lineage 2 API > Current Data Model > Key Decisions
text:
- Locations:
  - resolved by 2D nearest-anchor with a 10000-unit threshold, not
    polygon containment (`huntingzone-e.dat` carries center anchors
    only)
  - public DTO normalizes whitespace (trim + collapse internal runs);
    raw endpoints surface source spelling
  - a small audit-justified override map (`PRIMARY_LOCATION_OVERRIDES_BY_NPC_ID`

    detail's `primaryLocation?` for verified heuristic failures

head: CopilotKit
text: AI agent framework with three layers: **Frontend** (React/Angular/Vanilla) → **Runtime** (Express/Hono) → **Agent** (LangGraph/CrewAI/BuiltIn/Custom), communicating via the AG-UI protocol (event-based SSE).

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **Nx monorepo** — run workspace tasks through `nx` (`nx run`, `nx run-many`, `nx affected`). **Dashboard exception:** `showcase/shell-dashboard` is deliberately outside the workspace and has no Nx targets. Use its [standalone verification instructions](showcase/shell-dashboard/README.md#verification) instead of the general Nx rule. Do not add it to the workspace or change its lockfile to make an Nx command work.

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **Flat package structure** — All packages live under `packages/` with the `@copilotkit/` scope. Dual-version packages keep deprecated implementation code under `src/v1-deprecated/`, route the package root through `src/v1-deprecated-compatibility.ts`, and keep current code under `src/v2/`. These remain one published package; the deprecated source directory is not a public subpath.

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **Simplicity** — prefer the simplest correct solution. For non-trivial changes, consider if there's a cleaner approach before committing.

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **No changesets** — releases are conventional-commit-driven (`scripts/release/` reads commit subjects). This repo migrated off Changesets; never create `.changeset/*` files — nothing consumes them and CI fails on them. Describe the change in the commit subject instead, and leave `package.json` versions and `CHANGELOG.md` files to the release tooling.

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **Worktrees** — always work in a git worktree for isolation. See [Git & PRs](.claude/docs/git.md) for the full workflow.

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **Always start from fresh remote main** — at the start of every new task, before creating any branch or worktree, and before running `nx affected` or any base-sensitive comparison, run `git fetch origin main`. Create new work from `origin/main`, never from the local `main` ref. Local `main` may be arbitrarily stale and must not be used as an affected base. For an existing branch, compare against the fetched merge base explicitly (for example, `BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` followed by `nx affected --base="$BASE" --head=HEAD`).

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **Commit as you go** — every meaningful unit of work gets its own commit, pushed immediately. Don't let untracked files accumulate across a session. Tests belong in the commit that introduces the code being tested. Full rules in [Git & PRs](.claude/docs/git.md#commit-early-and-often-in-logical-chunks).

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **Documentation lives in shell-docs** — author CopilotKit docs in `showcase/shell-docs/src/content/`. The top-level `docs/` path is only a symlink to `showcase/shell-docs/`; never recreate the old `docs/content/docs/` tree for live documentation. AG-UI protocol docs are authored upstream in `ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui`, not directly in this repo. See [Documentation](.claude/docs/documentation.md).

head: CopilotKit > Essentials
text: - **Inspector UI work** — follow `skills/inspector-workbench/SKILL.md`. Start the standalone workbench and take screenshots after each visual change. Pane add/rename/remove also uses `skills/inspector-docs/SKILL.md`.

text: Individual developers may optionally create a `private-agents.md` file at the repo root. This file is gitignored and not shared with the team -- it contains personal agent instructions, workflow overrides, or context that applies only to that developer's work. If `private-agents.md` exists, read it and follow its instructions (they take precedence over the defaults in this file where they conflict).

head: AGENTS.md - z-shell/F-Sy-H > Repository contract
text:
F-Sy-H is a Zsh 5.8+ interactive syntax-highlighting plugin consumed directly
from Git. It is class 3, git-consumed source: `main` is both the integration
branch and the stable consumable branch. Version tags mark reviewed snapshots;
do not add release automation or a package-registry workflow.

head: AGENTS.md - z-shell/F-Sy-H > Repository contract

head: AGENTS.md - z-shell/F-Sy-H > Plugin boundaries
text:
The portable contract follows version 2 of the
[Zsh Plugin Standard](https://wiki.zshell.dev/community/zsh_plugin_standard).
`F-Sy-H.plugin.zsh` is the only entrypoint. Direct sourcing and conventional
plugin managers must work without manager-owned registries or capabilities.
Zi is the reference manager for documentation and validation, not a runtime
requirement.

head: Current Product Requirements
text: - This repository is a multi-user web product that calls Hermes Agent on behalf of hosted users. Treat every user prompt as untrusted input.

head: Current Product Requirements
text: - The current MVP uses one app-managed Hermes gateway with Hermes' official Docker terminal backend. Keep the boundary simple: Hermes must run with its own `HERMES_HOME`, temp, cache, and generated state under `.data/hermes-runtime` or `/opt/data`.

head: Current Product Requirements
text: - Hermes filesystem/process access is a product boundary, not a prompt instruction. Hosted/API Hermes may expose built-in `terminal` and `file` only when `terminal.backend=docker`, `docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace=false`, `docker_volumes=[]`, `docker_forward_env=[]`, and `container_persistent=false`.

head: Current Product Requirements
text: - The Docker socket may be mounted only into the trusted Hermes service so Hermes can create its official tool sandbox containers. Do not mount `/var/run/docker.sock` into `web`, do not expose Docker CLI/API as a user tool, and do not let prompts pass raw Docker API payloads or arbitrary host bind mounts.

head: Current Product Requirements
text: - Users must not be able to make Hermes or sandbox task containers inspect or modify VPS host files, operator home files, `.env` secrets, other users' uploads, other users' generated files, or the app repository unless that exact path was deliberately granted for the task.

head: Current Product Requirements
text: - User uploads/private files stay outside Hermes by default. If a task needs files, copy or grant only the minimum scoped files into a per-run sandbox workspace and clean temporary/generated files by lifecycle policy.

head: Current Product Requirements
text: - Hermes browser availability depends on the Hermes `agent-browser/local` provider. Plain Playwright installation or passing Playwright tests does not prove the Hermes browser tool is available.

head: Current Product Requirements
text: - Configure Hermes to use happyclaw `gpt-5.5` as the primary model with output token cap `4096`. OpenRouter `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` is the fallback model and should keep `provider_routing.only/order: [deepseek]` when OpenRouter is active.
