head: Repository guidelines > Project purpose
text:
roomform parses point cloud indoor scans into structured,
editable scenes: room boundaries (walls, floors, ceilings —
inferred through occlusion) + objects out.

head: Repository guidelines > Project purpose
text: The pipeline spine is four contracts (docs/data-contracts.md):

head: Repository guidelines > Project purpose
text:
The contracts ARE the architecture. Code changes happen behind them;
contract changes get an entry in the migration log in the same change.

head: Repository guidelines > Project purpose
text:
Keep this repo simple and readable. It is the public face of a larger
internal research effort — bring over the smallest working idea, not
the ceremony around it.

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text: The package lives in `roomform/roomform/` (no `src/` layout).

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text:
- `contracts/` owns the pydantic documents. Everything downstream
  consumes only these.

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text:
- `pipe/` owns the stages: `evidence/` (voxelize + channels),
  `lifting/` (SpatialLM boxes), `reconstruction/` (SAM 3D meshes),
  `fuse.py` (scene assembly + QA), `e2e.py` (the parallel driver).

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text:
- `model/` owns the ONE architecture (patch-graph ConvFormer). There
  is never a second copy of it anywhere in the repo.

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text:
- `inference/` owns running the model: `local.py` is canonical;
  `modal_app.py` is a thin remote shell over exactly the same code.
  All Modal stages go through `modal_adapter.StageApp` — never write a
  bespoke Modal app per stage.

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text: - `agent/` owns the multi-provider LLM harness.

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text:
- `export.py` owns artifacts -> display geometry (scene GLB +
  per-object mesh GLBs for the editor). `eval.py` owns the metrics.

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text:
- `viewer/` (top level, outside the wheel) owns the web viewers and
  their dev servers.

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text:
- `research/` owns training and experiments (not part of the pip
  package; nothing in `roomform/` may import from it). Its working
  rules live in `research/AGENTS.md`.

head: Repository guidelines > Project shape
text:
Outputs: pipeline results go to `artifacts/` (gitignored), weights to
`checkpoints/` (gitignored), secrets to `.env` (gitignored).

head: Repository guidelines > Hard rules
text:
- The evidence channel construction in `pipe/evidence/raw.py` is the
  training-time construction, ported verbatim. Do not "improve" its
  math (dedup, normalization, channel order) — any change silently
  breaks every existing checkpoint.

head: Repository guidelines > Hard rules
text:
- `EDGE_OFFSETS` order in `model/convformer.py` is a serialized
  contract (lexicographic forward half of the 26-neighborhood). Never
  reorder it.

head: Repository guidelines > Hard rules
text:
- Model outputs are a tuple; consume `outputs[:2]` for (node, edge)
  unless you know the checkpoint's optional heads.

head: Repository guidelines > Hard rules
text:
- Inline imports only for truly optional paid-service deps
  (`fal_client`). Everything else imports at module top.

head: Repository guidelines > Hard rules
text:
- Never orphan a spawned Modal app: keep the client context alive
  until `.get()` returns.

head: Repository guidelines > Development commands
text:
Credentials: `uv run modal setup` for lifting; `FAL_KEY` in `.env` for
live SAM 3D.

head: Repository guidelines > Coding style
text:
Target Python 3.11. Ruff enforces line length 79, import sorting, and
the configured lint set — run format + check before handing off.

head: Repository guidelines > Coding style
text:
Use `from __future__ import annotations`. Keep pydantic models and
helpers small; prefer plain functions and obvious control flow over
frameworks, registries, and fallback machinery. Module docstrings
state what the module owns and its usage line; comments state
constraints the code can't show, not narration.

head: Repository guidelines > Coding style
text: Commit messages: imperative subject, short body explaining the why.

head: Repository guidelines > Testing
text:
Add or update tests when behavior changes; keep them fast and free of
paid calls (no live Modal/FAL in tests). `tests/test_parity.py` is the
gate that matters — if you touch the model, config, or checkpoint
format, it must still pass unmodified checkpoints.

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 1. **Attr Reader Pattern for Immutable Data**
text: Models expose data through `attr_reader` attributes that are initialized in the constructor. Unlike PHP's readonly properties, Ruby uses instance variables with attr_reader:

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 1. **Attr Reader Pattern for Immutable Data**
text: - Instance variables are set in the constructor

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 1. **Attr Reader Pattern for Immutable Data**
text: - Use `attr_reader` to expose them

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 1. **Attr Reader Pattern for Immutable Data**
text: - Models and records are initialized from hash data (from JSON/DB)

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 1. **Attr Reader Pattern for Immutable Data**
text: - Records are composed objects (City contains City record, Location record, etc.)

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: Models follow clear inheritance patterns:

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: - `Country` → base model with country/continent data

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: - `City` extends `Country` → adds city, location, postal, subdivisions

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: - `Insights` extends `City` → adds additional web service fields (web service only)

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: - `Enterprise` extends `City` → adds enterprise-specific fields

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: Records have similar patterns:

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: - `Abstract` → base with `get` method for accessing hash data

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: - `Place` extends `Abstract` → adds names/locales handling

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 2. **Inheritance Hierarchies**
text: - Specific records (`City`, `Country`, etc.) extend `Place` or `Abstract`

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 3. **Get Method Pattern for Data Access**
text: Both models and records use a protected `get` method to safely access hash data:

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 3. **Get Method Pattern for Data Access**
text: - Returns `false` for missing boolean fields (starting with `is_`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 3. **Get Method Pattern for Data Access**
text: - Returns `nil` for missing optional fields

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 3. **Get Method Pattern for Data Access**
text: - Records store the raw hash in `@record` instance variable

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 3. **Get Method Pattern for Data Access**
text: Public methods expose data through the `get` method:

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 4. **Lazy Parsing for Special Types**
text: Some fields require parsing and are computed lazily:

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 4. **Lazy Parsing for Special Types**
text: - Use `defined?(@variable)` to check if already parsed

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 4. **Lazy Parsing for Special Types**
text: - Parse only once and cache in instance variable

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 4. **Lazy Parsing for Special Types**
text: - Handle nil cases before parsing

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 4. **Lazy Parsing for Special Types**
text: - Memoize nil results too, so repeated calls do not re-run the lookup

head: CLAUDE.md > Code Architecture > Key Design Patterns > 5. **Web Service Only vs Database Models**
text: Some models are only used by web services and do **not** need MaxMind DB support:

text: **Web Service Only Models**:

head: CLAUDE.md > Working with This Codebase > Adding New Fields to Existing Models
text: For database models (like AnonymousPlus):

head: CLAUDE.md > Working with This Codebase > Adding New Fields to Existing Models
text:
1. **Add a public method** that calls `get`:
   ```ruby
   # A description of the field.
   #
   # @return [Type, nil]
   def field_name
     get('field_name')
   end
   ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Working with This Codebase > Adding New Fields to Existing Models
text:
2. **For fields requiring parsing** (dates, complex types), use lazy loading:
   ```ruby
   def network_last_seen
     return @network_last_seen if defined?(@network_last_seen)

     date_string = get('network_last_seen')

     if !date_string
       @network_last_seen = nil
       return nil
     end

     @network_last_seen = Date.parse(date_string)
   end
   ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Working with This Codebase > Adding New Fields to Existing Models
text: For composed models (like City, Country):

head: CLAUDE.md > Working with This Codebase > Adding New Fields to Existing Models
text:

   ```ruby
   attr_reader :new_field
   ```

2. **Initialize in constructor**:

   ```ruby
   def initialize(record, locales)
     super
     @new_field = record['new_field']
   end
   ```

head: Night Errand Runner — CLAUDE.md > What This App Is
text: A night errand delivery web app for Novi Beograd, Belgrade, Serbia. A solo driver runs errands after midnight — pharmacy items, food, drinks, forgotten things — anything from anywhere that's open. Customers order via a mobile-first web app. Driver receives push, accepts, delivers. Customers get real-time status updates so they never have to call.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > What this is
text:
lgtv2mqtt is an MQTT interface ("bridge"/"adapter") for LG webOS smart TVs. It talks to
the TV via the [lgtv2](https://github.com/hobbyquaker/lgtv2) library (SSAP over
websocket, `wss://<tv>:3001` on current firmware, `ws://<tv>:3000` on pre-2018 TVs) and to
an MQTT broker, publishing TV state and accepting commands over MQTT, and announces the TV to
Home Assistant via MQTT discovery.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > What this is
text:
It is one of many `xyz2mqtt` adapters by the same author (lgsb2mqtt, airtunes2mqtt,
bravia2mqtt, hue2mqtt.js, hm2mqtt.js, ...). All follow the
[mqtt-smarthome](https://github.com/mqtt-smarthome/mqtt-smarthome) architecture.
Consistency with that convention and with the sibling adapters is a hard requirement — see
ROADMAP.md for the ongoing modernization/unification effort (the fleet-wide plan lives in
the lgsb2mqtt ROADMAP). lgsb2mqtt 1.0 and lgtv2mqtt 2.0 share the same layout (config, topics,
discovery, install); keep them aligned. When in doubt, prefer the fleet-wide standard over a
local quick fix.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > MQTT conventions (mqtt-smarthome)
text:
Topic structure is `<name>/<function>/<item>`, `<name>` is the instance name (default
`lgtv`, CLI option `--name`):

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > MQTT conventions (mqtt-smarthome)
text:
- `<name>/connected` — retained integer, published via LWT and on state changes:
  `0` = not connected to MQTT, `1` = MQTT but no TV, `2` = MQTT and TV (paired).

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > MQTT conventions (mqtt-smarthome)
text:
- `<name>/status/<item>` — retained state reports, friendly snake_case items (`power`,
  `volume`, `mute`, `sound_output`, `input`, `input_list`, `app`, `app_list`, `channel`,
  `channel_name`, `play_state`, `screen`, `model`, `firmware`, `mac`). `{val, ts, lc}` JSON by
  default, plain values with `--no-json-payloads`. Lists are JSON arrays.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > MQTT conventions (mqtt-smarthome)
text:
- `<name>/set/<item>` — commands, same item names plus set-only items (`volume_up`, `media`,
  `toast`, `button`, `text`, ...). Plain values; `{"val": ...}` JSON is accepted too.
  `<name>/set/<service>/<method>` is a raw SSAP passthrough, **off by default** (`--raw-set`).

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > MQTT conventions (mqtt-smarthome)
text: - `<name>/info` — retained JSON about the running instance.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > MQTT conventions (mqtt-smarthome)
text:
QoS 0 everywhere. Do not rename topics outside of a major release (see ROADMAP.md);
the 1.x → 2.0 migration table is in CHANGELOG.md.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text:
- `index.js` — `createAdapter()` from the core (MQTT, connected, info, maintenance, discovery
  publishing, shutdown) plus the TV part: set dispatch, TV subscriptions (volume,
  sound output, foreground app → input, media play state, power state, current channel while
  live TV is active), device info fetch on connect, discovery (re)publishing, shutdown.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text:
- `lib/commands.js` — `commandFor(item, value, state)`: pure mapping of `set/<item>` to a
  TV action (`request`/`button`/`pointer`/`wake`/`toast`). Extend here for new set items.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text:
- `lib/hadiscovery.js` — `discoveryModel()` builds the device block + entity map (core
  `entity()` helpers) from the last known status values (`input_list`, `app_list`, `model`, ... trigger a
  re-publish via `DISCOVERY_TRIGGERS` in index.js).

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text:
- `parsePayload`, `toBoolean`, `toVolume`, `StatusTracker`, the logger, the MQTT/connected/info/
  maintenance/shutdown wiring and the systemd template come from **mqtt-interfaces-core**
  (`../../mqtt-interfaces-core` when checked out next to this repo). Generic fixes go there.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text: - `lib/toast.js` — `set/toast` payload builder, loads `icon` from URL/file as base64.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text:
- `lib/install.js` — core `createInstaller()` for `lgtv2mqtt@<name>` plus `copyPairingKey()`
  (state dir `/var/lib/lgtv2mqtt/<name>` = `LGTV2_KEY_DIR`). Root-only parts are not unit tested.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text:
- `config.js` — adapter options (`OPTIONS`) on top of the core `parseConfig()`; every option also
  via `LGTV2MQTT_*` env vars. Exports camelCased (`config.mqttUrl`, `config.haDiscovery`).

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text: - `test/` — node:test unit tests (`npm test`) for every `lib/` module.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text:
- `scripts/e2e.sh` — manual end-to-end smoke test against lgtv2's mock TV (needs `../../lgtv2`
  checked out with dev deps) and a throwaway mosquitto container.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Code layout (ES modules, node >= 20.19)
text:
- The TV protocol lives in lgtv2 (`../lgtv2` when checked out next to this repo). Fix

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Style & practices
text:
- Plain JavaScript ES modules, no build step. 4-space indentation, semicolons,
  eslint + prettier (`npm run lint`, `npm run format`). **Let a failing lint stop you** —
  never pipe it through `tail`.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Style & practices
text: - Keep dependencies minimal; this runs on small always-on machines.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Style & practices
text: - Never make default config values point at personal infrastructure.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Style & practices
text:
- Log at `debug` with the `mqtt >`/`mqtt <`/`tv >`/`tv <` prefix style. An unreachable TV is
  `warn`, not `error`.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Style & practices
text:
- All TV requests go through `request()` (promise API of lgtv2); errors are logged, never
  allowed to crash the process.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Running
text:
First start: accept the pairing prompt on the TV; the key (and the learned MAC addresses)
are stored in `~/.lgtv2/` (or `LGTV2_KEY_DIR`, `/data` in the Docker image,
`/var/lib/lgtv2mqtt/<name>` for systemd instances).

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Known weak spots
text:
- Payload shapes differ between firmware versions; lgtv2 normalizes the known ones, but always
  guard `res` and check `err` in subscription callbacks (`subscribe()` helper in index.js).

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Known weak spots
text:
- A TV in deep standby does not answer at all; `status/power` is set to `off` on socket
  close and only Wake-on-LAN (`set/power true`) brings it back.

head: Agent instructions — lgtv2mqtt > Known weak spots
text:
- `set/screen` uses `turnOffScreen {standbyMode: 'active'}` as Home Assistant does; not
  verified on every firmware. `play_state`, `sound_output`, `input_list`, `app_list` come from
  endpoints the mock TV does not implement — verify on a real TV after changes.

text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > 项目概述
text: Singcast 是一个基于 [sing-box](https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box) 的轻量级代理内核。同时接受 **Clash Meta (Mihomo) YAML** 和 **sing-box JSON** 两种配置格式——运行时自动将 Clash 配置翻译为 sing-box 格式，统一由 sing-box 引擎执行。Go module 路径为 `github.com/mapleafgo/singcast`。

head: CLAUDE.md > 构建与测试
text: 构建系统使用 [Task](https://taskfile.dev)。所有构建和测试都需要 Go build tags: `with_clash_api,with_utls,with_quic,with_gvisor`（**不可省略**，sing-box 大量使用条件编译，缺少会编译失败）。

head: CLAUDE.md > 构建与测试
text:
运行单个测试或包：
```bash
go test -tags 'with_clash_api,with_utls,with_quic,with_gvisor' ./translator/...
go test -tags 'with_clash_api,with_utls,with_quic,with_gvisor' -run TestTranslateDNS ./translator/
```

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 三个入口
text: 1. **CLI** (`cmd/singcast/`) — `singcast run|convert|check|version`，使用 `urfave/cli/v3`。`run` 命令直接调用 `core.Service.StartWithContent`。

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 三个入口
text: 2. **桌面端 FFI** (`cmd/lib/`) — 通过 `cgo` 导出 C 共享库（`.so`/`.dylib`/`.dll`）。导出 `Core*` 系列函数包装 `core.Service`。内存所有权：返回的 `char*` 必须由调用方通过 `CoreFreeString` 释放。事件回调使用所有权转移模式（native 分配，消费者复制后释放）。

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 三个入口
text: 3. **移动端 SDK** (`mobile/`) — `gomobile bind` 目标，产出 AAR (Android) 和 xcframework (iOS)。`Singcast` 结构体包装 `core.Service`，增加移动端特有功能：TUN fd 注入、socket protector（VPN 绕过）、网络接口上报。

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 核心层 (`core/`)
text: `Service` 是核心运行时，状态机：`Created → Initialized → Starting → Running → Destroyed`。通过 `atomic` 状态 + CAS 循环实现线程安全。

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 核心层 (`core/`)
text: - `StartWithContent(content, ruleSetProxy)` — 检测格式，必要时翻译 YAML，创建 sing-box 实例

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 核心层 (`core/`)
text: - 移动端强制设置 `auto_detect_interface=true`，用于 VPN socket 保护

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 核心层 (`core/`)
text: - 状态变更通过统一回调发出事件（`EventStateChange`）

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 核心层 (`core/`)
text: - Clash API 服务提供流量跟踪、代理组、连接管理和模式切换

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 翻译器将 Mihomo YAML → sing-box JSON，在 `Convert()`/`ConvertWithMeta()` 统一入口中按 10 步流水线执行：

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 1. 格式检测 (`detect.go`) — 先尝试 JSON 解析，失败则为 YAML

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 2. 全局配置 → inbounds (`general.go`) — mixed/HTTP/SOCKS/redir/tproxy 端口、认证、sniffer

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 3. 代理节点 → outbounds (`proxy.go` + `translator/proxy/`) — 每种协议一个翻译器，位于 `proxy/` 子目录

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 4. 代理组 → outbounds (`group.go`) — Selector、URLTest、Fallback

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 5. 规则 → 路由规则 (`rule.go`) — GEOIP/GEOSITE 转为 rule_set 引用

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 6. DNS (`dns.go`) — nameservers、fallback、FakeIP、hosts

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 7. TUN (`tun.go`) — TUN 接口配置

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 8. 实验性功能 (`experimental.go`) — clash_api、cache

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 9. 组装 (`assemble.go`) — 注入内置规则、默认路由、将 REJECT 转为 route action、rule_set 定义

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 10. 校验 (`validation.go`) — 验证 outbound/route 引用是否存在

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 翻译器层 (`translator/`)
text: 核心数据类型：`RawConfig`（Mihomo YAML 结构，`types_mihomo.go`）、`singboxConfig`/`singboxRoute`/`singboxDNS`（sing-box 输出，`types_singbox.go`）、`translation`（流水线状态累积器）。

head: CLAUDE.md > 架构 > 平台层 (`core/platform.go`)
text: `PlatformIO` 提供移动端 I/O：socket protector 回调、TUN fd 存储、接口监控、WiFi 状态。桌面端为空操作。

head: CLAUDE.md > 关键约定
text: - sing-box 选项结构统一使用 `map[string]any`（非类型化结构体），保持灵活性

head: CLAUDE.md > 关键约定
text: - 翻译器返回 `(jsonString, warnings, error)` — warnings 是非致命问题，调用方应展示给用户

head: CLAUDE.md > 关键约定
text: - `RawConfig` 中的 YAML 字段名遵循 Mihomo 惯例（如 `mixed-port`、`socks-port`）

head: CLAUDE.md > 关键约定
text: - 协议翻译器位于 `translator/proxy/`，每个协议一个文件

head: CLAUDE.md > 关键约定
text: - 测试文件与源码同目录（如 `dns.go` + `dns_test.go`）

head: CLAUDE.md > 关键约定
text: - build tags `with_clash_api,with_utls,with_quic,with_gvisor` 在构建和测试中都必须指定

head: Working Agreement > Repository Memory
text: - Async LLM completions propagate through the full call chain: `LLM.acompletion()`/`LLM.aresponses()` → `_atransport_call()` (litellm `acompletion`/`aresponses`) → `RetryMixin.retry_decorator()` (tenacity `retry`, which wraps coroutines natively — there is no separate async retry path) → condenser `acondense()` → `Agent.astep()` → `LocalConversation.arun()` → `EventService.run()`. Every async method has a sync counterpart; base classes provide default delegations to sync so custom subclasses work without changes.   - Do NOT add comments that restate what the code already says, summarize the surrounding diff/PR, or narrate the change history ("previously we did X, now we do Y"). That kind of context belongs in the PR description or commit message, not in the source — `git blame` and the PR are the source of truth for *why* a change was made.

head: Agent Temporary Directory Convention
text: - **`RemoteConversation._wait_for_run_completion` and stop hooks**: Per-field WebSocket `FINISHED` status events are *hints*, not authoritative termination. The server-side `LocalConversation.run` loop releases its state lock at the end of each iteration, so a `FINISHED` status set by `agent.step()` is visible to clients before the *next* loop iteration runs stop hooks (`hook_processor.run_stop`). If a stop hook returns rc=2 (denying the stop), status flips back to RUNNING and the agent gets another iteration. The client's `_wait_for_run_completion` therefore must **not** return on the first WS-delivered FINISHED. Instead, post-run full-state WebSocket snapshots are authoritative; if that snapshot is missing, the time-based hard-fallback path (`TERMINAL_HARD_FALLBACK_SECS = 30.0`) accepts REST-confirmed terminal status after 30 continuous seconds. ERROR/STUCK still raise immediately through `_handle_conversation_status`. Empirically this caused agents to consume just 0–1 iterations after a hook block on programbench retry-16; fix shipped in `feat/programbench`.

head: Agent Temporary Directory Convention
text:
- **Hook events vs `state.events`**: `HookExecutionEvent` is emitted via `hook_processor.original_callback` (the chained `_on_event`), so it *should* land in `state.events` when the run is allowed to complete. But because the WS-FINISHED race above used to make the client snapshot `list(conversation.state.events)` *before* the server-side hook eval ran, `output.jsonl` history could miss hook events while on-disk persisted events under `/workspace/conversations/.../events/` had them — useful as a forensic signal that the race fired.
</KNOWN_RACES_AND_GOTCHAS>

head: Working on Token-Saver
text:
Token-Saver is a Python 3.10+ CLI-output compressor, with Claude Code and
Antigravity adapters and a Jekyll documentation site. Compression runs locally
and deterministically, without an LLM or network call in the compression path.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Read the relevant instructions
text:
This file applies to the repository. A nested `AGENTS.md` adds guidance for its
directory; read it before editing there. `CLAUDE.md` describes plugin behavior
and shell exclusions. Keep those guarantees consistent with code and tests.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Python style
text:
Use the [Google Python Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html)
as the review standard; `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents project tooling and exceptions.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Python style
text:
- Format Python to 80 columns. Preserve literal fixture data when wrapping would
  change its meaning; justify any narrow exception rather than disabling a rule.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Python style
text:
- Import modules by absolute package names and qualify their members. Typing
  symbols from `typing`, `typing_extensions`, and `collections.abc` are exempt.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Python style
text:
- Write meaningful Google-style docstrings for public interfaces and nontrivial
  behavior. Describe relevant `Args`, `Returns`/`Yields`, `Raises`, and public
  `Attributes`; do not mechanically restate signatures or test names.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Python style
text:
- Keep comprehensions simple: one `for` clause and at most one filter. Use loops
  for nested traversal and preserve processing order.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Python style
text:
- Catch specific exceptions. A broad catch requires an explicit isolation
  boundary or re-raise; record suppressed failures without commands, captured
  output, secrets, exception text, or traceback locals.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Python style
text:
- Include the repository's Apache 2.0 header in Python files. Preserve
  third-party copyright and license notices, including `.pylintrc`.
  Explain unavoidable local suppressions beside the relevant code.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Design and compatibility
text:
- Keep parsing/compression, orchestration, persistence, CLI presentation, and
  platform integration separate. Prefer small interfaces and injected
  dependencies where a real boundary exists; avoid abstract wrappers that add
  no behavior or independent test seam.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Design and compatibility
text:
- Extend the processor contract for a new command family instead of adding
  command-specific branches to the engine or platform hooks.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Design and compatibility
text:
- Preserve public CLI behavior, processor extension points, return shapes, and
  installed-tree imports during refactors. New `src` subpackages need explicit
  packaging and installer coverage; current copying discovers top-level source
  modules and processor modules.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Design and compatibility
text:
- Preserve failure details and secret redaction ahead of compression ratios.
  A redacted result must never be replaced by its unredacted input merely
  because a size threshold was not met.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Design and compatibility
text:
- Follow the existing Python 3.10 syntax and standard-library runtime approach.
  Use explicit UTF-8 for text files and text subprocess output.

head: Working on Token-Saver > Validation
text:
Run targeted tests while iterating. Before finishing changes to runtime code,
run the applicable repository checks (the CI workflow is authoritative):

head: Working on Token-Saver > Validation
Working on Token-Saver > Validation
text:
Use temporary homes/data directories for installer, tracker, and config tests.
Do not run installation, update, or uninstall commands against the developer's
real profile just to validate a change. A normal `benchmark` and the wrapper's
`--dry-run` execute their supplied command; use harmless fixture commands.
CLI `benchmark --dry-run` only inspects routing, and `benchmark --stdin` uses
already captured output without executing the command.

- Configuration defaults: `src/config.py` and the README's **Complete Parameter

- Releases: `src/__init__.py` is the version source. Synchronize both Claude

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Project overview
text: CLI tool for multi-criteria statistical comparison of GitHub repositories. Combines GitHub REST API data with local git clone analysis, scores each repo across ~10 criteria, and writes ranked results to a CSV file.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Tech stack
text: - **Language:** Go 1.26.3

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Tech stack
text: - **Module:** `github.com/fedir/ghstat`

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Tech stack
text: - **Dependencies:** `github.com/tidwall/gjson`, `github.com/joho/godotenv`

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Tech stack
text: - **CI/CD:** GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`)

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Tech stack
text: - **Releases:** GoReleaser — triggered automatically on `v*` tags; publishes binaries and Homebrew formula to `fedir/homebrew-tap`

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Authentication
text: Copy `.env.sample` to `.env` and set your token:

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Authentication
text: The token needs `repo` scope. The app loads `.env` automatically on startup. A shell environment variable takes precedence over `.env`.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Environment variables
text:
| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `GH_TOKEN` | — | GitHub personal access token (required) |
| `GH_HTTP_TIMEOUT` | `30` | HTTP request timeout in seconds |
| `GH_STATS_MAX_RETRIES` | `5` | Max retries when GitHub returns 202 (computing stats) |
| `GH_STATS_RETRY_INTERVAL` | `10` | Seconds between retries for 202 responses |

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Hybrid analysis
text: Each repository is analysed from two sources, merged into one record:

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Hybrid analysis
text:
| Data | Source | Why |
|------|--------|-----|
| Stars, forks, open issues, license | GitHub API | Real-time metadata |
| Author, location, followers | GitHub API | User profile data |
| Closed issues, tags, contributors | GitHub API | GitHub-specific concepts |
| **TotalCommits, Additions, Deletions** | **Local git** | `git rev-list` / `git log --numstat` — authoritative |
| **MediumCommitSize** | **Local git** | Derived from above |
| **AverageContributionPeriod** | **Local git** | Per-author first/last commit date span |
| **ReturningContributors** | **Local git** | Authors active in >4 distinct ISO weeks |
| **CommitsByDay** | **Local git** | More accurate commit count / repo age |

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Hybrid analysis
text: On first run, each repo is fully cloned to `tmp/projects/<owner>_<repo>/`. On subsequent runs the clone is updated (`git fetch origin` + `git reset --hard origin/HEAD`). If the clone fails, API data is kept as-is.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Output
text: - `-f` is required — no default output path

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Output
text: - `stats/` is created automatically if missing

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Output
text: - Results are written as CSV; headers come from `header` struct tags on `Repository`

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > HTTP cache
text: Responses cached under `-t` folder (default `test_data/`), keyed by SHA-256 of the URL. Cache is permanent until cleared with `make cache-clear` or `-cc`. Error responses (403/404) are not cached. The `stats/contributors` endpoint returns 202 when GitHub is computing stats; for all other endpoints the client retries up to `GH_STATS_MAX_RETRIES` times with `GH_STATS_RETRY_INTERVAL` second delays. For `stats/contributors` specifically, 202 is treated as empty (local git provides authoritative contributor data anyway). Local git stats always override the API result when available, so 202-forever repos are handled correctly.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Versioning and releases
text: Tags must follow strict semver: `vX.Y.Z` (e.g. `v0.9.0`). Do **not** use `v.X.Y.Z` — the leading dot breaks GoReleaser's semver parser. Previous tags before v0.8.0 used the wrong format; all new tags must use the correct one.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Versioning and releases
text:
To release:
```bash
git tag v0.9.0 && git push origin v0.9.0
```
GitHub Actions picks up the tag and GoReleaser publishes binaries + Homebrew formula automatically. No local goreleaser install needed.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Conventional commits
text: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `ci:`, `docs:`, `test:` — **single-line messages only**. No bullet lists, no multi-line body, no `Co-Authored-By` trailer. One line, under 72 chars, imperative mood. Example: `feat: add CNCF rating script with 404 robustness fixes`.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Lessons learned > Clone cache and `-t` flag for new scripts
text: New `bin/*.sh` scripts must pass `-t tmp` explicitly. Without it the tool defaults to `test_data/` which has no clones for new repo sets. The tool exits after writing only the repos whose clones finished before the others — producing a truncated CSV with no error message. Always verify row count after a run: `wc -l stats/*.csv`.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Lessons learned > test_data/projects disk usage
text: `test_data/projects/` accumulates full git clones and can grow to 60GB+. Use `make clean-data-<category>` to remove specific sets, or `make clean-data-all` to wipe everything. CNCF and Rust crates use `tmp/projects/` (via `-t tmp`); all other scripts use `test_data/projects/` (default).

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Lessons learned > 404 and 403 responses must not crash the tool
text: `httpcache` returns `[]byte{}` on 404 and 403. All JSON unmarshal callers must guard against empty input — use `if len(jsonResponse) == 0 { return }` before unmarshaling. Slice indexing on unmarshaled results (`commits[0]`, `commits[len-1]`) must also guard against empty slices. `log.Fatal`/`log.Fatalf` in fetch paths kills the entire batch — use `log.Printf` and return zero values instead.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Lessons learned > Ghost rows from failed fetches
text: When a GitHub API call fails silently (network error, 404, rate limit), `data.go` still sends a zero-value `Repository{}` to the channel. A filter in `ghstat.go` removes any repo with an empty `Name` before ranking and CSV write, and logs `WARNING: failed to fetch data for <repo>` so you can identify which repos are broken.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Lessons learned > `--ranking-by-age` flag
text: Age is excluded from the overall score by default (`none`). Use `newest-better` to restore the original behavior (rewards younger projects) or `oldest-better` to reward proven longevity. Excluding age prevents newly created projects from outranking mature, more active ones on the overall placement.

head: ghstat — Agent & Developer Guide > Lessons learned > GitHub search API rate limit (403) with large batches
text: The `/search/issues` endpoint has a stricter rate limit than the main API (~30 req/min). Running 50+ repos in parallel exhausts it immediately. The tool now logs and skips gracefully instead of fatally crashing. Closed issue counts will be 0 for repos that hit this limit — re-run later with a smaller batch or add a sleep between search calls.

head: AGENTS.md
text:
This file provides repository-specific instructions for coding agents working on Paimon C++.
For contributor-facing setup and the complete coding conventions, also read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [`docs/code-style.md`](docs/code-style.md).

head: AGENTS.md > Scope
text: These instructions apply to the entire repository. More deeply nested `AGENTS.md` files, if added later, may provide additional or more specific instructions for their directory trees.

head: AGENTS.md > Scope
text: Keep the requested scope exact. Do not include unrelated refactors, formatting changes, API redesigns, dependency updates, or generated files in a focused change.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `include/paimon/`: public C++ API headers.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `src/paimon/`: core implementation and most unit tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `test/inte/`: end-to-end integration tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `benchmark/`: benchmarks and benchmark-specific tests.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `examples/`: example programs.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `docs/` and `apidoc/`: user documentation and API documentation.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `cmake_modules/` and `build_support/`: CMake helpers and build infrastructure.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `ci/`: scripts used by continuous integration.

text: - `test/test_data/`: checked-in test fixtures.

text: - `third_party/`: third-party sources and patches.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: - `build/`, `build-release/`, and `output/`: generated or local build output.

head: AGENTS.md > Repository Layout
text: Do not edit `third_party/`, checked-in fixtures, generated output, or Git LFS objects unless the task explicitly requires it. Never add files from local build directories to a change.

head: AGENTS.md > Working Rules
text: 1. Inspect the current implementation, nearby tests, and relevant CMake target before editing.

head: AGENTS.md > Working Rules
text: 2. Search for an existing helper or established pattern before adding a new abstraction.

head: AGENTS.md > Working Rules
text: 3. Preserve user changes and untracked local files. Do not discard, overwrite, or reformat unrelated work.

head: AGENTS.md > Working Rules
text: 4. Prefer the smallest change that fully implements or fixes the requested behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Working Rules
text: 5. Add or update a focused regression test for behavior changes when practical.

head: AGENTS.md > Working Rules
text: 6. Do not claim a build or test passed unless the corresponding command completed successfully.

head: AGENTS.md > Working Rules
text: 7. Do not commit, push, amend commits, or create a pull request unless explicitly requested.

head: AGENTS.md > Working Rules
text: When changing a public API, check the declaration under `include/paimon/`, its implementation, symbol visibility, documentation, callers, and tests together.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: The full rules are in [`docs/code-style.md`](docs/code-style.md). In particular:

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Use C++17; do not introduce C++20 or later features.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Use `Status` and `Result<T>` for fallible operations. Do not use exceptions for production error propagation.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Propagate errors with the project macros, including `PAIMON_RETURN_NOT_OK` and `PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE`.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Use an explicit type, not `auto`, as the declaration in `PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE` and `PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE_FROM_ARROW`.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Prefer `std::unique_ptr` for sole ownership and use `std::shared_ptr` only for genuine shared ownership.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Use `static Create()` plus a private constructor when object initialization can fail.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Mark new public API symbols with `PAIMON_EXPORT`.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Reuse helpers under `src/paimon/common/utils/` instead of duplicating utility code.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Follow `.clang-format`; do not manually restyle unrelated code.

head: AGENTS.md > C++ Requirements
text: - Add the repository's Apache 2.0 license header to every new source or documentation file.

head: AGENTS.md > Build and Test
text: Use an existing configured build directory when it is compatible with the change. To configure a new debug build with tests:

head: AGENTS.md > Build and Test
text: Start with the narrowest relevant validation:

head: AGENTS.md > Build and Test
text: Then broaden validation in proportion to the change:

head: AGENTS.md > Build and Test
text: For changes to build configuration, public APIs, shared infrastructure, or cross-module behavior, run the relevant wider test suite. The CI-equivalent build entry point is `ci/scripts/build_paimon.sh`; it may rebuild all dependencies and take substantially longer than a focused local target.

head: AGENTS.md > Build and Test
text: If a required check cannot be run because of missing dependencies, unsupported hardware, or time constraints, report exactly what was and was not run.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Use GoogleTest and name test files `*_test.cpp`.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Place unit tests next to the corresponding implementation unless an existing target establishes another location.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Extend an existing test target when appropriate instead of creating a new executable for one small test.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Test externally observable behavior and failure cases; avoid coupling tests to incidental implementation details.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Use existing test utilities and temporary-directory helpers. Do not write tests that depend on developer-specific absolute paths.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Keep fixtures deterministic and small. Do not rewrite existing fixture data unless the task explicitly calls for it.

head: AGENTS.md > Testing Conventions
text: - Use `ASSERT_*` when later assertions depend on the condition succeeding.

head: AGENTS.md > Delivery
text: Before handing off a change:

head: AGENTS.md > Delivery
text: 1. Review `git diff` for accidental or unrelated edits.

head: AGENTS.md > Delivery
text: 2. Run `git diff --check`.

head: AGENTS.md > Delivery
text: 3. Run the narrowest relevant build and test, plus any wider checks justified by the risk.

head: AGENTS.md > Delivery
text: 4. Summarize the changed behavior and list the exact validation commands that ran.

head: AGENTS.md > Delivery
text: 5. Call out skipped validation, remaining risks, or follow-up work explicitly.

head: AGENTS.md > Delivery
text: 6. When explicitly asked to commit, follow the Conventional Commits requirements in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages-and-pull-request-titles).

head: AGENTS.md > Delivery
text: 7. When explicitly asked to open a pull request, follow [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages-and-pull-request-titles), use a Conventional Commits title, and complete every applicable section of [`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).

head: pi-project-workflows
text: **Aim — working substrate, not substrate management.** Substrate management is not the aim or purpose of this project. Working substrate is. A defect surfaced through this repo's own substrate is triaged to its tool-level cause and fixed in the tooling; managing this substrate's own items is a means, never the deliverable.

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context
text: The currently-active substrate is whatever `.pi-context.json`'s `contextDir` field names (the active-substrate pointer) — read it to establish which substrate is active. Do NOT assume the active substrate; confirm the resolved `contextDir` with the user before any read or write. Derive current project state (position, open work, recent history) from the active substrate itself — `contextState('.')` / `/context status` (below) plus `git log` — never from a stored narrative.

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context
text: Substrates can be switched (like switching git branches). Switching flips the active-substrate pointer in `.pi-context.json`; subsequent reads/writes target the newly-active substrate. Switch via the gated `context-switch` op (never the raw `flipBootstrapPointer` library call — the op routes through the seeded ceremony path):

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context
text: Replace `<target-substrate-dir>` with the substrate to activate (from the `listSubstrates` output above), e.g. `.context` or `.context-jit-spec-v2`. Default mode flips to an existing substrate (requires its `config.json` present); `--create_new true` bootstraps a fresh substrate at `--target_dir` AND flips in one operation; `--to_previous true` flips back to the pointer's `previous_contextDir` (`--target_dir` ignored). The op is auth-gated; the `--writer` identity is stamped on the switch.

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context > Commands
text: The operator `pi-context` CLI you dogfood with IS this working tree's code, installed by `npm run promote:cli` (`scripts/promote-cli.mjs`) as a publish-free packed COPY into the global npm prefix — NOT an `npm link` into the repo (which a `npm run build`'s `rm -rf dist` would clobber) and NOT the published registry release (stale). After editing/building any package, `npm run promote:all` refreshes ALL the globally installed packed copies so every running surface stays current with the working tree (automatic on any commit touching `packages/` via the `.husky/post-commit` hook); `promote:cli` remains the CLI-only subset, and a `release:*` run promotes automatically as its final step. Details: `packages/pi-context-cli/README.md`.

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context > Current status — derive it, never cache it
text: **Verify, don't narrate (binding).** Never assert any substrate / project / file / code-behavior fact from working memory or recollection — read it from its source (the relevant `pi-context` CLI op, `git`, the actual file) at the moment you claim it, and report what the read returns, not what you remember. State recalled across turns or a context compaction is stale by default; a remembered claim is not a verified one. This is the read-don't-recall complement to derive-don't-cache above.

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context > Canonical implementation pipeline (every code change, including in-loop fixes)
text: 0. **Milestone gate (the `milestone-validity-gate` convention in `.context`, binding):** before a milestone's first task enters the pipeline, a fresh agent strictly validates ALL member filed text (anchors, mechanisms, cross-member coherence, testability, provenance) against current code, and findings are corrected via provenance-gated grants first.

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context > Canonical implementation pipeline (every code change, including in-loop fixes)
text: 1. **Implement — explore → plan → agent.** Enter plan mode; investigate *exclusively* via Explore agents (the orchestrator never greps as investigation); resolve the approach into a written plan; approve via ExitPlanMode; a foreground coding subagent implements from the approved plan. The orchestrator never hand-writes source. Pre-step: clean git baseline; file the resolved plan into the substrate (TASK/FGAP/DEC) — decomposing a feature into tasks per the canonical `feature-decomposition` convention in `.context` (composed verbatim into decomposition work; do not decompose ad hoc); set the task in-progress; branch off the porcelain-clean integration branch (per `feature-branch-workflow`).

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context > Canonical implementation pipeline (every code change, including in-loop fixes)
text: 2. **Verify — runtime demo + adversarial probe.** Real end-to-end invocation (not a mocked assertion) plus a fresh-context adversarial probe that independently re-derives. Tests-pass is necessary, not sufficient.

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context > Canonical implementation pipeline (every code change, including in-loop fixes)
text: 3. **Iterate to zero — in terms of the SUCCESS CRITERIA.** The task's filed `acceptance_criteria` are the contract and the terminating condition: when every criterion is verified true and the deterministic gate is green, iterate-to-zero is satisfied — even if the audit's total findings are nonzero. **No infinite adversary:** an audit TESTS the criteria; it does not define them. Every finding maps to a criterion id — a finding that FALSIFIES a criterion re-enters this same pipeline through explore → plan → approve → agent, scoped to the finding's whole **class** (Explore enumerates the class; fix the class, not the one symptom); a finding that falsifies NO criterion is FILED (per Experience-Gap Handling / explore-before-file) and is not fixed in this task. Filed findings stay owed — filing is not burial, so criteria-anchored termination is not scope reduction.

head: How to establish exact current context for this project using pi-context > Canonical implementation pipeline (every code change, including in-loop fixes)

head: Mercury — building and running a local copy
text:
Mercury is a terminal harness for software development. This file covers a copy
of the source — build, run, check, report a problem — not the internals. The
repository is https://github.com/Whq02/MercuryCLI; README.md is its front door
and docs/README.md lists every page by task.

head: Mercury — building and running a local copy > Prerequisites
text:
A release install needs `git` only — the archive carries its own Node runtime.
Building from source needs Node `>=24.20.0 <25` (`.node-version` pins the patch
the archives vendor; below 24.20.0 a headless run that dispatched a tool aborts
at exit on Windows), bun 1.3.x (the build runtime, never vendored), and `git`.
On Windows, run PowerShell 7 inside Windows Terminal or the VS Code integrated terminal.

head: Mercury — building and running a local copy > Build and run
text:
The cockpit needs a real TTY, with no minimum terminal size. The full layout
starts at 100 columns and 26 rows; smaller windows use the compact layout.

head: Mercury — building and running a local copy > Build and run
text:
`setup` fetches the vendored packs (pyright · debugpy · js-debug · grammars ·
this machine's Node runtime · brush, the optional shell engine) and, with cargo
present, builds the voice capture addon and, with cmake beside it, the
on-device transcriber; with cargo it also builds the desktop driver addon
that computer use runs through, and a skipped pack is named by the health check.

head: Mercury — building and running a local copy > Build and run
text:
The first run walks theme and sign-in. Every interactive boot with no explicit
journey lands on the Boot face — the ten-row card: New Session,
Continue Last Session (once history exists), Boot Menu, MCPs & Skills, Agents,
Health Check, Saturn Scheduler, Logins, Session Concourse,
Sessions · Projects. How the screens connect and the flags that shape a boot are
[docs/SESSIONS.md](docs/SESSIONS.md); `node dist/mercury.mjs --help` lists the
headless verbs. Windows runs `node dist\mercury.mjs` directly; the guide is
[docs/INSTALL-WINDOWS-FROM-SOURCE.md](docs/INSTALL-WINDOWS-FROM-SOURCE.md).

head: Mercury — building and running a local copy > The launcher and the config home
text:
Configuration and sessions live in the config home: `~/.mercury`, or whatever
`MERCURY_CONFIG_DIR` names; the build never writes there. To make a build your
daily `mercury`, `scripts/ops/deploy-runtime.sh` publishes a clean-tree build to a
fresh `<config-home>/runtime/builds/<build>` folder behind the `runtime/current`
pointer (`runtime/dist` is the same link) and `scripts/ops/deploy-launcher.sh` installs the
launcher at `<config-home>/bin/mercury` — put that directory on your `PATH`;
`mercury --version` checks it. The launcher runs `MERCURY_NODE`, else the
vendored `vendor/node` beside the build, else a PATH node, and fails loudly
when none is there. A release install (README.md, Install) uses `mercury
install` and `mercury update` instead; neither touches sessions.

head: Mercury — building and running a local copy > Checks
text:
Run the suite nearest your change while iterating; `bun run verify` closes,
and its exit status is the verdict. A suite run by hand gets a fresh scratch
config home unless MERCURY_CONFIG_DIR names one; the operator's ~/.mercury is
never a proof's home. `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`
turns on the committed pre-push guard; the build never sets it.
BUILD-NOTES.md covers the build itself.

head: Mercury — building and running a local copy > Reporting a problem
text:
Inside Mercury, `/bug <what happened>` shows the exact report and files it
through your own signed-in `gh`; by hand, README.md ("Reporting a problem")
names the issue templates and what to paste. A security problem goes through
the repository's Security tab ([SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)), never an issue.

head: Workspace Conventions > Environment Variables

head: Workspace Conventions > Environment Variables

head: Overview
text:
This is a Nix flake that provides opinionated packages and Home Manager modules
for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, Crush, llmfit,
llmserve, ccusage, Claude Code UI, Vibe Kanban). All agents are configured with yolo/auto-approve mode by
default. Shared "skills" (domain knowledge documents) are distributed to every
agent.

text:
Note: `just build` defaults to a subset of packages. To build packages not in
that list (e.g. `playwright-cli`, `vibe-kanban`), use `nix build .#<name>`.

head: Overview > Architecture > Home Manager Modules (`home-manager/`)

head: Overview > Architecture > Skills (`skills/`)
text:
Shared domain knowledge documents installed into every agent's skills directory.
Each skill has a `SKILL.md` entry point and supporting markdown files.

head: Overview > Architecture > Automatic Updates (`.github/workflows/update.yml`)
text:
Runs 3× daily via cron. Executes `just update` which checks GitHub releases for
newer versions, updates package files with `nix-update`, commits, pushes, and
pushes built results to a Cachix binary cache.

head: Overview > Architecture > Global Agent Instructions (`home-manager/global-agents.md`)
text: A shared instructions file deployed as the top-level agent prompt for Claude Code (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`), Codex (`~/.codex/AGENTS.md`), and Gemini CLI (`~/.gemini/GEMINI.md`). Controlled via `coding-agents.agentsMdPath` option.

head: Overview > Architecture > Notes
text: - If you update or add a package, don't forget to update README.md too!

head: Overview > Architecture > Notes
text: - CRITICAL: `home-manager/pi-coding-agent/extensions` and `~/.pi/agent/extensions` are the same files via symlink. If you edit Pi extensions through `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, you are editing this repo.

head: Overview > Architecture > Notes
text: - Pi extension changes do not require applying the NixOS/Home Manager configuration because the extension directory is symlinked. Use Pi's `/reload` or start a new Pi process to load extension changes. Only apply the configuration when package or module changes must be activated.

head: Overview > Architecture > Notes
text: - `packages/pi-agent/` and `packages/emdash.nix` exist but are not wired into `flake.nix`.

head: Overview > Architecture > Notes
text: - `vibe-kanban` and `playwright-cli` are packages only (no Home Manager module).

head: CLAUDE.md > What Is This Project?
text: **Grafana Lens** is an OpenClaw extension that gives the AI agent **full, native access to Grafana** — for data visualization, monitoring, alerting, and delivery across 15+ messaging channels. Product spec: `/Users/mangquanshi/workspace/grafana/grafana-lens.md`.

head: CLAUDE.md > What Is This Project?
text: **Core philosophy: Everything is an agent tool.** 17 composable tools (query, query logs, query traces, create dashboard, update dashboard, alert, annotate, share, explore datasources, list metrics, search, get dashboard, check alerts, push metrics, explain metric, security check, investigate). No background automation — agent decides when to use Grafana; Grafana's own engines handle scheduled evaluation and rendering. Works with ANY Grafana datasource, not just `openclaw_lens_*` metrics.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture: Self-Contained Plugin
text: All Grafana interaction is handled by the bundled `GrafanaClient` — no external tools or MCP servers required.

head: CLAUDE.md > Key Design Decisions
text:
| Decision | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| Repo location | Standalone npm package | OpenClaw community model — `openclaw plugins install` |
| Grafana API calls | Bundled GrafanaClient (self-contained) | No external dependencies — no MCP servers |
| Everything is tools | 9 agent tools, no background automation | Agent decides when to act; Grafana handles scheduled evaluation |
| General-purpose | Works with ANY datasource/metric | Not limited to `openclaw_lens_*` metrics |
| Alerting | Grafana-native alert rules | Leverages Grafana's mature alerting engine, contact points, silences |
| Panel rendering | Grafana Image Renderer (not local Vega-Lite) | Keeps dashboards persistent + renderable; graceful fallback: image → snapshot → deep link |
| Image delivery | `MEDIA:<path>` + `{type: "image", data, mimeType}` in AgentToolResult | `imageResult()` not exported from plugin-sdk — construct manually. `MEDIA:` triggers attachment via `splitMediaFromOutput()` in `openclaw/src/media/parse.ts` |
| Render endpoint | `GET /render/d/{uid}?viewPanel={panelId}&kiosk=true` | NOT `/render/d-solo/` — verified from Grafana Image Renderer docs |
| Dashboard templates | 4 AI observability + 5 generic variable-based JSON files | All use `templating.list` for dropdown selectors; AI templates have log-to-trace correlation |
| Alert rule provenance | `X-Disable-Provenance` header on creation | Agent-created rules remain editable in Grafana UI |
| Config DX | Env var fallback: `GRAFANA_URL` + `GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` | Follows Grafana community conventions |
| Multi-instance | Named instances via `grafana.instances[]` array, optional `instance` param on tools | Conditional: param only visible when >1 instance configured; smart default to first/named instance |
| Metrics transport | OTLP HTTP push (`@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics`) | Aligns with LGTM stack; no scrape delay; immediate data availability |
| Extension pattern | Follows diagnostics-otel exactly | Proven pattern, same Plugin SDK |

head: CLAUDE.md > Agent Tools
text:
| Tool | What It Does | When Agent Uses It |
|------|-------------|-------------------|
| `grafana_create_dashboard` | Create dashboard from template or custom JSON spec. AI templates: llm-command-center, session-explorer, cost-intelligence, tool-performance | "Create a dashboard for X" / "Set up monitoring" |
| `grafana_update_dashboard` | Add/remove/update panels or change dashboard metadata | "Add a panel to my dashboard" |
| `grafana_query` | Run PromQL instant/range queries against any Prometheus datasource | "What's my token usage today?" |
| `grafana_query_logs` | Run LogQL queries against any Loki datasource | "Find error logs in the last hour" |
| `grafana_create_alert` | Create Grafana-native alert rules with PromQL conditions | "Alert me if daily cost > $5" |
| `grafana_share_dashboard` | Render panels as PNG → MEDIA: delivery to messaging channels | "Show me a chart of my costs" |
| `grafana_annotate` | Create/query annotations on dashboards | "Mark that deployment on my dashboard" |
| `grafana_explore_datasources` | Discover datasources configured in Grafana | "What data sources do I have?" |
| `grafana_list_metrics` | Discover available metrics from any Prometheus datasource | "What metrics are available?" |
| `grafana_search` | Search existing dashboards by title/tag | "Do I have a cost dashboard?" |
| `grafana_get_dashboard` | Get compact dashboard summary (panels, queries, datasources) | "What panels are on my overview?" |
| `grafana_check_alerts` | Check, acknowledge, or set up Grafana alert webhook notifications | "Are there any alerts firing?" |
| `grafana_push_metrics` | Push custom data (calendar, git, fitness, finance) via OTLP | "Track my daily steps in Grafana" |
| `grafana_explain_metric` | Get metric context: current value, trend, stats, metadata | "What does this metric mean?" / "Why did my bill spike?" |
| `grafana_security_check` | Run 6 parallel security checks, return threat assessment (green/yellow/red) | "Am I being attacked?" / "Security status" / "Security audit" |
| `grafana_query_traces` | Run TraceQL queries against Tempo — search traces or get full trace by ID | "Find slow traces" / "Show trace for session X" / "Debug distributed spans" |
| `grafana_investigate` | Multi-signal investigation triage — metrics, logs, traces, context in parallel with hypothesis generation | "Investigate this alert" / "What's wrong?" / "Triage" / "Root cause" |

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Fact IDs: one `:refer` per namespace, or use `:id`
text:
A fact's id is derived from its `:refer` metadata (`fact-id` in
`code.test.base.runtime`). **Two facts in the same namespace with the same
`:refer` collide: the later one overwrites the earlier one in the registry,
and the earlier fact never runs** — the suite still reports green, just with
fewer checks. `install-fact` now prints a `WARNING code.test: fact ... will
NOT run` line at load time when this happens; never let those warnings stand
in a namespace you own (many pre-existing ones remain elsewhere in the tree).

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Fact IDs: one `:refer` per namespace, or use `:id`
text: - Keep to one fact per `:refer` per namespace (the existing convention), or

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Fact IDs: one `:refer` per namespace, or use `:id`
text: - give every fact a unique explicit id: `^{:refer my.ns/fn :id test-my-fn-2}`.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Fact IDs: one `:refer` per namespace, or use `:id`
text:
To prove a test file's assertions actually execute, temporarily break one
expectation and confirm the run fails (the summary line shows
`FAILED L:<line>`), then revert. Don't trust the passed-check count alone.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Assert the intended result
text:
Tests must prove the function's semantic contract, not merely that execution
did not throw or that a delivery mechanism returned a success status.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Assert the intended result
text:
- Test a transport or handler delivery mechanism once. Tests for functions
  reached through it should then assert each function's actual return value or
  resulting state.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Assert the intended result
text:
- Preserve stable domain expectations exactly. For example, if an RPC is
  expected to return `"pong"`, assert `"pong"`; do not substitute a different
  RPC or weaken the expectation to a status, type, or non-nil check.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Assert the intended result
text:
- Use `promise-catch` as the asserted path only for intentional negative tests.
  Include an explicit rejection marker and assert the relevant error fields so
  that an accidentally resolved promise cannot satisfy the test.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Assert the intended result
text:
- A catch may help diagnose a positive flow, but catching an exception must
  never turn that positive test into a pass.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Assert the intended result
text:
- A status-only assertion is appropriate only when the function's documented
  domain result genuinely is status-only; say so in the fact description.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Assert the intended result
text:
- Seedgen transforms must preserve these semantic assertions across target
  languages. Prefer a language transform over suppressing or weakening a fact.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Conditional Namespace Skipping
text: Use `fact:global` with `:skip` to skip every fact in a namespace when a runtime condition is not met (for example, an external OS program is missing). Skipped facts are reported as skipped and their bodies are not executed.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Conditional Namespace Skipping
text: When `:skip` is truthy, namespace setup and teardown are also bypassed, so missing dependencies cannot cause setup failures.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Testing Framework > Conditional Namespace Skipping

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > code.doc - Documentation System > API resolution notes
text:
`[[:api {:namespace "..."}]]` elements resolve aggregate namespaces built with
`f/intern-in` / `f/intern-all` (e.g. `std.block`, `std.lib`, `code.test`), including
`[dst src]` alias vectors and one level of nesting (`std.block` → `std.block.heal`
→ `std.block.heal.core`). Analysis for docs also indexes `def`, `defonce`, `defn-`,
`definvoke` and `impl/defimpl` forms (the latter with generated `map->`/`->`
constructor entries) — scoped to code.doc via `code.doc.collect.reference/*doc-toplevel-forms*`,
so `code.manage` analysis is unaffected.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > code.doc - Documentation System > API resolution notes
text:
Vars generated by macros at runtime (e.g. `std.lib.bin` buffers,
`impl/build-impl` protocol wrappers) cannot be resolved statically. When the live
var exists, `create-api-table` marks the entry `:source {:generated true}` and fills
arglists/docstring from live metadata; the renderer shows a "Generated" badge and a
placeholder source block instead of "source not found", and `code.doc/check` does not
flag them. Stale `:refer` metadata in tests (renamed/moved vars) shows up as
`missing-source` — fix the refer, as in `test/std/concurrent/request_test.clj`.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > code.doc - Documentation System > Checking Documentation
text:
`code.doc/check` validates pages before publishing: missing `:api` namespaces,
unresolved `:reference` targets, api entries with no source or example
(rendered as "source not found" / "example not found"), typo'd `:only` vars,
unknown `[[:related]]`/`[[:links]]` data groups, and page load/parse errors.
With `:eval true` it also executes page facts and reports failing sections.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > code.doc - Documentation System > Checking Documentation
text:
Known flaky class: `prepare-error` reporting `Unable to resolve var ...` or
`namespace 'std.concurrent' not found` across `lib.*`/`std.concurrent*` pages.
These trace to `lang.core.script` issuing `(require ... :reload)` at namespace
load (src/lang/lang/script.clj:90-111): once `lang.core` loads mid-sequence it
force-reloads module namespaces and invalidates previously compiled records,
which aborts later `require`s. The failures are order/timing dependent and come
and go between JVMs. Running checks per site (e.g. `'[std]`) is far less
exposed than `:all`; the real fix is removing load-time `:reload` from
lang.core, which is a source-tree issue, not a docs one.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Seedgen and xtbench authoring
text: `test-lang/xt/**/*.clj` contains the **canonical seed tests**. Each seed is written once for the `:js` runtime and then generated into target-language bench files under `test-lang/xtbench/<lang>/...`. The generated namespaces are named `xtbench.<lang>.<path>-test`.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Seedgen and xtbench authoring
text: The goal is maximum parity: the same facts, assertions, and test flow should run on every target. Use the `:seedgen/*` metadata to adapt the seed, not to remove coverage.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Seedgen and xtbench authoring > Core principles
text: 1. **Keep the canonical `:js` seed intact.** Do not remove the `(l/script- :js ...)` form or `:js` checks to make another target pass. Fix the target implementation, the seed, or the metadata, then regenerate.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Seedgen and xtbench authoring > Core principles
text: 2. **Do not edit generated `test-lang/xtbench/**` files by hand.** They are derived output. Change the seed or the generator and regenerate.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Seedgen and xtbench authoring > Core principles
text: 3. **Prefer portable XT APIs first.** Only introduce per-language adapters when the API really differs.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Seedgen and xtbench authoring > Core principles
text: 4. **Prefer `:transform` over `:suppress`.** If a target needs a different function name or shape, use `:seedgen/base {:<lang> {:transform ...}}`. Reserve `:suppress` for capabilities that truly cannot be expressed on a target, and document why.

head: Agent Instructions for Foundation Base > Seedgen and xtbench authoring > Core principles
text: 5. **Regenerate and run both sides after a seed change.** Run the canonical source test (`lein test :only xt.<path>-test`) and the generated target test (`lein test :only xtbench.<lang>.<path>-test`).

head: Ageniti
text: This is the main agent-facing guide for the `ageniti/` package.

head: Ageniti > What Ageniti Is
text:
Ageniti is the action primitive layer for agentic applications. Define an
action once and the runtime makes it callable from CLI, HTTP, MCP, OpenAI
tools, AI SDK tools, JSON automation, a typed client, the React `useAction`
hook, and a local dev console — all from the same contract.

head: Ageniti > Core Model
text: The action contract is the source of truth.

head: Ageniti > Core Model
text:
Every surface goes through the shared runtime so validation, permissions,
confirmation, timeout, retry, idempotency, concurrency, logging, artifacts,
and output validation behave consistently.

head: Ageniti > Canonical Import
text: Use subpath imports when the host needs a narrower boundary:

head: Ageniti > Key Primitives > Foreign schema interop
text:
`defineAction({ input })` accepts Zod-style schemas (`.safeParse` / `.parse`) and
Standard Schema v1 directly — no rewrite needed:

head: Ageniti > Key Primitives > Bulk registration
text: CamelCase keys normalize to snake_case action names automatically.

head: Ageniti > Key Primitives > Streaming events
text: Every invocation emits live events any consumer can subscribe to:

head: Ageniti > Key Primitives > Streaming events
text:
Events come from `ctx.logger.*`, `ctx.progress.report()`, and
`ctx.artifacts.add()` inside the action. The stream always ends with one
`result` event.

head: Ageniti > Key Primitives > Typed client
text:
`createClient` returns a Proxy: `client.<action_name>(input, options?)` resolves
to `data` on success or throws `AgenitiClientError` on failure.

head: Ageniti > Key Primitives > React hook (state machine)
text:
Subscribes to `runtime.stream`, so `logs` / `artifacts` / `progress` update
live during the invocation. Component unmount auto-aborts.

head: Ageniti > Key Primitives > Test utilities
text:
Framework-agnostic — works with `node:test`, vitest, jest. Defaults to
`surface: "json"` and bypasses the confirmation gate so destructive actions
can be tested without ceremony.

head: Ageniti > Key Primitives > Codegen
text:
Emits a typed `.d.ts` so consumers get IDE autocomplete on action names,
inputs, and outputs.

head: Ageniti > Runtime Capabilities
text:
| Capability | How |
|---|---|
| Validation | input + output schema (built-in or wrapped Zod / Standard Schema) |
| Permissions | `permissionChecker` callback on `createRuntime` |
| Confirmation gate | destructive actions need `confirm: true` on cli/json/mcp/http surfaces |
| Idempotency | `idempotencyKey` in invoke options; LRU-bounded cache; replay marker in `meta.idempotent` |
| Concurrency | `concurrency: { max: N }` on the action; returns `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` (retryable) |
| Timeout + retry | per-attempt `AbortController` so retries see fresh signal |
| Cancellation | external `signal` + CLI SIGINT + React unmount all wired |
| Streaming | `runtime.stream()` async iterable of log/artifact/progress/result |
| Redaction | log fields, artifact metadata, error messages — default keys + custom |
| Hooks | `onInvocationStart` / `onInvocationEnd` for telemetry |
| Deprecated warn | warn log emitted on every invocation of a deprecated action |

head: AGENTS.md
text: **Audience:** AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) working on AAOSP. Humans are welcome to read it too, but the tone is written for agents — direct, imperative, load-bearing.

head: AGENTS.md
text: **Goal of this file:** encode the things that are expensive to rediscover on this project. Read it before you touch anything, and re-read §4 and §5 before you write prose or commit.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What AAOSP is, for the purposes of this file
text: AAOSP is a fork of Android 15 (`trunk_staging`, rebased on `android-15.0.0_r1`) that integrates:

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What AAOSP is, for the purposes of this file
text: - **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** as a native OS service — apps declare tools in their `AndroidManifest.xml` via an `<mcp-server>` block; the OS parses them at package-install time.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What AAOSP is, for the purposes of this file
text: - **An on-device LLM** (Qwen 2.5, default 3B Q4_K_M) running via llama.cpp inside `system_server`, exposed through `LlmManagerService` over a binder `ILlmService` API.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What AAOSP is, for the purposes of this file
text: - **An agentic loop** (`LlmManagerService.runChain()`) that dispatches model-emitted `<tool_call>` JSON to MCP services over binder, round-trips results, and runs a final natural-language pass.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What AAOSP is, for the purposes of this file
text: - **HITL consent** (`HitlConsentStore` + `ConsentGate`) for tools declared `mcpRequiresConfirmation="true"`.

head: AGENTS.md > 1. What AAOSP is, for the purposes of this file
text: Canonical source of truth: **`docs/AAOSP_ARCHITECTURE.md`**. If this file and that file disagree, that file wins.

head: AGENTS.md > 2. Repo topology
text: Nine repos make up AAOSP. **Only two are actual GitHub forks.** The rest are new repos sitting at AOSP tree paths — one build-glue wrapper, two orphan-root snapshots (repo-manifest shallow clones can't push ancestry), and four plain new repos. Do not assume "fork" from the name.
