head: AGENTS.md > 2. Repo topology > Verify the topology before citing it
text: If `fork: false`, it is not a fork. If `size: 0` and branches is empty, it is an empty shell. If there's exactly one commit with no parent, it is an orphan-root snapshot (check `AAOSP_OVERLAY.md` for what the overlay actually is).

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Build environment
text: **You cannot build AOSP on a laptop here.** The user's Mac is 8 GB and cannot complete `m -j32`. All builds happen on a cloud VM:

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Build environment
text: - VM: `aaosp-builder` in `us-east1-b`, GCP project `aaosp-build`

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Build environment
text: - **Stop the VM when you're done.** It costs money while running.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Build environment
text: - Full build: `source build/envsetup.sh && lunch aosp_cf_x86_64_phone-trunk_staging-userdebug && m -j32`

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Build environment
text: - **Never `m systemimage` alone.** It skips `boot.img` / `vbmeta.img`, and Cuttlefish drops into dm-verity recovery. Always `m -j32`.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Build environment
text: - Incremental is fine *after* the first full build, but any change touching the kernel, selinux, or vbmeta needs the full build again.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Build environment
text:
Memory: **16 GB** (`memory_mb=16384`). The 3B model mmaps ~2 GB for
its weights, plus Android's own footprint, plus the
conversation-history growth we've observed in testing — 8 GB was
survivable on v0.1.0 with the 0.5B model but tight under v0.5.1+
with 3B + multi-MCP chains. The build VM has 125 GB, so 16 GB for
Cuttlefish is no stress.

head: AGENTS.md > 3. Build environment
text: First boot sometimes drops into recovery with `set_policy_failed:/data/local`. Pick **Wipe data / factory reset**, reboot once, it'll be fine. This is a Cuttlefish quirk, not AAOSP.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Docs track code, live — not at tag time
text: **Core rule of this project:** documentation is updated as the code changes, in the same commit that lands the code. Not "later," not "at tag time," not "when we write the release notes." Live.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Docs track code, live — not at tag time
text: Why: every fabrication we've had to chase on this project came from docs drifting behind code between commits. The only defense is to keep them in lockstep.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Docs track code, live — not at tag time
text: What this means concretely:

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Docs track code, live — not at tag time
text: - If you change observable behavior, update `docs/CHANGELOG.md` (under `## Unreleased`) in the same commit. See §6.1a.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Docs track code, live — not at tag time
text: - If you change an AIDL, add/remove a class, rename a constant, swap a file path, or move install targets — update every doc that referenced the old state in the same commit. See §6.1b.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Docs track code, live — not at tag time
text: - If you change a version-facing claim (status table, tier table, bake-in path) — update README *and* ARCHITECTURE *and* CHANGELOG. These three diverge if you update only one.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Docs track code, live — not at tag time
text: - If you can't update the docs in the same commit (legitimate reason: the doc change needs a separate discussion), write the CHANGELOG entry anyway and add a TODO marker pointing to the unfinished doc.

head: AGENTS.md > 4. Docs track code, live — not at tag time
text: "I'll do the docs in a follow-up" is not a commitment mechanism on this project. Follow-ups get lost. The commit is the commitment mechanism.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate
text: **This section exists because LLM-written docs have introduced fabrications into this project.** Before any of the following, verify:

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.1 Version tags
text: **Rule:** never reference a version tag without confirming it exists.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.1 Version tags
text: Real AAOSP tags (2026-04-14): `v0.1.0`, `v0.3.0`, `v0.5`. There is **no `v0.2`, `v0.2.0`, or `v0.4` tag** — do not cite them. `v0.2` is an untagged milestone (commit `42af2cf`); reference it by sha, not by tag.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.2 Dates
text: **Rule:** any date in a CHANGELOG, README, or doc must come from `git`, not from your estimate.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.2 Dates
text: AAOSP's entire history is days old. If you're about to write a date spanning months, stop — it's wrong.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.3 Fork/new-repo status
text: **Rule:** do not label a repo as a "fork" without `gh api repos/... --jq .fork` returning `true`. Do not say a file lives "in-tree" if it has its own repo.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.4 Benchmarks and measurements
text: **Rule:** no number without a device. If we haven't run it, don't cite it. If we have, cite the target.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.4 Benchmarks and measurements
text: Today we run on Cuttlefish x86_64 (silvermont) on cloud-build CPU. Observed: ~0.6 tok/s with Qwen 3B Q4_K_M, threads=8. Phone-class numbers do not exist until we have a phone. Don't invent them.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.5 Code symbols and paths
text: **Rule:** when prose names a class, method, field, constant, or path, fetch the file and grep.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.5 Code symbols and paths
text: Do not write from memory. Memory goes stale.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.6 Verification results
text: **Rule:** only claim "verified on Cuttlefish" if there's a Loom, a video, a log, or a demo you or the user actually ran. "Designed and implemented" is not "verified." Use the honest phrase.

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.7 Status language
text: - "Shipped in v0.5, verification pending" — code is there, no recent demo

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.7 Status language
text: - "Designed but not yet wired" — spec only

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.7 Status language
text: - "Unverified" — literally don't know

head: AGENTS.md > 5. Don't fabricate > 5.7 Status language
text: Do not paper over uncertainty with confident prose.

1. **Pre-tag doc staleness grep.** Before updating CHANGELOG or cutting the tag, sweep for documentation that describes the *old* behavior of anything this release changed. Items shipped and docs untouched are the failure mode that produced the v0.5.1 follow-up cleanup. Run at least:
   ```bash
   # In the umbrella repo
   grep -rnE 'not yet wired|not yet built|designed in .docs/|TODO|scaffolded' README.md docs/ AGENTS.md
   # Any hit is suspect — fixed in the release? Strike/update. Still true? Fine.

   # Repo-specific: grep for any API / path / constant this release moved

   grep -rnE '10 ?s|35 ?s|\bstartActivity\b|\bPermissionRequestActivity\b' README.md docs/
   grep -rnE '2048|0\.5B|qwen2\.5-0\.5b' .    # model/ctx drift from the v0.5 3B swap

   Any hit that still describes pre-release behavior must be updated *in the same tag commit*. Cross-repo: run the same grep in `platform_frameworks_base`, `platform_packages_apps_*`, and any MCP repo whose surface changed.

text: **Load-bearing invariants. Do not break these:**

head: AGENTS.md > 6. When you touch one thing, touch these other things > 6.6 Changing the HITL threading model
text: - `ConsentGate` uses `CountDownLatch(1)` + `AtomicReference` for race-safety between the dispatcher thread parking on consent and the user's response thread arriving. Replace carefully or not at all.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. When you touch one thing, touch these other things > 6.6 Changing the HITL threading model
text: - `CONSENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000L` — auto-DENY on timeout. Don't lower this below the user's realistic response window.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. When you touch one thing, touch these other things > 6.6 Changing the HITL threading model
text: - `endSession(sessionId)` must both clear `SCOPE_SESSION` grants **and** wake any parked gates (via `cancel()`). Missing either leaks threads or grants.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. When you touch one thing, touch these other things > 6.6 Changing the HITL threading model
text: - Dispatcher thread must fire `STATUS_STARTED` *before* the consent gate parks, so the launcher's tool-call card appears immediately instead of after the user taps Allow.

head: AGENTS.md > 6. When you touch one thing, touch these other things > 6.7 Changing the temperature logic
text: Two passes, two temperatures:

head: AGENTS.md > 6. When you touch one thing, touch these other things > 6.7 Changing the temperature logic
text: - Tool-call pass: `min(request.temperature, 0.25f)` — `<tool_call>` JSON must be deterministic

head: AGENTS.md > 6. When you touch one thing, touch these other things > 6.7 Changing the temperature logic
text: - Answer pass: caller-controlled, default `0.7f`

head: AGENTS.md > 6. When you touch one thing, touch these other things > 6.7 Changing the temperature logic
text: If you "helpfully" unify them, Qwen at 0.7 drifts on tool arguments (names, numbers, email addresses) and you get hallucinated tool args. Leave the split alone.

head: AGENTS.md > 7. AOSP landmines (earned the hard way)
text: - `<tool>` / `<input>` `android:description` is `format="reference"` only — **inline strings are rejected by aapt2**. Use `@string/...`.

head: AGENTS.md > 7. AOSP landmines (earned the hard way)
text: - `<input>` required flag is `android:mcpRequired`, **not** `android:required`.

head: AGENTS.md > 7. AOSP landmines (earned the hard way)
text: - SQLite forbids expressions inside `PRIMARY KEY`. Using `COALESCE(session_id, '')` in a PK crashes the DB at `onCreate`. Normalize nullable cols to `""` at write/delete time and keep `NOT NULL` in the schema.

head: AGENTS.md > 7. AOSP landmines (earned the hard way)
text: - `adb push` to `/system` hits read-only. Need `adb disable-verity` → `adb reboot` → `adb remount` first. On FDE builds, this is a real detour.

head: AGENTS.md > 7. AOSP landmines (earned the hard way)
text: - At sampling temperature `0.1` with few-shot examples that include *trailing prose*, the model learns to skip the tool call and jump to a fabricated success line. Fix: truncate each example at the `<tool_call>` closing tag, and floor temperature at `0.25`.

head: AGENTS.md > 7. AOSP landmines (earned the hard way)
text: - Cuttlefish `m systemimage` without rebuilding `boot.img`/`vbmeta.img` → dm-verity recovery loop. Always `m -j32`.

head: AGENTS.md > 7. AOSP landmines (earned the hard way)
text: - Android 15 BAL (background-activity-launch) silently blocks in-app permission dialogs launched from a bound-service context — without throwing. Do not assume a `startActivity` from `invokeTool` will render; return `needs_permission` JSON and let the launcher proxy the request.

head: AGENTS.md > 7. AOSP landmines (earned the hard way)
text: - The AIDL for write-tool `confirmToolCall(sessionId, toolName, decision, scope)` is *asynchronous wake-up*, not request/response — the parked dispatcher thread wakes via `ConsentGate`, not via AIDL return value.

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: coolbpf is an eBPF development platform by Alibaba Cloud that wraps libbpf for simplified BPF program development. It has three main components:

head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > coolbpf library pattern
text: - Userspace code includes `.skel.h` and uses `coolbpf_object_new(skel)` or `coolbpf_object_open(skel)` macros

text: - `coolbpf_object` struct with `preload`/`preattach` callback function pointers

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > coolbpf library pattern
text: - Dual conditional compilation: headers used in both BPF (`#ifdef __VMLINUX_H__`) and userspace contexts

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > coolbpf library pattern
text: - Architecture-specific `vmlinux.h` in `arch/x86_64/` and `arch/aarch64/`

text: - eBPF probes capture kernel events via ring buffer: sslsniff, proctrace, procmon, filewatch

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > AgentSight data pipeline
text: - Multi-stage processing pipeline with typed event flow

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture > AgentSight data pipeline
text: - Storage: SQLite (local) + Alibaba Cloud SLS (cloud)

text: - HTTP API server (actix-web) with embedded React dashboard

def androidHome = System.getenv('ANDROID_HOME') ?: "${System.getProperty('user.home')}/Library/Android/sdk"
environment 'ANDROID_HOME', androidHome
```

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: The next wave of work must first make the domain language consistent.

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: - Product is the capability template.

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: - Device is the runtime instance.

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: - Asset is the managed business object.

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: - Gateway is the southbound protocol and child-device access runtime.

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: - EdgeNode is the managed edge runtime responsible for registration, heartbeat, capability reporting, task receipt and diagnostics.

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: - Collection templates define protocol, connection, point, transform, mapping and sampling behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: - Release tasks, configuration rollout, OTA and long-running operations must not be hidden inside the real-time rule-chain model.

head: AGENTS.md > Current Concept Realignment
text: Old `Produce` code and API surfaces are no longer compatibility targets. Current documentation, UI text, DTOs, contracts and active API surfaces should use Product language; historical EF migrations may still mention Produce only as database history.

text: AI is a cross-cutting capability for the three existing layers, not a separate rewrite track.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions
text: IoTSharp uses Product, Device, Asset, Gateway, EdgeNode and Collection Template as separate core concepts. Contributors and automation must preserve these boundaries when designing models, APIs, UI, rules, release flows, and AI workbench capabilities.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Product
text: Product defines the type and capability model for a class of devices or collection objects.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Product
text: - protocol and connection templates

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Product
text: - telemetry, attribute, command, event, and configuration definitions

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Product
text: - point templates, transform hints, and sample policies

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Product
text: - default credential policy, default rule chain, alarm templates, software and firmware compatibility

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Product
text: - model-level defaults shared by many device instances

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Product
text: Product should not represent a physical installation, business site, production line, runtime connection, device state, telemetry latest value, alarm instance, command execution record, or individual runtime instance.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Device
text: Device represents a real access instance connected to IoTSharp or reported through Gateway.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Device
text: - identity, credentials, and access lifecycle

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Device
text: - connectivity, heartbeat, runtime status, and telemetry

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Device
text: - attributes, commands, events, and real-time rule inputs

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Device
text: - binding to a Product for capability interpretation

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Device
text: - binding to an Asset when the device serves a business object

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Device
text: - binding to a Gateway or EdgeNode when the device is collected through a managed runtime

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Device
text: Device should not be used as a broad business hierarchy, site tree, or release scope substitute when the real target is an Asset or EdgeNode.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Asset
text: Asset represents a managed business object in the user's operational world.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Asset
text: - sites, parks, buildings, floors, rooms, workshops, production lines, stations, facilities, equipment systems, and other field objects

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Asset
text: - business ownership, spatial hierarchy, operational responsibility, alarm context, dashboard context, and permission scope

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Asset
text: - linking one or more Devices to the business object they observe or control

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Asset
text: - addressing configuration, release, diagnosis, and operational views by business scope when appropriate

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Asset
text: Asset is not a synonym for Device, Product, or DeviceGroup. Asset also does not mean static project resources such as images, fonts, CSS, or bundled frontend files; those resources should use names such as `static`, `public`, `media`, `wwwroot`, or framework-specific asset folders outside the domain model.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Gateway
text: Gateway is a special Device that owns southbound protocol access and child-device reporting.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Gateway
text: - protocol adapter execution

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Gateway
text: - child device discovery, creation and connectivity reporting

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Gateway
text: - uploading child-device telemetry, attributes, events and alarms

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Gateway
text: - receiving collection configuration, software tasks and diagnostics tasks

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Gateway
text: - reporting runtime capability, task receipt, task result and errors

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Gateway
text: Gateway should not store platform-side Product templates, bypass tenant permission checks, or depend on hidden IoTSharp database assumptions.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > EdgeNode
text: EdgeNode is a managed edge runtime instance.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > EdgeNode
text: - registration, heartbeat, version, instance identity and health state

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > EdgeNode
text: - capability reporting and runtime diagnostics

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > EdgeNode
text: - receiving configuration, software, firmware and diagnostic tasks

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > EdgeNode
text: - reporting task receipt, execution, completion, failure, timeout and rollback result

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > EdgeNode
text: Gateway and EdgeNode may be deployed together, but Gateway describes protocol and child-device access while EdgeNode describes managed runtime lifecycle and task closure.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Collection Template
text: Collection Template is the platform-side definition of collection behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Collection Template
text: - mapping policies to telemetry, attributes, alarms or command feedback

head: AGENTS.md > Core Domain Concept Definitions > Collection Template
text: Collection Template should belong to Product or a reusable template library, while runtime task delivery should target EdgeNode, Gateway or selected Devices.

text: - 第三方包的传递依赖不能自动等同于 IoTSharp 直接依赖；不能仅因为第三方内部使用某个库，就删除 IoTSharp 的数据库 provider、协议适配、规则链能力、API 文档/UI、SDK 生成、网关接入或运维发布能力。

head: AGENTS.md > Dependency and Component Removal Rules
text: - 如果必须替换一个第三方组件，应先证明替代方案覆盖原有入口、配置项、公开契约、运行时行为和回滚路径；无法完全覆盖时，要保留兼容层或明确列出兼容差异。

head: AGENTS.md > Dependency and Component Removal Rules
text: - 删除组件前必须单独说明影响面：用户可见能力、配置名称、数据库/迁移、API/SDK、文档、测试、部署脚本和跨项目契约；没有明确批准或废弃证据时，不做大范围删除。

head: AGENTS.md > Dependency and Component Removal Rules
text: - 依赖清理应尽量采用分层替换、适配器、功能开关或可选包隔离；不要把“去掉某个库”扩大成动摇平台根能力的重构。

head: AGENTS.md > Dependency and Component Removal Rules
text: - `NSwag.AspNetCore`、`RulesEngine`、`Jint` 是当前保留的基础组件；没有明确批准和等价替代验证时，不得删除、替换或弱化相关能力。

head: AGENTS.md > Dependency and Component Removal Rules
text: - 安全、许可证或供应链风险确需移除传递依赖时，应拆成独立变更，给出风险说明、迁移方案和验证清单，避免和无关功能调整混在一次提交中。

head: AGENTS.md > Code Documentation Rules
text: - IoTSharp 代码注释优先使用中文；只有外部协议、标准术语、API 名称或引用资料需要保留英文时才使用英文。

head: AGENTS.md > Code Documentation Rules
text: - 新增或修改方法时，尽量补充 XML 文档注释，尤其是 public、internal、扩展方法和跨模块调用的方法。

head: AGENTS.md > Code Documentation Rules
text: - 方法注释要说明功能目的、关键参数、返回值，以及不容易从签名看出的副作用或兼容行为。

head: AGENTS.md > Code Documentation Rules
text: - 注释要简洁、语义清楚；不要重复方法名，也不要解释显而易见的赋值或语法。

head: AGENTS.md > Code Documentation Rules
text: - 只有在控制流、转换规则、兼容逻辑或领域决策不直观时，才添加简短行内注释。

head: AGENTS.md > Immediate Execution Focus
text:
The platform code baseline through Release Center already exists. The next gap
is production business modeling and actual enablement, not another broad round
of feature development.

head: AGENTS.md > Immediate Execution Focus
text: Work must proceed in this order:

head: AGENTS.md > Immediate Execution Focus
text:
1. Model real Product capabilities and Asset ownership, then bind Devices to the
   correct Product and Asset business context.

head: AGENTS.md > Immediate Execution Focus
text:
2. Connect a real Gateway/EdgeNode runtime and verify registration, heartbeat,
   capability reporting, task receipt, and diagnostics with runtime evidence.

head: AGENTS.md > Immediate Execution Focus
text:
3. Create an approved Collection Template and immutable configuration version,
   then deploy it to that runtime and verify current/target version convergence.

head: AGENTS.md > Immediate Execution Focus
text:
4. Use Release Center to complete one controlled canary release and rollback,
   retaining target scope, approval, task, receipt, audit, and post-rollback
   evidence.

head: AGENTS.md > Immediate Execution Focus
text:
5. Only after that production loop is proven, enhance RuleChain trace, version,
   audit, and backpressure behavior.

head: AGENTS.md > Immediate Execution Focus
text:
The completed M1-M5 implementation milestones describe available platform
capabilities. They are not evidence that a real production model, runtime,
configuration, canary release, or rollback has been completed. Do not advance a
later step based only on API availability, local tests, mock receipts, or a
healthy process.

head: Agent Instructions
text:
This repository uses OpenSpec. These are the shared rules for all agents;
host-specific instructions link here instead of maintaining separate policies.

head: Agent Instructions > Route the Task
text:
- For questions and read-only reviews, inspect relevant files and report
  evidence. Do not start onboarding or create a spec just to answer a question.

head: Agent Instructions > Route the Task
text:
- For explicitly requested template maintenance, preserve placeholders and
  template-internal specs. Do not run onboarding or cleanup on the template.

head: Agent Instructions > Route the Task
text:
- Before taking an issue, check its auto-fix label, open PRs, and workflow runs.
  Reuse an existing agent draft PR; do not race an active run or bypass an
  agent's documented refusal. See [auto-fix](docs/OPENSPEC.md#issue-auto-fix-agent-opt-in).

head: Agent Instructions > Route the Task
text:
- For downstream implementation, check `.openspec/config.yaml`. If it contains
  `{{` tokens, follow [onboarding](docs/ONBOARDING.md) and confirm values before
  writing them. Missing config is an error, not proof that setup is complete.
  Any capable agent can guide onboarding.

head: Agent Instructions > OpenSpec Contract
text:
1. Find the matching `.openspec/specs/<slug>.spec.yaml` before source edits.
   If none exists, scaffold one with `bash scripts/openspec scaffold "<name>"`
   (add `--type bugfix` for a bugfix). Clarify scope with the user.

head: Agent Instructions > OpenSpec Contract
text:
2. Implement only when status is `review` or `approved`, with a meaningful
   description, at least one acceptance criterion, and at least one test-plan
   item. Never promote a draft merely to bypass this gate.

head: Agent Instructions > OpenSpec Contract
text:
3. Keep changes within the spec. Include the corresponding spec change and
   tests with implementation; tests belong in the same PR, not a follow-up.
   Existing specs can be updated instead of creating duplicate specs.

head: Agent Instructions > OpenSpec Contract
text:
4. Update README, CHANGELOG, or relevant docs when behavior or usage changes.
   For internal-only changes, explain any `skip-doc-drift` request to a maintainer.
  Use Mermaid for diagrams unless the user explicitly requests another format.

head: Agent Instructions > OpenSpec Contract
text:
5. Preserve security checks, human approvals, and branch protection. An AI
   review is advisory, never proof of correctness or permission to merge.

head: Agent Instructions > Small, Verifiable Steps
text:
- Start from relevant code or a failing test. State assumptions that affect
  behavior and resolve ambiguity before implementing it.

head: Agent Instructions > Small, Verifiable Steps
text:
- For a small change, the spec's acceptance criteria and test plan are enough.
  Do not require an extra plan document, ADR, specialist, or agent handoff.

head: Agent Instructions > Small, Verifiable Steps
text:
- For larger changes, implement one testable slice at a time. Run the cheapest
  relevant check immediately, then expand validation to the affected contract.

head: Agent Instructions > Small, Verifiable Steps
text:
- Prefer existing utilities and simple code. Add abstractions only when they
  remove demonstrated complexity. Do not clean up unrelated code.

head: Agent Instructions > Small, Verifiable Steps
text:
- Role names describe responsibilities, not a minimum team size. A solo
  maintainer may hold multiple roles where project policy permits. Never
  fabricate role assignments or approval; honor configured review requirements.

head: Agent Instructions > Small, Verifiable Steps
text:
- Load only the applicable spec, nearby code/tests, and relevant references.
  If `implementation_skill` (or the configured default) names a skill, load
  its actual instructions. Mentioning its name is not invoking it. If unavailable,
  report that and agree on a fallback rather than pretending it ran.

head: Agent Instructions > Small, Verifiable Steps
text:
- Delegate only when authorized and useful for independent work. Preserve the
  user's changes. Do not install skills, commit, push, or enable paid services
  without authorization. Use `git commit -s` when asked to commit.

head: Agent Instructions > Verification and Handoff
text:
- Run `bash scripts/openspec check`; use `--strict` when all specs must be
  implementation-ready. Run the configured `testing.test_command` with its
  required environment, plus focused checks for the changed behavior.

head: Agent Instructions > Verification and Handoff
text: - For template maintenance, use `check --template` and `make test-template`.

head: Agent Instructions > Verification and Handoff
text:
- For downstream work, run `verify <slug>` and inspect `status <slug>` before
  reporting completion. See [execution](docs/EXECUTION.md); automation is opt-in,
  and passing command evidence does not prove every acceptance criterion.

head: Agent Instructions > Verification and Handoff
text:
- Report acceptance criteria met, commands run and results, and anything not
  verified. Do not claim tests, security reviews, or deployments happened
  without evidence. Pause on failures; do not weaken checks to make them pass.

head: Agent Instructions > Verification and Handoff
text:
See [OpenSpec](docs/OPENSPEC.md) for the schema and lifecycle,
[adoption](docs/ADOPTION.md) for optional capabilities and known gate limits,
and [branch protection](docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md) before changing required checks.

head: CLAUDE.md
text: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this repo is
text: A personal knowledge base following Zettelkasten methodology. Markdown notes organized by topic folders, with wikilinks for connections between notes. Compatible with Obsidian as a vault. Multiple ingest paths: Obsidian Clipper (raw web captures), Claude Code, and Claude AI skills.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: Repo root holds framework files only; all content lives under `notes/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `CLAUDE.md` - this file; operating rules for the wiki

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `README.md` - landing page with methodology, topic overview, recent additions

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `index.md` - full catalog of all notes with one-line summaries, grouped by folder. The LLM reads this to navigate the wiki.

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `log.md` - chronological content operations (ingests, queries, lints, synthesis)

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `_docs/` - project documentation (requirements, architecture, guide, changelog)

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `_templates/` - Obsidian templates for new notes

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `_inbox/` - landing zone for raw, unprocessed notes (Obsidian Clipper dumps here)

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - Each topic is a folder under `notes/` (e.g., `notes/ai-tooling/`, `notes/patterns/`, `notes/mcp/`, `notes/claude-code/`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - `notes/assets/` holds images and attachments, scoped per domain (e.g., `notes/assets/wealth/*.svg`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Repo structure
text: - Notes are markdown files with YAML frontmatter. Obsidian resolves `[[wikilinks]]` by filename, so path depth does not matter.

head: CLAUDE.md > Session start check
text: At the start of every Claude Code session in this repo, check for uncompiled additions:

head: CLAUDE.md > Session start check
text: 1. Run `git log --oneline -10` to see recent commits

head: CLAUDE.md > Session start check
text: 2. Check if any notes were added via Claude.ai skill or direct git push that haven't been compiled (look for commits without corresponding `log.md` entries)

head: CLAUDE.md > Session start check
text: 3. If uncompiled notes exist, offer: "I see X new notes added since last compilation. Want me to run the compilation step on them?"

head: CLAUDE.md > Session start check
text: This catches notes pushed from Claude.ai or other sources that bypass Claude Code's compilation step.

head: CLAUDE.md > Note format
text: Notes follow specific templates defined in the user's global CLAUDE.md (knowledge capture rules). Key points:

head: CLAUDE.md > Note format
text:
- **Frontmatter fields**:
  - `title` (lowercase with selective capitalization)
  - `date` (YYYY-MM-DD)
  - `captured` (ISO timestamp)
  - `tags` (array)
  - `source` (where the knowledge came from)
  - `aliases` (array, optional; alternate titles for Obsidian link resolution)
  - `status`: one of `raw` | `refined` | `evergreen`
    - `raw`: just captured, unprocessed (typical for Clipper notes in `_inbox/`)
    - `refined`: reviewed, has frontmatter, placed in correct folder, has links
    - `evergreen`: mature note, well-linked, updated over time

head: CLAUDE.md > Note format
text: - **Depth types**: TIL (shallow), Atomic Note (default/medium), Article (deep), Definition (reference)

head: CLAUDE.md > Note format
text: - **Context is mandatory** for Atomic Notes and Articles

head: CLAUDE.md > Note format
text: - **Filename convention**: lowercase, hyphen-separated, descriptive (e.g., `redundant-api-pre-checks-in-wrapper-functions.md`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Note format
text: - **No em dashes**: never use `—` (em dash) anywhere in the repo. Use ` - ` (space-hyphen-space), commas, semicolons, or split into two sentences.

head: CLAUDE.md > Wikilinks and backlinks
text: This repo uses Obsidian-compatible `[[wikilinks]]` for connections between notes.

head: CLAUDE.md > Wikilinks and backlinks
text: - Use `[[filename-without-extension]]` to link to another note (Obsidian resolves shortest path)

head: CLAUDE.md > Wikilinks and backlinks
text: - Every refined/evergreen note should have a `## Related` section at the bottom with links to connected notes

head: CLAUDE.md > Wikilinks and backlinks
text:
- When linking, prefer linking to the concept, not just listing related files. Write a brief phrase explaining the relationship:
  ```
  ## Related
  - [[turing-completeness]] - foundational concept behind this pattern
  - [[redundant-api-pre-checks-in-wrapper-functions]] - another example of this anti-pattern
  ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Wikilinks and backlinks
text: - When moving or renaming a note, update all backlinks that reference it. Use `aliases` in frontmatter so Obsidian can still resolve old names.

head: CLAUDE.md > Inbox workflow
text: The `_inbox/` folder is the landing zone for raw captures:

head: CLAUDE.md > Inbox workflow
text: 1. **Obsidian Clipper** saves web clips directly to `_inbox/` with whatever format it produces

head: CLAUDE.md > Inbox workflow
text:
2. **Processing**: When asked to "process inbox" or "reorganize", Claude will:
   - Add/fix frontmatter (title, date, tags, status)
   - Determine the correct topic folder
   - Rewrite or restructure content to match note templates
   - Add `[[wikilinks]]` to related existing notes
   - Move the note from `_inbox/` to the topic folder
   - Set status to `refined`
   - Run the compilation step (see below)

head: CLAUDE.md > Inbox workflow
text: 3. Notes pushed via Claude Code/AI skill bypass `_inbox/` (they arrive already refined) but still trigger the compilation step

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: This is the core of the LLM Wiki pattern. Filing a note is not enough; the wiki must compile the new knowledge into the existing structure.

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: **Trigger phrases** (any of these means run the compilation step on the target notes):

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: - `compile <filename>` - scoped to one note

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: - `compile recent commits` / `compile recent` - walk recent commits, find notes missing from `log.md`

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: - `re-ingest` / `re-ingest recent` / `re-ingest the notes I just pushed` - same as above

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: - `process inbox` - implies compilation after refinement

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: Claude should also run this automatically without a command when the session-start check (above) detects uncompiled additions and the user confirms.

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: After adding or refining a note, Claude will:

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: 1. **Check for overlapping claims.** Search for existing notes that cover the same topic. If the new note adds to, refines, or contradicts existing notes, update the `## Related` sections on both sides with a note about the relationship.

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text:
2. **Flag contradictions.** If the new note contradicts an existing note, add a callout to both notes:
   ```markdown
   > [!warning] Contradiction
   > This note claims X, but [[other-note]] claims Y. See context for which may be more current.
   ```
   Do not silently resolve contradictions. Flag them for human review.

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: 3. **Update synthesis pages.** If a synthesis page exists for this topic cluster, update it to incorporate the new note. Add the new note to its links, and revise the narrative if the new information changes the synthesis. If no synthesis page exists but the cluster now has 4+ notes, suggest creating one.

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: 4. **Update `index.md`.** Add or remove the note entry with a one-line summary. On deletions or merges, remove stale entries. Do NOT maintain note counts; they churn every ingest and waste tokens.

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text: 5. **Update `README.md`.** Add the new note to the "Recent additions" section (keep it at 10 items, drop the oldest). Add rows to the Topics table when new folders appear, but do NOT track per-folder note counts.

head: CLAUDE.md > Compilation step (run on every note addition)
text:
6. **Append to `log.md`.** Record what was ingested and what pages were touched:
   ```
   ## [YYYY-MM-DD] ingest | <note title>
   Added to <folder>. Updated links on: <list>. Synthesis page: <updated/suggested/none>.
   ```

head: CLAUDE.md > Query operation
text: When the user asks a question that requires synthesizing across multiple notes, Claude will:

head: CLAUDE.md > Query operation
text: 1. **Read `log.md`** first to understand recent activity and context.

head: CLAUDE.md > Query operation
text: 2. **Read `index.md`** to find relevant pages by summary, then drill into them.

head: CLAUDE.md > Query operation
text: 3. **Synthesize an answer** from the compiled wiki, citing specific notes with `[[wikilinks]]`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Query operation
text: 4. **Offer to file the answer back.** If the synthesis is substantial (not a quick lookup), ask: "Want me to file this as a wiki page?" Good answers become new notes. This is how explorations compound.

head: CLAUDE.md > Query operation
text: 5. **If filed**, run the compilation step: check for overlaps, flag contradictions, update synthesis pages, append to `log.md` with operation type `query`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Query operation
text: The key principle: answers that required real synthesis across multiple notes are themselves valuable knowledge. They should not vanish into chat history.

For deletions: `delete: <path>`. For index updates: `docs: update note index`.
For reorganization: `refactor: reorganize <description>`.
For link updates: `docs: update backlinks`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What vSmartMOM.jl is
text:
A Julia package for **vectorized polarized atmospheric radiative transfer** using
the **Matrix Operator Method (MOM)**. Computes Stokes-vector radiances (I, Q, U,
V) leaving an inhomogeneous, scattering, absorbing, polarized atmosphere
illuminated by the sun, plus **analytic Jacobians**, on **CPU / CUDA / Metal**
via `KernelAbstractions`. Used for retrieval of trace gases, aerosols, surface
properties from hyperspectral satellite instruments (OCO-2/3, GOSAT, EMIT, …).

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > The narrative thread (memorize this — everything hangs off it)
text:
That's the spine. Every page in `docs/src/pages/concepts/` is one segment of
that thread.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Two non-obvious tricks that compound (read this twice)
text:
These two design choices make line-by-line RT on the GPU practical. They're
load-bearing in the prose; if you're explaining the package to anyone, lead
with these:

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Two non-obvious tricks that compound (read this twice)
text:
1. **Elemental kernel uses the EXACT finite-δ single-scatter formulas, not
   the linear approximation.** S2014 Eqs (19)–(20) are written in the
   `δ → 0` limit (linear in δ; equivalent to `1−exp(−x) ≈ x`). Many MOM codes
   stop there and need very thin elemental layers (large `N_doubl`) for that
   approximation to hold. vSmartMOM's `elemental.jl:207–252` instead uses
   `1 − exp(−δτ(1/μᵢ+1/μⱼ))` and `exp(−δτ/μᵢ) − exp(−δτ/μⱼ)` written via
   `-expm1(-x)` and `expdiff_neg(a,b)` for numerical stability. Result:
   thicker elemental layer at the same single-scatter accuracy → smaller
   `N_doubl` → less doubling round-off, stable in `Float32`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Two non-obvious tricks that compound (read this twice)
text:
2. **The elemental layer is sized by SCATTERING optical depth, not total
   optical depth.** `get_dtau_ndoubl` (`rt_kernel.jl:245–253`) picks
   `N_doubl` from `τ_scat·ϖ`; absorption is layered in via
   `τ_λ = τ_abs + τ_scat`, `ϖ_λ = τ_scat·ϖ / τ_λ`. The transmission factors
   inside the elemental kernel use the per-wavelength `dτ_λ`. Consequence:
   a layer with `τ_abs ≈ 50` (deep gas absorption) and `τ_scat ≈ 0.05`
   doesn't blow up `N_doubl`. SF2023-II Eqs (8)–(9) call this the
   "constant-`N_doubl` trick"; it's why a hyperspectral grid runs as one
   batched call per layer per Fourier moment.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Two non-obvious tricks that compound (read this twice)
text:
These two compose: small `N_doubl` (from #1) *and* `N_doubl` constant across
the spectral axis (from #2) → all wavelengths run together on GPU at full
bandwidth.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text:
Not marketing — each claim has a `file:line`. Mirror this list in user-facing
material when explaining the package:

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text: 1. **Operator-level analytic linearization.** RT kernel itself is hand-differentiated; AD is upstream-only. **Combined forward + linearized run costs less than 2× a forward-only run** — the closed-form chain rule on adding-doubling reuses the already-computed batched matrix inverses, so the dominant LU work is paid once. ForwardDiff would pay `(1+N_params)×`; finite differences `(1+N_state)×`. — `src/CoreRT/CoreKernel/elemental_lin.jl` (`get_elem_rt_fused!:456–591`, `get_elem_rt_SFI_fused!:602–815`), `{elemental,doubling,interaction}_lin.jl`. See `docs/src/pages/concepts/06_linearization.md` § "Why this is fast". *Status: production codebase implements the kernel-level fast path; a cleaner AD-upstream → analytic-downstream boundary (more idiomatic handoff struct, less manual chain-rule expansion in upstream code) is in active development.*

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text: 2. **One `@kernel` source compiles for CPU, CUDA, and Metal.** — `src/Architectures.jl:33–96`, `ext/vSmartMOMCUDAExt.jl:21–27`, `ext/vSmartMOMMetalExt.jl:19–22`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text: 3. **Hybrid AD across the GPU boundary.** `ForwardDiff.Dual` flows through `NNlib.batched_mul` on `CuArray`. — `ext/gpu_batched_cuda.jl:141–177`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text: 4. **Polarization is a type, not a runtime branch.** `Stokes_I/IQ/IQU/IQUV` specialize the kernels at compile time. — `src/Scattering/types.jl:92–143`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text: 5. **Optical properties as algebra.** `+` mixes scatterers; `*` stacks layers. — `src/CoreRT/types.jl:1063–1101`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text: 6. **Weak GPU dependency** (Julia 1.9+ package extensions). CPU-only installs first-class. — `ext/vSmartMOMCUDAExt.jl`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text: 7. **Three `(τ, ϖ, Z)` core variables per layer.** RT kernel differentiates against these directly. — `src/CoreRT/types_lin.jl:119–149`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > What sets vSmartMOM apart (anchored)
text: 8. **Exact finite-δ elemental** (point #1 above). — `src/CoreRT/CoreKernel/elemental.jl:207–252`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: (Detailed in CLAUDE.md; condensed here.)

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **Float-type generic.** Most types/functions are parameterized by `FT`. Don't hard-code `Float64`.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **`_lin` suffix** = linearized (Jacobian) variant of a function or type.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **Unicode in identifiers** is used directly: `τ`, `ϖ`, `μ`, `μ₀`, `Z⁺⁺`, `Z⁻⁺`, `R⁻⁺`, `T⁺⁺`, `r⁻⁺`, `t⁺⁺`. Don't romanize.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **Sign convention:** `+` = incoming/downward, `−` = outgoing/upward.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **Layer naming:** `CompositeLayer` fields are uppercase (`R, T, J`); `AddedLayer` fields are lowercase (`r, t, j`).

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **3D RT array layout:** `(NquadN, NquadN, nSpec)` where `NquadN = Nquad * n_stokes`. The third dim is **spectral** — that's what enables batched-matmul over wavelengths.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **Spectral units:** wavenumber (cm⁻¹) internally; wavelength (μm) for Mie.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **Profile direction:** TOA-to-BOA internally. GEOSChem data is BOA-to-TOA and gets flipped on read.

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **No co-author attribution in commits.**

head: AGENTS.md — Quick onboarding for AI coding agents > Conventions you must follow
text: - **Test discipline:** must `cd test/` before running tests — test files use relative paths (`test_profiles/`) that only resolve from `test/`.

head: TreeDist — Agent Instructions > Project Overview
text:
**TreeDist** is an R package (GPL ≥ 3) providing a suite of topological distance metrics
between phylogenetic trees. The mathematical core is implemented in C++17 and exposed to R
via Rcpp. The primary optimization goal is speed: many real analyses compute pairwise
distances over hundreds or thousands of trees, so inner loops must be tight.

head: TreeDist — Agent Instructions > Project Overview
text:
Current version: `2.12.0.9000` (development).  
CRAN package page: <https://cran.r-project.org/package=TreeDist>

head: TreeDist — Agent Instructions > Repository Layout
text:
**Sibling repository** — `../TreeTools` is a companion package that TreeDist links against
at the C++ level (`LinkingTo: TreeTools`). Edits to TreeTools headers (especially
`SplitList.h`) can affect TreeDist performance and can be pushed to CRAN independently
when ready.

|------|------|---------|

| `lap.h` | 15 KB | **CostMatrix** class; `LapScratch`; `lap()` declarations; cache-aligned storage; `findRowSubmin` hot path |
| `lap.cpp` | 10 KB | Jonker-Volgenant LAPJV linear assignment; extensively hand-optimized; includes only `lap.h` |

head: 后端规范 > PHP 8.5 写法约定
text: - **列表首尾元素**：用 `array_first()` / `array_last()`（空数组返回 null）；不要写 `$xs[array_key_last($xs)]`、`$xs[0] ?? null`，也不要用会移动内部指针的 `end()` / `reset()`。确实需要"键"本身时才用 `array_key_first()` / `array_key_last()`

head: 后端规范 > PHP 8.5 写法约定
text: - **管道运算符 `|>`**：三层以上的单参数函数嵌套链按数据流向书写，如 `array_merge($a, $b) |> array_unique(...) |> array_values(...)`；回调不在首参的函数（`array_map` 等）不必硬套管道，两层以内的嵌套保持原样即可

head: 后端规范 > PHP 8.5 写法约定
text: - **URL host 解析**：凡涉及安全判定（Origin/Referer 白名单、SSRF 校验、host 比对）必须用 `Uri\WhatWg\Url::parse()?->getAsciiHost()`（浏览器同款语义，IDN 归一为 ASCII），**禁止用 `parse_url()` 做安全判定**；非安全场景的普通取值可继续用 `parse_url()`

head: 后端规范 > PHP 8.5 写法约定

text: 注释一律用**直述型**描述当前行为与约束，站在"不了解代码历史的读者"视角写：

head: 注释规范 > 总体风格 > 直述型风格（硬约束）
text: - **禁止历史对比措辞**：不写「改为 / 改成 / 不再 / 此前 / 原来 / 旧版 / 旧逻辑 / 新增了 / 替换了 / 迁移到」等以旧实现为参照的说法；直接陈述现在是什么、为什么必须这样

head: 注释规范 > 总体风格 > 直述型风格（硬约束）
text: - **禁止辩解式注释**：不为"这次改动为什么对"辩护（那是 PR 描述的事）；注释只服务下一个读代码的人

head: 注释规范 > 总体风格 > 直述型风格（硬约束）
text: - 判定标准：一个不知道任何历史的读者读了是否受益；不受益则删除，受益但带历史参照则改写成直述

head: 注释规范 > 总体风格 > 直述型风格（硬约束）
text: - 允许的"时间性"表述：描述**运行时/数据生命周期**的先后（如「撤回后的消息不参与检索」「重投时跳过已投递记录」）不算历史对比；描述**外部系统版本差异**（如浏览器/第三方 API 行为）可保留版本限定语

head: 注释规范 > 总体风格 > 直述型风格（硬约束）

| Service | 类和每个方法都要 PHPDoc；写明封装的职责 |
| Enum | 类级 PHPDoc 说明领域约束或前端用途 |
| Settings | 类级 PHPDoc + 每个 public 字段的字段级 PHPDoc |
| Vue 页面 | 文件顶部 HTML 注释说明业务界面 |
| TS/JS | 文件顶部块注释说明用途 |

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）
text: 宁缺毋滥：覆盖率不是目的，验证真实业务行为/契约才是。以下形态属"为测而测"，不要新增，存量可删：

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）
text: - **同义反复**：断言 config 值等于其自身、容器能解析出某类、断言刚 `set` 的值又读出来比一遍

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）
text: - **断言提示词/常量字符串**：`toContain('某中文词')` 比对 prompt 文本、断言固定文案——改措辞就红却不验证任何行为

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）
text: - **工厂/注册表结构快照**：只断言工厂产出对象的类型/属性、反射读 protected 属性比对（protocol→provider 类映射这类纯分派除外，仍需配一条"未登记即抛"的有效断言）

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）
text: - **弱断言框架行为**：只断言 200/重定向/渲染了某组件/默认值，未触及业务分支或权限

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）
text: - **mock 后只验证 mock 被调用**：mock 业务 Action 再断言其返回值被原样透传

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）
text: - **脆弱守护/基准**：正则扫源码比对 i18n key 是否存在；依赖统计阈值（召回率 `>=0.x`）的基准断言

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）
text: - **判定相反的"高价值"信号（务必保留）**：走真实 HTTP+DB/TNTSearch 的 CRUD/权限/筛选/分页/状态流转；加密落库、token、外部 ID 命名空间等稳定契约；纯函数转换（分词器、分块器、消息映射、变量解析）；AI 功能测试只要断言的是**落库结果**（来源标记、人工值不被覆盖、幻觉值丢弃、阈值过滤）而非提示词，即属高价值

head: 测试规范 > 低价值测试判定（不要写，发现可删）

head: Repository Guidelines > Project Structure & Module Organization
text: The core package lives in `greeum/`, providing the STM/LTM memory managers, graph index logic, and shared utilities. Command-line tooling is under `cli/`, while `api/` exposes the REST/MCP layers used by Claude and other integrations. Reusable examples and smoke assets live in `examples/` and `data/`. Automated documentation, migration notes, and design briefs live under `docs/` and the top-level `*.md` reports. Tests are grouped in `tests/` for pytest suites, with scenario-specific regression harnesses in the `test_*/` directories that mirror production incidents.

head: Repository Guidelines > Coding Style & Naming Conventions
text: Target Python 3.10+ with 4-space indentation, type hints on public APIs, and descriptive snake_case identifiers. The repo favors single-purpose modules and keeps CLI entry points in `cli/*_commands.py`. Run `ruff check .` (line length 120, selected ignores in `pyproject.toml`) before submitting. Use `black .` to normalize formatting and `isort .` to order imports if you touch modules that mix CLI and service layers.

head: Repository Guidelines > Testing Guidelines
text: Place new tests under `tests/` mirroring the package path, and name files `test_<feature>.py`. Prefer `pytest` fixtures for database setup; avoid writing to real `data/` assets—use temporary directories. Keep long-running integration checks behind `@pytest.mark.slow` so `pytest -m "not slow"` stays quick. When altering memory flows or MCP tooling, extend the suites invoked by `run_all_tests.py` to cover regression cases.

head: Repository Guidelines > Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
text: Commits in this project emphasize clear release notes (`Release v3.1.1rc2.dev9: …`) or component tags (`cli:`, `stm:`) followed by an imperative change summary. Structure PRs with a concise description, linked issues, and verification steps (`pytest`, `tox`, or `run_all_tests.py`). Include configuration notes (e.g., env vars, new assets) and screenshots for CLI/API UX changes so agents consuming these docs can quickly validate behavior.

head: Repository Guidelines > Security & Configuration Tips
text: Never commit personal conversation logs or production data; scrub fixtures before upload. Document any required environment variables in the PR (notably `GREEUM_DATA_DIR`, `GREEUM_DISABLE_ST`, and tokens for external embeddings). Store secrets in a local `.env` and load them through `python-dotenv`; avoid hard-coding paths inside modules.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Request Pipeline
text: API routes follow a consistent pattern: `Route → CORS preflight → Zod body validation → Optional auth (extractApiKey/isValidApiKey) → API key policy enforcement → Handler delegation (open-sse)`. No global Next.js middleware — interception is route-specific.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Request Pipeline
text: **Combo routing** (`open-sse/services/combo.ts`): 20 public strategies (priority, weighted, fill-first, round-robin, p2c, random, least-used, cost-optimized, reset-aware, reset-window, headroom, quota-weighted, strict-random, auto, lkgp, context-optimized, cache-optimized, context-relay, fusion, pipeline). Each target calls `handleSingleModel()` which wraps `handleChatCore()` with per-target error handling and circuit breaker checks. The `fusion` strategy is the exception: it fans out to a panel of models in parallel, then a judge model synthesizes one final answer (`open-sse/services/fusion.ts`). See `docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md` for the 16-factor Auto-Combo scoring + the full strategy table and `docs/architecture/RESILIENCE_GUIDE.md` for the 3 resilience layers.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State
text:
OmniRoute has three related but distinct temporary-failure mechanisms. Keep their
scope separate when debugging routing behavior. See the
[3-layer resilience diagram](./docs/diagrams/exported/resilience-3layers.svg)
(source: [docs/diagrams/resilience-3layers.mmd](./docs/diagrams/resilience-3layers.mmd))
for an at-a-glance map.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: **Scope**: whole provider, e.g. `glm`, `openai`, `anthropic`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text:
**Purpose**: stop sending traffic to a provider that is repeatedly failing at the
upstream/service level, so one unhealthy provider does not slow down every request.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: - Core class: `src/shared/utils/circuitBreaker.ts`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: - Chat gate/execution wiring: `src/sse/handlers/chatHelpers.ts`, `src/sse/handlers/chat.ts`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: - Runtime status API: `src/app/api/monitoring/health/route.ts`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: - Shared wrappers: `open-sse/services/accountFallback.ts`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: - Persisted state table: `domain_circuit_breakers`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: **States** (4 — `src/shared/utils/circuitBreaker.ts`):

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: - `CLOSED`: normal traffic is allowed.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text:
- `DEGRADED`: early-warning band — failures crossed the degradation threshold but not the
  breaker threshold yet; traffic still flows, dashboards show the warning.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text:
- `OPEN`: provider is temporarily blocked; callers get a provider-circuit-open response
  or combo routing skips to another target.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text:
- `HALF_OPEN`: reset timeout has elapsed; allow a probe request. Success closes the
  breaker, failure opens it again.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text:
**Defaults** (`open-sse/config/constants.ts` → `PROVIDER_PROFILES`, consumed via
`DEFAULT_RESILIENCE_SETTINGS.providerBreaker` in `src/lib/resilience/settings.ts` →
`getCircuitBreaker(provider, …)` in `src/sse/handlers/chatHelpers.ts`). The whole-provider
breaker runs on `circuitBreakerThreshold` / `circuitBreakerReset`:

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text:
`PROVIDER_PROFILES` also defines `providerFailureThreshold` (10/15/2),
`providerFailureWindowMs` (15/30/5 min) and `providerCooldownMs` (5/10/1 min): these power the
**window gate of the opt-in global Provider Cooldown** (`PROVIDER_COOLDOWN_ENABLED`, default
off) — a provider-level entry in `open-sse/services/providerCooldownTracker.ts` only counts as
cooling after `providerFailureThreshold` failures inside `providerFailureWindowMs`, and then
cools for `providerCooldownMs`. They are NOT the live breaker's thresholds — do not tune them
expecting breaker behavior. Every default is overridable through the
`OMNIROUTE_PROVIDER_BREAKER_*` and `OMNIROUTE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_*` env vars; the
runtime-accurate reference table lives in `docs/architecture/RESILIENCE_GUIDE.md`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text: Only provider-level failure statuses should trip the provider breaker:

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text:
Do not trip the whole-provider breaker for normal account/key/model errors like most
`401`, `403`, or `429` cases. Those usually belong to connection cooldown or model
lockout. A generic API-key provider `403` should be recoverable unless it is classified
as a terminal provider/account error.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Provider Circuit Breaker
text:
The breaker uses lazy recovery, not a background timer. When `OPEN` expires, reads such
as `getStatus()`, `canExecute()`, and `getRetryAfterMs()` refresh the state to
`HALF_OPEN`, so dashboards and combo candidate builders do not keep excluding an
expired provider forever.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: **Scope**: one provider connection/account/key.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text:
**Purpose**: temporarily skip one bad key/account while allowing other connections for
the same provider to continue serving requests.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: - Write/update path: `src/sse/services/auth.ts::markAccountUnavailable()`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: - Account selection/filtering: `src/sse/services/auth.ts::getProviderCredentials...`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: - Cooldown calculation: `open-sse/services/accountFallback.ts::checkFallbackError()`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: - Settings: `src/lib/resilience/settings.ts`

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: Important fields on provider connections:

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: During account selection, a connection is skipped while:

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text:
Cooldowns are also lazy: when `rateLimitedUntil` is in the past, the connection becomes
eligible again. On successful use, `clearAccountError()` clears `testStatus`,
`rateLimitedUntil`, error fields, and `backoffLevel`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: Default connection cooldown behavior:

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: - OAuth base cooldown: `5s`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text: - API-key base cooldown: `3s`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text:
- API-key `429` should prefer upstream retry hints (`Retry-After`, reset headers, or
  parseable reset text) when available.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text:
- Repeated recoverable failures use exponential backoff:
```ts
baseCooldownMs * 2 ** failureIndex;
```

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text:
The anti-thundering-herd guard prevents concurrent failures on the same connection from
repeatedly extending the cooldown or double-incrementing `backoffLevel`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Connection Cooldown
text:
Terminal states are not cooldowns. `banned`, `expired` (which becomes terminal only after N bounded retries via `EXPIRED_RETRY_MAX`), and `credits_exhausted` are
intended to stay unavailable until credentials/settings change or an operator resets
them. Do not overwrite terminal states with transient cooldown state.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Model Lockout
text: **Scope**: provider + connection + model.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Model Lockout
text:
**Purpose**: avoid disabling a whole connection when only one model is unavailable or
quota-limited for that connection.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Model Lockout
text: - Per-model quota providers returning `429`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Model Lockout
text: - Local providers returning `404` for one missing model.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Model Lockout
text: - Provider-specific mode/model permission failures such as selected Grok modes.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Model Lockout
text:
Model lockout lives in `open-sse/services/accountFallback.ts` and lets the same
connection continue serving other models.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Debugging Guidance
text:
- If all keys for a provider are skipped, inspect both provider breaker state and each
  connection's `rateLimitedUntil`/`testStatus`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Debugging Guidance
text:
- If a provider appears permanently excluded after the reset window, check whether code
  is reading raw `state` instead of using `getStatus()`/`canExecute()`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Debugging Guidance
text:
- If one provider key fails but others should work, prefer connection cooldown over
  provider breaker.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Debugging Guidance
text: - If only one model fails, prefer model lockout over connection cooldown.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Resilience Runtime State > Debugging Guidance
text:
- If a state should self-recover, it should have a future timestamp/reset timeout and a
  read path that refreshes expired state. Permanent statuses require manual credential
  or config changes.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > File placement & repo-root hygiene
text: When creating _any_ validation tests or one-off logic scripts, default to `scripts/ad-hoc/` or `tests/unit/` according to your goals. Do not pollute the `/` root context.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > File placement & repo-root hygiene
text:
- **Root `_*` paths are private and NEVER tracked** (`_tasks/`, `_references/`, `_mono_repo/`,
  `_ideia/`, `_cache/` and any future `_<name>`): they live on disk only, are gitignored by the
  anchored patterns `/_*/` + `/_*`, and some are full git repositories of their own (`_tasks` →
  private remote `_tasks_omniroute`). Never `git add` anything inside them (a plain `add` is
  already blocked by the ignore; never use `-f`), and never "clean them up" from the main repo —
  untracking is done with `git rm --cached` so the disk content stays. The
  `check:tracked-artifacts` gate (pre-commit + CI) fails on ANY tracked root path starting with
  `_`, present or future. See Hard Rule #23 for the `_tasks` specifics.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Key Conventions > Error Handling

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Key Conventions > Security
text: - **Never** use `eval()`, `new Function()`, or implied eval

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Key Conventions > Security
text: - Validate all inputs with Zod schemas

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Key Conventions > Security
text: - Encrypt credentials at rest (AES-256-GCM); never log SQLite encryption keys

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Key Conventions > Security
text: - **Public upstream credentials** (for example, OAuth client_id/secret values or Firebase Web keys extracted from public CLIs): **MUST** be embedded via `resolvePublicCred()` from `open-sse/utils/publicCreds.ts` — **never** as string literals. See `docs/security/PUBLIC_CREDS.md` for the mandatory pattern.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Key Conventions > Security
text: - **Error responses** (HTTP / SSE / executor / MCP handler): **MUST** route through `buildErrorBody()` or `sanitizeErrorMessage()` from `open-sse/utils/error.ts` — **never** put raw `err.stack` or `err.message` in a response body. See `docs/security/ERROR_SANITIZATION.md`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Key Conventions > Security
text: - **Shell commands built from variables**: when calling `exec()`/`spawn()` with a script that needs runtime values, pass them via the `env` option (shell-escaped automatically) — **never** string-interpolate untrusted/external paths into the script body. Reference: `src/mitm/cert/install.ts::updateNssDatabases`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Key Conventions > Security
text: - **Secure-by-default libraries** ([tldrsec/awesome-secure-defaults](https://github.com/tldrsec/awesome-secure-defaults)): prefer Helmet.js, DOMPurify, ssrf-req-filter, safe-regex, Google Tink over custom implementations whenever adding new security-sensitive surfaces.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: **PR rule**: If you change production code in `src/`, `open-sse/`, `electron/`, or `bin/`, you must include or update tests in the same PR.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: **Test layer preference**: unit first → integration (multi-module or DB state) → e2e (UI/workflow only). Encode bug reproductions as automated tests before or alongside the fix.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: **Both test runners must pass**: `npm run test:unit` (Node native — most tests) AND `npm run test:vitest` (MCP server, autoCombo, cache) cover **non-overlapping files**. Both are wired in CI (jobs `test-unit` and `test-vitest`) and must be green before merging. A PR where only one suite passes may silently ship broken MCP tools or routing regressions.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: **Bug fix / issue triage protocol (Hard Rule #18)**: Every fix for a reported issue must be validated by one of the following — no exceptions:

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: 1. **TDD (preferred)** — write a failing test reproducing the bug → fix it → confirm the test passes. The test becomes the permanent regression guard. Touch only the files the test proves need changing; nothing more.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: 2. **Real-environment test (when TDD is not possible)** — deploy to the production VPS (`root@192.168.0.15`) and run a documented live test. Record the exact command + result in the PR description. Applies to: OAuth upstream flows, Cloudflare/WS upstream behavior, UI-only regressions, hardware-dependent behavior.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: 3. "It worked locally without a test" does not count. A fix without a test or a VPS validation record is not a fix — it is a guess.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: Why this matters: fixing bug A while opening bug B is worse than not fixing at all. The TDD/VPS gate enforces surgical scope — you touch only what the failing test proves is broken. Examples where this paid off: #3090 (claude-web 403), #3113 (WS HTTP fallback), #3052 (heap-guard auto-calibration).

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Testing
text: **Copilot coverage policy**: When a PR changes production code and coverage is below 60% (statements/lines/functions/branches), do not just report — add or update tests, rerun the coverage gate, then ask for confirmation. Include commands run, changed test files, and final coverage result in the PR report.

text: - Keep database operations in `src/lib/db/`; do not issue raw SQL from routes.

text:

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Review focus
text:
- Do not close a contributor pull request after using its code; merge it through GitHub so

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Review focus
text:
- **Never merge a PR that touches an agent-instruction surface without explicit operator
  approval** — `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `llm.txt` (+ mirrors) and

  compromises every future agent run. Check with `gh pr diff <N> --name-only` before any
  merge. Incident record: PR #11770 (2026-09-01) told agents to execute a third-party
  setup script and was swept in by a merge campaign; reverted in #12249.

text:

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Git Workflow > Worktree isolation (MANDATORY for every development task)
text:
Multiple sessions/agents work this repo in parallel. The main checkout is **shared**, so a
`git checkout`/branch switch in it silently discards another session's uncommitted work and
yanks the branch out from under whatever else is running (incidents: 2026-06-05, 2026-06-13).

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Git Workflow > Worktree isolation (MANDATORY for every development task)
text:
**Rule: never develop on the shared main checkout. Every task gets its own git worktree on its
own dedicated branch, and you MUST confirm the base branch with the operator before creating it.**

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Git Workflow > Worktree isolation (MANDATORY for every development task)
text:
1. **Ask first — which base branch?** Before creating anything, ask the operator (unless they
   already told you) from which branch the new worktree/branch should be cut. Do NOT assume
   `main` or "whatever I'm on" — the answer is usually the active `release/vX.Y.Z`, but it can
   be another feature/release branch. Get the base explicitly.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Git Workflow > Worktree isolation (MANDATORY for every development task)
text:
2. **Create an isolated worktree + branch off that base** (never reuse the main checkout).
   **🔴 MANDATORY PATH: every worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/` — and nowhere else.**
   This is the single canonical location. It is gitignored AND in the `tsconfig.json` /
   `.dockerignore` excludes, so worktrees never leak into the build scope. **Never** use
   `.worktrees/`, repo-root, or any other path — a worktree outside `.claude/worktrees/`
   (a) escapes the build-scope excludes and poisons `next build` (the `tsconfig`
   `include: **/*` globs ~70× the codebase → OOM; incident 2026-06-25) and (b) scatters
   worktrees across two dirs.
   ```bash
   BASE_BRANCH="release/vX.Y.Z"          # ← the branch the operator confirmed in step 1
   TASK="feat/your-feature"               # feat/ fix/ refactor/ docs/ test/ chore/
   git fetch origin "$BASE_BRANCH"
   git worktree add ".claude/worktrees/${TASK##*/}" -b "$TASK" "origin/$BASE_BRANCH"
   cd ".claude/worktrees/${TASK##*/}"
   # Reuse the main checkout's node_modules to skip a per-worktree npm install.
   # HARD LINKS (`cp -al`), never a symlink: ~5s for the whole tree and near-zero extra
   # disk (the inodes are shared), and unlike a symlink it does not break the dev server.
   cp -al "$(git -C <main_checkout> rev-parse --show-toplevel)/node_modules" node_modules
   # `.husky/_` is gitignored, so a fresh worktree does NOT have it and
   # `core.hooksPath=.husky/_` then points at a directory that does not exist —
   # every pre-commit gate goes silently mute. Copy it too.
   cp -a "$(git -C <main_checkout> rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.husky/_" .husky/_
   ```
   `scripts/dev/new-worktree.sh <branch> [base]` does all of the above (canonical path,
   hard-linked `node_modules`, `.husky/_`) and then **verifies** the hook is actually
   executable, so prefer it over running the steps by hand.
   **Never `ln -s` node_modules.** Turbopack rejects a symlink that resolves outside the
   project root, so `npm run dev` dies with a FATAL panic (`Symlink [project]/node_modules

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Git Workflow > Worktree isolation (MANDATORY for every development task)
text:
**A worktree without `.husky/_` runs NO pre-commit gate — and says nothing.** `git`
   resolves `core.hooksPath` relative to the worktree top; when the directory is missing it
   simply finds no hook and commits. Nothing is printed, the commit succeeds, and the
   identity/lint/docs gates never ran. This is how 59 commits carrying a stale identity
   override (name of a contributor + the maintainer's e-mail) got past
   `scripts/check/check-git-identity.sh` between 2026-08-29 and 09-02 — they were all made in
   `cp -al` worktrees. Verify with `ls .husky/_/pre-commit` inside a new worktree, or just use
   `scripts/dev/new-worktree.sh`, which fails loudly when the hook is not executable.

Before cutting a branch, merging the base into a PR branch, mass-retargeting PRs, or opening a

(`.github/workflows/nightly-release-green.yml`) publishes the verdict in a single deduplicated

If the base is red: never treat the inherited failures as your branch's defect; never "fix" them

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Git Workflow > Sync-back landings are fast-forward, never squash
text:
A `main → release/vX+1` sync-back (Phase 5 of `/generate-release`, or any later "bring main's
post-release commits over" PR) must reach the release branch as the merge commit it already is:
`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/release/vX+1 <head>` then
`git push origin <head>:refs/heads/release/vX+1` (GitHub marks the PR merged). Squash-merging it
drops `main` from the release branch's ancestry and the next sync-back re-conflicts on every file
main touched (551 conflicts on the v3.8.50 → v3.8.51 sync before the two-step merge). After
landing, `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main origin/release/vX+1` must be true — and check
that `config/quality/eslint-suppressions.json` / `quality-baseline.json` carried main's freezes
(they merge as "ours" silently). Details: `.agents/skills/generate-release/phases/phase-5-next-cycle.md`.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Environment
text: - **Runtime**: Node.js ≥22.22.2 <23 || ≥24.0.0 <27, ES Modules. This is the **only supported** runtime for the published `omniroute` CLI, the server, and the test suites (`node:test` + vitest) — `engines.node` is authoritative and end users never need Bun. A **best-effort `bun:sqlite` compatibility path** exists so a global Bun install (`bun install -g omniroute`) can start without `better-sqlite3` (driver adapter + Bun-aware process spawning); it is **not** a supported runtime — no support guarantees — and every Bun-specific runtime change MUST preserve the Node driver/fallback chain and ship a Bun test (`test:bun:db`) or an explicit reason why the path is Node-only.

head: OmniRoute agent guide > Environment
text: - **Bun (build/dev script runner + compatibility smoke only)**: Bun `1.4.2` is pinned as an **exact devDependency** (provisioned through the existing `npm ci` via the lockfile's `@oven/bun-*` platform binaries — no `setup-bun`/ad-hoc install). It is used **only** to execute a small, allow-listed set of TypeScript **gate/generator scripts** (replacing `node --import tsx` for startup speed): the CI checks `check:provider-consistency`, `check:compression-budget`, `check:known-symbols`, and the non-CI `gen:provider-reference`, `bench:compression` — plus the focused `test:bun:db` compatibility smoke suite for the best-effort `bun:sqlite` path. **Do NOT** widen Bun to `npm install`, the build (`build:cli*`), `check:pack-artifact`, the supported published runtime, or the main test runners — those stay on Node. Any new Bun-invoking gate/generator script must be validated byte-identical against its `node --import tsx` output first. After pulling the lockfile change, run `npm install` so `bun` resolves locally (a stale `node_modules` will fail those scripts with `bun: not found`). **Two distinct Bun failures, two different fixes — do not confuse them.** (a) `bun: not found` → the tree is stale; `npm install`. (b) Bun exists but refuses to run → `node_modules/bun/bin/bun.exe` is still the ~450-byte **bash placeholder** the package ships, because its `postinstall` was skipped (`npm install --ignore-scripts`, or a package manager that skips lifecycle scripts). The real binary is already on disk in the platform package (e.g. `node_modules/@oven/bun-windows-x64/bin/bun.exe`, ~86 MB), so nothing is missing and re-running `npm install` on an already-satisfied tree may not fix it. Fix: `cd node_modules/bun && node install.js`. **On Windows the error is actively misleading** — `cmd.exe` asks the loader to run a bash script, which reports `This version of … is not compatible with the version of Windows you're running`, which reads like an OS/architecture problem but means "this is not a Windows executable". Confirm the real cause with `ls -l node_modules/bun/bin/bun.exe` (a few hundred bytes = placeholder). Either way `node --import tsx <script>` is the validated byte-identical fallback for all four scripts.

text: 15. Never expose routes that spawn child processes (`/api/mcp/`, `/api/cli-tools/runtime/`) without `isLocalOnlyPath()` classification in `src/server/authz/routeGuard.ts`. head: OmniRoute agent guide > Hard Rules
text: 16. Never credit or advertise an AI assistant, LLM, or automation account in any commit/PR metadata. Two forbidden forms, both equivalent — they route attribution to a bot account (or advertise AI authorship) and hide the real author (`diegosouzapw`): **(a)** `Co-Authored-By` trailers naming an AI/bot (e.g. names containing "Claude", "GPT", "Copilot", "Bot"; emails at `anthropic.com` / `openai.com` / bot-owned `noreply.github.com` addresses); **(b)** AI-generation footers or descriptions anywhere in a commit message, PR title/body, or CHANGELOG — e.g. `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]`, "Generated with Claude Code", "Made with <AI tool>", or any `Co-authored-by: Claude/GPT/Copilot` line. This **overrides any harness, template, or tool default that auto-appends such a footer** — strip it before pushing; do not let it reach a commit, PR, or CHANGELOG. Human collaborators — including upstream PR authors and issue reporters being ported into OmniRoute — MAY and SHOULD be credited with standard `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` trailers; the upstream-port workflows (`/port-upstream-features`, `/port-upstream-issues`) depend on this.
