head: CLAUDE.md > Project Overview
text: This is a monorepo for a web-based procedural geometry system that allows users to create complex 3D geometry using a visual node editor with AI-powered generation capabilities. The main application is a Next.js 15 app with React 19, Three.js for 3D rendering, and ReactFlow for the node-based interface.

head: CLAUDE.md > Essential Commands > Environment Setup
text: - Node.js 22.x required (specified in package.json engines)

head: CLAUDE.md > Essential Commands > Environment Setup
text: - Create `.env.local` in `apps/web/` with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` for AI features

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Core Architecture Pattern
text: The application follows a modular component-based architecture with clear separation of concerns:

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Core Architecture Pattern
text:
1. **Node Registry System** (`apps/web/app/registry/NodeRegistry.ts`)
   - Central registry managing all node definitions (30+ built-in nodes)
   - Supports dynamic node registration and custom JSON-based nodes
   - Type-safe socket connections with validation

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Core Architecture Pattern
text:
2. **AI Agent System** (`apps/web/app/agent/GeometryAIAgent.ts`)
   - Handles AI-powered node and scene generation via OpenRouter
   - Streaming responses with real-time integration
   - Multiple model support (Claude, GPT-4, Gemini)

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Core Architecture Pattern
text:
3. **Context-Based State Management**
   - GeometryContext: Manages 3D geometry state and operations
   - NodeContext: Handles node graph state and connections
   - TimeContext: Controls animation and time-based parameters
   - Multiple UI contexts for modals, logging, and layout

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Core Architecture Pattern
text:
4. **Type System** (`apps/web/app/types/`)
   - Comprehensive TypeScript definitions for all geometry types
   - Socket type compatibility matrix
   - Parameter validation schemas

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Key Architectural Decisions
text: - **Monorepo with Turborepo**: Enables efficient builds and parallel development

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Key Architectural Decisions
text: - **App Router (Next.js 15)**: Modern React Server Components architecture

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Key Architectural Decisions
text: - **Three.js Integration**: React Three Fiber for declarative 3D rendering

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Key Architectural Decisions
text: - **ReactFlow**: Provides the visual node editor with custom node implementations

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Key Architectural Decisions
text: - **Tailwind CSS v4**: Modern utility-first styling with CSS variables

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Key Architectural Decisions
text: - **Clerk Authentication**: Middleware-based route protection

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Node System Implementation
text: 1. Node definitions are in `apps/web/app/registry/nodes/`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Node System Implementation
text: 2. Each node implements the `NodeDefinition` interface

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Node System Implementation
text: 3. Nodes must be registered in `apps/web/app/registry/nodes/index.ts`

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > Node System Implementation
text: 4. Custom nodes can be added via JSON definitions without code changes

text: - `/api/ai/generate-node`: Creates new nodes from prompts

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture & Key Systems > API Routes Structure
text: - `/api/ai/generate-scene`: Generates complete scenes

text: - `/api/ai/modify-node`: Modifies existing nodes

text: - `/api/ai/modify-scene`: Updates scene configurations

head: AGENTS.md
text: OpenCode plugin that adds the Google Gemini Antigravity CLI (`agy`) OAuth provider with dual compatibility for both OpenCode v1 and OpenCode v2 runtimes. This plugin intercepts `@ai-sdk/google` requests and rewrites them to the Antigravity Code Assist endpoint with OAuth bearer auth, project context resolution, and server-supplied model enum mapping. The plugin ships its own `agy_quota` and `agy_quota_summary` tools as well as CLI quota commands.

head: AGENTS.md > Dual v1 and v2 Architecture
text: The package exports a single composite default export from `index.ts` that provides simultaneous support for OpenCode v1 and OpenCode v2 runtimes without requiring separate packages.

head: AGENTS.md > Dual v1 and v2 Architecture > Runtime execution paths
text: - **OpenCode v1 (>= 1.18.29)**: The v1 runtime loads the default export and invokes the `server(options)` hook. This returns the v1 plugin object (`config`, `tool`, `auth`) defined in `src/plugin.ts`. Older v1 versions prior to 1.18.29 only supported function exports; 1.18.29 and newer support object exports with `server()`.

head: AGENTS.md > Dual v1 and v2 Architecture > Runtime execution paths
text:
- **OpenCode v2**: The v2 runtime inspects the default export for `id` and executes `setup(ctx)`. This adapter is orchestrated in `src/plugin/v2.ts` (using contracts defined in `src/plugin/types.ts`) and decomposed into modular units under `src/plugin/`:
  - `src/plugin/oauth-authorize.ts`: registers the `google-agy` OAuth integration method with PKCE flow.
  - `src/plugin/v2-fetch.ts`: `createV2FetchInterceptor` intercepts AI SDK client initialization (`ctx.aisdk.hook("sdk", ...)`) to inject dummy `apiKey` and handle Code Assist transformations.
  - `src/plugin/v2-session.ts`: session hooks `http.request`, `http.response`, and `retry` handle request rewriting, streaming transformation, and backoff.
  - `src/plugin/v2-storage.ts`: dual auth storage helpers reading and writing credentials to `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` alongside v2 auth store.
  - `src/plugin/headers.ts`: shared safe HTTP header and URL parsing utilities across v1 and v2.
  - `src/plugin/tier.ts`: shared model definitions (`STATIC_MODELS_SIMPLE`, `TIER_MAPPING`) and tier resolution (`resolveModelTier`).
  - `src/plugin/quota.ts` & `src/plugin/quota-summary.ts`: tool definitions and v2 command mappings (`agy-quota`, `agy-quota-summary`).

head: AGENTS.md > Dual v1 and v2 Architecture > Runtime execution paths
text:
- **Shared engine layer**: Both v1 and v2 adapters delegate all underlying business logic to `src/sdk/`:
  - Request preparation and endpoint transformations (`src/sdk/request/`)
  - Quota fetching and telemetry (`src/sdk/fetch_quota.ts`, `src/plugin/quota.ts`, `src/plugin/quota-summary.ts`)
  - Backoff retry algorithms and error parsing (`src/sdk/retry/`)
  - Models catalog resolution via `models.json` (`src/sdk/fetch_models.ts`, `src/sdk/request/prepare.ts`)
  - OAuth credentials and project context (`src/plugin/project/context.ts`)

head: AGENTS.md > Dual v1 and v2 Architecture > Capability mapping across versions
text:
| Capability | OpenCode v1 (`src/plugin.ts`) | OpenCode v2 (`src/plugin/v2.ts`) |
|---|---|---|
| Entrypoint | `server(options)` hook | `setup(ctx)` via `Plugin.define` / `defineOpenCodeV2Plugin` |
| Models & Provider | `config.provider[AGY_PROVIDER_ID] = ...` | `ctx.catalog.transform((catalog) => ...)` |
| OAuth Integration & Flow | `auth.loader` + custom OAuth flow | `ctx.integration.transform((editor) => { editor.add(...) })` with PKCE authorization and callback token exchange |
| AI SDK Configuration | Injected via custom fetch in provider | `ctx.aisdk.hook("sdk", ...)` injecting dummy apiKey and fetch interceptor |
| Tools (`agy_quota`, `agy_quota_summary`) | `tool` map in returned plugin object | `ctx.tool.transform((editor) => { editor.add(...) })` |
| Commands (`agy-quota`, `agy-quota-summary`) | `config.command[AGY_QUOTA_COMMAND] = ...` | `ctx.command.transform((editor) => { editor.add(...) })` |
| Request interception | `auth.loader` returning custom `fetch` | `ctx.session.hook("http.request", ...)` |
| Response handling | Custom fetch response wrapper | `ctx.session.hook("http.response", ...)` |
| Retry & backoff | Custom retry loop inside `fetch` interceptor | `ctx.session.hook("retry", ...)` |
| Credential Storage | `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` | Shared fallback reads/writes `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` alongside v2 auth store |

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: When a new `agy` CLI release lands (check `https://github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli/releases`), execute every step in sequence without skipping.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: **CRITICAL MANDATE**: Always audit backend and protocol additions. Upstream release notes primarily highlight user-facing UI changes, but minor/patch releases frequently introduce unannounced backend protocol updates, internal RPC routes, header adjustments, or payload schema changes. Never assume a bump is client-only without performing the full binary and server inspection.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 1. **Install or upgrade CLI locally**: Ensure `agy --version` matches the target release.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 2. **Audit changelog & release notes**: Read `https://github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli/releases/tag/<VERSION>` (note: tag is `<version>` without "v" prefix, e.g. `0.1.2`). Identify upstream bug fixes, protocol changes, new request parameters, error handling adjustments, or server-side capabilities.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 3. **Inspect local agy binary**: Run `strings $(readlink -f $(which agy)) | grep -E 'v1internal|daily-cloudcode|CodeAssist'` to discover internal RPC routes, header adjustments, or payload changes. Diffing binary strings against the previous version reveals unannounced backend protocol changes.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 4. **Inspect server response payloads & error structures**: Check live HTTP error payloads and retry headers (`retry-after-ms`, `error.details[]` structures like `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.RetryInfo` or `QuotaFailure`). Test live quota calls with the `agy_quota` and `agy_quota_summary` tools to confirm server schema compatibility.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 5. **Reconcile against surface review checklist**: Systematically cross-reference the [Surface review checklist](#surface-review-checklist) to verify whether any plugin component requires updates for new capabilities, endpoints, or error codes.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 6. **Report analysis findings**: Explicitly report findings to the user. State clearly whether actionable features or protocol adjustments exist to implement, or confirm with evidence that all upstream changes are client-only (e.g. CLI UI, terminal rendering, keyring handling).

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 7. **Implement relevant plugin adjustments**: If actionable backend fixes or protocol changes were discovered in steps 2-6, implement and test them before bumping constants.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 8. **Update version constants**: Update `src/sdk/agy-cli-version.ts` (`AGY_CLI_VERSION`) and `scripts/fetch-models.mjs` (`AGY_API_VERSION`) to the new version. This sets the `User-Agent` header on every Code Assist API request.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 9. **Update release config**: Update `.release-please-config.json` (`"release-as"` field) to the new version. Do **not** touch `.release-please-manifest.json`; release-please manages it automatically on PR merge.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 10. **Update NPM dependencies**: Proactively invoke the `dependency-upgrade` skill to audit and upgrade dependencies. Run `npm outdated` to identify all pending patch, minor, and major updates. Upgrade outdated dependencies (evaluate breaking changes for majors like Vitest, `@opencode-ai/*`, `@ai-sdk/*`, `@types/node`). Run `npm test` immediately after upgrading dependencies to verify backward compatibility and test stability before proceeding. (`@ai-sdk/google` is only a literal string reference in `src/plugin.ts`, so version bumps are zero-risk).

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 11. **Refresh model catalog & register models**: Run `npm run models:refresh` and verify diff (see [Refreshing models.json](#refreshing-modelsjson)). If new models appear (e.g. in `.models` or `agentModelSorts`), register them in `STATIC_MODELS_SIMPLE` and `TIER_MAPPING` in `src/plugin.ts` (see [Registering models in src/plugin.ts](#registering-models-in-srcplugints)). Also prune models from `STATIC_MODELS_SIMPLE` and `TIER_MAPPING` that are no longer usable or returned by the upstream `agy models` CLI command.

head: AGENTS.md > agy CLI bump workflow
text: 12. **Run full verification suite**: Execute `npm install && npm run test:coverage && npm run typecheck && npm run build && npm run smoke:node-import`. All tests and quality gates must pass cleanly.

text: Prior bump commits follow a consistent pattern. Run `git log --oneline | grep "bump agy cli"` for examples.

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: `models.json` is the Antigravity Code Assist internal model catalog returned by the `fetchAvailableModels` server API. It is **not** the same as the public-facing `agy models` command output, which is a filtered subset. The plugin's `src/sdk/request/prepare.ts` reads `models.json` at runtime to resolve model enum placeholders via `getModelEnum`.

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: 1. Reads `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` and extracts the `google-agy.refresh` field, whose format is `refreshToken|projectId|managedProjectId`.

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: 2. Refreshes the OAuth access token via `POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` using `AGY_CLIENT_ID` and `AGY_CLIENT_SECRET` (same values as `src/constants.ts`).

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: 3. Calls `POST https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:fetchAvailableModels` with body `{"project": managedProjectId}`.

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: 4. Writes the response (pretty-printed, 2-space indent) to `models.json` at the repo root.

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: - `--endpoint <url>`: override the Code Assist endpoint (default `https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`).

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: - `--output <path>`: write to a different file (default `models.json` at repo root).

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: - `--verbose`: emit progress to stderr.

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json
text: The script uses Node's built-in `fetch` (HTTP/2 capable). This is required because curl's HTTP/1.0 fallback fails due to network-level stream resets when sending the `Authorization` header against Google APIs from certain network environments; Node's HTTP/2 stream multiplexing handles it correctly.

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json > Verifying a refresh
text: After running `models:refresh`, diff old vs new `models.json` to identify:

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json > Verifying a refresh
text: - Model additions or removals in `.models` keys.

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json > Verifying a refresh
text: - Changes to `.defaultAgentModelId` (the agy CLI's default model).

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json > Verifying a refresh
text: - Changes to `.tieredModelIds.flash` (the tiered-flash parent model id, rotates across releases).

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json > Verifying a refresh
text: - New `.deprecatedModelIds` entries (model enum migrations).

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json > Verifying a refresh
text: - Changes to `.agentModelSorts[0].groups[0].modelIds` (the user-visible recommended list).

head: AGENTS.md > Refreshing models.json > Verifying a refresh
text: Always verify that `.deprecatedModelIds` for `gemini-3.1-pro-high` (mapping to `gemini-pro-agent` with enum `MODEL_PLACEHOLDER_M16`) is preserved. The plugin's `src/sdk/request/shared.ts:10` hardcodes a fallback rewrite of `gemini-3.1-pro-high` to `gemini-pro-agent`, which depends on this deprecation entry being present in `models.json` so `prepare.ts` `getModelEnum` resolves the correct enum.

head: AGENTS.md > Registering models in src/plugin.ts
text: When new user-facing models are added to `models.json` (for example, new series entries like `gemini-3.8-flash` or major releases appearing in `agentModelSorts[0].groups[0].modelIds`), register them in `src/plugin.ts` so OpenCode exposes them:

head: AGENTS.md > Registering models in src/plugin.ts
text:
1. **Add to `STATIC_MODELS_SIMPLE`**:
   - Define model key (e.g. `gemini-3.8-flash`) with `name`, `limit: { context: 1048576, output: 65536 }`, and default fallback `cost`.

head: AGENTS.md > Registering models in src/plugin.ts
text:
2. **Add to `TIER_MAPPING`**:
   - Map tier aliases (`low`, `medium`, `high`) to the underlying model ID string (e.g. `low: "gemini-3.8-flash-low"`, `medium: "gemini-3.8-flash-medium"`, `high: "gemini-3.8-flash-high"`).

head: AGENTS.md > Registering models in src/plugin.ts
text:
3. **Add unit test assertions**:
   - Update `test/plugin/plugin.test.ts` to assert that the newly registered model ID exists in provider models.

head: AGENTS.md > Registering models in src/plugin.ts
text: Note: internal preview strings or non-user-facing endpoints (like `chat_*` or internal tab models) should only remain in `models.json` for server enum mapping and do not need registration in `STATIC_MODELS_SIMPLE`.

head: AGENTS.md > Important distinctions
text: - `agy models` (or `agy --output-format stream-json models`) returns the public-facing filtered model IDs (e.g., `gemini-3.5-flash-low`). This is the list users see in the CLI's model picker.

head: AGENTS.md > Important distinctions
text: - The `fetchAvailableModels` API returns the full internal catalog including preview/internal models (e.g., `chat_20706`, `tab_flash_lite_preview`, `gemini-3.6-flash-tiered` with no `displayName`). This is what the plugin's `prepare.ts` reads at runtime.

head: AGENTS.md > Important distinctions
text: - Only `models.json` is used by the plugin at runtime; the `agy models` output is informational and not consumed by the plugin code.

head: AGENTS.md > Important distinctions
text: - `@ai-sdk/google` is never imported; it is only used as a literal npm-name string at `src/plugin.ts:179` and `src/plugin.ts:438`. Version bumps to this package are zero-risk regardless of API changes in the upstream package.

head: AGENTS.md > Important distinctions
text: - The plugin's OAuth token storage lives at `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` under the `google-agy` key. The agy CLI itself uses the OS keyring directly; the opencode plugin maintains its own auth storage for portability.

head: AGENTS.md > Important distinctions
text: - **Client Credentials**: `AGY_CLIENT_SECRET` in `src/constants.ts` and `scripts/fetch-models.mjs` is Google's public OAuth client secret for the Antigravity desktop/CLI OAuth client (RFC 8252 public client). It is embedded directly in the upstream binary distribution and is not a confidential server secret. Do not rotate or redact it without updating the paired public `AGY_CLIENT_ID`.

head: AGENTS.md > Important distinctions
text: - **Thinking / CoT Support**: Tiered Gemini models (`gemini-3.7/3.8-flash-high/medium`) currently have thinking suppressed by the upstream Code Assist server over SSE (it performs internal reasoning but does not stream raw `thought: true` parts back to the client, unlike Claude thinking models). When Google enables streaming thoughts for Flash tiers in future Code Assist protocol updates, add client response stream parsing and configuration support for them.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas
text: - `.release-please-manifest.json` is auto-managed by release-please; do not manually edit it.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas
text: - When the agy CLI is not logged in (`agy --version` works but `agy` interactive fails with "could not open TTY"), the `agy models` command still works and returns a cached or session-less model list.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas
text: - curl may show `HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request` from a network security appliance intercepting `Authorization`-header requests against Google APIs. Use Node `fetch` instead (HTTP/2 stream multiplexing works correctly through such appliances). This is why `scripts/fetch-models.mjs` uses Node's built-in `fetch` rather than shelling out to `curl`.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas
text: - The `managedProjectId` (third pipe-separated field of the refresh token, e.g., `citric-engine-kl9s4`) is the value passed as the `project` body parameter to `fetchAvailableModels`, not the user-facing project ID. The user-facing project ID (second field, e.g., `tone-workspace-cli`) is not directly accepted by the API.

head: AGENTS.md > Gotchas
text: - A fresh `fetchAvailableModels` response will overwrite the entire `models.json` file. Diff old vs new before committing to catch any unintended server-side removals. Pay particular attention to the `deprecatedModelIds` entry for `gemini-3.1-pro-high` which the plugin's `shared.ts:10` fallback depends on.

head: CLAUDE.md > What this is
text:
`voi` is a feature-voting / public-roadmap app (Canny-style). Users submit
posts, vote on them, and admins move posts through statuses
(`REVIEW → PLANNED → IN_PROGRESS → RELEASED / DISCARDED`).

  react-hook-form + zod (forms)

head: CLAUDE.md > Commands
text:
There is **no test runner configured** — no `test` script, no Jest/Vitest/Playwright
installed. If asked to "run the tests" or to follow strict TDD, flag this and ask
whether to add the toolchain rather than pretending tests exist.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **`app/`** — App Router. `app/(main)/` is the auth-gated route group (dashboard,
  profile). `app/api/` holds the Better Auth catch-all (`auth/[...all]/route.ts`),
  plus `search/` and `votes/count/`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **`components/ui/`** — shadcn primitives. Don't hand-edit; regenerate via
  `pnpm ui add <name>`. **`components/client/`** — feature-level client islands,
  every file is `'use client'`. **`components/icons/`** — icon barrel.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **`services/`** — Server Actions (`'use server'`): `posts.ts`, `users.ts`,
  `votes.ts`. Each action calls `getSession()` from `@/lib/auth` for authz and
  `revalidatePath()` after mutations. **Mutations live here, not in API routes.**

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:
- **`lib/auth.ts`** — Better Auth server config (OTP + admin plugin) + `getSession()`.
  **`lib/auth-client.ts`** — `authClient` for React (`useSession`, `signIn`,
  `signOut`, `emailOtp`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text: - **`lib/prisma.ts`** — Prisma singleton with `globalThis` dev-mode caching.

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture

  `use-loading`).

head: CLAUDE.md > Architecture
text:

  (Better Auth tables), `Post`, `Vote`, `Tag`. The `Status` enum drives the roadmap.

head: CLAUDE.md > Quirks that bite
text:

  Import from `@/prisma/client/client` (types + `PrismaClient`) and

head: CLAUDE.md > Quirks that bite
text:
- **`pnpm dev` is not just `next dev`** — it runs
  `pnpm compose up -d && pnpm watch && pnpm compose stop`. So `Ctrl+C` tears down
  Postgres + Mailpit. Use `pnpm dev:next` if you want the Next process alone.

  console fallback.

text: - Target protocol is DPS v1.01 / Padrão Nacional, not ABRASF 2.03, RPS, SOAP, or WSDL.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior
text:
- Em homologação, envio, consulta de NFSe e eventos usam a base
  `https://preprod-nfseapi.ima.sp.gov.br/notafiscal-ws/nfse`.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior
text:
- Em produção, a base é `https://nfseapi.campinas.sp.gov.br/notafiscal-ws/nfse`, com ativação em 21/09/2026 conforme
  o guia oficial atualizado em 18/09/2026; consulte `docs/references/v3/README.md` para fontes e divergências da
  página técnica.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior
text:
- A consulta de DPS exige mTLS e usa `GET /notafiscal-ws/nfse/dps/{idDps}`. A resolução prioriza
  `endpoints.consultaDps`, depois `endpoints.dps` explícito por compatibilidade e, por fim, a constante própria do
  ambiente. Ao sobrescrever o envio para um endereço diferente da consulta, informe também `consultaDps`.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior
text:
- The Campinas endpoint expects `Content-Type: application/json` with `{ dpsXmlGZipB64 }`; raw XML with
  `application/xml` returned `HTTP 415`.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior
text:
- Consulta de NFSe por chave de acesso está disponível via `GET /notafiscal-ws/nfse/{chaveAcesso}`. O retorno
  é JSON com `nfseXmlGZipB64` e `alertas`; preserve a resposta bruta e os alertas em erros HTTP.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior
text:
- Cancelamento de NFSe está disponível em homologação e produção via
  `POST /notafiscal-ws/nfse/{chaveAcesso}/eventos`. Envie JSON com `{ pedidoRegistroEventoXmlGZipB64 }`, contendo o XML
  `pedRegEvento` do código `101101` já assinado, compactado com GZip e codificado em Base64.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior
text:
- A fachada `cancelarNfse` gera e assina o `pedRegEvento` a partir de dados tipados; `signedXml` permanece como escape
  hatch para XML externo e deve ser transmitido sem alteração nem reassinatura.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior
text:
- Eventos em produção usam `PRODUCAO_EVENTOS_ENDPOINT` por padrão; `endpoints.eventos` continua disponível como

  demais eventos continuam não implementados.

head: AGENTS.md > Campinas v3 Behavior

head: AGENTS.md > Certificates And Transport

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- Do not turn the SDK into a full DPS/XSD validator. Local validation should be limited to fields the SDK needs to
  build IDs, sign/send requests, avoid runtime errors, or avoid silently changing user input during normalization.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- Do not add local checks solely because the official XSD or municipal service would reject missing domain/structural
  fields. Let the Prefeitura/NFS-e service be the source of truth for those rejections unless a product requirement says
  otherwise.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- Do not sanitize, strip, truncate, or "fix" fiscal/declarative text silently before signing. Preserve caller-provided
  values and let the Prefeitura/NFS-e service validate them.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- Normalization is allowed only for explicitly accepted input formats, such as punctuation removal from CPF/CNPJ/CEP
  when the original value matches one of the documented formats. Arbitrary text must not be cleaned into a different
  fiscal value.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- Monetary/decimal strings and fiscal/declarative codes such as `codigoTributacaoNacional`,
  `codigoTributacaoMunicipal`, and `codigoNbs` should be serialized exactly as supplied; use warnings if helpful, but do
  not reformat, pad, strip punctuation, round, or otherwise canonicalize them before signing.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text: - `validationMode: 'warn'` still blocks `severity: 'error'`; only `off` bypasses local validation.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- Dates must be real ISO dates/date-times accepted by Luxon; validation uses Luxon to reject impossible values and invalid
  `Date` objects without imposing a local timezone requirement.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- `serie` and `numeroDps` accept only digits before padding because they are used to build the DPS ID; do not silently
  strip letters/signs.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text: - CNPJ may be alphanumeric (`[A-Z0-9]{12}` + 2 numeric check digits); preserve uppercase letters in XML and DPS IDs.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text: - `idDps` override must match the DPS structure, allowing alphanumeric CNPJ in the 14-character federal-inscription block.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- Validate optional `tomador`/`destinatario` CPF/CNPJ and address municipality when supplied, but do not make optional
  parties mandatory.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text:
- `servico.codigoNbs` is only a warning when it does not look like 9 digits or the documented dotted format; serialize it
  exactly as supplied.

head: AGENTS.md > Validation Rules That Are Easy To Break
text: - Do not validate or normalize IBS/CBS domain codes locally; emit `cIndOp` and `cClassTrib` exactly as supplied.

head: Agent Guide
text: This repository is an alpha Flue-based harness for autoresearching agent skills. It evaluates a seed skill against repeatable fixtures, asks a researcher model to improve the skill, then reruns evals against the candidate skill and persists enough artifacts to audit what happened.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator
text: A static pod operator that manages the lifecycle of `kube-apiserver` on OpenShift control plane nodes. Built on the [library-go](https://github.com/openshift/library-go) static pod operator framework, it observes cluster configuration, rotates certificates, manages encryption at rest, and reconciles the target kube-apiserver config into static pod manifests. Installed by the [Cluster Version Operator](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-version-operator) (CVO).

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator
text: See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full design and data flow.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Build and Test
text: Go version: see `go.mod`.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Project Structure
text:
| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `cmd/cluster-kube-apiserver-operator/` | Operator binary entry point (operator, render, installer, pruner, startup-monitor, cert controllers, and more) |
| `cmd/cluster-kube-apiserver-operator-tests-ext/` | OpenShift Tests Extension (OTE) test runner entry point |
| `pkg/operator/starter.go` | Operator initialization — creates clients, informers, and starts all controllers |
| `pkg/operator/targetconfigcontroller/` | Renders observed config + defaults into kube-apiserver ConfigMaps/Secrets |
| `pkg/operator/configobservation/` | Configuration observers — each observer watches a cluster state to infer the operand config |
| `pkg/operator/certrotationcontroller/` | Certificate rotation for serving, LB, aggregator, kubelet, etc. certs |
| `pkg/operator/resourcesynccontroller/` | Syncs ConfigMaps/Secrets between namespaces |
| `pkg/operator/operatorclient/` | Namespace constants and operator client interfaces |
| `pkg/cmd/render/` | Bootstrap manifest renderer for cluster installation |
| `pkg/recovery/` | Disaster recovery API server pod generation |
| `bindata/` | Embedded assets: default config, static pod template, alerts, RBAC, bootstrap manifests |
| `manifests/` | CVO deployment manifests (namespace, deployment, RBAC, ServiceMonitors) |
| `test/e2e*/` | E2E test suites (operator, encryption, encryption-rotation, encryption-perf, KMS, SNO) |
| `test/library/` | Shared test utilities |

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Controller Pattern
text: Controllers use the library-go `factory.Controller` base. Each controller has a `sync(ctx, syncContext)` method called by the framework on informer events or periodic resyncs. The operator wires them in `pkg/operator/starter.go` via `RunOperator()`.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Controller Pattern
text: Config observers follow a specific pattern: each observer function receives the existing config and returns `(observedConfig, errors)`. Observers are registered in `pkg/operator/configobservation/configobservercontroller/observe_config_controller.go`.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Key Conventions
text: - **Namespaces:** `openshift-kube-apiserver-operator` (operator), `openshift-kube-apiserver` (operand), `openshift-config` (user config), `openshift-config-managed` (platform config). Constants in `pkg/operator/operatorclient/interfaces.go`.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Key Conventions
text: - **Logging:** `k8s.io/klog/v2` with verbosity levels

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Key Conventions
text: - **Error handling:** wrap with `fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err)`

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Key Conventions
text: - **Feature gates:** controllers that depend on feature gates use `FeatureGateAccessor` from library-go; wait for gates before starting

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Key Conventions
text: - **Cert rotation:** `Refresh` relative to `Validity` varies per certificate (e.g. ~50% for short-lived certs, ~80% for long-lived ones). The `certificates.openshift.io/refresh-period` annotation is informational — actual rotation is decided by `notBefore`/`notAfter` on the secret. Cert rotation logic lives in `library-go/pkg/operator/certrotation/`.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Key Conventions
text: - **Upstream changes:** controllers that wrap library-go functionality should have fixes made upstream in [library-go](https://github.com/openshift/library-go), not here

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Contributing
text: See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for full guidelines. Key rules:

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Contributing
text: - Do not modify files under `vendor/`. Use `go mod tidy && go mod vendor`.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Contributing
text: - `bindata/assets.go` uses Go's `embed` directive to embed asset files — update the embedded files, not this file.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Contributing
text: - Write unit tests for every change. E2E tests for significant features.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Contributing
text: - Backwards compatibility matters — deprecate before removing.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Contributing
text: - Before modifying the operator API, ensure there is a corresponding enhancement proposal in [openshift/enhancements](https://github.com/openshift/enhancements). API changes require design review and approval.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Testing
text: - **Unit tests:** co-located `*_test.go` files, table-driven, `go test ./pkg/... ./cmd/...`

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Testing
text: - **E2E tests:** suites under `test/e2e*/`, each with its own Makefile target. `test/e2e/` and `test/e2e-encryption-kms/` contain Ginkgo v2 specs for the OTE framework; `test/e2e/` also has standard Go test files. The remaining directories use standard Go testing only.

head: Cluster Kube API Server Operator > Testing
text: - **OTE framework:** `cluster-kube-apiserver-operator-tests-ext` binary. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#openshift-tests-extension-ote) for usage.

head: Ecosystem map > Krill platform background
text: Krill is a Kotlin Multiplatform peer-to-peer IoT control system on Linux/Pi. Everything is a typed, serializable **Node** with metadata, state, and parent/child hierarchy. Server: Ktor + H2; clients: Compose Multiplatform. State flows `ServerNodeManager` → DB → `SharedFlow` → SSE → clients. `krill-oss` ships the SDK, MCP server agents call, and Pi4J GPIO daemon. Deep dive: `shared/architecture-krill.md` (read on demand). Build details: `build-krill.md`, `build-krill-oss.md`.

head: Cross-repo protocol > Verify-Agent-Ghost handoff (PR-side, krill / krill-oss)
text: **Every reproduction step must name a concrete MCP tool call.** Ghost operates at the node-data layer via MCP and does not perform automated UI interactions (Xvfb is live at `:99` but is not used for GUI automation) — it cannot open or render a Compose UI, drive dialogs, tap slot pickers, or observe rendered output. head: Cross-repo protocol > Verify-Agent-Ghost handoff (PR-side, krill / krill-oss)
text: **On PASS, Blue enables automerge** (`gh pr merge --auto --squash`) — the PR lands on `agents` once CI is green; Blue does not merge manually and never merges to `main`. Ben ships by merging the permanent `agents → main` integration PR that Kraken maintains (its body is the accumulated release notes). head: Cross-repo protocol > Verify-Agent-Ghost handoff (PR-side, krill / krill-oss)
text: **If the `Verify Agent Ghost.yml` run itself errors before Ghost ever posts PASS/FAIL/SKIPPED** — e.g. the "Check out PR head into local krill clone" step fails with `git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)` — that's a runner-infrastructure fault, not a Ghost verdict, and not necessarily a code bug in the workflow YAML. Confirm the scope before assuming a one-off blip: check the preceding "Update sibling working copies" step's log for matching `WARN: fetch failed for ...` lines against `krill-oss` and `krill-agents` — `scripts/lib.sh::update_repo` swallows fetch failures there as non-fatal warnings by design, so that step can look all-green while every sibling repo's fetch silently failed for the same reason the krill checkout then hard-fails on (no `|| true` around its own `git fetch`). Matching WARNs across all repos in the same run means the ghost runner's job-level SSH auth (key or agent) is broken — file/flag that to Ben directly, since no repo's workflow code is at fault and there's nothing to fix via a GitHub issue. Regardless of the runner's SSH state, do not automerge and do not treat the error as a Ghost FAIL requiring a code fix on the PR branch — leave `needs-qa-verify` in place and comment the diagnosis + failing run link on the PR (`krill-agents#57`).

head: Workflow conventions
text: Applies to **Blue** in all three roles (`dev-krill`, `dev-krill-oss`, `dev-krill-agents`). Ghost's loop is in `roles/qa.md`.

head: Workflow conventions > Your name and identity
text: You are **Blue**. GitHub user: `krill-blue-bot`. Single identity across all three repos; the role bundle just narrows which tree you write into and which build commands apply. Your counterparts both file into your queue: **Ghost** (`krill-ghost-bot`, QA — files bugs and verifies your PRs) and **Kraken** (`krill-kraken-bot`, oversight/code-analysis — files Nightly-Bug-Hunt findings; no PR verification). When you need grounding in Ben's history (prior art, why a thing was decided), consult the **kraken corpus** MCP — see `ecosystem-map.md`.

head: Workflow conventions > Handoff model
text: You work *only* on issues where `assignee == krill-blue-bot`. **Assignment is the handoff signal**, not any umbrella label. Ghost assigns when filing a QA bug; Kraken assigns Nightly-Bug-Hunt / oversight findings. Ben assigns ad-hoc tasks. Cross-repo dev-to-dev filings (rare) also use `--assignee krill-blue-bot`. If none happened, it's not your queue — never pick up unassigned issues.

head: Workflow conventions > Handoff model
text: No claim race: the issue is already assigned to you when the workflow fires, so you don't need to add yourself as assignee.

text: Production: a `Dev Agent Blue.yml` GitHub Actions workflow lives on each of the three repos (`krill`, `krill-oss`, `krill-agents`). It fires on `issues:assigned` and only when `assignee == krill-blue-bot`. The workflow:

text: So by the time you read this, your `main` is current and an issue number is already in your prompt. Don't re-poll the queue — work the one issue you were handed and stop.

head: Workflow conventions > Acknowledge and report progress
text: Your work is asynchronous and the issue thread is the only place Ben (and Ghost, on the product repos) can see what you're doing. Treat it as a status log, not a silent workspace.

head: Workflow conventions > Acknowledge and report progress
text: **On pick-up — before any fix work** — acknowledge the issue:

head: Workflow conventions > Acknowledge and report progress
text:
1. Apply the `status:in-progress` label so the issue list shows at a glance which tickets are actively in flight. If the label doesn't exist on the repo yet, create it once and re-use it from then on:
   ```bash
   gh label create status:in-progress \
     --repo <my-repo> \
     --color BFD4F2 \
     --description "Blue is actively working this issue"
   ```
   The issue closes automatically when the PR that references `Closes #<n>` merges to `agents` or `main` — handled by the `close-issues-on-merge.yml` workflow, **where it's actually deployed** (GitHub's native auto-close only fires on the default branch; this workflow covers `agents`). Confirmed present on all three repos (`krill-agents`, `krill-oss` as of 2026-07-08; `krill` landed it 2026-07-08 via `krill#827`, closing the `krill-agents#52` gap) — if an issue stays open after its closing PR merges, don't assume the bot will catch up: check `ls .github/workflows/close-issues-on-merge*` on that repo first, close the issue by hand if it's missing, and file/reopen a friction issue rather than re-discovering the same gap silently.
   **Known race with `gh pr merge --auto`:** the workflow's `pull_request: types: [closed]` trigger can be delivered with `merged: false` still in the payload — GitHub queues an automerge's squash-commit asynchronously and the `closed` webhook can fire before it lands (observed 68s of lag between the `closed` event and the PR's actual `mergedAt` — `krill-agents#55`). All three repos' copies now re-fetch the PR (up to 6 retries, 15s apart) before concluding "closed without merging." If you ever see an issue stay open after an automerge you triggered, re-check the workflow run's conclusion before assuming the bot is broken — a `skipped`/no-op run on an old (pre-fix) copy of the workflow is the likely cause, not a permanent gap.

text: 3. **Branch from `agents`** (the release-train integration branch — **not `main`**). `git fetch origin && git checkout -b fix/<issue#>-<slug> origin/agents`. For doc-only fixes, prefer a markdown sanity test (e.g. assert the absolute phrasing is gone) so the regression has a guard. head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake
text: CI runs on hardware that doubles as a real Krill server: filesystem paths the production code expects (`/etc/krill/...`, `~/.krill/install_id`, `/var/lib/krill/...`, `/srv/krill/...`) actually exist, with real PIN files and install ids. Wall-clock-based assertions live next to background traffic. Anything that bakes assumptions about either is a flake waiting to happen — and CI treats it as a hard failure.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake
text: The rules below are absolute for any new test landing in a fix PR. If you can't satisfy them, the unit-under-test is wrong-shaped — either parameterise the seam (preferred) or skip the test and explain why in the PR.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Bans (hard fails — delete or rewrite the test)
text: - **No `delay()` (or `Thread.sleep`) to simulate time passing.** A test that fires N coroutines and waits 250 ms expecting "the first one wins" depends on `Dispatchers.Default`'s scheduling, which CI doesn't owe you. Use `runTest { … }` from `kotlinx-coroutines-test` and `advanceTimeBy(...)` / `advanceUntilIdle()` — virtual time, deterministic. The library is in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` as `kotlin-coroutines-test` but **not yet wired into every module's test classpath**; if the import fails, add `testImplementation(libs.kotlin.coroutines.test)` to the module's `build.gradle.kts` in the same PR.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Bans (hard fails — delete or rewrite the test)
text: - **No wall-clock-relative assertions in concurrency tests.** "Fired exactly once after a 250 ms window" is a timing race, not a correctness test. If the production code has a mutex/serialisation invariant, assert it without time — for example, count concurrent enters via a debug-only `Semaphore.tryAcquire()` probe in the production hot path, or feed the function ordered events through a virtual scheduler.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Bans (hard fails — delete or rewrite the test)
text: - **No reading or writing real production paths.** `/etc/krill/credentials/pin_derived_key`, `/srv/krill/data/krill_v3.db`, `~/.krill/install_id`, `/var/lib/krill/trusted` and their cousins are owned by deployed Krill instances. CI runners co-host real ones. Test fixtures that depend on those paths being absent fail on the runner; fixtures that write to them clobber a real install. Inject the path (or the value the path resolves to) as a constructor / function parameter and pass a fixture string in the test.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Bans (hard fails — delete or rewrite the test)
text: - **No network calls, even to localhost.** That includes Ktor `testApplication { … }` if it binds a real port. Use `MockEngine` from `io.ktor.client.engine.mock` against the route handler factory directly, or call the helper the route delegates to.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Bans (hard fails — delete or rewrite the test)
text: - **No tests that depend on `installId()`, `hostName`, `SystemInfo.isServer()`, or any other platform `expect-val`.** These read the environment + filesystem on first call. The production code may legitimately need them; the test should not. If your unit-under-test calls `installId()` internally, refactor it to take the id as a parameter and let the caller (route handler, processor `init`) resolve it once at the boundary. `Sautner-Studio-LLC/krill#190`'s `peerProjection(nodes, selfId)` is the canonical shape — pure helper, deterministic test, no `@BeforeEach` `mkdirs`.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Bans (hard fails — delete or rewrite the test)
text: - **No `@BeforeEach { File(somePath).parentFile?.mkdirs() }` or any other "make the environment look right before this test" setup.** That's the symptom of a missing seam. Fix the seam.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Positive patterns
text: - **Parameterise the platform seam.** Helper takes `selfId: String` (or `now: () -> Long`, or `clock: Clock`); the route handler resolves the real value once and passes it in. Tests pass a literal.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Positive patterns
text: - **Stub via `open` + subclass.** `PinProvider` is `open`; tests subclass with `override fun bearerToken(): String? = "fixed"`. Same shape applies anywhere the unit-under-test exposes one I/O surface.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Positive patterns
text: - **Virtual time over real time.** `runTest { advanceTimeBy(150.milliseconds); coroutine.cancelAndJoin() }` is deterministic at any CI load.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Positive patterns
text: - **`MockK` for collaborator boundaries, not for the unit under test.** Mock `ServerNodeManager`, not the function you're testing.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Positive patterns
text: - **Prove it with a hostile environment.** Before pushing, run the test once with `HOME=/nonexistent ./gradlew :module:test`. If it still passes, the test is environment-independent. PR #190 uses this as the verification step in its commit message.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Positive patterns
text: If a test legitimately needs a specific environment to be meaningful (integration, hardware-on-Pi), it doesn't belong in `:server:jvmTest` / `:shared:test` / etc. Mark it explicitly in the PR body, put it behind a JUnit tag the default `:test` task skips, or skip writing it and flag the gap.

head: Workflow conventions > Writing tests that don't flake > Background — why this section exists
text: `Sautner-Studio-LLC/krill#190` (the `/peers` route fix) had to delete three pre-existing tests for being environment-dependent: two `PinProviderTest` cases that assumed `/etc/krill/credentials/pin_derived_key` does not exist on the test host (it does, on the runner), and one `SilentAlarmWatchdogTaskTest` case that fired 20 concurrent launches and asserted single-fire after a 250 ms wall-clock delay. Don't recreate any of those shapes — and if you find existing ones in the codebase, prefer deleting them over fixing them up unless the underlying invariant is genuinely worth covering, in which case rewrite to virtual time + a parameterised seam.

head: Workflow conventions > Cross-repo case
text: If the trail leads to a different repo (krill ↔ krill-oss, or either → krill-agents), see `cross-repo-protocol.md` — file upstream, comment links on the originating issue, **don't** patch downstream.

head: Workflow conventions > Conventions
text: - **Branch:** cut **from `agents`**, never `main`. `fix/<issue#>-<slug>` for QA bugs; `chore/<slug>` for repo plumbing (CI, docs, templates); `feat/<slug>` only on explicit Ben ask. PRs target **base `agents`** and carry exactly one `risk:` label.

head: Workflow conventions > Conventions
text: - **Commit subject:** `<type>(<scope>): <imperative summary> (#<issue>)` — type ∈ `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `feat`, `refactor`, `test`. Body explains *why* in 2–3 sentences. End with the `Co-Authored-By:` trailer the harness already supplies.

head: Workflow conventions > Conventions
text: - **PR title:** mirror the commit subject. PR body follows `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`. Always include `Closes #<n>`.

head: Workflow conventions > Conventions
text: - **Labels mid-triage:** if QA mislabeled, re-tag — but **comment first** explaining why. Don't drop their labels silently.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** edit files outside your owned repo. Cross-repo work goes through GitHub issues.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** work an issue not assigned to `krill-blue-bot`. Ben assigns ad-hoc tasks; Ghost assigns reported bugs. If neither did, it's not your queue.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** start fix work silently. The first action on a picked-up issue is the acknowledging comment + `status:in-progress` label (see "Acknowledge and report progress").

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** disappear into a long fix without surfacing decisions in the issue thread. Comment at the inflection points listed in "Acknowledge and report progress" — Ben can't read your shell history.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** merge your own PR manually — automerge (`gh pr merge --auto --squash`) lands it on `agents` once the gate is satisfied.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** merge to `main` or target `main` with a PR (except a labeled `hotfix:`). `main` is Ben's ship gate, reached only via the `agents → main` integration PR.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** open a PR without exactly one `risk:` label.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** close a QA issue without an explicit Ghost **PASS** comment.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** skip the `docs/lessons/` entry.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** use `delay()` or `Thread.sleep` to simulate time passing in tests — virtual time only (`runTest` + `advanceTimeBy`). See "Writing tests that don't flake."

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** read or write a production filesystem path (`/etc/krill/...`, `~/.krill/install_id`, `/srv/krill/...`, `/var/lib/krill/...`) from a test. CI runners are deployed Krill servers; those paths are real. Inject the path (or the value it resolves to) as a parameter.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** assume the test host lacks Krill state. If a test needs the absence of a file or daemon, the test is wrong-shaped — parameterise the seam instead.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** apply the `qa` / `qa-agent` umbrella to an issue you (Blue) filed. Use `--assignee krill-blue-bot` instead so the upstream dev sees it in their queue (see `cross-repo-protocol.md`).

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** add `needs-qa-verify` to a PR on `Sautner-Studio-LLC/krill-agents`. That repo has no Verify Agent Ghost workflow; the label has no listener and would just confuse readers.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** apply `needs-qa-verify` when Ghost cannot verify the change via MCP — that includes UI-only rendering changes (`composeApp/`, `androidApp/`, `iosApp/`) and hardware-only physical-pin changes (`krill-pi4j/`). More broadly, never apply it to a no-risk PR (pure docs, comment-only, openspec, repo plumbing). Ghost's verify sweep burns tokens and runner time; only label it when you can name a specific MCP tool call that would confirm the fix works.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** apply `needs-qa-verify` when the PR body states "Skipping `needs-qa-verify`." The label and the PR body must be consistent — an inconsistent state fires Ghost's verify sweep on a PR Ghost cannot verify and forces a wasted SKIPPED run.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** apply `needs-qa-verify` without immediately posting an `@qa-agent please verify` comment with a copy-pasteable reproduction script (see step 8 and `cross-repo-protocol.md`). The label fires `Verify Agent Ghost.yml` immediately; if Ghost arrives and finds no reproduction comment, it must post SKIPPED — wasting the full build-and-install pipeline. Apply the label and post the comment as a single atomic step. Reproduction steps must name concrete MCP tool calls — steps that describe UI interactions (open dialog, tap picker, observe rendered output) are not exercisable by Ghost; if your repro has no MCP steps, you should not have applied the label.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** run destructive git ops (`push --force`, `reset --hard`, `branch -D`, `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`) without explicit confirmation from Ben.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** hardcode a version in a `build.gradle.kts` — use `gradle/libs.versions.toml`.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** hand-edit `version.txt` or synced version fields in fix PRs (krill repo). See `build-krill.md`.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** bump module versions in a bug-fix PR (krill-oss). Releases are a separate flow — see `build-krill-oss.md`.

head: Workflow conventions > Hard rules — don't violate
text: - **Never** file a new upstream issue without first searching for an existing one (`gh issue list --search …`).

Clear it and restart that one container:

head: CLAUDE.md > Development Commands > Local Development (Docker-based) > Restart the dev server after changing dependencies
text: This failure is easy to misdiagnose. SSR keeps returning 200, so pages look fine, but the browser console shows `504 (Outdated Optimize Dep)` for `svelte`, `esm-env`, and `devalue`, then `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: @sveltejs/kit/src/runtime/client/entry.js`. The client entry never loads, so **nothing hydrates**: the search editor renders as a plain input instead of a ProseMirror contenteditable, buttons like "Select Files" stay `disabled`, and most of the Playwright suite fails on unrelated-looking assertions. Check for those 504s before investigating an apparent regression. Vite logs `Forced re-optimization of dependencies` and needs one page load to settle after restarting.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents
text:
This file is for an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and the like) helping someone install and play
ArkWeb. `README.md` is the human overview; this file is the procedure. Follow it top to bottom the first time.
Later sessions ("Let's play ArkWeb") can jump to [Playing](#5-playing-session) and [While they play](#6-while-they-play).

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents
text:
ArkWeb runs **Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered** (the hidden *guest*) next to **Batman: Arkham Knight** (the
*host*, the window the user looks at). Spider-Man's own movement is played with a controller, Gotham's
collision is streamed into Spider-Man's physics, and his rendered frame is drawn into Arkham's view in
Batman's place. Three pieces must run together: `winmm.dll` in Spider-Man, `dinput8.dll` in Arkham Knight,
and the Python streamer `tools/gotham_stream.py`.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text:
- **Assume the user isn't technical and uses Windows only through its normal interface.** Run every command
  yourself. When they must do something, say exactly where to click (which app, which menu, which button); never
  ask them to open a terminal, type a command or edit a file.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text:
- **Ask before anything the user must do.** Before each step that needs them (closing or starting a game,
  loading a save, playing, testing), say what they'll do and roughly how long, then wait for an explicit OK.
  One OK doesn't cover the next step.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text:
- **Their Arkham Knight save follows Batman.** Arkham autosaves while Batman is the puppet. If Spider-Man ends up
  under the map, a save there can spawn Batman under the map for good. Back the save up before the first session
  (step 3), keep Spider-Man above the streets, and rescue him early (see [Rescue](#rescue)).

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text:
- **Never run `bin\link_test.exe` while either game runs.** It opens the live shared memory and writes fake
  state into it.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text:
- **Don't restart the streamer while the user plays.** A restart leaves seconds with no streaming, and
  Spider-Man can walk into an unbuilt tile and fall. If you must, restart with `--resume`.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text: - **Install or uninstall only with both games closed.**

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text:
- **No experiments on a running Arkham Knight.** An access violation inside Arkham is a crash, even inside
  `__try`. Stick to the commands in the README.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text:
- **Both games at once is heavy.** Builds run at low priority on one core by design. Don't add load-heavy work
  (big builds, scans, GPU tests) while the user plays.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 0. Ground rules
text: - When you watch the streamer's output, report errors and milestones only, not every status line.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > Getting the repository
text:
If the user started you in an empty folder and asked you to download ArkWeb, put the repository's files
**directly in that folder**, so that `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` sit at its top level and later sessions opened
there find this guide. Use `git clone https://github.com/luki-1/ArkWeb .` if git is installed. Otherwise download
`https://github.com/luki-1/ArkWeb/archive/refs/heads/main.zip`, extract it, and move the contents of its
`ArkWeb-main` folder up into the user's folder.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 1. Check the user's setup
text:
Do these checks yourself, then tell the user what's missing. Install missing tools yourself (for example with
`winget`) after asking them, rather than sending them to do it.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 1. Check the user's setup
text:
| Check | How |
|---|---|
| Windows 10 x64 | ArkWeb was built and tested there. Windows 11 is untested. |
| Spider-Man Remastered, Steam, **v4.0630** | `(Get-Item "<SM folder>\Spider-Man.exe").VersionInfo.FileVersion` must be `4.0630.0.0` (Steam app 1817070). Every hook is bound to that build's addresses. With another build the guest can't find what it hooks, and nothing works. |
| Batman: Arkham Knight, Steam | `<library>\steamapps\common\Batman Arkham Knight\Binaries\Win64\BatmanAK.exe` (Steam app 208650) |
| Game folders | Steam library paths are listed in `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\libraryfolders.vdf`. Spider-Man is `<library>\steamapps\common\Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered\`. |
| Other mods in the way | If `winmm.dll` is already in the Spider-Man folder, or `dinput8.dll` in Arkham's `Binaries\Win64`, it belongs to another mod and the install would overwrite it. Tell the user and back it up before installing. |
| Xbox-style controller | It's read as XInput controller 0. Without a controller, the keyboard fallback is in step 5. |
| Hardware | Both games run at the same time. The author used an RTX 3080 with 32 GB of RAM. |
| C++ build tools | Visual Studio 2019 Build Tools (x64 C++); `build.bat` calls `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2019\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`. A different VS version or edition needs that path changed (others are untested). `vswhere.exe` in `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\` finds installs. |
| Shader compiler | `fxc.exe` from the Windows 10 SDK; `build.bat` expects `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin\10.0.19041.0\x64\fxc.exe`. Point `FXC` at another SDK version if needed. |
| Python | 3.12 with `numpy scipy numba pefile capstone` (`python -m pip install numpy scipy numba pefile capstone`) |

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 2. Build
text: 1. Fix the `vcvars64.bat` and `FXC` paths in `build.bat` if step 1 found them elsewhere.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 2. Build
text:
2. Run `build.bat` from the repository root. It ends with `BUILD OK` and writes:
   - `bin\sm\winmm.dll` (the Spider-Man guest)
   - `bin\ak\dinput8.dll` (the Arkham Knight host)
   - `bin\link_test.exe` (an offline test of the shared-memory link)

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 2. Build
text: 3. Optional, **only with both games closed**: run `bin\link_test.exe` to check the link.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 3. Install
text:
1. Set the two game folders at the top of `install.bat` (`AK` = Arkham's `Binaries\Win64`, `SM` = the
   Spider-Man folder) and the same two paths in `uninstall.bat`. They hold the author's paths.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 3. Install
text:
2. Ask the user to close both games, then run `install.bat`. It copies the DLLs and writes an `arkweb.ini` next
   to each one. Keep those files: they point both games at this repository, where they exchange files with the
   streamer. Existing settings in them are kept. Optional keys for the `[ArkWeb]` section:
   `DrivePuppet=` (AK, default 1), `MimicCamera=` (AK, default 1), `Overlay=` (AK, default 1),
   `TickEvent=` (AK, default `PlayerTick`), `VirtualPad=` (SM, default 1), `ForceFocus=` (SM, default 0).

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 3. Install
text:
3. Back up the Arkham Knight save. Steam keeps it in `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\userdata\<id>\208650\remote\`
   (`BAK1Save*.sgd`). Copy that folder somewhere outside Steam.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 3. Install
text: To remove ArkWeb, close both games and run `uninstall.bat`. The `arkweb.ini` files can stay or go.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 4. Game settings to tell the user
text: These only need doing once.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 4. Game settings to tell the user
text:
- **Spider-Man**: play it **windowed**, at a moderate size (only Spider-Man himself is shown, cut out of this
  window; a bigger window looks sharper but costs GPU time). Turn **off** the HUD, motion blur, depth of field,
  film grain, HDR (use SDR) and frame generation. Any of these leaks into the cut-out or breaks the depth test
  that finds him.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 4. Game settings to tell the user
text: - **Arkham Knight**: windowed or borderless makes switching windows painless. Nothing else is required.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 4. Game settings to tell the user
text: - Both games play sound. Lowering Spider-Man in the Windows volume mixer is up to the user.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 4. Game settings to tell the user
text:
- Optional: Spider-Man's lighting follows New York's time of day. After the story, the research station lets the
  user choose night, which matches Gotham better.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 5. Playing session
text: Ask before each numbered step that needs the user.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 5. Playing session
text:
1. **Start both games and load into the open world in each.** Free roam, no mission, no cutscene. In Arkham,
   Batman should stand **on foot on a street** (not in the Batmobile, not on a rooftop edge): his feet become
   Spider-Man's starting spot. In Spider-Man, stand still on the ground. Leave **Arkham Knight in front**.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 5. Playing session
text:
2. **Start the streamer** in a background shell whose output you can read:
   ```bash
   cd tools && python gotham_stream.py
   ```
   It waits for both games, prints `origin: Batman's feet ...`, compiles its hull builder (a few seconds), builds
   the start area, then prints `start area built in Spider-Man: jumping up onto Gotham` and
   `Spider-Man stands on Gotham`. Gotham sits 2 km above New York (`--sky`), so New York's own ledges are out
   of reach. If it prints `the jump didn't hold`, it places Gotham at his feet instead, which also works. From
   then on, Batman follows Spider-Man and Spider-Man is drawn in his place.
   **Tell the user not to move Spider-Man until you say he's on Gotham.**

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 5. Playing session
text:
3. **Tell the user they can play**, and give them the controls:
   | Input | Does |
   |---|---|
   | Left stick / right stick | Move / Spider-Man's camera (Arkham's view copies it) |
   | RT (hold) | Web swing; hold while running at a wall to run up it |
   | A | Jump; release a swing with A for a swing jump |
   | B | Dodge |
   | LT + RT | Zip to the grapple point under the ring marker in Arkham's view |
   | After a zip | He perches on the point. A jumps or launches off; B drops. |
   | Fights | Automatic. When Arkham decides Batman is fighting, Arkham's own combat takes over (X strike, Y counter, and so on), with Spider-Man in Batman's place copying his moves. Control returns 2 s after the fight. |
   Without a controller (Arkham in front): WASD = left stick, Space = A, Left Shift = RT, Left Ctrl = B.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 5. Playing session
text:
4. **End of session.** Before quitting, have the user bring Spider-Man down to a street, so Batman (the save) is
   left somewhere normal. Stop the streamer (Ctrl+C or kill the process), then close the games in any order.
   When Spider-Man closes, Arkham takes Batman back wherever he is.

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 6. While they play
text:
The README explains how to send live commands to either game (*Live commands*, and the note at its top). The
streamer prints the hero's position and speed and the tiles it holds every few seconds; positions are Arkham
units (UU, centimeters, Z up).

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 6. While they play > Rescue
text:
| Situation | Do |
|---|---|
| Spider-Man is stuck inside a building, or the user asks to be teleported up | Spider-Man: `hero tp 0 200 0` (meters relative to him; the second number is up) |
| He fell under Gotham | The guest puts him back by itself once he is 150 m below Gotham. If it doesn't, `hero tp 0 <meters> 0`; work out the height from the streamer's position line first. |
| Batman is under the map or stuck after Spider-Man closed | Arkham: `tp -65886 -57301 -234` (a known-good street, Arkham units) |
| Batman stops following while Spider-Man is low | Batman refuses to follow below the streets (this protects the save). Rescue Spider-Man and Batman follows again. |

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > 6. While they play > Troubleshooting
text:
| Symptom | Likely cause and fix |
|---|---|
| Streamer: `ArkWeb mapping has an incompatible protocol` | The installed DLLs are from another build than `tools/arkweb_proto.py`. Rebuild, close both games, reinstall. |
| Streamer waits forever for both games | A game isn't in the open world yet, Spider-Man isn't standing still, or a DLL isn't installed: check that `dinput8.dll` and `arkweb.ini` are in Arkham's `Binaries\Win64` and `winmm.dll` and `arkweb.ini` in the Spider-Man folder. |
| Spider-Man doesn't react to the controller | Arkham must be in front; the controller is read through Arkham. |
| Spider-Man isn't drawn in Arkham | He is drawn only while he is on Gotham and linked (after `Spider-Man stands on Gotham`). Arkham: `overlay on` if it was switched off. |
| Spider-Man looks dark | Arkham: `overlay gamma 0.7` (under 1 is brighter; his lighting is New York's). |
| Batman visible next to Spider-Man | Arkham: `batman show`, then `batman auto`. |
| Spider-Man falls through a road or roof | The tile was scanned before Arkham loaded that district. The streamer rescans such tiles when he comes close. Rescue him with `hero tp`, and wait a few seconds before swinging back. |
| Stutter that grows over time | Watch the streamer's tile counts. Don't restart the streamer during play. |
| Spider-Man crashed | Its crash dumps are in `Documents\Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered\`; `python tools\minidump.py <dump>` reads them. |

head: ArkWeb: guide for AI agents > Known limits to set expectations
text:
Tell the user about the README's *Known issues* before the first session, so a glitch isn't mistaken for a
broken install. In short: hollow Arkham buildings and thin spires can be swung through, fast swings into
unloaded districts can leave gaps for a few seconds, blocked zips drop him, fights have no fists, and a suit
with a different skeleton turns the combat pose copy off.

head: What is Evolve?
text: Evolve is a Python library and service which enables AI agents to improve through self-reflection.

head: What is Evolve? > Key Concepts
text: - **Trajectory**: A recorded agent conversation

head: What is Evolve? > Key Concepts
text: - **Entity**: Anything which is appropriately stored in a vector database, such as a guideline, policy, or some other knowledge.

head: What is Evolve? > Key Concepts
text: - **Namespace**: Isolated storage for entities

head: What is Evolve? > Key Concepts
text: - **Conflict Resolution**: LLM-based merging of duplicate/conflicting entities

head: What is Evolve? > Key Concepts
text: - **Guidelines**: Instructions intended to assist an agent in completing some task

head: What is Evolve? > Architecture Flow
text: 1. Agent completes some task, and the resulting trajectory is automatically saved into a logging framework such as Langfuse or Arize Phoenix.

head: What is Evolve? > Architecture Flow
text: 2. The agent can call the sync MCP function, or the user can manually sync, which causes evolve to process the trajectory and save any generated guidelines.

head: What is Evolve? > Architecture Flow
text: 3. Generated guidelines are stored as entities with conflict resolution applied.

head: What is Evolve? > Architecture Flow
text: 4. Future agents can query the Evolve MCP server to fetch guidelines for similar tasks

head: What is Evolve? > Development Guidelines
text: - This project is managed by `uv`, not `python` or `pip`, so any python commands need to go through `uv`. All dependencies are defined in `pyproject.toml`.

head: What is Evolve? > Testing Instructions
text: - Run pytest verbosely with the `-v` flag by default so that you have more context when tests fail.

head: What is Evolve? > Testing Instructions
text: - Use `uv run pytest tests/.../<test_name.py>` to run tests individually.

head: What is Evolve? > Testing Instructions
text: - We use the pytest markers `e2e` for end-to-end tests, and `unit` for unit tests, and `phoenix` to test integration with Phoenix.

head: What is Evolve? > Testing Instructions
text: - When running `uv run pytest` it will skip the tests marked with `phoenix`.

head: What is Evolve? > Testing Instructions
text: - To run specific markers: `uv run pytest -m e2e` or `uv run pytest -m unit`

head: What is Evolve? > Testing Instructions
text: - To run all tests: `uv run pytest -m "e2e or unit or phoenix"`

head: What is Evolve? > Available Interfaces
text: - MCP Server: `get_entities()`, `get_guidelines()`, `save_trajectory()`

head: What is Evolve? > Available Interfaces
text:
- CLI: Run `evolve --help` if details are needed about its subcommands.
  Available subcommands include `namespaces`, `entities`, and `sync`

head: What is Evolve? > Available Interfaces
text: - Python Client: `EvolveClient()` for programmatic access

head: What is Evolve? > Coding Standards
text: - Use Ruff for linting and formatting (configured in pyproject.toml)

head: What is Evolve? > Coding Standards
text: - Always run `uv run ruff format .` and `git add -u` before committing to avoid pre-commit stash conflicts with ruff auto-fixes

head: What is Evolve? > Coding Standards
text:
- Write commit messages in the Conventional Commits format expected by `python-semantic-release`:
  - `feat(scope): description` — new feature, triggers a minor version bump
  - `fix(scope): description` — bug fix, triggers a patch version bump
  - `perf(scope): description` — performance improvement, triggers a patch version bump
  - `test(scope): description`, `chore(scope): description`, `docs(scope): description`, etc. — no version bump
  - Breaking changes: append `!` after the type/scope (e.g. `feat!:`) or add `BREAKING CHANGE:` in the footer

head: What is Evolve? > Coding Standards
text: - All new features need tests (unit + e2e where applicable)

head: What is Evolve? > Coding Standards
text: - Use uv to run Python commands, including pip.

text:

head: recurred: 1 > Working Agreements > Verify before claiming done

head: recurred: 1 > Working Agreements > Make changes safely
text:
- When renaming or changing a function/type/variable, grep for all of: direct
  references, type-level references, string literals, dynamic imports, re-exports/
  barrels, and tests/mocks. One grep rarely catches everything.

head: recurred: 1 > Working Agreements > Make changes safely
text:

  just edited — the edit tools fail loudly on a mismatch.

head: recurred: 1 > Working Agreements > Code quality
text:

  what the task requires, and clean up only your own mess.

head: recurred: 1 > Working Agreements > Code quality
text:

  working in before introducing new ones.

head: recurred: 1 > Working Agreements > Code quality

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
Default to no new TypeScript unit tests. Prefer typecheck, lint, focused
verifier scripts, manual smoke checks, or live read-only probes over `bun:test`,
Jest, Vitest, `*.test.ts(x)`, `*.spec.ts(x)`, or `__tests__/` coverage.

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
Keep or add a TypeScript test only when it protects an external contract or
invariant that would still compile while broken: money movement,
auth/session boundaries, confirmed-chain writes, generated SDK or wire-format
parity, public API discriminants, webhook retry behavior, DB
ownership/idempotency/conflict behavior, signer/secret/storage boundaries,
config parsing, or dangerous pure calculations.

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
Implement the core logic requested first. Only add or update tests after the
behavior exists, and only when the test still passes this rubric:

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
A test earns `+1` when it protects an external contract or invariant static
checks can miss, `+1` when it asserts an observable side effect or invariant,
and `+1` when TypeScript, lint, or a manual smoke check would not catch the
failure. Observable checks include write/no-write behavior, ordering, rejection
before mutation, retry/backoff, persisted state transitions, balance or amount
calculation, and instruction/account ordering.

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
Subtract `1` when the test mostly mirrors fields, defaults, copy, route
strings, source strings, `Object.keys(...)`, `typeof ...`, or third-party
library behavior. Subtract `1` when it mainly asserts mocked JSON, Drizzle call
order, every `.values()` field, a full response body, or that a mocked
dependency received the same mock data.

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
Keep only tests scoring at least `2`. For mixed files, delete or compress the
low-scoring blocks and keep only the contract/invariant checks.

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
Delete or compress tests that restate implementation shape. Do not keep tests
whose main value is asserting every mocked JSON field, every Drizzle `.values()`
field, object defaults, route-string builders, source substrings, copy that is
not a product or ops contract, `typeof ... === "function"`, `Object.keys(...)`
mirrors, or third-party library behavior.

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
Route tests should assert status codes, branch discriminants, caller-consumed
fields, and side effects only. Repository tests should assert persistence rules,
conflict/idempotency behavior, ownership boundaries, and state transitions.
Schema tests are allowed only for migrations, ownership boundaries, unique
constraints, conflict behavior, or cross-database routing.

head: recurred: 1 > Test Design Guardrails
text:
Live RPC/devnet tests must be opt-in smoke tests with explicit environment
requirements and no checked-in key material. They must not run in default
`bun test` suites.

head: recurred: 1 > Architecture > Loyal Web Earn Flow
text:
The Loyal web Earn UI lives under
`/apps/web/src/components/wallet-workspace/facelift/` (mounted via
`/apps/web/src/app/app/app-workspace-shell.tsx`) and
`/apps/web/src/components/wallet-sidebar/earn-detail-view.tsx`.
User-initiated Earn uses smart-account vault `accountIndex = 1` and the
canonical Kamino USDC reserve. Older auto-yield planning docs may discuss
agent-managed vault `0`; that is a separate flow.

head: recurred: 1 > Architecture > Loyal Web Earn Flow
text:
`packages/smart-account-vaults` is the instruction-building boundary. Use
`prepareEarnUsdcDeposit` and `prepareEarnUsdcWithdraw`; do not duplicate Kamino
or Squads policy instruction shape in React. First Earn deposits initialize the
yield-routing `ProgramInteraction` policy. Top-up deposits must call
`prepareEarnUsdcDeposit` with `initializeYieldRoutingPolicy: false` once
overview policies show an existing Earn policy (`state === "ProgramInteraction"`,
`accountIndex === 1`). The Earn vault index is always `1`, but the policy seed
is the actual Squads policy seed returned by policy creation or persistence; do
not assume policy seed `1`.

head: recurred: 1 > Architecture > Loyal Web Earn Flow
text:
After wallet confirmation, the frontend posts to

text:
The active Earn position read endpoint is
`/api/smart-accounts/yield-optimization/position`. It returns the active
aggregate position from `loyal_yield.user_yield_positions` for the authenticated
