head: AGENTS.md > Project Overview
text: C# SDK for the [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) API, auto-generated from the official OpenAI OpenAPI specification using [AutoSDK](https://github.com/tryAGI/AutoSDK). Published as the `tryAGI.OpenAI` NuGet package. Includes support for custom providers (Azure, DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama, OpenRouter, Together, and many more), a source generator for native C# function/tool definitions, pricing constants, and structured output helpers.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Code Generation Pipeline
text: The SDK code in `Generated/` is **auto-generated** -- do not manually edit files in `src/libs/tryAGI.OpenAI/Generated/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Code Generation Pipeline
text: 1. `src/libs/tryAGI.OpenAI/openapi.yaml` -- the OpenAI OpenAPI spec (fetched from Stainless)

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Code Generation Pipeline
text: 2. `src/libs/tryAGI.OpenAI/generate.sh` -- orchestrates: download spec, run AutoSDK CLI, output to `Generated/`

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Code Generation Pipeline
text: 3. CI auto-updates the spec and creates PRs if changes are detected

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Hand-Written Extensions
text: Unlike most other tryAGI SDKs, this repo has significant **hand-written code** alongside the generated code. Prefer moving behavior to AutoSDK/spec inputs when it improves client UX, and avoid maintaining manual `AsStream` wrappers when the generated surface can represent the same API directly.

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Hand-Written Extensions
text:
| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Metadata/` | Pricing constants and model metadata (chat, embedding, images, TTS, STT) |
| `Conversions/` | Implicit conversions for `ChatCompletionRequestMessage`, `CreateMessageRequest`, etc. |
| `Extensions/StringExtensions.cs` | Helper extension methods |
| `CustomProviders.cs` | Factory methods for Azure, DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama, OpenRouter, etc. |
| `ChatClient.CreateChatCompletion.As.cs` | Structured output (`CreateChatCompletionAsAsync<T>`) |
| `RealtimeConversationClient.cs` | Realtime API WebSocket client |
| `OpenAiApi.Headers.cs` | Custom header helpers |
| `TypeToSchemaHelpers.cs` | JSON schema generation helpers for tools |
| `Image.Bytes.cs` | Image byte conversion helpers |

head: AGENTS.md > Architecture > Project Layout
text:
| Project | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `src/libs/tryAGI.OpenAI/` | Main SDK library (`OpenAiClient` / `OpenAiApi`) |
| `src/tests/OpenAI.IntegrationTests/` | Integration tests against real OpenAI API and custom providers |
| `src/tests/CSharpToJsonSchema.SnapshotTests/` | Snapshot tests for schema generation |
| `src/tests/CSharpToJsonSchema.UnitTests/` | Unit tests for schema generation |
| `src/helpers/GenerateDocs/` | Documentation generator from integration tests |
| `src/helpers/TrimmingHelper/` | NativeAOT/trimming compatibility validator |

head: Obsidian community plugin > Versioning & releases
text: **Releases are produced by the `.github/workflows/release.yml` workflow, which triggers on any pushed tag.** The workflow builds the plugin, attests build provenance for `main.js`/`styles.css` (this is what earns the "verified GitHub artifact attestation" marks on the community scorecard), and runs `gh release create` with the `dist/` assets attached. **Never run `gh release create` yourself** — doing so makes the workflow's create step fail with "a release with the same tag name already exists" and risks publishing an asset the attestation does not cover.

head: Obsidian community plugin > Versioning & releases
text: Release a new version from `main` (example: `0.5.1`):

head: Obsidian community plugin > Versioning & releases
text: 1. **Bump the version** — `npm version 0.5.1 --no-git-tag-version`. This updates `package.json` and runs the `version` script (`version-bump.mjs`), which sets `manifest.json`'s `version` and appends to `versions.json` **only when `minAppVersion` changed** (the script skips `versions.json` when the current `minAppVersion` is already a value in it — so consecutive releases at the same `minAppVersion` correctly add no entry; do not "fix" this by hand).

head: Obsidian community plugin > Versioning & releases
text: 2. **Verify** — `npm run lint && npm test && npm run build`.

head: Obsidian community plugin > Versioning & releases
text: 3. **Commit** the bump to `main` with the version as the message (e.g. `0.5.1`), matching the existing history, and push `main`.

head: Obsidian community plugin > Versioning & releases
text: 4. **Tag and push** — the tag must exactly match `manifest.json`'s `version`, with **no leading `v`**: `git tag 0.5.1 && git push origin 0.5.1`. This is what triggers the release workflow.

head: Obsidian community plugin > Versioning & releases
text: 5. **Watch the workflow** — `gh run watch` (or `gh run list --workflow=release.yml`). When it completes it has created the GitHub release with `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css` attached.

head: Obsidian community plugin > Versioning & releases
text: 6. **Add release notes** — the workflow creates the release with an empty body, so add notes afterward: `gh release edit 0.5.1 --notes "..."`. Obsidian's scorecard flags a release with no description.

CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **24KB size limit** (Brotli-compressed WASM)

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Rust 1.91.0** (via rust-toolchain.toml)

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **No floating point** operations

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Yearly reactivation** required

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Stylus.toml required** since SDK 0.10.0

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **rust-toolchain.toml required** since SDK 0.10.0

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **src/main.rs required** — cargo stylus deploy uses `cargo run` to check constructors

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Package name must use underscores** — hyphens prevent cargo-stylus WASM lookup

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **crate-type = ["lib", "cdylib"]** — "lib" needed for bin target linking

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec}** — sol_storage! macro needs vec module in scope

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **print_from_args()** is the 0.10.0 ABI export function (NOT print_abi())

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **uint8 in sol_storage!** maps to Uint<8,1>, not u8 — prefer uint256

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **RawCall::new_with_value(self.vm(), amount)** — needs self.vm() as first arg + unsafe block

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **transfer_eth** — `use stylus_sdk::call::transfer::transfer_eth;` then `transfer_eth(self.vm(), to, amount)?` (needs `self.vm()` not `self`)

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **sol_interface! for interfaces** — use `sol_interface!` (NOT `sol!`) to define external contract interfaces for cross-contract calls

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Call contexts** — `Call::new()` for VIEW calls, `Call::new_mutating(self)` for STATE-MODIFYING calls. Extract Call to local var to avoid borrow conflict: `let call = Call::new_mutating(self);`

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **sol_interface! host argument** — `self.vm()` MUST be the FIRST argument when calling sol_interface! methods: `token.transfer(self.vm(), call, to, amount)?;` NOT `token.transfer(call, to, amount)?;`

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **sol! needs explicit import** — `use alloy_sol_types::{sol, SolError};` — sol! is NOT in prelude

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **sol! uses camelCase fields** — `tokenId` not `token_id`, `fromAddress` not `from_address` (Solidity convention)

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Dynamic arrays** — `uint256[] items;` in sol_storage!, append with `.push(val)` for primitives, `.grow()` for structs. Never `.setter(len).unwrap()`

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Borrow checker** — extract `.get()` values to local vars before combining with `.set()`. Never `self.field.setter(self.vm().something())`

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **B256 is FixedBytes, not Uint** — `B256::from_uint()` and `B256::from_limbs()` do NOT exist. B256 is `FixedBytes<32>`, not `Uint<256>`. Use `B256::from(value.to_be_bytes::<32>())` for U256→B256, `B256::from(U256::from_limbs([N, 0, 0, 0]).to_be_bytes::<32>())` for limbs, `B256::ZERO` for zero, `B256::with_last_byte(n)` for small values

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Const U256** — `U256::from()` is NOT const-compatible. Use `U256::from_limbs([N, 0, 0, 0])` for const declarations. `U256::ZERO` is fine.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **String mapping reads** — `mapping(uint256 => string)` — `.get(key)` returns `StorageGuard<StorageString>`, NOT `String`. Use `.getter(key).get_string()` to read. For writes: `.setter(key).set_str("value")`

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **abi_encode() on errors** — `.abi_encode()` is on the inner `sol!` error struct (SolError trait), NOT on the `#[derive(SolidityError)]` enum wrapper. WRONG: `MyErrors::NotOwner(NotOwner{...}).abi_encode()`. CORRECT: `NotOwner{caller, owner}.abi_encode()`

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **StorageString view functions** — When returning a `string` field from sol_storage! in a view function, ALWAYS call `.get_string()`: `pub fn name(&self) -> String { self.name.get_string() }`. NEVER return `self.name` directly — it is `StorageString`, not `String`. Do NOT use `.push_str()` on StorageString — extract first: `let s = self.name.get_string(); format!("{}{}", s, other)`

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **String imports in no_std** — `String` needs `use alloc::string::String;`. `.to_string()` also needs `use alloc::string::ToString;`. These are NOT in prelude in no_std.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **No const in #[public] impl** — `pub const` inside `#[public] impl` is unsupported by the proc macro. Move constants to module level before the impl block.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **sol! error/event type matching** — Solidity field types in sol! MUST match the Rust values passed. `address` → Address, `uint256` → U256. For comparison errors (InsufficientBalance, InsufficientStake), ALL value fields (have/want, available/required) should be `uint256`, NOT `address`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **ABI uses camelCase** — Stylus exports snake_case Rust fns as camelCase (`create_market` → `createMarket`). Frontend must use camelCase in `functionName`

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **View functions can't call external contracts** — `&self` view fns revert on cross-contract calls (unlike Solidity). Use `&mut self` or read from frontend

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Arbitrum L2 gas** — MetaMask may underestimate `maxFeePerGas` on Arbitrum Sepolia. Add explicit gas overrides if "max fee per gas less than block base fee"

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **No Debug with SolidityError** — sol! generated types do NOT implement Debug. `#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]` fails. Use `#[derive(SolidityError)]` only.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **No underscore fns in #[public] impl** — `#[public]` macro strips leading underscores for ABI selectors, so `fn _grant_role` and `fn grant_role` produce the same selector ("unreachable pattern"). Put internal helpers in a separate `impl MyContract { ... }` block without `#[public]`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **address[] deref** — `*self.list.get(idx).unwrap()` on `address[]` returns `FixedBytes<20>`, not `Address`. Use `Address::from(*self.list.get(idx).unwrap())`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **String mapping writes** — For `mapping(... => string)`, `.setter(key)` returns `StorageGuardMut<StorageString>` — call `.set_str(val)` directly. WRONG: `.setter(key).setter().set_str(val)`. CORRECT: `.setter(key).set_str(val)`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **Nested struct writes** — For `mapping(uint256 => MyStruct)`, `.get(key)` returns immutable `StorageGuard<MyStruct>` — CANNOT call `.setter()` on its fields. Use `.setter(key)` for writes. WRONG: `self.roles.get(role).members.setter(account).set(true)`. CORRECT: `self.roles.setter(role).members.setter(account).set(true)`.

head: CLAUDE.md > Stylus Development Guidelines > Key Constraints
text: - **No function overloading** — Rust does not support function overloading. Two `fn` with the same name in the same impl block is a compile error (E0428). If you need variants, use different names (e.g. `check_role`, `check_role_with_admin`). Never define a function twice.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > State Management
text: **Phase-gated reducers** (`useVault`, `useVaultMachine`, `useAuth`): component-scoped state machines using `useReducer` + `useEffect`. Follow these rules strictly:

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > State Management
text: 1. **Discriminated `Phase` union** — explicit states (e.g. `"idle" | "signingIn" | "signingOut"`). Every async operation gets its own phase.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > State Management
text: 2. **Pure exported reducer** — all state transitions are synchronous. Reducer is the single source of truth. Export it for unit testing.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > State Management
text: 3. **Phase-gated effects** — each async actor is one `useEffect`. First line: `if (state.phase !== "thePhase") return;`. Effect fires only when entering that phase.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > State Management
text: 4. **Effects only dispatch actions** — never mutate state, never set phase, never call other effects. On completion/error, dispatch an action back to the reducer.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > State Management
text: 5. **Auto-transitions in the reducer** — when state A should immediately proceed to state B (e.g. locked → unlocking when password available), do it in the reducer (see `maybeAutoUnlock`, `evaluate`), not in an effect.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > State Management
text: 6. **Cancellation in cleanup** — every async effect returns a cleanup that sets `cancelled = true` or calls `cancel()` from `createCancellableOperation`.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > State Management
text: Reference implementations: `useVault.ts` (simplest), `useAuth.ts` (most effects), `useVaultMachine.ts` (`evaluate` pattern).

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > Patterns to Avoid
text: - **Effect-to-effect communication** → effects reading results of other effects instead of going through the reducer. This is how useEffect hell starts.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > Patterns to Avoid
text: - **Dispatching in a useEffect to trigger another useEffect** → use auto-transitions in the reducer instead.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > Patterns to Avoid
text: - Multiple useEffects on shared state → race conditions; prefer Zustand store or phase-gated reducer

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > Patterns to Avoid
text: - Refs updated in one effect, read in async callback of another → stale values

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > Patterns to Avoid
text: - `cancelled` flag without operation cancellation → side effects still run

head: Ichinichi > Architecture > Patterns to Avoid
text: - Fire-and-forget `void promise.then(...)` → no tracking/cancellation/error handling

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > DO NOT: Use `as` Casts on External Data
text: All data entering the app from IndexedDB, Supabase, localStorage JSON, or decrypted payloads MUST pass through a parse function in `src/storage/parsers.ts`. Parse functions validate shape and return `T | null`.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > DO NOT: Swallow Errors Silently
text: Empty `catch {}` blocks hide bugs. Use `reportError()` from `src/utils/errorReporter.ts`:

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > DO NOT: Chain useEffects
text: New component-level async state MUST use the phase-gated reducer pattern. DO NOT chain useEffects where one effect's output triggers another via shared state or refs. Route ALL async state transitions through a reducer.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > DO NOT: Chain useEffects
text: - Max 3 useEffect calls per component/hook (lint warning). Max 5 (lint error).

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > DO NOT: Chain useEffects
text: - If you need 4+ effects, use a phase-gated reducer instead.

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > DO NOT: Chain useEffects
text: - Reference: `useVault.ts` (simplest), `useAuth.ts` (most effects), `useVaultMachine.ts` (`evaluate` pattern).

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > MUST: Generation Counter Discipline in Stores
text: After every `await` in a Zustand store method:

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > MUST: Generation Counter Discipline in Stores
text: 1. Check `if (gen !== _generation) return;` — abort if superseded

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > MUST: Generation Counter Discipline in Stores
text: 2. Check `if (get()._disposed) return;` — abort if store disposed (where applicable)

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > MUST: Generation Counter Discipline in Stores
text: 3. Re-read state via `get()` — never close over stale pre-await values

head: Ichinichi > Architecture Invariants > MUST: Use `reportError()` in New Catch Blocks
text: Every new `catch` block in stores, storage, or domain code must call `reportError(context, error)`. No exceptions. Genuinely intentional suppressions (e.g., DOM range errors, Intl API unavailability) keep `catch {}` but must include `// INTENTIONAL: <reason>`.

head: AGENTS.md > Build & Test
text:
- **Test runtime**: Keep each test under 20 seconds with `-c opt` and under
  60 seconds with `-c dbg`. Simplify oversized fixtures and avoid repeated
  compilation; keep large design benchmarks in their own repositories.

head: AGENTS.md > Build & Test
text:

  benchmark repositories. Test inputs must be provided by this repository or
  declared build dependencies.

head: AGENTS.md > Build & Test
text:
- **External simulators**: the default suite must not need iverilog, vvp,
  verilator or ninja. Optional independent event-simulator legs are skipped
  unless `LHD_EXTERNAL_SIM` is set:
  `bazel test --test_env=LHD_EXTERNAL_SIM=1 --test_env=PATH=<dir-with-tools>:$PATH <target>`.
  A requested leg whose tool is missing FAILS rather than skipping.

head: AGENTS.md > Sibling Repositories (DO NOT search the filesystem for these)
text: **Rule:** if you need anything from one of these libraries (e.g. `grammar.js`, `tree.hpp`, `graph.hpp`, `attr.hpp`), open it directly at the path above. Do **not** start a `find / ...`, `find . ...`, or recursive `grep` to locate them — they are always at these fixed sibling paths. The bazel build fetches them as git-pinned plain repos (`use_repo_rule git_repository` in `MODULE.bazel`, NOT `bazel_dep` + `git_override`, so livehd stays self-contained when consumed as a bazel dependency); each has a commented `local_repository` swap for co-development against the sibling checkout. Running a broad `find` is wasteful and frequently the wrong tool; go straight to the known path.

head: AGENTS.md > Tree library
text:
LiveHD's tree IRs (LNAST, parser AST) sit on top of HHDS (`@hhds//hhds:core`,
headers `hhds/tree.hpp`, `hhds/attr.hpp`). New tree code should use
`hhds::Tree` + `hhds::Forest` and attach per-node payload via `flat_storage`
attribute tags — see `lnast/lnast_attrs.hpp` for the pattern. Pass-local
state should live in `absl::flat_hash_map<Tree_class_index, T>` side maps
rather than registering throwaway attributes. Legacy `core/lhtree.hpp` is
gone; do not reintroduce `lh::tree` / `lh::Tree_index`.

head: AGENTS.md > lhd CLI (EPRP underneath)
text:
One stateless invocation per flow; pass flags ride `--set pass.flag=value`
(or a `--config lhd.toml`), outputs are typed `--emit`/`--emit-dir` slots,
per-step logs land under `--workdir`. Examples:
```
lhd compile foo.v --top foo --emit verilog:out.v
lhd compile foo.prp --emit-dir lg:foo_lgs/ --emit-dir lnast-dump:dumps/
lhd lec --impl verilog:out.v --ref verilog:foo.v --top foo
lhd synth foo.prp --top foo --workdir W --stats   # compile -> color synth -> abc -> opentimer, one shot
```
Graph compilation always runs constant propagation followed by bitwidth
inference. There is no optimization-level or `--recipe` selection. Comb
inlining defaults on; use `--set compile.upass.inline=false` when preserving
comb module boundaries is part of the flow.

head: AGENTS.md > lhd CLI (EPRP underneath)
text:
`lhd synth` is the fused synthesis flow (reports in `W/synth/`; `--emit-dir
lg:` / `verilog:` for the mapped netlist, `report:` for the sidecars); the
individual `lhd pass color|abc|opentimer` steps remain for any other
coloring or for inspecting intermediates. Every persistent reuse tier (the
compile cache, `abc_cache/`, `usyn_cache/` including its optional `tmap/` stage,
`sta_cache/`, the formal verdict cache) lives under a
user-named `--workdir` and follows the ONE switch `--set
lhd.incremental=true|false` (default true) — there is no per-tier cache flag.
Internally lhd drives the registered EPRP methods (conceptually the pipe
`inou.yosys.tolg |> pass.cprop |> inou.cgen.verilog`); pass/inou names in
`--set` and the step logs use that vocabulary.

head: AGENTS.md > lhd CLI (EPRP underneath)
text:
**Measuring reuse after a rebuild — read this before believing a cache miss.**
Each tier is salted by a build-time content hash of the code that produces what
it stores, so **the first run after you touch that code is a full miss, by
design**: the synthesis salts are layered -- `//pass/synth:synth_salt` hashes
`pass/synth` + the passes a mapped region depends on (graph, memory RTL,
cprop, enableopt, bitwidth, color, the DFF pick, formal, `pass/partition`),
`//pass/abc:abc_salt` hashes `pass/abc` + `synth_salt` + `MODULE.bazel` + the
ABC patch, and `//pass/usyn:usyn_salt` hashes `pass/usyn` + `synth_salt` (no ABC dependency) --
`//pass/opentimer:sta_salt` hashes `pass/opentimer` + `pass/partition` +
`MODULE.bazel`, `//lhd:formal_salt` hashes the prover (`pass/lec`, `pass/semdiff`,
the cvc5 pin) + the proof preparation whose output the verdict cache digests
(`pass/single_edge`, graph, cprop, `lhd/lhd_kernel_formal.cpp`), and
`//lhd:compile_salt` likewise. Even a `clang-format -i` counts. Always run the warm command **twice**
after a rebuild and read the second number, and never rebuild in the middle of a
measurement sweep — a cold pass stored under salt A and a warm pass loaded under
salt B looks exactly like "the cache forgot everything".

head: AGENTS.md > Running Pyrope Tests
text: - **Single test (harness)**: `python3 inou/prp/tests/pyrope_test.py -i inou/prp/tests/<dir>/<test>.prp`

head: AGENTS.md > Running Pyrope Tests
text: - **Direct pipeline (comptime)**: `./bazel-bin/lhd/lhd compile <test>.prp --set upass.verifier=true --set upass.verifier_pass=1 --set upass.verifier_fail=0 --emit-dir lnast-dump:dumps/ --workdir w` (the post-upass LNAST text lands in `dumps/*.lnast`; uPass stdout diagnostics in `w/logs/*pass_upass*.log`)

head: AGENTS.md > Running Pyrope Tests
text: - Test header `:type:` selects the pipeline (`parsing`, `lnast`, `upass`, `comptime`, `lgraph`, `compile`); `:verifier_pass:` / `:verifier_fail:` set expected cassert tallies for `comptime`.

head: AGENTS.md > Running Pyrope Tests
text:
- **Expected-failure tests** (`:type: error`, in `inou/prp/tests/errors/`): the program **must** emit a compile error (a diagnostic — see the *Diagnostics* section of the [LiveHD docs](https://masc-ucsc.github.io/docs/livehd/02-usage/)). The header's `:error:` and `:help:` values are matched (Python `re.search`, with a literal-substring fallback when the value is not a valid regex — so `')'` works) against the emitted diagnostic's `message` and `hint`. A compile error exits non-zero cleanly (no abort) in every build mode. To pin the **line**, put a `locate_error_here` comment on the expected-error line — the harness checks the diagnostic's `start_line` matches it (a marker survives inserting/removing lines above, unlike a hard-coded number; the token `locate_error_here` is reserved — don't use it in prose, and only use it when the diagnostic actually carries a span — many `upass` errors don't yet). Diagnostics are read from the JSONL file declared via `lhd --emit diagnostics:PATH` (the hermetic kernel ignores the old `LIVEHD_DIAG` env). Each `tests/errors/*.prp` auto-generates a `prp-<name>` `bazel test` target. Example:
  ```
  /*
  :name: unbalance
  :type: error
  :error: ')'
  :help: unbalance
  */
  comb foo( -> (z) { z = b#[1,4] }   // locate_error_here  (missing ')')
  ```

head: AGENTS.md > Running Pyrope Tests
text: - **Equivalence tests** (`inou/prp/tests/equiv/`): two axes, and a design can sit on both. `foo.prp` + a hand-written `foo.v` is the Pyrope↔Verilog pair (`:type: equiv`, target `prp-equiv-foo`). `foo.prp` + `foo_1.prp`, `foo_2.prp`, … is a Pyrope↔**Pyrope** group: every numbered sibling is LEC'd against the base by `inou/prp/tests/prplec.py` (target `prp-lec-foo_1`), wired by the file NAME alone — a new claim is one new file, no script and no BUILD edit. A HEADER-ONLY variant means "the base source with MY `:set:` flags" (that is how rolled-vs-unrolled is written without duplicating the design). Per-variant header tags `:lec_expect: proven|refuted`, `:lec_sweep:`, `:lec_grep:` / `:lec_grep_not:`; run one by hand with `./inou/prp/tests/prplec.py inou/prp/tests/equiv/foo.prp`. See `inou/prp/tests/equiv/README.md`.

head: AGENTS.md > Running Pyrope Tests
text: - **Expected-warning tests** (`:type: warning`, in `inou/prp/tests/warnings/`): the lint counterpart of `tests/errors/`. The program **must compile cleanly** (exit 0, no `error` diagnostic) yet emit at least one **warning** diagnostic. The header's `:warning:` and `:help:` values are matched (same `re.search` + literal fallback) against the warning's `message` / `hint`; a `locate_warning_here` comment pins the warning's `start_line`. Each `tests/warnings/*.prp` auto-generates a `prp-warn-<name>` `bazel test` target. See `inou/prp/tests/warnings/README.md`. Example: a pure expression used as a statement (`a + 1`) triggers `unused-expression`.

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Running Yosys tests
text: - **Single test**: `./inou/yosys/tests/yosys_compile.sh ./inou/yosys/tests/<test>.v` (or `bazel test //inou/yosys:yosys_compile-<test>`)

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Running Yosys tests
text: - **Full suite**: `./inou/yosys/tests/yosys_compile.sh`

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Running Yosys tests
text:
- The script drives `lhd compile`/`lhd lec`; each test gets a fresh scratch
  `--workdir` (no shared `lgdb` state to clean — the kernel is stateless).
  Per-step logs (yosys chatter included) are under `tmp_yosys/<top>/logs/`.

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Inspecting intermediates
text: - **Yosys RTLIL dump**: After running tolg, check `pp.il` for what Yosys produced (cell types, port connections, parameters).

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Inspecting intermediates
text: - **LGraph dump**: `./bazel-bin/lhd/lhd compile <file> --reader yosys-verilog --top <top> --emit-dir verilog:out/ --workdir w` then read the per-step logs in `w/logs/` and grep the cgen output in `out/*.v` for cell types (e.g., `grep -i mem`). (The REPL-only `lgraph.dump` text dump has no lhd emit yet.)

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Inspecting intermediates
text: - **Generated Verilog**: Check the `--emit-dir verilog:` per-module output; `tmp_yosys_mix/all_<top>.v` is the concatenated file used by LEC in `yosys_compile.sh`.

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Yosys memory pass
text: - `inou/yosys/inou_yosys_read.ys` controls the Yosys script. The `memory -nomap` pass collects `$memrd`/`$memwr`/`$meminit` into `$mem_v2` cells without decomposing into DFFs. Using plain `memory` decomposes small memories into DFFs+muxes, bypassing LGraph memory handling.

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Memory cell types
text: - Modern Yosys produces `$mem_v2` (not `$mem`). Match both: `cell->type == "$mem" || cell->type == "$mem_v2"`.

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Memory cell types
text: - Do NOT use `strncmp("$mem", 4)` — it catches `$memrd`/`$memwr`/`$meminit` which have different port structures.

head: AGENTS.md > Debugging Yosys-to-LGraph Flow > Memory cell types
text: - Memory RTL modules are in `ware/rtl/cgen_memory_*.v`. The `multiclock` variants have per-port clock inputs instead of a shared `clk`.

head: Memory System (nano-brain)
text: This project uses **nano-brain** for persistent context across sessions. Agents talk to the daemon via the registered MCP server `nano-brain` (streamable HTTP at `/mcp`).

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference
text: All operations are MCP tool calls. Every tool takes a `workspace` (SHA-256 hash; resolve once via `memory_workspaces_resolve` with `{path: "<project root>"}`).

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference
text:
| I want to... | MCP tool | Required args |
|---|---|---|
| Recall past work on a topic | `memory_query` | `workspace`, `query` |
| Find exact error/function name | `memory_search` | `workspace`, `query` |
| Explore a concept semantically | `memory_vsearch` | `workspace`, `query` |
| Save a decision for future sessions | `memory_write` | `workspace`, `content` (+ `tags`, `title`) |
| Catch up at session start | `memory_wake_up` | `workspace` |
| Fetch one doc by ID/path | `memory_get` | `workspace`, `path` |
| Check daemon health | `memory_status` | (none) |
| List all registered workspaces | `memory_workspaces_list` | (none) |

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > Session Workflow
text: **Start of session:** List workspaces first, then resolve and query.

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > Session Workflow
text:
**If you don't know the workspace path:**
```
memory_workspaces_list()  // → find workspace by name or path
```

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > Session Workflow
text: **End of session:** Save key decisions, patterns discovered, and debugging insights.

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > Code Intelligence Tools
text: Symbol-level analysis (requires the workspace to be indexed by the daemon's watcher — check `memory_status.queue_pending` if results are empty).

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > Code Intelligence Tools
text:
| I want to... | MCP tool |
|---|---|
| Find 1-hop callers/callees of a symbol | `memory_graph` |
| Assess risk of changing a symbol (reverse impact BFS) | `memory_impact` |
| Find what a symbol depends on (forward traversal) | `memory_impact` (direction="out") |
| Trace forward call chain from an entry point | `memory_trace` |
| Find a symbol by name/kind across the workspace | `memory_symbols` |

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > When to Search Memory vs Codebase vs Code Intelligence
text: - **"Have we done this before?"** → `memory_query` (searches past sessions + decisions)

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > When to Search Memory vs Codebase vs Code Intelligence
text: - **"Where is this in the code?"** → grep / ast-grep (searches current files)

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > When to Search Memory vs Codebase vs Code Intelligence
text: - **"How does this concept work here?"** → both (memory for past context + grep for current code)

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > When to Search Memory vs Codebase vs Code Intelligence
text: - **"What calls this function?"** → `memory_graph(node="<name>", direction="in")`

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > When to Search Memory vs Codebase vs Code Intelligence
text: - **"What breaks if I change X?"** → `memory_impact(node="<name>", max_depth=2)`

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > When to Search Memory vs Codebase vs Code Intelligence
text: - **"What does X depend on?"** → `memory_impact(node="<name>", direction="out")`

head: Memory System (nano-brain) > Quick Reference > When to Search Memory vs Codebase vs Code Intelligence
text: - **"Walk the call chain from entry point X"** → `memory_trace(node="<name>", max_depth=5)`

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply)
text: Reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Apply to every task regardless of scope.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply)
text: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 1. Think Before Coding
text: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 1. Think Before Coding
text: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 1. Think Before Coding
text: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them — don't pick silently.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 1. Think Before Coding
text: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 1. Think Before Coding
text: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 2. Simplicity First
text: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No features beyond what was asked.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No abstractions for single-use code.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 2. Simplicity First
text: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 2. Simplicity First
text: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 2. Simplicity First
text: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 3. Surgical Changes
text: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 3. Surgical Changes
text: When editing existing code:

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > 3. Surgical Changes
text: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture
text:
**Stack:** Go 1.23, PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector 0.8.2, Echo v4, sqlc, goose v3, zerolog, koanf, fsnotify.
**Binary:** `CGO_ENABLED=0` static build. No DI framework. Constructor injection throughout.
**Entry:** `cmd/nano-brain/` — CLI dispatcher + server startup. `internal/` — 17 packages.
**Injection pattern:** config, logger, `*pgxpool.Pool` passed at construction; `sqlc.Queries` wraps the pool.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture > Agent-Oriented Design Principles
text: nano-brain is **built for agents, not humans**. Every design decision optimizes for how agents actually work:

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture > Agent-Oriented Design Principles
text: 1. **MCP is the primary interface.** Agents call tools, not REST APIs. Every capability is a tool call.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture > Agent-Oriented Design Principles
text: 2. **50ms latency target for code intelligence.** Agents skip tools that are slow. `memory_impact`, `memory_trace`, `memory_graph` must be sub-50ms.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture > Agent-Oriented Design Principles
text: 3. **Impact analysis is the #1 use case.** "What breaks if I change this?" — the most common agent query. Pre-computed blast radius via reverse BFS.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture > Agent-Oriented Design Principles
text: 4. **Call chains > control flow.** Agents trace execution across files (inter-procedural), not within functions (intra-procedural). Optimize `memory_trace` and `memory_graph` over `memory_flowchart`.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture > Agent-Oriented Design Principles
text: 5. **Component composition > internal logic.** For frontend frameworks, "who uses this component?" is more valuable than "what does the template do?"

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture > Agent-Oriented Design Principles
text: 6. **Session continuity matters.** Agents work across sessions. `memory_write` at end of session, `memory_wake_up` + `memory_query` at start.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Project Architecture > Agent-Oriented Design Principles
text: 7. **Structured results, not raw bytes.** Agents don't want 500-line file dumps. They want structured data: symbol names, line numbers, edge lists, blast radius counts.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Autonomous Delivery Protocol (DEFAULT MODE)
text: When Tâm gives an implementation/bugfix directive — "fix …", "giải quyết …", "làm cái này/cái kia", or any request to change behavior (not a question) — drive it to **DONE** through the full GSD pipeline. Do not stop at each gate for approval; Tâm invokes rarely on purpose. Decide and proceed.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Autonomous Delivery Protocol (DEFAULT MODE)
text: 1. **Locate/create the phase.** Existing backlog/roadmap phase → use it. New work → add a phase first (`/gsd-phase` add, or `/gsd-capture --backlog`).

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Autonomous Delivery Protocol (DEFAULT MODE)
text: 2. **Run autonomously:** `/gsd-autonomous --only <N>` → discuss→plan→execute, auto-answered. In discuss, **spawn subagents** (`Explore`/scout) to find the root cause, form your own recommendation, and lock the decisions yourself. `workflow.auto_advance: true` is set so phases self-advance.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Autonomous Delivery Protocol (DEFAULT MODE)
text: 3. **Independent review:** after execute, spawn a **separate** reviewer agent (`gsd-code-reviewer` or `oh-my-claudecode:code-reviewer`) — the author never self-approves in the same context (R88). Apply the fixes it finds.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Autonomous Delivery Protocol (DEFAULT MODE)
text: 4. **Test with evidence:** `go test -race -short ./...` (+ `-tags=integration` when relevant) against **nanobrain_test / :3199** — never the dev DB / :3100, never broad-kill processes. Paste the real output.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Autonomous Delivery Protocol (DEFAULT MODE)
text: 5. **Ship:** `/gsd-ship` → branch from `origin/master`, open the PR.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Autonomous Delivery Protocol (DEFAULT MODE)
text: 6. **PR comments:** address review comments autonomously, re-test, push.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Autonomous Delivery Protocol (DEFAULT MODE)
text: **Stop to ask Tâm ONLY when** a decision is genuinely his: irreversible, a business/product choice, or a real blocker. Everything else — pick the sensible default, note it in passing, keep going.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Key forbidden practices
text: - **No `git push origin <branch>` without first verifying you are ON `<branch>`.** Always run `git branch --show-current` (or check `git status` header) before pushing. Pushing while on the wrong branch silently returns "Everything up-to-date" without error. Use `git push` (no args, relies on upstream tracking) when in doubt.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Key forbidden practices
text: - **Single-trunk model: `master` only.** All feature branches branch from `master` and PR back to `master`. The `b-main` staging branch was retired on 2026-06-01 — no more `b-main → master` promotion step. Every merge to `master` triggers `auto-tag.yml` → `release.yml` → npm publish.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Git push workflow (container environment)
text: `origin` is configured to HTTPS (`https://github.com/nano-step/nano-brain.git`) for both fetch and push — no SSH key required. Push uses the gh credential helper to inject the active token automatically.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Release flow
text: Date-based auto-release pipeline (master push → tag → binaries + npm publish):

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Release flow
text:
| Trigger | Workflow | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `master` push | `.github/workflows/auto-tag.yml` | Compute next tag `v{YYYY}.{M}.{D}.{N}` (e.g. `v2026.5.30.1`) → push tag via `RELEASE_PAT` |
| `v*` tag push | `.github/workflows/release.yml` | Cross-build 4-platform Go binaries (linux/darwin × amd64/arm64) → create GH Release with binaries → `npm publish --tag latest` both `@nano-step/nano-brain` and `nano-brain` (unscoped alias) |
| PR opened/sync | `.github/workflows/gemini-review.yml` → shared `gemini-review.yml@v1` | Gemini code review comment on PR |
| `master` push, PR | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `go build` + `go test -race -short` against ephemeral PG service |

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Release flow
text: Required repo secrets (set via `gh secret set --repo nano-step/nano-brain`):

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Release flow
text:
| Secret | Used by | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `RELEASE_PAT` | auto-tag | Classic PAT with `repo` scope. Required so the tag push re-triggers release.yml (tags pushed by `GITHUB_TOKEN` do NOT trigger downstream workflows — GitHub anti-recursion guard) |
| `NPM_TOKEN` | release.yml (npm-publish job) | `npm token create --read-only=false` (Automation type) for npmjs.org |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | gemini-review | https://aistudio.google.com/apikey |

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Release flow
text: **Tag scheme:** `v{YYYY}.{M}.{D}.{N}` where `N` is the daily run-number (starts at 1, increments per push). Example: `v2026.5.30.1`, `v2026.5.30.2`. The dot before `N` is mandatory — the prior no-dot scheme (`v2026.5.301`) collided between single-digit and multi-digit days.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Release flow

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > Engineering Harness > Release flow
text: **`package.json.version`** stays at `0.0.0-dev` on master. The auto-tag workflow rewrites it in-place from the tag value before `npm publish` — the bump is NEVER committed back to master.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > graphify
text: This project has a knowledge graph at graphify-out/ with god nodes, community structure, and cross-file relationships.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > graphify
text: When the user types `/graphify`, invoke the `skill` tool with `skill: "graphify"` before doing anything else.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > graphify
text: - For codebase questions, first run `graphify query "<question>"` when graphify-out/graph.json exists. Use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for focused concepts. These return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > graphify
text: - Dirty graphify-out/ files are expected after hooks or incremental updates; dirty graph files are not a reason to skip graphify. Only skip graphify if the task is about stale or incorrect graph output, or the user explicitly says not to use it.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > graphify
text: - If graphify-out/wiki/index.md exists, use it for broad navigation instead of raw source browsing.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > graphify
text: - Read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context.

head: Behavioral Guidelines (Always Apply) > graphify
text: - After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).
